title: Dom Perignon P2 2005
bodyHtml:
Originating from France in the Champagne wine region, specifically crafted from a prestigious selection of premier and grand cru vineyards across the Montagne de Reims, Vallée de la Marne, and Côte des Blancs—including the historic Abbey of Hautvillers—Dom Pérignon P2 2005 represents an elevated, deeply resonant, and luminously structured expression of late-disgorged prestige cuvée Champagne. As the flagship prestige cuvée of Maison Moët & Chandon, Dom Pérignon is committed exclusively to single-vintage declarations that embody the creative vision of long-serving chef de caves Richard Geoffroy and his successor Vincent Chaperon. The "P2" designation signifies the wine's Second Plénitude—a transformative stage of heightened energy, complexity, and textural integration achieved only after roughly 16 to 17 years of maturation on the lees in the house's subterranean chalk cellars in Épernay, nearly double the aging time of the original release. Crafted from a rigorous parcel selection of Chardonnay and Pinot Noir harvested during the low-yielding, intensely concentrated 2005 growing season, the wine underwent gentle pressing, temperature-controlled stainless steel fermentation with full malolactic conversion, and prolonged autolytic aging prior to disgorgement with a low Brut dosage. The result is an aristocratic, tactile Champagne celebrated for its dark, smoky mineral intensity, creamy persistence, and seamless structural poise.

The wine presents a luminous, deep golden-yellow colour with radiant amber reflections and an ultra-fine, persistent bead of microscopic bubbles. An expressive, deeply complex bouquet opens with noble aromas of roasted hazelnut, toasted brioche, candied blood orange, and dried apricot, interwoven with sophisticated notes of dark mocha, smoky flint, iodine, crushed chalk minerality, licorice, and warm pastry spice. On the palate, it is full bodied, silken, and energetic, delivering concentrated flavours of preserved lemon curd, baked quince, toasted almond, and savoury autolytic richness, all supported by a bright, mouthwatering spine of vibrant natural acidity. Framed by a creamy, velvety effervescence and a dense, multidimensional mid-palate structure, it concludes with an extraordinarily long, persistent finish marked by lingering citrus zest, toasted grain, and a clean, saline chalk grip. Composed of an intimate, harmonious dialogue between Chardonnay and Pinot Noir, this 2005 P2 release offers an optimal drinking window spanning 2023–2045+. Stylistically, it combines late-disgorged aromatic depth, chiselled mineral tension, and effortless textural refinement.

title: Martin's Lane Naramata Ranch Riesling 2023
bodyHtml:
Originating from Canada in the British Columbia wine region, specifically within the Naramata Bench sub-GI of the Okanagan Valley, Martin's Lane Naramata Ranch Riesling 2023 represents an aristocratic, laser-focused, and terroir-driven expression of single-vineyard cool-climate winemaking. Founded by proprietor Anthony von Mandl as a dedicated, ultra-minimalist winery focused exclusively on single-vineyard Pinot Noir and Riesling, Martin's Lane is housed in an iconic, six-level gravity-flow architectural masterpiece overlooking Okanagan Lake in East Kelowna. Under the visionary guidance of winemaker Shane Munn, the estate practices uncompromising, non-interventionist viticulture and vinification tailored to reveal the distinct geological fingerprint of each site. Sourced from the historic Naramata Ranch vineyard perched high on the eastern slopes above Okanagan Lake, the vines are rooted in glacial till soils rich in decomposed granite, silt, and gravel, cooled by prevailing lake breezes and pronounced diurnal temperature swings. Harvested manually at optimal physiological ripeness with rigorous cluster sorting, the fruit is gently whole-cluster pressed via gravity without mechanical pumping, fermented spontaneously with indigenous yeasts in temperature-controlled stainless steel tanks, and aged on its fine lees for approximately 10 months prior to bottling unfined and unfiltered. The result is a crystalline, bone-dry Canadian Riesling celebrated for its electrifying tension, crushed stone minerality, and multi-decade cellar longevity.

The wine presents a luminous, pale straw-gold colour with vivid green-gold and platinum reflections along the rim. An expressive, intensely aromatic bouquet opens with noble aromas of key lime zest, white peach, crisp green apple, and Meyer lemon blossom, interwoven with sophisticated notes of crushed granite minerality, wet slate, white jasmine, kaffir lime leaf, subtle honeycomb, and a whisper of classic Riesling flinty reduction. On the palate, it is light-to-medium bodied, silken, and electric, delivering concentrated flavours of tart citrus, underripe nectarine, and savoury mineral earth, all propelled by a searing, mouthwatering spine of vibrant natural cool-climate acidity. Framed by a tactile, phenolic mid-palate grip and a chiselled, seamlessly layered structural architecture, it concludes with an extraordinarily long, persistent finish marked by lingering lime pith, orchard fruit purity, and a clean, mouth-watering saline grip. Crafted exclusively from 100% Riesling, this 2023 release offers an optimal drinking window spanning 2025–2042+. Stylistically, it combines German Grosses Gewächs structural precision, Okanagan solar fruit purity, and effortless textural refinement.

title: Chateau Palmer 2023
bodyHtml:
Originating from France in the Bordeaux region, specifically within the Margaux AOC appellation in the Haut Médoc, Château Palmer 2023 represents an aristocratic, velvety, and transcendent expression of Left Bank winemaking. Classified as a Third Growth in the 1855 Classification, Château Palmer has long performed at the qualitative pinnacle of the Médoc, frequently rivaling First Growth peers in prestige and complexity. Situated in the heart of the Margaux appellation on the gentle knolls of the Cantenac plateau, the estate's 66 hectares of vineyards thrive on thin, well-draining Günzian gravel terraces intermingled with sand and clay that directly overlook the Gironde estuary. Under the visionary leadership of chief executive and winemaker Thomas Duroux, Palmer transitioned fully to certified biodynamic viticulture in 2014, treating the vineyard as a living polycultural ecosystem. The cellar work emphasizes plot-by-plot manual harvesting, spontaneous native yeast fermentation in conical temperature-controlled stainless steel vats, and patient maturation for 20 to 22 months in French oak barriques (approximately 50% to 60% new oak) alongside large neutral oak foudres to preserve aromatic purity. Defined by an unusually high proportion of old-vine Merlot for a Left Bank grand vin, the result is a wine of legendary fragrance, cashmere-like texture, and remarkable cellar longevity.

The wine presents a luminous, deep ruby-purple colour with vibrant crimson and violet reflections along the rim. An expressive, highly perfumed bouquet opens with noble aromas of ripe black cherry, crème de cassis, wild blackberry compote, and fresh damson plum, interwoven with sophisticated notes of crushed violet petals, dried lilac, pencil lead graphite minerality, dark cocoa nibs, subtle cigar box, and warm French oak cedar spice. On the palate, it is full bodied, silken, and energetic, delivering concentrated flavours of dark stone fruits, tart cassis, and savoury mineral earth, all supported by a bright, mouthwatering spine of natural cool-climate acidity. Framed by architectural yet remarkably fine-grained velvety tannins and a dense, multidimensional mid-palate structure, it concludes with an extraordinarily long, persistent finish marked by lingering dark berries, dried wild herbs, and a clean, graphite-like mineral grip. Composed of an almost equal blend of Merlot and Cabernet Sauvignon accented with a touch of Petit Verdot, this 2023 release offers an optimal drinking window spanning 2029–2055+. Stylistically, it combines Palmer's hallmark floral opulence, seamless textural luxury, and pure Margaux finesse.

title: Chateau Haut Brion 2023
bodyHtml:
Originating from France in the Bordeaux region, specifically within the Pessac Léognan AOC appellation in the Graves, Château Haut Brion 2023 represents an aristocratic, profound, and historically monumental expression of Left Bank winemaking. Tracing its documented viticultural heritage back to 1521, Château Haut Brion stands as the oldest luxury wine brand in the world and the solitary estate outside the Médoc included among the elite First Growths in the historic 1855 Classification. Situated just outside the city of Bordeaux, the property features a unique terroir composed of two high gravel terraces of Mindel and Günzian quartz, flint, and jasper stones resting over a deep clay-sand and limestone subsoil. Under the ownership of Domaine Clarence Dillon—stewarded by Prince Robert of Luxembourg and managed by deputy managing director Jean-Philippe Delmas alongside technical director Jean-Philippe Masclef—the estate practices rigorous canopy management, manual harvesting, and strict plot-by-plot parcel selection. Vinification occurs in thermo-regulated, double-walled stainless steel and epoxy-lined fermentation vats, followed by maturation for 18 to 22 months in fine-grained French oak barrels (approximately 65% to 75% new oak). The result is an intellectual, multifaceted First Growth celebrated for its intoxicating smoky perfume, seamless cashmere texture, and legendary half-century cellar potential.

The wine presents a luminous, deep opaque ruby-purple colour with vibrant garnet and crimson reflections along the rim. An expressive, highly perfumed bouquet opens with noble aromas of ripe blackcurrant, dark blackberry, cassis compote, and black cherry, interwoven with sophisticated notes of warm cigar box, crushed gravel minerality, dried autumn leaf, fresh violet petal, dark cocoa nibs, and subtle French oak cedar spice. On the palate, it is full bodied, silken, and energetic, delivering concentrated flavours of dark fruits, licorice, and savoury mineral earth, all supported by a bright, mouthwatering spine of natural cool-climate acidity. Framed by architectural, fine-grained velvety tannins and a dense, seamlessly layered mid-palate structure, it concludes with an extraordinarily long, persistent finish marked by lingering dark berries, dried wild herbs, and a clean, graphite-like mineral grip. Composed of a classic blend of Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon, and Cabernet Franc, this 2023 release offers an optimal drinking window spanning 2030–2065+. Stylistically, it combines sovereign First Growth gravitas, signature Graves smoky complexity, and effortless textural refinement.

title: Krug Brut 2000
bodyHtml:
Originating from France in the Champagne wine region, specifically from a meticulous mosaic of premier and grand cru vineyards across the Montagne de Reims, Vallée de la Marne, and Côte des Blancs, Krug Vintage 2000 represents an opulent, dramatic, and profoundly complex expression of prestige cuvée Champagne. Founded in Reims in 1843 by Joseph Krug, the House of Krug is celebrated for its uncompromising philosophy of individualistic parcel-by-parcel vinification and patient cellar maturation. Unlike the house's iconic non-vintage Grande Cuvée, which blends over a hundred wines from a dozen different years, a Krug Vintage is crafted exclusively from the finest wines of a single exceptional year—a release the house affectionately christened "Stormy Indulgence" to reflect the dramatic, tumultuous growing season of 2000. Under the direction of the Krug family and the house tasting committee led by chef de caves Éric Lebel, the selected base wines underwent primary fermentation in small, seasoned 205-litre Argonne oak casks without malolactic fermentation to preserve vital natural tension. Following assemblage, the bottles rested on their lees in Krug’s subterranean chalk cellars in Reims for well over a decade before disgorgement. The result is a monumental, multi-layered Champagne famed for its exotic aromatic richness, silken mousse, and multi-decade cellar longevity.

The wine presents a luminous, deep golden-amber colour with radiant copper-gold highlights and an ultra-fine, persistent bead of microscopic bubbles. An expressive, richly layered bouquet opens with decadent aromas of roasted hazelnut, toasted brioche, candied orange peel, and baked quince, interwoven with sophisticated notes of caramelised apple, gingerbread spice, dark mocha, crushed chalk minerality, dried apricot, and smoky grilled almond. On the palate, it is full bodied, silken, and energetic, delivering concentrated flavours of preserved lemon curd, nougat, roasted chestnuts, and savoury toasted grain, all supported by a bright, mouthwatering spine of vibrant natural acidity. Framed by a creamy, velvety effervescence and a dense, multidimensional mid-palate structure, it concludes with an extraordinarily long, persistent finish marked by lingering citrus zest, toasted pastry, and a clean, saline chalk grip. Composed of a classic Krug blend led by Pinot Noir alongside Chardonnay and Pinot Meunier, this 2000 release offers an optimal drinking window spanning 2014–2040+. Stylistically, it combines sumptuous, exotic richness, aristocratic structural power, and effortless textural refinement.

title: Krug Brut 2003
bodyHtml:
Originating from France in the Champagne wine region, specifically from a curated mosaic of premier and grand cru vineyards across the Montagne de Reims, Vallée de la Marne, and Côte des Blancs, Krug Vintage 2003 represents a singular, bold, and remarkably poised expression of prestige cuvée Champagne. Founded in Reims in 1843 by Joseph Krug, the House of Krug adheres to an uncompromising philosophy of individual plot vinification and extended lees aging. While the extreme heatwave of 2003 led many Champagne houses to bypass a vintage declaration entirely, Krug’s tasting committee, led by chef de caves Éric Lebel, discovered unexpected vibrancy and balance among select parcels, inspiring the house to christen this release "Vivacious Radiance." Crafted exclusively from wines harvested in 2003—with a higher-than-usual proportion of Pinot Noir from the Montagne de Reims alongside Chardonnay and Pinot Meunier—the base wines underwent primary fermentation in small, seasoned 205-litre Argonne oak casks without malolactic fermentation to preserve vital natural tension. Following assemblage, the bottles rested on their lees in Krug’s subterranean chalk cellars in Reims for approximately a decade prior to disgorgement. The result is an extraordinary, sun-kissed Champagne renowned for its expressive fruit generosity, chiselled structural energy, and surprising longevity.

The wine presents a luminous, deep golden-yellow colour with radiant amber reflections and an ultra-fine, persistent bead of microscopic bubbles. An expressive, richly layered bouquet opens with noble aromas of baked golden apple, ripe white peach, candied blood orange, and mirabelle plum, interwoven with sophisticated notes of toasted brioche, roasted almond, honeyed acacia, crushed chalk minerality, ginger spice, and subtle smoky oak pastry nuances. On the palate, it is full bodied, silken, and energetic, delivering concentrated flavours of lemon marmalade, poached pear, roasted hazelnut, and savoury toasted grain, all supported by a bright, mouthwatering spine of vibrant natural acidity. Framed by a creamy, velvety effervescence and a dense, multidimensional mid-palate structure, it concludes with an extraordinarily long, persistent finish marked by lingering citrus zest, warm brioche, and a clean, saline chalk grip. Composed of a Pinot Noir-driven blend balanced by Chardonnay and Pinot Meunier, this 2003 release offers an optimal drinking window spanning 2015–2038+. Stylistically, it combines solar aromatic opulence, unexpected cool-climate tension, and effortless textural refinement.

title: Ardbeg Traigh Bhan 19 Year Old - 700 ml
bodyHtml:
This highly allocated age-stated single malt Scotch whisky originates from the rocky southern coast of the Isle of Islay, crafted at the historic Ardbeg Distillery (founded in 1815). Named after the island’s famous singing sands, Ardbeg 19 Year Old "Traigh Bhan" is produced annually in strictly limited small batches, with each release carrying unique batch codes and slight profile variations. Specifically bottled at 50.3% ABV (100.6 proof)—this expression was distilled from heavily peated malted barley and matured for nearly two decades in a recipe predominantly comprising American oak ex-bourbon barrels paired with seasoned Spanish Oloroso sherry casks. Presented in a standard 700 ml green glass bottle, it is non-chill filtered and bottled with its natural, unadulterated color.

Spirit Description

This single malt displays a bright golden-honey hue with shimmering amber reflections, forming thick, slow-running tears along the glass. On the nose, it is intensely complex, salty, and aromatic, balancing mature maritime character with savory peat smoke. Aromas open with pungent wood smoke, charred pineapple, sweet lime zest, and kippers, followed by rich undertones of dark chocolate, sea spray, medicinal eucalyptus, and toasted hazelnut. On the palate, the 50.3% ABV delivery provides a full, oily, and mouth-coating texture. An initial wave of sweet fudge, lemon meringue, and treacle toffee is quickly matched by bold peat smoke, soot, and chimney ash. Mid-palate layers reveal cayenne pepper, clove, aniseed, and a rich, nutty sweetness derived from the Oloroso sherry wood. The finish is remarkably long, smoky, and warming, trailing off with lingering impressions of smoked paprika, bitter dark chocolate, salty sea brine, and lingering sweet peat embers.

Accolades

Ardbeg Traigh Bhan 19 Year Old stands as one of the most celebrated permanent age-statement series in modern peated whisky. Batch releases in this collection routinely capture Gold and Double Gold honors at the San Francisco World Spirits Competition and the International Spirits Challenge, consistently earning 93–96 point ratings across publications such as Whisky Advocate and The Spirits Business. Critics and collectors frequently praise Batch 3 for its elevated 50.3% ABV presentation, pointing to its harmonious tension between rich, spicy sherry wood and the softened, highly nuanced tertiary peat notes achievable only through prolonged maturation.

title: Mott's Clamato Caesar Original Domestic 341 ml - 24 Cans
bodyHtml:
Mott's Clamato Caesar (Original) is the undisputed king of Canadian Ready-to-Drink (RTD) cocktails and a beloved national institution. Invented in Calgary, Alberta in 1969 by bartender Walter Chell, the Caesar was brought into convenient, ready-to-pour canned format by Mott's—the creator of Clamato juice itself. Designed to capture the exact savory, spicy, and umami-rich profile of a freshly shaken bar Caesar, this domestic classic pairs real Canadian vodka with Mott's signature blend of tomato juice, clam broth, and aromatic spices. It stands as Canada’s ultimate savory cocktail staple, offering consistent, bold flavor in every single pull-tab.

Beverage Description

Mott's Clamato Caesar Original pours a rich, opaque, vibrant crimson-red with a naturally thick, pulpy suspension and a light, fizzy bead of carbonation that settles quickly into a smooth, savory liquid.

  • Aroma: The nose is bold, savory, and unmistakably recognizable. It leads with prominent notes of ripe vine-ripened tomato, briny clam broth, and cracked black pepper, layered over sharp, aromatic undertones of celery salt, Worcestershire sauce, horseradish, and a bright squeeze of fresh lime.

  • Palate: On the tongue, it is full-bodied with a rich, velvety, and lightly effervescent mouthfeel. It opens with an immediate, mouth-watering wave of savory tomato umami and coastal salinity, quickly followed by a warm, building kick of cayenne pepper, horseradish heat, and tangy vinegar. The mid-palate balances the robust spices with a subtle touch of natural tomato sweetness and crisp vodka warmth, concluding with a long, zesty, and deeply savory finish that lingers pleasantly on the tongue.

  • Profile: It sits at a classic cocktail strength of 5.5% ABV and 0 IBU, relying on rich tomato acidity, coastal salinity, and warm spice heat for its structural backbone.

  • Technical Notes: The domestic Canadian formulation is built around a base of pure Canadian grain vodka (unlike malt-based coolers found in other markets), blended directly with Mott's Original Clamato (water, tomato paste, glucose-fructose, vinegar, salt, dehydrated clam broth, and spice extracts). The addition of signature Caesar seasonings; including celery seed, onion powder, garlic, and pepper extracts, creates a shelf-stable emulsion that mirrors a bartender's classic bar-rail build, lightly carbonated to lift the aromatics and lighten the mouthfeel.

title: Silver Oak Napa Valley Cabernet Sauvignon 2022 - Bundle & Save
bodyHtml:
This wine originates from the United States, within California’s North Coast and the Napa Valley AVA. Founded in 1972 by Ray Duncan and Justin Meyer, Silver Oak is one of Napa Valley's most enduring icons, dedicated exclusively to crafting age-worthy Cabernet Sauvignon. First produced in 1979, the Napa Valley bottling is assembled from estate-owned and long-term grower vineyards across premier sub-appellations including Oakville, Rutherford, St. Helena, and Soda Canyon, marrying valley floor richness with hillside structural tension. Directed by the Duncan family and winemaker Nate Weis, Silver Oak’s hallmark philosophy centers on aging exclusively in 100% American oak barrels; crafted at the family’s own cooperage, The Oak Cooperage in Higbee, Missouri, for approximately 24 months, followed by an extended 18-to-20-month bottle aging period before release to ensure seamless integration and immediate drinkability.

Wine Description

This wine displays a deep, opaque ruby-purple hue. On the nose, it opens with a rich, concentrated bouquet of ripe blackcurrant, dark plum, and blackberry compote, interwoven with signature American oak notes of vanilla bean, toasted coconut, baking spices, sweet tobacco, and subtle hints of graphite and dark cocoa. On the palate, it exhibits a full, opulent, and velvety body with a dense mid-palate driven by dark berry fruit, espresso, and savory dried herbs. Fine-grained, muscular tannins and well-integrated natural acidity provide a firm, structured backbone beneath the generous fruit weight. The finish is remarkably long, lush, and persistent, echoing with sweet spice, mocha, and lingering cassis. The varietal composition is a classic Left Bank-inspired blend led by Cabernet Sauvignon (typically 75% to 85%) alongside Merlot, Cabernet Franc, Petit Verdot, and a touch of Malbec. It has an alcohol content of approximately 14.5% ABV and is produced from sustainably farmed vineyards (certified California Sustainable and Napa Green, though not certified organic).

title: Silver Oak Alexander Valley Cabernet Sauvignon 2022 - Bundle & Save
bodyHtml:
This wine originates from the United States, within Sonoma County, California, and the Alexander Valley AVA. Founded in 1972 by Ray Duncan and Justin Meyer, Silver Oak is one of California's most recognizable and iconic Cabernet Sauvignon producers, dedicated exclusively to crafting age-worthy Cabernet Sauvignon. The Alexander Valley bottling, first produced in 1972, is sourced primarily from estate-owned vineyards across the warm, alluvial valley floor and hillsides along the Russian River. Led by winemaker Nate Weis and the Duncan family, the winery’s signature philosophy centers on aging exclusively in 100% American oak barrels (primarily new oak crafted at Silver Oak's own cooperage in Missouri) for approximately 24 months, followed by an extended 14-month bottle-aging regimen prior to release so the wine arrives fully integrated and ready to enjoy upon release.

Wine Description

This wine displays a deep, saturated garnet-purple hue. On the nose, it opens with rich, expressive aromas of ripe blackberry, black cherry, and cassis, layered with signature American oak notes of vanilla bean, toasted coconut, sweet baking spices, cedar, and subtle hints of roasted coffee and dried sage. On the palate, it exhibits a full, plush, and generously textured body with a velvety mid-palate driven by concentrated dark berry fruit and dark chocolate. Ripe, finely integrated tannins and balanced natural acidity provide structure and lift without harshness. The finish is long, warm, and polished, echoing with sweet spice, mocha, and lingering dark fruit.

title: Bottega Gold Rose Brut - 1.5 Litre Bottle - Bundle & Save
bodyHtml:
Colour and Appearance - Brilliant, subtle pink colour, fine and persistent perlage.

Bouquet - Intense, elegant, complex, characterized by floral and fruity notes, mainly mixed berries, currants and wild strawberries.

Taste - Fresh, delicate, soft, structured, with balanced acidity and a pleasant and persistent aftertaste.

title: Burrowing Owl Meritage 2021
bodyHtml:
Burrowing Owl Meritage originates from Canada, specifically from the Black Sage Bench in the Okanagan Valley, British Columbia. Since its first vintage in 1997, it has served as the estate's flagship Bordeaux-style blend. Founder Jim Wyse and the winemaking team follow a philosophy of "premium estate-grown" quality, utilizing gravity-flow technology and careful barrel selection to create a wine that balances power with finesse. The 2020 vintage recently received significant acclaim, including a 94-point rating from Gismondi on Wine.

Wine Description

This Meritage is a bold and structured red, typically presenting a deep ruby to opaque garnet colour. The sensory profile is complex and evolving, featuring a "posh" nose of blackcurrant (cassis), plum, and orange zest, layered with savoury notes of desert sage, tobacco, cedar, and dark chocolate. On the full-bodied palate, it is plush and well-knit, delivering intense flavours of blackberry, blueberry pie, and anise, supported by ripe, silky tannins and a juicy freshness. The finish is long and persistent, often showing hints of graphite minerality and baking spices.

  • Varietal Composition: A blend of the five classic Bordeaux varieties: Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Cabernet Franc, Petit Verdot, and Malbec. Percentages vary by year; the 2020 vintage is 38% Cabernet Sauvignon, 24% Merlot, 23% Cabernet Franc, 8.5% Malbec, and 6.5% Petit Verdot.

  • ABV: Typically between 14% and 14.5%.

  • Ageing: Components are vinified and aged separately for 15–18 months in a combination of French (predominant), Hungarian, and American oak barrels before being blended and aged for an additional 3–4 months.

  • Cellaring: Built for longevity, this wine typically has a cellaring potential of 10+ years.

title: Chateau Canon 2023
bodyHtml:
Originating from France in the Bordeaux region, specifically within the Saint Émilion Grand Cru AOC appellation on the Right Bank, Château Canon 2023 represents an aristocratic, luminous, and chalk-driven expression of Premier Grand Cru Classé winemaking. Situated atop the prized limestone plateau of Saint Émilion, the historic estate has been owned by the Wertheimer family of Chanel since 1996. The vineyards benefit from an extraordinary terroir consisting of shallow clay-loam topsoils sitting directly atop a porous, fossil-rich Asteries limestone bedrock (calcaire à astéries), supplemented by parcels gently sloping down the southern hillside. This geological formation acts as a natural water reservoir, providing the vines with constant hydric balance and optimal drainage throughout hot, dry summer stretches. Under the meticulous stewardship of managing director Nicolas Audebert and cellar master Stéphane Bonnasse, the estate practices plot-by-plot viticulture, gentle manual harvesting in small crates, and optical berry sorting. Vinification takes place in gravity-fed, double-walled temperature-controlled stainless steel vats, followed by maturation for 16 to 18 months in fine-grained French oak barriques (approximately 50% new oak). The result is a benchmark Right Bank masterpiece celebrated for its crystalline red fruit purity, chiselled limestone tension, and multi-decade cellar longevity.

The wine presents a luminous, deep ruby red colour with brilliant magenta and violet reflections along the rim. An expressive, highly perfumed bouquet opens with noble aromas of ripe wild raspberry, red cherry, dark plum compote, and sweet cassis, interwoven with sophisticated notes of fresh crushed chalk minerality, violet petals, dried rosebuds, white pepper, subtle tobacco leaf, and warm French oak pastry spice. On the palate, it is medium-to-full bodied, silken, and energetic, delivering concentrated flavours of crisp red and black stone fruits, tart pomegranate, and savoury mineral earth, all supported by a bright, mouthwatering spine of natural cool-climate limestone acidity. Framed by architectural yet cashmere-textured structural tannins and a chiseled, seamless mid-palate structure, it concludes with an extraordinarily long, persistent finish marked by lingering red berries, dried wild herbs, and a clean, laser-sharp chalky mineral grip. Composed predominantly of Merlot balanced by a significant proportion of Cabernet Franc, this 2023 release offers an optimal drinking window spanning 2029–2055+. Stylistically, it combines Saint Émilion plateau precision, aristocratic weightlessness, and effortless textural refinement.

title: Chateau Calon Segur 2023
bodyHtml:
Originating from France in the Bordeaux region, specifically within the Saint Estèphe AOC appellation in the Haut Médoc, Château Calon Ségur 2023 represents a commanding, noble, and deeply structured expression of northern Left Bank winemaking. Classified as a Third Growth in the historic 1855 Classification, Château Calon Ségur is the northernmost classified growth in the Médoc and one of the oldest estates in the region, once famously owned by the Marquis Nicolas-Alexandre de Ségur. Owned by the French insurance group Suravenir since 2012, the property has undergone an ambitious modernization program, including extensive replanting to increase the proportion of Cabernet Sauvignon and the construction of a state-of-the-art gravity-fed cellar. The 55-hectare vineyard forms a single contiguous block entirely enclosed by ancient stone walls (enclos), situated on a high gravel mound overlooking the Gironde estuary. The soils feature a deep layer of Günzian quartz and gravel over a subsoil of fossil-rich Saint Estèphe limestone and clay, providing exceptional drainage alongside moisture retention during warm summer stretches. Under the direction of managing director Vincent Millet, the estate practices parcel-by-parcel manual harvesting, optical berry sorting, and gentle temperature-controlled fermentation in conical stainless steel vats. Maturation takes place for 18 to 20 months in 100% new French oak barriques. The result is a classic, aristocratic Saint Estèphe celebrated for its brooding dark fruit depth, chiselled mineral backbone, and extraordinary cellar longevity.

The wine presents a luminous, deep opaque ruby-purple colour with vibrant garnet and crimson reflections along the rim. An expressive, highly perfumed bouquet opens with noble aromas of ripe blackcurrant, crème de cassis, dark wild blackberry, and fresh black cherry, interwoven with sophisticated notes of crushed graphite minerality, pencil shavings, tobacco leaf, dark cocoa nibs, subtle dried violets, and warm French oak cedar spice. On the palate, it is full bodied, silken, and energetic, delivering concentrated flavours of dark fruits, licorice, and savoury mineral earth, all supported by a bright, mouthwatering spine of natural cool-climate acidity. Framed by muscular, fine-grained architectural tannins and a dense, multidimensional mid-palate structure, it concludes with an extraordinarily long, persistent finish marked by lingering dark berries, dried herbs, and a clean, saline gravel grip. Composed predominantly of Cabernet Sauvignon complemented by Merlot, Cabernet Franc, and Petit Verdot, this 2023 release offers an optimal drinking window spanning 2030–2060+. Stylistically, it combines classic Saint Estèphe structural power, crystalline mineral tension, and polished modern refinement.

It has an alcohol content of approximately 14.5% ABV and is produced from sustainably farmed vineyards (certified California Sustainable and Napa Green, though not certified organic).

Vintage Quality

The 2022 vintage in Napa Valley was characterized by a warm, dry growing season punctuated by a significant early-September heat spike, requiring meticulous canopy management, early morning picking, and strict berry sorting to retain freshness and prevent over-extraction. Across Silver Oak’s premier Napa Valley parcels, smaller berry sizes yielded grapes with intense color, concentrated dark fruit, and ripe, polished tannins. The 2022 Silver Oak Napa Valley balances generous youthful accessibility upon release with the structural depth to cellar gracefully for 15 to 25+ years.

title: Silver Oak Alexander Valley Cabernet Sauvignon 2022 - 3 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
This wine originates from the United States, within Sonoma County, California, and the Alexander Valley AVA. Founded in 1972 by Ray Duncan and Justin Meyer, Silver Oak is one of California's most recognizable and iconic Cabernet Sauvignon producers, dedicated exclusively to crafting age-worthy Cabernet Sauvignon. The Alexander Valley bottling, first produced in 1972, is sourced primarily from estate-owned vineyards across the warm, alluvial valley floor and hillsides along the Russian River. Led by winemaker Nate Weis and the Duncan family, the winery’s signature philosophy centers on aging exclusively in 100% American oak barrels (primarily new oak crafted at Silver Oak's own cooperage in Missouri) for approximately 24 months, followed by an extended 14-month bottle-aging regimen prior to release so the wine arrives fully integrated and ready to enjoy upon release.

Wine Description

This wine displays a deep, saturated garnet-purple hue. On the nose, it opens with rich, expressive aromas of ripe blackberry, black cherry, and cassis, layered with signature American oak notes of vanilla bean, toasted coconut, sweet baking spices, cedar, and subtle hints of roasted coffee and dried sage. On the palate, it exhibits a full, plush, and generously textured body with a velvety mid-palate driven by concentrated dark berry fruit and dark chocolate. Ripe, finely integrated tannins and balanced natural acidity provide structure and lift without harshness. The finish is long, warm, and polished, echoing with sweet spice, mocha, and lingering dark fruit.

Vintage Quality

The 2022 vintage in Sonoma County was defined by warm, dry conditions that culminated in an intense early-September heatwave, prompting careful canopy management and rapid, selective harvesting to preserve freshness and prevent over-ripeness. In Alexander Valley, vines with deep root systems and well-managed irrigation navigated the heat to produce smaller berries with concentrated dark fruit flavors, supple tannins, and vibrant depth. The 2022 Silver Oak Alexander Valley delivers immediate generosity and velvety polish upon release while offering the structural balance to cellar gracefully for 12 to 20 years.

title: Ardbeg 17 Year Old
bodyHtml:
This legendary peated single malt Scotch whisky originates from the rugged south coast of the Isle of Islay, produced at the historic Ardbeg Distillery (founded in 1815). Revered as one of the defining bottlings of the distillery's revival era following its reopening under Glenmorangie plc in 1997, Ardbeg 17 Year Old Single Malt Scotch Whisky showcases how heavily peated malted barley mellows, deepens, and rounds across extensive cask aging. Distilled in copper pot stills equipped with Ardbeg's distinctive purifier, the spirit was matured exclusively in selected ex-bourbon American oak casks. Bottled at 80 proof (40.0% ABV) in a standard 750 ml green glass bottle, it became a cult classic among Islay aficionados before its original discontinuation in the mid-2000s, later commemorated and revived in limited release for the Ardbeg Committee.

Spirit Description

This single malt displays a pale golden-straw hue with bright amber highlights and clean, slender tears along the glass. On the nose, it is remarkably delicate, aromatic, and nuanced compared to younger Islay powerhouses: soft, fragrant campfire smoke and maritime sea breeze mingle with candied lemon peel, fresh pine resin, and green apples, followed by creamy vanilla custard, sea salt, beeswax, and dried mint. On the palate, the 40.0% ABV delivery is exceptionally silky, gentle, and elegant. An initial wave of sweet malt, poached pear, and citrus oils glides over the tongue, immediately underscored by a restrained, earthy peat smoke—tar, chimney soot, and iodine—that is completely integrated rather than sharp. Mid-palate complexities reveal roasted almonds, white pepper, subtle aniseed, and delicate wood tannins. The finish is long, dry, and clean, trailing off with lingering embers of sweet peat ash, lemon zest, salty brine, and soft toasted oak.

Accolades

Ardbeg 17 Year Old occupies an iconic, almost mythical status in modern Scotch whisky history. In the early 2000s, it routinely collected Gold and Double Gold honors at the San Francisco World Spirits Competition and the International Wine and Spirit Competition (IWSC), earning 92–95 point ratings from esteemed critics such as Michael Jackson and Jim Murray. Connoisseurs and auction collectors celebrate it as the quintessential example of "gentle giant" Islay whisky, illustrating how patient warehouse maturation can tame intense phenols into exquisite floral, medicinal, and orchard-fruit complexity.

title: Darroze 1964 Armagnac - 700 ml
bodyHtml:
Darroze 1964 Armagnac (part of Les Grands Assemblages or the Unique Collection) is a prestigious vintage brandy curated and bottled by Maison Francis Darroze in Roquefort, Landes, in the heart of Bas-Armagnac, France. Founded by Francis Darroze and now led by his son Marc Darroze, the house is globally revered as one of the foremost independent négociants and cellar masters in Gascony. Rather than blending vintages across multiple decades, Darroze travels to small, family-owned estates throughout Bas-Armagnac to source single-harvest brandies—bottling them without chill filtration, caramel coloring, or artificial additives to preserve the unadulterated character of the 1964 vintage.

Spirit Description

Distilled in the autumn/winter following the 1964 harvest in traditional continuous column alambic armagnacais stills, this spirit is crafted predominantly from classic Bas-Armagnac grape varieties; principally Baco 22A, Ugni Blanc, Folle Blanche, and Colombard, grown in the prized iron-rich tawny sands (sables fauves) of the region. Following distillation, the brandy aged for over four to five decades in local Gascon black oak casks (Monlezun oak). Because Darroze bottles single-estate and single-vintage selections brut de fût (cask strength) or lightly reduced only at the final stage, a 1964 Darroze Armagnac displays extraordinary depth, rancio complexity, and antique wood integration.

  • Colour: Deep burnished mahogany with antique amber and copper highlights.

  • Aroma: Intensely complex, aromatic, and evolved. Opens with rich rancio notes of roasted walnuts, forest floor, and antique polished wood, layered with dried prunes, candied orange peel, dark chocolate, leather, and sweet pipe tobacco.

  • Palate: Full-bodied, velvety, and multi-dimensional on the entry. Lush flavors of baked figs, caramelized dark fruit, and wildflower honey merge seamlessly with toasted hazelnuts, bitter cocoa, espresso, nutmeg, and seasoned Gascon oak tannins.

  • Body: Full-bodied with a luxurious, unctuous, and mouth-coating viscosity.

  • Finish: Exceptionally long, warm, and lingering, trailing off with persistent notes of dried fruit compote, dark cacao, old leather, clove spice, and gentle oak warmth.

  • ABV: Typically bottled at natural cask strength between 44% and 50% ABV (88 to 100 Proof), depending on the specific estate bottling and bottling date.

title: Clarendelle Saint Emilion 2022
bodyHtml:
Clarendelle Saint Emilion is a premium red wine from France, specifically crafted within the prestigious Saint Emilion region of Bordeaux. Created in 2005 by the grandson of Clarence Dillon, the Prince of Luxembourg, the Clarendelle family was inspired by the heritage of excellence at Chateau Haut Brion. The winemaking philosophy focuses on producing high end Bordeaux wines that reflect balance, elegance, and complexity, utilizing the expertise of the oenologists from Domaine Clarence Dillon.

Wine Description

Brilliant colour, with a beautiful, dark red hue. The maturity is evident from the outset, with fleshy red berry aromas, particularly black cherry and blackcurrant. They are followed by some subtle animal notes, hints of forest floor and a dash of violet. The gentle extraction process has yielded a well-balanced and concentrated wine, with velvety smooth tannins. 

The palate is full-bodied and indulgent.  Full-bodied on the palate, it is delicious and very fruity, with notes of cocoa. Hints of spices and liquorice come through on the aftertaste. It displays long-lasting flavours and is silky and delicious throughout. All in all, a delicate yet powerful and wonderfully complex wine.

Food Pairing

This Saint Emilion is well suited to a variety of dishes, particularly those featuring grilled or roasted red meats like ribeye steak and lamb chops. It also pairs beautifully with mushroom based recipes, such as a truffle risotto, or hearty game dishes like duck breast and venison. For a simpler accompaniment, consider hard, aged cheeses like Comté or a rich Brie.

title: Clos du Marquis 2023
bodyHtml:
The name of Clos du Marquis, created in 1902, was inspired by the Petit Clos adjacent to the Château de Leoville, residence of the Marquis de Las Cases. The Clos du Marquis is produced from top terroirs of the Saint-Julien Appellation that were not exclusively part of the old Domaine de Leoville cadastre. These terroirs are located slightly to the west and are surrounded by prestigious Classified Growths, particularly Seconds Crus Classes of Saint-Julien and Pauillac.

The Clos du Marquis offers a fine expression of the Saint-Julien character: structure, complexity, harmony, distinction and ageing potential.

title: Massetino 2024
bodyHtml:
Originating from Italy in the upper Maremma region of coastal Tuscany, specifically within the Bolgheri area under the Toscana IGT classification, Massetino 2024 represents a vibrant, refined, and aristocratic second wine from the legendary Masseto estate. First introduced with the 2017 vintage to mark the official opening of Masseto’s subterranean winery, Massetino was created to allow a strict parcel selection for the grand vin while offering a focused, earlier-drinking window into the estate's blue clay terroir. Cultivated on the same historic coastal hill facing the Tyrrhenian Sea, the vines grow in pliocene-era blue clays (argille azzurre) intermixed with pebbles and marine fossils, which buffer summer heat and supply constant moisture to the root systems. Owned by the Frescobaldi family and directed by estate director Marco Balsimelli, the vineyard is managed with rigorous micro-parcel viticulture, manual harvesting in small 15-kilogram crates, and optical sorting. Vinification takes place in gravity-fed, plot-dedicated concrete tanks with indigenous yeasts, after which the wine ages for approximately 12 to 15 months in fine French oak barriques (around 50% new oak) followed by additional resting in bottle. The result is a luminous, high-calibre Tuscan red distinguished by immediate aromatic generosity, supple cashmere tannins, and pristine varietal tension.

The wine presents a luminous, deep ruby-purple colour with vibrant crimson and magenta reflections along the rim. An expressive, highly perfumed bouquet opens with noble aromas of ripe black cherry, wild blackberry, fresh damson plum, and sweet cassis, interwoven with sophisticated notes of Mediterranean scrub, dark cocoa nibs, dried violets, crushed blue clay minerality, pencil lead, and warm French oak cedar spice. On the palate, it is medium-to-full bodied, silken, and energetic, delivering concentrated flavours of dark stone fruits, tart red currant, and savoury mineral earth, all supported by a bright, mouthwatering spine of natural cool-climate acidity. Framed by architectural, extraordinarily fine-grained velvety tannins and a harmonious, seamlessly layered mid-palate structure, it concludes with a long, persistent finish marked by lingering dark berries, dried wild herbs, and a clean, saline graphite grip. Crafted predominantly from Merlot accented with a judicious proportion of Cabernet Franc, this 2024 release offers an optimal drinking window spanning 2027–2042+. Stylistically, it combines Mediterranean fruit generosity, vibrant structural lift, and effortless textural refinement.

title: Cupcake Red Velvet - Bundle & Save
bodyHtml:
Originating from the United States in California, sourced from top coastal and inland vineyards across regions like Monterey County, Central Coast, and Lodi, Cupcake Vineyards Red Velvet represents a classic, highly popular expression of everyday American red blending. Founded in 2008, Cupcake Vineyards focuses on crafting rich, approachable, and fruit-forward wines designed to feel like a treat. The winery's philosophy centers on blending distinct grape varieties harvested at peak ripeness to achieve a velvety texture, smooth tannins, and delightful aromatic complexity.

Wine Description

The wine presents a dark ruby red colour with deep purple highlights in the glass. An inviting and sweet-scented bouquet opens with plush aromas of ripe dark chocolate, wild blackberry, and juicy red plum, layered with warm accents of sweet vanilla bean, toasted oak, and coconut. On the palate, it is medium to full bodied, soft, and remarkably smooth, delivering generous flavours of black cherry, mocha, and raspberry jam supported by gentle, low-astringency tannins. Balanced by a hint of balanced acidity, it concludes with a rich, silky finish marked by persistent notes of cocoa and baking spice. Composed of a blend of Zinfandel, Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon, and Petite Sirah, it delivers a plush, velvety mouthfeel with lush, dessert-like warmth and easy-drinking appeal.

title: Dorrance Rouge
bodyHtml:
Originating from South Africa in the Western Cape wine region, specifically within the Coastal Region and Swartland/Stellenbosch appellations, Dorrance Rouge represents an expressive, Old World-inspired, and artisanal expression of Cape winemaking. Founded in 2000 by French-born winemaker Christophe Durand alongside his South African wife Sabrina, Dorrance Wines is a boutique urban cellar housed in a historic 19th-century heritage building on Bree Street in the heart of Cape Town. Christophe Durand draws directly on his French heritage and family roots in Rhône and Bordeaux winemaking, sourcing low-yielding, dry-farmed fruit from select decomposed granite, shale, and alluvial vineyard parcels across Paarl, Stellenbosch, and the Swartland. Viticulture emphasizes sustainable farming, low intervention, and harvesting at optimal physiological ripeness to preserve natural acidity. In the urban cellar, winemaking relies on gentle hand-sorting, spontaneous native yeast fermentation in small open-top fermenters, gentle punch-downs, and patient maturation in seasoned French oak barriques and demi-muids. The result is a poised, savoury red blend celebrated for its aromatic complexity, supple tannin architecture, and gastronomic versatility.

The wine presents a luminous, deep ruby red colour with vibrant garnet and crimson reflections along the rim. An expressive, lifted bouquet opens with noble aromas of ripe red cherry, wild blackberry, damson plum, and crushed raspberry, interwoven with sophisticated notes of fynbos scrub, black peppercorn, dried violet petals, graphite minerality, tobacco leaf, and subtle French oak spice. On the palate, it is medium-to-full bodied, silken, and energetic, delivering concentrated flavours of dark berries, tart red currant, and savoury mineral earth, all supported by a bright, mouthwatering spine of natural acidity. Framed by fine-grained, well-integrated tannins and a harmonious, seamlessly layered mid-palate structure, it concludes with a long, persistent finish marked by lingering dark fruits, wild herbs, and a clean, dry mineral grip. Crafted primarily from Syrah blended with Cabernet Sauvignon and supporting Mediterranean varietals, this release offers an optimal drinking window spanning 2024–2034+. Stylistically, it combines French structural finesse, South African coastal vibrancy, and effortless textural refinement.

title: Ogier Ventoux Cotes Du Rhone Red

Stéphane Ogier, who formally joined the family estate in 1997, leads the winery with a winemaking philosophy focused on precision, freshness, and the true interpretation of terroir minerals.

Wine Description

The nose is expressive and powerful, featuring aromas of fresh red fruits, cassis, and black cherry, with nuanced hints of liquorice, pepper, and dark chocolate. On the palate, it is full bodied and fleshy, offering a suave texture with silky, well integrated tannins and a fresh backbone of acidity.

title: Le Carillon d'Angelus 2023
bodyHtml:
Originating from France in the Burgundy-adjacent Right Bank of the Bordeaux region, specifically within the Saint Émilion Grand Cru AOC appellation, Le Carillon d'Angélus 2023 represents an opulent, supple, and masterfully vinified expression from one of Bordeaux's most celebrated estates. First created with the 1987 vintage at the historic Château Angélus, Le Carillon d'Angélus was historically conceived as the estate's second wine but has evolved into a singular, dedicated cru with its own distinct vineyard plots and a state-of-the-art, gravity-fed winery facility inaugurated in Saint Magne de Castillon. The de Boüard de Laforest family has tended the vines of Angélus for eight generations, emphasizing meticulous soil management and certified organic practices. The vineyard sources for Le Carillon thrive across a varied mosaic of cold clay and limestone soils intermixed with clay-sand and gravel, which provide optimal hydric balance and deep root penetration for late-ripening fruit. Under the stewardship of Stéphanie de Boüard-Rivoal and technical director Benjamin Laforest, the grapes are hand harvested, optically sorted, and fermented in temperature-controlled inverted truncated-cone stainless steel and concrete vats. Maturation occurs over 16 months in fine French oak barriques (approximately 50% new oak) and large neutral foudres. The result is an aromatic, silken red Bordeaux that combines immediate textural charm with genuine Right Bank depth and cellar longevity.

The wine presents a luminous, deep ruby red colour with brilliant violet and crimson reflections along the rim. An expressive, highly perfumed bouquet opens with noble aromas of ripe black cherry, wild plum, crushed dark blackberry, and sweet cassis compote, interwoven with sophisticated notes of fresh violet petals, licorice, subtle pencil lead minerality, dark cocoa dust, tobacco leaf, and warm French oak cedar spice. On the palate, it is medium-to-full bodied, silken, and energetic, delivering concentrated flavours of black stone fruits, tart red currant, and savoury mineral earth, all supported by a bright, mouthwatering spine of natural cool-climate acidity. Framed by supple, fine-grained velvety tannins and a dense, seamlessly layered mid-palate structure, it concludes with a long, persistent finish marked by lingering dark berries, dried herbs, and a clean gravelly grip. Composed predominantly of Merlot complemented by Cabernet Franc and a small touch of Cabernet Sauvignon, this 2023 release offers an optimal drinking window spanning 2026–2038+. Stylistically, it combines Right Bank solar fruit generosity, refined floral elegance, and impeccable textural precision.

title: Pichon Comtesse Reserve 2023
bodyHtml:
Originating from France in the Bordeaux region, specifically within the Pauillac AOC appellation in the Haut Médoc, Château Pichon Comtesse Réserve 2023 represents a poised, silky, and aristocratic expression of Left Bank winemaking from one of Bordeaux's premier estates. Château Pichon Longueville Comtesse de Lalande, classified as a Second Growth in the 1855 Classification, has been under the ownership of the Rouzaud family of Champagne Louis Roederer since 2007. First introduced in 1973 as Réserve de la Comtesse and later renamed to emphasize its estate heritage, this cuvée is sourced from selected parcels and younger vines across the property's deep Günzian gravel plateaus resting over clay-limestone subsoils. Situated directly alongside the Gironde estuary and adjoining Château Latour, the vineyards benefit from a moderating maritime microclimate and superb natural drainage. Under the direction of managing director and winemaker Nicolas Glumineau, the grapes are manually harvested, optically sorted, and fermented in gravity-fed, temperature-controlled conical stainless steel vats before maturing for 12 to 14 months in fine French oak barriques (approximately 35% to 40% new oak). The result is an accessible, perfumed, and velvety red Bordeaux that captures Pauillac's noble structural pedigree and the estate's signature textural suppleness.

The wine presents a luminous, deep ruby red colour with brilliant crimson and violet reflections along the rim. An expressive, highly perfumed bouquet opens with noble aromas of ripe blackcurrant, dark blackberry, fresh black cherry, and wild plum compote, interwoven with sophisticated notes of crushed violet petals, pencil lead graphite minerality, tobacco leaf, dark cocoa, cedarwood, and warm French oak pastry spice. On the palate, it is medium-to-full bodied, silken, and energetic, delivering concentrated flavours of crisp black fruits, tart cassis, and savoury mineral earth, all supported by a bright, mouthwatering spine of natural cool-climate acidity. Framed by fine-grained, seamless tannins and a polished, harmonious mid-palate structure, it concludes with a long, persistent finish marked by lingering dark berries, dried herbs, and a clean gravelly grip. Composed of a classic Pauillac blend of Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Cabernet Franc, and Petit Verdot, this 2023 release offers an optimal drinking window spanning 2026–2038+. Stylistically, it combines Pauillac's aristocratic structural drive, velvety fruit charm, and crystalline Left Bank precision.

title: Blason de L'Evangile 2023
bodyHtml:
Originating from France in the Bordeaux region, specifically within the Pomerol AOC appellation on the Right Bank, Blason de L'Évangile 2023 represents a sumptuous, finely textured, and accessible expression from one of Pomerol’s most historic and revered estates. Produced at Château L'Évangile, which has been under the ownership of Domaines Barons de Rothschild Lafite since 1990, Blason de L'Évangile was introduced with the 1990 vintage as the estate's second wine to offer an approachable window into the property's grand vin style while utilizing younger vine plots. Situated on the famous Pomerol plateau bordered by Château Pétrus and Château Cheval Blanc, the vineyard occupies an exceptional terroir composed of deep sandy clay intermingled with pure gravel resting on a subsoil of iron-rich sandstone known locally as crasse de fer. Under the technical stewardship of director Saskia de Rothschild and estate director Juliette Couderc, the property completed its conversion to certified organic viticulture in 2021. The winemaking philosophy emphasizes gentle manual harvesting into small crates, optical berry sorting, parcel-by-parcel fermentation in temperature-controlled concrete vats, and maturation for approximately 15 months in fine French oak barrels (around 20% to 30% new oak) alongside terracotta amphorae to preserve pure fruit vibrancy. The result is an alluring, supple red Pomerol marked by luscious dark fruit, refined mineral freshness, and immediate charm.

The wine presents a luminous, deep ruby red colour with vivid crimson and magenta reflections along the rim. An expressive, highly perfumed bouquet opens with noble aromas of ripe black cherry, wild plum, crushed dark blackberry, and sweet cassis, interwoven with sophisticated notes of fresh violet petals, subtle dark cocoa dust, truffle nuances, pencil lead minerality, and warm French oak pastry spice. Stylistically, it combines Pomerol plush fruit generosity, refined floral elegance, and effortless textural refinement.

title: Nikka Coffey Vodka - Bundle & Save
bodyHtml: Nikka Coffey Vodka is a vodka with flavour and texture.
