Corn and barley are separately distilled into various batches with slight difference in ABV and taste profile. These batches are carefully blended by experts and then refined with white birch charcoal. This vodka with zesty notes, rich sweetness and milky mouthfeel perfectly captures the exquisite fullness brought by the Coffey Still.

title: Old Forester Statesmen
vendor: 300614 - Bf Canada - A Division Of The Hive
bodyHtml:
Old Forester Statesman Kentucky Straight Bourbon Whisky is a premium expression produced by the historic Old Forester Distilling Co. in Louisville, Kentucky (owned by Brown-Forman). Introduced in 2017 in conjunction with 20th Century Fox's motion picture Kingsman: The Golden Circle, Statesman was created to embody the bold, dapper, and refined character of the fictional American allied intelligence agency, the Statesman. Far from a mere novelty movie tie-in, Master Taster Jackie Zykan and Master Distiller Chris Morris formulated the liquid to be a permanent, high-character staple in the Old Forester lineup, pulling exclusively from barrels matured in the hottest sections of the warehouse.

Spirit Description

Statesman is distilled from Old Forester’s signature mash bill of 72% corn, 18% rye, and 10% malted barley, utilizing their proprietary yeast strain and pure limestone-filtered Kentucky water. To achieve its distinctly robust, spicy profile, the liquid is drawn from hand-selected barrels located in the warmest, highest floors of Old Forester’s heat-cycled rackhouses. The sustained heat exposure drives the whiskey deep into the heavily charred white oak barrels, accelerating evaporation and producing pronounced caramelization, intense wood sugars, and bold baking spices. Bottled at a tailored 95 proof (47.5% ABV), it hits an ideal balance of viscosity, heat, and cocktail versatility.

  • Colour: Deep, shimmering amber with copper reflections.

  • Aroma: Bold, aromatic, and spicy upfront. Opens with devil's food cake, dark brown sugar, and toasted oak, followed by fiery cinnamon, cloves, ripe black cherries, and sweet pipe tobacco.

  • Palate: Rich, buttery, and assertive on the entry. Lush vanilla cream, candied citrus peel, and warm caramel lead off, swiftly balanced by bold black pepper, cinnamon heat, leather, and dark charred oak tannins.

  • Body: Medium-to-full-bodied with a warm, velvety, and oily mouthfeel.

  • Finish: Long, dry, and spicy, lingering with charred oak, bittersweet dark chocolate, leather, roasted nuts, and persistent baking spices.

  • ABV: Bottled at 47.5% ABV (95 Proof).

title: Glenfarclas 190th Anniversary - 700 ml
bodyHtml:
Glenfarclas 190 (190th Anniversary) is a landmark, limited-edition Highland single malt Scotch whisky produced by the historic Glenfarclas Distillery in Ballindalloch, Speyside, Scotland. Released in 2026 to commemorate 190 years since the distillery obtained its legal distilling license in 1836, this expression completes the distillery’s acclaimed "Anniversary Trilogy" following the earlier 175th and 185th Anniversary releases. Remaining fiercely independent and operated by the Grant family across six generations, Glenfarclas leverages its extensive warehouse reserves to deliver an intricate vatting that pays tribute to nearly two centuries of traditional direct-fired distillation.

Spirit Description

Glenfarclas 190 was constructed by Distillery Manager Callum Fraser and Managing Director Douglas Belford, who hand-selected and married 78 individual casks spanning five separate decades of distillation (including stocks from the 1970s, 1980s, 1990s, and 2000s). Maturation is predominantly ex-Oloroso sherry oak sourced from a long-standing, family-run bodega in Jerez, Spain. The whisky is bottled with natural color, without chill filtration, and brought specifically to 51.4% ABV, honoring the historic 90 British Proof. The result balances mature, vintage rancio and dark wood with fresh orchard ester complexity.

  • Colour: Deep amber-copper with warm mahogany highlights.

  • Aroma: Complex, layered, and elegant. Opens with fresh green apple, sherry sweetness, and plump sultanas, followed by toffee, black molasses, cocoa, delicate baking spices, and a wisp of earthy tobacco leaf.

  • Palate: Decadent, rounded, and velvety on the entry. Rich Oloroso sherry and spiced Christmas cake lead upfront, yielding to buttery toffee, caramel, milky mocha, roasted walnuts, and deep, malty sweetness.

  • Body: Full-bodied with a luxurious, mouth-coating viscosity.

  • Finish: Exceptionally long, warming, and drying, lingering with dark chocolate, espresso, old oak tannins, and aromatic tobacco.

  • ABV: Bottled at 51.4% ABV (90 British Proof), non-chill filtered and natural colour.

title: Captain Morgan Dark Rum - 1.14 Litre Bottle - Bundle & Save
bodyHtml: This Captain doesn't go unnoticed. With a rich taste and unique depth of flavour, Captain Morgan Dark Rum is the adventurers' delight. Deep amber brown this aromatic rum offers notes of molasses and light spice with toasted oak flavour and light sweetness that is balanced by a dry finish.

title: Lamb's Navy 151 Overproof Rum - Bundle & Save
bodyHtml: Alfred Lamb was known for producing the rum of choice for the British Navy. The hexagon shape of the bottle assured his smooth and refined rum wouldn't roll around on ships. At 151 proof, this rum is great for cocktail mixing.

title: Stolichnaya Vodka - Bundle & Save
bodyHtml: Stoli Vodka is the original premium vodka that combines modern distilling of the highest quality spirit with century-old traditions to create its bold character.

title: Grey Goose Berry Rouge - Bundle & Save
bodyHtml:
Grey Goose Berry Rouge, officially marketed as Grey Goose Essences Strawberry & Lemongrass, is a low-ABV botanical spirit produced in the Cognac region of France. Crafted by Cellar Master François Thibault under parent company Bacardi, the Essences line was created to meet the growing demand for natural, lower-alcohol, zero-sugar options. Combining classic French winter wheat vodka with real fruit essences and cold-distilled botanicals, this red-berry expression offers a light, aromatic alternative to traditional sweet flavored vodkas.

Spirit Description

Grey Goose Essences Strawberry & Lemongrass starts with the brand's core 100% soft winter wheat vodka from Picardie, continuous-distilled and blended with limestone-filtered spring water from Gensac-la-Pallue. Real field-ripened strawberries and cold-distilled lemongrass botanicals are infused into the distillate. Bottled with zero added sugars or carbs, it delivers a crisp, natural red-berry profile backed by clean herbal citrus.

  • Colour: Crystal clear, luminous, and transparent (utilizing natural essence extraction rather than artificial red dyes).

  • Aroma: Bright and highly aromatic, opening with ripe wild strawberry, fresh garden mint, and sweet citrus blossom, anchored by crisp, herbal lemongrass notes.

  • Palate: Crisp, light, and delicate on the entry. Upfront flavors of juicy red strawberry and light raspberry give way to zesty citrus peel, herbal lemongrass, and a clean wheat grain structure without any cloying syrup sweetness.

  • Body: Light-bodied, clean, and palate-cleansing.

  • Finish: Crisp, dry, and short-to-medium in length, leaving lingering notes of fresh strawberry, subtle citrus zest, and a herbal snap.

  • ABV: Bottled at 30% ABV (60 Proof).

title: Michter's US*1 Single Barrel Straight Rye
bodyHtml:
Introduction

Michter's US*1 Single Barrel Straight Rye is a straight rye whiskey from the country of the United States. The Michter's lineage traces its origins back to Shenk's Distillery, founded in 1753 in Schaefferstown, Pennsylvania, a legacy that Michter's honours as America's first whiskey company. The company today is headquartered in Kentucky, and its US*1 expressions are named to honour this heritage. This expression is a benchmark for rye whiskey and is bottled from a single barrel.

Spirit Description

Michter's US*1 Single Barrel Straight Rye is produced from a mash bill that meets the legal requirements for a straight rye, meaning it contains at least 51% rye grain. It is aged in fire-charred, new American white oak barrels. The whiskey has a rich, golden amber colour. On the nose, it is spicy and complex, offering aromas of dark fruit, plum, brown sugar, cinnamon, and subtle notes of tobacco and rye. The palate is full-bodied and soft, with a harmonious balance of deep spice and sweet fruit. It features notes of dark cherries, dried plum, honey, toffee, and a noticeable rye spice. The finish is long and dry, with warming pepper, balanced caramel, and a sweet, lingering spice. It is bottled at 42.4% ABV.

title: Hennessy Richard 2.0
bodyHtml:
Richard Hennessy is the crown jewel of Maison Hennessy, created in 1996 as a tribute to the Irish founder who established the cognac house in 1765. The modern iteration—often referred to as "Richard Hennessy 2.0"—was unveiled in 2022 featuring a striking, architectural redesign by visionary architect Daniel Libeskind. The bespoke Baccarat crystal decanter sits encased within a geometric crystal frame that contrasts sweeping curves with sharp, dynamic facets, revitalizing this ultra-prestige blend for contemporary luxury collectors.

Spirit Description

The liquid represents a pinnacle assemblage crafted from some of the rarest, oldest eaux-de-vie preserved in Hennessy’s historic Paradis cellar, with components dating back to the early 19th and 20th centuries.

  • Colour: Deep, glowing mahogany with fiery ruby and amber reflections.

  • Aroma: Exquisitely layered; opens with rich leather, tobacco leaf, and rancio, followed by candied orange peel, dried apricots, crushed hazelnuts, and antique French oak.

  • Palate: Silky, multidimensional, and remarkably dense. Waves of stewed dark plums, dried figs, and dark cocoa evolve into warm spices like nutmeg and cinnamon, framed by precious cigar box and beeswax.

  • Body: Full-bodied, velvety, and profound with an expansive viscosity that coats the entire palate.

  • Finish: Exceptionally long and resonant, echoing with lingering notes of warm rancio, leather, dried fruit compote, and subtle floral elegance.

  • ABV: Bottled at 40% ABV.

Accolades

Richard Hennessy is universally regarded by connoisseurs and sommeliers as one of the finest, most exclusive cognacs ever blended.

  • Design Prestige: The collaboration with Daniel Libeskind earned acclaim across design and luxury industries, marrying century-old craft with avant-garde sculpture.

  • Master Blender Legacy: Celebrated as a landmark creation bridging multiple generations of the Fillioux family, Hennessy’s hereditary Master Blenders.

  • Collector Benchmark: Produced in strictly limited annual quantities (often limited to roughly 12 tierçons per year), commanding valuations in the realm of five figures at retail and elite auctions.

title: Contucci Vino Nobile Riserva 2019
bodyHtml:
This wine originates from Italy, within the southeastern hills of Tuscany and the Vino Nobile di Montepulciano Riserva DOCG appellation. The Contucci family is among the founding viticultural families of Montepulciano, documenting winemaking roots back to the 11th century. Operating out of their historic multi-level cellars constructed beneath their Renaissance palace in Piazza Grande, the estate represents the pinnacle of traditional Tuscan winemaking. Sourced from the estate’s oldest, low-yielding plots across prime clay, sand, and limestone soils (between 280 and 450 meters elevation), this Riserva is produced only in favorable vintages. Contucci’s winemaking philosophy relies on classic extended skin contact, temperature-controlled fermentation with wild yeasts in concrete and stainless steel, and long aging for over three years in large, neutral Slavonian and French oak casks (botti) followed by extensive bottle aging, avoiding small barriques to ensure pure terroir transparency and structural integrity.

Wine Description

This wine displays a deep, luminous garnet-red color with brick-orange highlights at the rim. On the nose, it reveals a layered, traditional bouquet of wild red currants, black cherry, and dried cranberries, interwoven with dried herbs, blood orange peel, sweet tobacco, worn leather, and subtle hints of cocoa and forest floor. On the palate, it exhibits a medium to full body with a taut, tightly coiled, and deeply savory profile. The structure is built around dense, fine-grained, grippy tannins and a vibrant core of mouthwatering natural acidity. The finish is long, dry, and classically austere, echoing with notes of sour red cherry, iron, dried mint, and crushed stone minerality. The varietal composition is a traditional blend of 80% Prugnolo Gentile (Sangiovese), 10% Canaiolo Nero, and 10% Colorino.

title: Contucci Mulinvecchio Vino Nobile Di Montepulciano 2021
bodyHtml:
This wine originates from Italy, within the southeastern hills of Tuscany and the Vino Nobile di Montepulciano DOCG appellation. The Contucci family is among the oldest viticultural dynasties in Italy, cultivating vines in Montepulciano since the 11th century and operating from their historic Renaissance palazzo cellars in the town center. Mulinvecchio is the estate’s premier single-vineyard cru, sourced from approximately one hectare of 25-year-old vines perched between 350 and 450 meters elevation on Pliocene-era tufa sand and clay soils. Contucci’s winemaking philosophy is staunchly classical and non-interventionist: fermentation with indigenous yeasts in steel and concrete vats, followed by 30 months of maturation in traditional medium-to-large Slavonian and French oak casks (botti) and subsequent bottle aging, avoiding modern barrique influence to prioritize terroir transparency and savory structural longevity.

Wine Description

This wine displays a deep, luminous garnet-ruby hue. On the nose, it reveals a complex and traditionally styled bouquet of wild dark cherries, macerated plums, and dried roses, layered with notes of cured leather, pipe tobacco, forest undergrowth, dried herbs, and a subtle balsamic touch. On the palate, it exhibits a medium to full body with a firm, classically dry, and savory mouthfeel. Ripe red and black cherry flavors are tightly wound around a core of powdery, fine-grained structural tannins and a vibrant vein of refreshing acidity. The finish is long, linear, and earthy, with lingering echoes of sour cherry, dried orange peel, and crushed stone minerality. The varietal composition is a traditional Tuscan blend of 80% Prugnolo Gentile (Sangiovese), 10% Canaiolo Nero, and 10% Colorino.

title: Laurent Miquel Solas Albarino 2025
bodyHtml:
This wine originates from France, within the Languedoc-Roussillon region under the Pays d'Oc IGP (and Aude IGP) designation. Laurent Miquel, alongside his Irish wife Neasa, is renowned for pioneering non-traditional varieties in southern France and was among the very first French vignerons to plant and champion Albariño on French soil. The name Solas derived from the Irish Gaelic word for "light" embodies the range’s focus on pure, vibrant, and unencumbered fruit character. Grown on high-elevation limestone plots in the foothills of the Corbières and Aude valleys (at around 200 meters altitude), the vines benefit from cool night breezes. The winemaking philosophy focuses on night harvesting, gentle pneumatic pressing, cool temperature-controlled fermentation (around 16–17°C), and aging exclusively on the fine lees in stainless steel to retain zesty acidity, saline freshness, and varietal lift.

Wine Description

This wine displays a bright pale straw-yellow hue with green-gold highlights. On the nose, it reveals an expressive and refreshing bouquet of white grapefruit, crisp green apple, and fresh pear, intertwined with white peach, preserved lemon zest, delicate floral blossom, and subtle tropical nuances. On the palate, it exhibits a medium-light body with a clean, lively, and juicy mouthfeel. A vibrant core of stone fruit and exotic citrus is driven by a zesty spine of refreshing acidity and a distinct, lip-smacking saline minerality. The finish is crisp, mouthwatering, and dry, leaving persistent notes of citrus peel and crushed rock.

title: Laurent Miquel Solas Viognier 2025
bodyHtml:
This wine originates from France, within the Languedoc region under the Pays d'Oc IGP appellation. Established in 1791 at Château Cazal Viel, the family-owned Laurent Miquel estate is widely recognized as one of the pioneers of quality Viognier cultivation in southern France. Named Solas, the Irish Gaelic word for "light," chosen by Laurent’s Irish wife and co-vigneronne, Neasa, the cuvée is designed to deliver pure varietal expression without excessive heaviness or flabbiness. The estate's philosophy emphasizes nocturnal harvesting to preserve natural acidity, gentle pneumatic pressing, cool temperature-controlled fermentation, and maturation exclusively on fine lees in stainless steel vats to highlight aromatics, mineral cut, and freshness.

Wine Description

This wine displays a brilliant pale golden-straw hue with green highlights. On the nose, it opens with pure and lifted aromas of ripe apricot, white peach, and orange blossom, complemented by honeysuckle, green apple, and a delicate touch of raw almond. On the palate, it exhibits a balanced, medium body with a smooth, supple texture countered by clean natural freshness. Flavors of stone fruit and candied citrus zest are balanced by vibrant, food-friendly acidity that prevents the oily viscosity typical of warmer-climate Viognier. The finish is clean, dry, and persistent, echoing with delicate floral perfume and subtle mineral notes.

title: Ca dei Frati Rosa dei Frati 2025
bodyHtml:
This wine originates from Italy, situated in the Lombardy and Veneto border zone along the southern shores of Lake Garda, within the Riviera del Garda Classico DOC (historically classified under Garda Bresciano). Ca' dei Frati, whose estate records trace back to 1782 when it was documented as the "house of the friars," was revitalized in 1939 by Domenico Dal Cero and is recognized as the leading modern benchmark of the Lugana region. Sourced from calcareous, clay-rich morainic soils influenced by the microclimate and mild breezes of Lake Garda, the winery crafts "Rosa dei Frati" as a dedicated, estate-grown rosato rather than a byproduct saignée. The winemaking philosophy centers on direct gentle pressing, brief skin contact to extract delicate color and aromatics, and temperature-controlled stainless steel fermentation and lees aging to maximize freshness, floral lift, and mineral tension.

Wine Description

This wine displays a brilliant pale salmon-pink hue with copper reflections. On the nose, it opens with fragrant, vibrant aromas of wild strawberries, red currants, and tart cherries, complemented by white peach blossom, crisp green apple, and a distinct hint of crushed river stone. On the palate, it exhibits a light to medium body with a crisp, refreshing, and finely etched texture. A juicy burst of fresh red fruit is driven by a vibrant spine of zesty natural acidity and a characteristic saline, mineral core. The finish is clean, dry, and persistent, echoing with lingering citrus peel, small red berries, and delicate savory herbs. The varietal composition is a traditional Garda blend of Groppello, Marzemino, Sangiovese, and Barbera.

title: Domaine Henri et Gilles Buisson Chassagne Montrachet 'Les Encengnieres' 2024
bodyHtml:
Originating from France in the Burgundy region, specifically within the Chassagne Montrachet AOC appellation in the Côte de Beaune, Domaine Henri et Gilles Buisson Chassagne Montrachet 2024 represents a pure, certified biodynamic, and finely chiseled expression of village-level Chardonnay. Tracing their family winemaking lineage in the adjacent high-elevation amphitheatre of Saint-Romain back to 1758, Domaine Henri et Gilles Buisson stands as an early pioneer and benchmark of ecological viticulture in the Côte d'Or. Sourced from meticulously farmed parcels situated on gentle east- and southeast-facing slopes, the vines thrive in deep, stony clay-limestone soils strewn with fractured gravel and limestone marl. Under the direct stewardship of brothers Franck and Frédérick Buisson, the philosophy emphasizes manual harvesting in small bins, pneumatic whole-cluster pressing, spontaneous fermentation with indigenous ambient yeasts, and maturation for 12 to 14 months in fine French oak barrels (approximately 15% to 20% new oak) with light lees contact and no fining or filtration. The result is a vibrant, deeply mineral white Burgundy that unites Chassagne's signature stone fruit power and fleshy mid-palate with the estate's hallmark alpine tension, clarity, and laser-focused precision.

Wine Description

The wine presents a luminous, clear pale straw-gold colour with brilliant platinum and emerald reflections along the rim. An expressive, highly perfumed bouquet opens with noble aromas of ripe Meyer lemon, crisp Bosc pear, yellow apple, and white peach, interwoven with sophisticated notes of acacia flower, toasted hazelnut, crushed limestone minerality, beeswax, lemon verbena, and subtle French oak pastry spice. On the palate, it is medium-to-full bodied, silken, and energetic, delivering concentrated flavours of citrus oil, orchard fruits, and savoury mineral earth, all supported by a bright, mouthwatering spine of natural cool-climate acidity. Framed by a rich, chalky mid-palate structure and seamless phenolic grip, it concludes with a long, persistent finish marked by lingering citrus zest, toasted brioche, and a clean, saline chalky drive. Composed of 100% Chardonnay, this 2024 release offers an optimal drinking window spanning 2026–2036+. Stylistically, it combines biodynamic vitality, classic Chassagne textural breadth, and focused Côte de Beaune mineral energy.

title: Domaine Labruyere Prieur Santenay ‘Grand Clos Rousseau’ Premier Cru 2022
bodyHtml:
This wine originates from France, within the southern end of the Côte de Beaune in Burgundy and the Santenay appellation. Sourced through Labruyère-Prieur Sélection, the high-end négociant project formed between the Labruyère family (owners of Domaine Jacques Prieur since 1988) and long-time enologist Nadine Gublin, the label features premier plots from across the region. While Santenay has no official Grand Cru vineyards under INAO classification, Grand Clos Rousseau (often labeled in reference to Clos Rousseau) is regarded as one of the commune's finest Premier Cru sites. Situated near Maranges on south/southeast-exposed clay, marl, and limestone slopes, the fruit undergoes strict manual sorting, parcel-by-parcel temperature-controlled vinification, and aging in French oak to balance aromatic purity, depth, and structural finesse.

Wine Description

This wine displays a deep ruby color with violet reflections. On the nose, it offers expressive aromas of ripe wild raspberry, black cherry, and red currant, accompanied by notes of crushed violets, forest floor, subtle clove, and gentle toasted oak. On the palate, it exhibits a medium to full body with a focused, silky core of dark red fruit, supported by fine-grained, chalky tannins and vibrant natural acidity. The finish is persistent, clean, and savory with lingering minerality and earthy spice. The varietal composition is 100% Pinot Noir. It has an alcohol content of approximately 13.5% ABV and is not certified organic.

Vintage Quality

The 2022 growing season in Burgundy brought warm, sunny conditions throughout the summer, tempered by well-timed late-season rain that prevented hydric stress. This enabled the fruit from Grand Clos Rousseau to attain complete phenolic maturity while retaining good natural acidity, resulting in a wine of generous fruit density, balanced tannins, and solid medium-term cellaring potential.

title: Chateau Lynch Bages 2021
bodyHtml:
Originating from France in the Bordeaux region, specifically within the Pauillac AOC appellation in the Haut Médoc, Château Lynch Bages 2021 represents a commanding, refined, and classically styled expression of Left Bank winemaking. Classified as a Fifth Growth in the historic 1855 Classification, Château Lynch Bages has long transcended its official tier, consistently performing at the qualitative stature of a Super Second. Owned and stewarded by the Cazes family since the 1930s, the estate is situated on the famed Bages plateau just south of the town of Pauillac. The vineyard spans approximately 100 hectares of deep Günzian gravel terraces interspersed with sand and clay resting on a limestone subsoil, providing superb natural drainage and optimal heat retention. Under the leadership of Jean-Charles Cazes and technical director Nicolas Labenne, the 2021 vintage marks one of the earliest full harvests vinified in the estate's cutting-edge, gravity-flow winery designed by architect Chien Chung Pei. Harvesting is conducted manually with rigorous optical sorting, followed by fermentation in 80 temperature-controlled stainless steel vats dedicated to individual parcels. Maturation takes place over 18 months in French oak barriques (approximately 75% new oak). The result is an aristocratic, structured red Bordeaux characterized by pristine dark fruit delineation, muscular structural depth, and long-term cellar potential.

The wine presents a luminous, deep ruby red colour with intense violet and garnet reflections along the rim. An expressive, highly perfumed bouquet opens with noble aromas of ripe blackcurrant, crème de cassis, dark wild blackberry, and fresh black cherry, interwoven with sophisticated notes of crushed pencil lead graphite minerality, cedarwood, cigar box, subtle dark cocoa nibs, dried violet petals, and warm French oak pastry spice. On the palate, it is medium-to-full bodied, silken, and energetic, delivering concentrated flavours of crisp black fruits, tart cassis, and savoury mineral earth, all supported by a bright, mouthwatering spine of natural cool-climate acidity. Framed by architectural, fine-grained structural tannins and a chiseled, seamlessly layered mid-palate structure, it concludes with an extraordinarily long, persistent finish marked by lingering dark berries, dried wild herbs, and a clean gravelly grip. Composed predominantly of Cabernet Sauvignon accented with Merlot, Cabernet Franc, and Petit Verdot, this 2021 release offers an optimal drinking window spanning 2028–2050+. Stylistically, it combines classical Left Bank freshness, noble Pauillac structural drive, and polished modern precision.

title: JJ Prum Wehlener Sonnenuhr Auslese Riesling 2023
bodyHtml:
This wine originates from Germany, within the Middle Mosel subregion and the world-renowned Wehlener Sonnenuhr vineyard. Weingut Joh. Jos. Prüm, founded in 1911 by Johann Josef Prüm, stands as one of the Mosel's most celebrated and iconic traditional estates, currently directed by Dr. Katharina Prüm. The south-southwest-facing, precipitously steep slopes of Wehlener Sonnenuhr consist of deep, weather-beaten blue Devonian slate. The estate's philosophy centers on classic, non-interventionist winemaking: spontaneous fermentation with indigenous yeasts in cold stainless steel and traditional Fuder casks, minimal sulfur use, and late bottlings to craft benchmark Mosel Rieslings celebrated for crystalline minerality, delicate sweetness, and legendary multi-decade longevity.

Wine Description

This wine displays a brilliant pale green-gold color. On the nose, it opens with pure and lifted aromas of white peach, juicy lemon, grapefruit peel, and subtle tropical hints of ripe mango and pineapple, complemented by white spring florals, delicate slate smokiness, and faint reductive herbs characteristic of young Prüm bottlings. On the palate, it exhibits a light to medium body with a silky, filigreed, and succulent texture. Unctuous, unfermented natural grape sweetness is effortlessly sliced through by a razor-sharp, vibrant spine of slate-driven acidity and salty minerality. The finish is remarkably long, weightless, and poised, leaving a mouthwatering interplay of citrus, stone fruit, and wet stone. The varietal composition is 100% Riesling. It has an alcohol content of approximately 8.0% ABV and is not certified organic.

Vintage Quality

The 2023 growing season in the Mosel experienced mixed weather that demanded strict sorting in the vineyard. Pristine late-season conditions allowed the Wehlener Sonnenuhr parcels to achieve full, healthy physiological maturity with virtually no botrytis, yielding grapes of intense concentration and crystalline purity. The 2023 Auslese captures the classic Prüm harmony of feather-light weight, electric acidity, and profound aging potential, destined to evolve gracefully in the cellar for 30 to 50 years.

title: Woodford Reserve 'Master's Collection' Batch Proof 119.5 - 700 ml
vendor: 300614 - Bf Canada - A Division Of The Hive
bodyHtml:
This high-proof limited-edition Kentucky straight bourbon whiskey originates from Versailles, Woodford County, Kentucky, crafted at the historic Woodford Reserve Distillery (a National Historic Landmark established in 1812). Released under the distillery’s celebrated Master’s Collection series, Woodford Reserve Batch Proof 119.5 showcases the master blending art of Master Distiller Elizabeth McCall. Produced from Woodford's proprietary grain recipe—72% corn, 18% rye, and 10% malted barley—the spirit marries copper pot-still and column-still distillates fermented with a proprietary yeast strain and local limestone-filtered water. Drawn from a curated assemblage of barrels matured across the upper tiers of the estate's stone barrel warehouses, it is presented completely uncut and unfiltered at a full barrel strength of 119.5 proof (59.75% ABV) in a standard 700 ml heavy-base European export decanter, capturing the core flavor profile in its rawest, most concentrated form.

Spirit Description

This bourbon pours a deep, radiant dark mahogany-amber hue with burnished copper highlights, leaving thick, slow-running sheets of tears along the glass. On the nose, it is intensely aromatic, bold, and confectionery, leading with dark brown sugar, molasses, toasted oak, and Madagascar vanilla bean, swiftly accompanied by rich notes of dried dark cherries, blackberry preserves, and dark chocolate truffles. Beneath the initial richness lie secondary aromas of clove, nutmeg, candied orange peel, and seasoned cedar wood. On the palate, the 119.5 proof brings an exceptionally viscous, oily, and mouth-coating texture that completely carries the elevated alcohol. Waves of warm toffee, crème brûlée, and toasted pecan unfold across the tongue, counterbalanced by a firm kick of peppery rye spice, cinnamon bark, and bitter cocoa nibs. The toasted wood tannins provide firm structural grip without becoming dry or astringent. The finish is remarkably long, warm, and expansive, lingering with impressions of dark stone fruit, leather, charred oak sweetness, and a trailing, delicate baking spice warmth.

Accolades

Woodford Reserve’s Batch Proof series stands among the most critically lauded annual releases in American whiskey, consistently earning 94–96 point ratings across publications such as Whisky Advocate, Wine Enthusiast, and Paste Magazine. The 119.5 Proof release captured widespread acclaim from industry judges and whiskey reviewers, praised specifically for preserving the delicate five-source flavor profile of Woodford Reserve—grain, water, fermentation, distillation, and maturation—while elevating its weight and viscosity to full barrel strength. Critics routinely commend the blending balance, noting that the spirit drinks with extraordinary smoothness and balance despite its robust ~60% ABV frame.

title: GlenDronach Ode to the Valley - 700 ml
vendor: 300614 - Bf Canada - A Division Of The Hive
bodyHtml:
This expressive limited-release single malt Scotch whisky originates from the Valley of Forgue near Huntly, Aberdeenshire, produced at The GlenDronach Distillery (founded in 1826 by James Allardice). Inspired by the lush terroir, hedgerows, and natural flora surrounding the estate, The GlenDronach Ode to the Valley explores a multi-cask maturation profile uniting the distillery’s renowned Spanish sherry heritage with Portuguese fortified wine influence. Distilled from unpeated malted barley in classic copper pot stills, the whisky is aged in a marriage of Spanish Pedro Ximénez and Oloroso sherry casks, complemented by finishing in select Ruby Port casks. Bottled at 46.2% ABV (92.4 proof) in a standard 700 ml bottle, it is non-chill filtered and presented at its natural color without artificial caramel additions.

Spirit Description

This single malt displays a rich, radiant copper-amber hue with ruby-red highlights, leaving slow-forming, unctuous legs along the glass. On the nose, it is intensely fruity, floral, and vibrant, opening with aromas of fresh red berries, ripe blackberries, and black cherry compote, immediately followed by layers of orange marmalade, dark chocolate, and golden raisins. Subtle floral blossom notes and gentle undertones of toasted walnut and warm baking spices round out the bouquet. On the palate, the 46.2% ABV provides a silky, rounded, and mouth-filling texture. Rich flavors of stewed summer fruits, spiced plum pudding, and dark fruit leather glide across the tongue, counterbalanced by crisp citrus zest, nutmeg, and cinnamon bark. The Ruby Port casks contribute bright red fruit acidity and sweet tannins that elevate the rich, nutty depth of the Oloroso and Pedro Ximénez wood. The finish is long, elegant, and fruit-forward, lingering with notes of dark cocoa, dried cherries, toasted oak tannins, and a gentle, warming spice.

Accolades

The GlenDronach Ode to the Valley has earned warm praise from whisky reviewers, collectors, and spirits panels for its artful integration of sherry and port cask profiles. Tasting notes and spirits commentators regularly award it 92+ points, commending Master Blender Rachel Barrie for balancing the natural weight of GlenDronach’s robust Highland spirit with the lifted red-fruit vibrancy of Portuguese port casks. Critics highlight its ability to introduce brighter brambleberry and cherry tones while preserving the velvety, chocolate-and-dried-fruit backbone that defines the distillery's house style.

title: Glendronach Ode To Dark - 700 ml
vendor: 300614 - Bf Canada - A Division Of The Hive
bodyHtml:
This high-proof limited-release Highland single malt Scotch whisky originates from the Valley of Forgue near Huntly, Aberdeenshire, produced at The GlenDronach Distillery (established in 1826 by James Allardice). Positioned at an intensified strength of 50.8% ABV (101.6 proof), The GlenDronach Ode to the Dark represents the most concentrated, wood-driven expression within the distillery's narrative series. Distilled from unpeated Scottish malted barley using traditional copper pot stills, the liquid underwent extended maturation in the distillery’s traditional stone dunnage warehouses, resting exclusively in the darkest, most unctuous Pedro Ximénez and seasoned Oloroso sherry casks sourced directly from Andalucía. Bottled in a standard 700 ml format, it is non-chill filtered and bottled at natural cask-drawn color without added caramel coloring.

Spirit Description

This single malt pours a deep, near-opaque walnut-treacle hue with rich crimson-mahogany glints, leaving viscous, heavy tears that cling to the glass. On the nose, the 50.8% ABV delivers an immediate, potent aromatic wave of dense Spanish oak sugars: aromas of black treacle, sticky Medjool dates, stewed damson plums, and rum-soaked raisins merge with dark chocolate truffles, roasted espresso beans, and candied orange peel. Beneath the fruit intensity lie antique aromas of polished leather, cedar cigar box, and clove. On the palate, the elevated strength translates into a chewy, full-bodied, and deeply coating mouthfeel. Rich waves of dark plum compote, bittersweet cocoa, and molasses glide across the tongue, counterbalanced by assertive European oak tannins, cracked black pepper, cinnamon bark, and roasted walnuts. The interplay of sweet Pedro Ximénez syrup and dry, nutty Oloroso structure keeps the mid-palate balanced despite its weight. The finish is remarkably long, dry, and warming, trailing off with impressions of espresso crema, dark chocolate-covered cherries, sweet wood resins, and enduring baking spices.

Accolades

The 50.8% ABV presentation of The GlenDronach Ode to the Dark has garnered significant praise among collectors and sherry-cask purists who seek natural, higher-proof European oak extraction. Reviewers and competition judges applaud Master Blender Rachel Barrie's selection of casks, noting that the elevated proof holds the immense density of dried fruits and dark chocolate in tight focus. Tasting panels routinely score the expression 93–95 points, highlighting that the robust strength enhances the oily texture and spice backbone of GlenDronach's robust Highland spirit, preventing the heavy sherry wood influence from becoming cloying or one-dimensional.

title: GlenDronach Ode to the Embers - 700 ml
vendor: 300614 - Bf Canada - A Division Of The Hive
bodyHtml:
This specialized peated Highland single malt Scotch whisky originates from the Valley of Forgue near Huntly, Aberdeenshire, produced at The GlenDronach Distillery (established in 1826 by James Allardice). Released as an elevated-strength edition within the distillery's experimental narrative collection, The GlenDronach Ode to the Embers at 48.4% ABV (96.8 proof) showcases an intensified expression of GlenDronach’s 19th-century peated heritage. Distilled from barley kilned over regional Highland peat—yielding soft, aromatic wood smoke, earthy heath, and hearth embers rather than maritime brine—the spirit was matured in traditional dunnage warehouses in a curated marriage of Spanish Pedro Ximénez and Oloroso sherry casks from Andalucía. Presented in a standard 700 ml bottle, it is non-chill filtered and bottled at natural color.

Spirit Description

This single malt displays a deep, radiant copper-mahogany hue with polished walnut highlights, coating the glass with thick, slow-running legs. On the nose, the 48.4% strength delivers an intensified aromatic lift: upfront waves of smoldering heather, bonfire embers, and charred chestnut wood intertwine with unctuous Pedro Ximénez dark fruit—black treacle, Medjool dates, stewed plums, and Seville orange peel. Beneath the fruit and smoke lie nuances of dark cocoa nibs, toasted walnut, and clove. On the palate, the elevated ABV provides a viscous, muscular, and mouth-coating texture. An initial burst of sweet dark caramel, spiced raisin compote, and chocolate-covered cherries meets a surge of warm Highland peat smoke, cracked black pepper, tobacco leaf, and cinnamon bark. The nutty, dry tannins of the Oloroso wood provide firm structural counterpoint to the luscious dessert sugars. The finish is exceptionally long, warm, and drying, lingering with impressions of lingering sweet peat ash, dark chocolate, roasted espresso, and enduring oak spices.

Accolades

The GlenDronach Ode to the Embers has been celebrated by whisky reviewers and collectors who favor robust, non-chill filtered Highland malts. Critics and spirits tasting panels praise Master Blender Rachel Barrie for presenting the liquid at 48.4% ABV, noting that the higher proof carries the earthy, heather-smoke phenols with greater weight and viscosity. Connoisseurs frequently award it 93+ points, commending its balance: the spirit retains the distillery’s full-bodied, unctuous Spanish oak profile while delivering a campfire warmth that enhances rather than eclipses the dark fruit foundation.

title: Ardbeg Anthology: 'The Beithir's Tale' 15 Year Old
bodyHtml:
This innovative series of experimental, age-stated single malts originates from the south coast of the Isle of Islay, crafted at the historic Ardbeg Distillery (founded in 1815). The Ardbeg Anthology Collection is designed to explore rare, hybrid cask maturations by marrying Ardbeg’s iconic, heavily peated spirit with cask styles previously untried by the distillery. Each release in the series pairs a mythological creature with a minimum age statement of 14 to 15 years—beginning with the inaugural release, The Harpy’s Tale (13-Year-Old, finished in sweet Sauternes wine casks), followed by The Unicorn’s Tale (14-Year-Old, matured in Madeira wine casks). Bottled at 46.0% ABV (92 proof) in a standard 750 ml bottle, the range is non-chill filtered and bottled with natural color, representing a new frontier in the distillery's experimentation with sweet fortified and dessert wine wood.

Spirit Description

This single malt displays a rich, radiant amber-gold hue with pale straw reflections and clean, steady tears along the glass. On the nose, it is remarkably aromatic, balancing pungent Islay peat with delicate, sweet fruit and floral notes. Pungent aromas of chimney soot, smoked sea salt, and medicinal creosote are counterpointed by candied citrus zest, honeycomb, poached white peaches, and warm brioche. On the palate, the 46.0% ABV frame provides a supple, silky, and coating mouthfeel. Initial bursts of sweet dessert wine, lemon meringue, and apricot tart are immediately met by a wave of sharp, savory campfire ash, cracked black pepper, and eucalyptus oil. Mid-palate complexities reveal roasted hazelnuts, dark cocoa nibs, and a briny maritime salinity that keeps the residual wine sweetness crisp and balanced. The finish is long, complex, and drying, lingering with impressions of sweet wood ash, dried stone fruit, salted caramel, and subtle oak spice.

Accolades

The Ardbeg Anthology releases have garnered critical acclaim from international spirits writers and Scotch collectors, celebrated for seamlessly integrating dessert and fortified wine sweetness without subduing Ardbeg's fiery phenolic character. Reviewers in Whisky Advocate and leading competition panels routinely score releases in the series 92–94 points, specifically commending the distillery's balance: the prolonged secondary wood maturation enhances the oily, fruity esters of the mature spirit while allowing the maritime peat smoke to remain clearly defined and energetic.

title: Ardbeg Dolce
bodyHtml:
This experimental limited-edition single malt Scotch whisky originates from the rocky southern coast of the Isle of Islay, crafted at the historic Ardbeg Distillery (founded in 1815). Inspired by the Italian golden age of cinema and the classic concept of "la dolce vita", Ardbeg Dolce pairs Ardbeg’s intensely smoky, peated spirit with the sweet, rich influence of Italian wine maturation. Distilled from heavily peated malted barley, the spirit is matured in a combination of ex-bourbon barrels and finished in sweet Marsala wine casks seasoned with Sicilian fortified wine. Bottled at 47.8% ABV (95.6 proof) in a standard 700 ml green glass bottle, it is non-chill filtered and presented at its natural color without artificial additives.

Spirit Description

This single malt displays a rich, radiant amber-gold hue with warm copper reflections and slow, viscous tears along the glass. On the nose, it delivers an aromatic contrast between sweet Italian confectionery and pungent Islay peat: aromas of caramelized blood oranges, sweet candied figs, sun-dried apricots, and dark honey mingle directly with dense chimney soot, salted tar, creosote, and seaside bonfire smoke. On the palate, the 47.8% ABV provides an oily, velvety, and mouth-coating texture. An initial wave of sweet fortified wine, poached plums, and brown sugar pastry quickly meets a surge of bold, medicinal peat smoke, cracked black pepper, and bitter cocoa. Mid-palate complexities bring out toasted almonds, clove, orange zest, and a savory maritime salinity that balances the Marsala sweetness. The finish is long, warming, and multidimensional, trailing off with lingering sweet peat embers, dark dried fruit compote, roasted nuts, and a touch of drying citrus-oak tannin.

Accolades

Ardbeg Dolce has captured the attention of Islay collectors and spirits critics for its bold balance between high-phenolic peat smoke and fortified dessert-wine sweetness. Tasting panels and whisky reviewers commend Ardbeg's wood management, noting that the Marsala finishing casks soften the intense medicinal edges of the distillate by infusing sun-ripened Mediterranean stone fruits and sweet spices, without masking the signature salty, soot-laden campfire core that defines the house style.

title: Glenallachie Meikle Toir The Sherry One - 700 ml
bodyHtml:
Meikle Tòir "The Sherry One" is an artisanal peated single malt Scotch whisky produced by The GlenAllachie Distillery in Aberlour, Speyside, Scotland. Crafted under the vision of legendary Master Distiller Billy Walker, Meikle Tòir (Scottish Gaelic for "The Big Pursuit") represents GlenAllachie’s dedicated exploration of peated distillation. While Speyside is traditionally famous for unpeated, fruity malts, Walker set aside a small window each year to produce peated spirit using mainland St. Fergus peat. "The Sherry One" pairs this earthy, mainland peat smoke with Walker’s hallmark mastery of sherry wood maturation.

Spirit Description

The Sherry One is crafted from mainland Scottish peat harvested from St. Fergus in Aberdeenshire, which lends a softer, sweeter, tree-and-heather smoke profile compared to the medicinal, maritime peat of Islay. The spirit undergoes a lengthy fermentation of approximately 160 hours to build deep ester complexity before distillation. After an initial maturation in American oak ex-bourbon casks, the whisky undergoes secondary maturation in hand-selected first-fill Pedro Ximénez (PX) and Oloroso sherry puncheons and hogsheads. The whisky is bottled with natural color and non-chill filtered at a peated level of roughly 35 ppm.

  • Colour: Rich burnished mahogany with deep chestnut reflections.

  • Aroma: Warm, sweet, and smoky. Opens with rich dark chocolate, medjool dates, and sultanas, followed by campfire ash, sweet peat smoke, toasted honeycomb, and subtle cinnamon spice.

  • Palate: Full-bodied, velvety, and rich on the entry. Luscious dark berries, treacle toffee, and plum pudding are enveloped in earthy mainland peat smoke, roasted coffee beans, dark cocoa, and orange zest.

  • Body: Full-bodied with a viscous, coating mouthfeel driven by heavy sherry cask extraction.

  • Finish: Long, warm, and lingering, trailing off with persistent sweet peat embers, dried figs, dark chocolate, and drying sherry oak tannins.

  • ABV: Bottled at 48% ABV, non-chill filtered and natural color.

title: Osoyoos Larose Le Grand Vin Blanc 2023
bodyHtml:
Originating from Canada in British Columbia's Okanagan Valley, specifically within the warm, arid South Okanagan terroir of Osoyoos, Osoyoos Larose Le Grand Vin Blanc 2023 represents an ambitious, finely textured, and Bordeaux-inspired expression of Canadian white winemaking. Established in 1998 as a joint venture between Groupe Taillan (owners of Château Gruaud Larose in Saint-Julien) and local Canadian interests, Osoyoos Larose was conceived to showcase that the arid benches of the South Okanagan could yield world-class wines crafted with classical Bordelais precision. The estate vineyard is situated on an arid, west-facing bench elevated above Osoyoos Lake, planted on well-draining, gravelly-sandy loam soils intermixed with silica and granite scree that absorb daytime solar heat while encouraging deep root penetration. Under the direction of estate director and winemaker Michael Anderson, the winemaking philosophy bridges French tradition with desert-climate viticulture: hand harvesting, gentle pneumatic whole-cluster pressing, and temperature-controlled fermentation in seasoned French oak barrels followed by extended lees aging with periodic stirring (bâtonnage). The result is an expressive, layered white wine that harmonizes ripe stone fruit generosity with vivid natural acidity and a firm mineral foundation.

Wine Description

The wine presents a luminous, clear pale straw-gold colour with brilliant platinum and green reflections along the rim. An expressive, highly perfumed bouquet opens with noble aromas of ripe white peach, Meyer lemon, Bartlett pear, and fresh gooseberry, interwoven with sophisticated notes of honeysuckle blossom, crushed river stone minerality, grapefruit zest, beeswax, toasted almond, and subtle French oak pastry spice. On the palate, it is medium-to-full bodied, silken, and energetic, delivering concentrated flavours of crisp orchard fruits, candied citrus peel, and savoury mineral earth, all supported by a bright, mouthwatering spine of natural cool-climate acidity. Framed by a rich, delicately rounded mid-palate structure and seamless phenolic grip, it concludes with a long, persistent finish marked by lingering citrus oil, dried herbs, and a clean, stony mineral drive. Composed of a classic white Bordeaux blend of Sauvignon Blanc and Sémillon, this 2023 release offers an optimal drinking window spanning 2024–2031+. Stylistically, it combines Okanagan sun-ripened fruit intensity, crystalline mineral freshness, and classical Bordeaux textural refinement.

title: Domaine Labruyere Prieur Pommard ‘La Platiere’ Premier Cru 2022
bodyHtml:
This wine originates from France, within the Côte de Beaune subregion of Burgundy and the Pommard Premier Cru appellation. Sourced through Labruyère-Prieur Sélection, a collaborative high-end négociant arm established between the Labruyère family (owners of Domaine Jacques Prieur since 1988) and long-time enologist Nadine Gublin, the label highlights prestigious Premier Cru climats that complement the core estate holdings. La Platière is situated on mid-to-upper hillside slopes with iron-rich clay and limestone soils. The winemaking philosophy focuses on precise manual sorting, gentle parcel-by-parcel vinification, and thoughtful barrel maturation in French oak to showcase Pommard's classic depth and muscularity alongside aromatic elegance.

Wine Description

This wine displays a deep ruby-purple color. On the nose, it opens with an airy yet concentrated bouquet of ripe blackberry, dark cherry, and wild raspberry, complemented by notes of violet, forest floor, subtle smoke, and delicately integrated oak spice. On the palate, it exhibits a medium to full body with a vibrant, open texture and a juicy core of dark berry fruit. Fine-grained, polished tannins provide firm structural framing alongside a balancing spine of refreshing acidity, leading to a long, mineral-inflected, and gently chewy finish.

Vintage Quality

The 2022 vintage across Burgundy was an outstanding and generous year, defined by hot, sunny summer weather tempered by periodic, well-timed rainfall. Grapes achieved complete phenolic ripeness without sacrificing freshness. Harvested with ideal physiological maturity, La Platière produced a Pommard characterized by generous fruit expression, refined tannin integration, and significant medium- to long-term cellaring potential.

title: Amiral De Beychevelle 2023
bodyHtml:
This wine originates from France, within the Left Bank of the Bordeaux region and the Saint-Julien appellation. Amiral de Beychevelle is the second wine of Château Beychevelle, a celebrated 1855 Quatrième Grand Cru Classé (Fourth Growth) estate with origins dating back to the 16th century. Sourced from younger vines across the estate's deep Garonne gravel and clay-limestone soils, the wine is crafted with the same meticulous rigor and cellar care as the Grand Vin. The winemaking philosophy emphasizes accessibility, charm, and elegance, offering an approachable reflection of Beychevelle’s classical Saint-Julien refinement in its youth while maintaining traditional aging potential.

Wine Description

This wine presents a deep ruby hue with slight garnet glints at the rim. On the nose, it opens with bright aromas of blackcurrant, dark cherry, and red plum, layered with notes of cedar, pencil shavings, tobacco leaf, and subtle toasted oak spices. On the palate, it exhibits a medium to full body with a supple, fleshy mouthfeel, driven by a generous core of ripe dark fruits. The tannins are smooth, rounded, and finely polished, supported by balanced natural acidity that keeps the palate fresh and poised. The finish is persistent, clean, and gently savory, echoing with hints of cocoa, graphite, and dried herbs.

title: Marcarini Barolo ‘La Morra’ 2021
bodyHtml:
This wine originates from Italy, within the Piedmont region and the Barolo del Comune di La Morra DOCG appellation. Azienda Agricola Marcarini, situated in the heart of La Morra, is one of the zone’s historic, traditionalist benchmark estates, with grape-growing roots dating back to the mid-19th century. Introduced to highlight the distinctive Tortonian soil composition of the commune marked by calcareous blue marl (Sant’Agata Fossili) this bottling is crafted from select estate-grown vineyards across La Morra. The winemaking philosophy remains fiercely classical: spontaneous, temperature-controlled fermentation with long skin contact followed by extended maturation in large neutral Slavonian oak casks (botti grandi), emphasizing aromatic purity, silky refinement, and early structural approachability without sacrificing aging ability.

Wine Description

This wine displays a classic garnet-red color enriched with bright ruby reflections. On the nose, it opens with an airy, highly floral bouquet dominated by fresh red cherries, wild raspberries, and crushed rose petals, intertwined with violets, sweet dried herbs, licorice, and subtle hints of forest floor and white pepper. On the palate, it exhibits a medium to full body with a luminous, energetic mouthfeel. Fine, powdery, chalk-like tannins frame a vibrant core of sour red fruit, driven by an electric line of natural acidity that lends tension and poise. The finish is long, vertical, and savory, marked by lingering floral and mineral nuance.

Vintage Quality

The 2021 vintage in the Langhe is widely considered a benchmark, classically proportioned year in Piedmont. After a cool spring and a warm, steady summer free of extreme heatwaves, ideal late-season diurnal shifts permitted slow, complete phenolic ripening with excellent acid retention. In La Morra, these conditions yielded Nebbiolo of striking aromatic depth, firm yet polished tannins, and uncommon tension. The 2021 offers enticing early appeal with aeration while possessing the structural integrity to cellar comfortably for 12 to 20 years.

title: Glenallachie Meikle Toir The Chinquapin One - 700 ml
bodyHtml:
Meikle Tòir "The Chinquapin One" is an artisanal peated single malt Scotch whisky produced by The GlenAllachie Distillery in Aberlour, Speyside, Scotland, under the direction of Master Distiller Billy Walker. As part of GlenAllachie’s dedicated peated label, Meikle Tòir (The Big Pursuit in Scottish Gaelic), this expression highlights an adventurous maturation approach: pairing earthy mainland peat smoke with virgin Chinquapin oak casks sourced from the Northern Ozark region in Missouri, United States.

Spirit Description

The spirit is distilled from malted barley peated to approximately 35 ppm using mainland peat from St. Fergus in Aberdeenshire, which delivers a softer, heather-tinged, and sweeter wood smoke profile rather than the sharp, medicinal, or seaweed-heavy smoke common in coastal Islay malts. GlenAllachie employs an extended fermentation period of around 160 hours to develop rich fruity esters before distillation. Following primary maturation in American oak ex-bourbon barrels, the whisky undergoes secondary aging in virgin Chinquapin oak (Quercus muehlenbergii), which is air-dried for nearly 36 months before being medium-toasted and charred. This unusual virgin wood imparts pronounced baking spices, ginger, toasted nuts, and sweet wood tannins.

  • Colour: Rich amber-bronze with warm golden copper highlights.

  • Aroma: Vibrant, spicy, and smoky. Opens with toasted oak, candied ginger, and cinnamon sticks, layered over sweet heather smoke, campfire embers, warm honey, and crème brûlée.

  • Palate: Bold, full-flavored, and textural on the entry. Flavors of charred honeycomb, dark butterscotch, and sweet wood embers are balanced by freshly ground nutmeg, clove, roasted hazelnuts, and a splash of citrus zest.

  • Body: Medium-to-full-bodied with an oily, mouth-coating viscosity driven by virgin wood oils and extended fermentation.

  • Finish: Long, warming, and distinctly spicy, trailing off with sweet mainland peat smoke, lingering ginger warmth, toasted oak, and a dry, peppery snap.

  • ABV: Bottled at 48% ABV, non-chill filtered and natural colour.

title: Glenallachie Meikle Toir The Original - 700 ml
bodyHtml:
Meikle Tòir "The Original" is the foundational peated single malt Scotch whisky produced by The GlenAllachie Distillery in Aberlour, Speyside, Scotland, under the stewardship of Master Distiller Billy Walker. As the core pillar of GlenAllachie’s dedicated peated imprint; Meikle Tòir (The Big Pursuit in Scottish Gaelic) "The Original" showcases the pure, unmasked profile of the distillery's mainland peated spirit. Crafted to challenge the convention that peated whisky belongs exclusively to the Scottish isles, it offers a mainland alternative defined by sweet, earthy, and heather-forward smoke rather than maritime brine.

Spirit Description

The Original is made from Scottish malted barley peated to roughly 35 ppm using inland peat sourced from St. Fergus in Aberdeenshire. The mash undergoes an extended fermentation period of approximately 160 hours—more than double the industry average—fostering high levels of fruity esters before double distillation in GlenAllachie's copper pot stills. Maturation takes place in a tailored combination of first-fill American oak ex-bourbon barrels, virgin American oak casks, and rye whiskey casks. Bottled non-chill filtered and with natural color, this cask recipe creates a balanced dialogue between sweet oak vanilla, light baking spices, and mainland wood smoke.

  • Colour: Bright golden amber with polished brass highlights.

  • Aroma: Fresh, sweet, and aromatically smoky. Opens with baking spices, ginger, and honeyed malt, layered over sweet heather smoke, toasted almond, crisp orchard fruit, and charred oak.

  • Palate: Supple, vibrant, and textural on the entry. Flavors of crème brûlée, sweet vanilla pod, and roasted coffee beans meld with gentle campfire embers, dried apple peel, and a touch of rye spice.

  • Body: Medium-to-full-bodied with an oily, mouth-coating viscosity.

  • Finish: Long, warm, and clean, trailing off with lingering sweet peat smoke, cinnamon, toasted oak, and a soft peppery snap.

  • ABV: Bottled at 50% ABV (100 Proof), non-chill filtered and natural colour.

title: JJ Prum Wehlener Sonnenuhr Kabinett Riesling 2023
bodyHtml:
This wine originates from Germany, within the Middle Mosel subregion and the iconic Wehlener Sonnenuhr vineyard. Weingut Joh. Jos. Prüm, established in 1911 by Johann Josef Prüm and currently directed by Dr. Katharina Prüm, is one of the world's benchmark producers of traditional, terroir-driven Riesling. The vineyard’s south-southwest exposure and precipitous slopes composed of weathered blue Devonian slate create an optimal microclimate for slow, late ripening. The estate’s philosophy focuses on minimal cellar intervention, spontaneous fermentation with wild yeasts in cold stainless steel and traditional Fuder casks, and minimal handling to craft Kabinett Rieslings renowned for filigreed delicacy, razor-sharp precision, and decades-long cellaring potential.

Wine Description

This wine displays a bright, pale straw-yellow hue with faint greenish reflections. On the nose, it opens with pure, lifted aromas of white peach, crisp Asian pear, fresh lemon, and clementine, accented by honeysuckle, subtle smoke, and the faint reductive, slatey character typical of young Prüm wines. On the palate, it exhibits a light, weightless body with a silky, crystalline texture. A delicate thread of natural unfermented sweetness is seamlessly countered by a vibrant spine of electric, slate-driven acidity, yielding a juicy, saline, and mouthwatering profile. The finish is remarkably long, clean, and persistent, echoing with crushed wet stone and citrus zest. The varietal composition is 100% Riesling. It has an alcohol content of approximately 8.0% to 8.5% ABV and is not certified organic.

Vintage Quality

The 2023 vintage in the Mosel required rigorous vineyard work and precise picking decisions due to variable seasonal weather. A warm, dry early autumn allowed the Wehlener Sonnenuhr fruit to achieve pristine physiological maturity while retaining exceptionally bright, taut natural acidity. The resulting Kabinett exemplifies classic Mosel tension; combining low alcohol, crystalline purity, and balanced residual sugar that can be enjoyed in its youth or aged gracefully for 15 to 25+ years.

title: Weingut Willi Schaefer 'Graacher Domprobst' Riesling Spätlese 2024
bodyHtml:
This wine originates from Germany, within the Middle Mosel subregion and the celebrated Graacher Domprobst VDP.GROSSE LAGE vineyard. Weingut Willi Schaefer, based in Graach, is an iconic artisanal estate run by Christoph and Andrea Schaefer. Cultivating just four hectares of steep, south-to-southwest-facing terraced slopes, the domaine is revered for its classic, terroir-transparent style. Graacher Domprobst sits on deep, moisture-retaining blue and grey Devonian slate soils, typically yielding wines with darker mineral tension and deeper structural power than neighboring Himmelreich. The estate’s philosophy focuses on artisanal non-intervention: hand-picking, spontaneous indigenous yeast fermentation in traditional old German Fuder casks, and patient aging on the fine lees without fining.

Wine Description

This wine displays a brilliant pale straw-gold hue with shimmering green reflections. The nose is crystalline and aromatically complex, revealing ripe white peach, Mirabelle plum, candied lemon peel, and apricot, accented by elderflower, crushed flint, wet slate, and a characteristic subtle cassis leaf herbal note. On the palate, it exhibits a light, silky body balanced by striking energy and tension. Concentrated natural residual sweetness is effortlessly balanced by a vibrant, chiseled spine of slate-driven acidity, creating a succulent and buoyant mouthfeel. The finish is remarkably persistent, clean, and salty-mineral, echoing with stone fruit and citrus zest.

Vintage Quality

The 2024 vintage in the Mosel featured dynamic weather with early-season challenges, ultimately saved by a dry, sunny late summer and extended cool autumn hang time. These conditions fostered slow, optimal flavor and phenolic development with reduced yields. For Willi Schaefer’s steep parcels in Domprobst, 2024 yielded fruit of crystalline purity, high aromatic definition, and taut structural acidity, creating a Spätlese built for both captivating early drinking and 25 to 40+ years of graceful cellar evolution.

title: Weingut Willi Schaefer Graacher Domprobst Riesling Kabinett 2023
bodyHtml:
This wine originates from Germany, within the Middle Mosel subregion and the prestigious Graacher Domprobst vineyard. Weingut Willi Schaefer is a revered family estate in Graach, operated by Christoph and Andrea Schaefer. With merely four hectares under vine, their production is tiny and held in the highest esteem by classical Mosel enthusiasts. The Domprobst site is celebrated for its deep, moisture-retentive blue and grey Devonian slate, which tends to yield wines of deeper structural power, earthier slate tones, and savory complexity relative to the more overtly floral Himmelreich. The winemaking philosophy is strictly traditional and non-interventionist: meticulous hand-harvesting, spontaneous fermentation with wild yeasts in historic 1,000-liter neutral oak Fuder casks, and gentle aging on fine lees to safeguard site transparency and laser-sharp freshness.

Wine Description

This wine displays a luminous, pale straw-yellow hue with faint greenish highlights. On the nose, it opens with pure and detailed aromas of white vineyard peach, green apple, clementine, and lime blossom, accented by nuances of wild mint, cassis leaf, and an unmistakable hallmark of crushed smoky slate. On the palate, it exhibits a light, featherweight body animated by electrifying energy and tension. The delicate veil of natural grape sweetness is sliced through cleanly by a vibrant, chiseled spine of slatey acidity, producing an airy, succulent, and crystalline mouthfeel. The finish is exceptionally long, savory, and mouthwatering, leaving behind notes of salty minerals and lingering citrus zest.

Vintage Quality

The 2023 vintage in the Mosel required rigorous canopy management and strict sorting due to shifting summer weather, but a warm, dry September allowed the grapes to achieve optimal physiological maturity while locking in razor-sharp acidity. In Willi Schaefer's parcels within Domprobst, 2023 yielded an exemplary Kabinett marked by buoyant weightlessness, aromatic purity, and impeccable sweet-tart tension, offering immense immediate pleasure alongside the structure to evolve gracefully for 15 to 25+ years.

title: Glendronach 15 Year Sherry Cask - 700 ml
vendor: 300614 - Bf Canada - A Division Of The Hive
bodyHtml:
This benchmark sherried Highland single malt Scotch whisky originates from the Valley of Forgue near Huntly, Aberdeenshire, produced at The GlenDronach Distillery (established in 1826 by James Allardice). Historically celebrated as the legendary "Revival" bottling, The GlenDronach 15 Year Old showcases the distillery’s mastery of dual Spanish sherry wood maturation. Distilled from unpeated malted barley using traditional copper pot stills, the spirit matures for a minimum of 15 years in traditional dunnage warehouses in an assemblage of premier Spanish Pedro Ximénez and Oloroso sherry casks sourced from Andalucía. Bottled at 46.0% ABV (92 proof) in a standard 700 ml bottle, it is non-chill filtered and presented with its natural, cask-imparted mahogany color without any added caramel coloring.

Spirit Description

This single malt displays a radiant antique-gold hue with deep walnut and mahogany reflections, forming slow, viscous tears along the glass. On the nose, it offers an immediate, intoxicating burst of rich sherry fruit and warming spice: aromas of maraschino cherries, ripe brambleberries, and dark plum compote mingle with sweet Spanish brandy, wild honey, dark chocolate, and roasted chestnuts. Underlying notes of orange zest, fresh mint leaf, and antique walnut wood add aromatic complexity. On the palate, the 46.0% ABV delivery is velvety, rich, and deeply mouth-coating. Flavors of dark treacle, sticky toffee, and stewed figs roll across the tongue, counterbalanced by mid-palate notes of dried apricot, cracked black pepper, cinnamon bark, and bitter cocoa nibs. The dry, nutty tannins of the Oloroso wood provide structure and grip against the luscious, unctuous sweetness of the Pedro Ximénez casks. The finish is remarkably long, warm, and lingering, trailing off with impressions of honeyed dark fruit, espresso, toasted oak spices, and rich dark chocolate.

Accolades

The GlenDronach 15 Year Old holds an esteemed position among whisky connoisseurs and critics worldwide. Upon its original release and celebrated return to the core lineup under Master Blender Rachel Barrie, it captured widespread acclaim, including Double Gold and Best in Class honors at the San Francisco World Spirits Competition and the World Whiskies Awards. Reviewers across publications like Whisky Advocate routinely rate it 92–95 points, praising the expression for setting the benchmark for the 15-year age tier by marrying dense, brooding European oak extraction with vibrant, energetic orchard and berry fruit.

title: Jack Daniel's McLaren Halo Edition - 1 Litre
vendor: 300614 - Bf Canada - A Division Of The Hive
bodyHtml:
This high-profile collaborative Tennessee whiskey originates from Lynchburg, Moore County, Tennessee, crafted at the historic Jack Daniel Distillery (founded in 1866) in official partnership with the McLaren Formula 1 Team. Designed primarily as a flagship centerpiece for global travel retail, international duty-free circuits, and motorsport collector networks, this edition is presented in a generous 1 Litre (1000 ml) bottle format featuring McLaren’s signature Papaya accents and aerodynamic race-liveried packaging. Crafted using Jack Daniel’s heritage grain recipe—80% corn, 12% malted barley, and 8% rye—the distillate undergoes the foundational Lincoln County Process, filtering slowly drop-by-drop through ten feet of sugar maple charcoal before maturation in handcrafted, new charred American white oak barrels.

Spirit Description

This whiskey pours a deep, radiant amber hue with polished copper-gold highlights, leaving thick, uniform tears that slowly slide down the glass. On the nose, it is rich, aromatic, and distinctly Lynchburg: upfront waves of warm vanilla bean, brown sugar, and toasted oak lead into sweet notes of caramelized banana bread, candied orange peel, and dried stone fruits, anchored by a touch of charred oak and soft baking spices. On the palate, the elevated delivery offers an oily, coating, and rounded texture. Flavors of dark caramel, butterscotch, and sweet toasted marshmallow glide across the tongue, counterbalanced by vibrant mid-palate rye spice—cracked black pepper, cinnamon stick, and a hint of clove. The sugar-maple charcoal mellowing rounds off harsh ethanol edges, allowing the richness of the oak sugars to take center stage. The finish is long, warm, and lingering, trailing off with impressions of toasted pecans, pipe tobacco, melted dark chocolate, and sweet, lingering barrel char.

Accolades

The Jack Daniel's x McLaren partnership releases have achieved significant success within global travel retail and spirits collector communities. Industry critics and spirits journalists highlight the collaboration as a prime example of high-concept brand synergy that does not compromise on the liquid inside. Reviewers across spirits showcases and duty-free tasting panels praise the release for offering collectors substantial value in the 1-litre format, commending the distillery for providing a rich, quintessential Tennessee whiskey profile that balances accessibility for casual race fans with enough wood-driven depth to satisfy seasoned whiskey enthusiasts.

title: Jack Daniel's Single Barrel Heritage Barrel
vendor: 300614 - Bf Canada - A Division Of The Hive
bodyHtml:
This allocated limited-release Tennessee whiskey originates from Lynchburg, Moore County, Tennessee, crafted at the historic Jack Daniel Distillery (established in 1866). Introduced to honor the 19th-century barrel-making techniques championed by Jack Daniel himself, Jack Daniel's Single Barrel Heritage Barrel Tennessee Whiskey centers on specialized woodcraft. Produced from the distillery’s traditional mash bill—80% corn, 12% malted barley, and 8% rye—and mellowed drop-by-drop through ten feet of sugar maple charcoal via the Lincoln County Process, the spirit is matured in custom-crafted barrels. These unique barrels are heavily toasted for an extended period to caramelize wood sugars before receiving a light char. Positioned exclusively on the highest floors of select hilltop barrelhouses to experience extreme temperature variations, the whiskey is bottled at 100 proof (50.0% ABV) in a 750 ml decanter, non-chill filtered to preserve rich wood oils and complex toasted vanillins.

Spirit Description

This whiskey pours a deep, glowing mahogany-amber hue with rich copper highlights, leaving thick, slow-running tears along the glass. On the nose, it is intensely aromatic, decadent, and pastry-like, greeting the senses with sweet toasted oak, charred marshmallow, vanilla bean custard, and warm maple syrup. Beneath the initial dessert sweetness lie complex layers of baked banana bread, candied orange peel, warm pecan pie, and seasoned cedar wood. On the palate, the 50.0% ABV delivery is oily, full-bodied, and deeply mouth-coating. Flavors of rich dark caramel, butterscotch, and honeyed orchard fruit glide across the tongue, counterbalanced by vibrant baking spices: cinnamon stick, cracked nutmeg, and clove. The extended toasting process imparts heavy confectionery oak sweetness without astringent bitter tannins. The finish is exceptionally long, warm, and comforting, trailing off with impressions of toasted coconut, dark chocolate shavings, pipe tobacco, and sweet, lingering wood sugars.

Accolades

Jack Daniel's Heritage Barrel stands as one of the most celebrated and highly sought-after modern expressions in the distillery's portfolio. Upon its debut, it earned unanimous acclaim from top whiskey critics, securing a spot on Whisky Advocate’s prestigious "Top 20 Whiskies of the Year" with a 93-point score and earning Double Gold and Best in Class accolades across major international spirits competitions. Spirits writers and collectors routinely praise the release for bridging the gap between Lynchburg’s signature sweet banana-and-caramel distillate and the deeper, decadent confectionery notes typically found only in mature, high-end craft-toasted bourbon.

title: Old Forester Birthday Bourbon 2026 - 700 ml
vendor: 300614 - Bf Canada - A Division Of The Hive
bodyHtml:
This highly allocated vintage-dated Kentucky straight bourbon whiskey originates from Louisville, Kentucky, crafted by the historic Old Forester Distilling Co. (Brown-Forman). Released annually on September 2nd to commemorate the birthday of founder George Garvin Brown—who first bottled bourbon under a sealed glass bottle in 1870—the Old Forester Birthday Bourbon series represents one of the most prestigious, single-day vintage expressions in American whiskey. Sourced entirely from a single day's production and matured across select floors of Brown-Forman’s heat-cycled warehouses, each annual batch is curated by Master Distiller Chris Morris and Master Taster Melissa Rift. Produced from Old Forester's proprietary grain bill—72% corn, 18% rye, and 10% malted barley—the 2026 vintage marks the 26th annual release in the historic series, presented in the iconic retro 1950s-style decanter bottle. In line with the collection's traditional aging profile, the 2026 release is aged approximately 12 years and custom-proofed to showcase the specific barrel lot's optimal balance.

Spirit Description

This bourbon pours a radiant, deep copper-mahogany hue with warm reddish-gold reflections, forming long, oily tears that descend deliberately down the glass. On the nose, it delivers an aromatic bouquet that marries dessert richness with antique oak: vibrant aromas of dark brown sugar, butterscotch, and warm Madagascar vanilla bean mingle with stewed dark cherries, candied citrus peel, and juicy blackberries. Beneath the confectionery fruit core lie nuanced undertones of roasted pecans, sweet pipe tobacco, leather bookbindings, and fragrant cedar wood. On the palate, the mouthfeel is silky, viscous, and expansive. Initial waves of burnt caramel, maple syrup, and dark chocolate fondue give way to bright, spicy mid-palate tension: cracked black pepper, cinnamon bark, nutmeg, and aromatic mint leaf. The signature heat-cycled warehouse maturation yields deeply extracted, sweet wood lactones without introducing bitter or drying char tannins. The finish is remarkably long, warm, and elegant, trailing off with impressions of roasted walnuts, dark stone fruit leather, sweet barrel char, and lingering baking spices.

Accolades

Old Forester Birthday Bourbon is universally recognized as one of the "holy grail" allocated releases on the annual bourbon calendar, regularly fetching top honors across international competitions, including multiple Double Gold and Best in Show designations at the San Francisco World Spirits Competition. Reviewers from Whisky Advocate, Bourbon Review, and Wine Enthusiast consistently award Birthday Bourbon expressions 93–96 point ratings, applauding the heat-cycling technique that accelerates barrel extraction while preserving the vibrant fruit and floral esters of Old Forester's signature high-rye mash bill. Collectors and critics praise the series for offering a distinct, vintage-specific snapshot each autumn, making it a benchmark for mature, single-vintage blending.

title: Silver Oak Alexander Valley Cabernet Sauvignon 2021 - Bundle & Save
bodyHtml:
Silver Oak Alexander Valley Cabernet Sauvignon originates from the United States, within California's Sonoma County region and the Alexander Valley AVA subregion. Founded in 1972 by Raymond Twomey Duncan and Justin Meyer, Silver Oak established a singular focus on producing American oak–aged Cabernet Sauvignon capable of aging for decades. The estate's Alexander Valley winery, rebuilt in 2008, was the first winery in the world to earn LEED Platinum certification for building and operation, highlighting a commitment to sustainable viticulture across its gravelly benchland terroirs.

Wine Description

This red wine displays a deep ruby-garnet colour. The nose is rich, inviting, and highly aromatic, opening with vibrant scents of dark cherry, red plum, and blackberry intertwined with signature notes of cassis, vanilla, toasted coconut, dried sage, and sweet cedar wood. On the palate, it exhibits a full body with a smooth, velvety texture, supported by fine-grained tannins and balanced acidity. Stylistically, the wine delivers a classic harmony between rich berry fruit concentration and lush American oak spice, finishing long and supple with lingering notes of cocoa, coffee bean, and dark berry compote.

  • Varietal composition: Typically ~95% Cabernet Sauvignon, with small amounts of Merlot, Cabernet Franc, Malbec, and Petit Verdot
