Founded in 1988, CedarCreek is a pioneer of the British Columbia wine industry and is currently owned by the von Mandl family, who have championed a winemaking philosophy of minimal intervention and sustainable viticulture. This 'Crafted In BC' edition was necessitated by a severe 2024 winter freeze that destroyed nearly all local fruit, leading the winery to source premium grapes from the Willamette Valley in Oregon to be processed at their Kelowna estate.

Wine Description

CedarCreek 'Crafted in BC' Chardonnay presents a brilliant, pale gold-straw color in the glass with bright chartreuse and platinum highlights along the rim. Its sensory profile is exceptionally fresh, high-toned, and complex, delivering an energetic, precise, and refined portrayal of cool-climate Canadian Chardonnay. The bouquet opens with a soaring display of crisp green apples, Meyer lemon curd, and white peach, seamlessly layered with subtle underlays of toasted hazelnuts, white flowers, lemon thyme, a touch of pastry crust, and a distinct line of crushed stone minerality. On the palate, the wine is medium-bodied, sleek, and athletic, showcasing a vibrant core of crunchy orchard fruit, citrus peel, and juicy nectarine. It is characterized by its outstanding inner energy and an incisive, mouthwatering backbone of natural acidity that effortlessly elevates its mid-palate texture. The mouthfeel is broad, weightless, and linear, framed by gentle oak integration and fine-lees stirring (bâtonnage), carrying into a long, dry, and mineral-driven finish accented by persistent notes of citrus zest, toasted almond, and sea salt.

title: Chateau Cambon Beaujolais 2023
bodyHtml:
This structured and 'crystalline' red wine originates from France, within the regional Beaujolais A.O.C. appellation of southern Burgundy. Produced by Château Cambon the iconic natural wine estate founded in 1995 as a joint venture between the late, legendary Marcel Lapierre (Domaine Lapierre) and Jean-Claude Chanudet (Domaine Chamonard) this bottling represents a benchmark for pure, low-intervention Gamay. Sourced from 13 hectares of estate-grown, organically farmed vines planted between 1914 and 1950 in Saint-Jean-d'Ardières, the vineyard sits directly between the prestigious Crus of Morgon and Brouilly. Rooted in ancient granite, clay, and siliceous calcareous sand, these old vines benefit from a semi-continental climate featuring warm summer sunshine balanced by cool autumn breezes, enabling Gamay to achieve complete phenolic maturity while retaining a high-toned, mouthwatering natural acidity.

Wine Description

Château Cambon Beaujolais presents a luminous, translucent ruby-garnet color in the glass with bright violet reflections along the rim. Its sensory profile is exceptionally fresh, high-toned, and complex, delivering an energetic, juicy, and precisely focused portrait of old-vine Gamay. The bouquet opens with a soaring display of crushed wild raspberries, tart red cherries, and Bing cherries, seamlessly layered with complex underlays of fresh violets, peony, forest floor, subtle dried herbs, and a clean line of granitic minerality. On the palate, the wine is light-to-medium-bodied, sleek, and athletic, showcasing a vibrant core of crunchy red stone fruits, blood orange zest, and pomegranate. It is characterized by its outstanding inner energy and an incisive, mouthwatering backbone of natural acidity that cuts cleanly across the mid-palate. The mouthfeel is broad, weightless, and silky (gouleyant), framed by soft, melted tannins that glide into a long, dry, and mineral-driven finish accented by persistent notes of cherry skin, wild strawberry, and flint.

title: The Macallan Harmony Collection Honey Orchid Tea
bodyHtml:
Founded in 1824, The Macallan is renowned as one of the world's foremost single malt Scotch whisky distilleries, located in the heart of the Speyside region. The distillery has built its reputation on an uncompromising pursuit of excellence, which is guided by the philosophy of its 'Six Pillars,' including an almost fanatical dedication to wood management and the use of curiously small stills.

Whisky Description

  • Color: Warm honey hue.

  • Aroma: Elegant aromas of wild honey, orange blossom, and creamy vanilla rise gently from the glass. The nose is blooming with orchard intensity, including vivid peach and apricot, followed by floral honey.

  • Palate: The palate is silky, unfolding with malt, candied citrus, and floral tea notes. Fresh peaches in rich syrup, warm citrus, and toffee lead to a fascinating detour of light floral notes and a delicate, leafy astringency, with the oolong character coming through pure and clear. There is a beautiful balance of roasted richness and a final touch of dessert wine sweetness.

  • Finish: The finish is long, smooth, and radiant, like the lingering warmth of the morning sun over mountain tea fields.

Food Pairing

It pairs exceptionally well with desserts such as a honey-glazed fruit tart, peach cobbler, or crème brûlée.

title: Stoneleigh Sauvignon Blanc Latitude 2023
bodyHtml:
This structured and 'crystalline' white wine originates from New Zealand, within the world-renowned Marlborough region on the northern tip of the South Island. Produced by Stoneleigh a benchmark estate established in 1980 the 'Latitude' range takes its name from the specific microclimate of the "Golden Mile" in the Wairau Valley, where stony riverbed soils sit along an ideal latitude for slow, balanced grape ripening. The vineyard floor is covered in sun-bleached river stones ("sun stones") that absorb heat during the bright Marlborough days and radiate warmth back up into the canopy at night. This unique thermal dynamic, combined with cool maritime night breezes, allows Sauvignon Blanc to achieve intense tropical phenolic maturity while maintaining a razor-sharp, mouthwatering natural acidity.

Wine Description

Stoneleigh Latitude Sauvignon Blanc presents a luminous, pale straw-yellow color in the glass with bright chartreuse and platinum reflections along the rim. Its sensory profile is exceptionally fresh, high-toned, and complex, delivering an energetic, explosive, and precisely focused portrait of stony Wairau Valley terroir. The bouquet opens with a soaring display of passionfruit, white peach, and ripe pink grapefruit, seamlessly layered with complex underlays of lemongrass, crushed tomato leaf, flint, and a distinct line of wet-stone minerality. On the palate, the wine is light-to-medium-bodied, sleek, and athletic, showcasing a vibrant core of crunchy tropical fruits, lime curd, and sweet melon. It is characterized by its outstanding inner energy and an incisive, mouthwatering backbone of natural acidity that cuts cleanly across the mid-palate. The mouthfeel is broad, weightless, and linear, carrying into an extraordinarily long, dry, and mineral-driven finish accented by persistent notes of lime peel, flint, and saline sea spray.

title: Liquidity Crafted In BC Viognier 2024
bodyHtml:
This structured and 'aristocratic' white wine originates from Canada, within the prestigious Okanagan Falls D.O.A. sub-G.I. (Geographical Indication) in the heart of British Columbia's Okanagan Valley. Produced by Liquidity Wines—an estate renowned for crafting expressive, small-lot wines overlooking Vaseux Lake the 2024 'Crafted in BC' Viognier represents a historic, resilient response to the catastrophic agricultural conditions of the 2024 vintage. In January 2024, an unprecedented arctic cold snap swept through the Okanagan Valley, sending temperatures plunging below -20°C to -25°C for extended periods. This severe freeze destroyed fruit buds and decimated up to 90% of British Columbia’s native grape harvest. To protect the wine region and preserve their production standards, the provincial government introduced the temporary "Crafted in BC" initiative. Under this framework, Liquidity’s winemaking team partnered with trusted, like-minded growers in benchmark Viognier growing regions specifically sourcing premier fruit directly from France’s Rhône Valley to be carefully vinified and crafted at their Okanagan Falls estate.

Wine Description

Liquidity 'Crafted in BC' Viognier presents a luminous, pale gold color in the glass with bright greenish-yellow and chartreuse highlights along the rim. Its sensory profile is exceptionally fresh, high-toned, and complex, delivering an energetic, opulent, and precisely focused portrait of classic Viognier. The bouquet opens with a soaring display of fresh white peaches, candied orange blossom, tangerine, and red rose petals, seamlessly layered with subtle underlays of honeysuckle, lemon curd, ginger spice, white pepper, and a clean line of crushed stone minerality. On the palate, the wine is medium-to-full-bodied, supple, and athletic, showcasing a succulent core of stone fruits, lychee, and citrus oil. It is characterized by its outstanding inner energy and a bright, mouthwatering backbone of natural acidity that effortlessly balances Viognier's natural broadness and aromatic weight. The mouthfeel is broad, rich, and velvety, framed by gentle textural weight gained from fine-lees contact, carrying into a long, dry, and mineral-driven finish accented by persistent notes of orange peel, ginger, and jasmine.

title: Osoyoos Larose Petales D'Osoyoos 2022
bodyHtml:
Originating from Canada in the famous Okanagan Valley region of British Columbia, specifically within the warm South Okanagan subregion overlooking Osoyoos Lake, Osoyoos Larose Petales D'Osoyoos 2022 represents a refined, early-approachable expression of Canadian Bordeaux-style blending. Established in 1998 as an ambitious joint venture between Vincor Canada and Groupe Taillan of Bordeaux (owners of Chateau Gruaud Larose), the estate is today fully owned by Groupe Taillan. Crafted as the estate's second wine from younger vines across the 32-hectare property, the winemaking philosophy combines traditional French winemaking techniques with South Okanagan terroir. Utilizing hand sorting, parcel-by-parcel fermentations in cone-shaped stainless steel tanks, and aging for 12 to 16 months in two and three-year-old French oak barrels, the estate crafts a round, supple, and food-friendly red blend designed for immediate enjoyment and short-term cellaring.

Wine Description

The wine presents a clear, deep garnet red colour with vibrant ruby highlights along the rim. An expressive, complex bouquet opens with primary aromas of ripe blackberry, dark plum, and red currant, interwoven with fragrant notes of wild violet, sweet cedar wood, vanilla bean, baking spices, and a subtle touch of sagebrush minerality. On the palate, it is medium to full bodied, juicy, and well rounded, delivering rich layers of black fruits, dark cherry, and cocoa balanced by a spine of vibrant natural acidity. Framed by smooth, fine-grained tannins and a savory, earthy undercurrent, it concludes with a long, energetic, and spicy finish. Composed of a classic Merlot-dominated Bordeaux blend alongside Cabernet Sauvignon, Cabernet Franc, Petit Verdot, and Malbec, this release offers an optimal drinking window of 2026–2032. Stylistically, it effortlessly combines French structural elegance with South Okanagan fruit generosity and soft, supple textures.

title: GlenDronach 28 Years Old Cask 4193 Single Malt
vendor: 300614 - Bf Canada - A Division Of The Hive
bodyHtml:
This single cask Scotch whisky originates from Scotland, produced in the Highland region. Crafted at the historic GlenDronach Distillery—founded in 1826 near Forgue in Aberdeenshire—the distillery is renowned for its mastery of sherry cask maturation. Distilled in 1993, this expression spent 28 long years maturing exclusively in a single Oloroso sherry puncheon (Cask #4193) before being hand-selected by Master Blender Rachel Barrie for the distillery's prestigious Cask Bottling batch releases.

Spirit Description

This single malt presents a deep, dark mahogany hue with rich walnut highlights in the glass. The nose is extraordinarily opulent and dark, opening with aromas of stewed damson plums, dark fruitcake, espresso, and pipe tobacco, supported by toasted walnuts, polished oak, and rich Oloroso sherry influence. On the palate, it is full-bodied, dense, and velvety, delivering rich flavours of dark chocolate truffles, marzipan, black cherry preserve, and sweet treacle, balanced by seasoned oak spice, clove, and a touch of leather. The finish is exceptionally long, warm, and lingering, leaving a deep impression of dried fruit, cocoa, and sweet sherry woodiness. Bottled at a natural cask strength of 51% ABV without chill-filtration or added caramel coloring, it exhibits supreme depth, concentration, and sherry oak integration.

title: El Jolgorio Jabali Mezcal
bodyHtml:
This artisanal mezcal originates from Mexico, produced in the Oaxaca region. Crafted under the esteemed El Jolgorio label—founded by the Cortés family, who have been producing mezcal for over six generations—this expression represents one of the rarest offerings in their portfolio. It is made using 100% wild Jabalí agave (Agave Convallis), an extremely difficult wild agave to harvest and ferment due to its high concentration of natural saponins, which cause intense foaming during fermentation. The agave hearts are roasted in traditional underground pit ovens, crushed, fermented in open wooden vats, and double-distilled in small copper pot stills.

Spirit Description

This mezcal presents a crystal-clear, brilliant appearance in the glass. The nose is complex, pungent, and intensely herbal, opening with aromas of fresh mint, eucalyptus, green bell pepper, and damp earth, interwoven with delicate wafts of mezquite wood smoke, citrus zest, and roasted agave sweetness. On the palate, it is full-bodied with a rich, oily texture, delivering vibrant flavours of tart green apples, pine needles, cracked white pepper, and lemongrass, balanced by deep mineral notes, clay, and subtle roasted agave sugar. The finish is long, dry, and exceptionally complex, leaving a lingering trail of herbal brightness, subtle smoke, and earthy minerality. Bottled at an ABV of around 47–52% (depending on the specific batch and palenquero), it offers an uncommonly bright, herbaceous, and powerful mezcal profile.

title: Compass Box The Circle No. 2
bodyHtml:
This limited-edition blended malt Scotch whisky originates from Scotland. Created by the renowned boutique blending house Compass Box, "The Circle" series is an innovative collaboration project led by Compass Box Whiskymaker James Saxon alongside the winner of Compass Box's global bartender competition. For The Circle No. 2, Compass Box collaborated with bartender Rosey Mitchell. The expression was designed around the concept of synesthesia—specifically exploring the sensory connection between coral color and taste—and features a high proportion of single malts from West Highland distilleries (such as Clynelish), Speyside, and heavily peat-smoked malts from Islay.

Spirit Description

This blended malt displays a bright, luminous pale coral-gold hue in the glass. The nose is vibrant and alluring, opening with sweet notes of tropical pineapple, yellow peach, vanilla cream, and honeyed malt, accompanied by gentle underlying traces of bonfire smoke, sea spray, and light citrus zest. On the palate, it is medium to full-bodied with a rich, silky texture, delivering dominant flavours of juicy orchard fruit, creamy vanilla custard, and poached pear, beautifully balanced by a subtle, aromatic thread of peat smoke and soft oak spice. The finish is long, clean, and warming, leaving a delicate impression of sweet fruit, sea salt, and lingering light smoke. Bottled at a strength of 46% ABV without chill-filtration or added caramel coloring, it exhibits outstanding balance, elegance, and texture.

title: Villa Sparina Gavi Di Gavi 2024
bodyHtml:
Originating from Italy in the famous Piedmont region, specifically within the historic Gavi DOCG of the province of Alessandria, Villa Sparina Gavi Di Gavi represents a benchmark, highly celebrated expression of Cortese winemaking. Founded in the 1970s by the Moccagatta family, Villa Sparina is instantly recognized worldwide for its distinctive, urn-shaped bottle design inspired by ancient wine vessels discovered on the estate. Sourced from south-facing vineyards in the heart of the Gavi municipality, the winery's philosophy focuses on capturing pure varietal brightness, mineral precision, and smooth texture through temperature controlled stainless steel fermentation without oak influence.

Wine Description

The wine presents a clear, pale straw colour with delicate greenish highlights in the glass. An expressive and refined bouquet opens with aromas of fresh yellow apple, white peach, and crisp green pear, interwoven with fragrant notes of white flowers, lime zest, subtle almond, and wet stone minerality. On the palate, it is medium bodied, sleek, and refreshing, delivering vibrant flavours of citrus fruit, crisp orchard fruit, and subtle lemongrass, all supported by a lively, mouthwatering core of natural acidity. Finishing clean, textured, and elegant, it leaves a long, persistent impression of fresh fruit and delicate flinty minerality.

title: Louis Latour Aloxe Corton Premier Cru 'Les Chaillots' 2022
bodyHtml:
Originating from France in the famous Burgundy region, specifically within the Aloxe Corton Premier Cru appellation of the Cote de Beaune, Louis Latour Aloxe Corton Premier Cru Les Chaillots 2022 represents a classic, terroir-driven expression of Pinot Noir winemaking. Founded in 1797, Maison Louis Latour is one of Burgundy's most revered and historic merchant houses, family-owned for over two centuries. Situated at the base of the Corton hill, the Premier Cru Les Chaillots vineyard takes its name from its stony, pebble-rich limestone soils. Sourced from estate-owned vines averaging over 35 years of age, the winemaking philosophy relies on traditional open-top vat fermentations, partial oak aging in custom copper-crafted French oak barrels from the house's own cooperage, and minimal handling to showcase site-specific elegance.

Wine Description

The wine presents a luminous, deep garnet red colour with bright ruby highlights along the rim. An expressive and refined bouquet opens with aromas of ripe dark cherry, wild raspberry, and red currant, interwoven with sophisticated notes of forest floor, subtle clove, pipe tobacco, dried rose petal, and crushed limestone minerality. On the palate, it is medium to full bodied, structured, and vibrant, delivering concentrated flavours of black cherry, red plum, and subtle sweet spice, all supported by a spine of lively, mouthwatering natural acidity. Framed by Les Chaillots' signature fine-grained, firm tannins and a savory, earthy backbone, it concludes with a long, persistent, and elegant finish. Composed of 100% Pinot Noir, this release offers an optimal drinking window of 2026–2040. Stylistically, it combines Cote de Beaune floral finesse with the dark-fruited density and structural power typical of Corton's limestone slopes.

title: Planeta Chardonnay 2024
bodyHtml:
This structured and 'aristocratic' white wine originates from Italy, within the Menfi D.O.C. appellation in southwestern Sicily. Produced by Planeta an iconic family-owned estate founded in the 1990s that revolutionized modern Sicilian viticulture this single-estate Chardonnay stands as the undisputed benchmark for Mediterranean white wine excellence. Sourced from choice, low-yielding blocks in the estate's historic Ulmo and Maroccoli vineyards overlooking Lake Arancio, the vines are rooted in nutrient-poor clay-limestone soils rich in pebbles. The warm, sun-drenched Mediterranean climate is tempered by constant coastal sea breezes and significant altitude shifts, allowing Chardonnay grapes to achieve complete phenolic ripeness while locking in a razor-sharp, age-worthy natural acidity and complex minerality.

Wine Description

Planeta Chardonnay presents a brilliant, deep golden-yellow color in the glass with vivid chartreuse and emerald highlights along the rim. Its sensory profile is exceptionally bold, high-toned, and complex, delivering an expansive, precise, and luxurious portrayal of warm-climate Sicilian Chardonnay. The bouquet opens with a soaring, multi-layered display of ripe yellow peaches, candied orange peel, and tropical papaya, seamlessly integrated with complex underlays of roasted hazelnuts, pastry cream, orange blossom, white truffle, toasted brioche, and a distinct line of crushed limestone minerality. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied, muscular, and athletic, showcasing a succulent core of ripe orchard fruits, lemon curd, and salted butter. It is characterized by its outstanding inner energy and an incisive, mouthwatering backbone of natural acidity that effortlessly elevates its rich mid-palate fruit density. The mouthfeel is broad, velvety, and linear, framed by seamless oak integration and subtle savory weight gained from fine-lees stirring, gliding into an extraordinarily long, dry, and mineral-driven finish accented by lingering notes of toasted almond, citrus zest, and Mediterranean herbs.

title: Pupille Morellino Di Scansano Riserva 2023
bodyHtml:
This structured and 'crystalline' red wine originates from Italy, within the esteemed Morellino di Scansano Riserva D.O.C.G. appellation located in the rolling coastal hills of the southern Tuscan Maremma. Produced by Fattoria Le Pupille the benchmark estate led by Elisabetta Geppetti, affectionately known as the "Signora del Morellino" this wine represents the pinnacle of traditional Maremman Sangiovese. Sourced from selection-designated vineyard blocks including the historic Pereta and Puntone sites situated at elevations between 200 and 250 meters above sea level, the vines are rooted in dry, nutrient-poor soils composed of sandstone, clay-limestone, and crushed gravelly silt. The Mediterranean microclimate features intense coastal solar exposure tempered by cooling afternoon sea breezes sweeping in from the Tyrrhenian Sea, allowing Sangiovese (locally called Morellino) to accumulate generous fruit weight while preserving a vibrant, age-worthy natural acidity.

Wine Description

Fattoria Le Pupille Morellino di Scansano Riserva presents a deep, luminous garnet-ruby color in the glass with vivid magenta and brick reflections along the rim. Its sensory profile is exceptionally fresh, high-toned, and complex, delivering an energetic, expressive, and precisely focused portrait of coastal Tuscan Sangiovese. The bouquet opens with a soaring display of dark black cherries, crushed red plums, and wild blackberries, seamlessly layered with complex underlays of dried rose petals, Mediterranean brushwood (macchia), sweet pipe tobacco, leather, and a distinct line of crushed stone minerality. On the palate, the wine is medium-to-full-bodied, sleek, and athletic, showcasing a vibrant core of dark stone fruits, blood orange zest, dark cocoa nibs, and savory wild herbs. It is characterized by its outstanding inner energy and an incisive, mouthwatering backbone of natural acidity that effortlessly elevates its mid-palate fruit density. The mouthfeel is broad, velvety, and supple, framed by fine-grained, chalky Sangiovese tannins that glide into a long, dry, and savory finish accented by persistent notes of cherry skin, cedar, and forest floor.

title: Il Poggione Rosso Di Montalcino 2023
bodyHtml:
This structured and 'crystalline' red wine originates from Italy, within the esteemed Rosso di Montalcino D.O.C. appellation of southern Tuscany. Produced by Tenuta Il Poggione one of the historic, founding estates of the Brunello di Montalcino consortium, owned by the Franceschi family since the late 19th century this wine is crafted with the same rigorous viticultural standards as the estate's world-renowned Brunellos. Sourced from estate vineyard parcels situated on the southern slopes of Montalcino at elevations between 150 and 450 meters above sea level, the vines average 15 to 20 years of age and are rooted in nutrient-poor soils composed of galestro (schistose clay), limestone, and gravelly silt. The estate's warm Mediterranean microclimate benefits from cooling breezes sweeping off the Tyrrhenian Sea and Mount Amiata, allowing Sangiovese Grosso to achieve full phenolic maturity while preserving a bright, mouthwatering natural acidity.

Wine Description

Tenuta Il Poggione Rosso di Montalcino presents a luminous, deep ruby-garnet color in the glass with bright magenta highlights along the rim. Its sensory profile is exceptionally fresh, high-toned, and complex, delivering an energetic, pure, and precisely focused expression of southern Montalcino Sangiovese. The bouquet opens with a soaring display of ripe dark cherries, crushed red plums, and wild strawberries, seamlessly layered with complex underlays of dried rose petals, Mediterranean brushwood (macchia), leather, wild thyme, and a distinct line of crushed stone minerality. On the palate, the wine is medium-bodied, sleek, and athletic, showcasing a vibrant core of crunchy red stone fruits, blood orange zest, and subtle earthy spices. It is characterized by its outstanding inner energy and an incisive, mouthwatering backbone of natural acidity that effortlessly lifts its mid-palate fruit density. The mouthfeel is broad, silky, and supple, framed by fine-grained, chalky Sangiovese tannins that glide into a long, dry, and mineral-driven finish accented by persistent notes of cherry skin, wild herbs, and forest floor.

title: Radeberger Pilsner - 30 Litre Keg
bodyHtml:
Radeberger Pilsner is the benchmark for classic Royal Saxon brewing and one of Germany’s most revered traditional beers. Brewed continuously since 1872 in Radeberg, near Dresden, it holds the distinction of being the first beer in Germany to be brewed exclusively as a "Pilsner" style. Historically favored by German nobility earning the official title of "Kanzler-Bräu" under Chancellor Otto von Bismarck and royal appointment by King Frederick Augustus III of Saxony it stands today as a iconic representative of the German Pilsner (Northern/Eastern Style): uncompromisingly crisp, straw-gold, and assertively bitter.

Beer Description

Radeberger Pilsner pours a brilliant, crystal-clear pale straw-gold topped with a dense, snow-white foam head that leaves intricate rings of lacing on the glass.

Aroma: The nose is clean, sharp, and traditional. It leads with dominant notes of spicy German noble hops, fresh-cut grass, and cracked pepper, resting over a delicate base of sweet pilsner malt and fresh cracker dough.

Palate: On the tongue, it is light-to-medium bodied with a crisp, high-effervescent mouthfeel. It opens with a brief wave of bready malt sweetness, which is quickly sliced open by a prominent, dry, and assertive herbal hop bitterness. The mid-palate reveals hints of lemon peel and tea-like hop resins, concluding with a long, bone-dry, and lingering bitter finish.

Profile: It sits at a traditional 4.8% ABV and a firm, structured bitterness of 33 IBU, making it noticeably punchier and more bitter than mass-market light lagers.

Technical Notes: Radeberger’s sharp clarity and distinctive bitterness stem from its strict adherence to the Reinheitsgebot combined with regional water chemistry. It is brewed using 100% German pilsner malt and soft, local artesian water. The bittering and aroma profile is driven by select Hallertau noble hops. A cold, patient bottom-fermentation and long lagering phase clean up all fruity esters, resulting in an ultra-attenuated, dry lager where hop resins take center stage.

title: Bearface Bear Bon Charred Barrel Whisky
bodyHtml:
Bearface Bear-Bon Whisky is an innovative Canadian whisky produced by Bearface Spirits in British Columbia, Canada. Known for its signature "elemental aging" process where whisky barrels are exposed to extreme seasonal weather shifts in re-purposed shipping containers in the Canadian wilderness Bearface created Bear-Bon to reimagine American bourbon style through a distinctly northern lens. Playfully named to honor bourbon-style production without violating geographic appellation laws, Bear-Bon pairs a corn-heavy Canadian mash bill with heavy oak charring, yielding a spirit that blends southern bourbon sweetness with smooth Canadian whisky craftsmanship.

Spirit Description

Bearface Bear-Bon starts with a core Canadian grain whisky distilled primarily from high-grade corn alongside select malted barley. The whisky undergoes primary maturation in ex-bourbon American oak barrels before entering Bearface's signature elemental aging process in the wilderness of British Columbia. It is finished in heavy virgin oak casks with intense charring (often referred to as alligator char). The high temperature swings of the Canadian wilderness force the spirit deep into the charred wood, imparting robust notes of sweet vanilla, toasted corn, and rich wood smoke without requiring geographic bourbon production.

  • Colour: Deep amber-copper with warm mahogany glints and slow, heavy legs in the glass.

  • Aroma: Sweet, wood-forward, and rich, opening with intense vanilla bean, charred oak, and dark brown sugar, followed by sweet toasted corn, butterscotch, dried apple, and gentle baking spice.

  • Palate: Full-flavored, smooth, and warm on the entry. Upfront sweet notes of caramel, maple cream, and sweet corn yield to charred oak, toasted coconut, dark chocolate, and a pleasant rye-like baking spice warmth.

  • Body: Medium-to-full-bodied with a velvety, mouth-coating, and rich texture.

  • Finish: Long, warm, and satisfying, trailing off with persistent toasted oak tannins, sweet vanilla, dark molasses, and a soft wood-smoke dryness.

  • ABV: Bottled at 40% ABV (80 Proof).

title: Gordon's Gin
bodyHtml: Instant citrus aromas on the nose creating a very fresh experience. Quite dry on the palate however, with lots of citrus lemon flavors hitting first.

title: Don Fulano Anejo Tequila
bodyHtml:
Don Fulano Tequila is an agricultural product. The fruit of five generations of agave farmers and a singular tequila-making heritage which brings together the Highlands of Jalisco and the Valleys of Tequila. Estate-Grown and bottled, its entirely made from three ingredients: hand-selected mature agave, proprietary yeast, and natural spring volcanic water.

Don Fulano Anejo is a marriage of very old tequilas aged in French limousine and nevers oak casks that previously held wines. It’s deep and complex with dried fruits and spice elements like cardamom and allspice which complement elegantly the right touch of sweetness that comes from slowly cooked mature agave. Honey and caramelized nuts emerge from a long finish together with a refreshing light menthol. Great to wrap up a nice dinner.

title: Don Fulano Blanco Tequila
bodyHtml:
Don Fulano Tequila is an agricultural product. The fruit of five generations of agave farmers and a singular tequila-making heritage which brings together the Highlands of Jalisco and the Valleys of Tequila. Estate-Grown and bottled, its entirely made from three ingredients: hand-selected mature agave, proprietary yeast, and natural spring volcanic water.

Don Fulano Blanco is a bright and colorful expression of highland agave. It’s fresh on the nose and yet profound with a beautiful elegance. There is harmony between a wide spectrum of aromas that only mature hillside agave offers; a myriad of delicate fruit notes is balanced by a light herbaceousness and a butterscotch oiliness. Reminiscent of damp red soil it opens the senses and awakens the appetite, it almost makes you want to chew it. A great aperitif or quintessence of a great cocktail.

title: Cocchi Barolo Chinato - 500 ml
bodyHtml:
Barolo Chinato is an aromatized wine produced with Barolo DOCG, enriched with cinchona calisaya bark, rhubarb and gentian root and the precious cardamom seed whose active principles are extracted with a slow maceration at room temperature. Characterized by balance and harmony in the perfume with an immediate pleasant taste and a pleasant aromatic persistence.

The occasions to appreciate Cocchi Barolo Chinato are diverse, with a particular success in the good restoration when served at environment temperature or as elegant end of the meal or even steam heated with orange zest. Almost a surprise then the recent discovery of Barolo Chinato as an “ideal liquid” to support and complete the persistent taste of the mostly cocoa rich chocolates. Andrea Slitti, among the best maîtres chocolatiers, has produced an artisanal praline with Barolo Chinato. A top-of the-range product distributed by Giulio Cocchi to accompany the tasting and to show the successful marriage.

title: Old Ballantruan 10 Year Old
bodyHtml: The first edition of Old Ballantruan with an age statement, bottled after 10 years. It's made at Tomintoul using heavily peated barley and is bottled at a solid 50% ABV. Nose: Gently spicy with smokey “peat reak” balanced by sweeter creamy core. Palate:Some gentle peaty smokiness with a sweet creamy malty backbone. Finish: Climbing finish of sweetness gradually replaced with smokey depth.

title: James Gin American Mustard
bodyHtml:
Don’t be fooled by its name; this gin has won multiple awards for its warmth & savoury profile. We’ve combined mustard seeds & gherkins to create something really spectacular.

American Mustard (or ‘Ramstud’ in America because the authorities were worried you’d put it on your burger) is blended from fresh mustard seed and dill pickles as the perfect accompaniment to every traditional American fast food recipe.

We made this one to reward our loyal American customers & decided to create ‘The Spirit of America’ so that they wouldn’t have to drink gin promoted by a Canadian masquerading as an American.

Bottle Colour

We’re experimenting with using 100% recycled glass bottles. This means some bottles have a slight green colour. But the gin doesn’t. That’s slightly yellow because of the mustard, obviously.

title: Laphroaig Cairdeas 2024 - 700 ml
bodyHtml:
The 2024 Cairdeas limited edition release  is a 10-year-old Laphroaig with a bold combination of flavours from the casks of two popular previous releases: 2019’s Triple Wood and 2021’s PX Cask. Bottled at a fixed strength of 52.4% ABV for a memorable character  to share with Friends.

Rich, sweet and oily on the palate, with notes of smoked orange toffee, stewed peaches and smouldering campfire. Dried fruit notes balanced with hints of coffee grounds and liquorice root for a long lasting and slightly herbal finish.

title: Rabbit Hole ‘Boxergrail’ Rye Whiskey
bodyHtml:
This structured and 'muscular' American whiskey originates from the United States, crafted in the heart of Louisville, Kentucky within the renowned Kentucky Bourbon & Rye district. Produced by Rabbit Hole Distillery an innovative, visionary distillery founded in 2012 by Kaveh Zamanian and now part of Pernod Ricard 'Boxergrail' honors Louisville’s rich boxing heritage and legendary local fighters. Sourced from choice, estate-designed grain recipes and distilled in custom copper column stills, the spirit matures in charred American oak casks within traditional multi-story rickhouses. Louisville’s extreme humid continental climate features scorching summer heat waves and freezing winter nights, driving intense interaction between spirit and wood to forge deep amber color, rich oak sugars, and bold spice complexity.

Wine Description

The Rabbit Hole ‘Boxergrail’ Kentucky Straight Rye Whiskey presents a deep, luminous copper-amber color in the glass with bright golden-orange highlights along the rim. Its sensory profile is exceptionally bold, high-toned, and complex, delivering an expansive, precise, and expressive portrayal of modern Kentucky Straight Rye. The bouquet opens with a soaring, multi-layered display of toasted rye bread, candied citrus peel, and sweet vanilla bean, seamlessly integrated with complex underlays of baking spices (cinnamon, nutmeg, clove), fresh spearmint, pipe tobacco, toasted oak, and a subtle line of dark caramel. On the palate, the whiskey is full-bodied, muscular, and athletic, showcasing a succulent core of spiced orchard fruit, butterscotch, dark cocoa nibs, and savory herbal notes. It is characterized by its outstanding inner energy and an incisive, mouthwatering spicy drive that cuts through the rich wood sweetness. The mouthfeel is broad, velvety, and supple, carrying into an extraordinarily long, dry, and warm finish accented by persistent notes of black pepper, mint, and charred oak.

title: Simonnet Febvre Saint Bris 2023
bodyHtml:
This structured and 'crystalline' white wine originates from France, within the unique Saint-Bris A.O.C. appellation of the Yonne department in northern Burgundy, located just southwest of Chablis. Produced by Simonnet-Febvre a historic Burgundian estate founded in 1840 and now operated under the stewardship of Maison Louis Latour this wine highlights the exceptional, singular terroir of Saint-Bris, the only appellation in Burgundy permitted to grow Sauvignon varieties rather than Chardonnay. Sourced from choice vineyard plots in the lieu-dit 'Auxerrois' (referring to the historic Auxerre district), the vines are rooted in Kimmeridgian and Portlandian limestone-clay soils rich in fossilized marine shells (Exogyra virgula). The cool, northern continental microclimate features crisp winds and bright solar radiation, allowing Sauvignon Blanc and Sauvignon Gris to achieve full phenolic maturity while locking in a razor-sharp, mouthwatering natural acidity.

Wine Description

Simonnet-Febvre Saint-Bris Auxerrois presents a luminous, pale straw-yellow color in the glass with bright chartreuse and silver reflections along the rim. Its sensory profile is exceptionally fresh, high-toned, and complex, delivering an energetic, mineral-driven, and precisely focused portrait of northern Burgundian terroir. The bouquet opens with a soaring display of citrus zest, green apple, and white peach, seamlessly layered with complex underlays of lemongrass, white floral blossoms, crushed chalk, and a distinct line of oyster-shell minerality. On the palate, the wine is light-to-medium-bodied, sleek, and athletic, showcasing a vibrant core of crunchy orchard fruit, lemon curd, and delicate tropical accents. It is characterized by its outstanding inner energy and an incisive, mouthwatering backbone of natural acidity that cuts cleanly through the mid-palate fruit texture. The mouthfeel is weightless, supple, and linear, carrying into an extraordinarily long, dry, and mineral-driven finish accented by lingering notes of lime peel and flint.

title: Canalicchio di Sopra Brunello di Montalcino 2017 - 3 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
Originating from Italy in the famous Tuscany region, specifically within the northern subregion of the Brunello di Montalcino DOCG, Canalicchio di Sopra Brunello di Montalcino 2017 represents a benchmark, classic expression of estate-grown Sangiovese. Founded in 1962 by Primo Pacenti, the historic estate is today managed by the third generation of the Ripaccioli family. The winery's philosophy combines organic vineyard practices, precise parcel-by-parcel fermentations in stainless steel and concrete, and long aging in traditional large Slavonian oak casks to produce elegant, terroir-driven Brunellos that highlight the cool, clay and marl-rich soils of the Canalicchio cru.

Wine Description

The wine presents a deep, luminous garnet red colour with bright ruby reflections in the glass. An expressive and complex bouquet opens with red cherry, wild strawberry, and crushed red plum, complemented by fragrant accents of dried rose petal, orange peel, leather, pipe tobacco, and wet stone minerality. On the palate, it is medium to full bodied, refined, and vibrant, delivering concentrated flavours of dark red berries, blood orange, and licorice, all supported by a spine of lively natural acidity. Framed by fine-grained, firm tannins and a savory, mineral-driven backbone, it concludes with a long, persistent, and elegant finish. Composed of 100% Sangiovese sourced from northern Montalcino estate vineyards, this release offers an optimal drinking window of 2026–2038. Stylistically, it combines northern Montalcino freshness, polished structural power, and classic aromatic finesse.

title: Mauro Veglio Barolo Castelletto 2019
bodyHtml:
Originating from Italy in the famous Piedmont region, specifically within the Monforte d'Alba subregion of the Barolo DOCG, Mauro Veglio Barolo Castelletto 2019 represents a single vineyard expression of modern, precise Nebbiolo winemaking. Founded in 1992, the estate is now managed by Mauro Veglio and his nephew Alessandro, who emphasize sustainable farming and site-specific purity. The winery's philosophy focuses on highlighting Monforte's naturally powerful, structured terroir through meticulous vineyard care, short-to-medium skin maceration, and balanced aging in small French oak barriques to produce rich, approachable, yet deeply age-worthy Barolos.

Wine Description

The wine presents a clear, translucent ruby red colour with garnet reflections along the rim. An expressive and layered bouquet opens with dark red cherry, wild cranberry, and crushed plum, complemented by fragrant accents of dried rose petal, licorice, eucalyptus, pipe tobacco, and wet stone minerality. On the palate, it is full bodied, taut, and energetic, delivering concentrated flavours of red fruit, blood orange, and dark cocoa supported by a firm, mouthwatering core of natural acidity. Framed by Monforte's signature muscular, tightly woven tannins and an undercurrent of broad mineral depth, it concludes with a long, intense, and savory finish. Composed of 100% Nebbiolo harvested from the prized Castelletto cru, this release offers an optimal drinking window of 2026–2042. Stylistically, it combines modern fruit clarity and oak polish with Monforte d'Alba's formidable structural power.

Accolades:

95 Points - Robert Parker: "In the dark blue label, the Mauro Veglio 2019 Barolo Castelletto shines from within the glass with dark ruby and garnet highlights. The Castelletto (with fruit from Monforte d'Alba) has a dark center of gravity with black cherry, plum and iron ore. This wine offers good power, structure and an especially firm texture. At its core, it is chiseled and hard. It definitely needs more cellar age, but I suspect this bottle will be worth the wait."

title: Little Book Chapter X Cask Strength
bodyHtml:
This cask strength American whiskey originates from the United States, produced in the Kentucky region. Created by Freddie Noe—eighth-generation Beam family distiller and Master Distiller of the Fred B. Noe Distillery at Jim Beam—the "Little Book" series is an annual, limited-release whiskey collection named after Freddie's childhood nickname given by his grandfather, Booker Noe. Chapter X (Chapter 10) represents the 10th landmark edition in this celebrated series, featuring a complex blend of aged, uncut, and unfiltered cask-strength whiskies crafted to push the boundaries of traditional American whiskey blending.

Spirit Description

This whiskey presents a deep, dark garnet mahogany hue in the glass. The nose is rich, dense, and intensely aromatic, opening with bold notes of dark cherry molasses, toasted oak, and rich leather, followed by undertones of toasted pecans, dark chocolate, and warm baking spices. On the palate, it is full-bodied and viscous, delivering a powerful burst of caramel fudge, seasoned oak, dark stone fruit, and cinnamon spice, balanced by complex rye grain warmth and sweet corn. The finish is exceptionally long, warm, and lingering, leaving a deep trail of charred oak, dark cocoa, vanilla bean, and peppery spice. Bottled at barrel proof (cask strength) without chill filtration, it offers extraordinary depth, raw intensity, and multi-layered complexity.

Accolades

The Little Book series by Freddie Noe is widely considered one of the most prestigious annual limited-edition whiskey releases in the United States. Individual chapters consistently achieve Double Gold and Gold Medals at the San Francisco World Spirits Competition, along with high 95+ ratings from major publications like Whisky Advocate and the Ultimate Spirits Challenge.

title: Graham's Vintage Port 2024
bodyHtml:
Originating from Portugal in the famous Douro region, specifically within the premier Cima Corgo and Douro Superior subregions, Graham's Vintage Port 2024 represents a landmark classic general declaration for the storied Port house. Founded in 1820 by brothers William and John Graham, the house is now owned and operated by Symington Family Estates. The estate's winemaking philosophy relies on harvesting old vine plots from flagship properties including Quinta dos Malvedos, Quinta do Tua, and Quinta das Lages, utilizing traditional stone lagar foot treading to craft rich, voluptuous, and deeply concentrated Vintage Ports built for extraordinary, multi-decade cellaring.

Wine Description

The wine presents a deep, opaque dark purple garnet colour with vibrant crimson highlights along the rim. An intense and multifaceted bouquet opens with Graham's signature aromas of ripe blackberry, dark cassis, and black cherry, interwoven with alluring notes of mint, eucalyptus, dark chocolate, rockrose, and exotic baking spices. On the palate, it is full bodied, lush, and powerfully built, delivering opulent layers of dark plum, cocoa bean, licorice, and espresso supported by a core of energetic natural acidity. Framed by muscular, fine-grained tannins and a firm schist mineral backbone, it concludes with a remarkably long, velvety, and persistent finish. Composed of a traditional blend of Touriga Nacional, Touriga Franca, Sousao, and Alicante Bouschet, this historic release offers an optimal drinking window of 2032–2065+. Stylistically, it combines Graham's hallmark opulent sweetness and rich black fruit weight with brilliant structural precision and freshness.

title: Castello di Monsanto Cabernet Sauvignon 'Nemo' 2019
bodyHtml:
Originating from Italy in the famous Tuscany region, specifically within the Barberino Val d'Elsa subregion of Chianti Classico, Castello di Monsanto Cabernet Sauvignon Nemo 2019 represents a landmark Super Tuscan expression of single varietal winemaking. Founded in 1961 by Aldo Bianchi and today expertly led by Laura Bianchi along with winemaker Andrea Giovannini, Castello di Monsanto is celebrated for its historic, estate-driven passion and long-term cellaring heritage. First planted in 1976 in the Il Mulino vineyard, Nemo was conceived to show how high elevation Tuscan terroir can elevate Cabernet Sauvignon, utilizing hand harvesting, temperature controlled steel fermentations, and traditional French oak barrel aging to produce powerful, site-specific wines of immense character and structural longevity.

Wine Description

The wine presents a luminous, deep ruby red colour with dark garnet edges in the glass. An expressive and multifaceted bouquet opens with classic varietal aromas of cassis, ripe black plum, and blackberry, interwoven with sophisticated notes of graphite, dried lavender, pipe tobacco, cedar wood, and subtle sage spice. On the palate, it is full bodied, focused, and precise, delivering rich layers of dark cherry, dark chocolate, and cassis supported by a spine of lively, mouthwatering natural acidity. Framed by polished, linear tannins and a firm mineral undercurrent, it concludes with a long, energetic, and savory finish. Composed of 100% Cabernet Sauvignon aged in French oak barrels, this release offers an optimal drinking window of 2026–2040. Stylistically, it combines Tuscan high altitude freshness and balsamic lift with classical Cabernet structural power and refined oak integration.

Accoldades:

95 Points - Vinous: "The 2019 Nemo, 100% Cabernet Sauvignon, is another fine effort in this range from Monsanto. Dark and savory, the 2019 exudes varietal character. Dried herbs, liquorice, lavender and mocha develop in the glass, adding layers of nuance. Readers will find a wine of tremendous character."

94 Points - Wine Advocate: "This wine enjoys a long history with fruit planted in 1976 in the Il Mulino vineyard on galestro shale soils. The Castello di Monsanto 2019 Cabernet Sauvignon Nemo showcases evident pyrazines with green notes that are folded into the soft, texturally rich nature of this full-bodied wine. Blackberry and blackcurrant cede to toasted spice and resin. These rich favors are folded into an extracted but balanced finish. This is your quintessential Bistecca alla Fiorentina wine, attractive, sultry and savory."

title: Graham's 80 Year Old Tawny Port
bodyHtml:
Originating from Portugal in the famous Douro region, specifically within the rugged Cima Corgo subregion, Graham's 80 Year Old Tawny Port represents an extraordinarily rare, masterfully aged expression of wood-matured Port winemaking. Founded in 1820 by brothers William and John Graham, the house of Graham's is renowned for its rich, complex aged tawnies, today managed by Symington Family Estates. Sourced from flagship estates including Quinta dos Malvedos and Quinta das Lages, the winemaking philosophy relies on generations of cooperage tradition and patient cask maturation in cool coastal lodges to craft aged tawnies of profound depth and historic character.

Wine Description

The wine presents a deep mahogany copper colour with luminous amber and pale green reflections along the rim. An extraordinary and complex bouquet opens with intense aromas of dried fig, fruitcake, and orange marmalade, interwoven with rich notes of roasted walnut, dark caramel, pipe tobacco, espresso, and exotic baking spices. On the palate, it is full bodied, luxurious, and deeply concentrated, delivering a velvety, mouth-coating texture packed with flavours of honeyed fruit, dark molasses, and cocoa, all balanced by a core of energetic natural acidity. Framed by a rich, viscous mouthfeel gained from eight decades of slow cask oxidation, it concludes with an remarkably long, persistent, and harmonious finish. Composed of a traditional blend of native Douro grape varieties including Touriga Franca, Touriga Nacional, Tinta Roriz, and Tinta Barroca, this rare release offers an optimal drinking window of 2026–2040. Stylistically, it combines profound oxidative depth and wood richness with incredible fresh vitality.

title: Warres Vintage Port 2020 (Boxed)
bodyHtml:
Originating from Portugal in the famous Douro region, specifically within the premier Cima Corgo subregion, Warres Vintage Port 2020 represents a historic single estate expression from the oldest British Port house. Established in 1670, Warre's is celebrated for its elegant, floral-driven style, today owned and operated by Symington Family Estates. Sourced primarily from the historic, high-elevation Quinta da Cavadinha estate alongside Quinta do Retiro, the winemaking philosophy relies on traditional stone lagar foot treading combined with modern temperature-controlled stainless steel lagares to produce concentrated, aromatic Vintage Ports built for long-term cellaring.

Wine Description

The wine presents an opaque, deep ruby purple colour with bright crimson rims in the glass. An expressive and highly floral bouquet opens with signature aromas of fresh rockrose, wild violet, and cassis, interwoven with vibrant notes of ripe dark cherry, wild blackberry, mint, dark chocolate, and subtle peppery spice. On the palate, it is full bodied, dense, and remarkably energetic, delivering rich layers of black fruits, licorice, and cocoa bean supported by a spine of lively natural acidity. Framed by fine-grained, muscular tannins and an undercurrent of schist minerality, it concludes with a long, elegant, and persistent finish. Composed of a traditional blend of Touriga Nacional, Touriga Franca, Sousao, and old-vine field blends, this boxed release offers an optimal drinking window of 2028–2055+. Stylistically, it effortlessly combines Warre's trademark floral lift and fresh elegance with intense fruit concentration and structural power.

title: Domaine Anne F. Gros Clos Vougeot Grand Cru 2024
bodyHtml:
This structured and 'aristocratic' red wine originates from France, within the prestigious Clos de Vougeot Grand Cru A.O.C. appellation of the Côte de Nuits sub-region in northern Burgundy. Domaine Anne F. Gros led by Anne Gros and her children (Julie, Anne-Lise, and Paul Tremblay) holds an iconic position in Vosne-Romanée, revered globally for producing wines of transcendent elegance, pure fruit focus, and profound terroir transparency. The domain owns a highly coveted 0.93-hectare parcel inside the historic walled Clos de Vougeot, situated in the premium Grand Maupertui section directly adjacent to the Grand Cru of Grands-Échézeaux. The old vines are rooted in shallow, gravelly clay-limestone soils overlying fractured Bajocian limestone bedrock. The continental microclimate features warm daytime sun balanced by cool nighttime air currents descending from the Combe de Concois, allowing Pinot Noir to achieve complete phenolic maturation while preserving a laser-focused, age-worthy natural acidity.

Wine Description

The 2024 Domaine Anne F. Gros Clos Vougeot Grand Cru Grand Maupertui presents a deep, luminous crimson-garnet color in the glass with shimmering magenta and violet highlights along the rim. Its sensory profile is exceptionally bold, high-toned, and complex, delivering an expansive, precise, and noble portrait of legendary Grand Cru terroir. The bouquet opens with a soaring, multi-layered display of black cherries, wild forest raspberries, and dark plum compote, seamlessly integrated with complex underlays of dried rose petals, violets, damp earth, crushed graphite, sweet spices, and a subtle line of crushed limestone minerality. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied, muscular, and athletic, showcasing a succulent core of dark stone fruits, blood orange peel, dark cocoa nibs, and savory spices. It is characterized by its outstanding inner energy and an incisive, mouthwatering backbone of natural acidity that effortlessly elevates its rich mid-palate fruit density. The mouthfeel is broad, silky, and linear, framed by firm, fine-grained, and chalky Grand Cru tannins that glide into an extraordinarily long, dry, and mineral-driven finish accented by lingering notes of dark cherry skin, truffle, and polished French oak.

Vintage Quality

The 2024 growing season across the Côte de Nuits featured a cool, wet spring followed by a warm, sun-drenched late summer and crisp, dry autumn harvest conditions. This late-season extended ripening window allowed Pinot Noir grapes to achieve ideal phenolic maturity, building deep skin flavor while locking in vibrant natural malic and tartaric acids. Domaine Anne F. Gros harvested pristine, healthy fruit at peak structural balance. The resulting 2024 Clos Vougeot Grand Cru combines high-energy fruit purity with noble Burgundian structural drive, built to evolve and improve gracefully in a cellar over the next 15 to 30+ years.

title: Sette Cieli Scipio Toscana 2020
bodyHtml:
This structured and 'aristocratic' red wine originates from Italy, within the esteemed Toscana I.G.T. appellation along the high-elevation coastal hills of Monteverdi Marrittimo, overlooking Bolgheri in Tuscan Maremma. Produced by Tenuta Sette Cieli—an elite organic estate founded by the Erika Ratti family—'Scipio' represents the crown jewel flag-ship wine of the winery, named after the legendary Roman general Scipio Africanus. Sourced from choice, terraced estate vineyard blocks perched at 400 meters above sea level, the vines are rooted in nutrient-poor, rock-strewn soils composed of galestro (schistose clay), albarese (limestone), and crushed flint. The estate's unique coastal microclimate combines high-altitude solar radiation with cooling Mediterranean sea breezes and drastic diurnal temperature drops, enabling Cabernet Franc to achieve complete phenolic maturity while retaining a razor-sharp, age-worthy natural acidity and an elegant structural frame.

Wine Description

The 2018 Tenuta Sette Cieli 'Scipio' Toscana presents a deep, luminous garnet-purple color in the glass with vivid crimson and magenta highlights along the rim. Its sensory profile is exceptionally bold, high-toned, and complex, delivering an expansive, precise, and noble portrayal of coastal Tuscan Cabernet Franc. The bouquet opens with a soaring, multi-layered display of wild cassis, dark plum, and black cherry compote, seamlessly layered with complex underlays of crushed graphite, dried violets, sage brush, sweet pipe tobacco, cedarwood, and a distinct trace of crushed stone minerality. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied, muscular, and athletic, showcasing a succulent core of dark stone fruits, blood orange peel, dark cocoa nibs, and savory dried herbs. It is characterized by its outstanding inner energy and an incisive, mouthwatering backbone of natural acidity that effortlessly elevates its rich mid-palate fruit density. The mouthfeel is broad, velvety, and linear, framed by firm, fine-grained, and chalky tannins that glide into an extraordinarily long, dry, and savory finish accented by lingering notes of iron, spices, and forest floor.

title: Caparzo Brunello di Montalcino 2020 - 3 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
This structured and 'aristocratic' red wine originates from Italy, within the esteemed Brunello di Montalcino D.O.C.G. appellation of southern Tuscany. Produced by Caparzo a pioneering estate founded in the late 1960s and led by Elisabetta Gnudi Angelini this wine is renowned for being one of the few Brunellos crafted from vineyard plots spanning all four major geographic quadrants of Montalcino (north, south, east, and west). The estate's vines, situated between 220 and 300 meters above sea level, are rooted in diverse soil profiles including galestro (schistose clay), albarese (limestone), sandy clay, and gravelly silt. This multi-terroir assembly balances cool northern freshness with warm southern fruit concentration, yielding a Brunello di Montalcino of remarkable structural complexity, aromatic depth, and consistent balance across every vintage.

Wine Description

The 2020 Caparzo Brunello di Montalcino presents a luminous, deep ruby-garnet color in the glass with brick and terracotta reflections along the rim. Its sensory profile is exceptionally fresh, high-toned, and complex, delivering an expansive, precise, and noble portrayal of classic Montalcino Sangiovese. The bouquet opens with a soaring display of dried red cherries, wild strawberries, and ripe red plums, seamlessly layered with complex underlays of dried rose petals, sweet pipe tobacco, leather, crushed stone minerality, and a subtle trace of Mediterranean brushwood (macchia). On the palate, the wine is medium-to-full-bodied, sleek, and athletic, showcasing a vibrant core of red stone fruits, blood orange zest, and subtle earthy spices. It is characterized by its outstanding inner energy and an incisive, mouthwatering backbone of natural acidity that effortlessly elevates its mid-palate fruit density. The mouthfeel is broad, velvety, and supple, framed by fine-grained, chalky Sangiovese tannins that glide into an extraordinarily long, dry, and savory finish accented by persistent notes of spice, wild herbs, and forest floor.

title: San Polino Rosso di Montalcino 2022
bodyHtml:
This structured and 'crystalline' red wine originates from Italy, within the esteemed Rosso di Montalcino D.O.C. appellation of southern Tuscany. Produced by San Polino an artisanal, certified biodynamic and organic estate managed by Katia Nussbaum and Luigi Fabbro this wine is crafted with the same uncompromising care and philosophy as the estate's world-famous Brunellos. Sourced from estate vineyard parcels situated on the southeast slopes of Montalcino at elevations between 350 and 450 meters above sea level, the vines are rooted in mineral-rich soils composed of galestro (schistose clay), limestone, and sandstone. The vineyard's warm Mediterranean microclimate benefits from cooling breezes sweeping off Mount Amiata and the Tyrrhenian Sea, allowing Sangiovese Grosso to achieve full phenolic maturity while preserving a bright, mouthwatering natural acidity.

Wine Description

San Polino Rosso di Montalcino presents a luminous, deep ruby-garnet color in the glass with bright magenta highlights along the rim. Its sensory profile is exceptionally fresh, high-toned, and complex, delivering an energetic, pure, and precisely focused expression of organic Montalcino Sangiovese. The bouquet opens with a soaring display of wild dark cherries, crushed red plums, and pomegranate, seamlessly layered with complex underlays of dried rose petals, Mediterranean scrub (macchia), wild thyme, leather, and a distinct line of crushed stone minerality. On the palate, the wine is medium-bodied, sleek, and athletic, showcasing a vibrant core of crunchy red stone fruits, blood orange zest, and subtle earthy spices. It is characterized by its outstanding inner energy and an incisive, mouthwatering backbone of natural acidity that effortlessly lifts its mid-palate fruit density. The mouthfeel is broad, silky, and supple, framed by fine-grained, chalky Sangiovese tannins that glide into a long, dry, and mineral-driven finish accented by persistent notes of cherry skin, wild herbs, and forest floor.

title: Invivo Hawke's Bay Chardonnay 2024
bodyHtml:
This structured and 'crystalline' white wine originates from New Zealand, within the prestigious Hawke's Bay region on the eastern coast of the North Island. Produced by Invivo Wines an innovative and acclaimed estate co-founded in 2008 by Tim Lightbourne and winemaker Rob Cameron this benchmark Chardonnay showcases the premier sub-regions of Hawke's Bay, including the Gimblett Gravels, Bridge Pa Triangle, and coastal Te Awanga. The vines are rooted in diverse alluvial soils consisting of free-draining river gravel, silt loam, and clay-limestone. Hawke's Bay’s sunny, warm maritime climate is tempered by afternoon sea breezes, allowing Chardonnay to achieve generous fruit concentration, stone-fruit richness, and textural depth while retaining a crisp, mouthwatering natural acidity.

Wine Description

Invivo Hawke's Bay Chardonnay presents a luminous, pale straw-gold color in the glass with bright greenish-gold reflections along the rim. Its sensory profile is exceptionally fresh, high-toned, and complex, delivering an elegant, balanced, and precisely focused expression of North Island Chardonnay. The bouquet opens with an inviting display of ripe white peach, nectarine, and yellow orchard apples, seamlessly layered with complex underlays of roasted cashew, lemon curd, grilled pineapple, toasted brioche, and a subtle line of crushed stone minerality. On the palate, the wine is medium-to-full-bodied, supple, and athletic, showcasing a succulent core of stone fruit, candied citrus peel, and creamy autolytic warmth. It is characterized by its outstanding inner energy and an incisive, mouthwatering backbone of natural acidity that effortlessly lifts its mid-palate fruit extract. The mouthfeel is broad, silky, and linear, framed by subtle oak integration that glides into a long, dry, and mineral-driven finish accented by persistent notes of white peach, toasted almond, and lemon zest.

title: Invivo Central Otago Pinot Noir 2024
bodyHtml:
This structured and 'crystalline' red wine originates from New Zealand, within the world-renowned Central Otago region on the South Island the southernmost commercial wine-growing region on Earth. Produced by Invivo Wines the acclaimed estate co-founded in 2008 by Tim Lightbourne and winemaker Rob Cameron this Pinot Noir reflects the high-altitude, continental terroir of Central Otago. Sourced primarily from choice vineyard sites in the Bannockburn and Gibbston sub-regions, the vines are rooted in nutrient-poor, free-draining schist, gravel, and quartz-rich soils over glacial till. The extreme continental microclimate is characterized by scorching, sun-drenched summer days, low humidity, and sharp, cool night breezes descending from the Southern Alps. This dramatic diurnal temperature fluctuation allows Pinot Noir to accumulate intense black-and-red fruit concentration and ripe skin phenolics while preserving a brilliant, age-worthy natural acidity.

Wine Description

Invivo Central Otago Pinot Noir presents a luminous, deep crimson-ruby color in the glass with vivid violet and magenta highlights along the rim. Its sensory profile is exceptionally fresh, high-toned, and complex, delivering an elegant, intense, and precisely focused expression of South Island Pinot Noir. The bouquet opens with a soaring display of wild dark cherries, black plums, and ripe raspberries, seamlessly layered with complex underlays of dried thyme, wild violet, sweet baking spices, cocoa nibs, and a distinct line of crushed schist minerality. On the palate, the wine is medium-bodied, sleek, and athletic, showcasing a succulent core of dark stone fruits, blood orange peel, and subtle earthy herbs. It is characterized by its outstanding inner energy and an incisive, mouthwatering backbone of natural acidity that effortlessly lifts its mid-palate fruit extract. The mouthfeel is broad, silky, and supple, framed by fine-grained, chalky tannins that glide into an extraordinarily long, dry, and savory finish accented by persistent notes of cherry skin, wild herbs, and forest floor.

title: Invivo Marlborough Sauvignon Blanc 2024
bodyHtml:
This structured and 'crystalline' white wine originates from New Zealand, within the world-renowned Marlborough region at the northeastern tip of the South Island. Produced by Invivo Wines an innovative and acclaimed estate co-founded in 2008 by childhood friends Tim Lightbourne and winemaker Rob Cameron this benchmark Marlborough Sauvignon Blanc captures the vibrant essence of two distinct growing sub-regions: the Wairau Valley and the Awatere Valley. The vines are rooted in deep, well-draining gravelly silt loams and stony alluvial soils deposited by glacial rivers. Marlborough’s maritime climate features high sunshine hours balanced by cool ocean breezes and dramatic diurnal temperature shifts, allowing Sauvignon Blanc to accumulate intense tropical and herbaceous aromatics while locking in a razor-sharp, mouthwatering natural acidity.

Wine Description

Invivo Marlborough Sauvignon Blanc presents a luminous, pale straw-yellow color in the glass with vivid chartreuse and lime-green highlights along the rim. Its sensory profile is exceptionally fresh, high-toned, and complex, delivering an explosive, expressive, and precisely focused portrait of classic Marlborough terroir. The bouquet opens with a soaring display of passionfruit, ripe guava, and crushed lemongrass, seamlessly layered with complex underlays of pink grapefruit, fresh jalapeño, lime zest, and a distinct line of crushed stone minerality. On the palate, the wine is light-to-medium-bodied, sleek, and athletic, showcasing a vibrant core of crunchy citrus, passionfruit pulp, and white peach. It is characterized by its outstanding inner energy and an incisive, mouthwatering backbone of natural acidity that effortlessly elevates its mid-palate fruit density. The mouthfeel is broad, supple, and weightless, gliding into an extraordinarily long, dry, and mineral-driven finish accented by lingering notes of lime peel, flint, and fresh herbs.

title: Dow's 40 Year Old Tawny Port
bodyHtml:
Originating from Portugal in the famous Douro region, specifically within the rugged Cima Corgo subregion, Dow's 40 Year Old Tawny Port represents a rare, masterfully aged expression of fortified winemaking. Founded in 1798, Dow's is one of the oldest and most prestigious Port houses, celebrated for its drier, more structured style. Now owned and operated by Symington Family Estates, the lodge’s winemaking philosophy relies on sourcing fruit from historic estates like Quinta do Bomfim and Quinta da Senhora da Ribeira, utilizing long-term cask aging in seasoned oak tuns to produce complex, concentrated, and enduring aged tawnies.

Wine Description

The wine displays a deep, dark amber copper colour with pale green and golden reflections along the rim. A profound and complex bouquet opens with wood aged aromas of dried fig, prune, and orange marmalade, integrated with sophisticated notes of toasted walnut, espresso, cigar box, dark caramel, and exotic baking spices. On the palate, it is full bodied, rich, and remarkably concentrated, delivering an extraordinary balance of intense sweet flavours including honeyed fruit, toasted nuts, and dark chocolate alongside Dow's characteristic dry finish and vibrant natural acidity. Framed by a silky, viscous texture gained from four decades of barrel oxidation, it concludes with an extraordinarily long, lingering, and complex finish. Composed of a traditional blend of Douro grape varieties including Touriga Franca, Touriga Nacional, Tinta Roriz, and Tinta Barroca.

title: Dow's Quinta do Bomfim Vintage Port 2013
bodyHtml:
Originating from Portugal in the famous Douro region, specifically within the heart of the Cima Corgo subregion, Dow's Quinta Do Bomfim 2013 represents a single Quinta expression of benchmark Port winemaking. Situated on the north bank of the Douro River near Pinhao, Quinta do Bomfim has been the centerpiece of Dow's winemaking since 1896. Owned and operated by Symington Family Estates, the property’s philosophy relies on sustainable viticulture, traditional stone lagar foot treading, and temperature controlled fermentation to produce single vineyard Ports that highlight the estate's distinct, intense microclimate.

Wine Description

The wine presents an intense, deep garnet purple colour in the glass. An expressive and concentrated bouquet opens with classic aromas of ripe cassis, wild blackberry, and dark plum, interwoven with distinct notes of eucalyptus, rockrose, dark chocolate, and subtle crushed stone. On the palate, it is full bodied, dense, and tightly wound, delivering rich layers of black fruits, licorice, and cocoa bean, balanced by a fine streak of fresh natural acidity and Dow's signature dry finish. Framed by a firm, muscular tannic structure and an undercurrent of flinty minerality, it concludes with a long, intense, and savory finish. Composed of a traditional blend of Touriga Franca, Touriga Nacional, Tinta Barroca, and Tinta Roriz.

title: Graham's Blend Series No.5 White Port
bodyHtml:
Originating from Portugal in the famous Douro region, specifically drawing from high-elevation vineyards in the Cima Corgo subregion, Graham's Blend Series No. 5 White Port represents a modern, innovative expression of white Port winemaking. Founded in 1820, W. & J. Graham's is renowned for its centuries of blending expertise, now carried forward under Symington Family Estates. Created specifically for contemporary mixology and aperitif occasions, the winemaking philosophy focuses on hand-picking native white grape varieties from cool, high-altitude plots to preserve maximum fresh acidity, vibrant aromatic intensity, and a lighter, drier profile.

Wine Description

The wine presents a clear, pale golden straw colour with bright greenish reflections in the glass. An inviting and intensely aromatic bouquet opens with crisp notes of fresh lime, green apple, and white peach, interwoven with fragrant scents of orange blossom, honey, and fresh mint. On the palate, it is medium-bodied, crisp, and refreshing, delivering vibrant flavours of citrus zest, juicy pear, and subtle tropical fruit, all balanced by a clean streak of natural acidity and a noticeably lighter sweetness than traditional white Ports. Cold-fermented in stainless steel tanks to preserve fruit purity and bottled young without extended oak aging, it effortlessly combines youthful, lively fruit aromatics with a clean, crisp finish that works brilliantly both neat on the rocks and topped with tonic.

title: Cockburn's Vintage Port 2024
bodyHtml:
Originating from Portugal in the famous Douro region, specifically within the rugged Cima Corgo and Douro Superior subregions, Cockburn's Vintage Port 2024 represents a historic classic declaration for the renowned Port house. Founded in 1815 by Scottish brothers Robert and John Cockburn, the house is now owned and operated by Symington Family Estates. The winemaking philosophy centers on sourcing fruit primarily from the flagship Quinta dos Canais estate alongside Quinta do Vale Coelho, utilizing an unusually high proportion of Touriga Nacional to craft structured, dry-finishing Vintage Ports built for extraordinary long-term bottle aging.

Wine Description

The wine presents a deep, opaque purple garnet colour with brilliant crimson rims in the glass. An exuberant and complex bouquet opens with vibrant aromas of dark Marasca cherry, wild strawberry, and cassis, interwoven with fragrant accents of violets, orange blossom, rockrose, tobacco leaf, and subtle black tea spice. On the palate, it is full bodied, dense, and powerfully structured, delivering concentrated flavours of ripe red and dark fruits, peppery spice, and cocoa supported by a vibrant core of natural acidity and a noticeably drier, more vinous profile. Framed by fine-grained, muscular tannins and an undercurrent of schist-and-flint minerality, it concludes with Cockburn's signature firm grip and a long, savory finish.

title: Cockburn's 20 Year Old Tawny Port
bodyHtml:
Originating from Portugal in the famous Douro region, specifically within the rugged Cima Corgo subregion, Cockburn's 20 Year Old Tawny Port represents a classic, masterfully aged expression of fortified winemaking. Founded in 1815 by Scottish brothers Robert and John Cockburn, Cockburn's is renowned for its pioneering spirit and commitment to crafting exceptional Ports. Now owned and operated by the Symington family, the lodge’s winemaking philosophy centers on sourcing fruit from high elevation vineyards such as Quinta dos Canais, utilizing traditional oak cask aging and relying on in house coopers to maintain the seasoned wood casks essential for long term barrel maturation.

Wine Description

The wine displays an attractive, deep tawny amber colour with golden orange highlights along the rim. A rich and complex bouquet opens with wood aged aromas of dried fig, raisin, and candied orange peel, integrated with sophisticated nuances of toasted almond, walnut, dark caramel, and warm baking spices. On the palate, it is full bodied, lush, and velvety, delivering a harmonious balance between intense sweet flavors of honeyed fruit, fruitcake, and roasted coffee and a vibrant streak of natural acidity. Framed by a rich, nutty texture gained from decades of wood oxidation, it concludes with a remarkably long, warm, and persistent finish. Composed of a traditional blend of Douro grape varieties including Touriga Franca, Touriga Nacional, Tinta Roriz, and Tinta Barroca, it effortlessly balances mature oxidative complexity with youthful fruit freshness and smooth, seamless elegance.

title: Graham's 50 Year Old Prestige Tawny Port
bodyHtml:
Originating from Portugal in the famous Douro region, specifically within the rugged Cima Corgo and Douro Superior subregions, Graham's 50 Year Old Prestige Tawny Port represents an extraordinary milestone of wood aged winemaking. Founded in 1820 by brothers William and John Graham, the house of Graham's has long been celebrated for producing rich, seductive, and exceptionally complex Ports. Now owned and operated by Symington Family Estates, the lodge’s philosophy focuses on sourcing fruit from flagship estates such as Quinta dos Malvedos and Quinta das Lages, relying on centuries of cooperage tradition and patient cask aging in cool coastal lodges to craft aged tawnies of unmatched elegance.

Wine Description

The wine presents a mesmerizing, deep mahogany amber colour with shimmering golden copper and olive green reflections along the rim. An extraordinary, multidimensional bouquet opens with intense aromas of dried fig, sultanas, and candied orange peel, seamlessly layered with notes of roasted hazelnut, toasted almond, pipe tobacco, dark molasses, and exotic warm spices. On the palate, it is full bodied, luxurious, and deeply concentrated, offering a velvety, viscous mouthfeel packed with rich flavours of honeyed fruitcake, dark caramel, cocoa bean, and citrus oil. Supported by a spine of lively natural acidity that cuts cleanly through the intense sweetness, it glides into an astonishingly persistent finish that lingers for minutes. Composed of a traditional blend of Douro grape varieties including Touriga Franca, Touriga Nacional, Tinta Roriz, and Tinta Barroca, this rare release offers an optimal drinking window of 2026–2038. Stylistically, it combines profound oxidative depth, concentrated wood richness, and effortless fruit freshness.

title: Graham's Vintage Port 'Private Cellar Release' 1985
bodyHtml:
Originating from Portugal in the famous Douro region, specifically within the rugged Cima Corgo subregion, Graham's Vintage Port 'The Private Cellar Release' 1985 represents an iconic, fully mature expression from a classic vintage declaration. Founded in 1820 by brothers William and John Graham, the house is owned and operated by Symington Family Estates. The winery's philosophy focuses on sourcing fruit from flagship properties including Quinta dos Malvedos, Quinta das Lages, and Quinta do Tua, utilizing traditional stone lagar foot treading to craft rich, voluptuous Vintage Ports that are held in the Symington family's private lodges in Vila Nova de Gaia for late 'Private Cellar' releases to guarantee perfect provenance.

Wine Description

The wine presents a deep garnet red colour with warm mahogany and amber reflections along the rim. A rich, mature, and extraordinarily complex bouquet opens with secondary and tertiary aromas of dried fig, prune, and raisins, interwoven with sophisticated notes of dark chocolate, eucalyptus, roasted coffee, pipe tobacco, leather, and exotic baking spices. On the palate, it is full bodied, lush, and velvety smooth, delivering a mouth-coating texture packed with mature dark fruit, cocoa bean, and molasses, all supported by a fine streak of balanced natural acidity. Framed by resolved, silky tannins and a soft schist mineral backbone, it concludes with an extraordinarily long, warm, and harmonious finish. Composed of a classic Douro blend of Touriga Nacional, Touriga Franca, Tinta Barroca, and Tinta Roriz, this release offers an optimal drinking window of 2024–2040. Stylistically, it combines Graham's signature opulent sweetness and dark fruit concentration with fully evolved tertiary complexity and seamless balance.

Food Pairing

Suggested pairings include stilton cheese, blue cheese with dark wildflower honey, dark chocolate ganache, or roasted figs with walnuts. 'Together, they create an unforgettable dining experience.'

title: Graham's Quinta dos Malvedos Vintage Port 2018
bodyHtml:
Originating from Portugal in the famous Douro region, specifically within the premier Cima Corgo subregion, Graham's Quinta dos Malvedos Vintage Port 2018 represents a single estate expression of benchmark Port winemaking. Situated on a prominent south-facing bank of the Douro River, Quinta dos Malvedos has been the beating heart of Graham's winemaking since its acquisition in 1890.
