Glenfiddich Gran Reserva is crafted from 100% malted barley distilled through the distillery's signature small copper pot stills and matured for 21 years in a combination of traditional American ex-bourbon oak and European ex-sherry casks. Master Malt Blender Brian Kinsman then transfers the 21-year-old liquid into barrels previously used to age Caribbean rum for a secondary maturation period of approximately four months. This finishing step layers rich tropical fruits, warm brown spices, and molasses sweetness onto the spirit's delicate orchard-fruit foundation.

  • Colour: Rich dark gold with deep amber glints.

  • Aroma: Intense, sweet, and highly aromatic. The nose opens with sweet vanilla, rich toffee, and ripe tropical fruits (banana, mango, and fig), backed by floral undertones, fresh lime zest, new leather, and toasted oak.

  • Palate: Soft and silky on the entry, quickly becoming vibrant, warming, and complex. Upfront flavors of buttery toffee, vanilla bean, and baked orchard fruits yield to candied orange peel, ginger snaps, ripe papaya, dried figs, and warm cinnamon spice.

  • Body: Medium-to-full-bodied with a smooth, velvety, and rounded texture.

  • Finish: Long, warming, and elegant, trailing off with dry wood spices, ginger, toasted coconut, caramelized sugar, and a lingering citrus peel brightness.

  • ABV: Bottled at 40% ABV (80 Proof)

title: Glaswegin Gin - 700 ml
bodyHtml:
Glaswegin Distilled Gin is a contemporary Scottish craft gin produced in the heart of Glasgow, Scotland. Founded by Andy McGeoch and launched in 2018, Glaswegin was created as an homage to the frank, no-nonsense character of Glasgow and its people ("Glaswegians"). Famous for its striking, minimalist monochrome milk-carton-style bottle designed by Paul Gray, the spirit strips away unnecessary pretense to focus on a clean, frank botanical profile that balances traditional juniper with distinct regional ingredients.

Spirit Description

Glaswegin is distilled in traditional copper pot stills using a grain neutral spirit and a curated blend of 8 botanicals: Scottish milk thistle, Italian juniper, coriander seed, angelica root, orange peel, chamomile flower, bay leaf, and pink peppercorns. The inclusion of native Scottish milk thistle provides a creaminess on the palate, while pink peppercorn and bay leaf deliver a crisp, savory warmth that sets it apart from conventional London Dry gins.

  • Colour: Crystal clear, bright, and pristine.

  • Aroma: Clean and fragrant, opening with crisp piney juniper, zesty orange peel, and gentle chamomile floral notes, backed by subtle herbaceous bay leaf and cracked pepper.

  • Palate: Smooth, creamy, and well-rounded on the entry. Sweet orange citrus and resinous juniper blend into a velvety milk-thistle mouthfeel, followed by subtle herbal notes of bay leaf and a warm, spicy bite of pink peppercorn.

  • Body: Medium-bodied with a soft, surprisingly creamy, and smooth texture.

  • Finish: Crisp, long, and dry, trailing off with lingering citrus brightness, savory bay leaf, and a gentle peppery warmth.

  • ABV: Bottled at 41.1% ABV (82.2 Proof).

title: Vecchio Magazzino Doganale 'Washington' Orange & Herbs Amaro - 700 ml
bodyHtml:
Washington Orange & Herbs Amaro originates from Italy, within the southern region of Calabria. Crafted by the renowned rural distillery Vecchio Magazzino Doganale, the spirit celebrates local agricultural traditions and heritage recipes. The house pays homage to historic botanical infusions, utilizing organic citrus varieties harvested directly from the Calabrian countryside.

Spirit Description

This artisanal amaro presents a deep amber appearance with luminous golden flashes in the glass. The sensory profile opens with an aromatic, citrus-forward nose dominated by bright orange peel, bitter herbs, and subtle floral nuances, laced with soft notes of sweet vanilla and baking spices. On the palate, the body is rich, smooth, and delightfully complex, striking a delicate balance between the initial sweetness of sun-ripened oranges and a structured, herbal bitterness. The finish is remarkably long, dry, and persistent, leaving lingering undertones of citrus zest, gentle spice, and persistent botanicals. This craft amaro is bottled at an alcohol by volume of 28%.

title: Corte Manzini 'Bolla Rossa' Lambrusco Grasparossa di Castelvetro
bodyHtml:
This vibrant sparkling red wine originates from Italy, produced in the historic Emilia-Romagna region within the Lambrusco Grasparossa di Castelvetro DOC south of Modena. Founded in 1978 by the Manzini family, Corte Manzini is an artisanal estate dedicated to highlighting authentic, estate-grown Lambrusco. Situated on the clay and limestone foothills of San Polo di Castelvetro, the estate controls every step of production from vineyard to bottle. The 'Bolla Rossa' (Red Bubble) cuvée focuses on the Grasparossa clone, widely regarded as the most deeply colored, full-bodied, and structured of all Lambrusco grape varieties.

Wine Description

In the glass, 'Bolla Rossa' displays an intense ruby-violet color accompanied by a persistent, frothy dark purple mousse. The nose opens with a fragrant, fruit-driven bouquet of ripe blackberry, dark plum, black cherry, and wild raspberry, accented by notes of fresh violet and sweet spice. On the palate, the wine is medium-bodied, gently sparkling (frizzante), and fruit-forward. It features a harmonious balance of juicy red-and-black berry fruit sweetness, lively natural acidity, and a light tannic grip from the thick Grasparossa grape skins. Crafted primarily from Lambrusco Grasparossa di Castelvetro, the hand-harvested grapes undergo temperature-controlled fermentation in stainless steel before secondary fermentation in pressure tanks (Charmat method) to preserve maximum fresh fruit aroma and effervescence. The alcohol by volume typically sits at approximately 10.5% to 11.5%.

Food Pairing

The bright acidity, delicate sparkle, and rich fruit profile of this Lambrusco make it a classic match for the famously rich, savory gastronomy of Emilia-Romagna. It pairs exceptionally well with traditional cured meats like Prosciutto di Parma, Mortadella, Salame di Felino, and Culatello, especially when served with warm gnocco fritto or Piadina. Structurally, its effervescence cuts cleanly through rich pasta dishes like Lasagna alla Bolognese, tortellini in broth, pork sausages, barbecue ribs, and wood-fired pizza, as well as aged cheeses like Parmigiano-Reggiano.

title: Los Siete Misterios Doba Yej Mezcal
bodyHtml:
Los Siete Misterios Doba-Yej Mezcal originates from Mexico, in the southern region within the subregion of Oaxaca. Founded in 2010 by brothers Julio and Eduardo Mestre, the brand was created with a mission to preserve traditional mezcal making customs and support local master distillers. Named 'Doba-Yej'—the ancient Zapotec word for the Espadín agave—this artisanal expression represents the house's dedication to authentic, small batch craftsmanship.

Spirit Description

This artisanal young mezcal presents a crystal clear, luminous appearance with bright silvery flashes in the glass. The aromatic sensory profile features a vibrant, complex nose driven by cooked agave, crisp citrus notes of lemon and grapefruit, and floral violets, complemented by subtle baking spices and delicate woodsmoke. On the palate, the body is smooth and satiny, revealing an elegant balance of sweet caramel, fresh herbs, orange peel, and earthy agave character. The finish is remarkably long, dry, and balanced, leaving trailing hints of mineral salinity, light pepper, and a gentle, lingering smoke. This unaged spirit is traditionally bottled at an alcohol by volume ranging between 44% and 45%.

Accolades

As one of the standout artisanal offerings in the Los Siete Misterios portfolio, this expression has earned critical praise from spirits judges and mixologists worldwide. It is widely celebrated as a premier dual purpose mezcal, recognized across industry publications for its exceptional balance whether enjoyed neat or in craft cocktails.

Food Pairing

The vibrant citrus brightness, earthy agave depth, and delicate smokiness of this mezcal make it an outstanding companion for authentic Mexican and Latin American cuisine. It pairs brilliantly with fresh sea bass ceviche, fish tacos topped with lime, or grilled pork carnitas where the citrus cuts through the richness. For a lighter option, it can be served alongside fresh goat cheese, guacamole with salted tortilla chips, or tropical fruit drizzled with chili powder.

title: Nepeta Timous Amaro
bodyHtml:
Amaro Nepèta "Timous" (also known as Nepeta Timous Amaro Vero) is an artisanal, small-batch Italian herbal liqueur produced in the Siracusa countryside of southeastern Sicily, Italy. Produced organically, Timous is a modern interpretation of traditional, bone-dry herbal digestifs. Derived from ancient Greek terminology for wild thyme (Thymus capitatus), this expression sets itself apart by containing no added refined sugars—sweetened exclusively with a touch of raw Sicilian chestnut honey.

Spirit Description

Timous is produced via cold maceration of wild-foraged botanicals harvested across the Hyblaean countryside in Sicily. The spirit features an infusion of wild white thyme (thymus capitatus), Italian helichrysum (curry plant), Calabrian bergamot peel, angelica root, gentian, and rhubarb. The distinct infusions are cold-blended without filtration or artificial aging, creating an aromatic, green, and resinous herbal liqueur.

  • Colour: Light golden amber with bronze glints and a slightly opalescent, unfiltered clarity.

  • Aroma: Intensely balsamic, pungent, and herbaceous. The nose leads with wild thyme, piney crushed herbs, and bergamot citrus zest, underlaid by earthy notes of dried hay, cut grass, and chestnut honey.

  • Palate: Unusually dry, bitter, and savory compared to commercial amari. Upfront flavors of sharp white thyme and bitter gentian transition into bright bergamot spice, backed by subtle undertones of dark cocoa, vanilla, and honeyed earthy richness from the helichrysum.

  • Body: Medium-bodied with an oily, coating texture without cloying, syrupy weight.

  • Finish: Exceptionally long, warm, and dry. Leaves a lingering trail of dried herbs, cedar, hay, and an enduring herbal bitterness.

  • ABV: Bottled at 28% ABV (56 Proof).

title: Chateau Lafite Rothschild 2003
bodyHtml:
Introduction

Chateau Lafite Rothschild 2003 is a Premier Grand Cru Classé from the Pauillac appellation in Bordeaux, France. As one of the original five First Growths established in the 1855 Bordeaux Classification, the estate is renowned for its pursuit of elegance and quiet excellence. Owned by the Rothschild family since 1868, the winery currently operates under the leadership of Saskia de Rothschild, who continues a centuries-old tradition of meticulous vineyard management and ancestral winemaking know-how.

Wine Description

This 2003 vintage is characterized by a dense ruby and purple colour that extends to the rim. The nose is luxurious and aromatic, offering a bouquet of cedarwood, lead pencil shavings, white chocolate, cocoa, and cassis, accented by high-toned notes of coconut and vanilla. On the palate, the wine is full bodied, rich, and opulent with a fat, unctuous texture and relatively low acidity. Its structure is defined by soft, velvety tannins that provide a rounded mouthfeel and lead into a long, persistent finish. The varietal composition is a blend of 86% Cabernet Sauvignon, 9% Merlot, 3% Cabernet Franc, and 2% Petit Verdot. While it is currently in its plateau of maturity, this noble wine is expected to hold its peak quality for another 20 to 25 years.

Accolades

  • Wine Advocate - 100 points

  • James Suckling - 98 points

  • Wine Enthusiast - 97 points

  • Wine Spectator - 96 points

  • Vinous - 96 points

title: Laurent Perrier Grand Siecle No. 27
bodyHtml:
Laurent-Perrier Grand Siècle N°27 is a prestigious non-vintage cuvée from the Champagne region of France. The Champagne house was founded in 1812 by André-Michel Pierlot in the Grand Cru village of Tours-sur-Marne. Laurent-Perrier's philosophy, notably shaped by Bernard de Nonancourt, is built on an innovative spirit, which led to the creation of Grand Siècle with the ambition of 'recreating the perfect year' in every iteration by blending three exceptional vintages.

Wine Description

Grand Siècle N°27 is a blend of Chardonnay (in the majority) and Pinot Noir, sourced exclusively from a maximum of 11 of Champagne's Grands Crus. The wine presents an intense and deeply coloured appearance, dominated by gold and platinum shades.

The complex nose blends aromas of honeysuckle, candied lemon, hazelnut, and fresh almond, followed by notes of pastry, honey, and roasted tones. On the palate, the attack is fresh and vibrant, confirming the aromatic impressions with flavours of ripe fruit, dried apricot, and candied citrus. The Grand Siècle is known for its exquisite balance, silky texture, and delicate bubbles, leading to a long, harmonious finish with refined minerality and vitality. The house aims for a wine that has deep complexity and intensity while maintaining freshness and acidity. The wine has an exceptional aging potential, being a wine that is impressive today but can develop gracefully for many years. The wine is not specifically indicated as organic.

Accolades

Accolades are for the general blend type, or for the iteration immediately preceding No. 27:

  • James Suckling - 99 points (Iteration No. 27)

Food Pairing

The wine’s freshness, elegance, and purity make it a versatile pairing for fine cuisine. Grand Siècle N°27 is a true wine for the table. It pairs well with delicate and tender textures such as shellfish, noble fish, poultry, and veal fillet. Its complex profile also matches well with sophisticated fish dishes, perhaps with a rich sauce. A perfect match to enhance the wine’s complexity.

title: Joseph Drouhin Vosne Romanee 2024
bodyHtml:
France is the country of origin for this wine, originating from the Burgundy region within the prestigious Cote de Nuits subregion. Founded in 1880, Maison Joseph Drouhin has remained family owned across four generations, building a celebrated legacy rooted in organic and biodynamic viticulture. The estate follows a winemaking philosophy dedicated to purity, elegance, and deep respect for terroir, ensuring each parcel authentically captures the character of its origin.

Wine Description

Crafted from 100% Pinot Noir, Joseph Drouhin Vosne Romanee 2024 presents a brilliant ruby colour with luminous reflections. The nose reveals a refined bouquet of dark cassis, wild cherry, and red berries, interwoven with hints of nutmeg, fine leather, and subtle spice. On the palate, this medium bodied wine delivers impressive balance, displaying vibrant freshness, linear tannins, and pure red fruit flavour. The finish is remarkably long and harmonious, exemplifying classic Burgundian complexity.

title: Joseph Drouhin Clos des Mouches Rouge Premier Cru 2024
bodyHtml:
Maison Joseph Drouhin Beaune Premier Cru Clos des Mouches Rouge hails from France, specifically the Côte de Beaune subregion of Burgundy. Founded in 1880, this family-owned estate is deeply committed to organic and biodynamic viticulture, capturing the purest expression of Burgundian terroir. The Clos des Mouches vineyard—originally acquired parcel by parcel by Maurice Drouhin in the 1920s—is one of the house's most celebrated flagship sites.

Wine Description

This wine exhibits a bright, deep ruby-red hue with exceptional clarity. On the nose, it opens with vibrant aromas of Morello cherry, fresh raspberry, and blackberry, layered with delicate smoky accents, sweet liquorice, and earthy undertones. The medium-bodied palate delivers a fleshy, well-structured texture supported by silky tannins, crisp acidity, and a distinct mineral edge. Made entirely from 100% Pinot Noir, this Premier Cru displays remarkable balance and a long, refined finish.

title: Joseph Drouhin Greves Rouge Premier Cru 2024
bodyHtml:
This fine red wine originates from France, within the Côte de Beaune region of Burgundy and the esteemed Beaune Premier Cru subregion. Founded in 1880, Maison Joseph Drouhin has remained a family-owned estate dedicated to expressing the authentic terroirs of Burgundy through organic and biodynamic viticulture. The famed 'Les Grèves' vineyard, known for its gravelly soils, produces structured yet refined Pinot Noir that reflects the winery's commitment to elegance, balance, and minimal intervention.

Wine Description

The Joseph Drouhin Beaune Premier Cru Les Grèves Rouge presents a deep, bright ruby hue with a luminous sheen. On the nose, it delivers vibrant aromas of fresh Morello cherry, raspberry, and blackberry, accompanied by delicate hints of smoke and liquorice. The palate offers a clear-cut entry with a fleshy, velvety texture, medium body, and bright freshness supported by silky, integrated tannins.

title: Joseph Drouhin Pommard 2024
bodyHtml:
This fine red wine originates from France, within the prestigious Burgundy region and the renowned Cote de Beaune subregion. Founded in 1880, Maison Joseph Drouhin has been family-owned for four generations, building a legacy built on tradition, elegance, and respect for the terroir. The domain prioritises organic and biodynamic viticulture across its historic vineyards, ensuring each bottle authenticly reflects the character of its origin.

Wine Description

The wine displays an intense, bright red color. On the nose, it is powerful and brimming with vibrant black cherry and delicate spice notes, developing subtle hints of young leather over time. On the palate, it is medium-to-full-bodied with structured, firm tannins that are gracefully balanced by a silky, harmonious texture and rich fruit expression. The finish is long, elegant, and persistent with lingering dark fruit and spice flavours.

title: Antigua Porteno Rum Solera 21 Year Old
bodyHtml:
Antigua Porteño Sistema Solera 21 is a premium Colombian rum produced under the Antigua Porteño brand. Despite the "Antigua" name which often leads to confusion with the island of Antigua in the Caribbean this expression is crafted in Colombia utilizing the traditional Spanish-style Solera dynamic aging process. Engineered to showcase the complexity of long fractional maturation, the "Solera 21" designation signifies that the blend includes aged spirits matured for up to 21 years in select oak casks.

Spirit Description

Antigua Porteño Solera 21 is distilled from sugarcane molasses and aged through a multi-tiered Solera cascade. This method blends younger, vibrant rums with older, wood-rich reserves, creating a cohesive, silky spirit that marries dried tropical fruit notes with rich oak tannins, caramelized nuts, and warm baking spices.

  • Colour: Bright golden amber with rich copper and honeyed highlights.

  • Aroma: Warm, sweet, and aromatic, opening with caramelized nuts, brown sugar, and spiced mocha, backed by polished cedar wood, light coconut, and subtle tropical fruit.

  • Palate: Smooth, silky, and fruity on the entry. Upfront flavors of toasted coconut, crème brûlée, and sweet toffee blend into tropical fruit gelato, dried citrus peel, and gentle baking spices (cinnamon and nutmeg).

  • Body: Medium-to-full-bodied with a soft, rounded, and coating mouthfeel.

  • Finish: Medium-long, crisp, and stimulating, closing with lingering notes of roasted nuts, mocha, light leather, and dry cedar wood.

  • ABV: Bottled at 40% (80 Proof).

title: Bunnahabhain 18 Year Old Single Malt Whisky - 700 ml
bodyHtml:
Bunnahabhain 18 Year Old Single Malt Scotch Whisky originates from Scotland, in the Islay region. Established in 1881 near the northern mouth of the Sound of Islay, the historic coastal distillery was built to take advantage of local maritime trade routes. Today, the distillery is owned by Distell Group Limited, a subsidiary of Heineken, which continues to uphold its centuries old heritage of unpeated and gently sherried single malts.

Spirit Description

This single malt displays a rich mahogany appearance with golden highlights in the glass. The nose opens with a fragrant, complex bouquet featuring salted caramel, dried fruits, honeyed nuts, and subtle leather, laced with a gentle sea spray undertone. On the palate, the body is dense and oily, delivering balanced flavours of sweet sherry, roasted chestnuts, dark chocolate, and a distinct coastal salinity. The finish is long, dry, and warming, carrying lingering notes of oak spice, nutmeg, and a faint marine tang. This expression is non-chill filtered and bottled at an alcohol by volume of 46.3%.

Accolades

As one of the most celebrated expressions in the distillery's core portfolio, this 18 year old malt has consistently earned high honours in international spirit competitions. Notable accolades include Gold Medals at the International Wine & Spirit Competition and the International Spirits Challenge, as well as a Category Winner title at the World Whiskies Awards.

title: Francois Chidaine Clos de Baudoin 2024
bodyHtml:
This dry single-vineyard Chenin Blanc originates from France, within the Vouvray and Montlouis-sur-Loire appellation areas of the Touraine district in the Loire Valley. Domaine François Chidaine, established in 1989 by François Chidaine and his wife Manuela in Montlouis-sur-Loire, is globally recognized as a vanguard of biodynamic viticulture and dry Chenin Blanc winemaking. The historic Clos de Baudoin (or Les Argiles bottling depending on Vin de France labeling designations resulting from regional boundaries) is a legendary site in Vouvray characterized by deep flinty clay soils over tuffeau chalk. Chidaine’s meticulous organic and biodynamic vineyard management fosters exceptional vitality, yielding wines of soaring purity, electric minerality, and vibrant acidity.

Wine Description

In the glass, the 2024 vintage presents a bright, pale straw-gold color with vibrant green highlights. The nose is intense and deeply complex, opening with aromatics of fresh quince, green apple, white peach, and lemon oil, interwoven with signature flinty smoke, wet wool, honeycomb, and crushed chalk mineral notes. On the palate, the wine is medium-bodied with an astonishing core of dense fruit texture offset by a laser-sharp beam of crystalline acidity. Crafted from 100% Chenin Blanc harvested from old vines (30 to 90 years old), the fruit is hand-harvested, gently whole-cluster pressed, and fermented using only indigenous yeasts in demi-muids (600-liter oak barrels). Fermentation proceeds naturally until bone-dry, with no malolactic fermentation permitted to preserve the site's natural tension. The wine rests on its fine lees in neutral oak for approximately 11 to 12 months before bottling. The alcohol by volume sits at 13.5%.

Food Pairing

The piercing acidity, rich texture, and intense mineral drive of this classic dry Loire Chenin Blanc make it a versatile table partner for rich seafood, poultry, and goat milk cheeses. It pairs exceptionally well with seared scallops in beurre blanc sauce, pan-roasted pike perch, lobster thermidor, or grilled halibut. It also harmonizes effortlessly with roasted pork tenderloin with apples, roasted guinea fowl, or goat milk cheeses such as Sainte-Maure de Touraine, Valençay, or Crottin de Chavignol.

Vintage Quality

The 2024 growing season in the Loire Valley required intense vigilance due to cool spring dampness and rain, demanding precise biodynamic canopy management. However, favorable late-summer conditions allowed Chenin Blanc to achieve ideal sugar-acid equilibrium while preserving radiant freshness. The 2024 vintage showcases classic Loire freshness, showing lower potential alcohol and higher natural acidity than hotter recent vintages. The wine offers bright energetic fruit and mineral focus on release, with the structural concentration to evolve and gain complex honeyed, lanolin, and smoky nuances over 10 to 18+ years of cellaring.

title: Francois Chidaine Montlouis Sur Loire 'Les Choisilles' Chenin Blanc 2023
bodyHtml:
This dry single-cuvée Chenin Blanc originates from France, within the Montlouis-sur-Loire appellation of the Touraine region in the Loire Valley. Named after the local dialect word for the flint stones (choisilles) scattered throughout the vineyards, this bottling is an homage to the unique soil profile of the area. Domaine François Chidaine, led by master vigneron François Chidaine and his wife Manuela, is globally celebrated for pushing biodynamic viticulture to its absolute peak. Les Choisilles is crafted from a selection of old vines (30 to 90 years old) grown across multiple flint-and-clay over limestone (tuffeau) parcels, resulting in a bone-dry white wine renowned for its chiseled minerality, tension, and aromatic complexity.

Wine Description

In the glass, the 2023 Les Choisilles presents a luminous straw-yellow color with shimmering green undertones. The nose is striking and deeply expressive, opening with vibrant aromas of yellow apple, crunchy white peach, lemon verbena, and white flowers, accented by notes of wet stone, gunflint, honeycomb, and subtle chamomile. On the palate, the wine is dry, focused, and beautifully textured, showing a rich mid-palate weight that is seamlessly balanced by a razor-sharp beam of minerality and high natural acidity. Crafted from 100% Chenin Blanc, the hand-harvested grapes are gently whole-cluster pressed and fermented naturally with indigenous yeasts in 600-liter French oak demi-muids. No malolactic fermentation occurs, preserving the pristine acidity. The wine is aged on its fine lees in neutral oak for roughly 12 to 14 months before bottling, yielding a persistent, saline finish with an impressive echo of crushed flint. The alcohol by volume sits at 13.5%.

Food Pairing

The intense mineral tension, textural depth, and energetic drive of this dry Loire Chenin Blanc make it an exceptional partner for high-end seafood and poultry. Ideal culinary pairings include seared sea scallops with lemon-herb butter, wild turbot or pike perch in beurre blanc, grilled langoustines, and crab cakes. It also excels alongside roasted pork loin with caramelized apples, roasted guinea fowl, and traditional goat milk cheeses from the Loire Valley, such as Sainte-Maure de Touraine, Selles-sur-Cher, or Crottin de Chavignol.

Vintage Quality

The 2023 vintage in Montlouis-sur-Loire offered a harmonious return to classic Loire proportions after the hotter 2022 season. Generous spring rainfall restored water reserves, followed by warm, dry conditions in late summer that allowed for steady, full ripening while preserving vivid acidity. The 2023 Les Choisilles highlights pristine fruit clarity and a precise mineral backbone. While showing immediate charm, vibrancy, and palate length upon release, this wine possesses the depth and structure to cellar gracefully, expanding in complexity over 10 to 15+ years.

title: Canalicchio di Sopra Rosso di Montalcino 2024
bodyHtml:
This expressive, highly focused dry red wine originates from Italy, produced in the prestigious Montalcino DOC zone of southern Tuscany. Founded in 1962 by Primo Pacini, Canalicchio di Sopra is one of the founding estates of the Consorzio del Vino Brunello di Montalcino. Today, the estate is expertly managed by the third generation, Francesco, Marco, and Simonetta Ripaccioli. Sourced from two distinct terroirs within Montalcino, the clay-rich, mineral-dense soils of Canalicchio on the northern slopes and the stony, warmer gravels of Montosoli, their Rosso di Montalcino is treated as a true flagship wine in its own right, sharing the same vineyard pedigree and meticulous craftsmanship as their world-renowned Brunellos.

Wine Description

In the glass, the 2024 Rosso di Montalcino presents a bright, vibrant ruby red color with crimson reflections. The nose opens with an inviting and lifted bouquet of sour red cherry, fresh raspberry, and wild strawberry, interwoven with floral aromas of violet, dried rose petal, blood orange peel, and subtle Mediterranean garrigue herbs. On the palate, the wine is medium-bodied, remarkably energetic, and precise. A core of juicy red fruit is balanced by a silky yet firm tannic structure and a streak of stony minerality. Crafted from 100% Sangiovese (locally known as Sangiovese Grosso), the hand-harvested fruit is gently crushed and fermented in temperature-controlled stainless steel with skin contact lasting roughly 15 to 20 days. The wine is aged for approximately 12 months in large Slavonian oak casks (botti grandi) to build texture and complexity without obscuring the grape's natural fresh berry aromatics. It typically carries an alcohol by volume of 14.0%.

Food Pairing

The vibrant acidity, fine tannic grip, and bright fruit clarity of this Sangiovese make it an exceptionally versatile partner at the dining table. It pairs brilliantly with classic Tuscan dishes such as pici al ragù, wild boar pasta, pappardelle with duck ragù, and mushroom risotto. Excellent meat pairings include grilled pork chops, roasted rack of lamb with rosemary, Florentine steak (bistecca alla Fiorentina), or pan-seared duck breast. For cheese pairings, opt for medium-aged Tuscan Pecorino, Parmigiano-Reggiano, or Fontina.

Vintage Quality

The 2024 growing season in Montalcino yielded wines defined by aromatic freshness, energy, and elegant fruit purity. Adequate spring rainfall laid a healthy foundation, while warm, sunny summer days balanced by cool Tuscan night breezes allowed Sangiovese grapes to achieve complete phenolic maturity while preserving bright natural acidity. The 2024 Canalicchio di Sopra Rosso di Montalcino displays immediate elegance and drinkability upon release, while possessing the concentration and structural backbone to evolve gracefully in the cellar for 5 to 10 years.

title: Canalicchio di Sopra Brunello di Montalcino 2020
bodyHtml:
This prestigious dry red wine originates from Italy, within the renowned Brunello di Montalcino DOCG in southern Tuscany. Established in 1962 by Primo Pacini, Canalicchio di Sopra played a foundational role as one of the original 12 estates that created the Consorzio del Vino Brunello di Montalcino. Today, the estate is led by the third generation, siblings Francesco, Marco, and Simonetta Ripaccioli. The estate’s Brunello is a harmonious synthesis of two contrasting sub-zones of Montalcino: the cool, clay-rich soils of Canalicchio on the northern slope, which impart elegance, acidity, and aromatic intensity, combined with the stony, galestro-rich gravels of Montosoli, which contribute power, warmth, and structural depth.

Wine Description

In the glass, the 2020 Brunello di Montalcino displays a classic, luminous garnet red color with bright ruby highlights. The complex nose opens with an ethereal bouquet of sour red cherry, crushed cranberry, and wild strawberry, interwoven with floral undertones of dried rose petal and violet, leather, blood orange, crushed flint, and a hint of sweet spice from oak aging. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied, structured, and exceptionally refined. A deep core of juicy red fruit is anchored by fine-grained, chalky tannins and a vibrant beam of mineral-driven acidity that provides tension and balance. Crafted from 100% Sangiovese (Sangiovese Grosso), the hand-harvested grapes undergo careful sorting before temperature-controlled fermentation in stainless steel with skin contact for roughly 25 to 30 days. The wine is aged for 36 months in traditional 2,500- to 5,000-liter Slavonian and French oak casks (botti grandi), followed by significant aging in bottle before release. It carries an alcohol by volume of 14.5%.

Food Pairing

The firm tannic backbone, elevated natural acidity, and savory complexity of this classic Brunello make it an extraordinary partner for rich, traditional Tuscan fare and high-end meat preparations. It pairs seamlessly with Florentine steak (bistecca alla Fiorentina), slow-braised beef short ribs, roasted rack of lamb with rosemary, pan-seared duck breast with cherry reduction, and wild boar stew (spezzatino di cinghiale). It also harmonizes beautifully with fresh pasta dishes featuring truffle or wild mushroom ragù, as well as aged hard cheeses such as Pecorino Toscano, Parmigiano-Reggiano, or aged Gouda.

Vintage Quality

The 2020 vintage in Montalcino produced wines characterized by wonderful balance, aromatic elegance, and accessible charm, offering a highly harmonious profile following the more muscular 2019 season. A mild winter led into a warm, steady summer with well-timed precipitation and cool night breezes from Mount Amiata, allowing Sangiovese to achieve complete phenolic maturity while retaining fresh acidity. The 2020 Canalicchio di Sopra Brunello shows immense purity and textural finesse, making it remarkably captivating early with proper decanting, while boasting the concentration and tannic framework to age gracefully in the cellar for 15 to 25+ years.

Accolades

95 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

Pouring a jeweled red/ruby color, the 2020 Brunello Di Montalcino is attractive and layered on the nose, with pure notes of red cherries, sweet Mediterranean herbs, crushed roses, and mossy earth. Medium-bodied, it brings lovely energy to the palate and is upfront with mouthwatering salty notes, snappy ripe acidity, and a clean, balanced finish, with even ripeness and stone-fruited notes of apricot on the back palate. This highly appealing Brunello is hard to resist now but likely has the ability to go the long haul over the coming 15-20 years.

95 Points - James Suckling

Graceful style to this wine, with earthy strawberries, cinnamon and sweet violets. Almost yellow stone-fruit, too. Full in body with crisp if not zesty acidity and intense, extracted and firm tannins giving a tight mid-palate. Yet, the finish is long and polished.

95 Points - Vinous

A burst of black cherries and cloves gives way to shavings of cedar and lifting hints of mentholated herbs as the dynamic 2020 Brunello di Montalcino comes to life in the glass. This is soothingly round and pliant with an inner sweetness up front and crisp wild berry fruits that cascade across the palate. It's structured and firm, yet its tannins are sweet and round, tapering off with a pleasantly bitter tinge of blackberry and sour citrus. The 2020 aims to please and it is already incredibly approachable today. With no Riserva produced in 2020, all of the juice from Vigna Vecchia Mercatale was used to bolster this spectacular Brunello.

93 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

This is a standout wine that marries red and purple fruit flavors with tangy hints of green curry leaf, rhubarb and sweet earth. The Canalicchio di Sopra 2020 Brunello di Montalcino carries a distinct signature that recalls not only the Sangiovese grape but a sense of place. You can mistake this for nothing but a Brunello. The vintage manages power and aromatic intensity but is also magically leaner and definitely more elegant in terms of mouthfeel. The immediate results are perhaps more accessible and also quite pleasurable now in this 41,362-bottle release.

title: Canalicchio di Sopra Brunello di Montalcino 'Vigna Montosoli' 2018
bodyHtml:
This prestigious single-vineyard Cru dry red wine originates from Italy, crafted in the renowned Montalcino DOCG region of southern Tuscany. Managed today by the third generation—Francesco, Marco, and Simonetta Ripaccioli—Canalicchio di Sopra is one of the historic founding families of the Montalcino consortium. Vigna Montosoli represents the estate's crown-jewel single-vineyard bottling, sourced from a prized 5-hectare plot on the famed Montosoli hill north of Montalcino town. Characterized by stony galestro and albarese soils, slates, and quartz gravels paired with exceptional northern sun exposure, this site produces a Brunello globally revered for its soaring aromatic complexity, chiseled mineral tension, and supreme structural elegance.

Wine Description

In the glass, the 2018 Vigna Montosoli displays a luminous ruby-garnet color with bright orange-tinged reflections. The captivating nose opens with an array of aromatic aromas, featuring red cherry, wild strawberry, and blood orange peel, interwoven with crushed flint, dried rose petals, thyme, white pepper, and subtle leather. On the palate, the wine is medium-to-full-bodied, laser-focused, and incredibly vibrant. A core of pristine red fruit is underpinned by fine, chalky, vertical tannins and a brilliant streak of saline minerality that drives the palate forward. Crafted from 100% Sangiovese (Sangiovese Grosso), the hand-harvested grapes undergo spontaneous fermentation in stainless steel with skin maceration for roughly 25 to 30 days. The wine is aged for 36 months in traditional large Slavonian oak casks (botti grandi), followed by extensive bottle refinement before release. The alcohol by volume sits at 14.5%.

Food Pairing

The vibrant acidity, fine-grained tannic backbone, and complex mineral aromatics of this Montosoli Cru make it an exceptional pairing for refined, flavor-packed dishes. It pairs magnificently with prime cuts of red meat, such as dry-aged Florentine steak (bistecca alla Fiorentina), roasted rack of lamb with herbs, slow-braised beef short ribs, and venison tenderloin. It also harmonizes beautifully with fresh pasta dishes featuring wild boar ragù or shaved black truffles, as well as aged hard cheeses like mature Pecorino Toscano, Parmigiano-Reggiano, or aged Gouda.

Vintage Quality

The 2018 vintage in Montalcino was a classic, cooler season marked by steady spring rains and moderate summer temperatures, yielding wines defined by fresh elegance, high aromatic lift, and refined structure. The stony, well-draining soils of the Montosoli hill proved ideal for these conditions, permitting perfect, gradual phenolic ripening while maintaining sparkling natural acidity. The 2018 Canalicchio di Sopra Vigna Montosoli stands out as a triumph of precision and terroir expression, offering immense charm and clarity early after decanting while possessing the concentration and structural balance to cellar gracefully for 15 to 25+ years.

Accolades

96 Points - Jeb Dunnuck
Review Date: 02/2024

The 2018 Brunello Di Montalcino Vigna Montosoli is fresh with aromas of clove, orange peel, peppercorns, and candied cranberries. Medium-bodied, savory, and mineral-toned, with fine, present tannins, a more angular structure, and a crispy freshness throughout, it’s going to need another few years. Drink 2026-2040.

96 Points - Vinous
Review Date: 12/2022

The 2018 Brunello di Montalcino Vigna Montosoli is quite Burgundian in style, slowly awakening in the glass with a delicate mix of sweet herbs, crushed violet candies, hints of spiced orange and wild strawberries. It boasts a stunning purity of fruit and inner sweetness, seeming to hover across the palate, as red berries and saline-minerals slowly saturate under a purple-tinged air of inner florals. The 2018 leaves a grippy coating of fine tannins, yet balances them with a residual bump of zesty acidity, finishing long, lightly structured and with immaculate balance. This is the first official vintage of Vigna Montosoli, a wine that I've been following now for over two years, and each time it seems to only grow in both volume and depth. 96+

95 Points - Wine Advocate
Review Date: 03/2023

Here's an exciting new addition to the growing Canalicchio di Sopra portfolio. With fruit from one of the most celebrated subzones in the appellation, the 2018 Brunello di Montalcino Vigna Montosoli shows a unique profile. The wine opens to a solid core of red and purple fruits, all framed by light spice, crushed stone or chalky limestone. The fiber of this wine is lean, tight and elegantly streamlined. It hits the palate with intensity and softness, and it delivers especially fine tannins. Francesco Ripaccioli made 3,733 bottles and 200 magnums. (ML)

95 Points - Wine Spectator
Review Date: 06/2023

Medium-bodied and open-knit, offering tomato leaf, plum, cherry, licorice, earth and spice flavors. Stays focused, courtesy of good cut, with a silky texture and tannins that leave a slight sinewy feel on the finish. Overall, this is harmonious, complex and long. Best from 2025 through 2042. 344 cases made, 75 cases imported.

title: Canalicchio di Sopra Rosso di Montalcino 2021 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
This expressive dry red wine originates from Italy, within the renowned Montalcino DOC region of southern Tuscany. Bottled in a large 1.5-litre Magnum format, this wine is produced by Canalicchio di Sopra, an estate founded in 1962 by Primo Pacini and one of the original 12 founding members of the Consorzio del Vino Brunello di Montalcino. Today, managed by the third generation—Francesco, Marco, and Simonetta Ripaccioli—the estate treats its Rosso di Montalcino with the same viticultural care and precision as its iconic Brunellos. Sourced from the estate's dual terroirs—the clay-rich, mineral soils of Canalicchio on the northern slopes and the galestro-laden gravels of Montosoli—this cuvée captures the vibrant freshness and purity of Sangiovese.

Wine Description

In the glass, this wine presents a luminous ruby-red colour with brilliant garnet highlights. The nose opens with an inviting and aromatic bouquet of fresh red cherry, wild strawberry, and crushed cranberry, interwoven with delicate floral notes of violet and rose petal, blood orange peel, and subtle Mediterranean garrigue herbs. On the palate, it is medium-bodied, remarkably energetic, and precise. A core of juicy red fruit is supported by fine, chalky tannins and a streak of stony minerality. Crafted from 100% Sangiovese (Sangiovese Grosso), the hand-harvested grapes undergo fermentation in stainless steel before aging for approximately 12 months in large Slavonian oak casks (botti grandi). The 1.5L Magnum format allows for slower micro-oxygenation, enhancing aromatic freshness, structural integration, and overall aging potential. The wine typically carries an alcohol by volume of 14.0%.

Food Pairing

The vibrant acidity, fine tannic structure, and bright fruit profile of this Sangiovese make it a versatile pairing partner for rich Tuscan cuisine and group dining. It pairs brilliantly with classic pasta dishes such as pici al ragù, wild boar pappardelle, and mushroom risotto. Excellent meat pairings include grilled pork chops, roasted rack of lamb with herbs, Florentine steak (bistecca alla Fiorentina), and pan-seared duck breast. For cheese pairings, opt for medium-aged Tuscan Pecorino, Parmigiano-Reggiano, or Fontina.

Vintage Quality

Rosso di Montalcino benefits from Montalcino's sunny Mediterranean climate tempered by cool night breezes, allowing Sangiovese to achieve ideal phenolic maturity while preserving bright natural acidity. The 1.5L Magnum bottling offers enhanced temperature stability during cellar storage, allowing the wine to develop added complexity while retaining its signature fruit purity. While approachable and vibrant upon release, in Magnum format this wine holds the concentration and structure to evolve gracefully in the cellar for 8 to 12+ years.

Accolades

94 Points - Jeb Dunnuck:

"Marked by the estate's April frost, which reduced yields and helped bring extra focus to the vintage, the 2021 Rosso di Montalcino is one of the most complete Rossos I have tasted from Montalcino. The nose is bright and energetic with ripe red cherries, red berries, floral perfume, and sweet citrus. Medium-bodied, it has terrific drive and clarity on the palate, with ripe tannins, vibrant acidity, and a vertical, mouthwatering finish. Drink 2026-2040."

title: Blue Mountain Chardonnay 2023
bodyHtml:
The Blue Mountain Chardonnay is a premier expression from Canada's renowned wine region, the Okanagan Valley in British Columbia. Blue Mountain Vineyard and Cellars is a family run winery, established by the Mavety family, who have farmed this fertile bench overlooking Vaseux Lake since 1971. They are considered quality pioneers in the Okanagan Valley, releasing their first wines under the Blue Mountain label in 1991. The winery’s philosophy is to produce complex, age worthy wines that consistently express both the terroir of their South Okanagan site and the individual growing season.

Wine Description

The wine is made from 100% Chardonnay grapes. The fruit is hand harvested and whole cluster pressed, then barrel fermented and aged, typically for 14 months, in French oak barriques. The ABV for the Estate Cuvée Chardonnay is often around 14.40%. The wine presents a clear, bright, medium plus intensity lemon colour. On the nose, it offers medium plus intensity aromas of toast and ripe pineapple, complemented by subtle notes of roasted apple, sweet almond, and oak. The palate is dry, rich, and full bodied, showcasing a soft buttery texture with flavours of ripe pineapple, roasted apples, and toast. It is known for its intense flavour and creamy style, yet is pinned on fine acidity and minerality. The finish is long, leaving impressions of citrus, butterscotch, and toast. The wine is a testament to the purity of the fruit and is beautifully balanced, with a great balancing acidity.

title: Bittermens Commonwealth - 375 ml
bodyHtml:
Introducing Bittermans Commonwealth Tonic Liqueur, a harmonious blend of craftsmanship, innovation, and botanical artistry that redefines the boundaries of mixology. Created by the creative minds at Bittermans, this liqueur offers you a gateway to a world of cocktail possibilities, where the traditional charm of tonic meets the contemporary flair of a liqueur. 

When you uncork a bottle of Commonwealth Tonic Liqueur, you're inviting the aromas of a spice bazaar and a citrus grove to awaken your senses. These liqueur is an aromatic symphony, with hints of zesty grapefruit, aromatic spices, and the subtle bitterness of quinine, all meticulously blended to create an unforgettable bouquet. This infusion of flavors represents the artistry of liqueur crafting, where the finest ingredients and innovative techniques unite to create a liquid masterpiece.

title: Gekkeikan Traditional Junmai Sake - 18 Litre Box
bodyHtml:
Gekkeikan 'Traditional' is a classic junmai style sake.  It is herbaceous with hints of grapefruit and a light earthiness.  It has good acidity, is mineral-driven, and well-balanced with a clean, medium finish.

This versatile sake can be served warmed, at room temperature, or chilled. It is aged for approximately 6 months to achieve its mellow flavour.  'Traditional' pairs well with fish and shellfish, coconut-based Asian dishes, fresh green vegetable dishes, or used as a flavorful base for stocks and marinades.

Origin:   California, USA  |   Rice Polished to:   70%   |   Alcohol:  15.6%  |  Sulphite Free  |  Gluten Free

title: Koto Sen Nen Junmai Daiginjo - 720 ml
bodyHtml:
Koto Sen Nen Junmai Daiginjo is a premium sake originating from Japan, specifically produced in the Fushimi district of the Kyoto prefecture. The sake is crafted by Saito Shuzo Co. Ltd., a brewery with a heritage of brewing excellence in Kyoto that dates back to 1895. The Koto Sen Nen series is named 'Ancient Capital Millennium' to honour the eternal history of the city of Kyoto.

Description

This sake presents a clear appearance and features a deep, mellow, and elegant sensory profile. It offers a fruity Ginjo aroma with notes of cherry, candy floss, and sakura blossoms, which harmonizes with a delicate and extremely smooth palate. The body is medium with bright acidity, leading to a refined finish that carries a slight hint of white pepper and nutmeg. It is a well balanced and complex Junmai Daiginjo with an alcohol by volume of 15.2%.

Food Pairing

This versatile sake is an ideal match for delicate Japanese cuisine, particularly sushi, sashimi, and lightly seared scallops. Its fruity fragrance and crisp acidity also complement Western dishes such as caprese salad, poached white fish, or creamy cheeses like brie and camembert. For a unique pairing, it can be served alongside zesty melon salad or grilled chicken with a light citrus glaze.

title: Joseph Drouhin Nuits St Georges 2024
bodyHtml:
Joseph Drouhin Nuits Saint Georges 2024 originates from France, within the renowned Burgundy region and the Cote de Nuits subregion. Founded in 1880 by Joseph Drouhin, the family owned house has built a legacy spanning over a century across Beaune and the surrounding appellations. The estate is recognized for its commitment to biological and biodynamic vineyard management, prioritizing natural yeasts and minimal intervention to reflect the genuine expression of each terroir.

Wine Description

This red wine presents a deep, bright red colour. The nose is powerful and elegant, offering rich aromas of fresh cherry and blackberry alongside subtle notes of cedar wood, wild flowers, and light earthy undertones characteristic of the vintage. On the palate, it exhibits a medium to full body with a harmonious balance between elegant tannic structure and soft texture. Stylistically, the wine combines precision, freshness, and fruit delicacy with refined complexity, finishing with a persistent aftertaste reminiscent of fruit syrup and mild spices.

  • Varietal composition: 100% Pinot Noir

  • Alcohol by volume: 13.0%

title: Santa Julia El Burro Malbec Natural 2024
bodyHtml:
Santa Julia El Burro Malbec Natural originates from Argentina, located within the Mendoza region and the Maipu subregion. Bodega Santa Julia was established by the Zuccardi family and named in honour of Julia Zuccardi, reflecting the family's long term commitment to sustainable farming and community development. As one of the early pioneers of organic viticulture in Argentina, the winery emphasizes natural winemaking practices, producing minimal intervention wines fermented with wild yeasts and bottled without added sulphites or filtration.

Wine Description

This red wine displays a deep red colour with vibrant violet hues. The nose is expressive and fruit forward, presenting aromas of fresh dark cherry, ripe plum, mulberry, and floral violet notes complemented by a subtle, rustic earthy quality. On the palate, it features a medium to full body with a generous texture, balanced by lively acidity and soft, rounded tannins. Stylistically, the wine emphasizes freshness, purity, and drinkability, concluding with a persistent and pleasant finish tasting of plum jam.

  • Varietal composition: 100% Malbec

  • Alcohol by volume: 13.5%

  • Organic status: Certified organic and natural wine made without added sulphites

title: Haras de Pirque Albis 2021
bodyHtml:
This flagship icon red wine originates from Chile, crafted in the prestigious Pirque subregion of the Upper Maipo Valley (Maipo Alto). Situated at the foot of the Andes Mountains, Haras de Pirque is famous for its unique horseshoe-shaped gravity-flow winery and thoroughbred horse breeding history. Originally established as a joint venture between the Matte family and Italy’s legendary Marchesi Antinori, the estate came under full Antinori ownership in 2017. Albis represents the ultimate synthesis of Chilean terroir and Italian winemaking expertise, blending Cabernet Sauvignon with Carmenère grown in high-altitude organic vineyards where cool Andean night breezes preserve natural acidity.

Wine Description

In the glass, Albis 2021 displays an intense, deep ruby color with violet edges. The expressive nose delivers layered aromas of cassis, black cherry, and dark plum, framed by distinct herbal and spicy notes of eucalyptus, mint, graphite, black pepper, and subtle mocha from barrel aging. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied, refined, and exceptionally structured. The entry is concentrated yet elegant, showing fine-grained, polished tannins and a vibrant line of freshness that cuts through the rich fruit core. A blend typically led by Cabernet Sauvignon (around 80–85%) and completed by Carmenère (15–20%), the grapes are hand-harvested, optical-sorted, and gravity-fed into French oak vats for fermentation. The wine is aged for approximately 18 to 20 months in French oak barrels (a combination of new and second-use), resulting in a precise, long finish with persistent notes of cocoa and crushed stone. The alcohol by volume sits at 14.5%.

Food Pairing

The firm tannic backbone, savory herbal nuances, and rich dark fruit profile of this Maipo Alto red make it an ideal pairing for structured, rich meat dishes. Excellent culinary partners include prime ribeye steak, grilled rack of lamb with rosemary, roasted venison loin, or slow-braised beef short ribs. It also harmonizes beautifully with empanadas de pino, duck breast with dark fruit reduction, or mature cheeses such as Gouda, sharp Cheddar, and aged Manchego.

Vintage Quality

The 2021 vintage in the Maipo Valley was outstanding, characterized by a cool spring followed by a steady, moderate summer without extreme heatwaves. These conditions allowed for prolonged, uniform ripening, preserving elevated natural acidity, aromatic complexity, and vibrant fresh fruit flavors while permitting tannins to mature fully. The 2021 Albis is considered an exceptionally balanced and age-worthy expression of the estate, displaying remarkable elegance upon release and holding the potential to cellar beautifully for 10 to 15+ years.

title: Fireball Blazin Apple Whisky
bodyHtml:
Fireball Blazin' Apple is a flavored whisky liqueur produced by the Sazerac Company. Expanding upon the massive global success of the flagship Fireball Cinnamon Whisky, this line extension fuses Fireball's signature fiery cinnamon bite with the crisp, tart flavor of green apple. Designed as a sweet, approachable shooter and casual mixer, it offers a profile reminiscent of a liquid apple pie with a spicy kick.

Spirit Description

Fireball Blazin' Apple takes a base of Canadian whisky blended with real cinnamon spice and introduces natural sour and sweet apple flavorings. The resulting liqueur balances the sharp heat of cinnamon candy with a tangy, tart apple core, creating a sweet-and-spicy contrast on the palate.

  • Colour: Warm golden honey with bright amber highlights.

  • Aroma: Pungent and sweet, opening with artificial green apple, cinnamon red-hot candies, baked apple pie spices, and subtle vanilla syrup.

  • Palate: Sweet, bold, and intense on the entry. Crisp sour apple flavor strikes upfront before quickly surrendering to intense cinnamon heat, candied sugar, and subtle oak undertones.

  • Body: Medium-bodied with a syrup-like, coating sweetness.

  • Finish: Medium-to-long, trailing off with lingering sweet apple pie crust, hot cinnamon spice, and a warm chest glow.

  • ABV: Bottled at 33% ABV (66 Proof).

title: Dr Mcgillicuddy's Sour Raspberry
bodyHtml:
Dr. McGillicuddy's Sour Raspberry is a fruit-flavored liqueur produced by the Sazerac Company. Part of the iconic Dr. McGillicuddy's lineup a brand originally inspired by a mythical 19th-century Canadian doctor and homeopath known for crafting medicinal elixirs, this expression focuses on vibrant berry flavor. Designed as a sweet, approachable shooter and versatile mixer, it delivers a punchy balance of tartness and candy-like fruitiness.

Spirit Description

Dr. McGillicuddy's Sour Raspberry is crafted by blending neutral spirits with natural and artificial sour raspberry flavorings and sweetener. The profile centers on a sharp contrast between candy-like raspberry sweetness and a tangy citrus-style acidity, making it an easy-drinking options for casual settings.

  • Colour: Vivid, luminous electric ruby red.

  • Aroma: Bright, sweet, and fruit-forward, featuring aromas of red raspberry hard candy, candied cherry, fruit punch, and fresh citrus zest.

  • Palate: Tangy and sweet on the entry. Upfront flavors of juicy red raspberries and sour candy drop give way to subtle notes of lime zest, red berry jam, and sugary syrup.

  • Body: Light-to-medium-bodied with a smooth, sweet, and coating texture.

  • Finish: Crisp, tart, and medium in length, leaving a sweet raspberry candy flavor and a mild citrus lip-pucker.

  • ABV: Bottled at 21% ABV (42 Proof) in North America; 15% ABV in select regional formats.

title: Duckhorn Oakville Cabernet Sauvignon 2023
bodyHtml:
Duckhorn Oakville Cabernet Sauvignon 2023 originates from the United States, within California's Napa Valley region and the famed Oakville AVA subregion. Founded in 1976 by Dan and Margaret Duckhorn, Duckhorn Vineyards has established itself over five decades as a benchmark producer of premier Napa Valley wines. Released as part of the winery's 50th-anniversary milestone offerings, this bottling highlights Oakville's world-renowned terroir, known for generating Cabernet Sauvignon with rich structure, refined complexity, and age-worthy power.

Wine Description

This red wine displays a deep, dark ruby purple colour. The nose is expressive and layered, opening with aromas of black currant, dark plum, and black cherry compote alongside nuances of dried thyme, fig, crushed river stones, bitter chocolate, and subtle black truffle. On the palate, it exhibits a full body with a refined, supple, and dense texture supported by finely shaped, polished tannins and vibrant acidity. Stylistically, the wine balances bold fruit concentration with a savory, mineral thread and lingering oak spice, finishing long and smooth with notes of cardamom jam, licorice, and cocoa.

  • Varietal composition: 100% Cabernet Sauvignon

  • Alcohol by volume: 14.5%

title: Duckhorn Rutherford Cabernet Sauvignon 2023
bodyHtml:
Duckhorn Rutherford Cabernet Sauvignon 2023 originates from the United States, within California's Napa Valley region and the distinguished Rutherford AVA subregion. Founded in 1976 by Dan and Margaret Duckhorn, Duckhorn Vineyards has established itself over five decades as a benchmark producer of premier Napa Valley wines. Released alongside other single-AVA bottlings to celebrate the winery's 50th-anniversary milestone, this wine showcases the unique terroir of Rutherford—famed for its gravelly, alluvial soils that impart a signature dusty minerality and exceptional structure to Cabernet Sauvignon.

Wine Description

This red wine displays a deep, dark plum to dark ruby colour. The nose is complex and fragrant, offering aromas of blueberry, blackberry, and fig alongside floral violet notes, dark chocolate, sweet spice, potpourri, and a touch of ferric earth and pencil shavings. On the palate, it exhibits a full body with fine-grained, velvety tannins and bright acidity, underscored by Rutherford's characteristic signature dusty minerality. Stylistically, the wine is well-balanced, generous, and fruit-driven, leading to a long, supple finish accented by mild oak spice and dark fruit complexity.

  • Varietal composition: 100% Cabernet Sauvignon

  • Alcohol by volume: 14.5%

title: Chateau Pape Clement 2021
bodyHtml:
Chateau Pape Clement 2021 originates from France, within the Bordeaux region and the Pessac Leognan subregion. The estate boasts a rich winemaking history dating back to the 13th century when it was first planted by Bertrand de Goth, who later became Pope Clement V. Owned today by Bernard Magrez, the winery balances traditional craftsmanship with modern viticulture, managing ancient gravelly terroirs to produce world class, cellar worthy Grand Cru Classe wines.

Wine Description

This red wine displays a deep ruby plum to dark crimson colour. The nose opens with expressive aromas of sweet red berries, black cherry, and blackcurrant intertwined with complex notes of espresso roast, black truffles, scorched earth, and subtle cedar wood. On the palate, it exhibits a medium body with a polished, satiny texture, balanced by bright acidity and refined, integrated tannins. Stylistically, the 2021 vintage highlights a more classical, elegant, and fresh profile with attractive minerality, graphite, and savory spice lingering through a persistent finish.

  • Varietal composition: 50% Merlot, 47% Cabernet Sauvignon, 2% Cabernet Franc, 1% Petit Verdot

  • Alcohol by volume: 13.0%

title: Chateau Pape Clement 2022
bodyHtml:
Chateau Pape Clement 2022 originates from France, within the Bordeaux region and the Pessac Leognan subregion. The estate boasts a rich winemaking history dating back to the 13th century when it was first planted by Bertrand de Goth, who later became Pope Clement V. Owned today by Bernard Magrez, the winery balances traditional craftsmanship with modern viticulture, managing ancient gravelly terroirs to produce world class, cellar worthy Grand Cru Classe wines.

Wine Description

This red wine displays a deep, dark garnet purple colour. The nose is highly expressive and complex, presenting soaring aromas of ripe cassis, dark plum, and blueberry alongside nuances of crushed stone, white pepper, sweet tobacco, and cedar wood. On the palate, it exhibits a full body with a rich, layered texture and dense, polished tannins that provide firm structural backbone. Stylistically, the wine strikes a remarkable balance between power and vibrant freshness, showing exceptional precision, energy, and a long, lingering finish.

  • Varietal composition: 60% Merlot, 40% Cabernet Sauvignon

  • Alcohol by volume: 14.0%

Accolades

98 Points - #35 Jeb Dunnuck Top 100 of 2025

Black raspberries, cassis, graphite, scorched earth, and violet notes are just some of the nuances in the 2022 Château Pape Clément, a gorgeously textured, layered, seamless 2022. It's flawlessly balanced, has a class of tannins that's second to none, is full-bodied, has terrific concentration, and has a gorgeous finish. This classic, seamless, elegant, sensational layered, multi-dimensional. Rating: 98+

97 Points - James Suckling

A very well-balanced Pape Clement showing a solid structure, concentration and length. Fresh and complex, with a fine streak of minerals and aromas of cassis, berries, white pepper and tapenade. Some wood spices, but they’re quite restrained. Full-bodied, tight and long. A transparent and complete wine for the cellar.

title: Chateau Pape Clement Blanc 2022 - 3 Bottles
bodyHtml:
Chateau Pape Clement Blanc 2022 originates from France, within the Bordeaux region and the Pessac Leognan subregion. The estate boasts a rich winemaking history dating back to the 13th century when it was first planted by Bertrand de Goth, who later became Pope Clement V. Owned today by Bernard Magrez, the winery balances traditional craftsmanship with modern viticulture, managing ancient gravelly terroirs to produce world class, cellar worthy Grand Cru Classe white wines.

Wine Description

This white wine displays a brilliant golden colour with light greenish reflections. The nose is highly expressive and perfumed, presenting aromas of lemon curd, fresh grapefruit, white peach, spring flowers, and toasted brioche with a hint of warm spices. On the palate, it exhibits a medium to full body with a fleshy, satiny texture balanced by a vibrant line of saline acidity and fine mineral phenolics. Stylistically, the wine strikes a harmonious balance between luxurious richness, precision, and refreshing concentration, leading into a long, persistent finish.

  • Varietal composition: 63% Sauvignon Blanc, 35% Semillon, 2% Muscadelle

  • Alcohol by volume: 13.5%

title: Chateau Pape Clement 2019
bodyHtml:
Chateau Pape Clement 2019 originates from France, within the Bordeaux region and the Pessac Leognan subregion. The estate boasts a rich winemaking history dating back to the 13th century when it was first planted by Bertrand de Goth, who later became Pope Clement V. Owned today by Bernard Magrez, the winery balances traditional craftsmanship with modern viticulture, managing ancient gravelly terroirs to produce world class, cellar worthy Grand Cru Classe wines.

Wine Description

This red wine displays a deep garnet purple colour. The nose is intense, expressive, and highly complex, opening with bold aromas of ripe cassis, dark plum, and black cherry intertwined with nuances of lead pencil, cedar, tobacco, crushed stone, and subtle floral iris notes. On the palate, it exhibits a full body with a rich, velvety texture supported by dense, ultra-fine tannins and vibrant mineral energy. Stylistically, the 2019 vintage showcases remarkable freshness, power, and precision, finishing with extraordinary length and lingering spice.

  • Varietal composition: 50% Cabernet Sauvignon, 50% Merlot

  • Alcohol by volume: 14.0%

title: Chateau Leoville Las Cases 2010 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
Chateau Leoville Las Cases 2010 originates from France, within the Bordeaux region and the Saint-Julien subregion. Classified as a Second Growth (Deuxième Grand Cru Classé) in the historic 1855 Classification, the estate represents the largest portion of the original, historic Léoville estate. Managed by the Delon family, the vineyard sits adjacent to Château Latour, directly overlooking the Gironde estuary. Known as one of Bordeaux's premier "Super Seconds," Léoville Las Cases produces deeply structured, exceptionally long-lived wines that regularly match the quality of First Growths.

Wine Description

This red wine displays an opaque purple to deep garnet colour. The nose offers intense, layered aromas of blackcurrant, crème de cassis, dark plum, and fresh blackberries, complemented by subtle nuances of cedar wood, tobacco leaf, graphite, incense, and black truffle. On the palate, it is full-bodied, dense, and powerfully built, supported by silky yet firm, fine-grained tannins and bright, balancing acidity. Stylistically, the 2010 vintage represents a monumental, classical Las Cases—muscular, precise, and mineral-driven, finishing with remarkable length and exceptional cellaring potential.

  • Varietal composition: 82% Cabernet Sauvignon, 10% Merlot, 8% Cabernet Franc

  • Alcohol by volume: 13.7%

title: Berry's Own Craigellechie Single Malt 2012 (Cask 2949)
bodyHtml:
This single malt scotch whisky originates from Scotland, produced in the Speyside region. The Craigellachie Distillery was founded in 1891 by Peter Mackie and Alexander Edward, and it is currently owned by Dewar's, a subsidiary of Bacardi. Famous for its traditional copper worm tub condensers, the distillery is renowned for producing a uniquely robust, heavy, and characterful malt spirit. Independent bottler Berry Bros & Rudd selected this expression from cask reference 2949, aged for ten years in a refill butt.

Spirit Description

This expression presents a warm amber gold colour in the glass. The aroma opens with fragrant notes of dried barley, warm hay, and fresh shortbread, which slowly evolve into subtle Oloroso sherry undertones, soft caramel, and a delicate trace of smoke. On the palate, it delivers a full body with an exceptionally rich and waxy texture, offering flavours of juicy barley candy, caramelized pineapple, citrus, dried fruit, and toasted almonds balanced by cinnamon and white pepper. The finish is long, warm, and lingering, carrying accents of wood spice, charcoal, and sweet malt. With an ABV of 54.3%, this cask strength malt exhibits impressive depth, complexity, and spirit balance.

title: Chateau Angludet 2022
bodyHtml:
This structured and 'aristocratic' red wine originates from France, within the historic Margaux A.O.C. appellation on the Left Bank of Bordeaux. Château Angludet is one of the oldest estates in the Médoc, with origins dating back to the 12th century. Owned and passionately managed by the Sichel family since 1961, the property operates with the precision and dedicated care of a Cru Classé, despite holding the Cru Bourgeois Exceptionnel classification. Located on a gravel plateau in the commune of Cantenac, the vineyards are rooted in deep, free-draining Garonne gravel over clay-limestone subsoils. This singular terroir, combined with maritime influences from the nearby Gironde Estuary, allows Cabernet Sauvignon and its classic Bordeaux blending partners to achieve exceptional phenolic maturity, delicate floral perfume, and velvety structural elegance.

Wine Description

The 2022 Château Angludet presents a deep, vibrant crimson-purple appearance in the glass with bright ruby shimmers at the rim. Its sensory profile is exceptionally fresh, high-toned, and complex, delivering a textbook expression of Margaux's signature elegance combined with the incredible solar density of the vintage. The bouquet opens with a captivating display of crushed cassis, dark plum compote, and wild blackberries, seamlessly layered with complex underlays of dried violets, cigar box, graphite, fresh mint, and subtle toasted cedar. On the palate, the wine is medium-to-full-bodied, refined, and precisely focused, showcasing a generous core of black stone fruits, dark chocolate, and licorice. It is characterized by its outstanding inner energy and a lively, mouthwatering line of natural acidity that cuts through the mid-palate extract. The mouthfeel is broad, velvety, and supple, driven by remarkably polished, fine-grained tannins that glide into an extraordinarily long, harmonious finish accented by lingering notes of black tea, sweet spice, and mineral gravel.

title: Jermann Afix Riesling 2023
bodyHtml:
This structured and 'crystalline' white wine originates from Italy, within the prized Venezia Giulia IGT appellation in the far northeastern region of Friuli-Venezia Giulia. Produced by the world-renowned Jermann estate, founded in 1881 by Anton Jermann, this cuvée represents a visionary fusion of traditional Germanic varietal purity and Friulian technical finesse. Sourced from high-elevation vineyard sites in the rolling hills of Dolegna del Collio and Farra d’Isonzo, the vines are rooted in ponca a highly prized Eocene soil formation composed of alternating layers of calcareous marl and sandstone. The microclimate here is exceptionally favorable for Riesling: cool alpine breezes from the Julian Alps preserve laser-like natural acidity, while warm daytime currents from the Adriatic Sea promote full, complex grape ripening.

Wine Description

Jermann 'Afix' Riesling presents a brilliant, pale straw-yellow appearance in the glass with light greenish-silver reflections. Its sensory profile is exceptionally fresh, high-toned, and complex, delivering a masterfully precise and aromatic expression of Italian-grown Riesling. The bouquet opens with a captivating display of white peach, green apple, and fresh lime zest, seamlessly layered with complex undertones of jasmine, white flowers, lemongrass, candied ginger, and a subtle line of petrol and crushed flint minerality. On the palate, the wine is medium-bodied, sleek, and intensely focused, showcasing a vibrant core of citrus oils, tart stone fruits, and green pear. It is characterized by its outstanding inner energy and an incisive, mouthwatering backbone of natural acidity that cuts cleanly through the mid-palate density. The mouthfeel is supple yet weightless, carrying into a long, bone-dry, and mineral-driven finish accented by lingering notes of lemon curd, cold stone, and grapefruit peel.

This high-definition varietal expression is 100% Riesling (Riesling Renano), harvested by hand from low-yielding estate vineyards. Following a gentle cold pressing of whole clusters to preserve pure primary fruit character, the juice underwent slow, temperature-controlled fermentation in stainless steel vats. To safeguard its crisp linear tension and pure varietal aromatics, the wine did not undergo malolactic conversion and was matured on its fine lees in stainless steel tanks for approximately six months before bottling. It reaches an effortlessly balanced, food-friendly alcohol content (ABV) of 13.0% and is finished bone-dry.

title: Jermann Traminer Aromatico 2021
bodyHtml:
This structured and 'crystalline' white wine originates from Italy, within the esteemed Venezia Giulia IGT appellation in the far northeastern corner of Friuli-Venezia Giulia. Founded in 1881 by Anton Jermann, the estate reached international stardom in the late 20th century under the visionary leadership of Silvio Jermann, who revolutionized white winemaking in Italy by marrying low-intervention respect for terroir with hyper-precise cellar practices. Sourced from estate vineyards situated across the rolling hills of Farra d’Isonzo and Dolegna del Collio, the vines are rooted in Flysch di Cormòns a prized Eocene soil formation composed of alternating layers of calcareous marl and sandstone (ponca). The region’s unique alpine-continental microclimate, cooled by winds sweeping down from the Julian Alps and warmed by breezes off the Adriatic Sea, allows the highly aromatic Traminer Aromatico (Gewürztraminer) grapes to achieve profound aromatic depth while locking in crisp natural acidity.

Wine Description

Jermann Traminer Aromatico presents a brilliant, bright straw-yellow color in the glass with shimmering golden highlights. Its sensory profile is exceptionally fresh, high-toned, and complex, delivering an intensely fragrant and pristine expression of northern Italian aromatic winemaking. The bouquet opens with a captivating, multi-faceted display of fresh lychees, white peach, and passion fruit, seamlessly layered with floral undertones of rose petals, jasmine, yellow apple, and exotic nuances of candied ginger, clove, and grapefruit zest. On the palate, the wine is medium-to-full-bodied, elegant, and precisely focused, showcasing a lush, round core of tropical fruits, sweet citrus oils, and stone fruit. It is characterized by its outstanding inner energy and an incisive, mouthwatering backbone of natural acidity that balances its headnumbing aromatics and mid-palate density. The mouthfeel is broad, smooth, and supple, carrying into an extraordinarily long, dry, and mineral finish accented by lingering notes of orange blossom, subtle white pepper, and cool stone minerality.

This high-definition varietal expression is 100% Traminer Aromatico, harvested by hand from low-yielding, estate-selected vineyards. Following a gentle pressing of whole clusters and a short skin-contact cold soak to extract pristine aromatic compounds, the juice underwent slow, temperature-controlled fermentation in stainless steel tanks. To preserve pure primary fruit and floral aromatics, the wine did not undergo malolactic conversion and was aged on its fine lees in stainless steel vats for several months prior to bottling. It reaches a seamlessly integrated, food-friendly alcohol content (ABV) of 13.0% and is finished bone-dry.

title: Champagne Drappier Brut Nature Zero Dosage
bodyHtml:
This uncompromising zero-dosage sparkling wine originates from France, in the village of Urville within the Côte des Bar subregion of Champagne. The Drappier family traces its agricultural roots back to Saint Bernard, who established the historic Cistercian cellars in Urville in 1152, though the family estate was formally founded in 1808. Today, the eighth generation—Michel Drappier alongside his children Charline, Hugo, and Antoine—leads the house with an ardent focus on eco-responsibility, minimal intervention, and organic viticulture. Drappier is widely recognized as a pioneer of zero-dosage Champagnes, having launched this cuvée in the 1980s. Sourced from estate vineyards planted on rich Kimmeridgian limestone soils, this wine stands out as a pure, unadorned expression of southern Champagne terroir.

Wine Description

In the glass, this Blanc de Noirs shows a pale gold colour with copper reflections and a delicate, continuous mousse. The nose opens with vibrant aromas of fresh red apple, white peach, citrus zest, and quince, layered alongside subtle notes of warm brioche, white flowers, and crushed stone minerality. On the palate, it exhibits raw energy, precision, and structural focus. Crafted entirely from 100% Pinot Noir, only the first press (la cuvée) is used, with mechanical pumping minimized to prevent oxidation. The wine undergoes natural gravity-led settling (débourbage) and full malolactic fermentation, using minimal sulfur additions. It is aged on its lees in the cellar for 30 to 36 months before being finished completely bone-dry with 0 g/L dosage (Zero Dosage). The alcohol by volume sits at 12%.

Food Pairing

The strict dryness, high acidity, and broad vinous weight of this zero-dosage Pinot Noir make it a superb culinary companion. It excels when paired with raw and delicate seafood preparations, including fresh oysters, sushi, sashimi, tuna tartare, and sea bass carpaccio. Its laser-like tension cuts through rich, savory dishes like smoked salmon, pan-seared scallops, or grilled prawns. For non-seafood pairings, try it with roasted poultry, carpaccio of beef, or young artisanal goat cheese such as Sainte-Maure de Touraine.

title: Champagne Ployez Jacquemart Extra Quality Brut
bodyHtml:
This artisanal non-vintage Champagne originates from France, crafted in the Premier Cru village of Ludes within the Montagne de Reims. Founded in 1930 by Marcel Ployez and Yvonne Jacquemart, this boutique family-run house is today led by third-generation winemaker Laurence Ployez. The house operates on an uncompromising, craft-scale philosophy, sourcing fruit exclusively from Premier Cru and Grand Cru vineyards. Their viticulture relies heavily on deep limestone and chalk soils across key villages such as Ludes, Mailly, Vertus, and Cuis. The Extra Quality Brut serves as the signature emblem of the house, illustrating their commitment to rigorous selection, minimal intervention, and long cellar aging.

Wine Description

In the glass, the wine presents a brilliant golden-yellow hue accompanied by a delicate, fine-beaded mousse. The bouquet opens with fragrant notes of white flowers, yellow orchard fruits, and lemon rind, evolving into deeper aromas of wild honey, subtle hazelnut, and warm brioche. On the palate, it exhibits profound balance, tension, and texture. The house uses strictly la cuvée (the very first press) and allows the must to settle naturally twice before fermentation. The wine shows impressive body tempered by a streak of chalky acidity. Blended from roughly equal parts or a Chardonnay-dominant selection of Pinot Noir, Pinot Meunier, and Chardonnay, it undergoes upside-down lees aging (sur pointe) for a minimum of 4 years prior to disgorgement. Finished with a remarkably low dosage of around 5 g/L, it delivers a crisp, dry, and extraordinarily clean finish. The alcohol by volume sits at 12%.

Food Pairing

The vinous structure, vibrant minerality, and low dosage profile of this Champagne make it exceptional at the table. It pairs seamlessly with fresh seafood such as oysters on the half shell, sea bass carpaccio, caviar, and pan-seared scallops. The richness from extended lees contact allows it to handle roasted poultry, veal cutlets in cream sauce, pork tenderloin with apples, and refined cheeses such as aged Comté, Chaource, or Langres.

title: Champagne Moutard Pere & Fils Brut Grande Cuvee
bodyHtml:
This classic non-vintage sparkling wine originates from France, within the southern Champagne region of the Côte des Bar. The Moutard family has been rooted in the village of Buxeuil since 1642, though Lucien Moutard established the modern Champagne house in 1952. Today, the estate is managed by the family's fifth generation, led by François Moutard. The Grande Cuvée is the pillar of Moutard's production. Sourced from vines aged 10 to 20 years in Buxeuil and Polisy, the fruit benefits from the region’s distinct Kimmeridgian clay-limestone soils—geologically similar to those of Chablis—which grant both richness and mineral tension to the wines.

Wine Description
