The 2021 vintage in Saint Julien presented a less propitious growing season, but careful agronomy and meticulous winemaking successfully turned it into a brilliant triumph. Unpredictable regional weather conditions required strict sorting and precise management, leading the team to lower the percentage of Merlot and increase the Cabernet Franc to provide an energetic, fresh lift. The winemaker's skill in handling these challenges and aging the wine in 85% new French oak produced a highly praised release, with critics noting its exceptional cellaring capacity and longevity that will see it develop beautifully through 2065.

title: Lungarotti Umbria San Giorgio 1990 (Released 2000)
bodyHtml:
Lungarotti 'San Giorgio' 1990 is a historic red wine from the Torgiano region of Umbria, Italy. This specific bottling gained legendary status for its extraordinary ten-year maturation period at the estate before being released in 2000 to commemorate the new millennium. Originally created in 1977 by Giorgio Lungarotti, San Giorgio was the first "Super-Umbrian" blend, designed to break traditional rules by combining Cabernet Sauvignon with indigenous varietals. The wine's label features a detail from Raphael’s Saint George and the Dragon, a tribute to the traditional propitiatory bonfires lit in the Torgiano vineyards every April 23rd.

Wine Description

This 1990 vintage, benefiting from a decade of bottle aging before release, presents a very intense ruby red color with deep garnet reflections. The nose is remarkably complex and mature, leading with aromatic layers of leather, cassis, and kirsch, followed by notes of plum jam, cocoa, and cinnamon with a distinct balsamic background. On the palate, the wine is concentrated and dense, described by critics as "fleshy" with fully resolved, velvety tannins. Stylistically, it is a bold and structured red that balances the power of Cabernet with the elegance of Sangiovese, concluding with a long, persistent finish marked by notes of dark chocolate and licorice.

title: Chateau Giscours 2006
bodyHtml:
Introduction

Chateau Giscours 2006 is a classified Third Growth from the Margaux appellation in Bordeaux, France. The estate traces its origins back to a 1330 deed, with the first vines planted in 1552 by Pierre de Lhomme. Under the current ownership of the Albada Jelgersma family, the winery follows a holistic winemaking philosophy that treats the vineyard as a micro-garden, emphasizing biodiversity and sustainable viticulture to preserve the natural ecosystem.

Wine Description

This 2006 vintage presents a deep ruby, plum, or garnet hue in the glass. The aromatics are expressive and complex, mingling notes of blackcurrants, cherries, and plums with subtle nuances of tobacco leaf, roasted herbs, tar, and licorice. On the palate, the wine is medium to full bodied with a supple entry, featuring a core of pure blackberry and black cherry fruit accented by dark chocolate and black pepper. Stylistically, it offers a classic Margaux elegance with well-integrated, velvety tannins and a refreshing vein of stony minerality that leads to a saline finish. This blend of approximately 60% Cabernet Sauvignon and 40% Merlot has reached a beautiful stage of maturity and is best enjoyed through 2028.

Accolades

  • Wine Enthusiast - 94 points

  • Vinous - 91 points

  • Wine Spectator - 91 points

  • Decanter - 91 points

  • Robert Parker - 88 points

title: Chateau Haut Brion 2007
bodyHtml:
Hailing from the Pessac Leognan region of Graves, France, Chateau Haut Brion stands as a legendary pillar of winemaking with a history stretching back to 1533. This estate holds a unique status as both a 1855 Premier Grand Cru Classe and a Cru Classe de Graves. Under the stewardship of the Dillon family since 1935, the winery has championed a philosophy of technical progress, notably becoming the first First Growth to adopt stainless steel fermentation vats in 1961.

Wine Description

The 2007 vintage presents a striking visual of deep red-violet and crimson. Its aromatic profile is notably fragrant, weaving together scents of plum sauce, black cherry, and red fruit with earthier undertones of graphite, sandalwood, and crushed stone. On the palate, the wine is suave and medium-bodied, characterized by silky tannins and a savory, meaty finish that persists long after the first sip. A blend of 44% Cabernet Sauvignon, 43% Merlot, and 13% Cabernet Franc, this selection showcases a distinct mineral complexity. While it has reached its prime drinking plateau, it is expected to remain exceptional through 2040.

Accolades

  • Wine Enthusiast - 98 points

  • Wine Advocate (Neal Martin) - 94 points

  • Vinous - 94 points

  • Jeb Dunnuck - 93 points

  • Wine Spectator - 91 points

title: Chateau Latour Premier Grand Cru Classe 1995
bodyHtml:
Produced in France within the esteemed Pauillac appellation, Chateau Latour is a premier First Growth estate whose history is deeply intertwined with the heritage of the Médoc. Since the property was acquired by François Pinault in 1993, the estate has undergone a significant technical renaissance, emphasizing a winemaking philosophy of precision and uncompromising quality. The vineyard's unique location overlooking the Gironde estuary provides a temperate microclimate that is essential for producing the depth and power synonymous with the Latour name.

Wine Description

The 1995 vintage is a classic expression of Pauillac, characterized by a deep ruby to opaque purple colour. Its aromatic profile is intense and evolving, offering a complex layers of crème de cassis, violets, and black cherries, underscored by distinct notes of mineral-rich earth and cedar wood. On the palate, this full bodied wine is exceptionally structured and powerful, featuring firm, ripe tannins and a dense core of black fruit that leads into a persistent, clean finish. Composed primarily of 74% Cabernet Sauvignon, with the remainder being Merlot and Cabernet Franc, this wine has reached its optimal drinking window and is expected to remain vibrant through 2040.

Accolades

  • Robert Parker - 96 points

  • Wine Spectator - 96 points

  • James Suckling - 94 points

  • Decanter - 94 points

  • Vinous - 93 points

title: Chateau Lafite Rothschild 1998
bodyHtml:
Chateau Lafite Rothschild was concerned that the rainy harvest might dash their high hopes founded with the early blossoming, dry spring and scorching August. That turned out not to be the case. There was no rainfall until the harvest had already begun. The grapes were thus moistened but not penetrated, so maybe they can consider that divine intervention.

Once the first tanks had been worked, analyzed, and tasted, weary expressions changed to satisfied smiles. This vintage reflects the strength of our soil, with its deep colour and woody, fruity, and spicy palate. The "98" may be preserved for a very long time, and is rich and full with a silky and long finish.

Blend: 81% Cabernet Sauvignon, 19% Merlot

98 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

A blend of 81% Cabernet Sauvignon and 19% Merlot, this wine represents only 34% of Lafite's total harvest. In a less than perfect Medoc vintage, it has been spectacular since birth, putting on more weight and flesh over the last year. This opaque purple-colored 1998 is close to perfection. The spectacular nose of lead pencil, smoky, mineral, and black currant fruit soars majestically from the glass. The wine is elegant yet profoundly rich, revealing the essence of Lafite's character. The tannin is sweet, and the wine is spectacularly layered yet never heavy. The finish is sweet, super-rich, yet impeccably balanced and long (50+ seconds). Anticipated maturity: 2007-2035.

95 Points - Wine Spectator

Amazing aromas of crushed blackberries, toasted oak and currant, spices. Really a great nose. Full-bodied, with round and velvety tannins and a long, long finish. It lasts for minutes on the palate. Superb. Best wine of the Médoc, without a doubt.

94 Points - Decanter

Easy vintage until September, when conditions in the Medoc particularly became humid, which meant accelerating the harvest (it was one of those years when Lafite benefitted enormously from its ability to ramp up a bigger-than-expected team of pickers). Salin still calls this a lunch wine, because of its supple freshness, its balance that would work so perfectly with food.The vintage was a showcase for Bordeaux on the Right Bank, where it was considered great from the start. The Medoc and Graves were less well received at the time, but are ripe for rediscovering now. This still has a lovely deep ruby red colour, and on both the nose and palate you are getting to secondary aromas, a walk in the forest, mushrooms, cedars, heather, game – these are flavours you just don’t get in young wines, and amply reward the patience of holding bottles back. The surprise, and the Lafite signature, comes in its vibrancy, in its huge persistency and in the lift on the finish.

title: Chateau Angelus 2003
bodyHtml:
Produced in France, specifically within the Saint Emilion Grand Cru appellation on the Right Bank of Bordeaux, Chateau Angelus is a historic estate managed by the Boüard de Laforest family for eight generations. The name of the property is a tribute to the three local church bells audible from its vineyards, an image that remains central to the winery's identity and logo. Under the influential direction of Hubert de Boüard, the estate has prioritized a philosophy of constant technical challenge and precision, which led to its elevation to Premier Grand Cru Classé 'A' in 2012.

Wine Description

The 2003 vintage displays a dense, bluish-purple colour, reflecting a high level of concentration and ripeness. On the nose, it delivers an opulent and 'wild' aromatic profile featuring blackberry liqueur, roasted espresso, acacia flowers, and chocolate, underscored by nuances of curry and graphite. The palate is full-bodied and voluptuous, characterized by lush tannins and a velvety texture that masks a surprising freshness for such a torrid year. Notably, this vintage incorporates the highest percentage of Cabernet Franc ever used at the estate—approximately 55-58%—blended with Merlot. Having reached full maturity, this legendary wine offers a persistent, 60-second finish and is best enjoyed through 2035.

Accolades

  • Robert Parker - 98 points

  • Wine Enthusiast - 94 points

  • Wine Spectator - 94 points

  • James Suckling - 93 points

  • Vinous - 92 points

title: Chateau Leoville Las Cases 2007
bodyHtml:
Produced in France, specifically within the Saint Julien appellation of the Médoc, this wine is the Grand Vin of the historic Château Leoville Las Cases. As one of the oldest and largest estates in the region, it was formed from the historic heart of the original Domaine de Léoville after it was divided following the French Revolution. Currently owned and managed by Jean-Hubert Delon, the winery is renowned for a winemaking philosophy that prioritizes terroir expression and exceptional aging potential, often drawing comparisons to First Growth estates due to its proximity to Château Latour.

Wine Description

The 2007 vintage presents a dense, dark garnet color, reflecting its concentrated nature. The sensory profile is elegant and classic, with a nose that reveals ripe blackberries, red currants, and violets, layered with sophisticated notes of cedar, graphite, and tobacco leaf. On the medium to full-bodied palate, the wine is fresh and harmonious, showcasing silky tannins and a juicy core of cassis and black cherry. Stylistically, it is celebrated for its 'wily, feminine' character, balancing quiet concentration with a racy, refreshing acidity that leads to a long, peppery finish. Composed of 82% Cabernet Sauvignon, 10% Cabernet Franc, and 8% Merlot (or Petit Verdot according to some technical sheets), this wine has reached its plateau of maturity and is expected to provide enjoyment through 2035.

Accolades

  • Decanter - 95 points

  • James Suckling - 95 points

  • Wine Enthusiast - 94 points

  • Wine Advocate - 92 points

  • Vinous - 92 points

  • Wine Spectator - 91 points

title: Chateau Lafite Rothschild 2004
bodyHtml:
Château Lafite Rothschild, located in the Pauillac appellation of Bordeaux, France, is one of the most prestigious wine estates in the world. The 2004 vintage stands out for its elegance and complexity, reflecting the estate's commitment to excellence and the unique terroir of the region.

Vintage Overview

The 2004 growing season began with a rainy winter and cool spring, followed by a dry and warm June and July. August was milder, with September bringing favorable conditions that allowed for optimal grape ripening. This combination of weather patterns contributed to a vintage with balanced structure and refined character.

Tasting Notes

  • Appearance: Deep purple hue, still youthful in color despite its age.
  • Nose: Aromas of graphite, cassis, black cherries, and minerals, accented by subtle hints of cedar and earthy undertones.
  • Palate: Medium-bodied with silky tannins and perfectly balanced acidity. Flavors of blackberry, graphite, and cedar are prominent, leading to a long, refined, and elegant finish.

Critical Acclaim

  • Robert Parker’s Wine Advocate: 95 points – Praised for its sensual and pure bouquet, opulence, and structured balance.
  • Wine Enthusiast: 95 points – Highlighted for its power, dense structure, and velvety mouthfeel, featuring ripe black plum and fig flavors with refreshing acidity.

Serving and Cellaring

The 2004 Château Lafite Rothschild is best served at around 60°F (15.5°C) to allow its complex aromas and flavors to shine. Decanting is recommended to help the wine fully open up. While it is drinking beautifully now, this vintage has the potential to continue developing with further cellaring.

Conclusion

The 2004 Château Lafite Rothschild is a testament to the estate's mastery in crafting wines of timeless appeal. With its harmonious balance, depth, and aging potential, it remains a prized addition to any wine enthusiast’s collection.

title: Chateau Latour Premier Grand Cru Classe 2000
bodyHtml:
Hailing from the storied Pauillac appellation in France, Chateau Latour is a premier First Growth estate with a legacy stretching back to the 14th century. Since 1993, the property has flourished under the ownership of François Pinault, whose management team champions a philosophy of rigorous vineyard precision and ecological respect. The heart of the estate is the 'l'Enclos' vineyard, a unique site near the Gironde estuary where the microclimate provides natural frost protection and fosters grapes of immense power and character.

Wine Description

This 2000 vintage is a masterpiece of concentration, presenting an opaque, ink like purple colour that has remained remarkably vibrant over time. The aromatic profile is both profound and multi layered, unfolding with core scents of blackcurrant, graphite, and crushed stone, followed by sophisticated notes of roasted coffee and cedar. On the palate, the wine is quintessentially masculine and full bodied, defined by a massive yet seamless tannic structure that balances its monumental fruit intensity. Composed of 77% Cabernet Sauvignon, 16% Merlot, 4% Cabernet Franc, and 3% Petit Verdot, this blend is just beginning to enter its prime and possesses the stamina to evolve through 2050.

Accolades

  • Robert Parker - 100 points

  • James Suckling - 100 points

  • Wine Enthusiast - 100 points

  • Wine Spectator - 99 points

  • Decanter - 99 points

title: Chateau Margaux 2003
bodyHtml:
Château Margaux, located in the Margaux appellation of Bordeaux, France, is a Premier Grand Cru Classé estate renowned for its exceptional wines. Established in the 16th century, the estate has a storied history of producing wines that exemplify elegance and complexity. The Mentzelopoulos family has owned Château Margaux since 1977, ushering in a new era of quality and innovation.

Wine Description

The 2003 Château Margaux presents a deep, dark ruby-red color. On the nose, it offers an intense bouquet of dark fruits, including blackberry and cassis, complemented by notes of cedar, tobacco, and violet perfume. The palate is rich and opulent, showcasing flavors of dark cherries, licorice, and a touch of graphite. The wine's silky tannins and impeccable balance lead to a long, harmonious finish. This vintage is predominantly composed of Cabernet Sauvignon, with smaller proportions of Merlot, Petit Verdot, and Cabernet Franc. It exhibits remarkable freshness and precision, defying the expectations of the hot vintage, and can be enjoyed now or cellared for further development over the next 15-20 years.

Accolades

  • Wine Enthusiast – 96 points
  • Wine Advocate – 98 points ​
  • Decanter – 97 points ​

Food Pairing

This wine pairs exquisitely with roasted lamb, grilled beef tenderloin, or duck breast with a berry reduction. The wine's depth and character are highlighted when accompanied by earthy mushroom risotto or aged hard cheeses, creating an unforgettable dining experience.

title: Chateau Cheval Blanc 2003
bodyHtml:
There are places in the world which are made exceptional by history and chance. Cheval Blanc is one example. In the 18th century a large area of the current estate of Cheval Blanc was covered in vines. This can be seen on a map drawn up by Bellayme in 1764. one century later, a period of slow renovation began. In 1871, adjacent plots were acquired, giving the vineyard its definitive layout. drainage system and planting of the cabaret franc grape variety.

96 Points - Wine Spectator

Blackberry, mineral and lightly toasted oak. Subtle and complex. Full-bodied, with wonderfully sweet fruit character and ultrarefined tannins. Goes on and on. Gorgeous and seductive. 

93 Points - Wine Enthusiast

92 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

title: Chateau Mouton Rothschild 1982
bodyHtml:
Château Mouton Rothschild, located in the Pauillac appellation of Bordeaux, France, is renowned for producing some of the world's most exceptional wines. The 1982 vintage, in particular, stands out as one of the estate’s most celebrated offerings, earning perfect scores from esteemed critics and captivating wine enthusiasts globally.

Wine Description
The 1982 Mouton Rothschild displays a deep, rich ruby color with minimal signs of aging. The nose is profoundly aromatic, exuding notes of crème de cassis, lead pencil shavings, sweet tobacco, and subtle floral hints. On the palate, it offers full-bodied richness, a multidimensional and layered texture, and a long, resonant finish. This vintage is a blend of 85% Cabernet Sauvignon, 8% Cabernet Franc, and 7% Merlot. Despite its age, it remains remarkably youthful and is expected to continue evolving gracefully over the next few decades.

Accolades

  • Robert Parker’s Wine Advocate: 100 points
  • Jeb Dunnuck: 100 points
  • James Suckling: 100 points
  • Vinous: 99 points
  • Decanter: 98 points

Food Pairing
This wine pairs exquisitely with:

  • Herb-crusted rack of lamb
  • Grilled ribeye steak
  • Wild mushroom risotto
  • Aged hard cheeses like Comté or Manchego

These pairings enhance the wine’s depth and complexity, creating an unforgettable dining experience.

Vintage Quality
The 1982 vintage in Bordeaux is often hailed as one of the greatest of the 20th century, characterized by ideal weather conditions that led to wines of exceptional structure and longevity. Château Mouton Rothschild’s meticulous vineyard management and winemaking expertise are evident in this remarkable wine.

Rarity and Availability
Acquiring a bottle of the 1982 Château Mouton Rothschild is an immense challenge due to several factors:

  • Age and Limited Supply: Being over four decades old, the number of well-preserved bottles has significantly diminished over time.
  • High Demand: Its legendary status among collectors and connoisseurs has led to increased demand, further reducing availability.
  • Auction Presence: While occasionally appearing in prestigious auctions, bottles often command exceptionally high prices, reflecting their scarcity.
  • Retail Scarcity: Specialized retailers may have limited stock, but availability is sporadic and often subject to strict provenance verification.

Given these factors, obtaining a bottle requires diligence, timing, and a willingness to invest significantly, underscoring its status as a coveted gem in the wine world.

title: Chateau Latour Premier Grand Cru Classe 2001
bodyHtml:
Produced in France, specifically at the southern edge of the Pauillac appellation in the Médoc, this wine is the Grand Vin of the legendary Château Latour. Rated as a First Growth in the 1855 Bordeaux Classification, the estate's history dates back to 1331, with its modern reputation forged under the Ségur family in the 18th century. Currently owned by François Pinault through Groupe Artémis, the winery follows a philosophy of extreme precision, and the 2001 vintage holds particular significance as the first wine produced in the estate's then-new, state-of-the-art cellar facility.

Wine Description

This 2001 vintage presents a saturated ruby-purple colour that remains deep and virile even with age. The nose is highly expressive and complex, unfurling with aromas of crème de cassis, blackberry, and dried orange peel, layered with classic notes of graphite, cedar, and earthy truffles. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied and impeccably balanced, showcasing a refined structure with fine yet rigid tannins and crisp acidity. Stylistically, it is celebrated for its elegance and controlled power, moving away from the 'blockbuster' style of 2000 toward a more racy and aromatic profile. The final blend consists of 79% Cabernet Sauvignon, 18% Merlot, 2% Petit Verdot, and 1% Cabernet Franc. It has gracefully entered its plateau of maturity and is expected to drink beautifully through 2052.

Accolades

  • Jeb Dunnuck - 96 points

  • Vinous - 96 points

  • Wine Spectator - 95 points

  • Wine Advocate - 95 points

  • Decanter - 97 points

title: Chateau Haut Brion 1999
bodyHtml:
Wine Description
The 1999 Château Haut Brion exhibits a medium garnet colour with slight bricking, reflective of its maturity. The nose reveals inviting aromas of redcurrant, plum, cedar, and earthy undertones, complemented by hints of tobacco, graphite, and leather. Typically composed of around 52% Merlot, 39% Cabernet Sauvignon, and 9% Cabernet Franc, the palate is graceful and well-balanced, delivering supple red fruit, fine-grained tannins, and notes of spice and savoury herbs. Medium-bodied with a silky texture, the finish is long and refined, offering an elegant expression of a cooler, classic vintage. Best enjoyed now through the next few years.

Food Pairing
A delightful match for roast duck, herb-crusted pork loin, or mushroom risotto. Together, they create an unforgettable dining experience.

Vintage Quality
The 1999 vintage in Bordeaux was marked by a cool, wet growing season, requiring careful vineyard management and selective harvesting. Despite the challenges, Château Haut Brion produced a wine of notable charm and finesse, showcasing the estate's commitment to quality even in less favourable years.

title: Chateau Margaux 2005
bodyHtml:
Introduction

Château Margaux 2005 is a legendary red wine from France, produced in the Margaux appellation of the Médoc region in Bordeaux. This historic estate is one of only five wines to achieve First Growth (Premier Cru) status in the 1855 Classification of Bordeaux. Since 1977, the château has been owned by the Mentzelopoulos family, whose significant investments in the vineyards and cellars restored the property to the pinnacle of quality and prestige.

Description

The 2005 vintage is considered a modern masterpiece, characterized by extraordinary concentration and a classic structure.

  • Colour: It possesses a deep, opaque purple hue that remains vibrant despite its age.

  • Aroma: The nose is complex and hauntingly fragrant, featuring a signature bouquet of violets, spring flowers, and crushed blackcurrants interwoven with notes of liquorice, graphite, and toasted oak.

  • Palate: On the palate, the wine is rich and multifaceted, offering intense flavours of black fruits, red berries, and forest floor, complemented by subtle nuances of truffle and cedar.

  • Body: It is full bodied yet remarkably graceful, supported by a massive spine of fine, silky tannins and a vibrant acidity that provides perfect balance.

  • Finish: The finish is exceptionally long, pure, and majestic, lingering for over a minute with echoing notes of fruit and spice.

  • ABV: This wine is bottled at 13% alcohol by volume.

Accolades

  • Robert Parker's Wine Advocate - 98 points

  • Wine Spectator - 100 points

  • Vinous - 98 points

  • Decanter - 99 points

  • James Suckling - 100 points

title: Chateau Haut Brion 2004
bodyHtml:
Wonderful aromas of dried flowers, currant, berries and mineral. Full-bodied, yet reserved and refined. Lovely texture, with a pure silk feel. Seamless and beautiful. Great length. Even better than from barrel. Best after 2012.

96 Points - Wine Enthusiast

Of the pair of châteaux, La Mission Haut-Brion and Haut-Brion (both owned by the Dillon banking family) that face each other across the crowded streets of Pessac, Haut-Brion is the one with the structure, the darkness, the brooding character. This is so true of 2004, with its hugely firm structure underlying the initial supple fruit. At the end, the acidity is an enticing surprise, lifting the aftertaste.

95 Points - Wine Spectator

Wonderful aromas of dried flowers, currant, berries and mineral. Full-bodied, yet reserved and refined. Lovely texture, with a pure silk feel. Seamless and beautiful. Great length. Even better than from barrel. Best after 2012.

92 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Medium to deep garnet colour. The nose is still a little mute giving a moderate intensity of youthful aromas: ripe plums, cassis, Chinese five spice, moss and a fair amount of cedar. Oak tannins seem to dominate the structure contributing to the taut astringency of the palate yet there is a good amount of ripe berry and earthy fruit plus medium acidity to balance. Long earthy finish. Drink 2012 to 2034.

title: Chateau Margaux 2007
bodyHtml:
Produced in the prestigious Margaux appellation of Bordeaux, France, this first growth ('Premier Cru Classé') represents centuries of winemaking excellence. Originally discovered in the 12th century, the estate was purchased by André Mentzelopoulos in 1977 and is currently managed by his daughter, Corinne Mentzelopoulos. The winery's philosophy focuses on a rigorous selection process and a commitment to expressing the unique, elegant character of its historic terroir.

Wine Description

Chateau Margaux 2007 presents a bright, dark red to ruby colour in the glass. The bouquet is complex and aristocratic, featuring a fragrant blend of blackberry, redcurrant, and sweet cherry, accented by notes of spring flowers, incense, iris, and subtle tobacco. On the palate, the wine is suave and seamless with a light to medium body, offering vibrant flavours of cassis and black cherry supported by incredibly fine, noble tannins and fresh acidity. The finish is long and sweet with a characteristic menthol grip. This blend typically consists of 87% Cabernet Sauvignon, 11% Merlot, and 2% Cabernet Franc. While approachable now with decanting, its sophisticated structure suggests an optimal drinking window extending through 2043.

Accolades

  • Decanter - 95 points

  • Wine Enthusiast - 93 points

  • Vinous - 93 points

  • Wine Advocate - 92 points

  • James Suckling - 92 points

title: Chateau Cos d'Estournel 1982
bodyHtml:
Situated in the Saint-Estèphe appellation of the Médoc, France, Chateau Cos d'Estournel is a prestigious Second Grand Cru Classé estate famously known as a 'Super Second'. Founded in 1811 by Louis Gaspard d'Estournel, often called the 'Maharajah of Saint-Estèphe' due to his fascination with India, the estate is renowned for its unique Oriental-inspired architecture featuring Chinese pagodas. The winemaking philosophy emphasizes precision and innovation, having pioneered the use of a 100% gravity-fed winery to ensure the gentlest possible handling of the fruit.

Wine Description

The 1982 vintage is a monumental expression of Cos d'Estournel, presenting a deep ruby-purple hue that remains remarkably saturated despite its age. The sensory profile is opulent and complex, with a stunning bouquet of cassis, black cherries, and plums layered with scents of licorice, roasted chestnuts, aniseed, and a hint of truffle. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied, fleshy, and unctuous, revealing concentrated dark fruit flavours interwoven with notes of cedar, spice box, and lead pencil. It is characterized by its exceptional balance, seamless acidity, and sweet, powdery tannins that provide a silken texture and a very persistent, stylish finish. This blend of 60% Cabernet Sauvignon and 40% Merlot has reached full maturity but possesses the depth to hold well in a cold cellar for another decade or more.

Accolades

  • Jeb Dunnuck - 97 points

  • Robert Parker's Wine Advocate - 96 points

  • Decanter - 96 points

  • Vinous (Neal Martin) - 95 points

  • Wine Spectator - 95 points

title: Chateau Margaux 1998
bodyHtml:
Hailing from the historic Margaux appellation in Bordeaux, France, this first growth ('Premier Cru Classé') is a quintessential expression of its unique gravelly terroir. Since the late 1970s, the estate has flourished under the ownership of the Mentzelopoulos family, with Corinne Mentzelopoulos continuing her father André's legacy of meticulous quality control and innovation. The winery's philosophy is rooted in a five-hundred-year tradition of craftsmanship, emphasizing finesse and complexity above all else.

Wine Description

In the glass, the 1998 vintage displays a dense ruby-purple colour, now evolving into a mature garnet with slight amber tones at the rim. The bouquet is remarkably fresh and complex, offering primary red berry fruit and blackcurrant alongside secondary notes of vanilla, roasted coffee beans, and dried rose petals. On the palate, the wine is powerful yet elegant, featuring a medium body with firm, 'fat' tannins that have become polished and silky over time. Flavours of black cherry, cassis, and spice are complemented by subtle undercurrents of cedar, tobacco, and forest floor. This blend consists of 75% Cabernet Sauvignon, 20% Merlot, 3% Petit Verdot, and 2% Cabernet Franc. Now at peak maturity, it offers a sophisticated drinking window that remains open through 2035-2040.

Accolades

  • Wine & Spirits - 96 points

  • Decanter - 95 points

  • Wine Advocate - 91 points

  • Wine Spectator - 91 points

title: Chateau Mouton Rothschild 1986
bodyHtml:
Produced in France, this legendary Premier Cru hails from the Pauillac appellation within the Médoc region of Bordeaux. Château Mouton Rothschild is one of only two estates to have remained in the same family since 1855, and it famously became the only property to ever be elevated to First Growth status, a feat achieved in 1973 after decades of lobbying by Baron Philippe de Rothschild. The winery’s philosophy is a marriage of art and agriculture, characterized by its tradition of commissioning world-renowned artists—such as Bernard Séjourné for the 1986 vintage—to design its unique annual labels.

Wine Description

The 1986 vintage is a monumental wine, displaying an exceptionally deep, opaque ruby colour that remains remarkably youthful even after decades. The powerful and complex nose reveals a 'symphony' of graphite, cedar, and crème de cassis, layered with notes of black truffle, mint, and toasted oak. On the palate, it is massive and full bodied, offering intense concentration and a firm, masculine structure characterized by tightly knit tannins and vibrant acidity. This blend of 80% Cabernet Sauvignon, 10% Merlot, 8% Cabernet Franc, and 2% Petit Verdot spent 20 months in 100% new oak. A true vin de garde, this wine is currently in a 'legendary' drinking spot but has the potential to age for 50 to 100 years.

Accolades

  • Wine Advocate - 100 points

  • James Suckling - 100 points

  • Decanter - 100 points

  • Jeb Dunnuck - 100 points

  • Wine Spectator - 99 points

title: Chateau Lafite Rothschild 2006
bodyHtml:
Introduction

Produced in the prestigious Pauillac appellation of Bordeaux, France, Chateau Lafite Rothschild 2006 is a First Growth icon of viticultural history. Owned by the Rothschild family since 1868, the estate is defined by a winemaking philosophy that prioritizes elegance and finesse over raw power. The vineyard's unique terroir, characterized by deep gravel beds on limestone subsoil, allows for the production of grapes with extraordinary complexity and aging potential.

Wine Description

In the glass, the 2006 vintage displays a deep, dark ruby and purple hue. The aromatic profile is classic and sophisticated, offering a bouquet of graphite, cedar, and crème de cacao interwoven with intense notes of blackcurrant and black cherries. On the palate, the wine is medium to full bodied, characterized by a dense, concentrated core and a remarkably silky texture. It showcases a harmonious balance between its fresh acidity and firm, well integrated tannins, leading into a long and persistent finish. This blend consists primarily of 82% Cabernet Sauvignon, 16% Merlot, and 2% Cabernet Franc. While it began entering its drinking window around 2016, it is structured to evolve beautifully through 2040 and beyond.

Accolades

  • Wine Advocate - 97 points

  • Vinous - 96 points

  • Wine Spectator - 95 points

  • Decanter - 95 points

title: Chateau Leoville Las Cases 1998
bodyHtml:
Introduction

Produced in the prestigious Saint Julien appellation of Bordeaux, France, this wine is a benchmark of the Medoc. Chateau Leoville Las Cases was once part of the massive Leoville estate and has been owned by the Delon family since the late 19th century, with Jean Hubert Delon currently at the helm. Their winemaking philosophy centers on rigorous selection and a commitment to producing wines with immense structure and longevity, often referred to as having the 'soul of a First Growth'.

Wine Description

This 1998 vintage displays a deep, dark ruby colour with slight bricking at the rim. The aromatic profile is complex and evolving, featuring notes of blackcurrant, cedar, graphite, and tobacco leaf, complemented by subtle hints of spice and forest floor. On the palate, the wine is full bodied and powerful, showing great concentration of fruit balanced by firm, well integrated tannins and a fresh acidity. The varietal composition is a classic blend dominated by Cabernet Sauvignon, with smaller portions of Merlot and Cabernet Franc. Now nearly three decades old, this wine is within its optimal drinking window, showing beautiful maturity while retaining enough structure to last several more years.

Accolades

  • Wine Advocate - 93 points

  • Wine Spectator - 95 points

  • Vinous - 91 points

title: Chateau Latour Premier Grand Cru Classe 2009
bodyHtml:
Produced in France, specifically within the southern edge of the prestigious Pauillac appellation in the Médoc, this wine is the Grand Vin of the legendary Château Latour. The estate's history dates back to the 14th century, though its world-renowned vineyards were fully established in the 17th century. Currently owned by French billionaire François Pinault of Groupe Artémis, the winery is managed by Frédéric Engerer, who oversees a philosophy focused on precision, longevity, and a deep respect for the unique gravelly terroir of the central 'L’Enclos' vineyard.

Wine Description

The 2009 vintage exhibits an inky, deep garnet color and possesses extraordinary aromatic intensity. The nose offers a flamboyant symphony of bold blackcurrants, black cherries, and warm plums, interwoven with nuances of cedar chest, graphite, aniseed, and earthy truffles. On the full-bodied palate, the wine is concentrated and powerful, featuring a rock-solid frame of super-ripe, grainy tannins and fantastic freshness. Stylistically, it is celebrated for its 'skyscraper-like' texture and a remarkably long, mineral-driven finish that can last over a minute. Composed of 91.3% Cabernet Sauvignon and 8.7% Merlot, this monumental wine has a vast optimal drinking window between 2024 and 2080.

Accolades

  • Robert Parker's Wine Advocate - 100 points

  • James Suckling - 100 points

  • Wine Spectator - 99 points

  • Wine Enthusiast - 99 points

  • Decanter - 99 points

  • Vinous (Neal Martin) - 99 points

title: Gaja Barbaresco 2000 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
Gaja Barbaresco 2000 is an iconic red wine from the Piedmont region of Italy, crafted by the legendary Angelo Gaja. Angelo Gaja is widely credited with modernizing Italian viticulture, being among the first in the region to introduce single-vineyard bottlings and French oak barriques. This flagship DOCG wine is produced from 100% Nebbiolo grapes sourced from fourteen different estate vineyards located in the communes of Barbaresco and Treiso. The winemaking philosophy emphasizes a meticulous "parcel-by-parcel" approach to faithfully express the unique limestone-rich terroir of the Langhe district.

Wine Description

This vintage possesses a deep garnet-red colour with early amber edges at the rim. The nose is expansive and complex, unravelling layers of dried cherries, plums, and raspberries, intertwined with notes of liquorice, cloves, tobacco, and cedar. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied and powerful yet remarkably refined, featuring ultra-fine, integrated tannins and a racy acidity that provides a long, mineral-inflected finish. Stylistically, it balances a lush, ripe fruit profile with traditional savory elements of tar, smoke, and underbrush. The maturation process involved 24 months in barriques followed by 12 months in large Slavonian oak casks. While drinking beautifully now, it has a long life ahead, with an optimal drinking window extending toward 2030 and beyond.

Accolades

  • Wine Spectator – 95 points

  • Robert Parker, Wine Advocate – 92 points

  • James Suckling – 95 points

title: Krug Brut Grande Cuvee 172 Edition
bodyHtml:
Founded in 1843 in Reims, the House of Krug has remained a benchmark in prestige Champagne through six generations of the Krug family. Known for its uncompromising commitment to quality, Krug creates wines that transcend the limitations of individual vintages, with Grande Cuvée being its ultimate expression.

This 172ème Édition is composed of 146 wines from 11 different years, with the youngest from 2016 and the oldest dating back to 1998. The blend consists of 44% Pinot Noir, 36% Chardonnay, and 20% Meunier. In the glass, it reveals a brilliant golden hue with fine, persistent bubbles. Aromas of white flowers, citrus peel, marzipan, and lightly toasted brioche rise elegantly. On the palate, the wine is layered and expressive, offering flavours of hazelnut, nougat, apple tart, and subtle spices, supported by vibrant acidity and a long, silky finish. This cuvée is both powerful and refined, showcasing remarkable balance and complexity.

Accolades
Wine Enthusiast – 98 points.
James Suckling – 97 points.
Decanter – 97 points.

Food Pairing
Ideal with lobster in butter sauce, seared scallops, or aged parmesan, this Champagne elevates both refined dishes and simple pleasures. A perfect match to enhance the wine's complexity.

title: Another Hendrick's Gin
bodyHtml:
Another Hendrick's (stylized as Another Hendrick's) is a groundbreaking release from the Hendrick's Gin Palace in Girvan, Scotland. Launched in early 2026, it holds the distinction of being the first new permanent addition to the core Hendrick's lineup in nearly a decade. Master Distiller Lesley Gracie designed this expression to showcase a different, more "gourmet" side of the brand's personality, marking a significant departure from their usual focus on temporary "Cabinet of Curiosities" releases.

Spirit Description

This gin retains the legendary house signature of rose and cucumber but introduces a bold, idiosyncratic pairing of orange blossom and cacao bean. It is immediately recognizable by its striking, all-white apothecary bottle, contrasting with the classic dark glass.

  • Aroma: Vibrant juniper and bright citrus lift from the orange blossom, with a subtle, earthy depth.

  • Palate: The mouthfeel is velvety and rounded. Rich, decadent notes of cacao provide a soft "pull" that balances the floral brightness of the orange blossom and the cooling essence of cucumber.

  • Finish: Smooth and persistent, with a delicate hint of sweetness and a clean citrus exit.

  • ABV: 41.4% (Standard)

Serve Suggestion: The Another Hendrick's Spritz

To showcase its bright profile, the distillery recommends a Spritz: 50ml Another Hendrick's, 50ml Apple Juice, topped with Prosecco and Soda. Garnish with a cucumber slice and a lemon twist.

title: Mazzei Concerto di Fonterutoli Toscana 2020
bodyHtml:
This concentrated and 'beguiling' red wine originates from Italy, within the Tuscany region and the Toscana I.G.P. designation. Produced at the historic Castello di Fonterutoli, the Mazzei family has been making wine for 24 generations since 1435. Concerto, first released in 1981, was a pioneer of the 'Super Tuscan' movement, blending traditional Sangiovese with international Cabernet Sauvignon. The winery's philosophy emphasizes sustainable agriculture and the promotion of local varieties as an expression of regional identity, utilizing a modern underground cellar that respects the delicate hydro-geologic balance of the estate.

Wine Description

The 2020 Concerto presents a bright and punchy appearance with great 'terrific freshness'. The sensory profile is highly aromatic, featuring a nose of currants, flowers, and spices, layered with notes of plum, pomegranate, new leather, and blood orange. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied yet 'crunchy and juicy', showcasing crushed blackberries and raspberries underpinned by citrusy acidity and polished tannins. It is characterized by a savory quality and a 'slate texture' that provides a robust yet nuanced drinking experience. This blend consists of 80% Sangiovese and 20% Cabernet Sauvignon, typically reaching an ABV of 14.5%. The wine was aged for 18 months the Cabernet in small French oak barrels and the Sangiovese in tonneaux followed by three months in concrete tanks to reduce oak impact and preserve fruit purity. While Mazzei practices sustainable and respectful viticulture, this specific bottling is not certified organic.

title: Tenuta Belguardo 2019
bodyHtml:
This concentrated and 'seducing' red wine originates from Italy, specifically from the Maremma Toscana subregion in the southern part of Tuscany. Purchased by the Marchesi Mazzei family in the 1990s, Tenuta Belguardo is situated in the hills between Grosseto and Montiano, near the Tyrrhenian Sea. The Mazzei family, a historic dynasty producing wine since 1435, selected this estate for its stony, calcareous soil and Mediterranean climate, which they believe is the 'new frontier' for high-quality viticulture. Their winemaking philosophy focuses on enhancing natural terroir through customized organic practices and biodiversity preservation.

Wine Description

The 2019 Tenuta Belguardo (the estate's flagship Rosso I.G.T.) presents a dark ruby colour with intense violet reflections. The sensory profile is remarkably complex and multi-layered, featuring a nose of overripe blackberries, raspberry jam, and eucalyptus, underpinned by exotic notes and damp forest soil. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied and 'enveloping', showcasing a core of blackcurrant, plum, and herbal spices with a distinct touch of graphite. It is characterized by fine-grained, ripe tannins and a fresh, mineral finish that adds depth without being dominated by its oak maturation. This blend consists of 85% Cabernet Sauvignon and 15% Cabernet Franc, typically reaching an alcohol content (ABV) of 13.5% to 14%. The wine was matured for 18 months in small French oak barrels (70% new) and finished for 4 months in concrete tanks.

title: Ricasoli Lutelia Chardonnay 2024
bodyHtml:
This sophisticated white wine originates from Italy, within the Tuscany region and the Toscana I.G.T. designation. It is produced by Barone Ricasoli, one of the oldest and most historically significant wineries in Italy, with a lineage dating back to 1141. The Ricasoli family is legendary for defining the original formula for Chianti, but they also apply their centuries of expertise to international varietals like Chardonnay. The Lutelia vineyard is situated on well-drained sandstone and rocky soils (Macigno del Chianti) at high elevations of 400 to 500 metres, which foster complexity and structured acidity.

Wine Description

Lutelia Chardonnay presents a stylish and Burgundian-inspired profile with great structural balance. The sensory profile features a smoky and toasty nose with bright hints of lemon, apricot, and chestnut. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied and "leesy," showcasing well-crafted fruit and a satisfying texture that balances sweetness with a refreshing sourness. It is characterized by nuanced notes of dried fig and maple syrup, leading to a savory, salty finish that some critics liken to the complexity found in Sherry or Sauternes. This 100% Chardonnay reached an alcohol content (ABV) of 12.5%. While Ricasoli emphasizes sustainable research into vineyard microclimates and parcel-based vinification, this bottling is not officially certified organic.

title: King Maui Sauvignon Blanc 2025
bodyHtml:
This tropical and refreshing white wine originates from New Zealand, within the world-renowned Marlborough region. The King Maui label belongs to the Tiki Wine & Vineyards portfolio, a family-owned producer based in North Canterbury that manages vineyards across some of New Zealand's premier winegrowing areas. The winery's philosophy centres on producing 'spirited' wines with effortless appeal that celebrate the vibrant and expressive character of the Marlborough terroir.

Wine Description

King Maui Sauvignon Blanc presents a brilliant appearance characteristic of Marlborough white wines. The sensory profile features an intensely aromatic nose of passionfruit, grapefruit, and rockmelon, layered with subtle herbaceous notes of fresh-cut grass and green bell peppers. On the palate, the wine is 'bright and fresh', showcasing pristine fruit flavours of dried mangoes, dried pineapple, and Meyer lemon lifted by a crisp, lively acidity. It is characterized by a fine texture and a 'crunchy' energy that leads to a persistent, mouthwatering finish. This 100% Sauvignon Blanc was fermented to preserve its primary fruit energy and typically reaches an ABV of approximately 13%. While the producer emphasizes environmental stewardship, this specific bottling is not certified organic.

title: Wild Life White Grapefruit Gin
bodyHtml:
Wild Life White Grapefruit Gin originates from the mountain town of Canmore, Alberta, in the heart of the Canadian Rockies. Founded in 2017 by Keith Robinson and Matt Widmer, Wild Life Distillery is an artisanal producer that focuses on the 'mountain lifestyle' by using Rocky Mountain water and Alberta prairie grains. The distillery is known for its craftsmanship and deep connection to the local landscape, often incorporating regional ingredients into its small batch spirits.

Spirit Description

This seasonal expression is crafted by infusing ripe white grapefruit and delicate makrut lime leaf into the distillery's flagship Classic Gin. It presents a crystal clear appearance and a medium, zesty body. The aroma is highly aromatic, leading with bright citrus oils and a floral, herbal lift from the lime leaf. On the palate, it delivers a refreshing and juicy tartness where the tangy grapefruit profile mingles with traditional juniper and subtle spice. The finish is clean and crisp, leaving a lingering citrus zest and a hint of Mediterranean herbs. It is bottled at 40% ABV.

Food Pairing

The vibrant acidity and bright citrus notes of this grapefruit gin make it an ideal partner for light, fresh fare. It pairs exceptionally well with seafood dishes such as scallop ceviche, grilled shrimp with lime, or a citrus-marinated white fish. The gin's zesty profile also complements fresh summer salads featuring arugula, goat cheese, and a grapefruit vinaigrette. For a unique dessert option, consider serving it alongside a lemon tart or a refreshing pomelo sorbet, which echo the spirit's citrus-forward character.

title: Sine Qua Non - The Third Twin 'Nuestra Senora del Tercer Gemelo' 2019
bodyHtml:
97+ Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2019 Nuestra Senora Del Tercer Gemelo, entirely from The Third Twin estate vineyard, is composed of 33% Grenache, 23.5% Syrah, 19% Mourvèdre, 19% Petite Sirah, 4% Graciano and 1.5% Muskat. "I love Muskat in red wines, even better than Viognier," Manfred Krankl enthuses, and I have to agree—this barrel sample offers tremendous aromatic purity and complexity, as if the volume has been turned up and the camera has been focused. It boasts continually shifting, layered aromatics as it spends several hours in the glass: blueberry and blackberry jam, tar, coffee beans, thyme and botanicals, plus loads of floral nuances. Full-bodied yet light on its feet, its concentrated fruits are framed by abundant, super-fine tannins and seamless acidity, and it has a hauntingly long finish. It was made with 19% whole clusters, and matured about 33 months in 13% new French oak, with a large portion of the wine moved to cement tanks after about a year and a half in barrel. 

98+ Points - Jeb Dunnuck

The 2019 Nuestra Senora Del Tercer Gemelo comes from the Third Twin estate vineyard, which was purchased in 2000. At that time, the vineyard covered 14.33 acres planted to Syrah and Petite Sirah, and the Krankls planted a mix of different varieties starting in 2011. Today, the estate covers just over 35 acres, and this is a cooler, sandy terroir. The wine sports a deep purple hue as well as a monster bouquet of blackberries, Italian leather, dried herbs, smoke tobacco, and pepper. Full-bodied on the palate, it's another seamless, perfectly balanced red from this team that somehow manages to bring incredible richness and power while staying flawlessly balanced and elegance. A blend of 33% Grenache, 23.5% Syrah, 19% each of Mourvèdre and Petite Sirah, and the rest Graciano and Muscat, fermented with 19% whole clusters, it shows the more elegant, refined, silky style of this terroir beautifully. I like it today, but smart money will give bottles 2-4 years in the cellar. It should have 15-20 years of overall longevity.

97 Points - Vinous

The 2019 Nuestra Senora del Tercer Gemelo is the fourth vintage from estate vineyard in Los Alamos. Bright and punchy in the glass for such a big wine, the 2019 is so expressive today. Sandy soils lend aromatic presence to play off all that natural intensity. Rose petal, mint, lavender, sage and blood orange perk up a core of bright red/purplish berry fruit as this opulent, full-throttle Syrah-based blend shows off its allure.

title: Chateau Latour Premier Grand Cru Classe 2011
bodyHtml:
In the glass, the crimson color of the wine is deep and intense. The nose is elegant, combining both floral and fruity notes. In the mouth, the wine reveals a suave and fleshy texture, yet remains delicate with much promise. The finale is powerful and complex. An incredibly lengthy and structured Chateau Latour.

Blend : 84.5% Cabernet Sauvignon, 15% Merlot, 0.5% Petit Verdot

97 Points - Wine Enthusiast

Big tannins and impressive fruits are the hallmarks of this impressive wine. It is also subtle, not showing all its flavors at once, hiding beneath tannins and structure. For this fruity vintage, it shows a strong sense of direct, solid structure, only allowing the strong black plum and berry flavors to come through slowly. Cellar Selection

96 Points - Wine Spectator

This has a gorgeous core of steeped plum, boysenberry and black currant coulis flavors, backed by a prominent graphite note that drives through the lengthy finish, where extra hints of anise and sweet tobacco flitter in the background. Regal. Best from 2018 through 2035.

95 Points - James Suckling

The nose is complex, featuring smoke, meat and hints of wood, with currants, olives and berries underneath. Full body with super-velvety tannins. The strong acidity gives the wine an edginess. Love the spicy, subtly fruity finish. 

93+ Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

A blend of 84.5% Cabernet Sauvignon, 15% Merlot and 0.5% Petit Verdot, the 2011 Latour represents only 34% of the crop. It hit 13.1% natural alcohol. One of the vintage's most compelling wines, it possesses a dense ruby/purple color as well as a sweet, open-knit personality with ripe tannin, superb intensity, good purity and harmony, a medium to full-bodied mouthfeel, and lots of crushed rock, floral and black as well as blue fruit notes in addition to hints of ink and forest floor. This beautifully rich, savory Latour will be surprisingly drinkable in 4-5 years, and should age easily for two decades or more.

title: Sine Qua Non The Third Twin 'Nuestra Senora del Tercer Gemelo' 2020
bodyHtml:
The 2020 Nuestra Senora del Tercer Gemelo is a single-vineyard wine from The Third Twin estate vineyard, based around soils of pure sand. It's composed of 54% Mourvedre, 22% Grenache, 11% Syrah, 9.3% Petite Sirah, 3% Graciano, and 0.7% Viognier. It was made using 30% whole clusters and aged about 31 months in French oak barrels, 33% new. Very deep garnet-black in color, it charges out with savory notes of black truffles, black olives, and chargrill, giving way to a core of plum preserves, dried mulberries, lavender, crushed rocks, and cracked black pepper.

The full-bodied palate is pure seduction, chock full of rich black fruit preserves flavors and a fantastic array of savory and earth accents, supported by firm grainy tannins and bold freshness, finishing long and minerally. What a stunning expression of this vineyard! It was bottled in April 2023. 425 cases were made.

98 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

97 Points - Vinous

title: Les Griffons De Pichon Baron 2022
bodyHtml:
France’s Bordeaux region is home to some of the world’s most esteemed wineries, and Château Pichon Baron, located in the Pauillac appellation on the Left Bank, is a leading example. This estate, part of the AXA Millésimes portfolio since 1987, is known for producing age-worthy wines from its historic vineyards adjacent to Château Latour. Les Griffons de Pichon Baron is the château’s second wine, created to reflect a more immediate expression of the estate’s terroir while maintaining the depth and character of Pauillac.

Wine Description
Les Griffons De Pichon Baron 2022 displays a deep, radiant garnet hue. On the nose, it offers layered aromas of cassis, black cherry, and ripe plum, underpinned by graphite, violets, and a touch of cedar. The palate is medium to full-bodied, revealing a structured yet refined texture, with fine-grained tannins and a vibrant core of dark fruit. Notes of tobacco, licorice, and cocoa unfold alongside the fruit, delivering complexity and elegance.

Food Pairing
This wine pairs beautifully with herb-crusted lamb, grilled ribeye, or portobello mushroom risotto. Its depth and tannic structure also stand up well to aged cheeses like Comté or Manchego. This pairing highlights the wine’s depth and character.

title: Chateau Haut Brion 2020
bodyHtml:
99+ Points - James Suckling

This is a superb Haut-Brion with incredible tannins that are wonderfully fine-grained. It’s really powerful. This is very primary with so much grape-generated tannin structure. Very, very long, going on for minutes. Seductive and friendly at the start and then takes you on at the finish with so much structure. Wine of the vintage? 

98+ Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2020 Haut-Brion is a blend of 42.8% Merlot, 39.7% Cabernet Sauvignon and 17.5% Cabernet Franc, harvested from 7th to 29th September, with an estimated alcohol of 15% and a pH of 3.8. Opaque purple-black colored, it leaps from the glass with a first wave of vibrant black raspberries, ripe blackberries and mulberries scents, followed by a powerful core of warm cassis, dark chocolate and violets, before bursting into an array of crushed rocks, iron ore, tree bark and black truffles notes. The concentrated, densely packed, full-bodied palate is not in the least bit heavy, delivering a refreshing backbone of red berry and dried herbs suggestions, framed by seamless acidity and very finely grained tannins, finishing on an epically long, fragrant earth note. Simply stunning.

98+ Points - Jeb Dunnuck

Unquestionably one of the top wines in this impressive vintage, the 2020 Chateau Haut-Brion checks in as 42.8% Merlot, 39.7% Cabernet Sauvignon, and the balance Cabernet Franc, all of which will spend 15-18 months in 77% new French oak. Its deep purple color is followed by a thrilling nose of mineral-laced blackcurrants, black raspberries, toast, spice, scorched earth, and graphite. Possessing an almost Lafite-like elegance on the palate, it nevertheless has huge dry extract, full-bodied richness, flawless balance, and beautiful tannins. Per the spec sheet, the alcohol is an estimated 15% with a pH of 3.78, so it’s no shrinking violet, yet it never shows a hint of headiness or being over the top. I finished my note with “Where can I buy some?” I suspect this wine will require a solid decade to hit the early stages of maturity and will be a 30-, 40-, or possibly a 50-year wine.

96 Points - Decanter

Concentrated, powerful and precise; this takes a grip and holds on, layers of licorice, grilled coffee bean, chocolate, blackcurrant pastille, cassis bud and a more steely wet stone edge that gives a much needed balance to the richness of the overall feel of this wine. Gunsmoke curls out of the glass after half an hour - this is going to need serious ageing, impressive and powerful stuff.

title: Chateau Mouton Rothschild 2015
bodyHtml:
99 Points - James Suckling     Decadent and rich aromas of black cherries and plums with wet earth and sandalwood. Turns to dried mushrooms. Full-bodied, tight and closed with big, polished tannins, yet this is very closed and shy right now. Despite this, underneath it shows such depth and beauty. Tangy acidity. This is a combination of 2005 and 2009. Try it in 2024.

99 Points - Jeb Dunnuck     The crème de la crème from the northern Médoc is the 2015 Mouton Rothschild and this incredible wine flirts with perfection. Made from 82% Cabernet Sauvignon, 16% Merlot, and 3% Petit Verdot, this inky purple-coloured effort offers sensational Cabernet flare in its crème de cassis, graphite, lead pencil shavings, floral, and Asian spice aromas and flavors. It is full-bodied, dense, and incredibly concentrated, yet still has the sexy, opulent, seductive style of the vintage front and centre. It will be a candidate for perfection in 10-12 years and is going to be one of the longest-lived wines in the vintage. Hats off to Philippe Dhalluim and his team for this incredible effort that’s a step up over just about every other northern Médoc out there!

98 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate     The 2015 Mouton Rothschild is a blend of 82% Cabernet Sauvignon, 16% Merlot and 2% Cabernet Franc aged in 100% new oak with a mid-July 2017 bottling. Deep garnet-purple coloured, this Mouton pulls off an incredibly impactful entrance, emerging from the glass with profound notes of blackberry preserves, plum pudding, crème de cassis and grilled meats, featuring perfectly accessorized accents of sandalwood, cinnamon stick and fenugreek with wafts of dried roses, unsmoked cigars and tilled soil. Medium to full-bodied, the palate is completely packed with rich, ripe black fruits sparked with blue and red fruit undertones and an incredible structure of very firm, very ripe tannins, with seamless freshness and an epically long, earth-laced finish. Possessing striking natural beauty framed by impeccable crafting, this 2015 is a total diva and well worth attention. Give it a good 7-8 years in bottle, at least, and drink it over the next 30+ years.

98 Points - Decanter     My joint top wine (with Ch Margaux) of the vintage. A real firework display but still controlled. Very rich on the palate: broad yet silky, earthy yet so refined. This is Mouton at a new peak and it’s hard to imagine a better balance of elegance and power.

98 Points - Wine Enthusiast     This is a hugely opulent wine, packed with black fruits, rich tannins and great concentration. It is a gorgeous wine that's full of potential, with the dense, dark core showing how well this wine will age. Drink this complex wine from 2027.

96 Points - Wine Spectator     Offers a prodigious core of steeped fig, black currant and blackberry compote flavours, enmeshed with notes of smouldering tobacco, charcoal and liquorice. Broad, deep and long, with a deep foundation of graphite through the finish. Despite the heft, this manages to show off some purity too. Best from 2025 through 2045.

title: Produttori del Barbaresco - Barbaresco 'Montestefano' Riserva??
vendor: 300407 - Enoteca Bacco Importers Of Fine Wines &
bodyHtml:
Hailing from the Barbaresco DOCG in Italy’s Piedmont region, this potent red wine carries a rich heritage. The winery’s story began in 1958 when a village priest and local growers collaborated to protect the Nebbiolo grape and support the farming community. Today, the cooperative consists of fifty four families who exclusively grow Nebbiolo, adhering to a winemaking philosophy that prioritizes the unique expression of their premium vineyard sites.

Wine Description

The 'Montestefano' Riserva is a 100% Nebbiolo that showcases a deep ruby red colour. Often described as the most 'Barolo-like' of the cooperative's crus, it is renowned for its massive structure and incredible depth. The sensory profile features a powerful bouquet of dark cherries, strawberries, and black raspberries, interwoven with complex notes of licorice, tobacco, leather, and alpine herbs. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied and broad, offering a rich, explosive character with sturdy, well-integrated tannins and a persistent, mineral-driven finish. It is fermented at 30°C with 28 days of skin contact before aging for 30 months in large oak barrels and 9 months in the bottle. While possessing immense power, it maintains an elegant balance and is built for significant aging, with an optimal drinking window typically spanning 2027 to 2049.

Food Pairing

The substantial grip and intensity of 'Montestefano' make it an excellent match for hearty fare such as grilled ribeye, rack of lamb, or slow-braised venison. It also pairs beautifully with fresh egg pastas topped with rich meat ragù and aged cheeses like Parmigiano Reggiano. A perfect match to enhance the wine's complexity

title: Domaine Harmand Geoffroy Mazis Chambertin Grand Cru 2019
bodyHtml:
From the esteemed region of Burgundy, France, Domaine Harmand Geoffroy is a family-run estate based in Gevrey Chambertin, where generations have dedicated themselves to producing expressive, terroir-driven wines. With a heritage deeply rooted in traditional practices, the domaine focuses on low-intervention viticulture to highlight the character of its prestigious Grand Cru vineyards, such as Mazis Chambertin. This parcel is particularly celebrated for its old vines, which yield wines of remarkable depth and complexity.

Wine Description
The 2019 Mazis Chambertin Grand Cru presents a luminous ruby hue, revealing a captivating aromatic profile of ripe blackberries, black cherries, and wild strawberries, interwoven with hints of violets, earth, and subtle spice. On the palate, it unfolds with layers of dark fruit, liquorice, and delicate smoky undertones, supported by firm, velvety tannins and vibrant acidity. Full-bodied and powerful, this wine balances its richness with a refined elegance, culminating in a persistent, savoury finish. Composed entirely of Pinot Noir, the 2019 vintage is approachable in its youth but promises to evolve beautifully over the next 15–20 years, reaching its peak from 2027 onwards.

Accolades
Vinous - 93 points.
Wine Advocate - 92+ points.

Food Pairing
This Grand Cru pairs exquisitely with roasted duck breast, venison in a red wine reduction, or wild mushroom risotto. The depth and structure of the wine complement rich, earthy flavours, creating an unforgettable dining experience.

Vintage Quality
The 2019 vintage in Burgundy was marked by a warm and dry growing season, resulting in concentrated, ripe fruit and wines of impressive structure. Despite the challenges of heat and reduced yields, skilled winemaking preserved the freshness and balance essential to long-lived Pinot Noir.

title: Domaine Anne F. Gros Richebourg Grand Cru 2022
bodyHtml:
Dark, brooding aromas of red and black cherry, blackberry, and mulberry infused with smoky, toasted oak spice. So intense, complex, and concentrated yet beautifully balanced thanks to the juicy tannins and silky texture; it is so pure and harmonious with a core of further Autumn and hedgerow fruits fused with black pepper spice on the marathon finish. Effortlessly oozes class and sophistication. Stunning.

96+ Points - Jasper Morris

A brilliant purple, with a fascinating touch of spice to add to the depth of dark yet royal fruit. Just keeps getting more profound on the nose. Incredibly intense through the middle, excellent mineral acidity behind, and a length well above the others. Thank you for this perfection. 

96+ Points - Vinous

The 2022 Richebourg Grand Cru is intense on the nose: mainly black fruit with a pronounced marine/oyster shell influence. It gains complexity and nuance on the glass. The palate is well-balanced, and the 40-50% new oak neatly enmeshed (higher than previous vintages).

96 Points - Decanter

This is a thrilling wine, deceptively light in colour but aromatically powerful, with a concentrated pomegranate and black cherry fruit character and an extraordinary sense of density, substance, and length on the palate.

title: Louis Latour Chambertin 'Cuvee Heritiers Latour' Grand Cru 2020
bodyHtml:
At the heart of a constellation of Grands Crus from Cote de Nuits is to be found Le Chambertin. The terroir of Chambertin is legendary for its exceptional richness due to a geological phenomenon called an alluvial fan. This deeply complex terroir is characterized by brown calcareous soils. It breeds a powerful and complex wine with a long ageing potential, combining the robustness of Pinot Noir and the taste of the "terroir". At the end of the 19th century the Latour family acquired 0.81 hectares in the Chambertin Grand Cru appellation, forming a beautiful parcel extending from the top to the bottom of the hillside, closer to that of Latricieres rather than Clos de Bèze. We took the name of Chambertin "Cuvee Heritiers Latour", as the parcel has been passed down through the generations of Latour family descendants.

Our Chambertin Grand Cru "Cuvee Heritiers Latour" 2020 has a deep, dark color with ruby hues. Its nose reveals notes of undergrowth combined with liquorice. It has a nice roundness in mouth which reveals silky tannins with mocha and licorice aromas.

Pair with venison stew, roasted female deer with pepper and mashed celery, or soumaintrain cheese. 

100 Points - James Suckling

93+ Points - Wine Enthusiast

title: Chateau Haut Brion 2015
bodyHtml:
Very beautiful, deep, garnet-red colour. The nose is ripe and concentrated. After swirling in the glass, it becomes more complex with hints of very ripe but not excessively so red and black fruit. There are also liquorice nuances and clove. The wine starts out with a very soft mouth feel and immediately shows tremendous volume and depth in every respect, with flavours reminiscent of ripe fruit and cocoa beans. The long aftertaste features mocha and slightly bitter coffee nuances. Barrel ageing will undoubtedly bring out more of this wine's greatness and confirm its place among the finest vintages of Château Haut-Brion.

Blend: 50% Merlot, 42% Cabernet Sauvignon, 8% Cabernet Franc

100 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

A blend of 50% Merlot, 8% Cabernet Franc and 42% Cabernet Sauvignon, the medium to deep garnet-purple coloured 2015 Haut-Brion is reticent to begin, languidly revealing crushed black cherries, ripe black plums and wild blueberries with sparks of cinnamon stick, cloves, nutmeg, espresso, unsmoked cigars, tapenade, crushed rocks and lavender. The full-bodied palate possesses wonderfully complementary contrasts of bold black and blue fruit richness and delicately nuanced cherry fruit, baking spices and floral accents, strutting ripe, finely pixelated tannins and seamless acidity that is placed firmly in the background, finishing very long and with plenty of attitude. This impeccably poised, exquisitely perfumed 2015 Haut-Brion possesses the most alluring yet seemingly effortless beauty. While it bears only a passing resemblance in its opulent personality to the now legendary 1989, like that vintage the 2015 cannot fail to hedonically satiate and intellectually edify all lovers of great Bordeaux who drink it. What’s more, it also has the blue-blooded tenaciousness to remain this jawdroppingly impressive, throughout its many guises over time, and for a very, very long time.

100 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

The 2015 Haut Brion is a perfect wine that couldn’t be any better and is certainly at the top of this great vintage. A blend of 50% Merlot, 42% Cabernet Sauvignon, and the balance Cabernet Franc, this full-bodied, concentrated, backward, yet sensationally pure 2015 boast knockout notes of blackcurrants, smoked tobacco, ground herbs, and graphite, with a terrific damp earth/minerality quality emerging with time in the glass. Straight, focused, and built like a skyscraper, with a stacked mid-palate, forget bottles for 7-8 years and enjoy over the following three to four decades.

98 Points - James Suckling

This is all about seduction and beauty with tobacco, berries, tea and wet earth. Full-bodied, round and sexy. Love the polished and beautiful tannins. Racy and refined. Try in 2023.

98 Points - Wine Spectator

A brick house of a wine, loaded with roasted fig, warmed currant compote and plum reduction flavours that are as broad as they are deep, carried by warm tar, ganache and smouldering bay leaf and charcoal notes. A swath of tobacco through the finish pulls everything together and ties it up with a bow of roasted mesquite. The core shows lean, muscular strength in spades. Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon and Cabernet Franc. Best from 2025 through 2045.

title: Chateau Ducru Beaucaillou 2022 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
France, Bordeaux, Saint Julien. Château Ducru Beaucaillou, classified as a Deuxième Grand Cru Classé in 1855, is one of the most celebrated estates of the Médoc. Owned by the Borie family since 1941, the estate is renowned for its precision, elegance, and the unique gravel terroir (‘beaux cailloux’ or ‘beautiful stones’) that shapes its wines.

Wine Description

Deep garnet-purple in colour, it opens with captivating aromas of crushed blackcurrant, redcurrant preserve, and wild blueberry, layered with dark chocolate, violets, and hints of exotic spice. The palate is concentrated and powerful yet refined, with ripe black fruit, graphite, and floral undertones supported by finely polished tannins. Full-bodied and structured, the wine displays outstanding balance, freshness, and a long, mineral-driven finish.

Accolades

  • James Suckling – 97+ points

  • Vinous – 95+ points

  • Wine Advocate – 94+ points

  • Jeb Dunnuck – 97+ points

Food Pairing

This Saint Julien pairs beautifully with prime rib roast, venison, or beef Wellington. Earthy dishes such as wild mushroom risotto or truffle-infused pasta also complement its depth and complexity.

title: Domaine Michel Gros Richebourg 2022
bodyHtml:
On the palate, a refined bouquet of black berries, undergrowth, notes of morels mingle with light aromas of graphite. The palate is perfectly balanced, nicely full-bodied accompanied by silky tannins like velvet, an elegant wine. Light notes of white pepper at the end of the palate will reveal all the finesse and grandeur of this vintage.

94+ Points - Vinous

Aged entirely in new oak, the refined bouquet gradually builds in the glass: mainly dark berry fruit, forest floor, hints of morels and light graphite aromas. The palate is medium-bodied with very fine tannins. This is a more elegant take on Richebourg. It is harmonious with a satin texture, a peacock's tail towards the finish, and a dash of white pepper on the aftertaste. This marks a very impressive debut.

title: Harlan Estate 2020
bodyHtml:
The 2020 Harlan Estate is a red wine from Napa Valley, California. Renowned for its exceptional quality, Harlan Estate has consistently produced wines that exemplify the unique terroir of the region.

Vineyard and Production

Situated in the western hills of Oakville, Harlan Estate encompasses approximately 240 acres, with 40 acres under vine. The vineyards are planted on hillside sites with a combination of volcanic and sedimentary bedrock, featuring thin, well-drained soils. The 2020 vintage presented challenges, including regional fires and heat spikes; however, meticulous vineyard management and selection ensured that only the finest fruit contributed to the final blend.

Tasting Notes

  • Appearance: Deep ruby, nearly opaque, with an amaranthine rim.

  • Aroma: Expressive bouquet of dark cherry, plum, cedar, tobacco, chocolate, licorice, and dark spices.

  • Palate: Full-bodied and plush, featuring flavors of blackberries, cherries, and plums, complemented by notes of sweet tobacco spice, cocoa powder, and old cedar box. The wine exhibits fine-grained tannins, balanced acidity, and a lingering finish.

Critical Acclaim

  • Vinous: 95 points. Antonio Galloni describes the 2020 Harlan Estate as "one of the very best wines I have tasted from this challenging vintage so far," highlighting its balance and depth.

  • Decanter: 94 points. The review notes the wine's "coiled-up energy that delivers surprise and intrigue in every swirl and sip."

  • Jeb Dunnuck: 94 points. He remarks on its "pure bouquet of cassis, scorched earth, graphite, and violets," emphasizing its intensity and depth.

Serving and Pairing

To fully appreciate its complexity, decant the wine for at least an hour before serving at a temperature of 16-18°C (61-64°F). This wine pairs exceptionally well with hearty dishes such as grilled ribeye steak, braised short ribs, or aged cheeses. Its robust structure and depth also make it a suitable companion for rich stews and roasted game meats.

title: Casanova Di Neri Brunello Di Montalcino 2020
bodyHtml:
Italy’s Tuscany region is celebrated worldwide for its exceptional wines, and the area of Montalcino stands out as one of its crowning jewels. Casanova di Neri, founded in 1971 by Giovanni Neri, remains a family-run estate now led by his son, Giacomo Neri. The winery has earned international acclaim for its relentless pursuit of quality, with vineyards carefully sited across Montalcino’s most prized terroirs. This commitment to excellence has positioned Casanova di Neri among the modern icons of Brunello production.

Wine Description

This Brunello di Montalcino 2020 is crafted exclusively from Sangiovese, known locally as Brunello. It reveals a deep ruby hue with garnet reflections, offering an elegant nose layered with ripe red cherry, wild strawberry, dried rose petals, and subtle notes of spice and tobacco. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied yet remarkably graceful, displaying finely woven tannins and vibrant acidity that sustain flavours of crushed raspberry, black tea, and hints of earthy undergrowth. The finish is long and polished, lingering with notes of minerality and sweet herbs.

Accolades

  • Wine Spectator – 95 points.

  • Vinous – 94 points.

  • James Suckling – 96 points.

Food Pairing

Enjoy this Brunello with dishes that complement its layered complexity and structure. Braised veal shank, roasted game birds, or a rich mushroom risotto will beautifully echo its earthy undertones. Aged Pecorino or Parmigiano also pair exquisitely, highlighting the wine’s depth and finesse. Together, they create an unforgettable dining experience.

title: Produttori del Barbaresco - Barbaresco 'Muncagota' Riserva??
vendor: 300407 - Enoteca Bacco Importers Of Fine Wines &
bodyHtml:
Produced in the Barbaresco DOCG of the Piedmont region in Italy, Produttori del Barbaresco was established in 1958 by a village priest and local growers to preserve the identity of the Nebbiolo grape and support the farming community. The cooperative consists of fifty four families who exclusively cultivate Nebbiolo across 100 hectares of premium vineyards, emphasizing a philosophy of uncompromising quality and site-specific terroir expression.

Wine Description

The 'Muncagota' Riserva is a 100% Nebbiolo wine that showcases a ruby red colour with garnet reflections. Its complex and aromatic nose features a refined floral bouquet of rose and menthol, layered with notes of forest floor, leather, blood orange, and spice. On the palate, the wine is full bodied and vertical, offering intense mineral and spicy layers of raspberry, pomegranate, licorice, and mint. Characterized by its energy and firm, fine-grained tannins, it leads to a long and elegant finish. The wine undergoes fermentation at $30°C with 28 days of skin contact before being aged for 30 months in large oak barrels and an additional 9 months in the bottle. While possessing an optimal drinking window between 2029 and 2044, its exceptional structure allows for a longevity of up to 25 years from the vintage.

Food Pairing

The structured and vibrant profile of this wine makes it a perfect match for fresh egg pastas, such as tajarin or wild boar ravioli. It also pairs exceptionally well with roasted red meats, venison, game birds, or rich risottos. For cheese selections, consider aged hard cheeses or dishes featuring savoury spices and truffles. This pairing highlights the wine's depth and character.

title: Chateau d'Yquem 2019
bodyHtml:
France’s most iconic sweet wine, Chateau d’Yquem hails from the prestigious Sauternes appellation in Bordeaux. Owned by the luxury conglomerate LVMH since 1999, the estate boasts centuries of winemaking tradition dating back to the late 16th century. Known for its exceptional terroir and commitment to quality, Yquem is the only Sauternes classified as Premier Cru Supérieur in the 1855 classification.

Wine Description
The 2019 vintage displays a luminous golden hue with shimmering brilliance. On the nose, it bursts with vibrant aromas of apricot, honey, marmalade, orange zest, and subtle hints of ginger and white flowers. The palate is opulently layered with flavours of dried pineapple, candied citrus, and crème brûlée, wrapped in a silky, glycerol-rich texture. Balanced by a precise spine of acidity, the wine shows remarkable freshness despite its richness.

Accolades

  • Wine Advocate – 98 points

  • James Suckling – 97 points

  • Vinous – 96 points

  • Wine Spectator – 96 points

Food Pairing
