This elegant Sauternes shines alongside foie gras, blue cheese such as Roquefort, or rich seafood dishes like lobster in a butter sauce. It also pairs beautifully with fruit-based desserts like tarte Tatin or poached pears. This pairing highlights the wine’s depth and character.

title: Chateau Haut Brion Blanc 2018
bodyHtml:
This legendary Premier Grand Cru Classé dry white wine originates from France, within the Pessac-Léognan appellation of the Graves region in Bordeaux. Château Haut-Brion holds a unique place in wine history as the only estate outside the Médoc included in the 1855 Bordeaux Classification. Managed today under the leadership of Prince Robert of Luxembourg and Domaine Clarence Dillon, the estate produces an exceedingly rare white wine—often in quantities under 1,000 cases per vintage—that is widely celebrated as one of the greatest dry whites in the world. Grown on deep gravel terraces resting over clay and sand subsoils, Haut-Brion Blanc represents the ultimate expression of Graves terroir.

Wine Description

In the glass, the 2018 vintage displays a brilliant pale gold-yellow color with vibrant green highlights. The expressive and multifaceted nose opens with an incredible bouquet of white peach, candied lemon peel, pink grapefruit, and ripe pear, seamlessly integrated with nuances of honeysuckle, linden flower, toasted hazelnut, crush gravel minerality, and fine oak spice. On the palate, it is full-bodied, majestic, and immensely powerful, offering extraordinary textural volume and density balanced by a laser-like beam of precise natural acidity. The blend consists of 75.4% Sauvignon Blanc and 24.6% Sémillon. Hand-harvested with rigorous selection, the wine is fermented and aged in French oak barrels (around 50% to 70% new) on its fine lees with regular stirring (bâtonnage), yielding an exceptionally long, opulent, and saline finish. The alcohol by volume sits at 14.5%.

Food Pairing

The profound structural concentration, opulent texture, and vibrant acidity of this benchmark white Bordeaux demand world-class culinary pairings. It pairs brilliantly with butter-poached lobster, pan-seared sea scallops with truffle cream, roasted turbot in beurre blanc, and grilled langoustines. It also complements roasted veal sweetbreads, poulet de Bresse with wild moril mushrooms, and aged hard cheeses such as mature Comté or Beaufort.

Vintage Quality

The 2018 growing season in Bordeaux was marked by a wet spring followed by an exceptionally warm, sunny summer. While hot conditions accelerated sugar accumulation, the estate's terroir and meticulous canopy management allowed the white varieties to retain remarkable freshness and aromatic tension before an early harvest. The 2018 Château Haut-Brion Blanc is a monumental, power-packed vintage that combines opulent fruit concentration with exceptional cellar longevity, capable of aging gracefully in proper cellars for 20 to 30+ years.

99 Points - James Suckling

Opulent and perfumed for this great white in 2018, with lemon curd, cooked apple, lilac, lime flower, stone, rock and hints of sandalwood. It's full-bodied yet tight and compressed with layers of fruit that are integrated and focused. It needs time to open and show its true greatness but stunning. Try after 2025.

97 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

A Sauvignon Blanc-dominated release that includes just under 20% Sémillon, the 2018 Château Haut-Brion Blanc reveals a vivid light gold hue and gorgeous notes of crushed limes, white flowers, white grapefruit, and obvious crushed rock-like minerality. These carry a medium to full-bodied white with flawless balance in their fruit, acidity, and alcohol, beautiful mid-palate depth, and an undeniable elegance and purity that's something to behold. It's not a powerful house, but it has a chiselled, elegant, incredibly long style that will benefit from 2-4 years of bottle age and keep for 20 years or more.

94+ Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The Haut-Brion 2018 Blanc is a blend of 80.6% Sauvignon Blanc and 19.4% Sémillon. This is the highest Sauvignon Blanc in the blend ever. Unsurprisingly, it needs a lot of air at this youthful stage. Eventually, unfurling bit by bit to offer subtle scents of lemon peel, fresh grapefruit, green mango and yuzu, with emerging suggestions of wet pebbles, struck flint, orange blossom and lime leaves with a waft of oyster shells. The medium to full-bodied palate has a gorgeous satiny texture and lovely freshness, offsetting the intense stone and citrusy flavours, finishing long and layered. Give this a good 3-4 years, and drink it over the next 15 years or more. 2024 - 2039.

title: Billecart Clos St Hilaire 2007
bodyHtml:
This prestigious and singular white wine originates from France, specifically from the single-hectare Clos Saint-Hilaire vineyard in the Mareuil-sur-Aÿ subregion of Champagne. Founded in 1818 through the marriage of Nicolas François Billecart and Elisabeth Salmon, Maison Billecart Salmon has been family-owned and independent for over 200 years. The winemaking philosophy for this cuvée emphasizes ancestral methods, including the use of workhorses in the vineyard to increase biodiversity and soil porosity, which fosters the growth of concentrated grapes. The grapes come from an isolated, one-hectare plot of old vines planted in 1964, enclosed by a stone wall, and are vinified entirely in small oak barrels.

Wine Description

This 100% Pinot Noir (Blanc de Noirs) presents a sublime golden yellow hue enhanced by intense glints of coppery pink. The complex nose is noble and sensual, offering aromas of malted cereals, acacia flowers, and orange blossom, followed by roasted notes of coffee, blond tobacco, and sweet spices. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied and muscular, showcasing structure and roundness with flavours of candied citrus, ripened yellow fruits, quince paste, and apricot. Stylistically, it is characterized by mind-blowing precision, impeccable freshness, and a creamy, supple texture that avoids heaviness despite its concentration. The finish is long and authoritative, with a deliciously mineral chalkiness and persistent salinity. This wine has an ABV of 12.5%. While the vineyard uses biodynamic principles and eschews pesticides, it was officially certified organic in 2022, following the production of this vintage.

Vintage Quality

The 2007 vintage in Champagne is often recognized more for its Chardonnays, yet this cuvée produced only 4,800 numbered bottles of exceptional quality. The year provided conditions that allowed for vibrant energy and brisk acidity, which the winemakers preserved by blocking malolactic fermentation to enhance the wine's characteristic salinity and tension.

title: Cathiard Vineyard Cabernet Sauvignon 2020
bodyHtml:
Cathiard Vineyard is perched slightly above the valley floor on the lower slopes of the Mayacamas mountains with vineyards straddling both the Rutherford and St. Helena appellations. Over the decades, this historic property has featured numerous owners and vineyard and winemaking heritage dating back to the 1840’s.

The Cathiard vineyard Cabernet Sauvignon is 100% varietal and was harvested from the oldest Cabernet Sauvignon block on the property. This is the flagship bottling of the estate and only produced in very limited quantities. 

It shows a dense aromatic profile of earth, dark plum, Valrhona chocolate, tobacco and spice that dominate the nose. The palate is rich and round with seamless velvety tannins. A focused acidity complimented with a balanced, complete mouthfeel leads to a finish that displays the very best of the terroir farmed by Cathiard Vineyard.

97 Points - James Suckling

Wonderful aromas of blackcurrants, dark plums, mint, sage, and dried wood. Some sandalwood. Full- to medium-bodied with tannins that have the texture of fine velvet and run down the length of the wine. Extremely polished and refined. Sophisticated. Firm at the end. This will age beautifully. Pure cabernet sauvignon. 

97 Points - Wine Enthusiast

Extraordinary and opulent, this densely concentrated, luxuriously textured flagship Napa wine by Florence and Daniel Cathiard of Bordeaux is their first vintage from the former Flora Springs property. The wine is softly saturated with black currants, blueberries, spearmint and black olives for a comforting, mouthfilling expression that is at once powerful and gentle. It feels layered, deep and creamy.

96 Points - Decanter

Ripe and juicy blue fruit aromas on the nose with some soft wood spice, acaia, liquorice, a touch of California heat in the aromas but smells fresh and inviting. Clean, supple, lively, pure and focussed on the palate. Tannins take the fore, really quite mouthfilling with ash, smoke, tar, tobacco edges, leather and some meat, underpinning the blackcurrant, black cherry and blueberry fruit.

title: Chateau Le Pin 1995 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
Château Le Pin 1995 originates from France, within the Bordeaux region and the world-renowned Pomerol subregion. Founded in 1979 when the Thienpont family acquired a tiny 1.6-hectare parcel of vines, Le Pin rapidly redefined the fine wine world as the quintessential "garage wine" (vin de garage). Operating on a microscopic scale from its small, gravelly vineyard situated on a sunny plateau near Château Trotanoy, the estate's philosophy focuses on extreme selection, low yields, and meticulous hand-craftsmanship. The 1995 vintage stands as a legendary benchmark from this ultra-exclusive estate, exemplifying Pomerol's unmatched ability to produce wines of extraordinary concentration, opulent texture, and aristocratic elegance.

Wine Description

This red wine presents a deep, mature garnet-ruby appearance with slight mahogany hues along the rim. It possesses a full-bodied, rich, and remarkably seamless structure, boasting a velvety, mouth-coating, and expansive texture. The sensory profile is astonishingly aromatic and complex, opening with an intoxicating bouquet of black cherry preserve, roasted plums, cassis, and dried figs, seamlessly intertwined with secondary and tertiary nuances of truffle, cigar box, espresso, exotic spices, toasted oak, and damp forest floor. On the supple, opulent palate, it delivers a harmonious layer of sweet dark fruit balanced by resolved, silky tannins and a gentle thread of preserved acidity. The finish is exceptionally long, lingering, and decadent, ending with persistent echoes of dark cocoa, leather, sweet spices, and mineral earthy undertones.

  • Varietal Composition: 100% Merlot.

  • Stylistic Notes: The 1995 harvest saw extremely low yields of exceptionally concentrated fruit. The winemaking team performed malolactic fermentation directly in 100% new French oak barrels—a pioneering technique for the region—followed by aging in barrel for approximately 18 to 20 months. The wine was bottled unfiltered to preserve its profound natural depth and silken textural complexity.

  • ABV: 13.5%.

  • Enjoy now to 2035.

title: Ridge Vineyards Lytton Springs Estate 2023 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
#3 Wine Spectator Top 100 2025

The 2023 Ridge Vineyards Lytton Springs Estate has achieved significant critical acclaim, most notably being named the #3 Wine of the Year for 2025 by Wine Spectator. This prestigious ranking makes it the highest-rated Zinfandel ever in the history of the publication's annual Top 100 list.

Ridge Vineyards Lytton Springs Estate 2023 originates from the United States, specifically from the Dry Creek Valley region and the Sonoma County subregion in California. The vineyard’s history began in 1972 when Ridge made its first Lytton Springs wine from vines planted at the turn of the century; the estate was officially purchased by the winery in 1991. Ridge Vineyards follows a 'pre-industrial' winemaking philosophy, relying on natural primary and secondary fermentations with native yeasts and minimal intervention to preserve the fruit's distinctive character and site expression.

Wine Description

This red wine displays a dark crimson or deep garnet colour and a medium to full body with a structured, elegant frame. The sensory profile features a powerfully aromatic nose of raspberry, black pepper, licorice, and subtle vanilla, often accented by notes of potpourri and sandalwood. On the palate, it delivers a core of black cherry, plum, and marionberry fruit supported by supple tannins, bright acidity, and a stony minerality. The finish is remarkably long and layered, revealing complex notes of garrigue, dried herbs, and black tea.

  • Varietal Composition: A traditional field blend of 76% Zinfandel, 14% Petite Sirah, 7% Carignane, 2% Alicante Bouschet, and 1% Mataro.

  • Stylistic Notes: The 2023 vintage is noted for its refined mouthfeel, poise, and exceptional length, presenting a more nuanced and restrained expression compared to previous years.

  • ABV: Recorded at 14.4%.

  • Organic Status: This wine is produced from 100% organically grown estate grapes and is fermented without added industrial yeasts or enzymes.

Food Pairing

The structured elegance and peppery fruit profile of Lytton Springs make it an excellent companion for rich and savoury dishes. Suggested pairings include lamb tacos served with a sweet mole sauce or roasted lamb chops to complement the wine's earthy undertones. It also pairs effectively with hot Italian sausage sandwiches featuring roasted peppers, smoked brisket, or smash burgers. For a more casual pairing, it works well with mushroom based dishes or heavier salads that can stand up to its medium body.

Vintage Quality

The 2023 growing season in Dry Creek Valley was defined by a cool, wet winter and a mild summer that allowed for slow, even ripening. This remarkably cool season delayed the start of the harvest by approximately one month, resulting in a vintage characterized by greater restraint, vibrant acidity, and more refined fruit intensity than previous warmer years.

title: Billecart Salmon Blanc de Blancs Brut 2012 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
This Champagne is a Blanc de Blancs, meaning it is crafted from 100% Chardonnay, sourced from Grand Cru villages of the Côte des Blancs. Specifically, the blend includes Chardonnay from Mesnil-sur-Oger (60%), Cramant (23%), Chouilly (11%), and Oiry (6%). The wine displays a crystal clear pale gold colour with delicate glints and a persistent, fascinating effervescence.

On the nose, it offers an elegant, complex maturity with notes of yellow fruits and citrus, such as candied mandarin, limoncello, and conference pear, alongside subtle aromatic profiles of cedar and raw butter. A detailed sensory profile reveals incredible aromas of brioche, bread dough, and pie crust, with electrifying fruit like peaches and fresh apples.

The palate delivers a creamy sensation with beautifully chiselled finesse. Stylistic notes include a lovely refreshing balance and a sophisticated purity with a chalky, balanced, and crystalline character. It is described as a powerful wine with a majestic typicity and great structure, yet balanced and creamy. Flavours include zest of citron, almond biscuit, and white pepper, with a prolonged finish featuring sweet citrus fruits, cardamom, and vanilla-flavoured cream puffs. The low dosage of 3.9 grams per litre contributes to its pure and intense dimension. It is a very young Champagne that needs time to be at its best, with an optimal drinking window suggested from 2025 to 2037. There is no information provided to indicate if the wine is organic.

Accolades

  • James Suckling - 99 points

  • Vinous - 97 points

  • Decanter - 96 points

  • The Wine Advocate - 96 points

  • Jeb Dunnuck - 96 points

Food Pairing

Suggested pairings tailored to the wine's flavour profile and structure include a casserole of whole calf sweetbread from Corrèze, a creamy shellfish risotto, or abalone from Brittany and samphire. The House's head, Mathieu Roland-Billecart, also suggests pairing a Blanc de Blancs with a seafood platter, lobster, or caviar. A specific pairing recommendation is halibut with Champagne beurre blanc and caviar.
Together, they create an unforgettable dining experience.

title: Chateau Lafite Rothschild 2018
bodyHtml:
Château Lafite Rothschild, one of Bordeaux’s most legendary First Growths, exemplifies the artistry and heritage of Pauillac winemaking. With a history spanning centuries, this iconic estate is renowned for producing wines of grace, power, and exceptional aging potential, solidifying its place as a symbol of excellence.

Wine Description

The 2018 vintage is a triumph, displaying a deep garnet color with ruby highlights. On the nose, it offers a complex and captivating bouquet of blackcurrant, plum, and violets, layered with hints of cedar, graphite, and finely integrated oak. The palate is full-bodied and opulent, with polished tannins providing a velvet-like texture. Flavors of dark berries, licorice, and dark chocolate are balanced by a vibrant acidity and a pronounced minerality. The finish is extraordinarily long and harmonious, showcasing the wine's depth and precision.

Food Pairing

Pair this masterpiece with herb-crusted lamb, roasted game birds, or a selection of aged cheeses like Gouda or Parmigiano-Reggiano. Together, they create a culinary experience that highlights the wine’s sophistication.

Vintage Quality

2018 was a standout vintage in Bordeaux, marked by a warm growing season and exceptional ripening conditions. Château Lafite Rothschild 2018 captures the vintage's richness and structure, promising decades of graceful evolution in the cellar.

title: Domaine Thibault Liger Belair 'Richebourg' Grand Cru 2019
bodyHtml:
98 Points - Decanter

Liger-Belair owns 0.5ha, planted in 1936 just above DRC in the lower part of Les Richebourg. Initially somewhat reserved, this wine opened in the glass to reveal lush, plummy fruit and a savoury, smoky element and mineral notes. It is only with time that one realises the depth and strength of the tannins, so richly are they enrobed. An immense finish lingers long after you have finished. Superb.

94+ Points - Vinous

The 2019 Richebourg Grand Cru is matured with 35% whole bunch, and five of the six barrels are new. It has a very perfumed bouquet of floral red berry fruit laced with crushed rock and sous-bois scents. The palate is medium-bodied with solid tannins, more savory than, say, Grivot’s Richebourg, with liberally sprinkled cracked black pepper toward the finish. It will need several years in bottle.

title: Colgin IX Estate Proprietary Red Blend 2021
bodyHtml:
IX Estate Red is distinguished by complex fruit interplays, a luscious nose of rustic herbs, iron, clay, and black fruits, huge layers of flavor, and supple, sweet tannins that are impeccably well balanced. The number IX refers to the parcel number and is also significant as the date Ann and Joe were married: 9/9. Approachable when young, it ages most gracefully.

98 Points - Vinous

The 2021 IX Estate is such an elegant wine. Sleek, aromatic and refined, the 2021 is one of the most polished young wines I have tasted from this site. Red/purplish fruit, lavender, rose petal and mint abound. Silky and delineated, the 2021 is exceptionally beautiful and balanced. Clean saline notes and veins of tannin extend the explosive, sublime finish.

title: Chateau Margaux 2013
bodyHtml:
Château Margaux, an iconic first-growth estate in Bordeaux’s Margaux appellation, has been producing world-class wines since the 17th century. Under the stewardship of the Mentzelopoulos family, the estate continues to set benchmarks for elegance and refinement. The 2013 vintage showcases the estate's resilience and dedication to quality, even in a year of challenging weather.

Wine Description

The 2013 Château Margaux is a delicate expression, displaying a bright garnet hue and a bouquet of fresh red currants, wild strawberries, and a touch of rose petals. Hints of cedar, graphite, and a whisper of vanilla enhance the aromatic complexity. The palate is light to medium-bodied with silky tannins, vibrant acidity, and a graceful balance, leading to a clean, refined finish.

Food Pairing

Pair this wine with dishes like roasted quail, herb-crusted salmon, or a mushroom and truffle tart. Together, they create an unforgettable dining experience that emphasizes the wine’s finesse and subtlety.

Vintage Quality

The 2013 vintage presented significant challenges due to cooler temperatures and rain during harvest, resulting in a lighter, early-drinking style. While not as powerful as other years, it remains a testament to Château Margaux’s commitment to crafting wines of elegance and poise.

title: Chateau Haut Brion 2000
bodyHtml:
100 Points - Decanter

Is this as good as the 1989? Certainly it is lush and powerful, lingering and expanding in the mouth with sweet tobacco and cigar box notes, along with still young blackcurrant and blackberry fruits, all given lift by the trademark Haut-Brion aromatics. It beds in and shakes off early reticence after a good hour in the glass, suggesting that this is only just leaving its primary phase and has many decades left ahead of it. A great wine that highlights the success of Haut-Brion under the partnership of estate director Jean-Bernard Delmas, father of current director Jean-Philippe Delmas, and owner Joan Dillon the Duchess of Mouchy (president of the company until 2008 before handing over to her son Prince Robert of Luxembourg). A supremely confident wine that is hard to fault in its depth of expression.

99 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2000 Haut-Brion (a blend of 51% Merlot, 43% Cabernet Sauvignon, and the rest Cabernet Franc) showed incredibly at the tasting, and for me is one of the three or four most prodigious wines of the vintage. A compelling nose of roasted herbs, scorched earth, sweet blueberries, plums, black currants, and a hint of graphite is followed by a deep, layered, sumptuously textured, full-bodied Haut-Brion, but one with extraordinary complexity. This wine seems more evolved and approachable than I had expected it to be at age 10. My window of maturity is 2010-2050.

title: Chateau Haut Brion 2012
bodyHtml:
Blend: 65% Merlot, 33% Cabernet Sauvignon and 2% Cabernet Franc.

96+ Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Tasted blind at the Southwold 2012 tasting, the 2012 Haut-Brion has an open and generous bouquet with blackcurrant pastille, cassis and briary aromas the exude very pure Merlot. The palate is medium-bodied with a sumptuous opening that is rare in 2012: rounded and generous, caressing in the mouth with black plum and blackcurrant towards the finish, residues of truffle and white pepper lingering on the aftertaste that turn very savory after 15 minutes—bacon fat or Italian cured meats. There is a lot to love about this Haut-Brion although in this blind showing I scored it the same as La Mission Haut-Brion. Who will stick their neck out as the two wines mature? Tasted January 2016.

title: Echo De Lynch Bages 2015
vendor: 300747 - South By Southwest Wine Imports Inc.
bodyHtml:
Introduction

Echo de Lynch Bages is a red wine from the Pauillac appellation in the Médoc region of Bordeaux, France. The estate has been owned by the Cazes family since 1939, and this second wine was renamed in 2008 to better reflect its prestigious lineage. The winemaking philosophy focuses on precision viticulture and the use of a state of the art gravity flow cellar to ensure the faithful 'echo' of the main estate's character.

Wine Description

This wine presents a deep ruby colour and an expressive sensory profile. The aroma features intense notes of cassis, blackberry, and raspberry, layered with secondary scents of graphite and cedar. On the palate, it is medium bodied and supple, offering a smooth texture with well integrated, fine grained tannins and a fresh finish. The varietal composition for this vintage is 70% Cabernet Sauvignon and 30% Merlot. It has an ABV of 13% and an optimal drinking window that typically spans 10 to 15 years from the harvest. The wine is produced using sustainable practices, though it is not certified organic.

title: Chateau Margaux 2017
bodyHtml:
99 Points - James Suckling

There is ripeness and opulence to this, in an almost exotic and sassy way. Crushed berries with chocolate and spice. Floral and cashmere undertones. This starts off slowly and just rolls off the palate with beautifully polished tannins and a salty, minerally note to the long, extended tannins. Really brilliant. So classy. Structured. Try after 2025.

98 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

Despite Margaux being a slightly more difficult region for the Medoc in 2017, this estate has fashioned an incredible 2017 Chateaux Margaux that’s unquestionably in the same league as the 2015 and 2016, and that’s saying something. Based on 89% Cabernet Sauvignon, 8% Merlot, 2% Cabernet Franc and 1% Petit Verdot representing a draconian selection of just 22% of the total production, it reveals a deep purple/ruby hue as well as stunning notes of creme de cassis, blueberries, crushed violets, unsmoked tobacco, and Asian spice. With flawless tannins, medium to full body, brilliant concentration, and a great, great finish, it's easily one of the standouts in the vintage. It’s already stunning, yet a good 7-8 years of bottle age are warranted, and it should cruise for 20-25 years in cold cellars.

98 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2017 Chateau Margaux is a blend of 89% Cabernet Sauvignon, 8% Merlot, 2% Cabernet Franc and 1% Petit Verdot. Deep garnet-purple coloured, it needs a little coaxing to reveal alluring notes of blackcurrant cordial, Black Forest cake and black raspberries with suggestions of candied violets, tilled soil, fallen leaves, liquorice and espresso plus wafts of underbrush and rose hip tea. Medium-bodied, the elegance and finesse on the palate is simply bedazzling, exuding a quiet intensity of fresh black fruits layered with oh-so-subtle floral and earth nuances. It has a soft, velvety texture and seamless freshness to support the tightly wound flavours, finishing long and perfumed. Beautiful! This grand vin accounts for just 37% of the crop.

title: Chateau Mouton Rothschild 2006
bodyHtml:
Chateau Mouton Rothschild, a Premier Cru Classé from the Bordeaux region and one of the world's greatest wines, is owned by Baroness Philippine de Rothschild. 
 
97 Points - Wine Enthusiast     At the time it was shown as a barrel sample in early 2007, this was the best wine of 2006. That accolade remains. It has all the power of the Cabernet Sauvignon in Pauillac, which was the greatest success of the vintage. That power comes from the dense tannins as well as the black plum and spice flavours and minerality. The texture becomes velvet, giving a final richness, but never losing its long aging potential. In a year that is good, but not at the top, Mouton has made a great wine.
 
96 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate     It remains one of the standouts of the growing season and actually replicates previous showings just the week earlier and in January. As expected, the nose has quite brilliant delineation with blackberry, graphite, here an almost cold slate-like scent. The palate is harmonious with the carefully judged acidity, fine-grain tannin and immense detail on the finish. Recent bottles suggest that it may close up for several years, in which case, either enjoy this in the next few months or cellar this for a few years and receive vinous dividends down the line.
 
95 Points - James Suckling     This is an eye-opener with a tight core of complex fruit character as well as subtle chocolate and spices. Full body, firm tannins and a classy finish. Holding back. Much better than expected. A vintage forgotten. 
 
95 Points - Decanter    The breadth and depth of this wine is impossible to ignore. Tobacco notes blend with cappuccino, cedar and grilled almonds. This is classy, with just the right amount of abandon. Grilled black fruits are very Mouton, but with the touch of austerity and pulled-in, pared-down tannins that tell you it’s 2006. Complex and complete.
 
95 Points - Wine Spectator    This is in an interesting spot right now, still sporting some youthful blackberry, cassis and plum fruit, with only secondary hints starting to emerge. Yet those secondary hints are very tantalizing, with well-worn cedar, tobacco and sanguine notes adding range and cut. There's a freshness throughout, yet also a supple edge, which allows the fruit to drape prettily on the finish

title: Masseto 2021
bodyHtml:
Masseto, a distinguished winery in Tuscany, Italy, is renowned for producing one of the world's most celebrated Merlot-based wines. The estate's dedication to meticulous vineyard management and traditional winemaking techniques has solidified its reputation for excellence.

The 2021 Masseto is a stunning example of refinement and precision. Moving towards a more elegant style, this vintage showcases less intensity and extraction compared to past years. Crushed flowers, spice, blood orange, and vibrant red-toned fruit dominate the palate, accompanied by floral aromatics and a saline minerality. Crafted entirely from Merlot, the 2021 reflects the estate’s commitment to producing wines of extraordinary balance and complexity.

This exceptional wine pairs beautifully with dishes such as roasted lamb, aged cheeses, or hearty mushroom dishes. Together, these pairings enhance the wine’s depth and create an unforgettable dining experience.

The 2021 vintage in Tuscany offered ideal growing conditions, enabling the Merlot grapes to achieve perfect ripeness while maintaining balance and elegance. Masseto 2021 is a profound expression of its unique terroir and stands as a testament to the winery’s legacy of excellence.

title: Poggio Landi Brunello di Montalcino Riserva 2019
bodyHtml:
Poggio Landi Brunello di Montalcino Riserva 2019 is a red wine from Italy in the Tuscany region and the Brunello di Montalcino Denominazione di Origine Controllata e Garantita (DOCG) appellation. The wine is produced by the Poggio Landi winery, which is known for a style that favours an elegant and less extract-rich approach. The fruit for Poggio Landi's Brunello is harvested at altitudes between 200 and 300 metres above sea level. The Brunello di Montalcino Riserva from Poggio Landi is considered a wine of great prestige, appreciated for its elegance and depth.

Wine Description

This wine is a 'Riserva,' meaning it has undergone a longer period of ageing before release. The wine is aged for 48 months in French oak, with an additional minimum of six months in the bottle.

  • Colour: It is typically a very dark ruby red.

  • Aroma: The wine presents broad and varied olfactory profiles. Tasting notes mention clean, intense aromas with nuances of very ripe fruit and balsamic notes. Specific aromas include ripe cherry, raspberry, cranberry, and in the glass, an approachable and graceful style with intoxicating violet aromas, black cherries, and spicy depth.

  • Palate: It is described as well-balanced, fresh, and intense. The palate is full-bodied, powerful, and lively, with a healthy tension. The fruit is juicy and the tannins are fine and velvety.

  • Body: Full-bodied. It is well-structured and deep.

  • Finish: The finish is long and ethereal. The taste is led to an elegantly tannic and balsamic finish, with a long, fruity finish.

  • Varietal Composition: 100% Sangiovese.

  • ABV: 14.5% alcohol by volume.

  • Organic: It is made from organically grown grapes.

  • Optimal Drinking Window: Made for the long term, with a drinking window that extends to 2040+. It can be drunk now but is best from 2026.

title: Chateau Margaux 2006
bodyHtml:
Chateau Margaux, a Premier Grand Cru Classé Bordeaux, is one of the most famous wines in the world. Care has been lavished on the property by a line of owners with an abiding concern for the reputation of the estate.

This wine has an extraordinary aromatic finesse, a tannic richness and a particularly dense and tight knit texture. The finish is very long, fresh and lively, a little bit firm but already packed with flavour. Such balance is a brilliant expression of Chateau Margaux's noble terroir.

95 Points Wine Enthusiast

This is not a big Château Margaux, its style showing more elegance and discretion. The tannins are soft, although producing a dense web that lies underneath the black currant and plum fruit flavours. It is a wine that envelops the mouth, an edge of firmness over velvet fruit textures.

94+ Points Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

 It is worth noting that when the bottled 2006 Chateau Margaux, which appeared closed and less impressive than I had predicted from barrel, was re-tasted alongside the remarkable 2008, I elevated my score to 94+. It does not possess the size or power of the 2008 or 2005, but the 2006 exhibits impressive density, a deeper colour, and the beautifully textured, pure style that is a hallmark of this estate. Moreover, it is relatively precocious, and can be drunk now or cellared for 25+ years.

title: Robert Groffier Chambolle Musigny 'Les Amoureuses' Premier Cru 2020
Chateau Ausone 2020
bodyHtml:
Château Ausone, located in the Saint-Émilion appellation of Bordeaux, France, is revered as one of the Premier Grand Cru Classé A estates. The 2020 vintage exemplifies the château's dedication to crafting wines of extraordinary quality that reflect the unique character of their historic terroir.

Blend and Production

The 2020 Château Ausone is an equal blend of 50% Merlot and 50% Cabernet Franc. The wine is aged in 100% new French oak barrels, with some maturation taking place in 30-hectoliter oak casks, a method that enhances its complexity and aging potential.

Tasting Notes

  • Appearance: Deep garnet-purple hue with impressive intensity.
  • Nose: Aromas of ripe blueberries, black plums, and black raspberries mingle with notes of pencil shavings, iron ore, rose petals, truffle, and cedar.
  • Palate: Medium to full-bodied with layers of vibrant black and blue fruits. The wine is framed by ripe, fine-grained tannins and balanced by seamless freshness, leading to an exceptionally long, pure, and mineral-driven finish.

Critical Acclaim

  • Wine Enthusiast: 98 points – Recognized for its power, depth, and layered complexity, with a long aging potential.
  • Lisa Perrotti-Brown MW: 100 points – Praised for its perfumed elegance, energetic fruit layers, and epic length, highlighting its potential for aging.

Serving and Cellaring

The 2020 Château Ausone is best served at around 60°F (15.5°C) to fully appreciate its nuanced aromas and flavors. Decanting before serving is recommended to allow the wine to open up. While it can be enjoyed young, this vintage is built for long-term aging, with an optimal drinking window from 2028 to 2048.

Conclusion

The 2020 Château Ausone is a masterpiece that demonstrates the estate's unwavering commitment to excellence. With its harmonious balance of power, elegance, and longevity, it is a standout example of the exceptional quality that defines the Saint-Émilion appellation. This wine is a worthy addition to any fine wine collection and a testament to Bordeaux’s winemaking artistry.

title: Gaja Barbaresco 'Costa Russi' 2021
bodyHtml:
Gaja Barbaresco 'Costa Russi' 2021 is a distinguished red wine from the Barbaresco region in Piedmont, Italy. Crafted by the esteemed Gaja winery, this wine is produced exclusively from Nebbiolo grapes sourced from the 'Costa Russi' vineyard, renowned for its exceptional terroir.

Tasting Notes:

  • Color: Deep ruby red with a vibrant hue.

  • Aroma: The nose is expressive and elegant, featuring aromas of cherry, strawberry, and violet, complemented by subtle hints of black truffle and earthy nuances.

  • Palate: On the palate, the wine is medium to full-bodied with a harmonious balance of ripe red fruit flavors, including wild raspberries and plums. It exhibits a refined structure with well-integrated tannins and a refreshing acidity.

  • Finish: The finish is long and persistent, leaving a lasting impression of mineral notes and a touch of spice.

Serving Suggestions:

  • Temperature: Serve at 16-18°C (60-64°F) to fully appreciate its aromatic complexity.

  • Glassware: Use a large Bordeaux glass to allow the wine to breathe and reveal its full bouquet.

  • Food Pairings: Pairs excellently with dishes such as roasted lamb, beef tenderloin, and aged cheeses.

Accolades:

  • Wine Enthusiast: 97 Points.

  • Falstaff: 96 Points.

  • Jeb Dunnuck: 98 Points.

  • James Suckling: 97 Points.

  • Vinous: 97 Points.

  • Wine Spectator: 95 Points.

title: Louis Roederer Cristal Rose 2014
bodyHtml:
Pink hue with slightly coppery tints. Dynamic bubbles forming a lingering bead. Pure, precise and dazzling bouquet. The intense Pinot Noir aromas take us back to the harvest time with its pure, ripe and concentrated fruit: zesty red berries (red currants, wild raspberries, blackcurrants) and raspberry liqueur. Then come sweet spice and smoky notes with a hint of reduction (smoky, spicy) from the Pinot noir with its notes of undergrowth. Concentrated and broad on the palate, where the red fruit (strawberries, raspberries) is concentrated into a firm, dense texture.

98 Points - James Suckling

Extremely subtle and delicate, this has an enveloping nose of tiny red berries and dried flowers. This sparkling rosé masterpiece is just beginning to really open up. Fabulous velvety texture on the mouth-filling palate, the very fine mousse already spot on. Tons of structure behind all this, so this should age really well. From organically grown grapes.

97 Points - Wine Enthusiast

The epitome of great rose Champagne, this is beautifully intense. The fruit and balanced mineral edge are united with mature redcurrant flavors in a wine that is perfectly aged. It is an impressive wine that is ready to drink.

96 Points - Wine Spectator

This rose features rich, focused flavors of peach tart, poached apricot and mandarin orange fruit, plus accents of toasted brioche, pastry cream, pickled ginger and pink grapefruit sorbet. Exudes an overall vibrant impression, with a fine interplay of elegance and complexity, showing deft integration of the vivid acidity and the satiny mousse. Pinot Noir and Chardonnay.

title: Chateau Haut Brion 2003
bodyHtml:
Intense aromas of violets, berries and spices follow through to a full-bodied palate, with layers of super silky tannins and a long, long finish. Very classic in style. All in elegance and length. I like it better than the 2000. Best after 2009.

96 Points - Wine Spectator

Complex aromas of black liquorice, tobacco and cedar with red fruits. Full-bodied, with super seductive, silky tannins, loads of fruit and a finish that lasts for minutes. A beauty in all the sense of the word. Best after 2012.

96 Points - Wine Enthusiast

Restrained power combine with great style and elegance in this beautiful wine. The tannins are certainly solid and serious, but then they are also sweet, dusty ripe, sustaining dense dark plum flavours and only a hint of wood.

95 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Even better, and clearly the best wine made in the Haut-Brion stable in 2003 (the last vintage of the great Jean-Bernard Delmas as administrator), the 2003 Haut-Brion is a blend of 58% Merlot, 31% Cabernet Sauvignon and 11% Cabernet Franc that hit 13% natural alcohol, which seemed high at the time, but given more recent vintages is modest. Dark ruby/plum in colour, with no amber or orange at the edge, the wine exhibits an abundance of roasted herbs, hot rocks, black currants, plum, and balsamic notes. Quite rich, medium to full-bodied and more complete, with sweeter tannins than La Mission Haut-Brion, this full-bodied Haut-Brion has hit full maturity, where it should stay for at least a decade. Bravo!

title: Bond Quella 2019
bodyHtml:
The 2019 Bond Quella originates from a steeply sloped, southwest-facing 9-acre vineyard in the eastern hills of Napa Valley. This unique site, an ancient riverbed composed of cobble and rocks interwoven with pockets of tufa (volcanic ash), imparts a distinctive minerality to the wine. The 2019 vintage showcases the vineyard's characteristic ethereal quality of blue fruits, graphite, and a vibrant, subtle finish.

Tasting Notes
Color: Deep garnet-purple.
Nose: Expressive aromas of blackcurrants, black cherries, and blackberry pie, complemented by notes of cedar, charcoal, tar, pencil lead, and fragrant earth.
Palate: Full-bodied with a rock-solid structure of firm, grainy tannins and vibrant freshness supporting the generous black fruit flavors.
Finish: Long and layered, leaving a lingering mineral impression.

Accolades

  • Jeb Dunnuck: 98 points
  • Decanter: 97 points
  • Vinous (Antonio Galloni): 96 points
  • James Suckling: 99 points
  • Robert Parker's Wine Advocate: 95 points
  • Wine Spectator: 96 points

Optimal Drinking Window
2025–2050. While approachable in its youth, this wine will continue to evolve and gain complexity with extended cellaring.

Serving Suggestions
Decanting: 3 hours to allow the wine to fully express its aromatics and structure.
Serving Temperature: 16–18°C (60–64°F) for optimal enjoyment.
Pairings: Ideal with roasted game meats, grilled ribeye steak, or aged cheeses like Comté and Gouda.

title: Dalla Valle 'Maya' Proprietary Red Blend 2020
bodyHtml:
The 2020 Maya exudes confidence and elegance from the first sip. It is a classic Maya blend of Cabernet Sauvignon and Cabernet Franc, the core coming from "Maya’s Vineyard" Cabernet Sauvignon always blended with carefully chosen Cabernet Franc lots to harmonize and bring lift to the energetic qualities of the Cabernet Sauvignon. An exquisite symphony of frankincense, clove, and cedar jump from the glass in the beginning, then subtle fruit notes of rainier cherries and lingonberries meld together both on the nose and continue on the palate. The classic silky yet firm tannins leave a prolonged weight leading to a long finish. 

Blend: 60% Cabernet Sauvignon, 40% Cabernet Franc

97 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Perhaps there's a subtle added touch of leafy complexity to the 2020 Maya that the Cabernet Sauvignon doesn't show, but otherwise, this 60-40 blend of Cabernet Sauvignon and Cabernet Franc is reasonably similar, with black cherries, dark loamy notes, hints of cassis, cedar and vanilla. It's medium to full-bodied, richly textured and tannic but with a slightly open-knit feel and a ripe, softly wooly finish.

96 Points - James Suckling

Subtle yet transparent blackberry, black licorice and cassis bush. Some sage and lavender as well. Graphite, too. Full-bodied, yet tight and poised on the palate, with tight and refined tannins that are compact in the mouth. They are layered and run vertically down the wine. Turns nicely austere at the end. Very well done for the vintage.

96+ Points - Jeb Dunnuck

Even better, the 2020 Maya Proprietary Red Wine checks in as the usual blend of 60% Cabernet Sauvignon and 40% Cabernet Franc, and it's another full-bodied example of this cuvée that has a brilliant core of both red and black fruits as well as dark chocolate, leafy tobacco, spring flowers, and a kiss of chalky minerality. Structured, concentrated, and perfectly balanced, it doesn't get any better in 2020.

92 Points - Wine Spectator

Features a cassis and black cherry fruit core flanked by a prominent tobacco note, with a loamy edge driving through as well. The slightly taut finish is underscored by alder and warm paving stone accents. Shows its Cabernet Franc side more than the Cabernet Sauvignon component. Cabernet Sauvignon and Cabernet Franc. Best from 2024 through 2035.

title: Alter Ego De Palmer Margaux 2015 (by Chateau Palmer) - 5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
Produced in France, Alter Ego de Palmer 2015 is a distinguished expression of the Margaux appellation in Bordeaux. The estate is steeped in history, famously shaped by the Pereire brothers in the 19th century and the Royal Hussar Charles Palmer, who prioritized finesse and elegance in his winemaking. Today, the winery operates with a philosophy that listens to its unique terroir, utilizing biodynamic practices to create wines that transcend fleeting trends.

Wine Description

This vintage presents a medium to deep garnet purple colour. The aromatics are remarkably pure and expressive, featuring a bouquet of blackberries, dark chocolate, crushed cherries, and ripe plums, complemented by sophisticated notes of lavender, incense, and cedar. On the palate, the wine is medium to full bodied, showing a vivacious and finely crafted structure with polished, 'sensational' tannin tension. Its character is defined by a balance of ripe fruit and fresh acidity, leading into an elegant finish with hints of graphite and truffle. Composed of 52% Merlot, 42% Cabernet Sauvignon, and 6% Petit Verdot, this wine offers an optimal drinking window from 2020 through 2034.

Accolades

  • "James Suckling – 96 points."

  • "Wine Enthusiast – 94 points."

  • "Jeb Dunnuck – 93 points."

  • "Wine Advocate – 92 points."

  • "Decanter – 92 points."

title: Chateau Mouton Rothschild 2010
bodyHtml:
Chateau Mouton Rothschild is a legendary First Growth estate situated in the Pauillac appellation of the Médoc, France. Since being acquired by Nathaniel de Rothschild in 1853, the estate has remained under the visionary stewardship of the Rothschild family, most notably Baron Philippe de Rothschild, who achieved the historic reclassification to First Growth status in 1973. The winery's philosophy bridges the worlds of art and viticulture, famously commissioning a unique artist-designed label for every vintage since 1945.

Wine Description

The 2010 Chateau Mouton Rothschild is an opaque blueish-purple wine with an intense and multi-faceted sensory profile. The nose is complex and spellbinding, opening with aromas of crème de cassis, black cherry, and dark berries, followed by intricate layers of graphite, cedar, tobacco leaf, and subtle notes of incense and truffle. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied and powerful, featuring flawlessly integrated, velvety tannins and a deep, concentrated fruit core. The finish is exceptionally long, characterized by a refined mineral freshness and elegant floral nuances. Composed of 94% Cabernet Sauvignon and 6% Merlot, this remarkable vintage is built for the long term, with an optimal drinking window extending from 2025 through 2085.

Accolades

  • Decanter - 100 points

  • Jeb Dunnuck - 100 points

  • James Suckling - 100 points

  • Vinous - 100 points

  • Robert Parker - 98 points

title: Perrier Jouet Belle Epoque Blanc de Blancs 2014
bodyHtml:
Perrier-Jouet Belle Epoque Blanc de Blancs is the jewel of the collection – the quintessential expression of Chardonnay in the style of Maison Perrier-Jouet.

A pale, luminous hue, like the rising sun. Delicate nose, characterised by aromas of white flowers: rose & white-fleshed fruit. A firm attack & satiny texture. Subtle, precise worked cuvee with a hint of white pepper.

title: Produttori del Barbaresco - Barbaresco 'Ovello' Riserva??
vendor: 300407 - Enoteca Bacco Importers Of Fine Wines &
bodyHtml:
This distinguished red wine originates from the Barbaresco DOCG in the Piedmont region of Italy. The winery, Produttori del Barbaresco, is a world-renowned cooperative founded in 1958 by the village priest, Don Fiorino Marengo, who united nineteen small growers to continue the proud tradition of Nebbiolo production. Today, the cooperative comprises fifty four families who exclusively cultivate Nebbiolo, maintaining a philosophy of producing high-quality, site-specific wines that highlight the unique terroirs of their nine legendary 'Cru' vineyards.

Wine Description

The 'Ovello' Riserva is a powerful and highly structured expression of 100% Nebbiolo, sourced from one of the region's most iconic vineyards. Due to its northern exposure and clay-rich calcareous soils, the wine typically displays a shiny ruby red colour and a massive, linear profile. The aromatic profile is complex, featuring notes of macerated cherry, strawberry, and rose hip, layered with earthy accents of graphite, crushed rock, tobacco, and peppery spice. On the palate, it is full bodied and vibrant, characterized by dense, sturdy tannins and a long, energetic finish with a saline minerality. This Riserva undergoes fermentation at $30°C$ with 28 days of skin contact before aging for at least 30 months in large oak barrels. It is a wine built for the long haul, with an optimal drinking window typically spanning 10 to 25 years from the vintage.

Food Pairing

The robust structure of 'Ovello' makes it a superb match for rich Piedmontese cuisine, such as white truffle risotto, agnolotti, or tajarin with meat sauce. It also pairs exceptionally well with roasted red meats, braised beef (Manzo stufato), and game dishes like venison or wild boar. For a cheese course, opt for aged, pungent varieties like Castelmagno or Parmigiano Reggiano. This pairing highlights the wine's depth and character.

title: Gaja Barbaresco 'Sori San Lorenzo' 2021
bodyHtml:
Gaja Barbaresco 'Sori San Lorenzo' 2021 is a distinguished red wine from the Barbaresco region in Piedmont, Italy. Crafted by the esteemed Gaja winery, this wine is produced exclusively from Nebbiolo grapes sourced from the 'Sori San Lorenzo' vineyard, renowned for its exceptional terroir.

Tasting Notes:

  • Color: Deep ruby red with a vibrant hue.

  • Aroma: The nose is expressive and elegant, featuring aromas of cherry, strawberry, and violet, complemented by subtle hints of black truffle and earthy nuances.

  • Palate: On the palate, the wine is medium to full-bodied with a harmonious balance of ripe red fruit flavors, including wild raspberries and plums. It exhibits a refined structure with well-integrated tannins and a refreshing acidity.

  • Finish: The finish is long and persistent, leaving a lasting impression of mineral notes and a touch of spice.

Serving Suggestions:

  • Temperature: Serve at 16-18°C (60-64°F) to fully appreciate its aromatic complexity.

  • Glassware: Use a large Bordeaux glass to allow the wine to breathe and reveal its full bouquet.

  • Food Pairings: Pairs excellently with dishes such as roasted lamb, beef tenderloin, and aged cheeses.

Accolades:

  • Wine Enthusiast: 98 Points.

  • Falstaff: 98 Points.

  • Jeb Dunnuck: 98 Points.

  • James Suckling: 97 Points.

  • Vinous: 97 Points.

  • Wine Spectator: 95 Points.

title: Chateau Palmer 2016
bodyHtml:
Château Palmer, a distinguished Third Growth estate from the 1855 Bordeaux Classification, is located in the Margaux appellation of Bordeaux, France. Established in the early 19th century, the estate is renowned for producing exceptional wines that epitomize the elegance and complexity of Margaux.

Description: The 2016 vintage is a blend of 47% Merlot, 47% Cabernet Sauvignon, and 6% Petit Verdot. This wine exhibits a deep garnet-purple color and opens with compelling notes of blueberry compote, warm cassis, and kirsch, with emerging hints of violets, cigar box, black tea, sandalwood, and Sichuan pepper. On the palate, it is medium to full-bodied, rich, and concentrated, featuring super-ripe, velvety tannins and fantastic freshness, finishing long with floral and earthy sparks.

Tasting Notes:

  • Nose: Aromas of blueberry compote, warm cassis, kirsch, violets, cigar box, black tea, sandalwood, and Sichuan pepper.
  • Palate: Medium to full-bodied with rich, concentrated flavors, velvety tannins, and vibrant freshness.
  • Finish: Long and persistent, with floral and earthy nuances.

Accolades:

  • Jeb Dunnuck: 100 Points
  • Vinous: 100 Points
  • Wine Enthusiast: 100 Points
  • Decanter: 98 Points
  • James Suckling: 98 Points
  • Wine Advocate: 98 Points

Optimal Drinking Window: This wine is expected to develop beautifully with age and is best enjoyed from 2026 through 2050.

Serving Suggestions: Decanting for at least two hours is recommended to allow the wine to open up and reveal its full complexity. Serve at a temperature of 15.5°C (60°F).

title: Casanova Di Neri Brunello 'Cerretalto' 2019
bodyHtml:
Founded in 1971 by Giovanni Neri, Casanova di Neri is now under the stewardship of his son, Giacomo Neri, who continues to champion meticulous vineyard practices and an unwavering pursuit of quality. The estate is renowned for its ability to craft Brunellos of profound character and age-worthiness, with Cerretalto standing as its pinnacle expression.

Wine Description

This 100% Sangiovese Grosso unfolds in the glass with a deep ruby colour tinged with garnet reflections. The nose is intensely aromatic, offering layers of black cherry, plum, crushed rose petals, tobacco, exotic spices, and hints of graphite. On the palate, it reveals exceptional power and precision, with finely woven tannins supporting flavours of ripe dark berries, balsamic notes, and traces of dark chocolate. The full-bodied structure is lifted by vibrant acidity, carrying through to a long, elegant finish marked by minerality and savoury undertones.

Accolades

  • Wine Advocate – 99 points

  • James Suckling – 98 points

  • Vinous – 98 points

  • Decanter – 97 points

Food Pairing

Perfect with classic Tuscan fare such as bistecca alla Fiorentina, slow-braised wild boar ragù, or aged pecorino. This pairing highlights the wine’s depth and character, drawing out its intricate layers while complementing its robust structure.

title: Chateau Angelus 'Hommage A Elisabeth Bouchet' 2019
bodyHtml:
100 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

This is the first release of this new 100% Cabernet Franc wine from Chateau Angelus. Deep garnet in color, the 2016 Hommage a Elisabeth Bouchet hits the ground running with an intense, profound nose of blackberry preserves, boysenberries and redcurrant jelly, plus suggestions of beef drippings, black olives, damp soil and unsmoked cigars with wafts of pencil lead and truffles. The full-bodied palate bursts with vibrant, shimmery black and red fruits, inlaid with mineral accents and supported by firm, exquisitely ripe and finely grained tannins.

Electric sparks of bright acidity course through the densely packed core, delivering incredible energy and freshness to the finish, leaving you wanting more. That this estate has managed to craft such a complete, jaw-dropping beauty entirely from Cabernet Franc is a triumph and, I hope, not the last of its kind. A masterpiece!

title: Chateau Latour Premier Grand Cru Classe 2017
bodyHtml:
From France’s Bordeaux region, in the Pauillac appellation of the Médoc, Château Latour is one of the five First Growth estates classified in 1855. Owned by François Pinault since 1993, the estate is famed for its meticulous vineyard management and its emphasis on producing wines of exceptional longevity and structure. The vines within the iconic ‘l’Enclos’ are among the oldest and most prestigious in the region.

Wine Description

The 2017 Château Latour reveals a deep purple-black colour. On the nose, it exudes aromas of crème de cassis, blackberry pie, warm plums, violets, and star anise, complemented by cedar, pencil shavings, and subtle spice. The palate is medium to full-bodied, layered, and precise, showing flavours of dark berries, baker’s chocolate, and a mineral edge. Structured with fine-grained tannins, the wine delivers vibrancy and freshness, finishing long and savoury with a saline lift.

Accolades

  • James Suckling - 99 points

  • Decanter - 98 points

  • Wine Spectator - 98 points

  • Jeb Dunnuck - 96 points

  • Vinous - 96 points

  • Wine Enthusiast - 96 points

Food Pairing

Ideal with classic dishes such as roasted lamb, prime rib, or duck confit. Aged cheeses like Comté or aged Gouda also enhance the wine’s layered complexity.

title: Argiano Brunello Di Montalcino Vigna Del Suolo 2019 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
Founded in the late 16th century, Argiano is one of Montalcino’s oldest and most storied estates, with vineyards rooted in limestone-rich soils that give the Vigna del Suolo its name. This single-vineyard Brunello is crafted from the estate’s oldest vines, a true expression of Argiano’s philosophy of elegance and authenticity in winemaking.

Wine Description
This Brunello presents a bright ruby-red hue with garnet reflections. On the nose, it reveals floral tones of violet and lavender, layered with red plums, cherries, and subtle balsamic spice. The palate unfolds with precision and depth, offering flavours of black cherry, currant, leather, and hints of sun-dried tomato and oregano. Medium to full-bodied, with polished tannins and vibrant acidity, it is both powerful and refined. The finish is long, saline, and mineral-driven, with notes of clove, tea leaves, and earthy undertones.

Accolades

  • Wine Spectator - 97 points.
  • Vinous - 95+ points.

Food Pairing
This wine pairs beautifully with osso bucco, roasted lamb, and aged Pecorino Toscano. Its refined tannins and savoury complexity also make it a superb match for wild boar ragù or truffle-infused pasta. Together, they create an unforgettable dining experience.

title: Domaine Henri Rebourseau Chambertin Grand Cru 2019
bodyHtml: A great wine to taste at least once in your life! This wine, which obtained the AOC Grand Cru in 1937, is one of the essential references of the Burgundy vineyard. The 2019 vintage has magnified it by giving it a lot of breed and elegance and by giving it a beautiful dress of an intense raspberry red. The nose is not left out, quite the contrary. It exudes highly concentrated aromas of red fruits and slightly spicy blackberries. Some floral notes bring him a touch of sensuality. On the palate, a taste rich in sap and softness where finesse, elegance and fleshy fullness are combined. Its velvety tannins and beautiful balance make it an exceptional wine that will move Pinot Noir lovers. Although delicious from its youth, this nectar has a beautiful aging potential of up to fifteen years. Its nobility and breed make it an ideal partner for tasty meats such as a roast duck breast with honey and spices or a prime rib topped with a morel sauce.

title: Chateau Margaux 2015
bodyHtml:
Château Margaux 2015 is a masterpiece from one of Bordeaux’s most iconic estates, a wine that embodies the elegance, complexity, and heritage of the Margaux appellation. Crafted in a vintage celebrated for its near-perfect conditions, this wine is composed of 87% Cabernet Sauvignon, 8% Merlot, 3% Cabernet Franc, and 2% Petit Verdot. It is a dazzling expression of Château Margaux’s terroir and winemaking mastery, standing as one of the greatest wines in its storied history.

Tasting Notes
From the first glance, the wine captivates with its deep ruby hue, edged with vibrant purple highlights that hint at its youthful energy. The bouquet is breathtakingly complex, unveiling layers of crème de cassis, blackberry compote, and violet petals, interwoven with notes of cedar wood, vanilla, and toasted spices. As it opens, subtleties of graphite, mocha, and truffle emerge, adding depth and intrigue.

On the palate, Château Margaux 2015 is a symphony of elegance and power. It glides effortlessly, revealing silky, velvety tannins that envelop a core of ripe black fruits and crushed berries. The mid-palate bursts with flavours of dark chocolate, licorice, and a whisper of smoky oak, while its perfectly balanced acidity keeps the wine lively and fresh. The finish is monumental—long, persistent, and resonating with a medley of fruit, spice, and mineral nuances.

Accolades
Hailed as one of the finest wines ever produced by Château Margaux, the 2015 vintage achieved a historic milestone, receiving multiple perfect 100-point scores from leading critics:

  • Wine Enthusiast: "A sumptuous wine of unparalleled elegance and structure."
  • James Suckling: "Spellbinding...a wine of incredible harmony, purity, and grace."
  • Decanter: "A Margaux for the ages, destined to be one of Bordeaux’s greats."
  • Jeb Dunnuck: "Flawless, timeless, and utterly profound."
    Additionally, Robert Parker's Wine Advocate and Wine Spectator awarded it 99 points, further cementing its place as a legendary vintage.

Winemaking Process
Every detail of the winemaking process reflects Château Margaux’s pursuit of perfection. The grapes, meticulously hand-harvested and sorted, underwent fermentation in stainless steel tanks to preserve their purity and freshness. The wine then matured for 18 to 24 months in 100% new French oak barrels, where it gained complexity, refinement, and the silky texture that defines the estate’s signature style.

Food Pairing
Château Margaux 2015 is an exquisite companion to fine dining. It pairs impeccably with roasted lamb, beef Wellington, or duck confit, as well as earthy dishes like mushroom risotto or truffle-infused pasta. Aged cheeses, such as Comté or Parmigiano-Reggiano, also enhance its intricate flavours. These pairings elevate the wine’s luxurious depth, creating unforgettable culinary moments.

The Vintage
The 2015 growing season was near perfection, marked by a warm, dry summer and ideal conditions during harvest. These factors allowed the estate’s Cabernet Sauvignon to ripen fully, achieving remarkable concentration and balance. Château Margaux’s unparalleled attention to detail in both the vineyard and the cellar ensured that this exceptional vintage would become a timeless masterpiece.

Final Thoughts
Château Margaux 2015 is not merely a wine—it is an experience. Its extraordinary balance of finesse and power, combined with its unparalleled acclaim, secures its place among the finest wines of Bordeaux. While already a revelation, this wine promises decades of evolution, rewarding those who have the patience to let it unfold in the cellar.

title: E. Guigal Cote Rotie 'La Mouline' 2019
bodyHtml:
This iconic single-vineyard dry red wine originates from France, produced in the prestigious Côte-Rôtie appellation of the Northern Rhône Valley. E. Guigal, founded in 1946 by Étienne Guigal and elevated to global legend by Marcel and Philippe Guigal, is world-famous for its trio of single-vineyard Côte-Rôtie bottlings known affectionately as the "La La's" (La Mouline, La Turque, and La Landonne). La Mouline is sourced from a tiny 1-hectare amphitheater-like parcel within the Côte Blonde sub-zone, characterized by light-colored, gneiss-rich soils. First produced in 1966, La Mouline contains the highest proportion of Viognier among the trio, giving it an unmistakable floral elegance, velvety texture, and sensual perfume that set the benchmark for modern Northern Rhône Syrah.

Wine Description

In the glass, the 2019 vintage presents a deep, luminous ruby-purple color with intense clarity. The explosive nose is an intoxicating amalgam of dark and red berries—crème de cassis, wild blackberry, and black raspberry—fused with soaring aromatics of dried violets, honeysuckle, acacia blossom, cured meats, black olive tapenade, bacon fat, and sweet cedar oak spice. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied, hedonistic, and incredibly polished, demonstrating an opulent, silky texture that coats the mouth without feeling heavy. The notable inclusion of Viognier softens the structural frame, weaving fine-grained, cashmere-like tannins alongside a vibrant streak of natural acidity. Crafted from approximately 89% Syrah co-fermented with 11% Viognier from old vines (up to 75+ years old), the hand-harvested grapes undergo long temperature-controlled fermentation before Guigal’s signature, extended maturation of 42 months in 100% new French oak barrels crafted in their own cooperage at Château d'Ampuis. The alcohol by volume sits at 14.5%.

Food Pairing

The opulent texture, complex floral aromatics, and rich fruit depth of this legendary single-vineyard red call for top-tier culinary creations. Exceptional pairings include pan-seared duck breast with cherry or blackberry reduction, roasted rack of lamb with herbs, slow-braised venison loin, roasted squab, and dry-aged prime ribeye steak. It also pairs spectacularly with truffled poultry, wild mushroom risotto, and mature artisanal cheeses such as Saint-Marcellin, Époisses, or aged Comté.

Vintage Quality

The 2019 vintage across the Northern Rhône is widely acclaimed as a generational masterpiece, marked by warm, sunny summer weather that produced exceptional fruit concentration, ripe skin tannins, and towering structural balance. Thanks to the ancient vines and deep root systems of La Mouline, the grapes achieved complete phenolic maturity while retaining remarkable aromatic lift. The 2019 E. Guigal La Mouline is a monumental bottling—intensely aromatic and approachable after decanting in its youth due to its velvety core, yet possessing the concentration and structural depth to evolve gracefully in proper cellars for 30 to 40+ years.

Accolades

  • 100 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

    The 2019 Côte Rôtie La Mouline is a bigger, richer Côte Rôtie. Co-fermented with a solid chuck of Viognier and around 85% destemmed (the same as the La Turque), this full-bodied effort has a kaleidoscope-like bouquet of bloody black and blue fruits, tapenade, salted meat, woodsmoke, and a touch of violets. This cuvée is always an exotic wine, and the 2019 is no exception, offering full-bodied richness, a layered, multi-dimensional mouthfeel, plenty of structure, and a great finish.
    Barrel Sample: 97-100

  • 97 Points - James Suckling

    Great nose of summer flowers and ripe blackberries with a glaze of toasty oak. A very graceful wine in spite of all the power and concentration. Feels almost weightless until you get to the finish where you feel the enormous structure that lurks just below the surface. A cuvee of 89% syrah and 11% viognier. Matured in 100% new oak for 42 months. Drink or hold.

  • 97 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

    The 2019 Côte-Rôtie La Mouline is textural and concentrated, wafting from the glass with aromas of dark berries, spices, pepper, gentian and cedar, all framed by a delicate touch of oak. Full-bodied, broad and creamy, it’s enveloping and layered, built around a fleshy, deep core of fruit framed by sweet, powdery tannins, concluding with a long, perfumed and gently ethereal finish. This is a beautiful rendition of this emblematic cuvée.

title: Chateau Malescot St Exupery 2022
bodyHtml:
Located in the heart of the Margaux appellation in Bordeaux, Chateau Malescot St Exupery is a historic third growth estate classified in 1855. The estate was named in part after Count Jean-Baptiste de Saint-Exupéry, the great-grandfather of the famed writer and aviator Antoine de Saint-Exupéry. Owned by the Zuger family since 1955, the château is known for producing wines that blend classical elegance with modern precision.

Wine Description
The 2022 vintage of Chateau Malescot St Exupery reveals a vivid garnet-purple hue. On the nose, it bursts with cassis, ripe blackberry, violet, and hints of graphite and spice. The palate is full-bodied and layered, showcasing black cherry, dark plum, and cocoa with refined tannins and vibrant acidity. Structured yet graceful, the wine demonstrates excellent balance and freshness with a persistent, mineral-driven finish.

Accolades

  • Wine Advocate – 93–95 points

  • James Suckling – 96–97 points

  • Vinous – 93–95 points

  • Jeb Dunnuck – 94-96 points

Food Pairing
Ideal with grilled ribeye steak, duck breast with cherry sauce, or aged cheeses such as Comté or Gruyère. This pairing highlights the wine’s depth and character.

title: Chateau Palmer 2021
bodyHtml:
Château Palmer is a Third Growth estate located in the Margaux appellation of Bordeaux, France. Established in the early 19th century, it has consistently produced wines renowned for their elegance and complexity. Since 2014, Château Palmer has embraced biodynamic viticulture, reflecting a deep commitment to environmental stewardship and enhancing the expression of its unique terroir.

Wine Description

The 2021 Château Palmer displays a deep ruby hue. On the nose, it offers an enticing bouquet of blackberries, cherries, and mulberries, complemented by floral hints of violets and subtle spice notes of cinnamon and licorice. The palate is medium to full-bodied, revealing a concentrated core of ripe black fruits, framed by velvety tannins and vibrant acidity. The finish is long and expansive, leaving a lasting impression of freshness and depth. This vintage is a blend of 56% Merlot, 41% Cabernet Sauvignon, and 3% Petit Verdot. It is expected to evolve gracefully over the next several decades, with an optimal drinking window from 2028 to 2055.

Accolades

  • James Suckling – 97 points
  • Wine Enthusiast – 97 points
  • Vinous (Antonio Galloni) – 96 points
  • The Wine Advocate (William Kelley) – 95+ points

Food Pairing

The 2021 Château Palmer's rich fruit profile and refined structure make it an excellent companion to dishes such as roasted lamb with rosemary, duck breast with a blackberry reduction, or a wild mushroom risotto. These pairings highlight the wine's depth and character, creating an unforgettable dining experience.

title: Chateau Margaux 2020
bodyHtml:
The final blend is very similar to those of the most recent vintages. The Grand Vin represents 36% of the harvest. There is a perfect balance between the density and the fineness of its tannins. Several factors contributed to making this a superb wine: homogenous flowering, summer conditions that favored small berries and therefore concentrated wines, and excellent harvesting conditions. 

Blend: 89% Cabernet Sauvignon, 8% Merlot, 2% Petit Verdot, 1% Cabernet Franc

99+ Points - James Suckling

So floral and perfumed with blackcurrants, blackberries and some asphalt. Full-bodied with super, fine tannins. Extremely refined with great length and intensity. The wonderful combination of refinement and power is already evident. Superb finish. Another great Margaux.

99 Points - Decanter

A brilliant Margaux; one that takes a sigh and then releases the huge floral, eucalyptus and crushed mint whoosh that comes in waves though the palate. You get the concentration of the vintage in an entirely positive light, with a suave softness to the tannins that makes it stand head and shoulders above many others. Plenty in common with the 1996 vintage - the knitted down tannins, the completeness, the juicy blackcurrant purity and acidity on the finish, and the certainty of long ageing. Real clarity of flavour. Alcohol level is lower than both the 2018 and 2019, but tannins and anthocyanins are at the same level as in 2018. 36% of overall harvest, and 1% Petit Verdot completes the blend.

97+ Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2020 Château Margaux is a brilliant young wine, unfurling in the glass with aromas of dark berries and cherries mingled with hints of rose petals, iris, burning embers and pencil lead. Medium to full-bodied, deep and concentrated, with terrific tension, beautifully refined tannins and a long, penetration finish, this is a vibrant, dynamic Margaux that stands out as the most classically proportioned wine of the 2018, 2019 and 2020 trio.

97+ Points - Jeb Dunnuck

As to the Grand Vin, the 2020 Chateau Margaux is 89% Cabernet Sauvignon, 8% Merlot, and the rest Petit Verdot and Cabernet Franc, pulled from a tiny 36% of the total production, that spent 20 months in new barrels. It has that classic Chateau Margaux sense of elegance and complexity and offers full-bodied aromas and flavors of ripe currants, blueberries, acacia flowers, crushed stone, and sandalwood that develop with time in the glass. With remarkable purity as well as flawless balance, it's a seriously concentrated, powerful 2020 that still just glides across the palate with no hard edges, silky tannins, and a great finish. I love everything about this wine. It's going to flirt with perfection in 7-8 years and evolve for 50-75 years. It actually reminds me slightly of the 2016.

title: Vega Sicilia Unico 2013
bodyHtml:
The 2013 vintage of Vega Sicilia Unico is a powerful yet elegant expression from the Ribera del Duero region in Spain. Made predominantly from 97% Tempranillo (Tinto Fino) with a touch of 3% Cabernet Sauvignon, this wine exemplifies finesse with long aging potential.

Colour: Inky garnet with vibrant edges, indicating both depth and youth.

Aroma: It opens with complex aromas of poached plums, dark cherries, and tea leaves, complemented by hints of graphite, milk chocolate, and caramel.

Palate: The wine is medium-to-full-bodied, offering a silky texture with firm yet creamy tannins. Flavors of ripe red and black fruits are intertwined with notes of tobacco, oak, and a touch of mint tea, showing both richness and freshness.

Body: Full-bodied with precise structure, balanced acidity, and an underlying freshness that ensures longevity.

Finish: The finish is long and complex, with notes of mocha and star anise lingering gracefully.

This wine reflects Vega Sicilia's commitment to meticulous winemaking and is a great choice for collectors and enthusiasts alike.

title: Chateau Latour Premier Grand Cru Classe 2015
bodyHtml:
Château Latour 2010 originates from France, within the Bordeaux region and the world-renowned Pauillac subregion on the Left Bank. Classified as one of the original four Premier Grand Cru Classé (First Growth) estates in the historic 1855 Bordeaux Classification, Latour sits on a unique 92-hectare gravelly ridge overlooking the Gironde estuary. The absolute heart of the estate is L'Enclos, a famous 47-hectare parcel surrounding the château that provides the raw material for the Grand Vin. Under the ownership of François Pinault’s Artémis Group and the management of Jean-Garcin, Latour operates with an uncompromising, technical winemaking philosophy focused on extreme parcel selection, long-term cellaring, and biodynamic viticulture. The 2010 release—produced in a monumental, highly structured vintage—stands as one of the most powerful, precise, and ageworthy wines ever crafted in Pauillac.

Wine Description

This red wine presents an opaque, glass-staining deep dark garnet-purple appearance with an inky core and vibrant crimson reflections. It possesses a full-bodied, dense, and muscular structure defined by extraordinary textural weight, seamless concentration, and a wall of tightly knit, noble tannins. The sensory profile is highly intellectual, explosive, and multi-layered, opening with an intense bouquet of crème de cassis, wild blackberries, and dark plums, seamlessly intertwined with signature Pauillac notes of crushed graphite, pencil shavings, cigar box, wet stone minerality, fresh violets, and subtle smoked meats. On the expansive palate, it delivers a deeply concentrated stream of dark berry fruit framed by a piercing thread of refreshing natural acidity. The finish is epically long, architectural, and persistent, extending well past a minute with lingering notes of dark cocoa, crushed rocks, and savory tobacco.

  • Varietal Composition: 90.5% Cabernet Sauvignon, 8.5% Merlot, 0.5% Cabernet Franc, and 0.5% Petit Verdot. Only 36% of the estate's total harvest was selected for the Grand Vin in 2010.

  • Stylistic Notes: Hand-harvested with rigorous block-by-block selection, the grapes were destemmed and fermented in temperature-controlled, thermo-regulated stainless steel vats. The wine aged for approximately 18 to 22 months in 100% new French oak barrels.

  • ABV: 14.4%.

  • Organic Status: While the estate was mid-transition toward full organic and biodynamic conversion during the 2010 vintage (achieving full official organic certification in 2015), this release was farmed using sustainable, chemical-free, and natural canopy management techniques.

Food Pairing

The immense structural concentration, powerful tannic framework, and aristocratic graphite-fruit complexity of this historic First Growth require rich, elevated gastronomy.

  • Prime Meats: Pairs magnificently with dry-aged prime ribeye, roasted rack of lamb with rosemary and garlic, slow-braised beef short ribs, or tenderloin of beef served with a black truffle jus.

  • Game & Fowl: Ideal alongside pan-roasted duck breast with a dark currant reduction, roasted venison loin, or wild boar stew.

  • Earthy Specialties: Complements dishes featuring fresh black truffles, braised wild porcini mushrooms, and truffle-infused risottos or pastas.

  • Hard Cheeses: Matches gracefully with mature, firm cheeses such as 36-month Comté, aged Gouda, or Beaufort.

Vintage Quality

The 2010 vintage in Bordeaux is universally acclaimed as a generational masterpiece, defined by a dry, sunny summer with cool nights that preserved natural malic acidity while driving grape skins to extreme phenolic concentration. At Château Latour, the deep gravel terraces over clay-limestone subsoils in L'Enclos regulated water supply perfectly, producing tiny, thick-skinned berries with high natural sugar and massive tannic density. Universally awarded perfect scores by major international wine critics upon release, the 2010 Latour is a slow-evolving titan. While entering the early stages of its long drinking window after extended decanting, its sheer power and structural grip guarantee a cellaring potential of 60 to 100 years.

title: Bond Melbury 2020
bodyHtml:
Bond Melbury is one of Bond’s single-vineyard wines, sourced from a hillside site northeast of Rutherford. Known for its refined structure and expressive character, the 2020 vintage reflects the vineyard’s clay-rich soils, which enhance the wine’s depth and complexity. The vintage showcases remarkable purity of fruit, elegance, and minerality, embodying Bond’s commitment to producing site-driven wines of the highest quality.

Tasting Notes

Color: Deep ruby with violet reflections, showing intensity and depth.
Nose: Aromas of black cherries, cassis, and blueberries, layered with notes of graphite, crushed violets, cedar, and a touch of baking spice.
Palate: Silky yet powerful, featuring rich dark fruit, mocha, and anise, balanced by refined tannins and a precise mineral core. The wine has remarkable freshness and depth, reflecting the exceptional vineyard site.
Finish: Long and persistent, with lingering dark fruit and a fine-grained, polished texture.

Accolades

  • James Suckling: 98 points
  • Decanter: 96 points
  • Vinous (Antonio Galloni): 95 points
  • Jeb Dunnuck: 92 points

Optimal Drinking Window

2026–2045. While already showing depth and balance, extended aging will enhance its complexity and finesse.

Serving Suggestions

Decanting: 2–3 hours to allow the wine to fully express its aromatics and texture.
Serving Temperature: 16–18°C (60–64°F) for optimal enjoyment.
Pairings: Ideal with dry-aged ribeye, roasted duck, or wild mushroom risotto. Complements aged cheeses like Parmigiano-Reggiano or aged Gouda.

title: Bond Pluribus 2019
bodyHtml:
Bond's Pluribus vineyard is situated at elevations between 1,137 and 1,327 feet on Spring Mountain, encompassing a 7-acre site with steep exposures to the north, east, and southeast. The decomposed volcanic soils and surrounding conifer forest contribute to the wine's distinctive character. The 2019 vintage exemplifies the vineyard's signature power and concentration, delivering a wine with remarkable depth and complexity.

Tasting Notes
Color: Deep garnet-purple.
Nose: Expressive aromas of blackcurrants, black cherries, and blackberry pie, complemented by notes of cedar, charcoal, tar, pencil lead, and fragrant earth.
Palate: Full-bodied with a rock-solid structure of firm, grainy tannins and vibrant freshness supporting the generous black fruit flavors.
Finish: Long and layered, leaving a lingering mineral impression.

Accolades

  • Jeb Dunnuck: 100 points
  • James Suckling: 99 points
