  • Decanter: 98 points
  • Vinous (Antonio Galloni): 98 points
  • Robert Parker's Wine Advocate: 97 points

Optimal Drinking Window
2025–2050. While approachable in its youth, this wine will continue to evolve and gain complexity with extended cellaring.

Serving Suggestions
Decanting: 3 hours to allow the wine to fully express its aromatics and structure.
Serving Temperature: 16–18°C (60–64°F) for optimal enjoyment.
Pairings: Ideal with roasted game meats, grilled ribeye steak, or aged cheeses like Comté and Gouda.

title: Chateau Mouton Rothschild 2008
bodyHtml:
The wine has a dense, very dark color. On the nose, it offers a fine array of aromas in which red fruit, blackberry and blackcurrant mingle harmoniously with notes of violet and cedarwood. Quick and powerful on the palate, it releases silky, creamy tannins. Château Mouton Rothschild 2008 will be one of the most successful vintages of the early years of this century.

96 Points - Wine Enthusiast

A rich wine, opulent in character. There is power here, with richness of fruit and texture. It is both serious side and exuberant, with its bursting black berry fruits. 

96 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

The 2008 Mouton Rothschild checks in as a blend of 83% Cabernet Sauvignon and 17% Merlot brought up in mostly new barrels. Undeniably one of the top wines in the vintage, it offers a rare opulence and sexiness in its awesome bouquet of crème de cassis, Asian spices, chocolate, and crushed flowers. Deep, full-bodied, powerful, and still young, it fills the mouth with fruit, has sweet tannin, and a great finish. It's still ruby/plum-colored, with no signs of evolution, but is far from unapproachable and is drinking incredibly well today. It will keep for another two decades.

96 Points - Decanter

Another hit, although this is not as glamorous as some vintages of Mouton. The expression here is just a little more Pauillac, rather than Mouton. Layers of blackberry and grilled almonds are marked by a touch of austerity in the Cabernet which I almost never find in this wine. It remains a beautiful Mouton in a vintage where you don't always get this level of texture and expression. It's still young - we are actually nowhere near lift off yet.

95 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Tasted at the Mouton-Rothschild vertical in London, the 2008 Mouton Rothschild has always been in the shadow of the ensuing couple of vintages, but I was not the only person at this tasting that commented upon the class in show here. It replicated previous showings: cedar and graphite present and correct, though accompanied by something a little more exotic - eucalyptus maybe? The palate is beautifully balanced, very detailed and extremely fresh. This conveys so much energy and animation before reverting towards a more classic and structured, pencil lead finish. Those in the know will stash up on the 2008 Mouton Rothschild because it is destined to turn into one of the "dark horses" of the decade. 

94 Points - James Suckling

Aromas of roasted fruit plus hints of grilled meat and chocolate. Full body, firm and chewy tannins and bright acidity. Tangy and lively. Needs time still to come together to soften the tannins. A little hard. 

92 Points - Wine Spectator

This shows the cool, leafy profile of the vintage, with fresh tobacco and bay notes standing out, while the core of plum and blackberry fruit continues to fill in behind them. Shows wet earth and singed alder elements through the finish. This has nearly dropped its angular feel and is developing well, with just a slight twinge of crisp acidity on the finish.

title: Tesseron Vineyards 'PYM-RAE' 2019
bodyHtml:
98 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

The 2019 Chateau Pym-Rae is a textbook Mount Veeder Cabernet with its exotic red, blue, and black fruits as well as complex notes of mountain scrub brush, lavender, tobacco, and lead pencil. Hitting the palate with full-bodied richness, it has a layered, elegant mouthfeel, ultra-fine yet substantial tannins, and a great finish.

97 Points - James Suckling

Extremely aromatic with flowers, currants, plums, and cocoa. Full-bodied with compacted fruit and ultra-fine tannins giving it a suppleness and finesse, yet it’s very structured and long. Turns to sandalwood, hazelnut and subtle currants. Round and velvety texture at the end. Slightly deeper and denser. 

96+ Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Impressively ripe and concentrated, it offers scents of cassis, violet and hints of dark chocolate on the nose, while the full-bodied palate is silky-smooth, framed by dusty tannins on the long, focused finish. Yes, it's somewhat Bordeaux-like in shape, but it's fully ripe, with black cherries emerging on the finish, along with the slightest touch of alcoholic warmth.

title: Chateau de la Tour Clos Vougeot 'Hommage a Jean Morin' Grand Cru 2019
bodyHtml:
95+ Points - Rober Parker's Wine Advocate

Even more reserved than the Vieilles Vignes bottling, the 2019 Clos Vougeot Grand Cru Hommage à Jean Morin unwinds in the glass with notes of plums, smoky berry fruit, rich soil tones, spices, orange rind and cherries. Full-bodied, layered and concentrated, it's deep and textural, with prodigious reserves of fruit and rich, powdery tannin. Lively and perfumed, I can't wait to revisit it in the bottle.

title: Chateau Smith Haut Lafitte Rouge 2022 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
From France’s Bordeaux region, specifically Pessac Léognan in Graves, Château Smith Haut Lafitte is a distinguished Grand Cru Classé estate. Owned by Florence and Daniel Cathiard since 1990, the château has become renowned for its environmentally mindful approach and dedication to crafting wines that combine power with elegance. With a history dating back to the 14th century, the estate consistently delivers wines that reflect both its rich terroir and forward-looking philosophy.

Wine Description

This 2022 vintage presents a deep, intense ruby colour. The nose is layered with cassis, blackberry, and dark cherry, supported by notes of graphite, cedar, mocha, and subtle floral tones of violet and lavender. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied and dense, with concentrated black fruit, spice, and earthy mineral freshness. The tannins are firm yet refined, leading to a long, elegant finish.

Accolades

  • James Suckling - 97+ points

  • Decanter - 97 points 

  • Jeb Dunnuck - 96 points

  • Vinous - 95+ points

  • Robert Parker's Wine Advocate - 94+ points

Food Pairing

Ideal pairings include grilled ribeye steak, braised lamb shank, or roasted venison, where the wine’s firm tannins and layered complexity stand up beautifully to rich proteins. For a refined option, pair with duck breast in a red wine reduction.

title: Armand Heitz Corton Charlemagne Grand Cru 2018
bodyHtml:
In 2018, Domaine Heitz-Lochardet crafted a masterpiece with their Armand Heitz Corton-Charlemagne Grand Cru. This exceptional Burgundy white wine showcases the essence of its terroir with unparalleled elegance. The year blessed the vineyard with ideal weather conditions, resulting in grapes of exceptional quality.

On the border between the Cote de Nuits and the Côte de Beaune, between 280 and 330 meters in altitude, the Corton-Charlemagne is largely exposed to the southwest. This vine was offered by Emperor Charlemagne in 775 to the collegiate church of Saint-Andoche de Saulieu.  

The wine exudes a complex bouquet of citrus blossoms, honeyed notes, and subtle oak, leading to a palate of exquisite balance, rich minerality, and vibrant acidity. Its lingering finish leaves a lasting impression, making it a collector's dream.

title: Chateau Lafite Rothschild 2014
bodyHtml:
The nose is closed at first, then the fruit is expressed, with a slightly dominant woodiness. On the palate, the texture is tight and dense. Then the heart of the wine comes through, with solid, compact balance. Very dense finish, and yet the tannins are "almost light and airy"! Great length with long, lingering flavors.

98 Points - James Suckling

The aromas of stones, oyster shell, blackcurrants and mushrooms are very intense. Full-bodied, dense and powerful with lots of blackberries. Great finish. Super energy and depth. 

97 Points - Wine Enthusiast

This is a major wine. It has enormous tension, structure and a core of dark tannins. Amid all this, the wine is also packed with fruit and concentrated blackberry and black-plum flavors. It will age slowly and steadily with its enormous structure and concentration. 

95 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2014 Lafite-Rothschild, tasted with head winemaker Eric Kohler, has retained that very opulent and outgoing bouquet that dare I say actually reminded me of Mouton-Rothschild. There are layers of blackberry and boysenberry fruit, still that hint of juniper berry, certainly a more extrovert Lafite-Rothschild compared to recent vintages. The palate is medium-bodied with crisp tannin, very focused and quite linear, again with plenty of black fruit laced with cedar and tobacco. 

95 Points - Wine Spectator

Reserved for now, but the core of cassis, bitter plum and raspberry coulis flavors is pure and energetic, while extra black tea, iron and singed alder notes fill in steadily through the finish. This has a very focused, streamlined feel overall, yet there’s serious depth for the cellar. 

95 Points - Decanter

Lovely floral nose and almost understated compared to Mouton -? just a line of clarity and fruit purity that doesn't need description. Fine tannins and that wild violet lift over a firm textured depth of fruit, all in perfect harmony.

title: Bond Vecina 2020
bodyHtml:
Perched on an 11-acre hillside in the western foothills of Oakville, Bond’s Vecina vineyard is known for its rugged terrain and iron-rich volcanic soils. This distinctive site produces wines of remarkable intensity, structure, and longevity. The 2020 vintage captures the essence of Vecina’s power and depth, offering a complex interplay of dark fruit, minerality, and finely woven tannins.

Tasting Notes

Color: Deep purple-black.
Nose: Vivacious aromas of warm cassis, blackberry preserves, and juicy black plums, with underlying notes of wild sage, fragrant earth, and truffles.
Palate: Full-bodied and tightly wound, featuring layers of black berry and earthy flavors, supported by ripe, grainy tannins.
Finish: Long and lingering, with a minerally note.

Accolades

  • Vinous (Antonio Galloni): 95 points
  • James Suckling: 99 points

Optimal Drinking Window

2026–2050. While approachable now, this wine will benefit from additional aging to fully develop its complexity and depth.

Serving Suggestions

Decanting: 2–3 hours to allow the wine to fully express its aromatics and texture.
Serving Temperature: 16–18°C (60–64°F) for optimal enjoyment.
Pairings: Complements dishes such as grilled ribeye steak, roasted lamb, or aged cheeses.

title: Ulysses Cabernet Sauvignon 2019
bodyHtml:
Ulysses vineyard is situated along Napa Valley's Oakville bench at the foot of the Mayacamas range. This historic vineyard was part of the original Charles Hopper Ranch in the 1800s and was purchased by Christian Moueix in 2008. Since then, they have undertaken meticulous vineyard restoration, carefully studying the gravelly, clay loam soils and the property's microclimates. As part of their efforts toward sustainability and environmental stewardship, they dry farm to enhance root depth and resistance to drought as well as to further develop in their wine the character of an exceptional terroir.

Homer's Odyssey is the epic tale of Ulysses, who, after the Trojan War, travails to return to his homeland and family, a voyage of ten years. Christian Moueix, inspired by Ulysses' unending devotion to his quest, embarks on a new journey to produce a distinctive wine from the Ulysses vineyard in Oakville.

title: Hundred Acre Cabernet Sauvignon 'Wraith' 2018
bodyHtml:
One of California’s (perhaps the world’s) most flamboyant, talented, contrarian wine producers is Napa Valley’s Jayson Woodbridge, the owner of Hundred Acre winery. Woodbridge has been running in high gear since his debut 2000.

Wraith is a fusion of all three Hundred Acre single vineyard estates, but not just three wines blended together, that would be boring and muddled. Winemaker Jason Woodbridge chose these barrels for their perfect expression of only the ultra-unique qualities of the vintage and vineyard sites. These qualities are carefully woven together to create a super-intense, wildly fine structured, matchless expression of Hundred Acre, while at the same time still being able to see clearly the singular and exceptional characteristics of ARK, Kayli Morgan and Few and Far Between single vineyards that year through a single lens.

98+ Points - Jeb Dunnuck

The 2018 Cabernet Sauvignon Wraith is one of those wines that would be a perfect example of the expression “iron fist in a velvet glove.” Full-bodied, concentrated, and powerful, it has that classic 2018 frame that carries pure darker currant and cassis fruits as well as complex notes of leather, licorice, and spring flowers. 

97+ Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

A blend of fruit from the three single vineyards, the 2018 Cabernet Sauvignon Wraith offers up more cherries and cranberries beautifully complemented by deep loam and mocha undertones. It's full-bodied, lush and velvety in texture, with a long, vibrant finish. It's even a bit tart.

title: Dal Forno Amarone della Valpolicella 2009
bodyHtml:
Subtle aromatic things that range from black cherry, blueberry to chocolate anticipate the opulent expression of mature fruit that flows into the mouth. Nuances of truffle, tobacco and new leather wrap around the finish.

99 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The Dal Forno family considered the idea of releasing their Amarone ten years after the harvest. If that plan had been implemented, this would be the vintage on the market now. The 2009 Amarone della Valpolicella Monte Lodoletta is a full and generous expression that delivers thick lines and robust flavors of dried blackberry, camphor ash, exotic cedar wood, licorice and tarry road pavement. This vintage saw average temperatures throughout the growing season with a few hailstorms along the way. Very dry weather led to some mild drought in July and August, with ensuing ripening and concentration of the clusters. I found this monumental wine to be irresistible when I first tasted it five years ago, and I consider it to have improved since then. This is one of the most complete and comprehensive vintages produced at Dal Forno, and it gives us an ample 360-degree view onto the might, brawn and potential of this icon wine from the Veneto. Its evolutionary track shows no sign of slowing down.

98 Points - James Suckling

This is powerful and very rich with blueberries, flowers and hints of spices. Full body with velvety tannins and ripe fruits. Very beautiful and generous but not overdone. Superb.

94 Points - Wine Spectator

Rich, with aromatic herb and tarry smoke notes, this silky, supple red is framed by mouthwatering acidity and dusty tannins. Shows ripe and concentrated flavors of date, sun-dried cherry, forest floor and ground spice, displaying a sense of harmony and density that suggests a long future. The finish echoes the spice and sweet fruit character. Drink now through 2029.

title: Merryvale Profile 2019 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
Hailing from the United States, the Merryvale Profile 2019 originates in Napa Valley, California—specifically from the estate’s hillside Profile Estate Vineyard in St. Helena. Founded in 1983, Merryvale Vineyards is family-owned by the Schlatter family and is renowned for crafting Bordeaux-style wines with a deep respect for terroir and precision winemaking. The Profile label represents the pinnacle of the winery's production, focusing on power, structure, and age-worthiness.

Wine Description
The 2019 Profile is a robust and elegant Bordeaux-style red blend composed primarily of Cabernet Sauvignon, with smaller proportions of Petit Verdot, Cabernet Franc, and Malbec. Deep ruby in the glass, it opens with layered aromas of black cherry, cassis, graphite, and warm spice. On the palate, rich flavours of dark berries, espresso, and cocoa unfold with superb intensity and balance. Full-bodied and structured, the tannins are firm yet polished, leading into a long, savoury finish accented by minerality and toasted oak. The wine shows great freshness and precision, suggesting a cellar-worthy aging window through 2040.

Accolades
● Jeb Dunnuck - 96 points
● Wine Enthusiast - 95 points
● James Suckling - 94 points

Food Pairing
This bold and refined wine pairs beautifully with herb-crusted lamb, grilled ribeye steak, or braised short ribs. Its structure and depth also make it a compelling companion to aged cheddar or mushroom risotto. This pairing highlights the wine’s depth and character.

title: Chateau Gruaud Larose 2002
bodyHtml:
Chateau Gruaud Larose is an esteemed Second Growth estate located in the Saint Julien appellation of Bordeaux, France. Founded in 1725, the property has been overseen by several prominent families, including the Cordiers and currently the Merlaut family. The winery's philosophy emphasizes a deep bond between man and terroir, recently incorporating agroecological practices like organic and biodynamic agriculture to foster a sustainable ecosystem.

Wine Description

The 2002 Chateau Gruaud Larose displays a deep plum to purple colour. The sensory profile reveals elegant aromas of black cherry, cedar, and earthy tobacco, often accompanied by herbaceous and spice notes. On the palate, this medium-bodied wine offers a smooth mouthfeel with well-integrated tannins and a lingering finish. Composed of 57% Cabernet Sauvignon, 30% Merlot, 8% Cabernet Franc, and 5% Petit Verdot, it reflects a classic, understated style. While the optimal drinking window for this vintage was traditionally cited through 2018, its structural integrity allows it to be enjoyed for many years as a refined expression of Saint Julien.

Accolades

  • Wine Spectator - 89 points

  • Vinous - 91 points

  • Robert Parker - 90 points

title: Schrader Cabernet Sauvignon Beckstoffer To Kalon Library (2007, 2009, 2011) - 6 Bottles
bodyHtml:
This library 6 pack in wooden box includes: 

2 x Schrader Cabernet Sauvignon 'Beckstoffer To Kalon' 2007

2 x Schrader Cabernet Sauvignon 'Beckstoffer To Kalon' RBS 2009

2 x Schrader Cabernet Sauvignon 'Beckstoffer To Kalon' T6 2011

Originating from United States in the California region, specifically within the Oakville AVA appellation in Napa Valley, Schrader Cabernet Sauvignon 'Beckstoffer To Kalon' Library Collection represents an elite, rare, and benchmark presentation of modern Napa Valley Cabernet Sauvignon supremacy. Founded in 1998 by Fred Schrader, Schrader Cellars has earned unmatched critical acclaim, securing dozens of 100-point scores under the visionary hand of winemaking master Thomas Rivers Brown. Sourced exclusively from choice blocks within the legendary Beckstoffer To Kalon Vineyard in Oakville, these old-clone vines grow on benchland alluvial fan soils composed of deep gravel, loam, and volcanic clay. The winemaking philosophy centers on clone-specific micro-vinification, utilizing gentle destemming, native yeast fermentation, and maturation in 100% new French oak barrels (predominantly Darnajou and Taransaud) for 20 months. This rare 6 bottle Library Pack offers a rare comparative vertical featuring two bottles each of three defining Napa vintages: the opulent 2007, the expressive 2009, and the cool-climate, classic 2011.

Wine Description

The wines present in the glass with an opaque, deep dark garnet-purple core and rich crimson reflections along the rim. An expressive, multidimensional bouquet opens with noble aromas of creme de cassis, wild blackberry, black cherry, and plum compote, interwoven with sophisticated notes of graphite, crushed stone minerality, pipe tobacco, dark cocoa, sweet vanilla bean, and warm baking spice. On the palate, the collection offers full bodied, plush, and seamless depth, delivering concentrated flavours of black fruit preserves, dark chocolate, and savory earth, all supported by a bright, mouthwatering spine of natural acidity. Framed by rich, fine-grained, velvety tannins and an exceptionally opulent mid-palate structure, the collection concludes with long, persistent finishes marked by lingering cassis, mocha, and a clean gravelly mineral grip. Composed of 100% Cabernet Sauvignon, this 6 bottle library set (featuring 2 bottles each of 2007, 2009, and 2011) provides an incredible spectrum of drinking windows spanning 2024–2045+. Stylistically, it combines To Kalon's signature power, sweet fruit purity, and velvet texture with the distinct vintage signatures of a legendary Napa decade.

Accolades

Robert Parker Wine Advocate - 98 points (2007 Vintage).

Robert Parker Wine Advocate - 97 points (2009 Vintage).

Antonio Galloni - Vinous - 95 points (2009 Vintage).

Wine Spectator - 93 points (2011 Vintage).

title: Chateau Haut Brion 2006
bodyHtml:
Château Haut-Brion, the oldest First Growth estate in Bordeaux, has been producing world-class wines since the 16th century. Located in Pessac-Léognan, this iconic estate has set the benchmark for elegance and complexity in Bordeaux wines. Owned by the Dillon family since 1935, Château Haut-Brion has remained at the forefront of innovation while preserving its rich history and heritage.

The 2006 Château Haut-Brion is a blend of 57% Merlot, 41% Cabernet Sauvignon, and 2% Cabernet Franc, showcasing the estate’s skill in crafting harmonious wines. Deep ruby-red in colour, this vintage reveals a captivating bouquet of blackberry, red plum, cedar, leather, and hints of sage. On the palate, it is medium-bodied and velvety, with well-judged acidity and supple tannins. Flavours of kirsch, briary fruit, and earthy truffle unfold elegantly, leading to a long, savoury finish. While already showing great balance, this wine has the potential to age gracefully for another two decades.

This exceptional wine pairs beautifully with roasted lamb, wild game, or aged cheeses like Comté or Pecorino. These pairings enhance the wine’s depth and create an unforgettable dining experience.

The 2006 vintage was characterized by a cool growing season, which resulted in structured, tannin-driven wines with excellent ageing potential. Despite the challenges, Château Haut-Brion’s meticulous vineyard management and winemaking expertise yielded a wine of remarkable finesse and complexity, exemplifying the unique terroir of Pessac-Léognan.

title: Chateau Lafite Rothschild 2019
bodyHtml:
Château Lafite Rothschild, a jewel of the Médoc and one of the most esteemed First Growths in Bordeaux, continues its legacy of crafting wines of unparalleled elegance and finesse. With centuries of history, the estate’s vineyards are planted on exceptional gravelly terroir, producing wines that stand as benchmarks for Pauillac.

Wine Description

The 2019 vintage showcases a radiant deep garnet color, reflecting its youth and vibrancy. On the nose, it reveals an intricate bouquet of ripe blackberries, cassis, and dark cherries, interwoven with notes of cedar, graphite, and a subtle hint of fresh herbs. The palate is seamless, with velvety tannins and a refined structure. Layers of dark fruit, cocoa, and a touch of spice evolve gracefully, supported by a fresh acidity and mineral undertones. The finish is remarkably long, leaving a lasting impression of balance and sophistication.

Food Pairing

This wine is a sublime match for roasted duck, filet mignon with wild mushroom sauce, or aged Comté. Together, they enhance the wine's complexity and elegance.

Vintage Quality

The 2019 vintage is celebrated for its near-perfect growing conditions, producing wines of exceptional balance and purity. Château Lafite Rothschild 2019 is a testament to the estate’s mastery, offering both immediate appeal and immense aging potential.

title: Will Harlan 'Promontory' 2019
bodyHtml:
Taking points from some of Europe’s most successful long running wine families, the Harlans were inspired to create several unique experiences at their wineries and to pass on leadership and wisdom to future generations within the family.

With that being said Bill’s son, Will Harlan, is the Estate Director for Promontory and oversees everything from farming methods to hospitality in the tasting room. These wines reflect the uncompromising quality of Napa Valley established through tradition and a revolution of an entire family’s philosophy.

100 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

Ripe black fruits, chocolatey, lead pencil shaving, roasted herbs, and tobacco are just some of its nuances, and this beauty hits the palate with full-bodied richness, a deep, layered, concentrated mid-palate, ultra-fine tannins, and an incredible finish. It doesn’t get any better. This has the class of a First Growth from Bordeaux paired with a Napa sense of texture and fruit.

99 Points - Decanter

Beguiling scents of wild flowers, dark bramble fruits and some aniseed notes on the nose. Textured and fleshy, full and bright, but sleek and lean too, the tannins have real bit and angles giving this a little bit of an austere frame. Nothing overdone or too ripe about this though and in a sene atypical, but I love the finesse on show and the reigned-in sense to the flavours. Well shaped, well constructed, deep and layered, so dark and finely knitted. Not seductive but almost sultry in a severe way. I love the energy, the focus and the overall expression. Almost hands off, great acidity, piercing with pristine fruit.

99 Points - James Suckling

Purple-fruit, dark-licorice and conifer aromas follow through to a medium to full body with firmness and a linear flow that goes on for minutes. Racy tannins and focus.

98+ Points - Vinous

97 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

title: Chateau Haut Brion 2017
bodyHtml:
99 Points - Wine Enthusiast

The tannins are the secret of this bold wine granting longevity and great structure. At the same time, the ripe blackberry fruits are rich yet bright and fresh. The wine will take time to mature. Drink from 2025. 

97 Points - Decanter

A hugely captivating wine, one of the contenders for red of the vintage. There's an incredible plush, dense texture to the fruit here, with just the slightest pulling back on the final section that suggests the damson, cassis and black cherry fruit is not at the full extent of ripeness seen in 2016 and 2015, but there is absolutely no question that this is a successful, rich and well-expressed wine. It's extremely powerful and well constructed, with great tannins and a succulence which grows through the palate.

title: Gaja Barbaresco 'Sori Tildin' 2021
bodyHtml:
Gaja Barbaresco 'Sorì Tildin' 2021 is a single-vineyard wine from the renowned Gaja winery in Piedmont, Italy. The term "Sorì" refers to a south-facing hillside, while "Tildin" honors Clotilde Rey, the grandmother of Angelo Gaja, reflecting the family's deep-rooted heritage in winemaking. The 2021 vintage in Barbaresco benefited from favorable growing conditions, resulting in wines of great structure and balance.

Tasting Notes

  • Color: Bright ruby-garnet.
  • Aroma: Aromas of cherry, strawberry, rose, iron, tobacco, and sweet spices.
  • Palate: Rich and almost creamy in texture, with detailed flavors of cherry, strawberry, rose, iron, and tobacco, supported by lively acidity and dense tannins. Balanced and harmonious, this wine shows exceptional aging potential.

Accolades

  • Wine Spectator: 97 Points
  • Wine Enthusiast: 97 Points
  • Falstaff: 98 Points

Serving Suggestions

  • Temperature: Serve at 16-18°C (60-64°F).
  • Decanting: Decant for at least two hours before serving to allow the wine to open up and reveal its full complexity.
  • Food Pairings: Complements dishes such as truffle risotto, braised lamb, and aged cheeses.

Cellaring Potential

While approachable in its youth, this wine will benefit from further aging, with an optimal drinking window from 2027 to 2041.

title: Bond Vecina 2019
bodyHtml:
The 2019 Bond Vecina is sourced from an 11-acre east-facing vineyard situated in the western foothills of Oakville, just southeast of the Bond winery. The terraced slopes of this site are composed of iron-rich, volcanic soils, contributing to the wine's distinctive power and intensity. The 2019 vintage benefited from favorable growing conditions, resulting in a wine that harmoniously balances depth, complexity, and elegance.

Tasting Notes
Color: Deep garnet-purple.
Nose: Expressive aromas of blackcurrants, black cherries, and blackberry pie, complemented by notes of cedar, charcoal, tar, pencil lead, and fragrant earth.
Palate: Full-bodied with a rock-solid structure of firm, grainy tannins and vibrant freshness supporting the generous black fruit flavors.
Finish: Long and layered, leaving a lingering mineral impression.

Accolades

  • James Suckling: 99 points
  • Robert Parker's Wine Advocate: 99 points
  • Jeb Dunnuck: 100 points
  • Decanter: 99 points
  • Vinous (Antonio Galloni): 98 points

Optimal Drinking Window
2025–2050. While approachable in its youth, this wine will continue to evolve and gain complexity with extended cellaring.

Serving Suggestions
Decanting: 3 hours to allow the wine to fully express its aromatics and structure.
Serving Temperature: 16–18°C (60–64°F) for optimal enjoyment.
Pairings: Ideal with roasted game meats, grilled ribeye steak, or aged cheeses like Comté and Gouda.

title: Dal Forno Romano Amarone della Valpolicella 2008
bodyHtml:
Subtle aromatic hints, that range from black cherry, blueberry to chocolate, anticipate the opulent expression of mature fruit that flows into the mouth with inadvertent persistence. Nuances of truffle, tobacco and new leather wrap around the finish.

In order to create this wine, the finest bunches of grapes are selected, after which a meticulous manual control is carried out to eliminate all grapes that do not meet the standards required. The selected grapes are then placed in plastic plateaux and are then left to rest for 90 days in large open rooms, where an innovative ventilation system helps maintain an elevated and thorough air flow.

Fermentation takes place in steel tanks at a controlled temperature of around 28°, which are equipped with a sophisticated computerized system which allows for automated punching for a period of around 15 days, including the final maceration which takes two days.

After decantation in the middle of January, the Amarone, which still contains some residual sugar, is placed into new barriques, where it begins a slow fermentation process which will last for a further 18 months. The total amount of time that it remains in the barriques is 36 months.

96 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Production was skipped over in 2007 due to extreme hail damage. The fruit that would normally be destined to Amarone went to the lower tier Valpolicella Superiore instead. The 2008 Amarone della Valpolicella Monte Lodoletta marks a return to a slightly cooler vintage with a longer growing season slowed down during the summer's moderate temperatures. Indeed, harvest was wrapped up during the first days of November. The blend is mostly Corvina, at about 60%, with smaller parts Corvinone, Rondinella, Croatina and Oseleta. The new Dal Forno winery was finished in 2008, complete with the unique vacuum-sealed fermentation tasks that help to avoid any intrusive oxygen during winemaking. Indeed, this wine is balanced and elegant with fruit that is still crunchy and very much alive. The tannins are firm and nicely integrated into the wine's thick, fleshy consistency. This vintage is characterized by a very elegant and graceful approach, which must be taken into context given the enormity of a wine of this caliber. Happily, there is no doubt that this vintage should still evolve steadily over time.

94 Points - Wine Spectator

Game and ashy smoke details lead the way in this ripe red, followed by juicy plumped cherry, date, dark chocolate and woodsy spice notes on the plush-textured palate. Velvety tannins give this some brawn, but this is beautifully knit and balanced, showing an overall sense of finesse. Delivers a lasting finish of fruit and spice. Drink now through 2033.

94 Points - James Suckling

An all American oak vintage. A treat to taste this from winemaker Marco's cellar. A swathe of cherry liqueur, menthol, mint and eucalyptus verging into the alpine amaro spectrum. Fascinating, complex, somewhat sweet, and to be churlish, ever so slightly drying. A fascinating and compelling wine all the same.

94 Points - Decanter

This is a lighter, more elegant style from Dal Forno, reflecting the cooler vintage conditions in 2008. The juicy palate is balanced by a wonderful level of structure, with slightly generic but ripe plum and hedgerow fruit with violet lift. A textural mid-palate leads onto a creamy cherry fruit finish. Drinking Window 2018 - 2040.

90 Points - Wine Enthusiast

Dense and extracted, this conveys aromas of Asian spice, prune, raisin, black pepper and espresso. The concentrated, thick palate delivers black plum, raisin, blueberry extract and crème brûlée alongside smooth tannins and soft acidity. The heat of evident alcohol and syrupy texture would make this a nice wine that inspires meditation.

title: Chateau Lafite Rothschild 2012
bodyHtml:
Chateau Lafite Rothschild is a world-renowned First Growth estate located in the Pauillac appellation of the Médoc, France. Since 1868, the property has been owned by the Rothschild family, specifically the Domaines Barons de Rothschild branch. The winery’s philosophy is rooted in a commitment to elegance and finesse, utilizing a unique terroir dominated by deep gravel to produce wines that are celebrated for their longevity and structural harmony.

Wine Description

The 2012 Chateau Lafite Rothschild exhibits a deep, dark ruby colour with purple highlights. The aromatic profile is nuanced and sophisticated, offering notes of cedar, graphite, and blackcurrant, intertwined with subtle hints of violets and tobacco. On the palate, the wine is medium bodied and remarkably balanced, showing refined, silky tannins and a core of fresh red and black fruits. The finish is long, clean, and persistent, displaying the classic 'Lafite' elegance. This vintage is a blend of 91% Cabernet Sauvignon and 9% Merlot. While approachable now, its optimal drinking window is expected to last until at least 2040.

Accolades

  • Wine Spectator - 94 points

  • Vinous - 95 points

  • Decanter - 96 points

title: Carruades de Lafite 2018
bodyHtml:
Château Lafite Rothschild’s second wine, Carruades de Lafite presents similar characteristics to the Grand Vin, but with its own personality linked to a higher proportion of Merlot and to specific plots that are used to produce Carruades. The name comes from the Carruades plateau, a group of plots acquired in 1845 just next to the vines on the Château hilltop.

96 Points - James Suckling    This is an extremely fine-grained Carraudes with a complex character of chocolate, walnut, cedar and a hint of graphite. Medium-to full-bodied, tight and chewy but, at the same time, agile and light. Savory finish. Special.

96 Points - Jeb Dunnuck      The second wine of Lafite is the 2018 Carruades De Lafite (56.5% Cabernet Sauvignon, 38% Merlot, and the rest Cabernet Franc). This ruby/purple colored effort offers classic Lafite elegance and purity as well as lead pencil, red and black currants, and tobacco. Elegant, silky, ultra-fine and beautifully balanced, with ripe tannins, it's a smoking second wine that’s going to keep for 2-3 decades.

95 Points - Wine Enthusiast     This is a ripe, juicy wine that's rich and generous in texture, with light touches of spice and fine tannins. It has both weight and freshness, giving a wine that is elegant and ripe.

94 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate     The 2018 Carruades de Lafite is composed of 56.5% Cabernet Sauvignon, 38% Merlot and 5.5% Cabernet Franc. The Merlot was harvested September 17-24, the Cabernet Sauvignon was harvested September 25 to October 5, and the Cabernet Franc was harvested September 24. Deep garnet-purple coloured, it reveals a very serious nose of pencil shavings, black tea, violets and dark chocolate with earthy wafts of underbrush and mossy bark over a core of warm cassis, blackberry preserves and black raspberries. Medium to full-bodied, the densely packed, black-fruited palate is laced with loads of compelling mineral sparks with a firm, grainy frame and beautiful freshness to lift the long, earthy finish.

93 Points - Decanter     This has rich fruit notes with exotic spices, a silky texture and a seductive approachability that clearly translates the higher than usual amount of Merlot in the blend this year, as with Petit Mouton. It’s a wine that is bound to make a lot of people happy but also means that whereas Lafite is archetypal Lafite, this is perhaps a less classic Carruades. It still has the tannins of Pauillac, and as so often is the case this year the first time you taste feels easy then they steal up on you and start to layer but this is flexible and approachable, with a menthol finish. Carruades is continuing to benefit from the techniques brought to it under in-house R&D technician Manuela Brando which include honing vineyard mapping, detailing smaller plots and tracking vine vigour, all of which are particularly useful since Carruades' soils are less consistent than those of the main wine. 39% of production.

93 Points - Vinous     The 2018 Carruades de Lafite was picked from September 17 until October 5. I prefer the bouquet to that of the 2017; it offers more fruit, more purity and perfume, and an almost floral style, touches of pressed violets infusing the black fruit. The palate is medium-bodied with fine tannin and well-matched acidity. There is cohesion here, and disarming rondeur on the supple, lightly spiced finish. A dash of white pepper lingers on the aftertaste. Excellent. 

17.5/20 Points - Jancis Robinson     Dark core with narrow dark rim. Very ripe but not overripe black fruit. Rich and savoury at the same time, a really dark, elegant wine with good acidity. The tannins here are notable for their extreme finesse, dry, wonderful texture, with a hint of clean dry dark chocolate on the finish. Fabulous tannins. Juicy and so elegant at the same time. Light on its feet even with this concentration. High score is especially for the tannins.

title: Chateau Leoville Las Cases 2022
bodyHtml:
Château Léoville Las Cases 2022 originates from France, within the Bordeaux region and the prestigious Saint-Julien appellation on the Left Bank. Managed by the Delon family (Domaines Delon) and directed by Jean-Hubert Delon, this legendary estate—officially classified as a Second Growth (Deuxième Grand Cru Classé) in 1855—is universally recognized as operating at First Growth quality levels. The vineyard’s crown jewel is L'Enclos, an 80-hectare walled parcel featuring deep quaternary gravel and clay soils overlooking the Gironde estuary, directly adjacent to Château Latour. The estate's winemaking philosophy relies on rigorous parcel selection, moderate extraction ("infusion over extraction"), and precise balance. In the historic 2022 vintage, Léoville Las Cases delivered a monument of power, vertical precision, and unusual youthful charm.

Wine Description

This red wine presents an opaque, inky ruby-purple appearance in the glass with vibrant violet reflections. It possesses a full-bodied, deeply concentrated, and multi-dimensional structure underpinned by an extraordinary mineral tension and seamless, cashmere-like texture. The sensory profile is intense and brilliantly delineated, opening with an intoxicating bouquet of cassis, black cherries, wild blueberries, and crushed violets, layered over signature notes of graphite, pencil lead, Cuban tobacco, cedar, crushed stones, and subtle Asian spices. On the palate, it exhibits a massive, fruit-dense core balanced by a surprisingly fresh, cool thread of acidity and a wall of ultra-polished, fine-grained tannins. The finish is endless, extending past the 60-second mark with lingering notes of dark fruits, licorice, and stony minerality.

  • Varietal Composition: 83.5% Cabernet Sauvignon, 10.5% Cabernet Franc, and 6% Merlot. Notably, this vintage features a rare higher proportion of Cabernet Franc than Merlot in the Grand Vin.

  • Stylistic Notes: Hand-harvested between September 8 and September 30. The wine underwent precise fermentation with consultant Eric Boissenot, followed by aging for 18 months in 84–85% new French oak barrels.

  • ABV: 14.25% (pH 3.80).

title: Chateau Montelena Sauvignon Blanc 2024
bodyHtml:
This elegant white wine originates from the Napa Valley AVA in California, primarily sourced from a 40-year-old vineyard in the Oak Knoll District. Chateau Montelena, an iconic estate established in 1882, is world-renowned for its victory in the 1976 "Judgment of Paris," which fundamentally changed the global perception of California wine. The winemaking philosophy, led by Bo Barrett and Matthew Crafton, emphasizes restraint and site-driven precision, eschewing malolactic fermentation to preserve the grape's natural acidity and varietal purity.

Wine Description

The Chateau Montelena Sauvignon Blanc presents a beautiful pale gold hue with brilliant clarity. The nose is highly aromatic and fresh, featuring classic notes of grapefruit, white pepper, and fresh-cut flowers. On the palate, the wine threads the needle between Californian warmth and traditional varietal character; the inclusion of Sémillon adds a luxurious texture described as lemon curd and ripe pear, while a touch of Sauvignon Gris provides a distinctive spike of mid-palate acidity. It is characterized by a "mouth-watering" minerality and a clean finish with subtle toasty undertones from brief oak contact.

title: Jim Barry Shiraz 'The Armagh' - Mixed Vintage 3 Bottle Pack (2008, 2009, 2013)
bodyHtml:
Australia is the country of origin for this wine collection, hailing from the Clare Valley region in South Australia. Founded in 1959 by Jim Barry and his wife Sue, Jim Barry Wines remains a family owned benchmark of Australian viticulture. The iconic 'The Armagh' vineyard, planted in 1968 on north facing slopes, produces exceptionally low yields of concentrated fruit that reflect the winery's commitment to expressive single vineyard Shiraz.

Wine Description

Jim Barry Shiraz 'The Armagh' Mixed Vintage 3 Bottle Pack 2008 2009 2013 showcases three exceptional expressions of 100% Shiraz from this benchmark vineyard. Across all three vintages, the wine displays an opaque, deep garnet to inky magenta colour.

  • 2008 Vintage: Offers rich aromas of dark plum, milk chocolate, and crushed blueberry with overtones of mint and savory leather. The full-bodied palate delivers dense black fruit, muscular yet supple tannins, and a long, warming finish.

    • James Suckling: 96 points

    • Robert Parker (The Wine Advocate): 95 points

  • 2009 Vintage: Opens with intense aromas of dark cherry, star anise, dried herbs, and cocoa. On the palate, it exhibits a plush, seamless texture with ripe black fruit, fine integrated tannins, and balanced acidity.

    • Robert Parker (The Wine Advocate): 96 points

    • James Suckling: 96 points

    • Vinous (Josh Raynolds): 95 points

    • Wine Spectator: 93 points

  • 2013 Vintage: Reveals vibrant aromas of blackberry, dark chocolate, chai spice, and savory roasted meat. Full-bodied and composed, it presents silky, layered tannins and a lingering finish marked by red berry notes and orange zest freshness.

    • Robert Parker (The Wine Advocate): 96 points

    • Wine Enthusiast: 94 points

Crafted in a signature, age-worthy style, this trio offers remarkable depth, balance, and complexity.

title: Chateau Haut Brion 2019
bodyHtml:
Haut-Brion 2019 vintage is one of the most successful vintages produced after a hot and dry summer. This fine wine has the structure of 2005, with the freshness of 2010. A modern, richer version of the 1990 vintage.

100 Points - James Suckling

The is very refined and elegant with a fine-tannin line running through the center of the palate. It’s very intense and precise. Full-bodied with great, tight fruit. This is subtle and complex, then it opens on the palate and shows incredible depth and intensity. Great length, going on and on for minutes.

99 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2019 Haut-Brion is a blend of 48.7% Merlot, 43.2% Cabernet Sauvignon and 8.1% Cabernet Franc, harvested from the 10th of September to the 3rd of October. The estimated label alcohol degree is 14.5%. Displaying a deep garnet-purple colour, it comes off incredibly shy and reticent to begin, needing considerable coaxing to reveal notes of dark chocolate-covered cherries, blackberry preserves, woodsmoke and sandalwood, before launching into a full-scale fireworks display of iron ore, cumin seed, redcurrant jelly, red roses, oolong tea and Sichuan pepper scents plus a waft of cardamom. The medium to full-bodied palate delivers the most exquisitely ripe, finely grained tannins with a lively backbone of freshness supporting the tightly wound, earth-laced black fruit layers, finishing very long and minerally. This is one of the most finely structured, tightly knit wines of the vintage. Given time, I wouldn't be at all surprised if it goes atomic and eventually takes top place for the vintage.

98 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

Château Haut-Brion checks in as a classic blend of 49% Merlot, 43% Cabernet Sauvignon and the rest Cabernet Franc. Its deep purple hue is followed by a stunning bouquet of ripe black cherry and currant-like fruit as well as classic Graves cold fireplace, burning embers, tobacco, and cedar pencil. More regal, firm, and classically structured on the palate, this full-bodied beauty has a deep, concentrated mid-palate, building tannins, background oak, and a great, great finish. It's very much in the focused, elegant, yet still concentrated and powerful style of the vintage. It will need a solid decade of cellaring, but it’s a brilliant wine. Best after 2032. 

97 Points - Decanter

Powerful and confident, there is no mistaking this concentration of ripe damson and black cherry fruits, set against coffee, earth, sage and black chocolate. Tons of tannins on display but extremely fine, to the point that you almost don't notice them, then once the wine has left your mouth you suddenly realize how many there are, and how they are still exerting pressure. Great persistence, slowing everything down and asking you to stop and think. Clear ageing ability here.

title: Robert Groffier Pere & Fils Bonnes Mares Grand Cru 2020
bodyHtml: Perched between Morey-St-Denis and Chambolle-Musigny in the heart of the Cotes de Nuits this Grand Cru appellation can balance the best characteristics of both. Bonnes Mares wines combine fragrance and femininity with body and power. A seductive combination indeed.

title: Carruades de Lafite 2015
bodyHtml:
Beautiful deep colour that sparkles in the glass. The nose is of course still very young, with primary notes of early ageing. Superb notes of spices and fresh raspberries. On the palate, the attack is supple and rounded. The wine then presents young, lively tannins, whose excellent quality will be revealed with time. The finish is complex and harmonious with beautiful burnt notes. This Carruades needs five to seven years to open up, and has all the characteristics of a wine that will continue to improve for many more.

Blend: 57% Cabernet Sauvignon, 36% Merlot, 7% Cabernet Franc

94 Points - James Suckling

Lead-pencil aromas with currants and plums, too. Full body, silky tannins and a focused and very refined finish. It's the tannins that drive things. An excellent second wine of Lafite. Needs two or three years to soften. Start drinking in 2021.

94 Points - Wine Enthusiast

This second wine of Lafite comes from young vines and wines selected during the blending. The result is a wine with the structure and nobility of the Lafite character but one that will age more quickly. It has great layers of black-currant fruits and acidity, with firm tannins as a background and rich potential. Drink from 2025.

92 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

The second wine of Lafite Rothschild is the 2015 Carruades De Lafite and is a beautiful wine in its own right. Based on 57% Cabernet Sauvignon, 36% Merlot and the rest Cabernet Franc brought up mostly in used barrels, it has classy notes of cassis and lead pencil shavings as well as a medium to full-bodied, elegant, beautifully balanced style on the palate. It’s not a massive wine by any stretch, yet it exudes class and elegance, and is already a joy to drink.

91 Points - Decanter

A discreet nose of real finesse with the Lafite violets prettily present. While it seems on the light side now, time in barrel will add structure.

91 Points - Wine Spectator

Warm plum, fig and black tea notes mix here, with a charcoal frame and a smoldering tobacco accent running through the finish. The velvety and slightly rugged textures are intertwined, showing a nice tug of earth at the end. Best from 2022 through 2030.

title: Bond St. Eden 2020
bodyHtml:
Nestled on an 11-acre knoll just north of the Oakville Crossroad, Bond’s St. Eden vineyard is characterized by iron-rich, volcanic soils that impart remarkable depth and structure to the wine. The 2020 vintage exemplifies the site’s signature balance of power and refinement, delivering a wine with impressive concentration, layered complexity, and a refined tannin structure that speaks to its exceptional terroir.

Tasting Notes

Color: Deep purple-black.
Nose: Initially closed, it unfurls to reveal notes of dark chocolate, baked black plums, and crème de cassis, with underlying suggestions of charcoal and fertile loam.
Palate: Full-bodied with layers of energetic black fruits, a firm, grainy texture, and a long, fruity finish.
Finish: Long and expressive, with lingering dark fruit and subtle earthy undertones.

Accolades

  • James Suckling: 98 points
  • Jeb Dunnuck: 93 points

Optimal Drinking Window

2026–2040. While approachable now, this wine will benefit from additional aging to fully develop its complexity and depth.

Serving Suggestions

Decanting: 2–3 hours to allow the wine to fully express its aromatics and texture.
Serving Temperature: 16–18°C (60–64°F) for optimal enjoyment.
Pairings: Complements dishes such as grilled ribeye steak, roasted lamb, or aged cheeses.

title: Chateau Margaux 2008
bodyHtml:
96 Points - Wine Enthusiast

Definite richness alongside classic elegance. It’s a stylish wine, the fruit integrated into a beautiful structure. It’s not all refinement, because there is also a weight to the black plum skin and dark berry character. A wine that will age over many decades.

94 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

This is a stunning Chateau Margaux, made in a sexy, up-front, elegant style, with deep creme de cassis fruit intermixed with spring flowers, a solid inner core of richness and depth, but again, very sweet tannins as well as striking minerality and elegance. One of the most seductive Chateau Margauxs given its recent bottling, this blend of 87% Cabernet Sauvignon, 10% Merlot, and the rest tiny quantities of Cabernet Franc and Petit Verdot should drink beautifully for the next 25-30 years. Remarkably, a mere 36% of the entire production was selected for the 2008 Chateau Margaux.

title: Poderi Aldo Conterno Barolo Riserva 'Gran Bussia' 2012
bodyHtml:
Paolo Conterno's Gran Bussia Barolo 2012 is an exceptional wine with a remarkable rating of 95 points. It entices the palate with enticing aromas of ripe red berries, violets, truffle, and cedar. The flavours of cherries, plums, tobacco, and exotic spices are beautifully balanced, with velvety tannins and a long, persistent finish.
 
95 Points - Wine Spectator
The earthy, woodsy aromas show some evolution in this red, with just a hint of white truffle, yet there's still a hefty dose of spicy oak to be resolved. Rich and sumptuous midpalate, showing plum, cherry, tar and tobacco flavours shaded by vanilla and toasty spices, with firm, dusty tannins laying a grip on the long finish. Give this another year or two in the cellar.

title: Vega Sicilia Unico 2014
bodyHtml:
The 2014 Vega Sicilia Unico is a refined, elegant wine from Spain’s Ribera del Duero region, made with 94% Tempranillo (Tinto Fino) and 6% Cabernet Sauvignon. This vintage stands out for its balance, showcasing the finesse of a cooler, so-called Atlantic year. Despite the challenges of the climate, it benefits from ideal maturation conditions, resulting in a wine that is both fresh and complex.

Colour: Dark cherry with garnet edges, hinting at its depth and youth.

Aroma: Floral notes of wild rose and lily mix with herbs, licorice, cedar, and subtle hints of orange peel and spices, contributing to a sophisticated bouquet.

Palate: The wine offers layers of bramble fruit, black cherry, Asian spices, and tobacco, framed by silky tannins. A fresh, chalky finish adds vibrancy to its otherwise concentrated profile.

Body: Full-bodied with an elegant structure, combining power with subtlety, as is typical for Unico's style.

Finish: Long and polished, with persistent flavors that evolve gracefully over time.

Accolades: Critics have rated the 2014 Unico very highly, with scores up to 98 points from The Wine Advocate and other reviewers, commending its potential to age gracefully through 2040 and beyond.

This wine exemplifies Vega Sicilia’s mastery of long aging processes, spending about 10 years in both barrels and bottle before release. It reflects both the estate’s meticulous craftsmanship and the unique terroir of Ribera del Duero, making it a prized addition to any collection.

title: Produttori del Barbaresco - Barbaresco 'Asili' Riserva??
vendor: 300407 - Enoteca Bacco Importers Of Fine Wines &
bodyHtml:
This elegant red wine originates from the Barbaresco DOCG in the Piedmont region of Italy. The estate's history dates back to 1958, when the village priest and local growers united to safeguard the identity of the Nebbiolo grape and support the farming community. Today, the cooperative is composed of over fifty families who exclusively cultivate Nebbiolo across 120 hectares of premium vineyards, maintaining a philosophy of traditional winemaking and site-specific terroir expression.

Wine Description

The 'Asili' Riserva is a 100% Nebbiolo that displays a brilliant ruby red colour. Sourced from one of the region's most famous and refined vineyard sites, it is celebrated for its silky, mid-weight personality and high-toned elegance. The sensory profile features a complex bouquet of sweet red berries, primarily strawberry and tart cherry, layered with notes of crushed flowers, cedar, mint, and tobacco. On the palate, the wine is seamless and classy, offering vibrant acidity and firm yet fine tannins that lead to a long, graceful finish with hints of orange zest and delicate spices. It is fermented in stainless steel at 30°C for 24 days on the skins before aging for up to three years in large oak botti. While approachable in its youth, it possesses an optimal drinking window typically spanning 10 to 15 years, with the potential for further aging.

Food Pairing

The refined and silky nature of 'Asili' makes it an ideal companion for fresh egg pastas, mushroom risottos, and delicate white or red meats. It also pairs beautifully with game, venison, and matured cheeses such as Parmesan or Fontina. This pairing highlights the wine's depth and character.

title: Bond Melbury 2019
bodyHtml:
Bond Melbury is one of Bond's single-vineyard wines, sourced from a hillside vineyard northeast of Rutherford. The 2019 vintage exemplifies the vineyard's unique terroir, offering a harmonious balance of aromatic brightness, focus, and nuance, all in the mid-weight style that is characteristic of Melbury. 

Tasting Notes

Color: Deep ruby with violet reflections, indicating its youthful vibrancy.
Nose: Aromas of black cherry and floral notes, complemented by hints of pine needles.
Palate: Medium- to full-bodied with fine, dusty tannins; creamy and medium-round with fine, velvety tannins, showcasing finesse and refinement.
Finish: Long and persistent, with a harmonious balance of fruit and tannins.

Accolades

  • James Suckling: 98 points
  • Antonio Galloni (Vinous): 97 points

Optimal Drinking Window

2027–2045. While approachable now, this wine will benefit from additional aging to fully develop its complexity and depth.

Serving Suggestions

Decanting: 2–3 hours to allow the wine to fully express its aromatics and texture.
Serving Temperature: 16–18°C (60–64°F) for optimal enjoyment.
Pairings: Complements dishes such as roast leg of lamb with mint pesto and mustard crumbs.

title: Carruades de Lafite 2016
bodyHtml:
Carruades de Lafite, the esteemed second wine of Château Lafite Rothschild, hails from the Pauillac appellation in Bordeaux, France. The 2016 vintage is a blend of 49% Merlot, 44% Cabernet Sauvignon, 5% Cabernet Franc, and 2% Petit Verdot.

Tasting Notes

  • Nose: Enticing aromas of warm blackcurrants, blackberry preserves, and kirsch, complemented by hints of cast iron pan, cardamom, and mossy tree bark.
  • Palate: Medium-bodied with a fleshy core of ripe black fruits, fine-grained tannins, and seamless freshness, culminating in a finish of notable purity.
  • Finish: Long and refined, with a balance of freshness and depth.

Accolades

  • James Suckling: 94-95 Points
  • Wine Enthusiast: 93-95 Points

Optimal Drinking Window

This wine is expected to develop beautifully with age and is best enjoyed from 2019 through 2044.

Serving Suggestions

Decanting for about an hour is recommended to allow the wine to open up fully. Serve at a temperature of 16-18°C (60-64°F).

title: Biondi Santi Brunello di Montalcino Riserva 1988 - 2nd Release
bodyHtml:
​Biondi-Santi's Brunello di Montalcino Riserva 1988 is a testament to the winery's enduring legacy and commitment to excellence. Established in the late 19th century by Ferruccio Biondi-Santi, the estate pioneered the production of Brunello di Montalcino, positioning it among Italy's most esteemed wines. Located in Tuscany, the Tenuta Greppo estate has remained under the stewardship of the Biondi-Santi family, upholding traditional winemaking practices that highlight the unique characteristics of the Sangiovese Grosso grape.

Wine Description

This Riserva, crafted exclusively from the estate's proprietary BBS11 clone of Sangiovese Grosso, sourced from vines over 25 years old, showcases remarkable complexity and elegance. In the glass, it displays a deep ruby hue with garnet reflections. The nose is vibrant, offering an unexpected presence of fruit even after decades, accompanied by notes of forest floor, leather, menthol, and a hint of blood orange. On the palate, the wine is harmonious, with soft, fully integrated tannins and a bright, energizing acidity that imparts a youthful vigor despite its age. A subtle saline note adds depth and vibrancy to the finish, epitomizing ethereal sensations, elegance, and finesse.

title: Chateau La Mission Haut Brion 2019
bodyHtml:
Chateau La Mission Haut Brion 2019 is a prestigious red wine from the Pessac Leognan appellation in the Graves region of Bordeaux, France. Since 1983, the estate has been owned by the Dillon family of Domaine Clarence Dillon, who also own the neighbouring Chateau Haut-Brion. The winery’s philosophy focuses on precise parcel management and high vine density to produce intense wines that express the unique gravel and limestone terroir of its historic 25-hectare vineyard.

Wine Description

This vintage displays a beautiful, deep purple-red or crimson colour. The intense nose offers a complex bouquet of raspberry, blackberry, and wild plums, underpinned by signature notes of scorched earth, cedar pencil, and graphite. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied and opulent, featuring a dense mid-palate with juicy, velvety tannins and flavours of black fruit and liquorice. It is a powerful yet agile wine with remarkable balance and a long, expansive finish. The varietal composition is a blend of 53% Merlot, 39.5% Cabernet Sauvignon, and 7.5% Cabernet Franc. The optimal drinking window is approximately between 2032 and 2062, though some critics suggest it can age for 40 years or more.

Accolades

  • James Suckling – 100 points

  • Vinous – 98 points

  • Decanter – 97 points

  • Wine Spectator – 95 points

title: Chateau Margaux 2014
bodyHtml:
97 Points - James Suckling

The purity of cabernet sauvignon fruit is what impresses here. Subtle and energetic plum and currant aromas follow through to a gorgeously harmonized palate of wonderful fruit and an ultra-long finish. Current bush and light earth adds to the complexity. Lasts for minutes. 

97 Points - Wine Enthusiast

There is a sense of pure juicy black-currant fruit that shoots through this great wine. With tannins that are firm while not a jot too much, the wine is crisp, packed with fruit and set for many years of aging. It is beautiful, fruity and intensely structured.

95 Points - Wine Spectator

This is solidly packed, with layers of warm fig bread, plum compote and black currant preserves, carried by a silky yet substantial structure. As the fruit plays out, the anise, black tea and singed alder notes in the background come into clearer focus, giving this remarkable range. Everything glides beautifully through the suave, gently toasty finish. Best from 2020 through 2035.

95 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2014 Château Margaux represents 36% of the year’s total production and is a blend of 90% Cabernet Sauvignon, 5% Merlot, 3% Cabernet Franc and 2% Petit Verdot. Affording the glass five to ten minutes to open, the aromatics are very similar to those expressed out of barrel, those dark cherries and violets, tightly wound at first but unfurling beautifully and seemingly with each swirl of the glass. The palate is medium-bodied with very fine tannin and it appears to have fomented a little more finesse during its élevage. There is wonderful mineral tension and dash of spiciness on the persistent finish. There remains some tightness here, the implication that this is a Château Margaux determined to give long-term pleasure. Therefore, do not be afraid to give it a decade in the cellar.

title: Domaine Anne F. Gros Clos Vougeot Grand Cru 2022
bodyHtml:
From France’s esteemed Burgundy region, specifically the Côte de Nuits subregion, this wine hails from the historic Clos Vougeot Grand Cru vineyard. Domaine Anne Gros, a respected family-run estate now helmed by Anne Gros, is known for meticulous vineyard care and elegant expressions of Pinot Noir. With roots dating back to the 1900s, the domaine emphasizes minimal intervention to reflect terroir authenticity.

Wine Description

The 2022 Clos Vougeot Grand Cru displays a luminous ruby hue, offering immediate visual allure. Aromas unfold with layers of ripe red cherries, blackberries, and violets, interwoven with hints of earthy underbrush and subtle spice. On the palate, it is refined yet powerful, with silky tannins supporting flavours of red and dark berries, fine mineral undertones, and nuanced oak. Medium to full-bodied, it presents excellent depth and energy, leading to a long, graceful finish accented by floral and savoury notes.

Accolades

  • Vinous - 93–95 points.

Food Pairing

Pair this exceptional Clos Vougeot with herb-crusted rack of lamb, wild mushroom risotto, or aged Comté cheese. These combinations highlight the wine’s depth and character, allowing its intricate layers to shine.

title: Bond Pluribus 2020
bodyHtml:
Perched high on the slopes of Spring Mountain, the Pluribus vineyard spans 7 acres at elevations between 1,137 and 1,327 feet. The site’s steep terrain and volcanic soils contribute to a wine of incredible intensity, minerality, and structure. Surrounded by a dense conifer forest, the vineyard imparts an earthy, aromatic complexity that sets Pluribus apart. The 2020 vintage is a bold yet refined expression, showcasing deep concentration, vibrant freshness, and a long, layered finish.

Tasting Notes

Color: Deep purple-black.
Nose: Profound scents of blackcurrant jelly, black cherry compote, and boysenberry preserves, with touches of garrigue, licorice, and violets.
Palate: Full-bodied, energetic, and tense, framed by ripe tannins, with layers of pure black fruit and mineral notes.
Finish: Long and layered, leaving a lingering mineral impression.

Accolades

  • Decanter: 96 points
  • Vinous (Antonio Galloni): 94 points
  • Jeb Dunnuck: 94 points

Optimal Drinking Window

2026–2050. While approachable in its youth, this wine will continue to evolve and gain complexity with extended cellaring.

Serving Suggestions

Decanting: 3 hours to allow the wine to fully express its aromatics and structure.
Serving Temperature: 16–18°C (60–64°F) for optimal enjoyment.
Pairings: Ideal with roasted game meats, grilled ribeye steak, or aged cheeses like Comté and Gouda.

title: Chateau Mouton Rothschild 2004
bodyHtml:
The wine has a strong, dark and deep color, while the nose displays subtle complexity on fruity notes of black cherry, candied quince and licorice with touches of cold smoke, revealing very well-integrated oak. The attack is rich and full, with precise, refined tannins that elegantly enfold mocha flavors and toasted notes, leading into a close-knit and flavorful finish with attractive, very fresh length. A distinctive and stylish wine.

Blend: 69% Cabernet Sauvignon, 15% Merlot, 13% Cabernet Franc, 3% Petit Verdot 3%

95 Points - Wine Spectator

This shows lots of mulled spice, warm tobacco leaf and well-roasted cedar accents, but isn't short on fruit, offering enticing layers of red currant, plum and blackberry confiture. The long finish is riddled with sweet smoke, black tea and iron notes. A gorgeous wine from an overlooked vintage.

91 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Deep garnet colour. Aromas of warm cassis, dried plum, cloves and pencil shavings. Medium+ acidity and medium to firm, fine tannins. Long finish.

title: Biondi Santi Brunello di Montalcino Riserva 2016
bodyHtml:
Biondi-Santi's Brunello di Montalcino Riserva 2016 hails from Italy's esteemed Tuscany region, specifically the Brunello di Montalcino DOCG. Established in the late 19th century, Biondi-Santi is credited with pioneering the Brunello style, producing wines renowned for their longevity and elegance.

Wine Description

This 2016 Riserva showcases a vibrant ruby-red hue. The nose reveals complex aromas of ripe red cherries, dried violets, and subtle hints of forest underbrush. On the palate, it is full-bodied with refined tannins, offering flavors of wild berries, licorice, and a touch of balsamic. The wine's bright acidity ensures freshness, leading to a long, harmonious finish. Crafted exclusively from 100% Sangiovese Grosso grapes, this wine is poised to evolve gracefully over the next several decades.

Accolades

  • Wine Advocate – 99 points
  • James Suckling – 98 points
  • Wine Spectator – 98 points
  • Vinous – 96 points

title: Produttori del Barbaresco - Barbaresco 'Montefico' Riserva
vendor: 300407 - Enoteca Bacco Importers Of Fine Wines &
bodyHtml:
This concentrated red wine is a highlight of the Barbaresco DOCG in Italy’s Piedmont region. The estate’s legacy dates back to 1958, when the local priest and nineteen growers founded the cooperative to protect the Nebbiolo grape’s prestige. Today, the organization comprises fifty four families who exclusively cultivate Nebbiolo, adhering to a philosophy of terroir-driven winemaking and uncompromising quality.

Wine Description

The 'Montefico' Riserva is a 100% Nebbiolo that showcases a deep ruby red colour. Often compared to its neighbour Montestefano, it is renowned for its incredible mineral precision and austere, vertical structure. The sensory profile features a complex bouquet of dried cherries, pomegranate, and red currants, interwoven with high-toned notes of white pepper, flint, anise, and wild herbs. On the palate, the wine is full bodied and tightly wound, offering a laser-like focus with firm, chalky tannins and a long, saline finish. It is fermented at 180°C with 28 days of skin contact before aging for 30 months in large oak barrels and 9 months in the bottle. This wine is built for the cellar, with an optimal drinking window typically spanning 15 to 30 years from the vintage.

Food Pairing

The intense minerality and firm grip of 'Montefico' make it a superb partner for savory dishes such as herb-crusted lamb, roasted duck, or wild mushroom risotto. It also pairs harmoniously with truffle-infused pastas and aged, hard cheeses like Castelmagno or Pecorino. Together, they create an unforgettable dining experience.

title: Chateau Margaux 2019
bodyHtml:
Chateau Margaux 2019 is a Premier Grand Cru Classé wine from the Margaux appellation on the Left Bank of Bordeaux, France. The estate has a storied history dating back to the 12th century and has been owned by the Mentzelopoulos family since 1977, currently led by Corinne Mentzelopoulos. The winery is celebrated for its 'Versailles of the Médoc' neo-Palladian villa and a winemaking philosophy that combines meticulous precision with a transition toward organic and biodynamic farming.

Wine Description

This vintage presents a deep garnet-purple colour with remarkable clarity. The nose is soaring and complex, offering a perfumed bouquet of blackcurrants, raspberries, and violets, layered with sophisticated notes of pencil shavings, sandalwood, and a hint of truffles. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied yet agile, featuring a strikingly vibrant core of fruit framed by 'ultra-fine' filigreed tannins that provide a silky, raw silk texture. Stylistically, it is an 'iron fist in a velvet glove', noted for its effortless balance, freshness, and a long, savory finish with mineral undertones. The varietal composition is a blend of 90% Cabernet Sauvignon, 7% Merlot, 2% Cabernet Franc, and 1% Petit Verdot. The optimal drinking window for this vintage is approximately between 2029 and 2069.

Accolades

  • William Kelley, Robert Parker – 100 points

  • James Suckling – 100 points

  • Jeb Dunnuck – 100 points

  • Vinous – 99 points

title: Bond Quella 2020
bodyHtml:
Nestled in the eastern hills of Napa Valley, the 9-acre Quella vineyard sits on a steep, southwest-facing slope composed of cobble, rocks, and pockets of tufa (volcanic ash). This unique terroir gives the wine its signature minerality and precision. The 2020 vintage is a beautifully expressive example, balancing bright blue fruit, graphite, and a refined, energetic finish.

Tasting Notes

Color: Deep garnet-purple.
Nose: Lifted savory notes of sagebrush and thyme with blackberry and cherry fruits, nuanced by crushed stone minerality, tobacco, and black olive.
Palate: Medium-bodied with a saline mineral tinge to the red berry fruits, firm and very fine-grained tannins, and a vibrant freshness.
Finish: Long and layered, leaving a lingering mineral impression.

Accolades

  • James Suckling: 98 points
  • Decanter: 95 points
  • Vinous (Antonio Galloni): 94 points

Optimal Drinking Window

2024–2044. While approachable in its youth, this wine will continue to evolve and gain complexity with extended cellaring.

Serving Suggestions

Decanting: 2–3 hours to allow the wine to fully express its aromatics and structure.
Serving Temperature: 16–18°C (60–64°F) for optimal enjoyment.
Pairings: Ideal with roasted game meats, grilled ribeye steak, or aged cheeses like Comté and Gouda.

title: Verite 2019 - 3 Bottle Mixed Pack
bodyHtml:
This box contains 1 bottle of each of the following:

 

Verite Le Desir 2019

100 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Deep ruby-purple in color, its aromas unfold slowly and offer new nuances with each return to the glass: Morello cherries, warm chocolate, dried thyme, desiccated roses and dried herbs. The full-bodied palate offers concentrated, floral fruits, pixelated tannins, bursts of fresh acidity and a very long finish with layer after layer of detailed flavor.

100 Points - James Suckling

Sublime cabernet franc aromas of currants, flowers and citrus. Full-bodied with incredible purity of fruit and length. You don’t feel the tannins, but they are there. The acidity gives you dynamic reality and perfect length. A truly great wine.

98 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

94 Points - Decanter

 

Verite La Muse 2019

99 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Deep ruby-purple, it explodes with cassis, violets and aniseed, with wafts of thyme, tobacco and iron, offering new nuances with each return to the glass. The full-bodied palate is powerful and refined, with loads of rounded tannins, focused freshness and ethereal character.

99 Points - James Suckling

Blueberries, blackberries and crushed stones. Pure fruit. Full-bodied with round tannins that have powdery character. Creamy and round mouth-feel. Very unique. Great finish.

98 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

94 Points - Decanter

 

Verite La Joie 2019

99 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2019 La Joie is an elegant expression that offers power, freshness and expressive, floral character. A blend of 84% Cabernet Sauvignon, 7% Merlot, 5% Cabernet Franc and 4% Petit Verdot, it has a deep ruby color and opens slowly from black cherries and blueberries to accents of violets, ground coffee and licorice. The full-bodied palate has generous, grainy tannins, detailed, perfumed flavors and bright acidity, finishing with an alluring iron character.

99 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

The 2019 La Joie is compact and unfolds more slowly in the glass. The nose is rich with graphite, sage oil, and black plum. The palate is full of kirsch, fresh leather, currant, and tobacco, with fine tannins that go for ages, along with the fruit and well-balanced acidity.

98 Points - James Suckling

95 Points - Decanter

title: Kosta Browne Pinot Noir 'Gap's Crown Vineyard' 2022
bodyHtml:
Founded in 1997, Kosta Browne is one of North America’s most revered wineries, recognized for making some of the world’s finest Pinot Noirs and Chardonnays. Located in Sebastopol, Sonoma County, and guided by an acclaimed team that includes renowned Winemaker Julien Howsepian, Kosta Browne makes appellation and single-vineyard wines from the most coveted cool-climate vineyards across the Russian River Valley, Sonoma Coast, Anderson Valley, Sta. Rita Hills and Santa Lucia Highlands appellations. 
 
In addition to partnering with the finest growers in California, Kosta Browne has an estate program that features 170 acres of vineyards through ownership or long-term leases that includes the Cerise Vineyard in Anderson Valley, Keefer Vineyard in the Russian River Valley, and a prized section of the Gap’s Crown Vineyard on the Sonoma Coast. 
 
Kosta Browne has earned a place on Wine Spectator’s annual list of the world’s “Top 100 Wines” seven times since 2005, including “Wine of the Year” in 2011.
 
Bursting with fresh-picked blueberries, blackberries, baking spices, and lifted vanilla aromatics. An iconic palate with dark fruit flavors underscored by elongated velvety tannins. A finish with a wealth of energy, drive, and power.
 
94 Points - James Suckling
 
Lovely depth of fruit and beauty to this, with crushed-strawberry, hazelnut and floral undertones. Full and deep. White pepper and cloves at the end. Drink or hold.

title: Dana Estates Cabernet Sauvignon 'Lotus Vineyard' 2018
bodyHtml:
The 2018 Lotus Vineyard Cabernet Sauvignon expresses heady aromas of fresh blackberry, currant, graphite, and a hint of orange peel. Flavors of plums and summer blackberries mingle with sweet spices and cacao weave into the silky tannin canvas. The wine captures the essence of the vintage with its creamy texture, concentrated fruit which is balanced with an energetic backbone and savory saline finish.

100 Points - James Suckling    Seductive aromas of blackberries, blackcurrants, black olives, pine needles and violets follow through to a full body. The tannins are so poised and dynamic while being extremely fine and focused. It goes on for minutes. Caresses every millimetre of your palate. A truly great 2018 that highlights the balance, finesse and refinement of the vintage. Needs time to come completely together.

99+ Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate    Lotus Vineyard is just below Howell Mountain, not high enough to make that AVA. A very steep vineyard, 100% hand farmed, Lotus is by far the warmest site for this estate. The 2018 Cabernet Sauvignon Lotus Vineyard is 100% Cabernet Sauvignon (clones 15, 4 and 337), aged for 25 months in French oak barrels, 100% new. Deep garnet-purple colored, it sashays out of the glass with bold, flamboyant scents of chocolate-covered cherries, wild blueberries and warm cassis with hints of menthol, lilacs, clove oil and crushed rocks plus a waft of iron ore. Medium to full-bodied, the palate is wonderfully elegant, delivering vibrant black and blue fruits with a firm, exquisitely fine-grained texture and fantastic freshness, finishing with epic length and energy. Only 372 cases were made.

title: Gaja Barolo Sperss 2020
bodyHtml:
Gaja Sperss 2020 is a Barolo crafted by the renowned Gaja winery, located in the Piedmont region of Italy. Established in 1859, Gaja has been instrumental in elevating the reputation of Italian wines on the global stage. The term "Sperss," meaning "nostalgia" in the local dialect, reflects the winery's return to producing Barolo after a period of focusing on Barbaresco.

Tasting Notes

  • Color: Deep garnet red.
  • Nose: Intense aromas of blackberries, plums, thyme, rosemary, clove, and allspice, complemented by subtle notes of leather and tar.
  • Palate: Full-bodied and elegant, featuring juicy blackberries and cherries, with savory earth notes and fine-grained tannins providing structure.
  • Finish: Long and persistent, with a harmonious balance of fruit and spice.

Accolades

  • Wine Enthusiast: 98 Points – "Forward and lifted, this Barolo boasts blackberries, plums, thyme, rosemary, clove, and allspice. Elegant yet powerful, the lush palate is dominated by juicy blackberries and cherries, while savory earth notes emerge on the lengthy finish, supported by ultra-fine tannins. A mouth-filling and substantial wine with captivating depth."
  • Vinous: 96 Points – "The 2020 Barolo Sperss is a dark, brooding wine. Black fruit, leather, incense, game, gravel, and scorched earth convey the essence of Serralunga's seriousness. A touch of small oak torrefaction character actually works well in this wine."

Optimal Drinking Window

This Barolo is expected to develop beautifully with age and is best enjoyed from 2026 through 2044.

Serving Suggestions

  • Decanting: Decant for at least two hours to allow the wine to open up and reveal its full aromatic profile.
  • Serving Temperature: Serve at 18°C (64°F).
  • Food Pairings: Pairs excellently with rich dishes such as braised meats, truffle-infused pasta, and aged cheeses, which complement the wine's depth and complexity.

title: Domaine Anne F. Gros Echezeaux Grand Cru 2022
bodyHtml:
While each cru faithfully reflects its terroir, it is terroir as translated through Gros’ expert touch, offering richer aromatics, rounder curves, silkier tannins. The combination is irresistible, so much so that Gros’ very limited production is snapped up by global collectors faster and faster each vintage. 

95+ Points - Jasper Morris
