A fine pink purple colour. The nose is elegance personified but with a suggestion of fruit depth behind. A gorgeous suavity of fruit, fine at the front of the palate and continuing through behind. Little red berries and a faint touch of liquorice. 

94+ Points - Vinous

The 2022 Grands-Echezeaux Grand Cru is the maiden vintage under the Anne Gros label, the parcel having previously been vinified by Bernard Gros (Gros Frere & Soeur) under a fermage. It has a very well-defined bouquet, dark berry fruit intermixed with crushed limestone and wilted rose petals, understated at first and only gradually gaining intensity. The medium-bodied palate has filigree tannins, tensile from the start, with a keen thread of acidity. It fans out wonderfully towards the finish with a saline aftertaste. Precision is the keyword here rather than power. Superb.

91+ Points - Burghound

title: Fortunate Son The Warrior 2019
bodyHtml:
Fortunate Son is the culmination of more than two decades searching for small jewel vineyards and the fruit from them, handcrafted in the same,meticulous way as Hundred Acre.

Pure, total power and darkness. Sourced from a single, small, family-owned vineyard and aged for 24-30 months in the finest French oak barrique. The stave wood is hand-selected for ultra-tight grain, then air dried for three years before being made into barrels.

98 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

The 2019 Cabernet Sauvignon The Warrior is riveting stuff, offering an incredible array of sweet darker currants, tobacco leaf, lead pencil, and classy oak. It's a big, rich wine, yet it's not over the top and has a semi-opaque purple hue, medium to full body, seamless tannins, and a layered, silky, incredibly satisfying style that's going to evolve for two decades.

95 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Across the board, the 2019s at this address are riper and plusher than the 2018s, and Fortunate Son's 2019 Cabernet Sauvignon The Warrior is no exception. Black cherries and red cherries join cedar and vanilla shadings on the nose, while the full-bodied palate is expansive and plush, turning velvety on the long finish.

title: Bond St. Eden 2019
bodyHtml:
Bond's St. Eden originates from an 11-acre rocky knoll situated just north of the Oakville Crossroad. The iron-rich, red, rocky, volcanic soil of this north-facing site originates from high in the Vaca Mountains. The 2019 vintage exemplifies the vineyard's distinctive terroir, offering a harmonious balance of aromatic brightness, focus, and nuance.

Tasting Notes

Color: Deep ruby red with a purple tinge.
Nose: Aromas of ripe blackcurrant, cassis, wild cherry, and leafy herbaceous notes, complemented by sweet oak spices.
Palate: Rich and velvety texture with ripe firm tannins, vibrant acid backbone, and flavors of blackcurrant, wild cherry, and sweet oak spices.
Finish: Elegant and classy with a beautiful mouthfeel, leading to a long, satisfying finish.

Accolades

  • James Suckling: 98 points
  • Robert Parker's Wine Advocate: 98 points
  • Jeb Dunnuck: 98 points

Optimal Drinking Window

2027–2045. While approachable now, this wine will benefit from additional aging to fully develop its complexity and depth.

Serving Suggestions

Decanting: 3 hours to allow the wine to fully express its aromatics and texture.
Serving Temperature: 16–18°C (60–64°F) for optimal enjoyment.
Pairings: Pairs exceptionally well with Wagyu beef fillet, grilled kohlrabi, Jerusalem artichoke purée, and beef sauce. Alternatively, enjoy with grilled red meats accompanied by soft tacos and BBQ sauce.

title: Domaine Anne F. Gros Clos Vougeot Grand Cru 2023
bodyHtml:
This exceptional wine hails from France, specifically the Burgundy region in the Côte de Nuits, within the historic Clos Vougeot Grand Cru vineyard. Domaine Anne Gros is a renowned family-run estate led by Anne Gros since 1988. Under her stewardship, the domaine has become celebrated for its meticulous vineyard practices and a philosophy that emphasizes finesse and elegance, producing wines that express the profound character of Burgundy’s terroir.

Wine Description

This Clos Vougeot Grand Cru 2023 presents a luminous ruby hue, with vibrant clarity in the glass. The nose reveals a complex bouquet of red cherries, ripe strawberries, and delicate notes of rose petals, interwoven with hints of forest floor, fresh herbs, and a subtle undertone of spice. On the palate, it is medium to full bodied, offering a refined structure with silky tannins and a graceful minerality. Flavours of crushed raspberries, red currants, and a touch of licorice unfold, leading to a long, persistent finish with a whisper of savoury earthiness. Crafted entirely from Pinot Noir, this wine beautifully balances intensity with an airy freshness, embodying the hallmark elegance of Anne Gros’ winemaking.

Food Pairing

This wine pairs exquisitely with duck breast in a cherry reduction, herb-crusted lamb, or mushroom risotto. A selection of aged cheeses such as Comté or Gruyère also complements its layered profile. Together, they create an unforgettable dining experience, highlighting the wine’s depth and graceful complexity.

title: Chateau La Mission Haut Brion 2020
bodyHtml:
Chateau La Mission Haut Brion 2020 is a red wine from the Pessac Leognan appellation in the Graves region of Bordeaux, France. Managed by the Dillon family of Domaine Clarence Dillon since 1983, the estate shares a prestigious winemaking team with its neighbor, Chateau Haut-Brion. The winery follows a philosophy of viticultural precision, utilizing high vine density on deep gravel and clay banks to produce wines known for their unique intensity and aromatic complexity.

Wine Description

In the glass, the 2020 vintage displays a beautiful, dark purple or black-ruby hue. The nose is intense and captivating, opening with aromas of blackcurrants, wild strawberries, and ripe cherries, complemented by complex notes of burning embers, pencil shavings, violets, and forest floor. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied, fleshy, and thick, showing a muscular yet elegantly structured profile with incredibly fine-grained, powdery tannins. Stylistically, it is a paragon of balance and depth, offering a long, fragrant finish with hints of baker's chocolate, cardamom, and spice. The varietal composition is a blend of 48.6% Merlot, 43.2% Cabernet Sauvignon, and 8.2% Cabernet Franc. The optimal drinking window for this vintage is projected between 2030 and 2065.

Accolades

  • Robert Parker - 100 points

  • James Suckling - 99 points

  • Vinous - 98 points

  • Decanter - 98 points

title: Clos Fourtet 2022
bodyHtml:
The estate's history dates back to the 18th century and it was once a medieval fort, which is how it earned the name 'Camp Fortet' (little fort). Under the ownership of the Cuvelier family since 2001, led by Matthieu Cuvelier, the property is committed to expressing its unique limestone terroir through a blend of traditional methods and sustainable, often biodynamic, practices.

Wine Description

The complex aromatic profile includes notes of black cherries, blackberries, plums, rose petals, and violets, complemented by nuances of licorice, spice, crushed stone, and graphite. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied, deep, and concentrated, yet maintains a vibrant sense of freshness. It is seamless and opulent, showcasing a captivating mix of textural richness and classic structure.

Accolades

  • 'Decanter' – 98 points

  • 'Vinous' – 96-98 points

  • 'Jeb Dunnuck' – 96-98 points

  • 'James Suckling' – 97-98 points

  • 'The Wine Advocate' – 94-96 points

Food Pairing

The wine's rich dark fruit, structure, and earthy, mineral notes make it an excellent match for classic cuisine, such as roasted lamb, grilled prime rib with a reduction sauce, or beef tenderloin.

title: E. Guigal Cote Rotie 'La Landonne' 2019
bodyHtml:
To the eye, the wine is red black with deep dark tints. The nose is presented with powerful and intense aromas of small black fruits, liquorice and roasted notes and oriental spices. The palate immediately begins with a powerful attack of important tannic structure. Rich and concentrated, the wine is fully expressive of the terroir. Overall, there is great ageing potential, structured and concentrated with a rare intensity of flavor and color.

98+ Points - Jeb Dunnuck

A wine with perfection written all over it, it's one of the most impressive barrel samples to ever pass this critic's lips. Deep purple/black-hued with a massive, full-bodied, brooding style, it has classic smoky, meaty black fruits, a touch of iron, graphite, tobacco, and pepper, building tannins, and a huge finish.

98+ Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The impenetrably dark 2019 Cote Rotie La Landonne represents the essence of this fabled lieu-dit, combining peppery, herbal notions with espresso and roasted meat, all carried by ample plum and black cherry fruit. It's full-bodied, concentrated, richly tannic and long on the finish—simply a superb wine that should be flirting with perfection when it is released in a couple of years.

97 Points - James Suckling

Still very youthful, this has a deep nose of smoke, bitter chocolate and herbal liqueur. The gigantic tannin structure on the palate will need many years of further aging to completely resolve, but the tannins are fine which gives the super-long finish an extraordinary texture, like old-fashioned velvet. So much smoke and crushed rock character! 

97 Points - Wine Spectator

Firing on all cylinders, this simmers with massive power and range. Boasts a dark, brooding core of black plum, fig paste, strappy black licorice and fruitcake flavors supported by a formidable iron spine. Chewy in feel, with grilled aniseed and warm mesquite smoke adding salty sweetness.

title: Ovid Hexameter 2019
bodyHtml:
OVID Napa Valley represents fifteen acres of California's most distinctive terroir, located atop Pritchard Hill at 1,500 feet. Here, we seek a harmonic balance between ‘tension & intention’ through wines that balance warmth and generosity with nerve, power and finesse.

Notes of plum, Rainier cherry and boysenberry, all picked at their zenith, meld with rhubarb pie, lavender, sage and forest floor aromas. Layered and redolent, this wine strikes a perfect balance of depth, vibrancy and brawn that will reward you for decades to come.

97+ Points - Jeb Dunnuck

Incredible spring flowers, graphite, chocolate, and assorted blue fruits emerge from the full-bodied, ultra-pure, finesse-driven Cabernet Franc. Showing more minerality and scorched earth-like notes on the palate, it has wonderful purity of fruit, building yet polished tannins, and an excellent finish.

title: Domaine Faiveley Mazis Chambertin Grand Cru 2021
bodyHtml:
Founded in 1825, Bourgognes Faiveley has been handed down from father to son for over 175 years. As the sixth generation to take the reins, Francois Faiveley manages, with equal amounts passion and competence, the largest family domaine in Burgundy. Methodically reconstructing vineyards fractured by French inheritance laws, Bourgognes Faiveley today owns more appellations in their entirety (monopoles) than any other domaine in Burgundy.

95 Points - Wine Spectator

Cherry, boysenberry and floral flavors are the main themes, along with an earthy, feral note, shaded by sandalwood and sweet oak spices. This red is taut and linear as it plays out on the compact finish, and though difficult to see where it's going, this is intense and long.

title: Gaja Pieve Santa Restituta Brunello di Montalcino 2021 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
Gaja Pieve Santa Restituta Brunello di Montalcino 2021 is a distinguished red wine from the Montalcino subregion of Tuscany, Italy. Pieve Santa Restituta serves as the Gaja family's historic estate in Montalcino, marking their first venture outside of Piedmont when it was acquired in 1994. The property is named after the 'Pieve' (parish church) on-site that dates back to 462 AD, and the family’s winemaking philosophy focuses on capturing the precision and excellence of the Sangiovese grape within this unique high-altitude terroir.

Wine Description

This 100% Sangiovese displays a deep ruby red colour with silver highlights. The aromatic profile is highly expressive, featuring a bouquet of red cherries, wild strawberries, and sweet violets, alongside complex layers of earth, tamarind, and exotic spices. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied and sleek, showcasing a dense mid-palate with velvety, powerful tannins and cool-toned acidity. Stylistically, it is refined and balanced, offering a long, chewy finish with lingering notes of licorice, graphite, and sour cherry. While it is drinkable now, its structural power makes it ideal for cellaring, with an optimal drinking window beginning in 2027 and extending through 2036 or beyond.

Accolades

  • "James Suckling - 96 points"

  • "Vinous - 94 points"

title: Domaine des Perdrix Nuits Saint Georges 'Aux Perdrix' Premier Cru Quasi Monopole 2021
bodyHtml:
Le Domaine des Perdrix was not a renowned estate until the Devillard family took its management in 1996. Robert Parker says about this acquisition that it proves the existence of undiscovered great quality terroirs among the Grands Terroirs of Côte de Nuits.

The Estate is managed by Bertrand and Christiane Devillard and their children Amaury and Aurore since 1996. The Domaine des Perdrix is located in Côte de Nuits. It covers an area of 12 hectares within the villages of Nuits-Saint-Georges and Vosne Romanee. Nearly 5 hectares of the estate produce Nuits Saint Georges Premier Cru, among which the excellent “Aux Perdrix” is a quasimonopole (99%). The quality of the vineyards, with their rigorous management and vinification, have established the Domaine des Perdrix as a renowned Domaine, one of the best amongst the “Grands Vins de Bourgogne”.

The Domaine's vineyard 'Aux Perdrix' is one of the most beautiful and qualitative Premier Cru of Nuits-Saint-Georges. The plot is owned at 99% : it's almost a monopole. Domaine des Perdrix is  the only producer of this famous terroir!  Vines were planted between 1922 and 1955.

title: Prunotto Secondine Barbaresco 2017 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
Originating from Italy’s prestigious Piedmont region, the Prunotto Secondine Barbaresco 2017 is a remarkable expression of the Barbaresco DOCG. This winery, known for its commitment to quality and tradition, has been crafting exceptional wines since its founding in the 1950s. The Secondine vineyard, located in the heart of Barbaresco, is renowned for its optimal growing conditions, producing grapes that contribute to the wine’s elegance and complexity.

Wine Description
This wine showcases a deep ruby-red color, signaling its vibrant youthfulness. On the nose, expect a bouquet of delicate aromas, including ripe cherries, rose petals, and hints of earthy spices. The palate is structured with velvety tannins and balanced acidity, offering layers of dark fruit, leather, and a subtle smokiness. Full-bodied, with a long, persistent finish, this Barbaresco displays a harmonious blend of power and finesse. Made from 100% Nebbiolo grapes, the wine is best enjoyed between 2023 and 2035 for optimal aging.

Accolades

  • Wine Spectator – 92 points

  • Vinous – 94 points

Food Pairing
Pair this elegant wine with rich dishes such as braised meats, truffle risotto, or aged cheeses. The complex tannins and vibrant acidity will complement the depth of these flavors, creating an unforgettable dining experience.

title: Domaine Gerard Raphet Charmes Chambertin Grand Cru 2019
bodyHtml:
Raphet wines are a Burgundy lover's Burgundy. They are best appreciated by those familiar with the light colour and earthy flavours of classic Burgundian Pinot Noir. Raphet over decades has become the favourite Burgundy of customers and employees alike. They are wines that many feel "speak" especially and directly to them, not dissimilar to a work of art.

The wine's aromas depart from the traditional Burgundian violets to suggest a potpourri of cinnamon, clove and incense. The wine's light colour and fine texture require studied attention on behalf of the drinker. Hints of wood toast and a top note of herbal tea add breadth to the ripe and fresh aromas of red cherry, currant and lilac. The rich and relatively full-bodied flavours possess focused power on the balanced, youthfully austere and solidly persistent finale.

title: Catena Zapata Chardonnay Adrianna Vineyard 'White Bones' 2014
bodyHtml:
The 2014 Catena Zapata Adrianna Vineyard 'White Bones' Chardonnay is a white wine from the Gualtallary sub-region in the Uco Valley, Mendoza, Argentina. Sourced from one of the highest-altitude vineyards in the country, this Chardonnay reflects the unique mineral-driven terroir and the winery’s dedication to crafting world-class wines.

Vineyard and Production

  • Location: The Adrianna Vineyard is situated at 4,757 feet (1,450 meters) above sea level in Gualtallary, Uco Valley. The 'White Bones' parcel, covering 2.2 hectares, is named for its calcareous soils rich in fossilized remains, indicative of an ancient riverbed that imparts distinctive minerality to the wine.
  • Viticulture: The vineyard benefits from cool nighttime temperatures, allowing for slow ripening, enhanced aromatics, and vibrant acidity. The grapes are hand-harvested and selected for quality.
  • Vinification: The wine undergoes fermentation with native yeasts in 500-liter French oak barrels, followed by 12-16 months of aging on the lees, enhancing texture and complexity. Bottled unfiltered and unfined, the wine retains purity and expressiveness.

Tasting Notes

  • Appearance: Pale gold with greenish hues.
  • Aroma: Intense and layered, with citrus fruits, green apple, ginger, floral notes, and a pronounced minerality reminiscent of wet stones and chalk.
  • Palate: Vibrant and textured, displaying lemon zest, white peach, crisp apple, and a saline edge. The chalky texture and electric acidity lead to a long, mineral-driven finish.

Critical Acclaim

  • Robert Parker’s Wine Advocate: 95 points – Recognized for its remarkable freshness and striking minerality, even in a riper vintage like 2014.
  • James Suckling: 96 points – Described as full-bodied yet vivid and energetic, highlighting its stone, flint, and dried apple complexity.
  • Wilfred Wong: 100 points – Praised for its incredible depth and laser-like precision, noting its exceptional focus and extraordinary length.

Serving and Pairing

Serve chilled at 10-12°C (50-54°F) to fully appreciate its aromatics and texture. This Chardonnay pairs beautifully with fresh seafood, grilled shrimp, seared scallops, or oysters. It also complements creamy pasta dishes, roasted poultry, and soft cheeses like Brie and Camembert.

title: Chateau Duhart Milon 2015
bodyHtml:
A blend of 63% Cabernet Sauvignon and 37% Merlot, it displays an inky/blue/purple colour as well as a big, sweet nose of creme de cassis, forest floor, liqorice, lead pencil, cedar and subtle barrique smells. Viscous and full-bodied, it is the most concentrated and broadest example of this cuvee I have tasted in over three decades. It will last for three decades or more. Consumers looking to maximize value should be checking out Duhart Milon, as this may be the single smartest purchase in this great and historic vintage!

93 Points - James Suckling    The smoke, almond, dark-berry and plum character is impressive to this young Duhart. Full body, round and silky tannins and beautiful fruit and spice undertones. Plenty of coffee and cedar flavors at the end. A pretty Duhart. Needs four or five years bottle age. 

93 Points - Wine Enthusiast    Firm and tannic, this wine’s rich structure is balanced by a concentrated blackberry flavor and bright acidity. Drink from 2026. 

91 Points - Vinous    The 2015 Duhart-Milon comes across as much tighter and more reticent than it did from barrel, but some, or, perhaps, all, of that might be attributable the post-bottling shock. Time in the glass brings out the wine's plentiful sensual charms, with hints of crushed flowers, tobacco, mint, leather and smoke that add nuance throughout. The 2015 opens up nicely with air, which leads me to believe that all the 2015 needs is time in bottle.

91 Points - Wine Spectator    This has a mix of silky and charcoal-edged texture carrying gently steeped black currant, plum and cherry fruit flavors along, while lovely perfumed black tea and violet notes infuse the finish. Shows sneaky length, with a lingering iron detail. Just a touch shy on depth overall. Best from 2020 through 2031. 

90 Points - Decanter    This has an abundance of tobacco notes, with crushed black fruits and dark chocolate. We are clearly striding through Pauillac here, and this is a very good wine, but not the best Duhart of recent years - for me you have to head to 2016 for that. Things taper off quicker than expected through the mid-palate, although there is a black cherry sweetness that is very attractive. 50% new oak. 

90 Points - Jeb Dunnuck    The 2015 Duhart Milon is a surprisingly charming, elegant and medium-bodied Pauillac that’s 73% Cabernet Sauvignon and 27% Merlot that was brought up in 40% new French oak. With perfumed notes of spice-box, cedarwood, toast, and sweet black currant fruit, it has sweet tannin and is already accessible, yet will cruise for two decades. 

90 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate    Composed of 73% Cabernet Sauvignon and 27% Merlot and aged for 14 months in barrels, 50% new, the 2015 Duhart-Milon has a medium to deep garnet-purple color and an open, expressive nose of warm red currants, black raspberries and spice cake with nuances of cedar chest, bay leaves and tobacco plus a waft of rose hips. Medium-bodied, vibrant and refreshing in the mouth, it has a good amount of chewy tannins and layers of lively red and black fruits, finishing on an earthy note.

title: Chateau Montrose 2022
bodyHtml:
Chateau Montrose is an esteemed estate in Saint-Estèphe, Bordeaux, France. Situated along the Gironde estuary, it benefits from exceptional gravel soils ideal for Cabernet Sauvignon. Owned by the Bouygues family since 2006, Montrose is renowned for its rigorous vineyard management and investments in sustainability, producing wines of remarkable power and elegance.

Wine Description

This vintage presents a deep, opaque ruby hue. The bouquet unfolds with intense aromas of cassis, blackberries, and graphite, interwoven with hints of violet, cigar box, and subtle mocha. On the palate, it reveals a full-bodied structure with firm, polished tannins and layers of dark fruits, licorice, and crushed stones, leading to a long, mineral-driven finish.

Accolades

  • Jeb Dunnuck - 100 Points
  • Wine Advocate - 100 Points
  • Vinous - 100 Points

Food Pairing

Pair this exceptional Bordeaux with herb-crusted rack of lamb, prime rib roast, or wild mushroom risotto. This pairing highlights the wine’s depth and character.

title: The Mascot Cabernet Sauvignon 2021
bodyHtml:
The Mascot is a Napa Valley cabernet sauvignon made from distinct hillside vineyards; specifically, the younger vines of BOND, Harlan Estate, and Promontory. It started out as a small project shared among the family, winemaking team, and close friends. Drawing fruit from blocks of recently replanted vineyards, The Mascot shares a glimpse into the evolution of its parent estates: a youthful snapshot of their future.

This wine reveals itself first in the deep, brooding aromas of dark fruit, black tea, and herbal notes. The texture expands around a lifted structure, as powdery tannins gently resolve. This diffused, enigmatic softness is anchored on the mid-palate by a gratifying density, which prepares the senses for a flourish of hidden energy and vivid detail that illuminates the finish.

title: Joseph Drouhin Greves Rouge Premier Cru 2023
bodyHtml:
This structured and "thoroughbred" red wine originates from France, specifically from the Grèves Premier Cru vineyard in the Beaune appellation of the Côte de Beaune. Recognized as one of the most representative vineyards of Beaune, the "Grèves" site (named for its sandy, gravelly soil) sits at mid-slope and yields wines known for their unique combination of finesse and density. Joseph Drouhin owns a significant, steep parcel here, which they farm according to strict organic and biodynamic principles to ensure the "natural answer" to the terroir is expressed in the glass.

Wine Description

Joseph Drouhin Beaune Grèves 2023 presents an intense, bright ruby color with a sophisticated sensory profile. The nose displays vibrant aromas of red currant and black cherries, layered with spicy notes and hints of smoke. On the palate, the wine is powerful yet refined, showcasing a "seductive harmony" between its ripe fruit density and polished tannins. It is characterized by a distinct aftertaste of crème de cassis (blackcurrant cream) and delicate touches of well-integrated wood. This 100% Pinot Noir reached an ABV of 13% and was matured for 14 to 18 months in French oak (25% new).

Food Pairing

The structured tannins and spicy fruit of the Grèves Rouge make it an excellent partner for savory, high-quality meats. It pairs perfectly with herb-crusted rack of lamb, roasted pork, or grilled veal. Its mineral undercurrent and berry notes also complement roasted quail, duck, or a hearty meat stew. For a simple yet refined match, it is an ideal companion for wild mushroom dishes or semi-mature French cheeses. For the best expression, serve at a cool room temperature of 16°C.

title: La Chapelle d'Ausone 2022
bodyHtml:
Hailing from France’s renowned Bordeaux region, La Chapelle d’Ausone is the second wine of the prestigious Château Ausone, situated in Saint-Émilion on Bordeaux’s Right Bank. This historic estate, under the careful ownership of the Vauthier family, represents a lineage of viticulture that honours tradition while embracing precision and terroir expression. The steep, limestone-rich slopes of the estate contribute to the structure and longevity of its wines, and La Chapelle reflects the same meticulous craftsmanship as the grand vin.

A blend of predominantly Merlot and Cabernet Franc, La Chapelle d’Ausone 2022 displays a deep, garnet-purple hue. The nose is expressive with notes of blackberry compote, dark cherries, violets, and crushed stone, unfolding into hints of pencil shavings and wet earth. On the palate, the wine is medium to full bodied, with polished tannins and a refined, mineral-driven structure.

Food Pairing
Pair this elegant Bordeaux with herb-crusted lamb, duck breast with a berry reduction, or mushroom risotto. The earthy elements and refined tannins elevate umami-rich dishes, while the wine's freshness provides contrast to rich proteins. Together, they create an unforgettable dining experience.

title: Dom Perignon Brut 2012 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
Dom Pérignon Brut 2012 (1.5 Litre Bottle / Magnum) is a prestigious vintage Champagne from France, produced in the Champagne region. It is the flagship Cuvée de Prestige of Moët & Chandon. Named after the Benedictine monk, Dom Pierre Pérignon, who was influential in Champagne winemaking, this wine is only produced in exceptional vintage years. The 2012 vintage is celebrated for its duality, balancing the richness of a warm year with the tension of high acidity. Magnums (1.5L) of fine Champagne are highly prized because the larger format allows for a slower, more graceful aging process.

Wine Description

The wine has a bright and pale straw colour.

  • Aromatic Profile: The bouquet is complex, full, and varied. It mingles classic brioche, pastry, and toasted nuts with elegant notes of citrus (lime, tangerine, kumquat), apricot, white flowers, and a distinct chalky minerality.

  • Varietal Composition: Traditionally a blend of Pinot Noir and Chardonnay in nearly equal proportions. The 2012 vintage is noted as being around 51% Chardonnay and 49% Pinot Noir or 54% Chardonnay and 46% Pinot Noir.

  • Palate: The palate is tense, vibrant, and energetic, yet also dense and muscular. It offers layers of white peach, crisp stone fruit, crushed blackberry, and salted caramel, structured by racy acidity and a chalky grip.

  • Structure: It has a highly refined and polished pinpoint mousse, with an "athletic, slender, streamlined" profile. The wine is tightly wound and focused, possessing significant intensity and depth.

  • Aging: Aged on the lees for a minimum of seven years in the cellars.

  • Dosage: Low, typically around 5 g/L or 4 g/L.

  • ABV: 12.5%.

  • Optimal Drinking Window: Considered a young wine that will age beautifully. Recommended drinking is from 2023 to 2037 or as long as 2029 to 2075+ due to its density and structure. The 2012 is cited as being destined for a second life as a P2 (Second Plénitude) edition.

Accolades

The 2012 vintage is widely considered one of the greatest of the last quarter-century.

  • Decanter - 98 points

  • John Gilman (View From the Cellar) - 98 points

  • James Suckling - 97 points

  • Vinous (Antonio Galloni) - 97 points

  • Jeb Dunnuck - 97 points

  • Robert Parker's Wine Advocate - 96+ points

  • Wine Spectator - 96 points

Food Pairing

This prestigious Champagne is an excellent aperitif, but its structure allows it to pair with intense culinary sensations. Suggested pairings include:

  • Seafood and shellfish (oysters, mussels, lobster).

  • Savory poultry and creamy cheeses.

  • Spicy dishes that allow the wine to express its vibrancy.

Vintage Quality

The 2012 growing season was marked by extreme weather, including winter and spring frosts, hailstorms, and heavy rainfall, resulting in low yields. However, the warm, dry weather later in the summer concentrated the remaining fruit, leading to exceptional ripeness, density, and concentration. The final wine is defined by a paradox: a solar vintage with a surprising, racy acidity.

title: La Spinetta Barbaresco Starderi 2021
bodyHtml:
La Spinetta Barbaresco Starderi hails from the Neive municipality within the Barbaresco region of Piedmont, Italy. The Rivetti family, led by Giorgio Rivetti, acquired the 6.5-hectare Starderi vineyard in 1996, a site dedicated exclusively to Nebbiolo. Their winemaking philosophy emphasizes the essence of terroir and sustainable practices, producing wines that are un-fined and un-filtered to maintain their natural character.

Wine Description

This 100% Nebbiolo presents as a pale ruby red in the glass. The aromatic profile is complex and vibrant, offering hints of ripe red fruits, strawberry, and peach alongside floral notes of fresh rose petal and hibiscus. Subtle undertones of cinnamon, graphite, mint, and orange peel add further depth to the bouquet. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied and layered, displaying a dense concentration of dark fruit and blackberry preserves balanced by brisk acidity and herbal shades. Its structure is defined by soft, creamy tannins that lead into a long, spicy finish.

Accolades

  • "James Suckling - 97 points."

  • "Vinous - 97 points."

  • "Wine Spectator - 95 points."

  • "Wine Advocate - 95+ points."

Food Pairing

This powerful Barbaresco pairs exceptionally well with hearty, flavor-rich dishes such as grilled ribeye steak, slow-cooked beef stew, or wild game like venison and pheasant. It also complements traditional Piedmontese cuisine, including risotto or pasta with white truffle and aged cheeses like Parmigiano Reggiano or Gorgonzola.

title: Chateau Latour Premier Grand Cru Classe 2016
bodyHtml:
Château Latour 2016 originates from the prestigious Pauillac appellation in the Médoc region of Bordeaux, France. The estate, which dates back to the 14th century, has been under the ownership of François Pinault and his holding company, Artemis Group, since 1993. Under the leadership of Frédéric Engerer, the winery follows a philosophy of uncompromising quality, focusing on precision viticulture and biodynamic practices, with the Grand Vin produced from entirely organic fruit.

Wine Description

This wine displays a deep, almost opaque garnet-purple hue. The complex bouquet reveals layers of smoky blackcurrants, blackberries, and cassis, intertwined with quintessential notes of graphite, lead pencil shavings, violets, and rose petals. On the palate, it is medium to full-bodied, offering a powerful yet elegant structure marked by a core of concentrated fruit, lively acidity, and perfectly ripe, grainy tannins. The texture is seamless and builds into an exceptionally long, mineral-driven finish characterized by notes of wet stone, iron ore, and persistent salinity.

Accolades

  • "Decanter - 100 points"

  • "James Suckling - 100 points"

  • "Vinous - 100 points"

  • "Wine Spectator - 98 points"

  • "Robert Parker - 97 points"

Food Pairing

The robust tannins and intense structure of this Pauillac make it an ideal companion for rich, savoury dishes such as roasted ribeye steak with a pepper sauce or herb-crusted rack of lamb. It also pairs exquisitely with game meats like roast venison or duck breast, where the wine's acidity balances the richness of the meat.

title: Les Perrieres de Chateau Lafleur 2020
bodyHtml:
92+ Points - Vinous

The 2020 Les Perrieres from limestone soils is the first vintage with massal-selection Merlot (from Lafleur). It has an exceptionally pure bouquet of intense black berry and blueberry fruit, crushed stone and touches of Japanese nori. The medium-bodied palate is structured, tensile and very saline, with taut tannins and that limestone-driven pixelation clearly apparent on the finish. Vibrant, almost steely, this will require 2–3 years in bottle. 

94 Points - Decanter

This is a wine for those who really love going deep-diving into limestone. It performs the acrobatic, trapeze artist feat of tiptoeing high above the palate with gunsmoke, cool blueberry and redcurrant fruits and flowers curling upwards. Austere and fierce, stretching forward, then softening as it opens, although it takes its time to do so. There is really a feeling that they are doing something different here, thinking deeply about what it means to link wine's sense of a place to its expression in a glass. Brilliant.

94+ Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Unfurling in the glass with aromas of raspberries and cherries mingled with hints of rose petals and spices, the 2020 Les Perrières de Lafleur is medium to full-bodied, deep and velvety, with a concentrated core of fruit that's framed by beautifully refined tannins and animated by lively acids, concluding with a long, intensely mineral finish. As readers will remember, this exciting new project derives from holdings on the limestone plateau of Fronsac planted with massal selections from Lafleur. Best after 2027. 

92 Points - James Suckling

A fresh and vivid red with sliced berry and cherry aromas and flavors with hints of chocolate. Salted caramel. Medium body. Fine tannins.

title: Chateau Mouton Rothschild 2022
bodyHtml:
Chateau Mouton Rothschild, a First Growth estate since 1973, is located in the prestigious Pauillac appellation of Bordeaux. Owned by the Rothschild family since 1853, the winery is renowned for its artistic labels and for crafting wines of immense power, finesse, and ageing potential. Under the direction of Philippe Dhalluin and the Rothschild family, the estate continues to pursue excellence with cutting-edge vinification and meticulous vineyard management.

Wine Description
A deep, inky ruby in the glass, the 2022 Chateau Mouton Rothschild presents an extraordinary sensory experience. The bouquet is intense and complex, with vibrant notes of cassis, black cherry, cedar, graphite, and hints of violet and spice. On the palate, it is full-bodied, velvety, and opulent, with layers of ripe black fruit, dark chocolate, and exotic spices supported by firm, silky tannins and bright acidity. The finish is persistent and elegant, echoing its finely etched structure.

Accolades

  • Decanter - 98 Points

  • Jeb Dunnuck - 98+ Points

  • James Suckling - 98+ Points

  • Vinous - 96+ Points

  • Wine Advocate - 96+ Points

Food Pairing

Pairs beautifully with richly flavoured dishes such as roast lamb with rosemary, duck breast with cherry reduction, or a prime ribeye steak. Aged hard cheeses like Comté or Gruyère also complement its depth. This pairing highlights the wine’s depth and character.

title: Joseph Drouhin Clos des Mouches Rouge Premier Cru 2022
bodyHtml:
Rich and expressive, Joseph Drouhin Beaune Clos des Mouches is a Pinot Noir that embodies the soul of Burgundy. This Premier Cru red wine delights with notes of dark cherry, spice, and earth, with a firm structure and a lingering finish that will impress even the most discerning palate.

93 Points - Decanter

The highly esteemed white Clos des Mouches from Drouhin boasts marvellous aromas of ripe pear, hazelnut, acacia and beeswax along with the lovely, slightly bitter notes French tasters call 'beaux amers'. There is an elegant structure and enough freshness to ensure long ageing. The wine is assembled from 35 parcels covering roughly seven hectares; the domaine spends ten days picking the grapes – four different days for the white alone. 

92+ Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2022 Beaune 1er Cru Clos des Mouches (Domaine) is shaping up beautifully, revealing aromas of sweet cherries, cassis, licorice and spices deftly framed by toasty new oak. Medium to full-bodied, rich and layered, with a fleshy core of fruit, succulent acids and powdery tannins, the Drouhin's own fully 14 hectares of this prime premier cru, which is divided equally between Chardonnay and Pinot Noir.

title: Bodegas Roda 'Cirsion' 2015
bodyHtml:
Established in 1987, Bodegas Roda is situated in the historic Barrio de la Estación in Haro, within the Rioja region of Spain. Renowned for its dedication to innovation and quality, the winery focuses on producing wines that express the unique characteristics of their old-vine Tempranillo and Graciano vineyards. 'Cirsion' is their flagship wine, crafted from meticulously selected vines that exhibit exceptional tannin polymerization, resulting in a wine of remarkable elegance and complexity. ​

Wine Description:

  • Colour: Deep cherry with an almost impenetrable background.
  • Aroma: Intense and complex, featuring smoky notes, abundant black fruits like blackberries, subtle violet nuances, and sweet spices.
  • Palate: Elegant with bright red fruit flavours, hints of balsamic and chocolate, complemented by sweet, ripe tannins. The wine exhibits a smoky mineral salinity, leading to a long, complex, silky, and profound finish. ​
  • Body: Full-bodied with a balanced structure.​
  • Finish: Long and persistent, showcasing the wine's depth and character.

Accolades:

  • Robert Parker's The Wine Advocate - 95 points.
  • Wine Spectator - 94 points.

title: E. Guigal 'La La La' 2020 - 3 Bottle Wood Box
bodyHtml:
E. Guigal, a renowned producer in France's Rhône Valley, offers a variety of wines that are sometimes available in mixed packs. One notable example is the Guigal "La La's" Mixed Pack, which includes three of their esteemed Côte-Rôtie wines:

La Mouline: Known for its elegance and aromatic complexity.
La Turque: Recognized for its power and depth.
La Landonne: Celebrated for its structure and longevity.

These wines are celebrated for their exceptional quality and have garnered impressive ratings for the 2020 vintage:

La Mouline 2020:

  • James Suckling: 98 Points – "Such a concentrated, focused yet bright La Mouline for the vintage."
  • Vinous: 96-99 Points – "A seamless blend of elegance and power."
  • Decanter: 96 Points – "An aromatic masterpiece with exceptional finesse."
  • Wine Advocate: 94-96 Points – "A vibrant and layered Côte-Rôtie."

La Turque 2020:

  • Jeb Dunnuck: 97-99 Points – "Pure, seamless, full-bodied, and elegant profile."
  • Vinous: 96-99 Points – "A deep, structured expression with tremendous potential."
  • James Suckling: 98 Points – "Impressive intensity with incredible precision."
  • Decanter: 96 Points – "Rich and expressive, with powerful aromas and flavors."
  • Wine Advocate: 94-96 Points – "A powerhouse wine with superb balance."

La Landonne 2020:

  • Jeb Dunnuck: 97-99 Points – "A monumental effort with layers of texture and complexity."
  • Vinous: 96-99 Points – "Stunning concentration and a compelling finish."
  • James Suckling: 98 Points – "Exceptional depth and balance, a true standout."

title: Il Paradiso di Manfredi Brunello Di Montalcino 2018
bodyHtml:
Brunello di Montalcino of Manfredi's Paradise is one of the most authentic and, at the same time, original and unpredictable expressions of Montalcino. It is a great wine, complex and rich in fruit, produced without compromise and without additives, aged for 36 months in large oak barrels.

97 Points -  Wine Enthusiast

Carob, mature black-skinned berry, new leather and tobacco aromas follow over to the smooth, savoury palate along with ripe Marasca cherry and black olive. Liquorice and dried mint sensations linger on the close while velvety tannins provide the framework. It's well balanced, with fresh acidity. It's full of personality and already tempting but will develop even more complexity over the next few decades. Drink 2023–2043.

title: Beringer 8th Maker Cabernet Sauvignon 2016
bodyHtml:
The 2016 Beringer 8th Maker Napa Valley Cabernet Sauvignon is a red wine crafted to honor Mark Beringer, the winery's eighth winemaker. This limited-production Cabernet Sauvignon exemplifies the rich heritage and commitment to quality that Beringer Vineyards is renowned for.

Vineyard and Production

Sourced primarily from the Home Ranch Vineyard in St. Helena (85%) and the Steinhauer Ranch on Howell Mountain (15%), the grapes benefit from diverse terroirs. The 2016 vintage experienced a balanced growing season, allowing for optimal ripening. Hand-harvested fruit underwent meticulous sorting, followed by extended maceration for 21 days at 85ºF. Fermentation and aging occurred in 500-liter French oak puncheons and barrels, with the wine maturing for 24 months in 100% French oak (80% new).

Tasting Notes

  • Appearance: Deep garnet-purple hue.

  • Aroma: Exuberant scents of warm cassis and blackberry pie, complemented by subtle hints of dried Provence herbs, fertile loam, coffee, yeast extract, olives, and crushed rocks.

  • Palate: Full-bodied and plush, featuring flavors of dark berries, blackberries, and hot stones. The palate is marked by fine-grained tannins, seamless freshness, and a lingering minty lift on the finish.

Critical Acclaim

  • James Suckling: 99 points. Described as a dark and seductive Cabernet with stunning forest berries, enormous concentration, and freshness.

  • Jeb Dunnuck: 97 points. Noted for its massive, full-bodied profile, boasting classic crème de cassis fruit, chocolate, espresso, and tobacco notes.

  • Wine Advocate: 95+ points. Praised for its generous fruit, plush-yet-firm tannins, and seamless freshness.

Serving and Pairing

To fully appreciate its complexity, decant the wine for at least an hour before serving at a temperature of 16-18°C (61-64°F). This Cabernet Sauvignon pairs exceptionally well with hearty dishes such as grilled ribeye steak, braised short ribs, or aged cheddar cheese. Its robust structure and depth also make it a suitable companion for rich stews and roasted game meats.

title: Carruades De Lafite 2020
bodyHtml:
Chateau Lafite Rothschild’s second wine, Carruades de Lafite presents similar characteristics to the Grand Vin, but with its own personality linked to a higher proportion of Merlot and to specific plots that are used to produce Carruades. The name comes from the Carruades plateau, a group of plots acquired in 1845 just next to the vines on the Château hilltop.

96+ Points - James Suckling

This is very classically structured with a palate that starts off slowly. Full-bodied and chewy with a soft, creamy texture and a long finish. Savory. A touch austere. 52% cabernet sauvignon, 42% merlot and 3% cabernet franc, the rest petit verdot.

94+ Points - Wine Enthusiast

With its elegant tannins and velvety Merlot in the blend, the wine brings out both the richness of the year and its great fruit. Behind it all there is this superb structure that makes this second wine of Lafite-Rothschild a great wine in its own right. 

93 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

This Chateau has made truly legendary wines in 2020. Looking at the vintage, the harvest occurred all in September, and their second wine, the 2020 Carruades De Lafite, is based on 52% Cabernet Sauvignon, 42% Merlot, and the rest Cabernet Franc and Petit Verdot that was raised in 90% new French oak. The alcohol hit 13% and the pH is 3.84. It's much more open and expressive than the Grand Vin and offers beautiful darker red and black fruits as well as leafy tobacco, cedar pencil, and spicy nuances. Medium-bodied, layered, and concentrated, it has the vintage's more structured, firm feel on the palate, rock-solid mid-palate depth, and a great finish. It needs 4-5 years of bottle age but will evolve for two decades.

92 Points - Decanter

More Merlot than in 2019, but as you find repeatedly in 2020, the Cabernet Sauvignon plays an oversized role in the flavour profile. This has a ton of impact and intensity, coffee and black chocolate with angular tannins that will benefit from softening over ageing. Plenty of Pauillac signature here, with liquorice root and tobacco leaf. A slate texture gives definition to the end of play. 3% Petit Verdot completes the blend.

91+ Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Deep purple-black in color, the 2020 Carruades de Lafite, like its big sibling, is a little youthfully shy to begin, soon unfurling to offer notes of Morello cherries, raspberry leaves, baked blackberries and spice box, plus suggestions of pencil lead, lavender and Provence herbs. The medium-bodied palate is chock-full of juicy black fruits, framed by velvety tannins and tons of freshness, finishing long and lifted. This 2020 is a blend of 52% Cabernet Sauvignon, 42% Merlot, 3% Cabernet Franc and 3% Petit Verdot.

title: Dumol Hyde Chardonnay 2022
bodyHtml:
Introduction

DuMOL Hyde Vineyard Chardonnay riginates from the Carneros subregion of the Napa Valley in the United States. Founded in 1996, DuMOL is a vineyard-focused producer that has evolved under the leadership of winemaker and partner Andy Smith, who joined in 1999 and became full owner with an associate in 2015. The winery follows a 'vineyard up' philosophy, practicing classical and intuitive winemaking to translate the purest essence of unique sites into the bottle.

Wine Description

This wine presents a pale gold straw colour and features a sophisticated sensory profile. The aroma is defined by initial taut notes of lemongrass, bee pollen, and green herbs, which open into exotic scents of stone fruit, smoky flint, and seashell salinity. On the palate, the wine is electric and tangy, displaying persistent citrus flavours of grapefruit pith and lime zest alongside rich notes of nectarine, apple, and honey. It is medium-bodied with a chewy, silken texture and a long, mouthwatering finish marked by mineral acidity and earthy lees. This 100% Chardonnay is crafted from 30-year-old Old Wente clones and is farmed to precise organic specifications. The wine has an ABV of 13% and is noted for its deft balance between power and elegance.

title: Chateau Monbousquet 2020
bodyHtml:
The red wines produced on this exceptional terroir of this estate of 82 acres in one block are rich, with great complexity and aromas of ripe fruit.

96 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

The 2020 Chateau Monbousquet is lights-out good, offering a full-bodied, concentrated, opulent profile as well as notes of ripe black cherries, cassis, chocolate, and leafy herbs. With terrific purity, velvety tannins, and incredible richness as well as a remarkable sense of freshness, it's going to evolve for 15+ years in cold cellars. 

93+ Points - James Suckling

This is linear and creamy with lovely, fine tannins and dark-berry, violet, stone and licorice character. Medium-to full-bodied, racy and fresh. Charming. Freshness at the end.

93 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

With a deep purple-black color, it prances out of the glass with showy scents of crushed black plums, mulberries and Morello cherries, plus touches of dried Provence herbs, charcoal and forest floor. The medium to full-bodied palate delivers expressive black and red berry layers, framed by plush tannins and just enough freshness, finishing on a fragrant earth note.

title: Bouchard Pere & Fils Chambertin 'Clos De Beze' Grand Cru 2022
bodyHtml:
This exceptional red wine hails from the Gevrey-Chambertin region within France's Côte de Nuits. Founded in 1731, Bouchard Pere & Fils is one of Burgundy's oldest and most prestigious estates, maintaining a philosophy centered on expressing the unique nuances of each terroir. The estate manages a small 0.47-hectare parcel in the legendary Clos de Bèze, a vineyard mentioned in historical records as early as 640 AD.

Wine Description

This wine presents a deep ruby colour with a racy and intense nose of currants, raspberries, and cherry stones mixed with subtle toasted oak and spice. On the palate, this 100% Pinot Noir is medium to full bodied, displaying a luxurious texture with flavors of strawberry, sandalwood, and a light marine influence. It is a structured yet elegant wine that effortlessly balances power with a fine-grained tannin profile and a long, expansive finish.

Accolades

  • Wine Spectator - 96 points

  • James Suckling - 97-98 points

  • Vinous - 94-96 points

  • Wine Advocate - 94-96 points

Food Pairing

The wine's robust structure and complex aromatics make it a famous companion for red meats, venison, and game birds like duck or goose. It also pairs exquisitely with full flavoured cheeses, particularly the local Burgundian Époisses.

title: Domaine Nico 'Le Paradis' 2020
bodyHtml:
This fragrant and 'seductive' red wine originates from Argentina, within the Uco Valley region of Mendoza and the high-elevation subregion of Gualtallary in Tupungato. Domaine Nico is a specialized project from the prestigious Catena family, founded by Dr. Laura Catena out of her fascination with regionality and unique expressions of Pinot Noir. The estate's name honors Laura's daughter, Nicola, as well as her great-grandfather who founded Catena Zapata. Sourced from a tiny 1.1-hectare parcel planted in 2011 with Dijon clone 667, the winemaking team focuses on cultivating fruit at the extreme limits of high-altitude viticulture.

Wine Description

The 2020 Domaine Nico 'Le Paradis' Pinot Noir presents a beautifully round, medium-bodied appearance in the glass. Its sensory profile is wonderfully perfumed and complex, opening with delicate aromas of rose petals that gradually reveal a powerful bouquet of fresh raspberries and cherries. On the palate, juicy red fruits mingle seamlessly with a strong herbal and chalky character, offering refinement, balance, and a fine touch of spice. It is characterized by its transparent structure and subtle undertones of earth and fine oak that emerge gracefully after a few minutes of breathing. This 100% Pinot Noir reached an alcohol content (ABV) of 13.5%. The grapes were carefully handled using micro-vinifications with 50% whole clusters, followed by 16 to 18 months of maturation in French oak barrels, utilizing 30% new wood and 70% second-use barrels. While the vineyard is farmed with a philosophy of capturing pure varietal identity, this bottling is not certified organic.

title: Chateau La Gaffeliere 2016
bodyHtml:
Chateau La Gaffeliere 2016 is a red wine from the Saint Emilion Grand Cru appellation in the Libournais region of Bordeaux, France. The estate is one of the oldest family owned properties in the region, held by the Malet Roquefort family for over four centuries. Historically situated between the hills of Ausone and Pavie, the winery focuses on a philosophy of 'parcel by parcel' vinification to express the unique limestone and clay terroir of its south facing vineyards.

Wine Description

This vintage presents a deep garnet or inky colour with blue highlights. The nose is complex and aromatic, featuring scents of black cherries, wild blueberries, and kirsch, layered with notes of aniseed, truffles, and a hint of pencil lead. On the palate, the wine is medium to full bodied and elegant, showing a refined tannic structure that is silky and well integrated. Stylistically, it is noted for its remarkable balance, freshness, and a long, earthy finish that highlights its 3-dimensional complexity.

Accolades

  • Wine Spectator – 95 points

  • Vinous – 96 points

  • Decanter – 96 points

Food Pairing

This wine pairs exceptionally well with classic meat dishes such as roasted leg of lamb, beef steaks, or braised duck breast served with a red wine gravy. It is also a sophisticated match for earthy ingredients like truffled vegetables, wild mushrooms, or hearty pasta dishes.

title: Vina Cobos Malbec 'Hobbs Estate' 2020
bodyHtml:
Viña Cobos Malbec Hobbs Estate 2020 originates from Argentina, specifically from the Agrelo district in the Luján de Cuyo subregion of Mendoza. This estate was established over 25 years ago by pioneering American winemaker Paul Hobbs, who sought to explore the various Mendoza terroirs and elevate Malbec to global prestige. The winery operates with a philosophy described as 'wine crafted by science, refined by nature', utilizing an innovative scientific approach to refine the art of winemaking while honoring the heritage of the vineyard sites.

Wine Description

This Malbec presents a deep, near-opaque ruby red colour with dark violet hues. The aromatic profile is intense and multifaceted, featuring scents of blackberry compote, cassis, and juicy red plums, interwoven with delicate notes of violet, lavender, and graphite, along with hints of cardamom and tobacco. On the palate, it is full bodied and broad in structure, offering a rich and velvety mouthfeel with reactive tannins and a mineral, chalky undertone. The finish is long, persistent, and well-calibrated, showing significant internal energy and ageing potential. Crafted from 100% Malbec, the wine typically has an ABV of 14.8% and is aged for 18 months in French oak barrels. While the estate follows sustainable practices, it is not officially designated as organic.

Food Pairing

The structured tannins and intense fruit concentration of this estate Malbec make it an ideal companion for bold, grilled meats. Suggested pairings include grilled hanger steak with chimichurri and smoked sea salt, lamb chops with rosemary and black pepper, or braised short ribs in a Malbec jus. For vegetarian options, it pairs well with portobello mushrooms stuffed with blue cheese and walnuts. It also effectively complements aged hard cheeses such as Manchego or Parmigiano Reggiano.

Vintage Quality

The 2020 vintage in Mendoza was characterized as a warm growing season that resulted in early ripening and exceptionally healthy fruit with intense concentration. Yields were often lower than average across the region, but the warm conditions provided a ripe, powerful character with sweet tannins and significant aromatic depth. Winemakers, including the team at Viña Cobos, demonstrated skill in maintaining freshness and linear tension despite the heat, producing wines that are both powerful and balanced.

title: Gaja Pieve Santa Restituta Brunello Di Montalcino 'Sugarille' 2018
bodyHtml:
The story of Gaja can be traced to a singular, founding purpose--to produce original wines with a sense of place which reflect the tradition and culture of those who made it. This philosophy has inspired five generations of impeccable winemaking.

This wine is a deep ruby colour and offers an expressive aroma of wildflowers, ripe cherry and balsamic notes. It's full-bodied with flavours of fresh plum and herbs, well-integrated wood and silky tannins.

95 Points - Wine Spectator

A dark, brooding 2018, with accents of smoke, vanilla, iron and tar surrounding a core of cherry and plum flavors. Reveals balsamic elements of eucalyptus and wild herbs on the lingering finish. On the austere side now, with a core of fruit and mineral.

95 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Showing extra richness and textural weight, the 2018 Brunello di Montalcino Sugarille is structured, rich and intense. This wine represents fruit from a single site that is characterized by schistous galestro soils. These conditions give Sugarille its heavier center of gravity and its distinguished power and heft. Dark fruit, balsam herb and pencil shavings shape a beautiful and precise bouquet.

95 Points - Vinous

The 2018 Brunello di Montalcino Sugarille keeps me coming back to the glass again and again to take in its spicy yet also wonderfully lifted bouquet, as shavings of cedar and pine evolve to reveal mentholated herbs, flinty stone and dried black cherries. This is deeply textural, soothing with its combination of ripe red fruits and juicy acidity, as sweet spices and mint nuances resonate towards the close. The Sugarille doesn't miss a beat, tapering off with impeccable balance and regal structure, while allowing remnants of ripe wild berries and plum to linger on and on. The Gaja family has really outdone themselves in this idiosyncratic vintage.

title: Paolo Conterno Barolo Ginestra Riserva 2014
bodyHtml:
Paolo Conterno Barolo Ginestra Riserva is a remarkable wine that captures the essence of the prestigious Barolo region in Italy. Made with meticulous care and expertise, this wine showcases the unique characteristics of the Ginestra vineyard. Its deep ruby color hints at the complex layers that lie within.

On the nose, enchanting aromas of dark cherry, dried herbs, and leather intertwine, creating an alluring bouquet.

The palate is a symphony of flavors, with ripe red fruits, truffles, and hints of tobacco. Firm tannins and a long, elegant finish complete this exceptional Barolo, a testament to Paolo Conterno's winemaking mastery.

title: Chateau Palmer 'Historical XIX Century Blend' 2020
bodyHtml:
Château Palmer, a prestigious estate in the Margaux appellation of Bordeaux, France, has a rich history dating back to the early 19th century. Renowned for its innovative approach, the estate pays homage to 19th-century Bordeaux winemaking traditions with its 'Historical XIXth Century Blend.'

Description: The 'Historical XIXth Century Blend' is a unique cuvée that combines Bordeaux varietals with a touch of Syrah from the Northern Rhône, reviving a 19th-century practice known as "hermitaging." The 2020 release, labeled as Lot 20.20, comprises 44% Cabernet Sauvignon, 44% Petit Verdot, and 12% Syrah. This blend results in a wine with a deep, inky color and a complex aromatic profile featuring notes of black truffle, dark berries, and subtle spice. On the palate, it offers a velvety texture, precise tannins, and a harmonious balance between the richness of Bordeaux and the spiciness of Syrah.

Tasting Notes:

  • Nose: Aromas of black truffle, dark berries, and subtle spice.
  • Palate: Velvety texture with precise tannins, showcasing a harmonious blend of Bordeaux richness and Syrah spiciness.
  • Finish: Long and elegant, leaving a lasting impression of complexity and balance.

Optimal Drinking Window: This wine is approachable in its youth but will develop further complexity with age. It is best enjoyed from 2025 through 2040.

Serving Suggestions: Decanting for at least an hour is recommended to allow the wine to fully express its aromatic profile. Serve at a temperature of 16-18°C (60-64°F).

title: Domaine Anne F. Gros Vosne Romanee 'Les Chalandins' 2022
bodyHtml:
This exquisite Pinot Noir hails from France, specifically from the famed Burgundy region in the Côte de Nuits subregion, centred around the prestigious village of Vosne Romanée. Domaine Anne-Françoise Gros is a renowned family estate, now under the stewardship of Anne and her daughter Julie, that continues a rich winemaking tradition rooted in elegance and precision. The domaine is celebrated for its meticulous vineyard practices and restrained use of oak, producing wines that beautifully express their terroir.

Wine Description

This Vosne Romanee 'Les Chalandins' 2022 presents a luminous ruby colour in the glass. On the nose, it unveils layered aromas of ripe red cherry, raspberry, and subtle wild strawberry, intertwined with hints of rose petal, warm earth, and a delicate whisper of spice. The palate is silky and refined, offering vibrant red berry fruit, gentle notes of tea leaf and forest floor, all framed by fine tannins and a bright, balancing acidity. Medium-bodied, it finishes with graceful persistence, revealing touches of minerality and savoury complexity that linger elegantly.

Food Pairing

Pair this wine with dishes that mirror its elegance and subtle complexity, such as duck breast with cherry reduction, roasted quail, or a mushroom risotto topped with aged Parmesan. This pairing highlights the wine’s depth and character.

title: Catena Zapata Malbec 'Adrianna Vineyard Mundus Bacillus Terrae' 2021
bodyHtml: The Catena Family is entering its second century of winemaking in Mendoza, Argentina. Named after Nicolas Catena Zapata’s youngest daughter, the Adrianna Vineyard is located at almost 5,000 feet elevation in Mendoza. The soils in this 1.4 hectare parcel are filled with scattered limestone and marine deposits that covered the region millions of years ago. The limestone layers are well-drained and particularly rich in rhizobacteria, the microorganisms that help vine roots withstand stress and absorb nutrients. Thus, the name "mundus bacillus terrae" or "elegant microbes of the earth".

title: Opus One 2019
bodyHtml:
The essence of time is expressed in Opus One wine by the character of each vintage. Place, often defined as terroir, represents the geography, the climate and the essential human element which is captured in the wine's balance between power and finesse, structure and texture.

Guided by the vision of their founders, winemaker Michael Silacci combines intuition and technical acumen with the dual perspective of viticulturist and winemaker. From tasting berries to careful sorting and extended aging in new French oak barrels, each stage of the winemaking process is afforded the same meticulous consideration and attention.

99 Points - James Suckling

The purity of fruit is really something else here, with currants and fresh flowers, such as violets and roses. Flower stems as well. Fantastic length and structure to the wine, with tightness and focus. Wonderful fruit. Graceful. A blend of 78% cabernet sauvignon, 8% merlot, 7% petit verdot, 6% cabernet franc and 1% malbec. Try after 2028.

97-99 Points (Barrel Sample) - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Winemaker Michael Silacci commented that usually the blends are finished in January or February after the vintage. This year, with the 2019s, he was still tweaking the blend, but he did mention that this is "pretty close to the final blend." Deep garnet-purple in color, the 2019 Opus One leaps from the glass with notes of Black Forest cake, Morello cherries, mulberries and fresh blackcurrants plus hints of licorice, wilted roses, Sichuan pepper and iron ore. Full-bodied, the palate is jam-packed with juicy black, blue and red fruits, framed by velvety tannins and background freshness, finishing on a compelling earthy/mineral note. Tasted as a barrel sample, this is a truly magnificent Opus One in the making!

97 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

The 2019 Opus One is brilliant and certainly a worthy follow-up to the 2018. Pure cassis fruits, notes of violets, rose petals, and lead pencil, medium to full body, nicely integrated background oak, and terrific tannins all define this beauty, and while it has the vintage's up-front charm, it's going to age beautifully for 20+ years as well.

95 Points - Wine Spectator

This takes the opposite tack from 2018, with more of an opening flourish of enticing fruit in the form of damson pâte de fruit, gently warmed cassis and cherry compote flavors. Very polished, with a subtle alder accent adding some cut through the finish, where hints of red tea, iris and eventually loam peek in. A generous and modern Opus. Cabernet Sauvignon, Petit Verdot, Merlot, Cabernet Franc and Malbec.

title: Stag's Leap Wine Cellars Cabernet Sauvignon 'Cask 23' 2018
bodyHtml:
Introduction

Stag's Leap Wine Cellars Cabernet Sauvignon 'Cask 23' 2018 is a red wine from the United States, originating in the Napa Valley subregion of California. It is an exceptional blend of the famed S.L.V. (Stag's Leap Vineyard) and Fay Estate vineyards, which are located in the Stags Leap District appellation. Stag's Leap Wine Cellars is considered a 'first-growth estate' of Napa Valley, having gained international recognition after its 1973 S.L.V. Cabernet Sauvignon won the historic 1976 Judgment of Paris blind tasting, triumphing over top French wines.

The 'Cask 23' bottling began in 1974 when a lot of wine from S.L.V. was deemed so distinctive by the winemaking team that it was bottled separately and named for the large wooden cask it was aged in. The winery's philosophy revolves around achieving a delicate balance of ripeness and restraint, resulting in wines with complexity, harmony, and remarkable longevity. The wine is a highly regarded and collected blend that exhibits extraordinary depth and richness balanced by elegance.

Wine Description

The wine has a deep garnet-purple colour. It displays complex, stunning, and slightly lifted aromas of violets, cherries, cassis, dark-berry fruit, crushed rock, and fig. Further aromatic notes include plum reduction, blackberry puree, light alder, singed vanilla, tobacco leaf, beef drippings, dried Provence herbs, sandalwood, and wet stone.

'Cask 23' is a blend that, in the 2018 vintage, leans more heavily on the Fay Vineyard. The specific blend is 56.8% Fay and 43.2% S.L.V., and it is made from Cabernet Sauvignon, though the overall blend for the proprietary cuvée may include a small percentage of other Bordeaux varietals. The wine is medium to full-bodied, supple, silky, and elegantly styled. It offers juicy, bright, and effusive characteristics on the palate, with a cohesive, silky texture. Flavours include delicate black fruit layers, dark-berry fruit, cassis, fig, and plum. It features a line of finely grained tannins and possesses enough richness to evolve for the next two decades. The wine spent 21 months ageing in small French oak barrels. Stylistically, it is structured, expansive, and graceful, with ultra-fine tannins and flawless balance. The finish is long, dusty, minerally, and mouthwatering, exuding class all the way. The ABV is $15\%$. It is recommended for enjoyment from 2024 through 2040 or 2045.

Accolades

  • Wine Enthusiast - 98 points

  • The Wine Advocate - 97 points

  • Wine Spectator - 95 points

  • Decanter - 91 points

Food Pairing

While the search results for this specific vintage do not include tailored food pairings, CASK 23 is a profound Cabernet Sauvignon. Generally, wines of this style and structure from Stag's Leap Wine Cellars are recommended to pair with lamb, game (such as deer or venison), and mature or hard cheese.

Vintage Quality

The 2018 vintage in Napa Valley was near-perfect, with an idyllic growing season. It was a slightly cooler vintage with a moderate, benevolent-natured summer. Abundant rain in March and April ensured full soil profiles, and the mild summer, virtually uninterrupted by major heat spikes, allowed the fruit to accumulate flavour complexity gradually. A long growing season and extended hang-time contributed to excellent flavour development without overripeness. The vintage resulted in wines that are more medium-bodied, moderate-alcohol styles packed with vibrancy and energy, and possess balanced acidity and structure for long-term aging.

title: Chateau Lafite Rothschild Decade Mixed Case - 1990-2000-2010 - 6 Bottles
bodyHtml:
The Chateau Lafite Decade is a unique edition in a beautiful round box with rotating elements. Each box is numbered and a total of 800 were produced.

Each case contains 6 bottles of Chateau Lafite Rothschild:

2 bottles x Chateau Lafite Rothschild 1990

96 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Interestingly, a bottle of 1990 Lafite Rothschild I pulled from my cellar for a video blog on my web site was still buttoned down, tight, and even with extended decanting was not showing as much as I would have hoped. However, a bottle tasted, of all places, in Seoul, Korea in February, was only a few points short of perfection. That amazing performance motivated me to pull another bottle out of my cellar and follow it over the course of two days. Sure enough, by the second day the wine was roaring from the glass. The 1990 Lafite has turned out far better than my early assessment. While it still possesses some firmness, and performs like a late adolescent in terms of its evolution, it boasts gorgeous aromas of cedar, tobacco leaf, cassis, and lead pencil shavings. The explosive aromas are followed by a fleshy, full-bodied wine...

95 Points - Wine Spectator

Very serious fruit, with juicy berry, tobacco and cedar character. Slightly more body than the 1989, but they are very close in character. I would give this a little more time.

 

2 bottles x Chateau Lafite Rothschild 2000

100 Points - Wine Spectator

Subtle aromas of currants, leather, tobacco and cedar. Classic cigar box nose, with fruit. Full-bodied, with an amazing texture of silky, ripe tannins. This wine completely coats your palate, but caresses it at the same time. This is the best young Lafite ever made. A triumph. Best after 2012. 18,000 cases made.

99 Points - Wine Enthusiast

Perhaps of all the first growths in the totally un-classic 2000, this retains most of the classic Bordeaux. It is certainly almost black in color, while the new wood flavors are very present. But it shows an impressive restraint, leaving the power of the wine to be revealed over the years rather than immediately. This could well be the longest-lived of the Pauillac first growths.

98+ Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Since I gave this wine a perfect score, I suppose some could see this as a downgrade. I found everything still there for a perfect rating, but I was just struck by how tight and backward the wine was. A blend of 93.3% Cabernet Sauvignon and the rest Merlot, the wine still has a dark ruby/purple color and an extraordinarily youthful nose of graphite, black currants, sweet, unsmoked cigar tobacco, and flowers. The wine is rich, medium to full-bodied, but has that ethereal elegance and purity that is always Lafite. I originally predicted that it would first reach maturity in 2011, but I would push that back by 5-7 years now, although it has 50-60 years of life in front of it. Owners of this beauty are probably best advised to forget it for 5 years. Tasted next to a 1996 several days after the 2000 tasting, the 1996, which is a perfect wine, was far closer to full maturity than the 2000. 


2 bottles x Chateau Lafite Rothschild 2010

100 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Deep garnet in color, the 2010 Lafite Rothschild is a little mute on the nose at this stage, opening to reveal warm blackcurrants, baked plums and boysenberry scents with hints of chocolate mint, violets, cedar chest and pencil lead. Full-bodied, rich and densely packed with perfumed black fruit layers, it has a rock-solid backbone of fantastically ripe, grainy tannins and beautiful freshness, finishing very long and minerally. Still very youthful!

100 Points - Wine Enthusiast

Almost black in color, this stunning wine is gorgeous, rich and dense. It's grand and powerful, with a strong sense of its own importance. The beautiful tannins and the fragrant black currant fruits are palpable. It's a great wine, with huge potential. Cellar Selection.

99 Points - James Suckling

This is shy and not giving its all at the moment. Yet it is full and intense with a tightly intertwined tannic and fruit structure. Ethereal blackberry, currant, cedar, and nutty flavors. Dried flowers too. Cedar jewel box smell comes out with time. Great finish. So, so long and harmonious.

98 Points - Decanter

 

The youngest wine we had in the vertical, and clear evidence of how the 10 year rule for classified Bordeaux is far too soon for first growths in great vintages. For Lafite, this was the last great vintage before 2016 came around, and it probably needs another decade to really get into its stride - although five should do it to kick things off. The year began with a wet spring during flowering, so produced lower quantities than 2009. July, August and September were extremely dry with cool nights, perfect for the grapes, with a few touches of rain before harvest. The black fruit notes (cassis barely begins to cover it) have deepened and softened just the merest whisper since its first few years, and it's still extremely young and concentrated. The tannins are starting to take on a truly silky, elevated quality, where the bilberry and blueberry fruit starts to melt right into them, finessed with touches of liquorice and slate. This is hugely complex, and it's very hard to say when this will stop evolving.

title: Gambal Work Pinot Noir Bentrock Vineyard 2018
bodyHtml:
The darker, more mineral profile of Gambal+Work’s Bentrock Pinot Noir is reminiscent of a Burgundy from the Cotes de Nuits. It has the same splendid duality that the Francesca Pinot Noir conveys, but with more black (rather than red) fruit and a deeper, more tar-like mineral component, reflecting a warmer site. Like the Francesca, its suave texture and bright acidity make it hard to resist now. Similarly long, this energetic Pinot Noir, like its stablemate, finishes with the barest hint of bitterness, adding to its appeal. 

Grab some friends and try them side by side to experience the magic of terroir yourself.

title: Domaine de l'Enclos Chablis 'Vaudesir' Grand Cru 2023
bodyHtml:
Introduction

Produced in France, this prestigious white wine originates from the Burgundy region within the Chablis Grand Cru 'Vaudesir' subregion. Domaine de l'Enclos was established in 2016 by brothers Romain and Damien Bouchard, though they represent the fourth generation of their family to cultivate the classic Kimmeridgian soils of the area. The estate operates out of a historic 19th-century property in the heart of Chablis, where the philosophy focuses on certified organic viticulture and a gravity-fed, low-intervention winemaking process.

Wine Description

The 2023 Vaudesir Grand Cru presents a bright lemon yellow colour with crystalline reflections. On the nose, it is distinguished by fresh apple and citrus zest aromas, layered with subtle notes of toffee, freshly baked bread, and a delicate saline hint of oyster shell. The palate is creamy and enveloping, offering a full-bodied sensation with flavours of ripe apricot, yellow apple, and a touch of pineapple. It displays a perfect harmony between its velvety texture and a precise mineral structure, leading to a long finish with nuances of mint and salt.

Composed of 100% Chardonnay, the wine is sourced from a small 0.57-hectare plot replanted in 1992 on a steep, south-facing slope. It was fermented with indigenous yeasts and aged on its lees for roughly 13 months in a combination of French oak barrels and stainless steel tanks. While approachable in its youth for its freshness, this Grand Cru has the depth for cellaring, with an optimal drinking window typically spanning 5 to 10 years from the vintage.

Accolades

  • Tim Atkin - 93 points

title: Hundred Acre Morgan's Way Cabernet Sauvignon 2019 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
This ultra-premium red wine originates from the Napa Valley region of California, specifically from the Morgan's Way Vineyard (formerly known as Kayli Morgan) located toward the base of Howell Mountain. Established by Jayson Woodbridge, a former investment banker, Hundred Acre has become one of Napa Valley's most iconic cult wineries since its debut in 2000. The winemaking philosophy is defined by an obsessive 'no compromise' approach, which includes sorting fruit berry by berry and limiting yields to just one grape cluster per vine to ensure maximum concentration and purity.

Wine Description

The 2019 Hundred Acre Morgan's Way Cabernet Sauvignon presents a deep garnet-purple hue. The sensory profile is flamboyant and multi-layered, bursting with aromas of black cherries, blackcurrant preserves, and blackberry pie, complemented by nuances of Madagascar vanilla, cigar box, and Chinese five spice. On the palate, the wine is powerful and full-bodied, yet it maintains a remarkable tension and liveliness. Its texture is velvety and tightly wound, featuring perfectly ripe, fine-grained tannins that lead into an exceptionally long, spiced, and minerally finish. This 100% Cabernet Sauvignon has an ABV of 15.5% and is aged for extended periods in 100% new French oak. While the estate follows meticulous hand-farming practices, it does not hold official organic certification.

Food Pairing

The intense concentration and firm tannic structure of this Cabernet Sauvignon make it an ideal partner for rich, fatty meats such as a grilled ribeye or a New York strip steak served with a dark mushroom or peppercorn sauce. It also pairs beautifully with roasted lamb seasoned with rosemary and thyme, which complements the wine's herbal and spicy undertones. For a savoury vegetarian option, a creamy mushroom risotto or eggplant parmesan offers a heavy texture that can stand up to the wine's bold profile.

Vintage Quality

The 2019 vintage in Napa Valley is regarded as exceptional and 'bucolic,' characterized by a long, steady growing season with few heat spikes. These near-ideal conditions allowed for gradual ripening and extended hang time, resulting in wines with deep colour, plush tannins, and great aromatic complexity. Winemakers successfully navigated the season to produce high-quality fruit that exhibits both power and a classic structural balance.

title: Chateau d'Issan 2018
bodyHtml:
Chateau d’Issan is in the heart of the Margaux appellation, a truly privileged location, which explains the outstanding quality of its wines. The mild weather, regulated by being close to the sea and the Gironde Estuary, provides ideal conditions for vine growth. The vines at Château d’Issan benefit from close, on-going care designed to produce perfectly ripe grapes. Everything is organized so that each individual plot can be tended independently in order to get the very best out of its fruit. Château d’Issan is a Third Growth of the 1855 Imperial Classification. The wine is made from the old vines in the Château d’Issan enclosure in the middle of the Margaux appellation. The soil here is mainly made up of surface gravel on top of a clay subsoil, which contributes to optimal ripeness and freshness in our two grape varieties, Cabernet Sauvignon 65% and Merlot 35%. Château d’Issan expresses the exquisite bouquet so characteristic of Margaux, and stands out with its suppleness, subtlety, elegance and long keeping potential that come from its unique terroir.

96 Points - James Suckling

Aromas of blackberry, plum, cocoa, iodine, clove and graphite. It’s medium-to full-bodied with firm, silky tannins. Tightly wound and mineral at the moment, with dusty gravel and graphite notes, yet with focus and precision. Such balance and harmony for the vintage. 

96 Points - Decanter
