This is a vibrant ruby colour, with floral aromatics that are even more evident on the nose here than with the second wine, Blason. This is not always the case during En Primeur tastings, when it's the second wines that tend to be a little more open, but it's a feature of the 2018 vintage. This is a brilliant wine with richness and poise joined by a delicate acidity that pulls the fruit along. The tannins are deceptive, as they are supple and appealing, but the density and power builds over the palate and clearly indicates long ageing. A wine that feels like it's rooted in its appellation. 50% new oak. 40hl/ha yield, with 53% of production going into this wine, higher than in both 2017 and 2016. Eric Boissenot consults.

title: Domaine Dujac Morey Saint Denis Premier Cru 2023
bodyHtml:
Louis Seysses, biscuit manufacturer and gastronome, had a taste for good food and fine wines. His son Jacques Seysses quickly came to share his father's passion, and he decided he would not only like to drink the wine but make it as well. With the help of his father, Jacques began his career in wine with an apprenticeship with Gerard Potel at the Domaine de la Pousse d'Or. He spent two harvests there during which time he was lucky enough to talk and listen to the famous Burgundian winemakers of the times whom he greatly admired.

Possibly Jacques' greatest contribution to the Domaine has been to instill his desire to search for new ways to improve the wine and the way wine is made.

title: Casanova Di Neri Brunello 'Cerretalto' 2019 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
This remarkable Brunello hails from Italy, in the celebrated Tuscany region, specifically within the prestigious Montalcino area. Casanova di Neri, founded by Giovanni Neri in 1971 and now helmed by his son Giacomo, is recognized for elevating the global reputation of Brunello di Montalcino through a philosophy centered on meticulous vineyard management and bold, expressive winemaking. The estate's 'Cerretalto' vineyard is particularly revered for its unique terroir of iron-rich soils, yielding wines of profound depth and longevity.

Wine Description

The 2019 Casanova di Neri Brunello 'Cerretalto' is a striking garnet red with luminous ruby edges. On the nose, it unfurls complex layers of black cherry, wild raspberry, dried rose petals, and hints of balsamic herbs, intertwined with subtle notes of cocoa, tobacco, and crushed stone. The palate is powerful yet beautifully balanced, delivering ripe red and black fruits wrapped in finely grained tannins, with vibrant acidity that provides remarkable lift. The wine’s full body evolves toward a long, savoury finish accented by minerality and whispers of sweet spice.

Accolades

  • "Wine Advocate - 99 points."

  • "James Suckling - 98 points."

  • "Vinous - 97 points."

Food Pairing

Enjoy this distinguished Brunello with rich dishes such as braised beef short ribs, wild boar ragù over pappardelle, or aged pecorino. This pairing highlights the wine’s depth and character.

title: Guado Al Tasso 2022
bodyHtml:
This wine comes from Italy, within Tuscany's renowned Bolgheri region. Tenuta Guado al Tasso is owned by the historic Marchesi Antinori family, who have cultivated vines on this estate surrounded by the scenic Bolgheri Amphitheatre since the late 19th century. The winemaking philosophy focuses on capturing the unique coastal terroir and producing world-class expressions that marry Italian elegance with Bordeaux-style sophistication.

Wine Description

This intense ruby red wine offers rich aromas of red berries, fresh plum, and floral accents, intertwined with notes of graphite, licorice root, tobacco, and subtle sweet spices. On the palate, it exhibits a full body with a savory, silky texture, vibrant acidity, and refined, polished tannins that provide exceptional balance and dimension. The finish is remarkably long and fresh with complex lingering hints of dark cocoa and delicate herbs. The varietal composition consists of 44% Cabernet Sauvignon, 31% Cabernet Franc, and 25% Merlot. It has an alcohol content of 14% ABV and is not certified organic.

Vintage Quality

The 2022 growing season in Bolgheri experienced dry conditions and warm summer temperatures that led to smaller berry sizes and lower overall yields. Timely August rain showers refreshed the vines, allowing the winemaker to expertly adjust the blend by increasing the proportion of Cabernet Franc for added freshness and structure, resulting in a balanced, highly expressive vintage.

title: K Vintners King Coal 2020
bodyHtml:
Introduction

This red wine originates from the United States, specifically from the Royal Slope subregion of the Columbia Valley in Washington State. K Vintners was established in 1999 by self-taught winemaker Charles Smith, a former rock band manager who was named 'Winemaker of the Year' by both Food & Wine and Wine Enthusiast. The winery's philosophy emphasizes small-batch, single-vineyard productions that utilize native yeasts and traditional methods, such as whole-cluster fermentation, to create wines with a distinct sense of place and 'rockstar' personality.

Wine Description

K Vintners King Coal is a bold and structured red with a deep, shimmering crimson-purple colour. The nose is 'earthy with a capital E,' offering a brooding bouquet of currants, black olive, and wild green herbs accented by notes of graphite, tobacco, and white pepper. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied and intense, delivering a mélange of dark berries, black licorice, and sarsaparilla over a core of fine-grained, 'edgy' tannins. It is characterized by its commanding presence, mineral tension, and a long, multi-layered finish that replays notes of cacao bean and ancient spice.

Food Pairing

The 'mightily-structured' nature of King Coal makes it an ideal partner for rich and savoury dishes. It pairs perfectly with grilled ribeye steak, barbecued ribs, or a wild boar ragu served over pappardelle. Its earthy and herbal undertones also complement herb-crusted rack of lamb, venison medallions, or roasted winter vegetables with balsamic glaze. For a cheese course, consider serving it with an aged, sharp white cheddar or a complex smoked gouda.

title: Blankiet Red Blend 'Rive Droite' 2019
bodyHtml:
Blankiet Estate is nestled above Yountville on the western foothills of the Mayacamas Mountains. The Paradise Hills Vineyard is carved on steep hillsides just above the famed Dominus Estate Napanook parcel that was originally planted in 1838 by Yountville’s founder, George C. Yount.

With an ideal eastern exposure, the land is bathed with morning sun and benefits from natural shade in the hot afternoons, and cool breezes from the San Pablo Bay flow constantly across the land. It’s located on three volcanic knolls where soil profiles vary from deeply fractured rocks and volcanic ash, to thick clay deposits, meaning each parcel is distinguished by a unique subsoil and microclimate.

At just 6.5 hectares in size it’s a remarkably small site, yet the incredible complexity of the terroir allows for three distinct wines, each of a singular style. This is an Estate at the top of its game. Combined with the very talented winemaker Graeme MacDonald and owner Claude Blankiet’s attention to detail, is truly worthy of an exploration.

97 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

The 2019 Merlot Rive Droite is more broad and opulent, with a sexy, full-bodied profile loaded with notions of ripe black cherries, currants, loamy earth, chocolate, and hints of tobacco. I love its balance, it has great tannins, and one heck of a finish.

97 Points - Vinous

The 2019 Rive Droite Paradise Hills Vineyard is dense, plush and wonderfully expressive, with terrific freshness for the year. Inky dark fruit, chocolate, lavender and licorice are all amped up. This is an unusually powerful, dark vintage for the Rive Droite.

title: Petrolo Galatrona 2021
bodyHtml:
This Estate was bought by the Bazzocchi family in the 1940s and since the mid 80s has been headed by Lucia Bazzocchi Sanjust with the assistance of her son Luca. Petrolo Estate is located at the site of what was originally a small medieval town called Galatrona and a ower from this period (itself built on foundations dating back to the Roman era) still exists on the property.

98 Points - James Suckling

The aromas here are very distinct with dried flowers such as lavender and violets. Some sage as well. Black berries and black olive skin. Full-bodied yet linear and energetic with very fine tannins and fantastic length. Fresh and lively in the finish.

97 Points - Decanter

Vivid purple in the glass, gorgeous black cherry and blackcurrant aromas with touches of florality - this 100% Merlot smells wonderfully scented and inviting. Smooth, ample, really quite seductive on the palate, sensual almost in the silky but gripping tannins, beautifully ripe blackcurrant and cherry fruit and crunchy, crisp acidity that is not too sharp or too obvious but lifts the palate and gives a thrill and wonderful freshness to the overall expression. Beautifully presented, harmonious, balanced and totally enjoyable from the first to last sip. A gorgeous wine, intense yet energetic, full of flavour and textural nuance. Totally unputdownable, although with lots of potential for improvement over aging.

97 Points - Wine Enthusiast

The nose showcases a vast world of savory aromas, from sanguine to metallic to woody to earthy, with cranberries, currants and dark berries providing sweet contrast. A lively palate runs with the warmth of earth and just-ripened fruit, alongside austere tannin's that promise age worthiness. An absolutely acrobatic feat in Merlot.

96 Points - Wine Spectator

Though seamless and lusciously saturated with black currant, blackberry, violet, iron, tobacco and spice aromas and flavors, this red is also solidly built, with polished tannins. Nevertheless, this is more about finesse and elegance than power, with a vibrant profile and superlong finish.

title: Catena Zapata Adrianna Vineyard 'River' Malbec 2020
bodyHtml:
Introduction

This red wine originates from Argentina, specifically from the Gualtallary district of the Uco Valley within the Mendoza region. Founded in 1902 by Italian immigrant Nicola Catena, Catena Zapata is Argentina's oldest winery still managed by its founding family, now led by fourth generation vintner Dr. Laura Catena. The winery's philosophy is defined by its pioneering role in high altitude viticulture and the discovery of extreme terroirs like the Adrianna Vineyard, which is situated at an elevation of 1,450 metres and is often described as the 'Grand Cru' of South America.

Wine Description

Catena Zapata Adrianna Vineyard 'River' Malbec 2020 displays a glistening dark purple colour that is almost black at the centre with ruby flashes at the edge. The nose is exuberant and complex, offering aromas of blackberries, cassis, and sour cherry layered with floral scents of violets and rose hips, alongside aromatic suggestions of black licorice, chocolate, and a spicy twist of curry. On the palate, the wine is full bodied yet elegant, delivering a creamy and lush texture that balances polished tannins with a stony, saline undercurrent. It is characterized by its remarkable freshness, chalky minerality, and a long, persistent finish. This 100% Malbec features an ABV of 14% and is produced from the Adrianna Vineyard, which is certified organic. The optimal drinking window is from 2026 through 2035.

Accolades

  • Wine Advocate - 97+ points.

  • James Suckling - 98 points.

  • Vinous - 97 points.

  • Tim Atkin - 96 points.

  • Wine Enthusiast - 95 points.

  • Wine Spectator - 93 points.

Food Pairing

The structured tannins and intense minerality of this Malbec make it an ideal companion for high quality proteins and savoury dishes. It pairs perfectly with well marbled grilled steaks, traditional Argentine asado, or hearty meat stews like Carbonada Criolla. Its floral and spicy notes also complement red pasta dishes, gourmet burgers with blue cheese, and aged, full flavoured cheeses.

Vintage Quality

The 2020 vintage in Argentina was exceptionally good but challenging, marked by a dry winter and a hot summer that led to a historically early harvest. While the lack of water reduced yields, the high altitude of the Gualtallary vineyards helped preserve essential acidity and freshness, resulting in boldly coloured reds with excellent balance and fruit character.

title: Louis Latour Corton Charlemagne Grand Cru 2023
bodyHtml:
This legendary and majestic white wine originates from the Corton-Charlemagne Grand Cru appellation in the Côte de Beaune, Burgundy. Maison Louis Latour, the largest owner of this fabled vineyard (owning 10.5 hectares), is historically credited with being the first to plant Chardonnay on this section of the Corton hill after phylloxera destroyed the original Aligoté and Pinot Noir vines. The winery's philosophy leverages its high-altitude, limestone-rich terroir where the southeast exposure ensures maximum ripeness to craft a wine of immense power and aging potential.

Wine Description

The Louis Latour Corton-Charlemagne Grand Cru 2023 presents a brilliant pale yellow color. The sensory profile is opulent and multi-layered, featuring a complex nose of toasted almonds, vanilla, and white flowers, accented by notes of pear, mandarin oil, and freshly baked bread. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied and generous, showcasing sliced apples, stone, and flinty minerality balanced by a creamy, sappy texture. It is characterized by its "monumental" structure and length, leading to a long, persistent finish with hints of toasted coffee and white pepper. This 100% Chardonnay was fermented and aged for 8–10 months in 100% new French oak barrels from the estate's own cooperage, undergoing complete malolactic fermentation to enhance its richness.

Food Pairing

The power and complexity of this Grand Cru require equally prestigious and flavorful dishes. It pairs perfectly with lobster, scallops in cream sauce, or foie gras. Its toasty and mineral undertones also complement sea bass with a beurre blanc sauce, roasted poultry with truffles, and mature, nutty cheeses like aged Comté or Epoisses. Serve slightly chilled at 12°C to 14°C.

Vintage Quality (2023)

The 2023 vintage in Burgundy is regarded as an exceptional year for whites, producing wines with great aromatic volume and structural balance. Despite the warmth of the season, the high-altitude Corton Charlemagne vineyards maintained a "cool fruit" profile and vibrant acidity. Critics have described the 2023 release as having "fantastic depth," with the structural integrity to evolve beautifully in the cellar for 15–20+ years.

title: Aalto PS (Pagos Seleccionados) 2020 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
In 1999, after 30 years as technical director and world–renown winemaker for Vega Sicilia, Mariano Garcia founded Bodegas Aalto. From the beginning he has been guided by three principals: old-vine or massale selection Tinto Fino, a wide range of terroirs spread over nine villages in the province of Burgos, and his vast experience in viticulture and winemaking. 

Vineyard work at Aalto is entirely manual with the primary goal of maintaining low yields. With many of the vines being old, yields are kept low naturally but Mariano will also green harvest to ensure that the fruit at harvest is concentrated and evenly ripe.

Aalto PS is a long, fresh, and with well-integrated tannins wine. Its presence in the mouth is broad and with full of complex nuances derived from the ageing in barrels. It is fruity and elegant, and it will gain complexity over many years to come.

96 Points - James Suckling

Lots of depth here, with ripe blackberries and some nicely baked black cherries, roasted herbs, incense, dark spices, mussels and a balsamic tinge. An admirably fine dollop of tannins on the palate, which are immaculate and juicy, as they thoroughly dunk into the black fruit, melting into a persistent finish that lasts for over a minute. Very impressive.

95 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The heady and ripe 2020 PS follows the house style and the profile of the regular Aalto from the same vintage, with slightly higher ripeness, more creaminess and toastier oak. It's predictable and very good at it, with abundant, slightly dusty tannins and some chalkiness in the pungent, intense and oaky finish. It has 15% alcohol and mellow acidity.

title: Masseto 2022 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
Introduction

The Masseto 2022 is a red wine from Italy, specifically the Toscana region, in the subregion of Bolgheri on the Tuscan coast. Masseto is a single-estate wine, taking its name from the rock-hard clusters of 'massi' (blue clay) that characterize the unique vineyard. The estate, which is controlled by the Frescobaldi Family group, is celebrated globally for its uncompromising quality and obsession with a single vineyard. The winemaking philosophy is driven by the unique terroir—a blend of marine, alluvial, and volcanic soils with a vein of Pliocenic blue clay that governs the hydration of the vines, helping them survive dry spells. The first vintage was released in 1986, and the estate is known for producing what is considered the most prestigious Super Tuscan.

Wine Description

The wine is made from 100 percent Merlot. The colour is a vibrant, brilliant, powerful ruby with a slight purple tinge. The nose is pronounced and profound, expressing an immediate concentration of small red fruits. Aromatics include mineral notes of crushed dark stones and dissolved minerals, delicate peppery accents, black plum, red apples, lavender perfume, and sage. Other notes include cool, damp earth, dark hedgerow berries, Mediterranean scrub, cocoa, and wood. The palate is full-bodied, rich, and luscious, with good depth, velvety texture, and richness. It features bright cherry, succulent dark berries, and spice. The style is structured with ripe, firm, yet elegant tannins, and sensational freshness, achieving a perfect balance between strength and finesse. The finish is long and generous, with a touch of salinity and bitter herbs emerging. The wine undergoes rigorous ageing: 24 months in 100 percent new French oak barrels, followed by an additional 12 months in the bottle. The optimal drinking window is long, from 2028 through 2058. The Alcohol By Volume (ABV) is approximately 14.0 percent to 15 percent. The vineyard has been farmed organically since 2012.

Food Pairing

The Masseto 2022, being a bold and structured red wine, is an excellent pairing for rich dishes. Suggested pairings include beef and venison. Its richness and concentration would also complement fine cuts of roasted lamb or mature, hard cheeses.

title: Chateau Leoville Poyferre 2022
bodyHtml:
This exceptional wine hails from France's Bordeaux region, specifically the prestigious Saint-Julien appellation in the Médoc subregion. Château Léoville Poyferré, a Second Growth estate in the 1855 Classification, has been owned by the Cuvelier family since 1920. The estate is renowned for its meticulous vineyard management and modern yet terroir-driven approach to winemaking, blending tradition with innovation.

Wine Description
The 2022 vintage opens with an intense, deep garnet-purple hue. Aromas of blackcurrant, crushed violet, and blackberry compote unfold alongside notes of cedar, graphite, and a touch of dark chocolate. On the palate, it is full-bodied and densely layered, offering silky yet firm tannins, vibrant acidity, and flavours of ripe plum, espresso, and liquorice. The finish is long and elegant, marked by savoury minerality and refined spice.

Accolades

  • Jeb Dunnuck - 100 points
  • James Suckling - 99 points
  • Decanter - 96 points
  • Vinous - 96 points

Food Pairing
This wine pairs beautifully with roasted rack of lamb, duck confit, or grilled ribeye with truffle jus. Aged cheeses like Comté or mature cheddar also complement its depth. This pairing highlights the wine’s depth and character.

title: Chateau Lynch Bages 2010
bodyHtml:
Overlooking the Gironde estuary at the entrance to Pauillac, the vines of Lynch-Bages are located on the Bages plateau, on one of the finest gravelly rises in the appellation. The estate once belonged to the famous Lynch family, of Irish origin, and was acquired by Jean-Charles Cazes in 1934. His grandson, Jean-Michel Cazes restructured the estate in 1974, adding state-of-the-art winemaking equipment, while keeping the former wooden vats as a reminder of the 19th century.

The grapes are all hand picked and then carefully sorted before crushing. A very strict selection is made prior to blending and the wine is traditionally aged in oak barrels before bottling.

98 Points - James Suckling

What incredible precision and clarity here. Currants, mineral, mint and lead pencil. Full body, with super refined A wine with great beauty and finesse. Such elegance and ethereal quality for this estate. Full body, with ultra-fine tannins and a juicy delicious finish. Long and beautiful. This is the best Lynch in a long, long time. I love the precision here.

97 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Still a saturated ruby-black in hue, the 2010 Lynch-Bages offers up aromas of rich cassis fruit mingled with hints of pencil shavings, loamy soil and cigar wrapper. Full-bodied, deep and muscular, it's rich and layered, with a concentrated core of fruit that's framed by firm, powdery tannins and lively acids. 

97 Points - Decanter

Deep inky purple in colour, this is a majestic Pauillac to be savoured by Bordeaux lovers. Again we are far from it being ready to drink and the tannins continue to be dominant, although not hiding the layers of rich earthy loam, slate, pencil lead and concentrated cassis that lie underneath. It's impressive and built, muscular, taut and architectural. An excellent reflection of what 2010 brought to the wines in this corner of the Medoc.

96 Points - Wine Enthusiast

96 Points - Wine Spectator

94 Points - Wilfred Wong

title: Domaine Seguin Manuel Beaune 'Clos des Mouches' Premier Cru Blanc 2023
bodyHtml:
Seguin-Manuel has undergone a major rejuvenation since its acquisition by Thibaut Marion in 2004, 180 years after its foundation in 1824.

Coming from a ten-generation family of winegrowers, Chanson Père & Fils, Thibaut started his career -- and honed his skills for seven years -- at the family winery in Beaune. Today, he puts his experience, passion and energy at the service of the great wines of Burgundy. 

The range has thus been considerably extended through the acquisition of new vineyards et new grape suppliers. Every effort has been made at Seguin-Manuel to let the wines express their natural balance and each cuvée is crafted with the intention of reflecting its terroir with panache.

Seguin-Manuel's vineyards are grown organically with no use of chemicals, certified since 2015.

The smoothly textured "Clos des Mouches" offers ripe white fruits balanced by tangy acidity. It's a full, generous wine lifted by lively acidity.

title: Sena Red Blend 2022
bodyHtml:
Seña is a premier Chilean red blend from the Aconcagua Valley, established in 1995 as a historic joint venture between Eduardo Chadwick and the legendary Robert Mondavi. This partnership aimed to demonstrate Chile’s full potential by creating a world class 'Icon' wine that reached the quality level of a Bordeaux First Growth. The estate is deeply committed to biodynamic farming and sustainability, utilizing its 42 hectare hillside vineyard to produce wines with a profound sense of place and authenticity.

Wine Description

The wine presents a deep garnet or rich ruby red colour with violet nuances. The aromatic profile is perfumed and complex, offering intense notes of fresh red and black fruits, plums, and blueberries, layered with hints of lavender, graphite, cedar, and sweet spices. On the palate, the wine is full bodied yet vibrant, showing a beautiful balance between tension and ampleness. It features extremely polished, delicate tannins and a refreshing character, leading to a long, persistent finish marked by lingering notes of liquorice and maraschino cherry.

Accolades

  • James Suckling – 98 points

  • Wine Advocate – 97 points

  • Decanter – 97 points

  • Vinous – 96 points

  • Wine Spectator – 93 points

Food Pairing

The robust structure and dark fruit profile of this wine make it an ideal companion for hearty meat dishes such as pepper steak, roasted lamb, or gourmet burgers. It also pairs excellently with rich, savoury dishes like mushroom Wellington or aged cheddar, which help to soften the wine's firm tannins.

title: Chateau Angelus 2022 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
Founded in the early 20th century by the de Boüard de Laforest family, Château Angélus is one of Saint-Émilion’s most prestigious estates. Now under the direction of Stéphanie de Boüard-Rivoal, the eighth generation, the winery is celebrated for its dedication to tradition and innovation. The estate’s iconic bell tower and vineyards on the southern-facing slopes near Saint-Émilion define its distinctive identity and terroir-driven philosophy.

Wine Description
The 2022 Château Angélus displays a deep, intense purple hue. On the nose, it offers an expressive bouquet of black cherries, cassis, violets, and crushed stone, layered with hints of dark chocolate and spice. The palate is opulent and structured, with plush tannins and vibrant acidity that support flavours of ripe plum, blackberry, graphite, and subtle toasted oak. Full-bodied with remarkable depth and precision, the wine carries through to a long, mineral-laced finish.

Accolades

  • James Suckling - 98+ Points
  • Jeb Dunnuck - 97+ Points
  • Wine Advocate - 96+ Points

Food Pairing
This powerful yet elegant wine pairs beautifully with roasted lamb with rosemary, truffle-infused beef tenderloin, or duck confit. A perfect match to enhance the wine's complexity.

title: Poderi Aldo Conterno Barolo Bussia Colonnello 2020
bodyHtml:
The story of Poderi Aldo Conterno, one of the elite, historic Barolo producers, is a tale of great passion for winemaking that winds back across generations and crosses international borders. While the Langhe Rosso, Chardonnay “Bussiador”, Barbera d’Alba “Conca Tre Pile” and Nebbiolo “Favot” represent a nod to modern winemaking techniques, the Barolo wines remain firmly in the traditionalist camp, aged in large Slavonian-oak botte before bottling. Only indigenous yeasts and traditional fermenting techniques are used. 

97 Points - James Suckling

Freshly cut flowers with strawberry, peach and orange peel aromas that follow through to a full body with layers of velvety tannins, that have a fine texture and give a refined yet voluptuous mouthfeel. It shows class and harmony for this tannic vintage.

96 Points - Wine Spectator

There's a youthful exuberance to this polished red, as well as a good dose of new oak that frames the core cherry and raspberry fruit with notes of vanilla and sandalwood, plus a touch of coconut. The elegance, length and vigorous structure reveal this wine's full potential.

title: Chateau Latour Premier Grand Cru Classe 2010 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
100 Points - James Suckling

The aromas of flowers such as roses, violets, and lilacs jump from the glass and then turn to dark berries such as blueberries and blackberries. It's full-bodied, with velvety tannins and dense and intense with a chocolate, berry and currant character. This is juicy and rich, with wood still showing a bit, but it's all coming together wonderfully. Muscular yet toned. Another perfect wine like 2010. Try in 2022.

100 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2010 Latour is deep garnet in colour, and WOW, it erupts from the glass with powerful crème de cassis, Black Forest cake and blackberry pie scents, plus intense sparks of dried roses, cigar boxes, fragrant earth and smoked meats with aniseed and crushed rocks waft. Full-bodied, concentrated and oh-so-decadent in the mouth, it has a firm, grainy texture and lovely freshness, carrying the rich, opulent fruit to an epically long finish. It is incredibly tempting to drink now, but I suspect this hedonic experience isn't a scratch on the mind-blowing, otherworldly secrets this time capsule will have to reveal, given another 7-10 years in bottle and continuing over the following fifty years+.

99 Points - Wine Spectator

Unbelievably pure, with distilled cassis and plum fruit that cuts a very precise path, while embers of anise, violet and black cherry confiture form a gorgeous backdrop. A bedrock of graphite structure should help this outlive other 2010s. Powerful, sleek and incredibly long. Not perfect, but very close. Best from 2020 through 2050.

99 Points - Wine Enthusiast

Stern, almost severe initially, this great wine takes time to show its immense fruit power. Black currant and blackberry notes are packed into the wine, along with an impressive array of spices from new wood that gives a more exotic element. In the end, though, it has a fine, structured sense of proportion. Obviously, for aging over decades, so don't drink before 2022.

title: Chateau Pontet Canet 2021
bodyHtml:
Château Pontet-Canet, a renowned Fifth Growth estate from the 1855 Bordeaux Classification, is located in the Pauillac appellation of Bordeaux, France. The 2021 vintage is a blend of 58% Cabernet Sauvignon, 32% Merlot, 4% Cabernet Franc, and 6% Petit Verdot.

Tasting Notes

  • Nose: Aromas of blackberries, cloves, Indian spices, rose petals, bruised orchard fruit, and cherry pit.
  • Palate: Medium to full-bodied, ample and fleshy, with a layered mid-palate and refined tannins that assert themselves on the firm, saline finish.
  • Finish: Persistent and elegant, showcasing a balance of complexity and freshness.

Accolades

  • Wine Enthusiast: 97 Points – "The dense color and the perfumed aromas set the scene for a rich wine full of fruit. The balance is already there, complex with structure and dense juicy fruits. The wine is impressive."
  • James Suckling: 95 Points – "The 2021 Château Pontet-Canet is rock solid in the vintage and certainly shows the vibrant, vivid style of the estate today with its bright, exotic blue fruits, violets, and graphite-like aromatics."

Optimal Drinking Window

This wine is expected to develop beautifully with age and is best enjoyed from 2028 through 2049.

Serving Suggestions

Decanting for about 2-4 hours is recommended to allow the wine to open up fully. Serve at a temperature of 15.5°C (60°F).

title: La Chapelle d'Ausone 2019
bodyHtml:
La Chapelle d'Ausone hails from the Saint Emilion Grand Cru appellation in Bordeaux, France. Produced by the historic Château Ausone, the estate is currently managed by the Vauthier family, who maintain a philosophy of compulsive perfectionism and organic, biodynamic viticulture.

Wine Description

This 2019 vintage displays a deep garnet purple colour and a highly aromatic nose featuring blackberries, black cherries, kirsch, and red plum. Sweet oak influence adds layers of pastry, vanilla, cinnamon, and violet, while the full bodied palate is sumptuous and velvety. It offers a core of cherry pie and blueberry fruit, supported by extremely integrated, supple tannins and a complex finish of tobacco, sandalwood, and crushed stone.

Accolades

  • 'James Suckling - 96 points'

  • 'Vinous - 94 points'

  • 'Robert Parker Wine Advocate - 93 points'

Food Pairing

This wine pairs beautifully with rich starters such as goose liver pâté or main courses like roast lamb with rosemary, grilled ribeye steak, and wild mushroom risotto. It also complements aged cheeses like Comté or Roquefort.

title: Louis Jadot Corton Charlemagne 'Domaine des Heritiers' 2017
bodyHtml:
The House of Louis Jadot has been producing exceptional Burgundy wines since its founding in 1859 by Louis Henry Denis Jadot. For the past 150 years Louis Jadot has continued as one of the great names of Burgundy and has gained international reputation for its superb red and white Burgundy wines.

96 Points - James Suckling

This has beautiful purity with striking aromas of lemons and limes, as well as fresh yellow grapefruit and a strong, wet-stone edge. The palate has immense power with precision and focus, delivering a long and regal finish with such power and length.

93+ Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2017 Corton-Charlemagne Grand Cru (Domaine des Heritiers Jadot) is excellent, displaying a lovely bouquet of lemon oil, white flowers, crushed chalk and a discrete touch of new oak. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied, tensile and tight-knit, with chewy structuring dry extract, tangy acids and a long, grippy finish.

title: Wynns Shiraz Limited Release 'Michael' 2019
bodyHtml:
The 2019 Wynns Michael Shiraz is a flagship wine from the esteemed Coonawarra region in South Australia. Crafted only in exceptional vintages, this Shiraz is known for showcasing the unique terroir of Coonawarra with rich fruit intensity and elegance. Named after David Wynn’s son, the wine represents the best-of-vintage selection from Wynns’ premium vineyards.

  • Colour: Deep garnet with purple highlights.
  • Aroma: Aromatic notes of blackberries, mulberries, and dark plums, complemented by subtle hints of cedar, tobacco, and spice.
  • Palate: A harmonious balance of ripe black fruit, savory elements, and fine oak integration.
  • Body: Full-bodied with velvety tannins and vibrant acidity.
  • Finish: Long and complex, with lingering dark fruit and spice.

Accolades:

  • 97 Points - Halliday Wine Companion
  • 95+ Points - The Real Review

This Shiraz pairs beautifully with rich dishes such as grilled lamb, braised meats, or hearty stews. While approachable now with decanting, it will evolve and gain complexity with cellaring over the next 15-20 years, making it an excellent choice for collectors and wine enthusiasts alike.

title: Domaine Bouard Bonnefoy Chassagne Montrachet 'Vergers' Premier Cru 2023
bodyHtml:
This exceptional white wine hails from the village of Chassagne Montrachet, located in the Côte de Beaune subregion of Burgundy, France. Domaine Bouard Bonnefoy is currently managed by the fourth generation of the family, with Fabrice and Carine Bouard taking the helm in 2006, recently joined by their daughter Clara. The winery is celebrated for its commitment to traditional, authentic winemaking, famously using a hand cranked wooden press and bottling each wine by hand to capture the purest expression of their terroir.

Wine Description

The Domaine Bouard Bonnefoy Chassagne Montrachet 'Vergers' Premier Cru displays a brilliant gold colour with distinct green highlights. The aromatic profile is complex and inviting, featuring notes of hawthorn, acacia, and honeysuckle, which evolve into deeper scents of hazelnut, honey, and ripe pear with age. On the palate, the wine is opulent and well structured, offering a powerful yet fresh body balanced by a saline mineral quality and a touch of fresh butter.

Food Pairing

The natural power and opulence of this Premier Cru make it an ideal partner for noble white meats, such as veal in a creamy mushroom sauce or roasted chicken with fresh herbs. Its refined structure also complements rich seafood dishes like grilled lobster, langoustine, or even pan seared foie gras.

title: Catena Zapata Malbec Nicasia 2021
bodyHtml:
With a winning combination of cool weather, high elevation and well-draining alluvial soils, it is no surprise that Mendoza’s Uco Valley is one of the most exciting up-and-coming wine regions in Argentina. Healthy, easy-to-manage vines produce low yields of high-quality fruit, which in turn create flavorful, full-bodied wines with generous acidity.

Located in the far southerly growing region of Altamira in La Consulta, the Nicasia vineyard is the only planting of the special Catena Selection of Malbec cuttings in this traditional area for Malbec. La Consulta was Nicolas Catena’s father Domingo’s preferred Malbec location.

title: Castello di Montepo Poggio Ferro 2020
vendor: 300747 - South By Southwest Wine Imports Inc.
bodyHtml:
Introduction

This exceptional red wine stands as the ultimate expression of Sangiovese Grosso at Jacopo Biondi Santi’s Castello di Montepò estate in the Maremma. Poggio Ferro, or "Iron Hill," is a single-vineyard Cru named for its reddish, iron-rich galestro soils and its harsh, windswept location. Selected through painstaking micro-zonation studies, this plot is situated at 322–345 meters above sea level with a full southern exposure. It is a stressful environment for the vines, where strong winds from the Mediterranean constantly buffer the fruit, resulting in thicker skins and lower yields. Unlike its "Super Tuscan" siblings that embrace French varietals, Poggio Ferro is a return to pure Tuscan roots, showcasing the family's exclusive BBS11 clone in its most raw, powerful, and mineral-driven form.

Wine Description

Castello di Montepò Poggio Ferro 2020 displays a luminous, deep ruby red colour with garnet highlights. The nose is profound and brooding, characterized by the "ferrous" minerality that gives the vineyard its name, intermingled with intense aromas of blood orange, dried rose petals, and wild sour cherries. As it opens, it reveals complex layers of aromatic herbs, slate, and a whisper of white pepper. On the palate, the wine is statuesque and vibrant; it possesses a vertical structure defined by nervous, salty acidity and tannins that are firm yet ultra-fine—often described as "iron wrapped in silk." It lacks the fleshy softness of Merlot, offering instead a savory, tension-filled experience with a finish that is interminable and deeply spicy. This 100% Sangiovese Grosso (BBS11) typically has an ABV of 14.5%. Distinct from the estate's other crus, it is not aged in barriques; instead, it matures for 24 months in large 28.5 hl Slavonian oak casks to preserve the varietal's integrity, followed by 16 months of bottle refinement. The optimal drinking window is significant, easily spanning 20 to 30 years.

Accolades

The 2020 vintage of Poggio Ferro has been hailed as a masterpiece of varietal definition. It received 98 Points from The Tasting Panel (Jonathan Cristaldi), who described it as a "statuesque, radiant showstopper" with "tremendous staying power." It was also awarded 97 Points by Decanter, with critics noting its "poetic definition" and the unique interplay between the harsh terroir and the elegance of the wine. It is widely considered one of the most collectable and age-worthy Sangiovese wines produced in the Maremma.

title: Catena Zapata Malbec Nicasia 2022
bodyHtml:
Produced in the far southerly growing region of Altamira in the Uco Valley, Mendoza, Argentina, this wine originates from the esteemed Nicasia Vineyard. This specific site was a favourite of Domingo Catena, father of the pioneering Nicolás Catena, and remains the only location planted with a special selection of Malbec cuttings known as Catena Cuttings. The Catena Zapata family is dedicated to making profound wines that reflect the unique character of their historic high-altitude vineyards.

Wine Description

This 100% Malbec exhibits a deep red colour with striking violet hues. The sensory profile is concentrated and voluminous, featuring a nose of ripe plum, raspberries, and blue fruit accented by complex notes of tar, tapenade, and vanilla from its time in French oak. On the palate, it is medium to full bodied and juicy, displaying succulent tannins and a refined mineral finish. This bold yet balanced wine offers a sweet entry and soft, round tannins that lead into a long, lingering finish.

title: Pahlmeyer Chardonnay 2022
bodyHtml:
The 2022 Pahlmeyer Chardonnay is a distinguished white wine from Napa Valley, California. Crafted exclusively from Chardonnay grapes, this wine exemplifies Pahlmeyer's commitment to producing wines of exceptional quality and character.

Colour: Pale gold with a bright sheen, indicating its vibrancy and quality.

Aroma: Expressive bouquet featuring notes of spiced apples, baked pears, lemon cream, and cloves.

Palate: Full-bodied and well-structured, offering a harmonious blend of ripe yellow fruits and sweet pear, complemented by pleasant spices. The wine exhibits a luxurious texture with fine-grained tannins and balanced acidity.

Body: Full-bodied with a rich and velvety mouthfeel, showcasing both power and elegance.

Finish: Long and persistent, leaving a lasting impression of its complex flavors and refined structure.

Accolades:

  • 94 Points - Wine Enthusiast
  • 93 Points - Wine Spectator
  • 92 Points - Decanter
  • 91 Points - James Suckling

This wine exemplifies Pahlmeyer's dedication to producing wines that are both expressive and true to their terroir, offering a delightful experience for Napa Valley Chardonnay enthusiasts.

title: Chateau D'Armailhac 2015
bodyHtml:
Owned by the prestigious Baron Philippe de Rothschild family, Château d'Armailhac is a renowned Fifth Growth estate located in the Pauillac appellation of Bordeaux. With a history dating back to the 18th century, the estate is known for its commitment to quality and tradition, producing wines that express the unique terroir of its vineyards.

The 2015 Château d'Armailhac is a harmonious blend of 60% Cabernet Sauvignon, 29% Merlot, 9% Cabernet Franc, and 2% Petit Verdot. It pours a deep garnet red with a crimson tint, indicating concentration and potential for aging. On the nose, this wine displays an expressive bouquet of blackcurrant, blackberry, and fresh red fruits, with subtle notes of cedarwood. The palate is rich and fruit-forward, balanced by fine tannins and lively acidity, offering flavors of cassis, blackberry, and raspberry that evolve with elegance into a long, fresh finish.

Food Pairing Suggestions: This Bordeaux pairs beautifully with grilled lamb chops, roasted duck, or mushroom risotto, enhancing the wine's depth and complexity.

title: Guado Al Tasso 2021
bodyHtml:
Guado al Tasso 2021 is a red wine from the Bolgheri Superiore appellation in Tuscany, Italy. Produced by the renowned Antinori family at their Tenuta Guado al Tasso estate, this wine exemplifies the elegance and complexity associated with Super Tuscan wines.

Blend Composition

  • Cabernet Sauvignon
  • Cabernet Franc
  • Merlot

Tasting Notes

  • Color: Intense ruby red.
  • Aroma: Captivating aromas of currants, blackberries, and blood oranges, complemented by undertones of spices, tobacco, licorice, and roasted coffee.
  • Palate: Mouth-filling and persistent, with vibrant, silky tannins. The wine is powerful yet graceful, with outstanding aging potential.

Accolades

  • Vinous: 98 Points
  • James Suckling: 97 Points
  • Wine Spectator: 97 Points

Serving Suggestions

  • Temperature: Serve at 16-18°C (60-64°F).
  • Decanting: Decant for about an hour before serving to allow the wine to open up and reveal its full complexity.
  • Food Pairings: Complements roasted meats, game dishes, and aged cheeses.

Cellaring Potential

Guado al Tasso 2021 is expected to develop further complexity with additional cellaring over the next 15-20 years, making it a noteworthy addition to any wine collection.

title: Louis Jadot Chambertin Clos De Beze Grand Cru 2018
bodyHtml:
The House of Louis Jadot has been producing exceptional Burgundy wines since its founding in 1859 by Louis Henry Denis Jadot. For the past 150 years Louis Jadot has continued as one of the great names of Burgundy and has gained international reputation for its superb red and white Burgundy wines. 

This rich, sumptuous wine has an extraordinary balance of power and elegance. The finely wrought texture finishes with lingering notes of berries and oak. This wine will improve in the bottle for 20 to 25 years.

Serve with sophisticated dishes such as meat in sauce, game and strong cheeses.

96 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Revisited from bottle, Jadot's 2018 Chambertin Clos de Beze Grand Cru (Domaine Louis Jadot) is showing beautifully, wafting from the glass with a deep and complex bouquet of cherries, cassis and wild berries mingled with nuances of cinnamon, raw coca, dark chocolate and orange rind. Full-bodied, sumptuous and enveloping, it's deep and layered, with a seductively velvety attack, terrific concentration and a long, expansive finish. Beautifully balanced, it's bright and lively despite its broad shoulders. This has turned out especially well.

title: Vega Sicilia Pintia 2019 - 3 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
The 2019 Vega Sicilia Pintia is a powerful and expressive wine from the Toro region in Spain, made entirely from Tinta de Toro (Tempranillo). Known for its intense character, this wine reflects the region’s hot summers and complex soils.

Colour: Deep ruby with purple edges.
Aroma: Ripe black fruits like blackberries and plums, with delicate hints of cacao and spices.
Palate: Robust and concentrated, featuring flavors reminiscent of pomegranate, dark berries, and subtle spices, with a velvety texture.
Body: Full-bodied, with fine-grained tannins that add structure.
Finish: Long-lasting, with a profound and layered impression.

Accolades:
95 Points – James Suckling
94 Points – Luis Gutiérrez (The Wine Advocate)

The wine was aged for 13 months in a mix of French (70%) and American oak (30%), striking a balance between freshness and complexity. With an ABV of 15%, the 2019 Pintia is approachable now but will continue to evolve and improve through 2031. It pairs excellently with red meats or game, aligning with its bold and structured profile.

This release emphasizes a slightly softer vinification process to preserve fruit purity, making it a refined expression of Toro’s terroir while maintaining the hallmark intensity of Vega Sicilia wines.

title: Domaine Michel Gros Nuits Saint Georges Premier Cru 2022
bodyHtml:
Domaine Michel Gros is a Burgundian wine producer located in Vosne-Romanee. The Gros family is well regarded in the region, dating back six generations to 1830. The family estate was divided in 1995 between Jean Gros' children, of which Michel is the eldest. Michel has also purchased plots and rents further vineyards of his own.

Other Gros estates include Domaine A.F. Gros, Domaine Gros Frere et Soeur, and Domaine Anne Gros. The estate produces Pinot Noir from some of the best sites in Burgundy, and is well known for its Premier Cru monopole vineyard, Clos de Reas. The portfolio includes wines at Bourgogne and village-level, as well as in Premier and Grand Cru sites.

title: Chateau Calon Segur 2022
bodyHtml:
Chateau Calon Segur hails from France, specifically the Saint Estephe appellation in Bordeaux’s famed Medoc region. The estate, dating back to the 18th century, is steeped in history and once belonged to the Marquis de Segur, who also owned Lafite and Latour. Today, under the ownership of the Gasqueton family and subsequent investors, Calon Segur continues to uphold a reputation for crafting wines of profound elegance and structure.

Wine Description

This 2022 vintage of Chateau Calon Segur is a stunning expression of Saint Estephe terroir. It reveals a deep, opaque ruby colour in the glass. On the nose, the bouquet is rich with layers of cassis, dark cherry, and blackberry, interwoven with hints of graphite, violets, and subtle cedar. The palate is full bodied yet refined, offering ripe black fruits, fine-grained tannins, and a remarkable mineral backbone. The finish is long and persistent, underscored by freshness and a touch of savoury spice.

Accolades

  • Jeb Dunnuck - 97+ Points

  • Wine Advocate - 96+ Points

  • Decanter - 96 Points

  • James Suckling - 95+ Points

Food Pairing

Enjoy this distinguished wine with roast lamb seasoned with rosemary and garlic, prime rib with a rich bordelaise sauce, or aged cheddar and gruyere. These pairings highlight the wine’s depth and character, elevating both the dish and the experience to something truly memorable.

title: Valdicava Brunello di Montalcino 2019
bodyHtml:
Valdicava, located in the prestigious Montalcino region of Tuscany, is renowned for producing some of the finest Brunello wines. The estate has a strong reputation for its dedication to quality, combining traditional winemaking methods with meticulous vineyard management. This commitment has solidified Valdicava’s status among the top producers in the region.

Wine Description

The 2019 Valdicava Brunello di Montalcino presents a deep ruby-red color, offering an expressive nose of ripe black cherries, dried roses, tobacco, and hints of earthy minerals. The palate is both powerful and elegant, with vibrant acidity complementing the wine’s refined tannic structure. Layers of dark berries, leather, and a touch of spice unfold gracefully, leading to a long and persistent finish. Made exclusively from Sangiovese, this wine embodies the intensity and complexity of Brunello, with excellent aging potential.

Accolades

  • James Suckling: 97 points
  • Vinous: 95 points
  • Wine Spectator: 95 points
  • Decanter: 95 points

Food Pairing

This Brunello pairs beautifully with robust dishes such as wild boar ragù, grilled lamb chops, or aged Pecorino cheese. The wine’s structure and depth enhance the richness of these dishes, making for an unforgettable culinary experience.

Vintage Quality

The 2019 vintage in Montalcino is regarded as outstanding, characterized by balanced weather conditions that contributed to wines of exceptional structure and elegance. The result is a Brunello that showcases depth, complexity, and remarkable aging potential, reflecting both the vintage’s excellence and Valdicava’s masterful craftsmanship.

title: Tignanello 2015 (by Tenuta Tignanello)
bodyHtml:
Produced by the historic Marchesi Antinori family in the heart of Italy's Chianti Classico region, Tenuta Tignanello is situated in the Toscana IGT subregion. The Antinori family has overseen the estate for over 25 generations, maintaining a winemaking philosophy focused on an 'ongoing challenge and a never-ending passion' to showcase the potential of their unique terroir. This landmark vineyard, characterized by marine marlstone soils rich in limestone and schist, was the birthplace of the first Sangiovese wine to be aged in barriques and one of the earliest red wines in the region to exclude white grapes from its blend.

Wine Description

The Tignanello displays an intense ruby red colour. The aromatic profile is complex and deep, featuring dark berries, ripe red fruit, and cassis, seamlessly balanced with notes of sandalwood, Spanish cedar, liquorice, and sweet spice. On the palate, the wine is full bodied, rich, and vibrant, characterized by polished, fine grained tannins and a bright acidity that provides incredible depth. Stylistically, it achieves a remarkable harmony between power and elegance, offering a savory character with layers of black cherry and blackberry compote that lead into a long, persistent finish.

Accolades

  • James Suckling - 98 points

  • Vinous - 98 points

  • Wine Spectator - 97 points

  • Robert Parker's Wine Advocate - 96 points

  • Wine Enthusiast - 95 points

Food Pairing

The structured profile and vibrant acidity of Tignanello make it an ideal companion for roasted filet mignon with a rich beef stock reduction or seared lamb chops seasoned with mint and rosemary. It also pairs exquisitely with traditional Tuscan fare such as a veal stew prepared with porcini mushrooms and tomatoes.

title: Catena Zapata Chardonnay Adrianna Vineyard 'White Bones' 2023
bodyHtml: The nose lively citrus notes and white stone fruit . The palate is a voluptuous wine with intense flavors of pear, apple and subtle floral and mineral hints . The finish is long and clean with a strong mineral side.

title: Dom Perignon P2 2006
bodyHtml:
Dom Pérignon is produced by Moët & Chandon, one of the most iconic Champagne houses in the world. Named after the Benedictine monk credited with pioneering key Champagne-making techniques, Dom Pérignon represents the house’s prestige cuvée. The ‘Plénitude 2’ (P2) expression signifies a second maturation phase in the cellar, releasing the wine at a moment of heightened energy and complexity.

P2 2006 presents a luminous golden hue and a refined, expressive bouquet. Aromas unfold in layers: warm florals, dried citrus peel, stone fruit, and notes of toasted hazelnut, mocha, and brioche. On the palate, it is both broad and vibrant, with a creamy texture that gives way to fine mineral tension. The blend of 55% Pinot Noir and 45% Chardonnay is seamlessly integrated, offering depth and balance. The finish is long, saline, and subtly spiced. While drinking beautifully now, this Champagne has an extended aging potential well into the next decade. The wine is not certified organic.

Accolades:
Vinous – 98 points
Robert Parker – 95 points

Food Pairing:
Ideal with elegant dishes like butter-poached lobster, scallops with citrus beurre blanc, or veal with a light mushroom cream sauce. A perfect match to enhance the wine's complexity.

title: Chateau Lafite Rothschild 2017
bodyHtml:
Lafite has a soul, a beautiful, generous, kindly soul. Lafite turns bare earth into heaven. Lafite is harmony, a harmony between man and nature, because without our magnificent winegrowers, nothing would be accomplished.

98 Points - James Suckling     Deep and typical on the nose with blackcurrants, black tea, leather and graphite. The aromas draw you down to the palate. Full-bodied, creamy and beautiful with extremely polished, refined tannins. Yet, it’s powerful and long. Highest percent of cabernet sauvignon ever. Juicy and almost exotic, but very tidy with ripe tannins. Try after 2025 and onwards.

97 Points - Wine Enthusiast     This wine is poised, gathering freshness and good acidity in the same structured container as the pure black-currant fruits. With 97% Cabernet Sauvignon, the wine has a classicism about it: fruity and structured at the same time. Drink from 2024.

97 Points - Decanter     Deep ruby in colour but not so inky as to be impenetrable - that is not their style. Nose subdued at first, but on the palate it unfurls to show violet edging and rich but well defined black fruits. Lafite never tries overly hard to please everyone in its early years, and this will take some time to open up. There is plenty of concentration - there are hefty tannins but they are so finessed that you don't feel them at first. It will almost certainly take a full ten years to reach its drinking window, unlike many in 2017. Its 97% Cabernet Sauvignon means a lot of the power is implied at this point, with only a hint of Merlot to soften and gently layer up through the palate. Extremely impressive. A yield of 40hl/ha, only very lightly affected by frost. 99% new oak. 

97 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate     Composed of 97% Cabernet Sauvignon, 2.5% Merlot and 0.5% Petit Verdot, the 2017 Lafite Rothschild is deep garnet-purple colored. It opens slowly, cautiously with restrained notes of chocolate-covered cherries, mulberries, warm blackcurrants and wild blueberries, followed by emerging notions of smoked meats, fragrant earth, crushed rocks and lilacs with touches of cast-iron pan and Marmite toast. Medium-bodied, the palate is deceptively light and quite ethereal on entry, growing in the mouth to reveal elegant layers of energetic red and black fruits with tons of savory accents. Framed by exquisitely ripe, wonderfully fine-grained tannins, it has exhilarating freshness and a very long, hypnotically perfumed finish. On a final note, the alcohol here is a jaw-dropping 12.5%, which is something of a miracle considering the ripeness of the Cabernet. A total head-turner, I cannot wait to follow the development of this wine! Rating: 97+

96 Points - Wine Spectator     This is a youthful tumble of warmed black currant, fig and blackberry paste flavors, entwined with bay leaf, tobacco, savory, lilac, smoldering charcoal and warm cast iron notes. Terrific stony minerality zips everything up for now, but riveting acidity and excellent energy should carry this easily in the cellar. Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot and Petit Verdot. Best from 2025 through 2040.

94 Points - Jeb Dunnuck     The grand vin 2017 Chateau Lafite-Rothschild checks as a Cabernet Sauvignon-dominated blend that includes just 2.5% Merlot and less than 1% of Petit Verdot, brought up in new French oak. It shows the classy, elegant style of both the vintage and the estate, revealing a ruby/purple hue, complex notes of red and black currants, lead pencil, and cedary herbs, medium-bodied richness and depth, and both present tannins and acidity. It checks in behind the 2015 and 2016 yet is nevertheless a classic Lafite. It will benefit from a decade of bottle age and keep for 30 years or more.

title: Merryvale Profile 2019
bodyHtml:
Merryvale Vineyards is a family-owned Napa Valley winery dedicated to passionate winemaking and the fine art of living well. Merryvale is committed to protecting and preserving the environment through conservation, renewable energy and sustainable farming practices at our three estate vineyards. 

Silkily structured and loaded with fruit, this wine is the embodiment of powerful elegance. 2018 was a remarkable vintage—the long growing season allowed the grapes to achieve full phenolic maturity, while the lack of extreme weather created the ideal conditions for harvesting at peak ripeness. The resulting wine is both a winemaker’s and wine lover’s dream—fresh, tense, deep, complex and long. Aromatics of allspice, blue fruits, leather, cocoa and endless other descriptors impress as the waves of lush texture wash over the palate. Full bodied without being heavy, the wine’s natural acidity provides the freshness to balance the generous structure and fine mountain tannin. The finish is long and rewarding. 

97 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

The flagship from Merryvale is the 2019 Cabernet Sauvignon Profile, a blend of 99% Cabernet Sauvignon and 1% Cabernet Franc that’s all from the estate vineyard and spent 23 months in 80% new barrels. Just classic Napa Valley Cabernet goodness, with lots of cassis and currant fruits, notes of spice, graphite, and chocolate, full-bodied richness, and great overall balance, it’s impeccably made and well worth seeking out. I can’t imagine it not evolving for 25+ years if well stored.

96 Points - Wine Enthusiast

This massively structured and intensely flavorful wine is one for the cellar, as its firm tannins and deep black fruit flavors are impressive now but will only get better integrated and lead to more complex flavors with time. The wine is rich in black cherries, blueberries and dark chocolate.

94+ Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

From an estate vineyard in Conn Valley, I suspect readers' reactions to the 2019 Cabernet Sauvignon Profile will depend on their tolerance for richness and ripeness. It's hugely concentrated, with dense notes of dark chocolate and cassis that come across as almost fudge-like, then linger on the finish.

93 Points - Decanter

A lush, dark and slow-moving wine, offering a steady wave of mulled black currant and steeped blackberry flavors, with roasted vanilla, loam and tobacco leaf notes. The muscular finish is a touch stolid now, but there's depth. 

92 Points - James Suckling

Black fruits, dark chocolate, dried thyme and lavender on the nose. Some charcoal and roasted espresso. Full body with plush tannins. Rich and creamy with a deep core of dark fruit and chocolate.

title: Pahlmeyer Proprietary Red Blend 2019
bodyHtml:
Pahlmeyer Proprietary Red Blend 2019 is a distinguished wine from Napa Valley, California. Crafted by Pahlmeyer Winery, this blend showcases the estate's dedication to producing exceptional Bordeaux-style wines. The 2019 vintage is composed of 78% Cabernet Sauvignon, 15% Merlot, 4% Petit Verdot, and 3% Cabernet Franc, sourced from the winery's high-elevation vineyards. The wine was aged for 20 months in nearly 100% new French oak barrels, enhancing its complexity and aging potential. 

Colour: Deep garnet hue, indicative of its concentration and aging potential.

Aroma: An expressive bouquet featuring notes of wild blueberry, black plum, cassis, saddle leather, and cedar, offering a complex and inviting profile.

Palate: The palate is opulent and expansive, with captivating flavors of crushed ripe blackberry and Castelvetrano olive. The focused fruit core is framed by generous fine-grained tannins, surging long with an echo of earth and spice.

Body: Full-bodied with a velvety mouthfeel, showcasing both power and finesse.

Finish: Long and satisfying, leaving a lasting impression of its complex flavors and harmonious structure.

Accolades:

  • 98 Points - James Suckling
  • 96 Points - Wine Enthusiast
  • 95 Points - Wine Advocate
  • 95 Points - Decanter

title: Colgin IX Estate Proprietary Red Blend 2018
bodyHtml:
The 2018 "IX Estate" begins with granite, charcoal, and sage aromas which transform into wild blueberry and black cherry. Salivating spices of turmeric and ginger add wildness and intrigue, building a strong sense of character in the wine. The texture of the 2018 "IX Estate" is intensely structured with sculpted tannins. The wine’s vibrant minerality and chiseled dense core stand out in its youth, yet will lead to a long, velvety quality on the palate as the wine evolves with time.

100 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2018 IX Estate is a blend of 77% Cabernet Sauvignon, 14% Cabernet Franc, 8% Merlot and 1% Petit Verdot. Very deep purple-black colored, it needs a little coaxing to reveal earth and mineral scents of iron ore, tilled soil, forest floor and truffles with ripe red and black currants, kirsch, Black Forest cake and mulberries plus nuances of tar, lilacs and Sichuan pepper. Full-bodied and built like a brick house, the palate has a rock-solid frame of firm, grainy tannins and exhilarating freshness supporting the taut, muscular fruit. Mineral and savory accents linger long into the epic finish. A thought-provoking, pensive, mesmerizing wine.

100 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

Another perfect wine, the 2018 Cabernet Sauvignon IX Estate is mostly Cabernet Sauvignon with 14% Cabernet Franc, 8% Merlot, and 1% Petit Verdot, all from the estate on Pritchard Hill. A monster of a wine that needs serious bottle age, it reveals a dense purple hue as well as a mineral-drenched bouquet of pure crème de cassis, charcoal, spring flowers, tobacco, and earth. Just incredible on the palate, it’s full-bodied and flawlessly balanced, with remarkable purity and a finish that won’t quit. Cabernet – or red wine for that matter – doesn’t get any better! It needs a solid 5-7 years of bottle age. but this legendary wine will see its 50th birthday in fine form.

98 Points - James Suckling

Extraordinary aromas of black truffles, blackberries, bark and violets. Essence of blackberries. Then it goes to crushed stones and pine needles. Aromatic perfection. Full-bodied with well framed tannins and beautiful dark fruit. Superb finish and intensity. Mountain character. Tannic at the end. Cooler and fresher undertone. 77% cabernet sauvignon, 14% cabernet franc, 8% merlot and 1% petit verdot. Try after 2027.

97 Points - Wine Spectator

A broad, lush style, with a big wave of warmed cassis and plum reduction flavors rolling through, yet this settles relatively gently rather than crashing through the finish, thanks to well-embedded, loamy grip and an alluring backdrop of roasted alder, bay leaf and licorice root notes. A wine that walks softly but carries a big stick. Cabernet Sauvignon, Cabernet Franc, Merlot and Petit Verdot. Best from 2022 through 2040

title: Domaine Armand Heitz Pommard Clos des Poutures Premier Cru Monopole 2021
bodyHtml:
New to Domaine bottling but far from new to viticulture in Burgundy, Heitz-Lochardet is a rising star. Armand Heitz is the dynamic heir to his family's winery, which has a history back to the mid-19th century. Upon completion of enology school, Heitz made the giant leap to begin bottling at his Domaine after generations of traditionally selling fruit to top négoicants such as Drouhin. Sustainable viticulture with minimal interference is at the foundation of Heitz's approach, with the results being clear in a well-rounded array of terroir-specific transparent wines.

Clos des Poutures is a monopole vineyard, solely in Armand Heitz's hands, producing wines of balance, pure fruit and complexity. This wine offers a great sense of softness and round texture without being overly so.

title: Paolo Scavino Barolo 'Monvigliero' 2019
bodyHtml:
The Paolo Scavino estate, established in 1921 by Lorenzo Scavino and his son Paolo, is a family-run winery located in Castiglione Falletto in the heart of Barolo. Now managed by Enrico Scavino and his daughters Enrica and Elisa, the estate has earned a stellar reputation for crafting expressive Barolos that reflect the nuances of their vineyard sites. The Monvigliero cru, located in the northern commune of Verduno, is renowned for producing elegant, perfumed Barolos and is widely considered one of the top crus of the region.

This 2019 vintage offers a graceful and complex expression of Nebbiolo. In the glass, it reveals a bright garnet hue with luminous clarity. The nose is captivating, with aromas of rose petals, red berries, sweet spices, and a touch of menthol. On the palate, it is medium-bodied with refined tannins and a layered structure, unfolding notes of cherry, raspberry, and licorice alongside hints of tobacco and crushed herbs. The wine exhibits remarkable balance, a silky texture, and a persistent, mineral-laced finish. Crafted entirely from 100% Nebbiolo, this Barolo is best enjoyed from 2025 through 2040.

Accolades
Wine Advocate – 94 points
Vinous – 94 points
James Suckling – 96 points

Food Pairing
Pair this wine with truffle risotto, braised lamb shanks, or porcini mushroom tagliatelle. The wine's elegance and aromatic complexity shine when matched with earthy and savoury dishes. This pairing highlights the wine’s depth and character.

title: Chateau Cos d'Estournel 2018
bodyHtml:
Finely structured and vibrant, Cos d'Estournel 2018 is both powerful and balanced, with very soft tannins. It offers a multitude of nuances, including remarkably elegant spices and an extremely long and lingering finish. It is an outstanding vintage with immense cellaring potential that will surely count among the most legendary vintages of the estate.

98+ Points - Jeb Dunnuck

An incredible wine from this estate. The 2018 Château Cos D'Estournel checks in at 74% Cabernet Sauvignon, 23% Merlot, 2% Cabernet Franc, and 1% Petit Verdot that was brought up in 50% new French oak. While some 2018s are going to offer pleasure right out of the gate, this isn't one of them, but rather it's a backward, tannic powerhouse of a wine that has flawless balance as well as a level of purity that's off the charts. Thrilling crème de cassis fruit, notes of lead pencil, damp earth, cedarwood, violets, and acacia flowers, full-bodied richness, masses of ultra-fine tannins, and a great, great finish all make for a legendary Saint-Estèphe that will need a good decade of bottle age yet evolve for 50 years or more. If you are tempted to try a bottle in its youth, it needs lots of air. 

98+ Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2018 Cos d'Estournel is a blend of 74% Cabernet Sauvignon, 23% Merlot, 2% Petit Verdot and 1% Cabernet Franc, aged in 50% new oak barriques. The alcohol weighs in at just over 14.5%. Sporting a deep purple-black colour, it needs a lot of swirling to begin to unlock a powerful nose of crème de cassis, stewed plums, wild blueberries and chocolate-covered cherries, followed by nuances of Sichuan pepper, star anise, tree and clove oil, plus a waft of charcoal. The full-bodied palate is densely packed with taut, muscular black fruits and earthy layers, framed by super firm, ripe, grainy tannins and seamless freshness, finishing very long and wonderfully earthy. A very impressive behemoth, this is going to need a good seven to 10 years to truly show its stuff and should drink for a good 40 years and beyond. 

98 Points - James Suckling

The richness and beauty of this wine are impressive with blackcurrant, cherry, berry and fresh cloves. The fruit is so pure here. Full-bodied with tannins that are so integrated and refined that you don’t feel them, yet they are there! Very creamy and layered with great length and beauty. It turns to tar and licorice at the finish. Tight now, but the texture is special.

97 Points - Decanter

A little closed on the nose, and also on the attack. There is a wall of tannin here but backed up by voluptuously ripe fruits that major on damson and fig, overlaid with cinnamon and saffron spices. Lilting acidity through the finish keeps a sense of momentum. This is powerful with ambition, and it carries it off perfectly. 65% of production went into the grand vin. 1% Petit Verdot makes up the blend, and the wine was aged in 50% new oak (a little lower than the usual 60%).

96 Points - Wine Enthusiast

Rich and dense, this wine is happily poised between ripe fruits and a deceptively powerful structure. Smoky flavours from wood aging combine with solid black fruits that strain but never overstep an impressive balance. This wine will age, promising much for the future.

96 Points - Wine Spectator

This is a bird of a different feather, with a ripe, sleek, and very polished feel as creamed loganberry, plum and boysenberry flavours spill forth, flanked for support by singed alder and incense notes, while black tea and savoury threads curl around the finish. Long, showy and lovely. Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Cabernet Franc and Petit Verdot.

title: Trivento Eolo Malbec 2018
bodyHtml:
EOLO, the Keeper of the Winds, is the pinnacle of Triventos' pursuit of the best Malbec in Argentina. Found only in a small refuge in Lujan de Cuyo, the birthplace of premium Malbec, Eolo is brought to life by winemaker German Di Cesare.

German searched far and wide for a vineyard with such a remarkable story to tell. At a privileged point 3,200 feet above sea level, the Eolo vineyard, planted in 1912 by Italian immigrants whose ancestors still farm the vineyards today, spreads out above the northern bank of the Mendoza River. Surrounded by centuries-old olive trees, this venerable Malbec vineyard captures these wizened vines' intense concentration and complexity. Today, like in ages past, the farmer's guiding hands and the winemaker's guiding vision bring Eolo to life so that each vintage reveals the terroirs' true expression.

94 Points - Wine Enthusiast

Great complexity on the nose with enticing floral, blackberry, plum and subtle oak notes. This red is concentrated and lively with firm and silky tannins. Due to the intelligent use of oak, the palate delivers plenty of dark fruit flavours with hints of smoke and nice acidity. It is an elegant, full-bodied wine made from 100-year-old vines and has a lingering finish with fruit flavours.

title: Verite 'Le Desir' 2019
bodyHtml:
Le Desir has a rich violet hue, ringed by a slender rim of incandescent purple-ruby color. Beautifully characteristic of Cabernet Franc, the aromatics of this wine are expressive and exotic, showing fresh rose petal perfume, fresh cherry blossom, California bay laurel, crushed pomegranate, blackberry coulis, and well-integrated French oak aromas of ground cinnamon, and brown buttered toast.

On the palate, a robust structure defined by powdery tannins and lively acidity delivers a very fine balance, with an exceptionally long finish.

Blend: 83% Cabernet Franc, 8% Merlot, 5% Malbec, 4% Cabernet Sauvignon

100 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2019 Le Desir is an exceptional blend of 83% Cabernet Franc, 8% Merlot, 5% Malbec and 4% Cabernet Sauvignon, offering complex, layered flavors, soaring aromatics and very detailed expression. Deep ruby-purple in color, its aromas unfold slowly and offer new nuances with each return to the glass: Morello cherries, warm chocolate, dried thyme, desiccated roses and dried herbs. The full-bodied palate offers concentrated, floral fruits, pixelated tannins, bursts of fresh acidity and a very long finish with layer after layer of detailed flavor.

100 Points - James Suckling

Sublime cabernet franc aromas of currants, flowers and citrus. Full-bodied with incredible purity of fruit and length. You don’t feel the tannins, but they are there. The acidity gives you dynamic reality and perfect length. A truly great wine. 83% cabernet franc, 8% merlot, 5% malbec, and 4% cabernet sauvignon. 

98 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

The 2019 Le Desir is based on Cabernet Franc, with the remainder 8% Merlot, 5% Malbec, and 4% Cabernet Sauvignon. It is complex and layered, with hints of saddle leather, pencil shavings, tangy red cherry, and blackcurrant. The palate is full and elegantly structured, with mocha, red plum, and turned soil. This is an incredible wine with lots of underlying tension that will be a pleasure to revisit if afforded the opportunity. Drink over the next 20 or more years.

title: Biondi Santi Brunello di Montalcino Riserva (Mixed Vintages) - 3 Bottles
bodyHtml:
Biondi-Santi Tenuta Greppo Brunello di Montalcino Riserva Vertical Collection 3x750ml.

1 x Bottle of 1998 

98 Points by Wine Enthusiast

Boasting alluring scents of new leather, truffle, camphor, pipe tobacco and just a whiff of tar, this just re-released Riserva from the estate's cellar is absolutely gorgeous. Loaded with finesse, the polished, vibrant palate delivers dried cherry, orange zest, cinnamon and nutmeg alongside silky, smooth tannins before finishing on a note of black tea. Still amazingly fresh and going strong. 

94 Points - Wine Spectator

Outer quote mark Features beautiful perfume, evoking rose, cherry, licorice and tobacco. Elegant, delicate even, with fine harmony and refinement. Cherry and raspberry flavors are persistent. Lacks the power of a 2001 or 1997, but shows finesse and filigree. Should come around sooner than the 1997.

1 x Bottle of 2008

96 Points by Wine Enthusiast

Impeccably balanced and loaded with finesse, this subtle stunner opens with aromas of blue flower, forest floor, truffle, moist soil and bright berry. The delineated palate offers juicy red cherry layered with white pepper, cinnamon and mineral alongside brisk acidity and firm but elegant tannins. It already has great depth but it's still young and austere so give it time to develop fully. 

92 Points - Robert Parker's  Wine Advocate

Outer quote mark The 2008 Brunello di Montalcino Annata is quite pretty in this vintage. It displays a classic profile of underbrush, tobacco, smoke, licorice and black cherries. The tannins are firm but nicely balanced. I expect the 2008 will drink well with minimum cellaring. It is one of the more open Brunellos I can remember tasting here. Still, there is plenty of Biondi Santi kick in the wine’s acidity and tannin profile. 

92 Points - Wine Spectator

Outer quote mark A vivid red, courtesy of its high acidity, driving cherry and raspberry flavors to the long finish. Spice, briar and earth notes are complementary, and the conclusion mouthwatering. 

91 Points -  James Suckling

Outer quote mark Aromas of dried strawberries and sliced lemon peel. Full body, with firm tannins and a silky textured finish. Tight and chewy. Strong acidity. 

1 x Bottle of 2016 

96 Points - Vinous

 The last vintage harvested and vinified by the Biondi Santi family, the 2016 Riserva was subsequently blended by technical director Federico Radi under the new ownership of EPI. It is seamless but difficult to deconstruct in its youth. Eventually, the dark and earthy personality is revealed, doling out liquorice root, moss, wet soil and heather. The tannins are compact and tightly stitched but with such a suave texture of fine chalk. These yield just enough to allow inner fruit sweetness to shine through. Think red cherry and hints of tarragon; then a blood orange tang which melds effortlessly into a bright beam of racy acidity. (

97 Points - Decanter

 A harmonious, balanced red, this sets the stage perfectly for the cherry, strawberry, floral, iron and tobacco flavors. Fresh and detailed, with a linear profile and refined structure driving the seemingly endless finish. Superb. (BS)  (4/2023)

98 Points -  Wine Spectator

 Aromas of strawberries, flowers, fresh mushroom, forest flower, sandalwood, and hints of balsamic. Full-bodied and tight on the finish. This is a linear and fine-tannined red. Available in March 2023. Needs another five years or so to show its full potential. New classic.  (8/2022)

98 Points - James Suckling

 The 2016 Brunello Di Montalcino Riserva is layered and unfolds in the glass with incense, baking spice, ripe red cherry, and cedar. It has more concentration and length through the mid-palate and offers an impeccable balance of structure, ripeness, and tension. It is expressive on the nose, but it is even more impactful at this stage with its intensity through the palate, with nearly electric energy of wild raspberry, rose petal, tea leaf, and orange zest. Allow for cellaring another 3-4 years.

98 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

 Wow, here is a vintage I've been anxiously waiting to try. The 2016 growing season was one of the best in recent memory in Montalcino, and if we look back in time, this vintage marks the year Biondi-Santi was sold to a French group. The prestigious 2016 Brunello di Montalcino Riserva proves a mighty collector's bottle that will undoubtedly gain in complexity and depth with careful bottle age. The wine offers wild nuances of forest berry and tart cherry, and there are herbal side notes as well as floral tones of dried violet and lilac. The tannins are soft, powdery and feel like they melt away on the palate. 

99 Points Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

 Savory depths of sage, red currants, underbrush, dried roses, worn leather, hints of iodine and cedar smolder up from the darkly alluring 2016 Brunello di Montalcino Riserva. This impresses first with its purity, then with its energy, seamlessly silky and refined, yet almost racy in style, with saline-infused wild berries and nuances of sour citrus that drench the palate, lifted by a flourish of mint. The 2016 finishes with crystalline tannins, creating an almost-crunchy sensation, as tart red fruits and nuances of licorice slowly taper off. There’s an invigorating feel to the 2016 Riserva that I’ve never witnessed from a bottle of Biondi Santi Brunello, which, coupled with a depth of beautifully pure and delineated fruits, makes it a total pleasure to taste. That said, the 2016 is structured and built for a long and prosperous maturation.

title: Chateau Cos D'Estournel 2017
bodyHtml:
98 Points - James Suckling

Quite the bottle here! Spices, such as nutmeg and cinnamon, as well as dried meat and plums with cedar and sandalwood. Full body. Deep and dense in the center palate and a long, long finish. Shows finesse and tightness. Very polished tannins. Long and ethereal.

98 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Deep garnet-purple colored, the 2017 Cos d'Estournel needs a little coaxing to unfurl, revealing beautiful expressions of preserved plums, boysenberries, blackcurrant pastilles and wild blueberries with hints of Indian spices, menthol, lilacs and mossy tree bark plus a compelling suggestion of iron ore. Medium to full-bodied, the palate has a solid backbone of firm, grainy tannins and well-knit freshness supporting the tightly wound blue and black fruits layers, finishing long and fragrant.

95 Points - Wine Enthusiast

95 Points - Vinous

title: E. Pira e Figli Chiara Boschis - Barolo 'Cannubi' 2020
Opus One 2022
bodyHtml:
