Opus One 2022 is a hallmark red blend from the Oakville appellation in Napa Valley, California.

The estate was founded in 1978 as a historic joint venture between Baron Philippe de Rothschild of Château Mouton Rothschild and renowned vintner Robert Mondavi. Combining French tradition with American innovation, the winery's sole mission is the pursuit of uncompromising quality through a single, iconic wine. The estate vineyards are farmed organically, with a focus on vine health and maintaining a balanced ecosystem to preserve the founders' vision for future generations.

Wine Description

The 2022 vintage presents a sophisticated and inviting sensory profile, exuding charm with primary aromas of blueberry, cassis, and dried rose petals. Underlying layers of cigar box, olive, and graphite add a rich complexity to the bouquet. On the palate, the wine is harmonious and balanced, featuring bright red-fruit flavours, cocoa, and fresh orange peel. It is characterized by fine-grained tannins and a long, elegant finish that offers lingering notes of wet stone, vanilla, and coffee.

The varietal composition of the 2022 blend is 80% Cabernet Sauvignon, 8% Petit Verdot, 6.5% Cabernet Franc, 5% Merlot, and 0.5% Malbec. After 20 days of skin contact, the wine was aged for 18 months in new French oak barrels. This vintage has an ABV of 14.0%.

Accolades

  • 97 Points - Decanter: "Chocolate, cherry and rose petal aromas on the nose. Very open and alive - this has a great energy from the aromatics alone with soft cedar shavings, vanilla bean and bramble fruit. Juicy and lively, this is full of fun - fruity and concentrated. The tannins are just wonderful, creamy and slightly grippy, extending the flavours vertically. Tons of juicy, succulent fruit - this feels quite modern but still with that flash of sunshine and ripeness. Long lasting with purity and delicacy that make it so enjoyable. A wonderful creation from Michael Silacci. This is not your typical blockbuster at all, this is a darling of a wine. 0.5% Malbec completes the blend. The Opus team chose to pick early and quickly given the heat spikes in 2022, starting with the Merlot on 24th August. Ageing 18 months in French oak."

  • 96 Points - James Suckling: "Generous, with savory aromas of ripe blackcurrants and fresh black cherries and a gentle texture that shows a slight nip of tannin. It is well structured and a bit tight, which is normal for a young cabernet sauvignon-based red that’s a proven collectible. Gives up graphite and pencil shavings, some cocoa and espresso. Full-bodied. Spicy, toasty oak is really showing through right now. Best from 2028."

  • 95 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate: '"icked before, during and after the year's early September heat, the 2022 Opus One—a blend of 80% Cabernet Sauvignon, 8% Petit Verdot, 6.5% Cabernet Franc, 5% Merlot and 0.5% Malbec—admirably reflects the vintage, boasting a ripe, extroverted personality but also a slightly open-knit, coarser mouthfeel than either the 2021 or 2023. Rosemary and sandalwood notes accent cherries on the nose, while the medium- to full-bodied palate is expansive and plush, finishing with ample length and soft tannins."

Food Pairing

The structured tannins and rich fruit profile of Opus One make it an ideal companion for marbled red meats, such as a seared filet mignon with sautéed mushrooms or a classic beef Bourguignon. It stands up beautifully to rare, grilled prime cuts or wine-braised stews. For a more diverse pairing, it can be served alongside a traditional French cassoulet or aged hard cheeses.

title: Aalto PS (Pagos Seleccionados) 2022
bodyHtml:
From the celebrated Ribera del Duero region of Spain, Aalto PS (Pagos Seleccionados) is a flagship bottling by Bodegas Aalto, a renowned project founded in 1999 by Mariano García—former winemaker at Vega Sicilia—and Javier Zaccagnini. The winery is recognized for its precision in viticulture and crafting wines with power, elegance, and longevity from old-vine Tempranillo.

Wine Description
The 2022 vintage of Aalto PS is a commanding expression of Tempranillo, showing intense, opaque purple hues in the glass. Aromas are layered and luxurious, with ripe blackberries, cassis, espresso, crushed violets, and a touch of balsamic lift. On the palate, it is full-bodied and richly structured, delivering concentrated flavours of dark fruit, dark chocolate, liquorice, and toasted oak, supported by finely grained tannins. The finish is enduring and polished, reflecting both the depth of the old vines and the meticulous élevage.

Accolades

  • James Suckling – 98 points

  • Robert Parker’s Wine Advocate – 95 points

  • Guía Peñín – 96 points

Food Pairing
Ideal with aged ribeye steak, braised short ribs, or wild mushroom risotto. A bold Manchego or aged Spanish blue cheese will also complement its intensity. Together, they create an unforgettable dining experience.

title: Eisele Vineyard Cabernet Sauvignon 'Altagracia' 2021
bodyHtml:
Altagracia unfolds with earthy notes of forest soil, humus and pine needles. After a swirl or two, scents of violets, cinnamon and blackberry, spring out of the glass with a hint of sandalwood. The mouthfeel is supple, velvety yet vibrant with tight-knit tannins accompanied by a crescendo of red and black currants and blackberries. This impression extends into a lingering finish of tobacco, cumin and turmeric with a stunning powdery texture of a freshly picked fruit. This mineral expression of the volcanic hillsides is the blueprint of Altagracia’s personality and offers a glimpse of its ageing potential. A spectacular expression of the eastern parcels of Eisele Vineyard.

96 Points - James Suckling

A solid Altagracia with currants, blueberries and pine and bark aromas and some sweet tobacco. Aromas that follow through on the palate to a full body with a well-framed tannin profile. Crunchy at the end. Juicy too.

94 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

Coming from more hillside parcels and slightly more volcanic soils, the 2021 Cabernet Sauvignon Altagracia checks in as a blend of 89% Cabernet Sauvignon, 6% Petit Verdot, and 5% Cabernet Franc. Aged in 82% new barrels, it has a deeper ruby hue to go with a beautiful perfume of darker currants, red plums, toasted spices, new leather, and dried tobacco. Medium to full-bodied, it has plenty of classic Napa Valley fruit yet also brings beautiful balance, ripe tannins, and a great finish.

title: Bouchard Pere & Fils Beaune Greves Vigne de L'Enfant Jesus 2022
bodyHtml:
Introduction

This superb red wine is from France, specifically the Burgundy region, in the Côte de Beaune subregion within the Beaune Premier Cru appellation. Bouchard Père & Fils, established in 1731, acquired a monopoly on this exceptional vineyard in the heart of Beaune Grèves in 1791, during the sale of national properties. The name 'Vigne de l'Enfant Jésus' ('Vineyard of the Child Jesus') refers to a historical anecdote where a Carmelite nun, Marguerite du Saint-Sacrement, predicted the birth of King Louis XIV. The vineyard is considered a benchmark for the appellation and, by some, an unofficial Grand Cru.

Wine Description

This Premier Cru is made from 100% Pinot Noir. The colour is more crimson than purple, with a vivid but not overly intense hue. The bouquet is lovely, with alluringly ripe aromas of blackberries, dark red berries, plum, spices, violets, and rose petals, sometimes revealing a whiff of leather. On the palate, the wine is medium to full-bodied, dense, broad, and enveloping, with great concentration and finesse. It features fruit flavours of black cherry and dark red berries, along with notes of wood and spice. The tannins are fine, silky, and powerful, lending a robust, serious, and built-to-age structure. The finish is long, velvety, and lifted by a refined, mineral, and saline note, distinguishing this unique wine. The optimal drinking window extends significantly, with potential for ageing for 30 years or more after the harvest, typically best enjoyed from 2027–2055. The ABV is 13.5% or 13%. This wine is made from organically grown grapes and is produced under the philosophy of Agriculture Raisonnée (sustainable farming).

96 Points - Decanter: The 2022 Baby Jesus is a wine of gorgeous intensity, with alluringly ripe aromas of blackberry and plum with notes of peony and spice. The forward fruits continue on the palate as intensely sweet and silky, with a density and grip that are only apparent with time. The grapes are from nearly four hectares of vines, although only the oldest vines and most concentrated fruit are used for this bottling, with some declassified into Beaune du Château. This wine will open in five to seven years and should easily drink for 30 more after the harvest.

title: Castiglion Del Bosco Brunello di Montalcino 2013
bodyHtml:
Situated in the province of Siena where the renown area of "Brunello di Montalcino" is found, Castiglion del Bosco encompasses approximately 4,450 acres of land, 125 of which are vineyards with plans to plant 15 more acres. 

Complexity, superb structure, and an inviting, mouthfilling palate are the hallmarks of this Sangiovese grown in the 42-hectare Capanna vineyard facing towards the Mediterranean sea. A garnet-flecked ruby red, it releases generous, emphatic fragrances classic to Sangiovese, developing a near-endless progression notable for its beautiful balance.

94 Points - James Suckling

The rose petal and cherry character really come through. Full body, layered and spicy. Orange peel. Flavorful finish. Shows structure and intensity. I love the texture. 

94 Points - Vinous

Luminous medium-dark red. The captivating nose combines sour red cherry, violet, coconut, tobacco, minerals and a hint of white pepper. Densely packed and youthful but very fresh and lively; this already boasts a silky texture and considerable early appeal owing to its noteworthy sweetness of fruit. Subtle notes of red berries, herbs, graphite and flowers carry through into the rising, very long, vibrant finish. A knockout Brunello that further confirms winemaker Cecilia Leoneschi’s talent at making exceptionally good, very classic Brunellos. I can think of very few wines in all of Italy that have improved more than Castiglion del Bosco’s over the last decade. Well done.”

92 - Wine Spectator

Shows intense, ripe cherry flavors, bordering on jammy, yet stays fresh, courtesy of the bright acidity and dense tannins. Young yet well-proportioned, with a lingering aftertaste of earth, graphite and tobacco. 

92 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Here's a Brunello that will surely see a solid ten-year evolution. The 2013 Brunello di Montalcino offers excellent balance and carefully delivered power. Both characteristics help to fuel the wine's smooth momentum over the palate. Dark fruit, plum and dried blackberry appear on the bouquet. Those fruity tones are followed by spice, leather and grilled herb.

title: Chateau Lafite Rothschild 2021
bodyHtml:
Château Lafite Rothschild, located in the Pauillac appellation of Bordeaux, France, is one of the most renowned First Growth estates. The 2021 vintage showcases the estate's commitment to producing exceptional wines, even in a challenging growing season.

Blend and Production

The 2021 Château Lafite Rothschild is composed of 96% Cabernet Sauvignon, 3% Merlot, and 1% Petit Verdot. The wine was aged in 90% new French oak barrels, contributing to its complexity, elegance, and long aging potential.

Tasting Notes

  • Appearance: Deep garnet hue with remarkable clarity.
  • Nose: Aromas of dense blackberry, forest floor, pencil shavings, and subtle floral undertones emerge with time.
  • Palate: Medium-bodied with impressive structure and more weight than typical for the vintage. Flavors of graphite, black currants, and a saline minerality are prominent, leading to a long, refined, and persistent finish.

Critical Acclaim

  • Wine Enthusiast: 98 points – Recognized for its layered black currant fruit and ripe tannins, with a long potential for aging.
  • Vinous (Antonio Galloni): 95-97 points – Described as having an imposing presence with flavors of black fruit, menthol, licorice, and sage.
  • Decanter: 97 points – Praised for its clarity, precision, and aromatic complexity.

Serving and Cellaring

The 2021 Château Lafite Rothschild is best served at around 60°F (15.5°C) to reveal its intricate aromas and flavors. Decanting is highly recommended to allow the wine to open up and fully express its character. While approachable in its youth, this vintage is designed for long-term aging, with optimal drinking from 2028 to 2050.

Conclusion

The 2021 Château Lafite Rothschild exemplifies the estate's mastery in creating harmonious and profound wines that stand out, even in more challenging vintages. Its combination of elegance, structure, and depth ensures it remains a benchmark for Bordeaux excellence and a treasure for collectors.

title: Argot Sage Ridge Cabernet Sauvignon 2021
bodyHtml:
This concentrated red wine originates from the Napa Valley AVA in California, United States. Argot is a micro-boutique winery founded in 2007 by self-taught winemaker Justin Harmon, who transitioned from a career in chemical and software engineering to pursue small-lot, artisanal production. The winery's philosophy emphasizes meticulous vineyard sourcing and a collaborative winemaking model, focusing on creating wines with rich fruit expression and structural depth. This specific bottling is sourced from the Sage Ridge Vineyard, a rugged, high-elevation site perched between 850 and 1,480 feet above Lake Hennessey in the Vaca Mountains. The vineyard is renowned for its complex patchwork of steep, well-drained metamorphic and sedimentary soils that force the vines to struggle, resulting in extraordinarily intense and concentrated fruit.

Wine Description

The Argot Sage Ridge Cabernet Sauvignon 2021 presents an opaque purple-black colour. The sensory profile is powerful and vivacious, opening with intense aromas of black currant jelly, black raspberries, and mulberries, layered with sophisticated notes of rose oil, bay leaves, graphite, and a hint of cardamom. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied and mouth-coating, showcasing decadent layers of black fruit preserves supported by firm yet plush tannins and a seamless freshness. It is characterized by its big, concentrated structure and an epic length on the finish. This 100% Cabernet Sauvignon has an ABV of 15.4% and was aged for 22 months in 100% new French oak barrels. The wine was bottled unfined and unfiltered to preserve its natural intensity and purity.

Vintage Quality

The 2021 vintage in Napa Valley is regarded as one of the best in recent memory, following a period of acute drought that led to small clusters and tiny berries. These conditions resulted in wines of exceptional flavour concentration, deep colour, and a refined phenolic structure with impressive natural acidity. Winemakers benefited from a steady, uneventful growing season that allowed for a long, slow ripening period, producing fruit with incredible vibrancy and aromatic perfume.

title: Ridge Vineyards Cabernet Sauvignon Monte Bello 2020
bodyHtml:
Ridge Vineyards, established in 1959 by Stanford engineers, has been a pioneer in California winemaking. Under the guidance of Paul Draper, who joined in 1969, Ridge emphasized natural winemaking techniques, including the use of native yeasts and minimal intervention. The Monte Bello vineyard, perched above Silicon Valley, is renowned for producing wines that reflect the unique terroir of the region.

Wine Description
The 2020 Monte Bello is a blend of 84% Cabernet Sauvignon, 11% Merlot, 4% Petit Verdot, and 1% Cabernet Franc. It presents an opaque ruby hue with aromas of ripe cassis, plum, red currant, toasty oak, vanilla, fennel, juniper berry, and bay laurel.

title: Borgogno Barolo Liste 2019
bodyHtml:
The colour is ruby with a garnet nail or garnet red. On the nose, it offers fresh notes of rose petals, wild strawberries, spice, mint, and dried lavender. Other aromatic descriptors include pressed rose, camphor, wild red berry, pipe tobacco, macerated cherries with mixed spices, thyme, dried violets, and roses. The palate is pulpy, lively, and savory, delivering juicy red cherry, raspberry compote, star anise, and cake spice. It is noted for its high flavour, with a cohesive and persistent taste, concluding with a balsamic breath. It is a full-bodied, structured wine made from 100% Nebbiolo. It is vibrant and balanced, set against a firm backbone of fine-grained tannins. The wine is tight and more reserved in its expression, offering understated depth and persistence.Optimal drinking is suggested from 2026–2050. 
This wine is organic.

Accolades

  • Jeb Dunnuck - 97 points

  • Kerin O'Keefe - 96 points

  • Wine Spectator - 95 points

  • James Suckling - 94 points

  • Wine Enthusiast - 94 points

Food Pairing

  • Suggested pairings include red meat, such as grilled ribeye, roast meats, or stews. It is also an excellent match for game dishes, like venison or wild boar stew.

  • Its characteristics are well-suited to dishes featuring truffles, such as truffle risotto or tagliatelle with truffle butter, or other strong flavours like aged cheeses such as Castelmagno or Parmigiano Reggiano.

  • A perfect match to enhance the wine's complexity.

title: Gaja Barolo Dagromis 2021
bodyHtml:
Introduction

Gaja Barolo Dagromis is a red wine from Italy, produced in the Piedmont region and the Barolo D.O.C.G. appellation. The wine is made by the Gaja winery, one of Italy's most fabled wine estates. The name 'DaGromis' is given in homage to the Gromis family, the original owners of the highly regarded vineyard sites that Gaja purchased in 1995. The winery's philosophy is centred on showcasing a broader expression of the Langhe's terroir by blending fruit from the distinct terroirs of La Morra and Serralunga d'Alba.

Wine Description

The wine is 100% Nebbiolo. It has an intense red or deep garnet red colour. The aromatic profile includes mixed aromatic herbs, spices, rose, anise, and wild fennel. Aromas of violets, rose petals, white pepper, licorice, and rich red currant also combine with balanced oak. It has a solid structure and is medium to full-bodied. The initial aromatics flow across the palate with freshness and harmonious complexity, revealing juicy red orange and red grapefruit. The classic licorice and mineral austerity is supported by oak and noticeable tannins, which soften as the wine ages. Stylistically, it is a sensational Barolo famous all over the world, possessing extraordinary elegance and great importance. The grapes are fermented and macerated in stainless steel tanks for three weeks.

Food Pairing

This rich red wine with great importance is perfect with sophisticated main dishes. Suggested pairings include roasted or braised meat, game, mild game dishes, and risotto.

title: Chateau Duhart Milon 2022
bodyHtml:
Chateau Duhart Milon is a historic Bordeaux estate owned by Domaines Barons de Rothschild (Lafite) since 1962. Nestled on the western edge of Pauillac, this fourth growth estate under the 1855 Classification benefits from the exceptional terroir shared with its prestigious neighbour, Chateau Lafite Rothschild. Known for its rigorous vineyard management and traditional yet precise winemaking, Duhart Milon represents elegance and finesse.

Wine Description
This 2022 vintage reveals a deep ruby-purple hue with striking clarity. The nose opens with layers of cassis, blackberry, and violets, underpinned by cedar, graphite, and a touch of tobacco — hallmark traits of Pauillac. On the palate, it is medium to full-bodied, with fine-grained tannins and a poised structure. Flavours of dark plum, black cherry, and cocoa meld with savoury notes of forest floor and pencil lead. The finish is long and harmonious, delivering a sense of freshness and age-worthy balance.

Accolades
● Wine Advocate - 94 points.
● James Suckling - 96 points.
● Decanter - 94 points.

Food Pairing
Ideal alongside herb-crusted rack of lamb, dry-aged ribeye steak, or wild mushroom risotto. The wine's firm structure and dark fruit core make it a compelling match for hearty dishes, while its finesse elevates more refined preparations. Together, they create an unforgettable dining experience.

title: Luigi Baudana Barolo 'Baudana' 2021
bodyHtml:
This exceptional red wine originates from the Barolo DOCG in the Piedmont region of Northern Italy. It is crafted from the historic Baudana cru, a legendary vineyard site in the subregion of Serralunga d'Alba. For over 30 years, Luigi Baudana and his wife Fiorina tended to these vines before entrusting the estate to the Vajra family in 2009. Giuseppe Vajra now manages the property with a philosophy that respects the legacy of the Baudana family, who have inhabited this specific land for so long that their arrival predates local records.

Wine Description

The Luigi Baudana Barolo 'Baudana' presents a bright garnet red hue with ruby reflections. The nose is intensely fragrant, revealing a complex bouquet of dried cherries, blood orange, and raspberries, intertwined with notes of potpourri, cinnamon, and graphite. On the palate, the wine is full bodied and powerful, yet displays a smooth and velvety attack. It features firm, fine grained tannins and a refreshing acidity that provides remarkable tension and energy. The finish is long and precise, marked by a characteristic mineral salty vein and savory notes of eucalyptus and tobacco.

Accolades

  • James Suckling - 97 points

  • Wine Spectator - 96 points

  • Jeb Dunnuck - 96 points

  • Vinous - 95 points

  • Robert Parker's Wine Advocate - 95 points

  • Decanter - 94 points

Food Pairing

This Barolo is an excellent match for rich, savory dishes such as braised veal cheek with a red wine reduction or porcini mushroom risotto. It also pairs beautifully with aged cheeses like Castelmagno or Taleggio, which complement the wine's structured tannins.

title: Louis Latour Aloxe Corton Premier Cru 'Les Chaillots' 2020
bodyHtml:
Aloxe-Corton is the home village of the Latour family who have been closely involved in the affairs of the commune for over three centuries. Of the total hectarage of this Premier Cru, Domaine Louis Latour controls over 90% of the production centred on the famous Château and cuverie of Corton-Grancey. These vines are an important part of Domaine Louis Latour. 

The name 'Les Chaillots' refers to the stony, pebbly nature of the soil in this vineyard, as 'caillou' means pebble in french. There is an alliance in the wines of Aloxe-Corton between the finesse of a Cote de Beaune and the mellow, powerful appeal of the Côte de Nuits.

The Aloxe-Corton 1er Cru 'Les Chaillots' has a deep ruby colour and offers aromas of cherry, licorice and walnuts. The mouthfeel is very delicate and fresh. The finish is rather long and well balanced.

94 Points - James Suckling

92 Points - Wine Spectator

title: Domaine Maldant Pauvelot Corton 'Renardes' Grand Cru 2017
bodyHtml:
Domaine Maldant Pauvelot's Corton 'Renardes' Grand Cru 2017 hails from the esteemed Côte de Beaune region in Burgundy, France. This family-owned estate, established in 1893 by Jean Pauvelot, has been passed down through generations, expanding while preserving its founders' spirit. Today, under the guidance of sixth-generation owner Jean-Luc Maldant, the domaine is recognized for its commitment to traditional viticulture and modern oenological practices, producing wines that reflect the unique terroir of Burgundy.

Wine Description

This Grand Cru Pinot Noir presents an intense velvety crimson hue, deepening towards magenta. The nose offers a generous aromatic expression of fruit notes, including blueberry, gooseberry, and kirsch cherry, complemented by violet flowers. As the wine evolves, it reveals complex layers of underbrush, leather, pepper, and licorice. On the palate, it is well-built, powerful, and muscular, with a chewy body that comes to the forefront. Firm, frank, and fat, this wine requires time (4-12 years) to reach its peak, rewarding patience with a harmonious and opulent finish.

Accolades

While specific critic scores are not available, this wine holds an average rating of 4.4 out of 5 based on consumer reviews, indicating high appreciation among wine enthusiasts.

Food Pairing

This robust wine pairs excellently with richly flavoured meats such as roast or grilled beef, braised game, or dishes in sauce. It also complements strong, soft-centred cheeses and blue cheeses, creating an unforgettable dining experience.

Vintage Quality

The 2017 vintage in Burgundy was generally very good. Following a challenging 2016 season, the vines showed resilience, leading to wines with balance and depth. This vintage offers outstanding concentration and precision, reflecting both the terroir's excellence and the winemaker's expertise.

title: Carruades de Lafite 2020 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
Chateau Lafite Rothschild’s second wine, Carruades de Lafite presents similar characteristics to the Grand Vin, but with its own personality linked to a higher proportion of Merlot and to specific plots that are used to produce Carruades. The name comes from the Carruades plateau, a group of plots acquired in 1845 just next to the vines on the Château hilltop.

96+ Points - James Suckling

This is very classically structured with a palate that starts off slowly. Full-bodied and chewy with a soft, creamy texture and a long finish. Savory. A touch austere. 52% cabernet sauvignon, 42% merlot and 3% cabernet franc, the rest petit verdot.

94+ Points - Wine Enthusiast

With its elegant tannins and velvety Merlot in the blend, the wine brings out both the richness of the year and its great fruit. Behind it all there is this superb structure that makes this second wine of Lafite-Rothschild a great wine in its own right. 

93 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

This Chateau has made truly legendary wines in 2020. Looking at the vintage, the harvest occurred all in September, and their second wine, the 2020 Carruades De Lafite, is based on 52% Cabernet Sauvignon, 42% Merlot, and the rest Cabernet Franc and Petit Verdot that was raised in 90% new French oak. The alcohol hit 13% and the pH is 3.84. It's much more open and expressive than the Grand Vin and offers beautiful darker red and black fruits as well as leafy tobacco, cedar pencil, and spicy nuances. Medium-bodied, layered, and concentrated, it has the vintage's more structured, firm feel on the palate, rock-solid mid-palate depth, and a great finish. It needs 4-5 years of bottle age but will evolve for two decades.

92 Points - Decanter

More Merlot than in 2019, but as you find repeatedly in 2020, the Cabernet Sauvignon plays an oversized role in the flavour profile. This has a ton of impact and intensity, coffee and black chocolate with angular tannins that will benefit from softening over ageing. Plenty of Pauillac signature here, with liquorice root and tobacco leaf. A slate texture gives definition to the end of play. 3% Petit Verdot completes the blend.

91+ Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Deep purple-black in color, the 2020 Carruades de Lafite, like its big sibling, is a little youthfully shy to begin, soon unfurling to offer notes of Morello cherries, raspberry leaves, baked blackberries and spice box, plus suggestions of pencil lead, lavender and Provence herbs. The medium-bodied palate is chock-full of juicy black fruits, framed by velvety tannins and tons of freshness, finishing long and lifted. This 2020 is a blend of 52% Cabernet Sauvignon, 42% Merlot, 3% Cabernet Franc and 3% Petit Verdot.

title: Chateau Trotte Vieille 2016
bodyHtml:
98 Points - James Suckling

Complex aromas of blackberries, dried flowers and other dark fruit. Shows hints of cedar and blackberries. Full-bodied, dense and wonderfully integrated with rich tannins that just melt into the wine. Extremely fine and focused finish. Shows harmony and balance. 

96 Points - Tim Atkin

A wine that carries its 100% new oak lightly, especially at this young age, this is a serious, concentrated St Emilion that’s built for the longer haul, but already shows the poise, texture and filigree tannins that define the Trottevieille style. 

95 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

94 Points - Decanter

title: Chateau Mouton Rothschild 2003 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
The wine has a beautifully intense, garnet hue and a highly refined nose, rather typical of Cabernet, on aromas of blackcurrant and cedarwood along with caramel and stewed fruit. The attack is lush, the palate rich, on stylish, well-rounded tannins; fruit flavours rub shoulders with spice, Havana cigar and eucalyptus. The finish is very expressive, long and powerful, harmonious and silky.

Blend: 76% Cabernet Sauvignon, 14% Merlot, 8% Cabernet Franc, 2% Petit Verdot

95 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Backward, powerful, and extremely tannic, the dense purple-coloured 2003 Mouton-Rothschild, a blend of 76% Cabernet Sauvignon, 14% Merlot, 8% Cabernet Franc, and 2% Petit Verdot, fashioned from yields of 28 hectoliters per hectare, with finished alcohol of 12.9%, improves dramatically with aeration. With full-bodied, meaty, robust, dry flavours and a huge finish, this high-class wine should be at its finest between 2012-2040+. During its sojourn in barrel, it reminded me of a hypothetical blend of the 1982 and 1986 Moutons, but bottling appears different and even more tannic than those two vintages. I still believe the finest recent Mouton-Rothschild is the 2000.

94 Points - Wine Spectator

Blackberry, cherry and currant with just a hint of toasted oak. Full-bodied, with silky tannins and a lovely combination of ripe fruit and vanilla character. Goes on and on. Long and very stylish. Balanced and refined. Best after 2011. 23,330 cases were made.

title: Chateau Pavie 2022
bodyHtml:
From the prestigious Saint-Émilion appellation on Bordeaux’s Right Bank, Chateau Pavie hails from France’s renowned Bordeaux region. The estate, classified as Premier Grand Cru Classé ‘A’, is owned by Gérard Perse, who acquired it in 1998. Under his stewardship and the guidance of celebrated oenologist Michel Rolland, Pavie has become a benchmark for modern Bordeaux, known for its bold, structured style and meticulous viticultural practices.

The 2022 vintage showcases a deep, saturated ruby hue. On the nose, it offers a rich bouquet of black cherries, plums, crushed violets, graphite, and warm spices. The palate is full-bodied and layered, delivering velvety tannins and flavours of ripe dark fruits, licorice, espresso, and hints of dark chocolate. A persistent mineral streak and a long, elegant finish underscore its complexity.

Accolades

  • Jeb Dunnuck - 96+ points

  • Decanter - 96 points

  • James Suckling - 95+ points

Food Pairing
Pair this grand vin with roast lamb, duck breast with cherry sauce, or truffle risotto. The wine’s structure and depth also make it a fine match for dry-aged ribeye or braised short ribs. Together, they create an unforgettable dining experience.

title: Chateau Cheval Blanc 2020
bodyHtml:
Chateau Cheval Blanc 2020 is a prestigious red wine from the Saint Emilion Grand Cru appellation on the Right Bank of Bordeaux, France. Historically situated on the border of Pomerol, the estate has been managed for over 150 years with a philosophy of capturing a unique 'place in a glass' through its mosaic of 55 different vineyard plots. The winery focuses on micro-vinification in custom concrete tanks to ensure each parcel accurately reflects its specific terroir and the distinct climatic conditions of the vintage.

Wine Description

This vintage possesses a deep purple-black hue. The nose is extraordinarily complex and kaleidoscopic, revealing a bouquet of sweet red and black fruits, plum preserves, and blueberries, layered with scents of rose petals, violets, Indian spices, and sweet tobacco. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied and impeccably balanced, featuring 'cashmere-textured' fruits and refined, silky tannins. Stylistically, it is noted for its mind-blowing elegance, seamless harmony, and a long, saline finish that echoes with notes of graphite and liquorice. The varietal composition for this vintage is 65% Merlot, 30% Cabernet Franc, and 5% Cabernet Sauvignon. The optimal drinking window is approximately between 2027 and 2065.

Accolades

  • Jeb Dunnuck – 100 points

  • Vinous – 99 points

  • Decanter – 98 points

  • James Suckling – 98 points

  • Wine Spectator – 96 points

title: Timeless 2020 by Silver Oak Vineyards
bodyHtml:
Timeless Napa Valley is a tribute to Silver Oak co-founder Ray Duncan. Inspired by the song, Timeless, which his son David (Silver Oak Proprietor) co-wrote for Ray’s 85th birthday, this new single vineyard red wine embraces Ray’s entrepreneurial spirit and the lessons he taught us. To never take ourselves or life too seriously. Celebrate! And that true sustainability is about passing it on to the next generation.

A marriage of fruit from Timeless' brightest blocks, this wine has flavors of red raspberry, licorice and notes of fresh flowers kissed by a warm summer sun. There is a silky texture on the palate that unfolds with plushness and balanced weight, and the lingering finish is accentuated with a vibrant blackberry return. Well-integrated and nuanced, this wine is the personification of determination and beauty.

94 Points - Decanter

In 2020, this wine offers a fragrant, bright, and lifted nose with lovely red and black currants, savoury sagebrush, tobacco, and dried red florals with blood orange. Medium-bodied with a gorgeous tapestry of crunchy red cranberry, plums, and cherry. Crushed stone mineral notes form a solid base from which baking notes of dark chocolate emerge. The tannins are persistent, building, and turn chalky as they resolve. This wine has plenty of acid grip and a beautiful, quiet intensity. It has excellent cellar potential.

title: Azelia Barolo Margheria 2014
bodyHtml:
The Azelia 2014 Margheria Barolo is a beautiful example of this vintage. The scents of sliced strawberries, cherries, fresh-cut flowers, licorice, spices, and damp stones all gain shape as the wine slowly unwinds in the glass. It is elegant and classy. On the palate, this is tightly wrapped, has a core of brilliant red fruits that remain memorable throughout the extraordinarily long finish, and has a beautiful overall structure. There is no doubt about the 2014's quality, but it is still relatively restrained at this young age and needs a lot of time in the cellar to mature and soften. It undoubtedly can develop nicely over time, but persistence will be crucial.

93 Points - Wine Spectator

Savoury, boasting lavender, juniper and mint aromas, yet there are sweet ripe cherry and plum fruit flavours for balance. It builds to a long finish, where big tannins reign.

title: Borgogno Barolo Riserva 2017
bodyHtml:
Introduction

Borgogno Barolo Riserva 2017 is a red wine from Italy, produced in the Piedmont region and the Barolo D.O.C.G. appellation. Borgogno is one of the most historic Barolo producers, with a classic style and a history that dates back to 1861. The Riserva is a selection of the best grapes from the winery's most important Crus: Cannubi, Liste, and Fossati, which are three single vineyards in the Barolo district. The Farinetti family currently owns the estate, with Andrea Farinetti leading the winemaking direction.

Wine Description

The wine has an intense ruby red colour with luminous garnet hues. The nose is alluring and profound, offering attractive floral notes of dried red fruits, rose hips, dried rose petals, and forest berry. Further complexity includes sweet spices, cinnamon, licorice, walnuts, balsamic herbs, tarry smoke, and crushed stones.

The blend is 100% Nebbiolo. The wine is full bodied and robust. The palate is velvety, warm, powerful, concentrated, and vigorous, with sour cherry and cranberry flavours framed by firm tannins and racy acidity. It is layered and broad, with fine tannins that are firm and vibrant at the same time. It is aged for six years in large barrels of Slavonian oak, followed by six months of ageing in the bottle before release. Stylistically, it is a fine tuned, spicy, youthfully austere, and elegant wine that is destined for long ageing. The ABV is 14.5%. It is already approachable, but even better after four to five years and onward, with a longevity of over 15 years. Information on the organic status of the wine is not available in the sources.

Accolades

  • James Suckling - 96 points

  • Wine Spectator - 93 points

  • The Wine Advocate - 95+ points

Food Pairing

This wine is an ideal pairing for red meat main courses, important first courses, meat main courses, and aged cheeses. It is also a perfect companion for stews with red meat, game, mature hard cheeses, or truffle dishes.

Vintage Quality

The 2017 vintage for Piedmont was considered difficult. The winter was unusually warm and dry with no snow, which caused an early budbreak. The vintage is described as having produced a deep, tumultuous, and incisive wine.

title: Chateau Smith Haut Lafitte Rouge 2022
bodyHtml:
Château Smith Haut Lafitte, located in the Pessac-Léognan appellation of Bordeaux, France, is a historic estate dating back to 1365. Since its acquisition by Daniel and Florence Cathiard in 1990, the château has undergone significant renovations, elevating its reputation for producing exceptional wines that embody elegance and complexity.

Wine Description

The 2022 Château Smith Haut Lafitte Rouge is a blend of 64% Cabernet Sauvignon, 32% Merlot, 3% Cabernet Franc, and 1% Petit Verdot. This wine presents a deep garnet-purple hue. On the nose, it offers aromas of blackcurrant jelly, redcurrant preserves, boysenberries, and pencil lead, complemented by hints of lilacs, Sichuan pepper, and cedar chest. The full-bodied palate is structured with firm tannins and delivers mouth-coating black fruits with red berry sparks, finishing with a refreshing mineral lift.

Accolades

100 Points - Decanter: Deep and evocative, this bursts with blackcurrants, milk chocolate and floral perfume. Instantly captivating, the palate is silky yet structured, with tannins seamlessly supporting vibrant red and black berries. Broad and powerful, yet it glides, showcasing Cabernet’s structure, Merlot’s generosity and cool spiced fruit. A mineral core adds complexity, with flint-like nuances. A masterclass in power and balance - and unmistakably Smith. (GH)

100 Points - Jeb Dunnuck: Looking at the Grand Vin, the 2022 Château Smith Haut Lafitte checks in as a blend of 64% Cabernet Sauvignon, 32% Merlot, and the rest Cabernet Franc and Petit Verdot that was raised in 60% new French oak. Reminding me of a more elegant version of the 2010, it has a dense purple hue to go with a rich, powerful, full-bodied, sensationally complex nose of cassis and darker berries interwoven with woodsmoke, scorched earth, chocolate, and chalky minerality. Concentrated, deep, and layered on the palate with ripe, velvety tannins, it's a sensational, absolutely heavenly effort that will keep for 40-50 years. Along with the 2009, 2010, and 2020, this is one of the greatest wines to ever come from this address. Don't miss it.

97- 99 Points - Wine Enthusiast: The wine is dominated by fine Sauvignon Blanc. It has a marvelous poise between great freshness and richness, which is especially impressive given it's from a dry year. This is a powerful wine, a great success given the growing conditions. (RV)

98 Points - Jane Anson: The exceptional 2022 vintage and here they pull off the same trick as in 2018, where the vintage is exuberant and opulent, but not so big that it overpowers the estate signature. Layers, waves, flavours that are rooted to the spot and yet rising through the palate, no question about the longevity of this wine, and although expansive, it retains Cabernet Sauvignon character, with its cassis bud and crushed mint leaf edge that weaves through the tannic architecture. So good. Fabien Teitgen technical director.

98 Points - James Suckling: The vivid fruit character here is so impressive for this hot and dry vintage. It's medium- to full-bodied, showing gorgeous crushed grapes and dark berries. With density, clarity and beauty, it really speaks of great cabernet sauvignon. The tannins are integrated and go long, taking you deep and complete on the palate.

Food Pairing

This wine pairs exceptionally well with rich dishes such as grilled beef, lamb, and game meats. These pairings highlight the wine’s depth and character, creating an unforgettable dining experience.

title: Domaine Michel Noellat Vosne-Romanee 'Les Beaux Monts' Premier Cru 2021
bodyHtml: A wine with a very pretty colour and a nose of great complexity. On the palate, it is aromatic and generous.

title: Armand Heitz Meursault Premier Cru "Perrieres" 2021
bodyHtml:
Introduction

The Armand Heitz Meursault Premier Cru 'Perrieres' 2021 is a distinguished white wine from the Côte de Beaune region of Burgundy, France. The estate, currently managed by Armand Heitz, carries a winemaking legacy dating back to 1857 and is rooted in a philosophy of regenerative agriculture and permaculture to create a sustainable ecosystem. The winery emphasizes minimal intervention, allowing the precise expression of the 'Perrieres' terroir—renowned for its marly, stony soils—to shine through in every bottle.

Wine Description

This 100% Chardonnay presents a pale yellow hue with elegant golden reflections. The nose offers a complex aromatic profile featuring white flowers, fresh hazelnut, and subtle hints of fresh butter and citrus. On the palate, the wine is full bodied and powerful yet maintains a bright acidity and creamy texture, leading to a long finish characterized by distinct mineral and fruity notes. Aged for 11 months in oak barrels (20-40% new), it possesses a compact and concentrated structure with an optimal drinking window between 2026 and 2035.

title: The Pact by Faust 2021
bodyHtml:
The 2021 Faust "The Pact" Cabernet Sauvignon is a compelling expression of Napa Valley's Coombsville terroir. Known for its balance and vibrancy, this wine emphasizes both intensity and finesse.

Colour: Deep ruby with a bright, youthful hue.
Aroma: Bursting with vivid blue fruit, including blueberries and black cherries, complemented by notes of exotic spices like star anise, sweet tobacco, and olive.
Palate: Rich with flavors of black raspberry and blueberry, supported by graphite minerality and a savory touch of herbs. Its chalky tannins provide structure, while the acidity keeps it fresh and energetic.
Body: Full-bodied with a smooth, refined texture.
Finish: Long and complex, with iron-rich minerality adding depth to the lingering fruit and spice.

Accolades:
97 Points – James Suckling

This vintage benefits from near-ideal growing conditions, with a cool summer that allowed tannins to mature slowly, resulting in a balanced, structured wine. The 2021 Pact has the potential to develop further in the bottle over the next 15-20 years, making it a great candidate for aging. It pairs beautifully with game meats or grilled beef, enhancing the wine’s savory undertones and earthy nuances.

title: Chateau Pontet Canet 2022
bodyHtml:
This distinguished red wine hails from France, specifically the renowned Pauillac appellation in Bordeaux’s Left Bank. Chateau Pontet Canet, classified as a Fifth Growth in the 1855 Classification, has been under the stewardship of the Tesseron family since 1975. Known for their pioneering biodynamic practices in Bordeaux, the estate emphasizes a deep respect for terroir and nature, resulting in wines of exceptional purity and energy.

Wine Description

The 2022 vintage of Chateau Pontet Canet showcases a deep, opaque ruby hue that hints at its concentration. On the nose, it bursts with vibrant aromas of blackcurrant, blackberry, and blueberry, layered with subtle notes of violets, graphite, and cedar. The palate is full-bodied and opulent, yet impeccably balanced, displaying lush dark fruit, fine-grained tannins, and an undercurrent of crushed stone minerality. The finish is long and graceful, revealing touches of cocoa and spice.

Accolades

  • Jeb Dunnuck - 100 Points

  • Wine Enthusiast - 100 Points

  • James Suckling - 99 Points

Food Pairing

Pair this profound Pauillac with herb-crusted rack of lamb, aged ribeye steak, or a mushroom truffle risotto. This pairing highlights the wine’s depth and character, allowing its layered complexity to shine alongside rich, savoury dishes.

title: Castellare Di Castellina 'I Sodi di San Niccolo' 2019 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
Castellare di Castellina 'I Sodi di San Niccolo' 2019 originates from Italy, within the Tuscany region and the Chianti Classico area. The estate was founded in the late 1970s when Paolo Panerai merged four smaller farms with the goal of producing wine of the highest possible quality. The winemaking philosophy is rooted in a deep respect for tradition and the environment, which is reflected in the iconic labels featuring birds to represent the winery's commitment to avoiding synthetic chemicals that could harm the local ecosystem.

Wine Description

This red wine presents a deep, intense ruby red colour and possesses a full, structured body. The sensory profile is elegant and complex, featuring an aromatic nose of red berries, black cherries, and plums, complemented by notes of vanilla, liquorice, and tobacco. On the palate, it is concentrated and harmonious, delivering rich fruit flavours supported by firm, silky tannins and a vibrant acidity. The finish is exceptionally long and persistent, showcasing great depth and a refined spicy character.

  • Varietal Composition: A blend of 85% Sangioveto (a local Sangiovese clone) and 15% Malvasia Nera.

  • Stylistic Notes: The wine is celebrated for its incredible longevity and complexity, having been matured for 24 to 30 months in French oak barriques followed by 12 months in the bottle.

  • ABV: 14.5%.

  • Organic Status: While not certified organic, the estate strictly follows sustainable viticulture and has prohibited the use of herbicides and pesticides since its inception to protect local wildlife.

Food Pairing

The robust structure and refined tannins of this wine make it an ideal partner for flavourful and savoury dishes.

  • Meats: Pairs excellently with grilled red meats, Florentine steak, and roasted game such as wild boar or venison.

  • Savoury: Suggested pairings include traditional Tuscan pasta dishes with meat ragù or truffle infused risotto.

  • Cheese: Matches well with mature, hard cheeses like aged Pecorino Toscano or Parmigiano Reggiano.

Vintage Quality

The 2019 vintage in Tuscany is regarded as an exceptional and classic year, characterized by a balanced growing season with ideal temperature shifts. These conditions allowed for slow, even ripening, resulting in grapes with fantastic aromatic intensity and structural harmony. The winemaker's skill in managing the harvest during this high quality season has produced a wine that perfectly captures the elegance and power of the Castellina terroir.

title: Nicolas Maillart Brut Rose (NV)
bodyHtml:
Salmon-pink in colour with a fine, lingering mousse. Intense with notes of fruit (ripe and from the forest floor).

The initial impact is wonderfully fresh and vinous, followed by great finesse.

title: Purlieu Cabernet Sauvignon 2018
vendor: 300747 - South By Southwest Wine Imports Inc.
bodyHtml: Dark magenta in the glass, this muscular wine showcases Napa Valley terroir at its best. The nose opens with blue fruit and blackcurrant aromas that uplift and entice. A dense, richly fruited core of blueberry, boysenberry and blackcurrant commands attention, with subtler notes of graphite and baking spices adding dimension. Powerful and fresh, this full-bodied wine sustains spicy blueberry, clove and sweet dried mint aromas through a satisfying finish.

title: Talenti Brunello di Montalcino 'Piero' 2017
bodyHtml:
Selezione Piero has been created as a tribute to the work of Pierluigi Talenti, who has worked passionately with sangiovese over the years. The vineyard measures 1.95 Ha, not far from the winery, with unique soil and climate characteristics, distinguished from all the others by its attributes of constant quality. 

Intense red color, complex fresh aroma and rich in hints of ripe red fruit, plum, blackberry and raspberry, which combine with the spices of aging such as chocolate, tobacco and licorice. Powerful and tonic on the palate with good balance and softness, finally the tannins are sweet and elegant.

This wine is particularly suited to accompany red meat, game, cold meat and wild boar ragu.

92 Points - Wine Enthusiast

Forest floor, new leather, camphor and tobacco are some of the aromas you'll find on this full-bodied red. Elegantly structured, the polished palate delivers dried cherry, prune and mocha framed in velvety, supple tannins. Drink through 2027.

title: Borgogno Barolo Fossati 2019
bodyHtml:
The wine is a rich, transparent brick red or a ruby/brick colour with medium intensity. It is made from 100% Nebbiolo grapes, the varietal responsible for Italy’s finest aged wines. The aroma includes notes of tobacco, violet, ripe black-skinned fruit, and cake spice, with forward spices of anise, white pepper, smoky incense, and dried cherries. Other notes include red fruits, light oak, and chocolate. The full-bodied and enveloping palate delivers fleshy Morello cherry, black raspberry, cinnamon, and mocha, with citrus-inflected and rocky dried mineral notes. Additional flavours noted are cherries, plums, currants, light wood, spices, coffee, earth, dark chocolates, tobacco leaf, herbs, and black pepper. The wine is complex, with tension and nervous energy, showing fresh acidity and a clean feel. It has tightly woven, fine-grained tannins that lend a velvety texture and medium-plus finish with fine-grained tannins and tangy raspberries. 

The wine is made from organically grown grapes and the vineyard practices are transitioning to organic farming. The optimal drinking window is generally suggested as 2026–2046.

Accolades

  • Wine Enthusiast - 96 points

  • Kerin O'Keefe - 96 points

  • Jeb Dunnuck - 96 points

  • Raffaele Vecchione - 95 points

  • Wine Spectator - 93 points

Food Pairing

Suggested pairings include main courses of roast meats, stewed or braised meats, game, and aged cheeses. Traditional Piedmontese meat main courses, goulash, or Japanese gyoza are also suggested.

A perfect match to enhance the wine's complexity.

title: Chateau Giscours 2018
bodyHtml:
This Classified Growth in 1855 is the first label of Château Giscours. It is one of great finesse. Delicacy and power are combined in this flask to bring you the elegance expected of a great Margaux wine. The aging potential of this great wine is between 8 and 20 years or even more for the most exceptional vintages.

97 Points - James Suckling

Black currant, dried-blueberry, oyster-shell, black-olive, black truffle, and bitter-chocolate aromas. It’s full-bodied with firm, fine-grained tannins and fresh acidity. Savoury and mineral layers interplay with the black fruit. Powerful and chewy yet very polished and beautiful. Try from 2024.

96 Points - Wine Enthusiast

Always a significant wine, this latest release with powerful while also stylish black fruits fits into a well-regarded tradition. The density and broad fruitiness of the wine make fine foils for each other. It is firmly structured and set for aging. Drink this wine from 2027.

95 Points - Wine Spectator

 

Very expressive, with violet and lilac notes followed by creamed plum and mulled blackberry and black currant fruit flavours. Subtle anise, juniper and sanguine notes thread the very long finish. Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot and Petit Verdot. Best from 2024 through 2036.

91 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Deep garnet-purple coloured, the 2018 Giscours opens with fragrant notions of kirsch, black cherry compote and blackcurrant pastilles with suggestions of dried lavender, cinnamon stick and mossy tree bark. The medium to full-bodied palate delivers a good amount of red and black fruit flavours with compelling purity, framed by soft tannins and well-balanced freshness, finishing with a spicy lift.

title: Macauley Cabernet Sauvignon Beckstoffer To Kalon 2018
bodyHtml:
The Macauley Vineyard label was originally established in St. Helena in the early 1980s by Ann Macauley Watson and for several years produced a very well received late harvest Sauvignon Blanc with help from renowned winemaker, Ric Forman.  In the late summer of 2000, Ann’s son Mac went to work for Rudd Estate in Oakville. After several months of winery work and education he was inspired to revive the family label, and, working with winemaker and childhood friend Kirk Venge, crushed his first grapes in October 2001. 

Mac and Kirk have one goal: to source the highest quality fruit in Napa Valley and make wines of extraordinary depth and personality. The grapes they choose showcase the terroir of the vineyards and create a remarkable wine-drinking experience.

Opening to an inky hue of deep purple, the 2018 Macauley Beckstoffer To Kalon Vineyard Cabernet Sauvignon has a magical feel to it, as if you’ve just uncorked an enological genie in a bottle. Sourced from clones 337 and 4, and aged for 28 months in new Taransaud and Darnajou oak, this vintage of their most sought after wine has an elegance and seamlessness to it that flirts with perfection. Blueberry, crème de cassis, violets, dried cherries and chocolate levitate from the bouquet, while the mouthfeel lays out a magic carpet of dark fruit, espresso, and barrel vanilla.

93 Points - Wine Spectator    Features a loamy hint that guides a core of gently steeped plum and black currant fruit, slowly allowing alder, cedar and tobacco to work their way in before taking an encore on the finish. Best from 2024 through 2038.

title: Joseph Phelps Cabernet Sauvignon Napa Valley 2022 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
Hailing from the United States, this exceptional red wine represents the pinnacle of California viticulture within the prestigious Napa Valley region. Established in 1973 by visionary businessman Joseph Phelps, the winery became a pioneer in the region by championing a commitment to quality and sustainable farming practices.

Wine Description

In the glass, this wine displays a deep, brilliant garnet purple color. The nose opens with an enticing, lifted bouquet of black and red fruits, notably dark cherries, black plums, juicy cassis, and fresh pomegranate. These primary fruit layers are intricately woven with sophisticated aromatic notes of cedar box, tobacco leaf, fresh herbs, toasted coconut, and a touch of sweet vanilla bean. On the palate, the wine transitions beautifully into a medium to full bodied frame where plush layers of raspberry compote and dried wild berries unfold across a rounded, supple mouthfeel. The structural balance is exceptional, exhibiting great mid palate density, elegant energy, and softly integrated, satiny tannins that carry into a pleasantly savory and persistent finish.

Accolades

  • Wine Advocate - 90 points

  • Vinous - 92 points

  • Decanter - 93 points

Food Pairing

The structured body and vibrant fruit profile of this Napa Valley Cabernet Sauvignon make it a natural counterpart to rich, savory dishes. It pairs wonderfully with a charcoal grilled prime ribeye steak, slow braised lamb shanks, or robust pasta dishes tossed in a wild mushroom and truffle ragout.

title: Luigi Baudana Barolo Cerretta 2021
bodyHtml:
This distinguished red wine hails from the Serralunga d'Alba commune within the Barolo region of Italy. Established in 1975, the small Luigi Baudana estate is a 'garagiste' gem that was entrusted to the Vajra family in 2008 to ensure its unique legacy continued. The winemaking philosophy remains deeply traditional, respecting the authentic history of the estate while utilizing the Vajra family's expertise in sustainable viticulture to highlight the power and elegance of Serralunga’s terroir.

Wine Description

Cerretta presents a vibrant ruby red hue and opens with an assertive, complex bouquet of cherry, blackberry, and pomegranate, interwoven with delicate notes of dried roses, lavender, and violets. On the palate, it is full bodied and intensely structured, revealing layers of licorice, graphite, and exotic spices alongside hints of Earl Grey tea and mint. The wine's noble architecture is defined by searing yet elegant tannins and a mineral-driven acidity that leads to a long, expansive finish marked by crushed rock and spice.

Accolades

  • "Wine Spectator - 97 points."

  • "Vinous - 94 points."

  • "James Suckling - 95 points."

  • "Wine Advocate - 95 points."

Food Pairing

This Barolo is an exceptional companion for rich, savory dishes such as wild boar stew, braised osso buco, or a ribeye steak grilled with rosemary and thyme. It also pairs beautifully with earthy flavours like risotto with white truffles or matured cheeses such as Castelmagno and Gorgonzola.

title: Joseph Drouhin Corton Charlemagne Grand Cru 2023
bodyHtml:
Joseph Drouhin is a family-owned and operated winery with a history of over a century in Burgundy, France. The estate is known for its profound respect for 'terroir' and a winemaking philosophy rooted in organic and biodynamic practices. The winery, which is now run by the fourth generation, has vineyards across nearly 90 appellations in Burgundy. Their overarching philosophy is to produce wines that express the true character of the vineyard through meticulous methods like hand harvesting and careful selection of grapes.

Wine Description The Joseph Drouhin 'Corton Charlemagne' Grand Cru 2023 is made from 100% Chardonnay grapes. The wine shows an intense golden colour. On the nose, it offers a fragrant bouquet of yellow orchard fruit like pear and golden apple, along with notes of delicate flowers, fresh almond, citrus zest, honey, and subtle spice. The palate is full-bodied, satiny, and layered, with a deep core of fruit and a long, chalky finish. It is described as a majestic and well-balanced wine with 'generosity and freshness hand-in-hand'. The wine's structure, tension, and muscle suggest it has a long ageing potential, with an optimal drinking window of 8 to 15 years and a potential to develop for over 20 years.

Accolades

  • Robert Parker Wine Advocate - 93-95 points

  • Vinous (Neal Martin) - 94-96 points

  • James Suckling - a tasting note is available, but the score is not specified for this vintage

  • Jasper Morris - 94-96 points

Food Pairing As a grand cru white Burgundy, this wine is a fantastic match for poultry dishes such as chicken or turkey. The complexity and structure of the wine would be well-suited to a variety of richer preparations. This pairing highlights the wine's depth and character.

title: Guado Al Tasso 2018
bodyHtml:
Introduction

Guado al Tasso 2018 is a flagship Bolgheri Superiore DOC wine produced by the Antinori family at their Tenuta Guado al Tasso estate in the Maremma region of coastal Tuscany. This vintage is notable for a shift in composition; because the estate’s top 100% Cabernet Franc wine (Matarocchio) was not produced in 2018, its high-quality fruit was blended into this wine instead. The result is an exceptionally polished and elegant expression that emphasizes finesse over the raw power found in warmer years like 2017.

Wine Description

The 2018 vintage is defined by its "crystalline" purity and a sophisticated, slightly more herbal and balsamic profile compared to previous releases.

  • Varietal Composition: 60% Cabernet Sauvignon, 22% Cabernet Franc, and 18% Merlot.

  • Aromatic Profile: The nose opens with captivating notes of small dark fruits, ripe plum, and elderberry. These are layered with "sweet spices," licorice root, leather, tobacco, and a distinct "magnificent balsamic trace." Critics also note a leafy, almost herbal character and scents of crushed stones.

  • Palate and Body: On the palate, the wine is full-bodied yet remains agile and "gracious." It offers a silky and voluminous entry with flavors of blackcurrant, chocolate, and cedar. The texture is dense yet vibrant, moving away from a heavy style toward one of linearity and sharpness.

  • Structure: The tannins are described as "totally integrated" and silky, providing a refined frame. The finish is juicy and persistent, marked by a touch of citrus zest and a graphite minerality that reflects the estate’s alluvial soils.

  • Winemaking: Grapes were sorted twice to ensure only perfectly ripe berries were used. Each parcel was fermented separately in stainless steel vats for 15 to 20 days. The wine was then aged in new French oak barriques until bottling in April 2020.

  • ABV: 14%.

Accolades

The 2018 vintage has been widely praised for its elegance and "umami-like" complexity:

  • James Suckling: 96 points

  • Robert Parker's Wine Advocate: 96 points

  • Decanter: 96 points

  • Vinous (Antonio Galloni): 95+ points

  • Falstaff: 95 points

  • Wine Spectator: 93 points

  • Wine Enthusiast: 93 points

title: Masseto 2022
bodyHtml:
Introduction

The Masseto 2022 is a red wine from Italy, specifically the Toscana region, in the subregion of Bolgheri on the Tuscan coast. Masseto is a single-estate wine, taking its name from the rock-hard clusters of 'massi' (blue clay) that characterize the unique vineyard. The estate, which is controlled by the Frescobaldi Family group, is celebrated globally for its uncompromising quality and obsession with a single vineyard. The winemaking philosophy is driven by the unique terroir—a blend of marine, alluvial, and volcanic soils with a vein of Pliocenic blue clay that governs the hydration of the vines, helping them survive dry spells. The first vintage was released in 1986, and the estate is known for producing what is considered the most prestigious Super Tuscan.

Wine Description

The wine is made from 100 percent Merlot. The colour is a vibrant, brilliant, powerful ruby with a slight purple tinge. The nose is pronounced and profound, expressing an immediate concentration of small red fruits. Aromatics include mineral notes of crushed dark stones and dissolved minerals, delicate peppery accents, black plum, red apples, lavender perfume, and sage. Other notes include cool, damp earth, dark hedgerow berries, Mediterranean scrub, cocoa, and wood. The palate is full-bodied, rich, and luscious, with good depth, velvety texture, and richness. It features bright cherry, succulent dark berries, and spice. The style is structured with ripe, firm, yet elegant tannins, and sensational freshness, achieving a perfect balance between strength and finesse. The finish is long and generous, with a touch of salinity and bitter herbs emerging. The wine undergoes rigorous ageing: 24 months in 100 percent new French oak barrels, followed by an additional 12 months in the bottle. The optimal drinking window is long, from 2028 through 2058. The Alcohol By Volume (ABV) is approximately 14.0 percent to 15 percent. The vineyard has been farmed organically since 2012.

Food Pairing

The Masseto 2022, being a bold and structured red wine, is an excellent pairing for rich dishes. Suggested pairings include beef and venison. Its richness and concentration would also complement fine cuts of roasted lamb or mature, hard cheeses.

title: Chateau Lafite Rothschild 2022
bodyHtml:
Château Lafite Rothschild, a First Growth estate under the Bordeaux Wine Official Classification of 1855, is one of the world’s most prestigious wineries. Owned by the Rothschild family since 1868, the estate is revered for its tradition of excellence and its influence on the evolution of Bordeaux winemaking. The vineyard’s gravel-rich terroir, coupled with meticulous viticulture, contributes to the refined power and elegance for which Lafite is celebrated.

Wine Description
The 2022 vintage opens with a deep garnet colour and a strikingly expressive bouquet of ripe blackcurrants, graphite, violets, and cedarwood. On the palate, it reveals a full-bodied structure with layers of cassis, black cherries, tobacco, and subtle earthiness, all wrapped in exceptionally fine-grained tannins. The mouthfeel is both rich and lifted, leading to a lingering, harmonious finish that is mineral-driven and precise.

Accolades

  • James Suckling - 100 Points

  • Vinous - 100 Points

  • Decanter - 100 Points

  • Jeb Dunnuck - 100 Points

  • Wine Advocate - 100 Points

Food Pairing
Pair with dry-aged ribeye, rosemary lamb chops, or black truffle risotto. The wine’s complexity and structure make it an ideal partner to dishes that highlight umami and savoury depth. Together, they create an unforgettable dining experience.

title: Paolo Scavino Barolo 'Prapo' 2019
bodyHtml:
Soils comprise Formazioni di Lequio, yellow-red sand combined with silty gray marl. Fruit harvested by hand in the third week of October. Skin maceration took place over 12 days, followed by a 20-30 day fermentation in stainless steel with indigenous yeast. The wine aged in a combination of French barrique and large casks for two years before bottling.

94 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

This bold and opulent wine sources its fruit from Serralunga d'Alba. The Paolo Scavino 2017 Barolo Prapò delivers rich fruit weight with plummy black fruit, blackcurrant, iron ore, spice and cured spice. The vines at this site were re-planted in 2008, and the fruit shows depth and authenticity thanks to their advancing age. You get lingering mineral tones of rust and iron that marry this wine to a sense of place. The finish is bold but moderate in length.

94 Points -  James Suckling

Very fresh and perfumed with oranges, cherries, raspberries and flowers. Medium-bodied with firm tannins and a racy, fine-tannin finish. Linear and racy. Give it time to soften. Try after 2024.

title: Bibi Graetz Testamatta 2020
bodyHtml:
The Bibi Graetz winery was founded in 2000 in Fiesole, overlooking Florence, by Bibi Graetz, an artist who transitioned to winemaking. The winemaking philosophy is rooted in a deep respect for indigenous Tuscan varieties like Sangiovese and the use of old vines.

Wine Description

The wine has a relatively light, vibrant ruby or bright cherry red colour, with some notes mentioning a pale-garnet hue. The aromatic profile is complex and constantly evolving, offering an attractive combination of dried fruit and spices, black cherries, plums, and raspberries. You may also find aromas of flowers and fragrant sandalwood, perfumed blue flower, candied orange peel, wet earth, and hints of Tuscan brush. On the palate, this full-bodied wine shows a remarkable elegant character with flavours of juicy Marasca cherry, crushed raspberry, redcurrant, and a savoury edge.

Accolades

  • James Suckling - 97 points

  • Decanter - 96 points

  • Robert Parker's Wine Advocate - 94 points

  • Wine Enthusiast - 92 points

  • Wine Spectator - 90 points

Food Pairing

The savoury notes and firm structure stand up well to the richness of red meat and enhance the wine’s overall finesse.

title: Shafer TD-9 Cabernet Sauvignon 2023
bodyHtml:
Shafer Vineyards has produced classic Napa Valley wines for more than 40 years.  

Shafer’s wines, including its signature Cabernet Sauvignon, Hillside Select, are found in collectors’ cellars and on wine lists in top luxury hotels and restaurants throughout the world. The winery has a decades-long commitment to sustainability. Beginning in the 1980s Shafer embraced farming techniques that eliminate insecticides and herbicides, and carefully conserve water resources.

TD-9 fills the glass with irresistible aromas and flavors of fresh black cherries, black currant, red plum, thyme, rose petal, and cocoa. Lush and mouth-filling, this wine offers the kind of complexity and structure that ensures many years of enjoyment ahead.

title: Le Petit Mouton 2022
bodyHtml:
Introduction

This red wine comes from France, specifically the Bordeaux region, in the appellation of Pauillac. Le Petit Mouton is the second wine of Château Mouton Rothschild, which is recognized as a Premier Grand Cru Classé (First Growth) in the 1855 Bordeaux Wine Official Classification. The wine represents a significant portion of the estate's production, around 29% for the 2022 vintage. The estate is celebrated for its elegance and dedication to the classic, Cabernet-dominated Pauillac style.

Wine Description

The 2022 vintage of Le Petit Mouton is an intense and highly structured wine that has been compared to a Grand Vin. The colour is dark purple crimson or a deep, dark red-purple with a vivid purple rim. The aroma is rich and suave, offering a complex bouquet of Cabernet fragrance, blackcurrant notes (cassis), violet, blackberry, espresso roast, cigar wrapper, toasted sesame seed, and a hint of mint.

The varietal composition is primarily Cabernet Sauvignon. The blend is 71% Cabernet Sauvignon, 19% Merlot, 7% Cabernet Franc, and 3% Petit Verdot. The palate is full-bodied, velvety, and layered, showcasing dark, concentrated fruits like black cherry, dark berries, and black plum. Stylistically, it is rich, opulent, and concentrated, with an expansive, smoky, black-fruit-led finish. It has a core of powdery, finely integrated tannins that are substantial, as well as balanced acidity, giving the wine energy and structure. The finish is long and sustained, with notes of chocolate, mocha, and graphite. The wine is aged in 60% new oak barrels. The alcohol by volume (ABV) is 14%. The optimal drinking window is noted as starting around 2027 to 2030, with a potential to age until 2042–2054. Information on the wine being organic is not available, though it is labelled as 'Sustainable'.

title: Il Poggione Brunello di Montalcino Riserva Vigna Paganelli 2016
bodyHtml:
Intense ruby-red color. Layers of red fruit, savory spices and leather notes. The tannins are silky, and the fruit comes back in multiple layers. Its long finish confirms that this wine is ready to drink now but can be enjoyed for 20 years or more.

98 Points - Vinous

A beguiling mix of camphor and minty herbs, along with crushed stone, blows off slowly to reveal dark depths of black raspberry, licorice, autumnal spice and worn leather as the 2016 Brunello di Montalcino Riserva Vigna Paganelli unfolds in the glass. Its textures are unexpectedly soft and velvety-smooth, coupled with depths of intense red fruits that make an appearance just before a mix of brisk acids and tannins creates a more tactile and youthfully clenching expression toward the finale. This leaves the palate aching under the 2016's structural heft, yet with plenty of primary concentration to balance, as wild savory herbs and earthy mineral tones linger for up to a minute. The potential here is off the charts, but readers will need to be very patient. The Riserva Vigna Paganelli is a cru selection of old vines that refines for 48 months in large French oak barrels of 33-52 hectoliters.

96 Points - Wine Spectator

A beam of pure cherry permeates this sleek, elegant red, shaded by floral, mineral, wild herb and orange zest accents. Well-delineated and long, this has the balance, grip and intensity for a long life ahead.

96 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

This is the top-shelf wine from Il Poggione, and it's a must-have bottle for those who collect wines from this celebrated estate. From an icon vintage, the 2016 Brunello di Montalcino Riserva Vigna Paganelli is a beauty. It stands at the intersection of intensity, elegance and power. The fruit is shapely and dense with plenty of blackberry and black cherry, and you also get savory touches of campfire ash, tar, licorice, ferrous earth and balsam herb. Honestly, you get it all, including that distinctive Brunello power and abundance that is not easily achieved with such careful balance. The finish is structured, fresh and long, and with more time in the glass, the leathery or savory aromas become more pronounced (as does the alcohol).

96 Points - Decanter

The estate’s oldest plot, Vigna Paganelli is a 12-hectare vineyard planted in 1964. It boasts a rich diversity of old Sangiovese clones which are used for newer plantings. Spiced plum, cured leather and a roll-call of marjoram, tarragon and basil beckon generously. Though hefty in size, this carries its girth with charming ease. There is a richness and sweetness to the fruit, while ripe, granular tannins provide a framework. A mineral edge emerges underneath all the layers. It will be hard to resist young, but I suspect intricate details will become more apparent in time.

95 Points - Wine Enthusiast

Cedar, forest floor and new leather aromas come to the forefront along with violet and dried botanical herbs. Full-bodied and enveloping, the savory palate delivers dried cherry, orange zest, licorice and white pepper framed in velvety tannins.

94 Points - James Suckling

The freshness and depth are impressive, with floral, dark-berry and cherry character that follows through to a full body with chewy tannins that are polished and solid. Flavorful at the end. Needs time to soften.

title: Chateau Pichon Longueville Comtesse de Lalande 2021
bodyHtml:
One of Bordeaux’s iconic Second Growths, Château Pichon Longueville Comtesse de Lalande boasts a rich history dating back to the 17th century. Situated in the heart of Pauillac, this revered estate is known for its meticulous winemaking and distinctive, elegant wines that reflect the essence of the Médoc terroir. The 2021 vintage continues the château’s legacy of excellence, embodying precision and finesse despite a challenging growing season.

Wine Description

The 2021 vintage of Pichon Comtesse presents a deep ruby hue with purple reflections. Aromatically, it enchants with layers of cassis, dark cherry, and blackberry, interwoven with hints of cedar, graphite, and floral undertones of violet. On the palate, the wine is medium to full-bodied with refined tannins, vibrant acidity, and a harmonious balance. Flavors of blackcurrant, plum, and subtle spice lead to a long, elegant finish with mineral nuances. This vintage captures both the power and grace synonymous with the château's style.

Food Pairing

This wine pairs beautifully with classic French cuisine, such as roast lamb with herbes de Provence or duck breast with cherry sauce. It also complements hard cheeses like Comté or aged Gouda. Together, these pairings highlight the wine’s depth and complexity, creating an unforgettable dining experience.

Vintage Quality

The 2021 vintage showcases the estate’s skillful response to a cooler, wetter growing season. With lower yields but outstanding quality, this wine is a testament to the meticulous care taken in both the vineyard and winery. It is a collectible expression of Pichon Comtesse's timeless elegance.

title: Chateau Angelus 2016
bodyHtml:
The vineyard of Chateau Angelus is situated in a natural amphitheatre overlooked by the three Saint-Emilion churches. In the middle of this special site, the sounds were amplified and the angelus bells could be heard ringing in the morning, at midday and in the evening. They cadenced the working day in the vineyards and villages, calling the men and women to stop their labours for a few minutes and pray.

In the first-ever classification of Saint-Emilion wines in 1954, Chateau Angélus was a Grand Cru Classe. Already at the time, it benefitted from a solid reputation, which helped it survive the Bordeaux wine crisis of 1973 and take part in the oenological renewal of the 1980’s. 

100 Points - Wine Enthusiast

This is a rich, perfumed wine, with dense tannins and intense layers of black plum and spice. The palate is firmly built yet broadened out by plump dark-fruit tones and honed by a solid, dry core. 

99 Points - James Suckling

Subtle and profound aromas of blackberries, wet earth and sweet tobacco. Hints of spice, too. Full-bodied and so deep. It’s incredibly vertical and long. Just like looking down a well. Firm and powerful tannins, yet polished and balanced. Goes on for minutes. One of the greatest ever. 

98+ Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Sporting a deep garnet-purple color, the 2016 Angelus erupts from the glass with powerful notes of blackberry pie, ripe black cherries and juicy black plums with an undercurrent of star anise, rose petals, chocolate mint, pencil shavings and woodsmoke plus a waft of allspice. The palate is pure decadence. Medium to full-bodied, rich and generously fruited, this wine is by no means heavy—it positively glimmers with freshness and vivacity, lending an ethereal nature to all that richness and power, beautifully framed by velvety tannins and finishing with epic length. 

97 Points - Decanter

97 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

96 Points - Wine Spectator

title: La Clarte de Haut Brion 2018
bodyHtml:
La Clarté de Haut Brion originates from the Pessac Léognan appellation in the Bordeaux region of France. This wine serves as the second white label for two of the world's most prestigious estates, Château Haut Brion and Château La Mission Haut Brion, sharing the same legendary terroir and winemaking expertise. Owned by Domaine Clarence Dillon since 1935, the winery is renowned for its centuries-old tradition and its unique position as the only First Growth estate located outside the Médoc.

Wine Description

This wine presents a beautiful pale yellow colour with occasional green tinges. The aromatic profile is intense and vibrant, leaping from the glass with scents of grapefruit, lemon zest, and key lime pie, complemented by subtle hints of aniseed, white flowers, and a distinct mineral smokiness. On the palate, the wine is medium to full bodied, balancing a creamy, leesy texture with a lively backbone of acidity and phenolic tension. Flavours of dried apple, peach, and a touch of orange honey lead into a pure, zesty finish.

Accolades

Jeb Dunnuck - 93 points: Lots of honeyed citrus, salty mineral, white flowers, and a kiss of white grapefruit all emerge from the 2018 La Clarte De Haut-Brion Blanc, a medium-bodied, elegant, beautifully balanced white that has an approachable, layered style. It should keep for a decade, probably longer, although there's no need to delay gratification too much.

James Suckling - 95 Points: Wonderful aromas of honeysuckle, light apricot and citrus with hints of lemon curd and pie crust. It’s full-bodied, tight and composed with density and agility that make it unique for a white. Fantastic persistence. Try after 2024, but already a joy to taste and drink.

Food Pairing

The wine's rich texture and bright acidity make it an ideal companion for seafood dishes such as lobster with butter sauce, grilled scallops, or fresh oysters with a lime dressing. It also pairs beautifully with roasted chicken seasoned with herbs or a creamy truffle pasta. For a cheese course, consider soft, creamy selections like Brie or Camembert.

title: Spottswoode Cabernet Sauvignon 2019
bodyHtml:
Spottswoode is a historic, family-owned estate vineyard and winery on the western edge of St. Helena in Napa Valley. To ensure the highest quality, Spottswoode is dedicated to producing a handful of wines in very limited quantities: Spottswoode Estate Cabernet Sauvignon, Sauvignon Blanc, Lyndenhurst, and Field Book. The winery aims to produce exceptional, well-balanced, structured wines that exhibit texture, elegance, consistency and the ability to age well.

The 40-acre Spottswoode Estate Vineyard is an ideal terroir for growing wine grapes.
