Situated on the apex of the Sulphur Creek fan, the alluvial soils comprised primarily of sandy clay loam provide superb drainage. The gap between the Mayacamas Range and Spring Mountain admits cooling maritime breezes that temper the sun's heat, creating an ideal microclimate for wine growing.

98 Points -  Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The gorgeous 2019 Cabernet Sauvignon is already drinking beautifully, with incredible waves of black cherry and cassis fruit that have completely absorbed roughly two-thirds of new oak. On this occasion, the wine came across as rather forward and supple, with lush tannins framing ample fruit on the medium to full-bodied palate. Impeccably balanced, with tremendous length on the cool, refreshing finish, it manages to showcase the warmth and generous nature of the site and vintage without going over the top.

97 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

The 2019 Cabernet Sauvignon is another incredible wine from this reference point estate in the Valley. It has that classic Spottswoode refinement and elegance as well as medium to full-bodied aromas and flavours of cassis, tobacco, sandalwood, and flowers.

96 Points - James Suckling

Ripe blackberries, blackcurrants, cocoa powder, dried thyme and walnut husk on the nose. It's full-bodied, chewy and compact, with firm tannins and a broad, muscular palate. Structured, polished and well-balanced. From biodynamically grown grapes.

96 Points - Vinous

A bright, effusive wine, the 2019 Cabernet Sauvignon Estate is all finesse. Bright aromatics, vibrant red berry fruit and mid-weight structure, give it its charming, sensual personality.

title: Chateau Pichon Longueville Comtesse de Lalande 2020
bodyHtml:
A pure fresh nose of blackberry, blackurrant, peony, and that cedar association of Pauillac, On the palate, subtle and full-bodied with great powerful length and a sweetness that is both seductive and savory with a touch of elegance. The flavors confirm these blackcurrant and blackberry notes, with structured smooth tannins.

Blend: 77% Cabernet Sauvignon, 17% Merlot, 6% Cabernet Franc

98+ Points - Jeb Dunnuck

An estate that has been on fire of late, the 2020 Chateau Pichon-Longueville Comtesse De Lalande is another brilliant wine in a succession of brilliant wines. Revealing a dense purple hue as well as full-bodied aromas and flavors of blac currants, scorched earth, tobacco leaf, and violets, it hits the palate with an expansive, rich, yet pure, precise texture that carries fabulous tannins, perfect balance, and a stacked mid-palate. Based on 77% Cabernet Sauvignon, 17% Merlot, and 6% Cabernet Franc, it's an incredible wine that's going to flirt with perfection and is unquestionably one of the finest, if not the finest, Left Banks in the vintage. Bravo. 

96+ Points - Vinous

The 2020 Pichon-Lalande has a backward nose similar to that of its neighbor Pichon-Baron, and so I decanted the bottle for 45 minutes. It then revealed gorgeous scents of blackberry, wild hedgerow, seaweed (Japanese nori) and wild mint. The palate is medium-bodied with sappy black fruit and gentle but insistent grip. Very intense but not ripe; there is a coolness about this Pauillac that I like, while the finish is very classically styled and leaves behind a persistent, slightly briny aftertaste. This is a magnificent, cerebral Pichon-Lalande that will deserve serious aging and the patience of anyone still waiting for The Cure's new album. 

96+ Points - James Suckling

This is extremely structured, but with a level of polish and refinement that highlights the excellence of the terroir. Very long and expansive on the palate, showing class and beauty. Powerful.

95+ Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Deep purple-black in color, the 2020 Pichon Longueville Comtesse de Lalande begins on a single, well-defined, wonderfully pure note of ripe blackcurrants, opening out to a melody of redcurrant jelly, kirsch, ripe blackberries and tar, with emerging suggestions of dark chocolate, cardamom, ground cloves and violets, with a waft of black truffles. Medium-bodied, tightly wound and with loads of fantastically nuanced black fruit layers, it has a rock-solid frame of finely grained tannins and bags of freshness, finishing long and mineral laced. The blend this year is 77% Cabernet Sauvignon, 17% Merlot and 6% Cabernet Franc.

96 Points - Decanter

Softer and silkier than many Pauillacs in the vintage, this is a clear success. Hugely silky and seductive, with grip, power and finesse. One of the best of the appellation, with finessed tobacco, heather and plump blueberry and cassis fruit, expertly managing the low 30hl/ha yield. 60% new oak.

title: Chateau Cos D'Estournel 2016
bodyHtml:
Chateau Cos d'Estournel is a Grand Cru vineyard located in St. Estephe. Its oriental facade is adorned with three pagoda turrets, all cast in a soft golden sandstone. Chateau Cos d'Estournel today covers 170 acres separated from Chateau Lafite, along the southern edge, by the stream between St. Estephe and Pauillac. 

Cos d'Estournel is slow to reveal itself. Little by little, it evokes stories of distant places, market stalls brimming with unfamiliar fruits, spices and wares, village festivities warmed by the joy of revelers and the setting sun, and sumptuous visions of ladies and their voluptuous curves. A myriad of scents, colors and tastes appeals to the senses. The Grand Vin of Cos d'Estournel is both demure and deliberately sensuous, a fascinating and elegant nectar.

100 Points - James Suckling

This is muscular yet so well defined and toned. Full-bodied with deep and dense fruit on the palate, yet powerful and rich at the same time. So much sandalwood and blackberry character. Chewy and rich at the finish. This is a warm and generous wine, but the alcohol is just over 13 degrees. Not that high. Love the finish. Extravagant. Magical.

100 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Bottled in July 2018, it is deep garnet-purple colored and starts off a little closed and reticent, opening out slowly and seductively to reveal beautiful lilacs, rose hip tea, crushed stones and camphor nuances over a core of creme de cassis, kirsch, wild blueberries and mocha plus wafts of incense and wood smoke. The palate is simply electric, charged with an energy and depth of flavors that seem to defy the elegance and ethereal nature of its medium-bodied weight, featuring super ripe, densely pixelated tannins that firmly frame the myriad of fruit and floral sparks, finishing with epic length. Just. Magic.

99 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

One of the more seamless, pure, elegant versions of this cuvée out there, it boasts a saturated purple color as well as a monster nose of pure creme de cassis, gravelly, rocky minerality, tobacco leaf, crushed violets, and lead pencil shavings. One of those “iron fists in a velvet glove” wines, with full-bodied richness and beautiful structure that’s covered by thrilling levels of fruit and texture, it stays tight, compact, and incredibly focused on the palate. 

96 Points - Wine Enthusiast

96 Points - Wine Spectator

title: Chateau Calon Segur 2006
bodyHtml:
Chateau Calon Segur is located in the Saint Estephe appellation within the Medoc region of Bordeaux, France. As one of the oldest estates in the area, its history dates back to 1147 and it was famously owned in the 18th century by the Marquis de Segur, who also held the prestigious first growths Lafite and Latour. The winery's philosophy is rooted in a deep affection for this specific terroir, a sentiment immortalized by the Marquis's claim that his heart belonged to Calon, which is why a heart remains the central emblem on every label.

Wine Description

Chateau Calon Segur presents a deep ruby to crimson colour. On the nose, it offers an elegant and classic profile featuring aromas of cassis, black cherry, and forest floor, complemented by nuances of iron, woodsmoke, and violets. The palate is medium to full bodied, revealing a core of dark fruit, blackberry, and licorice, supported by a firm, chewy tannic structure that provides significant depth and focus. Stylistically, the wine is known for its balance and 'old style' charm, concluding with a long, fresh finish marked by notes of cedar and graphite.

Accolades

  • Wine Spectator - 92 points

  • Wine Advocate - 93 points

  • Decanter - 93 points

  • Vinous - 90 points

Food Pairing

This wine's robust structure and classic Bordeaux profile make it an ideal accompaniment to hearty meat dishes such as roasted lamb with garlic and rosemary, braised beef short ribs, or grilled venison. It also pairs exceptionally well with aged hard cheeses like Comte or earthy mushroom-based dishes.

title: Dal Forno Romano Valpolicella Superiore 2013 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
This dark and brooding wine begins with seductive aromas of ripe blackberries and dark cherries, which are laced with spices, cigar box, flowers, tar and smoky nuances all taking shape in the glass. This is full-bodied and beautifully polished, with an outstanding overall balance of ripe fruit and acidity. It continues to impress with incredible depth and concentration through the long, opulent finish. 

95 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

 

The 2013 Valpolicella Superiore Monte Lodoletta oozes forth with thick concentration and an inky black color. The mouthfeel is thick and impenetrable, and the senses are treated to a long succession of black fruit, tar, spice, smoke, mesquite and barbecue flavors. The wine is full-bodied and very opulent, but it carries that massive intensity with grace and precision. This Valpolicella Superiore is very nicely done.

95 Points - James Suckling 

A remarkably concentrated red, redolent of dark-cherry ice cream, stuffed with chocolate-chip flakes that turn into meatier, earthier nuances of steak tartar and forest floor. Full-throttle and lavishly chewy, the tannins pucker all sides of the mouth with mesmerizing intensity; nevertheless they remain polished and acutely detailed, like an extravagant, wool-woven, Moroccan veil.

title: Produttori del Barbaresco - Barbaresco 'Ovello' Riserva 2020
bodyHtml:
The Produttori del Barbaresco 'Ovello' 2020 is a red wine from the Piedmont region of Italy, specifically the Barbaresco DOCG appellation. It is a single-vineyard (Cru) wine sourced from the Ovello subregion, which is Barbaresco's northernmost and largest cru.

The Produttori del Barbaresco is a cooperative winery founded in 1958. It is renowned for setting the benchmark for classic Barbaresco, with its single-cru Riservas, like the 'Ovello', defining the expression of the region's finest noble vineyards. The winery's philosophy centres on traditional methods—such as ageing in large oak casks (botti)—to produce transparent wines that authentically showcase the region's finest terroirs

Wine Description

This wine is 100% Nebbiolo. It typically displays a powerful and structured expression due to the Ovello vineyard's cooler, northern exposures and predominately clayey soils.

The aroma is fragrant and complex, shaped by red berry, forest floor, new leather, and spice notes. Additional aromatic nuances include woodsy pine, black raspberries, sweet floral perfume, and liquorice candies. The palate is massive, packed, and full-bodied, often described as having a more linear style. It presents pure cherry and raspberry fruit with accents of white pepper, herbs, and mineral. The body is full, with a backbone of firm, chalky, and well-integrated tannins, balanced by vibrant, racy acidity. Stylistic notes include remarkable depth and complexity in the mid-palate, an energetic yet refined structure, and a long finish with a mineral core. The wine is intended for long-term cellaring. The optimal drinking window is generally suggested to be from 2026 to 2050. The wine is dry and produced using sustainable farming practices.

Accolades

  • Robert Parker - 95 points

  • Jeb Dunnuck - 95 points

  • Wine Spectator - 95 points

  • Vinous - 95 points

title: Terralsole Brunello di Montalcino Riserva 'Mario Bollag' 2007 -  1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
Introduction

This red wine originates from Italy, produced in the prestigious Tuscany region within the Brunello di Montalcino DOCG. Terralsole, meaning 'land toward the sun', was founded in 1996 by Mario Bollag and his wife Athena Tergis. The estate's philosophy is rooted in a 'micro-cru' approach that balances modern technology with a deep respect for traditional terroir, often blending Bollag's background as an artist and Tergis's musical talent into the spirit of their winemaking.

Wine Description

The Terralsole Mario Bollag Brunello di Montalcino Riserva 2007 displays an intense ruby red colour with garnet reflections that deepen with age. The nose is modern and deeply layered, offering aromas of soft cherry, tobacco, and violets, backed by complex hints of chocolate, caramel, liquorice, and a touch of dusty white pepper. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied and opulent, featuring a 'chewy' pulpiness of fruit that delivers extra intensity and a soft, velvety texture. It is characterized by its solid tannic backbone and bright acidity, leading to a long, structured finish with notes of dried fruits and spice. This 100% Sangiovese Grosso typically has an ABV of 14% to 15%. While Terralsole achieved 100% Organic Certification in 2018, the 2007 vintage was produced using sustainable and organic practices long before official certification. The optimal drinking window for this Riserva is estimated to extend through 2026 to 2030.

Accolades

  • Wine Enthusiast - 94 points.

  • James Suckling - 92 points.

  • Robert Parker's Wine Advocate - 91 points.

  • Vinous / IWC - 91+ points.

  • Wine Spectator - 90 points.

  • Jancis Robinson - 16+/20 points.

Food Pairing

The robust structure and savory profile of this Riserva make it an ideal partner for traditional Tuscan fare. It pairs exceptionally well with roasted red meats, game such as venison or wild boar, and hearty dishes like baciola-wrapped sablefish. It also complements wild mushroom tarts with sage truffle crème fraîche and hard, mature cheeses.

Vintage Quality

The 2007 vintage in Montalcino is regarded as superlative, characterized by a warm growing season that produced large-scaled, opulent wines with fabulous balance and proportion. Critics have highlighted the 2007s for their astounding consistency in quality and accessible, sweet tannins compared to the firmer structure of the 2006 vintage.

title: Chateau Figeac 2017
bodyHtml:
With its pedigree style, Chateau Figeac epitomizes the elegance of the great wines of Bordeaux. Its unique style gradually shows through and develops over time.

96 Points - Wine Spectator

This starts slowly, with black tea and sunbaked loam aromas leading off, followed by a deep well of black currant, fig and blackberry preserve flavours that form the core. From there, iron and espresso cream threads line the finish, where the fruit drips slowly and the aromas linger seductively. Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot and Cabernet Franc. Best from 2024 through 2042.

96 Points - James Suckling

This is a dense and layered red with blackberries, blueberries and hints of hazelnuts. Full-bodied, very tight and focused. Impressive young tannins. Velvety texture. Very pretty to taste. Juicy and delicious.

95 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Production was down by half this year, only producing 55,000 bottles. Made from 43% Cabernet Sauvignon, 47% Merlot and 10% Cabernet Franc, the deep garnet-purple coloured 2017 Figeac gives up expressive notes of black cherries, plum preserves, black raspberries and kirsch, giving way to hints of dried leaves, cinnamon toast and warm cassis plus a waft of lavender. Medium-bodied, the palate has wonderful vibrancy with a refreshing line cutting through the crunchy black fruits and a firm, finely grained frame, finishing long and spicy.

95 Points - Wine Enthusiast

The Cabernets, both Sauvignon and Franc, have produced a wine that is structured and firm, with plenty of backbone as well as fruit and acidity. It will be a juicy, rich wine that is sure to age well. The aftertaste is ripe and fruity. Drink from 2024.

95 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

The grand vin is the 2017 Figeac, which was made only from first-generation grapes and is 47% Cabernet Sauvignon, 43% Merlot, and only 10% Cabernet Franc that was brought up in new French oak. It offers a beautiful bouquet of creme de cassis, tobacco, violets, and tobacco, with a touch of forest floor and earth. Made in a pure, elegant, medium-bodied style, it's beautifully textured, seamless and elegant, with silky tannins and a solid spine of acidity. It's going to be drinkable in 4-5 years and cruise for 15-20 years.

93 Points - Decanter

An estate that saw a heavy frost, losing 55% of the crop and achieving yields of 22hl/ha, but has managed to deliver a lovely wine that majors on elegance, and that emphasizes the Cabernet over Merlot character to good effect. Not the intensity of 2015, 2016, 2018, but hard to disagree with the pleasure, confidence and poise of the wine. Firm tannins also, and the most gorgeous hint of cold ash and woodsmoke curling out of the glass, this will continue to develop and deepen over the next decade and beyond.

title: Alter Ego de Palmer 2022 (by Chateau Palmer)
bodyHtml:
From France’s prestigious Bordeaux region, the Alter Ego de Palmer hails from the renowned Margaux appellation on the Left Bank. This distinguished second label of Château Palmer, founded in the 19th century, reflects the same dedication to biodynamic viticulture and meticulous craftsmanship. Under the guidance of the Palmer team, Alter Ego has carved out its own identity, favouring suppleness and aromatic expression over sheer power.

The 2022 vintage offers a deep ruby hue with violet reflections. The nose is expressive, revealing layers of ripe blackberries, cassis, violets, and hints of graphite and baking spices. On the palate, it is medium to full bodied with silky tannins and vibrant acidity, showcasing flavours of dark cherry, plum, cocoa, and cedar. The finish is long and polished, with remarkable freshness and finesse.

Accolades

  • James Suckling - 96+ Points

  • Jeb Dunnuck - 93+ Points

  • Vinous - 93+ Points

Food Pairing

Perfect alongside roasted duck breast with cherry sauce, grilled lamb chops, or a mushroom risotto. This pairing highlights the wine’s depth and character.

title: E. Guigal Cote Rotie 'La Mouline' 2017
bodyHtml:
The Côte-Rôtie "La Mouline" is one of the most emblematic of the Guigal domain’s wines. Small quantities are produced each year from a vineyard in the heart of the ‘côte blonde’. This is a voluptuous, silky and intensely aromatic wine composed of 89% Syrah, 11% Viognier.

97+ Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2017 Cote Rotie La Mouline delivers waves of joyous blueberry fruit, accented by complex notions of violets and dried spices. It's full-bodied yet supple and plush, showing incredible balance, complexity and texture at this early stage of its development. 

97+ Points - Jeb Dunnuck

The 2017 Côte Rôtie La Mouline is more upfront and expressive, which is certainly in the style of this terrific vintage. Loads of spiced meats, chocolate, spring flowers, and assorted red and black fruits all soar from the glass. With full-bodied richness, incredibly complexity and nuance, building tannins, and just loads of upfront sex appeal, it’s going to benefit from 4-5 years of bottle age and cruise for 30 years or more.

96+ Points - Vinous

Highly perfumed, expansive aromas of cherry and blueberry liqueur, incense, exotic spices and vanilla, plus a bright mineral overtone that builds in the glass. Youthful, palate-staining red and blue fruit flavors show superb depth as well as energy, and a core of juicy acidity adds support and back-end cut. Finishes with building floral and spice nuances, gentle tannic grip and a resonating mineral note.

96 Points - Decanter

Beautifully Blonde in style, with macadamia nut and tobacco notes to the raspberry fruit. Very fine tannins on the palate, good acidity, and there's some density and body from the vintage and the Viognier. Good length, that's elongated by a subtle mineral note and resinous aspect from the fruit and oak. Just a little drying note on the tip of the tongue. You can enjoy this now, but this will age well too. The oak regime is robust - 40 months in new barriques. It's applied with skill and care, and is a strongly noticeable part of the wine. Lieu-dit Côte Blonde, from the Blonde side (gneiss bedrock).

96 Points - Wine Spectator

Racy-edged and still a bit coiled up, this has a core of dark cherry and currant fruit that has melded nicely with singed alder, tobacco and sanguine notes. Flashes of chocolate and espresso crema add a more taciturn edge to the finish, but time should bring that into the fold, as this has superior length and drive for cellaring.

title: Barbi Brunello di Montalcino Riserva 2020
bodyHtml:
Fattoria dei Barbi Brunello di Montalcino Riserva 2020 is a prestige red wine from the Montalcino region of Tuscany, Italy. Fattoria dei Barbi is one of the foundational historic estates of the appellation, with the Colombini family's winemaking roots in the area stretching back to 1352. Produced only in exceptional vintage years, the Riserva label is crafted from a rigorous selection of the estate's finest barrels. The winery's philosophy bridges centuries of tradition with modern precision, prioritizing structural power, extreme elegance, and unparalleled aging capability.

Wine Description

In the glass, this vintage exhibits a brilliant and deep ruby red color. The nose is intricate and multi-layered, bursting with an aromatic bouquet of strawberry, sweet cherry, and dark forest berries, interwoven with nuances of eucalyptus, orange peel, undergrowth, sweet tobacco, and a hint of smoky minerality. On the palate, the wine is warm, ample, and full-bodied. Stylistically, it stands as an austere yet sensual masterpiece with a tightly woven, sinewy tannin structure perfectly balanced by a vibrant, focused acidity. It concludes with a remarkably persistent, succulent finish carrying notes of balsamic, licorice, and exotic baking spices.

  • Varietal Composition: 100% Sangiovese, harvested from south-east facing vines rooted in marl soils.

  • Aging Process: Aged for a mandatory five years before commercial release, spending at least three years in oak casks followed by a minimum of six months resting in the bottle.

  • Optimal Drinking Window: Blessed with monumental longevity, this wine has an estimated cellaring potential of 20 to 80 years. Critics estimate its ideal drinking plateau will sit comfortably between 2029 and 2045.

title: Chateau La Gaffeliere 2022
bodyHtml:
From the storied vineyards of France, in the prestigious Saint-Émilion appellation on Bordeaux’s Right Bank, Château La Gaffelière is a Premier Grand Cru Classé estate with deep roots in the region. Owned by the Malet Roquefort family for over three centuries, the property’s commitment to expressing its unique limestone and clay terroir is at the core of its winemaking philosophy. The estate sits at the foot of the slope leading up to the famous town of Saint-Émilion, drawing fruit from some of the most revered plots in the area.

This 2022 vintage presents a radiant deep ruby colour. On the nose, it is aromatic and precise, offering layers of black cherry, cassis, violets, and hints of graphite and cedar. The palate is refined yet powerful, displaying a full-bodied structure with silky tannins and remarkable freshness. Notes of plum, mocha, and crushed stones unfold through a long, mineral-driven finish.

Accolades
● Wine Advocate – 96–97 points.
● Vinous – 95–97 points.
● James Suckling – 96–97 points.

Food Pairing
Pair this wine with duck breast with cherry sauce, rack of lamb with rosemary and garlic, or a hearty wild mushroom risotto. This pairing highlights the wine’s depth and character.

title: Bouchard Pere & Fils Meursault 'Les Clous' 2022
bodyHtml:
Bouchard Père & Fils is one of Burgundy's oldest wine estates, founded in Beaune by Michel Bouchard in 1731, and has been perpetuating this tradition for nearly three centuries and nine generations. Their winemaking philosophy is driven by an exceptional pursuit of excellence, especially in their work in the vineyards, with some premier and grand cru vineyards now farmed biodynamically.

Wine Description

It offers an intense bouquet of fruit and flowers, combined with a delicate mineral hint. On the palate, the wine is rich and subtle with good crispness, leading to a very balanced style. Tasting notes include ripe fruit aromas such as apples, lemons/limes, and grapefruit, alongside floral notes, wet stones, almonds, and a touch of smoky oak.

Food Pairing

Suggested pairings include fish dishes in sauce, as well as chicken and turkey.

title: Chateau Lafite Rothschild 2005 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
Chateau Lafite Rothschild 2005 originates from France, within the Pauillac appellation of the Medoc region in Bordeaux. This historic estate is a First Growth (Premier Cru Classe), a prestigious status it has held since the 1855 Bordeaux Classification. Owned by the Rothschild family since 1868, the winery follows a philosophy of precision and elegance, aiming to express the unique gravel soils of its 112 hectare vineyard through meticulous viticulture and traditional winemaking.

Wine Description

This vintage possesses a deep ruby or opaque purple colour with brilliant clarity. The sensory profile is exceptionally complex, featuring aromas of graphite, cedar, and pencil shavings, layered with notes of blackcurrant, violets, and subtle hints of truffle. On the palate, it is full bodied yet remarkably refined, offering flavours of concentrated black fruits, minerals, and spicy oak. The structure is defined by an incredible balance, fresh acidity, and high quality, fine grained tannins that lead to an endlessly persistent and harmonious finish. The varietal composition for the 2005 vintage is 89% Cabernet Sauvignon, 10.7% Merlot, and 0.3% Petit Verdot. It has an ABV of 13% and is produced using sustainable viticulture practices.

Food Pairing

The noble structure and complex aromatic profile of this wine make it a superlative partner for sophisticated meat dishes. Suggested pairings include roasted rack of lamb with herbs, grilled ribeye steak with a red wine reduction, and braised beef short ribs. It also complements wild game such as venison or pheasant, as well as dishes featuring black truffles or earthy mushroom sauces. For a cheese course, it pairs best with matured, hard cheeses like Comte or aged Mimolette.

Vintage Quality

The 2005 vintage in Bordeaux is legendary, characterized by a exceptionally dry and sunny growing season that produced grapes with perfect phenolic ripeness. Despite the lack of rain, the deep roots of the old vines at Lafite reached necessary water reserves, resulting in low yields of tiny, highly concentrated berries. The winemaking team successfully managed the powerful tannins of this year to create a wine with immense ageing potential and classic Pauillac elegance.

title: Domaine Jacques Prieur Beaune Clos de la Feguine Blanc 2022
bodyHtml:
This rare white expression originates from the same south-facing monopole (exclusive vineyard) in Beaune as the red. Managed by celebrated oenologist Nadine Gublin, the estate treats this white wine with the same meticulous care as its Grand Cru counterparts from Meursault and Montrachet.

Wine Description

The Domaine Jacques Prieur Beaune Clos de la Féguine Blanc is a vibrant and energetic Chardonnay.

  • Appearance: Luminous green-gold with shimmering silver reflections.

  • Nose: Sharp and subtle, the bouquet features refreshing notes of flint and wet stones alongside delicate spicy nuances. Aeration reveals white flowers, acacia, and Granny Smith apple.

  • Palate: The palate is defined by high energy and tension. It offers a sapid, chalky texture with flavors of citrus zest and pear. The finish is flavorful, generous, and marked by a powerful salinity.

Food Pairing

The wine’s piercing acidity and mineral core make it an excellent partner for rich fish dishes, such as salmon with a lemon-butter sauce or seared tuna. It also pairs beautifully with pasta in creamy sauces, cured meats, and mild soft cheeses. The sapid finish is a great counterpoint to the saltiness of fresh oysters or grilled shellfish.

title: Antica Cabernet Sauvignon 'Townsend' 2019
bodyHtml:
Set high on the ridge overlooking Rector Canyon with Napa Valley 1600 feet below, this 24-acre vineyard is planted on a west-facing slope of well-drained, volcanic soils. Townsend vineyard's architecture is based on Antinori's planting philosophy for new vineyards in Tuscany, with high-density vine spacing to ensure low production of fruit per vine, rows aligned from east to west for ideal sun exposure, and training the vines low to the ground to take advantage of radiant heat from the volcanic rock and soils.

Deep garnet-purple in colour, with bold aromas of preserved plum and blueberry pie. On the palate, the wine is richly fruited and full-bodied, with gorgeous velvety tannins, spicy black fruit and a lengthy finish.

title: Chateau Duhart Milon 2016
bodyHtml:
93 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Blended of 67% Cabernet Sauvignon and 33% Merlot, the 2016 Duhart-Milon has a deep garnet-purple colour and features plums preserves, wild blueberries and cassis scents with touches of violets and underbrush with a waft of tobacco. Medium-bodied and elegant, with a backbone of finely grained tannins and oodles of freshness, it has a great core of perfumed black fruit, finishing on an earthy note.

title: Biondi Santi Rosso di Montalcino 2021
bodyHtml:
Biondi-Santi, one of Tuscany’s most historic wineries, is widely credited with pioneering Brunello di Montalcino. Established in 1888, the estate has upheld a tradition of crafting wines with remarkable elegance and longevity. Situated in the heart of Montalcino, Biondi-Santi meticulously cultivates its vineyards using time-honored practices, ensuring exceptional quality in every bottle.

Wine Description
The 2021 Rosso di Montalcino is made from 100% Sangiovese Grosso, sourced from the estate's younger vineyards. It displays a vibrant ruby-red hue and entices with aromas of sour cherry, floral undertones, and hints of crushed mint. The palate is marked by velvety tannins and bright acidity, leading to a long, crisp finish. Aged for 12 months in Slavonian oak barrels, this wine showcases balance, freshness, and a classic Montalcino structure.

Accolades

  • Vinous - 92 points: "Distinctly savory, the 2021 Rosso di Montalcino wafts up with a dark and earthy blend of flowery underbrush and balsam herbs, giving way to dried black cherries."

Food Pairing
This wine pairs beautifully with grilled meats, especially beef, as well as hearty pasta dishes like pappardelle with wild boar ragu. A perfect match to enhance the wine’s complexity.

Vintage Quality
The 2021 vintage experienced a mild autumn and winter with generous rainfall, followed by a spring frost in early April. A dry period ensued until mid-August, leading to drought conditions. However, late August rains and temperature variations allowed the grapes to achieve optimal ripeness. The harvest began on September 9th, resulting in a wine with outstanding balance and depth.

title: Sette Ponti Oreno 2022
bodyHtml:
Introduction

The wine you are asking about is Tenuta Sette Ponti Oreno 2022. This is the flagship Supertuscan red wine from the Tenuta Sette Ponti estate in Tuscany, Italy. The estate is located in the heart of the Chianti region, near Arezzo, and the 'Oreno' vineyard is named after a stream that runs through the property. Oreno is one of the most highly-regarded Supertuscans, known for its powerful, modern style that showcases Bordeaux varietals grown in the Tuscan terroir.

Wine Description (Oreno 2022)

The 2022 vintage is anticipated to be a strong expression, following the estate's tradition of producing rich and concentrated wines.

  • Color: Typically presents a deep, intense ruby red, almost black colour.

  • Grape Varieties: Oreno is a blend of international Bordeaux-style grapes, with the precise composition varying slightly by vintage. The blend is often:

    • Merlot (typically 50-70%)

    • Cabernet Sauvignon

    • Petit Verdot (or occasionally Cabernet Franc)

  • Aromatic Profile: The nose is rich and complex, often showing pronounced aromas of dense black fruit (blackberry, cassis), black cherry, and dark chocolate. These are layered with notes of spice, cedar, tobacco, licorice, and vanilla derived from oak aging.

  • Palate: The wine is full-bodied, concentrated, and powerful on the palate. It is known for its richness, velvety texture, and depth of flavour. The structure is defined by firm yet plush tannins and balanced acidity that supports the dense fruit.

  • Aging: The wine is aged for approximately 18 months in new French oak barriques, followed by at least 10–12 months of bottle aging before release.

  • ABV: Typically high, around 14.5% to 15%.

  • Optimal Drinking Window: Due to its concentration and structure, the wine is built for aging, usually recommended for enjoyment after several years in the bottle, with potential to cellar for 15–20 years.

title: Chateau Grand Puy Lacoste 2022
bodyHtml:
Chateau Grand Puy Lacoste is an esteemed estate located in Pauillac, within the Médoc region of Bordeaux, France. This Fifth Growth under the 1855 Classification is renowned for its consistent quality and classic expression of Pauillac terroir. Owned by the Borie family since 1978, the château emphasizes traditional winemaking with a focus on expressing the power and finesse of Cabernet Sauvignon grown on its deep gravel soils.

Wine Description

The 2022 Chateau Grand Puy Lacoste presents a deep garnet-purple hue, indicating its concentration and youthful vibrancy. On the nose, it offers layered aromas of blackcurrant, cassis, and dark cherry intertwined with graphite, violet, and subtle cedar. The palate is medium to full-bodied, showcasing polished tannins and a core of ripe black fruits, complemented by hints of tobacco and spice. The wine is noted for its elegance and balance, with bright acidity giving lift and precision to the dense fruit, leading to a long, mineral-inflected finish.

Accolades

  • Vinous - 96+ Points

  • Decanter - 96 Points

  • Wine Advocate - 95+ Points

Food Pairing

This Pauillac pairs beautifully with herb-crusted lamb racks, grilled ribeye steaks, or duck breast with a cherry reduction. The firm tannic structure and freshness also make it excellent alongside aged hard cheeses like Comté. Together, they create an unforgettable dining experience.

title: Drouhin Vaudon Chablis 'Vaudesir' Grand Cru 2023
bodyHtml: An exquisite wine often drunk on its own as an aperitif. Pure and limpid color, with a faint greenish hint. On the nose, fresh aromas of flower and fruit (lemony flavors) and, at times, spicy notes of coriander. On the palate: harmonious aromas bringing character and elegance. The magnitude of its Grand Cru origin and the light salty notes from the Kimmeridgian soil are in evidence. Remarkably long and complex persistence in the aftertaste.

title: Masi Amarone Costasera 2007
bodyHtml:
This prestigious red wine originates from the Amarone della Valpolicella Classico DOCG in the Veneto region of Italy. The story of the Boscaini family, the owners of Masi Agricola, began in 1772 with the purchase of their first vineyards in the heart of Valpolicella Classica. The winery's philosophy is defined by its unrivalled expertise in the 'appassimento' technique, a traditional method dating back to Roman times where grapes are dried on bamboo racks throughout the winter to concentrate aromas and flavours. Costasera refers to the 'evening slopes'—the west and south-west facing hillsides that overlook Lake Garda, where the reflected sunlight and mild climate provide ideal conditions for ripening Amarone grapes.

Wine Description

The Masi Costasera Amarone Classico 2007 presents a very dark, opaque ruby red colour with violet-tinged edges. The sensory profile is rich and powerful, featuring a complex bouquet of baked fruit, plums, and cherries, layered with notes of coffee, cocoa, vanilla, and anise. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied and opulent, showcasing a dense, chewy texture with supple tannins and a balanced acidity that cuts through the natural sweetness of the dried fruit. It is characterized by its seamless integration of spicy flavours, such as cinnamon and clove, and a long-lasting finish that echoes ripe black cherry and mocha. This blend is composed of 70% Corvina, 25% Rondinella, and 5% Molinara, and it has an ABV of 15%.

Vintage Quality

The 2007 vintage in Valpolicella is considered excellent, characterized by a hot and dry summer that allowed grapes to reach perfect phenolic ripeness with a very low incidence of mildew. These favourable conditions resulted in concentrated fruit with high sugar levels and balanced tannins, making it one of the most successful vintages for the region in recent decades. Winemakers noted that the dry autumn weather was particularly beneficial for the start of the appassimento process, ensuring the health and aromatic purity of the drying clusters.

title: Chateau Langoa Barton 2022
bodyHtml:
Chateau Langoa Barton hails from France’s renowned Bordeaux region, specifically the Saint-Julien appellation within the Médoc. Established in 1821, the estate has remained under the ownership of the Barton family for over two centuries, making it one of the rare Bordeaux properties still family-run. This continuity reflects a deep respect for tradition, combined with a modern dedication to quality, ensuring each vintage faithfully represents the estate’s classic style.

Wine Description

The Chateau Langoa Barton 2022 presents a deep ruby hue, reflecting its youthful vibrancy. Aromas of ripe blackcurrant, cassis, and dark cherry are elegantly intertwined with hints of cedar, tobacco, and a subtle floral lift. On the palate, it reveals a medium to full-bodied structure with polished tannins and a fresh acidity that gives precision and length. Flavours of juicy blackberry, plum, and graphite unfold alongside delicate notes of spice and vanilla from well-integrated oak. The finish is long and graceful, marked by minerality and finesse.

Accolades

  • James Suckling - 96+ Points

  • Vinous - 95 Points

  • Jeb Dunnuck - 93+ Points

  • Wine Advocate - 93+ Points

Food Pairing

Enjoy this wine with roasted rack of lamb seasoned with rosemary and garlic, or a classic beef tenderloin with a peppercorn sauce. Mature cheeses such as aged Comté or Gruyère also make a fine match. Together, they create an unforgettable dining experience, accentuating the wine’s depth and refined character.

title: Araujo Estate Red Blend 'Altagracia' 2010
bodyHtml:
Since 1971, some of California's most ageworthy and intensely-flavored Cabernet Sauvignons have been made from grapes grown at the Eisele Vineyard, located on a benchland near the northern end of Napa Valley, just east of Calistoga. 

Protected by the Palisades Mountains to the north and cooled by westerly breezes from the Chalk Hill Gap, this 38-acre vineyard is planted on warm cobbly soils that produce a low-yielding crop of exceptionally concentrated fruit. 

Bart and Daphne Araujo acquired the Eisele Vineyard in 1990, and committed to producing only wines of the highest caliber and distinction.

title: Matthiasson Napa Valley Cabernet Sauvignon 2019
bodyHtml:
Matthiasson Napa Valley Cabernet Sauvignon 2019 originates from the United States, specifically from several cooler vineyard sites throughout the Napa Valley in California. Founded by Steve and Jill Klein Matthiasson in 2003, the winery is a family-run business that has become a pioneer in sustainable and regenerative viticulture. Their winemaking philosophy emphasizes restraint, elegance, and lower alcohol levels, purposefully avoiding the 'bigger is better' style often associated with the region.

Wine Description

This wine exhibits a dark crimson or deep red colour in the glass. The aromatic profile is expressive and refined, featuring bright red fruits like cherry, redcurrant, and cranberry, alongside darker notes of blackberry and mulberry. These fruit scents are framed by mineral and herbal characters, including graphite, cedar, pencil shavings, and a touch of rose petals. On the palate, the wine is vibrant and medium-bodied, delivering a seamless balance of red fruit, forest berries, and subtle roasted black plum. It is characterized by silky, moderate tannins and beautiful acidity that provides energy and a long, fruity finish. The 2019 blend is composed of 86% Cabernet Sauvignon, 5% Merlot, 5% Cabernet Franc, 2% Malbec, and 1% Petit Verdot. It was aged for 20 months in mostly used French oak (<20% new) and possesses a modest ABV of 13%. The wine is produced from 100% organically grown grapes.

Food Pairing

The elegant structure and fresh acidity of this Cabernet Sauvignon make it an ideal companion for classic meat dishes such as grilled steak, herb-crusted lamb, or venison. It also pairs well with earthy flavours, including wild mushroom risotto, roasted beets, or dishes seasoned with rosemary and black pepper. For a cheese pairing, consider aged hard cheeses like Parmigiano-Reggiano or Gouda.

Vintage Quality

The 2019 vintage in Napa Valley is celebrated as a stellar and high-quality year characterized by a long, steady growing season. While the year began with heavy winter and spring rains, a temperate summer allowed for long 'hang times' and perfect phenolic ripeness. The resulting wines are noted for their exceptional depth, harmonious balance of fruit intensity, and supple tannins, with some critics observing a 'miraculous' quality to the fruit harvested under ideal autumn conditions.

title: Elvio Cogno Barolo Riserva Vigna Elena 2017
bodyHtml:
Elvio Cogno is a prestigious winery located in the Ravera cru of Novello, within Italy's renowned Barolo region. Elvio Cogno founded the estate in 1990 after decades of winemaking, focusing on traditional methods and the unique terroir of Novello. The winery is now managed by his daughter, Elena, and son-in-law, Valter Fissore, who maintain a philosophy of minimal intervention and biodiversity to express the purest characteristics of the Nebbiolo grape.

Wine Description

This Barolo Riserva is a garnet red masterpiece crafted exclusively from the Rosé clone of Nebbiolo. The aromatic profile is ethereal and stratified, featuring intense notes of rose petals, wild cherry, and red berries layered with complex hints of incense, licorice, and tobacco. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied and refined, displaying a silky texture with polished, fine-grained tannins and a vibrant acidity that provides exceptional freshness. The finish is remarkably long and sapid, evolving into nuanced flavors of orange peel and flinty minerals.

Accolades

  • Wine Spectator – 97 points

  • Decanter – 96 points

  • Vinous – 99 points

  • Robert Parker's Wine Advocate – 95 points

Food Pairing

The wine's extraordinary depth and structure make it an exceptional match for rich, savory dishes such as white truffle risotto, roasted game birds, or a wild boar stew. It also pairs beautifully with aged steaks and mature cheeses like Castelmagno or Gorgonzola.

title: Pavillon Rouge du Chateau Margaux 2020
bodyHtml:
Pavillon Rouge represents 31% of the harvest. Even though their selection criteria was as strict as for previous vintages, the percentage of Pavillon Rouge is slightly higher this year thanks to the consistency of quality conducive to great vintages. Besides this year’s climatic conditions, they hope that this increased quality is also the fruit of their efforts in the parcels whose quality approaches that of the Grand Vin.

Blend: 75% Cabernet Sauvignon, 18% Merlot, 5% Petit Verdot, 2% Cabernet Franc

96+ Points- James Suckling

Blackberry and graphite with dark fruit and violets on the nose. Very complex. Full-bodied with lovely, fine tannins that are lightly chewy. Extremely long and polished. Really refined. Integrated tannins. Wonderful length.

94+ Points - Wine Enthusiast

The second wine of Château Margaux is beautiful, smoky with acidity that is intense and yet integrated with the perfumed fruits. The wine's freshness is very much a product of the vintage, giving the tannins a fine lift. Of course the wine will age. 

94 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

As to the reds, the 2020 Chateau Margaux Pavillon Rouge is classic Chateau Margaux with its finesse, elegance, and purity. A blend of 75% Cabernet Sauvignon, 18% Merlot, and 5% Petit Verdot aged in 50% new French oak, it has a great perfume of cassis and darker cherries as well as notes of dried flowers, sandalwood, and graphite. Beautifully balanced, layered, and concentrated, it's a gem of a second wine with plenty of Grand Vin character. It will benefit from just a few years of bottle age and keep for two decades. 

94 Points - Decanter

Sinewed muscle, nuanced aromatics, graphite, gunsmoke, fresh tobacco leaf and blackberry puree. Great purity of fruits, a ton of lift and freshly crushed mint leaf aromatics that grip and curl out of the glass. One of the really successful second wines in the vintage. 31% of the overall blend. 2% of Cabernet Franc completes the blend.

94 Points - Vinous

The 2020 Pavillon Rouge is just as gorgeous from bottle as it was from barrel. Rich and sumptuous, with no hard edges, the Pavillon Rouge captures the combination of fruit richness and energy that is such a signature of the year. Bright red-toned fruit, blood orange, cinnamon and mint are all beautifully delineated. Lively acids, sweet floral and vibrant saline notes extend the effortless finish. The 2020 is a gorgeous Pavillon Rouge. 

93+ Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2020 Pavillon Rouge is excellent, offering up aromas of raspberries and dark berries mingled with hints of cedar and rose petals, followed by a medium to full-bodied, vibrant palate with excellent depth and tension, concluding with a long, chalky finish. It's more tightly wound than the exceedingly demonstrative 2019, though in the fullness of time, it wouldn't surprise me if it ended up being just as good.

title: Colgin IX Estate Proprietary Red Blend 2014
bodyHtml:
The 2014 “IX Estate” exhibits a bouquet that marries richness with nuance. The vintage highlights the subtleties of each site. The classic black cherry and licorice at the foundation of this wine are threaded together beautifully with notes of Provençal herbs, iron mineral, and scorched earth. Fresh botanical herbal notes and savory bay leaf show the classicism of Napa Valley and Cabernet Sauvignon itself. The complex flavors are pure and delineated; its immense subtleties are intoxicating. The seamless texture of the 2014 “IX Estate” is suave and smooth, such that its elegance belies its intensity.

Blend: 67% Cabernet Sauvignon, 16% Cabernet Franc, 12% Merlot, 5% Petit Verdot

98+ Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

From their steep hillside vineyards on Pritchard Hill, the 2014 Proprietary Red IX Estate is an old-fashioned Médoc blend dominated by Cabernet Sauvignon, but with some Cabernet Franc (rarely seen in the Médoc these years) as well as Merlot and Petit Verdot. Striking aromatics of violets, forest floor, loamy soil nuances, blueberry, black raspberry and blackberry soar from the glass of this spectacular 2014. The acidity seems reasonable but on the lower side, the texture is magnificent, and the overall purity and equilibrium flawless. This is a wine pushing, even demanding, a three-digit score once again, but I’m holding back – at least for now. This magnificent effort from Colgin should drink beautifully for 25-30 years.

98 Points - James Suckling

Gorgeous aromas of lean pencil, blackcurrants and raspberries. So perfumed and glorious. Full-bodied, chewy and intense with great length and intensity. Silky and muscular yet agile and energetic. Needs three to four years to resolve some of the tannins.

98 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

The 2014 IX Estate is a normal blend of mostly Cabernet Sauvignon supported by Merlot, Cabernet Franc, and Petit Verdot. From a consistently warm, moderate growing season, this has a layered, forward style in its ripe black and blue fruits as well as loamy earth, tobacco leaf, and graphite, with perfectly integrated background oak. Full-bodied, supple, and utterly seamless on the palate, it’s another wine from Tauziet that delivers sensational richness and depth with no sensation of weight or heaviness. Drink bottles any time over the coming two decades.

93 Points - Wine Spectator

Aromas of loamy, dusty earth fold in nicely with the rich chocolaty core of dark berry. The tannins muster strength without overwhelming, adding the right touch of texture and traction. Cabernet Sauvignon, Cabernet Franc, Merlot and Petit Verdot. Best from 2020 through 2034.

title: Domaine Jacques Prieur Meursault 'Clos de Mazeray' 2020
bodyHtml: Colour: Luminous golden green with the silver reflections. Nose: Very smooth with slightly toasted (roasted hazelnut), fruity (citrus fruits, orange peel) and floral (white flowers, acacia) notes. Palate: Harmonious with fresh, delicately lemon-flavoured and crusty texture. Warm and delicious on the palate with beautiful sapidity.

title: Opus One 2022 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
Opus One is a prestige Bordeaux-style blend from the Oakville subregion of Napa Valley, United States. This iconic estate was born from the legendary partnership between Baron Philippe de Rothschild of Château Mouton Rothschild and Robert Mondavi, who sought to create a single, uncompromising wine that transcends geography.

Wine Description

This vintage presents a deep ruby colour with a purple-tawny rim. The aromatic profile is rich and inviting, offering primary scents of blueberry, cassis, and dried rose petals underscored by complex notes of olive, cigar box, and graphite. On the palate, the wine is harmonious and balanced, featuring bright red fruit flavours, cocoa, and fresh orange peel that lead into a long, elegant finish with touches of wet stone, vanilla, and coffee.

Accolades

97 Points - Decanter

Chocolate, cherry and rose petal aromas on the nose. Very open and alive - this has a great energy from the aromatics alone with soft cedar shavings, vanilla bean and bramble fruit. Juicy and lively, this is full of fun - fruity and concentrated. The tannins are just wonderful, creamy and slightly grippy, extending the flavours vertically. Tons of juicy, succulent fruit - this feels quite modern but still with that flash of sunshine and ripeness. Long lasting with purity and delicacy that make it so enjoyable. A wonderful creation from Michael Silacci. This is not your typical blockbuster at all, this is a darling of a wine. 0.5% Malbec completes the blend. The Opus team chose to pick early and quickly given the heat spikes in 2022, starting with the Merlot on 24th August. Ageing 18 months in French oak.

96 Points - James Suckling

Generous, with savory aromas of ripe blackcurrants and fresh black cherries and a gentle texture that shows a slight nip of tannin. It is well structured and a bit tight, which is normal for a young cabernet sauvignon-based red that’s a proven collectible. Gives up graphite and pencil shavings, some cocoa and espresso. Full-bodied. Spicy, toasty oak is really showing through right now. Best from 2028.

Food Pairing

The structured tannins and complex fruit profile of this wine make it an ideal companion for dry-aged ribeye, roasted duck with a cherry reduction, or a rich truffle risotto. It also pairs exquisitely with earthy dishes like roasted lamb with rosemary or aged Comté cheese.

title: Domaine Harmand Geoffroy Mazis Chambertin Grand Cru
bodyHtml:
France, Burgundy, Côte de Nuits, Gevrey Chambertin. Domaine Harmand Geoffroy is a historic, family-run estate with deep roots in Gevrey Chambertin, where they have been cultivating vines for over a century. With a focus on traditional winemaking and careful vineyard stewardship, the domaine is known for producing structured, age-worthy Pinot Noir from some of the region's most revered terroirs. The Mazis Chambertin Grand Cru parcel stands out as their flagship, showcasing the profound character of this prestigious appellation.

Wine Description
The Mazis Chambertin Grand Cru presents a deep ruby hue, reflecting its concentration and youth. Aromas are intensely expressive, with layers of black cherry, wild strawberry, violet, and earthy undertones of forest floor and spice. On the palate, it reveals remarkable depth, combining ripe red and black fruits with notes of liquorice, subtle oak, and savoury nuances. The full-bodied structure is supported by firm yet refined tannins, balanced acidity, and a long, mineral-driven finish. Crafted from 100% Pinot Noir, this wine promises excellent aging potential, with an optimal drinking window from 2027 to 2045. Stylistically, it is both powerful and elegant, embodying the classic complexity of Mazis Chambertin.

Food Pairing
This grand cru pairs beautifully with roasted duck breast, venison with berry reduction, or aged Comté cheese. The richness and structure of the wine complement hearty, flavourful dishes, elevating the dining experience. Together, they create an unforgettable dining experience.

Vintage Quality
The 2020 vintage in Burgundy was marked by warm, dry conditions leading to low yields but highly concentrated fruit. Despite the challenges of a hot growing season, skilled producers like Domaine Harmand Geoffroy achieved exceptional balance and freshness in their wines, making 2020 a standout vintage for long-term aging.

title: Joseph Drouhin Clos des Mouches Blanc Premier Cru 2023
bodyHtml:
From France, specifically the Burgundy region, within the Côte de Beaune subregion and the Beaune Premier Cru appellation. Maison Joseph Drouhin, founded in Beaune in 1880, is a family-owned operation that has been in the hands of the Drouhin family for the last 130 years. The winery is dedicated to showcasing the authenticity and subtle variations of Burgundy's diverse terroirs and operates with an ideal of perfection and elegance. The vineyard practices are biological and biodynamic, using only natural products and demonstrating the utmost respect for the soil, the vine, and the environment.

This 'outstanding wine' is made from 100% Chardonnay. It displays a pale yellow color with a brilliant sheen. The complex nose is both floral and fruity, offering scents of white lilac, white rose, sweet pear, peach, mandarin, and quince, which evolve toward notes of grilled hazelnut and almond.

On the palate, it is full-bodied, rich, and ample with a lively, sleek, and slightly oily texture. The flavour profile includes crushed stone, lemon curd, dried lime peel, and clementine sweetness. It is noted for its great depth, fine acidity, and harmonious fullness, achieving a complexity and elegance akin to a Bâtard-Montrachet. The finish is long and intense, often described as 'lusty'. The wine shows a seamless, satiny, textural profile. The house of Joseph Drouhin has adopted the biological and biodynamic approach to farming, and the alcoholic and malolactic fermentations occur in oak barrels. This wine will drink well for 15 plus years.

  • James Suckling – 96 points

  • Vinous – 94 points

  • Decanter – 94 points

  • Robert Parker – 94 points

  • Burghound – 92 points

Food Pairing

Suggested pairings include finely prepared fish and crustaceans, or roasted poultry and white meats, especially those served in a cream sauce. The wine's rich body and ample texture would be beautifully complemented by a dish like roasted John Dory with hazelnuts and chanterelle mushrooms. Together, they create an unforgettable dining experience.

title: Morlet Coeur de Vallee 2019
bodyHtml:
Morlet Coeur de Vallee 2019 originates from the prestigious Oakville appellation in the heart of Napa Valley, California.

The estate is owned by Luc and Jodie Morlet, who established the winery in 2006 to blend French winemaking heritage with California's unique terroir. Luc Morlet, a fifth generation winemaker from the Champagne region, utilizes a low intervention philosophy and classical Old World techniques learned in Burgundy and Bordeaux. This 2019 release marks the first vintage produced entirely from grapes grown at the family's own estate vineyard, which is situated on an alluvial fan with well drained, gravelly volcanic soils adjacent to the world renowned To Kalon vineyard.

Wine Description

This wine displays a deep, saturated ruby to opaque garnet colour with an inky core. The aromatic profile is intense and multifaceted, featuring layers of warm cassis, blackberry pie, and blueberry preserves interwoven with notes of mocha, graphite, and dried herbs like bay leaf and sage. On the palate, the wine is full bodied and rich, offering a creamy texture and a powerful mid palate filled with crunchy black fruits and juicy blue fruits. It is characterized by its seamless freshness, fine grained, velvety tannins, and a long, mineral laced finish.

Food Pairing

The structured and concentrated nature of this Cabernet blend makes it an ideal companion for high quality, grilled medium rare beef, such as a ribeye or A5 Wagyu. It also pairs exceptionally well with game meats like roasted venison with a huckleberry jus or Colorado lamb served with savory herbs. For a refined vegetarian option, it complements dishes featuring earthy ingredients such as black winter truffles or wild mushroom risotto.

Vintage Quality

The 2019 vintage in Napa Valley is regarded as exceptional, characterized by a long, cool growing season that allowed for gradual sugar accumulation and extended hang times. While late season heat required selective picking, the resulting wines are known for their tremendous concentration, deep fruit profiles, and excellent balance between richness and energy.

Jeb Dunnuck - 89 Points

"The 2019 Cabernet Sauvignon Coeur de Vallee is deep garnet-purple colored. It gallops out with expressive notions of warm cassis, blackberry pie, and blueberry preserves, followed by hints of cedar chest, tilled soil, bay leaves, and iron ore. The full-bodied palate is taut, with a nice combination of bright crunchy black fruits and juicy blue fruits, supported by firm, grainy tannins and seamless freshness, finishing long and mineral-laced. The Coeur de Vallee vineyard is in Oakville, just across the road from To Kalon, and is planted entirely to clone 4 with a small amount of Cabernet Franc (clone 1), which does well on the clay-loam soil. The 2019 blend is 94% Cabernet Sauvignon and 6% Cabernet Franc. 1300 cases were made."

title: Bodega Noemia Malbec Patagonia 2019
bodyHtml:
Bodega Noemia is one of the southern-most wineries in the world. A region of glacial origins with poor soil and limestone-rich bedrock, it benefits from the mineral-rich waters of the Limay and Neuquen rivers. First plated in 1932, the original pre-phylloxera rootstock of the vineyards was carefully resuscitated starting in 2001, and winemaker Hans Vinding-Diers oversaw the estate'd Massale selections in order to create tailored vineyard compositions. 

The bouquet of this wine is an intense dark fruit, with hints of coffee, dark chocolate and spice notes. Its flavor is well-balanced and elegant; well-integrated fruit, tannins and acidity; with a persistent, long finish.

97 Points - Vinous

The nose is a pure compendium of fresh plum and sweet and sour cherry along with violets and a hint of tea. The aging process flirts with revealing itself but is only really an insinuation. Things get even better in the complex mouth: the proportion of all the different parts – acidity, tannins and alcohol – ensures good balance and fits perfectly together in a way that they continue right through to a finish where the whole becomes more than the sum. A deliciously detailed wine.

title: Vinedo Chadwick 2019 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
98 Points - Robert Parker's wine Advocate

Deep nose, but also precise and nuanced, with high-grade cigar box, fresh red berries, currants, charcoal, grilled meat and olives. Fine cocoa bean and mint, too. Ultra-fine and polished with a very precise, rather linear palate for cabernet. Precise, restrained, classy and long with a hint of creme de cassis in the end. 100% cabernet sauvignon.

98 Points - James Suckling

Deep nose, but also precise and nuanced, with high-grade cigar box, fresh red berries, currants, charcoal, grilled meat and olives. Fine cocoa bean and mint, too. Ultra-fine and polished with a very precise, rather linear palate for cabernet. Precise, restrained, classy and long with a hint of creme de cassis in the end. 100% cabernet sauvignon.

title: Armand Heitz Pommard Pezerolles Premier Cru 2020
bodyHtml: In all classes at school, there is always a student who has his hair done, parted on the side, dressed very neatly. He is at the top of the class, a little heckled by his classmates but at the same time respected, because he has good grades. The 1er cru Pezerolles is its personality, a consensual wine that will please a lot. A good length, a pretty color, a rich palette of aromas, all the characteristics of a great wine.

title: Aalto PS (Pagos Seleccionados) 2021 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
AALTO Bodegas y Vinedos is a leading name in Ribera del Duero, and has established itself as one of the most distinguished brands in this beautiful wine region of Spain. AALTO Bodegas y Vinedos has produced two exceptional wines, Aalto and Aalto PS (Pagos Seleccionados), voted Spain's greatest red wine. These two superb red wines pay tribute to the emblematic grape variety of the Ribera del Duero, Tempranillo, known in the region as Tinto Fino.

AALTO Bodegas y Vinedos has been ranked among the top 100 wineries in the world in the very serious guide published by the great French critics Michel Bettane and Thierry Desseauve. A superb reference from the Ribera del Duero.

Its complex bouquet carries robust notes of dark berries, spice, and a hint of savoury oak, impeccably balanced with a rewarding depth of flavour. Crafted from Tempranillo grapes, handpicked from old vineyards, this full-bodied masterpiece dances with rich, concentrated textures and ends with a polished, lingering finish. A captivating blend of intensity and elegance, Aalto PS is an opulent delight, ideal for special occasions or as a luxurious treat for discerning wine enthusiasts.

title: Dugat Py Gevrey Chambertin Premier Cru 'Les Evocelles' 2022
bodyHtml:
France’s Burgundy region is renowned for its exceptional Pinot Noir wines, and within it, the Côte de Nuits subregion stands out. Domaine Dugat-Py, based in Gevrey-Chambertin, is a family-owned estate with deep roots in the area. Known for their meticulous vineyard practices and traditional winemaking techniques, the Dugat family has cultivated a reputation for producing wines of remarkable depth and longevity.

Wine Description

The 2020 'Les Evocelles' is crafted exclusively from Pinot Noir grapes sourced from vines averaging 65 years of age, situated on a hillside with clay-limestone soils. This wine presents a medium to full-bodied profile, showcasing a vibrant ruby hue. On the nose, it offers an intricate bouquet of wild berries, orange rind, exotic spices, wilted rose petals, and subtle smoky notes. The palate is layered and concentrated, with a velvety attack that transitions into a deep core of pure, vibrant fruit. Refined tannins and lively acidity frame the wine, leading to a balanced and mildly austere finish. Vinified with 50% whole clusters, this wine embodies freshness, complexity, and a mineral-driven character.

Accolades

  • Wine Advocate: 92–94 points

Food Pairing

This wine pairs excellently with roasted duck, Châteaubriand with maître d'hôtel butter, or pan-seared ribeye steak. These dishes complement the wine's depth and character, enhancing its complex flavour profile.

title: Continuum Red Blend 2019
bodyHtml:
Continuum is the culmination of four generations of the Mondavi family in wine. Tim and Marcia, along with their families, focused on finding an exceptional hillside site in pursuit of a wine that would rank among the greatest in the world. The Continuum estate is located on Pritchard Hill along the eastern ridge of Napa Valley, high above Oakville, Sage Mountain Vineyard is nested in nature, with rocky volcanic soils producing a small, precious crop. This site yields a wine of power, depth, nuance and verve.

Tim Mondavi believes that wine is an artistic expression of man's harmony with nature and as such, the winegrowing practices at Continuum estate honour and support the vineyards by balancing the essence of classic techniques with modern-day innovations and organic farming. Continuum's goal is to craft balanced wines of power, finesse and elegance, red wines that are expressions of the land, the people and the vintage.

99 Points - James Suckling

Blackberries, dark wet soil and blackcurrants. Graphite, too. So aromatic. Pure fruit. Full-bodied with superbly polished, fine tannins that draw you down through the center of the palate. Extremely layered and the texture is so curated, giving wonderful persistence. Real plushness and fine, velvety texture.

98 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Continuum's 2019 Proprietary Red is 50% Cabernet Sauvignon, 37% Cabernet Franc, 7% Petit Verdot and 6% Merlot, all from the estate vineyard on Pritchard Hill. Aged in two-thirds new French oak, with the balance in second or third-use barrels and a single concrete amphora, it's remarkably dark in hue, a deep, saturated purple in the glass. On the nose, it's floral and herbal yet fruit-driven, with violets, sage and bay leaf adding nuance to black cherries, while the palate is full-bodied, plush and silky. There's an enticing yin-yang to the interplay between high-toned herbals and bass notes of dark chocolate in this dense, concentrated effort that finishes lush and long. It's a magnificent wine that should drink well for at least two decades.

title: Chateau Lafite Rothschild 2001
bodyHtml:
Château Lafite Rothschild 2001 originates from France, within the Bordeaux region and the prestigious Pauillac subregion on the Left Bank. Officially classified as one of the elite five First Growths (Premier Grand Cru Classé) in the 1855 Bordeaux Classification, Lafite sits on a gravelly plateau with deep cobbly soil over limestone. Under the direction of Domaines Barons de Rothschild (DBR), the estate's operational philosophy centers on producing wines defined by balance, restraint, and aristocratic finesse rather than sheer power. Often overshadowed by the neighboring landmark 2000 vintage, the 2001 release is celebrated as a "classicist’s dream," demonstrating the estate's ability to craft precision-driven, long-lived Pauillac regardless of seasonal trends.

Wine Description

This red wine displays a deep, saturated plum and dark ruby-purple appearance in the glass with soft crimson reflections. It possesses a medium-to-full-bodied, svelte, and harmonious structure defined by a silky, fine-grained, and cashmere-like texture. The sensory profile is remarkably precise, vivid, and elegant, opening with signature Lafite aromas of lead pencil shavings (graphite), cedarwood, freshly rolled tobacco, and mint, interwoven with sweet cassis, blackberry, and subtle dried floral notes. On the svelte palate, it delivers a focused stream of blackcurrant and red berry fruit, supported by a lively natural acidity and fine, well-behaved tannins. The finish is remarkably long, graceful, and clean, leaving a lingering, truffle-tinged aftertaste touched with spice and earth.

  • Varietal Composition: 86.5% Cabernet Sauvignon and 13.5% Merlot.

  • Stylistic Notes: Only 43% of the estate's total harvest was selected for the Grand Vin in 2001. The wine was aged for approximately 18 to 20 months in 100% new French oak barrels made at the estate's own cooperage (Tonnellerie des Domaines), allowing oak nuances to seamlessly integrate without overpowering the pristine varietal fruit.

  • ABV: 12.5%.

title: Louis Latour Chateau Corton 'Grancey' Grand Cru 2022
bodyHtml:
#97 on Wine Spectator’s Top 100 Wines of 2024

This acclaimed French red achieved significant global recognition after being named #97 on Wine Spectator’s Top 100 Wines of 2024, a prestigious list released in late 2023.

The Louis Latour Chateau Corton 'Grancey' Grand Cru 2022 is a red wine from the Burgundy region of France, specifically the Côte de Beaune subregion in Aloxe-Corton. Maison Louis Latour, a family-owned winery, purchased the Château Corton Grancey in 1891. The winery's philosophy emphasizes making traditional-style, ruby-coloured wines that are appreciated for their delicacy and finesse. This particular wine is a blend of the best barrels from several Corton Grand Cru vineyards, including Les Bressandes, Les Perrières, Les Grèves, and Le Clos du Roi, with the proportions varying by vintage. It is only produced in vintages where the grapes achieve perfect ripeness.

 Wine Description

This Pinot Noir has a dark ruby colour. The aroma reveals notes of blackberry, pepper, and undergrowth. The palate is full and suave, with flavours of liquorice, coffee, and cherry. The finish is beautifully fresh and long-lasting. The wine is known for its concentration, fine tannins, and stony minerality. The average age of the vines used for this wine is over 40 years.

Accolades

  • James Suckling - 98 points

  • Burghound.com - 92 points

Food Pairing

Suggested pairings for this wine include roasted beef, roasted quail, wild boar, duck 'à l'orange', and mature cheeses. A perfect match to enhance the wine's complexity.

 Vintage Quality

The 2022 vintage in Burgundy is considered excellent, with both quality and quantity. The growing season experienced a number of notable conditions, including a cold start in April with frost threats, followed by a warm May and a downpour of rain in June. A very hot and dry summer then set in from July, which helped to prevent diseases but also caused some drought issues. The resulting wines are shaping up to be excellent, with good complexity, clear fruit, and a pleasant freshness. Winemakers were able to adapt to these challenges, with the wines displaying a "breezy joie de vivre" and textures with a "gloss" to them.

title: Calera Pinot Noir Jensen 2020
bodyHtml:
Calera’s Mt. Harlan Vineyards are located in the Gavilan Mountains 25 miles east of the Monterey Bay. The site was chosen for its limestone soils and ideal climate. At an average elevation of 2,200 feet it is among the highest and coolest vineyard sites in California.

At more than 40 years old, the coveted old vines of Jensen Vineyard have produced a stunning wine that offers depth, elegance and layered complexity. On the nose, aromas of ripe plum and persimmon flirt with more dramatic black fruit undertones. The palate is lush and mouth-filling, striking a seamless balance between energetic red berry flavors and deeper flavors of black cherry and blackberry that glide to a long, resonant finish.

title: Chateau Calon Segur 2017
bodyHtml:
96 Points - Wine Enthusiast   

Fine tannins give this wine its structure and its essence. It is a wine constructed with firmness, bringing out a dry core, allied to a more velvet character. The black fruits are developing well and the ensemble of the wine will be in perfect harmony. Drink from 2024.

95 Points - James Suckling   

Graphite, wild herbs, bracken, violets and such spicy black and blue berries. The palate has impressive concentration, yet very supple, charming texture. Such impressively articulated tannin detail with very fine, long tannins and deeply integrated oak. This wine is so full of flavor and interest from start to finish. A blend of 76% cabernet sauvignon, 13% merlot, 9% cabernet franc and 2% petit verdot. Needs three to four year to come around. Try in 2023 and onwards.

95 Points - Jeb Dunnuck   

As you’d expect, the grand vin ratchets up the intensity. The 2017 Chateau Calon Segur is 76% Cabernet Sauvignon, 13% Merlot, and 2% each of Cabernet Franc and Petit Verdot aged 20 months all in new barrels. This deep, inky hued 2017 boasts medium to full-bodied aromas and flavors of creme de cassis, leafy herbs, and mineral nuances. It stays tight and compact on the palate, has wonderful Saint-Estephe Cabernet character, ripe tannins, and is just a classic, balanced effort that will benefit from 4-6 years of bottle age and evolve for 25+ years.

95 Points - Decanter   

This is gorgeous. Rich, silky, bright and perky, and full of grace. A real purity to the blueberry and blackberry fruits, and soft elongated tannins. Highly recommend for its classicism. Has the austerity of 2017 but gives it real polish, and it raises its game through the palate. 19 months aging.

95 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate   

Medium to deep garnet-purple colored, the 2017 Calon-Ségur features warm plums, cassis, baked cherries and mulberries, earth, meats and cedar on the nose with notes of lavender and olives. The palate is medium-bodied, elegant and intense with firm, fine-grained tannins and great length, finishing minerally. This wine was aged in 100% new French oak barrels for 20 months. The blend is 76% Cabernet Sauvignon, 13% Merlot, 2% Cabernet Franc and 2% Petit Verdot.

93 Points - Wine Spectator   

Ripe and focused, featuring a solid core of plum and black cherry fruit, supported by a well-embedded cast iron note. Sweet tobacco, bay leaf and lavender details fill in the background while the fruit takes an encore on the finish. A very solid effort. Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Cabernet Franc and Petit Verdot. Best from 2021 through 2034.

title: Hundred Acre Morgan's Way Cabernet Sauvignon 2017
bodyHtml:
This ultra-premium red wine is produced in the Napa Valley region of California, specifically from the Morgan's Way Vineyard (formerly known as Kayli Morgan) located in the St. Helena subregion. The estate was founded by Jayson Woodbridge, a visionary who sought to create wines that express the pinnacle of Napa Valley terroir. Woodbridge's winemaking philosophy involves an obsessive dedication to quality, including hand-sorting individual berries and aging the wine for extended periods in 100% new French oak.

Wine Description

The 2017 Hundred Acre Morgan's Way Cabernet Sauvignon is characterized by an opaque, deep purple colour. The aroma is intense and multi-layered, featuring notes of crème de cacao, crème de cassis, and black cherries, accented by nuances of red roses, black soil, and a touch of pencil shavings. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied and incredibly rich, offering a plush, velvety texture with flavours of spicy black fruit preserves and dark chocolate. This 100% Cabernet Sauvignon displays remarkable freshness and an exceptionally long, mineral-inflected finish. The wine typically has an ABV of 15.5% and is produced using sustainable, high-precision farming methods, though it is not certified organic.

Food Pairing

The immense concentration and structural depth of this wine make it a perfect companion for prime cuts of beef, such as a dry-aged porterhouse or a slow-roasted wagyu ribeye. It also pairs exquisitely with game meats like venison with a blackberry reduction, or rich, earthy dishes such as truffle-infused mushroom risotto. For cheese, choose powerful and aged varieties like 36-month Parmigiano-Reggiano or a sharp, vintage cloth-bound cheddar.

title: Chateau Margaux 2021
bodyHtml:
The iconic Château Margaux, nestled in the heart of Bordeaux’s Margaux appellation, stands as a paragon of elegance and tradition. Owned by the Mentzelopoulos family since 1977, the estate boasts a legacy dating back to the 12th century, celebrated for producing wines of remarkable finesse and longevity. The 2021 vintage reflects the estate's commitment to excellence, even in challenging conditions.

Wine Description

The 2021 Château Margaux reveals a radiant ruby hue with fragrant aromas of violet, red currant, and graphite, intertwined with subtle hints of cedar and tobacco. On the palate, it is medium-bodied with finely woven tannins and a vibrant core of fresh berry fruit, underscored by a refined minerality. The finish is long and persistent, showcasing remarkable precision and purity—a hallmark of this legendary estate.

Food Pairing

Perfectly suited to refined dishes such as rack of lamb with rosemary, wild mushroom risotto, or roasted duck with cherry glaze. This pairing highlights the wine’s depth and character, elevating any fine dining experience.

Vintage Quality

The 2021 vintage, marked by cooler weather and meticulous vineyard management, exemplifies a classic style. It is a wine of elegance and restraint, offering great aging potential for collectors.

title: Jordan Cabernet Sauvignon 2021
bodyHtml:
This elegant and food-friendly red wine originates from the United States, specifically from the premier Alexander Valley in Sonoma County, California. Winemaker Maggie Kruse describes 2021 as an "intensely flavorful stunner" that marked a return to normalcy after the back-to-back challenges of previous years. The winery's philosophy remains rooted in creating a "St. Julien style" wine with California fruit—prioritizing balance, moderate alcohol, and silky tannins over pure power.

Wine Description

Jordan Cabernet Sauvignon 2021 presents an attractive deep ruby colour with a sophisticated and "pretty" sensory profile. The nose leads with aromas of cassis, black cherry, and boysenberry, layered with intriguing notes of graphite, anise, dried herbs, and vanilla cedar. On the palate, the wine is incredibly silky and fluid, showcasing a "harmonious balance" of blueberries, cranberry, and leather. It is characterized by its vibrant acidity and a surge of saline minerality, leading to a long finish with delicate hints of rose petals and clove. This blend reached an ABV of 13.8% and was matured in 100% French oak barrels. Due to extreme drought conditions that resulted in smaller Cabernet berries, the winemakers added a higher proportion of Merlot (sourced from Sonoma and Dry Creek valleys) to ensure the house's signature soft, elegant texture.

title: Almaviva 2022
bodyHtml:
Viña Almaviva 2022 originates from Chile, within the prestigious Puente Alto subregion of the Maipo Valley. Created in 1997 as an iconic joint venture between Baron Philippe de Rothschild (of Château Mouton Rothschild) and Viña Concha y Toro, Almaviva was established to blend French winemaking tradition with Chile’s exceptional terroir. The estate's 85-hectare vineyard in Puente Alto sits on stony, gravelly alluvial soils at the foot of the Andes Mountains, where cool mountain breezes moderate warm days. Operating with the exact precision of a Bordeaux First Growth, the winemaking philosophy focuses on meticulous parcel-by-parcel selection, gravity-fed processing, and balancing Andean fruit power with classical French elegance and structural freshness.

Wine Description

This red wine presents a deep, opaque ruby-purple appearance in the glass with vibrant violet reflections at the rim. It possesses a full-bodied, multi-layered, and supple structure supported by a plush, velvety texture and exceptional mineral energy.
