The sensory profile is rich, expressive, and aromatic, opening with an inviting bouquet of cassis, black cherries, wild blackberries, and blue plums, seamlessly layered with notes of crushed violets, dark chocolate, tobacco leaf, graphite, cedar, and roasted coffee beans. On the palate, it delivers a dense, concentrated core of dark fruits, perfectly framed by ripe, fine-grained tannins and a vibrant thread of natural acidity. The finish is remarkably persistent, long, and harmonious, leaving lingering nuances of black fruit, cocoa powder, and subtle sweet oak spices.

  • Varietal Composition: 72% Cabernet Sauvignon, 23% Carmenère, 4% Cabernet Franc, and 1% Petit Verdot.

  • Stylistic Notes: The grapes were hand-harvested and strictly double-sorted prior to gravity-fed fermentation in temperature-controlled stainless steel tanks. The wine aged for 20 months in 100% new French oak barrels, allowing the distinct spice and savory notes of Carmenère to integrate seamlessly with the structured Cabernet Sauvignon core.

  • ABV: 14.5%.

Food Pairing

The structural weight, complex spicy fruit core, and polished tannic frame of this Chilean icon make it a magnificent companion to rich, high-end gastronomy.

  • Fine Meats: Pairs exceptionally well with grilled prime ribeye steaks, roasted rack of lamb with garlic and herbs, braised short ribs, or tenderloin of beef with a truffle jus.

  • Game: Ideal when served alongside pan-roasted duck breast with cherry reduction, venison loin, or wild boar stew.

  • Earthy Dishes: Complements wild mushroom risottos, truffle-infused pastas, and roasted root vegetables with herbs.

  • Cheeses: Matches gracefully with mature, firm cheeses such as 24-month Comté, aged Gouda, or Manchego.

Vintage Quality

The 2022 growing season in Puente Alto was marked by a dry spring and a warm, sunny summer, balanced by cool, refreshing night winds descending from the nearby Andes Mountains. These extreme diurnal temperature swings preserved crucial natural acidity while allowing the grapes to reach complete, uniform phenolic maturity. The harvest proceeded smoothly with excellent fruit health, yielding grapes with small berries and high skin-to-juice ratios. The resulting 2022 Almaviva stands out as a triumphant, classic release, combining intense fruit purity, structural nobility, and polished finesse. It is approachable with decanting in its youth, yet possesses the structural concentration to cellar gracefully over 25 to 35 years.

title: Shafer Cabernet Sauvignon Hillside Select 2018
bodyHtml:
Shafer Vineyards' Hillside Select Cabernet Sauvignon is the iconic flagship wine from the Stags Leap District in Napa Valley, California. The 2018 vintage marks the 40th release of this celebrated wine, renowned for its power, complexity, and exceptional aging potential.

Winemaking and Aging

The 2018 Hillside Select is made from 100% Cabernet Sauvignon grapes, sourced exclusively from Shafer's hillside estate vineyards. These steep, rocky vineyards yield low quantities of intensely flavored fruit. The wine was aged for 32 months in 100% new French oak barrels, which contribute to its luxurious texture and complexity.

Tasting Notes

  • Appearance: Deep garnet-purple with a striking intensity.

  • Nose: Aromas of ripe blackberry, black cherry, and crème de cassis, accented by hints of graphite, violets, baking spices, and warm earth.

  • Palate: Full-bodied and layered, with opulent flavors of blueberry pie, dark chocolate, and blackcurrant, balanced by vibrant acidity. Fine-grained tannins provide structure, leading to a long, seamless finish with subtle notes of smoked herbs and cedar.

Critical Acclaim

  • Jeb Dunnuck: 100 points – The 2018 Cabernet Sauvignon Hillside Select is another perfect wine, although readers will need to have patience, as it’s still a baby. Deep purple-hued with a perfumed, vibrant bouquet of blue fruits, graphite, spring flowers, and lead pencil, it’s full-bodied, sensationally concentrated, has perfectly integrated acidity, tannin, and alcohol, not a hard edge to be found, and an incredible finish. This monumental Napa Valley Cabernet Sauvignon is 7-8 years away from maturity and will have 40-50 years of overall longevity.

  • Wine Advocate: 98+ points – Made from 100% Cabernet Sauvignon, the 2018 Cabernet Sauvignon Hillside Select displays a deep garnet-purple color. It charges out of the gate with bold crème de cassis, blueberry pie and black cherry preserves notes, plus hints of smoked meats, fragrant earth and tar, with a fragrant waft of violets and Provence herbs. Full-bodied, the palate is packed with muscular black fruits, supported by a solid foundation of firm, grainy tannins and compelling freshness, finishing long with an enticing herbal lift.

  • James Suckling: 99 points – So much black licorice in this, together with tar, blackcurrants, blackberries and slate. Full-bodied, but very toned and focused, with polish and energy. Extremely fine tannins and wonderful length. All about balance and purity. Gorgeous now, but this will age for decades to come. Great finish. Better after 2026.

Serving and Cellaring

The 2018 Hillside Select is best served at 60–65°F (16–18°C). Decanting for at least an hour before serving allows the wine to fully open and express its aromatic complexity. While it is approachable now, this wine will evolve beautifully over the next several decades, with an optimal drinking window from 2025 to 2055.

Conclusion

The 2018 Shafer Hillside Select Cabernet Sauvignon is a true masterpiece of Napa Valley winemaking. With its remarkable depth, luxurious texture, and outstanding aging potential, it embodies the pinnacle of Cabernet Sauvignon excellence.

title: Il Poggione Brunello di Montalcino 2019 - 3 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
Il Poggione Brunello di Montalcino originates from Italy, within the Montalcino subregion of Tuscany. Established in 1890 by Lavinio Franceschi, Tenuta Il Poggione is one of the three original producers of Brunello and a founding member of the local consortium. Currently owned by Leopoldo and Livia Franceschi, the estate follows a philosophy of diversified agriculture and traditional winemaking, utilizing meticulous vine care and long ageing to craft classic, cellar-worthy wines.

Wine Description

This red wine presents a deep ruby red colour that can show purple reflections in its youth. The sensory profile is intense and persistent, featuring a complex bouquet of dark cherry, blackberry, and plum, layered with notes of spice, leather, tobacco, forest floor, and dried flowers. On the full-bodied palate, it is warm and balanced, delivering concentrated fruit flavours supported by a 'steely' backbone and velvet-smooth, crunchy tannins. The finish is remarkably long and mineral-tinged, often revealing hints of orange zest, licorice, and graphite.

  • Varietal Composition: 100% Sangiovese (locally known as Brunello).

  • ABV: Typically recorded at 14.5% to 15%.

  • Ageing: The wine undergoes long maturation in large French oak barrels (30–50 hl) followed by additional bottle ageing.

  • Organic Status: The estate typically follows conventional cultivation practices.

title: The Spring Mountain Elivette Reserve 2016
bodyHtml:
This flagship red wine originates from the United States, specifically the Spring Mountain District of Napa Valley, California. Spring Mountain Vineyard is a historic estate formed from four 19th-century properties (Miravalle, La Perla, Chevalier, and Streblow). Elivette is the estate’s "signature assemblage," representing the highest expression of its 135 unique vineyard blocks spread across steep hillside terrain. It is crafted to be a classically styled Napa red with the structural longevity and balance typical of mountain fruit.

Wine Description

  • Appearance: Deep garnet-purple.

  • Nose: Highly aromatic and multifaceted. It features bright scents of wild berries, tart rhubarb, and boysenberries, transitioning into darker notes of plum, blueberry, and black cherry. These are accented by cracked pepper, sage, charcoal, and espresso.

  • Palate: The wine enters rich and round, offering concentrated layers of texture. It shows "heft as well as mouthwatering cut," with notes of lush blackberry and dark tobacco. A buried iron or mineral note resonates through a long, polished, and lingering finish.

Accolades

  • Wine Spectator: 96 points

Food Pairing

This wine's bold tannins and complex fruit profile make it a natural partner for rich, savory meats. It pairs excellently with grilled ribeye steak, braised lamb with rosemary, or a classic beef stifado. It can also stand up to bold international flavors like a tandoori mixed grill or hearty mushroom-based dishes. For a cheese pairing, consider strong, aged varieties such as a mature Cheddar or Manchego.

title: Domaine Seguin Manuel Vosne Romanee Aux Communes 2022
bodyHtml:
Seguin-Manuel has undergone a major rejuvenation since its acquisition by Thibaut Marion in 2004, 180 years after its foundation in 1824.

Coming from a ten-generation family of winegrowers, Chanson Père & Fils, Thibaut started his career -- and honed his skills for seven years -- at the family winery in Beaune. Today, he puts his experience, passion and energy at the service of the great wines of Burgundy. 

The range has thus been considerably extended through the acquisition of new vineyards et new grape suppliers. Every effort has been made at Seguin-Manuel to let the wines express their natural balance and each cuvée is crafted with the intention of reflecting its terroir with panache.

Seguin-Manuel's vineyards are grown organically with no use of chemicals, certified since 2015.

title: Chateau Clerc Milon 2018
bodyHtml:
96 Points - Wine Enthusiast

This opulent wine is as bold with its fruit as with its tannins. The initial velvet texture masks the dense structure allowing it to age impressively. Blackberry flavours, acidity and intense richness, are coming together in a welter of ripe fruits. Drink from 2026.

96 Points - Decanter

This is a highly successful Clerc Milon in a run of great vintages at the property. Lovely purity, clear big tannins, and natural poise and tension. Persistent, succulent, full of cassis, licorice and crushed mint. Seriously impressive and will go the distance. Harvest from 17 September to 10 October. Blend completed by 3% Petit Verdot and 1% Carmenère. 

95 Points - James Suckling

Blackcurrants, tobacco, graphite, cloves and dried leaves on the nose. It's medium-to-full-bodied with firm, tightly knit tannins. Structured and compact with a long, mineral finish. Tight and austere. Very pretty structure here. 

94+ Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2018 Clerc Milon is a blend of 60% Cabernet Sauvignon, 27% Merlot, 9% Cabernet Franc, 3% Petit Verdot and 1% Carménère. Medium to deep garnet-purple in colour, it has a pure, beautifully delineated nose of crushed blackcurrants, fresh black plums and boysenberries with hints of wild thyme, damp soil, tar and black olives. The medium to full-bodied palate offers taut, muscular black fruit with loads of savoury layers and a firm, grainy texture, finishing long and mineral-tinged. 

93 Points - Wine Spectator

This throws off a lovely stream of violet and cassis aromas and flavours that are sleek and pure in feel, picking up dark cherry, iron and sanguine details along the way. Refined and cellar-worthy. Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Cabernet Franc, Petit Verdot and Carmenère. Best from 2023 through 2035.

93 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

From an estate located on the east side of Highway D2 and between Château Lafite and Château Mouton Rothschild, the 2018 Château Clerc Milon is a ripe, sexy, full-bodied Pauillac that brings plenty of richness while still staying reasonably elegant. Blackcurrants, blackberries, smoked earth, new leather, and cedary herbs all flow to an impressively endowed, layered Pauillac with chewy tannins, terrific balance, and an excellent finish. Based on 60% Cabernet Sauvignon, 27% Merlot, and the rest Cabernet Franc and Petit Verdot, brought up in 50% new French oak, this outstanding 2018 needs 4-6 years of bottle age to round into form and will evolve nicely for 20-25 years.

title: Anakota Cabernet Sauvignon 'Helena Montana Vineyard' 2021
bodyHtml:
Introduction

This powerful red wine originates from the United States, specifically the Knights Valley AVA in Sonoma County, California. The Anakota estate was established in the late 1990s by the Jackson family, who sought a unique site capable of blending the opulence of Napa with the structural precision of Sonoma. Under the direction of Vigneron Pierre Seillan, the winery employs a 'micro-cru' philosophy, dividing the vineyard into small blocks to capture the distinct geological nuances of the volcanic, gravelly loam soils.

Wine Description

The 2021 Helena Montana is an inky, deep garnet-purple wine composed of 100% Cabernet Sauvignon. On the nose, it is characteristically intense, offering aromas of ripe red and black currants, blackberry, and violet, accented by notes of graphite, leather, and bouquet garni. The palate is full bodied and linear, featuring concentrated fruit and non-fruit layers like cocoa, sweet baking spices, and dark roast coffee. It is defined by a rock-solid structure of firm, grainy tannins and a juicy acidity that leads to a very long, mineral-driven finish. While powerful in its youth, this wine is built for extensive cellaring, with an optimal drinking window between 2027 and 2050.

Accolades

  • James Suckling - 97 points

  • Wine Advocate - 95 points

  • Jeb Dunnuck - 96 points

title: Mission Hill Oculus 2021
bodyHtml:
Mission Hill Oculus is the flagship Bordeaux style red wine from the Okanagan Valley in British Columbia, Canada. Named after the 'oculus' a circular window in the dome of the winery's underground barrel cellar. This wine represents the ultimate expression of the estate’s most meticulously nurtured vineyards. Owned by Anthony von Mandl, the winery operates with a philosophy that blends art, food, and culture, maintaining a deep commitment to sustainable and organic viticulture.

Wine Description

This vintage presents a deep and structured sensory profile with layered aromas of wild blackberry, blackcurrant, and acai. On the palate, the wine is powerful yet poised, offering rich flavours of dark chocolate and seamlessly integrated oak supported by sculpted tannins. The finish is noted for its remarkable clarity, detail, and lingering presence.

title: Chateau Leoville Poyferre 2015
bodyHtml:
97 Points - Jeb Dunnuck    The 2015 Leoville Poyferre is cut from the same cloth as the 2016, yet is more sexy, rounded and opulent. Notes of cassis, licorice, crushed rocks, lead pencil shavings and graphite all emerge from this unctuous, ripe, pedal-to-the-metal beauty that's absolutely loaded with fruit and texture. Reminding me of the 2003, yet only fresher, don't miss this beauty. It should be drinkable in 3-4 years and last for 3-4 decades.  

97 Points - Vinous    The 2015 Léoville-Poyferré is spectacular. Inky, dense and explosive, the 2015 possesses off the chart richness, with soft contours, no hard edges and exceptional balance. All the elements are simply fused together. inky blue/purplish fruit, chocolate, new leather, blueberry jam, exotic spice and violet notes are all beautifully delineated throughout. Fresh, vibrant and totally sexy, Léoville-Poyferré is one of the wines of the vintage. Don't miss it! Tasted two times.

96 points - Wine Enthusiast    Following the style that this estate has now adopted, this is an ultrarich, concentrated wine. However its acidity and bright black-currant fruits contrast well with this solid base. Drink this impressive wine from 2026.

96 Points - James Suckling    A rich and intense red with blackberries, tar and spices. Black tea and blueberries. Full-bodied, very layered and multi-dimensional. Very long and flavorful. Such great texture. A dynamic and superb red. Drink in 2023.

95 Points - Wine Spectator    Dark plum cake, blueberry reduction and açaí berry fruit tilts this to the exotic side of the ledger, with warm ganache, melted black licorice and tar notes providing the spine through the lush finish. Displays some serious latent grip, so there's no rush despite the showy fruit. Best from 2022 through 2040.

94 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate    The 2015 Leoville Poyferre is deep garnet-purple colored with a nose of grilled meats, baked plums, crème de cassis and baker's chocolate with nuances of dusty soil and iron ore plus a hint of bay leaves. Medium to full-bodied, very firm and muscular in the mouth, it is built like a brick house with a mineral-tinged finish.

title: Michele Chiarlo Barolo Cannubi 2020
bodyHtml:
This aristocratic red wine originates from the Barolo DOCG in the Piedmont region of Italy. Established in 1956, Michele Chiarlo is a family-owned winery known for vinifying the essence of Piedmont through its most prestigious crus. The winery's philosophy emphasizes minimal intervention and sustainable viticulture, evidenced by their V.I.V.A. and Equalitas certifications. The Cannubi vineyard, often considered the most historic and famous hill in Barolo, features steep, grass-covered terraces a meticulous design pioneered by Chiarlo to improve sun exposure and prevent erosion.

Wine Description

The Michele Chiarlo Barolo Cannubi presents a brilliant ruby red colour. The sensory profile is exceptionally complex, unfolding with an intense bouquet of ripe red fruits, cherry, and rose, layered with sophisticated notes of licorice, sweet tobacco, and fine spices like cinnamon. On the palate, the wine is powerful yet refined, showcasing a generous texture with silky, well-integrated tannins and a vibrant, incisive freshness. It is characterized by its elegant poise and a persistent, fruity finish with a clean mineral edge.

title: Penfolds Bin 707 Cabernet Sauvignon 2021
bodyHtml: Bin 707 perfectly reflects the Penfolds ‘House Style’ through a Cabernet Sauvignon lens: intensely-flavoured fruit, completion of fermentation and maturation in new oak, expressing a Penfolds understanding of multi-vineyard, multi-region fruit sourcing. Bin 707 was first vintaged in 1964. The wine was not made from 1970 to 1975 (when fruit was directed to other Penfolds wines) nor in 1981, 1995, 2000, 2003 or 2011 (when the fruit of the required style and quality was not available). Full-bodied and with proven cellaring potential, Bin 707 retains a secure place among the ranks of Australia’s finest Cabernets.

title: Aalto Crianza 2021 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
Established in 1999 by Mariano García, the celebrated former winemaker of Vega Sicilia, and Javier Zaccagnini, Aalto has become one of Ribera del Duero’s benchmark producers. The winery is devoted to expressing the complexity of the region’s old-vine Tempranillo through careful site selection and minimal intervention winemaking. With a focus on precision and balance, Aalto works with small plots from over 200 hectares of vines, many between 40 and 80 years old, to craft wines of depth and elegance.

Wine Description

Aalto Crianza 2021 presents a deep garnet colour with vibrant purple highlights. The nose is expressive and layered, offering aromas of black cherry, ripe plum, and wild berries, accented by subtle notes of liquorice, cedar, and sweet spices from its time in French and American oak. On the palate, this 100% Tempranillo is medium to full-bodied, showcasing a harmonious blend of concentrated dark fruit, polished tannins, and refreshing acidity. The wine reveals a silky texture with excellent balance, leading to a persistent, elegant finish with hints of cacao and clove. Ideal for drinking from 2024 to 2032, this vintage delivers both approachability in its youth and the structure for graceful ageing.

Accolades

  • "James Suckling - 94 points."
  • "Wine Advocate - 93 points."
  • "Vinous - 93 points."

Food Pairing

Aalto Crianza 2021 pairs beautifully with roasted pork tenderloin, grilled lamb skewers, or manchego cheese. The wine’s refined tannins and vibrant fruit complement a range of savoury dishes. A perfect match to enhance the wine's complexity.

Vintage Quality

The 2021 vintage in Ribera del Duero experienced cooler temperatures and increased rainfall, which contributed to wines of remarkable freshness and aromatic clarity. Thanks to precise vineyard management, Aalto achieved excellent ripeness and balance, producing a vintage that will be remembered for its finesse and ageing potential.

title: Verite 'La Muse' 2010
bodyHtml:
"The 2010 vintage was a long season for ripening after a beautiful flowering. This vintage will live for a long time — yet this racy, powerful, elegant wine can also be appreciated young. This vintage is a great example of what Sonoma can do with a diversity of soils and a grandiose climate. Harvest took place September 25th through October 16th."  – Pierre Seillan, Vigneron

A deep, rich, black cherry color in the glass opens with intriguing notes of licorice and white pepper on the nose. Red fruits and spice dance on the palate while licorice and black cherry linger, leading to a very long finish. Discreet tannins and a lively minerality indicate a wine with great aging potential. The 2010 vintage was a perfect year for Merlot, which is reflected in this balanced and elegant wine.

95 Points - Vinous     An exotic, nuanced beauty, the 2010 La Muse offers up an exotic concoction of white truffle, cassis, cloves. Captivating and totally beguiling, the 2010 takes over all of the senses and never lets up. A rush of blue and black-hued fruit flows through to the enveloping, deeply resonant finish. The 2010 shuts down in the glass, so it is best left alone in bottle for a number of years. What a gorgeous wine this is, especially if readers can be patient.

94 Points Robert Parker Wine Advocate - One of the more soft, opulent, precocious wines I have tasted from this estate, it exhibits abundant notes of spicy oak, plum, Asian soy, new saddle leather, barrique, black cherries and blackcurrants. Round and generous with considerable fat and succulence, it can be drunk in 2-3 years or cellared for 15-20

title: Fortunate Son 'The Diplomat' 2019
bodyHtml:
From the renowned talent behind the highly coveted Hundred Acre collection comes a "21st Century Claret" of unreserved energy and generosity. Some of the fruit for Fortunate Son even hails from Jayson Woodbridge’s own Hundred Acre vineyards, joined by fruit from select family vineyards he’s negotiated to farm. The Diplomat is mostly Cabernet Sauvignon, supported by Merlot and Petite Sirah. Bright notes of Morello cherries and black raspberries soar above a profound core of cassis with licorice and tobacco. The palate is plush with layers of powerful black fruit and a long, earthy finish.

Aged for 24-30 months in the finest French oak barrique. The stave wood is hand-selected for ultra-tight grain, then air dried for three years before being made into barrels.

94 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

The Merlot-dominated 2019 The Diplomat comes from a handful of sites and would give a great Pomerol a run for its money with its darker red and black fruits, smoky herbs, and earthy goodness on the nose. These carry to a full-bodied, rounded, opulent 2019 with sweet, building tannins and a great finish.

94 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Riper and substantially more expressive than the 2018, Fortunate Son's 2019 Red Wine The Diplomat is a plush, luscious wine, laden with black cherries, mocha and loam notes. It's full-bodied, rich, velvety and supple, with a lingering finish.

title: Solaia 2016 (by Tenuta Tignanello)
bodyHtml:
Solaia 2016 is a celebrated Super Tuscan produced at Tenuta Tignanello, part of the historic Antinori estate in Tuscany. The wine hails from the sunniest hillside known as the Solaia vineyard, characterised by limestone and schist-rich soils, ideal southwestern exposure, and elevation around 350–400 metres. The Antinori family has crafted this iconic bottling only in exceptional vintages since 1978.

Wine Description

This vintage is a bold and structured blend comprising approximately 73 per cent Cabernet Sauvignon, 20 per cent Sangiovese, and 7 per cent Cabernet Franc, matured for around 18 months in French oak barrels. It presents an intense ruby-red colour. The nose offers profound depth—ripe blackberry, plum jam, espresso, menthol, and licorice mingle with balsamic herbal undertones and spicy hints of white pepper. The palate is powerful yet refined, with silky, structured tannins, expressive dark fruit, mineral notes of campfire ash and graphite, and a vibrant, eternally lingering finish. Overall, the 2016 is considered both chiseled and elegant, deep yet light on its feet.

Accolades

  • The Wine Advocate – 100 points.

  • James Suckling – 100 points.

  • Vinous (Antonio Galloni) – 99 points.

  • Wine Spectator – 98 points.

Food Pairing

Ideal with rich fare—think rib-eye roast, venison, rack of lamb, or other hearty red meat dishes that mirror the wine’s depth and structure.

Vintage Quality

2016 was an outstanding vintage in Tuscany, allowing for perfectly ripe fruit and excellent concentration. The resulting Solaia showcases exceptional precision and ageing potential, promising to evolve gracefully over decades.

title: Caymus Cabernet Sauvignon 'Special Selection' 2018 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml: Caymus sets aside the best barrels of Cabernet Sauvignon from Napa Valley each year to produce Special Selection. Distinguished by excellent, velvety tannins and is enjoyable upon release or with ageing. A wine of structure with an intense concentration of supple flavours and dark fruits.

title: Armand De Brignac La Collection (Ace of Spaceds) - 6 Bottles
bodyHtml:
An opulent collection of Armand de Brignac’s iconic Champagnes, La Collection celebrates the ultimate Armand de Brignac experience, with a bottle each of Gold Brut, Limited Edition Green Golfer, Blanc de Blancs, Rose, Blanc de Noirs and Demi Sec.

Available in a limited number, the House's hand-applied pewter labels are updated against the collection of colourful bottles.

title: Giusti Amarone Della Valpolicella Classico 2018 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
Luxurious and opulent, Amarone della Valpolicella Classic DOCG is one of the quintessential wines of Veneto and Italy. It is the result of the vocation of the land combined with man’s technical expertise.

This wine is intense ruby red with a tinge of garnet in colour.  The nose has gorgeous notes of dried fruit with hints of plum and cherry.  Aromas of licorice and pepper are also evident.  The palate is full-bodied and elegant, round and warm with soft tannins. Excellent served with game, braised meats, mature cheese, and sweet and sour dishes.

title: Domaine Thibault Liger Belair Clos Vougeot Grand Cru 2019
bodyHtml:
95 Points - Decanter

Liger-Belair owns a 0.75ha parcel planted to old vines in the centre of the vineyard, on the border with Echézeaux, in the section of the Clos known as Baudes Basses. A large proportion of the grapes are fermented as whole clusters, producing remarkably pure, immediately attractive ripe black fruit, dressed with hints of spice and fresh violets. The texture is dense and firm, but very polished and elegant. A very sophisticated Clos de Vougeot. 

92+ Points - Vinous

From the southern side of the clos, the 2019 Clos Vougeot Grand Cru includes 40% whole bunch from the parcel planted in 1944. The bouquet is tightly wound at first, opening to reveal blackberry, briary, cedar and light loamy aromas. The palate is nicely structured with firm grip, touches of black pepper and blood orange infusing the mainly black fruit. The finish just needs to manifest a little more finesse, and that might happen during the remainder of barrel maturation, of course.

title: Domaine Harmand Geoffroy Gevrey Chambertin 'La Perriere' Premier Cru 2019
bodyHtml:
Based in the prestigious village of Gevrey Chambertin in Burgundy's Côte de Nuits, Domaine Harmand Geoffroy has been a family-run operation for generations, dedicated to traditional viticulture and authentic expressions of terroir. Among their Premier Cru holdings, 'La Perriere' is a particularly distinctive site, known for its shallow, stony soils and excellent drainage, which contribute to wines of precision and minerality.

Wine Description
The 2019 'La Perriere' Premier Cru presents a vibrant ruby colour with an aromatic profile of wild raspberries, red cherries, and cranberries, accented by hints of violets, fresh thyme, and a touch of spice. On the palate, it is medium-bodied and finely structured, offering a lively core of red fruit, subtle earthiness, and chalky minerality. The tannins are smooth and well-integrated, while a bright acidity lends freshness and drive, leading to an elegant, lingering finish. Composed entirely of Pinot Noir, this cuvée is approachable in its youth but will develop gracefully over the next 10–15 years, with optimal drinking from 2025 to 2037.

Accolades
Vinous - 91 points.

Food Pairing
This graceful Premier Cru pairs beautifully with herb-roasted chicken, grilled salmon, or a mushroom and leek tart. These dishes enhance the wine’s finesse and subtle complexity, creating an unforgettable dining experience.

Vintage Quality
The 2019 vintage in Gevrey Chambertin delivered ripe, concentrated fruit thanks to a warm and dry season. Producers skilfully balanced richness and freshness, allowing terroir-driven wines like 'La Perriere' to shine with clarity and ageing potential.

title: Beringer Cabernet Sauvignon Private Reserve 2021
bodyHtml:
This flagship red wine is produced in the Napa Valley region of California, sourced from several premium estate vineyards including the St. Helena Home Vineyard and Chabot Vineyard. Established in 1876 by brothers Jacob and Frederick Beringer, the estate is California's oldest continuously operating winery. The winemaking philosophy for the Private Reserve label, which was first created in 1977, centres on a minimalist approach to highlight the unique terroir of Napa Valley's finest vineyard lots.

Wine Description

The 2021 Beringer Cabernet Sauvignon Private Reserve is a black-opaque wine with a deep and alluring appearance. The sensory profile features an exuberant bouquet of fresh violets, blackberry, and blackcurrant, underpinned by complex notes of graphite, dusty cocoa, and espresso. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied and super-polished, offering a lush, creamy mid-palate with flavours of black plum and warm baking spices such as clove and cedar. It is characterized by structured, velvety tannins and a bright line of fresh acidity that leads to a long, sumptuous finish. This blend is composed of 80% Cabernet Sauvignon, 12% Cabernet Franc, 6% Merlot, and 2% Malbec, with an ABV of 15.1%. While the estate vineyards are third-party certified sustainable, this wine is not certified organic.

Food Pairing

The bold structure and rich fruit profile of this Cabernet Sauvignon make it an ideal companion for hearty red meat dishes such as tenderloin steak, beef brisket, or short ribs. It also pairs excellently with roasted lamb or savoury vegetarian options like grilled portobello mushrooms and eggplant parmesan. For a cheese course, hard varieties such as aged cheddar or gouda are recommended.

Vintage Quality

The 2021 vintage in Napa Valley is regarded as superb, characterized by even ripening and lower yields that led to intense fruit flavour development. Clear skies during the harvest period allowed for ideal pick times, resulting in a refined wine that captures the purity and transparency of the growing season.

title: Sena Red Blend 2021
bodyHtml:
From Chile’s Aconcagua Valley, Seña is an iconic wine estate founded in 1995 through a visionary partnership between Eduardo Chadwick and Robert Mondavi. Their goal was to demonstrate Chile’s ability to craft world-class wines, blending Old World tradition with New World innovation. Today, Seña stands as one of Chile’s most acclaimed producers, committed to expressing the unique character of its terroir.

Wine Description

The 2021 Seña Red Blend presents a deep ruby colour with violet highlights. Its aromatic bouquet unfolds with redcurrants, strawberries, blackcurrants, rose petals, cocoa, and hints of clove spice. On the palate, it is vibrant and layered, combining juicy red and black fruit with lively acidity and finely woven tannins. Subtle notes of vanilla, toast, and mineral freshness add to its depth and complexity. Medium to full-bodied, the wine carries a long, elegant finish with remarkable precision.

Accolades

  • James Suckling – 100 points

  • Wine Advocate – 98 points

  • Vinous – 97 points

  • Decanter – 97 points

Food Pairing

This wine’s structure and elegance make it an ideal companion to grilled lamb chops, braised short ribs, or roasted venison. For a vegetarian pairing, it shines alongside wild mushroom risotto or aged cheeses.

title: Chateau d'Issan 2016
bodyHtml:
Château d'Issan is a Third Growth estate located in the Margaux appellation of Bordeaux, France. With a history dating back to the 12th century, it has long been recognized for producing wines that epitomize the elegance and complexity of the region. Today, the estate is managed by the Cruse and Lorenzetti families, who uphold traditional winemaking practices while integrating modern techniques to enhance quality.

Wine Description
The 2016 Château d'Issan is a blend of 64% Cabernet Sauvignon and 36% Merlot. In the glass, it presents a deep garnet-purple hue. The nose is vibrant and expressive, with aromas of black cherries, blackcurrants, chocolate mint, beef drippings, black olives, and cigar box. On the palate, it is medium-bodied with an intensely flavored mid-palate, supported by firm, grainy tannins and a long, savory finish. This wine is crafted using sustainable viticulture practices.

Accolades

  • James Suckling – 96 points
  • Wine Advocate – 94+ points
  • Decanter – 97 points

Food Pairing
This wine pairs beautifully with classic meat dishes such as veal, pork, beef, lamb, duck, game, and roast chicken. It also complements hearty fish courses like tuna, as well as mushrooms, pasta, and a variety of cheeses. These pairings enhance the wine's depth and character, creating an unforgettable dining experience.

title: Chateau Lynch Bages 2012
bodyHtml:
Lynch-Bages 2012 is an intense red colour, while the aromas are a complex blend of black fruits, violet and pepper with subtle woody notes. The wine is balanced, combining aromatic elegance with fine tannins, and the first taste is full smooth and lively.

95 Points - Wine Enthusiast     The wine is very dry, layered tannins giving a major sense of structure. It will always have this dry, dense character, very firm, solid and powerful. 

92 Points - Wine Spectator     This has a very solid core of dark plum, crushed black currant and blackberry fruit, with lightly firm flesh and good drive through the finish, where alder and iron notes fill in. Shows excellent energy and depth, while harnessing the austere edge of the vintage. Best from 2018 through 2025.

92 Points - James Suckling     Aromas of blackcurrants, blueberries and lemons follow through to a full body, firm tannins and a fresh, clean finish. A little tight now but excellent. Precision to this. Back ended. Better in 2018.

91 Points - Wilfred Wong of Wine     Château Lynch Bages—the most celebrated wine of the Fifth Growths—has made an excellent wine in 2012. Ripe and generous, this wine exhibits loads of bright red fruit flavors. On the palate, it is a bit tight, and the tannins are just a bit noticeable. A few years in the cellar will resolve the hard edges.

title: Chateau Canon 2016
bodyHtml:
98 Points - Wine Enthusiast

This wine is impressive both from its structure and its fruit, one of the stars of the vintage in SaintÉmilion. It has great weight, concentration as well as style and aging potential. The ripe fruit shines through the structure, promising an elegant maturity. Drink from 2025.

98+ Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Composed of 74% Merlot and 26% Cabernet Franc and aged for 18 months in 70% new French barriques, the 2016 Canon is medium to deep garnet-purple in color, and—WOW—it opens with the most stunning perfume of violets, red roses and kirsch, giving way to a core of black cherry preserves, chocolate box, licorice, warm plums and Chinese five spice plus an earthy waft of underbrush. Medium to full-bodied, the palate is completely filled with expressive, perfumed black berry layers accented by lively red fruits and exotic spices, supported by impressively fine-grained tannins and fantastic tension, finishing very long with jaw-dropping energy. Tasted three times, I had one opportunity to taste the 2015 and 2016 Canon side by side. While I love the bold, rich, seductive nature of the 2015, this 2016 kicks it up a notch in terms of polish, precision, depth and persistence. Most notably, the superbly ripe, exquisitely fine-grained tannins on this 2016 bring to the table a whole other level of sophistication. Bravo!

97 Points - James Suckling

Complex aromas of blackberries, iodine, oyster shell and wet earth. Ever so perfumed. Full-bodied, yet reserved and tight with very silky tannins that are energized and minerally. Takes off at the end. The freshness lifts it. Try after 2024.

97 Points - Decanter

This has all the power that St-Emilion can deliver, but deals it out slowly with precision, gorgeous balance and a clean lift. It has great concentration, purity and depth, without sacrificing the integrity of the juicy blueberry and cassis fruits. It really is a great example of what the limestone plateau can do. The 2015 delivers a slightly more voluptuous edge to the fruits, whereas this vintage emphasises fresh mint leaf, salinity and grip. A wonderful wine, utterly delicious.

96 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

The 2016 Chateau Canon is another beautiful wine from this estate, made in a more streamlined, elegant style compared to the richer, sexier 2015. Checking in as a blend of 74% Merlot and 26% Cabernet Franc all from a magical terroir situated on the upper plateau just outside of the village of Saint-Emilion, it saw a small percentage of the blend go through malolactic fermentation in barrel, and the wine spent 18 months in 70% new French oak, with the balance in once-used. Gorgeous notes of blueberries, cassis, spring flowers, white truffle, and crushed rock nuances all come soaring from the glass and it has notable intensity as well as complexity. Medium to full-bodied, with vibrant acidity, ultra-fine tannins, and a straight, silky texture, I don’t think it matches the 2015 on concentration, but it’s perfectly balanced and has a texture to die for. It needs a good 4-5 years of bottle age (or more) and it’s going to be long-lived. Tasted three times.

95 Points - Wine Spectator

This delivers a pretty serious ball of fruit, with a mix of raspberry, blueberry and black currant flavors providing range, while sweet tobacco notes and chalky minerality impart texture and detail. There's a fresh savory echo on the finish. Much less reliant on toast than most of its peers. Best from 2022 through 2037. 6,667 cases made.

title: Zuccardi Fosil Chardonnay 2022
bodyHtml:
This high-altitude white wine originates from the San Pablo IG in the Tunuyán subregion of the Uco Valley, Mendoza, Argentina. Zuccardi Valle de Uco, led by third-generation winemaker Sebastián Zuccardi, is widely regarded as a global leader in terroir-driven winemaking, having been named "World’s Best Vineyard" for three consecutive years. The winemaking philosophy for the Fósil label is focused on capturing the "mountain identity" of the Estancia San Pablo vineyard, situated at a staggering 1,400 metres above sea level and only 300 metres from the start of the Andes Mountains.

Wine Description

The 2022 Zuccardi Fósil Chardonnay presents a pale yellow colour with greenish reflections. The sensory profile is austere and complex, opening with aromas of green apple peel, lime zest, and chamomile, layered with distinct notes of mountain herbs (such as huacatay) and a subtle pastry backdrop. On the palate, the wine is lean, dry, and intensely mineral, showcasing a chalky texture and "laser-focused" acidity reminiscent of fine Chablis. It is characterized by great energy and a saline finish that highlights the calcareous alluvial soils of its origin. This 100% Chardonnay has an ABV of 13% to 13.5% and was aged primarily in concrete vats (75%), with the remainder in used 500-litre French oak barrels. Notably, it undergoes no malolactic fermentation to preserve its racy, natural acidity.

Food Pairing

The vibrant mineral tension and citrus purity of this Chardonnay make it a sophisticated partner for meaty fish such as turbot, red mullet, or poached grouper. It also pairs elegantly with fresh shellfish, particularly oysters, or light salads featuring pomegranate, mint, and almonds. For a cheese course, opt for fresh goat cheese (chèvre) or soft, creamy varieties that can be cut by the wine's sharp acidity.

title: Catena Zapata Malbec Adrianna Vineyard Fortuna Terrae 2022
bodyHtml:
Catena Zapata Malbec Adrianna Vineyard Fortuna Terrae 2022 is a red wine from Argentina, produced in the Mendoza region, specifically the high-altitude Gualtallary district of the Uco Valley. The wine is made by the renowned Catena Zapata family winery, now run by fourth-generation vigneron Laura Catena. The winery's philosophy is centred on the deep belief that high-altitude vineyards, such as the Adrianna Vineyard, impart unique qualities to the Malbec grape. The 'Fortuna Terrae' parcel name means 'Luck of the Land' in Latin, referring to its deep loam soils with white stones covered in limestone that bestow unique character.

Wine Description

The wine is 100% Malbec. It has a deep purple colour and is clear and bright. The aromatic profile is pure, highly aromatic, and elegant, showing layers of blue fruits, red berries, and black fruit intertwined with notes of violet, lavender, and subtle hints of licorice, cocoa powder, and dried herbs. Notes of garrigue, cut grass, and a subtle hint of ink also emerge. It is a medium to full-bodied wine. The palate has a juicy and austere attack, with compact, concentrated dark and blue fruit. The texture is rounded and smooth, with finely chalky, seductive tannins, elevated acidity, and a saline, mineral edge. Stylistically, it is pure, floral, herbal, and elegant, embodying the finesse and intensity of a high-altitude Malbec. The wine is aged for 14 to 18 months in French oak barrels. The finish is exceptionally long, precise, and vibrant, gaining length and dimension with time in the glass. The ABV is 13.5% or 13.7%. The optimal drinking window is from 2024 to 2036, or from 2027 onwards.

Accolades

  • Robert Parker - Wine Advocate - 96 points

  • James Suckling - 96 points

  • Tim Atkin - 95 points

  • Wine Spectator - 95 points

Food Pairing

This full-bodied and robust wine is a great pairing for steaks, barbecue fare, and full-flavoured cheeses. Suggested pairings include beef bourguignon, roast duck legs, and braised red meat.

Vintage Quality

The 2022 vintage was exceptionally good for the quality of Mendoza wines, despite unpredictable weather conditions. The cool autumn allowed for slow and complete ripening of the grapes, ensuring remarkable concentration and balance in the vintage. The availability of glacial water helped keep the vineyards healthy.

title: Perrier Jouet Belle Epoque Rose Brut 2013
bodyHtml:
True to the free spirit of Maison Perrier-Jouet, Perrier-Jouet Belle Epoque Rosé is a resolutely original champagne which combines rarity with the ability to surprise. First created in 1978 and crafted only in exceptional years, and produced in extremely limited quantities. Perrier-Jouet Belle Epoque Rose is a fascinating Cuvee, subtle and delicate, yet warm and embracing as if it were wrapping you in silk. 

96 Points - James Suckling

Very pretty aromas with peach and crabapple characters, cotton candy and light nutmeg. Medium to full-bodied with fantastic bubbles that run the length of the wine and persist. Fine and beautiful. Ultra-complex and refined.

title: Joseph Drouhin Chassagne Montrachet Morgeot 'Marquis de Laguiche' Premier Cru 2023
bodyHtml:
This is a wonderful occasion to savour a great wine. Admirable light golden colour. Intense and elegant aromas come to the fore : hawthorn, apricot notes, evolving towards hints of blond tobacco. As the wine ages, there are nu- ances of dried fruit and rare spices. A silky texture and a subtle touch of tannin give a true personality to the wine. Remarkable aftertaste. A great white Burgundy.

Due to the refinement of their bouquet and the elegance of their flavors, these great white wines are unquestionably destined to accompany haute cuisine: shellfish cooked in a light wine sauce (court-bouillon) or any delicate fish (such as Dover sole) prepared grilled or poached.

title: Pio Cesare Barbaresco 'Il Bricco' 2022
bodyHtml:
Ranked No. 28 in James Suckling’s Top 100 Wines of Italy 2026

Hailing from Italy's renowned Piedmont region, within the prestigious Barbaresco subregion, Pio Cesare Barbaresco 'Il Bricco' represents a masterclass in regional typicity. Founded in 1881 by Cesare Pio, the winery remains family owned and is celebrated for its historical cellars located directly in the heart of Alba.

Wine Description

This 100% Nebbiolo pours a rich ruby colour adorned with a fine garnet rim. The intense and precise nose reveals an array of aromas, highlighting full flavours of raspberry and plum intermingled with nuances of tobacco, cardamom, cedar, and a subtle hint of mixed flowers. On the palate, the wine is medium to full bodied, delivering a compact and solid framework characterized by firm, savoury tannins that are expertly integrated. It displays magnificent balance and freshness, concluding with a remarkably long, harmonious finish showing notes of truffle and tobacco.

title: Delamotte Blanc De Blancs 2014
bodyHtml:
94 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2014 Blanc de Blancs has turned out very well indeed, opening in the glass with scents of citrus zest, crisp orchard fruit, fresh bread and wet stones. Medium to full-bodied, chiseled and incisive, with excellent depth at the core, racy acids and a chalky finish, this isn't as muscular as the 2008 or 2012, but it has real cut and persistence and should age very gracefully indeed.

92 Points - Wine Spectator

A finely meshed, linear Champagne, with racy acidity and a citrusy overtone driving flavours of poached apricot, biscuit, candied lemon peel and a toasty hint of brioche. Fine and creamy. Drink now through 2026.

title: Chateau d'Armailhac 2016
bodyHtml:
Chateau d'Armailhac, classified as a Fifth Growth in 1855, is a close neighbor of Chateau Mouton Rothschild. Its 123 acres of vines, surrounding the beautiful grounds of the main house, are planted with the typical varieties of the region: Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Cabernet Franc and Petit Verdot. Their wines, aged in oak casks, combine finesse and elegance with powerful, well-structured tannins and are highly sought after!

95 Points - James Suckling    This is a really driven d’Armailhac showing blackcurrants and fruit tea with hints of bark on the nose and palate. Full-bodied, very firm and structured with a long and powerful finish. Direct and linear. Try after 2023.

94 Points - Jeb Dunnuck     A thrilling bottle of wine that readers should snatch up is the 2016 Château d’Armailhac. This deeply colored, medium to full-bodied, powerful Armailhac gives up a lovely perfume of blackberry and plums fruits, violets, graphite, cedar pencil, and earthy, herbal nuances. Classic, ripe, layered, and just a beautiful Pauillac any way you look at it, it has plenty of upfront sex appeal but is going to keep for 20-25 years as well. Bravo! The 2016 is a blend of 62% Cabernet Sauvignon, 28% Merlot, 8% Cabernet Franc and 2% Petit Verdot.

93 Points - Wine Spectator    This juicy red sports dark plum, fig and boysenberry fruit backed by an equally strong wave of bramble and sweet tobacco notes. The cast-iron spine pins down the finish, so give this a little time to integrate fully. Best from 2023 through 2038.

93 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate    Deep garnet-purple coloured, the 2016 D'Armailhac opens with gregarious crème de cassis, blackberry pie and mulberries scents with hints of chocolate box, roses and charcoal with a waft of dried sage. Medium-bodied, the palate has a rock-solid frame of firm, grainy tannins and wonderful freshness, finishing long and earthy.

93 Points - Decanter    There's fairly high acidity on the attack here, and yet it's well balanced by a body that's richer and deeper than in many years of Armailhac. You can definitely feel the texture and the powerful depth of brambly fruit, and there are also some of the signature lilting floral notes, given extra charge through graphite, liquorice, cassis, and that pulsating acidity. Great quality. 2% Petit Verdot completes the blend.

90 Points - Wine Enthusiast    This is a ripe wine, full of black fruits with attractive tannins. It has depth but the wine is more about fruitiness and relatively quick development. Drink this already delicious, lightly spicy wine from 2022.

title: Wayfarer Pinot Noir The Estate Library Vertical - 6 Bottles
bodyHtml:
The Wayfarer Pinot Noir Estate Library Vertical is a curated collection showcasing four exceptional vintages—2016, 2017, 2018, and 2019—of the Wayfarer Vineyard Pinot Noir. Presented in an elegant wooden box, this set offers a unique opportunity to experience the evolution and distinct characteristics of each vintage from this renowned Sonoma Coast estate.

2016 Vintage:

  • Colour: Moderate garnet.
  • Aroma: Aromas of cherry, raspberry, dark rose petal, and sous-bois.
  • Palate: Mid-weight with earth-kissed flavors of black cherry and black raspberry, complemented by a hint of racy spice.
  • Body: Velvety mouthfeel with comforting tannins.
  • Finish: Appealing acidity on an extremely long, peacock tail finish.
  • Accolades:
    • 97 Points - Jeb Dunnuck
    • 95 Points - Wine Enthusiast
    • 94 Points - Vinous

2017 Vintage:

  • Colour: Bright ruby-tinged.
  • Aroma: Notes of raspberries, flowers, rose hips, and spice.
  • Palate: Feminine style with fine tannins, gliding smoothly over the palate.
  • Body: Incredibly elegant with a fine structure.
  • Finish: Long and satisfying, leaving a lasting impression.
  • Accolades:
    • 95 Points - Jeb Dunnuck
    • 95 Points - James Suckling

2018 Vintage:

  • Colour: Medium ruby.
  • Aroma: Perfume of garrigue, dried orange peel, prosciutto, and rose petals with mineral-laced cranberry and red and black berry fruits.
  • Palate: Medium-bodied, grainy, and incredibly fresh, slowly gaining in flavor amplitude and nuance.
  • Body: Balanced with a harmonious structure.
  • Finish: Ends in a fanfare of spicy detail.
  • Accolades:
    • 98+ Points - Wine Advocate
    • 96 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

2019 Vintage:

  • Colour: Medium ruby-purple.
  • Aroma: Broody aromas of blood orange, iron, rhubarb, and cranberry sauce with notes of dusty earth and dried herbs.
  • Palate: Incredible intensity, lift, and expansive flavor layers.
  • Body: Juicy with a very long finish that continually calls you in for another sip.
  • Finish: Persistent and inviting.
  • Accolades:
    • 95 Points - Wine Advocate
    • 94 Points - Wine Spectator

This collection exemplifies Wayfarer's dedication to producing wines that are both expressive and true to their terroir, offering a delightful experience for Pinot Noir enthusiasts.

title: Castello di Montepo Maceone 2020
vendor: 300747 - South By Southwest Wine Imports Inc.
bodyHtml:
Introduction

This exclusive red wine originates from the historic Castello di Montepò estate in the Maremma region of Tuscany, the private winegrowing domain of Jacopo Biondi Santi. Maceone is the estate’s premier "Cru" dedicated entirely to Merlot, standing as a counterpart to the Cabernet-based Fontecanese. Born from the rigorous micro-zonation studies conducted by Jacopo Biondi Santi, this wine is sourced from a specific, high-altitude vineyard plot rich in galestro soil that was identified as the perfect terroir for expressing the depth and elegance of the Merlot grape. It represents a modern, sophisticated interpretation of this international varietal, filtered through the lens of Tuscan tradition. The 2020 vintage, characterized by a balanced growing season, allowed for perfect phenolic ripening, resulting in a wine of exceptional softness and structural integrity.

Wine Description

Castello di Montepò Maceone 2020 displays a concentrated, luminous ruby red colour with slight purple edges. The nose is opulent and enveloping, offering a rich bouquet of ripe blackberries, dark plums, and blackcurrants, beautifully integrated with complex notes of sweet spices, vanilla, and a hint of roasted coffee bean. On the palate, the wine is the epitome of elegance and roundness; it is full-bodied and velvety, distinguished by soft, polished tannins that wrap around a dense core of dark fruit. Despite its plush texture, it maintains a vibrant acidity that provides lift and longevity. The finish is long, warm, and persistent, leaving lingering impressions of fruit compote and savory balsamic nuances. This 100% Merlot typically has an ABV of 14% and is aged for 24 months in un-toasted French oak barriques (Tronçais), followed by significant bottle refinement. The optimal drinking window is from release through approximately 15 to 20 years.

title: Kistler Pinot Noir Russian River 2024
bodyHtml: Founded in 1978, Kistler Vineyards is a small, family-owned and operated winery specializing in the production of Burgundian style Chardonnay and limited amounts of Pinot Noir. Grapes are estate grown and purchased from vineyards in Sonoma County. In 1992, Kistler Vineyards moved all production to its Vine Hill Road Vineyard in the Russian River Valley.

title: Chateau Malescot St Exupery 2019
bodyHtml:
Chateau Malescot St Exupery 2019 originates from France, within the Margaux appellation of the Médoc region in Bordeaux. This historic estate traces its roots back to 1616 and was famously classified as a Third Growth (Troisième Cru) in the 1855 Bordeaux Classification. Currently owned by the Zuger family and managed by Jean Luc Zuger, the winery combines traditional techniques with modern innovation, such as being one of the first in the region to utilize a gravity-fed winemaking system.

Wine Description

This wine displays a deep ruby or garnet purple colour with dark violet reflections. The aromatic profile is generous and expressive, featuring a well defined bouquet of cassis, black cherry, and blackberry mingled with floral notes, liquorice, and cedar. On the palate, it is full bodied and muscular yet refined, delivering layers of opulent dark red fruits supported by vibrant acids and ripe, powdery tannins. The finish is remarkably long, persistent, and detailed, often showing hints of espresso roast and loamy soil. The varietal composition for the 2019 vintage is 54% Cabernet Sauvignon, 35% Merlot, 6% Cabernet Franc, and 5% Petit Verdot. It has an ABV of 14% and is produced using sustainable viticulture practices, though it is not typically certified organic.

Food Pairing

The versatile structure and power of this Margaux make it an excellent match for a variety of classic dishes. It pairs perfectly with grilled or roasted red meats, such as filet mignon, entrecote, or roast lamb. It also complements wild game, roasted poultry like duck or coq au vin, and hearty mushroom based recipes. For a cheese course, it is best served with soft, flavourful varieties such as Brie or Camembert, as well as aged hard cheeses.

Vintage Quality

The 2019 vintage in Margaux is considered to be of exceptionally high quality, following a hot and dry summer that lasted until late September. Despite two significant heatwaves in June and July, the vines benefited from moisture retaining soils and a golden autumn, resulting in grapes with extraordinary concentration and freshness. The winemaking team successfully managed these conditions to produce a wine that balances richness with the characteristic finesse of the appellation.

title: Chateau D'Armailhac 2022
bodyHtml:
Château D'Armailhac is a distinguished Fifth Growth estate in Pauillac, part of the esteemed Domaines Barons de Rothschild (Lafite) portfolio since 1933. Formerly known as Château Mouton d'Armailhacq, it shares viticultural heritage with neighbouring First Growth Château Mouton Rothschild. The estate is renowned for its deep gravel soils and its blend of tradition and innovation in winemaking, crafting wines that express elegance and precision.

Wine Description
The 2022 vintage of Château D'Armailhac presents a deep, vibrant ruby colour in the glass. Aromatically complex, it opens with blackcurrant, ripe plum, and hints of violets, followed by undertones of graphite and tobacco leaf. On the palate, the wine is medium to full bodied with refined tannins and a structured core. Flavours of dark berries, crushed stones, and cedar lead to a persistent, harmonious finish.

Food Pairing
This Pauillac pairs beautifully with herb crusted rack of lamb, grilled ribeye, or roasted duck breast. The wine's structure and savoury depth also complement aged cheeses such as Comté or Manchego. A perfect match to enhance the wine's complexity.

title: Produttori del Barbaresco - Barbaresco 'Pora' Riserva 2020
bodyHtml:
This red wine comes from the Barbaresco region of Piedmont, Italy, specifically from the Pora subregion. Produttori del Barbaresco is widely considered the benchmark cooperative of the region, only admitting quality-minded farmers who represent the village's best terroirs. Managed by Aldo Vacca, the winery is dedicated to a philosophy of high-level winemaking that showcases the pure expression of its members' exceptional fruit.

Wine Description

The 2020 Barbaresco Pora displays a medium-light ruby red colour with garnet highlights. It offers an aromatic and effusive nose featuring crushed flowers, spice, leather, tobacco, and wild cherry. On the palate, the wine is medium to full-bodied with a gracious texture, delivering flavours of succulent cherry, cranberry, star anise, and balsamic notes of menthol and eucalyptus. This 100% Nebbiolo wine is characterized by its fluid balance, fine-grained tannins, and a long finish that hints at earth and licorice. The ABV is 14.5%. While approachable today, the optimal drinking window extends from 2025 through 2045. The vineyard is farmed using sustainable practices.

Accolades

  • Wine Spectator - 94 points

  • Jeb Dunnuck - 94 Points

  • Vinous - 93 points

  • Decanter - 93 points

  • Wine Advocate - 93 points

Food Pairing

This wine's elegant structure and bright fruit profile make it an ideal companion for rich pasta dishes like pappardelle with duck ragu or fresh egg pastas with truffles. It also pairs beautifully with hearty red meats such as beef tenderloin, venison, or lamb chops. For cheese selections, consider aged varieties like Parmigiano-Reggiano or spicy hard cheeses.

Vintage Quality

The 2020 vintage in Barbaresco is regarded as high quality, characterized by a balanced growing season with no extreme weather events. Though summer was warm, cool evenings in August and September slowed the ripening of Nebbiolo, resulting in wines with great aromatic richness and excellent tannin structure.

title: Louis Martini Cabernet Sauvignon Monte Rosso 2019
bodyHtml:
Produced in the United States, this distinguished red wine hails from the Moon Mountain District subregion of Sonoma Valley. Established in 1933 by Italian immigrant Louis M. Martini, the winery was a foundational pioneer in Napa Valley following the repeal of Prohibition. Today, under the ownership of E. & J. Gallo, the estate continues to focus on premium site expression from the historic Monte Rosso Vineyard, which features high-elevation volcanic soils and some of California’s oldest Cabernet Sauvignon plantings dating back to 1880.

Wine Description

This deep ruby Cabernet Sauvignon opens with an aromatic profile of toasted coconut, caramel, and baked cherries, layered with notes of fig and bay leaves. The full bodied palate reveals concentrated flavors of cherry pie filling, Santa Rosa plum, and allspice, complemented by hints of graham cracker.

Food Pairing

This robust Cabernet Sauvignon pairs exceptionally well with hearty dishes such as grilled ribeye steak, braised lamb shanks, or roasted venison. The wine's firm tannins and dark fruit profile also complement earthy flavors like wild mushrooms or aged cheddar.

title: Dom Perignon P2 'Plenitude' Brut - Mixed Vintage 3 Pack
bodyHtml:
Each vintage in this Dom Pérignon P2 'Plenitude' Brut mixed pack represents a unique expression of the house's style, shaped by the specific climatic conditions of its harvest year. While all three share the signature Plenitude 2 depth achieved through extended maturation on the lees, they vary significantly in their aromatic profiles and textural weight.

1 bottle of Dom Pérignon P2 1999

This vintage is often described as an 'intriguing' and 'atypical' release that emphasizes laser like focus over more traditional toasty qualities.

  • Aromatic Profile: The nose reveals a complex 'sensory chiaroscuro' of dried apricots, flower honey, and candied tropical fruit, underscored by darker notes of smoked peat and cocoa.

  • Palate and Texture: It features a sustained liveliness and textured richness, where umami notes sculpt the wine's contours against a surprising fruitiness characteristic of the 1999 harvest.

  • Finish: The experience concludes with an elegant, tactile finish marked by mineral nuances and saline toasted notes.

1 bottle of Dom Pérignon P2 2000

Known as the 'Millennium Vintage', this release is celebrated for its generous energy and seductive complexity.

  • Aromatic Profile: A ripe bouquet offers notes of stone fruit and bergamot, complemented by tertiary scents of iodine, tangerine, and oyster shell.

  • Palate and Texture: The entry is vibrant and satiny, showcasing a refined structure with flavours of baked peach, salted almond, and spun honey.

  • Finish: It presents a long and precise finish that is mouthwateringly saline, with subtle touches of bitterness and toasted malt.

1 bottle of Dom Pérignon P2 2002

Frequently cited as one of the greatest recent vintages, the 2002 P2 expresses a confident, enhanced maturity and authentic power.

  • Aromatic Profile: The initial nose is intensely floral with jasmine and saffron, slowly evolving into a more mysterious bouquet of orange oil, smoky peach, and praline.

  • Palate and Texture: Broad and fleshy on the palate, it unfurls with opulence and 'airy grace', revealing brilliant fruit notes that are sensual and forward.

  • Finish: The finish is exceptionally long and distinguished, marked by intense mineral energy, saline notes, and a slight hint of liquorice.

title: Chateau Mouton Rothschild 2000 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
Chateau Mouton Rothschild, a Premier Cru Classe from the Bordeaux region and one of the world's greatest wines, is owned by Baroness Philippine de Rothschild.

The wine has an attractively deep color with a garnet hue and an open, complex nose dominated by notes of humus and fern along with jammy fruit and prunes. Full on the attack, it shows opulence and attractive substance over close-knit, caressing tannins, developing intense roast coffee notes set off by a lovely reminder of the humus aromas on the nose. The powerful, full-bodied finish lingers long on the palate, revealing the expression and sheer class of great Mouton vintages, reminiscent in its richness and harmony of the very fine 1986.

97+ Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Deep garnet colored with a touch of brick, the 2000 Mouton Rothschild (composed of 86% Cabernet Sauvignon and 14% Merlot) boldly bursts from the glass with tantalizing Black Forest cake, dried mulberries, kirsch and blackcurrant pastilles notes plus wafts of iodine, incense, potpourri and cinnamon stick with a hint of cigar boxes. Medium to full-bodied, the palate packs in the muscular fruit, framed by firm, ripe, grainy tannins and seamless freshness, finishing with phenomenal length. This is an incredibly complex and multifaceted wine, and it's drinking deliciously now. 

97 Points - Wine Enthusiast

With its distinctive antique bottle and gold etched label dominated by a sheep, this is definitely a move away from classic Bordeaux bottling. It is good that the wine can support the presentation. The fruit is so ripe, it almost tastes of raisins, but that sweetness is finely balanced by the dry tannins and concentrated texture. To finish, there are exotic spices, giving an almost oriental character to the long aftertaste.

93 Points - Wine Spectator

Rounded, fleshy and a bit extracted in feel, with dark plum, blackberry and fig jam flavors that flirt with a pruny edge, picking up lots of warm mocha, singed vanilla bean and ganache notes through the finish. This relies more on easy opulence than on depth or purity on the end.

93 Points - James Suckling

The nose is very intense, super-ripe and rich, verging on jammy. Notes of leather, spices and prunes. Full-bodied, soft and beautiful with ripe tannins and a long finish. This is soft and yummy right now. Drink or hold.

title: Verite 'La Muse' 2019
bodyHtml:
La Muse shimmers with a deep violet-ruby core of color, expressing opulent fruit aromas of candied red & black cherry, and wild fresh blackberry, with perfumed notes of dried potpourri, dried rosemary, and essences of sandalwood, toasted cinnamon, nutmeg, and clove from French oak aging. The palate perfectly mirrors the nose, along with tannins reminiscent of dark cocoa nib, bright acidity, and petrichor minerality, all of which work to balance the supple texture of this wine, driving to a very long finish.

Blend: 90% Merlot, 5% Cabernet Franc, 5% Malbec

99 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2019 La Muse is a blend of 90% Merlot, 5% Cab Franc and 5% Malbec. Deep ruby-purple, it explodes with cassis, violets and aniseed, with wafts of thyme, tobacco and iron, offering new nuances with each return to the glass. The full-bodied palate is powerful and refined, with loads of rounded tannins, focused freshness and ethereal character. It's exceptionally expressive and structured and should be very long-lived in the cellar.

99 Points - James Suckling

Blueberries, blackberries and crushed stones. Pure fruit. Full-bodied with round tannins that have powdery character. Creamy and round mouth-feel. Very unique. Great finish. 90% merlot, 5% cabernet franc and 5% malbec. Best from 2026.

98 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

The 2019 La Muse offers a luxurious and layered perfume of red apple, sweet tobacco, and fresh leather. The palate is generous, with velveteen texture, notes of cassis, violets, and fresh earth, and a weightless feel. The most open of the three presented by Verite, this is an incredible wine and will be fantastic to check in on over the next two or more decades.

94 Points - Decanter

Smooth and well-defined, this Merlot-dominant wine has a nice delicacy to it. Lifted and bright, there is a sense of joy to this with excellent detail and definition to the fruit and the fine tannins. Clearly powerful with concentration but well delivered. I like the liquorice and the subtle herbal spiced edges - rosemary and cinnamon giving nuance as well as the slightly sweet but supple red and black cherry and blueberries fruit which mingle with scented dried flower notes. A refined style with a lifted finish that is really enjoyable. Ageing 16 months in French oak (95% new).

title: Sine Qua Non Syrah 'Distenta III' 2021
bodyHtml:
Sine Qua Non (Latin for 'absolutely indispensable') was founded in 1994 by Austrian emigrant Manfred Krankl and his wife Elaine. The winery quickly achieved cult status due to its bold, unique approach to winemaking, which includes giving each vintage a different, often whimsical, name and a unique bottle shape and label designed by Krankl himself. Their philosophy is to understand and react to 'Mother Nature's often oblique ways' to create wines that are ripe, flavourful, graceful, and balanced, all while striving for continuous improvement.

Wine Description

This red wine is a Syrah-dominant blend, with the final varietal composition being 81.7% to 82% Syrah, 11% to 11.3% Grenache, and the balance a mix of Mourvèdre, Petite Sirah, Petit Manseng, and Muscat. It pours an opaque ruby-purple or deep garnet-black colour. The complex aroma requires coaxing, eventually revealing notes of blackberry preserves, kirsch, red roses, black and red cherries, Turkish Delight, and violets, layered with savory undertones of bacon fat, tar, licorice, ground pepper, and espresso. The palate is full-bodied, yet exceptionally light on its feet, with incredible purity and vibrant, defined fruit flavours. The body is supported by firm, velvety, fine-grained tannins and bold freshness. Stylistically, it is noted for its statuesque energy, flawless balance, and a floral-laced, shimmery finish with epic length. The optimal drinking window is estimated to be 15 to 20 years, with the wine capable of long cellar ageing.

Accolades

  • 'Robert Parker’s Wine Advocate' – 100 points

  • 'Wine Independent' – 100 points

  • 'Jeb Dunnuck' – 99 points

Food Pairing

Given the wine’s powerful, intense, and rich profile, it is well-suited to robust, flavourful dishes. Suggested pairings include lamb, or heartier options such as mature ribeye steak (côte de bœuf maturée), Peking duck, or wild boar stew (civet de sanglier). A perfect match to enhance the wine’s complexity.

title: Chateau Cos d'Estournel 2022
bodyHtml:
Chateau Cos d'Estournel is a revered Second Growth estate located in the northern Médoc, just across the Jalle du Breuil from Pauillac. Founded in the early 19th century by Louis Gaspard d'Estournel, the estate is renowned for its exotic architecture and pioneering spirit. Today, it is owned by Michel Reybier, who has invested significantly in precision viticulture and cutting-edge winery technology to honour the château's bold identity.

Wine Description
The 2022 vintage of Chateau Cos d'Estournel is a compelling expression of Saint-Estèphe's terroir, boasting a deep garnet-purple colour. On the nose, it offers intense aromas of ripe blackberries, cassis, violets, crushed rocks, and exotic spices. The palate is full-bodied and layered, with a velvety texture and firm but polished tannins. Flavours of black cherry, cedar, cocoa, and graphite are supported by vibrant acidity and a long, powerful finish.

Accolades

  • Jeb Dunnuck - 98+ points
  • James Suckling - 98+ points
  • Decanter - 97 points
  • Vinous - 95+ points

Food Pairing
This bold yet refined Bordeaux pairs beautifully with roasted rack of lamb, beef Wellington, or aged ribeye with a red wine reduction. Earthy mushroom risotto and truffle-infused dishes also complement its savoury depth. This pairing highlights the wine’s depth and character.

title: Chateau de la Tour Clos Vougeot 'Hommage a Jean Morin' Grand Cru 2019 - Magnum
bodyHtml:
Located in a small subregion called Vougeot in the Cote de Nuits of Burgundy, Domaine Chateau de la Tour makes high-quality red Burgundy, including Hommage a Jean Morin Grand Cru. Domaine Chateau de la Tour wines are known for being complex in flavor. The estate’s most famous label, Hommage a Jean Morin, is not only known for its complexity, but also for being extremely rare, only produced in years when the quality of the fruit is particularly high.

Dark red with ruby tones, the wine's chocolatey ripeness takes on compelling floral lift and lively thyme and sage notes with time in the glass. A wonderfully silky, creamy Clos Vougeot with outstanding inner-mouth lift to its dark fruit and mineral flavors complicated by wild herbs and spices. This hugely dense wine finishes with massive but noble late-arriving tannins and explosive building length. Very few grand cru Burgundies manage such a combination of velvety texture and energy.

95+ Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate     

The Clos Vougeot Grand Cru Hommage a Jean Morin unwinds in the glass with notes of plums, smoky berry fruit, rich soil tones, spices, orange rind and cherries. Full-bodied, layered and concentrated, it's deep and textural, with prodigious reserves of fruit and rich, powdery tannin. Lively and perfumed, I can't wait to revisit it in bottle.

title: Luce Lux Vitis 2020
bodyHtml:
Produced in Italy, Luce Lux Vitis 2020 originates from the Montalcino region within the Toscana IGT appellation. The wine is crafted by Tenuta Luce, a renowned estate southwest of Montalcino founded as an ambitious project in the early 1990s by the Vittorio Frescobaldi and Robert Mondavi families, now under the full direction of the Marchesi Frescobaldi group. The winemaking philosophy focuses on capturing a unique individual style from the estate's pristine, biodiverse environment, utilizing a small three hectare parcel of Cabernet Sauvignon planted in 2004 on mixed sandy soils to deliver an exclusive, terroir driven wine.

Wine Description

This vintage presents an intense and impenetrable ruby red colour. The bouquet is stylishly refined and multi-layered, releasing prominent aromas of redcurrant, well ripened black fruit, and sweet violets, lifted by delicate undertones of cocoa powder. On the palate, the wine is full bodied yet velvet smooth on entry, supported beautifully by a refreshing acidity and elegant, enfolding tannins. The finish is remarkably long and persistent, leaving pungent impressions of roasted espresso bean and wild herbs. Composed primarily of Cabernet Sauvignon with a small amount of Sangiovese added to enhance its character, the wine was matured for 24 months in 100% new French oak barriques. It has a prolonged cellaring potential extending beyond 2038.

title: Chateau Cos d'Estournel 2019
bodyHtml:
Silky, delicate and immensely profound, this vintage embodies the quintessence of Cos d'Estournel. Multi-faceted, it delivers aromas of cinnamon and jasmine, fine mineral notes, and a touch of spice that perfectly structures the wine through its finish. A dazzling expression of the estate's terroir, exceptional and full of grace, Cos d'Estournel is an alluring wine with universal appeal that promises many wonderful years of cellaring.

Blend: 65% Cabernet Sauvignon, 35% Merlot

99 Points - James Suckling

This is so aromatic with blackcurrants, blackberries and raspberries. Pure fruit, together with coffee and nutmeg. Fresh and clean with bright spices. Full-bodied yet reserved and tight with fantastic structure. So long. This is a great Cos for the cellar. A real benchmark for the true character. 

98 Points - Decanter

Powerful and enjoyable Cos. Needs to be given time in the glass to reveal the impressively velvety texture and the sheer depth of bitter black chocolate, black truffle and coffee notes. The tannins sit back and then build slowly to full bristling impact by the close of play. Feels highly sophisticated, with the always-present Cos glamour.

96+ Points - Wine Enthusiast

The beautiful perfume of this stylish wine is the first impression. They set the scene for the wonderful black currant fruits and dark tannins that meld together on the palate. This structured wine is made with 65% Cabernet Sauvignon and shows long-term aging potential.

97+ Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2019 Cos d'Estournel has turned out brilliantly, exhibiting aromas of minty cassis, sweet wild berries and wild plums mingled with hints of spices, loamy soil and potpourri. Full-bodied, broad and enveloping, it's polished and seamless, its ample chassis of fine, velvety tannin entirely concealed in its deep core of succulent, crunchy fruit. 

96 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

Brought up in just 55% new French oak, it's a pretty, elegant, seamless Saint-Estephe with plenty of redcurrants and cassis-like fruit as well as lead pencil, graphite, and chalky minerality. Medium to full-bodied, it has supple, fine tannins, wonderful purity, and a classy, regal profile that will be loved by staunch traditionalists out there. 

96 Points - Wine Spectator

Dark and winey, featuring black currant, fig and blackberry preserve flavours with a smouldering hint of cast iron, plus notes of anise, apple wood, sweet bay leaf and warm earth. The finish offers a long sanguine thread that stitches it all up.

title: Catena Zapata Adrianna Vineyard 'River' Malbec 2019
bodyHtml:
Introduction

This red wine originates from Argentina, produced in the Mendoza region within the high-altitude Gualtallary subregion of the Uco Valley. Founded in 1902 by Italian immigrant Nicola Catena, Bodega Catena Zapata is Argentina's oldest family-owned winery and is currently managed by fourth-generation vintner Dr. Laura Catena. The winery's philosophy combines traditional winemaking with cutting-edge viticultural science, pioneered by Nicolás Catena Zapata, who was instrumental in discovering extreme high-altitude terroirs in the Andean foothills. The Adrianna Vineyard, often referred to as South America's 'Grand Cru', sits at nearly 5,000 feet above sea level and is renowned for its intense sunlight and limestone-rich soils.

Wine Description

The Catena Zapata Adrianna Vineyard 'River' Malbec 2019 displays a deep purple to red colour with vibrant violet hues. The nose is intense and nuanced, offering aromas of blackberries, plum, and sour cherry layered with floral scents of violets, lavender, and star anise, alongside hints of wet stones and sandalwood. On the palate, the wine is medium to full-bodied and exceptionally energetic, featuring a compact, lean structure with concentrated black and blue fruit flavours integrated with abundant but very fine, chalky tannins. It is characterized by its remarkable tension, mouth-watering minerality, and a long, persistent finish. This 100% Malbec typically has an ABV of 13.8% to 14% and was aged for 20 months in a combination of new and used French oak barrels and foudres. The winery is a leader in sustainable viticulture and follows the Catena Institute’s sustainability code. The optimal drinking window for this vintage is from 2024 through 2039.

Accolades

  • James Suckling - 99 points.

  • Robert Parker's Wine Advocate - 99 points.

  • Tim Atkin - 95 points.

  • Vinous - 95 points.

  • Wine Spectator - 96 points.

  • Descorchados - 96 points.

Food Pairing

The complex structure and mineral-driven profile of this high-altitude Malbec make it an exceptional partner for high-quality meats and savoury dishes. It pairs perfectly with leaner cuts of grilled red meat, such as sirloin or flank steak, as well as hearty stews and game dishes like venison. The wine's herbal and floral notes also complement dishes prepared with resinous herbs like sage or rosemary and pungent cheeses such as blue cheese or gorgonzola.

Vintage Quality

The 2019 vintage in Mendoza is regarded as exceptional, characterized by a cool and dry growing season that allowed for gradual ripening and healthy fruit.
