These conditions produced wines with great aromatic precision, healthy acidity, and a rare combination of power and elegance, reflecting the solar energy and untrammelled freshness of the high-mountain desert.

title: G d'Estournel 2022
bodyHtml:
From the heart of Bordeaux, France, the G d'Estournel hails from the Saint Estèphe appellation on the Left Bank of the Gironde estuary. This wine is produced by the esteemed Château Cos d’Estournel, known for its bold architectural flair and rich heritage dating back to the 19th century. Owned by Michel Reybier since 2000, the estate embodies a meticulous, terroir-driven approach to winemaking, crafting wines of structure and elegance.

Wine Description
This 2022 vintage presents a deep ruby hue with violet reflections. On the nose, it exudes fragrant notes of ripe blackberries, cassis, and violets, complemented by nuances of cedar, graphite, and a subtle hint of mocha. The palate is medium to full bodied with fine tannins and remarkable balance. Flavours of dark cherry, plum, and crushed stones unfold gracefully, supported by fresh acidity and a persistent mineral-laced finish.

Food Pairing
Ideal with grilled lamb chops seasoned with rosemary, roasted duck breast, or mushroom risotto with truffle oil. The wine’s structure and savoury depth make it a superb partner to umami-rich dishes. A perfect match to enhance the wine's complexity.

title: Bruno Rocca Barbaresco 'Rabaja' 2020
bodyHtml:
Bruno Rocca Barbaresco 'Rabajà' 2020 originates from Italy, within the Piedmont region and the Barbaresco DOCG subregion. Founded in 1978 when Bruno Rocca chose to estate-bottle his family's grapes, the estate relies on fruit from Rabajà—one of Barbaresco's most celebrated and historic cru vineyards, acquired by the family in 1958. Today managed alongside his children Luisa and Francesco, the winery practices sustainable and organic viticulture with minimal intervention, crafting deeply mineral-driven wines that honor the blue-grey marl and limestone soils of Rabajà.

Wine Description

This red wine displays a translucent, deep garnet hue with bright ruby reflections. The nose is lifted, complex, and intensely aromatic, opening with scents of fresh rose petals, wild raspberry, dark cherry, and blood orange, layered with nuances of crushed stone minerality, leather, tobacco, and sweet baking spice. On the palate, it exhibits a medium-to-full body with a multidimensional, seamless texture supported by fine-grained, firm tannins and energetic acidity. Stylistically, the 2020 vintage combines warm-vintage fruit richness with clarity, elegance, and precision, finishing long with lingering notes of licorice root, red fruit compote, and savory dried herbs.

  • Varietal composition: 100% Nebbiolo

  • Alcohol by volume: 14.5%

title: Chateau Leoville Las Cases 2001
bodyHtml:
Introduction

Chateau Leoville Las Cases 2001 is a prestigious red wine from France, produced in the Saint Julien appellation of the Medoc region in Bordeaux. As one of the oldest estates in the Medoc, its history dates back to 1638 when it was part of the original Leoville estate, once the largest in the region. Following the French Revolution, the estate was divided into three separate entities between 1826 and 1840, with Las Cases retaining the historic heart of the domain. The property has been managed by the same family since the late 19th century and is currently owned by Jean Hubert Delon.

Description

This 2001 vintage is a classic Bordeaux blend typically composed of 69% Cabernet Sauvignon, 19% Merlot, and 12% Cabernet Franc.

  • Colour: It displays a deep ruby to garnet hue with a touch of brick on the rim, reflecting its maturity.

  • Aroma: The nose is expressive and complex, offering aromas of cassis, blackberry preserves, and black cherries interwoven with notes of pencil shavings, cigar wrapper, star anise, and oolong tea.

  • Palate: It is medium to full bodied and concentrated, featuring flavours of kirsch, dried berries, and graphite complemented by exotic spice and floral notes.

  • Body: The wine is characterized by its exquisitely elegant structure, ripe structuring tannins, and a seamless freshness.

  • Finish: The finish is long and penetrating with impeccable poise and sophistication.

  • ABV: This wine is bottled at 13% alcohol by volume.

Accolades

  • Wine Enthusiast - 97 points

  • James Suckling - 95 points

  • Decanter - 95 points

  • Wine Spectator - 94 points

  • Robert Parker's Wine Advocate - 94 points

title: Chateau Palmer 2014
bodyHtml:
This exceptional red originates from the Margaux appellation in Bordeaux, France. The estate’s history began in 1814 when Major General Charles Palmer purchased the property, eventually tripling its size to include some of the finest terroirs in the region. Today, under the direction of Thomas Duroux, the winery is owned by the Mahler Besse and Sichel families and is renowned for its commitment to biodiversity, having fully transitioned to biodynamic farming in 2014.

Wine Description

Chateau Palmer presents a deep ruby and purple tinged colour, opening with a rich, opulent bouquet of blackcurrants, black cherries, and chocolate, layered with hints of graphite, tobacco, and pencil box. On the palate, the wine is medium to full bodied and beautifully concentrated, offering a silky, caressing texture with notes of bramble, plum, and exotic spices.

Accolades

  • "Decanter - 95 points."

  • "Wine Enthusiast - 96 points."

  • "James Suckling - 95 points."

  • "Jeb Dunnuck - 95 points."

  • "Robert Parker's Wine Advocate - 94 points."

Food Pairing

This wine pairs exquisitely with classic meat dishes such as roast venison, beef Wellington, or duck confit, as well as rich, earthy preparations like grilled mushrooms. It also complements aged cheeses such as Comte and Epoisses.

title: Mollydooker Velvet Glove Shiraz 2022
bodyHtml:
Mollydooker is a family owned and operated winery based in a charming part of the world that is McLaren Vale, South Australia. The dedicated team make a portfolio of wines that beautifully represent the warm, coastal climate of the region, but with the uniqueness that results from their trademarked winemaking techniques.

Dark in colour, deep in flavour and rich in texture; the Velvet Glove is Mollydooker's ultimate expression of Fruit Weight. Black plum, blueberries and roasted coffee intermingle with anise in its lifted fragrance. A supremely smooth mouth-feel like molten chocolate accentuates the precise balance of structure whilst liquorice and allspice linger on the palate. 

A Velvet Glove of incredible eminence and elegance that is truly the pinnacle of Mollydooker Wines.

title: Produttori del Barbaresco - Barbaresco 'Muncagota' Riserva 2019
bodyHtml:
This red wine is from the Barbaresco region of Piedmont, Italy, produced within the Muncagota subregion. Produttori del Barbaresco was founded in 1958 by local growers and a village priest to preserve the identity of Nebbiolo grapes and support the local farming community. The winery follows a philosophy of uncompromising quality, managing 100 hectares of premium vineyards to produce wines that serve as an international emblem of the region's unique terroir.

Wine Description

The 2019 Barbaresco Muncagota Riserva is a ruby red colour with garnet reflections. It features a complex and aromatic nose with notes of rose, menthol, forest floor, and leather, alongside hints of blood orange and spice. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied and structured, offering layers of raspberry, pomegranate, licorice, and mint. It is characterized by its energy, vertical feel, and firm, fine-grained tannins that lead to a long, mineral finish. This 100% Nebbiolo wine has an ABV of 14.5%. While it is approachable in its youth for those who enjoy tension, the optimal drinking window is between 2029 and 2044.

Accolades

  • Robert Parker's Wine Advocate - 95 points.

  • Wine Spectator - 95 points.

  • James Suckling - 94 points.

  • Wine Enthusiast - 94 points.

Food Pairing

The structured and vibrant profile of this wine makes it a perfect match for fresh egg pastas, such as tajarin or wild boar ravioli. It also pairs exceptionally well with roasted red meats, venison, and game birds. For cheese selections, consider aged hard cheeses or dishes featuring truffles and savory spices.

Vintage Quality

The 2019 vintage in Barbaresco is hailed as a classic and powerful year for Nebbiolo, benefiting from a long and balanced growing season. Despite a late-season hailstorm in early September, the grapes achieved full phenolic ripeness and significant pigment levels, resulting in structured wines with excellent aging potential.

title: Almaviva 2020
bodyHtml:
Almaviva 2020 originates from Chile, within the Puente Alto subregion of the renowned Maipo Valley. The estate is a prestigious joint venture established in 1996 between Baroness Philippine de Rothschild of Château Mouton Rothschild and Eduardo Guilisasti Tagle of Viña Concha y Toro. The winery's philosophy is rooted in the French 'château' concept, which emphasizes a single exceptional terroir, a dedicated winery, and a team focused on technical excellence. This fusion of Hispanic and French traditions is reflected in the name, which pays homage to Count Almaviva from Beaumarchais' 'The Marriage of Figaro'.

Wine Description

The 2020 vintage of Almaviva is a deep, intense, and vibrant ruby red. The sensory profile is complex and layered, with a generous bouquet of ripe blackberries, cassis, and wild strawberries associated with mineral hints and delicate notes of violet, vanilla, and dark chocolate. On the palate, the wine demonstrates outstanding balance, density, and structure, characterized by a voluptuous texture and refined, well-ripened tannins.

  • Varietal Composition: 68% Cabernet Sauvignon, 24% Carménère, 6% Cabernet Franc, and 2% Petit Verdot.

  • Stylistic Notes: The 2020 release marks the 25th anniversary bottling and is noted for its tension and taut texture, having been aged for 20 months in French oak barrels (73% new).

  • ABV: 14.9% to 15%.

  • Organic Status: Not specified as organic; however, the winery employs meticulous manual and optical sorting of grapes and gravity-fed processes without the use of pumps.

Food Pairing

The robust structure and dark fruit profile of Almaviva 2020 make it an excellent companion for rich, savory dishes.

  • Meats: It stands up well to grilled Wagyu, ribeye steak, and game meats.

  • Savoury & Rich: Suggested pairings include slow-braised short ribs, where the collagen and depth tame youthful tannins, or dishes featuring mushroom and truffle-based sauces.

  • Cheese: Complements aged, nutty, and firm cheeses such as 18–24 month cheddar, Comté, or aged Gouda.

  • Dessert: Pairs with 70–85% dark chocolate or a flourless dark chocolate torte, where the bittersweet profile harmonizes with the wine's cacao and cassis notes.

Vintage Quality

The 2020 vintage in Puente Alto was characterized by exceptionally dry conditions, with 75% less rain than usual between May and September. This led to an earlier harvest than normal, particularly for the Carménère, which was picked five weeks ahead of schedule to preserve freshness. Despite the heat and drought, the resulting wine is not 'green' but rather possesses more tension than previous dry years like 2017. The winemaker's skill in managing the water stress resulted in a concentrated vintage with well-polished tannins and remarkable harmony.

title: Silver Oak Alexander Valley Cabernet Sauvignon 2021 - 3 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
For 50 years, Silver Oak has produced delicious, distinctive and food-friendly Cabernet Sauvignon wines from their Napa Valley and Alexander Valley wineries.
 
Silver Oak Alexander Valley Cabernet Sauvignon has notes of red cherry, raspberry, blackberry, iris, vanilla and clove. Ruby in color, this elegant wine has great acidity and lift on the mid-palate. Black currant and warm baking spices linger with a deep and fruity finish.

title: Col d'Orcia Poggio al Vento Brunello di Montalcino Riserva 2016
bodyHtml:
Produced in Italy, within the renowned region of Tuscany and specifically the subregion of Montalcino, this wine represents one of the ultimate expressions of the territory. The historic Col d'Orcia estate, owned by the Cinzano family since the 1970s, is celebrated for its dedication to organic farming and the preservation of local biodiversity. The Poggio al Vento vineyard, planted in 1974 on the hill of Sant'Angelo at an altitude of approximately 350 metres, is considered an exceptional cru and is reserved exclusively for the production of the Riserva in outstanding vintages.

Wine Description

This wine presents an intense and brilliant ruby red colour with charming garnet reflections. On the nose, it offers a rich, complex, and elegant aromatic profile featuring notes of ripe cherry, plum, and red forest berries, embellished by nuances of dried rose, leather, sweet spices, tobacco, and a subtle mineral trace. The palate is structured, full, and deep, offering powerful yet finely chiseled and polished tannins accompanied by a bright savoury freshness.

Accolades

'98 Points - James Suckling'

'97 Points - Wine Spectator'

'97 Points - Vinous'

'96 Points - Decanter'

'96 Points - Wine Enthusiast'

'95 Points - Wine Advocate'

Food Pairing

Pairs magnificently with rich, structured traditional Tuscan dishes such as Florentine steak, braised meats, wild game, roasted red meats, and aged cheeses like Tuscan Pecorino PDO.

title: Duckhorn Three Palms Merlot 2020 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
This exceptional wine comes from the United States, specifically the renowned Napa Valley in California. Located in the Calistoga subregion, the Three Palms Vineyard is a legendary site named for its three iconic palm trees. Duckhorn Vineyards, founded in 1976 by Dan and Margaret Duckhorn, was one of the first 40 wineries in Napa Valley and a pioneer in producing luxury Merlot. Since their inaugural 1978 harvest from this vineyard, the estate has focused on a philosophy of quality and excellence, utilizing the site's lean, rocky soils to produce intense, age worthy wines with profound mineral layers. Today, winemaking is led by Renée Ary, who continues the legacy of mastering this world-renowned estate program.

Wine Description

The 2020 Three Palms Merlot is an elegant and profoundly complex red wine. It opens with alluring aromas of fresh cranberry, huckleberry, and raspberry, complemented by delicate notes of crushed rose petals and graham crackers. On the palate, it reveals mesmerizing layers of black fig and cocoa powder that mingle with lush berry flavors. Sophisticated notes of minerality emerge on the long, resonant finish.

This vintage is a blend of 98% Merlot and 2% Malbec. It was aged for 18 months in 100% French oak, with 75% being new barrels. While the wine shows immediate appeal with its juicy center and savory plum notes, it is built with broad-shouldered tannins that suggest an optimal drinking window from 2025 through 2031. This 1.5 litre magnum format is ideal for extended aging and special occasions.

🏅 Accolades

  • 'Wine Spectator - 91 points'

  • 'James Suckling - 91 points'

title: Gerard Raphet Morey Saint Denis 'Les Millandes' Premier Cru 2018
bodyHtml:
Introduction

This red wine originates from France, specifically from the Morey Saint Denis village in the Côte de Nuits subregion of Burgundy. Established in the 1920s, Domaine Gérard Raphet is a historic, family run estate that is currently led by fourth generation winemaker Gérard Raphet and his daughter, Marion. The winery's philosophy focuses on a traditional, minimal intervention approach, utilizing exceptionally old vines to create authentic expressions of terroir that prioritize finesse and purity.

Wine Description

Gérard Raphet Morey Saint Denis Premier Cru 'Les Millandes' displays a delicate ruby or garnet red colour. The nose is aromatic and surprising in its intensity, offering a complex bouquet of red and black berries, raspberry, and redcurrant layered with notes of warm baking spices, earthy forest floor, and chocolate powder. On the palate, the wine is structured and elegant, featuring flavours of dark cherry and bramble fruit balanced by a silken texture and fresh acidity. It is characterized by its fine, firm tannins and a long finish that reveals hints of smoke, minerals, and spices such as pepper and cinnamon. This 100% Pinot Noir typically features an ABV of 13% to 14% and is aged for 18 months in mostly older French oak barrels, with approximately 15% new wood used annually. While the estate follows sustainable practices and hand harvests all fruit, the wine is not certified organic. The optimal drinking window is generally from release through 8 to 15 years.

Vintage Quality

The 2022 vintage in Burgundy is regarded as a stunning year for both Pinot Noir and Chardonnay, characterized by a classical yet modern profile with excellent concentration. The growing season allowed for the development of wines with ripe tannins and a degree more richness than previous years, while still maintaining the finessed detail and pure fruit character for which the Raphet family is known.

title: Podere Sapaio di Sapaio 2022
bodyHtml:
Podere Sapaio 'Sapaio' 2021 is a red wine from Italy, produced in the Tuscany region and the Toscana I.G.T. (Indicazione Geografica Tipica) appellation. The winery was founded in 1999 by Massimo Piccin, a Venetian engineer with a deep passion for wine, in the renowned Bolgheri area. The winery's philosophy is to experiment and innovate, seeking new expressions of Bordeaux varieties in Bolgheri to produce wines that are strong, elegant, and long lasting. The wine uses the 'Sapaio' name, which refers to an ancient, forgotten Tuscan grape variety, as a sign of deep connection to the local terroir.

Wine Description

The wine has a deep ruby red colour with violet reflections. The aromatic profile is complex and seductive, with crushed redcurrants, hints of paprika, and wild strawberries, interwoven with spices, cedar wood, and tobacco. It is a full-bodied wine, showing extra volume and textural richness, while remaining incredibly focused. The varietal composition is a blend of 70% Cabernet Sauvignon, 20% Petit Verdot, and 10% Cabernet Franc. The palate is powerful and gripping, with silky tannins and a mouth-filling structure. Stylistically, it is a seamless, concentrated wine, described as showing brilliant sharpness that distinguishes this vintage. The wine is aged for 18 months in French oak barriques and 10 months in bottle. The finish is long and of balanced intensity. The ABV is 14.5%. The optimal drinking window is long-term, with potential storage noted for 2042+. The wine is organic.

Accolades

  • Wine Advocate - 97 points

  • James Suckling - 94 points

  • Falstaff - 94 points

Food Pairing

This powerful Supertuscan pairs well with rich, strong flavours. Suggested pairings include medium aged cheese, strong game dishes, and mild game dishes.

Vintage Quality

The 2021 vintage in Bolgheri was highly anticipated. The growing season produced a wine that shows extra volume and rich texture. The wine is surprisingly accessible in its youth, yet possesses huge potential for the coming decades.

title: Hess Collection Cabernet Sauvignon Mount Veeder 2022
bodyHtml:
From the United States, this wine hails from Napa Valley, California, specifically the Mount Veeder appellation. The Hess Collection estate, founded by Swiss entrepreneur Donald Hess, is celebrated for its mountain vineyards and commitment to sustainable viticulture. Today, the winery is guided by a philosophy of nurturing the land and crafting wines that express the unique terroir of Mount Veeder.

Wine Description

This Cabernet Sauvignon presents a deep, opaque ruby colour. Aromas of wild mountain raspberry, cassis, violet, and cocoa rise from the glass, accented by subtle vanilla and oak spice. On the palate, it delivers layers of black fruit, mocha, tobacco, and cedar, supported by firm yet refined tannins. The full-bodied structure is balanced by freshness and complexity, leading into a long, chocolate-tinged finish.

Food Pairing

This mountain Cabernet pairs beautifully with grilled beef, braised lamb shanks, or hard cheeses such as aged cheddar or Pecorino.

title: Domaine Harmand Geoffroy Gevrey Chambertin 'La Bossiere' Premier Cru 2020
bodyHtml:
From the storied region of Burgundy, France, Domaine Harmand Geoffroy is a small, family-run estate rooted in the village of Gevrey Chambertin. With generations of experience, the domaine focuses exclusively on Pinot Noir, crafting wines that reflect the complexity and nuance of their premier cru vineyards. 'La Bossiere' is a particularly rare monopole vineyard in the Combe de Lavaux, nestled in a cooler microclimate that promotes finesse and aromatic purity.

Wine Description
This 2020 vintage delivers a stunning expression of Pinot Noir with a medium ruby hue and glints of garnet at the rim. The nose is perfumed and vibrant, offering notes of crushed red berries, wild rose petals, earthy underbrush, and subtle spice. On the palate, it’s silky and poised, with flavours of ripe cherry, cranberry, and a whisper of smoked tea. The body is medium with finely integrated tannins and bright acidity, leading to a persistent, mineral-driven finish. The wine balances elegance and structure beautifully, offering freshness and depth in equal measure. 100% Pinot Noir. Best enjoyed from 2025 to 2035.

Accolades
Vinous – 92 points.
Burghound – 91 points.

Food Pairing
This refined Burgundy pairs exquisitely with roast duck breast, mushroom risotto, or grilled quail with thyme jus. The wine’s freshness and delicate structure also complement dishes like seared tuna or wild mushroom tart. A perfect match to enhance the wine’s complexity.

title: Piper Heidsieck Rare Brut 2013
bodyHtml:
Rare Millesime expresses the house’s signature, blending minerality with a tropical twist, in two stages. Despite its initially reserved appearance, this vintage unfurls delicious notes of pastries and spices in a saline tension that is both noble and full-bodied.

The effervescence of Rare Millesime is tinged with an intensely bright, light golden color.

The nose, at first subtle and clean, emerges in two stages combining tonicity and elegance. It all begins with the delicacy of white flowers, a hint of black tea and touches of citrus, kiwi and kumquat. On the second nose, notes of lime blossom, green tea and fern give way to aromas of white fruits such as greengage plums. Touches of chestnut honey, sweet spices, vanilla and marzipan round off the wine’s rich bouquet. The dual personality of Rare Millesime is confirmed in the mouth: smooth and vibrant, indulgent and dynamic. Its full-bodied attack reveals hints of meringue, whipped cream and marzipan. Kumquat, blood orange and kiwi then provide a refreshing tonicity.

98 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

A bright yellow hue, its aromatics are exquisite and well-balanced, with fresh notes of key lime, candied apple, fresh croissant dough, fresh pineapple, and honeysuckle. Medium to full-bodied, it fills the palate with a rounded and supple texture and a pillowy mousse. It’s long on the palate and has a silky personality as well as a long, pristine finish. It has fantastic balance of decadence and freshness, and I could drink this all day. It’s going to have a long drinking window.

95 Points - Wine Spectator

An elegant, finessed Champagne, with the creamy mousse carrying a finely meshed yet concentrated range of blackberry puree and poached apricot flavors, plus blood orange peel, salted pistachio and aromatic accents of verbena, chalk and oyster shell. Shows mouthwatering acidity that carries the complex profile on the long finish.

title: Ornellaia 2022 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
Ornellaia is a renowned wine estate located in the Bolgheri subregion of Tuscany, Italy. Owned by the Frescobaldi family, the winery was established in 1981 and has since become one of Italy's most iconic wine estates. Ornellaia is committed to crafting opulent wines with a distinct Mediterranean character that reflect the estate's unique terroir.

Wine Description

The Ornellaia 2022 is a blend of 55% Cabernet Sauvignon, 25% Merlot, 10% Cabernet Franc, and 10% Petit Verdot. The wine shows an expressive bouquet of black fruit, with notes of vanilla and tobacco. On the palate, the wine is generous and expansive, with a powerful tannic structure that leads to a savoury, enduring finish. The wine is described as full-bodied with a rich structure and balanced feel, where the abundant fruit weight gives way to elegantly integrated tannins. Some professional tasters have noted aromas of dried eucalyptus leaves, flowers, and hints of black cherries. This vintage has the potential to evolve through the early-to-mid 2050s.

Accolades

  • Vinous - 96 points

  • Decanter - 95 points

  • James Suckling - 97 points

  • Robert Parker's Wine Advocate - 97 points

  • Jeb Dunnuck - 96 points

  • Wine Spectator - 95 points

Vintage Quality

The 2022 vintage in Bolgheri was defined by a long, dry period lasting about 75 days, which presented a significant challenge to the vines. The vines experienced water stress, leading to a low-yield vintage. Fortunately, late-summer rainfall reactivated the vines, and cool night temperatures in September were perfect for the accumulation of sugar, aromas, and tannins. The winemaker's skill in adapting to these conditions is evident, as the resulting wine is once again marked by elegance and vibrancy.

Food Pairing

Suggested pairings for the Ornellaia 2022 include a prime rib or a porterhouse steak, game birds, or aged cheeses. This pairing highlights the wine's depth and character.

title: Cathiard Vineyard 'Hora' 2020
bodyHtml:
In Greek mythology, Ora or Hora is a group of goddesses representing the change of seasons. The autumn goddess displayed on the label is one of four sculptures found at Cathiard Vineyard, where Hora is produced by the estate’s dedicated team. Bearing the fruit of autumn’s harvest, Hora embodies the elegance and harmony of the vineyard which spreads through St. Helena and Rutherford. Mo

94 Points - Wine Enthusiast

This inviting, chocolaty wine is supersoft in mouthfeel at first, due to a full body and resolved tannins. But the tannins firm up on the finish to reveal a structure that can help it age well. Milk chocolate, blueberries and mint bring a lot of flavor.

93 Points - James Suckling

Perfumed aromas of tile, blackberry, bark, earth and pine needles follow through to a medium body with very fine tannins and a lovely savory finish. The balance and drinkability is really right. 60% cabernet sauvignon, 30% merlot and 10% malbec.

title: Dugat Py Gevrey Chambertin Cuvee 'Coeur de Roy' 2023
bodyHtml:
Produced in the Côte de Nuits region of Burgundy, France, this wine originates from the prestigious village of Gevrey Chambertin. Domaine Dugat Py, established in its current form in 1994, is overseen by winemaker Bernard Dugat and is renowned for its commitment to organic farming and traditional vinification. The estate's philosophy centers on the preservation of exceptionally old vines, with the fruit for this cuvee sourced from parcels planted between 1910 and 1965.

Wine Description

This 100% Pinot Noir displays an intense, dark fruit profile on the nose, complemented by a palate that is both juicy and gliding. The medium to full body is characterized by a fleshy core of fruit, including abundant forest berries and blackcurrant, alongside subtle notes of anise and licorice. It is a structured yet vibrant wine with suave tannins and a finish marked by a fresh, saline grip.

Accolades

  • Robert Parker Wine Advocate - 91 points

Food Pairing

The wine’s depth and structured tannins pair excellently with roast white meats, such as veal or poultry, as well as more robust dishes featuring red sauces or game. It also possesses the complexity to complement meaty fish or savory fried appetizers.

title: Dunn Vineyards Cabernet Sauvignon Napa Valley 2022
bodyHtml:
This robust and powerful red wine originates from the United States, specifically from the Napa Valley region in California. Founded in 1979 by Randy and Lori Dunn, Dunn Vineyards is located on Howell Mountain and has gained legendary status for producing uncompromising, long lived wines. The winery's philosophy is centred on maintaining a classic, mountain grown style that avoids the trend of high alcohol and excessive ripeness, focusing instead on structural integrity and the expression of the varied benchland and mountain terroirs within the Napa Valley.

Wine Description

The Dunn Vineyards Napa Valley Cabernet Sauvignon 2022 presents a dark ruby colour with purple reflections. The sensory profile is intense and complex, featuring an aromatic nose of crème de cassis, black cherries, and violets, layered with sophisticated notes of forest floor, cedar, and crushed rocks. On the palate, the wine is full bodied and tightly wound, showcasing a massive concentration of dark fruit balanced by a firm backbone of 'mountain style' tannins and a fresh, cooling acidity. It is characterized by its remarkable tension and structural depth, leading to a long, savory finish with hints of graphite and dried herbs. This 100% Cabernet Sauvignon typically has an ABV of 13.9%. While the vineyard practices are highly sustainable, this wine is not certified organic.

title: Gaja Pieve Santa Restituta Brunello di Montalcino 2021
bodyHtml:
This exceptional red wine comes from Italy, originating from the prestigious Brunello di Montalcino DOCG within the southwest hillsides of the Tuscany region. In 1994, the legendary Piedmontese winemaking family led by Angelo Gaja acquired the historic Pieve Santa Restituta estate, bringing their signature ethos of modern precision and classical structure to Montalcino. The winery’s philosophy focuses on crafting an intricate 'estate voice' by artfully blending fruit from their iconic southwest-facing vineyards with select parcels from the cooler, clay-rich northern zones of the appellation to capture the ultimate harmony of power and finesse.

Wine Description

The 2021 Brunello di Montalcino presents a dark, deep ruby red colour in the glass. The nose is graceful and beautifully restrained, releasing subtle aromas of red cherries, wild strawberries, and sweet violets, alongside complex undertones of crushed stones, licorice, and savory leather. On the palate, this full-bodied wine is dense, tense, and crisp, displaying a core of saturated black cherry, cassis, and wild herbs neatly balanced by a distinct graphite minerality and vibrant acidity. It strikes a gorgeous balance between natural fruit ripeness and structured power, framed by velvety, tight-edged tannins that provide an elegant, chewy frame. Composed of 100% Sangiovese, the wine was aged for 24 months in oak barriques followed by an additional six months of refinement in cement tanks before bottling. While it shows an approachable, open-knit feel early on, its noble structure indicates an optimal drinking window between 2027 and 2045.

Vintage Quality

The 2021 growing season is heralded as a triumph and a modern classic for Montalcino, defined by excellent conditions that imbued the fruit with striking structural clarity and fresh nerve. The estate's ability to blend fruit from water-retaining clay soils in the north with high-altitude sites allowed the vines to mature evenly, resulting in a successful vintage that mirrors the noble structure and long-term aging potential of the region's finest years.

title: Francois Mikulski Volnay Santenots Du Milieu 2023
bodyHtml:
The Francois Mikulski Volnay 2023 is a red wine from France, specifically the Burgundy region, within the subregion of the Côte de Beaune. The wine is a 'Premier Cru' from the 'Santenots du Milieu' vineyard, a southern part of Volnay that borders Meursault. Francois Mikulski, who inherited his first vines in 1992, established the domaine in Meursault with his wife Marie-Pierre, pursuing a vision of authenticity, purity, and elegance. The winery's philosophy is centred on practicing organic farming and sustainable soil management, treating vines as living organisms and using minimal intervention in the cellar.

Wine Description

  • Varietal Composition: This wine is made from 100 percent Pinot Noir. The fruit comes from old family-owned parcels planted in 1947 and 1976.

  • Colour: Based on typical Volnay from this producer, the wine would display a deep red or cherry to crushed raspberry robe.

  • Aroma: It is often described as having a luminous, subtle perfume, with aromas of red and black fruits, such as raspberry and cherry. Additional notes include mocha coffee, spice, and subtle floral notes like peony.

  • Palate & Body: The style is medium bodied or full bodied with a delicate and silky texture. The palate is often fresh and juicy with red fruit flavours, often centred on cherry, raspberry, and redcurrant.

  • Stylistic Notes: The 2023 is described as a wine of poise and power, built to evolve gracefully. It reveals a subtle balance between power and lightness, combining the delicacy of Volnay with a fine freshness. It has fine, mature, silky tannins, making it surprisingly soft and approachable.

  • Finish: The finish is long and elegant.

  • ABV: The Alcohol By Volume (ABV) is approximately 13.5 percent.

  • Certification: The domaine employs 'lutte raisonnée' and practices organic vineyard management, though it is not formally certified. The wine is aged for 12 to 14 months in oak barrels (35 percent new oak.)

Food Pairing

  • This structured Pinot Noir pairs well with cooked red meat and game.

  • Suggested pairings include 'veal casserole with carrots and mushrooms', 'oven baked guinea fowl with puréed potatoes and apples', or 'roast goose stuffed with dried fruits'.

  • It is also an ideal accompaniment for very good quality 'raw milk cheeses'.

title: Gerard Raphet Chambertin Clos de Beze Grand Cru 2022
bodyHtml:
Introduction

This red wine originates from France, specifically from the Chambertin Clos de Bèze Grand Cru vineyard in the village of Gevrey Chambertin within the Côte de Nuits subregion of Burgundy. Established in the 1920s, Domaine Gérard Raphet is a small, family run estate based in Morey Saint Denis that is currently led by third generation winemaker Gérard Raphet and his daughter, Marion. The winery's philosophy centres on a traditional, minimal intervention approach that utilizes exceptionally old vines, some ranging from 40 to 110 years of age, to produce soulful wines that emphasize purity and terroir over power.

Wine Description

Gérard Raphet Chambertin Clos de Bèze Grand Cru 2022 displays a delicate ruby colour in the glass. The nose is overtly spicy and aromatic, offering a complex bouquet of black cherries, wild berries, anise, and clove, accented by floral top notes and hints of tobacco and smoke. On the palate, the wine is rich and reasonably concentrated, featuring a supple and suave texture with flavours of baking spices and dark fruit balanced by fresh acidity. It is characterized by its elegant structure and fine grained tannins, leading to a long finish that can be youthfully austere. This 100% Pinot Noir typically has an ABV of 13.5% and was aged for 18 months in older French oak barrels, with only approximately 15% new oak used to preserve the vineyard's distinct characteristics. While the estate follows sustainable practices and minimizes chemical use, this wine is not certified organic. The optimal drinking window for this Grand Cru is estimated from 2034 through 2050.

Accolades

  • Burghound - 94 points.

  • Wine Searcher - 92 points.

Food Pairing

The complex aromatic profile and elegant structure of this Grand Cru make it a sophisticated match for high quality proteins and delicately spiced dishes. It pairs perfectly with roast pork, roasted chicken, or feathered game such as duck and goose. Its earthy and spicy notes also complement veal, venison, or robust vegetarian options like a wild mushroom and leek tart.

Vintage Quality

The 2022 vintage in Burgundy is regarded as excellent, characterized by a warm and dry growing season that produced healthy, concentrated fruit with exceptional aromatic clarity. While Gevrey Chambertin experienced a destructive storm and localized hail in June, the well timed rains alleviated hydric stress, allowing for a generous harvest of ripe grapes with refined tannic structures.

title: Purlieu Cabernet Sauvignon Missouri Hopper Vineyard 2018
vendor: 300747 - South By Southwest Wine Imports Inc.
bodyHtml: The 2018 vintage from the historic Beckstoffer Missouri Hopper vineyard delivered a paragon in Napa Valley finesse. Luminous purple fruit and earth aromas open into profound layers of ripe red fruits, purple plum, mocha, pink peppercorn and spice. Fresh and lithe, this wine boasts an exceptionally tender, satin texture with ultra-fine tannins and delicate oak touches that never overwhelm the aromatic fruit core. A soaring, high-toned huckleberry finish lasts for days.

title: Casa Raia Brunello di Montalcino 2009 Library Release
bodyHtml:
Casa Raia Brunello di Montalcino 2009 Library Release

Introduction

This wine is a Brunello di Montalcino DOCG from Tuscany, Italy. The estate, Casa Raia, sits on a promontory beneath the famed medieval town of Montalcino. The land once belonged to the patriarchal Biondi Santi family, and this soil saw the first roots of the Sangiovese vine over a century ago. In 2006, Frenchman Pierre Jean Monnoyer purchased the estate and began producing 'natural wines'. The winery's philosophy is encapsulated as "the vine determines the wine," reflecting a deep commitment to the uncompromising production of authentic, quality wines. Casa Raia is also one of the few vineyards in Montalcino making "natural" Brunello, being part of VinNatur and avoiding the use of industrial herbicides, pesticides, and fertilizers.

Wine Description

  • Varietal Composition: The Casa Raia Brunello di Montalcino 2009 is made entirely from $100\%$ Sangiovese Grosso, as required by law for Brunello.

  • Sensory Profile: The wine is described as a 'living wine' that is powerful, structured, and built to last. It presents an elegant and subtle character, having been made without sulphur dioxide, and is silky and judiciously oaked.

    • Aroma: The nose is complex and highly aromatic, with notes of ripe cherries, Asian spices, leather, earth, and crushed red berries. Further aeration may reveal eucalyptus, plum, dried cherry, vanilla, clove, old balsamic, and cigar.

    • Palate: It features a deep palate of fruit, spice, leather, and earth. It is full-bodied with a plump core of juicy, sweet fruit balanced by a fresh acid backbone. Tannins are substantial ("huge but beautifully ripened") but balanced.

  • Stylistic Notes: The wine is classical and harmonious, grounded on the same traditions that made Brunello one of the first DOCGs. It has been noted as a "very natural and unpolished feeling" wine that is fresh, light, and juicy, with a high drinkability factor. It is aged for 48 months in traditional 3000-litre French oak botte (large barrels).

  • Optimal Drinking Window: Although described as drinking wonderfully now due to its ripe fruit, it has the architecture to cellar mid-term, with some suggestions of a decade or more of ageing potential. It is recommended to decant for at least two hours.

Accolades

  • Wine Enthusiast - 95 points

  • CellarTracker - 93 points

Food Pairing

This bold, red Brunello wine is a "match made in heaven" with specific dishes, particularly those involving rich, red meats.

  • Suggested Pairings: Due to its structure and power, it pairs exceptionally well with Italian Brunello wine dishes. It is a good match for beef, veal, and lamb. Given the wine's depth and complexity, this pairing highlights the wine's depth and character.

title: Pessac Leognan Domaine De Chevalier 2014
bodyHtml: Domaine de Chevalier rouge has a good structure and a great deal of finesse, complexity, and ageing potential, which does not exclude a smooth, fruity quality that makes it enjoyable in its youth. Always balanced, never aggressive, power is by no means the priority. Chevalier's red wines are well-structured with round, very fine, tight-knit tannin. They are tremendously elegant and distinguished with a very long aftertaste and more delicacy than power.

title: Cheval des Andes 2021
bodyHtml:
Cheval des Andes is a prestigious red blend from Mendoza, Argentina, specifically sourced from the high-altitude subregions of Luján de Cuyo and Paraje Altamira. Founded in 1999, the winery is a celebrated joint venture between the iconic Saint-Émilion estate Château Cheval Blanc and Terrazas de los Andes, blending French 'savoir-faire' with Argentine terroir. The winemaking philosophy focuses on creating an 'Andean Grand Cru' by utilizing ungrafted old-growth Malbec vines, some planted as early as 1929, to produce wines defined by elegance, freshness, and exceptional ageing potential.

Wine Description

This vintage presents a refined sensory profile with a deep color and a complex nose featuring aromas of blueberries, fresh flowers, currant bush, and subtle hints of baking spices like nutmeg. On the palate, the wine is medium to full bodied, showing a seamless and layered mouthfeel with extremely fine, integrated tannins and a savory finish of cocoa and salted crackers. A blend of 49% Cabernet Sauvignon, 48% Malbec, and 3% Petit Verdot, it displays remarkable purity and a leafy, Bordeaux-like class. This elegant wine is built for longevity, with an optimal drinking window spanning from 2027 through 2044.

Accolades

  • James Suckling - 98 points: Complex aromas of blueberries, pie crust, fresh flowers and currant bush with hints of baking spices like nutmeg. Medium- to full-bodied with extremely fine tannins that are integrated and gorgeous. Graceful and refined, with super length. Interestingly, 20% of the wine was aged in large oak casks (2,500 liters), mostly from Slovenia. Try after 2027 but a joy to taste now.

  • Robert Parker - 97 points: The 2021 Cheval des Andes is seductive and savory on the nose, leading with pure, earth-tinged aromas of pipe tobacco, turned soil, dried herbs and rich yet composed dark fruits. Exotic, dark spice notes and a pleasantly integrated framing of new oak accents appear with further aeration. The palate is deliciously supple and impressively layered, with a harmonious, long and ever-expanding finish that highlights extreme delicacy. The tannins are persistent yet composed, gently yet persistently lengthening the finish and melding nicely with the vibrant acidity underneath—a beautiful combination of savory charm, serious depth and focused intensity. It's a blend of 49% Cabernet Sauvignon, 48% Malbec and 3% Petite Verdot that spent an average of 12-13 months in 50% barrique, 30% demi-muid and 20% foudre.

Food Pairing

The structured tannins and dark fruit profile of this blend make it an ideal companion for roasted red meats, such as a grilled flank steak or herb-crusted lamb. It also pairs beautifully with earthy dishes like wild mushroom risotto, salted mushrooms, or duck breast served with a berry reduction.

title: Silver Oak Alexander Valley Cabernet Sauvignon 2021 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
Family-owned for 50 years, Silver Oak produces Cabernets aged exclusively in American oak. Its exceptional, food-friendly wines are both drinkable upon release and worthy of cellaring for decades to come.

Silver Oak Alexander Valley Cabernet Sauvignon has notes of red cherry, raspberry, blackberry, iris, vanilla and clove. Ruby in color, this elegant wine has great acidity and lift on the mid-palate. Black currant and warm baking spices linger with a deep and fruity finish.

title: Penfolds Bin 144 Chardonnay Yattarna 2021
bodyHtml:
Introduction

Penfolds Bin 144 Chardonnay Yattarna 2021 is a prestige white wine from Australia, primarily sourced from the cool climate regions of Tasmania, Tumbarumba, and the Adelaide Hills. Launched in 1998 with the 1995 vintage, Yattarna was the result of 144 winemaking trials intended to create a white counterpart to the legendary Grange that would set a new standard for ultra fine Australian Chardonnay. The name Yattarna is drawn from local indigenous culture, meaning 'little by little, gradually', and reflects the winery's patience and commitment to a multi regional, merit based sourcing philosophy.

Wine Description

This masterful Chardonnay presents a pale straw colour with green hues. The nose is layered and evolving, offering complex aromatics of white peach, lemon curd, and nectarine, alongside savory notes of almond croissant, hazelnut, and struck match reduction. On the palate, the wine is firm and concentrated, bridgeing textural richness with a core of pink grapefruit and lime fruit balanced by a fine, filigreed line of acidity. It features a long, persistent finish defined by sustained fruit, pristine acidity, and a touch of chalkiness. The 2021 vintage is a 100% Chardonnay composition, matured for nine months in French oak barriques, of which 70% were new. It has an alcohol content of 13% ABV and an optimal drinking window from 2025 through 2046. This wine is not certified organic.

Accolades

  • Andrew Caillard MW - 100 points

  • Wine Advocate - 98 points

  • Tyson Stelzer - 98 points

  • Halliday Wine Companion - 98 points

  • James Suckling - 97 points

  • The Wine Front - 97 points

Food Pairing

The precision and structural depth of this Chardonnay make it an ideal partner for elevated seafood and poultry dishes. It pairs flawlessly with butter poached lobster with yuzu beurre blanc, seared scallops with a miso glaze, or grilled white fish. It also complements roasted chicken with hazelnut and thyme stuffing or creamy pasta dishes. For cheese pairings, it is best suited to Brie de Meaux with cumquat jam or rich triple cream cheeses.

Vintage Quality

The 2021 vintage is described as a 'unicorn year' for the region, marked by a welcome return to normal weather patterns and a cooler than average summer. These conditions allowed for extended hang time and exceptional flavour development, resulting in parcels of Chardonnay with a rare combination of intense concentration and phenolic precision.

title: Castello di Ama Chianti Classico Gran Selezione 'Bellavista' 2019
bodyHtml:
Ama is an old, fortified village situated near Radda and Gaiole in the heart of the Chianti Classico region. The Castello or Castle of Ama is surrounded by the beautiful Tuscan countryside and is near some of the original, noble families of the Chianti region. The meticulously cultivated vineyards are privy to optimal exposures and consist of fertile soils.

In the glass, pure ruby red. Pomegranate and exotic dark berries intrigue the nose with fragrant tobacco hints. The palate is succulent and juicy, with supple, silky texture and complex nuances. 

98 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The glorious Bellavista Vineyard appears under the sunlight over the slope of a hill as you approach Castello di Ama. The 2019 Chianti Classico Gran Selezione Vigneto Bellavista is only produced in the very best vintages, and annual production hovers from 5,000 to 6,000 bottles. Production was skipped in 2017, 2014, 2012 and 2010. This stunning wine reveals beautiful concentration with just the right amount of fruit weight, which feels rich but not heavy. The wine also appears compact and firm, with outstanding depth that is teased across aromas of wild berry fruit, crushed mineral, rose, tobacco and minty herb. The wine's complexity unfolds carefully with time in the glass.

97+ Points - Vinous

The 2019 Chianti Classico Gran Selezione Vigneto Bellavista soars out of the glass with breathtaking intensity in all of its dimensions. The aromatics alone are striking, but that's just the beginning. Rich and sumptuous on the palate, the 2019 is the most refined Bellavista I have ever tasted, and I have tasted them all. A healthy dollop of Malvasia Nera adds savory notes and a good deal of grip, while clean mineral nuances extend the finish. The tannins are specially polished, which they rarely are in a young Bellavista.

96 Points - James Suckling

Blackberry, brambleberry, bark and mushroom aromas follow through to a full body with deep and chewy tannins and a long finish. This is very structured.

title: Domaine Drouhin Vaudon Chablis 'Bougros' Grand Cru 2023
bodyHtml:
A delicate and ample wine, easy to appreciate. The pale yellow color is very pure, with light green reflections. On the nose, floral aromas of acacia harmonize with vegetal notes of fern and coriander. he aromas on the nose are amplified when the wine is in the mouth, together with new notes of orange or lemon marmalade. It has a soft, round, well balanced body. The aromas of fruit are enhanced by intense mineral notes evolving towards a slightly smoky flavour. Beautiful length on the aftertaste

92 Points - Vinous

The 2021 Chablis Bougros Grand Cru has a light, flinty bouquet with touches of orchard fruit and grass clippings. The palate is well balanced and perhaps lacks the weight of a top-flight Grand Cru, though there is an appealing spiciness that emerges towards the finish. A commendable Bougros that is just looking for that extra bit of spark.

title: Pio Cesare Barolo - 3 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
The Nebbiolo for this Barolo was sourced from a number of family-owned vineyards: Ornato in Serralunga d’Alba, Gustava in Grinzane Cavour, Roncaglie at La Morra, and Ravera in Barolo-Novello. The balance of the grapes comes from growers the Cesare family has worked with for years.

The fruit was fermented in stainless steel tanks (up to one month of skin contact), then the wine was transferred to French oak (the majority in 20 to 50 hectolitre casks, the remainder in smaller barriques) where it matured for three years.

Pio Cesare produces classic Barolo at a very high level. That expertise is apparent in the wine’s structure, harmony, gentle tannins, and balanced fruit. It is immediately approachable, but with very long ageing potential.

97 Points - James Suckling

Very primary fruit with beautiful aromas of peaches, strawberries, berries and flowers. It’s medium- to full-bodied, with bitter citrus, cedar, chocolate and coffee bean character. Tight at the end.

93+ Points - Jeb Dunnuck

title: Clos du Marquis 2016
bodyHtml:
Clos du Marquis is an exceptional red wine hailing from France, produced within the Saint Julien appellation of the historic Médoc region in Bordeaux. Created in 1902 by the Delon family, this dedicated estate originates from the 'Petit Clos' adjacent to Château Léoville Las Cases. Rather than acting as a traditional second wine, it is crafted from its own distinct, prestigious vineyard parcels surrounded by classified second growths.

Wine Description

This wine presents a deep, intense garnet purple color in the glass. The complex sensory profile opens with a concentrated, perfume-driven nose of small black cherries, cassis, and wild blueberries, layered with sophisticated aromas of pencil shavings, cedar, incense, and a hint of warm tar. On the palate, it is medium to full bodied and dynamic, striking an impeccable balance between power and vibrant freshness.

Accolades

  • Wine Spectator - 94 points.

  • Vinous - 94 points.

  • Decanter - 92 points.

Food Pairing

The structured body and savory complexity of this Saint Julien make it an exquisite partner for rich meat dishes. Ideal pairings include roasted rack of lamb with rosemary, prime rib eyes grilled over open flames, or braised duck breasts served with a dark berry reduction.

title: Tenuta Bocca di Lupo 'Arso' 2021
bodyHtml:
From the sun-drenched region of Puglia in Southern Italy, this wine is crafted by Tenuta Bocca di Lupo, part of the prestigious Antinori family estates. The winery is dedicated to organic viticulture in the Murge plateau, a terroir defined by limestone soils and Mediterranean breezes.

Wine Description

‘Arso’ 2021 is a 100% Cabernet Franc displaying an opaque purple hue in the glass. On the nose, it reveals intense aromas of blackberry, blueberry, and black cherry, layered with notes of forest undergrowth, rosemary, licorice, cocoa, vanilla, and white pepper. The palate is rich and full-bodied, offering plush fruit, refined tannins, and a vibrant freshness that balances its concentration. Silky and powerful, the finish is long, smooth, and lingering, showcasing both elegance and structure.

Food Pairing

This Cabernet Franc pairs wonderfully with grilled or roasted red meats, game, and herb-crusted lamb. Its herbal and spicy character also complements dishes featuring rosemary, thyme, or earthy mushrooms.

title: Chateau Phelan Segur 2022
bodyHtml:
Chateau Phelan Segur hails from France, in the prestigious Saint-Estephe appellation of Bordeaux’s Left Bank, within the Haut-Médoc region. Founded in the early 19th century by Irishman Bernard O’Phelan, this estate has become renowned for crafting wines that blend elegance with Saint-Estephe’s robust character. Now under the stewardship of Philippe Van de Vyvere, the estate is dedicated to meticulous vineyard management and a philosophy centred on expressing terroir.

Wine Description

This vintage displays a deep ruby colour with purple reflections. Aromas unfold with layers of ripe blackberries, cassis, and hints of violet, complemented by subtle notes of graphite and cedar. On the palate, it is medium to full bodied, offering a graceful structure with polished tannins and vibrant acidity. Flavours of dark plum, blackcurrant, and tobacco leaf are interwoven with touches of spice, leading to a long, savoury finish. The blend predominantly features Cabernet Sauvignon with Merlot, enhancing both depth and approachability.

Accolades

  • James Suckling - 96+ Points

  • Vinous - 95+ Points

  • Decanter - 95 Points

  • Jeb Dunnuck - 94+ Points

Food Pairing

Perfect alongside roasted lamb with rosemary, beef tenderloin, or duck confit. Aged hard cheeses, such as Comté or Manchego, also complement its layered complexity. This pairing highlights the wine’s depth and character.

title: Tignanello 2020 (by Tenuta Tignanello)
bodyHtml:
Produced in Italy, Tignanello originates from the renowned Tenuta Tignanello estate within the Chianti Classico region of Tuscany. Owned by the historic Marchesi Antinori family, whose winemaking heritage dates back to 1385, the estate is celebrated for its limestone-rich soils and innovative philosophy. Tignanello holds a significant place in viticulture history as the first Sangiovese-based wine to be aged in barriques and one of the first red wines in the region produced without white grapes.

Wine Description

This vintage displays an intense ruby red colour, leading to a complex sensory profile. The nose is expressive, featuring fresh notes of red fruit, cherries, and berries, accented by floral hints of lavender, mallow, and violets, alongside sweet aromas of white chocolate and roasted coffee. On the palate, the wine is vibrant and mouth filling with a layered texture, showcasing silky, supple tannins and a well-balanced acidity. The finish is remarkably long and persistent, echoing notes of cocoa powder, liquorice, and spicy white pepper.

Accolades

  • "James Suckling - 97 points"

  • "Vinous - 96 points"

  • "Wine Enthusiast - 96 points"

  • "Robert Parker's Wine Advocate - 95 points"

  • "Wine Spectator - 94 points"

Food Pairing

The structured and vibrant nature of this wine makes it a superb companion for rich, savory dishes such as Bistecca alla Fiorentina, wild boar ragu, or roasted lamb seasoned with rosemary and garlic. It also pairs exquisitely with earthy porcini mushroom risotto or aged cheeses like Pecorino Toscano and Parmigiano Reggiano.

title: Heitz Cellar Cabernet Sauvignon Martha's Vineyard 2017
bodyHtml:
Hidden in the shadows of the Mayacamas Mountains on the alluvial fan of western Oakville, Martha's Vineyard continues to embody the pedigree of being named the first single vineyard designated wine in Napa Valley. It showcases incredible concentration from this warm-weather vintage: Notes of ripe black fruit, dark chocolate, and sweet bay are lifted and enjoyed with the robust yet soft tannin and mouthwatering freshness.

95 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2017 Cabernet Sauvignon Martha's Vineyard boasts gentle eucalyptus and vanilla shadings accenting bolder notes of cassis and black cherries. It's medium to full-bodied and firmly structured, aristocratic even, with a streamlined shape on the palate and a long, silky-textured finish.

94 Points - Wine Spectator

Delivers lovely mint and sweet bay leaf notes mixed with iris and hibiscus accents, before giving way to a sleek, fine-grained core built on gently mulled red currant and cherry fruit, along with worn cedar, savory and sanguine notes. Keeps nice tension at the core while showcasing a flirtatious edge.

94 Points - Wine Enthusiast

This is an agile, muscular wine built on nervy acidity and braced with tannins that enliven red cherries, raspberries, smoky tea and hints of sage and cedar. Not too full in body, the wine maintains an elegant, lively texture.

title: Penfolds Chardonnay Reserve Bin 22A 2022
bodyHtml:
Australia’s most iconic producer, Penfolds, was founded in 1844 and has become synonymous with innovation and excellence in winemaking. The Reserve Bin A Chardonnay is sourced exclusively from the cool-climate vineyards of Adelaide Hills, a region celebrated for its refined, elegant Chardonnays. Since its debut in 1992, the Bin A series has set the benchmark for site-expressive Australian Chardonnay.

Wine Description
This Chardonnay shows a pale straw colour with green hues. On the nose, it opens with aromas of white nectarine, Granny Smith apple, citrus zest, cashew, nougat, and subtle flinty notes. The palate is taut and vibrant, delivering flavours of white peach, lime, poached pear, and mineral undertones, balanced by a creamy texture from malolactic fermentation and time on lees. French oak maturation contributes layers of almond meal, nougat, and roasted pistachio.

Accolades

  • Decanter – 96 points

Food Pairing
This expressive Chardonnay pairs beautifully with butter-poached lobster, roast chicken with herbs, or creamy mushroom risotto. The wine’s acidity also complements fresh oysters and delicate seafood dishes.

title: Chateau Lafite Rothschild 2020
bodyHtml:
Château Lafite Rothschild, a First Growth of the 1855 Bordeaux Classification, epitomizes the pinnacle of Pauillac winemaking. Nestled within the prestigious Médoc region, the estate has cultivated its legacy over centuries, combining tradition and innovation to craft some of the world’s most sought-after wines.

Wine Description

The 2020 vintage of Château Lafite Rothschild presents a deep ruby core with brilliant garnet highlights. Aromatically, it is captivating, offering a symphony of cassis, black cherries, and violets, layered with nuances of cedar, graphite, and delicate spice. The palate is precise and elegant, featuring a seamless texture and refined tannins. Rich flavors of dark berries, licorice, and hints of tobacco are beautifully balanced by a vibrant acidity and an extraordinary minerality. The finish is exceptionally long, showcasing the wine’s harmony and immense potential for aging.

Food Pairing

Pair this masterpiece with roasted rack of lamb, truffle-infused beef dishes, or a selection of aged cheeses like Gruyère or Manchego. Together, they create an unforgettable dining experience.

Vintage Quality

The 2020 vintage in Bordeaux was remarkable for its concentration and balance. Château Lafite Rothschild exemplifies this greatness, delivering a wine of profound depth and elegance, destined to be a legend in its lineage.

title: Vega Sicilia Unico 2011 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
Few wines have a history as distinguished as that of Vega Sicilia. Founded in the 1860’s, its reputation on its flagship vintage has for more than 100 years produced two great wines, each appropriately named "Unico."

It was at Vega Sicilia in Ribera del Duero, two hours from Madrid, that Tempranillo proved its potential for greatness. When the estate's original founder, Don Eloy Lecanda Chaves returned from France with cuttings of Bordeaux varietals, he planted them alongside the indigenous variety, then known simply as Tinto del Pais, or “Country Red”, but today known as Tinto Fino or Tempranillo. Surprisingly, it was the Tempranillo that produced the superior wine.

Today, the market for Vega Sicilia is one of scarcity and increasing demand. Vega Sicilia’s growing fame and desirability is testament not only to the estate’s enduring legacy but to the world’s craving for wines of history and noble bearing.

98 Points - James Suckling

Very ripe with plum, spice and dried-flower aromas, as well as chocolate, fresh flowers and sandalwood. Coffee and hints of meat. Sort of decadent. Full-bodied with round, creamy tannins and an intense, juicy feel. Unique cedar and walnut undertones. So delicious now, but one for the future, too.

95 Points - Wine Spectator

94 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

title: Joseph Drouhin Vosne Romanee 2023
bodyHtml:
Joseph Drouhin is a family-owned winery in Burgundy, France, founded in 1880. The estate is known for its profound respect for 'terroir' and has been practising organic viticulture since the late 1980s, followed by biodynamic viticulture in the 1990s. The fourth generation of the Drouhin family now manages the business, which includes vineyards across nearly 90 appellations. Their winemaking philosophy is based on providing "natural answers to natural problems".

Wine Description The Joseph Drouhin 'Vosne-Romanée' 2023 is a red wine made entirely from Pinot Noir grapes. It presents a beautiful, deep, and brilliant colour. The aromas are striking and diverse, with notes of wild cherry, nutmeg, camphor wood, and fine leather. Over time, a subtle aroma of truffle can also develop. On the palate, the wine is powerful and fleshy, with a sturdy body and a perfect balance between tannin and acidity. The finish is long and satisfying, characterized by a wealth of harmonious sensations.

Accolades

  • Wine Advocate - 93-94 points

  • Vinous (Neal Martin) - 93-95 points

  • John Gilman - 95 points

  • Jasper Morris - 94-97 points

  • Burghound (Allen Meadows) - 92-94 points

Food Pairing This red Burgundy is an excellent match for a variety of dishes. It pairs well with poultry, beef, game, and veal. Suggested pairings include roast duck breast, roasted veal liver, or various preparations of lamb. This pairing highlights the wine's depth and character.

title: Chateau d'Yquem 2020
bodyHtml:
Chateau d'Yquem 2020 is a prestigious sweet white wine from the Sauternes appellation in the Graves region of Bordeaux, France. As the only estate ever granted the title of Premier Cru Supérieur in the 1855 classification, it is widely considered the world's greatest sweet wine. Owned by the LVMH group since 1999, the winery maintains a legendary philosophy of excellence, often famously stated as 'yielding only one glass of wine per vine'.

Wine Description

This vintage possesses a pale lemon-gold colour. The nose is extraordinarily complex and ethereal, offering a bouquet of white peaches, nectarines, and apricots, intertwined with floral scents of honeysuckle and lilacs, plus exotic hints of pineapple and saffron. On the palate, the wine is medium to full-bodied and unctuous, yet it maintains a stunning harmony through a racy, vibrant acidity. Stylistically, it is noted for its purity and delicacy, featuring flavours of orange marmalade, candied ginger, and a subtle saline minerality that leads into a long, spicy finish. The varietal composition is 75% Sémillon and 25% Sauvignon Blanc. While delicious in its youth, it has an exceptional drinking window extending from 2023 to 2070 and beyond.

Accolades

  • Vinous – 97 points

  • Wine Spectator – 95 points

  • Decanter – 96 points

title: Chateau Lagrange 2021
bodyHtml:
Introduction

Chateau Lagrange 2021 is a prestigious red wine from the Saint Julien subregion of Bordeaux, France. This historic estate was classified as a Third Growth in the 1855 Classification and is currently owned by the Japanese liquor group Suntory. Since 1983, under the vision of uncompromised quality, the winery has undergone a spectacular restructuring of its vineyards and cellars to achieve the highest precision in its winemaking. The team, led by winemaker Matthieu Bordes, focuses on a plot by plot approach to vinification to faithfully express the diversity of its gravelly soils.

Wine Description

This wine exhibits a dark red colour with a crimson tint and lovely density. The nose is super floral and expressive, offering scents of peony, rose, and violet alongside notes of blackcurrant, red fruit, cedar, and tobacco. On the palate, the wine is medium bodied and supple with a fleshy attack, delivering flavours of wild berries, plum, and red cherry with hints of savoury slate and chocolate. It is characterized by its elegant balance, vibrant acidity, and silky but firm powdery tannins that provide a strong structure. The blend consists of 84% Cabernet Sauvignon, 14% Merlot, and 2% Petit Verdot, marking the highest percentage of Cabernet ever used at the estate. The ABV is 13% and the wine is produced following sustainable practices, including Terra Vitis and High Environmental Value level 3 certifications. The optimal drinking window is from 2025 to 2050.

Accolades

  • Wine Enthusiast - 94 points.

  • Vinous - 94 points.

  • Wine Advocate - 93 points.

  • Decanter - 93 points.

  • James Suckling - 93 points.

Food Pairing

This classic Saint Julien is best served with a variety of meat dishes such as roasted beef, lamb, veal, or duck. It is also an excellent match for braised and grilled dishes, game, hearty fish courses like salmon or tuna, and savoury mushroom based pasta. For cheese pairings, consider aged and firm varieties to complement the wine's tannic framework.

Vintage Quality

The 2021 vintage in Saint Julien is described as a 'winemaker's year' due to challenging weather conditions including frost, a cool growing cycle, and high mildew pressure. However, a risky decision to wait for a late harvest in October rewarded the estate with concentrated Cabernets of high aromatic precision and finer tannins. The resulting wines are often compared to the elegant style of the 2000s, featuring lower alcohol levels and a fresh, 'neo-retro' balance.

title: Don Melchor Cabernet Sauvignon 2020
bodyHtml:
Introduction

Don Melchor Cabernet Sauvignon is an iconic red wine from Chile, produced in the Maipo Valley. Specifically, it originates from the highly prestigious Puente Alto appellation, located at the foothills of the Andes Mountains on the north bank of the Maipo River. The history of the wine is linked to Don Melchor de Santiago Concha y Toro, who first planted Bordeaux grape varieties in the Maipo Valley in 1883. Don Melchor was first released in 1987 with the goal of creating a world-class wine that could compete in the premium category and showcase the quality of Chilean winemaking. Winemaker and CEO Enrique Tirado views the wine as an 'obsession' and a 'constant search for the best expression' of the Puente Alto terroir in each vintage.

Wine Description

The Don Melchor 2020 has a deep violet colour and is intense. It presents a great aromatic complexity of red fruits alongside floral notes of violets and roses. Reviewers also find notes of black olives, blackberries, blueberries, tobacco leaf, sweet red capsicum, ash, dried meat, and a hint of black chocolate. Additional aromatic layers include blackcurrant, sweet-tobacco, Spanish-cedar character, sappy herbs, eucalyptus, gravel, and graphite.

On the palate, it is described as a direct, tasty, and full-bodied wine. It has a soft spell of roses, superb freshness, and the characteristic elegance and power of Puente Alto. The wine is a blend of 92% Cabernet Sauvignon, 6% Cabernet Franc, 1% Merlot, and 1% Petit Verdot, and spent 15 months aging in French oak barrels (71% new and 29% second use). The texture is velvety, plush, and mouthcoating, with a firm yet composed structure. Stylistically, it balances concentrated berry and fig flavours against vibrant acidity, maintaining an elegant, well-structured profile with ultra fine tannins that build on the palate. The wine has a lush body and a very long, persistent finish. The optimal drinking window is now through 2038, with an aging potential of 35+ years.

Accolades

  • James Suckling - 97 points

  • Wine Spectator - 95 points

  • Geoffrey Moss MW - 94 points

Food Pairing

Given the wine's full-bodied and robust nature, it pairs excellently with grilled meat like steak, roast beef, or rack of lamb. It is also well-suited to full-flavoured cheeses.

Vintage Quality

The 2020 growing season in Chile was characterised by high temperatures and very dry conditions, with significantly less rainfall than the historical average for Puente Alto. The average temperature between January and April reached $19.5^{\circ}$C, which was higher than the historical $18^{\circ}$C for the ripening period. This led to an earlier harvest, which took place in March. Despite these warm, early-season conditions, the cold nights during the ripening period were crucial in preserving the intense fruit expression, freshness, and vivacity in the Cabernet Sauvignon grapes. Winemaker Enrique Tirado noted that the timely harvest of the 2020 vintage enabled the production of wines with excellent quality, very good concentration, and ripeness while maintaining freshness.

title: Gaja Pieve Santa Restituta Brunello di Montalcino 'Rennina' 2018
bodyHtml:
The story of Gaja can be traced to a singular, founding purpose--to produce original wines with a sense of place which reflect the tradition and culture of those who made it. This philosophy has inspired five generations of impeccable winemaking.

A slightly more concentrated ruby-red color than the classic Pieve Santa Restituta Brunello. Herbaceous Mediterranean notes of rosemary, thyme, and balsamic are more evident and persistent with hints of resin and spice. The palate shows complex tannins that are still reactive but well-made with savory qualities and fresh, balanced acidity making for a fresh and drinkable wine.

94 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Made with a blend of fruit from three vineyard sites with very different soil profiles, the Rennina maintains its distinct personality with elegant aromas of red fruit, forest berry, cassis, balsam herb and toasted almond. This vintage shows a hint of baked clay or black olive that underlines the warm vintage conditions. The wine is generous in terms of mouthfeel, with a nice fullness that remains graceful at the same time.

title: Chateau d'Armailhac 2020
bodyHtml:
Chateau d'Armailhac showcases all of the hallmarks of its big brother, Chateau Mouton Rothschild, which is right next door. This is seriously juicy. Succulent ripe fruits dominate the palate, with a cool and racy undertone. The wine is ripe, showing flair and full of gravitas. Aged in 50 percent new and 50 percent old oak from Mouton itself, it has a creamy, fulfilling character. This is a wine which will certainly benefit from spending a few years in the cellar. This could be a treat and might just be a bargain too.

95 Points - James Suckling

Bright aromas of currants and raspberries, oranges, and roses. Peach skin. Medium- to full-bodied with creamy and velvety tannins. So much finesse and balance. It’s savory and slightly salty. 

94 Points - Wine Spectator

Shows a core of lovely mulberry, cassis and plum reduction flavors that stretch out over a racy graphite note, in turn revealing flashes of anise, apple wood and sweet tobacco. Offers a late tug of warm earth, too. Rock-solid, with an old-school hint.

94 Points - Wilfred Wong

The 2020 Chateau d'Armailhac is fresh and active. This wine exhibits aromas and flavors of precise blackcurrants and a hint of oak. Serve it with rosemary and black peppercorn-accented grilled ribeye. 

93 Points - Decanter

A little austere on the opening beats. Carving out its place more clearly alongside its two Pauillac siblings, this has some excellent sappy dark fruits, plenty of tannins and power but also elegance and confidence. This Armailac is gorgeous, lovely mid palate dept, and plenty of juicy blueberry and bilberry fruit, with lift through the finish, 3% Petit Verdot completes the blend. 50% new oak. 

93 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2020 d'Armailhac is excellent, bursting with aromas of blackberries, violets, burning embers and licorice, followed by a medium to full-bodied, rich and fleshy palate that's broad but precise, with powdery tannins and a lively core of fruit. 

93 Points - Wine Enthusiast

Ripe and juicy fruits go along with intense background tannins, giving this wine richness as well as structure. Open and full of fruit, the wine still needs time.

91+ Points - Jeb Dunnuck

The 2020 Chateau D'Armailhac is a blockbuster that's going to reward patience. Based on 59% Cabernet Sauvignon, 30% Merlot, 8% Cabernet Franc, and the rest Petit Verdot, its inky purple hue is followed by a deep, concentrated, mouth-filling Pauillac offering classic darker currant fruits, notes of graphite and lead pencil, building tannins, and outstanding length.

title: Chateau Lafite Rothschild 2020 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
Chateau Lafite Rothschild is one of only four classified first growths and thus the designation as 1st er Cru. The vintage rankings of the Universal Paris Exposition in 1855 officially gave Lafite the rating as “Leader among fine wines.” While the first known reference to Lafite dates to 1234 with a certain Gombaud de Lafite, abbot of the Vertheuil Monastery north of Pauillac, Lafite’s mention as a medieval fief dates to the 14th century.

100 Points - James Suckling

Amazing aromas here with tobacco, crushed stone, cigar box, currants, tar, and lead pencil, as well as spices, iron, and dried ginger. Medium- to full-bodied, with a density and tightness. Very compact and complex. Racy. Delicacy with strength. Orange peel undertones. A wine to contemplate. You must understand it to understand the great Lafites of the past and those of the future.

100 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

As Lafite as Lafite gets, this ultra-classic reveals a dense ruby/plum hue as well as a tight, yet layered bouquet of ripe blackcurrants, smoked tobacco, freshly sharpened pencils, graphite, and subtle spice. Flawlessly balanced, deep, concentrated, and layered, it has an incredible mid-palate, building, perfect tannins, and a finish that leaves you salivating. Refined, elegant, and perfection are the buzz words here.

100 Points - Wine Enthusiast

Structured, dense and with great concentration, this wine is magnificent. Its black fruits and density indicate the power of the wine and its longevity. At the same time, the wine has the elegance that is always associated with this estate.

97 Points - Decanter

97 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

title: La Jota Cabernet Sauvignon Howell Mountain 2021
bodyHtml:
La Jota Cabernet Sauvignon Howell Mountain 2021 originates from the Howell Mountain American Viticultural Area (AVA) in Napa Valley, California. Established in 1898 by Frederick Hess, the La Jota Vineyard Co. is built on a legacy that began with some of the first vines planted on the mountain by pioneer W.S. Keyes in 1888. Under the guidance of winemaker Chris Carpenter, the winery practices a philosophy of maximum attention in the vineyards and minimal intervention in the cellar to express the unique mineral complexity and intense fruit of its high-elevation estate.

Wine Description

This vintage features a deep, saturated colour and offers a concentrated sensory profile characterized by its "mountain" intensity. The aroma is powerful and complex, delivering notes of black cherries, blueberries, cassis, and darker currants, accented by pine needle, scorched earth, and graphite. On the full-bodied palate, it is dense and powerful with robust, broad-shouldered tannins that possess a chocolaty texture. Flavours of black currant cordial and creme de violette meld with expressive ironstone minerality and fresh garrigue. The finish is long and gorgeously flavoured, showing a balance of freshness and polished tannins. The varietal composition for the 2021 vintage is 82% Cabernet Sauvignon, 6.5% Cabernet Franc, 5% Malbec, 4% Merlot, and 2.5% Petit Verdot. This wine has an ABV of 14.5%.

Food Pairing

The structured tannins and intense dark fruit of this mountain Cabernet make it an ideal partner for a thick, well-marbled steak, such as a New York strip or ribeye. It also pairs excellently with other rich red meats, including roasted rack of lamb with rosemary or espresso-encrusted short ribs. For vegetarian options, the wine's bold acidity and earthy undertones complement mushroom risotto, eggplant parmesan, or dishes featuring black truffles.

Vintage Quality

The 2021 vintage is regarded as superb in California, defined by a growing season that was one of the easiest in years despite very little rain. In Howell Mountain, yields were significantly lower—down approximately 30% to 35%—due to decreased sunlight exposure from heavy wildfire smoke in the previous season. However, these lower yields resulted in phenomenal character, with grapes producing wines of exceptional precision, focus, and saturated fruit density.

98 Points - Jeb Dunnuck: "Another incredibly concentrated, focused, insanely impressive wine in the lineup is the 2021 Cabernet Sauvignon Howell Mountain, which offers a powerful nose of darker currants, scorched earth, graphite, and savory herb aromas and flavors. This full-bodied, dense, concentrated, powerful, inward beauty needs 4-6 years in the cellar but will age forever."

title: Tignanello 2014 (by Tenuta Tignanello)
bodyHtml:
Produced in Italy, Tignanello is estate-grown at Tenuta Tignanello in the heart of the Chianti Classico region. The estate is owned by the Antinori family, who have been dedicated to winemaking since 1385 and were pioneers of the 'Super Tuscan' movement. This flagship wine was the first Sangiovese-based red to be aged in small oak barrels and to incorporate non-traditional international varieties, reflecting a philosophy that balances centuries of tradition with modern innovation.

Wine Description

This vintage presents an intense ruby red colour with purple highlights. The nose is captivated by aromas of red fruit, blackcurrant, and roses, intertwined with hints of leather, sweet spice, and underbrush. On the palate, the wine is ample and enveloping, featuring a vibrant acidity and supple, fine-grained tannins that respect the character of the Sangiovese grape. The body is medium yet structured, showing a savoury elegance and a finish of remarkable length and persistence.

Accolades

  • "Vinous - 96 points."

  • "Wine Enthusiast - 95 points."

  • "James Suckling - 94 points."

  • "Wine Spectator - 93 points."

  • "Robert Parker's Wine Advocate - 93 points."

Food Pairing
