The wine's vibrant acidity and structured tannins pair beautifully with rich Tuscan dishes such as wild boar ragu, roasted lamb with rosemary, or aged pecorino cheese. It also complements earthy flavours like truffle-infused pasta or grilled porcini mushrooms.

title: Chateau Cheval Blanc 2022
bodyHtml:
From France’s prestigious Bordeaux region, Chateau Cheval Blanc sits at the boundary of Saint Emilion and Pomerol, an area renowned for producing some of the world’s most elegant wines. The estate has a storied history dating back to the 1830s, and today it is co-owned by LVMH and the family of the late Belgian businessman Albert Frère. Cheval Blanc is celebrated for its pursuit of balance and expression of terroir, with vineyards planted on a rare combination of gravel and clay soils that lend remarkable complexity to its wines.

Wine Description

Chateau Cheval Blanc 2022 is a beautifully structured wine that embodies the estate’s refined style. It displays a deep, radiant ruby colour. The nose is intensely aromatic, offering layers of black cherry, cassis, and violet interwoven with hints of cedar and graphite. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied yet remarkably graceful, revealing ripe dark fruit, fine-grained tannins, and subtle notes of spice and fresh herbs. The finish is long and elegant, marked by an alluring minerality and persistent freshness.

Accolades

  • Jeb Dunnuck - 100 Points

  • James Suckling - 99+ Points

Food Pairing

Pair this wine with herb-crusted rack of lamb, roasted duck with cherries, or a wild mushroom risotto. These dishes complement the wine’s layered fruit profile and supple tannins. Together, they create an unforgettable dining experience.

title: Louis Jadot Clos de la Roche Grand Cru 2017
bodyHtml:
This prestigious red wine hails from France, specifically the Burgundy region within the Côte de Nuits subregion. Louis Jadot, established in 1859, is one of Burgundy's most iconic names, managing a vast portfolio that spans from regional bottlings to the most exclusive Grand Crus. The winery's philosophy, currently guided by winemaker Frédéric Barnier, emphasizes a classic, non-interventionist approach, often utilizing long macerations and aging in their own cooperage to capture the unique essence of each specific terroir.

Wine Description

The Louis Jadot Clos de la Roche Grand Cru 2017 displays a bright, deep red colour. The nose is spellbinding and complex, offering a refined bouquet of red raspberries, sour cherries, and rose petals, accented by notes of sandalwood, leather, and forest floor. On the palate, the wine is medium to full-bodied with a dense, silky texture and fine-grained tannins. It shows remarkable tension and linear focus, with flavours of strawberry and spice underpinned by a distinct mineral-earth character derived from the limestone soils. The finish is remarkably long and persistent. This wine is 100% Pinot Noir and has an alcohol by volume (ABV) of 13.5%. It is best enjoyed within a drinking window from 2027 through 2047.

Food Pairing

This powerful and structured Grand Cru is an ideal match for rich meat dishes such as roasted duck breast with a berry reduction or oven-baked guinea fowl. It also pairs beautifully with roasted game birds, veal in red wine sauce, or earthy dishes like pumpkin casserole and stuffed bell peppers. For a cheese course, consider medium-aged cheeses that do not overpower the wine's delicate nuances.

Vintage Quality

The 2017 vintage in Burgundy is described as a 'vigneron's vintage', providing much-needed relief with both quality and generous yields after the devastating frosts of 2016. The growing season was generally warm and dry, resulting in wines characterized by an airy transparency, bright fruit, and elegant tannins that beautifully express their individual terroir.

title: Domaine Comte Georges de Vogue Chambolle Musigny 2023
bodyHtml:
This legendary and ethereal red wine originates from the Chambolle-Musigny village in the Côte de Nuits, Burgundy. Domaine Comte Georges de Vogüé, established in 1450, is widely considered the ultimate guardian of the village's identity, owning over 70% of the fabled Musigny Grand Cru vineyard. The winery's philosophy, currently guided by winemaker Jean Lupatelli, centers on "taming the vines" through organic principles and minimal intervention to produce wines of unparalleled lace-like elegance and longevity.

Wine Description

The Domaine Comte Georges de Vogüé Chambolle-Musigny Village presents a brilliant, translucent ruby colour. The sensory profile is a "masterclass in Chambolle," featuring an aromatic nose of sweet raspberries, red cherries, and blood orange, layered with sophisticated notes of violets, rose petals, and a hint of iron-like minerality. On the palate, the wine is medium-bodied and "lacy," showcasing silky tannins and a vibrant, saline acidity. It is characterized by its "melting" texture and cool-climate energy, leading to a long, perfumed finish with hints of chalky strawberry and forest floor. This 100% Pinot Noir typically has an ABV of 13% and is aged in French oak with a very conservative use of new wood (approx. 15% for Village wines) to ensure the fruit remains the protagonist.

title: Kistler Chardonnay 'Les Noisetiers' 2023
bodyHtml:
Kistler Chardonnay "Les Noisetiers" 2023 is a highly sophisticated, benchmark white wine from the Russian River Valley in Sonoma County, California.

Founded in 1978, Kistler Vineyards is celebrated for its Burgundian approach to California fruit, relying on a proprietary heritage Chardonnay clone imported from Burgundy in the early 20th century. This specialized clone produces low yields and small berries with high natural acidity and immense flavor concentration. The "Les Noisetiers" bottling (named after the French word for hazelnuts) serves as the winery's iconic regional blend, meticulously combining fruit from prized estate vineyards—including Vine Hill, Dutton Ranch, and Trenton Roadhouse.

Wine Description

The 2023 vintage presents a beautiful pale gold color with bright green reflections. While Les Noisetiers is historically famous for its toasted hazelnut and almond signature, the 2023 vintage pivots toward an incredibly vibrant, citrus-driven, and floral-forward profile.

  • Aromas: The nose opens with lifted notes of lemon confit, tangerine oil, honeysuckle, and wet stone, with the classic nutty and buttery vanilla notes remaining more subtle and integrated in the background.

  • Palate: Full-bodied yet beautifully refined, the palate balances a juicy core of stone and tropical fruits—such as peach, apricot, pear, and pineapple—with a powerful streak of coastal acidity.

  • Finish: It concludes with an understated, resonant, and remarkably long finish marked by saline precision and a light chalky texture.

The wine is crafted from 100% Chardonnay grown in sandy Goldridge soils, which naturally impart finesse and mineral tension to the fruit. The grapes are harvested by hand in the cool of the night and whole-cluster pressed before undergoing barrel fermentation using indigenous yeasts. The wine is aged for 10 months on its fine lees in French oak cooperage and is bottled unfined and unfiltered to preserve its structural integrity. It features an ABV of 14.3%.

Food Pairing

The striking combination of rich fruit weight and high, linear acidity makes this Chardonnay incredibly food-friendly:

  • Seafood: Outstanding with rich seafood, particularly grilled lobster with tarragon butter, garlic prawns, or seared scallops.

  • Poultry: Pairs beautifully with traditional roasted chicken with lemon and thyme or an elegant stuffed chicken breast.

  • Cheese: A spectacular match for nutty, aged hard cheeses like Comté or Gruyrère, which complement the wine's subtle lees character.

Vintage Quality

The 2023 vintage in Sonoma County is being lauded by winemakers as one of the finest in recent memory for site differentiation and cool-climate precision. A long, unusually cool growing season provided an extended "hang time" for the grapes. This allowed the fruit to develop deep, concentrated flavors gradually without experiencing the sudden drops in acidity or spikes in sugar that can occur during late-summer heatwaves. The resulting 2023 Chardonnays are characterized by a spectacular balance of crystalline acidity, moderate alcohol, and elegant restraint. It is highly enjoyable now but will continue to evolve beautifully in the cellar over the next 5 to 10 years.

title: Borgogno Barolo Liste 2017
bodyHtml:
This prestigious red wine comes from the historic Borgogno winery, established in 1761 and located in the heart of Barolo, Italy. The Liste vineyard is one of the estate’s most prized crus, situated on a steep hillside with southern and southeastern exposure. The terroir here is unique; it was formed roughly 13 million years ago and is rich in calcareous marl and clay, with a "truffle forest" nearby that helps lower the microclimate's temperature by about 2°C compared to surrounding areas. This results in a Barolo of immense power, austerity, and legendary longevity.

Wine Description

The Borgogno Barolo Liste 2017 is a deep, brooding, and muscular expression of 100% Nebbiolo.

  • Appearance: Intense ruby red with characteristic garnet highlights.

  • Nose: A complex and evolving bouquet that requires time to open. It reveals aromas of iris, violet, and ripe dark fruits, layered with deep notes of leather, pipe tobacco, incense, and a hint of minty herbs.

  • Palate: Full-bodied and "tumultuous," the palate is defined by its gravitas. It features concentrated flavors of dried cherry, plum, and licorice. The tannins are solid and vibrant, leading to a long, mineral-tinged finish with persistent notes of iron and earth.

  • Technical Details: Spontaneous fermentation with indigenous yeasts in concrete tanks for 12 days, followed by an extensive submerged cap maceration of 40–60 days. The wine is aged for 4 years in large Slavonian oak casks (4500L) and refined for 6 months in the bottle. Alcohol content is 14.5% ABV.

Food Pairing

This is a wine for "important" dishes. It pairs perfectly with traditional Piedmontese main courses like braised beef (Brasato al Barolo) or oxtail pappardelle. Internationally, it is an excellent match for beef brisket, Japanese Black Cod marinated in miso, or Eastern European goulash. For a simpler pairing, it works wonderfully with aged hard cheeses or even a piece of high-quality dark chocolate for a "meditation" experience.

Vintage Quality

The 2017 vintage was notably hot and dry, leading to one of the smallest harvests in the estate's history. To counter the heat, the winery relied on the cooler microclimate of the Liste vineyard and avoided thinning the canopy to protect the grapes. The result is a wine with "sweet" yet powerful tannins and great aromatic concentration. While approachable now after decanting, it is built for a long plateau of drinkability through 2040.

title: Chateau Cantenac Brown 2020
bodyHtml:
Introduction

Cantenac Brown 2020 is a red wine from France, produced in the Bordeaux region and the Margaux appellation. Château Cantenac Brown is classified as a Third Growth in the 1855 Bordeaux Classification. The vineyard was founded over 200 years ago by a Scotsman, John Lewis Brown, and the property features a Tudor English Renaissance style in memory of his Scottish origins. The winery's philosophy is marked by the Cabernet Sauvignons of its exceptional terroirs, which instil its wines with depth and a very strong ageing potential.

Wine Description

The wine has a dark colour, often described as deep garnet-purple or intense purple with a violet hue. The aromatic profile is refined, complex, and spicy, exhaling aromas of dark cherry, plum, black fruits, and hints of flowers, spices, and graphite. Notes of chocolate, new leather, licorice, cloves, and crushed lead pencil also saturate the nose.

The varietal composition is a blend of 67% Cabernet Sauvignon and 33% Merlot. It is a medium to full bodied wine. The palate is harmonious, full, and dynamic, with sweetness and softness. Flavours include dark cherry, plum, cassis, and a savoury, earthy backend. The tannins are elegant, velvety, and sexy, yet firm and chewy, creating a balanced power. Stylistically, it is a potent, opulent Margaux with freshness and energy, possessing a measure of classicism. The wine was aged for 18 months in French oak barrels, with 60% new oak. The finish is long, persistent, and has a fine, sinewy quality. The ABV is 13% or 13.5%. The optimal drinking window is from 2026 or 2027 through 2040 to 2060. The vineyard is managed with respect for the environment, and fertilizers used are exclusively of plant origin.

Accolades

  • Antonio Galloni, Vinous - 97 points

  • James Suckling - 95 points

  • Neal Martin, Vinous - 94 points

  • Wine Advocate - 94+ points

  • Wine Spectator - 94 points

Food Pairing

Cantenac Brown is best served with all types of classic meat dishes, such as veal, pork, beef, lamb, duck, and game. It is also a perfect match with Asian dishes, hearty fish courses like tuna, mushrooms, and pasta as well as cheese.

Vintage Quality

The 2020 vintage in Bordeaux was characterized by capricious weather, including a very mild winter and a hot, dry summer, creating intense water stress. However, timely rain and careful vineyard management allowed the grapes to achieve a unique concentration and outstanding ripeness. The vintage is considered a 'winemaker's vintage,' successfully standing up to the challenge of the 2018 and 2019 vintages, with supplementary freshness.

title: Chateau Pichon Longueville Comtesse de Lalande 2015
bodyHtml:
Château Pichon Longueville Comtesse de Lalande 2015 is a Second Growth red wine from the Pauillac appellation in the Médoc region of Bordeaux, France.

The estate's history dates back to 1689 and was managed for over thirty years by May Eliane de Lencquesaing, whose leadership elevated the property's global consistency. Since 2007, the château has been owned by the Rouzaud family, owners of the Louis Roederer Champagne house. The vineyard comprises 86 hectares of Guntz gravel and clay soils, including twelve hectares situated within the Saint-Julien appellation, which contributes to the wine's unique complexity and elegance. The estate is currently certified organic and biodynamic.

Wine Description

This 2015 vintage displays an opaque purple or deep crimson colour. The sensory profile is powerful and sensuous, with a nose loaded with aromas of blackcurrant, blackberry, violets, and cassis, layered with nuances of sandalwood, cedar wood, and tobacco. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied, rich, and velvety, offering concentrated flavours of dark summer fruits, liquorice, and cedar. It is characterized by a silky texture, caressing tannins, and a long, lively finish driven by refined acidity.

The varietal composition for this vintage is 68% Cabernet Sauvignon, 29% Merlot, 2% Cabernet Franc, and 1% Petit Verdot. The wine was aged for twenty months in oak barrels, with 50% new oak used annually. It has an ABV of 13.6%.

Food Pairing

This opulent Pauillac pairs best with classic meat dishes including beef, venison, lamb, veal, and pork. It is also suitable for game, roast chicken, and roasted or braised dishes. Additionally, it can be matched with rich fish courses such as tuna, as well as mushroom-based dishes and pasta.

Vintage Quality

The 2015 vintage in Pauillac is noted for producing wines with excellent energy and cool freshness despite a growing season marked by drought. While weather conditions provided a nuanced complexity, some critics noted a sense of over-ripeness that was balanced by the characteristic Comtesse lift and poise. The harvest resulted in high-precision wines with seductive fruit and super tannin quality.

title: Catena Zapata Chardonnay Adrianna Vineyard 'White Stones' 2015
bodyHtml:
Introduction

This white wine is from Argentina, specifically from the Gualtallary sub-district of the Tupungato region in the Uco Valley, Mendoza. For over four generations, the Catena family has cultivated vines in the foothills of the Andes Mountains. The Adrianna Vineyard is one of the highest altitude sites in the region at nearly 1,500 metres, where the winemaking philosophy focuses on capturing the extreme minerality of the unique calcareous and rocky terrain.

Wine Description

The 2015 Catena Zapata Adrianna Vineyard 'White Stones' Chardonnay displays a bright lemon-yellow colour with golden highlights. The nose is complex and austere, offering subtle aromas of pears, apples, and white flowers underscored by flinty minerality, minty sagebrush, and a hint of vanilla. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied and precise, featuring a vertical structure with effervescent acidity and flavours of baked red apples, quince, and honey. It is celebrated for its salty, mouthwatering finish that lingers with notes of citrus and crushed rock. This 100% Chardonnay has an ABV of 13% and was aged for 12 to 16 months in used French oak barrels. The optimal drinking window for this vintage is from 2018 through 2025.

Accolades

  • Wine Advocate - 97 points

  • James Suckling - 95 points

  • Vinous - 93 points

  • Wine & Spirits - 94 points

Food Pairing

The intense minerality and vibrant acidity of this Chardonnay make it an ideal partner for full-flavoured fish and shellfish dishes. Suggested pairings include grilled langoustines with beurre blanc, lobster with drawn butter, or a grilled halibut steak. It also complements rich, creamy dishes such as mushroom risotto, pasta with chicken in a mushroom cream sauce, or aged cheeses like Manchego and Parmesan.

title: Francois Mikulski Meursault 2023
bodyHtml:
Meursault is great, how could it not be with this vintage to which all the superlatives apply.

Sophisticated pastry, pear and icing sugar, pink biscuit, cinnamon and Dulce de Leche, vanilla, coffee eclair and Puits d’Amour, Catalan cream then some herbs, chervil and coriander, sweet almond oil, hazelnut, cashew nut and peanut butter. Meaty palate, both a dense and supple consistency, hazelnut, Williams pear and apple, intense finish with a monster fruit that will stick to you like glue.

A finish that keeps you wanting more, an unprecedented level of persistence for a village with 25 years of professional tasting.

title: Penfolds Grange 2019
bodyHtml:
Penfolds Grange 2019 is a distinguished Australian Shiraz, embodying the winery's commitment to excellence. Established in 1844 in South Australia, Penfolds has become synonymous with quality and innovation in winemaking. Grange, their flagship wine, showcases the synergy between Shiraz and the diverse terroirs of South Australia.

Wine Description

The 2019 Grange is predominantly Shiraz (97%) with a touch of Cabernet Sauvignon (3%). In the glass, it presents a deep, dark, and vibrant hue. The nose is immediately recognizable, offering lifted aromas of dark chocolate, mocha, dark cherry, blackberry, panforte, and licorice. On the palate, it delivers a rich tapestry of flavours, including dark chocolate and blackberry fruits, complemented by fine graphite tannins and well-balanced mocha and espresso oak notes. The mid-palate is notably rich, leading to a chocolaty firm and long finish. This wine is expansive and full-bodied, with chewy, grainy tannins and balanced acidity, ensuring its longevity.

Accolades

  • Wine Enthusiast: 97 points.
  • Dave Brookes, Halliday Companion: 98 points.
  • Bob Campbell, The Real Review: 98 points.
  • Tyson Stelzer: 98 points.

Food Pairing

This robust and complex Shiraz pairs exceptionally well with hearty dishes such as grilled ribeye steak, slow-cooked lamb shanks, or aged cheddar cheese. These pairings highlight the wine's depth and character.

title: Marques de Marialva Confirmado Baga 1995
bodyHtml:
Introduction

Marquês de Marialva Confirmado Baga 1995, is a historic and limited-release red wine from the Bairrada region of Portugal. Produced by Adega de Cantanhede, this wine is part of the "Confirmado" series, which features exceptionally aged library releases that have been "confirmed" for quality before being re-released to the market.

The 1995 vintage was aged in the winery's cellars for 28 years before its release in late 2024, making it a rare "monument" to the aging potential of the Baga grape.

Wine Description

  • Appellation: Bairrada D.O.C., Portugal

  • Grape Variety: 100% Baga

  • Color: An evolved ruby color with significant brownish and garnet tones, showing its long maturity.

  • Aromatic Profile: A complex and intense bouquet featuring notes of toasted nuts, cigar smoke, roasted coffee, and cocoa. It also displays secondary characteristics of leather, tar, pine needles (caruma), and dried leaves.

  • Palate: Full-bodied and structured yet remarkably fluid. It offers flavors of stewed fruits, raspberry, and hints of black pepper and mushroom.

  • Structure: The wine maintains high acidity—a hallmark of the Baga variety—with tannins that have become rounded and silky over three decades of aging.

  • Alcohol (ABV): 13.5%

  • Service: Recommended to be served at 18°C.

The "Confirmado" Process

The name "Confirmado" refers to the winery's rigorous selection process for these library releases:

  1. Bottles are retrieved from long-term cellar storage.

  2. Each bottle is individually checked (confirmed) for suitability and quality.

  3. The original corks are replaced with new, high-quality natural corks to ensure many more years of life in the cellar.

Food Pairing

Due to its complexity and "gastronomic dryness," this wine pairs exceptionally well with rich, savory traditional dishes:

  • Meats: Roasted or stewed red meats and game (such as the traditional Bairrada suckling pig).

  • Cheese: Medium-aged or cured cheeses.

title: Chateau Ausone 2019
bodyHtml:
Chateau Ausone 2019 is a prestigious red wine from the Saint Emilion Grand Cru appellation on the Right Bank of Bordeaux, France. Perched on a limestone plateau, the estate has been managed by the Vauthier family for generations, currently under the guidance of Alain and Pauline Vauthier. The winery is celebrated for its minuscule production and a winemaking philosophy that emphasizes the incredible minerality and purity of fruit derived from its unique 7-hectare vineyard.

Wine Description

This vintage possesses a deep garnet-purple or inky colour. The sensory profile is highly aromatic, featuring a bouquet of fresh flowers, blackberries, and raspberries, alongside evocative scents of star anise, violets, and sandalwood. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied and concentrated, displaying incredibly polished tannins with a velvet-like texture and a 'killer line' of acidity. It offers multi-layered notes of cassis and subtle spice, concluding with a long, mineral finish with touches of pencil lead and white pepper. The varietal composition is a blend of 65% Cabernet Franc and 35% Merlot. While remarkably approachable in its youth, it has an optimal drinking window between 2029 and 2065.

Accolades

  • James Suckling – 100 points

  • Vinous – 99 points

  • Robert Parker Wine Advocate – 98+ points

  • Decanter – 97 points

title: Gaja Ca Marcanda 'Camarcanda' 2020
bodyHtml:
Perched atop a steep hill in the Langhe sits the small village of Barbaresco, home of the GAJA winery. The story of the GAJA Winery can be traced to a singular, founding purpose: to produce original wines with a sense of place which reflect the tradition and culture of those who made it. This philosophy has inspired five generations of impeccable winemaking.

Very expressive, this wine has a bright, purple-red color. The nose is austere yet impactful showing hints of small fruits such as blueberry and raspberry, with a hint of blood orange along with aromatic notes of licorice, Mediterranean pine, and rosemary all classic to Bolgheri. On the palate, the wine is fat and salty with silky tannins and a medium structure, ending with a long, persistent finish.

95 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Showing youthful primary fruit at this young stage, the wine delivers impressive balance and fruit versus oak integration. Angelo Gaja and his team are dedicated to the pursuit of elegance in these two grape varieties that can often deliver too much power and concentration when unchecked. Timing the harvest correctly and the careful use of French oak is key to these overall results, especially with regard to the medium to full-bodied mouthfeel and the long silkiness of this age-worthy vintage.

95 Points - Wine Spectator

The aromas in this red are a bit muted today, yet the black currant, blueberry, violet, cedar and wild herb flavors are expressive and well-delineated. Gains support from lively acidity and a dense matrix of tannins as this finishes long and palate-staining. 

95 Points - James Suckling

Currants, rose petals and ink with some fresh herbs as well. Medium-bodied with fine and tensioned tannins that give focus and beauty to the wine. This will come together beautifully. A blend of cabernet sauvignon and cabernet franc.

title: Castiglion Del Bosco Brunello Di Montalcino 2010
bodyHtml:
Complexity, superb structure, and an inviting, mouthfilling palate are the hallmarks of this Sangiovese. A garnet-flecked ruby red, it releases generous, emphatic fragrances classic to Sangiovese, developing a nearly endless progression notable for its beautiful balance. Excellent with stews, roasted meats and cheese.

96 Points - James Suckling

Fabulous aromas of oranges, peaches and mahogany follow through to a full body, with rich and chewy tannins and a long and flavorful finish. This is dense and tight and powerful. It is compressed and incredibly structured. Needs four to five years of bottle age to come out of it domancy.

94 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2010 Brunello di Montalcino is a ripe and fruit-forward expression that bursts with energy and red fruit intensity even at this young stage in the wine's life. Thick layers of cherry, blackberry, cassis, vanilla and cinnamon give the wine a bold, opulent personality. The tannins are super tame and docile, even for this more structured vintage. The wine boasts a medium build with bright garnet and ruby highlights. I think Castiglion del Bosco does a great job of executing and delivering this softer style of Brunello that works so well as a companion to the hearty, wintery foods we love most. You can drink it in the near or long term. It has that level of aging flexibility. The 2010 vintage is a great one to taste and buy.

94 Points - Wine Spectator

Complex and elegant, with cherry, licorice, leather and incense flavors. The firm grip of tannins quickly takes over, but this is long, echoing leather and spice. Best from 2019 through 2035. 2,100 cases imported.

title: Le Petit Mouton 2016
bodyHtml:
95+ Points - James Suckling

This is a very powerful Petit Mouton with so much rich fruit and power. Full-bodied, tannic yet polished and long. Muscular for the second wine of Mouton.

94 Points - Decanter

Petit Mouton always shows charm in a rich, seductive expression, even in muscular vintages like 2016. It has the most wonderful sweetness to it, a highly seductive mix of the austerity of 2016 with the natural joy and exuberance of Petit Mouton, showing lovely rich damson fruit and huge persistence. It need time in the glass to open up.

91+ Points - Wine Enthusiast

This wine has structure and a generous fruity character from the ripeness of the Merlot in the blend. It is full in the mouth, with a smoky character on the palate and acidity coming through on the close.

93 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2016 Le Petit Mouton is a blend of 62% Cabernet Sauvignon, 35% Merlot and 3% Cabernet Franc. It has a deep garnet-purple color and gives up an intensely plummy nose with cigar box and fallen leaves scents leading to aroma layers of kirsch, red and black currants and tilled soil. Medium-bodied with a racy line of freshness cutting through the muscular fruit and a good, firm frame of grainy tannins to support, it finishes on a lingering menthol note.

92 Points - Wine Spectator

The gently steeped plum and red currant fruit allows light anise, iron and cedar notes to enter slowly before taking hold on the slightly taut, savory-tinged finish. The iron element lingers longest in the end, giving this a sense of refinement. Best from 2022 through 2035.

title: Chateau Rauzan Segla 2022
bodyHtml:
Château Rauzan Segla, located in the prestigious Margaux appellation of Bordeaux, has been crafting exceptional wines since its founding in the 17th century. Under the ownership of the Chanel Group since 1994, the estate has undergone significant renovations, blending tradition with innovation to elevate its status among the finest Second Growths of the Médoc. The château's commitment to meticulous vineyard management and precision winemaking highlights the remarkable terroir of Margaux.

Wine Description
The 2022 vintage of Château Rauzan Segla presents a deep, garnet hue with purple reflections. Aromas are expressive and layered, offering notes of ripe blackberries, cassis, violets, and subtle hints of cedar and graphite. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied and concentrated, delivering a rich core of dark fruits complemented by refined tannins and vibrant acidity. The mouthfeel is polished and harmonious, leading to a persistent finish accented by nuances of spice and mineral tones. Composed primarily of Cabernet Sauvignon, with Merlot and small amounts of Petit Verdot and Cabernet Franc, this vintage showcases remarkable balance and ageing potential, with an optimal drinking window beginning around 2028 and extending for decades.

Accolades
"Wine Advocate - 95–97 points."
"Vinous - 95–97 points."
"James Suckling - 97–98 points."

Food Pairing
This Margaux pairs beautifully with herb-crusted lamb, roasted duck breast, or aged cheeses such as Comté. This pairing highlights the wine’s depth and character.

Vintage Quality
The 2022 vintage in Bordeaux was marked by a hot, dry growing season, which resulted in concentrated fruit and remarkable ripeness. Despite climatic challenges, the team at Rauzan Segla expertly managed water stress and maintained balance, producing a wine of power and finesse that stands as a testament to their skill.

title: Domaine Thierry & Pascale Matrot Meursault 'Perrieres' Premier Cru 2020
bodyHtml:
The greatest of all their Meursault wines. It has a mineral and crystalline initial bouquet. The terroir is omnipresent. Both fine and elegant, its powerful salinity awakens the taste buds. It is a vibrant, sapid, and exceptional wine, especially when opened after a few years.

91+ Points -  Vinous

The 2020 Meursault Les Perrieres 1er Cru has a delineated bouquet, demonstrating fine mineralite and tension, the oak here well integrated (no new barrels used here.) The palate is medium-bodied with fine grip and density, a satisfying bead of acidity, but my only quibble is that it does not quite deliver the stoniness, the mineralité of a great Perrieres on the finish. Still, there is impressive length and it should still age well in bottle.

title: Catena Zapata Malbec 'Argentino' 2023
bodyHtml:
This deep violet-hued Malbec presents an intense bouquet of ripe blackberry, dark cherry, and floral violet notes, complemented by hints of cocoa, graphite, and vanilla from oak aging. The palate is full-bodied yet remarkably refined, with layered flavors of plum, cassis, and baking spices unfolding over a velvety texture. Balanced acidity and finely integrated tannins lead to a long, elegant finish. This vintage captures the signature power and finesse of Argentina’s high-altitude Malbec.

Food Pairing

This structured Malbec pairs beautifully with grilled ribeye, lamb chops, or roasted wild mushrooms. Aged cheeses, such as Manchego or aged Gouda, also complement its rich depth.

title: Fratelli Barolo Monvigliero 2020 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
Wine Description

The Fratelli Barolo Monvigliero 2020 is made from 100% Nebbiolo grapes. It has a brilliant ruby-garnet colour. The wine presents an expressive bouquet of rose petals, red cherry, wild herbs, anise, and white pepper, with additional notes of red berry, spice, leather, and liquorice. On the palate, it is vibrant and layered, with a silky texture and a balance of flavours like raspberry, pomegranate, tobacco, and earthy minerality. This medium to full-bodied wine has a long, ethereal finish. The wine is also noted for being organic and for its finesse, complexity, and elegance. It is best enjoyed between 2026 and 2042.

Accolades

  • James Suckling - 99 points

  • Wine Enthusiast - 97 points

  • Wine Advocate - 95 points

  • Wine Spectator - 95 points

  • Decanter - 95 points

  • Vinous - 94 points

Food Pairing
This elegant Barolo pairs well with rich, hearty dishes. Suggested pairings include truffle risotto, wild mushroom tagliatelle, and braised veal shanks. Its acidity and supple tannins also complement aged cheeses like Parmigiano Reggiano. A perfect match to enhance the wine's complexity.

Vintage Quality
The 2020 vintage for Barolo is considered to be a successful one. The year was warm but not extreme, resulting in wines with a "supple, silky" texture, lifted aromatics, and delicate red fruit notes.

title: Biondi Santi Brunello di Montalcino Riserva 2015
bodyHtml:
It is a rare phenomenon that a wine can trace its origins to a single man. Brunello di Montalcino, however, owes its existence to Ferrucio Biondi-Santi and its fame to his family. Now on the seventh generation of winemakers, the Biondi-Santi family continues to produce wines renowned for their elegance and extraordinary longevity.

98+ Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Contemplative and exceedingly nuanced in personality, with wild berry, underbrush, ferrous earth and candied orange peel, this has everything to look forward to in terms of its future evolution in the bottle. It displays a pretty ruby color that borders on garnet and polished copper. A silky, mid-weight palate is accented by beautifully managed and silky tannins (this aspect of the mouthfeel is extraordinary), bright freshness and long-lasting fruit momentum. 

97 Points - James Suckling

Complex yet pure, subtle and refined nose that gently evolves, with mossy red cherries, dried roses, chalk, tar and dried orange peel. There is a lift of clove and eucalyptus that makes it so distinctive. A powerful, medium-to full-bodied Brunello, but seamless and bright, with a fine, transparent mid-palate and restrained, mineral austerity. Understated complexity that will need time to bloom.

97 Points - Vinous

The 2015 Brunello di Montalcino Riserva pulls you close to the glass with a deep and seductive display of black raspberry preserves complemented by sweet sage, dried roses and pipe tobacco. With further coaxing, it gains in volume and lift, taking on hints of mint and camphor. This greets the palate with undeniable elegance, casting velvety waves of violet-tinged wild berries and sweet spices across a motivating core of juicy acidity, as a subtle coating of round tannins forms toward the close. While structured and incredibly long, energy remains high, as nuances of cherry pits offset by sour citrus and hints of cedar fade.

title: Caprili 'AdAlberto' Brunello di Montalcino Riserva 2018
bodyHtml:
A sleek red, with juniper, sage, eucalyptus, iron and earth aromas and flavors highlighted by cherry and strawberry. Packs a vibrant, firm structure that keeps this delineated on the long, detailed finish.

96 Points - James Suckling

Restrained red cherry fruit with some vibrancy, enhanced by smoke, woodland, licorice, balsamic and cedar aromas. The palate is highlighted by a full body and firm, chalky tannins. It’s fierce yet ripe, integrated and lifted, with high acidity and a balanced finish. Youthful style, still rugged yet good. 

94 Points - Vinous

The 2018 Brunello di Montalcino Riserva Adalberto is a seductress, tempting the imagination with an array of exotic spices and sweet florals before grounding the experience with notes of blackberry and sage. This is like pure silk on the palate. Fresh acidity adds energy, and crisp wild berry fruits swirl throughout. Balsamic spice notes form toward the close as the 2018 finishes with crunchy tannins, all while maintaining a lovely, energetic feel. Beautifully done.

93 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The Caprili 2018 Brunello di Montalcino Riserva AdAlberto shows hints of licorice and balsam herb that give this wine an evolved personality. To the palate, this exhibits medium-body weight with tannins that are silky and resolved for the most part.

title: Chateau Lafite Rothschild 2009
bodyHtml:
Chateau Lafite Rothschild is one of only four classified first growths and thus the designation as 1st er Cru. The vintage rankings of the Universal Paris Exposition in 1855 officially gave Lafite the rating as “Leader among fine wines.”

The estate achieved wide popularity in the 1750s when it became the favorite wine of King Louis XV. Thomas Jefferson was also a steadfast customer and even visited the estate. After the 1973-1976 mini-crisis that hit Bordeaux, Baron Eric’s management of the estate made strides forward with a search for excellence and the gradual addition of a new technical team. In 1985 Baron Eric began a tradition of inviting fine-arts photographers to photograph Chateau Lafite. Today, his daughter Saskia de Rothschild represents the 6th generation of the family at the head of the winemaking properties. 

A deep bouquet of dark fruit and licorice. The palate is full-bodied and already expressive, but then becomes tighter, expressing power and exuberance. The youth of this Lafite does not hide its energy, but the distinctive elegance and complexity are already there.

100 Points - James Suckling

This is what the Medoc is all about. The freshness and delicacy of this wine in combination with its serious concentration and firm core are totally stunning. Time has already worked its magic and this is already delicious, but has decades in front of it. Drink or hold.

98 Points - Wine Spectator

This is stunning for its ability to take massively endowed fig, currant paste and crushed plum fruit flavors and harness them with ultrasuave freshly roasted espresso, black tea and ganache notes. A seductive style, long and velvety, with the dense core of black fruit and smoldering iron just waiting and waiting. Best from 2020 through 2040.

98 Points - Decanter

It displays, as Lafite always does, more of a laid back elegance than Latour, and the difference between the two once again highlights the huge differences in terroir between north and south Pauillac, with the deep gravels here giving finesse, composure, almost nonchalance. It tames with a whisper, bringing you to submission by gently, purposefully and ever so slowly layering one thing on top of another. It has gorgeously pure and precise fruit on the nose, while the palate displays a multitude of flavours, from charcoal to cassis to crushed stone, and yet no one thing dominates. There are a ton of tannins, but they are individually fine, and it's only in retrospect that you realise how many of them there are. The tone of Lafite is speaking over the vintage, and it's going to run and run.

97 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The deep garnet colored 2009 Lafite Rothschild bursts from the glass with red and black currant preserves, warm plums, mulberries and kirsch scents plus suggestions of sweaty leather, cigar box and menthol. Medium-bodied, elegant and firmly structured, it has wonderful freshness and a long earthy/meaty finish.

title: Chateau Cos d'Estournel 2020
bodyHtml:
Château Cos d'Estournel's 2020 vintage is a distinguished expression from the esteemed Saint-Estèphe appellation in Bordeaux, France. As a Second Growth estate classified in 1855, Cos d'Estournel is renowned for producing wines of exceptional quality and longevity.

Blend and Winemaking

The 2020 vintage is composed of 62% Cabernet Sauvignon and 38% Merlot. The harvest took place from September 10 to 24, yielding grapes of optimal ripeness. The wine was aged in French oak barrels, with 55% being new oak, contributing to its complexity and aging potential.

Tasting Notes

  • Appearance: Deep garnet-purple hue.

  • Nose: Initially reserved, it gradually reveals vibrant aromas of crushed blackcurrants, juicy blackberries, and kirsch, accompanied by hints of cinnamon stick, star anise, lilacs, and crushed rocks.

  • Palate: Medium-bodied with energetic black fruit and mineral layers, supported by fine-grained, ripe tannins and seamless freshness, culminating in a long, fragrant finish.

Serving and Cellaring

This wine is approachable in its youth after decanting but will benefit from extended cellaring. It is best enjoyed at a temperature of 16–18°C (60–64°F). Pair it with rich dishes such as roasted lamb, game meats, or aged cheeses to complement its depth and complexity.

Conclusion

The 2020 Château Cos d'Estournel exemplifies the estate's commitment to crafting wines of elegance, power, and longevity. Its harmonious balance of fruit, structure, and freshness ensures it will be a centerpiece in any collection and a delight for connoisseurs seeking the pinnacle of Saint-Estèphe excellence.

title: Chateau Calon Segur 2005 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
Introduction

The Château Calon Ségur 2005 is a legendary Third Growth (3ème Cru Classé) red wine from the Saint-Estèphe appellation in Bordeaux. This vintage is widely celebrated as one of the modern-day "triumphs" of the estate, emerging from a near-perfect growing season in the Médoc. The 1.5 Litre (Magnum) format is especially prized for this specific wine; because Calon Ségur 2005 is known for its formidable tannic structure and "backstrapping" traditional style, the larger bottle ensures a slower maturation, preserving the fruit's freshness while allowing the tannins to soften more gracefully over decades.

Wine Description

The 2005 Calon Ségur is a powerful, uncompromising Bordeaux that reflects the estate’s historic reputation for producing "masculine" and structured wines.

  • Varietal Composition: A blend of 60% Cabernet Sauvignon and 40% Merlot. (Some sources note small amounts of Cabernet Franc and Petit Verdot are also in the vineyard mix).

  • Aromatic Profile: The nose is complex and noble, featuring intense aromas of black cherry, crème de cassis, and plum. These are layered with sophisticated secondary notes of damp earth, wood smoke, cedar, and exotic Asian spices. Critics also note a subtle "ferrous" or mineral edge and hints of chocolate.

  • Palate and Body: This is a full-bodied and "broodingly tannic" wine. It possesses a dense, concentrated texture with layers of ripe black fruit. Despite its power, the 2005 vintage has put on significant weight with age, resulting in a textured, velvety mouthfeel that balances the high tannin levels.

  • Structure: Defined by its incredible density and "aristocratic poise." The tannins are firm but fine-grained, supported by fresh acidity that suggests a massive aging potential.

  • Winemaking: The Merlot was harvested in late September, followed by the Cabernet in early October. The wine was aged in 100% new French oak, providing a structural framework that is now beautifully integrated.

  • ABV: 13% to 13.5%.

Accolades

The 2005 vintage is one of the highest-scoring releases for Calon Ségur in the last 20 years:

  • Jane Anson (Inside Bordeaux): 96 points

  • Robert Parker's Wine Advocate: 94–96 points

  • James Suckling: 94 points

  • Decanter: 93 points (18.5/20)

  • Wine Spectator: 93 points

  • Vinous (Neal Martin): 94 points

title: Joseph Drouhin Vaudon Chablis 'Les Clos' Grand Cru 2022
bodyHtml:
Throughout the ageing process, decisions are taken only after careful tasting evaluation. The data obtained is completed through technical analysis. As with every other Joseph Drouhin wine, absolute priority is given to the true expression of terroir and character of the vintage.

A great wine, perhaps the one most able to express what the terroir of Chablis really is like. The colour is pale gold yellow, with greenish hints. Refined nose, with aromas of lily, honey or preserved lemon. Astounding depth and velvety sensation on the palate, with some delicate marine nuances. Intense and long aftertaste. After 5 or 6 years, even more complex and subtle aromas develop in the wine.

title: Chateau Quintus 2016
bodyHtml:
Introduction

Château Quintus 2016 is a red wine from France, produced in the Bordeaux region and the Saint-Émilion Grand Cru Classé appellation. The estate is owned by Domaine Clarence Dillon, the family behind the First Growth Château Haut-Brion. The 2016 vintage is particularly significant as it marked the sixth vintage under the Haut-Brion team's umbrella, solidifying its reputation for achieving great depth and focus. Critics widely regard the 2016 as a major success, showing depth never before achieved by the estate at the time.

Wine Description

The wine has a quite deep garnet-red or deep garnet-purple colour. The aromatic profile is complex and layered, with a quiet intensity of ripe dark fruits like plum preserves, blueberry pie, and mulberries. These are beautifully integrated with notes of tar, star anise, chocolate-covered cherries, dried lavender, and potpourri.

  • Varietal Composition: 70% Merlot and 30% Cabernet Franc. This was the highest proportion of Cabernet Franc since the debut 2011 vintage, lending impressive backbone.

  • Body and Palate: Medium to full-bodied, with a silky, caressing attack. The palate is plush, generous, and expressive, framed by beautifully ripe, soft tannins and a lively, fresh backbone.

  • Structure: The mid-palate is fleshy and tight, showing a concentrated, mineral, and almost graphite-like core. The elegance and freshness prevent the generous 15% alcohol from overwhelming the wine.

  • Aging: Aged in French oak barrels (approximately 35% new oak).

  • ABV: 15%.

  • Optimal Drinking Window: Long-term aging potential, typically from 2023–2027 through 2040–2050.

Accolades

The 2016 vintage is considered one of the estate's finest releases to date.

  • James Suckling - 97 points

  • Jeb Dunnuck - 95 points

  • Robert Parker's Wine Advocate - 94 points

  • Decanter (Jane Anson) - 94 points

Food Pairing

This powerful and balanced Saint-Émilion pairs wonderfully with all classic meat dishes. Suggested pairings include:

  • Beef, duck, and lamb.

  • Roasted, braised, and grilled dishes.

Vintage Quality

The 2016 vintage in Saint-Émilion was highly successful. A summer drought was broken by beneficial rains in mid-September, allowing for an optimal end to the maturity cycle. The combination of warm days and cool nights in October resulted in wines rich in colour, structure, and intense fruit, while retaining excellent freshness.

title: Kosta Browne Pinot Noir 'Bootlegger's Hill' 2017
bodyHtml:
96 Points - James Suckling

This is a cooler and later-ripening site planted to various clones. Dried flowers and forest wood aromas with leafy and sappy notes lead to a palate with ripeness and lighter fruit flavours. Nicely detailed and very silky tannins and latent, rich blue-fruit flavours. 

94 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

The 2017 Pinot Noir Bootlegger's Hill Vineyard reveals a medium ruby/translucent colour and a complex bouquet of redcurrants, leafy herbs, damp earth, iodine, and spice. Medium to full-bodied, with an elegant texture, lots of classic Russian River spice, and outstanding length.

91+ Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Pale to medium ruby, it gives up friendly aromas of strawberry and raspberry jam, tangerine, tree bark and mushroom, plus nuances of peppercorn, charcuterie and aniseed. Medium-bodied, it's earth-driven in the mouth with a sturdy framing of ripe tannins and just enough freshness on the long finish.

91 Points - Wine Spectator

Crushed mineral notes flank the zesty raspberry and red fruit flavours. The juicy finish features lively acidity and light, spicy accents.

title: Orin Swift Mercury Head Cabernet Sauvignon 2022
bodyHtml:
Orin Swift Mercury Head 2022 originates from the United States, within California’s premier Napa Valley AVA. Created by winemaking visionary Dave Phinney, Orin Swift is famous for crafting bold, full-throated wines wrapped in iconic packaging—most notably the Mercury Head, which features an authentic Liberty Head "Mercury" silver dime embedded directly into the glass of each bottle. Sourced from exceptional vineyard blocks across Napa Valley, including top benchland and hillside sites in Rutherford, Oakville, and St. Helena, the wine is built on a philosophy of uncompromising extraction, seamless oak integration, and opulent fruit depth. The 2022 release continues this tradition, delivering a dense, iconic Napa Valley Cabernet Sauvignon of immense power and concentration.

Wine Description

This red wine displays an opaque, deep dark ruby-purple appearance in the glass with an inky core and vibrant violet highlights at the rim. It possesses a full-bodied, rich, and mouth-filling structure defined by a plush, velvety texture and immense structural weight. The sensory profile is explosive, aromatic, and decadent, opening with an intense bouquet of crème de cassis, ripe black cherries, wild blackberries, and dark plum preserves, seamlessly layered with rich secondary notes of dark chocolate, espresso, cigar box, toasted vanilla bean, sweet cedar, and a hint of graphite. On the palate, it delivers a massive core of dark berry fruit held together by ripe, fine-grained tannins and a subtle thread of natural acidity that maintains balance. The finish is exceptionally long, warm, and persistent, leaving lingering echoes of dark cocoa, toasted oak spice, and sweet dark fruit.

  • Varietal Composition: 100% Cabernet Sauvignon.

  • Stylistic Notes: The grapes are hand-harvested from select micro-lots across Napa Valley and sorted with extreme precision. Fermentation takes place in stainless steel vats with extended cap management to maximize color and tannic extraction. The wine undergoes aging for approximately 15 to 18 months in French oak barrels (with a high proportion of new French oak), adding signature notes of vanilla, toasted wood, and sweet spice without masking the dark fruit purity.

  • ABV: 15.5%.

  • Organic Status: While Orin Swift partners with growers practicing sustainable viticulture and precision water management across Napa Valley, this bottling is not certified organic.

Food Pairing

The immense structural weight, plush fruit intensity, and rich oak profile of Mercury Head make it a decadent companion to bold, savory gastronomy.

  • Fine Meats: Pairs magnificently with grilled prime ribeye steaks, dry-aged New York strip, slow-braised beef short ribs, or tenderloin of beef served with a rich espresso or dark chocolate jus.

  • Game & Rich Poultry: Ideal alongside pan-roasted duck breast with blackberry reduction, venison tenderloin, or braised lamb shanks with rosemary.

  • Earthy Specialties: Complements dishes featuring braised wild mushrooms, truffle-infused pastas, and roasted root vegetables.

  • Cheeses: Matches gracefully with strong, aged cheeses such as sharp cheddar, smoked Gouda, 24-month Comté, or Gorgonzola Piccante.

title: Billecart Salmon 'Elisabeth Salmon' Brut Rose 2012
bodyHtml:
A luminous appearance with soft, coppery shimmers and a sustained salmon pink hue. A highly alluring ensemble with a lustrous, elegant sparkle. A refreshing yet sultry sensory experience of citrus peel and red and black berry jelly, with the exquisite sensation of a rich and complex aromatic range (blackcurrants, blackberries and blueberries). Gorgeously refined and mature olfactory notes bring out the inimitable fragrances of sweet spices and candied violets.

A distinctive mouthfeel arising from a measured strength which is simultaneously delicate and charming, with flavors developing in perfect harmony (panettone, candied clementines and ginger). A delicate character in the mouth revealing a chalky edge and persistent finish of citron zest.

This highly sophisticated wine presents its personality with wonderful delicacy of texture and flavor. An aromatic charm with an unusual mineral quality: pair with poached lobster, tartare of sakura leaf, tomato and rhubarb.

96 Points - Vinous

title: Chateau Mouton Rothschild 2011 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
2011 was one of the hottest, sunniest and driest of the last forty years. Hot weather in April and May gave the vegetation cycle a head start: flowering was recorded on 15 May, the earliest date in living memory, and veraison started two-and-half weeks earlier than usual. Conditions in July and August were very different, bringing less sunshine and significantly more precipitation. However, by the end of August, only 326 mm of rainfall had been recorded since 1 January, compared with an average of 519 mm. Fine weather returned to the Médoc in early September, and bright sunshine prevailed throughout the two weeks of the harvest, which began on 12 September. These auspicious conditions were highly beneficial, allowing the grapes to ripen fully. Picking ended on 28 September. Low yields have produced structured, deep, fresh wines, especially at Mouton. 2011 is thus a classic Bordeaux vintage, to be ranked among the finer or perhaps even the finest.

96 Points - James Suckling 

This shows lots of opulent aromas of ripe fruit, lightly toasted oak, walnut and dried meat. It's full-bodied, with chewy tannins and plenty of fruit. A muscular, solid wine.

95 Points - Wine Spectator

This delivers a gorgeously pure beam of cassis and cherry compote, with roasted apple wood, graphite and iron notes hanging in the background for now. Long and polished through the finish, showing profound depth in reserve.

95 Points - Wine Enthusiast

There is a lightness about this vintage of Mouton Rothschild. It doesn't take away from its quality but does give the wine poise and an attractive lift. The wine is based on solid tannins, and the ripe fruit builds layers of fruitiness and freshness. It is not likely to be one of the longest-aging Moutons, but it will be delicious. Drink from 2020.

92 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Tasted at the Mouton-Rothschild vertical in London, the 2011 Mouton-Rothschild is probably the "weakest" of the releases between 2008 and 2012. That would unfairly disparage what is perfectly respectable, if rather an unexciting Mouton. Here, it has those graphite and cedar aromas present and correct, the former a little more accentuated and with a light sea-spray note emerging with time. The palate is well balanced with cedar and a slight peat-like note infusing the black fruit, rigid in its youth but nicely delineated. As I discerned out of the barrel, it lacks that peacock's tail on the finish, bolting out of the exit door before you get to know each other.

title: Produttori del Barbaresco - Barbaresco 'Muncagota' Riserva 2020
bodyHtml:
The Produttori del Barbaresco 'Muncagota' 2020 hails from the Piedmont region of Italy, specifically the Barbaresco DOCG appellation. This wine is sourced from the Muncagota single-vineyard (MGA) in the Barbaresco subregion.

The Produttori del Barbaresco is a cooperative winery established in 1958, bringing together over fifty member families who cultivate Nebbiolo grapes. Their winemaking philosophy is centred on showcasing the land, or terroir, rather than the winemaker's skills, by allowing the grapes to express their purity and beauty without excessive manipulation. The co-op has a high reputation for delivering this true terroir-driven quality.

Wine Description

This Nebbiolo-based wine reveals a light red colour. The aroma is complex, featuring an intense balsamic fragrance with notes of camphor and eucalyptus, which are accented by forest floor, hay, and woodland berry. Other aromatic nuances include rosemary, mint, redcurrants, dried earth, and white pepper.

The palate is fresh, displaying dark fruit flavours like blackberry and plum, along with spice and ripe citrus. It is deceptively medium in body, offering good drive with taut, fine-grained, defined tannins and bright, lively acidity. The structure is complex and elegant, showcasing stylistic notes of freshness, salinity, and a distinct mineral core. The finish is long, intense, and persistent, with saline and savoury notes. The wine is 100% Nebbiolo and is generally drinkable between 2026 and 2032, though some critics suggest a wider window of 2025–2035. Information regarding organic status is not available from the sources.

Accolades

  • Wine Advocate - 94 points

  • Jeb Dunnuck - 96 points

  • Wine Spectator - 95 points

title: Azelia Barolo San Rocco 2014
bodyHtml:
This wine offers licorice, spices, cherry, currant and blueberry aromas. It is fleshy, velvety and ripe on the palate, with splendidly integrated tannins. A wine with great power, austerity and aging potential.

93 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2014 Barolo San Rocco is very expressive of the Serralunga d'Alba township, which always shows darker and denser fruit characteristics than Barolo's other main growing areas. This wine is aged in barrique for two years, of which only 10% is new oak. Your senses are treated to attractive layers of dark fruit, spice, wet earth and grilled herb. On average, the vines are 60 years old and show extra density and concentration. It follows that the mouthfeel is proportionally denser and more structured as well.

92 Points - James Suckling

Quite a concentrated wine for this challenging vintage. It shows some richness and grace. The tannins are already beautifully integrated. There's an attractive terracotta character here and notes of dried flowers and red cherries.

title: Chateau Ducru Beaucaillou 2022
bodyHtml:
Chateau Ducru Beaucaillou is a prestigious Second Growth estate located in the Saint-Julien appellation of Bordeaux’s Left Bank. Established in 1720, the estate has earned a reputation for producing some of the Médoc’s most elegant and age-worthy wines. Under the ownership of Bruno-Eugène Borie since 2003, the estate continues to blend tradition with precision viticulture and cutting-edge winemaking techniques.

Wine Description
The 2022 vintage of Chateau Ducru Beaucaillou presents a deep, opaque ruby colour with purple undertones. On the nose, it delivers a rich and complex bouquet of blackcurrants, dark cherries, violets, crushed stones, and subtle notes of graphite and cedar. The palate is full-bodied and structured, with layers of ripe black fruit, cassis, tobacco leaf, and dark chocolate, framed by refined tannins and vibrant acidity.

Accolades

  • James Suckling - 97+ points
  • Jeb Dunnuck - 97+ points
  • Decanter - 97 points
  • Vinous - 95+ points
  • Wine Advocate - 94+ points

Food Pairing
This structured and complex red pairs beautifully with herb-crusted lamb rack, grilled ribeye steak, or truffle risotto. Its depth and tension also complement aged hard cheeses such as Comté or Parmigiano-Reggiano. A perfect match to enhance the wine's complexity.

title: Castillo Ygay Gran Reserva Especial 2012
bodyHtml:
This iconic red wine hails from Spain, specifically from the Rioja Alta subregion of Rioja. The historic Marqués de Murrieta winery, established in 1852, has been led by the Cebrián Sagarriga family since 1983, who maintain a winemaking philosophy that balances deep-rooted tradition with modern innovation. The grapes for this Gran Reserva are sourced exclusively from La Plana, a 40 hectare vineyard planted in 1950 at the highest point of the Finca Ygay estate.

Wine Description

The 2012 vintage presents a deep ruby colour with elegant brick red hues. The complex nose unfolds layers of black cherry and ripe plum, interwoven with sophisticated notes of tea leaves, cedar wood, Mediterranean herbs, and dried flowers. On the palate, the wine is full bodied and harmonious, featuring a velvety texture with polished, well framed tannins and a streak of graphite that defines the long finish.

Accolades

  • "James Suckling - 100 points."

  • "The Wine Advocate - 97 points."

  • "Vinous - 97 points."

  • "Decanter - 97 points."

Food Pairing

This powerful and complex Gran Reserva is ideally suited for grilled red meats, lamb, and hearty game dishes served with rich sauces. It also pairs excellently with characterful aged cheeses and savoury stews.

title: Domaine Jean Paul & Benoit Droin Chablis 'Valmur' Grand Cru 2023
Domaine Faiveley Meursault 'Charmes' Premier Cru 2021
bodyHtml:
Founded in 1825, Bourgognes Faiveley has been handed down from father to son for over 175 years. As the sixth generation to take the reins, François Faiveley manages, with equal amounts of passion and competence, the largest family domain in Burgundy. Methodically reconstructing vineyards fractured by French inheritance laws, Bourgognes Faiveley today owns more appellations in their entirety (monopoles) than any other domain in Burgundy.

Ripe green fruit. Yellow apples, white peach, stone fruit, yellow plum and apricot. Ripe citrus of lemon pith and a hint of lime on the palate. A hint of tropical notes. Light minerality of chalk and pristine saline notes. Balanced butter and integrated toast from the barrel. Great concentration, acidity and intensity. Long finish. Beautiful 1. er Cru Meursault Les Charmes, balanced, elegant and light balsamic. Worth every penny!

title: Domaine Bouard Bonnefoy Chassagne Montrachet 'Les Chenevottes' Premier Cru 2023
bodyHtml: Domaine Bouard-Bonnefoy sets the standard for naturally made, profoundly flavourful white Burgundy. Consider the family's hand-cranked wooden press, the mini-family cellar and the bottling line, where each bottle is corked and labelled by hand, when someone says they are searching for an authentic wine far removed from today's hyper-technology and trends, they're looking for Bouard-Bonnefoy wines. This winemaking family represents a Burgundy one thought was long gone.

title: Chateau Lafite Rothschild 1995
bodyHtml:
Originating from France in the Bordeaux region, specifically within the Pauillac AOC appellation in the Haut Médoc, Château Lafite Rothschild 1995 represents an aristocratic, ethereal, and classically proportioned monument of Left Bank winemaking. Heading the prestigious 1855 Classification as the premier First Growth, Château Lafite Rothschild is revered globally for its aristocratic elegance, aromatic complexity, and legendary longevity. Owned by the Rothschild family since Baron James de Rothschild acquired the estate in 1868, the vineyard spans over 100 hectares situated on the northern boundary of Pauillac, separated from Saint Estèphe only by the Jalle du Breuil stream. The terroir comprises deep Günzian gravel knolls resting on a bedrock of tertiary limestone, providing superb drainage and forcing the old vine roots deep into the subsoil. Under the stewardship of Baron Éric de Rothschild and technical director Charles Chevallier, the 1995 vintage marked a definitive modern benchmark for the estate. Viticulture followed traditional parcel-by-parcel plot selection with manual harvesting and strict sorting. Fermentation occurred in large temperature-controlled wooden and stainless steel vats, followed by maturation for 18 to 20 months in 100% new French oak barriques crafted at the estate's own cooperage. The result is an icon of Left Bank restraint, mineral precision, and transcendent multi-decade cellar staying power.

The wine presents a deep, luminous garnet colour with a mature, brick-tinted mahogany rim. An expressive, highly perfumed bouquet opens with noble aromas of ripe blackcurrant, dried dark cherries, damson plum, and cassis compote, interwoven with sophisticated notes of lead pencil shavings, cigar box, crushed cedar, damp gravel minerality, dried violet petals, autumn forest floor, and warm French oak spice. On the palate, it is medium-to-full bodied, silken, and energetic, delivering concentrated flavours of mature dark fruits, savory truffles, and mineral earth, all supported by a bright, mouthwatering spine of natural cool-climate acidity. Framed by seamless, ultra-fine cashmere tannins and a dense, multidimensional mid-palate structure, it concludes with an exceptionally long, persistent finish marked by lingering dried berries, wild herbs, and a clean, graphite-etched mineral grip. Composed of a classic blend dominated by Cabernet Sauvignon with Merlot and a touch of Cabernet Franc and Petit Verdot, this fully mature 1995 release is in its prime drinking window spanning 2010–2045+. Stylistically, it combines sovereign First Growth poise, weightless density, and textbook Pauillac pedigree.

title: K Vintners Royal City Syrah 2020
bodyHtml:
This red wine originates from the United States, specifically from the Royal Slope subregion of Washington State. Produced by K Vintners, it was first released in 2006 by winemaker Charles Smith and became the first Washington wine to receive a perfect 100 point score from Wine Enthusiast. The winery's philosophy focuses on single vineyard Syrahs that utilise whole cluster fermentation and native yeasts to create a powerful, authentic expression of the site.

Wine Description

Royal City Syrah displays a deep ruby or magenta purple colour. The nose is highly complex and aromatic, offering a savoury mix of cured meats, black olives, and iron alongside dark fruits like blackberry and plum, with floral hints of lavender and anise. On the palate, the wine is full bodied and texturally rich, featuring a silky mouthfeel balanced by firm mineral tension, vibrant acidity, and a near everlasting finish. It is 100% Syrah with an ABV typically between 14.5% and 15%. The wine is not certified organic, and the optimal drinking window often spans 15 to 20 years.

Food Pairing

The intense savoury and meaty profile of this Syrah makes it an ideal match for hearty red meat dishes. It pairs exceptionally well with grilled lamb chops, smoked brisket, or venison seasoned with rosemary and black pepper. Its earthy and mineral undertones also complement dishes featuring wild mushrooms, truffle oil, or charcuterie platters with salty olives and aged cheeses.

title: Louis M. Martini Cabernet Sauvignon 'Lot 1' 2017
bodyHtml:
Lot No.1 is Cabernet Sauvignon at its peak form of expression. Its history dates back over 70 years when Louis M. Martini began a practice that would become a hallmark of his winery.

While tasting through Cabernet aging in the cellar, he began selecting exceptional lots, choosing ones that showcased the essence of Cabernet Sauvignon character and designating them to craft his finest wine.

95 Points - James Suckling

A soft, juicy red with licorice and aniseed undertones to the blueberries and sage. Candy. Medium to full body with agility and elegance.

94 Points - Wine Spectator

A rich, lush style, with creamed plum, blueberry and warmed blackberry compote flavors gliding along, laced with cocoa and warm earth notes. A black licorice note drapes over the fruit on the finish, and there's a violet note hanging in the background. Large-scaled and well-defined. 

94 Points - Wine Enthusiast

Woody, herbal and spicy in black pepper and clove, this bold, complete wine is layered and complex in structure. Notes of tobacco, dark chocolate, iron and meat highlight a muscular, grippy style that is built for aging.

92 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

title: Pavillon Rouge du Chateau Margaux 2022
bodyHtml:
1. Introduction

This red wine comes from France, specifically the Bordeaux region, in the appellation of Margaux. Pavillon Rouge is the second wine of Château Margaux, one of the original four First Growths (Premier Grand Cru Classé) from the 1855 Bordeaux Wine Official Classification. The Château Margaux estate, with a history spanning centuries, is known for embodying the elegance and finesse of the Margaux appellation. Today, the estate is led by the Mentzelopoulos family, with Alexis Leven-Mentzelopoulos serving as the CEO, continuing a legacy of visionary leadership, a commitment to quality, and a philosophy of precision and respect for nature.

2. Wine Description

The 2022 vintage of Pavillon Rouge is an exceptionally serious expression, representing 32% of the total harvest in that year. It is noted for its deep garnet-purple or bright ruby purple colour. The aroma is expressive, offering a fragrant and finessed bouquet of red plum, raspberries, mulberries, lilac, and violets, mingled with hints of cedar, chocolate, licorice, and spices.

The varietal composition is 64% Cabernet Sauvignon, 24% Merlot, 7% Petit Verdot, and 5% Cabernet Franc. The palate is medium to full-bodied, rich, layered, and concentrated, displaying a blend of dark fruits like blackcurrant pastilles, black cherries, and plums. Stylistically, it is described as plush, opulent, and elegant, possessing a silky texture and a muscular frame. It has a great backbone, with plenty of sweet, fine-grain, or chalky tannins and well-knit freshness, showcasing an exceptional balance and vibrancy. The finish is long and flavourful, with a fragrant lift and a peppery length. The alcohol by volume (ABV) is 14.8%. It is aged in French oak, with 60% new oak used. The wine is a powerful rendition for Pavillon Rouge. The optimal drinking window is noted as starting around 2028 to 2045. Information on the wine being organic is not available, though the estate predominantly uses organic farming methods.

title: Domaine Francois Mikulski Meursault Le Limozin 2023
bodyHtml:
1. Introduction

This white wine is from France, specifically the Burgundy region, within the Cote de Beaune and the village appellation of Meursault. Domaine François Mikulski was established in 1992 by François and his wife, Marie-Pierre, taking over family vineyards. François was born in Brussels to a Polish father and a Burgundian mother, and he spent his formative summers in Meursault, where he fell in love with the region and its agricultural lifestyle. The winemaking philosophy centres on producing authentic, elegant, and pure wines by practising non-certified organic viticulture and using a minimal amount of new oak barrels (typically 20%) to let the purity of the fruit and the terroir's minerality express itself. The 'Limozin' climat lies just below the prestigious Premier Cru 'Les Genevrières' and often produces wines of exceptional substance.

2. Wine Description

The 2023 Meursault Limozin displays a brilliant light gold colour, likely with slight green highlights. The nose is discreet but complex, with great depth, revealing notes of subtle dried fruits, white currants, cream puff, icing sugar, and white flowers, including lily and violet. On the palate, the wine is wonderfully fresh and energetic, with a full-bodied, generous, and juicy texture. It offers ample fruit, including pear, caramelised apple, apricot, and a mix of sweet spices, liquorice, and cardamom. The wine is long, focused, and precise, showcasing a distinct mineral structure on the finish, with notes of cast iron and other metals.

The wine is 100% Chardonnay. The optimal drinking window is suggested to be at least five years of cellaring from the time of bottling, and it is a safe bet that the youthful character will persist for a number of years. The wine's ABV is approximately 13.5%. The Domaine is a practitioner of lutte raisonnée and employs non-certified organic farming practices.

title: Clos du Marquis 2022
bodyHtml:
Clos du Marquis is a distinguished label created in the early 20th century by the Delon family, proprietors of the revered Château Léoville Las Cases. Situated in the Saint-Julien appellation of Bordeaux’s Left Bank, Clos du Marquis has earned its own identity, separate from its famous sibling estate, while benefiting from similarly meticulous winemaking and vineyard management practices.

A blend dominated by Cabernet Sauvignon, the 2022 Clos du Marquis displays a deep garnet hue. The nose opens with complex aromas of cassis, ripe blackberries, graphite, and violets, underpinned by hints of cedar and tobacco. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied with firm yet polished tannins, showcasing layers of dark fruit, espresso, and savoury spice. The mid-palate is concentrated and structured, leading to a long, precise finish with a mineral edge.

Food Pairing
Pair this wine with grilled ribeye steak, rosemary-crusted lamb chops, or a rich mushroom risotto. Aged cheeses like Comté or Tomme de Savoie also complement its complexity. This pairing highlights the wine’s depth and character.

96 Points - James Suckling: A scented, fresh and polished Clos du Marquis that shows tension. Medium- to full-bodied, this has blueberries and red berries with attractive minerality. A hint of pencil shavings as well. The tannins are fresh and really chalky and dissolved. 45.5% merlot, 44.5% cabernet sauvignon and 10% cabernet franc. Superb balance makes it pure, almost a bit ethereal and already inviting, but this should be approached after 2028.

97 Points - Jeb Dunnuck: I loved the 2022 Clos Du Marquis, which is a brilliant effort, if not the finest vintage of this cuvée I've tasted. Cassis, graphite, and floral notes all define the bouquet, and it's full-bodied, with ultra-fine tannins and flawless balance. It shows the ripe, concentrated, powerful style of the vintage yet is incredibly pure and seamless, with everything in the right places. It's going to round into form with just a few years of bottle age but have decades of prime drinking.

title: Chateau Guiraud Grand Vin Blanc 2020
bodyHtml:
This inaugural and sophisticated dry white wine originates from France, specifically within the Bordeaux region and the prestigious Sauternes territory. Produced by Château Guiraud, a Premier Grand Cru Classé in 1855, this specific cuvée was first launched with the 2020 vintage. The winery's philosophy is rooted in biodiversity and organic viticulture, having pioneered sustainable practices in the region since 1996. The Grand Vin Blanc Sec is designed to capture the natural richness of the estate’s mother vineyard but in a dry, precise style.

Wine Description

Château Guiraud Grand Vin Blanc 2020 presents a rich yet energetic profile. The sensory profile features a complex nose of white peach, pear, and herbaceous notes, layered with sophisticated hints of brioche and citrus. On the palate, the wine is described as having a "goldsmith's texture" precise and finely crafted showcasing a beautiful tension and great purity. It is characterized by its unusual fermentation process, spending three weeks in barrels previously used for the estate's flagship Sauternes, which imparts a unique depth and subtle sweetness to the aromatics while remaining dry. This blend consists of 70% Sauvignon Blanc and 30% Sémillon, reaching an ABV of 14%. The 2020 vintage is the 10th for the estate to be certified organic.

Food Pairing

The textured richness and crisp acidity of this dry white make it an ideal companion for refined appetizers and seafood. It pairs perfectly with crab-stuffed potato skins, artichoke dip, or a caprese-style chicken breast. Its brioche and fruit-driven character also complements seared scallops, lobster, and creamy risotto. For a simpler pairing, it is an excellent match for aged hard cheeses such as Manchego or Parmesan.

title: Poderi Aldo Conterno Barolo Bussia Cicala 2019
bodyHtml:
The story of Poderi Aldo Conterno, one of the elite, historic Barolo producers, is a tale of great passion for winemaking that winds back across generations and crosses international borders. 

While the Langhe Rosso, Chardonnay 'Bussiador', Barbera d’Alba 'Conca Tre Pile' and Nebbiolo 'Favot' represent a nod to modern winemaking techniques, the Barolo wines remain firmly in the traditionalist camp, aged in large Slavonian-oak botte before bottling. Only indigenous yeasts and traditional fermenting techniques are used. These are clean, polished and ethereal wines of great elegance that are guaranteed to offer years of sublime drinking while being terrific collector’s items.

The vineyard 'Cicala' is about 45-50 years old and its vines are replanted from time to time. The main variety of Nebbiolo is Lampia and its rootstock is Rupestris du Lot. Harvest is done manually, with grapes selected in the vineyard.

97 Points - Wine Spectator

Pure and supple in texture, boasting aromas and flavors of rose, cherry, raspberry, vanilla and toasty oak, this red is pretty seamless already, with refined tannins that emerge on the finish, needing time to absorb the oak. There’s also a saline mineral element that lingers at the end.

96 Points - James Suckling

Lots of burnt orange peel, nutmeg, hazelnut and ripe/dried strawberry aromas follow through to a medium to full body, with firm and linear tannins and a fresh and vivid finish. Energetic and fine.

title: Chateau Pichon Longueville Baron 2017
bodyHtml:
96 Points - Wine Enthusiast

This wine is both weighty and stylish. Its power comes from luscious black fruits that are juicy and powerful. Expect this wine to age well and drink from 2024.

96 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

A blend of 78% Cabernet Sauvignon and 22% Merlot aged 18 months in 80% new French oak, the 2017 Chateau Pichon-Longueville Baron sports a vivid purple hue as well as gorgeous notes of creme de cassis and black raspberry fruits are interwoven with classic Pauillac lead pencil, crushed rocks, chocolate, and violet notes. Full-bodied and concentrated, yet elegant and seamless, it has remarkable purity, flawless tannins, beautifully integrated acidity, and an excellent finish. It will hit the early stages of prime drinking in 7-8 years and cruise for 20-25 years or more.

95 Points - James Suckling

The currants, blackberries and spices are very pretty here on the nose. The palate is medium-to-full-bodied with round, compact tannins and a fresh, linear finish. Cool and racy. Strong and focused. Drink after 2023.

95 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Composed of 79% Cabernet Sauvignon and 21% Merlot aged for 18 months in French oak barrels, 80% new, the deep garnet-purple coloured 2017 Pichon-Longueville Baron slips sensuously out of the glass with provocative cherry preserves, baked raspberries and fresh blackcurrants scents, leading to nuances of red roses, charcoal, tilled soil and cardamom plus a waft of the forest floor. Medium-bodied, the palate is elegant, refreshing and refined, with a compelling line of soft, grainy tannins and lots of perfumed accents, finishing fragrant.

title: Chateau Le Pin 2022
bodyHtml:
Chateau Le Pin is a boutique estate located in the revered Pomerol appellation on Bordeaux’s Right Bank. Founded in the late 20th century by the Thienpont family, the estate quickly rose to cult status due to its minute production and meticulously crafted wines. The vineyard spans just over 2 hectares, making it one of the smallest but most prestigious in the region.

Wine Description
The 2022 Le Pin is a mesmerizing expression of Merlot-dominant Bordeaux, presenting a deep garnet hue. The nose is intensely aromatic with ripe black cherry, plum, violets, and exotic spices, lifted by hints of cedar and mocha. On the palate, it is full-bodied yet exceptionally graceful, showcasing silky tannins, vibrant freshness, and seamless integration of oak. The wine reveals layers of dark berry fruit, graphite, and truffle, culminating in a long, elegant finish.

Accolades

  • Wine Advocate – 95 points.
