  • James Suckling – 99 points.

Food Pairing
Pair with dishes that match its richness and finesse—slow-roasted duck breast with cherry sauce, beef Wellington, or wild mushroom risotto with truffle oil. A perfect match to enhance the wine's complexity.

title: Faiveley Gevrey Chambertin 'Les Cazetiers' Premier Cru 2020
bodyHtml:
95 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2020 Gevrey-Chambertin 1er Cru Les Cazetiers is brilliant, unwinding in the glass with aromas of dark berries, plums, dark chocolate, spices and vanilla pod. Medium to full-bodied, layered and concentrated, it's elegantly muscular, with a deep and multidimensional core and a long, expansive finish. It's worth a special effort to seek out.

95 Points - James Suckling

Explosive nose of sour cherry with notes of wet earth and spice, then a very energetic and structured, medium-bodied palate that doesn't leave any doubt, thanks to the intensity and wonderful harmony. Very long, focused finish that's very cool and clean.

title: La Croix Ducru Beaucaillou 2022
bodyHtml:
La Croix Ducru Beaucaillou is the esteemed second wine of Château Ducru-Beaucaillou, one of Saint-Julien’s most historic and respected estates. Under the ownership of the Borie family since 1941, the château has become synonymous with precision and elegance, with vines planted on a prime stretch of deep gravel soils overlooking the Gironde estuary. The wine reflects the estate’s dedication to excellence, guided by proprietor Bruno Borie’s commitment to terroir-driven, age-worthy wines.

Wine Description
Deep garnet in colour, the 2022 La Croix Ducru Beaucaillou opens with a seductive bouquet of blackcurrant, crushed violets, and dark plum, interwoven with graphite, cedar, and subtle vanilla spice from new oak ageing. On the palate, it delivers richness and refinement in equal measure—full-bodied yet impeccably structured, with layers of ripe blackberry, cassis, and mocha supported by firm but polished tannins. The finish is long, savoury, and mineral-driven, showcasing Saint-Julien's hallmark finesse.

Accolades

  • James Suckling - 95 points
  • Jeb Dunnuck - 94 points
  • Vinous - 94 points

Food Pairing
Pair this wine with herb-crusted rack of lamb, grilled ribeye steak, or mushroom risotto. The wine’s firm structure and dark fruit depth complement hearty meat dishes and rich umami flavours. A perfect match to enhance the wine's complexity.

title: Barons de Rothschild Brut
bodyHtml: This nicely balanced low dosage Brut Champagne displays fresh almond, pear, and citrus zest notes with light brioche notes. Rich and complex, it shows excellent freshness wrapped in a lightly creamy texture with patisserie apple, pastry, almond and meringue flavours. A smoky hint of minerality gains momentum on the finish.

title: Duckhorn The Discussion 2021
bodyHtml:
This iconic and powerful red blend originates from the United States, specifically from the premier Napa Valley region in California. The Discussion is the "pinnacle" of the Duckhorn Vineyards portfolio, first crafted in 2006 to embody the winery’s multi-decade mastery of Napa Valley estate fruit. The name is inspired by an intense, late-night debate at the Duckhorn family’s kitchen table between co-founders Dan and Margaret Duckhorn and their winemakers about whether to focus on single-varietal wines or to create the ultimate cuvée. The winemaking philosophy for this label is to represent the "timeless union" of Cabernet Sauvignon and Merlot, sourced 100% from prestigious estate vineyards.

Wine Description

Duckhorn "The Discussion" Napa Valley Red Wine presents a saturated and broad core with a complex, "bordeaux-style" profile. The sensory profile features a dense medley of brambly red currants, black raspberry, fig compote, and rose petals on the nose. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied and "voluptuous," showcasing deep flavours of black cherry, dark chocolate, and cinnamon, accented by hints of cloves and bay leaves. It is characterized by its velvety, "powdery" tannins and an energetic acidity that adds poise to its massive structure.

Food Pairing

The sophisticated structure and concentrated fruit of The Discussion make it an ideal partner for bold, savory, and umami-rich cuisine. It pairs perfectly with roast lamb, grilled ribeye steak, or a rich wild mushroom risotto. Its spicy undertones and dark fruit also complement venison, braised short ribs, and charcuterie featuring smoked meats. For a simpler pairing, it is an excellent match for aged cheeses such as sharp cheddar or aged Gouda.

title: Domaine Henri Rebourseau Charmes Chambertin Grand Cru 2019
bodyHtml:
Introduction

This prestigious red wine hails from France, specifically the Burgundy region within the Gevrey Chambertin village. Domaine Henri Rebourseau is an iconic estate with roots dating back to 1782, holding one of the most significant collections of Grand Cru vineyards in the Côte de Nuits. Now managed by the de Surrel family in partnership with the Bouygues family, the domaine employs organic and biodynamic farming practices to highlight the purity and individuality of their exceptional 'climat' sites.

Wine Description

The Domaine Henri Rebourseau Charmes Chambertin Grand Cru 2019 displays an intense raspberry red appearance with brilliant clarity. The nose is lush and perfumed, offering concentrated aromas of wild strawberries and jammy cherries, beautifully interwoven with vanilla spices, crushed rose petals, and violets. On the palate, the wine is sumptuous and full-bodied, exhibiting a silky, almost oily texture and a rich core of fleshy fruit. It is balanced by a firm yet fine tannic structure and a lingering, spicy finish. This wine is 100% Pinot Noir and is certified organic and biodynamic. The alcohol by volume (ABV) is 13.8% (often rounded to 14%). While approachable in its youth due to the solar nature of the vintage, it has an optimal drinking window extending up to fifteen years or more.

Accolades

  • Jasper Morris - Inside Burgundy - 93 points.

  • Vinous - 94 points.

  • Decanter - 93 points.

  • Wine Spectator - 93 points.

  • Burghound - 93 points.

Food Pairing

This rich and suave Grand Cru pairs exceptionally well with sophisticated meat dishes. Suggested pairings include roast duck breast with a honey and spice glaze, prime rib with a morel cream sauce, or feathered game such as pheasant. It also complements earthy flavours like truffle-infused dishes or a selection of refined Burgundian cheeses.

Vintage Quality

The 2019 vintage in Burgundy is considered outstanding, characterized by a hot and dry summer that led to high concentration and small, thick-skinned grapes. Despite two significant heatwaves, the wines preserved excellent freshness and mineral tension, resulting in a vintage that offers a rare combination of power, aromatic intensity, and structural balance.

title: Purlieu Cabernet Sauvignon Beckstoffer To Kalon Vineyard 2019
vendor: 300747 - South By Southwest Wine Imports Inc.
bodyHtml: Purple fruit and fresh violet aromas on the nose only hint at the concentration that awaits on the palate. A focused beam of juicy purple and black berries melds with refined mocha and fresh earth notes, which bring extra depth and dimension to the sweet To Kalon fruit. Rich, fine-grained tannins and an endless finish of sweet boysenberry caramel promise years of continued evolution and delight.

title: Chateau Margaux 2022
bodyHtml:
Château Margaux, located in the Médoc region of Bordeaux, France, is a Premier Grand Cru Classé estate renowned for its centuries-old winemaking tradition. Owned by the Mentzelopoulos family since 1977, the estate has consistently produced wines of outstanding quality, embodying elegance and complexity.

Wine Description

The 2022 Grand Vin is composed of 92% Cabernet Sauvignon, 6% Merlot, and 2% Cabernet Franc. This blend results in a deep garnet-purple hue. On the nose, it offers an array of aromas, including redcurrant jelly, blackberry pie, fresh blackcurrants, iron ore, lilacs, black licorice, and sandalwood, with a hint of wood smoke. The palate is full-bodied, densely packed with rich, concentrated black and red fruits, supported by exquisitely ripe, finely grained tannins and seamless freshness, culminating in a long, fragrant finish.

Accolades

  • James Suckling: 99 points.

  • Vinous (Antonio Galloni): 99 points.

Food Pairing

This wine's depth and structure make it an excellent companion to dishes such as roasted lamb, beef tenderloin, or duck breast with a berry reduction. These pairings enhance the wine's complexity and create an unforgettable dining experience.

title: Allegrini La Poja 2018
bodyHtml:
Hailing from Italy’s Veneto region, the Allegrini La Poja 2018 is a prestigious single vineyard expression from the Sant’Ambrogio di Valpolicella subregion. The Allegrini family has been a pioneering force in Valpolicella for generations, establishing a reputation for innovation when late family patriarch Giovanni Allegrini purchased the La Grola hilltop in 1979.

Wine Description

The wine pours a brilliant ruby red with a delicate, finessed clarity. The nose slowly unfurls to reveal an incredibly pure and lifted sensory profile, delivering aromas of dark raspberry, crushed rose petals, and wild blueberries. These vibrant fruit notes are complemented by sophisticated undertones of incense, blood orange, and a hint of dark chocolate. On the palate, this 100% Corvina Veronese showcases a contemporary style focused on a crystalline freshness and a lively, energetic acidity. It is medium to full bodied, presenting tight, fine grained tannins that seamlessly integrate into a structured mid palate.

Accolades

  • Decanter - 98 points.

  • Wine Enthusiast - 96 points.

  • James Suckling - 95 points.

  • Vinous - 94 points.

title: Antinori Brunello di Montalcino 'Pian delle Vigne' 2004 - 3 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
This classic red wine originates from the Brunello di Montalcino DOCG in the Tuscany region of Italy. The Pian delle Vigne estate was acquired by the historic Antinori family in 1995, a family with a winemaking heritage dating back to 1385. The winery's philosophy is centred on 'Vigna' (the vineyard), emphasizing the unique terroir of its 65-hectare site located south of Montalcino, where the combination of clay-rich soils and a warm microclimate produces a Brunello of significant body and elegance.

Wine Description

The Antinori Pian delle Vigne Brunello di Montalcino 2004 presents a deep ruby red colour with slight garnet reflections. The sensory profile is intense and complex, featuring an aromatic bouquet of ripe red fruits, plums, and blackberries, layered with sophisticated notes of tobacco, leather, spices, and a hint of balsamic. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied and supple, showcasing a broad texture with well-integrated, silky tannins and a balanced acidity. It is characterized by its remarkable structural harmony and a long, persistent finish that echoes dark chocolate and liquorice. This 100% Sangiovese has an ABV of 14% and was aged for over two years in large oak casks followed by significant refinement in the bottle.

Vintage Quality

The 2004 vintage in Montalcino is considered one of the greatest of the decade, frequently awarded a five-star rating by the local consorzio. After a relatively cool spring, a warm and consistent summer allowed for slow, even ripening of the grapes, resulting in wines with exceptional balance, vibrant acidity, and profound aging potential. Winemakers benefited from perfect harvest conditions in late September and October, producing fruit with excellent phenolic maturity and aromatic intensity.

title: Caparzo Brunello di Montalcino 'Vigna La Casa' 2020
bodyHtml:
The Brunello di Montalcino DOCG Vigna la Casa was born in 1977 in one of the most prestigious vineyards in the municipality of Montalcino, a wine with a gentle and elegant soul that can be considered a true oenological jewel. The La Casa vineyard (5 hectares), is located on the hill of Montosoli, with exposure, terrain and altitude such to preserve the grapes from the mists and spring frosts guaranteeing a high quality of the crops.

97 Points - James Suckling

Blueberry, blackberry and chocolate aromas yet subtle and perfumed. Full-bodied with chewy tannins and lots of structure. Shows depth and has a purpose.

95 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

Ripe and inviting, the 2019 Brunello Di Montalcino Vigna La Casa pours a deep ruby/red color and reveals intertwining notes of kirsch, fresh leather, dried roses, and sweet Mediterranean herbs. It’s elegant and full-bodied, with ripe tannins, a plush texture, and wonderful length that floats away gently.

95 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The Caparzo 2019 Brunello di Montalcino Vigna La Casa offers a balanced presentation of candied cherry, dried fruit and toasted spice. This is a lovely and joyous wine with velvety soft tannins and good inner energy that adds dimension and depth to the mouthfeel.

title: Gaja Ca'Marcanda Magari 2023
bodyHtml:
Gaja Ca'Marcanda Magari 2023 originates from Italy, within the Tuscany region and the coastal Bolgheri DOC subregion. The estate was established by the pioneering Piedmontese winemaker Angelo Gaja in the 1990s, requiring 18 rounds of intense discussion to finalize the acquisition. This history inspired the estate's name, Ca'Marcanda, which translates to 'the house of endless negotiations'. The winery's current operational philosophy centers on crafting top-quality expressions that rival world-class blends, utilising modern temperature-controlled winemaking and small oak barrels to capture the potential of the local maritime terroir.

Wine Description

This red wine presents a bright magenta or ruby appearance with a violet tinge in the glass and possesses a medium-to-full, dense structure with a silky, creamy, and generous texture. The sensory profile is remarkably intense, spicy, and layered, opening with a complex nose of mature flowers like rose and violet, seamlessly intertwined with aromas of blackcurrant, dark cherry, fresh rosemary, cedar, and toasted incense. On the balanced and crunchy palate, it delivers deep flavours of baked blackberry pie, plump berry fruit, plums, and balsamic herbs, cut through by a distinctive salty marine note, fresh acidity, and ripe phenolics. The finish is long and juicy, leaving trailing memories of sweet chocolate, tobacco, graphite, and a touch of subtle sweetness wrapped in robust, fine-grained tannins.

  • Varietal Composition: A classic Cabernet Franc-dominant Bordeaux blend consisting of 60% Cabernet Franc, 30% Cabernet Sauvignon, and 10% Petit Verdot.

  • Stylistic Notes: The wine is celebrated for its precise balance, elegance, and immediate pleasure on the palate, combining a vertical freshness with an appealing richness that avoids heavy extraction. To maximize varietal clarity and structural harmony, each grape variety is fermented separately before the components undergo 14 months of maturation in barriques.

  • ABV: 14% to 14.5%.

  • Organic Status: While the estate relies on meticulous parcel management and sustainable agriculture across its limestone-rich soils, this commercial release is not certified organic.

Food Pairing

The vibrant natural acidity, rich berry fruit profile, and robust tannic frame of this Super Tuscan make it an outstanding companion for full-flavoured gastronomy.

  • Game: Pairs beautifully with premium game birds, strong game dishes, or mild venison and deer preparations.

  • Meats: Suggested pairings include traditional roasted lamb, braised beef dishes, or savoury veal cutlets that mirror the wine's sweet spices.

  • Savoury & Italian Staples: Complements rich Italian pasta courses topped with slow-simmered meat ragù.

  • Cheese: Matches exceptionally well with structured artisanal platters of well-matured or raw milk cheeses.

Vintage Quality

The 2023 growing season along the Tuscan coast is regarded as an excellent and highly successful year that produced a crop defined by wonderful flavor concentration and pristine fruit health. The maritime microclimate of Bolgheri allowed the late-ripening Cabernet varieties to accumulate dense extract and complexity during sunny summer days, while refreshing coastal breezes preserved a lifting, energetic natural acidity. The winemaking team's skill in executing separate vinifications and precisely adjusting the barrique integration successfully brought out the maximum potential of the harvest. This careful handling resulted in a 2023 release built to evolve gracefully in the cellar for the next fifteen years.

title: Bodegas Caro Red Blend 2021
bodyHtml:
Bodegas Caro, a collaboration between Domaines Barons de Rothschild (Lafite) and Nicolás Catena, combines French and Argentine winemaking traditions to craft exceptional wines that highlight the unique terroir of Mendoza, Argentina.

Wine Description

The 2021 Caro is a blend of 79% Malbec and 21% Cabernet Sauvignon sourced from the Uco Valley. The wine presents a deep garnet-purple hue and offers expressive aromas of plum preserves, blueberry compote, and licorice, complemented by hints of candied violets and spice cake. On the palate, it is full-bodied and packed with perfumed black fruits, framed by super-ripe, plush tannins and refreshing acidity, culminating in a long and fragrant finish.

Accolades

  • Decanter: 95 points

Food Pairing

This wine pairs excellently with grilled meats such as lamb or beef, enhancing the wine's depth and character.

title: Chateau Clerc Milon 2022
bodyHtml:
Introduction

This red wine originates from France, specifically from the Pauillac subregion of the Médoc in Bordeaux. Classified as a Fifth Growth in 1855, Château Clerc Milon is situated between the First Growths Château Mouton Rothschild and Château Lafite Rothschild. The modern history of the estate began in 1970 when Baron Philippe de Rothschild acquired the then-neglected property, initiating a transformation that has seen it become one of the Médoc's most refined and consistent voices. The winery's philosophy emphasizes clarity and terroir expression, supported by a state-of-the-art gravity-fed winery inaugurated in 2011.

Wine Description

Chateau Clerc Milon 2022 presents a deep purple-red or dark ruby colour with plum reflections. The nose is multi-faceted and intense, offering a sensational perfume of crème de cassis, wild berries, and bilberry, layered with notes of spring flowers, spice, pepper, and violet. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied and concentrated yet retains a weightless, silky mouthfeel with powerful, well-integrated tannins. It is characterized by an exceptional balance between the freshness of liquorice and mineral notes and a controlled power that reveals elegance and precision. This blend consists of 59% Cabernet Sauvignon, 32% Merlot, 8% Cabernet Franc, and 1% Carménère. The ABV typically ranges around 14.5%, and the estate is HVE3 certified for sustainable viticulture. The optimal drinking window is from 2028 through 2055.

Accolades

  • Jeb Dunnuck - 97 points.

  • James Suckling - 96 points.

  • Yves Beck - 97 points.

  • Falstaff - 96 points.

  • Decanter - 95 points.

  • Robert Parker's Wine Advocate - 95 points.

Food Pairing

The intense structure and rich fruit of this Pauillac make it an ideal partner for classic meat-based dishes. It pairs perfectly with roast lamb, grilled beef, veal, and game. Its spicy and mineral undertones also complement savory mushroom-based pastas, braised duck, and hearty fish courses like tuna. For a local pairing, consider serving it with an entrecôte à la bordelaise.

Vintage Quality

The 2022 vintage in Pauillac was defined by an exceptionally hot and dry growing season with several heatwaves that produced small, highly concentrated berries. Despite these extreme conditions, the vines' deep roots and the June rains allowed for a rare balance of intensity, freshness, and velvety tannins. The winemakers' skill in managing gentle extraction resulted in a wine that embodies the concentration of the vintage while remaining elegantly poised.

title: Chateau La Mission Haut Brion 2021
bodyHtml:
Chateau La Mission Haut Brion 2021 is a red wine from the Pessac Leognan appellation in the Graves region of Bordeaux, France. The estate has been owned by the Dillon family of Domaine Clarence Dillon since 1983, a landmark acquisition that brought it under the same management as its illustrious neighbour, Chateau Haut-Brion. The winery’s philosophy emphasizes the unique historical significance of its terroir, which features deep Gunzian gravel hillocks that provide exceptional drainage and exposure for the vines.

Wine Description

This vintage presents a bold ruby or deep garnet-purple colour. The nose is complex and detailed, revealing aromas of plums, cassis, and black raspberries mingled with sophisticated notes of graphite, scorched earth, tobacco leaf, and sweet spices such as clove and allspice. On the palate, the wine is medium to full-bodied and seamless, characterized by a deep, concentrated core of fruit supported by bright acidity and supple, powdery tannins. Stylistically, it is lauded for its elegant and fresh profile—a 'masterclass in cool climate fruit delivery'—concluding with a long, muscular finish with mineral and savory undertones. The varietal composition is a blend of 48% Merlot, 46% Cabernet Sauvignon, and 6% Cabernet Franc. The optimal drinking window for this 2021 vintage is between 2027 and 2055.

Accolades

  • James Suckling – 96 points

  • Decanter – 95 points

  • Jeb Dunnuck – 94 points

  • Robert Parker Wine Advocate – 94–96 points

title: Chateau Batailley 2016
bodyHtml:
Produced in France’s esteemed Pauillac appellation within the Bordeaux region, Chateau Batailley is a historic Fifth Growth estate of the 1855 Classification. The winery, currently owned by the Castéja family and their Borie Manoux négociant house, derives its name from a 1453 battle fought on its grounds during the Hundred Years' War.

Wine Description

The wine presents a deep ruby-purple or garnet colour and a sophisticated sensory profile. The nose is intensely aromatic, featuring a 'quintessential Pauillac' bouquet of graphite, pencil shavings, and cassis, layered with subtle notes of mint, violets, and cedar. On the palate, the wine is medium to full-bodied with a firm yet polished tannin structure and bright acidity, offering flavours of blackcurrant jelly, plum, and tobacco-infused black fruit.

Accolades

  • "James Suckling - 96 points."

  • "Robert Parker's Wine Advocate - 95 points."

  • "Wine Spectator - 93 points."

  • "Decanter - 93 points."

  • "Vinous - 95 points."

Food Pairing

Classic roasted red meats such as a rack of lamb with rosemary or a grilled ribeye steak. Game dishes like roast duck with a cherry reduction or venison. Braised veal shank or rich stews featuring mushrooms and truffles.

title: Castiglion Del Bosco Brunello Di Montalcino 2004
bodyHtml:
Castiglion del Bosco, located in the northwest quadrant of Montalcino, is one of Tuscany’s most historic estates, dating back to the 12th century. Acquired by Massimo Ferragamo in 2003, the estate has undergone extensive restoration while maintaining a strong focus on terroir-driven winemaking. The winery is a proud member of the Brunello di Montalcino Consortium, and the estate vineyards, set at altitudes between 350–460 metres, are organically farmed and celebrated for their elegance and structure.

Wine Description
This 2004 Brunello di Montalcino is a textbook expression of Sangiovese, showcasing a brilliant garnet hue with slight bricking at the rim, reflective of its bottle age. On the nose, it opens with layers of dried cherry, leather, and cedar, accented by earthy notes of forest floor and hints of balsamic. The palate is refined and harmonious, offering red currant and dried cranberry framed by firm yet silky tannins and a lingering finish of tobacco and spice.

Accolades
● Wine Spectator – 92 points
● Wine Enthusiast – 94 points
● James Suckling – 93 points

Food Pairing
Pair this mature Brunello with braised veal shank, mushroom risotto, or aged Pecorino Toscano. The wine’s savoury notes and supple tannins harmonize beautifully with rich, umami-laden dishes. A perfect match to enhance the wine’s complexity.

title: Chateau de Pommard "Clos Marey Monge" Premier Cru 2012
bodyHtml:
Château de Pommard "Clos Marey-Monge" 1er Cru 2012 is a flagship Monopole (a vineyard owned by a single producer) from the heart of Pommard in the Côte de Beaune, Burgundy. The 20-hectare Clos Marey-Monge is one of the largest private vineyards in Burgundy, protected by a 19th-century stone wall. The estate was purchased in 2014 by Michael Baum, who transitioned the entire property to biodynamic viticulture, though the 2012 vintage was produced under the previous traditional management. The cuvée is named after the Marey-Monge family, who owned the estate for over a century and established its prestigious reputation.

Wine Description

  • Varietal: 100% Pinot Noir, blended from seven distinct clay and limestone soil micro-terroirs within the Clos.

  • Aroma: The 2012 vintage is now in its prime drinking window, displaying a complex bouquet of dried rose petals, forest floor, and leather, alongside core notes of black cherry and blackcurrant.

  • Palate: On the palate, it shows the "classic" Pommard power—dense and structured—but with the characteristic elegance of the Marey-Monge site. Expect flavours of dark fruit, licorice, and a touch of smoky tobacco.

  • Structure: The tannins have softened significantly with age, providing a silky yet firm frame, supported by the balanced acidity typical of the 2012 vintage.

  • Technical Details: The wine was aged for approximately 18 to 20 months in French oak barrels (around 35% to 50% new). It typically has an ABV of 13.5%.

Food Pairing

The maturity and structure of this 2012 Pommard make it an ideal partner for "earthy" and robust dishes:

  • Meats: Roasted duck with a cherry reduction, venison steak, or classic Beef Bourguignon.

  • Vegetarian: Wild mushroom risotto or a truffle-infused pasta.

  • Cheese: Epoisses, Langres, or a mature Comté.

Vintage Quality

The 2012 vintage in Burgundy is often called a "miracle" year. It was a low-yielding vintage plagued by frost, hail, and disease early in the season, but a glorious, sunny August and September saved the crop. The result is wines with incredible concentration, depth, and vibrant acidity. Critics consider 2012 to be one of the best vintages of the decade for the Côte de Beaune, as the small berries produced wines with intense phenolic ripeness and significant aging potential.

title: E. Guigal Cote Rotie 'La Turque' 2017
bodyHtml:
Côte-Rôtie "La Turque" is one of the flagship wines of the Domaine Guigal.  A powerful wine with spicy notes, its terroirs from côte brune with “blond accents” lends it a great elegance.  93% Syrah, 7% Viognier

97+ Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Wonderfully perfumed and floral, the 2017 Cote Rotie La Turque was singing at full voice when I tasted it. The marvelous blueberry and raspberry fruit is broad and expansive on the full-bodied palate without being heavy or overly rich, perfectly framed by soft, dusty tannins on a lingering finish. It will be fascinating to follow this wine and compare it over the decades to the 2015 and 2018.

97+ Points - Jeb Dunnuck

I loved the 2017 Côte Rôtie La Turque, which shows the sunny warmth of the vintage while staying balanced, pure, and light on its feet. Awesome notes of ripe black fruits, chocolate, spice box, and incense emerge from the glass and it’s full-bodied, has building tannins, a weightless texture, and a monster of a finish. This quintessential La Turque will deliver plenty of charm in its youth, yet benefit from 4-6 years of bottle age, and age for 30-35 years as well. 

97 Points - Decanter

La Turque is situated on a central part of Côte Brune, occupying less than 1ha, and was planted by Marcel Guigal in 1980 (first vintage in 1985) after having been abandoned since 1935. They claim the mica schist and iron oxide in the soil contribute to the strong tannins compared to La Mouline. This has intense fruit of searching depth - a deep cave of a wine - with incense, star anise and dried rose all echoing. Lashings of toasty oak spice appear on the finish, which is extremely long and resonant. The extraction is pushed as far as it can reasonably go, but the wine is well balanced with a firm beam of acidity, considerable internal sweetness of fruit, and a thick mass of ripe tannin. It will live longer than La Mouline, but not as long as La Landonne. 

96 Points - Wine Spectator

Very alluring, with silky waves of cherry puree and mulled plum fruit gliding through, infused gently with red tea, savory and sweet tapenade hints. Lingering minerality carries the finish, which has structure and grip to merit cellaring, though the fruit is so hard to resist.

95+ Points - Vinous

Expansive aromas of black raspberry, cherry and boysenberry, with exotic spice, floral oil and incense notes building in the glass. Energetic and focused on the palate, offering densely packed black/blue fruit liqueur flavors, along with intense violet pastille and cracked pepper notes. The floral quality builds steadily with air and carries through a very long, chewy finish that features resonating blue fruit and floral notes and youthfully gripping tannins.

title: Perrier Jouet Belle Epoque Brut 2016
bodyHtml:
Perrier Jouët Belle Epoque Brut 2016 originates from France, within the Champagne region. Founded in 1811, Maison Perrier Jouët has a long history of innovation, being the first house to produce a brut champagne in 1854. The Belle Epoque cuvée, first appearing in 1964, is the house's flagship vintage champagne and is instantly recognisable by its bottle adorned with Japanese white anemones designed by Art Nouveau master Emile Gallé in 1902. The winery's philosophy is deeply tied to the elegance of Chardonnay, which has been at the heart of their intricate floral style for over two centuries.

Wine Description

This champagne presents a pale golden yellow colour with greenish highlights or silvery reflections. The sensory profile is delicate and complex, featuring a nose of white flowers (linden and hawthorn), white peach, grapefruit, and spring flowers, evolving into notes of marzipan and sweet spices. On the palate, it is described as svelte and satingly, delivering a 'crystalline' freshness with flavours of poached pear, elderberry, and citrus energy, balanced by a chalky mineral character. The finish is long, stylish, and persistent, with well-integrated notes of toasted almond and grilled pineapple.

  • Varietal Composition: A blend of 50% Chardonnay, 45% Pinot Noir, and 5% Meunier.

  • ABV: 12.5%.

  • Organic Status: While the house celebrates biodiversity and the biological balance of the Champagne ecosystem, this specific cuvée is not typically certified organic.

  • Stylistic Notes: The wine is aged for approximately five years in the cellars and finished with a dosage of 8 to 9 g/L to enhance its elegance and refinement.

title: Verite 'Le Desir' 2009
bodyHtml:
The 2009 growing season was long and dry – not quite as warm and constant as the 2007 but the right conditions were present: cool nights from the influence of the Pacific Ocean, long sunny days and low humidity. These three elements are necessary to make a grand cru with balanced acidity, fruit, body and alcohol. We started harvest on September 12th with Malbec and finished on October 2nd with the last block of Cabernet Sauvignon – just before heavy rains came on October 13th.

Intense, deep inky color. Already expressing an aroma that is well-integrated, silky and refined but powerful. On the palate, an immediate explosion of complexity, where the Cabernet Franc shows its personality, its signature, its finesse, with power that makes the finish infinitely long. Very ripe currants, blackberry, plum, anise, licorice, white spice and discreet oak. A magnificent bottle.

97 Points - Jeb Dunnuck     The 2009 Le Desir is mostly Cabernet Franc and is another wine drinking beautifully today. Classic cassis and dark fruits as well as notes of bay leaf, sandalwood, and spice all flow to a full-bodied, elegant, concentrated red that has fine tannin, perfect balance, and one great finish. Drink it over the coming 20-25 years.

93 Points - Robert Parker Wine Advocate     The densest, most tannic and most forbiddingly backward of the 2009's, it exhibits an inky/purple colour along with copious aromas of graphite, spring flowers, blackberries and blueberries as well as a crushed liqueur of chalk-like character, and a huge, multilayered and multidimensional finish that lasts nearly 50 seconds. It requires 4-5 more years in the cellar, and should keep for three decades. If you have not yet experienced the wines of Vérité, they are true connoisseurs’ efforts that should be purchased by those with cold cellars and long lifelines.

title: Caymus Cabernet Sauvignon 'Special Selection' 2019 - 3 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
The Caymus 'Special Selection' Cabernet Sauvignon is an exceptional wine made from this storied Napa Valley estate.

Following some time to open, this incredible Cabernet begins to yield profound aromatics of black cherry compote, blueberry pie and boysenberry along with creosote, black tar, milk chocolate and licorice all soaring from the glass. The mouthfeel is rich, voluptuous and intense, as this wine offers exceedingly dense, concentrated flavors of black cherry reduction, blueberry pie, raspberry liquor and boysenberry, alongside milk chocolate shavings and tar, all cascading on to the long mouth coating finish. 

Each year, Caymus sets aside the best barrels of their Cabernet Sauvignon from Napa Valley to produce Special Selection.

title: Produttori del Barbaresco - Barbaresco 'Rio Sordo' Riserva 2020
bodyHtml:
Introduction

This red wine is produced in the Barbaresco region of Piedmont, Italy, specifically from the Rio Sordo subregion. The Produttori del Barbaresco cooperative was founded in 1958 and is renowned for its commitment to the Nebbiolo grape. The winery maintains a philosophy of showcasing the unique characteristics of the village's diverse crus through traditional winemaking techniques.

Wine Description

The 2020 Barbaresco Rio Sordo Riserva exhibits a medium ruby colour with garnet reflections. The aromatic profile is expressive and floral, featuring scents of red berries, rose petals, spice, and a hint of liquorice. On the palate, the wine is medium to full bodied and elegant, offering flavours of ripe cherry, pomegranate, and herbal notes. It is celebrated for its silky texture, refined tannins, and a long, fresh finish. This 100% Nebbiolo wine has an ABV of 14.5% and is produced using sustainable viticulture. The optimal drinking window for this vintage is between 2026 and 2045.

Accolades

  • Vinous - 94 points.

  • Wine Advocate - 94 points.

  • Wine Spectator - 94 points.

  • Jeb Dunnuck - 96 points.

Food Pairing

This wine pairs exceptionally well with traditional Piedmontese cuisine, such as agnolotti dal plin or risotto with wild mushrooms. It is also an excellent match for roasted poultry, grilled veal chops, or rack of lamb. For a cheese pairing, consider semi-soft cheeses or aged Pecorino.

Vintage Quality

The 2020 vintage in Barbaresco was highly successful, benefiting from a balanced growing season with timely rainfall and warm summer days. These conditions allowed the grapes to achieve excellent phenolic ripeness, resulting in wines with vibrant acidity and harmonious structures.

title: Sea Smoke Pinot Noir 'Ten' 2022
bodyHtml:
Sea Smoke Cellars is a renowned winery located in the Santa Rita Hills AVA of California's Central Coast. Established in 1999, the estate is celebrated for its commitment to producing exceptional Pinot Noir and Chardonnay. The 'Ten' Pinot Noir is a flagship wine that showcases the vineyard's dedication to quality and its unique terroir.

Wine Description
The 2022 'Ten' Pinot Noir is a blend of ten distinct Pinot Noir clones, all sourced from Sea Smoke's estate vineyard. This wine offers a deep, brooding character with aromas of blueberry, cassis, and lavender, complemented by notes of hazelnut, thyme, and licorice. On the palate, it presents a rich and structured profile with firm, mature tannins, indicative of its excellent aging potential. The wine is aged for 16 months in French oak barrels, 56% of which are new, contributing to its complexity and depth.

title: Chateau Les Grandes Murailles 2020
bodyHtml:
Château Les Grandes Murailles, a Grand Cru Classé of Saint-Émilion, is located near Clos Fourtet, and also belongs to the Cuvelier family. Blessed with a great terroir on the right bank of Bordeaux, the Cuvelier family is driven by the desire to produce timeless wines of great finesse and significant ageing potential. The Château Les Grandes Murailles vineyard covers an island of 1.46 hectares in the heart of Saint-Émilion. It is planted in the clay-limestone soils typical of the appellation. The vines are cultivated in accordance with natural balances and sustainable agriculture.

The Saint-Émilion Grand Cru Classé Château Les Grandes Murailles reveals a dark and deep colour. Notes of tobacco mingle with floral touches and notes of red fruits that charm the nose. The attack is round, taut and full of freshness. The palate reveals silky and straight-forward tannins. The crunchiness of the fruit comes through in the finish, giving the finish a great persistence.

title: Chateau Montelena Chardonnay 2023
bodyHtml:
Chateau Montelena Chardonnay 2023 originates from the United States, within the Napa Valley region of California. The winery's history is world-renowned, specifically for its 1973 vintage which triumphed at the 1976 'Judgment of Paris' tasting, proving that California could produce world-class Chardonnay. The winemaking philosophy emphasizes the purity of the fruit, vineyard, and vintage, eschewing the heavy oak and buttery styles typical of the region in favour of structure, acidity, and grace. Since its inception, this approach has defined the estate's style, focusing on balance and age-worthiness.

Wine Description

This white wine presents a pale straw colour with green-gold reflections. The sensory profile is described as linear and vibrant, opening with an expressive nose of Meyer lemon, green apple, white peach, and orange blossom, laced with notes of flinty minerals, jasmine, and wet stone. On the palate, it offers a fabulous core of dense citrus and orchard fruit supported by a gorgeous mouthfeel with unexpected weight and gravitas. The wine is characterized by a crisp, crunchy acidity and a fine minerality, concluding with a clean, enduring finish featuring enticing notes of toasted Marcona almond.

  • Varietal Composition: 100% Chardonnay.

  • Stylistic Notes: The 2023 release highlights tension and racy acidity; the wine is aged for approximately 10 months in French oak to add depth and texture while preserving fruit purity.

  • ABV: Typically recorded between 13.5% and 14.1%.

  • Organic Status: While the estate employs high-quality, sustainable viticulture, this specific bottling is not generally specified as certified organic.

Food Pairing

The vibrant acidity and mineral drive of this Chardonnay make it a versatile companion for both delicate and rich dishes.

  • Seafood: Pairs excellently with raw or grilled oysters, baked salmon, grilled tuna steaks, and ahi poke.

  • Meats: Suggested pairings include roasted poultry like steamed chicken with ginger and lemon, or pork dishes such as porchetta stuffed with herbs.

  • Vegetarian: Complements winter squash, legumes, potatoes, and dishes featuring porcini mushrooms.

  • Cheese: Matches well with sheep's milk cheeses like Ossau-Iraty or soft goat cheeses.

Vintage Quality

The 2023 vintage in Napa Valley is remembered as one of the best of the last decade, characterized by one of the longest growing seasons in recent memory. It featured a mild, consistently sunny summer that promoted even ripening and allowed for extended 'hang time' for the grapes. However, a significant heat system in early September shifted the vintage's character from purely 'elementary' and classic toward greater concentration and suppleness. The resulting wines are noted for their outstanding balance and racy acidity, with cool-vintage characteristics that suggest they will mature more slowly and gracefully than warmer-vintage counterparts.

title: Chateau Leoville Barton 2022
bodyHtml:
Introduction

The Château Léoville Barton 2022 is a historic and highly acclaimed release from the Saint-Julien appellation in Bordeaux. This vintage is particularly significant as it is the first to be produced in the estate's newly built, state-of-the-art gravity-fed winery, which more than doubled the number of vats and allowed for precise, sub-plot vinification. Critics have hailed it as one of the stars of the Médoc, often comparing it to or suggesting it may surpass the legendary 2016 and 2019 vintages.

Wine Description

The 2022 vintage is defined by a blend of classic Saint-Julien elegance and the concentrated richness of a warm, dry growing season.

  • Varietal Composition: 83% Cabernet Sauvignon, 11.5% Merlot, and 5.5% Cabernet Franc.

  • Aromatic Profile: The nose is "immediately arresting," featuring pure and intense aromas of crème de cassis, black cherries, and violets. It is underscored by sophisticated notes of pencil shavings, graphite, smoky tobacco, and a hint of estuarine/oyster shell minerality.

  • Palate and Body: It is medium-to-full bodied with a suave, velvety texture. The palate is dense and concentrated yet maintains a "fabulous precision" and a "killer line of acidity." Flavors include bilberry, damson, and black cherry, with a touch of cocoa bean and mandarin.

  • Structure: The wine is framed by "finely chiseled" and "dusty" tannins. While opulent due to the vintage, it remains remarkably linear and poised, showing the "sharpness of a samurai sword."

  • Winemaking: Aged for 16 to 18 months in French oak barrels, of which 60% are brand new. The wine was produced using entirely gravity-fed processes for the first time.

  • ABV: 14.1%.

Accolades

The 2022 Léoville Barton has received elite scores across the board, ranking as #23 on the Vinous Top 100 of 2025:

  • Jeb Dunnuck: 98 points

  • Jane Anson: 98 points

  • James Suckling: 98 points

  • Robert Parker's Wine Advocate: 97+ points

  • Wine Spectator: 97 points

  • Vinous (Neal Martin): 97 points

  • Decanter: 96 points

Pricing and Availability

  • Average Price: Typically ranges from $110 to $145 per 750ml bottle, though it is often sold in cases of 6 or 12 as it is a highly collectible "Vin de Garde."

  • Market Value: It is frequently noted by critics as a "no-brainer buy" from the vintage due to its exceptional quality-to-price ratio compared to other Second Growths.

Serving and Drinking

  • Optimal Drinking Window: This is a wine built for the long term. While approachable from 2027 with significant decanting, it will reach its peak between 2030 and 2055–2070.

  • Food Pairing: Best served with classic meat dishes such as roast lamb with rosemary, grilled ribeye, or wild boar ragu. It also pairs well with hard, aged cheeses like Comté.

title: Cakebread Cellars Cabernet Sauvignon Dancing Bear Ranch 2021
bodyHtml:
From the Winemaker - "Our Dancing Bear Ranch is perched high above northern Napa Valley on the steep, rugged slopes of Howell Mountain. Planted in dry, rocky, volcanic soils elevated between 1,100 and 1,900 feet, the vines are subject to nearly 360 degrees of exposure to the elements. As a result, vines in this location are routinely stressed and yield small crops of intensely flavorful grapes. The vines are separated into 24 blocs based on sun exposure, soil profile, clonal selection and varietal type (cabernet sauvignon, merlot and cabernet franc). We precisely manage and irrigate the crop on each vine to achieve optimal flavour development and the extraordinary quality for which Dancing Bear Cabernet Sauvignon is renowned.

Our goal with Dancing Bear is to capture the intense mountain character of fruit from this unique site; small-lot wine making allows our winemaker to monitor extraction during fermentation so that each lot achieves just the right balance between fruit and tannin. Aging in French oak, barrels-predominantly new oak adds depth to this remarkable wine.

This big, dramatic wine has become a cult classic among Howell Mountain Cabernet Sauvignon lovers, including the bears who call this high-elevation estate home. This wine offers generous black cherry and fig aromas that carry over onto a concentrated, fleshy palate."

title: Tignanello 2022 (by Tenuta Tignanello)
bodyHtml:
Tignanello 2022 is an iconic red wine from Italy, specifically produced in the Tuscany region within the Chianti Classico subregion. The wine is crafted by the historic Marchesi Antinori family, who have been involved in Florentine winemaking for 27 generations since 1385. Tignanello is celebrated as the original 'Super Tuscan', a category it helped define upon its debut in 1971 by being the first Sangiovese based wine to be aged in barriques and one of the first in the region to eliminate white grapes from its blend.

Wine Description

This landmark wine presents an intense ruby red colour enhanced by purple highlights. The aromatic profile is complex and heady, offering a bouquet of red and black cherries, pomegranate, and violets, balanced by balsamic hints and suggestions of sweet pipe tobacco, vanilla, and loamy earth. On the palate, the wine is powerful and supple, delivering a dense core of blackcurrant and crème de violette fruit that is supported by velvety tannins and a vibrant mineral freshness. It finishes long and echoing with floral and fruity notes. The 2022 vintage is a blend composed of 78% Sangiovese, 18% Cabernet Sauvignon, and 4% Cabernet Franc. It has an alcohol content of 14% ABV and an optimal drinking window extending from 2026 through 2046.

Accolades

Wine Advocate - 98 points

James Suckling - 96 points

Kerin O'Keefe - 96 points

Vinous - 95 points

Food Pairing

The structural poise and savory intensity of Tignanello 2022 make it a classic partner for hearty Tuscan fare. It pairs exceptionally well with 'bistecca alla Fiorentina', wild boar ragù with pappardelle, or roast lamb seasoned with garlic and rosemary. The wine also complements rich meaty lasagne, venison tenderloin, and aged cheeses such as Pecorino Toscano.

Vintage Quality

The 2022 vintage in Tuscany was characterized by a warm growing season that tended to deliver wines with higher concentration, volume, and extra fruit weight. Despite rain episodes at the end of the season, the estate's steep and well draining hillsides allowed the fruit to achieve excellent phenolic maturity while maintaining a poised and elegant structure.

title: Lokoya Cabernet Sauvignon Spring Mountain District 2021
Penfolds St Henri Shiraz 2018
bodyHtml:
Penfolds St Henri Shiraz is a premium red wine from South Australia, primarily sourced from the Barossa Valley, McLaren Vale, and Clare Valley. Founded in 1844 by Dr. Christopher and Mary Penfold, the winery is one of Australia's oldest and most prestigious producers, now under the ownership of Treasury Wine Estates. St Henri is celebrated as an alternative expression of Australian Shiraz, defined by a winemaking philosophy that avoids new oak to showcase unadulterated fruit purity and regional character.

Wine Description

This garnet-red wine features a dark purple core and an intensely fragrant nose of blackberry, graphite, and roasted walnut, layered with 'fruits of the forest' such as strawberry flan and rhubarb tart. On the palate, it is full-bodied and savoury, offering a unique umami profile of Japanese nori and olive brine alongside fresh blueberry and exotic spices like turmeric and pimento. The structure is defined by tactile, 'Dutch cocoa' tannins and a long, mineral finish.

Food Pairing

The wine's savoury depth and structural complexity make it an ideal companion for rich, umami-forward dishes such as braised lamb shoulder with rosemary, beef short ribs with mushroom risotto, or seared duck breast with a cherry reduction.

title: Laroche Chablis Grand Cru Les Clos 2023
bodyHtml:
The influence of this exceptional terroir appears in the pure mineral character and the intensity of aromas. Quite restrained at first, this Grand Cru offers finesse, complexity and a superb length. 

Lush and shot through with lemon cake, apple and vanilla flavors, backed by a lively structure, this is long and nicely balanced in the end, with a lingering aftertaste of spice and citrus.

title: Nicolas Maillart Mont Martin Premier Cru 2019
bodyHtml:
Nicolas Maillart is one of the brightest shooting stars on the grower Champagne scene these days. Based in the small village of Ecueil in the central Montagne de Reims, the estate's vineyards are all Premier and Grand Cru classified. Although there is evidence of the family's involvement with vine growing going back more than 300 years, there is nothing old school going on here, or, for that matter, any resting on laurels.

The Mont Martin is a single varietal Pinot Meunier from the Premier Cru village of Villers-Allerand. Meunier is commonly known for its soft allure, but is perfectly capable of more structured and savoury expressions, which is exactly what this is. 

The wine was fermented and matured in neutral oak barrels on its fine lees for 9 months, before bottling and secondary fermentation. Disgorged after 3 years, without dosage. The oxidative influence from elevage in barrel clearly shows in the textural breadth and aromatic depth of the wine, though never to a point of heaviness or a lack of drive. Expect an assertive, mineral and saline wine, with scintillating freshness and purity.

title: Chateau Margaux 2012
bodyHtml:
Introduction

Château Margaux 2012 is a red wine from France, produced in the Bordeaux region and the Margaux appellation. Château Margaux is one of the most famous wines in the world and is classified as a Premier Grand Cru Classé (First Growth) in the 1855 Bordeaux Classification. The winery's philosophy is centred on producing wines that possess a rare combination of finesse, elegance, complexity, and intensity. The 2012 vintage was a top-class effort from the late Paul Pontallier and his team.

Wine Description

The wine has a dense ruby-purple colour. The aromatic profile is nuanced and refined, with wonderful aromas of flowers such as roses and violets. It possesses hints of spring flowers intermixed with blueberries, blackberries, and cassis fruit. Further notes include pencil lead, blond tobacco, cedar, and star anise.

The varietal composition is a blend of 87% Cabernet Sauvignon, 10% Merlot, 2% Cabernet Franc, and 1% Petit Verdot. This was made from only 34% of the overall harvest. The wine is medium bodied, though it became more structured and dense in the bottle than from the cask. The palate is graceful, silky, and finely tuned, with flavours of raspberry, redcurrant, and warm cherry confiture. It is guided by waves of fine, firm tannins, which are long-lived. Stylistically, it is an elegant, masculine, and refined wine, showcasing finesse and a life-affirming sense of balance. The ABV is 13.5%. It has a long, structured finish that shows minerals and chalk. The optimal drinking window is from 2023 through 2040, or even 2042. Information on the organic status of the wine is not available in the sources.

Accolades

  • Jane Anson - 97 points

  • Wine Advocate - 96 points

  • Decanter - 96 points

  • Wine Enthusiast - 95 points

  • James Suckling - 95 points

Food Pairing

Margaux wines pair well with a wide range of grilled, braised, or roasted meats, including beef, veal, lamb, pork, duck, and game. It is also excellent with roasted chicken, mushrooms, truffles, or other earthy dishes.

Vintage Quality

The 2012 vintage for Château Margaux was considered "almost" a great vintage, possessing purity, balance, and charm. The harvest of the reds took place between September 25th and October 16th, before the weather really deteriorated. Wineries with the financial capacity to rigorously sort the grapes produced the best wines.

title: La Chapelle d'Ausone 2020
bodyHtml:
La Chapelle d'Ausone 2020 originates from the prestigious Saint Émilion Grand Cru appellation in the Right Bank region of Bordeaux, France. The estate is under the dedicated stewardship of the Vauthier family, whose presence in Saint Émilion dates back to the 17th century. This second wine is crafted with the same artisanal philosophy as the grand vin, utilizing fruit from the estate’s historic limestone plateau and vines that average 50 years of age.

Wine Description

This deep garnet-purple wine offers a profound sensory profile. The nose is highly aromatic, revealing layers of black raspberries, wild blueberries, and cherries intertwined with nuances of violets, lavender, and incense. On the palate, the wine is medium to full bodied and energetic, showcasing a tightly knit structure with silky, 'chewy' tannins and a distinct mineral tension derived from the limestone soils. Notes of candied orange peel, licorice, and Indian spices lead to a long, saline finish.

Accolades

  • James Suckling - 95 points

  • Vinous - 95 points

  • Wine Enthusiast - 95 points

  • Decanter - 94 points

  • Wine Advocate - 92 points

Food Pairing

The structured yet fresh profile of this wine makes it a superb companion for classic meat dishes such as roasted lamb with rosemary, braised beef short ribs, or duck confit. Its earthy and spicy undertones also pair beautifully with mushroom risotto or aged hard cheeses like Comté.

title: Stag's Leap Wine Cellars Cabernet Sauvignon 'Fay' 2019
bodyHtml:
Considered one of the "first growths" of Napa Valley, Stag's Leap Wine Cellars produces renowned Cabernet Sauvignon from its historic Stags Leap District estate vineyards.

Fay Cabernet Sauvignon delivers fragrant aromas of ripe raspberry and boysenberry along with hints of jasmine, gardenia and nutmeg. The wine has a lively mouthfeel with polished tannins, a juicy mid-palate and a silky finish bursting with red fruits and berries.

Try pairing this estate-grown Cabernet with baby back ribs with saba glaze, maple-soy glazed salmon or eggplant parmesan.

97 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

Just about pure perfection, the 2019 Cabernet Sauvignon Fay reveals a vivid purple hue as well as spectacular aromatics of blueberries, black cherries, sappy herbs, and tobacco. Full-bodied and perfectly balanced, with a great mid-palate and building tannins, it’s another utterly classic Napa Valley Cabernet Sauvignon from this estate that will benefit from 4-5 years of bottle age and evolve for 2-3 decades.

95 Points - James Suckling

Concentrated, with lots of black and purple fruit and crushed violets. Broodingly dark and youthful at this stage, but remains elegant. Fleshy, dense and full-bodied with a mouthful of finely polished tannins that dissipate into the black fruit. Silky, opulent texture here, with fresh, medium acidity.

93 Points - Wine Spectator

Packed with bramble, blackberry and black currant pâte de fruit notes, this has good energy, while lacings of licorice and mocha fill out the finish. 

92+ Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2019 Cabernet Sauvignon Fay Vineyard offers a perfumed nose marked by delicate purple raspberry notes and a touch more herbal, tea-like nuances than the 2018. It's medium to full-bodied in the mouth but delicate and elegant, with a long, silky finish.

title: Joseph Drouhin Pommard 2023
bodyHtml:
This robust and "muscular" red wine originates from France, specifically within the Pommard appellation of the Côte de Beaune in Burgundy. Founded in 1880, Maison Joseph Drouhin is one of the most respected family-owned houses in the region, known for its extensive estate holdings and elegant style. The winery's philosophy is deeply committed to biodynamic and organic viticulture, having eliminated synthetic chemicals in the 1980s. For their Pommard, the Drouhin family sources fruit from diverse parcels to capture the village's reputation for producing the "most powerful" of all Burgundy wines.

Wine Description

Joseph Drouhin Pommard presents a deep, dark red appearance. The sensory profile is intense and "manly," featuring a nose of blackberries and bilberries, layered with sophisticated notes of musk, smoke, and occasionally dark chocolate or leather with age. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied and "upright," showcasing a firm structure with flavours of ripe dark fruit and earthy undertones. It is characterized by its strong tannins and a solid backbone that provides great longevity, leading to a lingering, savory finish. This 100% Pinot Noir typically reaches an ABV of 13% to 13.5% and is matured for 12 to 15 months in French oak (approximately 20% new). The estate is certified organic, with many sites managed biodynamically.

title: Colome 'Autentico' Malbec 2015 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
Bodega Colomé 'Auténtico' Malbec 2015 originates from Argentina, specifically from the Molinos region within the Calchaquí Valleys of Salta. Founded in 1831, Bodega Colomé is the oldest continuously operating winery in Argentina and is recognized as a pioneer in extreme-altitude viticulture. The 'Auténtico' label serves as a tribute to the winery’s pioneers and its original 19th-century winemaking style, sourced from a 90-year-old estate vineyard planted at 2,300 metres above sea level. The estate’s philosophy focuses on sustainable and biodynamic farming to achieve a pure expression of terroir with minimal intervention.

Wine Description

This red wine displays an intense purple colour, reflecting its high-altitude origins. The sensory profile is fragrant and concentrated, featuring a nose of red cherries and blackberries, complemented by floral notes of violet and elegant hints of spice, minerals, and jarilla. On the medium-to-full-bodied palate, it is described as juicy and silky with ripe, round tannins and a soft texture. The finish is remarkably long and fruity, showcasing the purity of the variety without the influence of wood.

  • Varietal Composition: 100% Malbec.

  • ABV: Typically 14.5%.

  • Organic Status: Produced using sustainable farming practices and indigenous yeast fermentation.

  • Stylistic Notes: 'Auténtico' is an unoaked expression matured for 10 months in tanks followed by 10 months in the bottle; it uses ancient techniques such as pigeage (punch-down) to retain freshness and fruit purity.

title: Bruno Giacosa Barolo Vigna le Rocche del Falletto 2019
bodyHtml:
One of the legendary winemakers of the world, Bruno Giacosa crafted the most prestigious single-vineyard Barolo and Barbaresco wines during a career that spanned nearly eight decades. 

Intense red garnet color. The bouquet is intense and elegant, with floral notes such as rose and fruity notes of blackcurrants, pomegranate and raspberries. On the palate it is structured with excellent tannic plot that enhances roundness and persistence.

98 Points - James Suckling

Gorgeous aromas of roses that fill the glass along with ripe strawberries, raspberries and forest fruits. Very structured and right with finely toned tannins that are tight, sleek and racy. 

96+ Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

With the white label, the 2019 Barolo Falletto Vigna Le Rocche is a generous and expansive wine that hits the palate from all sides. It offers lingering sensations of sweet fruit with a good amount of intensity and muscle power pushing from behind. That forward momentum is fueled by dark fruit, rusty earth, wet clay and blood orange. It shows elegance, substance and finely tuned tones with considerable tension and tightness.

95 Points - Wine Spectator

This round, rich red is laced with cherry, raspberry, iron, earth and underbrush aromas and flavors. There's a firm structure, with burly yet well-integrated tannins providing support and the ability to age. Overall, this is balanced and long, with a persistent aftertaste of fruit, mineral and savory notes.

title: Aia Vecchia Orleto Cabernet Franc 2021
bodyHtml:
This rare, monovarietal red wine originates from the Bolgheri region of Tuscany, Italy. Produced by Aia Vecchia, a winery founded in 1995 by the Pellegrini family, Orleto represents the culmination of decades of research into Cabernet Franc’s potential on the Tuscan coast. It is the winery's first new release in over 20 years, joining their established icons like Sor Ugo and Lagone. The vineyards are located at an elevation of 80 metres, benefiting from the region’s unique microclimate where sunlight is reflected off the Tyrrhenian Sea, allowing the grapes to reach optimal ripeness.

Wine Description

The Aia Vecchia Orleto is a bold and structured 100% Cabernet Franc. It presents a dark, sumptuous profile with an expressive nose of blackberry, plum, and mocha, layered with sophisticated notes of espresso, leather, tobacco, and incense. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied and rich, showcasing a plush, velvety texture and a core of dark fruit balanced by mineral and earthy depth. It is characterized by well-integrated but firm tannins and a long, persistent finish. The wine underwent a 30-day maceration in stainless steel followed by 24 months of aging in barrique and an additional 12 months in the bottle. It has a robust ABV of 15%.

title: E. Pira e Figli Chiara Boschis - Barolo 'Via Nuova' 2021
bodyHtml:
Produced in the heart of Piedmont, Italy, this wine is a masterfully crafted Barolo DOCG that represents a blend of fruit from six renowned vineyard sites across the Barolo, Monforte d'Alba, and Serralunga d'Alba subregions. The historic E. Pira e Figli estate was famously taken over in 1990 by Chiara Boschis, who became one of the first female winemakers in the region and a leader in the 'Barolo Boys' movement.

Wine Description

Via Nuova presents a luminous cherry red colour with medium transparency, characteristic of young, high-quality Nebbiolo. The nose is multi-layered and charming, offering a bouquet of ripe cherries, plums, and blood orange, interwoven with rose petals, mint, and delicate hints of cinnamon and almond. On the palate, this medium-bodied wine is bright and energetic, featuring a firm inner fiber and a lively acidity structure. The tannins are ripe and polished, leading into a long, persistent finish that lingers with notes of floral fruit pips and aniseed.

Accolades

  • "Wine Advocate - 96 points."

  • "Vinous - 96 points."

  • "James Suckling - 95 points."

Food Pairing

This wine is ideally suited for rich, savoury dishes such as Brasato al Barolo (Barolo-braised beef), ossobuco, or a decadent mushroom risotto. It also pairs beautifully with aged hard cheeses like Parmigiano Reggiano or Castelmagno, and traditional Piedmontese tajarin with truffles.

title: Alter Ego de Palmer 2019 (by Chateau Palmer)
bodyHtml:
Alter Ego de Palmer is the second wine of the Château Palmer, a Third Classified Growth from the Margaux appellation in Bordeaux, France. The estate is known for its high proportion of Merlot, giving its wines a supple and rich style that is closer to those of Pomerol and St-Émilion than typical Left Bank wines. Since 2004, the property has been managed by Thomas Duroux, who has spearheaded a move towards biodynamic farming, with the estate becoming fully certified biodynamic in 2017. Alter Ego was first produced in 1998, offering a different expression of the same terroir: a more spontaneous, round, and approachable wine with the same elegance and silky tannins as its older sibling.

Wine Description

The 2019 Alter Ego de Palmer has a deep garnet-purple colour. On the nose, it offers an explosive aromatic profile with notes of red fruits like raspberries and redcurrants, alongside hints of spring flowers. The wine's blend is 51% Merlot, 40% Cabernet Sauvignon, and 9% Petit Verdot. The palate is lively and refreshing, with a soft, long, and supple texture. It presents layers of blackcurrant, bilberry, and tobacco notes, with very precise but pliable tannins that are almost "feathery". The wine is medium- to full-bodied, with a beautiful balance of intensity and freshness. It is noted for its purity and aromatic clarity. The optimal drinking window is from 2025 to 2035.

Accolades

  • James Suckling - 96 points

  • Decanter - 94 points

  • Vinous - 93 points

Food Pairing

This wine is a versatile partner for a variety of classic dishes, including veal, pork, beef, lamb, duck, and game. It also pairs well with rich fish dishes like tuna, mushrooms, and pasta. This pairing highlights the wine's depth and character.

Vintage Quality

The 2019 vintage in Bordeaux was marked by a hot and dry summer, which was mitigated by cooler evenings that helped grapes retain acidity. Winemakers like Thomas Duroux demonstrated skill in adapting to the challenging conditions. The result was a vintage with concentrated, rich fruit that also maintains a remarkable sense of freshness and elegance.

title: Dominus Estate 2021
bodyHtml:
Dominus Estate, under the stewardship of Christian Moueix, is renowned for producing exceptional Bordeaux-style blends from its historic Napanook Vineyard in Napa Valley. The 2021 vintage stands as a testament to the estate's commitment to excellence, reflecting both the unique terroir and the meticulous winemaking practices employed.

Blend and Production

The 2021 Dominus is composed of 95% Cabernet Sauvignon and 5% Cabernet Franc. The growing season was characterized by a dry winter and spring, with total rainfall amounting to 14 inches, less than half the historical average. These conditions led to early hydric stress, promoting the development of small berries with concentrated flavors and phenolic compounds. Harvest took place from September 16 to October 1, 2021.

Tasting Notes

  • Appearance: Opaque purple-black hue.

  • Nose: Intense aromas of freshly crushed blackcurrants, blackberry preserves, and stewed plums, complemented by nuances of violets, licorice, tar, and a hint of cedar.

  • Palate: Full-bodied with a rich, dense texture. The wine reveals a complex interplay of dark fruits, floral notes, and savory elements, supported by firm yet polished tannins. The finish is long and layered, suggesting significant aging potential.

Critical Acclaim

  • Jeb Dunnuck: 100 points – "One of the legendary Dominus, the 2021 Cabernet Sauvignon is unquestionably in the same league as the 2018, 2016, 2015, 2013, 2010, and 1991, and to my mind, wine simply doesn't get any better."

  • The Wine Independent: 100 points – "Full-bodied with super integrated tannins that are wonderfully polished, giving a cashmere texture that is really luxurious to taste at this early stage."

  • James Suckling: 99 points – "The purity of the cabernet fruit is so enticing, with blackcurrant, rose petals, nettles, and subtle graphite."

Serving and Cellaring

While approachable in its youth after decanting, the 2021 Dominus will benefit from extended cellaring. Optimal drinking is anticipated between 2027 and 2050, allowing the wine to develop further complexity and integration.

title: Chateau Mouton Rothschild 2019
bodyHtml:
This legendary red wine originates from the Pauillac appellation on the Left Bank of the Gironde Estuary in Bordeaux, France. The estate was acquired in 1853 by Baron Nathaniel de Rothschild, but it was under the visionary leadership of his great-grandson, Baron Philippe de Rothschild, that it achieved global prominence, pioneering chateau bottling in 1924 and artist-designed labels in 1945. In 1973, it became the only winery ever elevated to First Growth status in the 1855 Bordeaux Classification; today, it remains under the dedicated ownership of the Rothschild family.

Wine Description

The 2019 Chateau Mouton Rothschild is an intense garnet red with a distinct purplish hue. The nose is highly expressive and precise, revealing aromas of cassis, blackberry, and black cherry mingled with rich layers of cedar, cigar wrapper, and violets, accented by mineral and liquorice undertones. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied, opulent, and multi-dimensional, enfolding powerful yet rounded tannins with a succulent sweetness and a core of fresh black fruit. It is characterized by an elegant, seamless profile and a long, resonant finish that features hints of graphite and spices. This blend consists of 90% Cabernet Sauvignon, 9% Merlot, and 1% Petit Verdot, with an ABV of 13.5%. While the estate follows meticulous hand-farming and sustainable practices, the wine is not certified organic.

Food Pairing

This robust First Growth is best paired with high-quality meat dishes such as a perfectly grilled entrecôte, roast beef, or a rack of lamb with rosemary. Its structured tannins and complex fruit profile also complement game meats like venison and wild boar, as well as rich, earthy dishes featuring truffles or porcini mushrooms. For a cheese course, it pairs excellently with hard, aged varieties such as Comté or vintage Cheddar.

Vintage Quality

The 2019 vintage in Pauillac is considered exceptional, beginning with a record-warm winter followed by a summer that balanced extreme heatwaves with welcome rain in July and August. These conditions, followed by a long, clear harvest period, allowed the Cabernet Sauvignon to achieve optimal ripeness and high sugar concentration while retaining essential acidity. The resulting wines are noted for their self-balancing ability, offering both power and a refined, satin-smooth structural elegance.

title: Fattoria Le Pupille Saffredi 2022
bodyHtml:
The Fattoria Le Pupille Saffredi is a red wine from Tuscany, Italy, known for its rich, dark fruit flavors and complex profile. It is a blend of Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, and Petit Verdot.

  • Grape Varieties: 60% Cabernet Sauvignon, 30% Merlot, and 10% Petit Verdot.  

  • Aroma: Notes of blackcurrants, blackberries, plums, violets, oak spices, and Mediterranean herbs.  Flavor: Dense and velvety on the palate, with firm tannins and juicy freshness. 

  • Style: A Bordeaux-style blend, known for its depth, elegance, and aging potential.  

  • Aging: The wine is aged for 18 months in French oak barriques, with 75% new oak.  

  • Tasting Notes: The wine is described as having a complex flavor profile with a good balance of fruit, tannins, and oak.

title: Albert Brenot Corton Les Chaumes Grand Cru 2018
bodyHtml: Founded in 1849 by Albert Brenot in Savigny-lès-Beaune, Doudet-Naudin is one of the oldest Burgundy wine Maisons. In 1933 it was acquired by the Doudet family, who have developed and expanded the Maison while preserving its fundamental values: respect for traditions and excellence. Christophe Rochet, the current head of Doudet-Naudin, is committed to maintaining the values of this well-respected Maison while restructuring it.

title: Continuum Novicium 2019
bodyHtml:
Novicium displays its predecessors' signature approachability with a fresh and playful nose of red fruit and candied apple mixed with autumn leaves, bay laurel and the slightest hint of dewy spring peonies. A vibrant and direct wine, Novicium has a plush entry and weighted mid-palate of dark chocolate, black fruit, brown spice and tapenade. A friendly and powerful vintage character, with Sage Mountain Vineyard's iron core and a brightly expressed structure and finish.

96 Points - James Suckling

Very fruity on the nose with black cherries, blueberries and graphite. Full-bodied with a middle palate of ripe fruit and dark chocolate. Iron, too. Soft tannins and a flavorful finish. Layered.

title: Cain Five 2009
bodyHtml:
The Cain Vineyard site is truly spectacular, cradled in a bowl overlooking St. Helena from the top of the Spring Mountain District. In 1980, Joyce and Jerry Cain purchased part of the McCormick Ranch, a homestead dating back to the 1840's. The Cains were in search of a unique mountain property where they could realize their dream of planting the five classical Bordeaux varietals from which to draw one ideally structured wine, which would result as a blend of all five varieties.

96 Points - James Suckling

A fascinating wine with dark berries, spice, sliced raw meat and minerals. Black berries. It changes all the time. Full body with spice, black pepper, blueberry, mushroom and walnut.

title: Domaine Faiveley Corton Charlemagne Grand Cru 2020
bodyHtml:
Founded in 1825, Bourgognes Faiveley has been handed down from father to son for over 175 years. As the sixth generation to take the reins, Francois Faiveley manages, with equal amounts passion and competence, the largest family domaine in Burgundy. Methodically reconstructing vineyards fractured by French inheritance laws, Bourgognes Faiveley today owns more appellations in their entirety (monopoles) than any other domaine in Burgundy.

The nose reveals oaky, fruity and floral notes. The palate is concentrated and well-balanced with excellent aromatic persistency. The rich aromas make this Grand Cru enjoyable in its youth although it only develops its full character after a few years of bottle age. An exceptional wine with depth and minerality.

Serve with veal, sweetbreads with morel mushrooms, salmon in a sorrel sauce, grilled lobster.

94+ Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2020 Corton-Charlemagne Grand Cru has turned out especially well, opening in the glass with aromas of pear, peach, white flowers, freshly baked bread, nutmeg and hazelnuts. Full-bodied, layered and multidimensional, it's unusually textural and broad-shouldered for this Ladoix-derived cuvee, displaying bright acids and chalky structuring extract.

title: La Spinetta Barbaresco Gallina 2022
bodyHtml: This wine is ruby red and has hints of ripe raspberry, gardenia and blackcurrant aromas. On the palate it has a full-flavored start, with mineral notes and a good presence of soft tannins. The finish is long and persistent.

title: Castello Di Ama Chianti Classico Gran Selezione 'San Lorenzo' 2022 - 3 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
Originating from Italy in the Tuscany region, specifically within the Chianti Classico Gran Selezione DOCG appellation in Gaiole in Chianti, Castello di Ama Chianti Classico Gran Selezione 'San Lorenzo' 2022 represents an historic, benchmark estate expression of Tuscan terroir. Named after the picturesque valley where the historic 18th century estate villas stand, 'San Lorenzo' is crafted from a rigorous selection of fruit sourced from the estate’s four premier historic vineyard sites: Bellavista, Casuccia, San Lorenzo, and Montebuoni. Situated at high elevations between 460 and 525 metres above sea level on gravel-rich clay-limestone soils, the vines benefit from exceptional diurnal temperature variations. The winemaking philosophy under technical director Marco Pallanti involves parcel-by-parcel manual harvesting, ambient yeast fermentation in stainless steel vats, and maturation in fine French oak barriques (approximately 22% new) for around 10 to 12 months. The result is a Gran Selezione of extraordinary harmony, vibrant red and black fruit concentration, and sublime Gaiole freshness.

Wine Description

The wine presents an opaque, deep dark ruby red colour with bright purple-garnet reflections along the rim. An expressive, highly complex bouquet opens with noble aromas of ripe black cherry, wild strawberry, dark plum, and elderberry, interwoven with sophisticated notes of crushed violet petals, sandalwood, dried lavender, cinnamon spice, graphite, and leather. On the palate, it is medium-to-full bodied, ample, and dense, delivering concentrated flavours of dark fruit, cassis, and mineral earth, all supported by a bright, mouthwatering spine of natural acidity. Framed by taut, supple, finely knit tannins and a driving mid-palate structure, it concludes with an extraordinarily long, persistent finish marked by lingering red berries, savory herbs, and a clean chalky mineral grip. Composed of 80% Sangiovese blended with 13% Merlot and 7% Malvasia Nera, this 2022 release offers an optimal drinking window of 2027–2045. Stylistically, it combines grand cru-like refinement and aromatic complexity with impressive vintage depth, structure, and cellaring capability.

title: Pio Cesare Barbaresco 2018
bodyHtml:
A very classical style Barbaresco: elegance and velvety, with ripe and spicy fruit. Strong tannins, but elegant. Good structure and concentration. Very long life.

94 Points - James Suckling

Strawberries with hints of walnuts, asphalt and bark. Dried flowers, too. Full-bodied with fine, racy tannins and a very long, pretty finish. Refined tannins. Shows excellent length for the vintage.

93 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Pio Cesare excels when it comes to the classics, and this wine is one of those. The 2018 Barbaresco (released one year later compared to its peers) delivers some mild candied raspberry ripeness with lilac, tarry smoke, cedarwood and spice. The mouthfeel is silky smooth with softly integrated tannins.

title: Chateau d'Issan 2015
bodyHtml:
Chateau d’Issan is in the heart of the Margaux appellation, a truly privileged location, which explains the outstanding quality of its wines. The mild weather, regulated by being close to the sea and the Gironde Estuary, provides ideal conditions for vine growth. The vines at Chateau d’Issan benefit from close, on-going care designed to produce perfectly ripe grapes. Everything is organized so that each individual plot can be tended independently in order to get the very best out of its fruit.

Chateau d’Issan shows a medium crimson color with purple tints and is fresh, fruity and floral on the nose. It offers black currant and black plums aromas with pleasant hints of licorice. The tannins are round and soft. This wine is very structured and elegant and delivers a long as well as fresh finish.

96 Points - James Suckling

Very complex aromas of currants, blackberries and iodine with hints of dried mushrooms and flowers. Full-bodied, very fine and silky with a very, very long finish. Shows tension and finesse. Structured yet shows an ultra-fine texture. Deep, dense center palate, yet it's all so polished.

95 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

Offering a spectacular bouquet of blackcurrants, lead pencil, chocolate and espresso, this full-bodied, incredibly sexy Margaux boast sweet, sweet tannin, lots of oak, a stacked mid-palate and a huge finish.

93+ Points - Wine Enthusiast

This is a serious, structured wine. It has plenty of black plum flavor, although the firm tannins will play an important part in its development. The ample acidity and fresh finish are other harbingers for the wine's good future. 

93 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

93 Points - Decanter

title: Les Forts de Latour 2010
bodyHtml:
96 Points - James Suckling

Aromas of currants, blueberries and blackberries with a dark chocolate undertone. Perfumes and beautiful. Full body, with velvety tannins that are fine-tuned and tentative. It lasts for minutes. Gorgeous fruit and richness. Perhaps the greatest Les Fort ever?

95 Points - Wine Spectator

A solid, briary, grippy, tarry Pauillac, with a sappy edge to the kirsch, blackberry, plum skin and steeped fig notes, liberally laced with anise and tar. Shows good energy through the finish, with a cassis bush note echoing.

94 Points - Wine Enthusiast
