Powerful, yet beautiful and smoothly structured. It has ripe, rich fruits, spice and sweet acidity. As a contrast, there is a dense core of tannins where the wine shows some severity and youth.

title: Tardieu Laurent Cote Rotie 2016
bodyHtml:
Tardieu Laurent is one of the top Rhone wine negociant firms. They are one of the few domaines that strives to use biodynamic farming techniques. Tardieu Laurent is not shy about using new oak, or modern winemaking techniques. Many of their wines are very modern in style. As Tardieu Laurent makes wine from purchased fruit, they focus on obtaining the best sources possible.

94 Points Wine Spectator ... Tightly wound, with a solid core of dark currant, raspberry and blackberry reduction notes, laced with sweet tobacco, singed mesquite and sanguine details. Shows piercing focus on the finish, with serious length as the mineral edge lingers. Best from 2021 through 2035.

94 Points Wine Enthusiast... This beautifully structured Côte-Rôtie balances ripe, concentrated black-cherry and plum flavors against elegant notes of fresh thyme, rosemary and bacon. It's penetrating and freshly fruited but vibrantly balanced in acidity. The finish is long, edged by finely integrated but gripping tannins.

title: Marchesi di Barolo 'Barolo Sarmassa' 2019
bodyHtml:
The Marchesi di Barolo 'Barolo Sarmassa' hails from the prestigious Barolo DOCG in the Piedmont region of Northern Italy. Established in 1814 by Juliette Colbert de Maulévrier and Carlo Tancredi Falletti, the estate is widely considered the birthplace of modern Barolo. Since 1929, the Abbona family has stewarded this legacy, maintaining a winemaking philosophy that marries historic traditions with modern precision. The Sarmassa vineyard is a significant site characterized by its southeast exposure and complex Tortonian and Serravallian soils, which provide a unique blend of clay, silt, and stones that naturally limits vine vigour and ensures optimal grape ripening.

Wine Description

This Barolo presents an intense ruby red hue with brilliant garnet highlights. The sensory profile is deep and captivating, opening with a bouquet of candied red fruits, dog rose, and violet, layered with sophisticated notes of licorice, vanilla, and sweet tobacco. On the palate, the wine is full bodied and elegantly structured, showcasing a beautiful concentration of ripe berries and earthy minerality. Its tannins are finely chiseled and prominent, balanced by a fresh acidity that leads into a long, lingering finish marked by spicy and woody accents.

Food Pairing

The wine's robust structure and complex aromatics make it a perfect match for braised red meats, wild game, and traditional Piedmontese dishes like porcini risotto or agnolotti with meat sauce. It also pairs exceptionally well with aged cheeses such as Castelmagno, Parmigiano Reggiano, or Pecorino.

title: Chateau Margaux 2000
bodyHtml:
They were unaware at that time that they were harvesting one of the greatest vintages of the late 20th century. The grapes had rarely, perhaps never, been as concentrated, particularly the Cabernets. In certain cases they surpassed the already historic levels of the 1986 and 1995 vintages, with an elegance and softness on the palate, reminiscent also of the 1990 and 1996 vintages. It seemed in fact that 2000 was setting a new benchmark in quality, never before attained, at least in terms of style. Throughout the barrel ageing time, these first impressions were gradually confirmed. The wine has now acquired a slightly tighter texture and at the same time keeps such a soft and especially long finish that it seems to go on forever. The bottling took place in November 2002, after over 2 years of barrel ageing. Such a long ageing is unusual but not as rare as one might think. Most of the greatest vintages are aged for that length of time.

100 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Absolutely compelling in two tastings of this vintage, the 2000 Margaux is composed of 90% Cabernet Sauvignon and 10% Merlot. The extraordinary seductiveness, complex aromatics, and purity it exhibits lead me to believe it has reached its window of full maturity. Medium-bodied, with layers of concentration, stunning blue, red, and black fruits intermixed with spring flowers, a subtle dosage of new oak, and a distinctive personality that is elegant while at the same time powerful and substantial, this is a multi-dimensional wine that was extremely approachable and drinkable in both tastings I had of it. The colour remains a healthy, even opaque bluish/purple, but there is no reason to hesitate to drink it. It should evolve for another 30-40 years, so there is no hurry either.

title: Chateau Angelus 2014
bodyHtml:
The vineyard of Chateau Angelus is situated in a natural amphitheatre overlooked by the three Saint-Emilion churches. In the middle of this special site, the sounds were amplified and the angelus bells could be heard ringing in the morning, at midday and in the evening. They cadenced the working day in the vineyards and villages, calling the men and women to stop their labours for a few minutes and pray.

This vintage has a very pure, elegant nose. The attack is clear, and the wine progressively gets bigger, reaching a very sophisticated balance between the magnificent quality of the tannins, substance, tension and freshness. There is 50% Cabernet Franc in the blend, which elevates the elegance of the wine’s tannic structure and makes the finish complex and long.

97 Points - Wine Enthusiast

Effectively half-and-half Merlot and Cabernet Franc, this is a tremendous wine. With very fine tannins, spice from a touch of wood and swathes of ripe fruits give this wine its concentration and its huge potential. The wine has weight and a dark, dense structure that will allow it to age for many years. 

96 Points - James Suckling

Wow. This is really decadent and fascinating with forest flowers, chocolate, tea and currants on the nose, which follows through to a firm and silky palate with lots of fruit and balance. Very long and beautiful. Citrusy undertones.

95 Points - Wine Spectator

This has a dense, muscular core of warm blackberry, black currant and fig paste flavors, shrouded under a cloak of tobacco and loam. Not shy on toast and balanced by a hefty ganache edge, this isn't heady at all, just a terrific expression of the muscular, loamy style.

95 Points - Decanter

94+ Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

title: Joseph Phelps 'Insignia' 2019 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
Highly rated! The 2019 Insignia is made with 93% Cabernet Sauvignon, 5% Petit Verdot and 2% Malbec. The vineyard sources this year include 32% Yountville (Oak Knoll District), 23% Banca Dorada (Rutherford), 14% Suscol (South Napa Valley), 14% Home Ranch (St. Helena), 12% Las Rocas (Stags Leap District), 3% Barboza (Stags Leap District) and 2% El Venadito (Oak Knoll District). The wine is aging for 24 months in 100% new French oak barrels.

The 2019 Insignia is made with 93% Cabernet Sauvignon, 5% Petit Verdot and 2% Malbec. The vineyard sources this year include 32% Yountville (Oak Knoll District), 23% Banca Dorada (Rutherford), 14% Suscol (South Napa Valley), 14% Home Ranch (St. Helena), 12% Las Rocas (Stags Leap District), 3% Barboza (Stags Leap District) and 2% El Venadito (Oak Knoll District). The wine is aging for 24 months in 100% new French oak barrels.

98 Points - James Suckling

A very aromatic Insignia with pencil-shaving and graphite highlights the dark fruit and blackberries. Full-bodied, yet tensioned and vertical, with very fine tannins that run deep and layered in the wine, fantastic tension and structure.

(96-98) Points - Robert Parker Wine Advocate

The 2019 Insignia is composed of 93% Cabernet Sauvignon, 5% Petit Verdot and 2% Malbec. Deep garnet-purple in colour, it needs a little swirling to unlock a gorgeous perfume of black cherry compote, stewed plums and blackcurrant pastilles with hints of bay leaves, red roses, underbrush and pencil lead plus a hint of menthol. Medium to full-bodied, the palate delivers impactful black fruit preserves layers with finely grained tannins and seamless freshness, finishing long and layered.

(96-98) Points - Jeb Dunnuck

The 2019 Insignia offers a gorgeous perfume of crème de cassis, chocolate, lavender, dried flowers, tobacco, and leafy herbs. Possessing full-bodied richness, a layered, seamless texture, gorgeous tannins, and just a classy, balanced character, this beauty is going to shine with just 3-4 years of bottle age yet still cruise in cold cellars for 30 years. It actually reminds me slightly of the 1997 vintage. 

94 Points - Wine Spectator

A solidly built Cabernet with a very direct persona, as dark currant, warmed fig reduction and blackberry fruit paste are bolted together with licorice root and singed cedar. Features an espresso crema hint on the finish, which keeps this on the dark, muscular side. Cabernet Sauvignon, Petit Verdot and Malbec. Best from 2023 through 2038.

title: Bruno Giacosa Falletto Barbaresco Rabaja 2021
bodyHtml:
This prestigious and monumental red wine originates from the Rabajà MGA in the village of Barbaresco, Piedmont. Bruno Giacosa, often referred to as the "Prophet of Neive," was one of the greatest winemakers in history, known for his uncompromising standards and ability to select the finest fruit in the region. The Rabajà bottling comes from the estate's Falletto property, specifically a small 0.60-hectare plot with a southwest exposure that produces some of the most powerful and structured wines in the appellation.

Wine Description

The Bruno Giacosa Falletto Barbaresco Rabajà presents a deep red garnet colour with light orange highlights at the rim. The sensory profile is exceptionally complex and "saturating," featuring an aromatic nose of cherry, plum, and wild berries, layered with sophisticated notes of violets, mint, tobacco, and licorice root. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied and muscular, showcasing a "solid spine" of firm, velvety tannins and a vibrant acidity that ensures immense longevity. It is characterized by its remarkable consistency and length, leading to a persistent finish marked by minerality, flint, and savory elements. This 100% Nebbiolo has an ABV of 14.5% and underwent 25 days of maceration in oak vats, followed by 19 months of aging in oak barrels and 17 months in the bottle before release.

title: Chateau Latour Premier Grand Cru Classe 2013
bodyHtml:
93 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate     Composed of 95.2% Cabernet Sauvignon, 4.4% Merlot and 0.4% Petit Verdot, the 2013 Latour offers an open-knit, fragrant nose of liquorice, sandalwood, rose petals and cigar box over a core of Black Forest cake, stewed plums, mulberries and redcurrant jelly, plus a waft of cast-iron pan. The elegantly styled, medium-bodied palate (13% alcohol) fills the mouth with intense red and black berry preserves layers, framed by evolved, soft-textured tannins and well-knit freshness, finishing long and spicy. This vintage does not have the power and backbone of an outstanding vintage of Latour, but it is aging gracefully and, still possessing a lot of discernible fruit with plenty of tertiary pizazz, is absolutely delicious to drink right now. This sweet-spot stage is likely to continue for another 5-7 years, before the wine plateaus at a maturity peak and holds for a further 15+ years.

92+ Points - James Suckling     This is really racy with ultra-fine tannins. Pretty mint, currants, blackberries and fresh. Full body, with firm tannins and a long and intense finish. Finesse and textured. Tannic backbone.

90+ Points - Wine Spectator     Tight and primal, with a taut plum pit and iron frame around a core of red currant, cherry and raspberry fruit. Flecks of white pepper line the finish, which features a long iron spine that shows an impressive cut. Comes up short on flesh, but the precision is there, offering echoes of pomegranate, blood orange and bitter cherry allied to the minerality. Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot and Petit Verdot. Tasted non-blind.

title: Chateau Mouton Rothschild 2009
bodyHtml:
Chateau Mouton Rothschild, situated in the esteemed Pauillac appellation of Bordeaux, is a Premier Cru Classe estate renowned for its exceptional wines. The estate spans 84 hectares (207 acres) of vines, with Cabernet Sauvignon, first planted there in the early 19th century, reaching its finest expression.

Wine Description

The 2009 vintage presents a very deep, almost black colour with glittering highlights. The stylish and complex nose offers a wide array of aromas, including bilberry, blackcurrant, and blond tobacco, mingling with subtle cedarwood and spice. On the palate, the wine immediately shows all its density and refinement: very forward ripe fruit flavours are perfectly integrated with patrician, well-rounded tannins, revealing remarkable structure and balance. The opulent and long finish confirms the very great success of this Mouton Rothschild, fully expressing the exceptional qualities of the 2009 vintage.

Accolades

  • Wine Advocate – 99 points: "Opulently textured and full-bodied with gorgeous levels of creme de cassis, melted licorice, espresso roast, and chocolate. It possesses high but sweet, velvety tannins, massive body, and fabulous purity as well as length."

  • Vinous – 97 points: "The 2009 Mouton-Rothschild has a more refined bouquet compared to the 2009 Latour, with scents of blackberry, graphite, undergrowth, and hints of pressed rose petals. The palate is medium-bodied with a rounded entry. The intense black fruit is laced with pencil shaving and white pepper notes. This is a multi-dimensional First Growth with a very persistent finish."

Food Pairing

This wine's depth and complexity make it an excellent match for richly flavoured dishes such as roasted lamb with rosemary, beef Wellington, or aged hard cheeses. These pairings highlight the wine's depth and character.

title: Chateau Pontet Canet 2014
bodyHtml:
98 Points - James Suckling
 
A stunning wine for this vintage although it’s still a bit shy on the nose with more spice than fruit showing than now. There’s wet earth, too, but on the palate it’s bursting with ripe yet subtle flavours. Very long and complex finish that goes on and on.
 
96 Points - Decanter
 
Classic Cabernet nose of cassis. Lovely purity and depth with a silky texture that caresses the palate, more obviously Pontet-Canet than Pauillac. An extremely fine wine almost in a class of its own.

title: Dom Perignon Brut 2012- 3 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
Dom Pérignon is a prestigious Champagne from France. It is produced in the Champagne region, with the historic Abbey of Saint Pierre d'Hautvillers considered the birthplace of Champagne. The brand's legacy is tied to the Benedictine monk Dom Pierre Pérignon, who worked at the Hautvillers Abbey starting in 1668.

Wine Description

In the glass, it typically presents a luminous golden hue. The bouquet is complex, mingling white flowers, apricot, and mirabelle plums with fresher notes of rhubarb and mint, and mineral elements like ash. The wine's mouthfeel is elegant yet vibrant, offering a foundation that is refined and silky. On the palate, there is an immediate sensation of energy and tonicity, with a finish marked by penetrating tautness, often revealing flavours of citrus, nutty characteristics, and toasted accents. 

Food Pairing

Traditional pairings include shellfish, such as oysters, crab, and lobster. It also beautifully complements dishes like freshly made sushi, fried chicken, or caviar.

title: Borgogno Barolo Cannubi 2019
bodyHtml:
The Borgogno Barolo Cannubi 2019 is made from 100% Nebbiolo grapes, often displaying an intense ruby red colour. On the nose, it offers a captivating plot of red fruits, spices, and an ethereal floral nature of roses and violets, or notes of baked cherry, pine, and savory porcini. Some note ripe fruit with aromas of dried cherry skin or plum, while others find notes of framboise, fresh leather, licorice, and rosemary. The palate is full-bodied, yet elegant, deep, and broad, with juicy fruits and fine spices. Stylistic notes include a balance between vigor and grace, with a fresh floral finish, a forward-driving acidity, and sweet, persistent, and refined tannins. The wine is characterized by power and shows intensity and focus, remaining refined and elegant. Made with organically farmed grapes, it is noted to be one of the most approachable single cru wines in this vintage. The optimal drinking window is quite wide, with recommendations to drink from 2025–2050 or to try after 2028.

Accolades

  • 'Kerin O’Keefe - 98 points.'

  • 'Jeb Dunnuck - 97 points.'

  • 'James Suckling - 95 points.'

  • 'Wine Advocate - 93 points.'

  • 'Vinous - 92 points.'

  • 'Decanter - 92 points.'

Food Pairing Suggested pairings are tailored to the wine's broad structure and high acidity, making it an ideal companion for robust and complex dishes.

  • Braised meats, such as beef braised in Barolo or stewed game

  • Roast red meats, especially big pieces of steak or venison

  • Mature cheeses of great character like Parmigiano Reggiano aged over 30 months or Castelmagno

  • Traditional Piedmontese dishes, such as brasato (braised meat), tajarin al ragù (thin egg pasta with a meat sauce), or mushroom/truffle risotto

This pairing highlights the wine's depth and character.

title: Domaine Michel Gros Chambolle Musigny 2019
bodyHtml:
93 Points - Wine Spectator

Presents pure black cherry, blackberry and violet flavours, which permeate this sleek red. Linear in profile, with enough flesh for balance and charm. Tightens up on the long finish, which shows dashes of fruit and earth. Best from 2024.

Passionate but also very rigorous, Michel Gros brings constant care to the development of his wines by mastering all the stages of production, from vine through to bottling. Modest and unassuming, he expresses himself through his wines: generous, delicate, elegant, of reliable and even quality.

title: Blason d'Issan 2018 (by Chateau d'Issan)
bodyHtml:
94 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

Blackberry, blueberry, graphite, clove, tobacco and mahogany on the nose. It’s medium-to full-bodied with firm, fine-grained tannins. Very tight and refined with a mineral finish. Pretty finesse and focus. Second wine. 

93+ Points - James Suckling

Very intense and tannic with a compact palate of blue fruit, such as blueberries. Full-bodied. Tight and powerful at the finish.  

90 Points - Decanter

With a lot of upfront tannic bite, this definitely benefits from five minutes in the glass to show the cassis and charcoal notes. A bitter dark chocolate washes over the finish, again showing that these are big tannins.

title: Dunn Vineyards Cabernet Sauvignon Howell Mountain 2018 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
High atop Howell Mountain, nestled among 150-year-old fir trees, is Dunn Vineyards. Since 1979 the Dunn's have been producing Cabernet Sauvignon. Their total production is now at 4500 cases, split between the Howell Mountain and Napa Valley appellations.

This signature wine contains only fruit farmed on Howell Mountain. The wine comes in a distinctive bottle that is hand dipped in red wax. Aged 32 months in 100% new French oak.

97 Points - Vinous

The 2018 Cabernet Sauvignon Howell Mountain is elegant, deep and classy. Inky dark purplish fruit, savory herbs, menthol, licorice and spice. The purity of the fruit is remarkable today. There is plenty of youthful Howell Mountain tannin, so readers will have to be patient. Bright floral accents lift the red/purplish berry fruit nicely. This is such an expressive, alluring Cabernet.

96 Points - Wine Spectator

Ripe and very juicy, with a youthfully compact set of plum, boysenberry and blackberry compote flavors wrapped in licorice and violet notes. This is both racy and grippy, showing serious power but with the freshness and drive to match. Delivers a long, iron accent that scores the fruit through the finish. Best from 2024.

95+ Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2018 Cabernet Sauvignon Howell Mountain is a typically long-term proposition, coated in dusty tannins and cedary oak. It will take time for the cassis, blueberry and slightly pine-scented backbone of this wine to emerge, as for the moment it's almost difficult to taste. Yes, the concentration is present, the tannins are almost silky-ripe, but the structure of this medium to full-bodied wine is unassailable. Hands off for at least five years, and probably more, to judge by how past vintages have evolved.

title: Heitz Cellar Cabernet Sauvignon Martha's Vineyard 2016
bodyHtml:
#3 Wine Spectator Top 100 of 2021
 
96 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate
 
The 2016 Cabernet Sauvignon Martha's Vineyard barely hints at eucalyptus on the nose, with much more emphasis given to black cherries and cassis. This is full-bodied and rich, nicely balancing richness and texture against linear shape and focus and picking up hints of blueberries and spice on the long, mouthwatering finish. 
 
95 Points - Wine Spectator
 
This throws off an overt and alluring mint aroma, while sweet bay leaf, violet, damson plum, red tea and steeped griotte notes all glide through together, carried by remarkably fine-grained tannins. Ends with a gentle echo of mint on the finish, while subtle minerality chimes through as well. A stylish wine, with plenty of charm now, but also a pristine balance for cellaring. Best from 2022 through 2038.

title: Jean Louis Chave Hermitage Rouge 'Farconnet' 2021
bodyHtml:
Introduction

JL Chave Sélection Hermitage Rouge 'Farconnet' 2020 is an elegant red wine from France, hailing from the prestigious Hermitage appellation in the Northern Rhône Valley. The Chave family are legendary vignerons who have been tending vines in the region since 1481, spanning 16 generations. While the family's domaine wines are among the world's most sought-after, the 'JL Chave Sélection' label was created by Jean-Louis Chave to offer an accessible but refined expression of the region's diverse terroirs through both estate-grown and long-term contract fruit. The name 'Farconnet' honours the nobleman who sold the Chave family their first parcel in the Bessards vineyard during the 19th century.

Wine Description

The 2020 'Farconnet' presents a saturated violet to inky ruby colour. The aromatic profile is classic and expressive, featuring cracked pepper, lavender, and smoky bacon interwoven with vibrant scents of blackberry, boysenberry, and candied violet. On the palate, the wine is juicy and energetic, offering a harmonious blend of dark fruit, liquorice, and olive paste underpinned by a deep core of minerality. It is crafted from 100% Syrah sourced from three distinct parcels on the Hermitage hill: Diognières for spice, Péleat for finesse, and Greffieux for structure. The wine is aged in oak barrels for 18 to 24 months, resulting in fine-grained tannins and a penetrating, persistent finish. This balanced and focused frame is accessible now but possesses the potential to age gracefully through 2034.

Accolades

  • Vinous – 95 points

  • Wine Spectator – 94 points

title: Enzo Boglietti Barolo Case Nere 2019
bodyHtml: Deep, dark ruby colour. Very intense bouquet of red and black fruit, sweet spice and fine oak. A full-bodied Barolo with soft tannins and a pleasant spicy finish. Approachable now and with very good aging potential.

title: Chateau Cordeillan Bages 2005
bodyHtml:
Introduction

This red wine originates from the prestigious Pauillac appellation in Bordeaux, France. Chateau Cordeillan Bages is a small, distinct estate owned by the Cazes family, who are also renowned for Chateau Lynch Bages. The vineyard covers only two hectares situated near the Relais & Châteaux hotel of the same name, producing a boutique wine that benefits from the same expert team and meticulous care as its famous neighbour.

Wine Description

The Chateau Cordeillan Bages 2005 exhibits a deep ruby colour that suggests its concentration and maturity. The nose offers a complex bouquet of black fruit, particularly blackberry and blackcurrant, intermingled with notes of spice, earth, and a hint of chocolate. On the palate, it is medium to full-bodied with a soft, round mouthfeel and tannins that have softened over time, leading to a smooth, elegant finish. This blend comprises 80% Cabernet Sauvignon and 20% Merlot. It has reached its peak drinking window and is best enjoyed now. The alcohol by volume (ABV) is 13%.

Food Pairing

This wine's developed structure and savoury depth make it a classic match for roasted red meats, such as a ribeye steak with beef dripping or a traditional roast lamb. It also pairs well with comforting dishes like shepherd's pie or a selection of aged hard cheeses like Cheddar or Comté.

Vintage Quality

The 2005 vintage in Bordeaux is widely considered legendary, characterized by a warm, dry growing season that allowed for perfect ripening across all grape varieties. The weather conditions produced small, concentrated berries with thick skins, resulting in wines with exceptional depth, structure, and aging potential.

title: Domaine Anne F. Gros Pommard Premier Cru 'Les Pezerolles' 2024
bodyHtml:
This wine is a seamless, supple, superb expression of Pommard with density yet a soft luscious finish that belies its position on the Beaune border.

Medium deep colour, offering a soft but powerful bouquet, with the fruit lifting attractively. Fills the mouth very well, with Pommard’s solid style. Some darker fruit at the back, the tannins being folded in to the flesh. Good length. Not too far from being approachable. There is a pretty little touch of ripe but balanced fruit at the back.

title: Piper Heidsieck Brut 2014
bodyHtml:
Since its founding in 1785, the House of Piper-Heidsieck has proven its innovative prowess in selecting and blending wines of exception. A quest for excellence and open-mindedness are reflected in the entire range of champagnes created by Chief Winemaker Emilien Boutillat, serve as guarantor the Piper-Heidsieck style.

Piper-Heidsieck Vintage 2014 is a refined and intense champagne, a stunning expression of a brilliant vintage. 

“Vintage 2014 expresses a perfect balance between spicy, warm aromas and remarkable freshness on the palate,” Emilien Boutillat, Cellar Master at Piper-Heidsieck.

title: Domaine Comte Georges de Vogue Bonnes Mares Grand Cru 2022
bodyHtml:
Domaine Comte Georges de Vogüé's 'Bonnes Mares' Grand Cru 2022 is a distinguished red wine from Burgundy's Côte de Nuits, exemplifying the depth and complexity of Pinot Noir from this esteemed vineyard.

Vineyard and Terroir
The Bonnes Mares Grand Cru vineyard spans approximately 15 hectares, with Domaine Comte Georges de Vogüé owning a significant portion. The vineyard's diverse soil composition, ranging from clay-limestone to marl, contributes to the wine's robust structure and nuanced character.

Winemaking Process
The 2022 vintage benefited from favourable weather conditions, resulting in healthy, ripe grapes. Traditional vinification methods were employed, including hand-harvesting, fermentation in temperature-controlled vats, and aging in French oak barrels, a portion of which were new, to enhance the wine's complexity and aging potential.

Tasting Notes

  • Appearance: Deep ruby red with a vibrant hue.
  • Aroma: Enticing floral notes, complemented by red and dark fruit aromas, with hints of spice and earthiness.
  • Palate: Silky and seamless, with fine-grained tannins and a harmonious balance between fruit and acidity, leading to a long, elegant finish.

Accolades
The 2022 vintage has received high praise from critics:

  • James Suckling: 98 points, noting its cool restraint and expansive palate with delicate, spicy almond and cream character.
  • Jasper Morris: 97 points, highlighting its top-notch quality.
  • Decanter Magazine: 96 points.
  • Robert Parker's Wine Advocate: 95 points.
  • Burghound: 94 points.

Food Pairing
This wine pairs exquisitely with dishes such as roasted duck breast, mushroom risotto, or fine cheeses like Époisses. Its refined structure and aromatic complexity enhance the dining experience, creating a harmonious match with elegant cuisine.

Serving Recommendations
For optimal enjoyment, serve at 16-18°C (60-64°F). Decanting for about 30 minutes before serving can help the wine open up, revealing its full aromatic potential.

title: Louis Latour Romanee St. Vivant Grand Cru 'Les Quatre Journaux' 2019
bodyHtml:
Introduction

This red wine originates from France, specifically from the prestigious Romanée-St-Vivant Grand Cru vineyard in the Vosne-Romanée village of the Côte de Nuits subregion. Maison Louis Latour, founded in 1797, is one of Burgundy's most historic independent and family-owned négociant-éleveurs, currently in its 11th generation of ownership. The winery's philosophy emphasizes a commitment to traditional techniques, sustainable viticulture, and the unique use of gravity-flow winemaking in its historic Corton Grancey cuverie. The "Les Quatre Journaux" cuvée comes from a magnificent 0.8-hectare parcel situated just meters from the legendary Romanée-Conti vineyard, named after an old Burgundian land measurement called a "journal".

Wine Description

Louis Latour Romanée-St-Vivant 'Les Quatre Journaux' 2019 displays a deep ruby colour with a garnet hue. The nose is powerfully aromatic and ethereal, offering an intense perfume of black cherry, wild raspberry, and blackcurrant bud layered with notes of fresh violets, rose petals, pepper, and liquorice. On the palate, the wine is generous, fresh, and full-bodied, featuring a concentrated but graceful personality with seamlessly integrated baking-spice notes and silky, fine-grained tannins. It is characterized by its remarkable elegance, "essense-of-Burgundy" depth, and an extraordinary, mouth-watering persistence on the finish. This 100% Pinot Noir has an ABV of 14% and was aged for 10 to 12 months in 100% new French oak barrels produced by the winery's own onsite cooperage. While the estate has practiced sustainable viticulture since the 1990s, this specific bottling is not certified organic. The optimal drinking window is estimated from 2024 through 2054.

Accolades

  • James Suckling - 100 points.

  • Robert Parker's Wine Advocate - 93-95 points.

  • Burghound - 92 points.

title: Sena Red Blend 2021 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
This iconic red wine originates from the Aconcagua Valley in Chile, specifically from a 42-hectare single vineyard located in Ocoa, about 40 kilometres from the Pacific Ocean. Established in 1995 as a joint venture between Eduardo Chadwick (of Viña Errázuriz) and the legendary Robert Mondavi, Seña was created with the mission to prove that Chile could produce world-class "First Growth" quality wines. The estate is a pioneer in South American viticulture, operating with a philosophy deeply rooted in biodynamic farming to authentically express its unique hillside terroir.

Wine Description

The 2021 Seña is a deep ruby red with violet highlights and is widely considered one of the finest and most elegant vintages in the estate's history, earning a perfect 100-point score from some critics. The bouquet is intensely fragrant and complex, revealing layers of strawberries, cassis, and rose petals framed by nuances of clove, cocoa, and fresh mint. On the palate, the wine is medium to full-bodied and remarkably pure, showcasing a vertical structure with juicy acidity and ultra-refined, fine-grained tannins. Flavours of blackcurrants and dark chocolate are balanced by a savory, mineral tension that leads into a persistent, seamless finish. The 2021 blend consists of 50% Cabernet Sauvignon, 27% Malbec, 17% Carmenere, and 6% Petit Verdot. It has an ABV of 14% and was aged for 22 months in French oak barrels (70% new) and 10% in large oak foudres. The wine is produced from certified organic and biodynamically grown grapes.

Food Pairing

The structural elegance and vibrant acidity of this blend make it a sophisticated partner for high-end cuisine. It pairs exquisitely with herb-crusted rack of lamb, lamb shank confit, or roasted duck breast. Its complexity also complements well-marbled steaks, beef Bourguignon, or pan-fried quail. For vegetarian options, consider a hearty vegetable borscht, wild mushroom risotto, or a selection of aged hard cheeses.

Vintage Quality

The 2021 vintage in the Aconcagua Valley is defined by moderately cool conditions, following the path of other classic years like 2016 and 2018. A slow, steady ripening season with no extreme summer heat spikes allowed the grapes to achieve perfect phenolic maturity while maintaining lower alcohol levels and exceptional aromatic finesse. This "cooler" profile resulted in a wine of great brilliance and tension, possessing extraordinary aging potential that will allow it to evolve gracefully through 2040.

title: Dugat Py Monthelie 'Vieilles Vignes' 2023
bodyHtml:
This Pinot Noir hails from France, specifically the Côte de Beaune subregion of Burgundy. Domaine Dugat Py was established in its current form in 1994, though the family’s viticultural roots in Gevrey Chambertin extend back to the 19th century. The estate is renowned for its commitment to organic and biodynamic farming, featuring extremely old vines and a winemaking philosophy that prioritizes balance, finesse, and natural vineyard work.

Wine Description

The Dugat Py Monthelie displays a vibrant ruby colour. The sensory profile is defined by a savory and classic style, offering aromas of spicy red fruit, cherry, and subtle herbal notes. On the palate, the wine reveals a velvety texture with fine tannins and a cool, fresh sweep that leads into a persistent finish characterized by powdered chalk and zesty tension.

Food Pairing

This elegant Pinot Noir is a natural match for roasted duck, goose, or game birds. It also pairs beautifully with earthy dishes like mushroom risotto or a classic roast prime rib.

title: Silver Oak Alexander Valley Cabernet Sauvignon 2021
bodyHtml:
This benchmark dry red wine originates from the United States, produced in the warm, gravelly heart of the Alexander Valley AVA in Sonoma County, California. Founded in 1972 by Raymond Twomey Duncan and legendary winemaker Justin Meyer, Silver Oak established a singular, uncompromising philosophy from its inception: crafting pure, age-worthy Cabernet Sauvignon aged exclusively in American oak barrels. Drawing fruit from estate-owned sites, including their LEED Platinum-certified Alexander Valley winery—as well as long-term grower partners, Silver Oak’s Alexander Valley expression is celebrated worldwide for its lush, fruit-forward style, velvety texture, and signature warm oak spice.

Wine Description

In the glass, the 2021 vintage exhibits a deep ruby-purple color with an opaque core and dark violet highlights. The nose opens with an inviting, intensely aromatic bouquet of ripe cassis, black cherry, and plum, seamlessly integrated with Silver Oak’s hallmark aromas of vanilla bean, coconut, toasted oak spice, dried sage, and subtle tobacco leaf. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied, supple, and plush. A lush entry leads into a generous mid-palate of dark berry fruit, framed by fine-grained, velvety tannins and balanced natural acidity. Crafted predominantly from Cabernet Sauvignon (typically complemented by small percentages of Merlot, Cabernet Franc, Petit Verdot, and Malbec), the hand-harvested grapes are vinified in temperature-controlled stainless steel. The wine undergoes 24 months of aging in American oak barrels (roughly 50% new and 50% second-use) crafted at the winery’s own cooperage in Missouri, followed by an additional 15 months of bottle maturation prior to release. The alcohol by volume sits at 14.4%.

Food Pairing

The opulent fruit depth, velvety tannic structure, and warm vanilla-oak spice of this iconic Alexander Valley Cabernet make it an outstanding match for rich, savory red meats. It pairs magnificently with prime ribeye steak, braised beef short ribs, roasted rack of lamb with herbs, grilled venison chops, and duck breast with a blackberry reduction. It also complements hearty dishes such as wild mushroom risotto, bacon-wrapped tenderloin, and aged hard cheeses like sharp Cheddar, Gouda, or mature Parmigiano-Reggiano.

Vintage Quality

The 2021 growing season in Sonoma County was defined by warm, dry conditions and lower yields, producing grapes with extraordinary flavor concentration, small berry size, and deep color. The steady harvest conditions allowed Cabernet Sauvignon to achieve complete phenolic maturity while preserving bright aromatic lift and structural balance. The 2021 Silver Oak Alexander Valley Cabernet Sauvignon offers immense immediate pleasure and lush polish upon release after decanting, while holding the concentration and tannic frame to cellar gracefully for 15 to 20+ years.

title: Chateau de La Tour Clos de Vougeot Vieilles Vignes Grand Cru 2019
bodyHtml:
96 Points  - Allen Meadows, Burghound

In contrast to the regular Cuvee, where aggressive swirling quickly dissipated the reduction, here that didn't help enough to reveal the underlying fruit. On the palate, though, there is a noticeably better size, weight and concentration to the bigger-bodied flavours that possess a highly seductive mid-palate texture thanks to the large dry extract that buffers the markedly firm tannic spine shaping the serious, austere and borderline chewy finish where the only nit is a hint of warmth. This is impressive though I underscore that my rating is, of course, contingent on the nose eventually cleaning up with age.

96 Points - Decanter

This super-cuvee is made using only the first bunch after the graft on vines at least 100 years of age and is not made yearly. The 2019 is spectacular. Slightly reserved at present, the tightly packed black and red fruit opens on the palate, accented with notes of violets, minerals, earth and wild herbs. This is powerful and rich, with firm tannins, lots of body, and the ability to age almost indefinitely.

94+ Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2019 Clos Vougeot Grand Cru Vieilles Vignes is very promising, unwinding in the glass with notes of dark berry fruit, orange peel, rose petals, rich soil tones and spices. Full-bodied, layered and multidimensional, it's deep and concentrated, with rich, powdery tannins, lively acids and a long, resonant finish. This was a fascinating tasting with father François Labet and son Edouard, who are pushing Domaine Pierre Labet and the Château de la Tour to new qualitative heights. Organic and now biodynamic farming in the vineyards, vinification within red—appreciable percentages of whole clusters in the winery and long élevage in the cellars are the order of the day. Perfumed, seamless and concentrated, the 2019s are immensely promising. In a richer, more overtly muscular register, the 2018s (which I took the opportunity during my visit to re-taste in bottle) have turned out very well, too. I hope to spend more time at this address later in 2021 and plan to report back in more detail.

title: Poggio di Sotto Brunello di Montalcino 2018
bodyHtml:
Poggio di Sotto is a highly-regarded 'cult' winery located in Tuscany, Italy, in the subregion of Montalcino. The estate was established in 1989 by Piero Palmucci, who meticulously researched the region's soil and climate to find the ideal location for Sangiovese Grosso grapes. Poggio di Sotto became part of the ColleMassari Wine Estates in 2011, when it was acquired by Claudio Tipa. The winery is known for its traditional winemaking, using natural and non-interventionist methods, including long aging periods in large Slavonian oak barrels and no filtering before release. The vineyards are organically farmed.

Wine Description

This 100% Sangiovese wine has a deep ruby red colour with garnet reflections. The aroma is intense and complex, offering a sensory profile of red cherry, raspberry, and cassis, along with hints of fragrant wet leaves, woody rosehip, and blue flowers. The palate is pure and fluid, with a tension between astringent orange and creamy mocha. The wine has a graceful harmony and a fine, elegant feel with chalky, silky tannins that are well-integrated and persistent. It is described as a lighter and brighter wine than most, yet it has impressive depth. This wine can be enjoyed over the coming 20 years, with some suggesting a drinking window of 2028-2046.

Accolades

  • Wine Enthusiast - 95 points

  • Wine Enthusiast - #1 Cellar Selection of 2023

  • The Wine Advocate - 96+ points

  • Wine Spectator - 93 points

  • James Suckling - 93 points

 

Food Pairing

The Poggio di Sotto Brunello di Montalcino 2018 is a good match for robust, structured dishes with rich sauces. Suggested pairings include classic Tuscan dishes such as wild boar ragu with pappardelle pasta or a Florentine T-bone steak. It also pairs well with aged cheeses like Parmigiano-Reggiano and Pecorino Toscano. The wine's acidity and tannins cut through the richness of these dishes, while its earthy and herbal notes harmonize with the food. A perfect match to enhance the wine's complexity.

Vintage Quality

 The 2018 vintage was considered a more difficult and uneven year in the region. Botrytis, a fungal disease, decimated at least 25% of the harvest. However, thanks to the winemaker's meticulous vineyard work, including a rigorous selection process and low yields, Poggio di Sotto was able to produce a wine that is elegant and well-balanced. The resulting wine is firm and pure, with a graceful balance despite the challenges of the vintage.

title: Domaine des Beaumont Gevrey Chambertin 'Les Cherbaudes' Premier Cru 2020
bodyHtml:
The origin of the wine-growing activity in the Beaumont family goes back more than seven generations. Today installed in the 3 communes of Morey-Saint-Denis - headquarters of the exploitation - Gevrey-Chambertin and Chambolle-Musigny, the vineyard, almost exclusively planted with Pinot Noir cultivated in sustainable viticulture, covers very beautiful plots in Grand Cru.

Beautiful balance, red fruits, nuanced texture, melted and warm tannins, bears the imprint of the terroir of Gevrey-Chambertin. The nose is very expressive on red fruits and black cherries. The mouth is structured by round tannins. Its concentration gives it remarkable aging potential.

title: Chateau Figeac 2022
bodyHtml:
Château Figeac is one of the most historic and prestigious estates in Saint-Émilion, Bordeaux. Owned by the Manoncourt family since 1892, it is renowned for its unique terroir dominated by gravel soils, which favours the use of Cabernet grapes. Figeac has long embraced a philosophy of elegance, structure, and ageing potential, and under the leadership of the late Thierry Manoncourt and now Frédéric Faye, the estate has solidified its place among Bordeaux’s elite.

Wine Description
The 2022 vintage of Château Figeac presents a brilliant, deep garnet hue. Aromas unfold in layers, with cassis, blackberry, black cherry, graphite, violet, and hints of cigar box and spice. On the palate, the wine is opulent and full-bodied, yet refined, delivering a rich core of dark fruit, fine-grained tannins, and mineral tension.

Accolades

  • Wine Advocate - 100 points
  • Vinous - 97+ points
  • Decanter - 98 points
  • James Suckling - 97+ points
  • Jeb Dunnuck - 96+ points

Food Pairing
Pair this powerful yet graceful Bordeaux with herb-crusted rack of lamb, roast duck breast with cherry reduction, or aged Comté. The wine’s structure and finesse complement complex, savoury dishes with both richness and nuance. Together, they create an unforgettable dining experience.

title: Caparzo Brunello di Montalcino Riserva 2007
bodyHtml:
The origins of the place named Caparzo are still unknown. According to some people, the name is derived, as shown by ancient maps, from Ca’ Pazzo; according to others, the term should derive from the Latin Caput Arsum, indicating "a place touched by sun”. 

The history of Caparzo dates back to the end of the 1960s at the dawning of Brunello di Montalcino, when a group of friends, fond of Tuscany and of wine, purchased an old ruin with vineyards at Montalcino. The farm estate was renovated, modernized, and new vineyards were planted. In a short time, Caparzo made itself known in the Brunello market. In 1998, 30 years after the first rows of vines were planted, the farm estate came to a turning point when Elisabetta Gnudi Angelini purchased Caparzo. With the help of her son, Igino, and daughter, Alessandra, she immediately carried out her objective: combining tradition with innovation to create a high-quality wine that is the expression of an excellent territory.

Caparzo Brunello di Montalcino Riserva is a garnet red, intense and billiant, with light orange tints. With a penetrating bouquet, very full and varied, reminiscent of wild berries. On the palate, the wine is dry, full-bodied, harmonious, delicate and austere at the same time, and has a long finish.

96 Points - Wine Spectator

There's a delicacy to this version, showing a latent structure and a distinctive spiciness surrounding the core flavors of cherry, raspberry, licorice and mineral. Harmonious and persistent, featuring a long finish. A compelling Brunello riserva. Best from 2015 through 2032.

92 Points - James Suckling

Very pretty pure fruit with cherries and plums on the nose. Full body, with sweet and ripe fruit. Medium full tannins and a fresh finish. Very silky.

92 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

A big, broad-shouldered wine, the 2007 Brunello di Montalcino Riserva is endowed with superb richness and depth. Sweet black cherries, tobacco, smoke, scorched earth and tar all explode from the glass. Despite its textural richness, the 2007 remains mid-weight and gracious for the year. At times the 2007 is quite feminine, while at other moments its more virile side comes through, creating contrasts that are intriguing to follow. Caparzo has done a terrific job with their 2007 Riserva.

92 Points - Wine Enthusiast

Voted among the best Brunellos by a group of winemaking peers, Caparzo’s riserva is beautifully balanced and layered with chocolate, cherry, leather, blackberry and lingering spice notes. The wine shows freshness and elegance on the finish thanks to the silky nature of the mouthfeel.

title: Chateau Montelena Cabernet Sauvignon Napa Valley 2022
bodyHtml:
Produced in the United States, this wine originates from the world renowned Napa Valley region in California, with fruit primarily sourced from the estate in Calistoga and supplemented by vineyards in the Oak Knoll District. Chateau Montelena is a historic cornerstone of American winemaking, famously gaining international acclaim during the 1976 'Judgment of Paris'. Under the guidance of winemaker Matthew Crafton, the winery maintains a philosophy of transparency and adaptability, allowing each vintage to express its unique environmental narrative through a balance of classic structure and modern approachability.

Wine Description

The 2022 Napa Valley Cabernet Sauvignon presents a rich and intense sensory profile driven by dark fruit. On the nose, it reveals a concentrated bouquet of blackberry and cassis, followed by aromatic layers of spicy clove, vanilla, pipe tobacco, and a touch of caramel. The palate is characterized by supple tannins that navigate between a subtle streak of minerality and a zesty acidity that provides freshness to the body. Flavors of strawberry and cranberry sauce emerge toward the finish, which concludes with notes of cola, graphite, and black cherry. This wine is a blend of Cabernet Sauvignon and Merlot, crafted for enjoyment in its youth but possessing the structure to age for 15 to 20 years.

title: Dugat Py Monthelie Les Riottes Premier Cru 2023
bodyHtml:
This rare and powerful red wine originates from the Monthélie Premier Cru appellation in the Côte de Beaune, Burgundy. While Monthélie is often overshadowed by its neighbors, Volnay and Meursault, Domaine Dugat-Py treats this terroir with the same "Grand Cru" intensity as their legendary Gevrey-Chambertin holdings. The winery's philosophy is defined by Loïc Dugat’s commitment to very old vines, some over 100 years old, and rigorous organic and biodynamic farming to achieve the "quintessence of each terroir".

Wine Description

The Dugat-Py Monthélie Premier Cru Les Riottes presents a deep, saturated ruby colour. The sensory profile is notably more concentrated and darker-fruited than typical Monthélie, featuring an intense nose of blackcurrants, wild cherries, and pomegranate, layered with sophisticated notes of turned earth, exotic five-spice, and a touch of smokiness. On the palate, the wine is dense and structured, showcasing a "firm but really smooth" tannic frame and a refreshing mineral core. It is characterized by its remarkable depth and aging potential, leading to a long, persistent finish with hints of salted caramel and dark chocolate. This 100% Pinot Noir is crafted from low-yielding old vines, fermented with a portion of whole bunches, and aged for 16–18 months in French oak barrels (typically around 60% new for the Premier Crus).

title: Verite 'La Joie' 2010
bodyHtml:
"The 2010 vintage was a long season for ripening after a beautiful flowering. This vintage will live for a long time — yet this racy, powerful, elegant wine can also be appreciated young. This vintage is a great example of what Sonoma can do with a diversity of soils and a grandiose climate. Harvest took place September 25th through October 16th." – Pierre Seillan, Vigneron

A beautiful wine with intense color and a red crown along the edges, the 2010 La Joie reveals a silky, soft and voluptuously fruity nose with a touch of discreet oak and fine spices. It opens with an opulent palate of red and black fruits, spices and licorice before giving way to an impressively long finish. This is a wine with very fine tannins; a wine of balance between fruit and minerality. While it can be enjoyed young this wine will age at least 20 years.

94 Points - Vinous     Graphite, plums, smoke, licorice and incense jump from the glass in the 2010 La Joie. Rich, sumptuous and beautifully layered, the 2010 captures the essence of the vintage. The fruit is intense and super-concentrated, but at the same time, there is plenty of vibrancy and sheer verve in the glass. The 2010 needs at least a few years in bottle for the Cabernet Sauvignon tannins to start softening. 

92+ Points Robert Parker Wine Parker - Copious aromas of incense, unsmoked cigar tobacco, Christmas fruitcake, cedar, underbrush, blackcurrants and a hint of espresso roast emerge from this medium to full-bodied, rich, concentrated red. It needs 4-5 years of cellaring and should keep well for 2 to 3 decades

title: Catena 'Nicolas Catena Zapata' 2005
bodyHtml:
Introduction

This red wine originates from Argentina, specifically from the high-altitude districts of the Mendoza region. Founded in 1902 by Italian immigrant Nicola Catena, Bodega Catena Zapata is a world-renowned family estate currently led by third-generation vintner Nicolás Catena and his daughter, Dr. Laura Catena. The winery's philosophy is rooted in pioneering high-altitude viticulture and meticulous scientific research through the Catena Institute of Wine, aiming to produce Argentine wines that can compete with the finest 'First Growths' in the world.

Wine Description

Catena 'Nicolás Catena Zapata' 2005 displays a deep, saturated purple-black colour with bluish tones. The nose is complex and brooding, offering intense aromas of cassis jam, blackberry, and black cherry layered with notes of lavender, violet, espresso, and toasted oak. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied and opulent, delivering a dense core of blackcurrant, dark chocolate, and mocha balanced by bright acidity and a stony minerality. It is characterized by its impeccable structure, featuring fine-grained, velvety tannins and an exceptionally long finish that can exceed 60 seconds. This blend is composed of 78% Cabernet Sauvignon and 22% Malbec, with an ABV of 14%. While the estate follows sustainable practices and minimalist winemaking, this specific vintage is not certified organic. The optimal drinking window for this mature vintage is from release through 2035.

Accolades

  • Robert Parker's Wine Advocate - 98 points.

  • Decanter - 95 points.

  • Wine Enthusiast - 94 points.

Food Pairing

The dense structure and concentrated fruit profile of this high-altitude blend make it an exceptional companion for rich, savoury meats. It pairs perfectly with a grilled bone-in ribeye steak, roast lamb, or cordero al horno (oven-roasted lamb). Its complex notes of spice and dark fruit also complement beef tenderloin, hearty stews, and blue-veined cheeses.

title: Brandlin Estate Cabernet Sauvignon Mount Veeder 2019
bodyHtml:
Introduction
From the United States, in California’s Napa Valley, the Brandlin Estate vineyard lies high on the slopes of the Mount Veeder appellation. The Brandlin family first planted vines here in the 1920s, and today the estate is part of the Cuvaison family, which is dedicated to preserving the land’s legacy while producing wines that reflect the character of this rugged terrain. The combination of steep, volcanic soils and elevated vineyards produces Cabernet Sauvignon with exceptional structure, freshness, and complexity.

Wine Description
Deep and opaque in colour, this Cabernet Sauvignon offers aromas of blackberry, boysenberry, and cassis, accented by hints of cardamom, allspice, and black tea. On the palate, concentrated dark fruit flavours are layered with notes of olive, tobacco, and cocoa. The texture is plush and full-bodied, with supple yet firm tannins providing structure and length. The finish is long and refined, with lingering spice and savoury undertones.

Accolades
Wine Enthusiast – 93 points.
Wine Spectator – 93 points.
James Suckling – 94 points
Wine Advocate – 95 points

Food Pairing
This wine pairs beautifully with ribeye steak, braised lamb shank, or roasted duck breast. The bold flavours and firm tannins of the Cabernet enhance the richness of these dishes, creating an unforgettable dining experience.

title: Silver Oak Napa Valley Cabernet Sauvignon 2018 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
Silver Oak was started in 1972 with a simple driving philosophy - to focus production on only one varietal, Cabernet Sauvignon. What's more, they resolved to create a wine with a style all its own: not another hard, tannic red wine requiring years of aging to enjoy, but a wine of fully developed flavors and a velvety soft texture on the day it is released for sale.

The Silver Oak Napa Valley Cabernet Sauvignon is ruby in color with notes of strawberry, fresh carnation, black pepper and vanilla. This wine builds in strength and body across the mid-palate with a blackberry character on the finish and bright cherry return. With integrated tannins, it’s expressive yet luxurious with an even, balanced finish.

93 Points - Wilfred Wong

The 2018 Silver Oak Napa Valley Cabernet is rich in flavors and sturdy on the palate. This wine excels with aromas and flavors of red and blackberries, with a nice balance of oaky notes. Enjoy it with baked lamb chops in saffron rice.

title: Produttori del Barbaresco - Barbaresco 'Asili' Riserva 2020
bodyHtml:
Introduction

Produttori del Barbaresco Barbaresco Asili Riserva 2020 originates from the Piedmont region of Italy, specifically from the historic Asili vineyard within the Barbaresco subregion. The Produttori del Barbaresco is a world renowned cooperative founded in 1958, currently uniting over 50 growers who exclusively produce Nebbiolo across some of the region's most prestigious sites. The winery's philosophy centers on traditional winemaking to express the distinct terroir of individual vineyards, only releasing these single cru Riservas in exceptional vintages.

Wine Description

This elegant red wine presents a brilliant garnet red colour with shades of orange. The aromatic profile is highly fragrant and complex, opening with alluring scents of dog rose, eucalyptus, and lavender, followed by deeper notes of new leather, forest floor, and dark spice. On the palate, it is medium to full bodied and impeccably balanced, delivering juicy flavours of Morello cherry, raspberry, and blood orange alongside star anise and a hint of truffle. The wine is characterized by its fine grained, silky tannins and a vibrant acidity that provides great linear structure and finesse. It concludes with a long, persistent finish marked by mineral notes, licorice root, and crushed rocks. This 100% Nebbiolo varietal composition was aged for 36 months in large oak barrels followed by 12 months in the bottle. The alcohol content is 14.5% ABV, and the optimal drinking window extends from 2026 through 2045.

Accolades

Wine Spectator - 95 points

Vinous - 96 points

Wine Advocate - 95 points

Jeb Dunnuck - 95 points

Food Pairing

The structural poise and intense fruit of Asili Riserva make it a superb partner for sophisticated, earthy dishes. It pairs beautifully with roasted or braised red meats such as lamb chops and beef stew, as well as game birds like pheasant. The wine's herbal and mineral nuances also complement mushroom risotto, pasta with rich meat sauces, and aged cheeses like Parmigiano Reggiano or Pecorino.

Vintage Quality

The 2020 vintage in Barbaresco is considered extremely good, characterized by a mild spring and a warm summer with well timed rains that prevented water stress. Cool nights through late September helped the Nebbiolo grapes achieve excellent aromatic concentration and balanced acidity, resulting in a harvest of healthy grapes with perfect maturity and more supple tannins than the preceding 2019 vintage.

title: Schrader Heritage Clone Cabernet Sauvignon 2018 (by Schrader Cellars)
bodyHtml:
Schrader Cellars' 'Heritage Clone' Cabernet Sauvignon is a distinguished wine sourced from the renowned To Kalon Vineyard in Oakville, Napa Valley, California. Established by Fred Schrader in 1998, Schrader Cellars has built a reputation for crafting exceptional Cabernet Sauvignons from some of Napa Valley's most esteemed vineyards. The 'Heritage Clone' specifically originates from a low-yielding block planted with Clone 39 Cabernet Sauvignon vines, contributing to the wine's unique character.

Sensory Profile

This wine presents a deep, dark ruby hue with an opaque core and subtle purple highlights. The bouquet is intensely aromatic, featuring notes of blackberries, dark cherries, nougat, sweet tobacco, and hints of vanilla. On the palate, it delivers a full-bodied experience with rich flavors of ripe black fruits, graphite, iron, and subtle scorched earth nuances. The wine is well-structured, showcasing fine tannins and a velvety texture that leads to a long, complex finish. While approachable in its youth, this Cabernet Sauvignon is expected to evolve gracefully over the next two decades.

Food Pairing

This robust Cabernet Sauvignon pairs exceptionally well with richly flavored dishes. A prime recommendation is a 12-ounce boneless Wagyu ribeye steak, seasoned with kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper, and prepared with a green peppercorn and brandy cream sauce. This pairing accentuates the wine's depth and character, creating an unforgettable dining experience.

title: Kosta Browne Pinot Noir 'Santa Rita Hills' 2021
bodyHtml:
Introduction

Kosta Browne Pinot Noir 'Santa Rita Hills' 2021 is a red wine from the United States, produced in the Central Coast region of California and the Sta. Rita Hills appellation. Kosta Browne began in 1997 with a passion for excellence and a drive to create wines that rival the best in the world. The winery's philosophy is centred on low intervention and showcasing the purity and quality of the fruit from top vineyard sites. The Sta. Rita Hills appellation, located in Santa Barbara County, is a cool climate growing region with a unique east-west mountain range orientation that funnels cool coastal fog and wind to the vines.

Wine Description

The wine is 100% Pinot Noir. It is medium light garnet in colour. The nose features a refined bouquet of bright red fruit, blueberries, strawberries, orange peel, and earthy, floral notes. Delightful aromas of earth, pine, clove, and cinnamon stick are also present.

It is a medium bodied and delicate wine. The palate is soft and generous, with juicy cranberry, cherry, and strawberry fruit notes. Subtle citrus and hints of Earl Grey tea leaves add nuance to the flavours. The tannins are fine, dusty, and feathery, lying on a bed of finely grained tannin. Stylistically, it is a subtle, pretty, and layered wine with extraordinary fruit character, great balance, and finesse. The wine was matured for 15 months in $48\%$ new French oak, with a portion also aged in wood cask and new Austrian oak. The finish is long and smooth, with a savory, layered, and extended quality. The ABV is 14.1%. Information on the organic status of the wine is not available in the sources.

Accolades

  • Decanter - 95 points

  • Wine Enthusiast - 94 points

  • James Suckling - 93 points

  • Wine Advocate - 93 points

  • Wine Spectator - 92 points

Food Pairing

Our wine experts think this Californian Sta. Rita Hills Pinot Noir Red wine would be a match made in heaven with veal and mushrooms. General food pairings include chicken and turkey.

Vintage Quality

The 2021 Sta. Rita Hills Pinot Noir was harvested over three weeks during an ideal growing season. The vintage is described as having produced a subtle and brilliant wine. The cool climate of the appellation allows the vines to grow with more complexity and depth of flavour.

title: Catena Zapata Malbec Argentino 2004
bodyHtml:
Winery Background:
Bodega Catena Zapata, founded in 1902 by Italian immigrant Nicola Catena, has played a pivotal role in establishing Argentina as a world-class wine region. Under the stewardship of Nicolás Catena and his daughter Laura, the winery has pioneered high-altitude viticulture, pushing the boundaries of Malbec and demonstrating the diversity of Mendoza’s terroirs.

Wine Description:
The 2004 Catena Zapata Malbec 'Argentino Vineyard' displays a deep, dark violet hue with intense blackish-purple tones. Its aromatic complexity is remarkable, revealing layers of wood smoke, creosote, black cherry, blackberry, and hints of pepper and clove. On the palate, the wine unfolds with a generous texture, offering sweet black cherry flavors intertwined with notes of dark chocolate and spicy black pepper. The finish is long and refined, supported by velvety tannins and vibrant acidity.

Accolades:

  • Robert Parker's Wine Advocate - 98 points
  • James Suckling - 95 points
  • Vinous - 95 points
  • Wine Spectator - 95 points

Food Pairing:
This expressive Malbec pairs beautifully with grilled ribeye, roasted lamb, and aged cheeses, enhancing the wine’s richness and depth. Together, they create an unforgettable dining experience.

Vintage Quality:
The 2004 vintage in Mendoza was exceptional, marked by optimal ripening conditions that contributed to the wine’s impressive structure and aging potential. The winemaking team at Catena Zapata expertly harnessed the vintage’s strengths, resulting in a Malbec that showcases both the vineyard’s distinct character and the year’s remarkable quality.

title: Chateau Montelena Estate Cabernet Sauvignon 2019
bodyHtml:
The 2019 Chateau Montelena Estate Cabernet Sauvignon is a distinguished wine from Napa Valley's Calistoga region. Sourced from meticulously cultivated vineyards, this vintage showcases the winery’s commitment to producing exceptional, terroir-driven Cabernet Sauvignon.

Tasting Notes

  • Aroma: The nose is rich with floral notes of fresh lavender, ripe plum, sandalwood, and cherry compote. Hints of Earl Grey tea add complexity.
  • Palate: A powerful yet refined structure, opening with flavors of fresh blueberries, blackberry pie, and cassis. These dark fruit notes are complemented by layers of baking spices, including vanilla and cinnamon, leading to a long, elegant finish.
  • Texture: Silky tannins provide structure, balanced by vibrant acidity that ensures aging potential.

Critical Acclaim

  • Decanter: 99 points – Praised for its precision, depth, and seamless integration of fruit and tannins.
  • Robert Parker's Wine Advocate: 96 points – Recognized for its layered complexity, balanced structure, and remarkable aging potential.

Serving and Pairing

This Cabernet Sauvignon is best enjoyed at 60–65°F (16–18°C). Decanting for at least an hour enhances its aromatic complexity. It pairs beautifully with grilled meats, braised short ribs, and aged cheeses, complementing the wine’s richness and depth.

Aging Potential

The 2019 vintage has exceptional aging potential, with well-integrated tannins and acidity that allow it to evolve gracefully over 20+ years. While already impressive, cellaring will bring out additional layers of complexity.

Conclusion

The 2019 Chateau Montelena Estate Cabernet Sauvignon is a masterful expression of Napa Valley, offering power, elegance, and longevity. With its deep fruit character, balanced structure, and critical acclaim, this vintage stands as one of the finest representations of the estate’s renowned craftsmanship.

title: Conti Costanti Brunello di Montalcino 2020
bodyHtml: Deep ruby red with brilliant garnet reflections, the bouquet is rich, ample and intense, with notes of brushwood, berries, plums, violets, spices and vanilla confirmed on the palate. Incredible elegance and balance, lush concentration, voluptuous body and silky, smooth tannins. It shows power and finesse all at once. An excellent accompaniment to red meat, stews, complex dishes and aged cheese.

title: Las Alas de Frontonio Garnacha Macabeo 2019
Castello di Montepo Schidione 2020
vendor: 300747 - South By Southwest Wine Imports Inc.
bodyHtml:
Castello di Montepò Schidione 2020 is a bold and structured red wine from the Maremma region of Tuscany, Italy. Produced by Jacopo Biondi Santi, heir to the family that pioneered Brunello di Montalcino, the estate is located in the Scansano district within an imposing 12th-century fortress. The winery's philosophy bridges tradition and innovation, utilizing the family's exclusive Sangiovese Grosso BBS11 clone alongside international varieties to create labels with contemporary style and vigorous individuality.

Wine Description

The 2020 Schidione exhibits an inky dark core with a ruby rim. The sensory profile is complex, featuring a nose of balsamic notes, spicy dark cherry, and crushed berries interwoven with tobacco and fine wood. On the palate, it is muscular and dense with fine proportions, offering youthful flavours of fresh dark fruit and ripe extract. This Super Tuscan blend typically consists of 40% Sangiovese (the prized BBS11 clone), 40% Cabernet Sauvignon, and 20% Merlot. It is characterized by its harmony and balance, with firm yet luscious tannins and a long, lingering finish. While vibrant in its youth, it is built for significant ageing, with an optimal drinking window often extending decades.

94 points, Decanter

title: Corte Sant'Alda Amarone della Valpolicella Valmezzane 2016
bodyHtml: Corte Sant'Alda is an organic and biodynamic wine estate in Veneto. Proprietor, Marinella Camerani excels with bold, powerful Valpolicellas and Amarones. Zyn found this Amarone to have extraordinary concentration and complexity and rivals the best wines produced in the Veneto.

title: Domaine Boigey Freres Vosne Romanee 1er Cru Les Suchots 2022 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
Introduction

This red wine originates from France, specifically from the prestigious village of Vosne-Romanée within the Côte de Nuits subregion of Burgundy. Founded in 2017 by brothers Guillaume and Olivier Boigey, Domaine Boigey Frères is a rising star in the region, established to recover family vineyards previously leased to other producers. The winery's philosophy is rooted in a deep family heritage dating back generations in Vosne, focusing on meticulous, sustainable vineyard management and hand-harvesting to produce wines that emphasize finesse, balance, and clear terroir expression.

Wine Description

Domaine Boigey Frères Vosne-Romanée 1er Cru Les Suchots 2022 displays a beautiful garnet or deep red colour. The nose is expressive and impressively elegant, offering magnificent aromas of cherry and delicate red fruits layered with noble herbs and a hint of spice. On the palate, the wine is powerful and structured yet incredibly silky, delivering fresh and deep fruit flavours with a refined acidity that belies the warmth of the 2022 vintage. It is characterized by its remarkable energy, hedonistic charm, and a long, fruit-forward finish with mineral undertones. This 100% Pinot Noir typically features an ABV of 13.5% to 14% and was aged for 10 to 18 months in oak barrels. The estate follows sustainable (culture raisonnée) practices, and the wine is bottled at the domaine without fining or filtration. The optimal drinking window for this vintage is estimated to be from 2026 through 2040.

Accolades

  • Winehog (Steen Öhman) - Vins d'émotion (Hedonistic/Lively).

  • Jasper Morris, Inside Burgundy - 91–93 points.

  • Vivino Community - 4.2 points.

  • Wine-Searcher Critic Average - 93 points.

Food Pairing

The powerful yet silky structure of this Premier Cru Pinot Noir makes it a versatile partner for sophisticated and savoury dishes. It pairs perfectly with grilled red meats like Charolais beef, roast pork with chestnuts, or game birds such as pheasant. Its refined acidity and spicy notes also complement flank steak with shallots and intense, extra-mature cheeses like those from the Abbaye de Cîteaux.

Vintage Quality

The 2022 vintage in Burgundy is regarded as exceptional, characterized by a warm growing season that produced wines with surprising levels of energy and freshness alongside a hedonistic fruit profile. Winemakers like the Boigey brothers were highly successful in this vintage, managing to carve out "diamond-like" structures with fine-grained tannins that ensure a promising and durable future for the wines.

title: Vega Sicilia Pintia 2017 - 3 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
The talent of rebelliousness The independent member of the Vega Sicilia family. Pintia is young, intense and ground-breaking in nature. Proud of its origin, it has managed to reinterpret the Vega Sicilia culture in an innovative, brave and daring manner at the head of the emergence of a new generation of Toro wines.

These wines are highly intense in colour and depth, cherry red in tone with purplish hues. It is broad, very clean, expressive and elegant on the nose, with a great fruit intensity cocooned in a subtle way and of great quality. It has a great structure and an excellent tannic presence in the mouth and is persistent, fresh and very pleasant to the palate. Floral hints in retronasal.

title: Chateau Talbot 2015
bodyHtml:
​Château Talbot 2015 is a distinguished red wine from the Saint-Julien appellation in Bordeaux, France. Renowned for its consistent quality, this Fourth Growth estate has been under the stewardship of the Cordier family since 1918.

Wine Description

In the glass, the wine exhibits a deep purple hue, indicative of its richness. The nose is refined, offering aromas of red fruits intertwined with delicate oak nuances. On the palate, it is medium-bodied with fine tannins, delivering flavors of blackberries, cassis, and subtle hints of tobacco and graphite. The finish is elegant, marked by persistent black fruit notes.

Accolades

  • Wine Enthusiast: 94 points

  • James Suckling: 94 points

  • Wine Spectator: 92 points

  • Jeb Dunnuck: 91 points

Food Pairing

This wine pairs excellently with grilled meats, roasted lamb, or dishes featuring earthy mushrooms. The combination enhances the wine's depth and character, culminating in a memorable dining experience.

title: Luce Lux Vitis 2020 - 3 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
Luce Lux Vitis originates from Italy, within the renowned Tuscany region and the specific subregion of Montalcino. Tenuta Luce was established in the early 1990s as an ambitious collaboration between the Frescobaldi family and Robert Mondavi. Since 2004, the estate has been directed solely by Lamberto Frescobaldi, whose guiding winemaking philosophy focuses on capturing the fullest expression of the local terroir through a highly distinctive and elegant individual style.

Wine Description

This exceptional red blend possesses an intense, deep ruby red colour. The multi-layered aromatics unfold with a brief aeration, releasing a bouquet of redcurrant, well-ripened fruit, and sweet violets, all lifted by a delicate touch of cocoa powder. On the palate, the entry is full-bodied yet velvet-smooth, beautifully supported by a vibrant, refreshing acidity and elegant, enfolding tannins. Complex and beautifully integrated flavors of roasted espresso bean and wild herbs linger on a near-ending, persistent finish.

title: Armand Heitz Santenay 'La Comme' Premier Cru 2020
bodyHtml: Continuing the Morgeot de Chassagne climate, this terroir has all the characteristics to produce remarkable wines. Made from old vines, the wine is complex and long in the mouth. Empyreumatic or flinty notes are typical of the plot. Fans will appreciate this aromatic profile. In order not to accentuate this character trait too much and make the wine coarse, they opted for freshly heated barrels and aging with very little sulfur.

title: Domaine de Chevalier Rouge 2021
bodyHtml:
96 Points - Wine Enthusiast

Outer quote mark This grand Bernard family estate in Léognan is legendary for its white wine. This is a ripe, spicily wood-aged wine. Its background of young acidity brings out a tangy edge that will soften and fill out into a long-lived wine.

95+ Points - James Suckling

A medium-bodied DC with a pretty core of ripe fruit that shows licorice, blackberry and some currant character. Spice box, too. Very long, with fine tannins and plenty of energy.

94 Points - Decanter

94 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

94 Points - Vinous

93 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

title: Cheval des Andes 2018
bodyHtml:
Intense shiny red with purple hints. Very intense aromatic expression. The bouquet of aromas of red fruit (cherry, wild strawberries) and spices is intensified by the freshness and complexity of the wine. On the palate, the balance of this wine is predominant. A supple and fresh attack add a lovely liveliness. Soft, precise tannins bring an attractive structure with an elegant finish.

Blend: 70% Malbec and 30% Cabernet Sauvignon

98 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2018 Cheval des Andes is a blend of 70% Malbec and 30% Cabernet Sauvignon fermented in small lots in 3,000- to 8,000-liter tanks and matured 40% in 225-liter oak barrels, 40% in 400-liter oak barrels and the remaining 20% in 2,500-liter oak vats for 13 months. Ninety percent of the oak used was French and the rest a blend of Austrian, Slovenian and German oak, 50% of it new. 2018 has been one of the best vintages in recent times in Mendoza, and the wine shows it. It's a cooler vintage, and the wine has improved in freshness and elegance without losing any clout. It's 14.5% alcohol and has a pH of 3.73. This is young, juicy, elegant and balanced and still has some herbal and toasted notes; it's medium to full-bodied, with the creamy and luxurious texture of the modern Bordeaux, ultra fine tannins and a long, dry and precise finish. It's still undeveloped and seems to have all the components and the balance between them for a long and positive development in bottle. With wines like this, I sometimes wish I had a time machine so I could see them in 20 years from now... I think this is the finest Cheval des Andes I've ever tasted.

98 Points - James Suckling

This is a plush, rich Cheval with blueberry and floral aromas and flavors. HInts of tar and fresh lavender. Full body. The depth and richness are impressive, as are the ripe yet fresh tannins. Very long and structured, yet controlled and in balance. This will be a great wine indeed. Release in September 2021. Drink after 2023.

95 Points - Wine Enthusiast

This blend of 70% Malbec and 30% Cabernet Sauvignon offers a delicate nose of ripe plum, cumin, and dried herbs. Well balanced and elegant, it features juicy black-fruit flavors and hints of rosemary. A light note of chocolate adds complexity to the palate. Silky tannins and good acidity provide a good structure, suggesting the wine will age beautifully.

92 Points - Wine Spectator

Big and rich, with expressive beef and earthy notes to the dark plum and roasted dark cherry flavors, which are backed by firm tannins and acidity. Creamy in the midpalate, with hints of dried green herbs and dark chocolate on the finish. Malbec and Cabernet Sauvignon.

title: Chateau Palmer 2006 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
Château Palmer is a Third Growth estate in the Margaux appellation of Bordeaux, France. Established in the early 19th century, it has built a reputation for producing wines of exceptional elegance and complexity. The 2006 vintage is a testament to the estate's commitment to quality and tradition.

Wine Description

The 2006 Château Palmer displays a deep ruby color with slight evolution at the rim. The nose is rich and dense, offering aromas of ripe currants, spices, and juicy berries. On the palate, it is medium to full-bodied, with a sumptuous layer of dusty tannins surrounding a core of ripe fruit flavors. The wine is harmonious, with a silky texture and a lingering finish that showcases its freshness and depth.

Accolades

  • Wine Enthusiast – 94 points
  • Wine Spectator – 93 points
  • Robert Parker's Wine Advocate – 92 points

Food Pairing

The 2006 Château Palmer pairs excellently with rich dishes such as roasted lamb, beef tenderloin, or duck confit. Its complex flavor profile also complements aged cheeses and mushroom-based dishes, enhancing the wine's depth and character.

Vintage Quality

The 2006 vintage in Bordeaux experienced a hot and dry growing season with significant weather fluctuations. Despite these challenges, Château Palmer produced a wine that harmoniously blends richness with powerful tannins, showcasing elegance, subtlety, and depth.

title: Shafer Relentless 2019
bodyHtml:
Shafer Relentless hails from the United States, specifically from the ridgetop and foothill vineyards of Napa Valley situated just south of the Stags Leap District. Shafer Vineyards has been a benchmark producer in Napa Valley for nearly 50 years, cultivating 240 acres of estate fruit to craft world class wines. This particular bottling serves as a tribute to long time winemaker Elias Fernandez, celebrating his 'relentless' pursuit of quality and his significant impact on the estate's winemaking philosophy.

Wine Description

This deep purple hued Syrah based blend is a bold and complex blockbuster that delivers immense richness without a sensation of heaviness. The aromatics are intensely savory, opening with notes of grilled meat, black pepper, sage, and roasted almonds, complemented by hints of black cherry and Kirsch. On the palate, the wine is mouth filling and soul satisfying, featuring vivid flavors of blueberry, black tea, and wet stone balanced by blood orange acidity.

Accolades

  • Decanter – 97 points

  • Jeb Dunnuck – 96 points

  • Wine Enthusiast – 96 points

  • James Suckling – 95 points

  • Vinous – 94 points

  • Wine Advocate – 93+ points

  • Wine Spectator – 92 points

Food Pairing
