The savory profile and significant structure of this wine make it an ideal companion for hearty dishes such as grilled game, braised lamb shanks, or classic barbecue. It also pairs beautifully with aged cheeses like Asiago or clothbound cheddar, which stand up to the wine's depth.

title: Domaine de Vougeraie Gevrey Chambertin 'Les Evocelles' 2023
bodyHtml:
This elegant Pinot Noir hails from the Gevrey Chambertin appellation in the Côte de Nuits region of Burgundy, France. Domaine de la Vougeraie was created in 1999 by the Boisset family, who consolidated their premium vineyard holdings into a single estate dedicated to organic and biodynamic viticulture.

Wine Description

'Les Evocelles' presents a bright mid ruby purple colour and a complex sensory profile. The nose is highly aromatic and floral, featuring a mixture of red and black fruits such as cherry and raspberry alongside darker notes of blackberry and cassis. Subtle spiciness, including hints of cracked black pepper, Earl Grey tea, and vanilla, adds further depth. On the palate, the wine is medium bodied and silky, exhibiting a vibrant energy and a fine-boned structure. It displays a commendable persistency and a saline, fresh finish, balanced by well-judged tannins.

title: Luce Brunello di Montalcino 2018
bodyHtml:
Luce Brunello shows an intense ruby red color. The nose is complex and fragrant, with notes of ripe red fruit, supported by pleasant sensations of blond tobacco and exotic spices. In the mouth, the wine is harmonious, rich and highly structured, with silky tannins that together with freshness give a very long persistence. A sophisticated and powerful wine.

96 Points - James Suckling

A finely structured and focused Brunello with a complex array of cherries, blackberries, dried roses, bark, licorice and hints of praline. Iodine and oyster shells, too. Medium-to full-bodied with firm, very fine tannins. Beautiful texture and balance. Remains fresh and fine until the end. 

93 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2018 Brunello di Montalcino is generous and open in personality, but like many other wines from this vintage, the alcohol content is just too high at 15.5%. This is a particular problem when it comes to Sangiovese from Montalcino, a denomination that plays its best cards in terms of elegant, age-worthy wines. A vintage like this is better suited to near and medium-term drinking. It shows sweet cherry, dried raspberry, spice and fragrant rose. The wine is presented in a heavy glass bottle that is graphically beautiful despite its less environmentally friendly implications.

93 Points - Wine Spectator

Rich and plump, this juicy red features cherry, black currant and Mediterranean scrub flavors, with flashes of graphite backed by a swath of muscular tannins, which exert their presence on the finish. Shows fine balance overall.

title: Chateau Trotanoy 2005
bodyHtml:
When ready, this wine shows enormous complexity and concentration and belongs to the most sought-after Pomerols. It can easily be kept 25 years or more in great vintages.

96 Points - Wine Enthusiast

Certainly, it is firm, with impressive power. But the smoothness of the ripe black fruits combined with the beautifully judged wood shows a contrast of tension with the dense, chewy core. This wine is dark, solid, and concentrated at its heart, promising long aging.

96 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Tasted at the Trotanoy vertical in Hong Kong, the 2005 Trotanoy has been an awesome Pomerol since birth. Now at 12 years old, the "giant" is beginning to flex its muscles. It has more red than black fruit, more floral than the likes of the 2000 or 2001, beautifully defined with raspberry coulis, wild strawberry, clove and bay leaf, iris and violet unfurling with continued aeration. The palate has a lovely grainy texture and fine salinity. The acidity is extremely well judged, and the structure and backbone, perhaps even the stubbornness, define this great vineyard. There is enormous potential here. Tasted November 2016.

title: Chateau Rauzan Segla 2009
bodyHtml:
The wines at Chateau Rauzan-Segla have delighted many well-know figures, most famously Thomas Jefferson who came across this wine during his visit to the vineyards of Bordeaux, placing an order for several cases of it. He thus became a fervent admirer or Rauzan-Segla wines. Some decades later, the 1855 Classification ranked Chateau Rauzan-Segla as a Second Growth.

Looking, smelling and tasting a glass of Rauzan-Segla wine is an invitation to a journey like no other. This journey of pleasure begins with the eye. The beauty of a color so intense that is impossible to take one's eye off of it. A color that draws us in and makes us want to discover it secrets. The pleasure of its luxurious aromas disclosing cigar bo notes which combine harmoniously with aromas of ripe fruit. The first sip coats the palate seductively with a combination of finesse, elegance and unparalleled charm. The wine's smooth, complex texture will make you want to linger over the tasting experience. To taste a glass of Rauzan-Segla is to savor its fruity freshness and let yourself be transported by its silky smooth texture, the result of over three centuries of winemaking expertise.

96 Points - James Suckling

Deep, spicy and earthy, but with plenty of Cabernet Sauvignon cassis aroma and solid tannins giving it a serious structure. It's not the most polished Medoc of the vintage, but there's plenty of concentration and energy driving the long firm finish. Give it more time. Try after 2021.

95 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

The 2009 Rauzan-Segla shows the style of the vintage perfectly and is a ripe, mouthfilling, sexy Margaux that’s just begging to be drunk. It doesn’t have the sheer density of the 2010 but offers a more weightless, full-bodied, layered style as well as fabulous notes of dark fruits, roasted herbs, graphite, chocolate, and tobacco.

95 Points - Wine Enthusiast

A rich and opulent wine, very ripe, packed with luscious blackberry and damson fruit as well as sweet tannins. It is a fruit salad of fruit flavors given structure by a core of dryness. Already a gorgeous wine, but one that will also age.

94 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Deep garnet colored, the 2009 Rauzan-Segla bursts from the glass with bold, vivacious Black Forest cake, blackberry pie and warm blueberry scents plus nuances of cardamom, candied violets, smoked meats and Chinese five spice with a waft of dusty soil. Full-bodied, rich, plush and decadent, it completely coats the palate with densely packed preserved black berries layers, finishing very long and spicy. 

94 Points - Vinous

93 Points - Decanter

92 Points - Wine Spectator

title: Chateau Pontet Canet 2016
bodyHtml:
Introduction

Château Pontet Canet 2016 is a red wine from France, produced in the Bordeaux region and the Pauillac appellation. Château Pontet Canet is a highly renowned estate classified as a Cinquième Cru Classé (Fifth Growth) in the 1855 Bordeaux Classification. Under the ownership of the Tesseron family, the winery has become one of Bordeaux's leading estates, pioneering the use of biodynamic farming since the early 2000s. The winery's philosophy is centred on a deeply personal connection to the terroir, expressed through natural, minimal intervention viticulture and winemaking.

Wine Description

The wine has a deep, dense, inky purple colour. The aromatic profile is complex and profound, offering scents of crushed blackcurrant, black cherry, dried violets, and cedar. Further nuances include graphite, licorice, wood smoke, and an unmistakable purity of fruit.

The varietal composition is a blend of 62% Cabernet Sauvignon, 32% Merlot, 4% Cabernet Franc, and 2% Petit Verdot. It is a full-bodied wine. The palate is rich, powerful, and concentrated, yet impeccably balanced and elegant. The mouthfeel is smooth and velvety, guided by wonderfully refined, lush tannins. Stylistically, it is a magnificent, profound wine that showcases the purity and textural excellence achieved through biodynamic farming. The wine was aged for 16 to 18 months, with 50% in new French oak barrels and 35% in concrete amphorae. The finish is incredibly long, fragrant, and pure. The ABV is 13.5%. The optimal drinking window is to drink now through 2050. The vineyard is certified organic (Ecocert) and biodynamic (Demeter).

Accolades

  • James Suckling - 100 points

  • Vinous - 98 points

  • The Wine Advocate - 97 points

  • Decanter - 97 points

Food Pairing

This powerful and complex Bordeaux pairs ideally with rich, classic dishes. Suggested pairings include roasted leg of lamb, ribeye steak, seared duck breast, truffle-infused dishes, and aged hard cheeses.

Vintage Quality

The 2016 vintage is one of the greatest in recent Bordeaux history, marked by a warm, dry summer and perfect, sunny conditions in September and October that allowed for a leisurely, optimal harvest. This resulted in wines with both great power and finesse, characterized by high concentration and impeccable balance.

title: Secret Door Cabernet Sauvignon Hirondelle Vineyard 2021
bodyHtml: Hirondelle Vineyard is located in the center of the famous Stags Leap District of the Napa Valley. Planted in 1996 it has fully mature vines producing world-class quality Cabernet Sauvignon. The Stags Leap District is noted for Cabernet Sauvignon wines that exhibit complexity, supple tannins and both ripe fruit as well as floral notes in the flavours.

title: Lignier Michelot Morey Saint Denis 'Aux Cheseaux' Premier Cru 2021
bodyHtml: These are the oldest vineyards on the estate: some of them are over 65 years old. This Morey-Saint-Denis Premier Cru is one of the emblematic cuvees of the estate. Whatever the vintage, it is a wine that reveals a very great terroir with a remarkable aromatic palate. A complete and seductive Morey-Saint-Denis.

title: Romitorio Brunello di Montalcino 'Filo di Seta' 2020
bodyHtml:
Italy’s Tuscany region is renowned for its iconic wines, and at its heart lies Montalcino, home to the prestigious Brunello. Castello Romitorio, situated in the northwest part of the appellation, was acquired and restored by artist Sandro Chia in the 1980s. The estate is celebrated for its fusion of art and winemaking, producing elegant expressions of Sangiovese that reflect the area's unique terroir.

Wine Description
The 2020 'Filo di Seta' is a luminous garnet-red wine with a captivating bouquet of black cherry, dried rose petals, forest floor, and subtle hints of tobacco and spice. On the palate, it delivers layered flavours of red currant, blood orange, cedar, and sweet herbs, all framed by finely woven tannins and vibrant acidity. Full-bodied and structured, the wine shows exceptional balance, energy, and a persistent mineral-driven finish.

Accolades
● Wine Advocate – 98 points

Food Pairing
This Brunello pairs beautifully with herb-crusted lamb, mushroom risotto, or aged Pecorino Toscano. These pairings emphasize the wine's complexity and savoury elegance. Together, they create an unforgettable dining experience.

title: Opus One 2021
bodyHtml:
The essence of time is expressed in Opus One by the character of each vintage. Place, often defined as terroir, represents the geography, the climate and the essential human element which is captured in the wine’s balance between power and finesse, structure and texture.

99 Points - James Suckling

An enticing aroma of violets, cherry blossoms, fresh blue and black fruit and great structure define this beautiful, age-worthy wine. Subtle layering of fruit and oak spices between firm, fine-grained and supportive tannins gives it a calm intensity. So elegant and polished. Hints of cinnamon and graphite accent blackcurrant and blueberry flavors that linger and grow in a long finish. Already attractive to drink, but best after 2029.

98 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

Based on 93% Cabernet Sauvignon, 4% Cabernet Franc, 2% Petit Verdot, and splashes of Merlot and Malbec, the 2021 Opus One is gorgeous and just pure class. Cassis, graphite, charcoal, lead pencil, and violet-driven aromatics all emerge from the glass. Full-bodied, layered, and concentrated, with ripe, polished tannins, it exemplifies the fresh, focused, incredibly classy style of the vintage.

97 Points - Vinous

The 2021 Opus One is dark, powerful and super- concentrated. Lavender, rose petal, dark cherry, plum, mocha and gravel race across the palate. Still very much a youngster, the 2021 is shaping up to be a jewel of a wine. All the elements are so well balanced for a young Opus One out of barrel. There’s real palate presence and weight here.

96+ Points - Jeb Dunnuck

More in the structured style of the 2018 as opposed to the voluptuous style of the 2019, the 2021 Opus One is another riveting wine from this estate. Pure cassis, graphite, chocolate, and nicely integrated oak, as well as an undeniable sense of minerality, all emerge from the glass, and it hits the palate with medium to full-bodied richness, building tannins, wonderful purity and precision, and a great finish.

title: Caymus Cabernet Sauvignon 'Special Selection' 2019
bodyHtml:
The Caymus 'Special Selection' Cabernet Sauvignon is an exceptional wine made from this storied Napa Valley estate.

After some time to open, this incredible Cabernet begins to yield profound aromatics of black cherry compote, blueberry pie and boysenberry, creosote, black tar, milk chocolate and licorice, soaring from the glass. The mouthfeel is rich, voluptuous and intense, as this wine offers exceedingly dense, concentrated flavours of black cherry reduction, blueberry pie, raspberry liquor and boysenberry, alongside milk chocolate shavings and tar, all cascading onto the long mouth coating finish.  

Caymus sets aside the best barrels of its Cabernet Sauvignon from Napa Valley each year to produce a 'Special Selection.'

94 Points - Wine Spectator
"Flashy, with boysenberry and mulberry pâte de fruit notes that roll through, throwing off licorice snap and acai berry notes as well. Ends with a high-gloss toasty finish."

title: Masi Amarone Costasera 2009
bodyHtml:
This prestigious red wine originates from the Amarone della Valpolicella Classico DOCG in the Veneto region of Italy. The history of the Boscaini family, owners of Masi Agricola, began in 1772 with their first harvest in the 'Vaio dei Masi' valley. The winery's philosophy is defined by its unrivalled expertise in the 'appassimento' technique, a traditional method where grapes are dried on bamboo racks during winter to concentrate aromas and flavours. Costasera refers to the sunset-facing slopes in Valpolicella Classica, which benefit from extended daylight and a mild climate reflected from nearby Lake Garda.

Wine Description

The Masi Costasera Amarone Classico 2009 presents a very dark ruby red colour. The sensory profile is rich and intense, featuring a nose of baked fruit, plums, and cherries with hints of coffee, cocoa, and spice. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied and well-balanced, showcasing generous black cherry flavours alongside notes of raisin, chocolate, and baking spices like nutmeg and cinnamon. It is characterized by smooth, velvety tannins and a compelling intensity, followed by a long and pleasing finish. This blend is composed of the traditional varieties Corvina, Rondinella, and Molinara, and it has an ABV of 15%.

Vintage Quality

The 2009 vintage in Valpolicella is considered outstanding, with wines that have aged better than many experts initially predicted. A wet late winter was followed by a hot spring and a very hot summer, which provided the grapes with extraordinary depth and darkness while maintaining a surprising freshness and fruity character. Top winemakers successfully managed the harvest in late September to produce wines with elegant, well-structured profiles and significant aging potential.

title: Bruno Paillard Brut Premiere Cuvee (NV)
bodyHtml:
The Premiere Cuvee Champagne is a very personal interpretation of the whole region, through the selection of 35 of the 320 crus of champagne.  An excellent aperitif. It matches divinely with cheese (Brie de Meaux, Camembert, aged salers), poultry and shellfish.

45% Pinot Noir, 33% Chardonnay, 22% Pinot Meunier

A straw gold colour and very fine bubbles. Its delicate hue comes from to the use of a high percentage of Chardonnay and of the first pressing only. The first aromas reveal the citrus character of the Chardonnay, such as lime and grapefruits. Red fruit aromas then come out, including redcurrant, raspberry and morello cherry, typical of Pinot Noir. On leaving the wine to open up, candied fruits, even exotic fruits of Pinot Meunier appear with aromas of banana and pineapple. The palate is lively. The nose is confirmed by the first taste, including citrus, almonds, toasted bread and brioche, but also redcurrant jelly and dark fruits like cherry, fig or blackberry. The palate is full, quite long, with a very clean finish. Elegant, but not without complexity, this wine perfectly illustrates what is "the house style".

92 Points - Decanter

A whiff of flint precedes fresh lemon notes that pervade the entire wine with vivid freshness. The palate is taut and bright, with a rather salty, iodine savoriness. Lovely depth from the great proportion of reserve wines. The finish is brisk, with citrus and umami.

91 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The NV Brut Première Cuvée (Disgorged 07/2016) has a bright straw-gold color. The blend of Pinot Noir (45%), Chardonnay (33%) and Pinot Meunier (22%) opens with a clear, fresh and open, very elegant and generous bouquet of bright, ripe fruits (melons, lemons) with beautiful chalk, brioche and toast flavors as well as emerging notes of sweet cherries and wild strawberries. Nice purity. This is a highly elegant, fresh, textured and tightly woven but very well balanced cuvée with lovely purity and a persistently salty, citrus-fresh and cleansing finish with good grip. This is an extraordinary effort.

91 Points - James Suckling

An attractive, fresh mix of citrus and peach fruits here. The gently spicy, biscuity complexity sits amid nicely played autolysis characters that make this fresh and lively. The palate has plenty of bright and sweet-peach and melon-fruit flavors. It's really easygoing, in fact, displaying generous punchy flavors and zesty acid crunch that holds it all together.

title: Tenuta Corte Pavone Brunello Di Montalcino 2018
bodyHtml:
Wine Description
Made from 100% Sangiovese grapes, this wine has a deep ruby red colour with garnet reflections. On the nose, it presents aromas of black cherries and wild berries, along with notes of spices, leather, and tobacco. The palate is full-bodied with a fresh, balanced flavour profile and firm tannins. It's described as an expressive wine with a precise structure and authentic Tuscan character, and while it is ready to drink now, it also has the potential to age well. This wine is organic.

Accolades

  • Robert Parker - 94 points

  • James Suckling - 93 points

  • Wine Enthusiast - 91 points

  • Winescritic - 92 points

  • Jeb Dunnuck - 91 points

Food Pairing
This wine is a classic partner for traditional Tuscan dishes such as wild boar ragu or Bistecca alla Fiorentina. It also pairs well with other rich dishes like braised lamb, beef stews, or risotto with mushrooms or truffles. Aged cheeses such as Pecorino Toscano or Parmigiano-Reggiano are also a perfect match, as their nutty and savoury notes complement the wine's tannins and fruitiness. A perfect match to enhance the wine's complexity.

title: Argot Wines 1555 Cabernet Sauvignon Oakville 'Bonny's Vineyard' 2021
bodyHtml:
Born in the Midwest, to a large Irish family, wine did not play a role in Justin's life while growing up. Milk was the beverage of choice at the dinner table, and the industrial beers of the Midwest fueled family parties. He does not pinpoint a specific moment that his passion for wine was ignited but, instead, attributes it to a series of experiences, places visited, bottles opened and friendships forged. At this point in life, he can not imagine a life without the joys of all things wine! 

Hailing from the historic Bonny's Vineyard in the heart of Oakville. Gravel-rich soils promote vine roots to plumb deep into the valley floor, while leaf canopies harvest Napa's persistent summer sunshine. These conditions conspire to produce a profound Cabernet Sauvignon terroir at this marquee Oakville site. 

After dialling in the vines with aggressive farming practices, what resulted was a particularly late harvest by this site's standard of exquisitely ripe and delicious Cabernet Sauvignon grapes.  Pouring a deep opaque red-violet, 1555's Cabernet personality leaps from the glass balancing opulent fruit, damp earth, chilling minerality, and an alluring spicy note that keeps pulling us back for more. Exquisitely ripe tannins provide a refined, velvety structure that expertly delivers a deep and seductively rich palate. A stunning Cabernet Sauvignon of undeniable pedigree.

title: Domaine William Fevre Chablis Grand Cru 'Les Clos' 2022
bodyHtml:
​Domaine William Fèvre, established in 1959, is a renowned winery in Chablis, Burgundy, France. With a deep respect for the region's terroir, the estate owns 4.1 hectares of the 25-hectare Les Clos Grand Cru vineyard, with approximately half of these vines planted between 1948 and 1952 by William Fèvre's father.

Wine Description

The 2022 Chablis Grand Cru Les Clos presents a translucent lemon and lime colour. The bouquet is currently reserved, hinting at sublime purity. On the palate, it offers a harmonious array of white fruit, complemented by a touch of spice and vibrant acidity. The wine is full-bodied, dense, and satiny, with a layered and concentrated structure that promises significant aging potential.

Accolades

  • Robert Parker's Wine Advocate: 96 points.

  • Decanter: 95 points.

Food Pairing

This Chablis pairs excellently with dishes such as seared scallops, grilled lobster, or creamy mushroom risotto. These pairings highlight the wine's depth and character.​

title: Joseph Phelps 'Insignia' 2019
bodyHtml:
Joseph Phelps Vineyards, established in 1973 in Napa Valley, California, is renowned for its dedication to producing exceptional estate-grown wines. Founded by Joseph Phelps, the winery pioneered Bordeaux-style blends in the United States, with its flagship wine, 'Insignia,' first introduced in 1974. Over the decades, 'Insignia' has become a benchmark for American Bordeaux-style wines, earning international acclaim.

The 2019 'Insignia' is a blend of 93% Cabernet Sauvignon, 5% Petit Verdot, and 2% Malbec, sourced from seven estate vineyards across Napa Valley. This vintage presents a deep garnet-purple hue, reflecting its concentration and richness. On the nose, it reveals enticing aromatics of crème de cassis, red fruits, leafy tobacco, and delicate dried rose petals. The palate is dense and layered, offering juicy flavours of blackberry, raspberry, black currant, and dark chocolate. Its structure is complemented by refined tannins and balanced acidity, resulting in a wine of energy, length, and complexity. Approachable now, the 2019 vintage will continue to develop gracefully over the next two decades.

This exceptional wine pairs beautifully with roasted lamb, grilled ribeye steak, or aged cheeses like Gouda and Cheddar. These pairings enhance the wine’s depth, creating an unforgettable dining experience.

The 2019 growing season in Napa Valley began with a wet winter and cooler spring, leading to a slightly delayed bud break. Warm summer days followed by cool nights allowed for even ripening and the development of nuanced flavours. Joseph Phelps Vineyards’ meticulous vineyard management and winemaking practices have culminated in a wine that exemplifies the excellence of this vintage.

title: Les Forts de Latour 2017
bodyHtml:
The vineyards of the Chateau Latour have been producing wines since the 16th century. Today, the vineyards in production cover 80 hectares, including 48 around the chateau, known as the "Enclos." This Enclos consists of a ridge that peaks at 16 meters above the level of the Gironde, bordered to the north and to the south by two streams and to the east by the "Palus" alluvial land along the Gironde.

Les Forts de Latour is produced with the same meticulous care as the Grand Vin, both in the vineyard and in the winery. The only notable difference, apart from the origin of the grapes, is the proportion of new barrels (50 to 60%) used in the maturing stage.

94+ Points - James Suckling

This is really minerally with crushed stones and dark berries. Some licorice. Medium to full body, firm and silky tannins and a beautiful, tight and focused finish. Such energy, delivered down a straight line. 

94 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

A blend of 65.2% Cabernet Sauvignon, 33% Merlot, 0.8% Cabernet Franc and 1% Petit Verdot, the 2017 Les Forts de Latour is deep garnet-purple in color and strides confidently out of the glass with classic notes of plum preserves, warm cassis and pencil shavings with nuances of mulberries, pencil lead, Indian spices and forest floor. Medium-bodied, the palate packs a lot of fruit into a very elegant, tightly knit palate, delivering expressive blackberry and spicy flavors with a firm frame of grainy tannins and bold freshness, finishing long with a peppery kick.

94 Points - Wine Enthusiast

This bold, structured wine is packed with blackberry fruits and ripe tannins. Freshness and structure from the Cabernet Sauvignon are very present, giving a crisp edge to the solid backbone.

93 Points - Wine Spectator

93 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

92 Points - Decanter

title: Chateau La Mission Haut Brion 2009
bodyHtml:
A bewitching wine, from beginning to end of the end of the tasting experience! The colour is very deep and the nose is intense, with plenty of character. This rich and utterly delicious wine spreads out beautifully on the palate. The tannin is smooth and sweet. 2009 La Mission Haut-Brion inevitably reminds tasters of one of the estate's finest successes: the 2000 vintage. The concentration, class, and balance between power and freshness are the hallmarks of both 2000 and 2009. However, 2009 has greater concentration, as well as another dimension and even stronger sensations.

2009 Chateau La Mission Haut-Brion is already mythical. Blend: 47% Merlot, 47% Cabernet Sauvignon, 6% Cabernet Franc.

100 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

A candidate for the wine of the vintage, the 2009 La Mission Haut-Brion stood out as one of the most exceptional young wines I had ever tasted from barrel, and its greatness has been confirmed in the bottle. A remarkable effort from the Dillon family, this is another large-scaled La Mission that tips the scales at 15% alcohol. A blend of equal parts Cabernet Sauvignon and Merlot (47% of each) and the rest Cabernet Franc, it exhibits an opaque purple colour as well as a magnificent bouquet of truffles, scorched earth, blackberry and blueberry liqueur, subtle smoke and spring flowers. The wine-s remarkable concentration offers up an unctuous/viscous texture, a skyscraper-like mouthfeel, sweet, sumptuous, nearly over-the-top flavours and massive density. Perhaps a once-in-a-lifetime La Mission Haut-Brion, the 2009 will take its place alongside the many great wines made here since the early 1920s. It should last for 50-75+ years.

title: Joseph Drouhin Gevrey Chambertin 2024
bodyHtml:
Maison Joseph Drouhin, established in Beaune in 1880, is one of Burgundy’s most historically significant and revered négociant-éleveurs. For four generations, the Drouhin family has championed an elegant style that favors finesse and precision over heavy, over-extracted power.

Their village-level Gevrey-Chambertin represents a masterful blend of select plots spanning this iconic Côte de Nuits commune. The chalky, clay-marl soils here naturally endow Pinot Noir with robust muscle and structure, which Drouhin expertly shapes into a remarkably fluid, bright, and classical expression.

Wine Description

The Joseph Drouhin Gevrey-Chambertin 2024 features a brilliant, clear ruby color in the glass. True to the house style, the nose is intensely aromatic and exceptionally fresh, bursting with notes of ripe black cherries, wild blackberries, and a fine hint of licorice. A very discreet, integrated oak profile wraps around the fruit, yielding whispers of light baking spice and nutmeg.

On the palate, the 2024 vintage showcases a lighter, delightfully purist "Burgundian" energy. It is medium-bodied with an elevated, mouthwatering acidity that underscores the purity of the red and black fruits. The tannins are incredibly fine-grained and powdery, lacking any rustic harshness.

Crafted from 100% Pinot Noir, the fruit was fully destemmed and fermented using indigenous yeasts. The wine was aged for 14 to 16 months in French oak barrels sourced from high-density forests, with a restrained 20% to 25% new oak. To ensure seamless wood integration, Drouhin insists on weathering their stave wood for a full three years before barrel coopering. This youthful, vibrant vintage can be enjoyed early with aeration but will age comfortably for 8 to 13 years.

title: La Chapelle d'Ausone 2012
bodyHtml:
La Chapelle d'Ausone 2012 hails from the Saint Emilion Grand Cru appellation in the Bordeaux region of France. This wine is the second label of the historic Château Ausone, where Alain Vauthier and his daughter Pauline maintain a reputation for compulsive perfectionism on their decomposed limestone slopes.

Wine Description

This 2012 vintage presents a dense ruby purple colour and an expansive sensory profile. The nose is highly aromatic, revealing refined layers of plum, blueberry, and black raspberry, accented by spring flowers and the estate's signature note of powdered chalk. On the palate, the wine is medium to full bodied with a silky yet structured texture, featuring ripe tannins and a fresh, vibrant acidity. Stylistically, it displays remarkable purity and a long, lingering finish that balances rich fruit with mineral complexity.

Accolades

  • James Suckling - 95 points

  • Robert Parker's Wine Advocate - 93 points

  • Wine Enthusiast - 93 points

Food Pairing

This wine's generous fruit profile and velvety tannins make it an excellent companion for grilled meat dishes, such as herb-crusted lamb or prime rib. It also pairs beautifully with roasted poultry or a selection of aged hard cheeses.

title: Booker Vineyard Syrah 'Fracture' 2019
bodyHtml:
Booker Vineyard's Fracture Syrah hails from the Paso Robles region in California, USA. Established by Eric Jensen, Booker Vineyard is renowned for its commitment to organic and biodynamic farming practices, producing wines that reflect the unique terroir of their 100-acre estate. The vineyard's calcareous limestone soils, which tend to 'fracture,' inspire the name of this flagship Syrah.

Wine Description

This Syrah pairs exceptionally well with robust dishes such as grilled lamb, braised short ribs, or venison stew. The wine's depth and character are highlighted when accompanied by rich, savory meats, creating an unforgettable dining experience.

title: Chateau Quintus 'Le Dragon de Quintus' 2016
bodyHtml:
Chateau Quintus is the 5th child within the Domaine Clarence Dillon family of wines. Its name is a tribute to the Gallo-Romans, creators of Saint-Emilion’s vineyards, who had the custom of naming their fifth child Quintus. The environmental specificity of Château Quintus lies in its Mediterranean Green Belt, a real haven of biodiversity, as well as in the woods and grounds of the estate.

Le Dragon de Quintus is the second wine of Chateau Quintus. The name originates from the dragon statue that towers above the magical terroir of Saint-Emilion, perched high upon the promontory, where the estate is located.

Beautiful red colour with mauve highlights.  Ripe and fairly intense bouquet of crunchy red fruit (cherry). The oak is already well-integrated. The wine starts of quite smooth on the palate, immediately going on to reveal excellent fruit. It develops softly on the palate with plenty of tannin, but that is rich and never aggressive.

title: Perrier Jouet Belle Epoque 2013 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
This elegant and famous champagne was first made in Epernay early in the nineteenth century. Created by Nicolas Perrier and his wife Adele Jouet, the brand was an instant success. They recognized the potential of overseas markets and Perrier-Jouet sent its first consignment to Great Britain in 1815 and to the U.S. in 1822.

French it may be, but in 1861, Champagne Perrier-Jouet was the favorite of Queen Victoria, and the House became not only the official supplier of the British monarchy, but also of the Swedish royal family and the King of Belgium.

Perrier-Jouet’s most famous champagne is its Prestige Cuvee, Fleur de Champagne, ensconced in the Emile Galle designed “flower” bottle that pays tribute to the Belle Epoque era.

title: Castiglion del Bosco Brunello di Montalcino 'Campo del Drago' 2011
bodyHtml:
Campo del Drago is a Brunello di Montalcino Cru from the finest vineyard in the Capanna area, a hectare and a half at the highest elevation (560 meters) and with the best exposure. The major presence of Tuscan stone Galestro makes the wine extremely complex, with well present tannins and great ageing potential. A Brunello with character and structure, ruby red, dense and "bright", with a superb acidity that supports and enhances it.

93 Points - James Suckling

Bright and fruity yet I like the rich and decadent palate of chocolate and berries. Medium to full body and silky tannins. Savory finish.

91 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2011 Brunello di Montalcino Campo del Drago is more immediate and fleshed out compared to the same wine from the previous vintage. Warm summer temperatures have contributed to the wine's openness and its generosity. It offers a succession of red cherry, sweet spice, leather, cola and balsam herb aromas. It also shows an evident dose of oak spice and toast that still needs time to integrate. Campo del Drago requires an additional two to four years of bottle aging.

90 Points - Wine Spectator

Cherry and strawberry flavors are framed by oak spice in this polished red. Bright and well-proportioned. Needs a little time to integrate.

title: Montes Purple Angel 2020 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
This red wine originates from Chile, specifically from the Apalta and Marchigüe subregions within the Colchagua Valley. Viña Montes was founded in 1987 by a visionary quartet including Aurelio Montes, who is widely credited with pioneering Chile's quality revolution and elevating Carmenère to international acclaim. The winery's philosophy emphasizes a 'pre industrial' approach and 'sustainable dry farming,' allowing the unique granite and clay soils of their estate vineyards to produce fruit with exceptional concentration.

Wine Description

Montes Purple Angel 2020 displays an impressive deep purplish red colour with garnet reflections. The nose is intense and sun kissed, offering outstanding aromas of ripe blackberry, plum, and blueberry jam layered with notes of sweet spices, dark chocolate, mocha, and a balsamic backdrop. On the palate, the wine is full bodied and voluminous, featuring a juicy flow and soft, ample tannins that provide a luxurious and well structured foundation. It is characterized by its remarkable complexity and freshness, leading to an elegant, long finish with hints of toasted nuts and sweet spice. This blend consists of 92% Carmenère and 8% Petit Verdot, with 70% of the wine aged for 18 months in new French oak barrels. The ABV is 14.5%. While Montes follows rigorous sustainable practices, including the use of grazing animals to manage weeds, this bottling is not certified organic. The optimal drinking window is from 2025 through 2040.

Accolades

  • James Suckling - 98 points.

  • Tim Atkin - 97 points.

  • Natalie MacLean - 96 points.

  • Vinous - 94 points.

  • Wine Spectator - 93 points.

Food Pairing

The bold structure and opulent fruit of this Carmenère blend make it an ideal companion for rich and savoury meat dishes. It pairs perfectly with roast lamb seasoned with rosemary, grilled beef tenderloin, or barbecue pork ribs. Its spicy and chocolatey undertones also complement game meats, wild mushroom risotto, or pasta dishes like cannelloni. For a cheese pairing, consider a mature blue cheese or a hard, aged cheddar.

Vintage Quality

The 2020 vintage in the Colchagua Valley was characterized by a warm year that resulted in low yields and highly concentrated berries. Despite the heat, the controlled water stress and the winemaker's skill in managing extraction produced a wine that maintains a remarkable balance of energy and sweetness.

title: Chateau Mouton Rothschild 2021
bodyHtml:
Château Mouton Rothschild, a celebrated first-growth estate in the Pauillac appellation, is synonymous with artistry and excellence. Owned by the Rothschild family since 1853, the estate is famed for its iconic label art and its meticulous winemaking. The 2021 vintage reflects a year of challenges in Bordeaux, highlighting the estate’s commitment to crafting wines of precision and elegance.

Wine Description

Mouton Rothschild 2021 displays a deep ruby hue, with an expressive bouquet of blackcurrant, wild blackberry, and violet, complemented by notes of cedar, graphite, and a touch of mocha. On the palate, it is medium-bodied and finely structured, with polished tannins, a vibrant acidity, and a layered complexity. Flavors of dark berries, tobacco, and crushed stone lead to a long, refined finish with remarkable freshness and poise.

Food Pairing

This vintage pairs beautifully with dishes like grilled rack of lamb, braised short ribs, or aged Comté cheese. Together, they enhance the wine’s depth and character, offering a harmonious and memorable culinary experience.

Vintage Quality

The 2021 vintage, characterized by a cooler growing season and meticulous vineyard care, presents a classic Pauillac profile. While not as powerful as some recent vintages, it is defined by its elegance, precision, and aging potential, making it a must-have for collectors and enthusiasts.

title: Bollinger Champagne PN AYC18
bodyHtml:
Bollinger, one of Champagne’s most prestigious houses, is renowned for its rich, Pinot Noir-driven style. Founded in 1829 in Aÿ, this family-owned maison has built its reputation on meticulous vineyard management and long lees aging, ensuring complexity and depth in every bottle. The PN AYC18 is part of Bollinger’s PN series, showcasing the expressive character of Pinot Noir from specific terroirs, with this edition highlighting fruit from Aÿ.

Wine Description

Brilliant golden in hue, the PN AYC18 delivers an intricate aromatic profile, brimming with orchard fruits, citrus zest, toasted almonds, and subtle smoky undertones. The palate is vibrant yet structured, displaying layers of baked apple, brioche, and a fine minerality that reflects its Aÿ origins. The mousse is creamy and persistent, complementing the wine’s balanced acidity and elegant, lingering finish. A composition dominated by Pinot Noir, it reflects Bollinger’s commitment to bold yet refined expressions of Champagne.

Food Pairing

The PN AYC18 pairs exceptionally well with roasted poultry, mushroom-based dishes, or creamy cheeses such as Comté. It also complements shellfish and caviar, enhancing their briny depth with its bright acidity and rich texture. A perfect match to enhance the wine's complexity.

Vintage Quality

Sourced predominantly from the 2018 vintage, the PN AYC18 benefits from a warm growing season, yielding ripe fruit with concentrated flavors. The addition of reserve wines ensures a signature Bollinger depth and longevity, making this a compelling Champagne to enjoy now or cellar for future enjoyment.

94 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Based on the 2018 vintage, complemented by reserve wines aged in magnum dating back to 2009, Bollinger's newly released NV Brut Blanc de Noirs PN AYC18 was disgorged this year with six grams per liter dosage. Foregrounding the village of Aÿ, a commune crucial to Bollinger's distinctive style, the wine wafts from the glass with aromas of golden orchard fruit, honeycomb, buttered toast, freshly baked bread and dried white flowers. Medium to full-bodied, pillowy and vinous, with an ample core of fruit that's girdled by lively acids and animated by an elegant pinpoint mousse, this suave, charming Champagne concludes with a chalky finish. This has turned out beautifully.

93 Points - Decanter

The fourth edition of Bollinger's limited PN series is the most expressive yet, with a hugely satisfying, expansive character. Dried pear, stewed Bramley apple and nectarine melt into the depths of reserve wine complexity, with chestnut honey and perfectly pitched savoury interest. It's surprisingly silky, the texture surprisingly weightless, the shape rounded and cushioned rather than strict or driving. A highly rewarding Champagne, ready to drink but with interesting potential to evolve over the next five years. 100% Pinot Noir, predominantly from Aÿ, with support from the villages of Tauxières and Verzenay. Based on the 2018 vintage, with 50% reserve wines back to 2009.

93 Points - Wine Spectator

Mouthwatering and finely meshed, with density to the satiny texture, this marries bright acidity with flavors of ripe white cherry, biscuit, pickled ginger and candied grapefruit peel. Opens slowly on the palate, revealing layers of fragrant spices, mineral and dried flowers on the finish. Disgorged January 2023. Best from 2025 through 2033. 900 cases imported.

93+ Points - Jeb Dunnuck

Including the 2018, 2017, 2016, and 2009 vintage, the pale straw-copper hued NV Champagne PN AYC18 opens with stunning notes of jasmine and tropical flowers, followed by pure and expressive aromas of wild cherry, fresh orange, wet stone, and fresh roses. Full-bodied, with freshness throughout and a hint of warmth on its beautiful finish, this is the most successful of the wines from this line that I have tasted to date, offering fantastic length and gorgeous depth of fruit. It’s going to only improve with another few years in bottle, but it’s gorgeous now.

title: Eisele Vineyard Cabernet Sauvignon 'Altagracia' 2020
bodyHtml:
The 2020 Altagracia is sourced exclusively from clay-rich parcels on the eastern slopes of the 38-acre Eisele Vineyard in Calistoga. Altagracia is an all-estate blend of 96% Cabernet Sauvignon and 4% Petit Verdot.

Very fragrant and expressive, the 2020 Altagracia unveils a floral nose with dried rose petals intertwined with wild strawberries, red currant, cranberry, and a hint of pink pepper and santal. The mouthfeel is round and silky with subtle flavors of black tea, cinnamon, orange peel and cocoa. The texture of tight-knit tannins coating the palate, leads to a long aniseed finish.

title: Joseph Drouhin Meursault 'Perrieres' Premier Cru 2023
bodyHtml:
Maison Joseph Drouhin was founded in Beaune in 1880 and is now overseen by the fourth generation of the Drouhin family. The winery's philosophy is rooted in a profound respect for nature, embracing organic and biodynamic practices to ensure the authentic expression of the land and the elegance of great Burgundies.

Wine Description

On the nose, it presents a complex and varied palette of aromas, including syrup, grilled almond, and preserved fruit, alongside notes of yellow fruits mingling with flower hints. One critic notes aromas of honey, flowers, and dried apples, with crushed stones and a light graphite undertone. The palate is silky and ample, full bodied, and combines generosity, freshness, and finesse. It runs long on the palate, with a lengthy finish that recalls grilled bread and fruit jam. 

Accolades

  • James Suckling - 95 points

Food Pairing

Excellent pairings include rich fish such as grilled or poached delicate fish like Dover sole, as well as rich fish in cream sauce.

title: Perrier Jouet Belle Epoque Rose 2010 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
True to the free spirit of Maison Perrier-Jouet, Perrier-Jouet Belle Epoque Rose is a resolutely original champagne which combines rarity with the ability to surprise. First created in 1978, it is crafted only in exceptional years and produced in extremely limited quantities.

A shimmering, pastel-toned salmon pink with luminous orange highlights. Aromas of strawberry and peony with the tartness of kumquat and white currant. Notes of pink grapefruit and mandarin combined with the generosity of brioche on the palate.

Ideal pairings include salmon or tuna cooked on one side only, salmon with cranberry sauce or thinly sliced duck breast.

91 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2010 Brut Rosé Belle Epoque bursts from the glass with a rich bouquet of peaches, strawberries, warm biscuits, smoky red berries and ginger. On the palate, it's medium to full-bodied, broad and fleshy, with a generous core of fruit that's tempered by some delicate phenolics and underpinned by ripe acids. This is a charming, nicely balanced Rosé Belle Epoque.

title: Mission Hill Oculus 2013 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
Mission Hill Oculus is the flagship Bordeaux style red wine from the Okanagan Valley in British Columbia, Canada. Established in 1981 by proprietor Anthony von Mandl, Mission Hill Family Estate is a pioneer of upscale winemaking in the region, known for its iconic bell tower and its 'vineyard first' philosophy. The Oculus, named after the circular window in the estate's underground barrel cellar, represents the pinnacle of the winery's production, crafted from grapes specifically nurtured from the most prestigious vineyard blocks.

Wine Description

This vintage presents a deep ruby red colour and a bold, structured sensory profile. The nose offers seductive aromas of fleshy ripe dark fruit, violets, and black cherry, accented by complex notes of cedar smoke, cocoa, and warm spices. On the palate, it is full-bodied and dry with a creamy mouthfeel, displaying layered flavours of plum, fruitcake, and chocolate. While the tannins are well-integrated and smooth, they provide enough grip to suggest a long future, leading to a lengthy finish of rich dark plum and spice.

title: Chateau Pavie 2020
bodyHtml:
Chateau Pavie hails from France, specifically from the Saint Emilion region of Bordeaux. The estate traces its roots back to the 4th century when the Romans first planted vines on its south-facing limestone slopes.

Wine Description

This vintage presents an opaque purple black colour and a flamboyant sensory profile. The bouquet is complex, offering intense aromas of black cherry, crème de cassis, and blueberry pie, layered with hints of smoked tobacco, star anise, and crushed limestone. On the palate, the wine is full bodied and powerful yet surprisingly agile, featuring a core of concentrated black and red fruits supported by very fine grained, velvety tannins.

Accolades

  • James Suckling - 100 points

  • Jeb Dunnuck - 100 points

  • Robert Parker's Wine Advocate - 99 points

  • Vinous - 99 points

  • Decanter - 97 points

Food Pairing

The intense concentration and structured tannins of Chateau Pavie 2020 make it an ideal partner for robust dishes such as charcoal-grilled lamb chops, roast duck magret, or ribeye steak served with truffle-infused sauces.

title: Eisele Vineyard Cabernet Sauvignon 2019 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
The 2019 Eisele Vineyard Cabernet Sauvignon is a distinguished red wine from Napa Valley, California. Crafted predominantly from Cabernet Sauvignon grapes, this wine exemplifies Eisele Vineyard's dedication to producing wines of exceptional quality and character.

Colour: Deep garnet-purple hue, indicating its concentration and maturity.

Aroma: An expressive bouquet featuring notes of violets and roses over a core of kirsch, boysenberries, and cassis, complemented by hints of redcurrant jelly and menthol, with wafts of pencil lead and truffles.

Palate: Full-bodied and well-structured, offering flavors of crème de cassis, blueberry preserves, and fresh black plums, complemented by firm, very fine-grained tannins and alluring freshness.

Body: Full-bodied with a rich and velvety mouthfeel, showcasing both power and elegance.

Finish: Long and persistent, leaving a lasting impression of its complex flavors and refined structure.

Accolades:

  • 100 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate
  • 100 Points - The Wine Independent
  • 100 Points - James Suckling

title: Azelia Barolo Margheria 2021
bodyHtml:
Originating from Italy in the Piedmont region, specifically within the Barolo DOCG appellation in Serralunga d'Alba, Azelia Barolo Margheria 2021 represents a legendary, single-vineyard Cru expression of Nebbiolo. Produced by Azienda Agricola Azelia under fifth-generation winemaker Luigi Scavino and his son Lorenzo, the family estate is renowned for its old vine preservation and meticulous organic farming. Sourced from the historic Margheria vineyard, where 60-year-old vines thrive in iron-rich clay and calcareous marl soils at 340 metres elevation, the winemaking philosophy combines traditional craftsmanship with modern precision. Following careful manual harvesting and extended skin contact during fermentation, the wine undergoes long aging in large traditional Austrian and Slavonian oak casks (botti) for 28 months, capturing the site's intense mineral depth, powerful structural frame, and age-worthy elegance.

Wine Description

The wine presents a clear, deep garnet red colour with vibrant orange and ruby highlights along the rim. An intense, deeply complex bouquet opens with classic Serralunga aromas of wild dark cherry, ripe red plum, and dried cranberry, interwoven with sophisticated notes of crushed rose petal, tar, damp earth, licorice, eucalyptus, and iron-like minerality. On the palate, it is full bodied, muscular, and refined, delivering concentrated flavours of dark fruit, blood orange zest, and savory herbs supported by a vibrant, mouthwatering spine of natural acidity. Framed by Margheria's signature firm, fine-grained, and chiseled tannins, it concludes with an exceptionally long, structured finish marked by lingering dark fruit and intense mineral complexity. Composed of 100% Nebbiolo, it combines the formidable power and longevity of Serralunga d'Alba with luminous purity and aromatic grace.

title: Pio Cesare Barolo 2021
bodyHtml:
This classic and structured red wine originates from the Barolo DOCG in Piedmont, Italy. Pio Cesare, founded in 1881, is one of the most historic family-owned estates in the region. The winery's philosophy for this signature bottling is to provide a "comprehensive portrait" of the vintage by blending Nebbiolo from various family-owned vineyards across five major communes: Serralunga d’Alba, La Morra, Grinzane Cavour, Monforte d’Alba, and Castiglione Falletto.

Wine Description

The Pio Cesare Barolo 2021 presents a brilliant garnet colour with a ruby core. The sensory profile is exceptionally deep and complex, featuring an aromatic nose of ripe cherry, wild strawberry, and pomegranate, layered with sophisticated notes of black truffles, dried rose petals, graphite, and cedar. On the palate, the wine is powerful and "chewy yet polished," showcasing a dense core of fruit balanced by firm, fine-grained tannins and a vibrant, "glassy" acidity. It is characterized by its remarkable energy and "inner tension," leading to an exceptionally long, mineral-driven finish with hints of iron ore, dried herbs, and terra cotta. This 100% Nebbiolo was aged for three years in oak, with 70% in large Slavonian casks (botti) and 30% in mid-toasted French oak barriques to enhance texture while preserving the purity of the fruit.

title: Schrader Cabernet Sauvignon 'Old Sparky' 2021 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
98 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

 A best-barrel selection and blend chosen and made by Thomas Rivers Brown, the 2021 Cabernet Sauvignon Old Sparky Beckstoffer To Kalon Vineyard essentially takes the characters of the Beckstoffer To Kalon Vineyard bottling and ratchets up the intensity. Raspberries, blackberries and black cherries cascade over a base of deep Oakville loam and dried spices. It's full-bodied, rich, concentrated and almost creamy in texture, finishing lush and long.

title: Penfolds Bin 149 California Cabernet Sauvignon 2019
bodyHtml:
Introduction

Penfolds Bin 149 California Cabernet Sauvignon 2019 is a red wine from the United States, produced in California. Penfolds is an iconic Australian winery established in 1844, and this release is part of its global initiative to transcend geographical boundaries and explore high quality viticulture internationally. The Bin 149 designation signifies the inclusion of 14.9% Australian Cabernet Sauvignon wine, blended with the finest Californian fruit. This blend embodies the winery's philosophy of combining different terroirs and creating "Wines of the World". The Californian grapes are sourced from multiple prestigious regions across Napa Valley, including Rutherford and Calistoga.

Wine Description

The wine has a deep, saturated purple red colour. The aromatic profile is complex and intense, offering notes of blueberry, blackcurrant, dark chocolate, sweet spice, and cherry compote. Further aromatic nuances include dark plum, crème de cassis, tobacco leaf, vanilla bean, and cedar.

The wine is predominantly Cabernet Sauvignon, with the blend containing 14.9% Australian wine and 85.1% Californian wine. It is a full bodied wine. On the palate, it is plush, layered, and balanced, with abundant fine grained tannins and a concentrated core of fruit. Flavours include plum, blackcurrant, graphite, and toasted baking spices. Stylistically, it is a rich, powerful, and seamless wine with great structure and energy, combining the plushness of California with the savoury tension of Penfolds' Australian character. It was aged for 16 months in $80\%$ new French oak barrels. The finish is long, persistent, and features a minerally, chalky structure. The ABV is 14.5%. The optimal drinking window is now through 2045 or longer. Information on the organic status of the wine is not available in the sources.

Accolades

  • Jeb Dunnuck - 98 points

  • The Wine Advocate - 97 points

  • James Suckling - 97 points

  • Vinous - 95 points

  • Decanter - 93 points

Food Pairing

This powerfully structured Cabernet Sauvignon pairs beautifully with classic beef preparations such as slow roasted prime rib, grilled ribeye steak, or braised short ribs.

Vintage Quality

The 2019 vintage in Napa Valley, which makes up the majority of this blend, was widely considered excellent. It featured a long, moderate, and mild growing season, which allowed for slow, even ripening. The resulting fruit was intensely concentrated with polished tannins and great freshness.

title: Opus One 2022 - 3 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
Opus One 2022 is a hallmark red blend from the Oakville appellation in Napa Valley, California.

The estate was founded in 1978 as a historic joint venture between Baron Philippe de Rothschild of Château Mouton Rothschild and renowned vintner Robert Mondavi. Combining French tradition with American innovation, the winery's sole mission is the pursuit of uncompromising quality through a single, iconic wine. The estate vineyards are farmed organically, with a focus on vine health and maintaining a balanced ecosystem to preserve the founders' vision for future generations.

Wine Description

The 2022 vintage presents a sophisticated and inviting sensory profile, exuding charm with primary aromas of blueberry, cassis, and dried rose petals. Underlying layers of cigar box, olive, and graphite add a rich complexity to the bouquet. On the palate, the wine is harmonious and balanced, featuring bright red-fruit flavours, cocoa, and fresh orange peel. It is characterized by fine-grained tannins and a long, elegant finish that offers lingering notes of wet stone, vanilla, and coffee.

The varietal composition of the 2022 blend is 80% Cabernet Sauvignon, 8% Petit Verdot, 6.5% Cabernet Franc, 5% Merlot, and 0.5% Malbec. After 20 days of skin contact, the wine was aged for 18 months in new French oak barrels. This vintage has an ABV of 14.0%.

Accolades

  • 97 Points - Decanter: "Chocolate, cherry and rose petal aromas on the nose. Very open and alive - this has a great energy from the aromatics alone with soft cedar shavings, vanilla bean and bramble fruit. Juicy and lively, this is full of fun - fruity and concentrated. The tannins are just wonderful, creamy and slightly grippy, extending the flavours vertically. Tons of juicy, succulent fruit - this feels quite modern but still with that flash of sunshine and ripeness. Long lasting with purity and delicacy that make it so enjoyable. A wonderful creation from Michael Silacci. This is not your typical blockbuster at all, this is a darling of a wine. 0.5% Malbec completes the blend. The Opus team chose to pick early and quickly given the heat spikes in 2022, starting with the Merlot on 24th August. Ageing 18 months in French oak."

  • 96 Points - James Suckling: "Generous, with savory aromas of ripe blackcurrants and fresh black cherries and a gentle texture that shows a slight nip of tannin. It is well structured and a bit tight, which is normal for a young cabernet sauvignon-based red that’s a proven collectible. Gives up graphite and pencil shavings, some cocoa and espresso. Full-bodied. Spicy, toasty oak is really showing through right now. Best from 2028."

  • 95 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate: '"icked before, during and after the year's early September heat, the 2022 Opus One—a blend of 80% Cabernet Sauvignon, 8% Petit Verdot, 6.5% Cabernet Franc, 5% Merlot and 0.5% Malbec—admirably reflects the vintage, boasting a ripe, extroverted personality but also a slightly open-knit, coarser mouthfeel than either the 2021 or 2023. Rosemary and sandalwood notes accent cherries on the nose, while the medium- to full-bodied palate is expansive and plush, finishing with ample length and soft tannins."

Food Pairing

The structured tannins and rich fruit profile of Opus One make it an ideal companion for marbled red meats, such as a seared filet mignon with sautéed mushrooms or a classic beef Bourguignon. It stands up beautifully to rare, grilled prime cuts or wine-braised stews. For a more diverse pairing, it can be served alongside a traditional French cassoulet or aged hard cheeses.

title: Laurent Perrier Brut Millesime 2018
bodyHtml:
Laurent-Perrier is highly selective and only produces a vintage in the best years. While staying true to the House style of freshness and elegance, the Vintage also aims to show the quintessential character of the individual year.

With equal parts of Chardonnay and Pinot Noir, the blend is made from the most prestigious growths in Champagne and is bottle-aged in their cellars for a minimum of seven years. The result is an elegant and rounded Champagne with a zesty finish. This Vintage Champagne is white gold in colour with a fine, delicate sparkle. The nose holds elegant fruit aromas leading to a lively palate with a deep and satisfying finish.

title: Verite 'La Desir' 2015
bodyHtml:
Vérité 'Le Désir' 2015 originates from the United States, specifically from Sonoma County, California. The winery was founded in 1998 as a partnership between vigneron Pierre Seillan and American wine visionaries Jess Jackson and Barbara Banke. Seillan, who began his career in Gascony and Bordeaux, utilizes a 'micro-cru' philosophy, tending to a mosaic of more than 50 distinct vineyard sites across Sonoma to create complex, multi-layered wines. The estate is part of the Jackson Family Wines portfolio and is renowned for its Saint-Émilion-inspired blends that emphasize the depth and nuance of Sonoma's diverse terroirs.

Wine Description

This red blend presents a very deep garnet-purple colour and a medium to full body. The sensory profile is incredibly complex, featuring high-toned aromatics of wild strawberries, cherries, and black raspberries, interwoven with signature Cabernet Franc herbal tones such as pea shoots and tomato vine. The aroma is further layered with notes of new leather, cigar box, black truffles, and red licorice. On the palate, the wine is structured and precise, showing a profound core of iron-rich graphite minerality and firm, elegant tannins. The finish is linear and silky, resounding with a floral bouquet of lilacs and violets.

  • Varietal Composition: 64% Cabernet Franc, 27% Merlot, 5% Cabernet Sauvignon, and 4% Malbec.

  • Stylistic Notes: The wine is bound by precision and grace, offering a balance between 'softness and hardness' with intense muscular mid-palate depth.

  • ABV: 14.4% or 14.5%.

  • Organic Status: While produced with meticulous vineyard care and a micro-cru approach, the estate is not typically certified organic.

Food Pairing

The structured tannins and savory, earthy layers of Le Désir 2015 make it an exceptional match for robust and sophisticated dishes.

  • Meats: Pairs excellently with grilled beef, roasted venison, and lamb chops.

  • Savoury & Rich: Complements earthy dishes such as cappelletti with black truffles or wild mushroom risotto.

  • Classic Pairings: Matches well with rich game stews or intense charcuterie like salami and pâté.

Vintage Quality

The 2015 vintage in Sonoma was defined by low yields but exceptional quality, resulting in wines with high concentration and structure. A mild and dry winter led to early budbreak in mid-March, followed by a cool spring that extended the bloom period into June. The warm, dry summer culminated in a compact 12-day harvest starting on August 31, allowing the fruit to achieve a hallmark precision and 'driving expression' that has earned this vintage a perfect 100-point score from several critics.

title: Opus One 2018
bodyHtml:
Opus One 2018 is a prestigious red blend from the Oakville American Viticultural Area (AVA) in Napa Valley, California. This iconic winery was established in 1979 as a joint venture between Baron Philippe de Rothschild of Château Mouton Rothschild and renowned Napa vintner Robert Mondavi. Their shared winemaking philosophy focuses on creating a single, exceptional wine that seamlessly blends Old World Bordeaux traditions with New World innovation and the unique terroir of the heart of Napa Valley.

Wine Description

This vintage features a very deep garnet-purple colour and a seductive, highly aromatic profile. The bouquet offers profuse scents of blackberry, cassis, and black cherry, layered with elegant notes of violets, rose petals, white pepper, and earthy touches. On the palate, it is medium to full bodied with a round, satiny mouthfeel and a crescendo of fresh, juicy black-fruit flavours accented by hints of orange zest, licorice, and dark chocolate. The structure is beautifully balanced by smooth, fine-grained tannins and a racy beam of acidity that leads into a long, persistent, and mineral-tinged finish. The varietal composition for the 2018 vintage is 84% Cabernet Sauvignon, 6% Petit Verdot, 5% Merlot, 4% Cabernet Franc, and 1% Malbec. This wine has an ABV of 14.0% and was aged for 17 to 18 months in 100% new French oak.

Food Pairing

The elegant structure and polished tannins of this wine make it a versatile partner for all types of classic meat dishes, including roast or grilled beef, lamb, and game. Specific suggestions include a rack of lamb with ratatouille, braised short ribs, or filet mignon. It also pairs effectively with savoury truffle-based dishes, hearty mushroom courses, and fine hard cheeses such as aged Gruyère.

Vintage Quality

The 2018 vintage in Napa Valley is regarded as exceptional, benefiting from idyllic growing conditions and milder, more consistent temperatures. Well-timed rainfall before budbreak provided necessary water for canopy development, followed by flawless conditions during flowering that led to higher-than-average yields. This moderate growing season allowed for a long, steady ripening period, resulting in a harvest—starting September 19th—that yielded fruit with remarkable freshness, purity, and concentration.

99 Points - James Suckling:

Extremely perfumed and floral with lavender, lilacs and violets to the sweet, ripe berries, such as blackberries and blackcurrants. Some slate and graphite, too. It’s full-bodied, yet ever so balanced and refined, with super fine tannins that last for minutes. Fresh herbs, such as bay leaf and lemon grass highlight the dark fruit. The quality of tannin is exquisite with wonderful polish and refinement. Lasts for minutes. So wonderful to taste now, but better after 2026.

title: Querciabella Batar 2022
bodyHtml: Batar shines in the glass, with its bright yellow core and golden hues. The bouquet is broad and fragrant, with acacia flowers, chamomile, peach, yellow plum and melon interlaced with buttery aromas, sweet spices, saffron, and cedar wood. A flinty, mineral quality adds precision to the intricate frame. On the palate, the wine is voluptuous yet elegant, showing great finesse and intense aromatic persistence. The mouthfeel is balanced and lifted.

title: O'Shaughnessy Cabernet Sauvignon Howell Mountain 2022
bodyHtml:
This structured and 'muscular' red wine originates from the United States, within the prestigious Howell Mountain A.A.V. (a sub-appellation of Napa Valley) in northern California. Founded in 1997 by Betty O'Shaughnessy and led by acclaimed winemaker Sean Capiaux, O'Shaughnessy Estate Winery is widely recognized as a benchmark producer of high-altitude mountain Cabernet Sauvignon. Sourced from the estate's two distinct Howell Mountain vineyard sites Rancho del Oso and the Estate Vineyard—the vines sit above the fog line at elevations ranging between 1,600 and 1,800 feet. The vines are rooted in volcanic tufa, red clay, and gravelly iron-rich soils (ironstone). The intense mountain sunshine combined with cool daytime breezes produces exceptionally low yields of micro-sized berries, generating wines with formidable tannic architecture, deep fruit concentration, and a distinct line of crushed-rock minerality.

Wine Description

The 2022 O'Shaughnessy Cabernet Sauvignon Howell Mountain presents an intense, opaque purple-black appearance in the glass with bright magenta shimmers along the rim. Its sensory profile is exceptionally bold, deep, and high-toned, offering a masterfully concentrated and complex expression of mountain terroir. The bouquet opens with a lavish display of crème de cassis, wild mountain blackberries, and black cherry reduction, seamlessly layered with complex underlays of crushed granite, dark cocoa, espresso bean, graphite, sweet pipe tobacco, dried sage, and a subtle touch of wild thyme. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied, dense, and powerfully structured, showcasing a mouth-coating core of black fruits, dark chocolate, and licorice. It is characterized by its outstanding inner energy and an incisive, mouthwatering backbone of natural mountain acidity that elevates its massive extract. The mouthfeel is broad, muscular, and athletic, driven by firm, ripe, and fine-grained tannins that glide into an extraordinarily long, dry, and savory finish accented by persistent notes of iron, toasted oak spice, and crushed rock.

title: Domaine Comte Georges de Vogue Chambolle Musigny Premier Cru 2023
bodyHtml:
Introduction

Domaine Comte Georges de Vogüé Chambolle Musigny Premier Cru 2023 originates from France, specifically from the Burgundy region and the Côte de Nuits subregion within the Chambolle Musigny appellation. The estate is a pillar of Burgundian history, dating back to 1450 and remaining under the same family ownership for over 20 generations. Winemaking is currently led by Jean Lupatelli, who took over from the long serving François Millet in 2021. The winery's philosophy emphasizes a deep respect for terroir, utilizing organic principles such as horse plowing and estate made organic compost, though the property is not officially certified.

Wine Description

This Premier Cru is unique because it is exclusively crafted from the younger vines of the Musigny Grand Cru vineyard. In 2023, the production was limited to only five barrels, all sourced from a plot planted in 2007 located just below the Musigny Blanc vines.

  • Aroma: An archetypal 'Chambolle' nose featuring small berried, rich raspberry fruit and crystalline raspberry fruit aromas.

  • Palate: The palate is described as 'kaleidoscopically perfumed,' where crystalline raspberry fruit competes with notes of rose petals.

  • Finish: The finish is long and fine, marked by an abundance of 'retro perfume'.

  • Varietal Composition: 100% Pinot Noir.

  • ABV: Typically recorded around 13% to 13.5% for this estate's Premier Crus.

  • Stylistic Notes: While younger vines are used, the wine often displays a concentration and depth that hints at its Grand Cru origins, balanced by a lively and supple structure.

Food Pairing

The elegant structure and aromatic complexity of this Pinot Noir make it a classic partner for refined poultry and game dishes.

  • Meats: Roast duck, goose, and game birds such as teal or Anjou pigeon served with swiss chard and Madeira jus.

  • Savoury Classics: Duck with cherries or oeufs en meurette (eggs poached in red wine sauce).

  • Cheese: Pairs exceptionally well with Comté cheese.

Vintage Quality

The 2023 vintage in Burgundy is described as 'brilliant' and was characterized by a relatively benign winter followed by a tumultuous spring. Despite these variations, the year produced good maturity and healthy yields. Winemaker Jean Lupatelli noted that the 2023 wines possess a maturity similar to 2009 but without the sensation of high alcohol, and they feature finer tannins than those seen in 2018. The resulting wines are noted for their freshness, piquant fruit notes, and excellent structural balance.

title: Zuccardi Piedra Infinita 2020
bodyHtml:
This extraordinary red wine originates from the Paraje Altamira IG in the San Carlos subregion of the Uco Valley, Mendoza, Argentina. Zuccardi Valle de Uco, spearheaded by the visionary Sebastián Zuccardi, established the Finca Piedra Infinita vineyard in one of the most challenging environments in the world a landscape so dominated by massive granite rocks that over a thousand truckloads of stone had to be moved just to plant the vines. The winemaking philosophy is one of "conquering the stone," focusing on micro-parcel vinification to express the raw, vertical energy of this high-altitude alluvial fan.

Wine Description

The 2020 Zuccardi Piedra Infinita is a "true mountain wine" with a saturated, deep ruby-purple colour. The nose is ethereal and highly precise, revealing layers of blue and black fruits, crushed violets, and red currants, underpinned by savory notes of black olive tapenade and a distinct mineral scent of iron and graphite. On the palate, the wine is taut and vertical, showcasing a rich, chalky texture and a powerful structural frame. It is characterized by vibrant acidity and "colossal" yet fine-grained tannins that lead into a long, mineral-streaked finish with hints of blood orange and sour cherry. This 100% Malbec was fermented in concrete vats with native yeasts, with aging primarily in concrete to ensure a pure expression of terroir without oak interference.

Food Pairing

This wine's structural intensity and mineral grip make it an ideal partner for roasted game birds with fruit reductions or a classic roasted turkey. It is equally well-suited for traditional Argentine pairings like grilled ribeye steak or beef tartare with capers and herbs, which highlights the wine's raw elegance. For an earthy vegetarian option, a roasted beetroot and goat cheese salad provides a perfect tangy counterpoint to the wine’s calcareous minerality.

title: Chateau La Mondotte 2016
bodyHtml:
La Mondotte is located on the eastern part of the Saint-Emilion plateau next to Troplong-Mondot. This 4.5 hectare vineyard is an absolute gem. Its outstanding terroir (clay limestone soil with very silty clay and a rocky subsoil) has all the natural qualities to produce very great wine. Excellent hydric regulation encourages the vines to sink their roots deep into the soil. The superb sun exposure and fine natural drainage due to the steep slope make this a very early-maturing terroir.

As the wines of La Mondotte age, they offer massive tannins and flamboyant fruit, while maintaining elegance.

98+ Points - Jeb Dunnuck

A blend of 85% Merlot and 15% Cabernet Franc, this behemoth boasts a deep purple color as well as a brilliant array of creme de cassis, blackcurrants, crushed rocks, and graphite. Full-bodied and beautifully concentrated, with liquid minerality emerging with time in the glass, this legendary Saint-Emilion in the making needs 5-7 years of bottle age and will keep for 3-4 decades.

97 Points - James Suckling

So much black truffle and blueberry on the nose. Decadent and aromatic. Wet soil. Indian ink. Full-bodied, polished and so velvety with fantastic depth of fruit and ripe tannins, yet powerful and fresh. Slightly minerally and salty underneath.

96 Points - Wine Spectator

This shows a dark, toasty style at first, with notes of ganache and plum reduction, but it unwinds steadily and slowly, revealing pure cassis, cherry and raspberry fruit flavors gilded liberally with violet and anise accents. The long finish is laced with a superfine chalky minerality that imparts mouthwa-tering cut even as the fruit gains steam.

96 Points - Wine Enthusiast

Made by the winemaking team of Canon la Gaffeliere, this wine is stylishly elegant, restrained in its structure and tannins. Its intensely juicy character is already attractive, giving the wine almost a refreshing character. 

93+ Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The palate is silky smooth on the entry, but underneath the bonnet, there is considerable tannic backbone that certainly can be felt more towards the finish that exerts a light grip. In a strange way, it reminds me a little of Chateau Canon!

title: Aalto PS (Pagos Seleccionados) 2022 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
From the celebrated Ribera del Duero region of Spain, Aalto PS (Pagos Seleccionados) is a flagship bottling by Bodegas Aalto, a renowned project founded in 1999 by Mariano García—former winemaker at Vega Sicilia—and Javier Zaccagnini. The winery is recognized for its precision in viticulture and crafting wines with power, elegance, and longevity from old-vine Tempranillo.

Wine Description
The 2022 vintage of Aalto PS is a commanding expression of Tempranillo, showing intense, opaque purple hues in the glass. Aromas are layered and luxurious, with ripe blackberries, cassis, espresso, crushed violets, and a touch of balsamic lift. On the palate, it is full-bodied and richly structured, delivering concentrated flavours of dark fruit, dark chocolate, liquorice, and toasted oak, supported by finely grained tannins. The finish is enduring and polished, reflecting both the depth of the old vines and the meticulous élevage.

Accolades

  • James Suckling – 98 points

  • Robert Parker’s Wine Advocate – 95 points

  • Guía Peñín – 96 points

Food Pairing
Ideal with aged ribeye steak, braised short ribs, or wild mushroom risotto. A bold Manchego or aged Spanish blue cheese will also complement its intensity. Together, they create an unforgettable dining experience.

title: Silver Oak Napa Valley Cabernet Sauvignon 2019
bodyHtml:
Introduction

This red wine originates from the United States, specifically from the Napa Valley region in California. Silver Oak was founded in 1972 by Raymond Twomey Duncan and Justin Meyer with a singular vision to focus exclusively on Cabernet Sauvignon aged in American oak. Still family owned and operated by the Duncan family, the winery is a leader in environmental stewardship, with its Napa Valley facility being the first large-scale production winery to achieve LEED Platinum certification.

Wine Description

Silver Oak Napa Valley Cabernet Sauvignon 2019 displays a deep ruby colour in the glass. The nose is complex and fragrant, offering nuanced aromas of Bing cherry, black raspberry, and muddled huckleberry layered with tobacco leaf, cedarwood, and dried sage. On the palate, the wine is medium to full bodied with a velvety texture, showcasing flavours of black plum, cassis, and dark chocolate accented by exotic oak spices and mint. It is characterized by impeccable balance, a firm backbone of fine-grained tannins, and a lengthy, energetic finish with notes of vanilla and roasted espresso beans. This blend consists of 77% Cabernet Sauvignon, 18% Merlot, 2% Cabernet Franc, 2% Petit Verdot, and 1% Malbec, with an ABV of 14.8%. While Silver Oak is dedicated to sustainable practices and has achieved net-zero emissions goals, this specific bottling is not certified organic. The optimal drinking window is from 2025 through 2045.

Accolades

  • Natalie MacLean - 97 points.

  • Decanter - 96 points.

  • James Suckling - 95 points.

  • Wine Spectator - 91 points.

Food Pairing

The structured tannins and opulent fruit profile of this Cabernet make it an ideal partner for rich and savoury dishes. It pairs perfectly with ribeye steak with herb butter, wine-braised short ribs, or slow-cooked lamb shanks. Its complex oak notes and acidity also complement roasted duck, mushroom risotto, or truffle-infused pasta. For a cheese course, consider serving it with aged Gouda, sharp English cheddar, or Pecorino Romano.

Vintage Quality

The 2019 vintage in Napa Valley is regarded as exceptional, characterized by a wet spring that replenished soil moisture followed by a long, warm summer with few extreme heat events. These conditions allowed for extended hang time, resulting in fruit with deep colour, abundant texture, and a classic, plush profile. Winemakers successfully navigated a mild finish to the season to produce wines that are highly expressive and approachable even in their youth.

title: Domaine Dujac Clos de la Roche Grand Cru 2023
bodyHtml:
1. Introduction

This fine red wine originates from France, specifically the Burgundy region, in the Côte de Nuits subregion and the Grand Cru appellation of Clos de la Roche. Domaine Dujac, situated in Morey Saint Denis, was established in 1967 when Jacques Seysses transitioned from a banking career to winemaking. The estate now spans nearly 12 hectares and boasts prime old-vine parcels in Clos de la Roche, one of the most profound and long lived sites in the Côte de Nuits. The winemaking philosophy centres on achieving aromatic lift using whole clusters, intensity from low yields, and a remarkable balance between elegance and structure.

2. Wine Description

The 2023 Clos de la Roche presents an impressive deep ruby purple colour. The aroma is utterly refined and offers a rich, extravagant constellation of red plums, redcurrant, and red and black cherry notes, complemented by rose petal, potpourri, graphite, and subtle spice. On the palate, the wine combines richness with precision, showing a dense core of fruit that is beautifully judged. It is a lavish and sensual wine, featuring plush, fine grained, and feisty tannins, with a fine bead of acidity that ensures a great sense of freshness and balance. The wine is full bodied and the finish is long, mineral driven, and complex, with an almost crystalline quality.
