97+ Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate     Deep garnet-purple colored, the 2016 Lynch Bages comes charging out of the gate with pronounced cassis, chocolate-covered cherries, mulberries and menthol notions, backed up by scents of garrigue, tilled soil and a waft of tapenade. Medium to full-bodied, rich and fantastically concentrated, the generous fruit is superbly framed by firm, ripe, grainy tannins with tons of pepper, cinnamon and cloves layers coming through on the finish. Truly, a legendary Lynch Bages!

97 Points - James Suckling     Very rich and exotic with blackberry, black-tea, graphite and lead-pencil aromas. Full-bodied, dense and structured with lots of ripe tannins and a long, flavorful finish of currants and forest floor, combined with fresh mushrooms and bark. Needs four to five years to show its true potential. Try after 2024.

97 Points - Wine Spectator     This is built for the cellar, with a generous core of kirsch, raspberry paste and plum preserve flavors waiting to unfurl. Will take time, due to the licorice snap, roasted apple wood and sweet tobacco elements draped over the fruit. Should meld with age, as the structure is invigorating in feel, showing both acidity and tannins in lockstep with the fruit. Best from 2025 through 2040.

96 Points - Decanter     Harvest started a week later than in 2015, allowing a longer, slowing ripening as Pauillac fully benefitted from the conditions of the vintage. Touches of reduction for the first minute emphasise the redcurrant notes in with the cassis and bilberry. The acidity is clear, and the layers of fine tannins build to show an extremely impressive construction: thickly sliced black fruits, fresh menthol, toast, tobacco and grilled, almost tarry almonds. 2% Petit Verdot makes up the blend. Eric Boissenot consults.

95 Points - Wine Enthusiast     Rich, jammy and powerful, this wine is all about concentration and firm tannins. Ripe black-currant flavors add great juiciness at the end. The wine has magnificent potential. Drink from 2025.

95 Points - Jeb Dunnuck     The flagship 2016 Château Lynch Bages is a powerhouse, checking in as 75% Cabernet Sauvignon, 19% Merlot, 4% Cabernet Franc, and 2% Petit Verdot raised in 75% new French oak. This deep, concentrated, powerful 2016 is going to be one for the ages, but if you’re looking for instant gratification, this isn’t for you. Saturated purple-colored, with thick black fruits, graphite, and scorched earth aromas and flavors, it fills the mouth with fruit, has masses of tannins, and beautiful overall balance. Don’t even think about opening bottles before 7-8 years from now, and it’s going to have 3-4 decades of longevity.

title: Chateau Montrose 2023
bodyHtml:
Chateau Montrose originates from France, within the Bordeaux region and the Saint Estephe subregion. Classified as a Second Growth in the historic 1855 classification, the estate was managed for over a century by the Charmolle family before being run by brothers Martin and Olivier Bouygues. The winery's operational philosophy relies on a nucleus of excellence across its 95-hectare single-block vineyard, which sits majestically overlooking the Gironde estuary. This unique location yields gravel terraces over deep clay that provide natural drainage and a moderated microclimate, enabling the team to focus on rigorous fruit selection to craft exceptionally long-lived, powerful, and refined wines.

Wine Description

This red wine presents a deep, intense ruby or dark garnet-purple appearance with incredible density in the glass and possesses a heavy, full-bodied structure with an opulent, muscular, and silky-smooth texture. The sensory profile is highly delicate, complex, and hedonistic, opening with an expressive nose of crushed blackberries, preserved plums, cassis, and white flowers, intricately woven with star anise, cedar chest, underbrush, Indian spices, iron ore, and an emerging waft of pressed violets. On the powerful, full, and decadent palate, it delivers a deeply concentrated stream of sweet black fruit, currant, and dark chocolate, seamlessly balanced by a rock-solid backbone of exquisitely ripe, fine-grained tannins, bright natural acidity, and a light estuarine, crushed-stone minerality. The finish is remarkably long, precise, and persistent, leaving a lingering trail of exotic spice, smoky accents, graphite, and bitter cocoa.

Food Pairing

The immense structural concentration, dense tannic architecture, and rich dark fruit profile of this Saint Estephe make it a perfect match for hearty, upscale gastronomy.

  • Meats: Pairs beautifully with roasted red meats, a traditional grilled beef rib, prime rump steak, or roasted poultry seasoned with forest herbs.

  • Savoury Accents: Suggested pairings include heavy main courses incorporating grilled mushrooms or dishes rich in earthy undertones.

  • Cheese: Matches gracefully with structured artisanal platters of well-matured, hard cheeses or a generous selection of aged blue varieties.

title: Chateau Figeac 2016
bodyHtml:
98 Points - Decanter

A testament to the work being undertaken at Figeac in recent years, this has depth and intensity while retaining the smile of the fruit. Richness combines with gorgeous length and intensity, every bit as impressive as it was during en primeur. Touches of violet and a silky texture precede hugely precise slate walls that pull the fruit into place through the palate. It takes its time in the glass to fully open, only slowly revealing the black olives, pungent white pepper and rosemary aromatics. Bottled in late July. 100% new oak.

98+ Points - Jeb Dunnuck

Another brilliant wine from the genius of Frédéric Faye, the 2016 Château Figeac checks in as 38% Cabernet Sauvignon, 36% Merlot, and the rest Cabernet Franc that spent 19 months in new French oak. Roughly 75% of the production made it into the grand vin. This deeply colored beauty is a legendary wine in the making and offers ultra-pure aromas and flavors of crème de cassis, smoke tobacco, dried herbs, chocolate, truffle, and graphite. Showing more violets notes with time in the glass, it builds incrementally on the palate, with flawless balance as well as incredible elegance, no hard edges, and a finish that won't quit. Readers will have a blast comparing the 2016 and 2015 vintages over the coming 3-4 decades and this estate is firing on all cylinders. This will most likely merit a triple-digit rating in 7-8 years and keep for 4 decades or more.

97+ Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2016 Figeac is comprised of 38% Cabernet Sauvignon, 36% Merlot and 26% Cabernet Franc. Deep garnet-purple colored, the nose is a little broody and reticent at this very youthful stage, slowly unfolding to reveal profound plum preserves, crème de cassis, black raspberries and star anise with hints of moss-covered bark, truffles and tilled loam plus a waft of red currants and raspberry leaves sparks. Medium to full-bodied, the palate is practically quivering with energy, offering glimpses at tightly wound black fruit and mineral/ferrous layers, framed by very firm, ripe tannins and wonderful tension, finishing long with the spices coming through. This will need a good 7-8 years to come round and then should cellar for 40+ years. Very serious, beautifully poised and sophisticated personality this vintage.

96 Points - James Suckling

This is a very linear and driven Figeac with smooth and fine tannins. Full-bodied, yet compact and reserved. Blackberry, chocolate and hazelnut flavors. Direct and structured. A blend of 38 per cent cabernet sauvignon, 36 per cent merlot, and 26 per cent cabernet franc. Better after 2024.

96 Points - Wine Spectator

A gutsy, fully endowed wine, brimming with dark currant, warm fig and steeped blackberry notes, as well as waves of smoldering tobacco and warm gravel. Features a serious bass line, but everything works together, while flecks of savory and iron dart in and out.

93 Points - Wine Enthusiast

While this wine still has serious layers of tannins, it also delivers considerable ripe black-fruit flavors. The estate in the Figeac sector of Saint-Emilion has produced a powerful wine that is firm and that will age further.

title: Chateau Canon 2022
bodyHtml:
Hailing from France, Château Canon is nestled in the prestigious Saint-Émilion appellation on Bordeaux’s Right Bank. This historic estate, dating back to the 18th century, is owned by Chanel, which has invested heavily in vineyard renewal and cellar modernization. The estate is celebrated for its meticulous viticulture and dedication to expressing Saint-Émilion’s distinctive limestone terroir.

Wine Description

The Château Canon 2022 is a poised and elegant blend dominated by Merlot with Cabernet Franc. In the glass, it reveals a deep ruby hue. Aromas unfold gracefully, offering layers of red and black cherries, fresh violets, crushed stones, and subtle hints of cedar. On the palate, it is medium to full-bodied, with a seamless texture and bright acidity that supports finely woven tannins. Notes of ripe plum, graphite, and gentle spice lead to a long, mineral-driven finish.

Accolades

  • Jeb Dunnuck - 100 Points

  • Wine Advocate - 100 Points 

  • James Suckling - 99 Points

  • Vinous - 99 Points

Food Pairing

Pair this distinguished Saint-Émilion with herb-crusted rack of lamb, wild mushroom risotto, or aged hard cheeses like Comté. This pairing highlights the wine’s depth and character.

title: Chateau Canon La Gaffeliere 2018
bodyHtml:
Chateau Canon La Gaffeliere's terroir consists of clay-limestone and clay-sand soil that is very permeable and particularly efficient at retaining heat. Reflecting the estate's soil, the proportions of grape varieties are rather atypical for the appellation: a perfect 50/50 divide between Merlot and Cabernet Sauvignon. Cabernet Sauvignon ripens early on Canon La Gaffeliere's warm soil, adding power and aromatic complexity to Merlot's opulence to create wines of natural elegance and finesse. The wine is classy, remarkably well-structured, complex, pure, and always elegant.

Blend: 50% Merlot, 35% Cabernet Franc, 15% Cabernet Sauvignon

97 Points - Vinous   

The 2018 Canon La Gaffelière is bright, punchy and full of character, just as it was from barrel. Sage, blood orange, mocha and spice add pretty aromatic top notes to a core of inky red/purplish berry fruit. All the elements are so well balanced in this super-expressive Saint-Émilion. Bright floral and savory Franc notes punctuate the salivating finish, mineral-drenched finish. The 2018 needs a lot of air to open, but when it does, it is dynamite. 

96 Points - Wine Spectator    


This has a lovely core of mulled cassis, damson plum and raspberry reduction notes, framed with an applewood note that integrates nicely while red tea, savoury and chalky mineral notes develop through the finish. Restrained style, precise and very long. Merlot, Cabernet Franc and Cabernet Sauvignon. Best from 2024 through 2038.

96 Points - James Suckling    


Fantastic depth and richness to the nose with plums, mushrooms, bark and some mahogany. Full-bodied, tight and focused with very fine tannins and a long, creamy finish. Lovely polish, balance and clarity. Drink after 2025.

96 Points - Wine Enthusiast   

This already shows sophistication in a stream of black currant fruit set alongside the firm tannins that are still developing. Its structure and juicy berry fruits give richness and freshness at the end while also promising aging. 

95 Points - Decanter   

This has the clear edge over La Mondotte for me because it combines the polish and glamour of a St-Emilion Premier Grand Cru Classé with the salt taffy tang of limestone. Still a silky texture but a more attractive slate edge coming in on the finish to temper the sweet fruit and slow things down. A highly impressive wine. The harvest ran from 19 September to 4 October, with a yield of 35hl/ha. 50% new oak. Certified organic. 

95 Points - Jeb Dunnuck   

Another beautiful vintage for this cuvée, the 2018 Château Canon La Gaffelière is based on 50% Merlot, 35% Cabernet Franc, and the rest Cabernet Sauvignon, brought up in 50% new French oak, with the balance all in used barrels. It's never the biggest or richest wine in the vintage yet always has a classic Saint-Emilion elegance as well as brilliant minerality. The 2018 reveals a dense purple hue to go with an already complex bouquet of kirsch, blackberries, new saddle leather, bouquet garni, tobacco, and flowery incense. With medium to full-bodied richness, a seamless, elegant texture, ripe tannins, and a great finish, it builds nicely with time in the glass and is a complex, flawlessly balanced Saint-Emilion that offers both hedonistic and intellectual pleasure. It's going to keep for 20-30 years, and I'd recommend a healthy decant or a good 4-6 years of bottle age.

95 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate   

Medium to deep garnet-purple colored, the 2018 Canon la Gaffeliere out of the gate delivers a seductive nose of plum preserves, kirsch and Black Forest cake with nuances of lilacs, underbrush, Indian spices and dusty soil. The medium to full-bodied palate is filled with black fruit preserves and loads of spicy accents, supported by chewy tannins and well-balanced freshness, finishing long and savory.

title: Freemark Abbey Cabernet Sauvignon 'Sycamore Vineyard' 2018
bodyHtml:
Introduction

Freemark Abbey Cabernet Sauvignon 'Sycamore Vineyard' is a red wine from the United States. It is produced in the Napa Valley subregion of California, specifically from the Rutherford appellation. Sycamore Vineyard is located on the southern end of the Rutherford Bench, with its proximity to the Mayacamas mountains helping to provide the perfect climate for growing a rich, textured Cabernet Sauvignon. Freemark Abbey is considered a 'historic, classic, pedigreed producer' in Napa Valley, and was one of the earliest wineries in the region to offer tastings to visitors, dating back to 1949. The winery's enduring philosophy centres on quality, balanced, vineyard-driven wines.

Wine Description

The wine is deep garnet in colour. The aromatic profile includes black currant, pomegranate, baking spice, forest floor, and espresso. Further notes include gorgeous aromas of blackberries and fresh herbs, such as lavender, sage, and bay leaf. The wine is a blend of 77% Cabernet Sauvignon, 9% Merlot, 8% Cabernet Franc, and 6% Petit Verdot. It matured in 65% new French oak.

On the palate, it is rich and expansive, loaded with succulent red cherry, plum, mocha, espresso, licorice, and dried herbs. It is full-bodied, with rich and textured flavours of black cherry, dark chocolate, leather, and warm oak spices. The structure is sturdy and firm, with strong, bold, yet integrated tannins. Stylistically, it is large-scaled, complex, and full-bodied. It has a polished feel overall, with a juicy, mouthwatering, long, and minerally finish that contains hints of dark chocolate, espresso, and a dusty, chalky texture. The ABV is $14.20\%$. The wine is built to age effortlessly for 20 years or more. It is recommended for drinking now through 2032 or 2035.

Accolades

  • Vinous - 95 points

  • Wine Advocate - 95 points

  • Decanter - 95 points

  • James Suckling - 94 points

  • Wine Spectator - 92 points

  • Wine Enthusiast - 92 points

Food Pairing

This Cabernet Sauvignon is a 'classic T-bone steak wine'. It is well-paired with fine meats like beef, lamb, and game.

Vintage Quality

The 2018 harvest in California was a welcome relief after the 2017 wildfires, with an extremely good growing season for much of the region. The season was calm, with a cooler-than-normal spring. For the Sycamore Vineyard, which is more gravelly and receives more afternoon shade, the harvest took place approximately two weeks later than other sites. This later harvest and the cool, calm season helped to produce a solid vintage.

title: Chateau Leoville Barton 2015
bodyHtml:
In 1826, Hugh Barton, already proprietor of Chateau Langoa, purchased part of the big Leoville estate. His part then became known as Leoville Barton. Six generations of Bartons have since followed, and continued to preserve the quality of the wine, classified as a Second Growth in 1855.

One of Saint Julien's best historically, the estate of Leoville, was the largest in the Medoc in the 18th century.

97 Points - Wine Enthusiast

Rich, generous and elegant, this is a very dense wine but with great black fruits to balance this structure. The elements are already coming together to create another great wine from this property.

97 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

Cassis, smoked earth, graphite, tobacco leaf, and thrilling amounts of minerality all emerge from this inky colored, full-bodied, power-packed, brut of a Saint-Julien that holds everything together and stays pure, balanced and elegant on the palate. It has a lot of tannins, yet more than enough fruit. 

96 Points - James Suckling

This is a very focused Barton with ultra-fine tannins that are so polished and chalky. It drives through the center palate with currant and berry character. Full-bodied, polished and straightforward with driving tannin. Love the texture. Class. Yes.

95 Points - Wine Spectator

This delivers some serious wow, dripping with warm fig, blackberry and boysenberry reduction notes, along with melted black licorice and fruitcake flavors. Shows ample grip but remains beautifully polished, letting the fruit sail on. Don't worry though, as long echoes of roasted apple wood and tar signal that this is built for the long haul.

95 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Elegant, medium-bodied and sporting great freshness, the taut, tightly wound palate of intense red fruits and floral accents is well-framed with firm, grainy tannins, finishing on a lingering mineral note.

93 Points - Decanter

Fine concentration of fruit and lovely fragrance; quite discreet for this chateau. The controlled vigour of better vintages has been replaced by classic ripeness, integrated tannins and fine balance.

title: Carruades de Lafite 2002
bodyHtml:
Introduction

Carruades de Lafite 2002 is the highly esteemed second wine of the First Growth estate, Château Lafite Rothschild, located in the Pauillac appellation of Bordeaux, France. The estate's history is remarkably deep, dating back to 1234, though its modern winemaking structure was largely established in the late 17th century by the Ségur family. Acquired by Baron James de Rothschild in 1868, the winery has long maintained a philosophy of producing the most elegant wines in Pauillac, focusing on finesse and aromatic nuances rather than sheer power. Carruades de Lafite specifically takes its name from the Carruades plateau, a group of plots purchased by the chateau in 1845 that sit adjacent to the estate's finest hilltop vineyards.

Wine Description

The 2002 vintage of Carruades is a savory and classic Bordeaux blend, predominantly composed of 71% Cabernet Sauvignon, 25% Merlot, 3% Cabernet Franc, and 1% Petit Verdot. It displays a dark red colour and an expressive, dense nose featuring alluring aromas of blackcurrant, blackberry, and plum, accented by the signature Lafite fragrance of lead pencil shavings, cedar, and chocolate. On the palate, the wine is medium to full bodied with firm, dense tannins and a tart acidity that provides a sense of freshness and finesse. While leaner and less concentrated than the Grand Vin, it offers a svelte, fleshy texture with lingering flavours of loganberry, black cherry, and loganberry. This vintage was aged for 16 to 20 months in oak barrels, typically using 10% new oak.

title: Chateau Pichon Longueville Baron 2016
bodyHtml:
#8 Wine Spectator Top 100 of 2019

Château Pichon Baron 2016 has a beautiful, intense garnet red colour. The nose reveals aromas of red and dark fruit such as blueberry, black cherry and blackcurrant, followed by very lightly toasted notes with a hint of vanilla and spices. The fleshy, powerful attack is balanced by richness and a certain fullness. The tannins are silky, opulent and lengthy, with some crispness. The finish is precise. Altogether it is dominated by the tipicity of the grapes and by tension, and is dense and full-bodied.

Blend: 85% Cabernet Sauvignon, 15% Merlot

99 Points - James Suckling

The concentration and largesse of the 2016 Pichon Baron is apparent from the get-go with incredibly alluring, ripe and expansive fruit aromas in the blackberry, dark-cherry, mulberry and plum zone. Espresso and cedar, as well as a slate-like, stony mineral edge add complexity. The palate has incredible depth, drive and detail. Fine and plush tannins stretch the palate in every direction. So fresh and vivacious, this is the greatest Pichon Baron since 1989 and has a long future. Try from 2024.

97 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Deep garnet-purple coloured, the 2016 Pichon-Longueville Baron offers a suave and seductive nose of warm red and black currants, black plum preserves, truffles, tapenade and rose hip tea with touches of sandalwood and Chinese five spice plus a waft of iron ore. Medium to full-bodied, firmly structured and packed with mineral and exotic spice-laced black fruits, it finishes very long with compelling herbal sparks.

97 Points - Wine Enthusiast

As often with this estate, this wine combines opulent richness and an elegant structure. It is a bold wine, ripe and full of black fruits. But it holds together impressively, with nothing in excess. The wine will age well and drink from 2025.

title: Eisele Vineyard Cabernet Sauvignon 'Altagracia' 2019
bodyHtml:
Altagracia Cabernet emerges out of the glass with intense aromas of black cherries, black currant liqueur and blackberry pie spiced up with cinnamon, nutmeg and a hint of rosewood and sandalwood. The mouthfeel is ample and supple, velvety yet vibrant with fine powdery tannins, a bright freshness and sparkling energy. The long and savory finish lingers with

spices framed by a hint of saltiness. As the wine opens, layers of floral notes, pencil shavings and volcanic stones add to the complexity. This is a very enticing and captivating Altagracia that reflects the complexity of its soils, the generosity of its climate and the vitality of its plants; in other words: a wine true to its terroir.

97 Points - James Suckling

There’s purity and focus to this wine with blackberry, blackcurrant and spices, such as nutmeg. Ink pot, bark and asphalt, too. So long and polished. Chewy tannins. Hints of stone and ash. 88% cabernet sauvignon. 7% cabernet franc and 5% petit verdot. Give it time to soften, but already a beauty. Drink after 2026.

95 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Very deep garnet-purple in color, the 2019 Cabernet Sauvignon Altagracia springs from the glass with vibrant scents of crushed black cherries, ripe, juicy blackcurrants and blackberry coulis, plus hints of cardamom, cumin seed, tree bark and crushed rocks. Medium to full-bodied, the palate is chock-full of expressive black fruits with firm and fine-grained tannins and beautiful freshness, finishing long and spicy.

title: Borgogno Barolo Cannubi 2016
bodyHtml: 93 Points - Vinous...    The 2016 Barolo Cannubi is the first Borgogno Barolo made from organically farmed vineyards, which represents a pretty significant shift here. Bright and beautifully lifted in the glass, the Cannubi is so expressive today. Succulent red berry fruit, spice, blood orange, rose petal and star anise build as this sensual, open-knit Barolo shows off its allure, which is considerable.

title: O'Shaughnessy Cabernet Sauvignon 'Napa Valley' 2021
bodyHtml:
Proprietors Betty O'Shaughnessy-Wools and Paul Wools purchased land in Oakville in 1990, driven by a passion for food and wine and a desire to return to their farming roots. Over the following years, they acquired additional vineyards on Howell Mountain and Mount Veeder, completing their winery and caves in time for the 2003 harvest.

Wine Description

This is a classic Napa Valley Cabernet Sauvignon with an opaque purple color and perfumed aromas of blackberry compote, orange blossom, cassis, creme brulee, and cocoa. On the palate the wine is plush and concentrated with well-integrated tannins and a vibrant finish. Lush enough to be consumed now and structured enough to hold for decades thanks to the mountain heritage of this beautiful wine.

Accolades

  • "Decanter - 94 points."

  • "Jeb Dunnuck - 94 points."

  • "Vinous - 93 points."

  • "James Suckling - 93 points."

  • "Robert Parker's Wine Advocate - 92 points."

Food Pairing

Suggested pairings include red meats such as steak (especially fattier cuts like ribeye) and grilled lamb.

title: Biondi Santi Rosso di Montalcino 2020
bodyHtml:
Biondi Santi, located in Montalcino, Tuscany, Italy, is a historic winery renowned for its pivotal role in establishing Brunello di Montalcino as one of Italy's premier wines. The estate's legacy dates back to the late 19th century, with a commitment to producing wines that embody elegance, longevity, and a true sense of place.

Wine Description

The 2020 Rosso di Montalcino showcases a vibrant ruby-red hue. Aromas of juicy red berries and plums emerge energetically, complemented by floral notes of violets and red roses, alongside refreshing hints of citron peel, blood orange, and Mediterranean herbs. On the palate, it is vibrant and lively with fine-grained tannins, bright acidity, and succulent, crunchy fruit leading towards a long-lasting, savoury finish.

Accolades

  • Wine Enthusiast - 96 points.

title: M by Michael Mondavi 2019
bodyHtml:
The 2019 M by Michael Mondavi Family is a red wine from Napa Valley, California. This wine embodies the Mondavi family's dedication to excellence, showcasing the unique terroir of their estate vineyards and their commitment to sustainable viticulture.

Vineyard and Production

Sourced from a sustainably farmed, volcanic hillside vineyard located on the slopes of Atlas Peak, the vines benefit from rocky, well-drained soils that impart intensity and complexity to the fruit. The 2019 growing season featured ample rainfall and a warm summer with minimal extreme heat events, allowing for even ripening and the development of vibrant flavors. Harvested between October 17th and 25th, the grapes underwent fermentation in small lots to preserve their distinct character. The wine was aged for 21 months in French oak barrels, 75% of which were new, enhancing its structure and depth.

Tasting Notes

  • Appearance: Deep, iridescent ruby hue.

  • Aroma: Aromas of rose, cherry blossom, violets, and currant leaf, complemented by notes of black cherry, roasted chestnuts, vanilla, and cocoa.

  • Palate: Flavors of rhubarb, currant, fig, and marzipan, with toasty oak nuances and well-integrated tannins. The wine offers a harmonious balance between fruit and oak, leading to a long, satisfying finish with a subtle hint of tobacco.

Critical Acclaim

  • James Suckling: 96 points. Praised for its complex bouquet and well-structured palate, highlighting the wine's elegance and aging potential.

  • Jeb Dunnuck: 96 points. Noted for its depth, opulence, and seamless integration of flavors, with a recommendation for extended cellaring to fully appreciate its evolution.

  • Robert Parker's Wine Advocate: 94 points. Recognized for its vibrant acidity, ample texture, and the promise of an exceptional vintage.

Serving and Pairing

To fully appreciate its complexity, decant the wine for at least an hour before serving at a temperature of 16-18°C (61-64°F). This wine pairs exceptionally well with rich dishes such as braised short ribs, roasted lamb, or aged cheeses. Its balanced acidity and robust structure also make it a suitable companion for hearty stews and grilled steaks.

title: Bouchard Pere & Fils Gevrey Chambertin 2021
bodyHtml:
This Pinot Noir is from France, specifically the Gevrey-Chambertin appellation in the Burgundy region. Bouchard Père & Fils is one of the oldest wine estates in Burgundy, founded in 1731 by Michel Bouchard. The estate has grown over centuries through the acquisition of prestigious vineyards and now holds 130 hectares of vines, making it the largest vineyard owner in the Côte d’Or. The winery prioritizes sustainability and focuses on expressing the authenticity of each individual terroir.

Wine Description

The wine is 100% Pinot Noir. It presents a deep ruby colour with violet undertones. The bouquet is intense and perfumed, offering aromas of red and black berries combined with delicate woody and spicy notes. On the palate, it is a refined and well-balanced wine that marries power and elegance. It has silky tannins and a velvety texture, with fruity and subtly woody flavours. The wine’s structure leads to a lingering and well-balanced finish. It has good aging potential and can be kept for about 10 years or more.

Accolades

  • Vinous - 97 Points

  • Robert Parker - 95 Points

Food Pairing

The intense aromas of this wine make it a perfect match for rich and flavourful dishes. Suggested pairings include saddle of lamb, bœuf bourguignon, or coq au vin. It also pairs well with mature cheeses. A perfect match to enhance the wine's complexity.

title: Domaine Faiveley Gevrey Chambertin 'Lavaux Saint Jacques' Premier Cru 2021
bodyHtml:
The 2021 'Lavaux Saint-Jacques' Premier Cru from Domaine Faiveley is an esteemed red wine from the Gevrey-Chambertin appellation in Burgundy, France. Crafted exclusively from Pinot Noir grapes, this wine showcases the unique terroir of the Lavaux Saint-Jacques vineyard, one of the top three Premiers Crus in Gevrey-Chambertin. The south-facing, 1-hectare parcel, planted on fossil-rich rock and clay soil, contributes to the wine's complexity and finesse.

Colour: Deep ruby red with a bright, clear hue, indicative of its freshness and vibrancy.

Aroma: An expressive bouquet with redcurrant and wild strawberry notes, alongside hints of forest floor (sous-bois) and truffle for a layered, inviting profile.

Palate: Balanced and refined with finely-chiseled tannins, offering flavors of crunchy black fruit and a touch of spice. The wine is nuanced, with a delicacy and elegance characteristic of the region.

Body: Medium-bodied with a harmonious blend of acidity and tannins, delivering a smooth and polished mouthfeel.

Finish: Long and elegant, leaving a refined impression of its complex flavors and structure.

Accolades: The 2021 vintage has received praise from critics, including 92-94 points from Vinous for its expressive bouquet, and 92-94 points from Jasper Morris, who noted its aging potential and appealing character.

title: Vieux Chateau Certan 2021
bodyHtml:
Vieux Château Certan is located on the prestigious clay and gravel plateau of Pomerol, France. Established in the mid-1700s, it is one of the oldest and most revered estates in the appellation. Since 1924, the property has been under the stewardship of the Thienpont family, whose winemaking philosophy emphasizes authenticity, sustainable vineyard management, and a pursuit of pure, elegant expressions of their unique terroir.

Wine Description

The 2021 vintage presents a deep garnet-purple colour and opens with a highly aromatic and perfumed nose featuring dried violets, rose petals, and graphite, intertwined with black cherry, plum, and exotic spices. On the palate, this medium to full bodied wine is characterized by its vibrancy and precision, displaying a core of juicy red and black fruit wrapped in ultra-refined, silky tannins.

Accolades

  • "Vinous - 98 points."

  • "James Suckling - 97 points."

  • "Wine Enthusiast - 97 points."

  • "Decanter - 96 points."

  • "Robert Parker's Wine Advocate - 95 points."

Food Pairing

This wine's elegant structure and vibrant acidity make it a sophisticated companion for roasted duck breast with a cherry reduction or herb-crusted lamb chops. It also pairs beautifully with game birds, earthy truffle-infused dishes, and aged hard cheeses such as Comté.

title: Chateau Montelena Estate Cabernet Sauvignon 2018
bodyHtml:
This wine is the flagship Cabernet Sauvignon from Chateau Montelena, an iconic and storied producer in the Napa Valley, California. The estate is located in the Calistoga appellation, at the base of Mount Saint Helena. Chateau Montelena's history dates back to 1882, but it was purchased by Jim Barrett in 1968, who set about replanting the vineyard with the dream of creating wine on par with the great First Growths of Bordeaux. The winery's philosophy centres on a long-term perspective and "farming the right way" to capture the majesty and distinctive character of their estate vineyard site. The estate's history was cemented in 1976 when its 1973 Chardonnay won the famous "Judgment of Paris" blind tasting.

Wine Description

  • Country of Origin, Region, and Subregion: The wine is from the United States, specifically California, within the Napa Valley and the Calistoga appellation.

  • Varietal Composition: The blend is predominantly Cabernet Sauvignon (98%), with 1.5% Petit Verdot and 0.5% Cabernet Franc.

  • Sensory Profile: The wine is described as a wine of reserve, balancing power with an extraordinary ability to age.

    • Colour: It presents a dark garnet, nearly violet colour in the glass.

    • Aroma: The nose is fresh and lively, opening effusively with raspberry, mint, and plum sauce. Baking spices follow, leaning toward clove, with plenty of cedar and vanilla. Ripe fruit elements, such as cassis and fig, lurk beneath, along with hints of graphite and toasted sage.

    • Palate: The texture and mouthfeel are driving factors, initially feeling tightly wound. The dynamic tension on the mid-palate magnifies layers of black cherry, cocoa powder, and black pepper, before turning slightly earthy and dusty.

    • Finish: The structure is pronounced yet harmonious. Acidity materializes on the finish in an almost candy-like fashion, providing a beautiful contrast to the supple tannins. The density of the wine shines elegantly, with persistent length and depth.

  • Stylistic Notes: It is aged for 22 months in 100% French oak barrels (40% new). The unusually low nighttime temperatures of the vintage magnified the acidity in the fruit, which created an elegant structure for extended ageing, rather than an overtly jammy flavour. This wine is not indicated as organic in the sources.

  • Optimal Drinking Window: Described as "superb" and "impressive," this young Cabernet needs time in the bottle to fully come together.

Accolades

  • Vinous - 96 points

  • Decanter - 93 points (Also cited as 96 points)

  • Robert Parker's Wine Advocate - (94+) points

  • Ken's Wine Guide - 93 points

Food Pairing

The wine's robust nature, firm tannins, and smoky, spicy complexity make it ideal for rich, savoury dishes.

  • Suggested Pairings: Suggested pairings include smoked beef brisket, rare porterhouse steak, or prime rib. This pairing highlights the wine's depth and character.

title: Castiglion del Bosco Brunello di Montalcino 'Campo del Drago' 2019
bodyHtml:
Campo del Drago is a Brunello di Montalcino cru from the finest vineyard in the Capanna area, a hectare and a half at the highest elevation. Superbly-structured and with a distinctive personality. Campo del Drago is the most refined expression of Sangiovese produced at Castiglion del Bosco.

Campo del Drago enjoys one of its highest expressions when paired with the succulence and softness of pigeon, whose breast is served here at its most delicate. The bold spicing of the wine is perfectly at one with the flavour combination bestowed to the meat by the beetroot, celeriac and the exotic overtones of coffee.

97 Points - James Suckling

95 Points - Vinous

93 Points - Decanter

title: Chateau d'Yquem 2017 - 375 ml
bodyHtml:
Chateau d'Yquem originates from the Sauternes appellation within the Gironde region of France. This historic estate, the only one to receive the Premier Cru Superieur rating in the 1855 classification, has been a symbol of winemaking perfection since the 18th century and is currently part of the LVMH luxury group. The winery's philosophy is rooted in a centuries old ideal of uncompromising quality, famously relying on the development of 'noble rot' (Botrytis cinerea) to create its legendary sweet wines.

Wine Description

This vintage presents a pale lemon gold colour with youthful flashes of green. The nose is intensely aromatic, offering a fresh bouquet of apricot, baked pear, honeycomb, and white flowers, alongside pure notes of yuzu, lemon barley water, and fresh ginger. On the palate, the wine is full bodied and unctuous yet perfectly balanced by a vibrant, racy acidity that prevents it from feeling heavy. Complex flavours of grilled orange, salted butter caramel, and vanilla pod lead into an endless, epic finish.

Accolades

  • "James Suckling - 99 points."

  • "Wine Spectator - 96 points."

  • "Decanter - 96 points."

  • "Vinous - 97 points."

Food Pairing

The wine's rich texture and bright acidity make it a versatile partner for a variety of dishes. It is traditionally paired with foie gras or strong blue cheeses like Roquefort, but it also complements roasted chicken or spicy Asian cuisine.

title: Le Clarence de Haut Brion 2022
bodyHtml:
Le Clarence de Haut Brion is the distinguished second wine of Château Haut Brion, one of Bordeaux’s oldest and most revered estates, with records of wine production dating back to the 16th century. Owned by Domaine Clarence Dillon since 1935, the estate is renowned for its meticulous winemaking philosophy, blending tradition with innovation to create wines of enduring prestige.

Wine Description

In the glass, it shows a deep ruby-purple hue. The bouquet reveals expressive aromas of dark berries, tobacco, graphite, spices, and crushed rose petals, alongside subtle notes of leather, menthol, and truffle. On the palate, it is medium to full-bodied, with layers of blackcurrant, plum, and savoury herbs balanced by fine tannins and a fresh, structured finish.

Accolades

  • Wine Enthusiast - 94 points

Food Pairing

This wine’s rich texture and savoury depth make it a superb companion to roasted lamb with rosemary, braised short ribs, or duck confit. Earthy dishes such as mushroom risotto or truffle-infused pasta also highlight its complexity.

title: Chateau Cantenac Brown 2016 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
The quality of the wines is no accident: the predominantly gravelly slope in the village of Cantenac produces some of the best wines in the world and is location of many Crus Classes of Margaux. The soils, poor and generous at the same time, added to deep rooted vines and the vintners’ know-how lead to fine, elegant and perfectly balanced wines. Cabernet Sauvignon and Cabernet Franc produce subtle wines with an intense bouquet, well-suited for laying down. Merlot makes up the remainder of the vines and contributes to color, richness and roundness.

Today, the Chateau Cantenac Brown vineyard covers 42 hectares in the south of the Margaux appellation, mainly in the Cantenac commune. Located in the communes of Arsac, Soussans, Margaux, Cantenac and Labarde, the Margaux appellation terroirs are terraced groups of gravel, ensuring good natural drainage. Each terroir is different and produces a unique wine.

95 Points - Decanter

Poised and precise, this is excellent quality with well-defined black fruits. It feels like the fruit is ripe but not overly so, carefully delineated by great freshness and touches of slate, rosemary and dark chocolate. The extremely precise nose slowly reveals itself, gaining in power. I loved this en primeur and it's even more striking today. A great job by the Cantenac Brown team, it lives up to the quality of their 2015.

94 Points - James Suckling

This has a very delicious and attractive nose offering ample dark berries and plums with cocoa and freshly cut bracken. The palate has a smooth, fan-like array of fine but sturdy tannins that carry very fresh and upbeat into the finish. Try from 2023.

94 Points - Wine Enthusiast

Richly structured, this dense wine has solid tannins that balance with the black fruits. It is a complex wine, poised and confident while not losing sight of the Margaux elegance. Drink from 2025.

93+ Points - Jeb Dunnuck

Black cherries, currants, smoke tobacco, graphite, and hints of earth all emerge from this beautifully layered, medium-bodied, and concentrated 2016 that shines for its purity and precision, while still offering beautiful depth of fruit. Give it 3-4 years and enjoy this fabulous effort over the following 2-3 decades.

93 Points - Wine Spectator

92+ Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

title: Perrin Chateau De Beaucastel Roussanne Vieilles Vignes 2022
bodyHtml:
Wine Description

Château de Beaucastel's 2022 Châteauneuf-du-Pape Vieilles Vignes is a white wine made from 100% Roussanne grapes sourced from very old vines. This wine is certified organic. The wine presents a deep, intense golden colour. On the nose, it is powerful and complex, with aromatic notes of honey, ripe fruit, apricots, peaches, and brioche. The palate is dense, rich, and silky, with flavours of beeswax, citrus, and sun-ripened fruit. It has a great balance and a silky texture, with a refreshing acidity that keeps it from being heavy, leading to a long and luxurious finish with hints of wood spice and honey. The recommended drinking window is within the first three years of bottling or after 15 years.

 Accolades

  • Jeb Dunnuck - 100 points

  • Wine Advocate - 97 points

  • James Suckling - 97 points

  • Decanter - 96 points

  • Wine Spectator - 96 points

  • Vinous - 95 points

  • Jancis Robinson - 17.5/20 points

Food Pairing

This wine pairs beautifully with richly flavoured dishes. Suggested pairings include roasted poultry with a creamy mushroom sauce, lobster in butter sauce, truffle-infused dishes, foie gras, and aged cheeses like Comté or Beaufort. A perfect match to enhance the wine's complexity.

Vintage Quality

The 2022 vintage experienced a series of contrasting climatic conditions, including a mild and very dry winter and spring, which helped maintain the excellent health of the vines. The summer was hot and sunny, but timely rainfall in mid-August allowed the grapes to continue ripening slowly. The initial tastings of the red wines from this vintage suggest they are particularly balanced. The white wines, in particular, flourished in this exceptional terroir.

title: Duval Leroy Prestige Premier Cru Brut Rose
vendor: 300575 - Vintage West Wine And Spirits Inc.
bodyHtml:
The NV Duval-Leroy Champagne Premier Cru Prestige Rose offers a salmon/amber color as well as impressive notes of orange blossoms, dried strawberries, burnt toast, and hints of minerality.

Made in a medium-bodied, concentrated, yet elegant style, it has a fine, crisp mousse, and terrific length. It's an impressive rosé that should evolve gracefully.

title: Paolo Scavino Barolo 'Cannubi' 2018
bodyHtml: Cannubi is the most historic vineyard in the Barolo region, in Barolo village. They vinified this cru in 1985, and this is one of the two oldest vineyards planted in 1946 on the central crest of Cannubi hill. Here comes this Barolo's concentration and richness, whereas Nebbiolo's charm is fully expressed. Harmonious and has a very fine texture.

title: Dom Perignon Brut 2010 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
Dom Pérignon is a prestigious Champagne from France. It is produced in the Champagne region, with the historic Abbey of Saint Pierre d'Hautvillers considered the birthplace of Champagne. The brand's legacy is tied to the Benedictine monk Dom Pierre Pérignon, who worked at the Hautvillers Abbey starting in 1668.

Wine Description

In the glass, it typically presents a luminous golden hue. The bouquet is complex, mingling white flowers, apricot, and mirabelle plums with fresher notes of rhubarb and mint, and mineral elements like ash. The wine's mouthfeel is elegant yet vibrant, offering a foundation that is refined and silky. On the palate, there is an immediate sensation of energy and tonicity, with a finish marked by penetrating tautness, often revealing flavours of citrus, nutty characteristics, and toasted accents. 

Food Pairing

Traditional pairings include shellfish, such as oysters, crab, and lobster. It also beautifully complements dishes like freshly made sushi, fried chicken, or caviar.

title: Shafer Cabernet Sauvignon Hillside Select 2019 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
This iconic wine is a benchmark Cabernet Sauvignon from the United States, specifically from the California region and the Stags Leap District subregion of Napa Valley. Shafer Vineyards has been crafting world-class wines in the Stags Leap District for nearly 50 years. Hillside Select is a wine of its place, exclusively sourced from Shafer’s own hillside vineyards on steep, rocky slopes, a key aspect of their winemaking philosophy which highlights the significance of the terroir.

Wine Description

The wine presents a deep purple hue with inky intensity. It is a single-varietal wine, made from 100% Cabernet Sauvignon. The aroma is effusive, offering notes of black cherry, cassis, and juicy red summer berries, complemented by cedar, violets, camphor, and spring flowers. On the full-bodied palate, it is rich, dense, and concentrated, showcasing dark fruit flavours like blackcurrant and blackberry, interwoven with notes of dark chocolate, tobacco, espresso, black olive, and black tea. The wine achieves a masterful balance and complexity, supported by ultra-fine, velvety, and seamlessly integrated tannins that add great depth and structure.

Accolades

  • Jeb Dunnuck - 98+ points

  • Robert Parker’s Wine Advocate - 98+ points

  • Vinous - 98 points

  • James Suckling - 98 points

  • Decanter - 98 points

  • Wine Enthusiast - 97 points

  • Wine Spectator - 94 points

Food Pairing

This bold and complex Cabernet Sauvignon pairs beautifully with rich, substantial dishes. Suggested pairings include grilled steaks, roasted lamb, and hearty stews.

title: Antinori Brunello di Montalcino Riserva 'Pian delle Vigne Vignaferrovia' 2015
bodyHtml:
Antinori Brunello di Montalcino Riserva 'Pian delle Vigne Vignaferrovia' 2015 originates from Italy, within the Tuscany region and the prestigious Brunello di Montalcino DOCG. The 2015 vintage is particularly significant as it represents an exceptional year in Montalcino, allowing the Antinori family to produce this single-vineyard Riserva from their 4.5-hectare "Vignaferrovia" parcel. The estate’s philosophy for this bottling focuses on creating a "Cru" that highlights the gravel and clay-rich soils of the site, resulting in a Sangiovese of remarkable density and structural longevity.

Wine Description

The 2015 Riserva presents an intense ruby red colour with light garnet highlights. The sensory profile is exceptionally complex and "grand," opening with an aromatic nose of ripe black cherries, plums, and blackberries, seamlessly integrated with notes of tobacco, leather, and sweet spices like vanilla. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied and supple, delivering a rich, enveloping texture with ripe, velvety tannins and a vibrant balsamic freshness. The finish is remarkably long and persistent, marked by lingering notes of dark fruit and cocoa.

  • Varietal Composition: 100% Sangiovese.

  • Stylistic Notes: The wine was aged for 24 months in large oak barrels followed by significant bottle ageing to ensure the tannins are polished and the complex secondary aromas are fully developed.

  • ABV: 14.5%.

  • Organic Status: While the estate follows meticulous, sustainable vineyard management, this bottling is not certified organic.

Food Pairing

The majestic structure and mature fruit profile of the 2015 Riserva make it a peerless companion for rich, traditional Italian fare.

  • Meats: Pairs perfectly with grilled Florentine steak (Bistecca alla Fiorentina), roasted game such as wild boar or venison, and braised beef in red wine.

  • Savoury & Rich: Suggested pairings include Pappardelle with a rich hare or duck ragù, or truffle-infused dishes that complement the wine's earthy undertones.

  • Cheese: Matches well with very mature, hard cheeses like aged Pecorino Toscano or 36-month Parmigiano-Reggiano.

Vintage Quality

The 2015 vintage in Montalcino is widely considered "legendary" and a benchmark for the region. It was characterized by a perfect growing season with a warm, sunny summer and critical diurnal temperature shifts that allowed Sangiovese to reach flawless polyphenolic ripeness while retaining essential acidity. This allowed the winemaker to produce a Vignaferrovia that balances immense power with a refined, silk-like elegance. Experts suggest this vintage has a very long life ahead, with a drinking window extending well into the 2040s.

title: Altesino Brunello di Montalcino Vigna Montosoli 2021
bodyHtml:
Produced in the heart of Tuscany, Italy, this wine hails from the renowned Montalcino region. Altesino, established in 1970 and owned by the Gnudi Angelini family since 2002, is a pioneer in the region, having introduced the 'cru' concept to Montalcino with the legendary Montosoli vineyard in 1975. The winery's philosophy bridges deep-seated respect for Tuscan tradition with a forward-looking, eco-sustainable approach to winemaking.

Wine Description

This 100% Sangiovese Grosso displays a deep ruby hue that will gracefully transition to garnet with age. The bouquet is remarkably complex and savory, unleashing layers of crushed blackberries, violet, and rosemary, complemented by hints of balsamic, pink pepper, and damp forest floor. On the palate, the wine is medium to full-bodied with a silken texture and a firm core of finessed, edgy tannins that provide an aristocratic structure. It exhibits brilliant acidity and a concentrated trail of red fruits and autumnal spices, culminating in a long, linear finish.

Accolades

  • "James Suckling - 98 points"

  • "Decanter - 97 points"

  • "Jeb Dunnuck - 96 points"

  • "Vinous - 98 points"

title: Chateau Pichon Longueville Baron 2020
bodyHtml:
#8 Wine Spectator Top 100 of 2023

99 Points - James Suckling

This young Bordeaux is totally seamless with fine, velvet-like tannins that are integrated and refined. Underlying freshness and verve. It’s full-bodied, linear and long with a compact palate.

96+ Points - Jeb Dunnuck

The inky hued 2020 Chateau Pichon-Longueville Baron checks in as a blend of 76% Cabernet Sauvignon and 24% Merlot that spent 18 months in 70% new barrels. It's a dense, rich, powerful 2020 offering loads of pure cassis and almost blue fruits as well as full-bodied richness, a round, lush, incredibly sexy texture, sweet tannins, and ample classic Pauillac lead pencil, tobacco, and violet aromas and flavors. It's unquestionably in the same ballpark as the 2015, 2016, and 2018, and given its sweet tannins and beautifully integrated acidity, it should have some up-front appeal as well, yet still age at a glacier pace.

97 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2020 Pichon-Longueville Baron is a blend of 76% Cabernet Sauvignon and 24% Merlot aging for an estimated 18 months in French oak barrels, 70% new. The production of the grand vin represents 48% of the harvest this year. Opaque purple-black in color, it comes bounding out of the glass with exuberant notions of blackberry pie, preserved plums and crème de cassis, plus suggestions of Chinese five spice, chocolate mint, graphite and cedar chest with a touch of violets. The medium-bodied palate is built like a brick house, featuring firm, ripe, grainy tannins and bold freshness to support the taut, muscular black fruits, finishing long and spicy.

96 Points - Decanter

Intense, concentrated, rippling with power while still delivering finesse. A muscular Pichon Baron, layered with liquorice and chocolate shavings. Unmistakably Pauillac, and hugely Cabernet dominant, with savoury spice notes of grilled cumin and the same muscular, saline-backed tannins that you find in Les Griffons, just here with more definition and depth.

title: Chateau Pichon Longueville Baron 2022
bodyHtml:
Château Pichon Longueville Baron, located in Pauillac on Bordeaux’s Left Bank, is one of the region’s historic Second Growth estates, classified in the 1855 Médoc classification. Dating back to the late 17th century, the estate is known for its majestic château and meticulous winemaking philosophy that emphasizes precision, structure, and age-worthy elegance. Since 2007, the estate has been under the ownership of AXA Millésimes, who have modernized the facilities while preserving traditional values.

This 2022 vintage offers a deep, opaque ruby hue. Aromatically, it unfolds layers of cassis, blackberry, and dark plum, complemented by hints of cedar, pencil shavings, and violets. On the palate, the wine is powerful yet refined, showing a dense core of dark fruit, firm tannins, and fresh acidity. The texture is full-bodied and structured, with graphite and tobacco nuances leading into a persistent, savoury finish.

Accolades

  • Vinous - 98 Points
  • Jeb Dunnuck - 96+ Points
  • James Suckling - 96+ Points
  • Decanter - 96 Points
  • Wine Advocate - 95+ Points

Food Pairing
Ideal with herb-crusted lamb, grilled ribeye, or duck breast with blackberry reduction. This pairing highlights the wine’s depth and character.

title: Castellare Di Castellina 'I Sodi di San Niccolo' 2019
bodyHtml:
Castellare di Castellina 'I Sodi di San Niccolo' 2019 originates from Italy, within the Tuscany region and the Chianti Classico area. The estate was founded in the late 1970s when Paolo Panerai merged four smaller farms with the goal of producing wine of the highest possible quality. The winemaking philosophy is rooted in a deep respect for tradition and the environment, which is reflected in the iconic labels featuring birds to represent the winery's commitment to avoiding synthetic chemicals that could harm the local ecosystem.

Wine Description

This red wine presents a deep, intense ruby red colour and possesses a full, structured body. The sensory profile is elegant and complex, featuring an aromatic nose of red berries, black cherries, and plums, complemented by notes of vanilla, liquorice, and tobacco. On the palate, it is concentrated and harmonious, delivering rich fruit flavours supported by firm, silky tannins and a vibrant acidity. The finish is exceptionally long and persistent, showcasing great depth and a refined spicy character.

  • Varietal Composition: A blend of 85% Sangioveto (a local Sangiovese clone) and 15% Malvasia Nera.

  • Stylistic Notes: The wine is celebrated for its incredible longevity and complexity, having been matured for 24 to 30 months in French oak barriques followed by 12 months in the bottle.

  • ABV: 14.5%.

  • Organic Status: While not certified organic, the estate strictly follows sustainable viticulture and has prohibited the use of herbicides and pesticides since its inception to protect local wildlife.

Food Pairing

The robust structure and refined tannins of this wine make it an ideal partner for flavourful and savoury dishes.

  • Meats: Pairs excellently with grilled red meats, Florentine steak, and roasted game such as wild boar or venison.

  • Savoury: Suggested pairings include traditional Tuscan pasta dishes with meat ragù or truffle infused risotto.

  • Cheese: Matches well with mature, hard cheeses like aged Pecorino Toscano or Parmigiano Reggiano.

Vintage Quality

The 2019 vintage in Tuscany is regarded as an exceptional and classic year, characterized by a balanced growing season with ideal temperature shifts. These conditions allowed for slow, even ripening, resulting in grapes with fantastic aromatic intensity and structural harmony. The winemaker's skill in managing the harvest during this high quality season has produced a wine that perfectly captures the elegance and power of the Castellina terroir.

title: Chateau Bourgneuf 2022
bodyHtml:
Château Bourgneuf is a family-owned estate located in France, in the prestigious Pomerol appellation of Bordeaux’s Right Bank. Since 1927, it has been owned and operated by the Vayron family, now in its eighth generation, with Frédérique Vayron at the helm. The estate covers 9 hectares of vineyards adjacent to Château Trotanoy, with a winemaking philosophy that balances tradition and precision.

This 2022 vintage offers a richly expressive sensory profile. Deep ruby in colour, it opens with aromas of black cherries, violets, graphite, and subtle oak spice. The palate is layered and concentrated, showing ripe plum, blackcurrant, and savoury minerality, supported by firm tannins and a polished texture.

Food Pairing
This elegant Pomerol pairs well with roasted lamb, duck breast, mushroom risotto, or aged cheeses like Comté or Gruyère. Together, they create an unforgettable dining experience.

title: Chateau La Mission Haut Brion 2006
bodyHtml:
96 Points - Wine Enthusiast

Wonderful sweet fruit, velvet in texture, with concentrated ripe fruits and red berries. This is a wine that rolls sumptuously around the mouth, the tannins certainly dense but full of the same sweetness as the fruit. The final flavour is perfumed and fresh. Deceptively attractive, it will profit from aging.

95 Points - Wine Spectator

Almost jammy, with vanilla bean and coffee undertones. Full-bodied and very powerful, with big, juicy tannins and a long finish. Very big and generous for the vintage, showing exceptional quality.

95 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2006 La Mission Haut-Brion is showing very well at age 15 (tasted in 2021), and even though it's still five or six years away from the beginning of its plateau of maturity, it is already quite expressive, wafting from the glass with aromas of blackberries and blackcurrants mingled with notions of smoke, cigar wrapper, black truffle and loamy soil. Full-bodied, fleshy and muscular, with a richly layered core of fruit framed by an abundance of ripe, powdery tannin, in a blind tasting I suspect many would confuse it with a 2005.

title: Domaine Tollot Beaut Aloxe Corton 2023
bodyHtml:
Aloxe-Corton Les Vercots 1er Cru is a special wine for Tollot-Beaut. This wine was produced from 50% old vines with some of the plantings dating to before WWII. Les Vercots is now produced from a ten-year-old sélection massale on deep soil with a high limestone content. The climate sits mid-slope on the Corton hill and faces due south.

Wine Description

Aloxe Corton is a refined red wine crafted from 100% Pinot Noir. It presents a perfumed and fragrant profile with deep, lush aromas of Crème de Mure, cherry, and raspberry, layered with exotic sweet spices and a hint of vanilla. On the palate, the wine is elegant and supple, featuring plush tannins and a vibrant freshness that balances its ripe fruit character. This medium bodied wine shows excellent complexity and a long, persistent finish.

title: Chateau Ducru Beaucaillou 2021
bodyHtml:
Chateau Ducru-Beaucaillou, a prestigious Second Growth estate in the Saint-Julien appellation of Bordeaux, is renowned for producing wines of exceptional depth and elegance. The 2021 vintage continues this legacy, showcasing the estate's commitment to excellence.

Blend and Production

The 2021 Château Ducru-Beaucaillou is composed of 98% Cabernet Sauvignon and 2% Merlot. The grapes were harvested from September 21 to October 10, 2021. Vinification occurred in wooden tronconic tanks, and the wine is being aged for 18 months in 100% new French oak barrels.

Tasting Notes

  • Appearance: Deep ruby/plum hue.

  • Nose: Aromas of pure crème de cassis, graphite, crushed stone, and violets, with subtle hints of tobacco and spicy oak.

  • Palate: Medium to full-bodied, deep, rich, and concentrated, with a beautiful mid-palate, ripe, building tannins, and a gorgeous finish.

Critical Acclaim

  • Jeb Dunnuck: Described the 2021 Chateau Ducru-Beaucaillou as "one of the top wines of the vintage," highlighting its deep ruby/plum hue and classic Ducru notes of pure crème de cassis, graphite, crushed stone, and violets, with a kiss of background tobacco and spicy oak.

title: Chateau Cos d'Estournel Blanc 2021
bodyHtml:
Château Cos d'Estournel, renowned for its exceptional red wines, also produces a distinguished white wine: Cos d'Estournel Blanc. The 2021 vintage exemplifies the estate's dedication to crafting wines of elegance and complexity.

Blend and Production

The 2021 Cos d'Estournel Blanc is a blend of Sauvignon Blanc and Sémillon grapes, sourced from vineyards located in the northern Médoc region. The precise blend ratio and vinification details are proprietary to the estate.

Tasting Notes

  • Appearance: Pale lemon-yellow with slight green tints.

  • Nose: Pure aromas of pea-pod and passion fruit, with subtle hints of cedar and vanilla.

  • Palate: Lovely intensity with superbly integrated cedar and vanilla notes, leading to a harmonious and refreshing finish.

Accolades

97 Points - James Suckling:

Aromas of sliced pears, green apple, matchstick, and dried papaya follow through to a full body with a solid core of fruit and phenolics that give it structure and tightness. Slightly chewy at the end. Very structured. Give this time to open and show its true self.

95 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

The Grand Vin in white, the 2021 Château Cos D'Estournel Blanc includes slightly more Semillon and is 71% Sauvignon Blanc and 29% Semillon raised in 8% new barrels. It's a slightly more closed and tight white, revealing beautiful citrus fruit that gives way to more mint, floral, and chalky mineral-like nuances with air. Medium-bodied and balanced, it plays in the fresher style of the vintage but is still concentrated and serious, and it will benefit from a year or three of bottle age. It’s built for the cellar and will benefit from 2-3 years and drink well for at least a decade. This is 12.3% alcohol with a pH of 3.13.

94 Points - Decanter

Green apple skin, gooseberry and soft floral nuances. Lovely juicy core, high but balanced acidity gives the life while the toasted, quite bitter (grapefruit, orange, wood) elements come in towards the mid palate giving extra layers of nuance and depth and interest. It's not complete yet but good potential. Feels clean and precise and well worked. Maybe loses a touch of push and persistence on the finish, but there's nice purity and vibrancy from start to finish.

Serving and Pairing

Serve chilled at 50–54°F (10–12°C). This wine pairs beautifully with seafood dishes, poultry, and creamy cheeses.

title: Tua Rita Redigaffi 2022
bodyHtml:
This legendary red wine originates from the Toscana IGT appellation in the Suvereto subregion of coastal Tuscany, Italy. Tua Rita was founded in 1984 by Rita Tua and Virgilio Bisti, starting as a small 'boutique' estate that quickly gained international acclaim for its uncompromising quality. The winery’s philosophy is defined by a meticulous, handcrafted approach to viticulture and a commitment to expressing the unique iron-rich soils of the Colline Metallifere, which impart a distinct mineral signature to their wines.

Wine Description

The Tua Rita Redigaffi 2022 presents an intense, deep ruby red colour. The sensory profile is profoundly complex and opulent, featuring an expansive nose of blackberries, blueberries, and dark cherries, layered with sophisticated notes of sandalwood, graphite, black liquorice, and exotic spices. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied and seamless, showcasing a dense, velvety texture with ultra-fine, polished tannins and a remarkable structural tension. It is characterized by its incredible flavour concentration and a monumental finish that lingers with echoes of dark chocolate, crushed stones, and wild herbs. This 100% Merlot has an ABV of 15% and was aged for approximately 18 to 20 months in 100% new French oak barrels.

Accolades

James Suckling 98 Points - "Aromas of crushed fruit and white pepper with dried lavender and hints of violets and sage flowers. Stony undertones, too. Medium- to full-bodied, tight and focused, with reserve and beauty. And then it grows on the palate with polished and focused tannins that take it to another level. Exudes freshness and length, despite the hot growing season. A sophisticated red and with a long future ahead. Try after three to four years."

Vintage Quality

The 2022 vintage in coastal Tuscany was marked by an exceptionally hot and dry growing season, which resulted in low yields and highly concentrated berries. Despite the solar intensity, the proximity of Tua Rita's vineyards to the Tyrrhenian Sea provided cooling maritime breezes that preserved essential acidity and aromatic freshness in the fruit. Winemakers exercised extreme precision in harvest timing and extraction to produce wines that marry the vintage's natural opulence with surprising elegance and poise.

title: Domaine Henri Rebourseau Mazy Chambertin Grand Cru 2019
bodyHtml:
Introduction

This prestigious red wine originates from France, specifically the Burgundy region within the Gevrey Chambertin commune. Domaine Henri Rebourseau is one of the most historic estates in the Côte de Nuits, managing an exceptional heritage of Grand Cru vineyards since the late 18th century. Now a partnership between the Rebourseau and Bouygues families, the winery follows a philosophy of biodynamic viticulture and minimal intervention to ensure that each unique parcel of land is authentically expressed in the glass.

Wine Description

The Domaine Henri Rebourseau Mazy Chambertin Grand Cru 2019 displays a brilliant, deep ruby colour. The nose is complex and refined, revealing layers of wild raspberries, red cherries, and dried floral notes, underpinned by hints of licorice, forest floor, and a distinct smoky minerality. On the palate, the wine is powerful yet elegant, featuring silky, well integrated tannins and a vibrant acidity that provides remarkable lift. The finish is persistent and saline, reflecting the classic limestone character of the Mazy vineyard. This wine is 100% Pinot Noir and is currently entering its long aging window, with potential to develop for 15 to 20 years. It is certified organic and biodynamic, with an alcohol by volume (ABV) of 13.5%.

Accolades

  • Jasper Morris - Inside Burgundy - 93-96 points.

  • Vinous - 92-94 points.

  • Burghound - 91-94 points.

  • Jancis Robinson - 17.5/20 points.

Food Pairing

This sophisticated Grand Cru pairs excellently with refined dishes such as roasted duck breast with a cherry reduction, venison loin, or a classic beef bourguignon made with high quality meat. It also complements earthy dishes like wild mushroom risotto or truffled poultry, and pairs beautifully with mature Burgundian cheeses like Epoisses or Citeaux.

Vintage Quality

The 2019 vintage in Burgundy is widely regarded as exceptional, characterized by a warm and dry growing season that produced small, concentrated berries. Despite the heat, the wines have maintained a surprising amount of freshness and acidity, resulting in a vintage that offers both immediate pleasure and extraordinary potential for long term cellaring.

title: Raen Pinot Noir Royal St. Robert 2023
bodyHtml:
The Royal St. Robert bottling is a dedication to the Mondavi brothers' grandfather, Robert Mondavi, a significant figure in Napa Valley's history. Raen (which stands for Rejuvenating Agriculture Environment Naturally) winery was founded in 2013 by brothers Carlo and Dante Mondavi with a vision to craft world-class Pinot Noir from the remote, cool, and rugged western hills of the Sonoma Coast.

Wine Description

On the nose, expect captivating aromas of crushed wild berries, black cherries, rose petals, and coastal moss, evolving into black tea, bergamot, forest floor, and delicate floral notes. Additional notes include blood orange, cola, redwood forest, rosemary, and wild mushroom flavours.

The palate is medium-bodied and taut, showing a silky texture and vibrant clarity. Flavours include red cherry, raspberry plum, blood orange marmalade, black cherry, dried raspberry, and pomegranate. Savoury herbs and exotic spice box notes intertwine with the fruit core, all supported by fine-grained tannins and a firm backbone of crunchy acidity.

Accolades

  • 'James Suckling - 99 points'

  • 'Decanter - 95 points'

  • 'Wine Spectator - 94 points'

  • 'Vinous - 93 points'

  • 'Robert Parker's The Wine Advocate - 93 points'

Food Pairings

Pairs well with duck, braised pork belly, or a mushroom risotto.

title: Grgich Hills Cabernet Sauvignon Miljenko's 100th Birthday 2019
bodyHtml:
From the Napa Valley region in California, this special wine from Grgich Hills Estate celebrates the 100th birthday of founder Miljenko 'Mike' Grgich. A Croatian immigrant, Mike Grgich became internationally famous as the winemaker behind the 1973 Chateau Montelena Chardonnay that won the white wine category at the historic 'Judgment of Paris' tasting in 1976. He established Grgich Hills in 1977 with a philosophy of making age-worthy, terroir driven wines from their own estate vineyards and farming with great respect for the earth. The winery farms all of its vineyards organically and uses regenerative agriculture practices.

Wine Description The 2019 'Yountville Old Vine' Cabernet Sauvignon is a rich and elegant wine made from grapes planted in 1959. The old vines produce fewer grapes, but the fruit has more concentrated, intense flavours. The wine is a blend of 86% Cabernet Sauvignon, 8% Petit Verdot, and 6% Cabernet Franc. It has complex aromas of brambly blackberry, rosehip, red currant, and blood orange. The palate follows with flavours of sweet cherry, blueberry, rosemary, and dry peat. The tannins are soft, round, and velvety, leading to a long, luscious finish. This full bodied wine has a heritage feel, like a great Cabernet from the 1980s, and is expected to age well. The optimal drinking window is through at least 2033. All of Grgich Hills' vineyards are certified organic, and the grapes are grown without artificial pesticides or herbicides.

Accolades

  • Wine Enthusiast - 94 points

  • Natalie MacLean - 94 points

  • Wine Advocate - 93 points

  • Decanter - 98 points

Food Pairing The wine's rich and elegant profile pairs well with a variety of dishes. Suggested pairings include lamb Bolognese, beef enchiladas, barbecued ribs in sauce, hamburgers, or hard cheese. A perfect match to enhance the wine's complexity.

Vintage Quality The 2019 vintage in Napa Valley was an exceptional and uneventful growing season with plenty of rain in the winter and minimal extreme heat events. This allowed for a long hangtime, giving winemakers the luxury of picking grapes at optimal ripeness. The resulting wines are often described as having a "purity" of fruit that reflects Napa Valley's terroir.

title: El Enemigo 'Gran Enemigo' Gualtallary Single Vineyard 2020
bodyHtml:
Winemaking is spread between the Catena family winery in the Uco Valley and Alejandro's own barrel room in his garden of Chachingo - The Republic - where his young son rides a horse among olive trees and where dogs and chickens share the grounds with the Vigil family and the winery.

El Gran Enemigo SV Gualtallary shows a deep purple color with red highlights. Its aromas are intense and elegant. Cabernet Franc brings sweet spices, black pepper and light notes of eucalyptus and thyme. Malbec brings notes of ripe black fruits, blackberries and black cherries. The oak aging gives a touch of chocolate and vanilla to blend.

The taste is complex, sweet impact with structured tannins, and a very long and persistent finish. This wine was made in honor of the old Pomerol style where Cabernet Franc was blended with the other Bordeaux varieties.

99 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2020 Gran Enemigo Gualtallary Single Vineyard is nothing but phenomenal. It's very fresh and balanced and, for a warm year like 2020, doesn't show any heat or excess; it's subtle and has an ethereal character within the powerful and exuberant character from Gualtallary. It fermented in concrete with indigenous yeasts and some full clusters, sometimes up to 70% of the volume. It's intense and powerful, but something makes if feel light on its feet and with great inner power.

title: Casanova Di Neri Cabernet Sauvignon 'Pietradonice' 2021
bodyHtml:
Casanova di Neri is a prestigious estate founded by Giovanni Neri in 1971, today managed by his son Giacomo Neri. Renowned for crafting some of the most lauded Brunellos, the estate is equally respected for its innovative spirit, which led to the creation of Pietradonice—a testament to their adventurous approach to terroir and varietals.

Wine Description

The 2021 Pietradonice is a 100% Cabernet Sauvignon that dazzles with its deep, opaque ruby hue. The nose opens with pronounced aromas of ripe blackcurrant, blackberry, and cassis, intertwined with subtle notes of graphite, mint, and a delicate cedar spice. On the palate, it is full-bodied and powerful yet impeccably balanced, offering layers of dark fruits, tobacco, and dark chocolate supported by firm, polished tannins.

Accolades

  • "Wine Advocate - 95 points."

  • "James Suckling - 94 points."

Food Pairing

Pair this superb Cabernet Sauvignon with grilled Florentine steak, lamb chops with rosemary, or aged Pecorino Toscano. These combinations enhance the wine’s depth and underscore its savoury character. Together, they create an unforgettable dining experience.

title: Sea Smoke Pinot Noir 'Southing' 2022 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
Introduction

This red wine originates from the United States, specifically from the Sta. Rita Hills AVA in Santa Barbara County, California. Founded in 1999 by Bob Davids, Sea Smoke Cellars is named after the cooling marine fog that rolls through the Santa Ynez River canyon, creating a unique microclimate for cool-climate viticulture. The winery's philosophy centres on the meticulous 'micro-management' of its estate vineyards, which have been farmed organically since 2005 and increasingly follow biodynamic and regenerative principles. Southing is one of the estate's flagship Pinot Noirs, named for its origin on the south-facing hillside bluffs of the property.

Wine Description

Sea Smoke Pinot Noir Southing 2022 displays a deep, brilliant ruby colour. The nose is highly aromatic and ever-changing, offering an elegant bouquet of Montmorency cherry, sage, and hibiscus layered with notes of lavender, rose water, and dried flowers. On the palate, the wine is generous and well-structured, featuring sweet cherry flesh, strawberry, and red plums balanced by a bright minerality and characteristic cool-climate acidity. It is characterized by its fine-grained tannins and savoury undertones of wild herbs, baking spices, and a hint of smoky sea salt on the persistent finish. This 100% Pinot Noir has an ABV of 14.2% to 14.5% and was aged for 16 months in French oak barrels (approximately 42% new). The wine is bottled without fining or filtration to preserve its complexity. The optimal drinking window for this vintage is from 2025 through 2035.

Accolades

  • Wine Enthusiast - 94 points.

  • Decanter - 94 points.

  • James Suckling - 95 points.

Food Pairing

The elegant structure and vibrant acidity of Southing make it an exceptional partner for a variety of refined and savoury dishes. It pairs perfectly with roasted duck, mushroom risotto, or herb-crusted rack of lamb, which complement its earthy and spicy notes. Its bright red fruit profile also harmonises with roasted chicken, turkey, or grilled salmon served with a cherry reduction. For a cheese course, consider aged varieties or creamy cheeses like Brie and Camembert.

Vintage Quality

The 2022 vintage in the Sta. Rita Hills was a reliable, long growing season that allowed for full flavour maturation and tannin development. Despite being a warm vintage, winemakers successfully maintained the region's signature precision, resulting in wines with focused energy, concentrated fruit, and a near-everlasting finish.

title: Faiveley Clos de Vougeot Grand Cru 2021
bodyHtml:
Deep ruby red with complex fruity and floral notes (rose, violet) and a subtle hint of oak on the nose. The attack is smooth with powerful tannins. This well-structured and very persistent wine is an honor to the reputation of this exceptional Grand Cru.

94 Points - Wine Spectator

There's an openness to this red, from its enticing cherry, strawberry, spice and sun-kissed vegetal aromas and flavors to its bright acidity and light-weight, dusty tannins. Balanced and persistent, with a deft use of oak and a spice-tinged aftertaste.

title: Castiglion del Bosco Brunello di Montalcino Riserva Millecento 2015 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
Castiglion del Bosco was purchased by Massimo Ferragamo, son of the Italian shoe designer who founded the luxury goods company Salvatore Ferragamo. This estate, which is a part of the Val d'Orcia National Park UNESCO site, has undergone significant investment to bring it back to its fashionable and elite finest.

The finest Sangiovese matured in French oak for three years and then a further two years in the bottle before release, Castiglion del Bosco Brunello di Montalcino Riserva Millecento 2015 is the epitome of elegance.

97 Points - James Suckling

Opulent aromas of cherry, plum, dried meat and orange peel with some bark and cedar. Full-bodied with firm yet polished tannins that fill mouth and carry far down the wine to the end. It’s creamy-textured and chewy. Purity and integration. Very drinkable now, but needs another two or three years to come around. Try after 2022. 

95 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The Castiglion del Bosco 2015 Brunello di Montalcino Riserva Millecento represents a happy return for a wine that we have not seen in a few years. This Riserva draws its fruit from an eight-hectare parcel with schistous galestro soils surrounded by thick forests and wildlife. Some 10,000 bottles were made. There is soft and rich cherry fruit at the core with light shadings of spice, cinnamon, tilled earth and a more sanguine tone of rust or iron ore. 

94 Points - Wine Spectator

A firm structural edge keeps macerated cherry, plum and underbrush flavours defined, while a lively acidity drives them to a lingering conclusion. Fresh and shows fine tension. Best from 2024 through 2045. 

93 Points - Vinous

The 2015 Brunello di Montalcino Millecento Riserva of Castiglion del Bosco takes no prisoners, boasting a striking bouquet of crushed medicinal cherry and plum complemented by confectionary spices. It floods the palate with velvety textures and dark ripe fruits, offset by vibrant acids and salty tension. There’s a density and primary feel to the Millecento which, combined with its fine-grained tannin, promises years of development. Baker’s chocolate and hints of cedar linger on the long and structured finish. The 2015 Riserva spent thirty-six months in thirty hectoliter French oak barrels and another six months in porous concrete vats prior to bottling. It’s a large-scale yet balanced effort.

title: Chateau Lascombes 2022
bodyHtml:
Originating from France in the prestigious Bordeaux region, specifically within the iconic Margaux subregion, Chateau Lascombes 2022 represents a distinguished Second Growth (Deuxieme Grand Cru Classe) from the historical 1855 Classification. The estate traces its origins back to the 17th century with the Lascombes family and has evolved through centuries of refining its terroir-driven approach. Today, under the ownership of Lawrence Wine Estates, Chateau Lascombes blends centuries of Medoc winemaking tradition with modern precision to produce opulent, highly expressive wines from its diverse gravel, clay, and limestone soils.
