Wine Description

The wine presents an inky, saturated ruby purple colour in the glass. The bouquet opens with vibrant aromas of dark cassis, wild blueberry, and damson plum, underpinned by complex hints of crushed rocks, violets, espresso, liquorice, and toasted cedar spice. On the palate, it is broad, lush, and full bodied, delivering rich layers of black cherry compote, dark chocolate, and graphite. Supported by a firm backbone of fine, velvety tannins and a streak of refreshing acidity, it lingers through an extraordinarily long, mineral-inflected finish. Composed predominantly of Cabernet Sauvignon alongside Merlot and small portions of Petit Verdot and Cabernet Franc, this release offers an optimal drinking window of 2028–2055. Stylistically, it combines classic Margaux aromatic elegance with remarkable fruit concentration, structural power, and creamy texture.

title: Chateau Giscours 2019
bodyHtml:
Château Giscours, a distinguished Third Growth estate in the 1855 Bordeaux Classification, is situated in the Margaux appellation of France's Médoc region. With a rich history dating back to the 14th century, the estate has been under Dutch ownership and management, along with its sister property Château du Tertre. The 95 hectares of vineyards are planted with 60% Cabernet Sauvignon, 32% Merlot, 5% Cabernet Franc, and 3% Petit Verdot.

The 2019 Château Giscours is a blend of 65% Cabernet Sauvignon and 35% Merlot. This vintage presents a deep, dark ruby-red color with purple hints at the rim. The nose offers restrained aromas of violet and blackberry. On the palate, it has good freshness and initially displays pure blackcurrant fruit. The mid-palate is closed up by cedary tannins.

Optimal Drinking Window: The 2019 Château Giscours is approachable upon release and can be enjoyed over the next 5 to 7 years, allowing its flavors to develop further with short-term cellaring.

Food Pairing Suggestions: This Margaux pairs beautifully with grilled meats, such as lamb or beef, as well as hearty stews and aged cheeses.

title: Chateau Canon La Gaffeliere 2017
bodyHtml:
Located on the famous slope (and the foot of the slope) south of the medieval village of Saint-Emilion, Chateau Canon La Gaffeliere has belonged to the Counts von Neipperg since 1971. Representing some eight centuries of family winegrowing tradition, Count Stephan von Neipperg has succeeded in placing Chateau Canon La Gaffeliere among the top Grands Crus Classes of Saint-Emilion thanks to a winegrowing philosophy that gives priority not only to quality, but also respect for the environment.

97 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Medium to deep garnet-purple colored, the 2017 Canon la Gaffeliere comes roaring out of the glass with exuberant notes of baked blackberries, blueberry compote and redcurrant jelly plus hints of forest floor, dried roses and cedar chest with a waft of fallen leaves. Medium to full-bodied, the palate has fantastic density with a firm frame of finely grained tannins and tons of freshness, finishing with lingering layers of bright, energetic fruit.

94 Points - Wine Spectator

Features a deliciously ripe and inviting core of plum, boysenberry and blackberry compote flavors, backed by anise and apple wood notes. Juicy in feel through the finish, with the fruit lingering. Tobacco and iron accents wait in reserve.

94 Points - Wine Enthusiast

This open wine brings out delicious black-currant fruits as well as the essential core of dark tannins. The solid backbone will stand the wine in good stead as it matures, softening the juicy, forward fruitiness.

93 Points - James Suckling

92+ Points - James Suckling

92 Points - Decanter

title: Chateau Petrus 2019
bodyHtml:
Château Pétrus, nestled in Bordeaux’s renowned Pomerol appellation, is a pinnacle of winemaking excellence, revered for its rarity and exceptional quality. Managed by the Moueix family, the estate’s unique terroir of blue clay imparts unparalleled depth and character to its wines, earning it a legendary status among collectors and connoisseurs.

The 2019 vintage is a masterful expression of this iconic estate. Deep garnet in color, it exudes aromas of ripe blackberries, plums, and violets, interwoven with earthy undertones of truffle, graphite, and mocha. On the palate, the wine is opulent yet exquisitely balanced, with velvety tannins and layers of dark fruit, spice, and a touch of minerality. The finish is remarkably long and elegant, promising decades of graceful evolution. This wine is best savored from 2030 to 2060, allowing its full complexity to unfold.

Pair it with roasted duck breast with cherry reduction, wild mushroom risotto, or an aged Gruyère for an elevated culinary experience. Together, these combinations highlight the wine’s depth and create an unforgettable harmony. James Suckling praised the 2019 Château Pétrus, noting it as "a wine of profound elegance and power, destined to age beautifully over the decades."

title: Castello dei Rampolla d'Alceo 2020
bodyHtml:
Hailing from Italy, in the renowned Tuscan subregion of Chianti Classico's Panzano, Castello dei Rampolla stands as a pioneer of biodynamic viticulture and high-density planting. Since the mid-1960s, the di Napoli Rampolla family has steered this historic estate, crafting wines that reflect the rugged terroir and solar warmth of their famous Conca d'Oro vineyards.

Wine Description

This rich, unfiltered red presents a deep, inky purple-ruby colour. The complex nose unfurls expressive aromas of blackcurrant, dark fruit, and violets alongside delicate nuances of lavender, sweet licorice, pencil shavings, and mocha. On the palate, it exhibits a full body with extraordinary concentration, supported by a firm, velvety tannin structure and lively, balancing acidity.

title: Azelia Barolo Cerretta 2019
bodyHtml:
The Azienda Agricola Azelia, in the centre of the area of Barolo production, is composed of 16 hectares and it produces, on average, 80,000 bottles per year. Luigi is supported by his wife Lorella and his son Lorenzo, who bears the name of his grandfather and who represents the fifth generation of wine producers. Great care is given to the work in the vineyards. Wine is made there from old vines which produce very few grapes. The low yields are further reduced through the green harvest, indispensable to select fruits, to have a uniform ripening and an impeccable quality. 

An explosive energy of Serralunga d’Alba shows in this wine, with grace and vigor. Black cherries, wild berries and plums with menthol, sage and saline notes. Pure ardor. The wine is aged 30 months in large casks.

title: Chateau La Clotte 2019
bodyHtml:
Introduction

Château La Clotte 2019 is a Saint-Émilion Grand Cru Classé from the Right Bank of Bordeaux, France. The estate's history dates back to at least the 16th century, and it was acquired in 2014 by the Vauthier family, owners of the neighboring legendary Château Ausone. The winemaking philosophy is overseen by Alain Vauthier and his daughter Pauline, focusing on 'haute couture' production from a tiny 4-hectare vineyard situated on a prime limestone plateau.

Wine Description

This vintage presents a powerful and expressive sensory profile with radiant black fruit aromas matched by scents of spring flowers, red berries, and wilted rose petals. On the medium-bodied palate, the wine is ripe and beautifully poised, offering pure flavours of black and blue fruit interspersed with cedar, spice, and mahogany. The structure is defined by pliant, velvety tannins and a lively freshness that leads into an elegant, refined finish with great purity. The varietal composition is a Merlot-dominant blend, typically consisting of around 85% Merlot complemented by Cabernet Franc and occasionally a small amount of Cabernet Sauvignon. This wine has an ABV of 13.5% or 14% depending on the bottling, and while the estate practices sustainable winegrowing, it is not certified organic.

Food Pairing

The plush fruit and soft tannins of this Saint-Émilion make it an excellent companion for roasted red meats such as prime rib of beef, leg of lamb with thyme, or roast venison. It also pairs traditionally with Right Bank specialities like mushroom and truffle risotto, duck breast, or pork tenderloin. For a cheese course, semi-soft or aged varieties such as Comté, Brie, or Camembert are recommended.

Vintage Quality

The 2019 vintage in Saint-Émilion is regarded as potentially the most terroir-expressive year Bordeaux has ever crafted, defined by a signature 'energy' and freshness. The growing season began with an early budbreak and survived a scorching, dry July thanks to critical rainfall late in the month. These conditions allowed the Merlot and Cabernet grapes to reach optimal phenolic ripeness, resulting in wines with exceptional fruit purity and concentration.

title: Chateau Grand Puy Lacoste 2018
bodyHtml:
Grand-Puy-Lacoste 2018 is one of a series of great vintages. The blend has a majority of Cabernet Sauvignon (78%) whose character and charm so perfectly express the richness and quality of this distinguished terroir. This wine is deep magenta, intense and brilliant. The bouquet reveals aromas of ripe black fruits and liquorice, underlining the grapes' perfect maturity, whilst keeping a pretty freshness and good minerality. On the palate, the attack is precise, very dense and complex. This 2018 has a very fine balance combining power, elegance and complexity. It has a long, very aromatic and tannic finish. The whole emphasizing the great ageing potential of this wine.

95 Points - Wine Spectator    Juicy and compact now, with dark currant, blackberry and fig notes at the core, surrounded by lots of warm earth, singed alder and tobacco leaf notes. Cast iron note helps extend the finish, with the fruit and earth notes keeping pace. Has a slight throwback feel, so if you like old school, age-worthy Pauillac, this is your wine. Cabernet Sauvignon and Merlot. Best from 2024 through 2038.

95 Points - Decanter    Sweet black cherry fruits, bilberry and hedgerow. A little austere at this stage but confidently so, with a slice of bitter black chocolate. Big Pauillac tannins, no question, a little more prominent than they were en primeur. The wine has taken on weight over ageing so I am slightly extending the drinking window. Harvest 21 September and 5 October. 12% press wine. 75% new oak. Drinking Window 2026 - 2044.

94 Points - Jeb Dunnuck    A beautiful Pauillac, the 2018 Château Grand-Puy-Lacoste has a classic nose of ripe blackcurrants, scorched earth, cedarwood, and tobacco. This carries to a medium to full-bodied 2018 offering wonderful balance, ripe, polished tannins, and gorgeous purity of fruit. A wine that grows on you with time in the glass, it has building mid-palate depth and tannins, again, terrific balance, remarkable purity of fruit, and outstanding length on the finish. It should round into form in 4-5 years and keep for 20+.

94 Points - James Suckling    Cherries and walnuts with dried flowers on the nose. It’s medium-to full-bodied with very fine tannins, creamy texture and a bright, vivid finish. Plenty of currant and tar. Such polish and beauty. Drink after 2023.

94 Points - Wilfred Wong of Wine    The 2018 Château Grand-Puy-Lacoste shows greatness from start to finish, and it is built like a tank. This wine offers aromas and flavors of black fruit, mineral notes, savory spices, and oak. Enjoy its powerful presence with grilled beef kebabs in a mushroom, white wine reduction sauce.

93 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate    The 2018 Grand-Puy-Lacoste displays a deep garnet-purple color and slowly emerging notes of ripe blackberries, blackcurrant pastilles and redcurrant jelly plus hints of cedar, underbrush, cinnamon stick and potpourri. The medium-bodied palate has well-managed, slightly chewy tannin's and a refreshing line lifting the black and red berry layers, finishing earthy.

92 Points - Wine Enthusiast    This is a relatively soft wine, its tannins already embracing the black-currant fruits. The structure is there, smoothly textured and ripe with fruitiness as well as good acidity. This wine is likely to develop relatively quickly, so drink from 2024.

title: Gaja Barbaresco 2023
bodyHtml:
Originating from Italy in the Piedmont region, specifically within the Barbaresco DOCG appellation, Gaja Barbaresco 2023 represents the ultimate benchmark, iconic, and world-renowned expression of Nebbiolo. First produced by Giovanni Gaja in 1859, this flagship bottling is the signature backbone of the Gaja family estate, currently stewarded by Angelo Gaja and his children Gaia, Rossana, and Giovanni. Sourced from 14 distinct estate vineyard plots situated across the communes of Barbaresco and Treiso planted on steep limestone and clay-marl soils, the winemaking philosophy combines meticulous plot-by-plot hand harvesting, separate temperature-controlled fermentation in stainless steel vats, and maturation for 12 months in barriques followed by 12 months in traditional large oak botti. Blended with masterly precision from all 14 parcels, the result is a wine of extraordinary harmony, ethereal floral complexity, and monumental cellaring capability.

Wine Description

The wine presents a clear, luminous pale garnet red colour with bright ruby-orange reflections along the rim. An expressive, highly complex bouquet opens with noble aromas of wild sour cherry, red plum, dried raspberry, and blood orange, interwoven with sophisticated notes of crushed dried rose petals, pipe tobacco, crushed flint, leather, liquorice, and subtle forest floor spice. On the palate, it is medium-to-full bodied, taut, and aristocratically structured, delivering concentrated flavours of tart red fruits, pomegranate curd, and savory mineral earth, all supported by a bright, mouthwatering spine of natural acidity. Framed by ultra-fine, chalky, fine-grained Nebbiolo tannins and a driving, coat-the-mouth mid-palate structure, it concludes with an extraordinarily long, persistent finish marked by lingering red fruit, dried herbs, and a clean limestone grip. Composed of 100% Nebbiolo, this 2023 release offers an optimal drinking window of 2028–2055+. Stylistically, it effortlessly combines ethereal perfumed elegance and high-altitude tension with deep concentration, structural muscle, and timeless aging potential.

title: Jane Eyre Savigny Les Beaune Premier Cru Aux Vergelesses 2020
bodyHtml:
The vineyard is located in the upper part of this famous climate, on an eastern slope, which gives it a fresher style. This year, its fragrance is intensely reminiscent of juicy black cherries, the ones from the markets, bursting with sunshine. The palate remains, beyond the richness of the year, of an incredible finesse of tannins while offering a real volume in the mouth. 2020 is certainly a great year for Savigny. Drink now and over 10 years.

The 2020 Savigny-les-Beaune Aux Vergelesses Premier Cru has a delightful bouquet with cranberry, raspberry and briary aromas. The palate is medium-bodied with crunchy, ripe black and red fruit, fresh and well-defined, the 30% whole bunch imparting a pleasant peppery note on the finish. This is worth seeking out.

title: Chateau Clerc Milon 2017
bodyHtml:
95 Points - James Suckling    This is a rich and profound red with blackberries, blackcurrants, pine needles and graphite. Black licorice, too. Full-bodied, crisp and creamy with fantastic tannin backbone and length. Deep. A blend of 60% cabernet sauvignon, 23% merlot, 14% cabernet franc, 2% petit verdot and 1% carmenere. Try after 2022.

95 Points - Decanter    Creamy weight through the body, although as with the 2001 this is a vintage that stays on the lighter side of its Pauillac tannins. As it opens, you get subtle layers of blackberry, flint, graphite, cassis, touches of smoked coffee beans. A separate vineyard and cellar team had been in charge here since 2009, headed up by ex-Opus One winemaker Jean-Emmanuel Danjoy. The 300 plots of the vineyard had been reworked down to 70 or so plots through careful land purchases, and the vineyard worked carefully to ensure the roots could travel deeper. Blend completed with 2% Petit Verdot and 1% Carmanère, because at this point a new wine cellar with smaller tanks made it possible to vinify them apart. Drinking Window 2025 - 2044.

94 Points - Wine Spectator    This starts with a kick of violet before a well-built beam of black currant, fig and plum paste flavors enters authoritatively. Very solid through the finish, with chestnut, alder and graphite notes adding a defined bass line. Fresh acidity is well-embedded throughout, keeping all the elements in line. A strong showing. Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Cabernet Franc, Petit Verdot and Carmenère. Best from 2022 through 2038.

94 Points - Wine Enthusiast    With its elegant structure and a layer of firm tannins, this wine has density, a dry core and the blackcurrant freshness that comes with the vintage. The tannins will allow this wine to age well. Drink from 2023.

94 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate    The 2017 Clerc Milon is medium to deep garnet-purple colored and offers up a gorgeous nose of potpourri, cinnamon stick, candied violets and kirsch over a core of warm cassis, plum preserves and boysenberries with a waft of garrigue. Medium to full-bodied, the palate delivers loads of muscular fruit with a firm, fine-grained texture and tons of freshness, finishing long and perfumed. Rating: 94+

93 Points - Jeb Dunnuck    The 2017 Chateau Clerc Milon checks in as 60% Cabernet Sauvignon, 23% Merlot, 14% Cabernet Franc, and the rest Petit Verdot and Carmenere brought up in 50% new French oak. It's a much straighter, more focused, serious wine than the Pastourelle and has classic red and black currant fruits as well as medium to full body, a ripe, spicy, textured mid-palate, building tannins, and a great finish. It's another classic, balanced, nicely textured 2017 that's going to evolve well for 3-5 years and keep for two decades.

91 Points - Wilfred Wong of Wine    The 2017 Château Clerc Milon is generous and substantive on the palate. This wine exhibits attractive black aromas and flavors with a hint of dust and earth. Enjoy it with slowly-braised meat dishes.

title: Spottswoode Cabernet Sauvignon 2021
bodyHtml:
The 2021 Spottswoode Cabernet Sauvignon from Napa Valley marks the estate’s 40th anniversary, delivering an elegant, complex, and finely balanced expression. This vintage features 87% Cabernet Sauvignon, blended with 9% Cabernet Franc and 4% Petit Verdot, aged for 20 months in mostly French oak. Known for its purity and vibrant character, the wine offers both immediate appeal and long aging potential.

  • Colour: Deep garnet-purple.
  • Aroma: Rich scents of crème de cassis, mulberries, violets, and pencil shavings, with hints of lilacs and clove.
  • Palate: Layers of blackcurrant, plum, and licorice unfold with notes of gravelly earth and spice.
  • Body: Medium to full-bodied with firm, silky tannins.
  • Finish: Long and elegant, with lingering floral, mineral, and baking spice notes.

Accolades:

  • 99 Points - The Wine Independent
  • 99 Points - James Suckling
  • 98+ Points - Wine Advocate
  • 98+ Points - Jeb Dunnuck
  • 97 Points - Vinous
  • 97 Points - Wine Spectator

This vintage, praised for its finesse and structure, will develop beautifully over the next few decades. While approachable with a 90-120 minute decant now, it will reward patience, offering optimal drinking from 2027 and beyond. This wine pairs exceptionally well with rich meats and hearty dishes, showcasing Napa Valley's best qualities.

title: Silver Oak Alexander Valley Cabernet Sauvignon 2020 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
Produced in the United States, this Cabernet Sauvignon hails from the Alexander Valley in Sonoma County. Founded in 1972, Silver Oak is dedicated to crafting exceptional Cabernet Sauvignon aged exclusively in American oak, a philosophy supported by their ownership of a private cooperage to ensure total quality control. The winery is renowned for its focus on sustainable viticulture and its commitment to creating wines that are both approachable upon release and capable of long term cellaring.

Wine Description

This wine displays a deep ruby hue with vibrant garnet reflections. The aromatic profile is complex and inviting, featuring notes of blackberry bramble, red cherry, and raspberry layered with cedar, vanilla, and sage. On the palate, it is medium to full bodied and elegantly opulent, offering flavors of blackcurrant, plum, and cocoa balanced by a refined acidity. The finish is long and harmonious, characterized by polished, silky tannins and a hint of sweet spice.

Accolades

  • Wine Enthusiast - 94 points

  • James Suckling - 94 points

  • Decanter - 95 points

Food Pairing

The wine’s robust fruit and refined structure make it an excellent companion for grilled ribeye with chimichurri, roasted lamb with herbs, or mushroom risotto with thyme. It also pairs beautifully with hearty stews and aged cow's milk cheeses.

title: Castiglion del Bosco Brunello di Montalcino 2019
bodyHtml:
This Brunello di Montalcino originates from Capanna vineyard, located in the north-west area of Montalcino. The peculiar characteristics of this vineyard, such as the natural isolation along with the altitude and the type of soil, which shows presence of clay shale and marl (Galestro rock), give to this prestigious wine a refined elegance as well as great personality.

The colour is clear and vibrant to the eye. The intense nose plays on floral and herbal hints. In the mouth the tannins are balanced and well integrated, making a pleasant wine with enjoyable peaks of freshness. On the finish a clean and harmonious aftertaste.

96 Points -  James Suckling 

This is really fine on the palate, with wonderfully integrated tannins that give tension and focus. It’s medium-bodied with lovely berry, cherry, cedar and spice. Peaches and flower stems, too. Creamy texture. Extremely long and vivid. Structured, but showing beautiful drinkability with wonderful balance and form. One to drink or hold.

title: Bouchard Pere & Fils Corton Charlemagne 2022
bodyHtml:
Introduction

The Corton-Charlemagne is a prestigious Grand Cru produced from estate-owned vines (Domaine) located at the very top of the hill of Corton, specifically in a 3.65-hectare plot directly below the forest where the soil is characterized by yellow marl and limestone pebbles.

Wine Description

The 2022 vintage is recognized as a powerful and substantial expression that successfully reflects a warm growing season while maintaining remarkable fresh acidity and mineral tension.

  • Varietal Composition: 100% Chardonnay.

  • Aromatic Profile: The nose is spectacularly complex, featuring notes of rose hips, ripe peach, and yellow plums. These are interwoven with refined scents of toasted almonds, rising bread dough, and the "gunflint" or stony minerality typical of the appellation.

  • Palate and Body: This is a full-bodied and multidimensional wine. It offers an ample, "fat" texture on the mid-palate with flavors of lemon curd, apricot, and pastry. The warmth of the summer is evident in subtle tropical hints of mango or pineapple, which are perfectly balanced by a silver bead of acidity.

  • Structure: The attack is tense and precise, leading to a long, vibrant finish. It is noted for its "remarkable mineral salinity" and a texture that feels both creamy and chiselled.

  • Winemaking and Aging: The grapes are organically grown and hand-harvested. After a meticulous sorting and whole-bunch pressing, the wine is aged for 16 to 20 months in French oak casks (approximately 25% to 30% new oak), with the final few months spent in large foudres to harmonize the blend.

  • ABV: Typically 13.5% to 14%.

  • Optimal Drinking Window: While accessible in its youth after decanting, this is a legendary white wine built for the long term. It is best enjoyed from 2025 or 2026, with the potential to evolve gracefully for 15 to 20 years (through 2042+).

Accolades

The 2022 vintage has received elite scores from major wine critics:

Professional Ratings

97 Points - James Suckling: The nose of this very beautiful Corton-Charlemagne transports me to an Alpine meadow, when all the wild flowers are blossoming. I love the restrained, citrusy richness that is effortlessly interwoven with the stony minerality on the medium- to full-bodied palate of this graceful, yet highly-structured wine. Still quite tight at the very salty finish, but so much to give. From a 3.65 hectare plot at the very top of the hill of Corton, directly below the forest with a yellow mark soil. From organically grown grapes. Drinkable now, but best from 2025.

94 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate: Aromas of pear, green apple, white flowers and wet stones introduce the 2022 Corton-Charlemagne Grand Cru, a deep, medium to full-bodied wine that's taut, chiseled and racy, with excellent depth at the core and an abundance of chalky structuring extract. As usual, it derives from the domaine's holdings on the Ladoix side. Barrel Sample: 93-94

94 Points - Wine Spectator: A creamy style, boasting lemon curd, peach and pastry aromas and flavors. Builds to a crescendo midpalate before turning more focused on the lemon-, mineral- and spice-tinged finish. Multidimensional and long.

title: Albert Brenot Nuits St Georges 'Les Murgers' Premier Cru 2020
bodyHtml:
Founded in 1849 by Albert Brenot in Savigny-lès-Beaune, Doudet-Naudin is one of the oldest Burgundy wine Maisons. In 1933 it was acquired by the Doudet family, who have developed and expanded the Maison while preserving its fundamental values: respect for traditions and excellence. Christophe Rochet, the current head of Doudet-Naudin, is committed to maintaining the values of this well-respected Maison while restructuring it.

The color is deep, a bright ruby. The nose is of great finesse. We find notes of red fruits and spices. The palate is fresh and in his youth sits on a beautiful fruit (cherry, blackcurrant and kirsch) with a lovely elegance. This wine, very feminine, is highlighted by the finesse and elegance of the tannins that advertise great potential to keep.

title: Vega Sicilia Unico 2012 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
Few wines have a history as distinguished as that of Vega Sicilia. Founded in the 1860’s, its reputation on its flagship vintage has for more than 100 years produced two great wines, each appropriately named "Unico."

Today, the market for Vega Sicilia is one of scarcity and increasing demand. Vega Sicilia’s growing fame and desirability is testament not only to the estate’s enduring legacy but to the world’s craving for wines of history and noble bearing.

Unico Tinto is concentrated, juicy, silky, and well-defined. Notable characteristics included the healthiness, the strong coloring, and very ripe tannins suitable for ageing. An excellent vintage.

97 Points - James Suckling

Berry, smoke, violet and sandalwood aromas follow through to a full, layered palate that shows super polished tannins that are caressing and long. It’s tight and very long.

96 Points - Wine Spectator

This is at once fresh and elegant on first impression, with lovely hints of fragrant Turkish bazaar spices, game and dried mint lacing the crème de cassis, violet, and black and red licorice notes. But gliding across the palate, buoyed by fresh acidity and sculpted tannins, this expands to show deep notes of tarry smoke, fig cake, espresso and iron alongside the appealing fruit and spice. Long and creamy, offering both power and grace.

96 Points - Wine & Spirits

There’s a delicate side to this wine from a dry season, with floral notes of violets and honey, touches of capsicum spice in the tannins and plenty of bold, luscious fruit to draw your attention. It leaves a lasting impression of the textural grace of spicy old-vine tempranillo—a fascinating sensation of refined power, rooted in earthy depths that will reward long aging.

95 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

95 Points - Decanter

title: Chateau Ducru Beaucaillou 2016
bodyHtml:
100 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

The 2016 Château Ducru-Beaucaillou is a legendary wine from the genius of Bruno Borie, who has managed this estate brilliantly since he arrived in 2003. A blend of 85% Cabernet Sauvignon and 15% Merlot brought up all in new oak, the 2016 has a mammoth bouquet of crème de cassis, espresso, camphor, crushed violets, toasty oak, and graphite. Full-bodied, concentrated, and backward on the palate, it has perfectly integrated acidity and building tannins, a robust, layered texture, off-the-charts purity of fruit, and a finish that won't quit. Give this powerful, concentrated wine a solid 7-8 years of bottle age and enjoy it over the following 50 years or more.

99 Points - James Suckling

Super perfumed, attractive violets with a thread of fresh blueberries, cassis, blackberries and dark plums, delivering a very enticing impression. Beautiful ripeness here. The tannins are perfectly ripe, and layers meld into each other, carrying deep, graceful, plush, velvety dark fruit long into the vibrant, seductive, chocolate-laced finish. Great potential. Try from 2024.

98+ Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Very deep purple-black in colour, the 2016 Ducru-Beaucaillou delivers a pronounced, enticing nose of baked plums, blueberry preserves, fruitcake and boysenberry with suggestions of lilacs mocha, hoisin and exotic spices, plus a waft of cedar chest. Full-bodied, rich and opulent in the mouth, the palate has layer upon layer of black fruit preserves and spicy nuances, matched by a very firm, grainy frame, finishing with epic length and depth.

98 Points - Wine Enthusiast

This wine conveys density, but its richness is sublimated by the complex structure and beautiful ripe fruit. Its power comes from the structure as much as the fruit, promising a wine with an immensely long life ahead of it. Drink from 2025.

title: Pavillon Rouge du Chateau Margaux 2019
bodyHtml:
The grapes used to produce the Pavillon Rouge 2019 were carefully selected and represent only 27% of the harvest. The wine has body with a soft tannin structure and is remarkably balanced on the palate. It would probably have formed an integral part of the assemblage of our Grands Vins two decades ago. In our vineyards and cellars, we make the same painstaking effort to produce the batches used for the Pavillon Rouge as we do for our Grand Vin. Both wines undoubtedly have the same style and some of the same aromas. One almost indefinable detail is sometimes missing, which means the batch is not included in the composition of the Grand Vin.

Blend: 76% Cabernet Sauvignon, 19% Merlot, 3% Petit Verdot, 2% Cabernet Franc

96+ Points - James Suckling

Succulent and gorgeous with such supple tannins, it's full-bodied and rich. It's very savoury, too. Dense yet polished on the palate, showing fresh, minerally and salty notes. You want to drink it already. 27% of the crop and a blend of 76% cabernet sauvignon and 19% merlot, the rest Petit Verdot and Cabernet Franc.

title: Chateau d'Armailhac 2021
bodyHtml:
Chateau d'Armailhac is an esteemed Fifth Growth estate located in the prestigious Pauillac appellation of Bordeaux. Formerly known as Mouton d’Armailhacq, the château was acquired by Baron Philippe de Rothschild in 1933 and remains under the ownership of the Rothschild family. With a history dating back to the 18th century, the estate plays a vital role in the Rothschild wine legacy, embodying a tradition of excellence and innovation.

Wine Description
This vintage displays a deep garnet hue with violet reflections. The bouquet opens with expressive aromas of ripe blackcurrant, blackberry, and dark cherry, interwoven with notes of cedar, tobacco leaf, and graphite. On the palate, it is full-bodied and structured, showing silky yet firm tannins and a fresh, elegant acidity. Flavours of cassis, plum, and mocha evolve into hints of pencil shavings and crushed stone, culminating in a long, precise finish.
Composed predominantly of Cabernet Sauvignon with Merlot, Cabernet Franc, and Petit Verdot, this wine offers superb ageing potential and will evolve beautifully over the next 15–20 years. It balances youthful vibrancy with the promise of graceful maturity.

Accolades
● Wine Advocate – 92–94 points
● Vinous – 91–93 points
● James Suckling – 94–95 points

Food Pairing
Ideal with grilled lamb chops, beef tenderloin with a red wine reduction, or aged hard cheeses such as Comté or Manchego. This pairing highlights the wine’s depth and character.

title: Chateau Haut Batailley 2022
bodyHtml:
Château Haut Batailley is a Fifth Growth estate located in the esteemed Pauillac appellation of Bordeaux. With roots dating back to the 19th century, the property was separated from Château Batailley in 1942 and has flourished under the Cazes family since 2017. Known for its refined style and meticulous vineyard management, Haut Batailley represents a balance of tradition and innovation in Pauillac winemaking.

Wine Description
This 2022 vintage presents a deep garnet-purple hue with striking aromatic intensity. The bouquet unfolds with notes of cassis, black cherry, and blackberry pie, complemented by hints of clove oil, lilac, and crushed stone. On the palate, it delivers flavours of ripe blackcurrant, tobacco leaf, melted chocolate, and espresso, underscored by iron-tinged minerality and floral elegance. Medium to full-bodied, the wine shows a firm yet polished tannic structure, balanced by freshness and a long, mineral-laced finish.

Accolades
Jeb Dunnuck – 94+ points.

James Suckling – 94+ points.

Decanter – 93 points.

Vinous – 93+ points.

Wine Advocate – 91+ points.

Food Pairing
Ideal with roasted lamb, grilled ribeye steak, or mushroom risotto.

title: Borgogno Barolo Cannubi 2018
bodyHtml:
The Borgogno Barolo Cannubi stands out as a symbol of Nebbiolo, hailing from the renowned Cannubi Vineyard in the heart of Barolo. This noble wine rises in complexity and elegance, a living tribute to the exclusive terroir from which it originates. Positioned between 290 and 320 meters in altitude, facing south to optimally embrace the sun, the vineyard benefits from a soil rich in calcareous and clay marls with sandy nuances, creating the ideal habitat for Nebbiolo and thus defining the distinctive character of the wine.

The vinification process follows a respectful and traditional path, with spontaneous fermentation in concrete tanks using indigenous yeasts and carefully monitored temperatures to preserve the integrity of the grape. This is followed by an extended maceration, which enhances depth and texture. The wine's elegance matures through refinement in Slavonian oak barrels for two years and eight months, further perfected in concrete before bottling and then in the bottle for six months before release, culminating in a wine of rare complexity and velvety softness.

The Cannubi's bouquet weaves a captivating plot of red fruits, spices, and an ethereal floral nature of roses and violets, emitting a welcoming and seductive scent. The taste reveals a choreography of juicy fruits and fine spices, progressing towards a long and elegant finale, embellished with soft and harmonious tannins. This Barolo's fame rests on the supreme balance between vigor and grace, a true manifestation of the soul of its historic cru.

The versatility of the Barolo Cannubi makes it an ideal companion to a wide selection of robust dishes of red meat or game but also hard texture cheeses. Capable of masterfully accompanying Piedmontese meats, it also splendidly adapts to recipes from various international traditions, enhancing every meal with its distinguished presence, whether it involves complex preparations or simple dishes.

title: Screaming Eagle 'The Flight' 2019
bodyHtml:
This red wine originates from the United States, specifically from the Oakville subregion of the Napa Valley in California. Screaming Eagle was founded in 1986 by real estate agent Jean Phillips, who purchased a 57 acre vineyard and was encouraged by Robert Mondavi to produce her own wine. Now under the sole ownership of Stanley Kroenke, the estate is arguably the most famous cult winery in North America, with a winemaking philosophy led by Nick Gislason that focuses on the energy and confident delicacy of the fruit.

Wine Description

Screaming Eagle 'The Flight' 2019 is a dark, powerful, and brooding red blend with a deep ruby or purplish hue. The nose is extraordinarily aromatic and floral, featuring intense scents of violets, lavender, and crushed flowers layered over a core of red cherries, raspberries, and black olives. On the palate, the wine is medium to full bodied with a virile and explosive character, showing off its arresting beauty through waves of graphite, black cherry, and plum. It is characterized by its remarkable finesse, vibrancy, and firm, fine grained tannins that run the length of the wine, leading to a long finish with a greenish undertone of spearmint and green tea. This blend consists of 65% Merlot, 30% Cabernet Sauvignon, and 5% Cabernet Franc, with an ABV of 14.7%. While not certified organic, the estate's vineyard management is held to the highest standards. The optimal drinking window for this vintage is from 2028 through 2050.

Accolades

  • James Suckling - 99 points.

  • Vinous - 97 points.

  • Jeb Dunnuck - 94 points.

  • Wine Transit - 100 points.

Food Pairing

The structured tannins and elegant profile of this Merlot based blend make it a natural partner for high quality meats and savory vegetarian dishes. It pairs perfectly with roasted lamb seasoned with rosemary and thyme, grilled ribeye steak, or a classic beef tenderloin with a red wine reduction. Its floral and mineral undertones also complement mushroom risotto, hearty pasta dishes with rich sauces, and aged hard cheeses like Gouda or aged cheddar.

Vintage Quality

The 2019 vintage in Napa Valley is considered exceptional, characterized by a steady growing season that produced velvety wines with great balance and concentration. Conditions included a wet spring and a warm summer with few extreme heat events, allowing the fruit to achieve ideal ripeness with low yields and small berries that contribute to the wine's impressive density.

title: Chateau Ducru Beaucaillou 2018
bodyHtml:
100 Points - Wine Enthusiast

The 2018 vintage was generous to the style of Ducru-Beaucaillou. The rich character of wines from this estate is enhanced by the ripeness and concentration of its wine. At the same time, it keeps a fantastic freshness from the acidity. This wine will go down in the annals of this historic estate, and it is not likely to approach drinkability before 2028. 

99 Points - James Suckling

Aromas of blackberries, blackcurrants, new leather and bark follow through to a full body with a dense, deep palate that goes on and on but is still shy and reserved. A large amount of ultra-fine, cashmere-like tannins that are silky, sleek and wonderfully integrated. Extremely long and focused. It needs at least four to five years to start opening—a beautiful wine for the cellar. Try after 2027. 

96+ Points - Wine Spectator

It is brimming with nearly exotic blackberry, plum, blueberry and acaí berry reduction notes, bristling with brambly energy and racing through a graphite-edged finish. Shows gorgeous perfume throughout, despite the reasonably obvious level of concentration.

98 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

The Grand Vin 2018 Chateau Ducru-Beaucaillou checks in as 85% Cabernet Sauvignon and 15% Merlot that was harvested at the end of September through October 10 and aged in new French oak. This is a gorgeous, incredibly complete, classic expression of this terroir, offering a heavenly nose of creme de cassis, cedar wood, unsmoked tobacco, new leather, spring flowers, chocolate, and a touch of chalky minerality. It's one of the vintage's most concentrated, impressive wines with full-bodied richness, a monster of a mid-palate, remarkable pure, and an excellent finish. It might also be one of the longest-lived. It reminds me of an improved version of the 1996 or a hypothetical mix of the 2010 and 2016.

98 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2018 Ducru-Beaucaillou is composed of 85% Cabernet Sauvignon and 15% Merlot, aged 18 months in 100% new barriques. Deep purple-black coloured, it has a powerful nose of baked black cherries, blackberry preserves and creme de cassis with nuances of menthol, pencil lead, cedar chest and Indian spices, plus fragrant wafts of violets and licorice emerging after a few minutes. Medium to full-bodied, the palate bursts with impactful black fruits and exotic spices layers, supported by firm, ripe grainy tannins and bags of freshness, finishing on a lingering fragrant earth note. There is a brightness to the wine, surprising freshness, yet it remains vibrant and hedonic, presenting an extraordinary vinous paradox that will blow away fans of this great estate.

title: Domaine Des Beaumont Chambolle Musigny 'Les Chardannes' 2020
bodyHtml:
The origin of the wine-growing activity in the Beaumont family goes back more than seven generations. Today installed in the 3 communes of Morey-Saint-Denis – headquarters of the exploitation – Gevrey-Chambertin and Chambolle-Musigny, the 6 ha vineyard, almost exclusively planted with Pinot Noir cultivated in sustainable viticulture, covers very beautiful plots in Grand Cru (Charmes-Chambertin, Mazoyeres-Chambertin) and 1er Cru (Chambolle-Musigny “Les Chabiots”, Gevrey-Chambertin 1er Cru “Les Combottes”…). Thierry Beaumont is passionate, he is a key figure in the Cote de Nuits, tourist plane pilot and fine hunter...                                       

This Chambolle-Musigny from Domaine des Beaumont releases a pretty fruit with aromas of small red fruits. Very fresh on the palate, it evolves on finesse rather than power. Then, it lets express a wise woodiness and already well softened tannins, a guarantee that it can be appreciated in its youth. The fruit is there, which provides intense pleasure and lasts a long time in the palate.

title: Bruno Giacosa Barolo Vigna Le Rocche Falletto 2019 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
One of the legendary winemakers of the world, Bruno Giacosa crafted the most prestigious single-vineyard Barolo and Barbaresco wines during a career that spanned nearly eight decades. He joined the family business at the age of 15, representing the third generation of his Langhe winemaking family. Giacosa’s unfailing pursuit of perfection, his unrivalled palate and his intimate knowledge of vineyards in the Langhe quickly drew recognition and helped establish Piedmont as a leading wine region.

Intense red garnet color. The bouquet is intense and elegant, with floral notes such as rose and fruity notes of blackcurrants, pomegranate and raspberries. On the palate it is structured with excellent tannic plot that enhances roundness and persistence.

98 Points - James Suckling

Gorgeous aromas of roses that fill the glass along with ripe strawberries, raspberries and forest fruits. Very structured and right with finely toned tannins that are tight, sleek and racy.

96+ Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

With the white label, the 2019 Barolo Falletto Vigna Le Rocche is a generous and expansive wine that hits the palate from all sides. It offers lingering sensations of sweet fruit with a good amount of intensity and muscle power pushing from behind. That forward momentum is fueled by dark fruit, rusty earth, wet clay and blood orange. It shows elegance, substance and finely tuned tones with considerable tension and tightness.

95 Points - Wine Spectator

This round, rich red is laced with cherry, raspberry, iron, earth and underbrush aromas and flavors. There's a firm structure, with burly yet well-integrated tannins providing support and the ability to age. Overall, this is balanced and long, with a persistent aftertaste of fruit, mineral and savory notes.

title: Opus One 2019 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
The Opus One originates from the Oakville AVA in California’s Napa Valley, United States. This iconic estate was born from a historic 1970s collaboration between Baron Philippe de Rothschild of Château Mouton Rothschild and Robert Mondavi, who sought to create a singular wine of uncompromising quality.

Wine Description

This deep garnet-purple wine offers intense aromas of black plum, blueberry, and blackcurrant, layered with dried rose petals, violet, and mineral undertones. The palate is full-bodied and jam-packed with juicy black and blue fruits, framed by a creamy, satiny texture and fine-grained tannins. Stylistically, it demonstrates a subtle tension between its fresh acidity and complex notes of savory herbs, espresso, and cocoa, leading to a lingering finish of delicate dark chocolate bitterness.

Accolades

99 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate:

Winemaker Michael Silacci commented that usually the blends are finished in January or February after the vintage. This year, with the 2019s, he was still tweaking the blend, but he did mention that this is "pretty close to the final blend." Deep garnet-purple in color, the 2019 Opus One leaps from the glass with notes of Black Forest cake, Morello cherries, mulberries and fresh blackcurrants plus hints of licorice, wilted roses, Sichuan pepper and iron ore. Full-bodied, the palate is jam-packed with juicy black, blue and red fruits, framed by velvety tannins and background freshness, finishing on a compelling earthy/mineral note. Tasted as a barrel sample, this is a truly magnificent Opus One in the making!
Barrel Sample: 97-99

Food Pairing

The structured elegance of this vintage makes it a superb companion for grilled meats such as prime rib, roasted lamb with rosemary, or venison. It also pairs beautifully with earthy dishes like mushroom risotto, aged cheeses, or hearty braised beef stews.

title: Produttori del Barbaresco - Barbaresco 'Paje' Riserva 2020
bodyHtml:
This red wine originates from Italy, specifically from the Barbaresco region in the Piedmont subregion. Produttori del Barbaresco was formed in 1958 by a local priest and small-scale growers after a previous cooperative founded in 1894 was closed under fascism. It currently unites more than 50 family vineyards to produce wines known for their honesty, consistency, and transparent expression of terroir. The winery's philosophy emphasizes traditional methods, utilizing an 18 to 21-day primary fermentation and aging for up to three years in large oak barrels to showcase the region's finest single-vineyard sites.

Wine Description

The Produttori del Barbaresco Barbaresco Paje Riserva 2020 displays a deep ruby to garnet red colour. The nose is intense and aromatic, offering enticing scents of red cherry, raspberry, blood orange, and floral notes of rose and violet, layered with balsamic and spicy hints of white pepper and eucalyptus. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied and supple, delivering flavours of dark berries, strawberry compote, and wild herbs integrated with a firm, dense matrix of tannins. It is characterized by its vertical structure, lively acidity, and a long, persistent finish that reveals salty and mineral undertones. This 100% Nebbiolo has an ABV of 14.5% and was aged for 30 months in large oak barrels followed by nine months in the bottle. The wine is not certified organic, and its optimal drinking window is estimated from 2025 through 2045.

Accolades

  • Vinous - 95 points.

  • Wine Spectator - 94 points.

  • Wine Advocate - 93 points.

  • Jeb Dunnuck - 96 Points.

Food Pairing

The powerful structure and complex fruit profile of this Riserva make it an ideal partner for substantial and flavourful dishes. It pairs beautifully with fresh egg-pasta dishes, mushroom risottos, and roasted red meats such as rack of lamb or osso bucco. Its savoury and spicy undertones also complement game birds, porcini mushrooms, and aged, full-flavoured cheeses like sharp cheddar or Parmesan.

Vintage Quality

The 2020 vintage in Barbaresco is regarded as a ripe and intense season that produced wines with great transparency and approachable tannins. Despite a warm growing season, the harvest yielded fruit with exceptional balance and aromatic precision, allowing winemakers to craft wines that are expressive in their youth yet possess significant aging potential.

title: Eisele Vineyard Syrah 2015
bodyHtml:
Eisele Vineyard is the new name of the former Araujo Estate, one of Napa Valley’s most heralded producers. Araujo was owned and operated by Daphne and Bart Araujo from 1990 through 2013, when they sold it to the Artemis Group, a French company that owns Château Latour and other estates in Bordeaux, Burgundy and the Rhone Valley. The Artemis Group is owned by financier and industrialist Francois Pinault and his family. By acquiring the Napa estate, the Artemis Group now owns one of the greatest terroirs in California. The 38-acre estate has been a premier vineyard since the late 19th century, and for much off the 20th century it was a source of top-quality grapes for such producers as Ridge, Conn Creek and Joseph Phelps.

The Araujo Estate Cabernet Sauvignon became one of the legendary cult Cabs of the 1990s and it has maintained its reputation as one of Napa’s first growth Cabernet Sauvignons. The estate is organic and is certified biodynamic. Francoise Peschon was Araujo’s winemaker for 14 years, and she is now Eisele’s consulting winemaker. Hélène Mingot is Technical Director of Winemaking and Winegrowing. Under French ownership, the estate continues to impress. Robert Parker Jr. wrote in late 2016 that a tasting of recent Eisele wines indicated that the change in ownership “is proceeding brilliantly….so the greatness from this fabulous terroir continues unabated.”

The 2015 vintage is exotic and spicy. The nose reveals aromas of cured meat with a savory character recalling middle eastern spices. It opens up with summer fruit: strawberry, peach flower, greengage plums. The attack is supple and silky with velvety tannins and layered ripe fruits sustained by a hint of cinnamon and vanilla, bringing delicious complexity. 

94 Points - Wine Spectator     Rich, polished and densely complex, with expressive blackberry, bay leaf and smoky pepper flavors that take on intensity toward refined tannins.

94 Points - James Suckling     Spice and blackberry aromas with hints of smoked meat. Graphite and leaves. Autumnal. Full-bodied and round with a juicy mouthfeel. Round tannins and a savory finish.

title: Bouchard Pere & Fils Clos De La Mousse Premier Cru 2022
bodyHtml:
The history of 'Clos de la Mousse' is ancient, with the oldest trace dating back to 1220. At that time, it was bequeathed to the chapter of Notre-Dame de Beaune. The vineyard was fragmented during the French Revolution, but the Bouchard family, driven by the desire to build an exceptional estate since their founding in 1731, gradually reassembled the entire plot in the 19th century, with the final acquisition occurring in 1872. Bouchard Père & Fils' winemaking philosophy is guided by their cellar master's motto of 'no rules,' preferring to adapt to each terroir and vintage to coax out the purest expression and finest emotions.

Wine Description

This Premier Cru is made exclusively from the Pinot Noir grape variety. It displays a superb, deep, and bright red colour with brilliant highlights.

On the nose, it conveys a powerful expression of red fruit—mellow yet jammy, fresh yet very ripe—combined with fruit aromas and subtle toasted notes. The palate offers a fleshy and delicate attack that is particularly charming. It is both fleshy and refined, revealing its charms with delicacy. The tannins are present yet refined, expressing the high maturity of the plot. The complex finish is a revelation, with a resurgence of wild fruit aromas, smoothness, and a saline quality that imparts a crisp, fresh impression. The long ageing potential is notable, generally ranging from 7 to 10 years and more.

93 Points - Wine Spectator: This aromatic red evokes sandalwood, juniper, tomato leaf, incense and ripe cherry and currant flavors. Lithe and linear, with a firm line of acidity and tannins driving the persistent finish. Shows lovely harmony and a gossamer texture. Drink now through 2040.

title: Castiglion del Bosco Brunello di Montalcino 2006
bodyHtml: Plush and softly textured, this modern expression of Brunello boasts generous tones of black fruit, cherry, tobacco, leather and cola with smooth, silky tannins. You could age this wine many more years, or drink it sooner thanks to the inherent softness here.

title: Masi Amarone Della Valpolicella Campolongo Di Torbe 2013
bodyHtml: It has vibrant aromas of plum and cherry jam, then a minty hint that turns to deeper notes of chocolate and spices. The palate is dense, taut, and rich, with velvety tannins, topped off by a gratifying finish.

title: Henschke Shiraz Mount Edelstone 2018
bodyHtml:
This iconic wine originates from Australia, specifically the Eden Valley region within South Australia. The Henschke family's winemaking tradition spans six generations, beginning when Johann Christian Henschke emigrated from Germany and settled in the Eden Valley in the mid-19th century. The Mount Edelstone vineyard, planted exclusively to Shiraz in 1912, is one of the country's oldest single-vineyard Shiraz sites, with the first single-vineyard bottling occurring in 1952. Viticulturist Prue Henschke manages the ancient, dry-farmed, ungrafted vines using organic and biodynamic practices, highlighting the family's philosophy of minimal intervention and deep respect for the land.

Wine Description

The Henschke Mount Edelstone Shiraz typically presents a deep crimson to medium garnet colour with purple hues. The wine offers intense aromas of dark fruits, such as blackberry, blackcurrant, blueberry, and plum, layered with lifted herbal and savoury notes of sage, bay leaf, black pepper, and anise. On the palate, it is concentrated yet graceful, displaying rich fruit flavours like blackberry, mulberry, and red plum, underscored by savoury complexity and hints of cured meat, olive, and mint. This wine has a full body, with fine-grained, velvety tannins and vibrant acidity that provides structure for long ageing. It carries through to a long, persistent, almost endless finish. The varietal composition is 100% Shiraz. The wine's alcohol by volume (ABV) is approximately 14.5%. The vineyard uses organic and biodynamic practices. The optimal drinking window can extend for thirty years or more, depending on the vintage.

Accolades

98 Points – Decanter: They call it a "gem of an old-vine wine" and an "opulent, complex wine." Most tellingly, the reviewer noted that over several days of continuous tasting, they preferred the 2018 Mount Edelstone to Hill of Grace. It boasts a seductive, supple mouthfeel interwoven with trademark savory bay leaf, sage, and peppercorn, grounded by velvety tannins built for decades of cellaring.

97+ Points – Robert Parker’s Wine Advocate: The 2018 Mount Edelstone Vineyard Shiraz is inky and powerful, sweetly fruited and bright. The tannins are almost lost in the abundance of the plush fruit power. This is an impressive wine, one that shows a splay of savory tannins and looks just as fresh as the day I tasted it. If anything, it is more impressive today—it feels as if it has not moved in the eight years since its harvest. This is excellent. It has a pH of 3.54, 6.47 grams per liter of total acidity and 14.5% alcohol.

title: Pavillon Rouge du Chateau Margaux 2010
bodyHtml:
Chateau Margaux, a Premier Grand Cru Classe Bordeaux, is one of the most famous wines in the world. Care has been lavished on the property by a line of owners with an abiding concern for the reputation of the estate.

For more than five hundred years, season after season, generations of vineyard-workers, grapeharvesters, cellar-workers, coopers and many other craftsmen have all played a part in making Chateau Margaux what it is today: a wine with an incomparable personality, reflected in the elegant Palladian building which adorns its label.

96 Points - James Suckling

This the greatest Pavillon Rouge ever made. Aromas of flowers, smoke, currants and raspberries follow through to a full body, with super silky tannins and a long, long finish. This is balanced and refined with wonderful depth. Hard to believe it's a second wine. Better after 2018.

94 Points - Wine Spectator

This is lovely, with a powerful backdrop of graphite and tar, harnessed by flavors of velvety plum, steeped fig and black currant preserves. The long incense- and black tea-filled finish completes the seduction. Refined, defined and poised. Best from 2014 through 2025.

94 Points - Wine Enthusiast

Dense and structured, this second wine from Château Margaux is magnificent. There are hints of bitter chocolate, along with tarry fruit. It is very textured, just hinting at extraction. The tannins are rounded and velvet-like in character. It's a wine for medium-term aging.

91+ Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Deep garnet in color, the 2010 Pavillon Rouge du Chateau Margaux offers up scents of blackcurrant cordial, wild thyme and fertile loam with hints of cedar chest, pencil lead and tar. Medium-bodied, the palate is just a tad lean with chewy tannins and bold freshness, finishing on an herbal note.

title: Bruno Giacosa Barolo del Falletto Vigna Le Rocche Riserva 2017
bodyHtml:
One of the legendary winemakers of the world, Bruno Giacosa crafted the most prestigious single-vineyard Barolo and Barbaresco wines during a career that spanned nearly eight decades. He joined the family business at the age of 15, representing the third generation of his Langhe winemaking family. Giacosa’s unfailing pursuit of perfection, his unrivalled palate and his intimate knowledge of vineyards in the Langhe quickly drew recognition and helped establish Piedmont as a leading wine region.

 His legacy rests with daughter Bruna, who continues to uphold her father’s winemaking philosophy to respect traditional techniques while using the best of modern technology. The goal is for each distinguished site to produce articulate, unique wines. 

 98 Points - James Suckling

 Roses and lavender with other flowers. Peaches. Glorious fruit of dark plums and ripe strawberries. This is dense and intense but there are layers of very fine tannins, like fine cashmere. Goes on for minutes. Opens in the mouth. Almost endless.

title: Dugat Py Gevrey Chambertin Premier Cru 'Les Evocelles' 2023
bodyHtml:
This wine hails from the village of Gevrey Chambertin in the Côte de Nuits region of Burgundy, France. Domaine Dugat Py, established in its current form in 1994, is managed by the family whose winemaking roots in Gevrey date back to the 19th century. Under the stewardship of Loïc Dugat, the estate employs natural, biodynamic practices and horse plowing in its top vineyard sites to produce wines known for their power and refinement.

Wine Description

'Les Evocelles' is a red wine crafted from 100% Pinot Noir sourced from very old vines, often designated as 'Très Vieilles Vignes'. It displays a medium-dark ruby colour that is bright and clear in the glass. The aromatic profile is complex, revealing notes of plum, persimmon, and dried florals interwoven with earthy scents of turned soil, sandalwood, and leather. On the palate, the wine is medium bodied and finely textured, offering a round expression of red fruit accented by dark spice and a distinct mineral depth. Balanced by integrated acidity and silky tannins, it concludes with a long finish featuring notes of fig and incense.

Accolades

  • "Wine Advocate - 91 points."

Food Pairing

This Gevrey Chambertin pairs exceptionally well with roasted red meats, such as a grilled rib steak or roast lamb with rosemary. It also complements small game dishes like roast quail or more rustic fare such as rabbit in a mustard sauce.

title: Vieux Chateau Certan 2022
bodyHtml:
Vieux Château Certan is a historic estate located in the heart of Pomerol on Bordeaux’s Right Bank. Owned by the Thienpont family since 1924, the château is renowned for its exceptional terroir and meticulous winemaking. Alexandre Thienpont, the current winemaker, has upheld the estate’s reputation for crafting elegant, complex wines that age beautifully.

Wine Description
The 2022 vintage of Vieux Château Certan is a blend of 80% Merlot, 20% Cabernet Franc. Deep garnet-purple in colour, it opens with captivating aromas of black cherries, violets, cigar box, and crushed stones. The palate is rich and layered, revealing notes of dark plum, cassis, graphite, and subtle spice, all framed by polished tannins and vibrant acidity. Full-bodied yet refined, the wine exhibits a harmonious balance of power and finesse, with a persistent, mineral-laced finish.

Accolades
● Wine Advocate – 98–100 points.
● Vinous – 96–98 points.
● James Suckling – 97–98 points.
● Decanter – 98 points.
● Jeb Dunnuck – 98–100 points.

Food Pairing
Ideal with dishes such as herb-crusted lamb, mushroom risotto, or duck breast with cherry glaze. The wine’s structure and depth also complement aged cheeses like Comté or Gruyère. Together, they create an unforgettable dining experience.

title: Austin Hope Cabernet Sauvignon Reserve 2022
bodyHtml:
The making of Austin Hope Cabernet Reserve begins with small lot fermentations separated by individual vineyard blocks which receive daily pump-overs for maximum extraction. These lots are constantly supervised, tasted & analyzed for tannin and anthocyanins in order to determine optimal length of extended maceration after fermentation. Once drained and pressed, the young wines are barreled down into a combination of once used and neutral French Oak.

Wine Description

On the nose, fresh blueberry cobbler, burnt sugar, vanilla bean and a touch of earth evolve onto the palate and seamlessly display flavors of coco powder, baking spices with additional silky vanilla. The beautifully integrated tannins frame this robust Cabernet Sauvignon to reveal a luxurious full mouth feel that allows this wine to linger.

title: Poderi Aldo Conterno Barolo Bussia Colonnello 2018
bodyHtml:
The Barolo Bussia Colonnello from Poderi Aldo Conterno is a distinguished expression of Nebbiolo from the esteemed Bussia vineyard in Monforte d'Alba, Piedmont. This wine exemplifies the estate's dedication to traditional winemaking and the unique terroir of the Colonnello sub-cru.

Colour: Deep garnet red with subtle brick hues, indicative of its developing maturity.

Aroma: A complex bouquet featuring notes of red cherries, rose petals, and hints of tar, complemented by nuances of licorice and tobacco.

Palate: Full-bodied and well-structured, offering flavors of ripe red fruits, earthy undertones, and a touch of spice. The tannins are firm yet refined, providing a balanced and elegant mouthfeel.

Body: Medium to full-bodied with a harmonious balance between acidity and tannin structure.

Finish: Long and persistent, with lingering notes of red fruit and a subtle minerality.

title: Biondi Santi Brunello di Montalcino Riserva 2010 - 2nd Release
bodyHtml:
Biondi Santi, situated southeast of Montalcino, is renowned for its pivotal role in the history of Brunello di Montalcino wines. The estate spans 26 hectares, with many vines exceeding 80 years in age. In 1865, Clemente Biondi achieved international acclaim for a wine named Brunello, marking the inception of this esteemed varietal. Today, the family continues its legacy, producing Brunello Annata and Riserva wines celebrated for their elegance and remarkable longevity, often aging gracefully for over a century.

Wine Description

The 2010 Brunello di Montalcino Riserva showcases a clear ruby hue. On the nose, it presents intense aromas of cherry, cranberry, and goji berry. The palate is marked by great tension and juiciness, with well-integrated acidity and fine-meshed tannins, culminating in a finish rich with clear fruit flavors, especially sour cherry.

Accolades

  • Wine Enthusiast – 100 points
  • James Suckling – 97 points
  • Decanter – 96 points​
  • Wine Advocate – 96 points​
  • Vinous – 95 points​
  • Wine Spectator – 95 points​

Food Pairing

This wine pairs exquisitely with rich dishes such as braised short ribs, wild boar ragù, or aged Tuscan pecorino cheese. These pairings enhance the wine's depth and character, creating an unforgettable dining experience.

title: Araujo Estate Red Blend 'Altagracia' 2012
bodyHtml:
Since 1971, some of California's most ageworthy and intensely-flavored Cabernet Sauvignons have been made from grapes grown at the Eisele Vineyard, located on a benchland near the northern end of Napa Valley, just east of Calistoga. Protected by the Palisades Mountains to the north and cooled by westerly breezes from the Chalk Hill Gap, this 38-acre vineyard is planted on warm cobbly soils that produce a low-yielding crop of exceptionally concentrated fruit. 

This Altagracia is a generous wine reflecting the exceptional quality of the vintage. The wine reflects the character of the eastern parcels of the Eisele Vineyard, and its fine-grained tannins provide a perfect foil for the intensity and richnessof the layered fruit.

93 Points - James Suckling

This is a savory and balanced second wine with plums, berries and spices such as cloves and pepper. Full-bodied and velvety with bright acidity underneath and a flavorful finish. They say they used a little press wine in this and it gives a lift to the wine. Lots of currants and hints of pepper. Traditional. 

91+ Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Araujo's second wine, the 2012 Proprietary Red Altagracia exhibits beautiful blueberry, black raspberry and cassis fruit which reflects the purity that frequently comes from this vineyard. The tannins are soft, and the wine is lighter than its bigger sibling, but it possesses medium body, velvety tannin, and a gorgeous mouthfeel.

title: Anakota Cabernet Sauvignon Helena Montana Vineyard 2019
bodyHtml:
Introduction

Anakota Cabernet Sauvignon Helena Montana Vineyard is a prestigious red wine from the Knights Valley AVA in Sonoma County, United States. The Anakota estate was founded in 2001 by the Jackson family and winemaker Pierre Seillan, who sought to find a site that combined the concentration of Napa with the precision and acidity of Sonoma. Seillan employs a proprietary 'micro-cru' winemaking philosophy, dividing the estate vineyards into small, distinct blocks to mirror the intricate patchwork of volcanic soils and microclimates found on the rugged flanks of the Mayacamas Mountain Range.

Wine Description

This wine displays a deep garnet-purple colour in the glass. The sensory profile is characteristically powerful and complex, featuring an aromatic bouquet of ripe black and red currant, plum preserves, and stewed black cherries. These fruit notes are layered with sophisticated hints of mossy tree bark, dried bouquet garni, and fragrant earth, alongside sweet baking spices like toasted clove, cinnamon, and nutmeg. On the palate, it is medium to full bodied with a dense, concentrated core that balances mouth-coating black fruits against vibrant acidity. The finish is very long and balanced, marked by firm, finely grained tannins that provide a compelling lift. Crafted from 100% Cabernet Sauvignon sourced from a steep 60-acre vineyard at 950 feet elevation, the wine has an ABV of 14.5%. While the estate follows meticulous, sustainable vineyard practices, this specific bottling is not certified organic.

Food Pairing

The robust structure and concentrated flavours of this Cabernet Sauvignon make it an ideal partner for rich, savoury dishes.

  • Meats: It pairs excellently with port wine braised beef short ribs, roasted duck breast, or grilled steaks.

  • Classic Dishes: Suggested pairings include simple meatballs or 'minute' rump steak with snails and garlic butter.

  • Hearty Fare: Its firm tannins and acidity also complement dishes with rich dark fruit or herbal elements, such as those featuring dried herbs de Provence or sage.

title: Signorello Chardonnay Hope's Cuvee 2022
bodyHtml:
The Hope’s Cuvee is a single vineyard block wine that has been historically bottled for the last 35 years. The 5-acre parcel of Chardonnay was initially planted in 1980. The fruit is picked in 4 different picks based on vine age, clonal differences and maturity profile. The grapes are sorted, whole-cluster pressed and fermented in oak barrels with native yeast. Based on the lots and the acidity, the wines are further developed through the malolactic process. Sur lie aging with occasional stirring for 8 months in 50% new French oak provides texture and depth with evolution in aromatics. The wine is unfined and unfiltered to preserve the wine’s density and concentration.

Hope’s Cuvee Chardonnay is a gorgeous wine with striking richness and depth. Citrus peel, lemon custard, apricots, honey and subtle floral notes give the wine a complex bouquet. The wine is more generous on the palate with a creamy texture, balanced acidity which is well representative of the opulent vintage. The wine finishes with a saline minerality framed in notes of French oak, hazelnut and spice.

title: Bouchard Pere & Fils Montrachet Grand Cru 2018
bodyHtml:
Bouchard Père & Fils Montrachet Grand Cru 2018 is a monumental white Burgundy from one of the most celebrated vineyard sites in the world.

The estate holds a significant 0.89-hectare parcel of this Grand Cru, situated on the Puligny-Montrachet side of the slope. Bouchard's philosophy for this prestigious bottling focuses on capturing the 'sumptuous and dramatic' power of the terroir while maintaining the legendary precision associated with the house. The wine is vinified with extreme care, often transitioning from barrel to foudre to refine its structure and ensure the oak remains a supporting frame for the intense fruit concentration.

Wine Description

This 2018 Grand Cru presents a clean and pure light colour in the glass. The aromatic profile is expansive and multifaceted, bursting with scents of honeyed peaches, toasted nuts, white flowers, orange oil, and fresh bread. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied, textural, and enveloping with a satiny mouthfeel. It features a 'massive bench' of white fruit and orange zest flavours, balanced by lively acidity and a frame of aromatic, vanilla spicy oak. It is characterized by its incredible poise, masterfully defined structure, and a sublime, persistent finish where subtle nuances continually emerge.

The wine is 100% Chardonnay, sourced from East/South-East facing vines grown in thin, stony soils over limestone. It is hand-harvested and aged for 12 to 13 months in French oak, with up to 100% new oak used depending on the vintage to match the wine's significant extract. This 2018 release has an ABV of 14.5% and is recognized for its immense power and scale.

Accolades

  • 98 Jasper Morris: 'Racked from barrel to foudre. Clean pure light colour. Great tension on the nose, clearly very high class, no detail to speak of, and nor should there be. A massive bench of white fruit, suggests the nose. This completely masters the palate but brilliantly cleanly defined, nothing heavy. Sublime length and now the little nuances do start to appear. Barrel Sample: 95-98'

  • 95 Decanter: 'Bouchard Père have a substantial 0.9ha of the Grand Cru on a slope on the Puligny-Montrachet side. This is certainly at the riper end of the scale in 2018, but the class and poise of the terroir shine through, with orange zest and lemon tart flavours, plenty of extract and concentration and a frame of aromatic, vanilla spicy oak.'

  • 95 Robert Parker's Wine Advocate: 'Sumptuous and dramatic, Bouchard's 2018 Montrachet Grand Cru bursts with aromas of honeyed peaches, toasted nuts, white flowers, orange oil and fresh bread. Full-bodied, textural and enveloping, it's satiny and gourmand, with lively acids and a rich, expansive finish. If this year's Cabotte is more tightly wound and incisive, the Montrachet is irresistible for its power and scale.'

Food Pairing

The extraordinary depth and richness of this Montrachet require equally sophisticated pairings, such as lobster with ginger butter, sea bass in a salt crust, or Bresse poultry in a cream sauce. It is a magnificent match for pan-seared foie gras or scallops with black truffles. For a cheese course, it pairs beautifully with aged, nutty cheeses like a 24-month Comté or a delicate Brillat-Savarin.

Vintage Quality

The 2018 vintage in Burgundy was characterized by a very warm and dry growing season, which resulted in an early harvest and high sugar levels. While the conditions led to a riper style of wine, the best Grand Cru sites like Montrachet were able to translate this warmth into impressive concentration and 'dramatic' scale while retaining the necessary acidity for balance. The vintage is noted for producing generous, accessible white wines with significant mouthfeel and immediate appeal.

title: Chateau Troplong Mondot 2021
bodyHtml:
Chateau Troplong Mondot 2021 is a prestigious red wine from the Saint Emilion region of Bordeaux, France. This historic estate, which dates back to the 17th century, is currently owned by the French insurance group SCOR and managed by Aymeric de Gironde, who has steered the winery toward a philosophy of purity and elegance. Perched at the highest point of the Saint Emilion plateau, the vineyard is celebrated for its unique clay-limestone soils and its commitment to precision winemaking, including the use of organic farming techniques.

Wine Description

The 2021 vintage presents a deep garnet-purple colour and a complex sensory profile. The nose is captivating and fragrant, offering aromas of dark chocolate, pink flowers, and exotic spices mingled with plums, wild berries, and a hint of cedar. On the palate, the wine is medium to full bodied, delivering a vibrant energy with waves of red fruit, tangy strawberry, and black cherry flavours.

Accolades

  • "Vinous - 96 points."

  • "Decanter - 96 points."

  • "Robert Parker Wine Advocate - 95 points."

  • "James Suckling - 95 points."

Food Pairing

This wine is best served with classic meat dishes such as roast beef, grilled lamb, or braised duck. It also complements hearty fish courses like tuna, mushroom-based pasta, and a variety of aged cheeses.

title: Bouchard Pere & Fils Nuits Saint Georges 'Les Cailles' Premier Cru 2021
bodyHtml:
Introduction

This red wine comes from France, specifically the Burgundy region in the Côte de Nuits subregion. The specific vineyard, 'Les Cailles,' is a Premier Cru site located on the southern part of the Nuits-Saint-Georges commune. Bouchard Père & Fils is one of Burgundy’s oldest wine houses, founded in 1731 and is based in Beaune. Its history includes the acquisition of the historic Château de Beaune in 1820, where the cellars beneath the former royal fortress provide ideal conditions for ageing the wine. The winemaking philosophy is centred on expressing the terroir and respecting the vintage.

Wine Description

This Premier Cru is a red wine made entirely from Pinot Noir. It presents a purple colour with black and violet reflections. The bouquet is intense, offering notes of black fruit blended with oaky touches and delicate spice. Other aromatic notes include black cherry and blueberry, along with licorice. On the palate, the wine is full and fleshy, ample, and round, with a medium to full body. It has an elegant structure based on delicate tannins. The wine shows a very good potential for ageing. The optimal drinking window extends to 2045. The ABV is 13.5% or 13%. The wine is produced under the philosophy of Agriculture Raisonnée (sustainable farming), and its grapes are hand-harvested and manually sorted. The source material did not indicate if the wine is organic.

Food Pairing

Suggested pairings for this powerful red wine include game, venison, and meats in sauce. It also pairs well with duck, goose, and other game birds.

title: Tignanello 2001 (by Tenuta Tignanello)
bodyHtml:
Marchesi Antinori has been dedicated to winemaking for over 26 generations, since Giovanni di Piero Antinori joined the Florentine Winemaker's Guild in 1385. The Tenuta Tignanello estate, located in the Chianti Classico area of Tuscany, Italy, is where two of the estate's most prestigious vineyards, Tignanello and Solaia, are found. The Tignanello wine was a pioneer of the 'Super Tuscan' wines and was the first Sangiovese wine to be aged in small oak barrels.

Wine Description

The Tignanello 2001 has a deep ruby-red colour. The wine is a blend of 85% Sangiovese, 10% Cabernet Sauvignon, and 5% Cabernet Franc. The nose offers complex aromas of ripe red fruits, cherries, and plums, with additional notes of vanilla, chocolate, and sweet spices. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied and well-structured, with velvety tannins and a long, persistent finish. The wine's flavour profile includes notes of plum, cassis, sweet herbs, and saddle leather.

Accolades

  • Wine Advocate - 93 points

  • Wine Enthusiast - 93 points

  • Wine Spectator - 91 points

  • Vinous - 92 points

 

Food Pairing

Suggested pairings for this wine are tailored to its flavour profile and structure. The Tignanello 2001 is ideal with rich meat dishes, such as roasts and braised meats. A perfect match to enhance the wine's complexity.

Vintage Quality

The 2001 vintage in Tuscany benefited from an early bud break, followed by warm weather with some showers, which led to a high-quality harvest, especially for the Sangiovese grapes, which were deep in colour and rich in tannins. The Tignanello 2001 vintage is known for its excellent aging potential, displaying depth and structure.

title: Chateau La Conseillante 2021
bodyHtml:
Chateau La Conseillante is situated in the prestigious Pomerol appellation of Bordeaux, France, bordering Saint Emilion. The estate has been under the continuous ownership of the Nicolas family since 1871. Under the direction of winemaker Marielle Cazaux, the winery maintains a philosophy of precision and 'parcellaire' management, utilizing a state-of-the-art circular vat room to preserve the unique expression of its 18 distinct vineyard parcels.

Wine Description

This wine presents a medium to deep garnet-purple colour. The aromatic profile is highly complex, leaping from the glass with scents of black raspberries, mulberries, and wild blueberries, layered with violets, rose petals, and exotic spices. On the palate, the wine is medium-bodied and suave, displaying a velvety texture and a vibrant core of red and blue fruits. It is framed by ultra-refined, silky tannins and a refreshing spine of acidity that leads to a long, perfumed finish with hints of graphite and black truffle.

Accolades

  • "James Suckling - 96 points."

  • "Decanter - 96 points."

  • "Vinous - 96 points."

  • "Wine Advocate - 95 points."

Food Pairing

The elegant structure and vibrant fruit of this Pomerol make it an excellent companion for roasted duck with a light spice rub or herb-crusted rack of lamb. It also pairs beautifully with earthy dishes featuring truffles or cep mushrooms, as well as fine cheeses such as mild goat cheese.

title: Louis Jadot Corton Charlemagne 'Domaine des Heritiers' 2019
Ridge Vineyards Cabernet Sauvignon 2021
bodyHtml:
Inky purple hues with dark plum, black cherry, cedar, cola and sweet toasted oak on the nose. A full-bodied entry with black berry, cocoa powder, brown spices and peppermint on the palate. Layered textures and focused tannins lead to a long finish.  

95+ Points - Jeb Dunnuck
