Pure creme de cassis, leafy tobacco, spring flowers, and graphite are just some of its nuances, and it hits the palate with medium to full-bodied richness, a pure, concentrated, layered mouthfeel, beautiful tannins, and a great finish.

94 Points - James Suckling

Graphite, tobacco, grilled plums, black olives and black cherries are held firmly by velvety tannins on a medium body at 13.3% alcohol. Tense, concentrated, linear and acid-driven while deep in black fruit and subtle oak accents. Grapes grown on Ridge’s Monte Bello property at lower elevations on the slopes.

92+ Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Aromas of blackcurrant, blackberry, cocoa nibs and charred wood lead to a vibrant, satiny palate that is fresh and light on its feet. The finish combines juicy, muddled berry flavors with tense, chocolaty tannins of good length.

92 Points - Wine Spectator

A gutsy, gravelly style, offering black currant and blackberry compote notes lined with charcoal, cast iron and tar accents. Shows good cut and energy, with iron minerality punching through the fruit on the finish.

title: Borgogno Barolo Fossati 2017
bodyHtml: The most historical winery in Barolo, dating back to 1761. The Langa's underground cellars are still a rare historical memory. The wines are still prepared according to tradition: extended spontaneous fermentation in concrete tanks without using chosen yeasts and long aging periods in big Slavonian oak barrels.

title: Biondi Santi Brunello di Montalcino 2017
bodyHtml:
Biondi Santi, established in the 19th century, is credited with creating the Brunello di Montalcino wine. The estate has remained a benchmark for quality and tradition in the region, producing wines renowned for their elegance and longevity. In 2013, Jacopo Biondi Santi, son of Franco Biondi Santi, took over Tenuta Greppo, continuing the family's legacy. ​

Wine Description

The 2017 Brunello di Montalcino showcases a bright garnet red color. On the nose, it opens with notes of tea, delicate nuances of rose petals, cherry, and some raspberry. The palate offers vivid fruit, opening with grippy, firm tannins, fresh acidity, and mineral, accentuated earthy notes on the finish. Composed entirely of Sangiovese Grosso, this wine is expected to evolve gracefully, with an optimal drinking window from 2026 to 2045. ​

Accolades

  • James Suckling: 96 points

  • Wine Advocate: 96 points

  • Wine Spectator: 94 points

Food Pairing

This Brunello pairs excellently with rich dishes such as braised beef, wild boar ragù, and aged pecorino cheese. These pairings highlight the wine's depth and character.​

title: La Rioja Alta Aster Finca El Otero 2019
bodyHtml:
This prestigious and powerful red wine originates from the Ribera del Duero region in Spain. While La Rioja Alta, S.A. is legendary for its Rioja wines, Áster is their dedicated estate in Ribera del Duero, established to produce a modern, "terroir-driven" expression of the Tinta del País (Tempranillo) grape. The Finca El Otero is the estate's flagship "Single Vineyard" bottling, sourced from a unique 7-hectare plot of old vines situated on a dry, erosion-prone hillside with poor soils, which naturally limits yields to produce fruit of extraordinary concentration.

Wine Description

The La Rioja Alta Aster Finca El Otero 2019 presents an intense, deep cherry-red colour with a dark garnet rim. The sensory profile is remarkably complex and "masculine," featuring a powerful nose of blackcurrant, blackberry, and licorice, layered with sophisticated notes of freshly roasted coffee, pastry, and spice. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied and robust, showcasing a "vibrant structure" with powerful yet ripe tannins and a well-integrated acidity. It is characterized by its significant volume and a long, balsamic finish with hints of dark chocolate and mineral-rich earth. This 100% Tinta del País (Tempranillo) has an ABV of 15% and was aged for 16 months in new French oak barrels, with malolactic fermentation also occurring in new oak to enhance its creamy texture.

Vintage Quality

The 2019 vintage in Ribera del Duero is widely regarded as an excellent and powerful year. A relatively dry and warm growing season resulted in small, highly concentrated berries with exceptional phenolic ripeness. Despite the heat, the Finca El Otero vineyard maintained its signature freshness and mineral tension, producing a wine that critics have hailed as one of the best releases in the estate's history. This wine is built for the long haul and is expected to develop beautifully in the cellar for the next 15–20 years.

title: Hundred Acre Cabernet Sauvignon 'Ark Vineyard' 2017
bodyHtml:
Hundred Acre is located in the United States, within California's Napa Valley and the specific subregion of Howell Mountain. Founded in 2000 by Canadian investment banker Jayson Woodbridge, the winery is known for its meticulous, 'berry by berry' harvesting process and a philosophy of complete estate ownership that allows for total creative freedom. Woodbridge, an autodidact in winemaking, manages the estate alongside his wife Helen Mawson, focusing on producing iconic Cabernet Sauvignon from unique volcanic terroirs.

Wine Description

The Cabernet Sauvignon Ark Vineyard presents a deep garnet-black colour, opening with a provocative sensory profile of baked black cherries, plum preserves, and crème de cassis. On the palate, this full bodied wine is rich and spicy, supported by a rock-solid backbone of grainy tannins and lively acidity that leads to a long, exotic finish. Composed of 100% Cabernet Sauvignon, it displays complex notes of black truffles, Chinese five spice, and earthy forest floor.

Accolades

  • "Wine Advocate - 98 points."

  • "Jeb Dunnuck - 99 points."

Food Pairing

This bold and structured Cabernet Sauvignon pairs exceptionally well with premium cuts of steak, rich game dishes such as venison, or artisan cheeses. The wine's intense fruit and spicy undertones complement the savoury depth of slow-roasted meats.

title: Domaines des Perdrix Vosne Romanee 2018
bodyHtml: Seductive spice notes, refined pure black and red fruit. ZYN likes the texture here, together with the powerful, sappy and unbelievable length! This is actually approachable now though it should age for at least two decades on the incredible balance it has.

title: Pio Cesare Barolo 2020
bodyHtml:
Introduction

Pio Cesare Barolo 2020 is produced in the Piedmont region of Italy, specifically sourced from family-owned vineyards across five different villages: Serralunga d'Alba, Monforte d'Alba, La Morra, Grinzane Cavour, and Novello. Founded in 1881 by Cesare Pio, the winery has been managed by the same family for five generations, maintaining a dedication to the distinct terroir of the Langhe region. Their winemaking philosophy emphasizes minimal intervention and a commitment to quality that captures the traditional essence of the Barolo appellation.

Wine Description

This wine features a youthful ruby colour with garnet reflections. The sensory profile is highly aromatic, offering primary fruit notes of peaches, strawberries, and cherries, layered with rose petals, anise, and dusty earth. On the palate, it is medium to full bodied and elegant, revealing flavours of wild cherry, licorice, bitter citrus, and hints of cedar and coffee bean. The structure is defined by fine-grained, velvety tannins and a lively acidity that leads to a long, harmonious finish with notes of spice and tobacco. This wine is a 100% Nebbiolo varietal and has an ABV of 14.7%. While the winery employs sustainable practices, this specific bottling is not classified as organic.

Food Pairing

The complex structure and high tannin levels of this Barolo make it a superb accompaniment for rich, savoury dishes such as braised beef (brasato al Barolo), roasted lamb with rosemary, or wild boar stew. It also pairs traditionally with Piedmontese specialties like white truffle risotto, mushroom pasta, and aged cheeses such as Castelmagno, Gorgonzola, or Parmigiano Reggiano.

title: Jean Louis Chave 'Blanche' Hermitage Blanc 2021
bodyHtml:
Hailing from the prestigious Northern Rhône region of France, Jean Louis Chave 'Blanche' Hermitage Blanc is a masterfully crafted expression from the historic Hermitage subregion. The Chave lineage boasts an illustrious winemaking history that has been passed down from father to son since 1481.

Wine Description

This exceptional white wine presents a beautiful medium golden-gold color in the glass. The bouquet is wonderfully exotic and complex, weaving together aromas of white blossoms, vanilla, and honey with vibrant notes of pear, peach, quince, and subtle tropical undertones. On the palate, it is full bodied, rich, and plush, balanced beautifully by a soaring acidity and a distinct crystalline minerality.

Accolades

94 Points - Wine Spectator

A creamy, rich white, with salty concentration behind its cascade of creamed melon and apple, spiked with spices, ginger and white mocha -- plus a flattering brush of warm brioche. Dried garrigue and smoldering flint bring contrast, driving the long, briny finish, with grapefruit pith. Marsanne and Roussanne.

title: Solaia 2003  (by Tenuta Tignanello) - 6 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
Solaia is a wine of massive proportion, dominated by rich black fruits, currants, minerals and a slight earthiness. Powerful yet fine grained tannins provide the framework for black fruit flavors and slight oaky hints. The palate is soft, well-balanced and lingering. This wine can be drunk immediately but has excellent ageing potential.

95 Points - Wine Spectator

92 Points - Wine Enthusiast

title: Chateau Barde Haut 2015
bodyHtml:
96 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

An awesome Saint Emilion, the 2015 Château Barde-Haut showed even better on this occasion than on release. A huge nose of sweet crème de cassis, jammy blackberries, violets, leather, and dried herbs gives way to a full-bodied wine that has a great mid-palate, ripe, silky tannins, not a hard edge to be found, and a great, great finish. I love it even today, yet it has a full two decades of prime drinking ahead of it.

95 Points - James Suckling

Aromas of blackberries, blueberries, wet earth and black tea. Full-bodied, dense and layered with medium, chewy tannins and a flavourful finish. Shows focus and power.

93 Points - Wine Spectator

A restrained style, with a core of damson plum, raspberry and cassis flavours held in check for now by fine-grained cedar, sanguine and iron hints. Best from 2022 through 2032.

title: Joseph Drouhin Puligny Montrachet 2024
bodyHtml:
The Joseph Drouhin Puligny-Montrachet is an elegant white Burgundy that represents one of the region's most famous villages. This village-level bottling is produced using grapes and musts sourced from long-term partners, all vinified under the strict biological and biodynamic standards for which Maison Joseph Drouhin is known.

Wine Description

  • Varietal Composition: 100% Chardonnay.

  • Aromatic Profile: The nose is pure and bright, evoking trees in bloom (hawthorn, acacia) and white-flesh fruits like white peach and apple. Distinct notes of vanilla pod, sweet stone fruit, and linden are also present.

  • Palate and Body: It is a medium-to-full-bodied wine with a silky, velvety texture. It delivers a sensation of "fresh silkiness" on the palate, with citrus and white fruit flavors harmoniously meshed together.

Food Pairing

The elegant floral and fruity wealth of this Puligny-Montrachet makes it a "match made in heaven" for refined dishes:

  • Seafood: Grilled white fish, scallops, or shrimp in a light butter sauce.

  • Poultry: Classic roast chicken or turkey with herbs.

  • Vegetarian: Rich pasta dishes, risotto with spring vegetables, or rice-based dishes.

title: H. Billiot Fils Brut Millesime 2014
bodyHtml:
Delicious, classy and complex are attributes everyone wants in a fine wine, and if it’s affordable, then even better. Personifying all these virtues, CHAMPAGNE H. BILLIOT FILS Champagnes have often become a go-to choice for Champagne lovers. Billiot’s wines are packed with plenty of flavour, yet they combine their depth with a rare elegance and harmony that sets them apart from many of their peers. They are also very much wines of place, and some of the purest expressions of Ambonnay to be found.

This Champagne has a deep amber colour although clear and bright. A good amount of small-ish bubbles. On the nose this has some strawberries, slight hay, dried floral notes and a slightly nutty quality. On the palate, the strawberries come thru with some light cherries.

title: Chateau L'Evangile 2022
bodyHtml:
Château L'Évangile is a historic Pomerol estate dating back to the mid-18th century. Located between Château Pétrus and Cheval Blanc, it has long been recognized for producing wines of elegance and depth. Owned by Domaines Barons de Rothschild (Lafite) since 1990, the estate merges traditional Bordeaux winemaking with precise vineyard management and a philosophy of expressive terroir-driven wines.

Wine Description
Deep ruby in colour with purple reflections, this 2022 vintage opens with a compelling bouquet of black cherries, plums, violets, truffle, and subtle cedar. On the palate, it is rich yet graceful, offering layers of dark fruit, cocoa, and savoury spices. The body is full with velvety tannins, lifted by a fresh mineral streak and a lingering finish marked by graphite and floral notes.

Accolades

  • James Suckling – 96 points.

  • Robert Parker’s Wine Advocate – 95+ points.

Food Pairing
Pair this refined Pomerol with roast lamb, duck breast with cherry reduction, or mushroom risotto with truffle oil. It also complements veal or grilled portobello mushrooms layered with savoury herbs.

title: Luce della Vite 2020
bodyHtml:
Introduction

Luce 2020, often known as Luce della Vite, is the iconic flagship red wine from Tenuta Luce, located in Montalcino, Tuscany. Founded in the 1990s as a historic collaboration between the Frescobaldi and Robert Mondavi families, it was the first wine in Montalcino to blend the structure of Sangiovese with the roundness of Merlot. The 2020 vintage is described as a balanced and straightforward expression of the estate's high-altitude terroir, successfully navigating a hot, dry summer with late-August rains that ensured perfect ripening.

Wine Description

The 2020 vintage is an intense ruby red wine characterized by its international polish and deep concentration.

  • Varietal Composition: An equal blend of 50% Merlot and 50% Sangiovese.

  • Aromatic Profile: The nose is complex and elegant, featuring ripe black fruits like blackberry and mulberry, joined by secondary notes of cocoa, tobacco, sweet spices (cardamom), and floral hints of violet.

  • Palate and Body: It is a full-bodied wine with a harmonious and lively mouthfeel. The palate is dense and powerful, dominated by black cherry and cassis, with highlights of iron and vanilla.

  • Structure: The wine possesses a serious structure with vibrant acidity and soft, silky tannins that provide a long, persistent, and spice-infused finish.

  • Aging: The wine was aged for 24 months in French oak barriques (80% new and 20% one-year-old).

  • Alcohol Content: 14.5%.

  • Optimal Drinking Window: While approachable with aeration, it is built for long-term aging through 2040–2044.

title: Chateau Lagrange 2016
bodyHtml:
Introduction

Château Lagrange 2016 is a red wine from France, produced in the Bordeaux region and the Saint-Julien appellation. Classified as a Troisième Grand Cru Classé (Third Growth) in the 1855 Bordeaux Classification, the estate spans 118 hectares in one block within Saint-Julien. Since its acquisition by the Japanese group Suntory in 1983, the château has undergone spectacular restructuration and investment, leading to its acknowledgement as one of the best-performing estates in the Médoc. The winery's philosophy emphasizes great care in the vineyard and plot-by-plot vinification, giving birth to a rich and elegant wine.

Wine Description

The wine has a deep garnet-purple or dark, almost black colour with purple light reflections. The aromatic profile is intense, focused, and expressive, featuring layers of black cherry, blackcurrant, blueberry pie, and cassis. Notes of cedar, graphite, liquorice, and spices (like pepper) are also present. The varietal composition is typically 70% Cabernet Sauvignon, 24% Merlot, and 6% Petit Verdot. It is a medium to full-bodied wine. The palate is full of juicy black fruits, with great energy, precision, and a vibrant, tight texture. The tannins are finely textured, chalky, and persistent, leading to a vivacious, spicy, and almost peppery finish. Stylistically, it is a harmonious, seamless, and elegant wine, considered one of the best ever produced at the property. The wine is aged for 21 months in French oak barrels, 60% of which are new. The finish is long, focused, and persistent. The ABV is either 13.4% or 13.5%. The optimal drinking window is long-term, from 2022 to 2047, or until 2040 and beyond. The winery practices sustainable viticulture and is certified ISO 14001.

Accolades

  • Jane Anson - 97 points

  • Vinous (Neal Martin) - 97 points

  • James Suckling - 95 points

  • Robert Parker's Wine Advocate (Lisa Perrotti-Brown MW) - 95 points

  • Jeb Dunnuck - 94 points

  • Wine Spectator (James Molesworth) - 94 points

  • Decanter - 95 points (Jane Anson)

Food Pairing

This exceptional Bordeaux pairs excellently with meat dishes. Suggested pairings include roasted rack of lamb, beef Wellington, honey-glazed duck, veal, pork, game, and grilled or braised dishes. It also complements aged hard cheeses like Comté.

Vintage Quality

The 2016 vintage in Bordeaux is widely regarded as one of the great years of the 21st century. A rainy spring was followed by one of the hottest and driest summers ever, leading to small berry sizes. The result is a wine with complexity, density, and great balance, combining the exuberant texture of 2009 with the precision of the 2010 vintage.

title: Luce Brunello di Montalcino 2019
bodyHtml:
Luce Brunello di Montalcino 2019 is a red wine from Italy, produced in the Tuscany region and the Montalcino D.O.C.G. appellation. The wine is made by Luce della Vite, a joint venture between the Frescobaldi and Mondavi families, and is the first Brunello di Montalcino to be created by blending Sangiovese and Merlot. Luce's philosophy is centred on innovation within a traditional landscape, emphasizing Sangiovese for elegance and Merlot for softness and richness. The wine's name, 'Luce' (Italian for light), symbolizes the radiance and quality of the Montalcino terroir.

Wine Description

The wine is 100% Sangiovese. It has an intense, dark ruby red colour. The aromatic profile is complex and refined, offering scents of black cherry, wild plum, cranberry, mint, and candied fruit. Further notes include tobacco, clove, liquorice, and cedar.

It is a full bodied wine. The palate is rich and harmonious, with concentrated fruit flavours. It has a lively, yet silky texture, with elegant, powerful, and persistent tannins that lend structure. Stylistically, it is a magnificent, profound, and well balanced wine that possesses both power and elegance. It was aged for 24 months in new French oak barrels. The finish is long, complex, and memorable. The ABV is 14.5%. The optimal drinking window is to drink now through 2045 or beyond. Information on the organic status of the wine is not available in the sources.

Accolades

  • James Suckling - 98 points

  • Vinous - 97 points

  • The Wine Advocate - 95 points

  • Decanter - 95 points

Food Pairing

This powerfully structured wine is a superb partner for all red meat main courses, especially roasted or grilled beef, as well as game and mature hard cheeses.

Vintage Quality

The 2019 vintage in Montalcino was characterized by balanced weather conditions, including a rainy spring and a warm, dry summer with cool nights. This led to a long, slow ripening period that resulted in Sangiovese grapes with great aromatic complexity, concentration, and a perfect balance of alcohol and acidity. The 2019 vintage is widely regarded as one of the best in recent history.

title: Joseph Drouhin Meursault 2022
bodyHtml:
Since 1880, Maison Joseph Drouhin has built a reputation for wines that primarily reflect their individual terroir and vintage. Faithfully preserving the individuality of each appellation, the Drouhin firm constantly strives for wines of breed, finesse and elegance.

A refined wine, well appreciated in the whole world. A beautiful golden color and a great aromatic palette: honey, linden flower (“tilleul”), hazelnut butter, sometimes even chamomile or hawthorn. On the palate, a silky roundness. Long on the aftertaste, with flavors of yellow plum and gingerbread.

94 Points - James Suckling

Nicely broad and rich in aromas but kept refined and elegant in the Drouhin style, with fresh apples, crisp pears, minerals and a hint of butter. This has the purity and polish of the appellation and is tempting to drink now.

90 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2022 Meursault Village delivers aromas of honeyed pears, toasted nuts, white flowers and peach, followed by a medium to full-bodied, satiny and suave palate of impressive length and structure. Like its Puligny counterpart, this will show well young.

title: Quinta Do Vale Meao 2021
bodyHtml: Complex black fruits with floral elements and notes of herbs, liquorice and tar. The palate is rich, ripe and concentrated with intense red and black fruits. A powerful, ripe wine with lots happening.

title: Allegrini Amarone della Valpolicella 2019
bodyHtml: From the first sip, experience a powerful and vigorous palate that gradually tapers into an elegant dance of acidic and savory notes, leaving you with a clean, dry finish. This exceptional bottle effortlessly compliments traditional pairings like game, roasted meats, and matured cheeses, but its unique profile also makes it an adventurous companion to exotic sweet and sour Asian or Middle-Eastern dishes.

title: Chateau Leoville Poyferre 2021
bodyHtml:
Like its neighbour Leoville Barton, Poyferre is always good value for money. Consultant oenologue Michel Rolland produces wines with a smoother, more fleshy character than the seriously structured wines of its neighbours. The result is a delicious St Julien that can usually charm early in its life and can stand the test of time. The wine is usually a little more plump and exotic than the other two Leovilles.

95+ Points - James Suckling

This is very typical for St.-Julien with violets, berries, blackcurrants and crushed stone. Medium to full body with very fine tannins that run the length of the wine. Powdery tannins and a rich finish. Velvety texture.

95 Points - Decanter

Beautifully fragranced on the nose - floral-edged ripe bramble fruits. Nicely detailed and presents, despite a clear youthful tannic structure this has layers of flavour with ripe and sweet fruit nuances balanced by a mineral grip, salty touches and cool fresh mint leaf notes.

94+ Points - Jeb Dunnuck

93+ Points - Vinous

93+ Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

title: Chateau Pavie 2019
bodyHtml:
Blend: 50% Merlot, 32% Cabernet Franc, 18% Cabernet Sauvignon

98 Points - James Suckling

Lots of blackberries and grilled meat with earth and spice. Some smoky undertones, too. Blackcurrants. Complex. Full-bodied with round, juicy tannins, yet they turn excellent and very linear and go on for minutes. Great length. A blend of 50% merlot, 32% cabernet franc and 18% cabernet sauvignon. Best after 2027, but already a joy to drink.

97 Points - Wine Spectator

Dreamy right from the start, with a seductive mouthfeel to its mix of raspberry puree, cassis and creamed plum flavours infused with rooibos tea, black licorice and alder accents. Long and extremely fine-grained through the finish, with subtle floral lift and a lingering hint of chalky minerality. Gorgeous. Merlot, Cabernet Franc and Cabernet Sauvignon. Best from 2025.

title: Albert Grivault Meursault 'Clos du Murger' 2022
bodyHtml: Albert Grivault is one of the stars of Meursault, working with some of the best parcels of vines and exercising complete control over one of the most renowned vineyards in the region. In addition to it's monopoly over the premier cru Clos des Perrieres vineyard, efforts are underway to upgrade the classification to Grand Cru status, previously unheard of in Meursault. The wine-making style at Grivault encourages highly developed mineral characteristics, fresh, pure fruit aromas and a clean acidic profile. The wines age beautifully and many require several years to fully show-off their true complexity and style.

title: Bouchard Pere & Fils Le Corton Grand Cru 2022
bodyHtml:
Bouchard Père & Fils Le Corton Grand Cru 2022 is a monumental red wine from the Côte de Beaune in Burgundy, France.

The hill of Corton is unique as the only Grand Cru site for Pinot Noir in the entire Côte de Beaune, and Bouchard Père & Fils has owned the historic Château de Beaune for over two centuries. The winery's philosophy emphasizes a profound respect for nature and the 'inspiration of the terroir', utilizing gravity-flow production and five-meter-deep underground galleries to provide optimal aging conditions. This specific cuvée is sourced from a 3.55-hectare parcel of shallow red-clay and white stony soils located at the top of the slope, directly below the forest.

Wine Description

This 2022 Grand Cru presents a deep and concentrated appearance typical of a stellar vintage. The intense bouquet offers a 'berry explosion' of mulberry, black plum, and crushed cherries, interwoven with complex layers of violets, liquorice, and sweet oak spice. On the palate, the wine is rich, dense, and powerfully structured, yet it maintains a seamless, velvety texture. It is characterized by its aristocratic poise, featuring supple tannins and a long, compact finish underscored by a distinct saline mineral note.

The wine is 100% Pinot Noir, with 40% of the 2022 crop fermented as whole clusters to enhance its aromatic profile and distinction. It is aged in French oak barrels within the estate's subterranean cellars and is produced from organically grown grapes. This vintage has an ABV of 13.5% and is built for significant longevity, with critics suggesting it will drink beautifully for over 25 years.

Food Pairing

The tannic power and earthy complexity of Le Corton make it an ideal partner for full-flavoured dishes such as venison, roast beef, or a spiced rib roast en croûte. It pairs exceptionally well with game birds like duck or goose, as well as hearty game animals. For a cheese pairing, its robust personality is a classic match for pungent Epoisses or other full-flavoured, mature cheeses.

Vintage Quality

The 2022 vintage in Burgundy is regarded as an outstanding success, defined by one of the warmest and driest growing seasons on record. Despite the heat, the vines at the top of the Corton hill benefited from good acid retention and moderate alcohol levels. The resulting wines are noted for their stunning concentration and lush, balanced profiles, with the 2022 Le Corton specifically lauded for its majestic structure and incredible precision.

Accolades

96 Points - Decanter

96 Points - James Suckling

96 Points - Wine Spectator

95 Points - Jasper Morris

title: Opus One 2012
bodyHtml:
Opus One 2012 is a prestigious red wine from the Oakville American Viticultural Area (AVA) in Napa Valley, California. This iconic winery was established in 1979 as a pioneering joint venture between two of the most influential figures in the wine world: Robert Mondavi and Baron Philippe de Rothschild of Château Mouton Rothschild. Their shared winemaking philosophy seeks to combine traditional Bordeaux-style structure and elegance with the rich, powerful fruit expression unique to Napa Valley's microclimate.

Wine Description

This vintage displays a deep, solid purple colour with subtle ruby hues. The aromatic profile is complex and refined, featuring fresh dark fruit notes of blackberry, cassis, and black cherry, accented by forest floor, graphite, tobacco, and cedar. On the palate, the wine is full bodied yet elegant, offering a round mouthfeel with satiny tannins and flavours of cassis, black currant, mocha, and anise. The structure is defined by seamless integration and lively acidity, leading to an exceedingly long and polished finish with lingering notes of licorice and dark spice. The varietal composition for the 2012 vintage is 79% Cabernet Sauvignon, 7% Cabernet Franc, 6% Petit Verdot, 6% Merlot, and 2% Malbec. It has an ABV of 14.5% and was aged for 18 months in new French oak barrels. While the estate utilizes sustainable viticulture, this bottling is not classified as organic.

Food Pairing

The sophisticated structure and rich fruit profile of this wine make it an ideal companion for high-quality red meats, such as dry-aged ribeye steak, roasted rack of lamb, or filet mignon with a black currant demi-glace. It also pairs excellently with earthy dishes featuring mushrooms or truffles, braised short ribs, and savoury game meats. For a cheese course, it complements hard, aged varieties such as Gruyère or aged Cheddar.

Vintage Quality

The 2012 vintage in Napa Valley is considered nearly ideal, characterized by a dry-warm winter followed by abundant sunshine and moderate temperatures throughout the growing season. These consistent conditions allowed for even ripening without harsh heat spikes, resulting in a harvest of exceptional balance, concentration, and fruit purity. Critics have praised this year as one of the best for Opus One in recent history, noting its remarkable poise and significant ageing potential of up to 30 years.

title: Pierre Paillard Extra Brut Bouzy Grand Cru Les Parcelles '18th Edition'
bodyHtml:
Pierre Paillard Brut Bouzy Grand Cru Les Parcelles '18th Edition' is a Champagne from France, originating in the Montagne de Reims region and the Bouzy appellation. The wine is produced by the family-owned Champagne house Pierre Paillard. The Paillard family has been cultivating vines in Bouzy, which is classified as a Grand Cru, since 1768. The house is considered an independent vigneron committed to showcasing the distinctiveness of the Bouzy terroir. 'Les Parcelles' is the Paillard family's signature, non-vintage cuvée, designed to express the purest essence of the Bouzy Grand Cru vineyard. The number '18' denotes the 18th blend, or 'edition,' of this particular wine.

Wine Description

The wine has a crystalline, medium yellow colour. The aromatic profile is noted for its freshness and precision, featuring notes of citrus fruit, white flowers, and red fruit, which is characteristic of the Bouzy Pinot Noir. Further notes include red apple, white peach, toasted grain, mint, crushed stone, saline, and a touch of chalk.

The blend for the 18th edition is 60% Pinot Noir and 40% Chardonnay, which is typical for the house's style, giving it a balance of flesh and finesse. The wine includes a high proportion of reserve wine, with 32% reserve wine from a perpetual reserve started in 2005, giving the wine complexity and depth. It is a medium-bodied wine. On the palate, it is fresh and broad, featuring notes of lemon peel, red apple, and red fruit. It has chalky minerality, excellent purity, and a great precision. Stylistically, it is taut, fresh, and vinous, with a powerful structure and a focused core. The finish is long, complex, clean, and refreshing. It is Brut, with a low dosage of 2.5 grams per litre (g/L). The ABV is $12.5\%$.

Accolades

  • Vinous - 93 points

  • The Wine Advocate - 92 points

  • Robert Parker - 92 points

  • Wine Spectator - 91 points

Food Pairing

This Champagne is a fine gastronomic wine that can be enjoyed with a variety of meals. It is a perfect match for richer fish dishes, poultry, and white meats. Suggested pairings include roast chicken, seafood, or even light-to-medium-bodied cheeses.

Vintage Quality

This wine is based on the 2018 vintage (with reserve wines blended in). The 2018 growing season in Champagne was characterised by excellent weather conditions, leading to a large and high-quality harvest. The year benefited from a warm and sunny summer, resulting in ripe, healthy grapes that provide the wine with its ample fruit and focused complexity.

title: Faiveley Puligny Montrachet 'Les Referts' Premier Cru 2022
bodyHtml:
Located at the bottom of the village of Puligny-Montrachet, on the edge of Meursault, "Les Referts" is a great classic of the appellation. Extending majestically over a plot of 0.37 ha, within a larger area of ​​5 hectares, this appellation is the signature of an exceptional terroir. The marly and compact soils give it a pronounced minerality and remarkable tension. The soil's resistance to drought provides an authenticity and depth that make this wine an essential appellation for connoisseurs.

This wine seduces with its nose that is both subtle and captivating, where the scents of citrus and exotic fruits blend harmoniously with light toasted notes. On the palate, it offers a sweetness evoking fresh almond, balanced with a subtle mineral tension. This wine is distinguished by its elegance and beautiful aromatic persistence.

title: Domaine des Beaumont Morey Saint Denis 2020
bodyHtml:
The origins of the wine-growing business in the Beaumont family goes back over seven generations. Thierry took over in 1991, creating the name Domaine des Beaumont and began to sell in bottles from 1999.

Now established in the three villages of Morey-Saint-Denis – the headquarters - Gevrey-Chambertin and Chambolle-Musigny, the estate has constantly invested in modern work tools, without neglecting the cultural, wine practices used by our ancestors. With a concern for passing down the great potential of this "Terroir" to future generations as best possible, Thierry Beaumont is developing environmentally-friendly and sustainable wine-growing.

Deep purple color. On the nose, notes of black fruits, spices and liquorice. On the palate, powerful body and good length on black fruits.

title: Chateau La Mission Haut Brion 2022
bodyHtml:
Chateau La Mission Haut Brion 2022 is a red wine from the Pessac Leognan appellation in the Graves region of Bordeaux, France. Founded in the 16th century by the de Lestonnac family and later administered by Lazarist priests, the estate has been owned by the Dillon family and Prince Robert of Luxembourg since 1983. The winery’s philosophy centres on preserving its unique historical significance and deep gravel terroir, with a commitment to sustainability reflected in its High Environmental Value (HEV) and ISO 14001 certifications.

Wine Description

This vintage possesses a deep garnet-purple or crimson colour. The nose is dark and explosive, offering a gregarious bouquet of plum preserves, crème de cassis, and blueberry compote, accented by exotic spices, smoky tobacco, and delicate floral notes of violets. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied and seamless, featuring a multi-dimensional mouthfeel charged with energetic black fruits and silky, fine-grained tannins. Stylistically, it is lauded for its magnificent balance, pure class, and a long, resonant finish with mineral undertones of flint and crushed stone. The varietal composition is a blend of 51.7% Cabernet Sauvignon, 43.2% Merlot, and 5.1% Cabernet Franc. The projected optimal drinking window for this vintage is approximately between 2032 and 2083.

Accolades

  • Vinous (Antonio Galloni) – 100 points

  • Jeb Dunnuck – 100 points

  • James Suckling – 98 points

  • Decanter – 97 points

title: Domaine Michel Gros Vosne Romanee 'Clos Des Reas' Monopole Premier Cru 2022
bodyHtml:
Winery Background: Domaine Michel Gros, established in 1830, is a family-owned estate in Vosne-Romanée, Burgundy. The Gros family has cultivated vineyards for seven generations, emphasizing traditional winemaking methods to express the unique terroir of their plots. The jewel of the estate is the Vosne-Romanée Premier Cru 'Clos des Réas', a monopole vineyard owned exclusively by the Gros family since 1860.

Wine Description: This 100% Pinot Noir wine presents a bright ruby hue. The bouquet is perfumed and floral, offering aromas of redcurrant, cranberry, and strawberry. On the palate, it is medium-bodied with fine tannins and nuanced flavors, expanding with zeal toward the finish. While currently a bit strict, it shows promise for further development.

Accolades:

  • Vinous: 92-94 points.
  • Burghound (Allen Meadows): 91-93 points.

Food Pairing: This wine pairs excellently with dishes such as roasted duck breast, coq au vin, or mushroom risotto. These pairings enhance the wine's depth and character.

title: Tignanello 2022 (by Tenuta Tignanello) - 3 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
Tignanello 2022 is a 'Super Tuscan' wine produced by the Antinori family at the Tenuta Tignanello estate in Italy's Tuscany region, in the heart of Chianti Classico. The Antinori family has been in the winemaking business for over 26 generations, since 1385. Tignanello was a pioneering wine for the Chianti Classico region, being one of the first red wines to be made without white grapes, and the first to age Sangiovese in small oak barrels (barriques).

Wine Description

This wine is a blend of 78% Sangiovese, 18% Cabernet Sauvignon, and 4% Cabernet Franc. It presents an intense ruby red colour with purple highlights. The aroma is a captivating blend of cherry, ripe black cherries, and pomegranate, with notes of violet, fresh balsamic hints, and subtle vanilla and candy floss nuances. On the palate, the wine is dynamic, dense, and fresh, with supple, savory tannins. It is described as elegant, balanced, and complex, with a long finish that echoes the aromatic notes. The optimal drinking window is from 2026 to 2040.

Accolades

  • Robert Parker - 98 points

  • James Suckling - 96 points

  • Vinous - 95 points

  • Wine Spectator - 94 points

Food Pairing

Tignanello is a versatile wine that pairs well with a variety of foods, including roasted and grilled meats like a Florentine T-bone steak or roast lamb with rosemary and garlic. Its depth and complexity also make it a great match for hearty pasta dishes, such as pappardelle with wild boar ragù or porcini mushroom risotto. Additionally, it pairs well with aged cheeses like Pecorino Toscano or Parmigiano Reggiano.

Vintage Quality

The 2022 growing season in Tuscany was characterized by hot and dry conditions, with lower-than-average rainfall until August. Despite these challenges, the vines demonstrated resilience, with rainfall in mid-August bringing cooler temperatures and restoring ideal day/night temperature swings for ripening. This allowed the grapes to achieve outstanding quality, highlighting the winemaker's skill in adapting to the climate

title: Quilceda Creek Cabernet Sauvignon 2021
bodyHtml:
Established in 1978 by Alex and Jeannette Golitzin with the first vintage produced in 1979, Quilceda Creek is Washington State’s 12th bonded winery after Prohibition, but the family’s storied history with winemaking dates back to the late 1800s. 

Quilceda Creek Cabernet Sauvignon is a wine for the ages. Potent aromas jump out of the glass, showing framboise candy, black tea, and a strong classic note of sandalwood. Savory cumin, sage, and garrigue round out this powerful nose. The palate is sweet and velvety, leading to an amazing crescendo of power and refinement.

98+ Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2021 Cabernet Sauvignon erupts with a classic Quilceda Creek expression. A big, bold and boisterous wine, it presents a fresh, juicy attack with gobs of succulent, ripe, fresh fruit tones complemented by plenty of oak essences. The palate is full-bodied, fresh, layered and complex, showcasing balanced acidity and fine-grained tannins. 

98 Points - James Suckling

With 90% of the grapes from Champoux Vineyard and 10% from Mach One Vineyard, this blend could have been labeled Horse Heaven Hills and is certainly no less a standout than the vineyard-designate bottlings. Mint, black fruit, cinnamon, sandalwood, blueberry and floral notes form a seamless whole, wrapped in beautifully integrated, fine tannins.

title: Louis Latour Gevrey Chambertin 2022
bodyHtml:
​Louis Latour's Gevrey Chambertin 2022 originates from the esteemed Côte de Nuits region in Burgundy, France. Maison Louis Latour, established in 1797, is renowned for its dedication to producing exceptional Pinot Noir wines that reflect the unique terroir of Burgundy.

Wine Description

This 100% Pinot Noir wine presents a dark ruby-red hue. The nose offers aromas of liquorice and cloves, complemented by subtle smoky notes. On the palate, it is full and round, revealing flavours of grilled coffee and mocha. The wine's velvety tannins contribute to its elegance. It is recommended to enjoy this wine within 3 to 5 years of its vintage.

Accolades

  • James Suckling: 93 points.

title: Chateau Mouton Rothschild 2000
bodyHtml:
Chateau Mouton Rothschild, a Premier Cru Classe from the Bordeaux region and one of the world's greatest wines, is owned by Baroness Philippine de Rothschild.

The wine has an attractively deep color with a garnet hue and an open, complex nose dominated by notes of humus and fern along with jammy fruit and prunes. Full on the attack, it shows opulence and attractive substance over close-knit, caressing tannins, developing intense roast coffee notes set off by a lovely reminder of the humus aromas on the nose. The powerful, full-bodied finish lingers long on the palate, revealing the expression and sheer class of great Mouton vintages, reminiscent in its richness and harmony of the very fine 1986.

97+ Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Deep garnet colored with a touch of brick, the 2000 Mouton Rothschild (composed of 86% Cabernet Sauvignon and 14% Merlot) boldly bursts from the glass with tantalizing Black Forest cake, dried mulberries, kirsch and blackcurrant pastilles notes plus wafts of iodine, incense, potpourri and cinnamon stick with a hint of cigar boxes. Medium to full-bodied, the palate packs in the muscular fruit, framed by firm, ripe, grainy tannins and seamless freshness, finishing with phenomenal length. This is an incredibly complex and multifaceted wine, and it's drinking deliciously now. 

97 Points - Wine Enthusiast

With its distinctive antique bottle and gold etched label dominated by a sheep, this is definitely a move away from classic Bordeaux bottling. It is good that the wine can support the presentation. The fruit is so ripe, it almost tastes of raisins, but that sweetness is finely balanced by the dry tannins and concentrated texture. To finish, there are exotic spices, giving an almost oriental character to the long aftertaste.

93 Points - Wine Spectator

Rounded, fleshy and a bit extracted in feel, with dark plum, blackberry and fig jam flavors that flirt with a pruny edge, picking up lots of warm mocha, singed vanilla bean and ganache notes through the finish. This relies more on easy opulence than on depth or purity on the end.

93 Points - James Suckling

The nose is very intense, super-ripe and rich, verging on jammy. Notes of leather, spices and prunes. Full-bodied, soft and beautiful with ripe tannins and a long finish. This is soft and yummy right now. Drink or hold.

title: Chateau Beychevelle 2022
bodyHtml:
Château Beychevelle, a distinguished Fourth Growth estate in the Saint-Julien appellation of Bordeaux, has crafted an exceptional wine in its 2022 vintage. This vintage reflects the estate's commitment to quality and the unique terroir of its vineyards.

Vintage Overview

The 2022 growing season presented challenges, including early frost in April and a particularly dry and warm summer. Despite these conditions, the vineyards benefited from well-timed rainfall in June, which replenished soil moisture and supported vine health. These factors contributed to the development of grapes with concentrated flavors and balanced acidity.

Blend and Production

The 2022 Château Beychevelle is a blend of 54% Cabernet Sauvignon, 42% Merlot, and 4% Petit Verdot. The harvest took place from September 12 to September 29, yielding 36 hectoliters per hectare, with 60% of the harvest designated for the Grand Vin. The wine was aged in French oak barrels, enhancing its complexity and structure.

Tasting Notes

  • Appearance: Deep, dark black-purple color, virtually opaque.

  • Aroma: Sweet spices over lifted cassis fruit, with notes of ripe blackcurrant, bramble, and damson.

  • Palate: Silky, fresh, vibrant, and concentrated, with flavors of ripe blackcurrant, bramble, and damson fruit, leading to concentrated licorice and graphite on the mid-palate.

  • Finish: Long and satisfying, delivering a wealth of sweet red and black fruits, creamy textures, and a chalky finish that lingers.

title: Joseph Drouhin Meursault 2023
bodyHtml:
For the last 140 years, Maison Joseph Drouhin has been managed by the Drouhin family, with the fourth generation currently at the helm, driven by the same foundational passion. The winery has embraced a biological and biodynamic approach, utilizing only natural products in the vineyards and demonstrating the utmost respect for the soil, the vine, and the environment.

Wine Description

This Meursault is made entirely from 100% Chardonnay, the varietal best suited to balance creamy notes with fresh white fruit flavours. It presents a beautiful golden colour and a great aromatic palette. On the palate, the wine has a silky roundness or creamy texture, with flavours of yellow plum and gingerbread. Stylistic notes include a magical balance between smoothness and freshness, with a good cut and a saline finish.

Food Pairing

Suggested pairings for this oaky white wine include delicate fish dishes, lobster, foie gras, and poultry such as chicken and turkey. It also pairs well with creamy pasta dishes or fresh goat cheese. A classic match is boiled and buttered lobster, where the wine's creaminess echoes the butter, and its acidity cleanses the palate.

Accolades

94 Points - James Suckling: Aromas of ripe apples, chalk and stone with hints of crushed oyster shells, following through to a full body with a creamy texture and a long, crunchy finish. Subtle Meursault.

title: Schrader Cabernet Sauvignon LPV Beckstoffer Las Piedras Vineyard 2018
bodyHtml:
For more than a decade, Schrader Cellars has produced benchmark Cabernet Sauvignon from the most prestigious vineyards in the Napa Valley, notably the first-growth Beckstoffer To Kalon Vineyard in Oakville, along with Beckstoffer Georges III Vineyard in Rutherford, Beckstoffer Las Piedras in Northwest St. Helena, and newly the Monastery Block To Kalon Vineyard in Oakville. Thomas Brown, a South Carolina native, didn’t grow up in the wine business, but after extensively exploring the wine regions of France, Italy, and Northern California, he knew where he belonged. In 1996, Thomas moved to Napa Valley and began working in a wine shop. Wanting to cut his teeth in winemaking, he began working in acclaimed cellars with industry legends. In 2000, destiny circled around and Thomas met Fred Schrader at the same fine wine shop. Although Thomas had yet to make a bottle of Cabernet Sauvignon, Fred recognized his unwavering passion, fantastic natural ability, and dedication to winemaking, and hired him to do just that for his namesake brand, Schrader. Since then, the duo has developed a portfolio of benchmark Cabernet Sauvignons renowned for their “no holds barred” character. Thomas has achieved unprecedented success in record time and has revealed himself to be a true visionary of wine.

98 Points - James Suckling

Wonderful aromas of currants, crushed berries and flowers. Very deep and complex. Full-bodied and layered with loads of ripe tannins, yet they are polished and very fine. Extremely long finish. Give it at least five years to come together and refine. Try after 2025.

98 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

The 2018 Cabernet Sauvignon Beckstoffer Las Piedras Vineyard LPV comes from a rocky site just outside of St. Helena, next to the Dr. Crane vineyard. Despite its close proximity, this vineyard always seems to yield a more red-fruited, elegant wine compared to the more powerful style from Dr. Crane. Deep ruby/purple-coloured, with a killer bouquet of savoury red and black fruits, tobacco, chocolate, dried flowers, and bay leaves, it hits the palate with full-bodied richness, a seamless, multi-dimensional texture, perfect balance, and a great, great finish. This is a gorgeous, utterly thrilling 2018. It should probably merit a triple-digit rating in 4-5 years and evolve for 30+ years or more.

97 Points - Wine Spectator

Packed for sure, but there's a lot of freshness and inner brightness too, with a core of cassis, plum puree and Linzer flavours gliding through atop polished structure, while violet, anise and roasted apple wood notes fill in liberally through the finish, which sports a buried but discernibly racy graphite edge. Gorgeous. Best from 2022 through 2040.

96 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Schrader’s “LPV” comes from Beckstoffer’s Las Piedras vineyard, produced from 337 clones grown on the C block. One hundred percent Cabernet Sauvignon, it was aged for 18 months in 100% new Darnajou and Taransaud French oak barrels. Deep garnet-purple in colour, the 2018 Cabernet Sauvignon Beckstoffer Las Piedras Vineyard Lpv slowly unfurls to reveal fragrant notes of red roses, cherry pie, mulberries and warm cassis with hints of fallen leaves, potpourri and Indian spices. The medium-bodied palate delivers fantastic intensity with loads of exotic spice accents complementing the crunchy red and black fruits, framed by firm, grainy tannins and a lively backbone. It finishes with a beautiful fragrant-earth signature.

title: Chateau Branaire Ducru 2015
bodyHtml:
From the Saint-Julien appellation in Bordeaux, France, Château Branaire-Ducru is a Fourth Growth estate that was part of the original Bordeaux Wine Official Classification of 1855. The history of the estate dates back to 1680, and since 1988 it has been owned by the Maroteaux family. The vineyard is located on the gravelly hills of the Saint-Julien appellation, with the vines rooted in deep gravel and clay soils. The winery's philosophy, or 'House Signature', focuses on creating wines with a distinct balance of fruit, freshness, and elegance.

Wine Description Château Branaire-Ducru 2015 has a deep, garnet-purple colour. The wine is a blend of 65% Cabernet Sauvignon, 26% Merlot, 5% Petit Verdot, and 4% Cabernet Franc. The nose offers notes of black cherry, cassis, plum preserves, red berries, and hints of Indian spices, fragrant soil, and cedar. On the palate, it is full-bodied and packed with juicy black fruits. The wine has a lively, fresh acidity with a fine tannin structure. It is described as elegant, supple, and harmonious, with a long, layered finish.

Accolades

  • Vinous - 95 points

  • Wine Enthusiast - 95 points

  • Decanter - 94 points

  • Wine Spectator - 94 points (No. 33 in Top 100 Wines of 2018)

  • James Suckling - 93 points

Food Pairing This wine is an excellent match for red meat, veal, pork, lamb, and grilled dishes. It also pairs well with aged hard cheeses like Comté or Pecorino, mushroom risotto, and dishes with truffle or earthy spice. A perfect match to enhance the wine's complexity.

title: Produttori del Barbaresco - Barbaresco 'Montefico' Riserva 2020
bodyHtml:
Produttori del Barbaresco Barbaresco Montefico Riserva 2020 originates from the Piedmont region of Italy, specifically from the prestigious Montefico vineyard in the Barbaresco subregion. Established in 1958, the Produttori del Barbaresco is an esteemed cooperative uniting over 50 small family vineyards that exclusively cultivate Nebbiolo. The Montefico vineyard is a south-southeast facing amphitheatre located away from the warm air of the Tanaro River Valley, featuring active limestone soils that contribute to an austere and assertive character in the final wine. The winery's philosophy is rooted in traditional practices, utilizing only large Slavonian oak barrels (grandi botti) to ensure an authentic expression of the terroir.

Wine Description

This structured red wine presents a deep ruby red colour with garnet hues. The aromatic profile is complex and seductive, opening with notes of black cherries, forest berries, and ripe sour cherries, leading into distinct herbal layers of dried rosemary, lavender, mint, and cedar. On the palate, it is full-bodied and compact in texture, offering a core of dark-toned fruit balanced by an even acidity and a rich sapidity. The finish is precise, long-lasting, and marked by a characteristic minerality and chalky feel. This 100% Nebbiolo varietal composition was fermented with 28 days of skin contact before aging for 30 to 36 months in large oak barrels and a further 8 to 12 months in the bottle. It has an alcohol content of 14.5% ABV and is suitable for vegans. While the estate utilizes nature-close cultivation, it is not certified organic. The optimal drinking window extends from 2026 through 2050.

Accolades

  • Jeb Dunnuck - 97 points

  • Wine Advocate - 96+ points

  • Vinous (Antonio Galloni) - 96 points

  • Kerin O'Keefe - 96 points

  • Wine Spectator - 94 points

Food Pairing

The structured tannins and intense minerality of Montefico Riserva make it a profound partner for savory and robust dishes. It is a perfect accompaniment to fresh egg pastas, mushroom risotto, or pasta dishes topped with truffles. The wine's noble body also pairs exceptionally well with red meats, game such as venison, and braised dishes. For a simpler pairing, it complements a variety of mature or full-flavoured cheeses.

Vintage Quality

The 2020 vintage in Barbaresco is rated as extremely good with points of excellence, producing wines that are complete and complex. While not as full-bodied as some preceding vintages, the season allowed for a fruitier profile with ample richness and texture that provides medium-to-long aging potential.

title: Heitz Cellar Cabernet Sauvignon Lot C-91 2018
bodyHtml:
Heitz Cellar’s legacy runs as deep as the roots throughout the Napa Valley; a winery legend that has helped shape the history of Napa Valley winemaking. In the late 1950’s, pioneering vintner Joe Heitz ushered in Napa’s modern era with his iconic, globally celebrated wines, including Napa Valley’s first vineyard-designated Cabernet Sauvignon, the renowned Heitz Cellar Martha’s Vineyard.

The 2018 Heitz Cellar Lot C-91 is a distinguished Cabernet Sauvignon from Napa Valley, California. This wine pays homage to the original Lot C-91 blend crafted in 1969, showcasing a meticulous selection of grapes from Heitz's renowned single vineyards, including Martha’s, Trailside, Ink Grade, Linda Falls, and The Only One. The 2018 vintage benefited from abundant spring rains and a balanced growing season, resulting in exceptional fruit quality.

Colour: Deep ruby red with a vibrant hue, indicating its concentration and youthfulness.

Aroma: Expressive bouquet featuring notes of blueberries, cassis, plums, and spiced orange, complemented by savory elements such as cured meats, rosemary, and sage.

Palate: Full-bodied and well-structured, offering a harmonious blend of red and black fruits with subtle hints of black pepper and cured meats. The wine exhibits a luxurious texture with fine-grained tannins and balanced acidity.

Body: Full-bodied with a rich and velvety mouthfeel, showcasing both power and elegance.

Finish: Long and persistent, leaving a lasting impression of its complex flavors and refined structure.

Accolades:

  • 95 Points - Decanter

  • 93 Points - Wine Spectator

  • 93 Points - Wine Enthusiast

This wine exemplifies Heitz Cellar's dedication to producing wines that are both expressive and true to their terroir, offering a delightful experience for Napa Valley Cabernet Sauvignon enthusiasts.

title: Castello di Ama Chianti Classico Gran Selezione 'La Casuccia' 2022
bodyHtml:
Originating from Italy in the Tuscany region, specifically within the Chianti Classico Gran Selezione DOCG appellation in Gaiole in Chianti, Castello di Ama Chianti Classico Gran Selezione 'La Casuccia' 2022 represents an historic, opulent, and majestic single-vineyard expression of Tuscan terroir. First produced in 1985 alongside 'L'Apparita', Vigneto La Casuccia is a benchmark cru vineyard spanning 12.58 hectares at approximately 480 metres elevation, featuring nine distinct sub-parcels planted on stony clay-limestone soils. The winemaking philosophy under winemaker Marco Pallanti involves meticulous hand harvesting, co-fermentation of varieties in ambient temperature-controlled vats with native yeasts, and aging in fine French oak barriques (approximately 40% new) for around 15 months. Produced only in exceptional vintages and in strictly limited quantities, 'La Casuccia' delivers a Gran Selezione of profound, fleshy dark fruit depth, velvety texture, and high-altitude refinement.

Wine Description

The wine presents an opaque, deep dark ruby red colour with intense purple-garnet reflections along the rim. An expressive, highly complex bouquet opens with opulent aromas of ripe black cherry, wild blackberry, dark plum, and cassis, interwoven with sophisticated notes of dark chocolate, pipe tobacco, crushed dried violet petals, forest floor, graphite, and sweet French oak spice. On the palate, it is full bodied, fleshy, and velvety, delivering concentrated flavours of dark berry fruit jam, tart cherry curd, and savory mineral earth, all supported by a bright, mouthwatering spine of natural acidity. Framed by rich, fine-grained, rounded tannins and a deep, coat-the-mouth mid-palate structure, it concludes with an extraordinarily long, persistent finish marked by lingering black fruit, cocoa powder, and a refined chalky limestone grip. Composed primarily of Sangiovese blended with a small proportion of Merlot, this 2022 release offers an optimal drinking window of 2028–2050+. Stylistically, it combines Merlot-driven mid-palate richness and sensuality with Gaiole's high-elevation tension, Gran Selezione structure, and long-term aging potential.

title: Fontodi Flaccianello della Pieve 2022 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
The 'Flaccianello della Pieve' hails from the Colli della Toscana Centrale IGT in the Tuscany region of Italy. Fontodi is a certified organic estate, comprising 130 hectares with about 70 planted to vines. The Manetti family, prominent in Chianti for centuries and originally known for terracotta production, owns the winery. Winemaker Giovanni Manetti has led Fontodi, focusing on biodynamic principles to achieve self-sufficiency and respect for nature in their agriculture.

Wine Description

This single varietal wine is composed of 100% Sangiovese. It presents a rich, deep dark ruby red colour. The complex sensory profile includes aromas of plums, black cherries, fresh violets, and licorice, with touches of leather and graphite. On the palate, this full-bodied wine displays a well-tamed, structured profile with firm tannins coated in fruit and chewy acidity that maintains a fresh and balanced finish.

Accolades

  • James Suckling - 97 points

  • Wine Spectator - 96 points

  • Vinous - 94 points

Food Pairing

Suggested pairings include charcuterie, sausage pasta, or a classic Steak Florentine.

title: Chateau Angelus 2022
bodyHtml:
Château Angélus is an iconic estate located on the south-facing slopes of Saint-Émilion, Bordeaux. Owned by the de Boüard de Laforest family since 1909, it is now led by Stéphanie de Boüard-Rivoal, representing the eighth generation. The estate’s philosophy combines meticulous vineyard management with precise vinification to express the exceptional terroir of the property.

Wine Description

A blend of Merlot (60%) and Cabernet Franc (40%), the Château Angélus 2022 displays a deep, vibrant purple hue. The nose is intense and multi-layered, revealing notes of ripe blackberries, blueberries, lilacs, graphite, and hints of dark chocolate. On the palate, it is full-bodied, rich, and structured, yet remarkably elegant, with silky tannins and a long, persistent finish.

Accolades

  • "James Suckling - 97-98 points."

  • "Wine Advocate - 95-97 points."

  • "Vinous - 95-97 points."

  • "Decanter - 96 points."

Food Pairing

This refined Saint-Émilion pairs beautifully with rack of lamb with rosemary, duck breast with cherry sauce, or aged ribeye steak. It also complements earthy dishes such as wild mushroom risotto or truffle-infused pasta, highlighting the wine’s depth and character.

title: Krug Rose Brut 29th Edition
bodyHtml:
Founded in Reims in 1843 by Joseph Krug, the House of Krug is a pillar of excellence guided by an uncompromising philosophy to craft the very best Champagne every year, regardless of climatic variations. Krug Rosé was first created in 1976 by the fifth generation of the Krug family, inspired by the Maison's blending artistry to be recreated each year.

Wine Description

The nose opens with delectable aromas of red fruits such as raspberry, strawberry, and ripe cherry, enriched by delicate toasted nuances. Other notes include grapefruit zest, redcurrant, apple pie, Sichuan pepper, and a whisper of rosewood oil. On the palate, it is medium- to full-bodied, vinous, and textural, with flavours reminiscent of raspberry charlotte, soft biscuits, and notes of prune. A refined hint of blood orange and a touch of pink grapefruit bitterness elevate the finish. It offers a deep core of fruit and tangy acidity.

Accolades

  • Vinous - 94 points

  • Robert Parker's Wine Advocate - 94 points

Food Pairing

Suggested pairings include game, spicy cuisine, wild boar fillet, grilled cauliflower tacos with romesco salsa, vegetable and jalapeño quiche, or grilled sardines.

title: Produttori del Barbaresco - Barbaresco 'Ovello' Riserva 2019
bodyHtml:
This red wine is produced in Italy, specifically in the Barbaresco region within the esteemed Ovello subregion. Produttori del Barbaresco was established in 1958 when the local parish priest, Don Fiorino Marengo, united 19 small growers to protect their vineyards and the future of the Nebbiolo grape. Today, the winery operates as a premier cooperative with over 50 members who collectively manage 120 hectares of premium vineyards. Their winemaking philosophy focuses on a pure, clean expression of the territory, ensuring that single vineyard Riservas are only bottled during exceptional vintages to maintain the highest quality standards.

Wine Description

The 2019 Barbaresco Ovello Riserva presents a bright ruby red colour with garnet reflections. The aromatic profile is deep and complex, featuring scents of crushed violets, black raspberries, tea leaf, and sweet herbs, alongside savory hints of turned soil and tobacco. On the palate, the wine is full bodied and intensely linear, delivering flavors of ripe Marasca cherry, cranberry, star anise, and ground clove. It is characterized by its massive structure, vibrant acidity, and firm, close-grained tannins that lead into a long finish with saline and mineral notes. This 100% Nebbiolo wine has an ABV of 14.5%. While the wine currently shows youthful tension, its optimal drinking window is between 2026 and 2050.

Accolades

  • Wine Spectator - 94 points

  • Wine Enthusiast - 95 points

  • Wine Advocate - 94 points

  • James Suckling - 93 points

Food Pairing

The firm structure and high acidity of this wine make it an excellent companion for rich, savory Italian dishes. Suggested pairings include fresh egg pastas such as tajarin with a meat ragu or risotto finished with truffles or wild mushrooms. It also pairs well with roasted red meats, venison, or braised beef. For cheese courses, aged hard cheeses are recommended to balance the wine's youthful tannins.

Vintage Quality

The 2019 vintage in Barbaresco is regarded as a 'classic' year, marked by a long and balanced growing season that allowed for exceptional phenolic ripeness. Cooler temperatures in the spring delayed budbreak, while ideal warm weather in September resulted in grapes with excellent sugar levels, vibrant acidity, and an extraordinary structural harmony.

title: Tignanello 2019 (by Tenuta Tignanello)
bodyHtml:
Introduction

This red wine is from Italy, specifically from the Toscana IGT region in Tuscany. Produced by Marchesi Antinori, Tignanello is a historic milestone in Italian viticulture as the first Sangiovese-based wine to be aged in barriques and the first modern red from the Chianti Classico area to exclude white grapes while incorporating non-traditional varieties like Cabernet. The estate's winemaking philosophy focuses on reconciling tradition and modernity, sourcing fruit exclusively from a 57-hectare vineyard situated between 350 and 400 metres above sea level with limestone-rich soils.

Wine Description

The 2019 Tignanello is an intense ruby red colour. Its complex nose offers exceptional depth with aromas of red berries, cherry, and pomegranate, layered with delicate notes of apricot, vanilla, chocolate, and Mediterranean herbs like mint and lavender. On the palate, the wine is robust yet elegant, featuring silky, vibrant tannins and flavours of dark berry fruit, blood orange, and roasted coffee. It is characterized by its sinewy tension, refined structure, and a lengthy finish with hints of bitter chocolate. The varietal composition is approximately 80% Sangiovese, 15% Cabernet Sauvignon, and 5% Cabernet Franc. It has an ABV of 14% and is best enjoyed from 2025 through 2042.

Accolades

  • Robert Parker's Wine Advocate - 96 points

  • Wine Spectator - 96 points

  • Natalie MacLean - 96 points

  • James Suckling - 95 points

  • Wine Enthusiast - 95 points

  • Vinous - 94 points

Food Pairing

This Super Tuscan pairs excellently with rich meat dishes such as roasted lamb, duck, or venison. Its structured tannins and vibrant acidity also complement classic Italian fare, including Ragu Bolognese, pasta with truffles, and hearty red meat preparations. For cheese, it is ideally suited to aged varieties or savoury selections like prosciutto.

Vintage Quality

The 2019 vintage in Tuscany is regarded as 'classic', benefiting from a balanced growing season with cool spring rains and a warm summer without extreme heat spikes. These favourable conditions, including a ripening phase with excellent day-night temperature swings in late August and September, resulted in grapes of outstanding quality and refined structural harmony.

title: Domaine Michel Noellat Nuits Saint Georges 2019
bodyHtml: Sixth generation winemakers at Domaine Michel Noëllat, cousins Sebastien Noëllat and Sophie Noëllat-Sirugue are beginning to carve out a significant international reputation, and deservedly so. With vines averaging 60-70 years, a reduced reliance on oak, and the adoption of a pragmatic investment strategy, quality has been on the rise since they began working together. The Clos Vougeot is their top wine, while the Echezeaux is a proper gem. Their entire range is wonderful, the wines deep, round and super-generous, the tannins soft like graphite, the terroir shining through.

title: Chateau Bellevue Mondotte 2019
bodyHtml:
Partly enclosed by Chateau Pavie-Decesse, on the clay-limestone plateau of Saint-Emilion, Chateau Bellevue-Mondotte truly benefits from an "immense" terroir, as Gerard Perse likes to emphasize. Overlooking the Dordogne valley by more than 80 meters, the small estate (2.5 hectares) combines in an optimal way the qualities required for high-level viticulture: natural poverty of the soils, excellent sunshine thanks to the southern exposure, natural drainage of the grounds because of the slope, very little gelling character of the vineyard protected from the northern wind.

In the vineyards as well as in the cellar, the Perse spirit reigns with a lot of rigour, passion and attention, with the aim of elaborating the most beautiful harvests for the most precise vinifications. The annual production is very small, around 400 cases.

98 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

The Merlot-dominated 2019 Bellevue Mondotte just about jumps out of the glass with its ripe, spicy red, blue, and black fruits as well as spring flowers, graphite, chalky mineral, and violet-like aromas and flavours. Almost Pomerol-like with its seamless, polished tannins and gorgeous mouthfeel, it's flawlessly balanced, has a deep, layered mid-palate, and a great, great finish.

94+ Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Very deep garnet-purple coloured, it comes bounding out of the glass with exuberant black cherry preserves, blueberry compote and boysenberries scents plus hints of wilted roses, cumin seed, aniseed and cardamom. Full-bodied, the palate has fantastically ripe, silky tannins and gorgeous freshness supporting all that perfumed black and blue fruit, finishing long and harmonious.

94+ Points - James Suckling

The purity of fruit is impressive here with crushed blackberries, blueberries and dark chocolate with some coffee. It’s full-bodied, yet integrated and chewy. Rich finish.

92+ Points - Wine Enthusiast

This is a really stylish wine from the same ownership as Chateau Pavie. There are some generous tannins that give balance to the bold fruitiness. This is a wine for aging.

title: Poggio di Sotto Brunello di Montalcino 2019
bodyHtml:
Poggio di Sotto is widely regarded as one of the great names of Brunello, and the 2018 release shows why. This is a luminous, elegant expression of the vintage, balancing ripe fruit with savoury complexity and poised structure.

On the nose, aromas of cherry, strawberry, dried roses and balsamic sweetness mingle with notes of herbs, incense, sandalwood and exotic spice. The palate unfolds with juicy red and black berries, cranberry, leather, and a touch of garrigue, lifted by vibrant acidity and wrapped in velvety tannins. Hints of white pepper, licorice and a saline edge add intrigue and length, while the finish is long, graceful and harmoniously mid-weight.

Vinified with the estate’s hallmark precision and aged 30 months in large oak casks, the 2018 is approachable in its youth yet built to evolve beautifully over the next two decades. It captures the freshness of a cooler, classic vintage while retaining Poggio di Sotto’s signature finesse and aromatic intensity.

Accolades:

  • 96 points – Monica Larner, Robert Parker Wine Advocate (Nov 2024)

  • 94 points – Eric Guido, Vinous (Mar 2024)

  • 96 points – Susan Hulme, The Wine Independent

Drinking Window: 2025 – 2045

title: Bodega Chacra Pinot Noir 'Treinta y Dos' 2022
bodyHtml: Red cherries, strawberries, spiced plums, violets, cloves, dried herbs, undergrowth and a hint of smokiness on the nose. It is medium bodied with firm, tight-grained tannins. Firm, mineral tannins with a quality similar to tea. Very focused and structured.

title: Kistler Pinot Noir Sonoma Coast 2023
bodyHtml: Founded in 1978, Kistler Vineyards is a small, family-owned and operated winery specializing in the production of Burgundian style Chardonnay and limited amounts of Pinot Noir. Grapes are estate grown and purchased from vineyards in Sonoma County. In 1992, Kistler Vineyards moved all production to its Vine Hill Road Vineyard in the Russian River Valley. Kistler Pinot Noir is fermented in small open top fermenters and the free run juice is barrel aged and remains in barrel for fourteen to eighteen months until bottling.

title: Chateau Lafite Rothschild 2021 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
Château Lafite Rothschild, located in the Pauillac appellation of Bordeaux, France, is one of the most esteemed wine estates in the world. As a First Growth under the 1855 Bordeaux Classification, it has a storied history of producing wines that exemplify elegance and longevity. The estate is renowned for its meticulous vineyard management and a winemaking philosophy that emphasizes tradition and terroir.

Wine Description

The 2021 vintage of Château Lafite Rothschild is a blend of 96% Cabernet Sauvignon, 3% Merlot, and 1% Petit Verdot. In the glass, it presents a deep garnet-purple hue. The nose is expressive, offering aromas of ripe blackcurrants, fresh blackberries, and black raspberries, complemented by hints of cedar, graphite, cloves, and a subtle floral note reminiscent of roses. On the palate, the wine is medium to full-bodied, with a velvety attack that transitions into an elegantly dense and structured mid-palate. The tannins are sweet yet abundant, framing the wine beautifully and leading to a long, penetrating finish. This vintage showcases Lafite's signature finesse and balance, with a harmonious integration of fruit, acidity, and tannin.

Accolades

  • James Suckling: 97–98 points
  • Decanter: 96 points

Food Pairing

This wine pairs exquisitely with classic dishes such as roasted lamb, filet mignon, or duck breast with a berry reduction. It also complements aged hard cheeses like Comté or Gruyère. These pairings highlight the wine's depth and character, creating an unforgettable dining experience.

title: Lokoya Cabernet Sauvignon Howell Mountain 2019
bodyHtml:
100 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

Coming all from the from the Keyes Vineyard on Howell Mountain, the 2019 Howell Mountain Cabernet Sauvignon (100% Cabernet Sauvignon) was brought up in 91% new French oak. Incredible crème de cassis, chalky minerality, iron, spring flowers, and black olive tapenade all define the nose, and It's full-bodied on the palate, with building tannins, integrated oak, wonderful sweetness of fruit, and a great, great finish. It opens up beautifully with time in the glass, and while it has classic Mountain structure and concentration, it also has a wealth of fruit and texture, and unquestionably offers pleasure even today. Nevertheless, do your best to hide bottles for 4-5 years if you can. It's a 30- to 40-year wine.

98 Points - Decanter

Incredibly rich and opulent. Sumptuous aromas of ripe cassis, boysenberry, blackberry and mountain herbs. The incredibly vivid dark berry fruit – deep and penetrating – is accompanied by a tapestry of granular mountain tannins that are long and laced with a saline minerality. The finish reveals a plethora of pie spices, blueberry compote, chocolate and very fine oak. A powerhouse Cabernet that is pleasure-packed.

97 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Sourced from two blocks of the Keyes Vineyard at La Jota, the 2019 Cabernet Sauvignon Howell Mountain shows more caramel, barrel toast and mocha notes, derived from the choice of Demptos as the cooper. Cassis and blueberry flesh out the flavor profile of this full-bodied, rich, velvety effort. Mouth-filling and plush, it's broad and expansive in the mouth, finishing long and intricately textured.

96 Points - James Suckling

The purple fruit is prevailing, together with conifer, lead-pencil and ink-pot aromas, following through to a full body with layered, ripe tannins and lightly toasted oak at the finish. Give it three to four years to come around. Try after 2025.

94 Points - Wine Spectator

Vivid, with açaí, boysenberry and blackberry puree steaming through, buttressed by a prominent cast iron note that lends a racy, driven feel from start to finish. A wine of fresh power. Best from 2023 through 2036.

title: Bevan Cellars Red Blend Ontogeny 2021
bodyHtml: Vibrant blueberry, boysenberry and creme de cassis with super concentrated fruit, and with the weight and tannin in the back palate that will allow this wine to age gracefully. Deep, dark and powerful.

title: Clos du Marquis 2019
bodyHtml:
96 Points - Wine Enthusiast     The wine from a single vineyard within the Léoville Las Cases estate shows power with discretion. Its tannins and rich black currant fruits from Cabernet Sauvignon are solid, ripe and also stylish. That makes for a wine that will have balance between structure and fruit, concentration and openness. The wine is set for long aging.

95 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate     The 2019 Clos du Marquis is composed of 70% Cabernet Sauvignon, 7% Cabernet Franc and 23% Merlot, harvested between the 21st of September and 9th of October. It is aging in French oak barriques, 50% new. The alcohol is 14.1% with a pH of 3.62 and an IPT of 79. Displaying a deep purple-black color, the nose is a little reticent to begin, but with just a little coaxing, it soon opens out to show off impressively flamboyant notes of blackberry preserves, baked plums and blackcurrant pastilles with suggestions of cinnamon toast, Darjeeling tea, licorice and camphor plus a hint of wilted roses. Medium to full-bodied, the palate layers in all of these exciting mineral sparks with with the energetic, fresh black fruits, supported by rock-solid, ripe, grainy tannins and bold freshness, finishing long and earthy. This a very polished and sophisticated Clos du Marquis!

95 Points - Vinous     The 2019 Clos du Marquis was picked from 21 September to 9 October and matured in 50% new oak. It has a deep and quite penetrating bouquet: blackberry, hoisin intermingling with cedar and light pencil shaving scents. It becomes noticeably richer with aeration. The palate is medium-bodied with firm tannins that frame the vivid blackberry and wild strawberry fruit laced with orange sorbet. There is a citric freshness towards the end of this accomplished Clos du Marquis. Excellent. 

93 Points - James Suckling     So much gravel and dark-fruit character with raspberries and blackcurrants, as well as currant leaf. It’s medium-to full-bodied with very fine, rounded tannins and a bright finish. 70% cabernet sauvignon, 23% merlot and 7% cabernet franc. Drinkable now, but even better in 2024.

92 Points - Decanter     First made in 1902, this is a blend of various parcels, some close to Léoville Las Cases, others near Talbot. In this vintage a second wine, La Petite Marquise, was created, strengthening the identity of Clos du Marquis as a fine wine in its own right. Flamboyant and vibrant nose, with juicy blackcurrant fruit. Concentrated and velvety, it nonetheless has power and grip. Tannins are well integrated. Admirable depth of flavour; spicy and persistent finish.

title: Pahlmeyer Proprietary Red Blend 2021
bodyHtml:
Pahlmeyer Proprietary Red captures the essence of this stellar low-yielding vintage: powerful yet refined, intense yet luscious. Aromas of lingonberry and boysenberry interplay with flickerings of green peppercorn, saddle leather, and forest floor, culminating in a beautifully lifted bouquet. The tightly wound palate frames a core of intense plum and cassis layered with licorice spice. Polished tannins give way to a mid-palate rich with macerated blackberry and freshly grated nutmeg. 

95+ Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Right now, it offers compelling fruit-driven aromas of ripe cherries, cassis, and blueberries—the oak is well concealed. Full-bodied and rich, this is dense and velvety on the palate, with a long, mouthwatering finish, despite an ample amount of dusty tannins.

title: Napanook 2018 (by Dominus Estate)
bodyHtml: In the late 1960s, while attending the University of California at Davis, Christian Moueix fell in love with the Napa Valley and its wines. His love of Napa Valley lingered, and in 1981, he discovered the historic Napanook vineyard, a 124-acre site west of Yountville that had been the source of fruit for some of the finest Napa Valley wines of the 1940s and 1950s.

title: Isole e Olena Cepparello 2020
bodyHtml:
#80 Wine Spectator Top 100 of 2023

The flagship wine consists of 100% Sangiovese aged in French oak barrels.
