Over the years, Paolo has refined his Cepparello by giving it more air during vinification and increasing time spent in oak from 12-14 months to 18-20 months. Although De Marchi started focusing on the use of better quality oak around 1993, it is the increased age of the vineyards themselves that have given Cepparello its overall finesse. The wine is made from a top selection of the estate’s best fruits from the vineyards in Barberino Val d’Elsa in the northern part of Chianti Classico.

97+ Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

One of the icon wines of Tuscany, the Isole e Olena 2019 Cepparello is all Sangiovese crafted by the loving hands of a winemaking legend, the great Paolo De Marchi (who finalized the sale of his beloved estate when this wine hit the market). Indeed, this wine opens a discussion on the future of this celebrated IGT Toscana, a wine that followed a strict vision and style under De Marchi. It is elegant and rich with fine aromas of black and purple fruit. It ferments in oak and ages in French barrique for 20 months, with one-third new oak. With 58,000 bottles released, this is a sure candidate for long cellar aging.

96 Points - Vinous

Time in the glass brings out gorgeous Sangiovese fruit, along with hints of blood orange, spice, cedar, mint and tobacco, all wrapped together by plush, silky contours. The purity of the fruit is just striking. In 2019, Cepparello is more finesse than power. I expect it will age beautifully over the next several decades.

95 Points - Decanter

The weather in 2019 was beautiful, with a hot, even summer with no temperature spikes, continuing into September with high variation between daytime and nighttime temperatures. Fragrant potpourri and medicinal aromas are reminiscent of the 2006, while the textured palate features pure, ripe cherry with some damp earth and even an umami hint of mushroom, cut through by bright acidity. Lively and dimensional, it's still in its youthful phase but should be superb once it's had time to grow into itself.

94 Points - James Suckling

So much licorice and fennel seed with black cherry and a hint of tomato paste. Medium body, round texture and savory flavors. Pretty and fresh at the end, with subtle flavors. Drink now or hold.

title: Saxum James Berry Vineyard White Paso Robles 2021
bodyHtml:
The James Berry White stands as Saxum’s rarest cuvee and has garnered a cult-flowing among Saxum aficionados. For us, the Grenache Blanc in Paso Robles is the best in the world, so it goes without saying that Justin’s is going to sit at the top of the tree! Always and eclectic blend, this is a rich and deep wine that shimmers with energy throughout.

Blend: 44% Grenache Blanc, 29% Roussanne, 20% Chenin Blanc, 7% Chardonnay.  Vintage production: 347 cases

title: Chateau Smith Haut Lafitte Rouge 2020
bodyHtml:
Château Smith Haut Lafitte, located in the Pessac-Léognan appellation of Bordeaux, France, is known for crafting wines of exceptional elegance and depth. The 2020 vintage is a testament to the estate’s commitment to quality, offering a bold yet balanced expression of the region’s unique terroir.

Blend and Production

The 2020 Château Smith Haut Lafitte Rouge is composed of 65% Cabernet Sauvignon, 30% Merlot, 4% Cabernet Franc, and 1% Petit Verdot. The wine was aged for 18 months in French oak barrels, with 60% new oak, enhancing its complexity and structure while preserving the integrity of the fruit.

Tasting Notes

  • Appearance: Deep garnet-purple with striking intensity.
  • Nose: Aromas of blackcurrant, chocolate-covered cherries, and licorice, layered with notes of ground cloves, wood smoke, and crushed stones.
  • Palate: Full-bodied and concentrated, with lush layers of black fruit, firm, grainy tannins, and a vibrant freshness. The finish is long and earthy, with lingering hints of spice and minerality.

Critical Acclaim

  • Jeb Dunnuck: 100 points – Described as "absolutely pure gold," highlighting its incredible richness, opulence, and aromatic complexity.
  • Robert Parker's Wine Advocate: 95+ points – Praised for its structure, depth, and vibrant energy, with a profound core of cassis, violets, and minty undertones.
  • James Suckling: 98 points – Noted for its precision, balance, and exceptional aging potential.

Serving and Cellaring

The 2020 Château Smith Haut Lafitte Rouge is best served at 60–65°F (16–18°C). Decanting for at least an hour before serving will allow the wine to fully open up, revealing its intricate layers. This vintage is built to age gracefully, with an optimal drinking window from 2025 to 2050.

Conclusion

The 2020 Château Smith Haut Lafitte Rouge is a masterpiece of balance and complexity, combining vibrant fruit, fine tannins, and remarkable depth.

title: Chateau Calon Segur 2021
bodyHtml:
Château Calon Ségur is located in the Saint Estèphe appellation of the Médoc region in Bordeaux, France. As one of the oldest estates in the Médoc, its history dates back to at least 1147. The winery is currently owned by the French insurance company Suravenir, which acquired the property in 2012 and has since implemented a significant modernization program, including a gravity-powered winery and high-density vineyard replanting. The estate is famed for the heart on its label, inspired by the 18th-century owner Marquis de Ségur, who famously declared that while he made wine at Lafite and Latour, his heart was at Calon.

Wine Description

Château Calon Ségur presents a deep purple hue and a complex sensory profile. The bouquet is highly aromatic, featuring notes of cassis, violets, black cherry, and raspberry coulis, layered with hints of pencil shavings, Indian spices, menthol, and espresso. On the palate, the wine is medium to full-bodied with a velvety, seamless texture and ultra-fine, powdery tannins. It displays impressive density and vertical intensity, balanced by fresh acidity and a long, mineral-laden finish.

Accolades

  • Vinous – 97 points

  • Wine Enthusiast – 97 points

  • Decanter – 95 points

  • The Wine Advocate – 95+

Food Pairing

This robust Saint Estèphe is best paired with rich, savoury dishes that complement its structured tannins and complex aromatics. Excellent choices include grilled ribeye steak, roasted lamb chops with asparagus, or beef Wellington. For a more regional match, consider earthy dishes featuring truffles, wild mushrooms, or aged cheeses such as Comté or Manchego.

title: Veuve Clicquot La Grande Dame 2015
bodyHtml:
Veuve Clicquot, established in 1772, is one of Champagne's most iconic houses, renowned for its pioneering spirit and dedication to quality. Madame Clicquot, affectionately known as the "Grande Dame of Champagne," revolutionized the industry in the early 19th century with innovations such as the riddling table, which clarified Champagne. Today, the house continues her legacy, crafting wines of unparalleled elegance and complexity.

La Grande Dame 2015 is a tribute to Madame Clicquot’s visionary leadership. This vintage is crafted predominantly from Pinot Noir (90%), sourced from historical Grand Cru vineyards, and complemented by 10% Chardonnay. It displays a brilliant golden hue, with a fine and persistent mousse. The nose is vibrant, offering floral notes of acacia and jasmine, alongside aromas of white fruits such as Granny Smith apple and pear, accented by citrus nuances of grapefruit and clementine. On the palate, it is elegant and precise, revealing a silky texture with flavours of white pepper, ginger, and a distinct chalky minerality. The finish is long and refined, highlighting the wine’s freshness and depth. While enjoyable now, this vintage has remarkable aging potential and will continue to evolve beautifully over the next two decades.

This exquisite Champagne pairs wonderfully with seared scallops, lobster in a light cream sauce, or aged Comté cheese. Together, these pairings elevate the wine’s depth and complexity, creating an unforgettable dining experience.

The 2015 vintage in Champagne was marked by a warm growing season, producing ripe, concentrated fruit. Veuve Clicquot’s meticulous vineyard management and blending expertise have resulted in a wine that harmoniously balances richness and elegance, reflecting the distinctive terroir of its Grand Cru vineyards.

title: Patrimony Cabernet Sauvignon 2019
bodyHtml:
Hailing from Lebanon by way of Paris, France, Georges and Daniel moved to the United States as young men and soon achieved business success. But that was just the beginning. From their family history and worldview was now imagined a fearless goal—to produce the world’s finest Cabernet Sauvignon, and to curate a lifestyle to match. From terroir to winemaking to architecture, they leave no detail unexplored, so that this wine, and this place, may never fail to astonish.

This vintage is the epitome of a terroir-driven wine that has immense power without sacrificing any elegance. The wine explodes out of the glass with boysenberry fruit, creme de cassis, cedar, cigars, crushed stone and lead pencil accompanied by a perfume of violets. Deep and full-bodied, rich with astonishing texture, it manages to stay fresh and balanced throughout with a finish that does not stop. 

98 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2019 Patrimony Cabernet Sauvignon was made with free-run juice and matured for 30 months in 100% new French oak. It has a deep ruby color and alluring tones of truffle, brown sugar and coffee to begin, opening with time to very pure cassis, boysenberry, tobacco, garrigue and aniseed. The palate is supple and fresh with surprisingly restrained, mineral-laced fruits and a fan of spicy accents across the long finish. This ultra sleek, elegant Cabernet evolves continually in the glass and has the harmonious structure it needs to go the distance in the cellar.

98 Points - Decanter

A benchmark California Cabernet Sauvignon which showcases the strength and tenacity of this revered grape. On the nose, a juxtaposition of expressive, bright fruit plus a grounded earthiness. The delicacy yet force of this wine creates a most pleasant tension that you seek to reconcile with each sip. Flavours of blackberry, bramble and dark chocolate sit side by side with floral and sweet cedar notes. Tannins display laser-sharp integration. A wine with thoughtful, intentional power.

97+ Points - Jeb Dunnuck

The 2019 Cabernet Sauvignon continues to show brilliantly. (I rated it 97-100 from barrel last year.) It has a quintessential Cabernet nose of pure crème de cassis, crushed stone, lead pencil, graphite, and tobacco that gains depth and richness with time in the glass. Deep, full-bodied, rich, and incredibly textured, yet still fresh, light on its feet, and beautifully balanced, this gorgeous Cabernet shows what's possible with the variety from Paso Robles.

95 Points - James Suckling

Deep, rich and plush on the nose showing cassis, blackberries with hints of dark olives, fennel, dark chocolate, cigar box and elderberry characters. Full-bodied and fleshy on the palate with an abundance of tannins, which are extremely fine-grained. Restrainedly opulent, deep, structured and long.

title: Chateau Angelus 2017
bodyHtml:
Produced in the Saint Emilion appellation on the Right Bank of Bordeaux, France, Chateau Angelus is a historic estate overseen by the de Boüard de Laforest family since 1782. Currently led by Stéphanie de Boüard-Rivoal, the eighth generation of her family at the helm, the winery is renowned for its philosophy of excellence and commitment to organic viticulture. The estate's name and its iconic bell logo are inspired by the three Angelus bells that can be heard from the vineyards, which are situated in a natural amphitheatre that enhances the sound of the daily call to prayer.

Wine Description

The 2017 Chateau Angelus presents a deep garnet-purple hue and a remarkably pure aromatic profile. The nose reveals a complex bouquet of black cherries, wild strawberry, and cassis, layered with sophisticated notes of black truffle, pencil shavings, and sweet tobacco. On the palate, the wine is medium to full-bodied, showcasing a dense mid-palate with tight-grained, silky tannins and a fresh, earthy character. The finish is exceptionally long and elegant, marked by an uplifting freshness that provides energy and balance.

Accolades

  • James Suckling - 97 points

  • Wine Enthusiast - 96 points

  • Decanter - 96 points

  • Robert Parker Wine Advocate - 95 points

  • Vinous - 93 points

Food Pairing

The richness and structured tannins of this wine make it a superb accompaniment to roasted lamb shanks, beef tenderloin with a mushroom duxelles, or duck confit. Its complex spice notes also pair well with game meats like wild boar or pigeon with olives.

title: Chateau Figeac 2018
bodyHtml:
Figeac is the largest estate of Saint-Emilion, covering 54 hectares (133 acres). Besides its 40 hectares (99 acres) of vines, various landscapes combine to form a balance in nature. Figeac has large areas of space which add to the majesty of the place and allow flora and fauna to flourish. Figeac has an outstanding terroir consisting of three gravelly rises. In keeping with the nature of this soil, Figeac is the Right Bank estate with the highest percentage of Cabernet. This atypical combination accounts for elegant, long-lived wines and is highly well-reputed.
 
An attractive, deep, bright purple colour. An expressive, air-light nose leads on to Figeac freshness and aromatics, followed by floral notes mingling harmoniously with nuances of fruit and underpinned by aromas of blackcurrants and raspberries. The palate is expressive and vibrant, cadenced by a clean, powerful entry, an enveloping and velvety mid-palate reminiscent of 2015 vintage, and a fresh, lean finish accompanied by tannins of finesse and minerality that recall the 2016 vintage. The greatness of this vintage is embodied by the remarkable harmony between the round and developing Merlot, the fresh and elegant Cabernet Franc, and the lace-textured, tender Cabernet Sauvignon. The Chateau Figeac 2018 delivers the perfect chord from its famous three grape varieties. Blend: 37% Merlot, 33% Cabernet Sauvignon, 30% Cabernet Franc.
 
100 Points - Wine Enthusiast
With its rich swathe of Cabernet Sauvignon, this wine has density and immense structure balanced by stunning black fruits that give impressive promise. This powerful wine is probably the greatest ever produced from this estate. Drink from 2027.  *Cellar Selection*
 
98 Points - James Suckling
A powerful, structured Figeac, offering loads of blackberry, blueberry, chocolate, walnut and mushroom with some tobacco. It's full-bodied with layered, chewy tannins that are polished and beautiful. So impressive and solid. Better than the great 2010? Time will tell. Goes on for a long time. Try after 2026.
 
98 Points - Decanter
Back to a more traditional blend after last year's frost impact, Figeac has done a wonderful job of harnessing the luxury of the vintage while maintaining freshness. This is extraordinarily focussed and precise, with a silky texture and inky depths, developing complexity as the flavours unfurl. These are big tannins, but they steal up on you, doing that subtle creep that's such a marker of the vintage. Powerful, utterly gorgeous, and a wine that will age well, this is equal to the estate's excellent 2016.
 
98 Points - Jeb Dunnuck
Reminiscent of the 2016 with its incredible purity and elegance, the 2018 Château Figeac offers a terrific perfume of crème de cassis, redcurrants, dried earth, tobacco, lead pencil, spring flowers, and exotic spice-driven nuances. Playing in the medium to full-bodied end of the spectrum, it's flawlessly balanced, has silky, polished tannins, and a stunning sense of purity. It doesn't have the sexiness of the 2015, but it's very much in the style of the 2018 vintage with its pure, elegant, haut couture-like style. And it doesn't show a hint of its 100% new oak élevage. Give bottles 4-5 years of bottle age and enjoy over the following 20-30 years. It's not the biggest or richest Saint- Emilion, yet the balance, finesse, and elegance are something to behold. I think it will check in behind the 2015 (and maybe the 2019) when all is said and done, but it's unquestionably one of the greatest Figeac in the past 20-30 years.
 
97+ Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate
The 2018 Figeac is composed of 37% Merlot, 33% Cabernet Sauvignon and 30% Cabernet Franc, with a 3.7 pH and 14% alcohol. Deep garnet-purple in colour, it soars out of the glass with opening notes of freshly crushed red and black cherries, mulberries and ripe, juicy plums, followed by hints of violets, damp soil, cedar chest, crushed rocks and pencil shavings. The medium-bodied, elegantly styled palate features bags of freshness and exquisitely ripe, beautifully poised tannins to support the bright, energetic black and red fruit layers, finishing on a lingering fragrant earth note. Rating: 97+
 
96 Points - Wine Spectator
Sleek and tightly focused, this is a racy style marked by a pure beam of cassis and cherry purée and infused with red tea, bergamot and bay hints. Very fresh and refined through the finish, with a long chalky thread lingering after everything else. Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon and Cabernet Franc. Best from 2024 through 2038.

title: Joseph Drouhin Puligny Montrachet Folatieres Premier Cru 2023
bodyHtml:
This precious and harmonious white wine originates from France, specifically within the Puligny-Montrachet Premier Cru appellation in the Côte de Beaune. "Les Folatières" is the largest Premier Cru in Puligny, situated at a mid-slope position on stony, marly limestone soils that are considered among the finest in the "Côte des Blancs". Founded in 1880, Maison Joseph Drouhin has been a pioneer in sustainable viticulture, and this cuvée represents the family's "double identity" of Burgundian tradition and innovation, managed under strict biodynamic and organic principles since the 1990s.

Wine Description

Joseph Drouhin Puligny-Montrachet Premier Cru Folatières presents a golden and bright colour. The sensory profile is complex and distinctive, featuring a nose of honey, honeysuckle, and fresh almond, which as it matures, evolves toward notes of dried fruit and delicate spice. On the palate, the wine expresses a perfect balance between freshness and a velvety, rounded texture. It is characterized by a firm structural "backbone" and an exceptionally long, refined finish with elegant floral notes. This 100% Chardonnay typically reaches an ABV of 13.5%. While some Folatières fruit is sourced from partner growers, all are selected according to Drouhin's rigorous organic and biodynamic standards.

title: Bussola Amarone della Valpolicella Classico Riserva 2013
bodyHtml:
The Bussola Amarone Classico Riserva 2023 is from Italy, specifically the Veneto region in the Valpolicella Classica subregion. The winery is a family run operation, now managed by Tommaso Bussola's sons, Paolo and Giuseppe. Tommaso Bussola, a former stonemason, took over his uncle's small domaine in 1977 and later drove a turning point in 1983 by personally selecting the grapes for Amarone and Recioto. The winery's philosophy emphasizes patience, innovation, and a deep respect for nature, aiming to make the best possible normale wines while selecting the best grapes for its elite 'TB' (Tommaso Bussola) line, which includes the Riserva.

Wine Description

This Riserva is a powerful, rich, and intense red wine. The wine's varietal composition typically consists of Corvina, Corvinone, and Rondinella, often in a blend of 45% Corvina, 30% Corvinone, and 25% Rondinella. The wine presents a rich, dark garnet red colour. The aroma is compact, offering notes of dried plum and porcini mushrooms, with an undercurrent of sandalwood. On the palate, it is described as elegant, soft, and robust, with fine tannins that dry the palate. Stylistically, it is powerful, almost baroque, and full of dried fruits and spices. Given the extensive maturation process—66 months in wood followed by two years in bottle before release—this wine is built with a substantial structure that promises excellent ageing potential, making the optimal drinking window very long. The winery is a participant in the SQNPI integrated farming program and practises organic viticulture, which aims to eliminate the use of herbicides and chemical pesticides.

Accolades

  • Enoteca Corsi - 97/100.

  • Falstaff - 92/100.

Food Pairing

The wine's bold structure and rich flavour profile make it an excellent match for equally robust dishes. Suggested pairings include elaborate main courses such as pheasant with walnuts and truffle or duck. It pairs wonderfully with braised meats and slow cooked stews. The wine's rich character is also complemented by aged cheeses like 36 month old Parmigiano Reggiano, Taleggio, or Pecorino di Fossa. For a regional pairing, it is classic alongside Risotto all'Amarone or fresh pasta with a duck ragu. Finally, for dessert, its richness can stand up to dark chocolate.

Vintage Quality

The 2023 vintage in the Valpolicella Classica zone was described as erratic and atypical, marked by cooler temperatures in spring, but persistent rain and localized hail in July. Harvest was slightly later than average for most growers. Rigorous selection of grapes was fundamental due to these challenging conditions, and the vintage is expected to favour Amarone over lighter Valpolicella. The Amarone wines from 2023 are tracking to be dense and generous in both alcohol and fruit, offering a rich structure with notable ageing potential.

title: Sette Ponti Vigna dell Impero 2019
bodyHtml:
This rare and historic red wine originates from the Valdarno di Sopra DOC in the heart of Tuscany, Italy. Tenuta Sette Ponti’s Vigna dell'Impero (Vineyard of the Empire) is a flagship "cru" that represents the estate’s most traditional and historic side. The wine is sourced from a single, three-hectare terraced vineyard planted in 1935 by Duke Amedeo of Savoy-Aosta, making it one of the oldest and most prestigious Sangiovese sites in Tuscany. The winery’s philosophy for this label is one of extreme fidelity to the terroir; it is produced only in exceptional vintages, released in limited, numbered bottles, and farmed organically.

Wine Description

The Tenuta Sette Ponti Vigna dell'Impero 2019 presents an intense ruby red colour with elegant garnet reflections. The sensory profile is exceptionally pure and ethereal, featuring a complex bouquet of sour cherry, blood orange, and red berries, woven together with sophisticated notes of leather, tobacco, and dried Mediterranean herbs. On the palate, the wine is medium-to-full-bodied and remarkably gessoso (chalky) in texture, showcasing silky, fine-grained tannins and a vibrant, saline acidity. It is characterized by its tension and structural elegance, leading to a long, mineral-driven finish with persistent hints of wildflower and spicy oak. This 100% Sangiovese has an ABV of 14.5% and was aged for at least 24 months in large oak casks to preserve its varietal character, followed by 12 months of refinement in the bottle.

Food Pairing

The refined tannins and lively acidity of this old-vine Sangiovese make it a superb companion for sophisticated Tuscan cuisine. It pairs perfectly with grilled or roasted red meats, such as a traditional Bistecca alla Fiorentina, and wild game including venison or feathered game like pheasant. Its earthy and savory profile also complements rich pasta dishes featuring porcini mushrooms or truffles, as well as well-matured hard cheeses like Pecorino Toscano or 36-month Parmigiano-Reggiano.

Vintage Quality

The 2019 vintage in Tuscany is widely celebrated as a benchmark year, particularly for Sangiovese. A mild winter followed by a hot yet breezy summer allowed for uniform budding and slow, even ripening. September provided ideal conditions for the harvest, resulting in fruit with exceptional phenolic maturity and concentration while maintaining a "racy" freshness. Critics have noted that the 2019 Vigna dell'Impero is one of the most balanced and elegant releases to date, showing a transparency and finesse that allows the 87-year-old vines to truly speak of their origin.

title: Guado Al Tasso 2003
bodyHtml:
This exceptional wine hails from Italy, specifically the Bolgheri region on the Tuscan coast. Guado al Tasso is crafted by Marchesi Antinori, one of Italy’s most esteemed wine families with over six centuries of winemaking heritage. The estate covers approximately 320 hectares near the Tyrrhenian Sea, where the unique terroir of alluvial soils and maritime breezes shapes wines of remarkable elegance and power.

Wine Description

The 2003 Guado al Tasso is a deep ruby red with garnet reflections, showing the maturity of its age. On the nose, it opens with rich aromas of ripe dark berries, plum, cassis, and hints of tobacco, complemented by notes of leather, cedar, and sweet spices. The palate is full-bodied and lush, with velvety tannins enveloping flavours of blackberry, dark cherry, mocha, and a touch of graphite. Well-integrated oak provides subtle vanilla nuances. Its finish is long and persistent, marked by balanced acidity and savoury undertones that give it finesse despite the warm vintage.

This vintage is typically composed of Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, and Syrah, though the exact percentages vary by year. Best enjoyed now through the next couple of years to capture its mature tertiary nuances.

Accolades

  • Wine Spectator - 93 points.

  • Decanter - 92 points.

Food Pairing

Pair this wine with grilled ribeye, roasted lamb with rosemary, or a mushroom risotto. These dishes complement the wine’s depth and structure beautifully. Together, they create an unforgettable dining experience.

title: La Chapelle De La Mission Haut Brion 2022
bodyHtml:
Château La Mission Haut Brion, located in the Pessac Léognan appellation of Bordeaux, is a legendary estate with roots dating back to the 16th century. Now under the stewardship of Domaine Clarence Dillon, the estate shares ownership with the neighbouring Château Haut Brion, both revered for their meticulous winemaking and historical significance. La Chapelle is the second wine of the estate, crafted with the same precision and terroir-driven philosophy as its grand vin.

Wine Description
This 2022 vintage offers a deep ruby colour with violet highlights. The nose opens with refined notes of black cherry, blueberry, and cedar, underpinned by subtle touches of graphite and pencil shaving. On the palate, it is medium to full bodied, with a supple texture and elegant tannins, delivering flavours of ripe plum, blackberry, dark chocolate, and a hint of forest floor. The finish is long and layered, showcasing freshness and finesse. 

Accolades

  • Wine Advocate – 92+ points.

  • James Suckling – 95 points.

  • Vinous – 91 points.

Food Pairing
Pair this refined Bordeaux with herb-crusted lamb, duck confit, or a mushroom risotto. Aged cheeses like Comté or aged Gouda also complement its depth and savoury character.

title: Damilano Barolo Cannubi 2018
bodyHtml:
Founded in 1890, Damilano is one of the historic wineries of Barolo, passed down through generations and today managed by the great-grandchildren of founder Giuseppe Borgogno. The Cannubi vineyard, often called the heart of Barolo, is a legendary cru whose distinctive terroir imparts a singular elegance and complexity to its wines. Damilano’s dedication to tradition and vineyard expression is at the core of its winemaking philosophy.

Made exclusively from 100% Nebbiolo, this wine reveals a luminous garnet colour with delicate orange reflections. The nose is lifted and complex, offering classic aromas of red cherry, rose petals, violet, licorice, tobacco, and subtle balsamic notes. On the palate, it is dry and full bodied, showing fine-grained tannins balanced by fresh acidity. Red berry fruit, leather, cocoa, and earthy undertones glide through a persistent, mineral-driven finish.

Accolades
Wine Spectator – 93 points
James Suckling – 94 points
Wine Advocate – 94 points

Food Pairing
Ideal with braised meats, wild mushroom risotto, and truffle-infused dishes. Firm aged cheeses such as Parmigiano Reggiano also make excellent companions.

title: Catena 'Nicolas Catena Zapata' 2004
bodyHtml:
The 2004 Catena 'Nicolás Catena Zapata' is a flagship red blend from Bodega Catena Zapata, one of Argentina's most wineries. This wine exemplifies the winery's dedication to producing world-class wines that reflect the unique terroir of Mendoza.

Vineyard and Production

  • Grape Composition: Predominantly Cabernet Sauvignon (72%) and Malbec (28%).

  • Vineyards:

    • La Pirámide Vineyard: Located at 3,117 feet (950 meters) in the Agrelo District, Luján de Cuyo Region.

    • Domingo Vineyard: Situated at 3,675 feet (1,120 meters) in the Villa Bastías District, Tupungato Region, Uco Valley.

    • Adrianna Vineyard: At an elevation of 4,757 feet (1,450 meters) in the Gualtallary District, Tupungato Region, Uco Valley.

  • Soil: Diverse compositions ranging from deep alluvial loam with clay in La Pirámide, gravel-covered surfaces in Domingo, to alluvial, gravelly soils with limestone deposits in Adrianna.

  • Vinification: Hand-harvested grapes undergo de-stemming and whole berry fermentation in new French oak barrels for 18 days, followed by 24 months of aging in French oak.

Tasting Notes

  • Appearance: Saturated black-purple hue.

  • Aroma: A complex bouquet featuring notes of pain grillé, mineral, espresso, saddle leather, cassis, black currant, and black raspberry.

  • Palate: Opulently textured with ripe, sweet flavors, balanced by elegance and power. The wine exhibits a harmonious integration of fruit, tannins, and acidity, leading to a long, persistent finish.

Critical Acclaim

  • Robert Parker's Wine Advocate: 98 points. Described as Argentina’s equivalent of a great vintage of Lafite-Rothschild, with potential to age gracefully for decades.

  • Decanter: 96 points. Noted for its firm structure and potential for further development.

  • James Suckling: 95 points. Praised for its depth, complexity, and refined character.

Serving and Pairing

Decant the wine for at least an hour before serving at 16-18°C (61-64°F) to allow its full expression. This robust and elegant blend pairs exceptionally well with grilled meats, roasted lamb, game dishes, and aged cheeses.

title: Chateau d'Yquem 2022
bodyHtml:
Chateau d'Yquem 2022 is a Premier Cru Supérieur sweet white wine from the Sauternes appellation in the Bordeaux region of France. The estate, managed by Lorenzo Pasquini and owned by the LVMH group, is renowned for its centuries old commitment to quality and is the only Sauternes to hold the highest rank in the 1855 classification. This 2022 vintage is historic as it marks the estate's first certified organic production.

Wine Description

This vintage features a complex and energetic bouquet of rose, confit citrus, exotic fruits, and orange marmalade. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied, lush, and powerful, offering deep flavours of clementine, wild honey, quince, and roasted meringue with hints of saffron and turmeric. Stylistically, it is characterized by an incredible harmony between its high residual sugar—reaching 160 grams per litre—and a racy acidity that ensures a fresh, non-cloying profile. The finish is exceptionally long and zesty, often lasting over 60 seconds. The varietal composition is 80% Sémillon and 20% Sauvignon Blanc. Its optimal drinking window is projected from 2027 to 2100.

Accolades

  • James Suckling – 100 points

  • Vinous – 98 points

  • Robert Parker Wine Advocate – 98 points

  • Wine Spectator – 97 points

title: Mayacamas Cabernet Sauvignon Mount Veeder 2019
bodyHtml:
Founded in 1889, Mayacamas stands as one of the most storied vineyard and winery operations in the history of American wine. Through its more than 125 years of production, Mayacamas has earned its place as a standard-bearer of traditional winemaking, and the source of some of California’s most iconic and longest-lived bottles.

Mayacamas Mt. Veeder Cabernet Sauvignon opens with lilac, dried sage, and graphite. Wild mountain blueberry, maraschino cherry, and blackberry round out the fruit profile. A very elegant wine with wonderful detail and nuance.

97 Points - Vinous

The 2019 Cabernet Sauvignon is a pretty rich, bombastic wine, especially for Mayacamas. A blast of dark fruit, incense, tobacco, licorice, spice and mocha hits the palate. I would give the 2019 at least a few years in bottle to settle down, as it is quite the powerhouse today. This is an unusually flamboyant wine with plenty of richness and a bit less in the way of subtlety. The opulence of the vintage comes through loud and clear.

96 Points - Wine Spectator

Loaded with character and energy, this version reveals heavy notes of zesty sweet bay leaf and sassafras that infuse a core of steeped red currant and mulberry fruit, all carried by bright acidity and iron-laced tannins. The long finish pulls everything together, with the fruit, savory and mineral elements in harmony. Showing an old-school touch, this has a long life ahead.

94 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2019 Cabernet Sauvignon remains true to the winery's historic style, offering complex notes of dried herbs and mixed berries, carried across the palate by a wine that's medium-bodied, crisp and somewhat lean by modern Napa standards. It finishes long and dusty, promising well for the future.

title: Domaine Michel Gros Morey Saint Denis "En la Rue de Vergy" 2022
bodyHtml:
Winery Background:
Domaine Michel Gros, established in 1830, is a family-run estate in Vosne-Romanée, Burgundy. Over six generations, the Gros family has cultivated a reputation for producing elegant and expressive wines, reflecting their commitment to traditional winemaking practices and respect for terroir.

Wine Description:
This 2022 Pinot Noir showcases a vibrant ruby hue. The nose reveals enticing aromas of cranberry, white strawberry, and subtle black fruits, complemented by a delicate hint of tobacco. On the palate, fine tannins and well-judged acidity harmonize gracefully with the fruit profile. The wine's richness is balanced by a tangible frisson on the finish, promising complexity and depth with further aging.

Accolades:

  • Neal Martin: 90-93 points.

Food Pairing:
This wine pairs excellently with roasted duck, game birds, or mushroom-based dishes. These pairings highlight the wine’s depth and character, creating an unforgettable dining experience.

title: Stag's Leap Wine Cellars Cabernet Sauvignon SLV 2019
bodyHtml:
Considered one of the "first growths" of Napa Valley, Stag's Leap Wine Cellars produces renowned Cabernet Sauvignon from its historic Stags Leap District estate vineyards.

This S.L.V. Cabernet Sauvignon offers generous dark fruit aromas of black currant, plum and candied fig along with cocoa dust. On the palate the wine has dense, yet polished, tannins that meld with layers of dark fruit, fig and violet. The tannin structure, dark fruit, and pleasing minerality point to this wine’s ability to age.

96 Points - James Suckling

Deep yet floral nose with pure cassis, blackberry and blueberry concentrate, as well as hints of sandalwood and pine. Quite ample on the palate, laden with velvety tannins in a mealy form. Rich and primary, yet juicy and supple. Densely packed.

95+ Points - Jeb Dunnuck

Pure creme de cassis, violets, and lead pencil shaving nuances emerge from the 2019 Cabernet Sauvignon S.L.V., a concentrated, structured, almost austere 2019 that has terrific balance as well as a great mid-palate. Possessing youthful tannins and remarkable purity of fruit, this ultra-classic, flawlessly put together Napa Valley Cabernet Sauvignon will benefit from 4-5 years of bottle age and keep for 20-25 years. Count me impressed – this is brilliant juice. 

95 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2019 Cabernet Sauvignon S.L.V. features perfumed aromas of violets and cassis. It's medium to full-bodied on the palate, nicely elegant while being powerful and sturdy at the same time. No, it's not made in a modern, blockbuster style, but it's true to its heritage, with subtle herb shadings and a long, silky finish.

title: Domaine Faiveley Corton Clos des Cortons Grand Cru 2022
bodyHtml: Founded in 1825, Bourgognes Faiveley has been handed down from father to son for over 175 years. As the sixth generation to take the reins, Francois Faiveley manages, with equal amounts passion and competence, the largest family domaine in Burgundy. Methodically reconstructing vineyards fractured by French inheritance laws, Bourgognes Faiveley today owns more appellations in their entirety (monopoles) than any other domaine in Burgundy.

title: Naudin Echezeaux Grand Cru 2023
bodyHtml:
This exceptional red wine originates from France, specifically the Burgundy region, within the Côte de Nuits subregion. The wine is produced by Domaine Naudin-Ferrand, overseen by owner and winemaker Claire Naudin. Claire continues a long family tradition, having inherited 22 hectares of vines from her father, Henri Naudin, in the late 1990s. The estate is renowned for reflecting the unique terroir of Burgundy, with a focus on sustainable and environmentally-friendly viticultural practices, showing a commitment to organic and biodynamic viticulture.

Wine Description

The Naudin Echezeaux Grand Cru is a red wine crafted from 100% Pinot Noir. Echezeaux is known for producing powerful yet delicate wines. While still very young, Grand Cru Echézeaux wines from this vintage exhibit a beautiful finesse and great elegance. Characteristic notes often include red fruits and minerality, with a long, cohesive, and persistent finish.

Food Pairing

This Grand Cru Pinot Noir is a superb partner for refined French cuisine. It pairs beautifully with game birds and game animals. Other excellent pairings include roasts, sirloin or rib of beef, and fine cheeses such as Époisses.

title: Raen Fort Ross - Seaview Pinot Noir 2021
bodyHtml:
This cool-climate red wine originates from the Fort Ross-Seaview AVA in Sonoma County, California. Established in 1994 by South African natives Lester and Linda Schwartz, Fort Ross Vineyard was a pioneering project on the steep, rugged ridges of the extreme West Sonoma Coast. The winery operates with a philosophy of minimal intervention, utilizing only estate-grown fruit from 30 individual vineyard blocks perched above the coastal fog line to ensure optimal ripening and concentration.

Wine Description

The 2021 Fort Ross Seaview Pinot Noir is remarkably deep in colour, ranging from a semi-opaque ruby to a dense garnet hue. The bouquet is complex and evolving, opening with a foundation of red and dark berry aromas, such as black raspberry and boysenberry, followed by delicate rose petal, clove, and savory hints of sage. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied and generous, showcasing exuberant flavours of black cherry, juicy plum, and bramble berries supported by soft, velvety tannins. A hallmark spine of youthful acidity provides fine structure and leads to a persistent, spicy finish with notes of toasted cedar and orange peel. This wine is a meticulous blend of Calera, Pommard, Swan, and Dijon 115 clones and has an ABV of 13.8%.

Food Pairing

The robust structure and vibrant acidity of this Pinot Noir make it an ideal companion for grilled ribeye steak or barbecue pork ribs. It also pairs elegantly with roasted poultry such as duck or smoked turkey, as well as earthy dishes like mushroom risotto. For a seafood option, its coastal profile complements meaty grilled salmon or tuna steaks.

Vintage Quality

The 2021 vintage was marked by a second consecutive year of drought, which forced vine roots to dig deep and resulted in lower-than-average yields with intense flavour concentration. Moderate summer temperatures and the absence of heatwaves allowed for an even ripening process, producing wines regarded for their density, aromatic purity, and exceptional quality.

title: Chateau Cos d'Estournel 2015
bodyHtml:
The rigor of the selection combined with the large proportion of Cabernet Sauvignon has revealed a wine with unique balance, very precise, very pure with a wide-ranging of aromatic complexity, both fruity and spicy. On the palate, the tannins are silky and intense, with a particularly long and brilliant finish.

98 Points - James Suckling 

Super aromas of nutmeg, cloves and dried flowers with plums and blackberries. Subtle yet so complex. Full-bodied, tight and integrated with ultra-fine tannins and a beautiful finish. Lasts for minutes. Very, very Cos. Harmony. Texturally marvellous. Drink in 2024.

97 Points - Wine Enthusiast

Ripe, dusty tannins give a dry edge to the full, rich fruits. It has a structure that comes out of old Cabernet vines that form the core of this wine. Dark, full and with considerable concentration, the wine is dense and will need many years to develop.

95+ Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate 

Composed of 76% Cabernet Sauvignon, 23.5% Merlot and 1.5% Cabernet Franc, the deep garnet-purple coloured 2015 Cos d'Estournel is muted at this very early stage. The nose offers fleeting glimpses at provocative cherry tart, chocolate mint, baked redcurrants, warm cassis and wild blueberry scents plus suggestions of lilacs, cinnamon stick and Indian spices. Medium to full-bodied, the palate explodes with vibrant red and black fruit bursts and tons of exotic spice accents, framed by super ripe, super firm tannins and a lovely line of freshness, finishing very long.

95 Points - Decanter

Rich fruit that is full of that classic exotic Cos spice, yet more restrained than in the past with a slatey graphite base. Beautifully put together; an exciting wine that will grow in complexity and flavour.

93 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

The 2015 Cos D'Estournel is a classic wine from this estate and a terrific effort from the northern Médoc. Compared to both 2007 and 2004 by the estate and representing only 39% of the total production, it offers a fresh, classy bouquet of crème de cassis, black raspberries, toasty oak, graphite and damp earth. Made from 75% Cabernet Sauvignon, 23% Merlot and the rest Cabernet Franc, this medium to full-bodied 2015 has solid mid-palate depth, fine, polished tannin, and a great finish. It’s going to improve with short-term cellaring and keep for two decades.

title: Frescobaldi Ripe Al Convento Brunello di Montalcino Riserva 2018
bodyHtml:
Frescobaldi CastelGiocondo Ripe al Convento Brunello di Montalcino Riserva originates from Italy, within the prestigious Tuscany region and the world-renowned Brunello di Montalcino DOCG subregion. Owned by the historic Frescobaldi family, the CastelGiocondo estate dominates the southwest slopes of Montalcino. The operational philosophy behind this flagship Riserva revolves around exalting the ultimate expression of a single, highly privileged vineyard plot—"Ripe al Convento"—perched at an elevation of 450 meters on galestro and schistose soils. By harvesting only the finest Sangiovese fruit from these sun-drenched, well-ventilated heights, the estate crafts a classic Tuscan icon defined by longevity, power, and precise regional identity.

Wine Description

This red wine presents a brilliant ruby red appearance in the glass, holding its deep intensity right to the rim. It possesses a full-bodied, dense, and structured body framed by a mouthfilling, silky, and polished texture. The sensory profile is rich, complex, and evolving, opening with an expressive bouquet of ripe cherries, wild raspberries, and pomegranate, interwoven with floral rose petal notes and an intricate kaleidoscope of tertiary aromas, including graphite, bitter cocoa, cigar box, and dried autumn leaves. On the potent yet well-balanced palate, it delivers a deep stream of dark stone fruit, plums, and sweet spices, held together by a dense, fine-grained, and chalky tannic backbone alongside a refreshing natural acidity. The finish is remarkably long, resonant, and persistent, leaving a lingering impression of wild herbs, mineral graphite, and subtle leather notes.

  • Varietal Composition: 100% Sangiovese (Sangiovese Grosso).

  • Stylistic Notes: Celebrated for its regal composure and tertiary depth, the grapes undergo rigorous hand selection in the vineyard and on cellar sorting tables. Fermentation in stainless steel with controlled pumping over is followed by extensive aging in oak casks. In accordance with Riserva requirements, the wine matures for over five years prior to commercial release, including dedicated refinement in bottle.

  • ABV: 15.0%.

  • Organic Status: While the estate practices precision viticulture to maintain soil health across its high-altitude vineyards, this commercial bottling is not certified organic.

Food Pairing

The dense tannic architecture, elevated alcohol warmth, and complex savory profile of this Brunello Riserva make it a stellar match for rich, slow-cooked gastronomy.

  • Meats: Pairs beautifully with roasted red meats, grilled Florentine T-bone steak (Bistecca alla Fiorentina), or braised beef short ribs.

  • Game & Ragoûts: Suggested pairings include traditional Tuscan wild boar ragù over pappardelle, braised venison, or roasted pheasant.

  • Cheese: Matches gracefully with structured platters of mature, hard cheeses, particularly aged Pecorino Toscano or Parmigiano-Reggiano.

title: Inglenook Rubicon 2013
bodyHtml:
In 1879, Finnish explorer and adventurer Gustave Niebaum searched the Napa Valley with the goal of establishing a wine estate to rival the finest chateau of France. For decades his wines won acclaim and remain some of the most admired in American wine history's classic period. By the mid-1960's, his property was divided, and estate-wine production ceased.

A decade later, Francis Ford Coppola purchased 1,500 acres of this historic property and revived Captain Niebaum's fine winemaking tradition. In 1995, Niebaum-Coppola acquired the remainder of the property and restored the Inglenook Estate to its original dimensions.

Highly expressive with extraordinary quality and character, Inglenook's 2013 Rubicon offers upfront aromas of cherries, black currants, and dark chocolate with substantial presence of oak, toast, and floral notes that continue evolving as the wine opens up. A dense, voluminous palate imbued with very fine tannins showcases flavors of dark crushed berries, cassis, and smoky wood.

As the flavors gradually broaden, nuances of tobacco leaves and spices emerge. There is a precision and elegance to this vintage, which finishes with freshness due to the balanced natural acidity. Expect beautiful development as this wine matures.

97 Points - James Suckling

An aromatic and complex red with currant, white-chocolate and rose-petal character. Full-bodied, tight and polished. Fine and long.

97 Points - Decanter

Starting to show its full character at seven years old, this is definitely in sight of peak drinking, although going nowhere for another couple of decades. Sit back and enjoy the layers of blueberry and cassis primary fruits, now softening into campfire, leather and black truffle edging. This is so good, with a still muscular structure that is turning into a slow stretch of supple tannins.

93 Points - Wine & Spirits

93 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

title: Chateau Lafon Rochet 2019
bodyHtml:
Introduction

Château Lafon Rochet 2019 is a red wine from France, produced in the Bordeaux region and the Saint Estèphe appellation. The estate's origins date back to the 17th century. Château Lafon Rochet was distinguished in 1855 by gaining the title of Grand Cru Classé. The winery, which features a distinctive golden yellow façade, is a recognized standard of the Saint Estèphe appellation.

Wine Description

The wine displays a vibrant ruby purple or intense red colour with purple reflections. The aromatic profile is pure, precise, and elegant, showing lots of ripe currant, plum, tobacco, Asian spice, and cedar pencil aromatics. Red fruits such as raspberry and redcurrant emerge on the nose. The varietal composition is a blend of 65% Cabernet Sauvignon, 30% Merlot, and 5% Cabernet Franc. It is a medium to full bodied wine with a compact core of fresh black and ripe red fruit. The palate is fresh and saline, with fine-boned, seamless tannins. Stylistically, it is classic, concentrated, and elegant, showing nobility and a 'crunchy' finish. The wine is aged for 12 months in barrels. The finish is long and elegant with very elegant tannins. The ABV is either 14.3% or 14%. The optimal drinking window is from 2025 to 2050 or 2023 through 2038. The winery experiments with organic and biodynamic farming techniques, with nearly 100% of the vines farmed using organic methods in 2016.

Accolades

95 Points — Jeb Dunnuck

“Brilliant stuff... pure, precise, elegant, yet at the same time concentrated. Showing lots of ripe currant, plum, tobacco, Asian spice, and cedar pencil aromatics... beautifully done and well worth seeking out.”

95 Points — Vinous (Antonio Galloni)

“The 2019 Lafon-Rochet is every bit as compelling today as it was from barrel. There is a feeling of elegance to the 2019 that is so striking... not huge nor obvious, as some Saint-Estèphes are, but it is absolutely compelling.”

94 Points — James Suckling

“Ripe blackcurrants and blackberries with hints of sweet tobacco, walnuts and dark chocolate... Bold and solid, classic St.-Estephe.”

Food Pairing

This wine is a superb match for meat dishes. Suggested pairings include veal, pork, beef, lamb, duck, and game. It also pairs well with roasted, braised, stewed, and grilled dishes.

Vintage Quality

The 2019 vintage shows the best of the vintage in Saint Estèphe with its pure, precise, and concentrated style. The growing season produced a wine with plenty of depth and structure to support sustained bottle age. The terroir of Château Lafon Rochet, with its gravel and clay soils, helps to regulate water stress, contributing to the wine's quality.

title: Les Forts de Latour 2016
bodyHtml:
The leader on the Left Bank in number of first growth classified producers within its boundaries, Pauillac has more than any of the other appellations, at three of the five. Layers of gravel in the Pauillac region are key to its wines’ character and quality. The layers offer excellent drainage in the relatively flat topography of the region allowing water to run off into “jalles” or streams, which subsequently flow off into the Gironde.

The vineyards of the Chateau Latour have been producing wines since the 16th century. Today, the vineyards in production cover 80 hectares, including 48 around the chateau, known as the "Enclos." This Enclos consists of a ridge that peaks at 16 meters above the level of the Gironde.

Beautiful dark and intense crimson hue. Aromatically very pure and enticing with ripe red and black fruits, delicious cocoa and tobacco notes and a hint of citrus zest. Succulent on the attack with a powerful mouthfeel and great tension mid-palate that leads to a lingering, languorous finish.

96 Points - James Suckling

The fresh currant and violet aromas are so complex and beautiful on the nose. Full body, ultra-refined tannins and lovely tannin tension. Shows focus and such finesse. Beautiful finish.

95 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The Les Forts de Latour is superb, unwinding in the glass with notions of blackcurrants, wild berries, sweet loamy soil, cigar wrapper and English walnuts. Medium to full-bodied, deep and layered, it’s concentrated and tightly wound, with superb depth at the core, lively acids and ripe, powdery tannins. This is an impeccably balanced, utterly classical Forts de Latour worth a special effort to seek out.

95 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

The second wine of this great chateau, the Les Forts De Latour continues to impress. I commented on release that it was the best wine in the vintage, and my opinion hasn't changed. This beauty offers plenty of classic Latour character as well as notes of blackcurrants, saddle leather, lead pencil shavings, and dried flowers. It's a gorgeous Pauillac.

95 Points - Decanter

Violet scented dark black cherries and figs on the nose, quite powerful. Tannins are generous but they're juicy and plump, soft almost chalky, they have a really great impact, filling the mouth together with the fruit. Everything has melded together, super balanced and all very harmonious - still clearly powerful with precision and sculpting of the fruit and a long finish with the flavours going on and on.

94+ Points - Wine Enthusiast

This is a great wine, with superb tannins and rich fruit flavors that are in balance. Made from 64% Cabernet Sauvignon, the palate is dominated by black-currant flavor and a pleasant structure from the very fine tannins.

94 Points - Wine Spectator

A bit fleshier and more caressing than a typical Pauillac, this has flavors of warm fig, currant and blackberry preserves inlaid with charcoal and smoldering tobacco notes. There's grip for sure and a twinge of warm cast iron on the finish, but the fruit detail keeps the upper hand throughout, showcasing the purity on the finish. Very, very solid.

title: Giacomo Fenocchio Barolo Riserva 'Bussia 90 di' 2019
bodyHtml:
Wine Description

The wine displays a deep garnet red colour with subtle orange reflections. The bouquet is intense and typical of Nebbiolo, featuring captivating notes of rose, truffle, and leather. On the palate, it reveals hints of black cherry, truffle, spices, and aromatic herbs. The texture is subtle and refined, supported by velvety tannins.

Food Pairing

Suggested pairings include game dishes like venison or pheasant, rich red meats, and stews. It is also magnificent with traditional Piedmontese food such as truffle-based dishes (e.g., risotto with white truffle) and aged cheeses like Castelmagno or Gorgonzola.

title: Domaine Jamet Cote Rotie 2022
bodyHtml:
This benchmark dry red wine originates from France, produced in the steep, terraced vineyards of the Côte-Rôtie appellation in the Northern Rhône Valley. Domaine Jamet, steered by Jean-Paul Jamet alongside Corinne and their son Loïc, is widely considered the torchbearer of traditional, non-interventionist Côte-Rôtie. The flagship cuvée is an intricate assemblage of fruit drawn from more than 25 distinct lieux-dits across the appellation, seamlessly uniting the mica-schist soils of the Côte Brune (parcels such as Côte Brune, Chavaroche, and Moutonne) with the pale, granite-rich soils of the Côte Blonde (such as Lancement). Jamet remains celebrated for its steadfast commitment to high whole-cluster fermentation and neutral oak maturation, crafting wines defined by site transparency, savory complexity, and structural longevity.

Wine Description

In the glass, the 2022 vintage displays a deep, saturated ruby-purple core with brilliant magenta reflections at the rim. The nose is intensely aromatic and quintessential Jamet, exploding with aromas of wild black raspberry, dark cherry, and cassis, seamlessly framed by pungent savory notes of crushed black peppercorn, tapenade, smoked bacon fat, dried violet florals, iron filings, and wild scrubland garrigue. On the palate, the wine is medium-to-full-bodied, showing remarkable depth and flesh balanced by an energetic mineral drive. Ripe, fine-grained, powdery tannins provide firm structural architecture around a concentrated core of dark fruit, leading into a long, savory, schist-tinged finish. Vinified from 100% Syrah (with negligible co-planted Viognier rarely exceeding 1%), Jamet utilizes a high proportion of whole clusters (typically 80% to 100%). Fermentation relies exclusively on indigenous yeasts in stainless steel, followed by 22 months of aging in French oak demi-muids and barriques, with only about 15% new oak to preserve terroir purity. The alcohol by volume sits at 13.5%.

Food Pairing

The intense savory aromatics, peppery spice, firm tannic structure, and energetic acidity make this Côte-Rôtie a profound partner for savory game and roasted meats. Ideal culinary matches include roasted squab or pigeon, pan-seared duck breast with a green peppercorn and blackberry reduction, braised venison shanks, roasted rack of lamb crusted with rosemary, and slow-cooked beef short ribs. It also harmonizes with earthy dishes highlighting wild morels or black truffles, cured charcuterie like wild boar saucisson, and mature French cheeses such as Saint-Marcellin, Rigotte de Condrieu, or aged Comté.

Vintage Quality

The 2022 vintage across the Northern Rhône was characterized by a warm, dry summer with notable heat spikes that accelerated ripening, balanced by well-timed late-summer rains that replenished the vines and ensured phenolic completion. In the hands of Jean-Paul and Loïc Jamet, the old vines and high proportion of whole clusters provided exceptional freshness, aromatic lift, and structural framing that offset the warm conditions. The 2022 Domaine Jamet Côte-Rôtie delivers slightly richer fruit volume and immediate generosity compared to the classical 2021, yet preserves the savory tension, peppery precision, and tannic backbone required to evolve gracefully in the cellar for 15 to 25+ years.

Accolades

  • 96 Points - Decanter:

    A tasting through the different terroirs in this wine revealed a fresh, intense, highly structured year; not as generous as 2019 or 2020, certainly more austere, and will take longer to come round. Many of the samples had an appealing floral expression, occasionally with herbal nuances from the use of whole bunches, and often really quite dark, dense black fruit on the palate. Tannins, while not green, are decidedly tight and will take time to finesse. A vintage where patience is required and which I suspect will shut down shortly after bottling. (MW)

  • 95 Points - James Suckling:

    A velvety, balanced and textural Cote-Rotie with lots of crunch. Notes of dark cherries, spiced plums, dried herbs, stones and peppercorns. It's medium-bodied with fine tannins and fresh acidity. Lively and bright with tension. Full of vitality and transparency with a long, precise finish.

title: Chateau Figeac 2021
bodyHtml:
Château Figeac, a Premier Grand Cru Classé estate in Saint-Émilion, is celebrated for its unique identity and dedication to producing exceptional wines. With a history dating back to the 2nd century and a reputation solidified in the modern era, Figeac embodies the balance of tradition and innovation in Bordeaux winemaking.

Wine Description

The 2021 vintage of Château Figeac exudes elegance and finesse, characteristic of a cooler vintage. Its medium ruby color hints at its refined nature. On the nose, aromas of red currants, blackberries, and violets are beautifully interwoven with earthy notes and hints of graphite. The palate is precise and fresh, showcasing a harmonious blend of red and dark fruits, underscored by a vibrant acidity and polished tannins. Its medium body and delicate structure lead to a graceful, mineral-driven finish, reflecting the château’s hallmark style.

Food Pairing

Pair this wine with roasted duck breast, veal medallions, or a wild mushroom risotto. Together, these dishes highlight the wine’s depth and elegance, creating a memorable dining experience.

Vintage Quality

The 2021 vintage posed challenges with cooler weather and careful selection, yet Château Figeac crafted a wine of remarkable poise and freshness, emphasizing finesse over power and promising graceful aging.

title: Joseph Phelps Cabernet Sauvignon Napa Valley 2022
bodyHtml:
This exceptional red wine originates from the United States, specifically the renowned Napa Valley region in California. Founded in 1973 by visionary Joseph Phelps, the winery became a pioneer in the region, helping to shape the modern landscape of Napa Valley winemaking. Guided by a philosophy of estate growth and meticulous craftsmanship, the estate focuses on showcasing the distinct terroir of its premier vineyard selections, blending tradition with modern precision.

Wine Description

Deep garnet purple in color, this wine opens with an enticing, fragrant bouquet of fresh cassis, dark plum, and juicy black cherry, beautifully intertwined with notes of cedar spice, tobacco leaf, and a touch of toasted coconut. On the palate, layers of raspberry compote, wild berries, and a hint of savory graphite unfold across a beautifully balanced, medium to full bodied frame.

Accolades

  • Wine Advocate - 93 points.

  • Jeb Dunnuck - 93 points.

  • Vinous - 93 points.

title: La Croix Ducru Beaucaillou 2018
bodyHtml:
Hailing from the Saint Julien appellation in Bordeaux, France, La Croix Ducru Beaucaillou 2018 is the distinctive expression of the historic Chateau Ducru Beaucaillou. The estate, which dates back to the 13th century, is currently led by the perfectionist Bruno Borie, whose family has managed the property since 1941. The winery's philosophy emphasizes a rigorous, 'elitist' approach to selection, treating this label with the same dedication and excellence as the grand vin.

Wine Description

This 2018 vintage presents a deep, vivid purple black colour. The aromatics are open and generous, featuring a rich bouquet of crushed blueberries, blackcurrant cordial, and baked plums, intertwined with notes of violets, graphite, and liquorice. On the palate, the wine is full bodied and opulent, offering a creamy, caressing texture supported by a sturdy frame of firm, grainy tannins. This powerful Saint Julien displays a complex profile of ripe black fruits, chocolate, and spice, finishing with remarkable length and freshness.

Accolades

  • James Suckling – 94 points

  • Wine Enthusiast – 94 points

  • Decanter – 93 points

  • Vinous – 93 points

  • The Wine Advocate – 92 points

Food Pairing

The wine’s concentrated tannins and rich fruit profile make it an ideal companion for roasted or grilled meats, particularly beef, lamb, and game. It also pairs effectively with earthy mushroom risotto, braised veal, or aged cheeses.

title: Chateau Beychevelle 2016
bodyHtml:
Blend: 47% Cabernet Sauvignon, 47% Merlot, 5% Petit Verdot, 1% Cabernet Franc

96 Points - Jeb Dunnuck     I was able to taste the 2016 Château Beychevelle on two occasions, and it showed beautifully both times. This is also the first vintage made in the new cellar. Medium to full-bodied, incredibly seamless and elegant on the palate, yet beautifully concentrated, it offers a heavenly perfume of spring flowers, violets, saddle leather, and blueberry and cassis fruit. A blend of 47% Cabernet Sauvignon, 47% Merlot, 5% Petit Verdot and the rest Cabernet Franc, brought up in 50% new oak, it’s still tight, taunt, and reserved on the palate, yet has the hallmark purity of fruit and balance of the vintage front and center. Hide bottles for 4-6 years, and it will keep for 25+ years or more.

95+ Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate     The 2016 Beychevelle is comprised of 47% Cabernet Sauvignon, 47% Merlot, 5% Petit Verdot and 1% Cabernet Franc. It spent 18 months aging in 50% new and 50% second-use barrels. Medium to deep garnet-purple colored, it is a little broody to begin, opening slowly to reveal subtle savory notes of dried herbs, charcuterie and black olives before breaking through to a profound core of warm cassis, baked black plums, red currant jelly and candied violets. The palate is medium-bodied and delicately played with a quiet intensity of tightly wound nuances and fantastic freshness, finishing with a lingering savory lift. This latent beauty will require a bit more time than most 2016s, but promises to over-deliver to those prepared to wait. Around 19,000 cases were made.

94 Points - James Suckling     Stacks of cassis, graphite and smoke on the nose of this rather full-bodied St.-Julien with a ton of velvety tannins that drive the long finish that’s simultaneously sweet, fresh and powdery. Try in 2022.

94 Points - Wine Enthusiast     Now with a brand-new, see-through glass winery, this estate is showing its true elegance. The wine does not have great power but it offers a ripe, smooth, sophisticated texture and black fruits. It already shows delicious flavors that will improve. Drink from 2025.

93 Points - Wine Spectator     This has a slightly beefy edge, with warmed plum and blackberry paste flavors pumping through. Shows a touch of heft on the back end, with dark tobacco and earth notes leaving a subtly chewy feel, though there's ample fruit to soak that up. Best from 2024 through 2038.

92 Points - Decanter     By this vintage, the gravity-operated vat room and cellar were in operation, with smaller steel vats allowing for greater parcel selection. Still closed on the nose, though with firm blackcurrant and blackberry aromas in the background, it’s suave and concentrated, showing ripe tannins and ample acidity. The wine seems balanced, though it’s not showing much complexity yet. Structured and persistent. Drinking Window 2024 - 2045

title: Paul Jaboulet Aine Hermitage 'La Chapelle' 2018
bodyHtml:
Excellent from Jaboulet!

98+ Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The beautifully proportioned 2018 Hermitage La Chapelle comes across as a complex, complete version of this renowned bottling, with no rough edges—just moderate spice, cassis, red berries and cedar on the nose. It's medium to full-bodied, silky and fine, brimming with harmony and elegance on the palate, while the finish is long, echoing with cassis, charcoal and crushed stone. The tannins firm up a bit on the finish, so I suspect this will close down soon, then blossom sometime after 2025.

98+ Points - Jeb Dunnuck

As I wrote last year from the barrel, the 2018 Hermitage La Chapelle is a backward, primordial Hermitage built for the ages. Incredible crème de cassis, blueberries, scorched earth, burning embers, and liquid violet-like aromas and flavours dominate the bouquet, and this beauty is full-bodied, concentrated, and powerful on the palate. With just hints of the smoky, meaty, beefy character that emerges from all aged examples of this cuvée, it has incredible tannins, perfect balance, and a monster of a finish. Don't think about touching bottles for at least 7-8 years, and it's going to keep for 50 years or more.

96 Points - James Suckling

Seems a little shy at the moment, but you can tell that this has serious poise and pedigree with subtle clove, crushed-brick, iron, black-cherry and plum-skin character. It’s full-bodied, yet very tight and reserved with super refined tannins that are so fine-textured, yet intense. Give this three or four years to show its true self. From organically grown grapes.

96 Points - Vinous

Opaque ruby. Displays powerful, highly perfumed aromas of black/blue fruit preserves, licorice, cola, baking spices and potpourri, along with an exotic suggestion of incense. Utterly stains the palate with intense blackberry, cherry, cassis, and spice cake flavours that deliver a suave blend of weight and energy. Youthfully solid tannins add shape and grip to an extremely long, mineral- and floral-accented finish that shows outstanding clarity and dark fruit thrust.

title: Chateau d'Yquem 2016 - 375 ml
bodyHtml:
Chateau d'Yquem, the sole Premier Cru Superieur in Sauternes, is renowned for producing exceptional sweet wines. The 2016 vintage exemplifies the estate's commitment to quality, offering a harmonious balance of richness and freshness.

Tasting Notes

Color: Pale golden hue.
Nose: Aromas of honey, apricots, pineapple, and subtle notes of caramel and ginger.
Palate: Full-bodied and viscous, with flavors of honey, mandarin orange, apricots, and a hint of burnt sugar.
Finish: Long and lingering, with a vibrant acidity that balances the sweetness.

Accolades

  • James Suckling: 99 points
  • Vinous: 95 points
  • Wine Spectator:- 94 points
  • Robert Parker's Wine Advocate: 98 points
  • Jeb Dunnuck: 99 points
  • Wine Enthusiast: 95+ points

Optimal Drinking Window

2020–2064. While enjoyable now, this wine will continue to develop complexity with extended cellaring.

Serving Suggestions

Decanting: Not necessary; however, allowing the wine to breathe for a few minutes can enhance its aromatic profile.
Serving Temperature: 10–12°C (50–54°F) to fully appreciate its complexity.
Pairings: Ideal with foie gras, blue cheeses, or fruit-based desserts.

title: Castiglion del Bosco Brunello di Montalcino 'Campo del Drago' 2018
bodyHtml:
Castiglion del Bosco was the first to produce and bottle Brunello di Montalcino in the sixties and today represents one of the most important properties of this region. This estate prides itself on the highest level of quality combined with respect for tradition.

Campo del Drago is surprisingly fresh on the nose with floral and citrus notes. The perfectly completed phenolic maturity is distinguished in the mouth, with a tense and long finish.

Serve with rich meat dishes, game, roasted meats and strong cheese.

95 Points - James Suckling

Fascinating nose of pungent mushroom, almost truffly notes, together with ripe red berries and a twist of more exotic dates. Full-bodied with an excellent balance of ripe fruit, velvety but not chewy tannins and a long, tasty finish.

95 Points - Decanter

It's more brooding that the classic Brunello, showing sweet spice and cedar-infused black currants and plum. Full but not rich, it's shored up by gravelly tannins and scores of acidity. The palate hints at forest undergrowth, mint and stone, though this will need a few more years to reveal all of its nuances.

94 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Packaged in a heavy glass bottle, the Castiglion del Bosco 2018 Brunello di Montalcino Campo del Drago was born in one of the most beautiful panoramic vineyards you will ever see in Tuscany. This wine pays homage to this magical place. It delivers extra intensity and power that you most definitely perceive on all the senses. There is more fruit weight here, more black and purple berries and more soft concentration that drives a long finish. 

93 Points - Wine Spectator

Though rich and focused on a core of bright cherry fruit, this vibrant red also evokes iron, wild herbs and Mediterranean scrub. This has visible but well-integrated tannins, remaining juicy and extending through the long finish.

title: Domaine Jean Louis Chave Hermitage Blanc 2023
bodyHtml:
Domaine Jean-Louis Chave is a legendary estate with roots tracing back to 1481. Still family-run, it has passed through 16 generations, each dedicated to showcasing the full breadth of Hermitage’s complex terroirs. Their philosophy emphasises meticulous parcel selection and traditional winemaking, resulting in benchmark expressions of both red and white Hermitage.

Wine Description

Hermitage Blanc reveals a deep golden hue in the glass. Aromas unfold with almond, quince, jasmine, lemon zest, and subtle honeyed tones, framed by mineral accents. On the palate, it is full-bodied and richly textured, balancing ripe orchard fruit with chalky minerality and a hint of phenolic grip. Lower in acidity than cooler vintages, its concentration and density give a layered, almost tactile impression. The finish is long and persistent, with notes of baked apple, spice, and a refined stony edge. 

Food Pairing

Ideal with rich seafood dishes such as lobster thermidor, seared scallops, or halibut with beurre blanc. It also pairs elegantly with roast poultry, creamy veal dishes, or mushroom risotto.

Accolades

98 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

Just bottled but certainly not showing any worse for it, the 2023 Hermitage Blanc offers up gorgeous aromatics of quince, honeyed white flowers, and blanched almond on the nose. It's medium to full-bodied, round, incredibly pure, and seamless on the palate, with a supple, vibrant texture and a gorgeous finish. This is an absolute lights-out Hermitage Blanc that I wish every reader could taste. I love it even today, yet it's going to cruise in cold cellars for at least two decades. Drink 2026-2046.

title: Chateau Troplong Mondot 2016
bodyHtml:
Chateau Troplong Mondot is located in France, within the Saint Emilion Grand Cru appellation of Bordeaux. Dating back to the 17th century, the estate gained its name in 1850 when it was acquired by Raymond Troplong. Perched at the highest point of the appellation, the vineyard’s philosophy emphasizes a deep respect for its unique clay-limestone terroir and long-term environmental stewardship, having abolished pesticides in 2002.

Wine Description

This 2016 vintage presents a deep garnet-purple colour and opens with a profound aromatic profile of plum preserves, blackberry pie, and candied violets, accented by notes of licorice, chocolate, and smoked earth. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied, opulent, and decadently textured, showcasing tightly wound black fruit layers framed by firm, ripe tannins and a limestone-driven minerality.

Accolades

  • Wine Spectator - 95 points

  • Vinous - 96 points

  • James Suckling - 96 points

  • Robert Parker - 95+ points

Food Pairing

The robust structure and rich fruit profile of this Saint Emilion pair beautifully with hearty dishes such as roast beef, grilled duck, or wild game. Its intense tannins and chocolate undertones also complement savory pastas or wood-fired pizzas.

title: Sea Smoke Chardonnay Santa Rita Hills 2022
bodyHtml:
This elegant Chardonnay presents a luminous golden hue. The nose is greeted with aromas of lemon curd, star fruit, fresh-cut peach, and wet stone, complemented by subtle notes of satsuma mandarins and a hint of hazelnut. On the palate, it offers a focused mid-palate with refreshing acidity, characteristic of the estate's cool-climate vineyard. The wine is 100% Chardonnay, sourced exclusively from Sea Smoke Estate Vineyard, and aged for 10 months in French oak barrels, 24% of which are new. It underwent native yeast fermentation and was bottled without fining or filtration.

Food Pairing

This Chardonnay pairs beautifully with dishes such as roasted chicken, seared scallops, or creamy pasta primavera. The wine's vibrant acidity and nuanced flavours enhance the depth and character of these dishes.

title: To Kalon Vineyard Company Eliza's Red Blend 2022
bodyHtml:
To Kalon Vineyard Company's 'Eliza's' Red Blend originates from the esteemed To Kalon Vineyard in Oakville, Napa Valley, California, USA. Established by H.W. Crabb in the 19th century, To Kalon—Greek for 'Highest Beauty'—has garnered a reputation for producing exceptional wines that embody the vineyard's unique terroir. The 'Eliza's' cuvée is named in honor of Eliza Yount, a notable Napa Valley pioneer and widow of Yountville's founder, who once owned a portion of this historic vineyard. 

Wine Description

The 'Eliza's' Red Blend is a meticulously crafted wine composed of 63% Cabernet Sauvignon and 37% Cabernet Franc. It exhibits a deep, rich garnet color. The nose is greeted with enticing aromas of blackcurrant, dark cherries, and subtle hints of lead-pencil shavings, sweet tobacco, and licorice. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied with very fine tannins that spread across the palate, leading to an extremely long finish. The harmonious integration of Cabernet Franc introduces exotic spice notes and floral nuances, while the Cabernet Sauvignon provides weight, structure, and a deep, rich, black fruit character.

This robust red blend pairs exquisitely with grilled prime beef, lamb dishes, or aged hard cheeses. The wine's depth and complexity complement the rich flavors of these dishes, enhancing the overall dining experience.

title: Vina Cobos Cabernet Sauvignon 'Hobbs Estate' 2019
bodyHtml:
Vina Cobos makes wines that are authentic expressions of the terroir from which they come. Paul Hobbs, founding partner and winemaker at Vina Cobos, has worked since 1988 in the exploration of the different terroirs of Mendoza, looking for the most distinguished regions in Lujan de Cuyo and the Valle de Uco, to produce wines that uniquely express their origins.

Sustainable farming methods in the vineyard contribute to consistent yields of healthy fruit. In the winery, careful treatment of the grapes and meticulous winemaking techniques result in complex and elegant wines of subtlety and balance.

Deep color of violet and black tones. On the nose, it shows aromas of black tea, violets, blueberries and dark berries. It presents freshness, fine grain tannins and minerality on the palate.

title: Tenuta di Arceno Arcanum Toscana 2019
bodyHtml:
Tenuta di Arceno Arcanum hails from the historic hills of Tuscany, Italy, crafted within the prestigious Toscana IGT appellation. Nestled in the southernmost corner of the Chianti Classico region, this ancient estate dates back to the Etruscan era and is today celebrated for its meticulous micro-cru philosophy championed by visionary winemaker Pierre Seillan.

Wine Description

This landmark Super Tuscan is a 100% Cabernet Franc that pours a clear, rich ruby red with a slightly brightening edge. The nose is deeply expressive and inviting, unravelling layered aromas of sweet mint, vanilla bean, and white pepper spice, alongside notes of cassis and pickled plums. On the palate, the wine exudes elegance and absolute complexity, offering a mouth-filling texture balanced by a distinctive brightness and beautifully soft, fine tannins. Flavors of tart cherries and black licorice build depth before transitioning into a long, fruit-driven finish accented by lingering notes of cedar and balsamic.

title: Joseph Drouhin Vaudon Chablis 'Les Clos' Grand Cru 2023
bodyHtml:
Introduction

Joseph Drouhin Vaudon Chablis 'Les Clos' Grand Cru is a white wine from France, produced in the Burgundy region and the Chablis appellation. The Joseph Drouhin house has a long history, founded in 1880, and is now led by the fourth generation of the family. The house acquired its own Chablis estate, Domaine Vaudon, to secure long term supplies of the highest quality. 'Les Clos' is one of the seven historic Chablis Grand Cru vineyards, known for its exposure and very steep slope, producing the most powerful and structured wines of the region.

Wine Description

The wine is 100% Chardonnay. It typically has a bright, light gold colour. The aromatic profile is complex, opening with notes of fresh citrus, mineral, and marine tones that evolve into hints of honey, almond, and brioche after time in the glass. On the palate, it is full bodied and powerful, with a dense, mouthfilling texture. Flavours include ripe orchard fruit, white peach, and a strong backbone of minerality. Stylistically, it is a great wine of power, complexity, and impressive concentration that remains elegant and balanced. It is a dry wine. The finish is long, intense, and persistent. The ABV is 13.5%. It has tremendous ageing potential and will continue to improve for 15 to 25 years. The vineyards are farmed using organic and biodynamic practices.

title: Domaine Tortochot Gevrey Chambertin Premier Cru 'Les Champeaux' 2019
bodyHtml:
This premier cru originates from France, within the Côte de Nuits region and the prestigious subregion of Gevrey Chambertin. Domaine Tortochot is a historic family estate founded in 1865 by Paul Tortochot, and it is currently managed by his great-granddaughter, Chantal Tortochot. The domain is committed to organic viticulture, having earned Ecocert certification in 2013, and focuses on minimal intervention to ensure each plot faithfully reflects the unique richness and complexity of Burgundian soils.

Wine Description
