This 100% Pinot Noir presents a medium ruby colour and opens with a pronounced, complex nose featuring aromas of dark cherries, raspberry, and blackcurrants layered with notes of liquorice, mushrooms, and elegant floral touches of rose and wallflower. On the palate, the wine is full bodied and well structured, displaying a 'masculine' character with firm yet velvet tannins and a refreshing acidity.

Food Pairing

The structured tannins and savory profile of 'Les Champeaux' make it an ideal partner for rich dishes such as roast duck, goose, or game birds. It also pairs exquisitely with regional specialties like beef charolais, coq au vin, or mature cheeses such as Comté and Epoisses.

title: Billecart Salmon Vintage Extra Brut 2016
bodyHtml:
An ideal blend allowing the personality of the Champagne region’s great Pinot Noirs to dominate, combined with the elegance and subtlety of Chardonnays and that signature touch of Pinot Meunier. The yellow color has soft golden undertones, naturally enhanced by a fine, dynamic effervescence. A shining, very radiant effect that brings out the full potential of nine years of maturation in our ancestral chalk cellars. 

The delicious intensity of precise fruit with citrusy and nutty notes (grapefruit pulp, slivered almonds). A nuanced sensory development built around pastry scents (raw butter, white fruit jelly). A masterful aromatic expression with a refined, refreshing purity. A nervy, charming, tactile delight (chestnut cream, fresh blueberries, and shortbread), emphasized by a delicate texture. The wine rises to a distinguished complexity with a persistent finale, crisply structured by the high-quality potential of such a sought-after vintage. A deeply sculpted vintage with a noble, exquisitely distinctive character.

Enjoy to the fullest with red tuna, papaya, and avocado, or with pan-fried foie gras, peaches, verbena, rhubarb, and verjuice (prematurely harvested grape juice).

title: Argiano Brunello Di Montalcino Vigna Del Suolo 2018 - 3 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
The nose is extremely complex and broad. Classic Sangiovese notes are on display, particularly marasca cherry and flowers, but there are also scents of orange peel, sage, and balsamic, among others. Dense, structured, and savory in the mouth with silky, integrated tannins and a fragrant acidity. Very long finish.

97 Points - Wine Spectator

This sleek, delineated red grabs your attention with a beam of cherry and black currant, while pointed tannins line the finish. Shows earth, menthol, white pepper and juicy red berry flavors that are expressive and mouthwatering. Superlong finish.

96 Points - James Suckling

A very fine and polished Brunello with fine, creamy tannins that are polished and very curated. Cherry and bark character. Medium to full body with ripe tannins. Juicy. Orange peel.

95 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

A more serious and mysterious profile emerges in the 2018 Brunello Di Montalcino Vigna Del Suolo, with unfolding layers of cherry liqueur, leather, smoky cedar, licorice, and rocky earth. Medium to full-bodied, with fantastic structure and balance, it has depth without weight, offering ripe tannins that are well-integrated and driving acidity that creates fantastic tension throughout. Notes of tea leaves, bergamot, clove, and turned soil all work together harmoniously.

95 Points - Decanter

While it demonstrates greater density than the estate bottling, do not expect a brawny beast - this is exquisitely refined and midweight, though not insubstantial. Gorgeous scents of raspberry, rooibos tea and rhubarb greet the nose. The palate is pure-fruited and invigorating, with crunchy acidity. Grainy tannins grip confidently, and it closes with a long, energetic and mouthwatering finish.

title: Azelia Barolo Bricco Fiasco 2014
bodyHtml:
Azienda Agricola Azelia is located within the commune of Castiglione Falletto, a small town in the heart of the area where Barolo is made. It was established in 1920 by Cavalier Lorenzo Scavino, great-grandfather of the present owner Luigi Scavino, and at the beginning it was a small farm. Luigi is now supported by his wife Lorella and by his son Lorenzo, named after Luigi’s father, and who represents the fifth generation of wine producers. Luigi continues to apply what he learnt from his father, together with modern techniques and respect for tradition and he exclusively vinifies the grapes from his estate vineyards.

92 Points Wine Advocate ... The 2014 Barolo Bricco Fiasco offers a carefully balanced and elegant bouquet that is partially based on vibrant primary fruit and partially based on the more ethereal varietal notes you get from Nebbiolo. These aromas recall powdered liquorice and balsam herb. Vines in the Fiasco vineyard were planted in the 1940s, and the Fiasco site in Castiglione Falletto has a greater component of sand, which helps to establish those fine fruity and floral aromas. Simply delicious!

title: Casanova Di Neri Brunello 'Giovanni Neri' 2020
bodyHtml:
From the rolling hills of Italy, this exquisite wine hails from Montalcino in the Tuscany region. Casanova di Neri, established by Giovanni Neri in 1971, remains a family-owned estate now led by his son Giacomo. The winery is celebrated for its commitment to showcasing the unique terroir of Montalcino through meticulous vineyard practices and innovative winemaking that combines tradition with modern precision.

Wine Description

This Brunello displays a brilliant deep ruby colour with garnet reflections. On the nose, it unfolds with layered aromas of ripe red cherries, crushed raspberries, rose petals, and hints of sweet spices, tobacco, and earth. The palate is full-bodied and elegant, revealing refined tannins and a vibrant acidity that drives flavours of wild berries, black tea, and subtle mineral notes. The finish is long and graceful, underscored by a remarkable balance and a delicate savoury edge.

Accolades

  • Vinous - 97 points.

  • James Suckling - 96 points.

  • Wine Spectator - 95 points.

Food Pairing

Pair this distinguished Brunello with dishes such as braised lamb shanks, aged Pecorino, or a classic Tuscan wild boar ragù. These combinations accentuate the wine’s depth and structure. Together, they create an unforgettable dining experience.

title: Domaine Comte Georges de Vogue Chambolle Musigny Les Amoureuses Premier Cru 2023
bodyHtml:
This rare and heart-stopping red wine originates from the Chambolle-Musigny Premier Cru appellation in the Côte de Nuits, Burgundy. While technically a Premier Cru, Les Amoureuses (The Lovers) is universally regarded by critics and collectors as a "Grand Cru in all but name," often commanding higher prices and prestige than many official Grand Crus. Domaine Comte Georges de Vogüé, the historical titan of the village, owns a tiny 0.56-hectare parcel of this fabled site, located just downslope from their Musigny Grand Cru.

Wine Description

The Domaine Comte Georges de Vogüé Les Amoureuses presents a brilliant, deep ruby-to-purple colour. It features a hauntingly aromatic nose of wild strawberries, loganberries, and red currants, layered with sophisticated notes of violets, rose petals, damp earth, and a "chiseled" limestone minerality. On the palate, the wine is medium-bodied and "suave," showcasing silky, suave tannins and a vibrant, "glassy" energy. It is characterized by its incredible transparency of terroir, leading to a long, perfumed finish with hints of orange peel, truffle, and savory spice. Under the direction of winemaker Jean Lupatelli, recent vintages (like 2022) have introduced 50% whole-cluster fermentation to add even more structural quality and aromatic lift while maintaining the wine's legendary charm. It typically has an ABV of 13% to 13.5%.

title: Dugat Py Bourgogne Rouge 2023
bodyHtml:
The Dugat-Py Bourgogne Rouge is a carefully crafted wine from Burgundy, reflecting the domaine's commitment to traditional winemaking practices. Made from 100% Pinot Noir, this wine comes from vines averaging 35 years old, located in several small parcels within the Côte de Nuits.

Colour: Bright ruby red.
Aroma: Fragrant notes of fresh raspberries, cherries, and subtle earthy undertones.
Palate: Lively and smooth, showcasing red fruit flavors with hints of spice and minerality. Fine tannins and balanced acidity enhance its elegance.
Body: Light to medium-bodied with good structure.
Finish: Crisp and clean, with a lingering fruity and slightly spicy finish.

This wine was aged between 18 to 24 months in oak barrels, a portion of which is new oak, to add complexity while maintaining the purity of the fruit.

Sources: Dugat-Py's production details and general tasting reviews indicate this wine maintains the high quality expected from the estate.

title: Patrimony Caves des Lions 2019
bodyHtml:
Patrimony is the creation of brothers Georges Daou and Daniel Daou, proprietors of DAOU Vineyards & Winery.

Hailing from Lebanon by way of Paris, France, Georges and Daniel moved to the United States as young men and soon achieved business success. But that was just the beginning. From their family history and worldview was now imagined a fearless goal—to produce the world’s finest Cabernet Sauvignon, and to curate a lifestyle to match. From terroir to winemaking to architecture, they leave no detail unexplored, so that this wine, and this place, may never fail to astonish

A marriage of Cabernet Sauvignon and Cabernet Franc, one cannot but be taken by the uber-dark color of this wine. Yet when the first sip is taken, an unexpected profile emerges from the glass with elegance and freshness accompanied by a wealth of minerality. The nose explodes with aromas of cassis, cured meats, coffee, licorice, dark chocolate, and spice. Full-bodied, this flawlessly balanced wine will keep you thinking for a long time while the finish does not stop. 

99 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2019 Caves des Lions is a blend of free-run Cabernet Sauvignon (52%) and Cabernet Franc (48%) matured for 22 months in 100% new French oak and bottled in December of 2021. Opaque ruby in color, it has layered aromas of blackcurrant, lilac, graphite, fried savory herbs and game meats. The full-bodied palate is powerful yet balanced, its restrained, mineral-laced fruit complemented by mouthwatering acidity, and it boasts a long, graceful finish. Harmonious and latent, it will demand plenty of patience as it unwinds in bottle—the Patrimony wines tend to age at a glacial pace.

97 Points - James Suckling

Deep and fragrant nose with a lift of currant leaf freshness to the cassis, nori, Spanish chocolate, roasted jalapeño pepper, sumptuous blackberries and some cigar box. Full-bodied and compact on the palate with firm but ultra-fine tannins here that are powerful but not grippy. Long and juicy.

97 Points - Decanter

Pronounced aromatic intensity on a nose of dark fruits including blackberries, plus sweet wood, cigar box and toast. An almost impossible delicacy to this wine which was birthed from two powerful grapes and showcases the expert handling in the winery. Notes of coffee bean and dark chocolate round out the finish.

96+ Points - Jeb Dunnuck

More cassis, crushed stone, graphite, and chocolate emerge from the 2019 Caves Des Lions, and it's beautifully textured, with full-bodied richness, building yet ripe, polished tannins, a gorgeous mid-palate, and one heck of a great finish. For all its richness and depth, it stays lively, fresh, and weightless, and it’s a beautiful wine.

title: Domaine Harmand Geoffroy Gevrey Chambertin 'Lavaux St Jacques' Premier Cru 2020
bodyHtml:
From France’s famed Burgundy region, specifically the Côte de Nuits in Gevrey Chambertin, this Premier Cru wine hails from the Lavaux Saint Jacques climat, renowned for its mineral-rich slopes and cooling influence from the nearby Combe de Lavaux. Domaine Harmand Geoffroy, a family-run estate for several generations, is celebrated for its traditional, terroir-driven Pinot Noir that expresses depth, complexity, and long ageing potential.

Wine Description
This 100% Pinot Noir presents a deep ruby colour with youthful vibrancy. Aromas reveal layers of black cherry, cassis, and ripe plum, interwoven with notes of grilled meat, warm earth, cocoa, and subtle spice. On the palate, it is structured yet elegant, with finely knit tannins supporting a core of concentrated dark fruit and mineral energy. Medium to full-bodied, the wine’s precision and freshness carry through to a long, mouthwatering finish, showing both immediate charm and the promise of decades of evolution.

Food Pairing
Pairs beautifully with roast duck, beef bourguignon, or wild mushroom risotto. The wine’s structure and depth elevate rich, savoury dishes, creating an unforgettable dining experience.

title: Chateau Cheval Blanc 2021
bodyHtml:
Chateau Cheval Blanc is a property that needs no introduction. The wines of Cheval Blanc have been described as, “the finest cashmere,” and “elegance in motion,” by Pierre Lurton who oversees this Saint-Emilion Premiere Grand Cru Classe A Estate. Though the estate has never been ranked in the 1855 Classification, Chateau Cheval Blanc produces wines with quality that is on par with Left Bank First Growths. Though the wines of Chateau Cheval Blanc are considered some of the best in all of Bordeaux, if you ask any member of the team at the property, they will humbly tell you it is all about terroir. 

97+ Points - James Suckling

This is so finely textured with very precise, tight tannins. Medium to full body. Lots of layers here with black and blue fruit, stones, tar, dark cocoa and spices. Dried herbs. Long and persistent. Stays focused all the way. So precise. 

96+ Points - Vinous

The 2021 Cheval Blanc is one of the wines of the vintage. Vertical and aristocratic in bearing, Cheval is just stunning. Time in the glass brings out compelling inner sweetness and perfume to play off a core of rich dark fruit, gravel, spice, menthol and dried flowers. 

96 Points - Decanter

Incredible aromatic complexity on the nose, just wow, the beautiful bitter dark chocolate, blackcurrant, blackberries, fragrant violets and roses, coffee, toffee, caramel, smoked earth, liquorice and tobacco, I could smell it for hours! It wows on the palate too giving succulence, freshness and juiciness balanced by integrated acidity and a backbone of spice coming from the Cabernet Franc - the highest percentage since 2011 and the first time outweighing Merlot at 52%. Perfume continues on the palate also, the soft fragrance giving the nuance while the satin tannins coat the mouth with bite and chew. 

95+ Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

A terrific achievement, the 2021 Cheval Blanc is a blend of 52% Cabernet Franc, 33% Merlot and 5% Cabernet Sauvignon. Unfurling in the glass with aromas of raspberries and cherries mingled with notions of cigar wrapper, vine smoke, rose petals and violets, it's full-bodied, layered and concentrated, with an elegantly muscular chassis of ripe, powdery tannin and lively animating acids.

94+ Points - Jeb Dunnuck

title: Azelia Barolo San Rocco 2021
bodyHtml:
Azelia Barolo San Rocco 2021 originates from Italy, specifically from the Piedmont region and the Serralunga d'Alba subregion within the Barolo DOCG. Established in 1920 by Lorenzo Scavino, the family owned estate is now managed by the 4th and 5th generations, Luigi and his son Lorenzo. Their winemaking philosophy focuses on respecting the traditions of their forefathers while utilizing modern techniques to produce 'jewels' of uncompromising quality from historic crus. The San Rocco vineyard is known for its steep, southwest facing slopes and 65-year-old vines that yield wines of power, austerity, and immense aging potential.

Wine Description

This red wine presents a mid ruby to deep garnet colour, often showing orange tinges with age. The sensory profile is highly intricate, featuring an aromatic nose of red currants, strawberries, and dried rose petals, layered with complex notes of smoke, iron, white pepper, and eucalyptus. On the medium to full bodied palate, the wine marries finesse with power, offering concentrated red fruit and savory orange citrus flavors supported by firm, chalky tannins and a notable saline infused vibrancy. The finish is long, refreshing, and mineral focused, revealing myriad shades of nuance over time.

  • Varietal Composition: 100% Nebbiolo from the San Rocco cru in Serralunga d'Alba.

  • Stylistic Notes: Characterized by its austere elegance and 'monumental' structure, the wine undergoes long maceration with a submerged cap and is aged for 24 months in large Slavonian, French, and Austrian oak casks.

  • ABV: Typically around 14.5% to 15% (standard for Barolo from Serralunga).

  • Organic Status: The estate follows integrated pest management and utilizes organic fertilizers, focusing on sustainable vineyard management.

Food Pairing

The powerful tannins and robust structure of the San Rocco 2021 make it a natural partner for rich, hearty cuisine. Suggested pairings include:

  • Meats: Braised beef short ribs, osso buco, wild boar stew, or venison steak with a red wine reduction.

  • Truffle & Earthy Dishes: White truffle risotto, tagliatelle with porcini mushrooms, or earthy stews seasoned with thyme and rosemary.

  • Cheeses: Matured or semi-soft cheeses such as Castelmagno, Gorgonzola, or Fontina.

  • Tip: Decant at least one hour before serving to allow the complex aromas and firm tannins to soften.

Vintage Quality

The 2021 vintage in Barolo is hailed as a modern classic, characterized by a snowy winter that replenished water reserves and a long, balanced growing season. A spring frost naturally thinned yields by roughly 10%, leading to healthier grapes with exceptional concentration and tannin maturity. Winemakers adapted to a dry August with minimal canopy management to protect the skins, resulting in wines with vivid colours, purity of aroma, and a vibrant backbone of acidity.

title: Aalto Crianza 2022 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
Aalto 2022 is a distinguished red wine from Spain's Ribera del Duero region, crafted by Aalto Bodegas y Viñedos. Established in 1999 by renowned winemaker Mariano García and Javier Zaccagnini, the winery is celebrated for producing high-quality wines that reflect the unique terroir of the area.

Sensory Profile

  • Colour: Deep, elegant purple hue.​

  • Aroma: Intense notes of ripe red fruits, complemented by hints of sweet spices and subtle undertones of liquorice.

  • Palate: Full-bodied and well-structured, featuring rich flavours of dark berries and spices. The wine's balanced acidity and silky tannins lead to a long, satisfying finish.

Accolades

  • Tim Atkin: 94 points.​

  • Guía Peñín: 93 points.​

  • James Suckling: 93 points. ​

Food Pairing

This wine pairs exceptionally well with grilled red meats, roasted lamb, and aged cheeses. These combinations enhance the wine's depth and character, creating a memorable dining experience.

title: Domaine Comte Georges de Vogue Musigny Vieilles Vignes Grand Cru 2022
bodyHtml:
Domaine Comte Georges de Vogüé's 'Musigny Vieilles Vignes' Grand Cru 2022 is a distinguished red wine from Burgundy's Côte de Nuits, epitomizing the elegance and depth of Pinot Noir from the esteemed Musigny vineyard.

Vineyard and Terroir
The Musigny Grand Cru vineyard is renowned for its limestone-rich soils and optimal exposure, contributing to the wine's finesse and complexity. The 'Vieilles Vignes' designation indicates that the wine is produced from old vines, typically over 25 years in age, which impart greater concentration and depth to the wine.

Winemaking Process
The 2022 vintage involved meticulous hand-harvesting of the Pinot Noir grapes, followed by traditional vinification methods. Fermentation occurred in temperature-controlled vats to preserve the purity of fruit, and the wine was aged in French oak barrels, a portion of which were new, to enhance structure and complexity.

Tasting Notes

  • Appearance: Deep ruby red with a vibrant hue.
  • Aroma: Expressive bouquet of red cherries, raspberries, and blood orange, complemented by floral notes of rose petals and subtle hints of vine smoke.
  • Palate: Full-bodied and rich, with layers of fleshy red fruit, balanced by a deep mineral core. The wine exhibits a harmonious balance between concentration and elegance, leading to a persistent, refined finish.

Accolades
The 2022 vintage has garnered high praise from critics, with Jasper Morris awarding it a score between 95-100 points, noting its succulent red fruit and top-notch quality. 

Food Pairing
This wine pairs exquisitely with dishes such as roasted duck breast, mushroom risotto, or fine cheeses like Époisses. Its refined structure and aromatic complexity enhance the dining experience, creating a harmonious match with elegant cuisine.

Serving Recommendations
For optimal enjoyment, serve at 16-18°C (60-64°F). Decanting for about 30 minutes before serving can help the wine open up, revealing its full aromatic potential.

title: Kosta Browne Chardonnay 'One Sixteen' 2022
bodyHtml: Expressive aromatics of fresh mango, honeyed lemon peel and toasted brioche encompass the senses. Stunningly balanced with a refined, smooth palate, lively acidity, and a weightless texture on the finish.

title: Bouchard Pere & Fils Chevalier Montrachet Grand Cru 2022
bodyHtml:
The Bouchard Père & Fils Chevalier-Montrachet Grand Cru (Domaine) 2022 is one of the most prestigious white wines in Burgundy. Bouchard is the largest landowner in the legendary Chevalier-Montrachet vineyard, possessing 2.33 hectares that span all four terraces of the slope. The 2022 vintage is noted for being unusually textural and muscular, successfully translating a warm growing season into a wine of immense power and precision.

Wine Description

The 2022 expression is described as a "tour de force," balancing the solar ripeness of the vintage with the cooling mineral influence of the upper-slope limestone soils.

  • Varietal Composition: 100% Chardonnay from organically grown estate vines.

  • Aromatic Profile: The nose is explosive and complex, featuring "Amalfi lemon," pineapple, and yellow orchard fruits (pear, apricot). These are layered with wildflowers, fresh hazelnuts, and the signature "gunflint" and wet stone minerality of Chevalier.

  • Palate and Body: It is a medium- to full-bodied wine with a rich, unctuous, and layered texture. It offers intense concentration, with flavors of citrus confit, honeysuckle, and orange rind.

  • Structure: Despite its richness, the wine maintains incredible tension and a line of vibrant acidity. The finish is described as "extravagantly long" and linear, with a saline, stony grip that persists.

  • Winemaking and Aging: The grapes were hand-harvested and fermented in French oak. The wine was aged for 12 to 13 months in barrels (using approximately 15% new oak) to provide structural support without masking the delicate floral and mineral nuances.

  • ABV: 13.5%.

  • Optimal Drinking Window: This is a monumental white Burgundy built for decades. It is recommended to begin drinking around 2027–2030, with the potential to cellar through 2050–2070.

Accolades

The 2022 vintage has received some of the highest possible scores from international critics:

  • James Suckling: 100 points

  • Wine Spectator: 97 points

  • Decanter: 97 points

  • Tim Atkin: 97 points

  • Jasper Morris (Inside Burgundy): 94–96 points

  • Vinous : 95–97 points

  • Robert Parker's Wine Advocate: 94–95 points

title: Tesseron Vineyards 'PYM-RAE' 2016
bodyHtml:
Depth, balance and freshness, every detail is carefully considered to reveal the potential of this rare vineyard, and gracefully highlight its unique character. The first vintage of Pym-Rae stays true to the spirit of the Tesseron family, and is both the culmination of a long journey as well as the beginning of a new adventure.

98 Points James Suckling    This is the debut vintage of this wine from the esteemed Bordeaux owner, Alfred Tesseron, who bought the property in the Napa mountains in 2016. Aromas of plums, wet earth, fresh herbs and tobacco. Some green olives. Turns to blueberries and blackberries. Full-bodied, yet reserved and layered with chocolate, walnuts and plums. Firm yet polished tannins give a framed sense to the wine. Savoury. Racy and beautifully structured, it’s extremely drinkable already.

97 Points Robert Parker's Wine Advocate    A blend of 76% Cabernet Sauvignon, 17% Merlot and 7% Cabernet Franc, the 2016 Pym-Rae displays a deep garnet-purple colour and reveals wonderfully fragrant notes of candied violets, wilted roses, damp soil and black tea over a core of red and black currants, black cherries and warm blackberries plus touches of cigar box and camphor. Medium to full-bodied, the palate is evocatively singular, offering that rock-solid structure of mountain fruit, yet these are wonderfully ripe, silt-like tannins that beautifully support the elegant red and black fruit layers, finishing very long and very perfumed.

title: Dugat Py Gevrey Chambertin Vieilles Vignes 2022
bodyHtml: This legendary estate located in Gevrey-Chambertin has been producing spectacular wines for 13 generations. The wines of Dugat-Py have been praised by many great wine critics. The domaine is also one of only 13 in the Côtes de Nuits to be awarded 3 stars in the very prestigious and respected Revue du Vin De France, next to the likes of DRC, Domaine Leroy and Georges Roumier to name a few.

title: Domaine Anne F. Gros Pommard 'Les Arvelets' Premier Cru 2023
bodyHtml:
This exceptional Pinot Noir hails from France, in the heart of Burgundy’s Côte de Beaune, specifically the revered Pommard appellation. Domaine Anne-Françoise Gros, founded by Anne-Françoise Gros—who carries on the esteemed Gros family tradition—is celebrated for crafting wines of profound elegance and precision. The domaine emphasizes meticulous vineyard care and minimal intervention in the cellar, allowing each terroir to express its distinctive character.

Wine Description

This Premier Cru Pommard displays a luminous ruby colour. On the nose, it offers intricate aromas of ripe red cherries, wild raspberries, and crushed violets, woven with subtle notes of earth, spice, and delicate oak. The palate is refined yet powerful, with layers of juicy red fruit, hints of forest floor and fine-grained tannins providing structure. Medium-bodied with remarkable balance, it finishes long with bright acidity and mineral nuances that speak to its limestone-rich soils.

Food Pairing

Savour alongside duck breast with cherry reduction, mushroom risotto, or roast pork tenderloin. This pairing highlights the wine’s depth and character.

title: Timeless 2018 by Silver Oak Vineyards
bodyHtml:
"Silver Oak's first new label in 20 years is a wine worth the wait." -Robb Report

A tribute to Silver Oak co-founder Ray Duncan, Timeless Napa Valley is a proprietary red blend from their Soda Canyon Ranch vineyard nestled in the southeastern hills of the Napa Valley. Decades of experience at this unique site allow Silver Oak winemaker Nate Weis and team to highlight the individual merits of each block. Combining the strongest lots from each resulted in a refined and harmonious bottling.

The 2018 vintage rested in French oak barrels for 16 months, developing flavours of vanilla and baking spice. Velvety tannins dance across the palate of bright and lingering cassis. With a smooth finish, this is a comforting wine of elegance and depth, a sophisticated expression of the sedate summer.

title: Domaine Thibault Liger-Belair Vosne Romanee 'Aux Reas'
Chateau Branaire Ducru 2022
bodyHtml:
France’s renowned Bordeaux region is home to Chateau Branaire Ducru, situated in the prestigious Saint-Julien appellation on the Left Bank of the Gironde. The estate traces its roots back to the 17th century and today is celebrated for its dedication to purity of fruit and elegant expressions of terroir. Owned by the Maroteaux family, Chateau Branaire Ducru has steadily refined its winemaking approach, emphasizing meticulous vineyard work and gravity-flow vinification.

Wine Description

This 2022 vintage is a brilliant, deep ruby red, offering vibrant aromas of cassis, blackberry, violets, and subtle cedar. On the palate, it displays a harmonious blend of dark fruit, graphite, and gentle spice, supported by velvety tannins and a fresh acidity. Medium to full-bodied, the wine unfolds with precision and finesse, finishing long with delicate mineral notes.

Accolades

  • Decanter - 97 Points

  • James Suckling - 96+ Points  

  • Jeb Dunnuck - 95+ Points

  • Wine Advocate - 95+ Points

Food Pairing

Pair this Saint-Julien with roasted lamb seasoned with rosemary and garlic, or a classic entrecôte bordelaise. Aged cheeses such as Comté also bring out the wine’s depth and character. Together, they create an unforgettable dining experience.

title: Chateau Montelena Cabernet Sauvignon Napa Valley 2021
bodyHtml:
Chateau Montelena is located in the United States, within California's renowned Napa Valley. Founded in 1882 north of Calistoga, it was once one of the largest wineries in the state before being revitalized in 1968 by Jim Barrett. The estate is celebrated for its commitment to sustainable farming and a winemaking philosophy that balances classic 'old world' structure with ripe California fruit.

Wine Description

This Cabernet Sauvignon presents as dark garnet, nearly violet, in the glass. The nose is rich and intense, driven by blackberry and cassis, followed by spicy notes of clove, vanilla, pipe tobacco, and a hint of caramel. On the palate, the wine is fresh and dynamic, featuring flavors of cranberry, cola, and raspberry jam supported by a dense, supple structure. The body is medium to full, with laser focused acidity and tannins that transition from supple to a fine, sandy texture on the finish. Complexity is enhanced by savory touches of cedar, black pepper, and toasted hazelnut.

Food Pairing

The wine's robust structure and dark fruit profile make it an ideal match for rich meat dishes such as rare porterhouse steak, smoked beef brisket, or braised venison. For vegetarian options, savory wild mushroom risotto or grilled Portobello mushrooms complement the wine's earthy cedar and spice notes.

title: Vincent Latour Meursault Rouge 'Les Cras' Premier Cru 2018
bodyHtml:
Vincent is hand-crafting exceptional Meursault from eight hectares of vines. His father used to sell off their grapes, but when Vincent took over from him in 1998, he decided to bottle all of their production, roughly 4,000 cases. Vincent made improvements over the years, including using whole cluster fermentation, integrating demi-muids and foudres into the mix, and a longer élévage. A mix of used and new demi-muids, barrels, and foudres are used for aging to control the oak influence better. Work in the vineyard follows lutte raisonée methods, and native yeasts are used for fermentation. After pressing, must goes into 600L barrels or foudres. 

The winery's name was changed from Latour-Labille to Domaine Latour, starting with the 2010 vintage.

title: Chateau Figeac 2020
bodyHtml:
Figeac: a name that shines brightly and echoes among lovers of fine Saint-Emilion wines all over the world. Two syllables which tell the story of one of the brightest stars in the wine firmament. As it slides into the glass, Figeac murmurs like the most outstanding voice of its appellation, with exactly the right tessitura if you know how to pitch it, and a touch of graphite to give it an edge; the energy infused with elegance becomes persistent, reflecting Figeac's desire to be enjoyed again and again. The true dimension of the wine appears with time, as notes of subtly spiced cedarwood offer the absolute quintessence of what a great wine is all about.

100 Points - James Suckling

A mesmerizing nose here with flowers such as violets and red roses, then shows cherries and currants with some mineral and black truffles. Full-bodied yet so refined and harmonized with ultra-fine tannins that run the length of the wine. Flavors of perfectly ripened fruit (al dente) with a hazelnut character that comes from the seeds. Incredibly transparent young red. Breathtaking. 37% merlot, 32% cabernet franc and 31% cabernet sauvignon.

100 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2020 Figeac is the finest wine that has been bottled to date at this estate since its renaissance began a decade ago. Wafting from the glass with aromas of blackberries and raspberries mingled with cigar wrapper, pencil shavings, licorice and black truffles, it's medium to full-bodied, deep and concentrated, with a suave, harmonious profile, vibrant acids, and beautifully refined structuring tannins. This sapid, complex wine represents the essence of this great terroir. Two years after extensive soil studies of the estate were carried out, and the first growing season to see cover crops used in the vineyards year-round, the 2020 benefited from more coherently demarcated parcels and more precise elevage, which taken together help to account for its edge over the excellent 2019. Best After 2030

98+ Points - Jeb Dunnuck

The Grand Vin 2020 Chateau Figeac checks in as 37% Merlot, 32% Cabernet Franc, and 31% Cabernet Sauvignon that spent 18 months in new barrels. They also utilize plenty of press wine, and the 2020 has 8% in the blend. Straight-up awesome aromatics of creme de cassis, ripe black cherries, iron, spring flowers, and an almost bloody, salty character emerge from the glass, and it's full-bodied, with a seamless mouthfeel, gorgeous tannins, plenty of mid-palate depth, and absolutely perfectly integrated oak. It's still tight and reserved, which is certainly the vintage, so do your best to hide these in the cellar. It should hit the early stages of its prime drinking window in 8-10 years and will have 30+ of overall longevity. It will unquestionably flirt with perfection at maturity. Best After 2031. Rating: 98+

97 Points - Wine Enthusiast

 Newly promoted to Premier Grand Cru Classé A, the very highest rung of Saint-Emilion’s hierarchy, this estate is at peak performance. This new release, rich in Cabernet Sauvignon, has an impressive structure as well as modulated, velvet tannins. It is a serious, concentrated wine, still just starting out.

96 Points - Decanter

This delivers concentration and intensity, a ton of black fruits, definitely Cabernet dominant in terms of fruit, and its slightly serious character, with a whoosh of juice on the finish. An extremely elegant and controlled wine, with savoury bilberry and loganberry, then peony and tobacco leaf as it opens. Tannins are finely layered but there are a lot of them. Not an exuberant Figeac, but this is rarely a wine that rushes out to seduce, it takes its time and has ageing potential in spades. The gravel soils in the drought of the summer meant the grapes slowed their ripening process, although only the youngest vines suffered blockages, and that combined with the high Cabernet content of Figeac means lower alcohols than the past few years, giving a classic balance and a feeling of effortless success. 

96 Points - Wine Spectator

A broad-shouldered wine that captures the vintage's heat well in a core of cassis and blackberry fruit flavors, which are dotted with lively savory, tobacco leaf and warm earth accents. Reveals a tarry, grippy edge as well as polish as this pulls deeply from its terroir, leaving an echo of warm paving stone at the very end. Merlot, Cabernet Franc and Cabernet Sauvignon.

title: Gaja Langhe Conteisa Barolo 2019
bodyHtml:
Intense and enveloping notes, blood orange, plum, and mineral aromas. In the mouth, voluminous with sweet tannins, finishing with an inviting licorice note.

98+ Points - Jeb Dunnuck

The 2019 Barolo Conteisa is a noble wine, with angular and drying tannins, as well as more mineral expression. Notes of medicinal herbs, crushed stones, and pure cherry lead to a wine that is more restrained right now but will be fantastic. Through the palate, it has compact but wonderful concentration and a driving structure and is more herbaceous, savory, and mineral than fruity and floral. It is outstanding. Drink the 2020s while waiting for the 2019s.

97 Points - Vinous

The 2019 Barolo Conteisa is stunning. A wine of grace, power and finesse, the 2019 is immediately captivating. Crushed flowers, cinnamon, red berry fruit and rose petal are all beautifully lifted, all wrapped by silky La Morra tannins that add to its finesse. Readers will find an exquisite Barolo endowed with tremendous class. The 2019 is just sublime.

94 Points - James Suckling

A powerful and tannic wine with mushroom, forest flower, bark, and black tea aromas and flavors. Full and chewy. This is a young nebbiolo that needs time to soften.

94 Points - Wine Spectator

Earthy and spicy, with core cherry and raspberry flavors accented by iron, white pepper and eucalyptus. Firm and linear, this ends with a sinewy feel, despite its superb balance and refined texture. Superlong aftertaste.

title: La Dame de Montrose 2022
bodyHtml:
This wine hails from France’s renowned Bordeaux region, specifically the Saint-Estèphe appellation on the Left Bank of the Gironde estuary. La Dame de Montrose is the second wine of Château Montrose, an esteemed Second Growth estate owned by the Bouygues family since 2006. The château is celebrated for its commitment to sustainable viticulture and its meticulous attention to detail from vineyard to cellar.

Wine Description
La Dame de Montrose 2022 displays a deep ruby colour with violet highlights. The nose is expressive and elegant, offering aromas of ripe blackberries, cassis, crushed violets, graphite, and hints of cedar. On the palate, it is medium to full-bodied with silky tannins and a fresh mineral edge, showing flavours of dark plum, tobacco leaf, and baking spices. The wine is beautifully balanced, with a refined texture and a persistent, savoury finish.

Accolades

  • James Suckling - 95 Points
  • Vinous - 94 Points
  • Jeb Dunnuck - 93 Points
  • Wine Advocate - 93 Points

Food Pairing
This wine pairs well with grilled lamb chops, duck breast with blackberry reduction, or a mushroom risotto. The savoury elements and firm structure make it versatile for hearty dishes, while its elegance allows for more refined culinary matches. A perfect match to enhance the wine's complexity.

title: Caymus Cabernet Sauvignon 'Special Selection' 2020
bodyHtml:
Caymus Cabernet Sauvignon 'Special Selection' 2020 originates from the United States, specifically from the Napa Valley region and the Rutherford subregion in California. Founded in 1972 by Chuck Wagner and his parents, the winery remains a 100% family owned operation that has achieved legendary status for its 'Special Selection' label. The winemaking philosophy focuses on 'hang time,' allowing grapes to remain on the vine longer to develop the highly concentrated fruit and supple tannins characteristic of the estate's signature style.

Wine Description

This wine presents a deep midnight purple colour and a full body with an opulent, velvety texture. The sensory profile features a complex aroma of blackcurrant, ripe blackberry, and dark cherry, accented by notes of espresso, saddle leather, and tobacco leaf. On the palate, it delivers layers of plum compote, chocolate covered espresso beans, and dark cocoa, supported by refined, powdery tannins and a sweet smoky oak character. The finish is remarkably long and luxurious, showing lingering notes of mocha and cedar.

  • Varietal Composition: 100% Cabernet Sauvignon..

  • Stylistic Notes: The wine is celebrated for its massive concentration, structural depth, and a seamless balance between rich fruit and toasted French oak.

  • ABV: Typically recorded between 15% and 15.8%.

  • Organic Status: This wine is produced using traditional viticultural methods and is not typically certified organic.

title: Blankiet Proprietary Red Paradise Hills Vineyards 2019
bodyHtml:
Blankiet Estate is nestled above Yountville on the western foothills of the Mayacamas Mountains. The Paradise Hills Vineyard is carved on steep hillsides just above the famed Dominus Estate Napanook parcel that was originally planted in 1838 by Yountville’s founder, George C. Yount.

With an ideal eastern exposure, the land is bathed with morning sun and benefits from natural shade in the hot afternoons, and cool breezes from the San Pablo Bay flow constantly across the land. It’s located on three volcanic knolls where soil profiles vary from deeply fractured rocks and volcanic ash, to thick clay deposits, meaning each parcel is distinguished by a unique subsoil and microclimate.

At just 6.5 hectares in size it’s a remarkably small site, yet the incredible complexity of the terroir allows for three distinct wines, each of a singular style. This is an Estate at the top of its game. Combined with the very talented winemaker Graeme MacDonald and owner Claude Blankiet’s attention to detail, is truly worthy of an exploration.

A Bordeaux Medoc blend of predominantly Cabernet Sauvignon with Merlot, Cabernet Franc and Petit Verdot. This wine is sheer power in a silk glove.

97+ Points - Jeb Dunnuck

The 2019 Cabernet Sauvignon Blankiet Estate Proprietary Red is straight-up incredible, with medium to full-bodied aromas and flavors of cassis, graphite, lead pencil shavings, and tobacco leaf. It reminds me of a great vintage of Château Lafite with its elegance and purity, and it builds slowly on the palate, with ripe tannins, a seamless mouthfeel, and a great finish.

title: Domaine Jamet Cote Rotie Fructus Voluptas 2024
bodyHtml:
This vibrant and approachable red wine originates from the Côte-Rôtie DOC in the Northern Rhône Valley of France. Domaine Jamet is a legendary producer, traditionally known for long-lived, whole-cluster fermented wines. The Fructus Voluptas cuvée, first produced in 2008, represents a deliberate departure from the flagship bottling. While the estate’s primary wine is built for decades of aging, the philosophy behind Fructus Voluptas literally "Fruit of Pleasure" is to provide a more immediate and fruit-driven lens through which to experience Jamet's winemaking.

Wine Description

The Jamet Fructus Voluptas presents a luminous, deep magenta colour. The sensory profile is exceptionally aromatic and fresh, featuring a core of ripe blackberry and cherry liqueur, layered with overt floral notes of candied violet and a savory undercurrent of crushed rock, smoke, and black pepper. On the palate, the wine is round and concentrated, showcasing polished tannins and a vibrant core of minerality that provides a refreshing lift. Unlike the flagship Côte-Rôtie, this 100% Syrah is made from de-stemmed fruit sourced from younger vines (averaging 20 years old) planted in schist soils. It has an ABV of 12.5% to 13% and was aged for 16 months in used oak barrels.

Food Pairing

The pure fruit expression and refined tannins of this cuvée make it a versatile companion for traditional Rhône-style gastronomy. It pairs perfectly with herb-crusted rack of lamb, spiced roasted woodcock, or grilled beef. Its savory and peppery notes also complement duck, game, and hearty pasta dishes featuring mushrooms or truffles. For a more casual pairing, it is excellent with grilled sausages or eggplant-based dishes.

title: Don Melchor Cabernet Sauvignon 2021
bodyHtml:
#1 in the Top 100 Wines of 2024

Don Melchor Cabernet Sauvignon 2021 is a distinguished red wine from the Puente Alto appellation in Chile's Maipo Valley. This vintage is composed of 93% Cabernet Sauvignon, 4% Cabernet Franc, and 3% Merlot, reflecting the unique terroir of the region.

Tasting Notes
The wine presents a deep purple colour and offers complex aromas of red fruits, berries, and floral notes of violets. On the palate, it is full-bodied with fine, delicate tannins, showcasing a balance between elegance and intensity.

Accolades
The 2021 vintage has received significant acclaim:

  • Wine Spectator: Ranked #1 in the Top 100 Wines of 2024

  • James Suckling: 99 points

  • Vinous: 97 points

Winemaking Process
The grapes are hand-harvested and undergo meticulous selection. Fermentation occurs in small stainless steel tanks, followed by aging for 15 months in French oak barrels, 68% new and 32% second use.

Food Pairing
This Cabernet Sauvignon pairs beautifully with grilled meats, hearty stews, and aged cheeses, enhancing the dining experience with its depth and complexity.

The 2021 vintage in Puente Alto benefited from favourable weather conditions, allowing for optimal ripening of the grapes. Don Melchor's meticulous vineyard management and winemaking practices have resulted in a wine that exemplifies the elegance and complexity characteristic of the region.

title: Gaja Costa Russi Barbaresco 2022
bodyHtml:
1. Introduction

The Gaja Costa Russi 2022 is a red wine from Italy, specifically from the Piedmont region and the Barbaresco subregion. The Gaja winery was founded in Barbaresco in 1859 by Giovanni Gaja. Angelo Gaja, the great-grandson of the founder, revolutionized the winery in the 1960s by introducing techniques such as reducing yields. The winery's philosophy emphasizes the quality of the grapes and aims to produce wines that reflect the unique characteristics of the terroir and the grape varietals.

2. Wine Description

This wine is made from the Nebbiolo grape varietal. It pours a bright ruby colour with a fine garnet sheen. The aroma shows pronounced floral elements like violets and lilac, along with an intense and clear nose of crisp raspberry and cherry. On the palate, the wine is rich and multifaceted, with notes of red berries, blue currant, and plum. It has a medium to full body, displaying good density and weight. Stylistically, it is described as incredibly fine-tuned and delicate with an exquisite balance. The wine presents very fine, polished, and velvety tannins, with a refreshing acidity that contributes to an elegant tapering finish. The optimal drinking window is anticipated to be from 2027 to 2048. The production type is conventional, indicating it is not organic.

3. Accolades

  • Robert Parker Wine Advocate - 95 points

  • Falstaff - 97 points

  • Antonio Galloni - 97 points

  • James Suckling - 96 points

  • Jeb Dunnuck - 97 points

4. Food Pairing

Suggested pairings for a Barbaresco with this profile, which features structure and depth, include roasted lamb or beef tenderloin. Its firm tannins and complex flavours would also pair excellently with aged cheeses.

5. Vintage Quality

The 2022 vintage in the area saw heat and sunshine, which ripened the fruit well. Despite the challenging conditions of a robust vintage, the winemaker demonstrated skill, with the decision to use 10% whole-cluster fermentation reinforcing impressions of freshness in the hotter year and contributing to the wine's chiseled and elegant character. The quality of the vintage was good, and the Gaja family was pleased enough to produce all three of their single-vineyard Barbaresco wines.

title: Chateau Leoville Las Cases 2020
bodyHtml:
The Grand Vin is the product of exceptional terroirs from the former Leoville estate. These terroirs are located mainly in the Clos Leoville Las Cases, which you pass as you leave Saint- Julien village for Pauillac. They extend over nearly 60ha producing Cabernet Sauvignons and Cabernet Francs with a complex, polished expression and characteristics which are totally unique to the Grand Vin of Leoville du Marquis de Las Cases and have been widely recognized for years.

98+ Points - James Suckling

This is incredibly classic in style with so much currant, lead pencil, crushed stone and sweet tobacco. It’s full-bodied with minerally, stoney and powerful tannins. It goes on and one. Real Las Cases here. Solid as a rock. Progresses to violet, graphite and licorice at the end.

96+ Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2020 Leoville Las Cases is a blend of 81% Cabernet Sauvignon, 11% Cabernet Franc and 8% Merlot, aging in 80% new French oak barriques, weighing in with an alcohol of 13.68%, a pH of 3.8 and an IPT (tannins index) of 79. The Cabernet Sauvignon was harvested from the 21st to the 27th of September, the Merlot from the 12th to the 15th of September and the Cabernet Franc on the 18th and 19th of September. With an opaque purple-black color, it slowly unfurls to reveal beguiling notes of fresh blackcurrants, Morello cherries, candied violets and dark chocolate, giving way to an undercurrent of crushed rocks, unsmoked cigars, clove oil and fragrant earth. The medium-bodied palate is a powerhouse of energy, delivering tightly wound red and black fruits, mineral and floral layers, supported by fantastic tension and incredibly ripe, silt-like tannins. The finish has jaw-dropping fragrance and depth.

96+ Points - Wine Enthusiast

The wine's richness comes both from the dark tannins and the pure, classic black currant flavors. Acidity, yes, but surrounded by dense fruits and tannins that give the wine considerable structure and the potential to age for many years. An impressive wine.

95+ Points - Jeb Dunnuck

The flagship 2020 Chateau Leoville Las Cases checks in as 81% Cabernet Sauvignon, 11% Cabernet Franc, and 8% Merlot, raised in 80% new French oak. Hitting 13.68% in alcohol with a Ph of 3.8 and an IPT of 79, it shows the dense, concentrated, focused style of the vintage and it's going to be one of the longer-lived wines of the vintage. Deep purple-hued, with an incredible sense of minerality in its blackcurrant and black cherry fruits, it's full-bodied, has a rich, layered mid-palate, lots of tannins, and a great finish. It's a beautiful wine and holds onto the more inward, concentrated style of the vintage while still showing serious depth of fruit. It's going to take a decade (or more) of bottle age to get anywhere close to the early stages of maturity but will keep for 30-40 years.

96 Points - Decanter

A subtle intensity where the power steals up on you through the palate - this is an excellent example of what Las Cases can deliver. Intellectual, concentrated and reined in for the foreseeable future. You get the full array of serious St-Julien character - pencil lead, cigar box, cassis bud, bilberry, earth and granite-edged tannins, this needs time. Very little press wine was used because this has such a plainly evident natural intensity. Needs time, but knowing how this estate is a slow burner even in generous vintages, you are going to need a lot of patience for this vintage to reach its drinking window. Impressive, not yet showing its heart. May be upscored once in bottle.

title: Chateau Palmer 2017
bodyHtml:
Blend: 54% Merlot, 42% Cabernet Sauvignon, 4% Petit Verdot.

Today, the 2017 vintage at Chateau Palmer is precise, without excess. The wines exhibit the elegant balance of our most classic vintages. Their velvety tannins and aromatic depth are promises of splendid ageing potential.

98 Points - James Suckling

Very perfumed and subtle with dried flowers and citrus, as well as blue fruit. Full-bodied with wonderfully diffused, integrated tannins that just run over the edges of the wine. It’s extremely polished and very, very long. Fresh and bright. Energetic finish. A thoughtful wine. A blend of 54% merlot, 42% cabernet sauvignon and 4% petit verdot. Drink after 2023.

97 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

A blend of 54% Merlot, 42% Cabernet Sauvignon and 4% Petit Verdot, the deep garnet-purple colored, 2017 Palmer gives a very serious nose of pronounced blackcurrant cordial, warm plums and blackberry preserves with hints of cedar chest, pencil shavings, violets, dark chocolate and star anise plus exotic wafts of sandalwood and cassia. Medium-bodied, the palate features fantastically vibrant, crunchy black fruits with a firm texture of ripe, grainy tannins and tons of freshness, finishing very long and mineral laced. It will need a good 5-7 years to really blossom with all those tightly wound nuances, but it should be a stunner!

title: Blankiet Proprietary Red Paradise Hill Vineyards 2018
bodyHtml:
Blankiet Estate is nestled above Yountville on the western foothills of the Mayacamas Mountains. The Paradise Hills Vineyard is carved on steep hillsides just above the famed Dominus Estate Napanook parcel that was originally planted in 1838 by Yountville’s founder, George C. Yount.

With an ideal eastern exposure, the land is bathed with morning sun and benefits from natural shade in the hot afternoons, and cool breezes from the San Pablo Bay flow constantly across the land. It’s located on three volcanic knolls where soil profiles vary from deeply fractured rocks and volcanic ash, to thick clay deposits, meaning each parcel is distinguished by a unique subsoil and microclimate.

At just 6.5 hectares in size it’s a remarkably small site, yet the incredible complexity of the terroir allows for three distinct wines, each of a singular style. This is an Estate at the top of its game. Combined with the very talented winemaker Graeme MacDonald and owner Claude Blankiet’s attention to detail, is truly worthy of an exploration.

98+ Points - Jeb Dunnuck

A more brooding, backward wine, it reveals a dense purple hue to go with primordial notes of black and blue fruits, graphite, crushed stone, smoked tobacco, and a hint of violets. As with all these latest releases from Blankiet, the purity is just about off the charts, it's flawlessly balanced, and has ample structure as well as a great finish. 

98 Points - Vinous

The 2018 Proprietary Red Paradise Hills Vineyard has really shut down since I tasted it last year. Energetic and vibrant, the 2018 sizzles with all of the energy of this cool, late-ripening vintage. Time in the glass brings out all of the savory and mineral intensity that is such a signature of the Blankiet wines these days. 

96+ Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Composed of 84.1% Cabernet Sauvignon, 7.5% Merlot, 4.4% Cabernet Franc and 4% Petit Verdot, the deep garnet-purple colored 2018 Proprietary Red Paradise Hills Vineyard delivers impactful scents of chocolate-covered cherries, crushed black currants, warm plums and mulberries with touches of camphor, iron ore, forest floor and black truffles. The medium-bodied palate is as elegant as it is intense, offering electric black fruit and earthy layers with loads of mineral sparks and a fine-grained frame, finishing with great length and compelling restraint.

title: Saxum Heart Stone Vineyard 2022
bodyHtml:
This prestigious red blend originates from the United States, specifically the Adelaida District within the Paso Robles AVA of California’s Central Coast. Saxum Vineyards is a cult-favorite estate founded by Justin and Heather Smith. The winery is renowned for its "superstar" status, specializing in Rhône-style blends from limestone-rich soils. The Heart Stone Vineyard is a small, 7-acre site planted on a gentle south-facing slope of limestone and shale, which contributes to the wine's characteristic minerality and structural depth.

Wine Description

The Saxum Heart Stone Vineyard 2022 is a bold, "overwhelmingly impressive" red.

  • Appearance: Deep garnet-purple.

  • Nose: Intense and multifaceted, featuring aromas of baked black plums, boysenberries, and mocha, accented by savory flower, bay leaves, herbes de Provence, and black cardamom.

  • Palate: Full-bodied and velvety. It delivers a mouth-filling experience of roasted fig, blackberry sauce, and star anise. The texture is defined by grainy, "sandy" tannins and refreshing acidity that offsets the high concentration of fruit.

  • Technical Details: The 2022 blend is composed of 31% Syrah, 29% Grenache, 22% Graciano, and 18% Mataro (Mourvèdre). It is known for its high alcohol content, reaching 16.0% ABV. It is aged with very little new oak, mostly in larger puncheons, and bottled unfined and unfiltered.

Accolades

  • Wine Enthusiast: 98 points.

  • Jeb Dunnuck: 96 points.

Food Pairing

This wine's "heavy artillery" style and rich texture make it a natural partner for robust meat dishes. It pairs exceptionally well with grilled or roasted lamb, dry-aged beef, or gamey dishes like goat curry. Its savory, peppery undertones also complement bold Asian flavors such as beef japchae or hearty smoked meats like brisket. For a cheese pairing, try a pungent, aged Mimolette.

title: Zuccardi Finca Los Membrillos 2020
bodyHtml:
This distinguished single-vineyard red originates from the Paraje Altamira IG in the southern Uco Valley, Mendoza, Argentina. Located at the eastern limit of the appellation at 1,060 metres above sea level, Finca Los Membrillos is named after the quince trees (membrilleros) that traditionally surround the vineyard—a hallmark of the region's historic viticulture. The estate was planted over 20 years ago and acquired by the Zuccardi family in 2008; since then, winemaking director Sebastián Zuccardi has focused on expressing the site's "indelible stamp" and complex, calcareous-rich soils.

Wine Description

The 2020 Zuccardi Finca Los Membrillos is a powerful and refined 100% Cabernet Sauvignon with an intense red colour and black hues. The nose is complex and savory, offering aromas of cassis, black plum, and dark cherry, layered with fresh herbal nuances, sweet tobacco leaf, and a hint of flinty minerality. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied and juicy, showcasing a vibrant acidity and a massive quantity of silky, feathery tannins. It is characterized by its elegant structure and a prolonged finish marked by saline and mineral notes. This wine has an ABV of 14% and was fermented in concrete vats with native yeasts before being aged entirely in used 500-litre French oak barrels to ensure the fruit remains the primary focus.

title: Vincent Latour Meursault Blanc 'Clos des Magny' 2022
bodyHtml:
Latour handcrafts 5,000 cases, with a focus on Meursault, from his 8 hectares of vineyards. Vincent Latour comes from a family who has been making wine since 1792. The Domaine used to sell off their grapes, but when Vincent took over from his father in 1998, he decided to bottle all of their production.

An elegant white Burgundy coming from a mere .93 hectare parcel. Most of the vines are over 40 years in age. The grapes were fermented with native yeasts and with whole clusters. The wine then aged in demi-muids on the lees (no stirring) for a year before bottling.

title: E. Guigal 'La La La' 2021 - 3 Bottle Wood Box
bodyHtml:
The 'La La La' Mixed Pack comprises the three legendary single vineyard Côte-Rôtie wines from E. Guigal: 'La Landonne,' 'La Mouline,' and 'La Turque'. These wines hail from France, specifically the Northern Rhône Valley region, within the highly esteemed Côte-Rôtie appellation. E. Guigal, one of the world's most lauded producers, is an extraordinary, family-run négociant firm founded in 1946 by Étienne Guigal. The family's philosophy centres on purchasing only vineyards capable of producing truly great wines, and they are famous for their traditional approach of long ageing—up to three and a half years—in 100% new French oak barrels, which integrates tannins and creates wines of immense complexity and refinement.

Wine Description

The 'La La La' trio are all primarily Syrah-based wines from specific, steeply terraced parcels in the Côte-Rôtie appellation, known for their unique character derived from different soil compositions. They are aged for an exceptionally long 42 months in new French oak barrels.

  • La Landonne: 100% Syrah. Powerful and intense with aromas of blackberries, smoked meats, graphite, and dark plums. Features charred bark, earth, smoke, and baking spices. Full bodied, dense, and structured with firm, fine-grained tannins. Driven, ultra classic, concentrated, and built for long ageing. Optimal Drinking Window: Best from 2028 through 2045.

  • La Mouline: 89% Syrah, 11% Viognier. The most 'feminine' wine, offering ethereal floral aromas of violet, orange blossom, and rose petal, with red berries, fresh licorice, and mocha. Voluptuous, silky, and elegant with refined, velvety tannins. Silky, voluptuous, layered, and refined, with great balance and concentration. Optimal Drinking Window: Drinking Window 2028–2040.

  • La Turque: 93% Syrah, 7% Viognier. Displays a complex bouquet of dark fruits, spices, cinnamon, iris, and blackberries. Palate is full-bodied, concentrated, and firmly structured, with notes of smoked meats, gingerbread, and candied oranges. Full-bodied, concentrated, and structured with a powerful and elegant aromatic intensity. Optimal Drinking Window: Best from 2026 through 2040.

All three wines are made from Syrah, with the inclusion of Viognier in La Mouline and La Turque adding aromatic complexity.

Accolades

La Landonne 2021:

  • James Suckling - 98 points

  • Jeb Dunnuck - 97 points (Barrel Sample)

  • Wine Spectator - 96 points

  • Robert Parker's Wine Advocate - 96 points

La Mouline 2021:

  • Wine Advocate - 95 points

  • Vinous Media - 95 points

  • Jeb Dunnuck - 95 points

  • Wine Spectator - 95 points

La Turque 2021:

  • Wine Spectator - 96 points

  • James Suckling - 96 points

  • Robert Parker's Wine Advocate - 96 points

  • Jeb Dunnuck - 96 points (Barrel Sample)

title: Joseph Drouhin Montrachet 'Marquis de Laguiche' Grand Cru 2023
bodyHtml:
Joseph Drouhin Montrachet 'Marquis de Laguiche' Grand Cru 2023 originates from France, within the southern part of the Côte de Beaune region of Burgundy. The estate of the Marquis de Laguiche is entirely situated on the Puligny side of the legendary Montrachet appellation. This 2.06-hectare property is the largest single parcel within the vineyard and has been owned by the Laguiche family since 1363. Since 1947, the Drouhin family has been responsible for the cultivation and vinification of this 'heirloom treasure', maintaining its global prestige.

Wine Description

This Grand Cru presents a glowing mid-lemon colour and a full body. The sensory profile is elegant and deeply layered, featuring a complex nose of white peach, pear, golden apples, and honey, interwoven with floral nuances of lily of the valley and citrus blossoms. These primary notes are complemented by undertones of toasted nuts, light vanilla, and chalky soil tones. On the palate, the wine is unctuous and richly textured, yet impeccably balanced by a fine thread of acidity that provides precision and energy. The finish is long and stony, characterized by mineral drive and a hint of bitter lemon zest.

  • Varietal Composition: 100% Chardonnay.

  • Stylistic Notes: The wine is celebrated for its majestic structure and harmonious roundness, avoiding any sensation of heaviness while offering superb focus and subtle complexity.

  • ABV: Typically recorded around 13.5% vol for regional whites in this vintage.

  • Organic Status: Joseph Drouhin has long practised biodynamic and organic viticulture, with the Laguiche estate cultivated using these principles to extract maximum nuances from the terroir.

Food Pairing

The majestic and satiny nature of this Grand Cru makes it an ideal companion for the most refined cuisine.

  • Seafood: It pairs exceptionally well with noble fish such as roast turbot, especially when prepared with white truffles.

  • Rich Fare: The wine’s creamy texture and lively acidity complement oily fish or shellfish served with rich, buttery sauces.

  • White Meats: Suggested pairings include delicate poultry dishes, such as poached or herb-grilled chicken, where the wine's body does not overwhelm the meat.

title: Penfolds RWT Bin 798 Shiraz 2021
bodyHtml:
This striking Shiraz hails from Australia’s famed Barossa Valley, a region celebrated for producing some of the world’s most expressive and powerful Shiraz wines. Penfolds, founded in 1844 by Dr. Christopher and Mary Penfold, remains one of Australia’s most storied and innovative wineries. Known for their meticulous blending techniques and pursuit of excellence, Penfolds continues to showcase the depth and diversity of South Australian terroir through wines like the RWT Bin 798.

Wine Description

The 2021 Penfolds RWT Bin 798 Shiraz is a testament to both vineyard and vintage. Deep crimson in the glass, it reveals an opulent bouquet of ripe blackberry, mulberry, and dark cherry layered with hints of violets, dark chocolate, and warm spices. On the palate, this wine is full-bodied yet beautifully composed, delivering rich, plush dark fruit interwoven with licorice, anise, and a subtle minerality. Silky tannins and finely integrated French oak provide structure and finesse, leading to a long, elegant finish accented by black pepper and roasted coffee notes.

Accolades

  • Wine Advocate - 97 points.

  • James Suckling - 97 points.

  • Wine Spectator - 95 points.

Food Pairing

This wine pairs beautifully with grilled lamb chops adorned with rosemary and garlic, or a rich braised beef short rib. Aged hard cheeses such as aged gouda or manchego also complement its depth and spice. Together, they create an unforgettable dining experience.

title: Albert Brenot Meursault 2023
bodyHtml:
Founded in 1849 by Albert Brenot in Savigny-les-Beaune, Doudet-Naudin is one of the oldest Burgundy wine Maisons. In 1933 it was acquired by the Doudet family, who have developed and expanded the Maison while preserving its fundamental values: respect for traditions and excellence. Christophe Rochet, the current head of Doudet-Naudin, is committed to maintaining the values of this well-respected Maison while restructuring it.

Elegant wine charms  with richly textured and well balanced tannins. Strict foundation is already apparent at a young age, and eventually wine should develop in the bottle its structure and density.

title: Armand Heitz Pommard Rugiens Premier Cru 2020
bodyHtml: The image of the Pommard appellation, in general, is totally influenced by the Rugiens: masculine, powerful, slightly rustic wines. It is undoubtedly the great vintage of Pommard! It has always been recognized for its personality and quality. High-toned, straight. Good tension. Fine tannins. Intensity. Straight and pure and savoury, salty finish.

title: Silver Oak Napa Valley Cabernet Sauvignon 2021
bodyHtml:
This Cabernet Sauvignon originates from the prestigious Napa Valley region in California, USA. Silver Oak was founded in 1972 by Ray Duncan and Justin Meyer with a singular, dedicated focus on crafting Cabernet Sauvignon that is aged extensively in American oak. The winery remains under the multi-generation stewardship of the Duncan family, who maintain a winemaking philosophy of creating wines that are approachable upon release yet possess the structural integrity to age for decades.

Wine Description

This Napa Valley Cabernet Sauvignon presents a deep, concentrated profile with a panoply of blackberry, black cherry, and warm cassis aromas, interwoven with notes of smoked paprika, tobacco, and loamy earth. On the palate, the wine is full bodied and polished, showing generous black fruit, cocoa, and graphite minerality supported by a firm spine of juicy acidity and lengthy, fine grained tannins.

Accolades

  • "James Suckling - 97 points."

Food Pairing

This powerful and structured Cabernet Sauvignon is an ideal match for hearty dishes such as ribeye steak with herb butter, wine braised short ribs, or slow cooked lamb shanks. It also pairs excellently with aged, sharp cheeses like cheddar or smoked gouda, which help to soften the wine's firm tannins.

title: Argiano Brunello di Montalcino 'Vigna del Suolo' 2018
bodyHtml:
The nose is extremely complex and broad. Classic Sangiovese notes are on display, particularly marasca cherry and flowers, but there are also scents of orange peel, sage, and balsamic, among others. Dense, structured, and savory in the mouth with silky, integrated tannins and a fragrant acidity. Very long finish.

97 Points - Wine Spectator

This sleek, delineated red grabs your attention with a beam of cherry and black currant, while pointed tannins line the finish. Shows earth, menthol, white pepper and juicy red berry flavors that are expressive and mouthwatering. Superlong finish.

96 Points - James Suckling

A very fine and polished Brunello with fine, creamy tannins that are polished and very curated. Cherry and bark character. Medium to full body with ripe tannins. Juicy. Orange peel.

95 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

A more serious and mysterious profile emerges in the 2018 Brunello Di Montalcino Vigna Del Suolo, with unfolding layers of cherry liqueur, leather, smoky cedar, licorice, and rocky earth. Medium to full-bodied, with fantastic structure and balance, it has depth without weight, offering ripe tannins that are well-integrated and driving acidity that creates fantastic tension throughout. Notes of tea leaves, bergamot, clove, and turned soil all work together harmoniously.

95 Points - Decanter

While it demonstrates greater density than the estate bottling, do not expect a brawny beast - this is exquisitely refined and midweight, though not insubstantial. Gorgeous scents of raspberry, rooibos tea and rhubarb greet the nose. The palate is pure-fruited and invigorating, with crunchy acidity. Grainy tannins grip confidently, and it closes with a long, energetic and mouthwatering finish.

title: Guado Al Tasso 2000
bodyHtml:
Introduction

This red wine originates from Italy, produced in the Bolgheri Superiore subregion of Tuscany. The Tenuta Guado al Tasso estate is owned by the Marchesi Antinori family, who have shaped Italian winemaking for over six centuries. The vineyard is situated within a natural amphitheatre that faces the Tyrrhenian Sea, creating a unique microclimate with constant breezes that mitigate extreme temperatures. The estate's winemaking philosophy focuses on capturing the complexity and elegance of the Bolgheri terroir through meticulous grape selection and gravity-flow vinification.

Wine Description

The Guado al Tasso 2000 presents a dark blackish ruby colour. The nose is wide and expressive, offering high-toned aromas of blackberry, sandalwood, and clove alongside complex notes of tobacco and leather. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied and rich, delivering powerful flavours of plum confiture, crushed cherry, and roasted coffee bean. It features a thick, velvety texture and is well-balanced with enough acidity to ensure freshness, leading to a long, mineral-driven finish. This blend is composed of 60% Cabernet Sauvignon, 30% Merlot, and 10% Syrah. The wine has an ABV of 13.5% and is reaching its peak of maturity, with an optimal drinking window extending until approximately 2030 in well-stored formats.

Accolades

  • Wine Enthusiast - 95 points.

  • Vinous - 93 points.

  • Wine Spectator - 93 points.

  • Gismondi on Wine - 92 points.

  • Falstaff - 91 points.

title: Domaine Latour Giraud Meursault 'Charmes' Premier Cru 2023
bodyHtml: Specializing in white wines (80% of production), this estate has been in operation since the end of the 17th century. Renowned for producing powerful and intense wines, the Premier Cru "Charmes", located on the edge of Puligny, is the largest in the Meursault appellation. Its name would be a deformation of "stubble", a term designating poor land devoid of vegetation.

title: Dugat Py Auxey Duresses 'Sur Melin' Rouge 2023
bodyHtml:
Dugat-Py Auxey-Duresses Sur Melin Rouge originates from the Burgundy region of France, specifically within the Auxey-Duresses appellation of the Côte de Beaune. Domaine Dugat-Py is a historic estate with family roots in Gevrey-Chambertin dating back to the 19th century, though its current iteration was established in 1994. Under the leadership of Loïc Dugat, the winery emphasizes a philosophy of 'biological' viticulture and minimal intervention, utilizing very old vines—often exceeding 65 years of age—to produce wines of exceptional concentration and purity.

Wine Description

This red wine, crafted from 100% Pinot Noir, displays a beautiful intensity of ruby red that can evolve toward tiled reflections with age. The bouquet is well-balanced, offering rich aromas of small black fruits like blackberry and blackcurrant, complemented by subtle scents of peony, undergrowth, and white pepper. On the palate, the wine is refined and meaty with a supple attack, showcasing notes of spice, leather, and a distinct mineral intensity. The body is concentrated yet fresh, finishing with velvety tannins and impressive aromatic persistence.

Food Pairing

The velvety tannins and vibrant fruit profile of this Auxey-Duresses make it an ideal partner for delicate red meats, roasted veal, or rabbit 'à la forestière'. It also pairs beautifully with grilled poultry or charcuterie and can stand up to flavorful, aged cheeses such as Comté or Camembert.

title: Salvioni Brunello di Montalcino 'La Cerbaiola' 2019
bodyHtml:
The Salvioni family has been growing Sangiovese grapes for generations, starting in the early 1900s. Thanks to the last descendant, Mr. Giulio Salvioni, this winery also vinifies and bottles Brunello di Montalcino. The first production dates back to 1985.

The ruby red color of a young Brunello attenuates during its evolution leaving hints of light garnet which change as the wine ages. The structure is rich in dry extracts which reach up to 32-33gr/l. Tannins are present but soft with a long finish.

This Brunello is excellent with roasted red meats and skewers of wild game.

96 Points -  Decanter

The abundant 2019 vintage resulted in Salvioni releasing both a Rosso and Brunello. The latter is a stunning follow-up to the former: restrained yet captivating in its aromatic presentation, chestnut, fragrant wet forest, and underbrush accented by dried heather and juniper. The tannins are commanding and pervasive but roll over the palate gracefully, conferring a tactile, powdery texture. Still understated, this hints at raspberries, currants and black tea, particularly on the long finish. As discreetly compelling as this is now, it will benefit from cellaring and possesses the power for a long stint there.

title: Beaux Freres Pinot Noir Willamette Valley 2022
bodyHtml:
Playful, candy-coated raspberry aromas bounce from the glass along with sweet cigar spice, followed by a lush palate of dark cherry and soft yet pithy tannin. Finishes with quenching acidity and lingering, velvety texture.

94 Points - Decanter

The Willamette Valley bottling shows such freshness and bright fruit with tart cranberry aromatics balanced by a squeeze of blood orange and dusty red brambles. The finish is tart and fresh, with mint framing the delicate red berries, violet florals and tart Montmorency cherries. Delightful.

94 Points - Wine Spectator

Graceful and detailed, with lilting raspberry and cherry flavors that unfurl to reveal fresh violet, cinnamon and orange peel accents as this builds richness and complexity toward polished tannins.

title: Orin Swift Papillon Bordeaux Red Blend 2019 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
It's rare to find a wine from the Napa Valley composed of all five Bordeaux-style varietals. But, for many years, that has been Papillon's focus. The raw strength and prestige of Cabernet Sauvignon buttressed by the opulence of Merlot, the spiciness of Cabernet Franc, the depth of Malbec and the sheet unctuousness of Petit Verdot come together seamlessly. 

The dark crimson core and brick rim sets the stage, as aromas of currant, blackberry, blue fruits, anise, lavender and brioche float from the glass. Enveloping and coating becomes mixed berry pie, sarsaparilla, cola and blackcurrant with structured heft through the mid-palate. Chalky tannins a la black tea or baking chocolate round out the wine with a pleasing finish of sweet oak.

title: Salvioni Brunello di Montalcino 'La Cerbaiola' 2021
bodyHtml:
This exceptional red wine originates from Italy, specifically from the prestigious Brunello di Montalcino DOCG within the Tuscany region. The boutique estate, La Cerbaiola Salvioni, is situated just outside the village of Montalcino on a breezy hillside ridge at an altitude of 420 to 440 metres above sea level. Founded by Giulio Salvioni and his wife Mirella, the winery operates as an artisanal, family led venture alongside their children, David and Alessia. Salvioni follows a strict quality driven philosophy, producing only a limited pool of around 8,000 to 13,000 bottles of Brunello annually. They prioritize meticulous vineyard care and low yields, famously vowing to entirely declassify their harvest to Rosso di Montalcino if the fruit fails to meet their exacting standards for absolute excellence.

Wine Description

The 2021 Brunello di Montalcino La Cerbaiola displays a sparkling, intense ruby red colour with a fine garnet sheen that will gracefully attenuate with age. The nose is wonderfully detailed, inviting, and complex, unfurling radiant aromas of ripe dark cherries, fresh plums, and dried roses, beautifully layered with hints of cedar, fresh leather, sweet tobacco, mint, and subtle peppery nuances. On the palate, the wine delivers a full bodied, supple, and noble structure rich in dry extracts. It balances a transparent and finely tuned core of primary red fruits against a crisp, firm nerve of vibrant acidity and beautifully managed, fine meshed tannins. Despite its robust 14.5% to 15% alcoholic volume, it remains incredibly balanced, elegant, and energetic, culminating in a radiant, long, and mineral driven finish accented by a touch of licorice and lavender. Crafted from 100% Sangiovese Grosso, the wine underwent indigenous fermentation and was aged traditionally for up to 36 months in large Slavonian oak casks before seeing extended bottle refinement. It enters its optimal drinking window in 2027 and will cellar magnificently through 2050.

Vintage Quality

The 2021 growing season is heralded as a triumph and a modern classic for Montalcino, defined by cool Tramontana winds that imbued the fruit with striking structural clarity, fresh nerve, and bounds of energy. The estate's southeast facing, well ventilated pebbly slopes and high elevation acted as a perfect microclimate, effortlessly tempering seasonal conditions to achieve a rare harmony of sweet acidity and deep phenolic maturity.

title: Frescobaldi Brunello di Montalcino CastelGiocondo 2019 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
Uccelliera Brunello di Montalcino 2018
vendor: 300747 - South By Southwest Wine Imports Inc.
bodyHtml:
Uccelliera, nestled in the southeastern part of Montalcino, Italy, is renowned for producing exceptional Sangiovese wines that reflect the unique terroir of the region. The 2018 Uccelliera Brunello di Montalcino exemplifies this dedication to quality and tradition.

Colour: Intense ruby red tending to garnet, indicating its depth and aging potential.

Aroma: Aromas of leather, tobacco, berries, and spices create a complex and inviting bouquet.

Palate: Flavors of juicy cherry and red currant are complemented by a fresh, lively finish due to the acidity. The palate is harmonious, with a long and subtle finish. 

Body: Full-bodied with a rich and velvety mouthfeel, showcasing both power and elegance.

Finish: Long and satisfying, leaving a lasting impression of its complex flavors and refined structure.

Accolades:

  • 96 Points - Jeb Dunnuck
  • 95 Points - Wine Spectator
  • 94 Points - Wine Enthusiast

title: Thibault Liger Belair Nuits Saint Georges Premier Cru 'Les Saint Georges'
Luigi Bosca Paraiso 2019
bodyHtml:
Bodega Luigi Bosca Paraiso is a prominent wine producing vineyard located in Argentina's renowned Mendoza region.
