Established in 1901, the winery has been producing premium wines for more than a century. The vineyard comprises 250 hectares of land situated at an elevation of over 1,200 meters above sea level. The altitude and favourable climatic conditions make it an outstanding location for producing high-quality grapes with a distinctive character. The winery's portfolio includes an exquisite array of wines ranging from red to white, including the iconic Gran Single Vineyard line. Bodega Luigi Bosca Paraíso's unwavering commitment to quality and tradition has made it a well-respected and recognized producer of Argentina's finest wines.

Graceful and broad in the mouth, its fruity character is very well integrated with the ageing notes. It is fresh, accurate harmonious and smooth in the palate, while its persistent finish allows us to perceive its great ageing potential.

96 Points - Vinous

title: Bruno Giacosa Barolo le Rocche del Falletto Riserva 2017 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
One of the legendary winemakers of the world, Bruno Giacosa crafted the most prestigious single-vineyard Barolo and Barbaresco wines during a career that spanned nearly eight decades. He joined the family business at the age of 15, representing the third generation of his Langhe winemaking family. Giacosa’s unfailing pursuit of perfection, his unrivalled palate and his intimate knowledge of vineyards in the Langhe quickly drew recognition and helped establish Piedmont as a leading wine region.

Intense red garnet color with orange hints. The bouquet is complex and elegant, with notes of small ripe red fruit, blackcurrants, pomegranate and raspberries. On the palate it is full bodied, with an excellent tannic structure, the tannins are silky that give an excellent persistence to the wine.

98 Points - James Suckling

Roses and lavender with other flowers. Peaches. Glorious fruit of dark plums and ripe strawberries. This is dense and intense but there are layers of very fine tannins, like fine cashmere. Goes on for minutes. Opens in the mouth. Almost endless.

97 Points - Wine Spectator

This supple red is elegant and powerful, driven by an underlying mineral element. Strawberry, cherry, rose, iron and wild thyme aromas and flavors persist, building to a long aftertaste, while dense, refined tannins lend support. Offers superb balance and length.

97 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

This wine is very open-knit, and it reveals dark concentration in the form of ripe blackberry, candied cherry and spice. The tannins show a loose, granular quality that adds considerably to the textural impact of this Riserva.

title: Mazzei Siepi 2021
bodyHtml:
Siepi, has been owned by Mazzei family since 1435. A unique location, a special microclimate, the foresight in the early 1980's to plant Merlot as the ideal grape to complement Sangiovese in a very particular "terroir", produce a wine which is perfectly balanced between elegance, power and complexity.

Monumentally built, crispy notes of elder, plum, berries, sandalwood, tobacco, with a very long, bright finish.

Food pairing: Flavourful, textured dishes, dark sauces, game, blue cheese.

title: Domaine Armelle et Bernard Rion Nuits Saint Georges 'Cuvee Dame Marguerite' 2019
bodyHtml:
The earthy, spice-fruited nose screams Nuits. The Rions really know how to handle this old-vine villager. It has fine body and depth. This is drinking surprisingly nicely at such an early stage. Fine effort!

This is an old vine, village wine (which can be from grapes anywhere within its appellation) from 4 Pinot Noir plots all in the same part of northern Nuits, right on the border of Vosne-Romanée. 

 The grapes for this cuvée, named for Bernard's grandmother, Marguerite, were de-stemmed and gently pressed.  The juice fermented 16 days before aging 15 months in oak barrels - 45% new.

title: Kosta Browne Pinot Noir Sonoma Coast 2021
bodyHtml:
Introduction

This highly-regarded Pinot Noir hails from the United States, specifically California, within the Sonoma Coast appellation. Kosta Browne was founded in 1997 by two friends, Dan Kosta and Michael Browne, who were working at a local Santa Rosa restaurant and pooled their tips to make their first barrel of Pinot Noir. The winery quickly gained a reputation for crafting some of California's most sought-after Pinot Noir, focusing on a meticulous approach to viticulture and cellar practices to create wines with elegant intensity and upfront opulence. Their dedication was cemented when their 2009 Sonoma Coast Pinot Noir was named Wine Spectator's #1 Wine of the Year in 2011.

Wine Description

The 2021 Sonoma Coast Pinot Noir presents a lucid dark ruby with a violet rim. It is a vivid and elegant expression of the Sonoma Coast, successfully blending coastal energy with dark-fruited depth. The wine is a varietal expression of 100% Pinot Noir.

  • Aroma: A compilation of ripe, red and blue fruit ignites the senses. Specific notes include red berries, framboise, rosemary, incense, allspice, brown sugar, red cherry, cranberry, tea leaves, lavender, and subtle hints of forest rain.

  • Palate: Soft and smooth on the palate, with pure, electric dark berry flavors like juicy pomegranate and raspberry. Savory notes include forest floor and conifer.

  • Body: Medium-bodied.

  • Finish: Long, spicy finish with notes of cocoa nib and a hint of salty undertone.

The wine offers fantastic balance, with fine, velvety, and unified tannins, fresh seamless acidity, and a good purity of fruit. It was aged for 15 months, primarily in French oak, with 38% new French oak. This wine is a very attractive drinking experience now and has the structure to continue to provide prime drinking over the next 12 or more years.

Accolades

  • Jeb Dunnuck - 96 points

  • James Suckling - 94 points

  • Wine Advocate - 93 points

  • Decanter - 93 points

title: Chateau Beau Sejour Becot 2021
bodyHtml:
Chateau Beau Sejour Becot is a Premier Grand Cru Classé B estate situated on the limestone plateau of Saint-Émilion on Bordeaux’s Right Bank. Owned by the Bécot family since 1969, the vineyard is known for its clay-limestone soils, old vines averaging over 30 years of age, and a philosophy that combines tradition with innovation. The estate produces wines celebrated for their elegance, minerality, and ability to age gracefully over decades.

Wine Description
The 2021 vintage is composed primarily of Merlot, complemented by Cabernet Franc and a small proportion of Cabernet Sauvignon. It shows a deep purple colour with violet highlights. Aromas of ripe cherries, sloe, and blackberries are layered with floral tones, chalky minerality, and a subtle touch of truffle. On the palate, it is medium to full-bodied, with flavours of dark berry fruit, dark chocolate, and refined toasty nuances. The tannins are silky and well-integrated, balanced by vibrant freshness. The finish is long, saline, and mineral-driven, reflecting the limestone plateau terroir.

Accolades
Wine Advocate – 93+ points.
Vinous – 95+ points.

Food Pairing
This wine pairs beautifully with roasted or grilled red meats, game such as venison with forest sauce, wild mushrooms, and aged cheeses. This pairing highlights the wine’s depth and character.

title: Prunotto Mosconi Barolo 2019
bodyHtml:
This wine presents a deep garnet red colour with ruby reflections. The bouquet is complex, offering aromas of red fruit, violets, and lilacs, followed by notes of delicate spices, aniseed, and a hint of crushed stone or forest floor. The palate is intense and structured, characterized by soft, elegant tannins. It is balanced and lively, delivering flavours of macerated cherry, strawberry, and menthol, with a savory, lengthy aftertaste. The wine is made from 100% Nebbiolo grapes.

Food Pairing

Suggested pairings for this Barolo include hearty and meaty dishes such as braised beef or veal, lamb, and game like deer or venison. It would also pair well with richer pasta dishes like tagliatelle with a sausage ragù, or mushroom or cheese risotto, especially those featuring truffles. A perfect match to enhance the wine's complexity.

title: Chateau Pontet Canet 2020
bodyHtml:
98+ Points - James Suckling

This is integrated, with superb density and beauty, offering blackcurrant, mineral and some bark. Full-bodied, yet so polished and refined. Crushed stone. Lots of expression and texture to this wine. Creamy. Pure and precise. Elegant, yet layered. Slightly plusher than the 2019. Dense, yet agile. Fresh as always. 60% cabernet sauvignon, 32% merlot, 4% cabernet franc and 4% petit verdot. 50% new oak 15% old oak and 35% concrete amphorae. 

Barrel Sample (96-98)+ Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2020 Pontet-Canet is a blend of 60% Cabernet Sauvignon, 32% Merlot, 4% Cabernet Franc and 4% Petit Verdot, aging in 50% new French oak barriques, 35% concrete amphorae and 15% in one-year-old barrels. Harvest began on the 14th of September for the Merlot, and the final lot of Cabernet Sauvignon was harvested on 30th of September. Opaque purple-black in colour, it needs significant aeration and swirling to coax out evocative notes of black cherry preserves, raspberry pie, blackcurrant pastilles and damp soil before launching into gorgeous floral and spice notions of red roses, cinnamon stick, star anise and cardamom, with a waft of crushed rocks. The medium to full-bodied palate reveals a lot of depth and polish, delivering mouth-coating red and black fruits with loads of fragrant earth and floral sparks, framed by velvety tannins and seamless freshness, finishing long and mineral-tinged. Barrel Sample: (96-98)+

96+ Points - Wine Enthusiast

Aromatic black currant and spice aromas give way to a wine that has richness while having impressive balance. The freshness shines with tannins that give a velvet character to the wine's texture. The fruitiness should not deceive from its longevity, so age this wine for many years. Organic and biodynamic.

97 Points - Decanter

Highly successful Pontet, one of the few Pauillacs that, for me, overperforms on its 2019. Inky purple with ruby reflections in colour. Lots of firm but upright tannins, a good dollop of graphite, pencil lead and cassis bud, there is depth through the mid-palate shot through with wild blackberry, hawthorn, sage, rosemary and wild mint. It has personality and is a little old school in the best possible way. Recommended.

title: Chateau Canon 2006
bodyHtml:
93 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2006 Château Canon has a vivid, kirsch and wild strawberry bouquet with touches of orange zest and marmalade, a touch of mushroom in the background. The palate is medium-bodied with supple ripe black cherry and blackcurrant fruit, sage and melted tar. There is wonderful structure here, and superb salinity, completely fulfilling the promise it demonstrated out of bottle. Perhaps yes, I was a little over-enthusiastic at that time, but after ten years, it has foraged wonderful focus and vivacity. Seek this out. Tasted January 2016.

93 Points - Wine Enthusiast

A big, dark, rich wine with an impressively opulent structure allied to fresh, bright Merlot character. The flavours of black berry juice are followed by chocolate, bitter coffee and vibrant acidity, which gives freshness to the finish.

title: Chateau Petrus 2020
bodyHtml:
Chateau Petrus 2020 is a legendary red wine from the Pomerol appellation on the Right Bank of Bordeaux, France. Owned by the Moueix family, the estate is situated at the highest point of the Pomerol plateau, famed for its unique 11.4-hectare vineyard of 40-million-year-old 'blue clay'. The winery follows a philosophy of meticulous manual care and minimal intervention, famously implementing green harvesting to ensure extreme concentration and quality in every berry.

Wine Description

This vintage possesses a deep, limpid purple or garnet-purple colour. The nose is a powerful 'fragrance bomb', erupting with aromas of black raspberries, wild blueberries, and crème de cassis, layered with exotic spices, violets, and a distinct marine influence of oyster shell. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied, dense, and concentrated, yet it retains a remarkable 'inner energy' and symmetry. Stylistically, it is lauded for its velvety, fine-grained tannins that provide a massive structure without losing freshness, concluding with an effortlessly long, mineral finish. The varietal composition is 100% Merlot. While youthfully reserved, its optimal drinking window is projected between 2028 and 2070.

Accolades

  • Robert Parker - 100 points

  • James Suckling - 100 points

  • Decanter - 100 points

  • Vinous - 98 points

  • Wine Spectator - 96 points

title: Chateau Pichon Longueville Baron 2021
bodyHtml:
Château Pichon Longueville Baron, a distinguished Second Growth estate in the 1855 Bordeaux Classification, is situated in the Pauillac appellation of Bordeaux, France. Established in the late 17th century, the estate has a rich history of producing exceptional wines that exemplify the Pauillac terroir.

Description

The 2021 vintage is a blend of 88% Cabernet Sauvignon and 12% Merlot, reflecting one of the highest proportions of Cabernet Sauvignon in the estate's history. This wine exhibits a deep purple hue and opens with aromas of cassis, blackberries, cigar wrapper, loamy soil, pencil shavings, and licorice. On the palate, it is medium to full-bodied, with concentrated dark fruit flavors, fine-grained tannins, and a refined, elegant profile.

Tasting Notes

  • Nose: Dark berries, blackcurrants, cigar wrapper, loamy soil, pencil shavings, and licorice.

  • Palate: Concentrated dark fruit flavors with fine-grained tannins, medium to full-bodied.

  • Finish: Long and refined, showcasing the wine's elegance and balance.

Food Pairing

This wine pairs beautifully with grilled lamb, roasted duck, or aged cheeses. Its structured tannins and rich fruit make it an excellent match for bold, savory dishes.

Accolades

  • Wine Advocate: 94-96+ Points

  • James Suckling: 96-97 Points

  • Jeb Dunnuck: 94 Points

Optimal Drinking Window

This wine is expected to develop beautifully with age and is best enjoyed from 2028 through 2042.

Serving Suggestions

Decanting is recommended to allow the wine to open up and reveal its full complexity. Serve at a temperature of 16-18°C (60-64°F).

title: Tenuta Sette Ponti Oreno 2015
bodyHtml:
This prestigious red wine originates from the Toscana IGT appellation in the Tuscany region of Italy. Tenuta Sette Ponti has been owned by the Moretti Cuseri family since the 1950s, though the estate's viticultural history dates back to the mid-18th century. The winery's philosophy is rooted in a commitment to excellence and high-density planting, with Oreno serving as the estate's flagship 'Super Tuscan' blend named after the river that runs through the property.

Wine Description

The Tenuta Sette Ponti Oreno 2015 presents a deep, dark ruby red colour with purple reflections. The sensory profile is rich and multi-layered, featuring a complex bouquet of blackberries, ripe plums, and dark currants, layered with sophisticated notes of chocolate, balsamic, tobacco, and sweet oak spices. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied and opulent, showcasing a velvety texture with powerful, fine-grained tannins and a vibrant acidity that maintains structural balance. It is characterized by its immense depth and a long, persistent finish that reveals hints of espresso and Mediterranean herbs. This Bordeaux-style blend is composed of 50% Merlot, 40% Cabernet Sauvignon, and 10% Petit Verdot, with an ABV of 14.5% to 15%. The wine was aged for 18 months in new French oak barrels followed by one year of refinement in the bottle.

Vintage Quality

The 2015 vintage in Tuscany is regarded as a legendary and 'textbook' year, characterized by a perfect growing season with a warm, dry summer and cool nights that allowed for optimal phenolic ripeness. These ideal conditions resulted in wines of extraordinary balance, power, and aromatic intensity, with many critics considering 2015 to be one of the greatest vintages for Super Tuscans in recent history. Winemakers benefited from a tranquil harvest period, producing fruit with exceptional health and concentration.

title: Chateau Talbot 2022
bodyHtml:
#13 Wine Spectator Top 100 of 2025

Chateau Talbot 2022 is a distinguished red wine from the Saint Julien appellation in the Bordeaux region of France. Classified as a Quatrième Cru Classé (Fourth Growth) in the 1855 classification, the estate is one of the largest and most emblematic in the Médoc. The property is currently managed by Nancy Bignon-Cordier and her husband, Jean-Paul Bignon, representing the fourth generation of the Cordier family since their purchase of the estate in 1917. The winery is named after John Talbot, Earl of Shrewsbury, a famous 15th-century English commander, though the estate has been under French family ownership for over a century, maintaining a philosophy of consistency and technical precision.

Wine Description

The 2022 vintage offers a dense and powerful sensory profile with a beautiful dark purple, glossy appearance. The nose is highly aromatic, featuring notes of blackcurrants, blackberries, and cherries mingled with dried flowers, fresh herbs like basil and rosemary, and subtle hints of tobacco, cedar, and pencil lead. On the palate, it is medium to full bodied with a velvety, layered texture and firm, fine grained tannins that provide a strong structure. The finish is exceptionally long and persistent, marked by a 'cast iron edge' and notes of licorice and violet.

The varietal composition of the 2022 grand vin is a blend of 70% Cabernet Sauvignon, 25% Merlot, and 5% Petit Verdot. It was aged for 15 to 16 months in barrels, 60% of which were new oak. While expressive in its youth, this wine is built for long term aging; its optimal drinking window is anticipated from 2027 through 2050.

title: Chateau La Connivence 2015***
bodyHtml:
This rare and exclusive red wine originates from the Pomerol appellation on the Right Bank of Bordeaux, France. Château La Connivence is a "boutique" estate born from the friendship of three associates, including former French footballer Johan Micoud. The winery's philosophy is defined by ultra-limited production often fewer than 2,500 bottles per year from a tiny 1.4-hectare vineyard situated on the prestigious plateau of Pomerol, sharing the same gravelly-clay soils as legendary neighbours like Pétrus and La Conseillante.

Wine Description

The Château La Connivence 2015 presents a deep, saturated purple garnet colour. The sensory profile is exceptionally opulent and refined, featuring an expressive nose of crushed black cherries, blueberries, and plum preserves, layered with sophisticated notes of violets, truffles, liquorice, and dark chocolate. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied and powerful yet remarkably elegant, showcasing a velvety texture with ripe, seamless tannins and a core of intense black fruit. It is characterized by its profound depth and a long, spicy finish that echoes with hints of graphite and espresso. This blend is composed of 70% Merlot and 30% Cabernet Franc, with an ABV of 14.5%, and was aged for 15 to 18 months in 100% new French oak.

Food Pairing

The richness and structural harmony of this Pomerol make it a natural partner for high-end gastronomy. It pairs exceptionally well with roasted or braised red meats, such as a salt-crusted ribeye, lamb noisettes with truffles, or traditional duck confit. Its earthy and savory undertones also complement dishes featuring wild mushrooms, porcini risotto, or feathered game like pheasant and pigeon. For a cheese pairing, it is best suited to creamy, aged varieties like Saint-Nectaire or Brie de Meaux.

Vintage Quality

The 2015 vintage in Pomerol is widely considered a modern masterpiece, often cited as one of the greatest years for the Right Bank in decades. A warm, dry spring followed by a hot summer allowed the Merlot to reach perfect ripeness with thick skins and concentrated juice. Timely rains in August provided the necessary relief for the vines to maintain freshness, resulting in wines that marry monumental power with refined acidity. Critics have hailed the 2015 La Connivence as a "towering achievement" for the estate, noting its exceptional balance and long-term aging potential.

title: Chateau La Conseillante 2019
bodyHtml:
Chateau La Conseillante is an esteemed estate located in the Pomerol appellation of Bordeaux, France. The property was acquired in 1871 by the Nicolas family, who have managed the 12-hectare vineyard for five generations while maintaining its original layout and mosaic of plots. The estate's philosophy focuses on a commitment to quality and sustainability, utilizing precision winemaking and plot-by-plot vinification to preserve its unique terroir of blue clay and gravel.

Wine Description

This wine presents a deep garnet-purple colour and an exquisitely pure bouquet featuring striking aromas of raspberries, dark cherries, and blueberries, interwoven with notes of crushed violets, raw cocoa, and sweet soil tones. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied and concentrated yet maintains incredible finesse and a seamless, satin-textured middle. It displays vibrant black fruit flavours supported by spicy notes and ultra-fine, perfectly judged tannins that lead to a long, driven finish.

Accolades

  • "Wine Advocate - 99 points."

  • "Vinous - 98 points."

  • "Decanter - 97 points."

  • "James Suckling - 99 points."

  • "Jeb Dunnuck - 100 points."

Food Pairing

The structured elegance of this Pomerol makes it an ideal companion for roasted game, such as venison or pheasant, as well as classic meat dishes including grilled beef, lamb, and braised veal. It also pairs beautifully with earthy mushroom-based pasta or hearty fish courses like seared tuna. Together, they create an unforgettable dining experience.

title: Chateau Duhart Milon 2020
bodyHtml:
In the early 18th century, Pauillac began widespread grape cultivation at the urging of the Lafite lords. The Milon wines served as additional income for Lafite’s master, and became Château Lafite’s second wine. The 1855 classification recognized the quality of Duhart-Milon’s soil by ranking it as the only 4th growth wine in Pauillac.

Chateau Duhart-Milon’s grand vin is often described as a model of the Pauillac appellation. The broker Guillaume Lawton noted as early as 1815 that “it is very robust, with a fine color, and quite pronounced sappiness” (he describes the “sappiness” of the Medoc’s premiers crus as “something like the odor given off by finest sealing wax when it is burned”). 

95+ Points - James Suckling

This is so refined with beautiful currant, berry and some subtle chocolate and coffee. It’s full and very subtle with fine tannins that have a long finish. Such purity and finesse with structure. Fresh and savory.

95 Points - Decanter

Restrained and sombre at first, but carefully constructed, with a rippling muscular texture, full of firm tannins with bright acidities underneath. Like the precision and the slightly austere cool blue fruits, pencil lead and liquorice root. Elegant, precise, feels very Pauillac in its density combined with fine tannins that have life and lift on the finish.

94+ Points - Jeb Dunnuck

The 2020 Chateau Duhart-Milon is a much more concentrated, serious wine. Based on 72% Cabernet Sauvignon and 28% Merlot hitting 12.5% natural alcohol, with a pH of 3.91, its deep ruby/plum color is followed by medium to full-bodied aromas and flavors of darker currants, cherries, damp earth, ripe tobacco, and graphite. Beautifully balanced, elegant, and straight-up seamless, it shows the classic, focused style of the vintage and will be a modern day classic from this terroir.

94 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

94 Points - Wine Enthusiast

title: Chateau Mouton Rothschild 2012
bodyHtml:
Introduction

Chateau Mouton Rothschild 2012 is a prestigious First Growth red wine from the Pauillac appellation of Bordeaux, France. This vintage marks a historical milestone for the estate as the first to be vinified in the winery's newly constructed, state-of-the-art gravity-feed vat room. The estate's destiny was shaped by Baron Philippe de Rothschild and his daughter Baroness Philippine; today, it is managed by her three children: Camille Sereys de Rothschild, Philippe Sereys de Rothschild, and Julien de Beaumarchais de Rothschild. Following the tradition started in 1945, the 2012 label features original artwork, this year by Catalan artist Miquel Barceló, depicting two rams in a symmetrical fresco that symbolizes the balance and harmony achieved through human craftsmanship.

Wine Description

The 2012 vintage presents a dense, opaque, and almost black colour with a brilliant glint. The complex and refined nose offers primary aromas of cassis, blackcurrant, and crushed blackberry, which evolve with aeration to reveal sophisticated notes of cigar box, graphite, and spice. On the palate, the wine is full bodied and substantial, characterized by mature, crisp tannins and a dense body that displays flavours of chocolate and vanilla. It is noted for its "irrepressible panache" and a long, fresh, mineral finish. The varietal composition is 90% Cabernet Sauvignon, 8% Merlot, and 2% Cabernet Franc. While opulent and showy in its youth, it has the tannic architecture to age gracefully for 25 to 30 years, with an optimal drinking window extending to 2045.

Accolades

  • James Suckling - 97 points

  • Wine Enthusiast - 97 points

  • Robert Parker (Wine Advocate) - 96 points

  • Wine Spectator - 95 points

  • Decanter - 95 points

Food Pairing

This powerful and structured Pauillac is a perfect match for classic, high-quality meat dishes. It is particularly well suited for rare, grilled beef, roasted lamb, or game meats like venison. Its complex spicy and earthy notes also allow it to pair successfully with mushroom-based pastas, rich fish courses like salmon or tuna, and a variety of mature cheeses.

title: Paolo Scavino Barolo Ravera 2021
bodyHtml:
Paolo Scavino winery was founded in 1921 in Castiglione Falletto from Lorenzo Scavino and his son Paolo. Enrico Scavino together with the daughters Enrica and Elisa, fourth generation, run the family Estate. Through 70 years of work, Enrico Scavino has researched and purchased some of the most historic vineyards cultivated with Nebbiolo for Barolo to experience and show the uniqueness of each site.  

The Scavino family owns 30 hectares entirely in the Barolo area and vinifies grapes from their own vineyards located in the villages of Castiglione Falletto, Barolo, La Morra, Novello, Serralunga d’Alba, Verduno, Roddi and Monforte d’Alba. 

The approach to both viticulture and winemaking is scrupulous, respectful and is aimed at preserving and therefore enhancing the expression and peculiarities of each vineyard in the wines. 

Brilliant ruby to garnet red in color. Among the aromatics we recognize rose hip, violet, iodate perfumes, ashes, tobacco, white peaches, red cherries, balsamic elements such fresh mint to name some. On the palate it’s s full on energy and all about freshness and finesse. The acidity is sharp, the tannins have a beautiful tension yet they are harmonious in the structure.

title: Chateau Leoville Barton 2018
bodyHtml:
97 Points - Wine Spectator

Cassis, crushed plum and steeped blackberry fruit are all packed into this wine, along with tar, violet and roasted apple wood notes, plus a terrific tug of warm earth. It shows lots of energy in reserve, with a tightly knit finish pulling everything together. Cellaring required. Cabernet Sauvignon and Merlot. Best from 2026 through 2040.

97 Points - James Suckling 

Sweet berries, blackberries, raspberries and violets follow through to a full body with incredibly creamy, polished tannins that caress the palate. It's really long and polished. Gorgeous finish. Drink after 2025.

97 Points - Wine Enthusiast

This wine's refined and rich tannins partner with powerful black plum and blackcurrant fruits. Densely textured while also having swathes of rich fruits, the wine shows both a firm side and one that offers total deliciousness. As it matures, both these aspects will come together. Drink from 2027.

97 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

This estate has been on fire in recent vintages, and the 2018 Château Léoville Barton is up there with the best of them. Based on 82% Cabernet Sauvignon and 18% Merlot brought up in 60% new French oak, this classic, flawlessly balanced, straight-up awesome Saint-Julien has loads of cassis and mulberry fruits as well as notes of freshly sharpened pencils, leafy tobacco, chocolate, and earth. Rich, medium to full-bodied, and concentrated on the palate, it has building tannins and healthy acidity. Yet, the fruit is pure, perfectly ripe, and wonderfully integrated with all the wine's components. As is usual with this cuvée, it closes down with extended air and will take a solid 8-10 years of bottle age to reach the early stages of maturity. It's going to evolve for 30-40 years in cold cellars.

96 Points - Decanter

Well-polished blackcurrant, cassis and bilberry, everything pretty silky and firm. Not fully showing its generosity at this point, but no question that it is going to get there soon. Clear charcoal, graphite and woodsmoke as it opens up—a ton of life ahead and an appealing sense of mint freshness. Lives up to its en primeur promise - this is Léoville Barton at its most confident. Drinking Window 2026 - 2040.

94+ Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Deep garnet-purple in colour, the 2018 Léoville Barton needs a little swirling to coax out delicate notions of fresh blackberries, mulberries and cassis, plus touches of pencil shavings, and clove oil, charcoal and black truffles. The medium to full-bodied palate delivers a great intensity of earth and mineral-laced black fruit flavours, supported by firm, ripe, grainy tannins and seamless freshness, finishing on a lingering ferrous note. Give it a good 4-5 years in bottle and drink it over the next 20 years+.

title: Dugat Py Gevrey Chambertin 'Petite Chapelle' Premier Cru 2022
bodyHtml:
Domaine Dugat-Py, a distinguished estate in Burgundy's Côte de Nuits, is renowned for its meticulous craftsmanship and dedication to producing wines that authentically express the unique terroir of Gevrey-Chambertin. The 2022 Gevrey-Chambertin 1er Cru 'Petite Chapelle' exemplifies this commitment, offering a harmonious blend of richness and elegance.

Vineyard and Vinification:

  • Location: The 'Petite Chapelle' vineyard is situated directly downslope from the esteemed Chapelle-Chambertin Grand Cru, benefiting from optimal sun exposure and well-drained soils.
  • Vine Age: The vines average 70 years, contributing to the wine's depth and complexity.
  • Winemaking: Approximately 75% of the grapes were fermented as whole clusters, enhancing aromatic complexity and structure.

Tasting Notes:

  • Colour: Deep ruby red with garnet reflections, indicating its concentration and aging potential.
  • Aroma: An expressive bouquet featuring notes of dark wild berries, blackberry, mulberry, and floral nuances, creating a complex and inviting profile.
  • Palate: Full-bodied and well-structured, offering flavors of ripe black fruits with a touch of spice, supported by firm tannins and balanced acidity. The palate is harmonious, with a long and subtle finish.
  • Finish: Long and satisfying, leaving a lasting impression of its complex flavors and refined structure.

Accolades:

  • 96 Points - Decanter

This wine exemplifies Domaine Dugat-Py's dedication to producing wines that are both expressive and true to their terroir, offering a delightful experience for Burgundy enthusiasts.

title: Catena Zapata Malbec Adrianna Vineyard Fortuna Terrae 2021
bodyHtml:
Introduction

Catena Zapata Malbec Adrianna Vineyard Fortuna Terrae 2021 is a red wine from Argentina, produced in the Mendoza region, specifically the Uco Valley subregion and the high-altitude Gualtallary district. The wine is made by the legendary Catena Zapata family winery, which is renowned for its role in elevating Argentine Malbec to global acclaim. Now run by fourth-generation vigneron Laura Catena, the winery's philosophy is centred on the deep belief that high-altitude vineyards, such as the Adrianna Vineyard, possess exceptional, hidden qualities for grape growing. The 'Fortuna Terrae' parcel name means 'Luck of the Land' in Latin, referring to its cool, comparatively deep loam soils that impart freshness to the wine.

Wine Description

The wine is 100% Malbec. It exhibits a dark purple hue. The aromatic profile is intensely expressive, with enticing floral notes of violet, hibiscus, lavender, and dried flowers. These are layered over a foundation of black fruit, mountain herbs, orange peel, and spice. It is a full-bodied wine. The palate is rich, taut, and deeply concentrated, offering compelling combination of dryness and juiciness. Flavours include black cherry, raspberry coulis, red currant, and hints of dark chocolate and graphite. Stylistically, it is a beautifully mineral red with impeccable purity, showcasing a harmony of power and etherealness. The wine underwent a meticulous 16-month aging process in foudres and concrete vats. The finish is exceptionally long, transparent, and mineral-driven. The ABV is 13.9%. The optimal drinking window is to enjoy a few years or decades after harvest, or after 2023.

This full-bodied and robust Malbec is a great pairing for steaks, barbecue fare, and full-flavoured cheeses. Examples of great pairings include grilled steak, roast beef, and rack of lamb.

Vintage Quality

The 2021 vintage is noted for having produced a particularly dynamic wine that continuously gains power, depth, and tensile structure in the glass. The high altitude and deep soils of the Adrianna Vineyard impart optimal acidity and freshness to the wines.

title: Araujo Estate Red Blend 'Altagracia' 2011
bodyHtml:
Since 1971, some of California's most ageworthy and intensely-flavored Cabernet Sauvignons have been made from grapes grown at the Eisele Vineyard, located on a benchland near the northern end of Napa Valley, just east of Calistoga. Protected by the Palisades Mountains to the north and cooled by westerly breezes from the Chalk Hill Gap, this 38-acre vineyard is planted on warm cobbly soils that produce a low-yielding crop of exceptionally concentrated fruit. 

The Eisele Vineyard has again shown its ability to deliver wines of distinction in atypical vintages. The minerality and quality of tannins which are Eisele hallmarks couple with fine, generous texture to give us a delicious wine of particular vitality and elegance. This Altagracia bears the signature of this unique place.

91 Points - James Suckling

Juicy and savory. Extremely well done for the second wine of Araujo. Iodine and stone. Drink or hold.

title: Bouchard Pere & Fils Chambertin 'Clos De Beze' Grand Cru 2020
bodyHtml:
Bouchard Père & Fils Chambertin 'Clos de Bèze' Grand Cru 2020 is a profound red wine from France, produced in the Gevrey Chambertin village at the northern end of the Côte de Nuits. Founded in 1731 by Michel Bouchard, the house is one of Burgundy's oldest wine-merchant families and is currently the largest owner of Grand Cru and Premier Cru vineyards across the Côte d'Or. The winery's philosophy is rooted in a 'quest for excellence', combining nearly three centuries of tradition with modern sustainable practices to create an authentic expression of its historic terroirs.

Wine Description

This 2020 vintage presents a dark ruby red colour and a racy nose defined by aromas of currant, raspberry, and cherry stone mixed with woody, toasted notes and floral wisps. On the palate, the wine is round, rich, and elegantly structured, showcasing flavours of cherry, strawberry, and plum complemented by spicy accents of clove and a hint of graphite. It is 100% Pinot Noir, sourced from a prestigious 14.53-hectare plot where brown chalk and calcareous clay soils provide a solid base for its distinguished tannins. Stylistically, it is noted for its suave intensity and 'sappy' dry extract, which balances a firm tannic spine and leads to a long, persistent finish marked by minerality and finesse. While showing great energy now, it has an optimal drinking window of 15 to 20 years or more.

Accolades

95 Points - Wine Spectator: This round, supple red focuses on the fruit, with cherry and strawberry notes, plus floral and spice accents. Shows a solid base of tannins, which lend support and gain presence as this winds down on the finish. Tips toward the tannins, and is less forthcoming than many 2020s at this stage, with plenty of energy and fine potential. Best from 2027 through 2048.

Food Pairing

This Grand Cru serves as a famous companion to roasted duck, beef tenderloin, and game birds. Its complex structure also pairs beautifully with mushroom-based sauces or aged cheeses such as Époisses, Comté, or Gruyère. Together, they create an unforgettable dining experience.

title: Domaine Zind Humbrecht Pinot Gris Clos St Urbain Rangen de Thann 2022
bodyHtml:
Medium golden yellow with copper reflections. Aromas of bitter orange, candied orange peel, dried apricots, candied ginger, peach, pear, honeydew melon, spices such as cardamom and cinnamon, incense, as well as smoky, flint-like notes.

Full-bodied flavour with mild tannins, accentuated and precise acidity, a salty, almost crystalline structure, and a long finish.

Pair with risotto with crab meat and grilled green asparagus, pike-perch fillet with Middle Eastern spice mix, accompanied by chickpeas and barley risotto, grilled wild pigeon with quinoa, exotic fruits and rum-lemon cream.

title: Chateau de la Tour Clos Vougeot Grand Cru 'Vieilles Vignes' 2019 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
Clos Vougeot is surely one of the most famous Grand Cru vineyards of the Cote de Nuits as it is located right next to the Musigny and Romanee-Conti domains. This unmistakable winery is located in the middle of the vineyard and you can't miss it as you drive by the famous vineyard.

With almost 15 acres planted, it the largest parcel of Clos de Vougeot with some of oldest vines, over 100-years-old. Chateau de la Tour wines are the only Clos-Vougeot Grand Cru to be harvested, vinified, raised and bottled within the walls of Clos de Vougeot, just like in the old days of the monks.

On the palate, the Vielles Vignes carries notes of black fruits, orange peels, rose petals, fresh earth, and spices. Aromas of black cherry and berries are complex and layered. A full-bodied, powerful and multi-dimensional wine, it's deep and concentrated, with rich tannins, crisp acids and a long finish. 

96 Points - Decanter     

Slightly reserved at present, the tightly packed black and red fruit opens on the palate, accented with notes of violets, mineral, earth and wild herbs. This is powerful and rich, with firm tannins, lots of body, and the ability to age almost indefinitely.

94+ Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate     

Clos Vougeot Grand Cru Vieilles Vignes is very promising, unwinding in the glass with notes of dark berry fruit, orange peel, rose petals, rich soil tones and spices. Full-bodied, layered and multidimensional, it's deep and concentrated, with rich, powdery tannins, lively acids and a long, resonant finish.

title: Chateau Lagrange 2002
bodyHtml:
Introduction

Chateau Lagrange 2002 is a red wine from the Saint Julien appellation within the Médoc region of Bordeaux, France. Classified as a Third Growth in the historic 1855 Classification, the estate was once a vast property known as 'Grangia' during the Middle Ages. Since its acquisition by the Japanese group Suntory in 1983, the winery has undergone a significant renaissance, focusing on a philosophy of 'uncompromising quality' and precision viticulture across its 103 distinct vineyard plots.

Wine Description

This wine displays a rich and deep purple red colour with ruby nuances. The aromatic profile is dominated by fresh red fruits, such as raspberries and redcurrants, alongside complex notes of blackberries, currants, lead pencil, and toasty new oak. On the palate, the entry is well structured and ample, evolving into a generous and powerful mid-palate with flavours of cassis, black pepper, and spiced herbs. It is a full bodied wine with a very long finish that offers sweetness without tannic harshness, supported by ultrafine tannins and fresh acidity. This blend typically consists of Cabernet Sauvignon and Merlot, with small amounts of Petit Verdot and Cabernet Franc. It possesses an ABV of approximately 13% and has an optimal drinking window that extends through 2030. The estate is not certified organic.

Food Pairing

The structured tannins and vibrant fruit of this Saint Julien make it an excellent companion for rich meat dishes such as braised lamb shanks with tomatoes or a classic rib of beef served with bone marrow. Its earthy and herbal undertones also pair well with savoury mallard duck breast, veal cheek ravioli with wild morels, or hearty short ribs. For a cheese course, consider serving it with mature cheddar or Manchego to complement its dark fruit and spice profiles.

Vintage Quality

The 2002 vintage in Bordeaux was a challenging year saved by an 'Indian summer', as a cold spring and wet August initially threatened the ripening of Merlot. A wave of intense heat and sunshine in September allowed the Cabernet Sauvignon to achieve remarkable ripeness and concentration, resulting in wines known for their traditional charm, vibrant acidity, and refined structure. Winemakers at Chateau Lagrange successfully navigated these conditions, as the estate often excels in less predictable vintages by utilizing precise plot management.

title: Catena Zapata Malbec Adrianna Vineyard Fortuna Terrae 2020
bodyHtml:
Catena Zapata Malbec Adrianna Vineyard Fortuna Terrae 2020 is a red wine from Argentina, produced in the Mendoza region and the high-altitude Gualtallary district of the Uco Valley. The wine is made by the renowned Catena Zapata family winery, which is famous for discovering and cultivating high-altitude vineyards. The winery's philosophy is rooted in the deep belief that the cool climate and intense mountain sunlight at this extreme elevation create wines of incredible depth and complexity. The 'Fortuna Terrae' parcel name means 'Luck of the Land' in Latin, referring to its deep loam and clay soils with white limestone-covered stones.

Wine Description

The wine is 100% Malbec. It exhibits a garnet colour with violet reflections and a medium to high layer intensity. The aromatic profile is very expressive, with a striking purity and cleanness, featuring telltale violets from the Malbec grape. Other notes include black fruit, dark plums, dried earth, tar, paprika, lavender, and cedar. It is a medium to full-bodied wine. The palate is beautifully concentrated and structured, with a tremendous freshness and a 'crisp' touch. The fine-grained tannins impart a chalky limestone sensation, and the wine is both dense and unctuous. Stylistically, it is a pure, precise, and elegant wine, described as a 'Burgundian' style that pulsates with tension and finesse. The wine was aged for 14 to 18 months in French oak barrels. The finish is long, fresh, wonderfully persistent, and coated by chalky minerality. The ABV is either 13.9% or 14.3%. The optimal drinking window is from 2024 to 2032, or 2025 onwards. The Adrianna Vineyard wines are certified organic by Letis.

Accolades

  • Wine Advocate - 98 points

  • James Suckling - 98 points

  • Decanter - 96 points

  • Vinous - 95 points

  • Gismondi On Wine - 95 points

  • Wine Spectator - 93 points

  • Wine Enthusiast - 94 points

Food Pairing

This full-bodied and robust wine is a great pairing for steaks, barbecue fare, and full-flavoured cheeses. Suggested pairings include roasted meats, grilled veal fillet with foie gras shavings, and red meats prepared on charcoal with chimichurri sauce.

Vintage Quality

Despite being a warmer year, the 2020 vintage produced an exceptionally expressive, pure, and precise wine, showing no signs of coming from a challenging year. The Fortuna Terrae plot, with its deep soils and high altitude, performed well, retaining optimal acidity and floral aromas.

title: Domaine Anne F. Gros Vosne Romanee 'Les Chalandins' 2023
bodyHtml:
From the heart of Burgundy in France, Domaine Anne-Françoise Gros is located in Vosne-Romanée, within the Côte de Nuits subregion of the Côte d'Or. Anne Gros, daughter of François Gros, continues her family's rich winemaking legacy, managing the estate with meticulous attention to terroir expression and balance. The estate is renowned for producing elegant Pinot Noir wines that emphasize finesse over power, rooted in the philosophy of minimal intervention and deep respect for the vineyard.

Wine Description

This Vosne-Romanée ‘Les Chalandins’ 2023 displays a bright ruby hue. On the nose, it offers alluring aromas of ripe red cherries, raspberries, and subtle floral notes of violets, layered with hints of sweet spice and damp earth. The palate is supple and refined, delivering pure red fruit flavours intertwined with nuances of forest floor and gentle oak. Medium-bodied with silky tannins, the wine finishes long and graceful, marked by delicate mineral notes that echo the vineyard’s limestone-rich soils.

Food Pairing

Pair this wine with roasted duck breast, mushroom risotto, or herb-crusted pork tenderloin. This pairing highlights the wine’s depth and character, allowing its delicate aromatics and fine tannins to shine alongside savoury, earthy dishes.

title: Gianni Brunelli Brunello di Montalcino 2019 - 3 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
Introduction

Gianni Brunelli is a prestigious, boutique estate in Montalcino, Italy, currently managed by Laura Brunelli. The estate is widely celebrated for its commitment to a traditional, elegant style of Brunello di Montalcino that avoids the over-extraction or heavy oak influence sometimes found in modern expressions. By blending fruit from two distinct vineyard sites—Le Chiuse di Sotto in the north and Podernovone in the south—the winery achieves a "Sangiovese heaven" that balances aromatic lift with structural depth.

Winemaking Philosophy

The estate follows a "vines-first" philosophy, emphasizing organic farming and meticulous manual labor.

  • Terroir: Fruit is sourced from two main plots. Le Chiuse di Sotto (250m altitude) provides freshness and elegance, while Podernovone (500m altitude) contributes mineral tension and structure.

  • Method: Winemaking is traditional, utilizing indigenous yeasts and long macerations (often 25–30 days).

  • Aging: The wine is matured for approximately 30 months in large Slavonian oak casks (botti grandi) rather than small French barriques, preserving the purity of the Sangiovese fruit.

  • Production: Very limited, with annual production for the Brunello typically hovering around 15,000 to 25,000 bottles.

title: Domaine Tollot Beaut Savigny Champ Chevrey Premier Cru 2020
Domaine Michel Gros Nuits Saint Georges 2023
bodyHtml:
Winery Background: Domaine Michel Gros, established in 1830, is a family-owned estate in Vosne-Romanée, Burgundy. The Gros family has cultivated vineyards for six generations, emphasizing traditional winemaking methods to express the unique terroir of their plots. The Nuits-Saint-Georges appellation is renowned for producing robust and complex Pinot Noir wines.

Wine Description: This 100% Pinot Noir wine exhibits a bright ruby hue. The bouquet is perfumed and floral, offering aromas of redcurrant, cranberry, and strawberry. On the palate, it is medium-bodied with fine tannins and nuanced flavors, expanding with zeal toward the finish. While currently a bit strict, it shows promise for further development.

Food Pairing: This wine pairs excellently with dishes such as roasted duck breast, coq au vin, or mushroom risotto. These pairings enhance the wine's depth and character.

title: Domaine William Fevre Chablis 'Bougros' Grand Cru 2021
bodyHtml:
Founded in 1959, Domaine William Fevre is at the very heart of the Chablis vineyards. Since its founding, Domaine William Fevre has been taken up with the desire to produce indisputable genuine and fine wines, bringing along a very personal experience in Chardonnay. All the efforts have but one goal – to finely express the subtle most variations in the greatest Chablis crus. Today, Domaine William Fevre is one of the most established and renowned estates in Chablis.

Chablis Bougros Grand Cru has a rich bouquet with intense mineral notes. It is full and round, yet firm and massive on the palate.

Pairs well with fish, shellfish and other seafood, poultry and white meat, all grilled or in a cream sauce.

95 Points - Decanter

On very steep slopes (up to 30%) the clay/gravel soils are low-yielding and lead to intense, ageworthy wines. Much more mineral in terms of both perfume and texture on the palate, citrus fruit is more to the fore here with plenty of acidity suggesting the wine needs several years in bottle before opening. Great precision and laser-like focus. A very fine Grand Cru.

94+ Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2021 Chablis Grand Cru Bougros Côte Bouguerots is superb, unwinding in the glass with aromas of orange zest, white flowers, fresh mint, buttery pastry and clam liquor, followed by a medium to full-bodied, deep and satiny palate with a sweet core of fruit, a bright spine of tangy acidity and a long, orange oil-inflected finish.

title: Produttori del Barbaresco - Barbaresco 'Montestefano' Riserva 2020
bodyHtml:
Produttori del Barbaresco Barbaresco Montestefano Riserva 2020 originates from the Piedmont region of Italy, specifically from the historic Montestefano vineyard within the Barbaresco subregion. Established in 1958, the Produttori del Barbaresco is a world renowned cooperative founded by a local priest and 19 growers to rescue the reputation of the region's Nebbiolo grapes. Today, the cooperative unites over 50 members who exclusively produce Nebbiolo, adhering to traditional winemaking methods that prioritize transparency of terroir. The Montestefano vineyard, first released as a single cru Riserva in 1967, is known for its higher clay content and typically produces some of the most dark and austere wines in the cooperative's prestigious range.

Wine Description

This elegant red wine presents a deep ruby colour with garnet highlights. The aromatic profile for the 2020 vintage is especially refined, offering an intricate bouquet of violet, rose, red skinned fruit, forest floor, and new leather, underscored by notes of blood orange, mint, and cedar. On the palate, it is medium to full bodied and polished, delivering juicy flavours of raspberry compote, red cherry, and star anise balanced by a vibrant acidity. The finish is long and resonant, marked by refined tannins and lingering notes of white pepper, minerality, and licorice. This 100% Nebbiolo varietal composition was fermented for 28 days with skin contact before aging for 30 months in large oak barrels followed by nine months in the bottle. It has an alcohol content of 14.5% ABV and an optimal drinking window from 2025 through 2045. While the estate follows sustainable practices, this wine is not certified organic.

Accolades

  • Vinous - 97 points

  • Wine Spectator - 96 points

  • Jeb Dunnuck - 93 points

Food Pairing

The structured elegance and savory character of Montestefano Riserva make it a versatile partner for rich Italian cuisine. It pairs exceptionally well with fresh egg pasta dishes, mushroom risotto, and white or red meats. The wine's polished tannins also complement game dishes such as venison and a variety of mature cheeses.

Vintage Quality

The 2020 vintage in Barbaresco is described as extremely good, characterized by a mild spring and warm summer with regular rain storms that prevented vine stress. While the wines are noted for being a bit lighter in body than some previous years, they are complete and complex with seductive fruit concentration and excellent aging potential.

title: Chateau Quintus 2015
bodyHtml:
Introduction

Château Quintus 2015 is a red wine from France, produced in the Bordeaux region and the Saint-Émilion Grand Cru Classé appellation. The estate is owned by Domaine Clarence Dillon, the family behind the First Growth Château Haut-Brion, and benefits from the expertise of their winemaking team. The 2015 vintage is part of a string of critically acclaimed years for the estate, recognized for its density, aromatic purity, and great potential.

Wine Description

The wine has a deep garnet-purple or deep, almost inky colour. The aromatic profile is noted for its complexity and vibrancy, featuring notes of black and red cherries, stewed plums, and mulberries, lifted by exotic spice. Hints of dark chocolate, cinnamon stick, licorice, and fragrant earth add depth.

  • Varietal Composition: 80% Merlot and 20% Cabernet Franc.

  • Body and Palate: Full-bodied and richly fruited, with an abundance of black fruit flavors. The wine shows tremendous richness on the mid-palate.

  • Structure: The texture is smooth, dense, and velvety, supported by fine-grained, firm tannins. Critics note its excellent balance and purity of fruit.

  • Aging: Aged in French oak barrels (35% new oak for the 2015 vintage).

  • ABV: 14.8%.

  • Optimal Drinking Window: Long-term aging potential, typically from 2022 to 2045.

Accolades

The 2015 is considered one of the estate's top-performing vintages.

  • James Suckling - 97 points

  • Jeb Dunnuck - 95 points

  • Robert Parker's Wine Advocate - 94 points

  • Decanter (Jane Anson) - 93 points

  • Vinous (Antonio Galloni) - 93 points

Food Pairing

This rich and powerful Saint-Émilion pairs beautifully with all classic meat dishes. Suggested pairings include:

  • Roasted and braised meats, such as beef, veal, and lamb.

  • Duck and game dishes.

Vintage Quality

The 2015 vintage in Saint-Émilion was celebrated as a modern classic. Favourable weather conditions throughout the year, especially a warm and dry summer, led to grapes with excellent phenolic maturity and high concentration. The resulting wines are marked by their richness, smooth tannins, and potential for long-term cellaring.

title: Sottimano Barbaresco 'Basarin' 2018
bodyHtml:
Characterized by balsamic herbs, minerality, and spices. The palate offers a hint of wild fruit and an intense fruity texture, characterized in particular by cherry and strawberry. Long and velvety tannins accompany a spicy note, typical of this particular area of the municipality of Neive, facing the municipality of Treiso.

95 Points - Wine Enthusiast

Balsamic aromas of camphor mingle with earthy whiffs of forest floor, new leather, cedar, and wild berries on this elegant, full-bodied red. The tight, linear palate is delicious and loaded with personality, delivering ripe Morello cherry, mocha, licorice, and an earthy note of truffle framed in firm, fine-grained tannins. Fresh acidity keeps it well-balanced. 

95 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The Sottimano 2018 Barbaresco Basarin shows tart cherry fruit and plum backed by lovely layers of crushed mineral, iron ore, spice and crushed flowers. The wine reveals an inner brightness or tartness that tastes terrific next the more nuanced character of the Nebbiolo grape. Basarin shows power and elegance in equal measure, and that is never an easy feat for any winemaker to accomplish.

93 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

Located in the southeast of Neive, the 2018 Barbaresco Basarin has spiced aromatics of tobacco, confected cherry, and anise. The palate is lifted with tangy cranberry, dried violets, and clove spice, and fine tannins emerge on the finish.

title: Chateau Giscours 2020
bodyHtml:
Château Giscours, a prestigious Third Growth estate in Margaux, embodies the grandeur of Bordeaux winemaking. With centuries of history and a dedication to excellence, this château seamlessly combines tradition with modern techniques to craft wines of remarkable complexity and elegance.

Wine Description

The 2020 vintage boasts a deep garnet color with vibrant, purple highlights. On the nose, it reveals aromas of blackberries, cassis, and violets, complemented by notes of graphite and a whisper of vanilla. The palate is full-bodied and layered, offering a lush texture with polished tannins and flavors of dark fruits, cocoa, and subtle spices. The wine finishes with impressive length, marked by a harmonious balance of power and finesse.

Food Pairing

This wine pairs beautifully with beef Wellington, herb-crusted rack of lamb, or wild mushroom risotto. A perfect match to enhance the wine's complexity.

Vintage Quality

The 2020 vintage is widely regarded as exceptional in Bordeaux, benefiting from optimal ripening conditions. Château Giscours 2020 stands out for its concentration and purity, capturing the essence of an outstanding vintage.

title: Tenuta Di Biserno 'Biserno' 2021
bodyHtml:
Tenuta Di Biserno is situated in the municipality of Bibbona within the Upper Maremma region of Tuscany, Italy. Founded in 2001, the estate is a prestigious collaboration between brothers Marchese Lodovico and Piero Antinori, alongside their nephew Niccolò Marzichi Lenzi. The winery’s philosophy focuses on a parcel-by-parcel study of their diverse terroir—rich in alluvial sands and volcanic soils—to craft world-class wines with a distinct coastal identity.

Wine Description

The Biserno presents an intense, deep, and lively ruby red colour in the glass. The nose offers a complex aromatic harmony, opening with balsamic and Mediterranean scents interwoven with sweet toasted notes and a fruity bouquet of strawberry and black fruit. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied and enveloping, characterized by an intriguing savouriness and well-integrated tannins.

Accolades

  • Wine Spectator - 90 points

  • James Suckling - 94 points

  • Robert Parker - 92 points

Food Pairing

This powerful red is an ideal companion for rich, savoury dishes such as a grilled rack of lamb with rosemary and garlic or a beef stew with red wine sauce. It also pairs beautifully with earthy flavours like wild mushroom risotto drizzled with truffle oil.

title: Brumont Chateau Montus 'La Tyre' 2008
bodyHtml: Alain Brumont’s pride, La Tyre vintage, is 100% iconic Tannat. The exceptional Madiran carries abundance, depth, complexity and great concentration. Fresh, and consistent, La Tyre is marked by red and black fruit compote scents with intense spices and smoky hints. To the palate, this Château Montus offers a more supple texture, followed by rich, fleshy impressions, and tasty, fine tannins.

title: E. Guigal Cote Rotie Chateau d'Ampuis 2020
bodyHtml:
This structured and 'aristocratic' red wine originates from France, within the prestigious Côte-Rôtie A.O.C. appellation in the northern Rhône Valley. Produced by Maison E. Guigal the iconic estate founded in 1946 by Etienne Guigal and elevated to international legend by Marcel and Philippe Guigal Château d'Ampuis represents one of the crowning jewels of the northern Rhône. Sourced from seven exceptional historic estate vineyard plots spanning both the Côte Blonde and Côte Brune (including Le Clos, La Garde, La Grande Plantée, La Pommière, Lancement, Les Rochins, and Le Lardin), the vines average over 50 years of age. Planted on dizzyingly steep, terraced slopes rooted in schist, granite, iron-rich limestone, and mica-schist soils, the vines thrive under a continental microclimate. Mediterranean warmth is tempered by cool alpine winds down the Rhône river corridor, allowing Syrah and Viognier to achieve complete phenolic maturity while retaining a chiseled natural acidity and profound mineral drive.

Wine Description

E. Guigal Côte-Rôtie Château d'Ampuis presents an opaque, deep black-ruby color in the glass with bright violet and garnet reflections along the rim. Its sensory profile is exceptionally bold, high-toned, and complex, delivering an expansive, precise, and authoritative portrayal of roasted slope terroir. The bouquet opens with a soaring display of crushed dark plum, black raspberry compote, and cassis, seamlessly layered with complex underlays of fresh violets, cured bacon fat, cracked black pepper, dark chocolate, espresso bean, pipe tobacco, and a distinct line of smoky iron-ore minerality. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied, dense, and athletic, showcasing a succulent core of dark fruits, licorice, blood orange zest, and savory spices. It is characterized by its outstanding inner energy and an incisive, mouthwatering backbone of natural acidity that effortlessly elevates its immense mid-palate density. The mouthfeel is broad, velvety, and linear, framed by firm, muscular, yet fine-grained tannins that glide into an extraordinarily long, dry, and mineral-driven finish accented by persistent notes of tapenade, roasted coffee, and toasted cedar.

title: Poderi Aldo Conterno Barolo Bussia Romirasco 2019
bodyHtml:
The 2019 Poderi Aldo Conterno Barolo Bussia Romirasco is an expression of Nebbiolo from the renowned Bussia cru in Monforte d’Alba, Piedmont. This wine reflects the mastery of the Conterno family in crafting structured and elegant Barolo with exceptional depth and aging potential.

Vineyard and Production

Sourced from the Romirasco vineyard, one of the finest sites within Bussia, this wine benefits from calcareous-clay soils rich in iron, which contribute to its power and complexity. The vines, averaging 50–55 years old, enjoy optimal sun exposure, allowing the fruit to achieve perfect ripeness. Hand-harvested in mid-October, the grapes undergo 30 days of maceration in stainless steel, followed by extended aging in large Slavonian oak casks to enhance its balance and refinement.

Tasting Notes

  • Appearance: Deep garnet red with ruby reflections, evolving to orange hues with age.
  • Aroma: A layered bouquet of red cherries, wild strawberries, and dried roses, with hints of spice, tobacco, and earthy truffle.
  • Palate: Full-bodied and structured, with fine-grained tannins, vibrant acidity, and flavors of red fruit, licorice, leather, and balsamic undertones. The finish is long, persistent, and refined, with a touch of minerality.

Critical Acclaim

  • 98 points (community reviews) – Celebrated for its depth, elegance, and aging potential.

Serving and Pairing

Decanting for at least an hour enhances its aromatic complexity. Best served at 16-18°C (61-64°F), this Barolo pairs beautifully with braised meats, wild game, aged cheeses, and truffle-based dishes. Its structure also makes it an excellent companion to hearty pasta dishes like tajarin with ragù.

title: Achaval Ferrer Finca Altamira 2019
bodyHtml:
Achaval Ferrer, established in 1998, is a renowned Argentine winery celebrated for its dedication to crafting world-class, terroir-driven red wines. Located in the Uco Valley of Mendoza, the Finca Altamira vineyard was planted in 1950 at the foothill of the Andes just below the Tunuyán River.

Wine Description

The 2019 Finca Altamira Malbec displays a deep ruby hue. On the nose, it offers captivating aromas of violets, ripe blackberries, and a touch of minerality. The palate is opulent yet structured, with flavors of dark fruits and a hint of mocha. The finish is long and graceful, leaving a lasting impression. Crafted entirely from Malbec grapes, this wine is expected to evolve gracefully over the next 15 to 20 years.

Accolades

  • James Suckling – 97 points.
  • Wine Advocate – 96 points.

Food Pairing

This Malbec pairs exquisitely with Argentine Angus steaks, enhancing the wine's depth and character. Additionally, it complements rich dishes such as braised lamb shanks or aged cheeses, creating an unforgettable dining experience.​

title: Echo de Lynch Bages 2022
bodyHtml:
France, Bordeaux, Pauillac. Echo de Lynch Bages is the esteemed second wine of Château Lynch Bages, one of Pauillac’s most renowned estates. The property, owned by the Cazes family since 1939, is celebrated for producing wines that balance power with elegance, showcasing the unique gravel terroir of the Médoc.

Wine Description

This vintage presents a deep ruby hue with violet reflections. The nose offers layered aromas of cassis, blackberry, and blueberry, intertwined with subtle notes of graphite, tobacco leaf, and a hint of mint. On the palate, it reveals a medium to full body with fine tannins, a supple texture, and lively acidity. Flavours of blackcurrant, forest herbs, and cocoa unfold with precision, leading to a mineral-tinged, persistent finish.

Accolades

  • Vinous - 90+ points

Food Pairing

Ideal pairings include grilled ribeye, roast lamb, or venison with herb jus. Mature hard cheeses such as aged Comté or sharp cheddar also complement the wine’s dark fruit and earthy notes.

title: Chateau Smith Haut Lafitte Rouge 2016
bodyHtml:
Smith Haut Lafitte rouge is a deep, concentrated, nearly black color. The bouquet displays a range of red and black fruit aromas, as well as ones reminiscent of spice and warm herbs. With aeration, the wine reveals magnificent black fruit, licorice, clove, and graphite nuances.

The wine has an extremely well-focused structure and taste. The long aftertaste of licorice, red fruit, and black fruit also features more subtle underlying flavors of hot stones and warm earth.

100 Points - Decanter

Pure perfection in a glass, the 2016 offers notes of cherry, liquorice, smoke, graphite, plum and eucalyptus. It is fresh and racy. This is a perfectly balanced wine, full of energy and freshness, juicy and fleshy on the palate, with a classic tannic frame and a long yet persistent finish. Drink it over the coming two or three decades. Bravo!

98 Points - Wine Spectator

Quite ripe, with lush waves of cassis, cherry preserve and raspberry puree flavors gliding through in no hurry, but maintaining definition and cut along the way as bramble, tar and melted licorice snap notes slowly emerge throughout. The finish features an intense echo of pastis and sweet tobacco, showing serious latent grip.

98 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Composed of 65% Cabernet Sauvignon, 30% Merlot, 4% Cabernet Franc and 1% Petit Verdot and matured in 60% new oak for 18 months, the 2016 Smith Haut Lafitte has a very deep garnet-purple color, opening with sensuous scents of warm black cherries, blackberry pie, star anise and fragrant lilacs with hints of chocolate box, cigar box and pencil lead plus wafts of truffles and crushed rocks. Medium to full-bodied, rich and seductive, it completely fills the palate with perfumed black berry preserves and superbly plush tannins, finishing epically long and beautifully layered.

97 Points - James Suckling

The blackcurrant and blueberry aromas are lifted and beautiful. Lots of flowers, too, together with some mushroom and dried-flower undertones. Full-bodied with firm and very silky tannins giving a lovely texture. Bright acidity lifts the finish and gives it drive and force. 

97 Points - Wine Enthusiast

This hugely dense wine is complex and full of juicy, succulent, smoky Cabernet Sauvignon. The tannins are at the service of the fruits. The wine still has a long way to go before maturity.

97 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

It’s undeniably a more elegant, reserved style from this estate, yet it still offers full-bodied richness and depth, with a classic perfume of cassis, black currants, cold fireplace, wood smoke, and tobacco. Deep, nicely concentrated, seamless, and, again, incredibly elegant, it’s going to flesh out nicely with short-term cellaring and keep for 20-30 years.

title: Domaine des Beaumont Morey Saint Denis Blanc 2020
bodyHtml:
In addition to great reds, Domaine des Beaumont also produces energetic and pure whites in the Cote de Cuits. Not just any white – the ideal balance between creamy rich and crispy fresh.

Morey-St-Denis Blanc has an expressive scent with dominant notes of both fresh and sweet pear. It is a combination between minerality and strength. It has a clean attack, which is typical for white wine from the Cote de Nuits, very complex in the middle and a fine, nicely finished end. 

A wine with a lot of expression, power and energy. In the taste, the aromas are confirmed once again and the wine ends soft and creamy with freshness and a lingering aftertaste.

title: Louis Jadot Chassagne Montrachet 2020
bodyHtml:
A deeply colored, full-bodied wine of depth and intensity with a persistent, earthy finish.

An excellent companion to fish, shellfish, poultry and cheeses.

92 Points - Wine Spectator

Rich and charming, with lemon cake, white peach and spice flavors finely woven into the creamy texture. Balanced and leaves a mouthwatering impression on the finish.

title: Masseto 2020 - 6 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
‘Masseto’ is one of the most sought-after Merlot-based wines in the world. Produced by Tenuta dell’Ornellaia, Masseto is a testament to the exceptional terroir of its namesake vineyard—a rare blue clay soil site that yields wines of extraordinary depth and complexity. Since its inaugural vintage in 1986, Masseto has achieved cult status, celebrated for its power, elegance, and aging potential.

Wine Description

The 2020 ‘Masseto’ unveils a deep, almost opaque ruby-red colour. The nose is intensely aromatic, offering layers of ripe black cherry, plum, and dark chocolate, accented by nuances of violet, graphite, and subtle sweet spices. On the palate, it is opulent yet refined, with velvety tannins supporting a rich core of black fruits, espresso, and tobacco. The wine’s structure is impeccably balanced, with fresh acidity ensuring vibrancy and a long, lingering finish laced with hints of cedar and mineral undertones. This vintage is poised for decades of graceful evolution.

Accolades

  • Decanter - 100 points
  • James Suckling - 99 points
  • Wine Enthusiast - 99 points
  • Wine Spectator - 97 points
  • Robert Parker's Wine Advocate - 96 points

Food Pairing

Pair this world-class Merlot with dry-aged ribeye, braised duck, or black truffle risotto. The wine’s depth and silky texture also complement aged Pecorino or Parmigiano-Reggiano. A perfect match to enhance the wine’s complexity.

Vintage Quality

The 2020 vintage in Bolgheri was marked by a warm growing season with steady conditions, resulting in exceptional ripeness and concentration. The well-timed harvest allowed for perfect phenolic development, creating a wine that balances richness with finesse. This vintage underscores Masseto’s legacy as one of Italy’s most iconic and age-worthy wines.

title: Domaine Michel Gros Echezeaux 'Les Loachausses' Grand Cru 2022
bodyHtml:
Domaine Michel Gros, established in 1979, is a renowned family-owned winery located in Vosne-Romanée, within Burgundy's esteemed Côte de Nuits region. The Gros family has been cultivating vineyards in the area since the 19th century, with Michel Gros representing the sixth generation of winemakers. The estate is celebrated for its dedication to traditional viticulture and meticulous winemaking practices, resulting in wines of exceptional quality and character.

Wine Description

The 2022 Echezeaux 'Les Loachausses' Grand Cru is the inaugural release from a 0.38-hectare parcel previously managed by Gros Frère & Soeur, now under the stewardship of Michel Gros. This 100% Pinot Noir wine showcases a vibrant garnet hue. On the nose, it reveals an expressive bouquet of red berry fruits, Japanese yuzu, Seville orange marmalade, and subtle forest floor nuances. The palate is smooth and harmonious, offering plush textures with a toasty finish attributed to its maturation in 100% new oak. The wine's ample body and silky tannins are balanced by a lively acidity, culminating in a long, sumptuous finish. While approachable in its youth, this wine will benefit from several years of cellaring to fully integrate its oak components and develop further complexity.

Accolades

  • Vinous - 93-95 points.
  • Burghound - 92-94 points.

Food Pairing

This elegant Grand Cru pairs excellently with:

  • Roasted duck breast with a cherry glaze.​
  • Wild mushroom risotto.​
  • Aged Comté cheese.

title: Lignier Michelot Morey Saint Denis Vieilles Vignes 2022
bodyHtml: Matured with 80% whole bunches, the Morey-Saint-Denis Vieilles Vignes has potent marine oyster shell scents on a nose that is very focused and poised. The palate is medium-bodied with fine-grained tannin, superb minerality and a supremely well-proportioned finish.

title: Martoccia Brunello di Montalcino Riserva 2016
bodyHtml:
This Brunello Riserva is a deep ruby red colour, tending towards garnet with age.

The complex and intense aroma offers layers of dark cherry, raspberry, licorice, and balsamic notes. Critics have also noted a floral profile reminiscent of lavender and magnolia blossoms, alongside notes of red plums, strawberries, and spices.

It is a full-bodied wine that is elegant yet powerful. The palate features dark and red fruit flavours, such as dried morello cherry, plum, and raspberry, with notes of black tea and rosemary.

The structure is balanced by fine, smooth tannins and a lively, well-integrated acidity. The finish is long, layered, and fresh.

The varietal composition is 100% Sangiovese Grosso.

The optimal drinking window extends at least to 2033, with some reviews suggesting best from 2025 onwards.

The wine is produced using organically farmed grapes, though the winery is not officially certified as organic.

Accolades

  • Raffaele Vecchione - WinesCritic.com - 93 points

  • Wine Spectator - 93 points

  • Jeb Dunnuck - 92 points

  • Decanter World Wine Awards - 92 points

  • Falstaff - 90 points

Food Pairing

Suggested pairings include red meats, both grilled and stewed, as well as game such as wild boar.

It pairs wonderfully with richly seasoned first courses, such as pasta with a hearty meat or wild boar ragout.

The wine is also an ideal match for long-seasoned cheeses and very mature rich cheeses.
A perfect match to enhance the wine's complexity.

Vintage Quality

  • The 2016 vintage for Brunello di Montalcino is widely classified as a five-star vintage, characterized by a long, cool growing season with optimal weather patterns.

  • The climate trend, including a cold winter, sufficient spring rain to build water reserves, and significant diurnal temperature variations in the summer, was nearly perfect for developing aromatic intensity and quality tannins.

  • The resulting wines are known for combining fruit richness, tannic power, freshness, and finesse, with a structure built for long-term aging.

title: Chateau Haut Brion 2014
bodyHtml:
Chateau Haut-Brion is the oldest and by far the smallest of the "Premiers Grands Crus" vineyards of the Gironde 1855 classification. Chateau Haut-Brion is one of the few remaining family-owned domains of the Bordeaux region with a history going back to the 16th century. It has been owned by the American Dillon family since 1935. Thanks to its long history as one of Bordeaux's most prestigious wines, the estate has left its mark on the region for centuries.

Deep, dark red color. The nose is very deep with powerful aromas of black fruit and spice. The wine starts out quite powerful on the palate, but softens on the middle palate, developing a lovely velvety texture. The finely polished tannic structure is enhanced by considerable concentration and full, luscious body.

100 Points - Wine Enthusiast

Full of ripe fruit, opulent and concentrated, this is a fabulous and impressive wine. It has a beautiful line of acidity balanced with ripe fruits. The wood aging is subtle, just a hint of smokiness and toast. This is one of those wines, from a great white wine vintage, that will age many years. Drink from 2024. 

97 Points - James Suckling

Beautifully perfumed with rose petals, violets and currant bush. Full body, very silky tannins and bright acidity. Tannins are super fine-grained. Goes on for minutes. Racy and refined. Persistent. Drink in 2025.

96 Points - Wine Spectator

Loaded with warm tar, singed juniper, plum reduction and cassis notes that are perfectly melded, giving this a remarkably supple edge. The finish lets tobacco, bay leaf and incense accents glide in. Shows lovely mouthfeel and superior refinement overall. Best from 2020 through 2035.

96 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

96 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

95+ Points - Decanter

title: Vina Cobos Malbec Hobbs Estate 2021
bodyHtml:
Produced in Argentina, this exceptional Malbec hails from the Agrelo district within the Luján de Cuyo region of Mendoza. Viña Cobos was founded in 1999 by visionary American winemaker Paul Hobbs, who is widely credited with elevating Argentine Malbec to the international stage. The winery’s philosophy centers on a meticulous, 'Grand Cru' study of specific parcels to capture the purest expression of the terroir.

Wine Description

This wine presents a deep ruby red colour with distinct violet tones. The aromatic profile is captivating and elegant, featuring a blend of red fruits, plum, and violets underscored by sophisticated notes of graphite, dark chocolate, and spearmint. On the palate, the wine is opulent and full bodied, offering a juicy mouthfeel with layers of blueberries and blackcurrants supported by silky, well polished tannins.

Accolades

  • James Suckling - 96 points

  • Vinous - 96 points

  • Wine Advocate - 95+ points

  • Wine Spectator - 93 points

Food Pairing

The wine’s rich fruit and structured tannins make it an ideal companion for a hearty steak, such as a grilled ribeye with chimichurri, or gamey meats like venison and lamb. It also pairs wonderfully with earthy mushroom dishes or pungent cheeses like gorgonzola.

title: San Polo Brunello di Montalcino 'Podernovi' 2020
bodyHtml:
This distinguished red wine hails from the Montalcino region within Tuscany, Italy. Purchased by the Allegrini family in 2007, the San Polo estate is managed with a commitment to sustainability and regenerative agriculture, holding a CasaClima Wine certification for its eco-friendly underground cellar. The 'Podernovi' vineyard is a specific single-vineyard plot characterized by its high altitude and soils rich in marl and clay, which the winery uses to produce an elegant, archetypal expression of the terroir.

Wine Description

Podernovi presents a clear ruby red colour with purple reflections. On the nose, it offers an expressive and seductive profile of raspberry, cherry, and violets, complemented by hints of mint, hibiscus, and aromatic wood. The palate is juicy and well-structured, featuring flavours of currants, dark cherries, and a touch of marzipan. This medium-bodied wine is defined by its gripping acidity, integrated tannins, and a long, savoury finish.

Accolades

  • Wine Spectator - 93 points

  • James Suckling - 94 points

Food Pairing

The wine’s elegant structure and vibrant acidity make it a superb companion for red meats, wild game, or dishes featuring mushrooms and truffles. It also pairs beautifully with aged cheeses such as Parmigiano Reggiano or Tuscan pecorino.

title: Castello di Montepo Fontecanese 2020
vendor: 300747 - South By Southwest Wine Imports Inc.
bodyHtml:
Introduction

This rare and ambitious red wine originates from the Castello di Montepò estate in the Maremma region of Tuscany, the private domain of Jacopo Biondi Santi. Distinct from the family's Sangiovese-focused legacy, Fontecanese is Jacopo’s challenge to the world of international varietals, a "Cru" conceived to be one of Italy's premier expressions of Cabernet Sauvignon.
