The wine is sourced exclusively from a tiny, distinct vineyard plot rich in galestro (rocky, schistous clay) located between 357 and 377 meters above sea level. Selected after years of meticulous micro-zonation studies for its unique exposure and soil composition, this site yields fruit of extraordinary concentration and character. It represents a "Super Tuscan" of purity and precision, showcasing how the rugged Maremma terroir can transform a noble French grape into a distinctly Italian masterpiece.

Wine Description

Castello di Montepò Fontecanese 2020 displays a deep, impenetrable ruby colour with youthful purple nuances. The nose is profound and aromatic, characterized by a dazzling interplay of ripe blackberries, raspberries, and dark plums, interwoven with high-toned herbal notes that "crackle with vibrancy." As it opens, it reveals complex layers of cedarwood, dark chocolate, black truffle, and a sophisticated hint of black tea or tarragon. On the palate, the wine is medium-to-full bodied and defined by remarkable compactness and tension. It offers a core of juicy, vivid fruit that balances a natural sweetness with a savory, saline undercurrent. The tannins are "chiseled" and architectural, firm yet ultra-fine, leading to a very long, structured finish. This 100% Cabernet Sauvignon undergoes native yeast fermentation and is aged for 24 months in French oak barriques, followed by roughly 16 months of bottle refinement. The optimal drinking window is from release through the next 20+ years.

Accolades

The 2020 vintage of Fontecanese has received extraordinary critical acclaim, marking it as a benchmark year for this label. It was awarded a perfect 100 Points by Jonathan Cristaldi for The Tasting Panel, who described it as having "power and precision on display throughout." Additionally, it has garnered high praise from Decanter, receiving 96 Points, with critics noting its complexity and "Tuscan light" that shoots through the Cabernet profile.

title: Massetino 2023
bodyHtml:
Massetino is the esteemed 'second wine' of the legendary Masseto estate, a jewel in the portfolio of the Marchesi de’ Frescobaldi family, who have been winemakers for over 700 years. The estate’s winemaking philosophy centres on the uncompromising pursuit of excellence and expressing the unique character of their terroir, which is defined by ancient Pliocene blue clays ideally suited for Merlot.

Wine Description

The bouquet is already very pleasant, offering fresh and intoxicating red fruit aromas mingled with notes of restrained bramble fruit, vanilla, cloves, eucalyptus, and leather. It also displays tertiary notes of damp earth, Mediterranean scrub, and chocolatey nuances.

On the palate, Merlot and Cabernet Franc merge to exalt the wine’s concentration. It is full-bodied, yet defined by a steely energy and a lovely line of acidity that runs through the body, giving it a freshness and juicy character. The structure is vertical and supported by firm, velvety tannins and notes of graphite and chocolate flavours, with a slight tangy note persisting on the long finish.

Accolades

  • "Decanter - 96 points."

  • "James Suckling - 95 points."

  • "Wine Spectator - 92 points."

Food Pairing

This elegant, approachable red blend is a versatile partner for a range of flavorful dishes. Its fresh fruit and balanced structure pair beautifully with roasted red meats, savory stews, and grilled lamb.

title: Gaja Barolo Sperss 2021 - 3 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
1. Introduction

This wine originates in Italy, specifically from the esteemed Barolo subregion within the Piedmont region. The Gaja winery, founded in Barbaresco in 1859, has grown to be one of Italy's most influential producers under the leadership of Angelo Gaja. The 'Sperss' bottling, which means 'nostalgia' in the local dialect, is a tribute to Angelo Gaja’s father, who had always loved the Serralunga d'Alba site where the grapes are sourced. The Gaja philosophy blends tradition with innovation, focusing intensely on vineyard quality and biodiversity.

2. Wine Description

The Gaja Barolo Sperss 2021 is made entirely from the Nebbiolo grape varietal. It displays a jewelled ruby colour. The sensory profile is marked by pure notes of black raspberries, sweet flowers, fresh herbs, and apricot. A distinctive ferrous note of rusty nail or soft earth is also present, which frames a core of dark fruit.

On the palate, this is a full bodied, dense, and complex wine with a powerful, concentrated fruit. It exhibits a beguiling matched balance of power and finesse. The wine possesses a backbone of firm but refined tannins and impressive acidity that keeps it vibrant. It has an austere but positive texture. The optimal drinking window is considered to be best after 2026, with an ageing potential of several decades, perhaps until 2046 or 2059. There is no information to indicate that the wine is organic. 

3. Accolades

  • Jeb Dunnuck - 100 points

  • Kerin O'Keefe 99 points

  • Robert Parker's Wine Advocate - 98+ points

  • Antonio Galloni - 97 points

4. Food Pairing

This powerfully structured Barolo is an excellent partner for rich, hearty, and savoury dishes. Its firm tannins and acidity are well suited to cleansing the palate of rich, fatty meats. Traditional pairings include braised meats like Brasato al Barolo (veal, lamb, or wild boar braised in wine), or veal chops. The wine’s earthy notes and complexity also make it a classic match for Piedmontese specialities featuring truffles or mushrooms, such as risotto or tajarin pasta with a rich butter or sage sauce. Strong, mature cheeses like Castelmagno DOP are also highly complementary. 

5. Vintage Quality 

The 2021 vintage in Barolo is highly regarded and is considered by many critics to be one of the best in recent history, standing alongside 2010 and 2016 for its high quality and consistency. The season featured a beneficial amount of snowfall in the winter which replenished water reserves, followed by a mostly dry, sunny summer without major heat spikes. Cooler nights helped the Nebbiolo grapes achieve slow, perfect ripening, resulting in a combination of classic Barolo power, high acidity, elegant tannins, and excellent freshness.

title: Ayala Blanc de Blancs 2017
bodyHtml: Champagne AYALA is one of the longest-established champagne Houses; it has been based in Aÿ, at the heart of the great champagne vineyards, since it was founded over 150 years ago. Independent and family-owned, it is still today the archetype of a great and historic House, producing top quality wines which are enjoyed throughout the world for their freshness and elegance. Edmond de Ayala, founder of the House in 1860, came from a family that had always aspired to go one step further.

title: Diamond Creek Cabernet Sauvignon Volcanic Hill 2019 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
76% Cabernet Sauvignon, 14% Merlot, 7% Malbec and 3% Petit Verdot.

This south-facing hillside terraced vineyard with its grey ashy volcanic sandy soils yields another big, bold expression with a suitably dark black opaque colour. But there is nothing broody about the wine’s aromatics that burst out the glass with notes of gingerbread, saline black currant, melted tar, stewed black cherries, camphor and hints of graphite.

The palate is focused and powerful with a big concentration of creamy black and blue berry fruits, very fine grained, stern, mineral graphite tannins and an incredibly compact, precise yet generous mouthfeel. Lovely balance and seductive power. A real WOW wine!

title: Chateau Lafite Rothschild 2002
bodyHtml:
Introduction

Château Lafite Rothschild 2002 is a legendary red wine from France, hailing from the prestigious Pauillac appellation in the Médoc region of Bordeaux. This historic estate is one of only five producers originally awarded First Growth (Premier Cru) status in the 1855 Classification of Bordeaux wines. Since 1868, the château has been owned by the Rothschild family, beginning with Baron James de Rothschild and continuing today under the leadership of Saskia de Rothschild, who became the first female chairwoman of the family's wine business in 2018.

Description

This 2002 vintage is a 'savory and classic' Bordeaux blend composed of 87% Cabernet Sauvignon, 9.5% Merlot, and 3.5% Cabernet Franc.

  • Colour: It possesses a deep ruby to garnet hue, showing impressive concentration for its age.

  • Aroma: The nose is complex and intense, offering scents of blackberry, currant, and plum interwoven with delicate notes of pencil lead (graphite), cedar, mint, tobacco, and black olive.

  • Palate: On the palate, the wine is medium to full bodied and concentrated, featuring a seductive entry and silky texture with layers of dark berries, figs, and earthy minerality.

  • Body: It is characterized by its quintessentially elegant and suave structure, supported by a strong spine of acidity and finely chiselled, velvety tannins.

  • Finish: The finish is long, racy, and persistent, building incrementally with finesse and power.

  • ABV: This wine is bottled at 12.5% alcohol by volume.

Accolades

  • Wine Spectator - 95 points

  • Robert Parker's Wine Advocate - 94 points

  • Decanter - 93 points

  • Vinous - 92 points

title: Stag's Leap Wine Cellars Cabernet Sauvignon SLV 2018
bodyHtml:
The 2018 S.L.V. Cabernet Sauvignon has generous aromas of violet, plum dark fruit, cocoa dust and graphite. On the palate the wine has a rich, gravelly structure with pure fruit, dusty tannins and a long, savory finish. The tannin structure, dark fruit, and pleasing minerality point to this wine’s ability to age.
 
97 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate    The 2018 Cabernet Sauvignon S.L.V., a barrel sample, reveals a deep garnet-purple colour and expressive notions of blackberry preserves, black cherry coulis and warm cassis with suggestions of eucalyptus, dark chocolate, lavender and tobacco leaf. Medium to full-bodied, the palate is tightly wound with black fruit and savoury layers, supported by a rock-solid frame of grainy tannins and just enough freshness, finishing long and lifted.
 
97 Points - James Suckling    This is one of the best SLVs I have tasted with total balance and structure that highlights what was possible in 2018. It’s full-bodied, yet tight and poised, with layer upon layer of fine tannins that give depth and beauty to this young red. Blackcurrant, blueberry and floral flavours.
 
94 Points - Wine Spectator    Polished and open at first, showing a fan-friendly set of creamed plum and warmed cassis flavors, laced with melted licorice and sweet toast accents. Features alder and warm earth hints that check in on the finish, adding extra range and length while giving the fruit a grounded feel in the end. Very solidly built. Drink now through 2038.

title: Catena Zapata Adrianna Vineyard 'River' Malbec 2022
bodyHtml:
Introduction

This red wine originates from Argentina, specifically from the Gualtallary subregion of the Uco Valley within the Mendoza region. Founded in 1902 by Italian immigrant Nicola Catena, Catena Zapata is Argentina's oldest family-owned winery, currently managed by fourth-generation vintner Dr. Laura Catena and Chief Winemaker Alejandro Vigil. The winery's philosophy is rooted in a 'vineyard lot revolution' that uses scientific research to understand high-altitude terroirs. The Adrianna Vineyard, situated at nearly 5,000 feet elevation, is often called the 'Grand Cru' of South America, and this specific cuvée comes from the 'River' parcel, an ancient, stony riverbed.

Wine Description

Catena Zapata Adrianna Vineyard 'River' Malbec 2022 displays a deep red colour with vibrant violet hues. The nose is incredibly aromatic and ethereal, offering scents of blackberry, ripe plum, and wild berries layered with floral notes of lavender, violets, and rosehips, alongside herbal hints of sage, arugula, and white pepper. On the palate, the wine is medium to full-bodied with a taut, spry, and weightless texture that evokes the elegance of a Pinot Noir. It is characterized by its chalky intensity, mineral-tinged tension, and a seamless, long-lasting finish. This 100% Malbec has an ABV of 13.5% and was aged for up to 21 months in French oak barrels. The Adrianna Vineyard is farmed sustainably and is certified organic. The optimal drinking window is from 2026 through 2042.

Accolades

  • James Suckling - 99 points.

  • Wine Advocate - 98+ points.

  • Vinous - 98 points.

  • Wine Enthusiast - 97 points.

  • Descorchados - 98 points.

  • Jeb Dunnuck - 96 points.

  • Wine Spectator - 94 points.

Food Pairing

The elegant structure and mineral drive of this Malbec make it an exceptional partner for refined, savoury dishes. It pairs perfectly with Patagonian lamb seasoned with fresh herbs, beef tenderloin with chimichurri, or cocoa-rubbed duck breast. The wine's vibrant acidity and stony salinity also complement mushroom and truffle risottos, as well as strong cheeses or red pasta dishes.

Vintage Quality

The 2022 vintage in Mendoza was characterized by a warm summer followed by a cooler autumn, which resulted in beautifully balanced wines with fresh acidity. Despite a challenging start with a cool spring and water shortages, the high-altitude Gualtallary vineyards produced fruit with exceptional aromatic concentration and finesse.

title: E. Pira e Figli Chiara Boschis - Barolo 'Mosconi' 2020
bodyHtml:
This Barolo originates from the Mosconi vineyard in the Monforte d'Alba subregion of Piedmont, Italy. The historic E. Pira e Figli estate was acquired in 1981 by the Boschis family, who entrusted the winery to Chiara Boschis, one of the first female winemakers in the region and a leading figure in the 'Barolo Boys' revolution. Her winemaking philosophy focuses on marrying the traditional power of Barolo with modern elegance and approachability, utilizing certified organic farming and meticulous manual vineyard management.

Wine Description

The Barolo 'Mosconi' presents a rich ruby red colour with a slight garnet reflection. The nose is aromatically complex, offering vibrant notes of red raspberry, black cherry, and dried roses, underpinned by savory hints of eucalyptus, menthol, anise, and dusty earth. On the palate, the wine is full bodied, broad, and authoritative, featuring a core of morello cherry and plum. It displays the muscular structure typical of Monforte, with dense, ripe tannins and a chalky texture that leads into a long, mineral finish with pure notes of apricot and iron.

Accolades

  • Jeb Dunnuck - 98 points

  • James Suckling - 97 points

  • The Wine Advocate - 96 points

  • Vinous - 95 points

  • Wine Spectator - 93 points

Food Pairing

This powerful and structured Barolo is ideally suited for rich, savoury dishes such as braised beef, roasted game, or wild mushroom risotto. It also pairs excellently with aged cheeses like Castelmagno or Pecorino.

title: Chateau Brane Cantenac 2015
bodyHtml:
Established in the 18th century, it was known as "Gorce" this large estate is located on the best gravelly outcrops of Cantenac. A century before the 1855 classification, it was considered one of the best second growths in the Medoc. In 1833, Baron de Brane (called "Napoleon of the Vines") sold his estate in Pauillac, Brane-Mouton, and bought Gorce, which he renamed "Brane-Cantenac", ten years later.

Lucien Lurton's grandfather acquired the estate in 1925 and was succeeded by his grandson in 1956. Lucien Lurton's son, Henri, currently manages the estate and puts all his efforts into producing a great Margaux in every vintage, reflecting Brane-Cantenac's superb vineyard soil.

96 Points - Wine Enthusiast

Rich, fruity and with great potential, this ripe wine is also dense with firm tannins. Its juicy fruits are a part of a package with concentrated tannins and smoky wood flavours that allow for long aging. This is an impressive wine from one of the Margaux properties owned by the Lurton family. Drink from 2025.

94 Points - James Suckling

Quite impressive ripe dark plums and blackberries with sweet, earthy depth and cedary background oak on the nose. The palate has smooth, slick tannins that carry rich dark fruit that is long and fresh. This has terrific energy and depth. Vibrant. Incredible length. Drink from 2022.

94 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

The 2015 Chateau Brane-Cantenac checks in as a mix of 70% Cabernet Sauvignon, 26% Merlot and the balance Cabernet Franc and Carmenere brought up in roughly 75% new French oak. This medium to full-bodied beauty excels on all accounts and gives up gorgeous notes of blackcurrants, lead pencil, spice and hints of toasted bread. Polished, impeccably balanced, concentrated, and with ripe tannin, it's a rock star in 2015 that can be drunk young or cellared for 20-25 years. Bravo!

93 Points - Wine Spectator

Silky and refined, with seductive crushed plum and raspberry fruit that glides along, perfectly melded with singed alder and mesquite notes along with black tea and warm licorice details. A violet element hangs in the background, adding to the elegance. Best from 2020 through 2035.

93 Points - Decanter

Beautifully concentrated floral, fragrant fruit plus minerally depth with smoothness to come. A very fine wine from this on-form second growth.

92 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2015 Brane-Cantenac is medium to deep garnet-purple in colour with a nose of crushed blackberries and chocolate-covered cherries with touches of fried herbs and tilled soil. It has an herbal lift on the finish, is medium-bodied, refreshing and elegant in the mouth, with chewy tannins.

title: Domaine Daniel Etienne Defaix Chablis 'Vaillon' Premier Cru 2016
bodyHtml:
Domaine Daniel-Etienne Defaix Chablis 1er Cru Vaillon is a historic and highly individual white wine from the Chablis region of Burgundy, France. The Defaix family is one of the oldest winegrowing dynasties in the region, with roots in Chablis dating back to 1610 across 14 generations. The winery is famous for being a "last bastion of the Chablis of yore," famously holding its wines in the cellar for 10 to 15 years before release. Winemaker Daniel-Etienne Defaix follows a philosophy of extreme patience, allowing the wines to mature on their fine lees for up to a decade to achieve a depth and complexity rarely seen in modern Chablis.

Wine Description

This 100% Chardonnay is sourced from a prime four-hectare parcel in the historic heart of the Vaillon vineyard, which the family labels as "Vaillon" (singular) rather than the expanded "Les Vaillons" to emphasize its superior original location.

  • Colour: The wine develops a deep straw or pale gold colour as it ages.

  • Aroma: The nose is intensely complex, featuring smoky and stony minerality alongside evolved notes of honey, nuts, and earthy mushroom, with bright citrus and floral undertones.

  • Palate: It is notably rich and dense, showing a textural "gourmand" profile that contrasts with the typical tartness of Chablis. Flavours include ripe lemon, pear, and waxy honey, underpinned by a persistent saline minerality.

  • Technical Details: Defaix is strictly in the "unoaked" camp; the wine is fermented with indigenous yeasts and aged for years exclusively in stainless steel tanks. This extended period of yeast autolysis (lees contact) acts as a natural antioxidant and promotes a generous, waxy texture. The wine typically has an ABV of 13%.

  • Farming: The estate follows traditional and sustainable farming practices, avoiding chemical fertilizers and herbicides.

Food Pairing

The maturity and richness of this 1er Cru allow it to pair with more substantial and complex dishes than younger Chablis:

  • Seafood: It is a classic partner for premium shellfish like grilled lobster, scallops with truffles, and oysters.

  • Poultry and Meat: Suggested pairings include Bresse chicken with morel mushrooms, roasted white meats, or veal chops in a cream sauce.

  • Rich Dishes: It complements snails in garlic butter, mushroom risotto, and smoked eel.

  • Cheese: The wine’s acidity and body cut through rich cheeses such as Epoisses, Munster, or aged Comté.

title: Mission Hill Oculus 2020
bodyHtml:
Mission Hill Family Estate, located in British Columbia's Okanagan Valley, has been a pioneer in Canadian winemaking since its establishment in 1981. Under the leadership of proprietor Anthony von Mandl, the winery has garnered international acclaim for its commitment to quality and innovation. The 2020 vintage of their flagship wine, Oculus, marks a significant milestone as Canada's first red wine to receive a perfect 100-point score.

The 2020 Oculus is a Bordeaux-style blend, predominantly composed of Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon, and Cabernet Franc. It exhibits a deep garnet hue and opens with enticing aromas of cassis, dark cherry, and spice. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied with long and silky tannins supporting flavours of dark fruits and a hint of chocolate. The finish is remarkably long and refined, showcasing the wine's impeccable balance and potential for longevity. This vintage is best enjoyed between 2025 and 2040, allowing its full complexity to unfold. 

This exceptional wine pairs beautifully with dishes such as roasted lamb with herbs, wild mushroom risotto, or aged cheeses like Gouda or Comté. Together, these pairings enhance the wine’s depth and create an unforgettable dining experience.

The 2020 vintage in the Okanagan Valley was characterized by ideal growing conditions, resulting in one of the finest harvests the region has experienced. Mission Hill's meticulous vineyard management and winemaking practices have culminated in a wine that not only reflects the excellence of the vintage but also sets a new benchmark for Canadian red wines.

As wine critic John Schreiner noted, "The wine begins with appealing aromas of cassis, spice and dark cherry. The long and silky tannins support flavours of dark fruits with a hint of chocolate."

title: Shafer Cabernet Sauvignon Hillside Select 2019
bodyHtml:
Shafer Vineyards' Hillside Select Cabernet Sauvignon is a benchmark wine from the Stags Leap District in Napa Valley, California. The 2019 vintage continues the tradition of excellence, showcasing the estate’s commitment to crafting wines of extraordinary depth, elegance, and age-worthiness.

Winemaking and Aging

The 2019 Hillside Select is made entirely from 100% Cabernet Sauvignon, sourced from Shafer's estate hillside vineyards. These steep, rocky slopes produce low-yielding vines with intensely concentrated fruit. The wine was aged for 32 months in 100% new French oak barrels, contributing to its luxurious texture and layered complexity.

Tasting Notes

  • Appearance: Deep purple with inky intensity.
  • Nose: Aromas of ripe black cherry, cassis, and red summer berries, complemented by notes of cedar, violets, and subtle hints of camphor and spice.
  • Palate: Full-bodied and velvety, with flavors of blackcurrant, blackberry, and dark chocolate. The wine is flawlessly balanced with fine-grained tannins and vibrant acidity, leading to a seamless, long, and elegant finish.

Critical Acclaim

  • Robert Parker's Wine Advocate: 98 points – Lauded for its intense aromatics, concentrated palate, and extraordinary depth.
  • Jeb Dunnuck: 98+ points – Highlighted as "another magical vintage," with exceptional balance, power, and refined complexity.
  • Wine Enthusiast: 97 points – Praised for its opulent texture and remarkable aging potential.

Serving and Cellaring

The 2019 Hillside Select is best served at 60–65°F (16–18°C). Decanting for at least an hour is recommended to allow the wine to open fully and reveal its intricate aromas and flavors. While already showing its promise, this vintage will age gracefully for decades, with an optimal drinking window from 2025 to 2055.

Conclusion

The 2019 Shafer Hillside Select Cabernet Sauvignon is a masterpiece that reflects the pinnacle of Napa Valley winemaking. With its depth, balance, and exceptional complexity, this wine is a true collector’s gem and a testament to Shafer’s legacy of excellence.

title: Altesino Brunello di Montalcino Riserva 2020
bodyHtml:
Elegance, finesse, and a fruitier, richer style are the trademarks of Altesino’s wines and have earned the estate a position among the very top producers of Brunello. This achievement is even more impressive considering Brunello is perhaps the most recognized Italian appellation.

This Brunello Riserva offers a solid, full body and excellent aging potential. Its ample and complex bouquet is reminiscent of violets, wild berries, cedar, leather, tobacco and spices. On the palate, it is austere and seductive with a perfect blend of fruit, acidity and mouth coating tannins. This is the perfect bottle for Brunello lovers.

Pair with steak au poivre, rack of lamb or beef carpaccio.

title: John Duval Shiraz Eligo 2019
vendor: 300575 - Vintage West Wine And Spirits Inc.
bodyHtml: Elegant expression of rich dark fruits with some earthy savouriness and smoked meat flavours. Deep and intense with excellent fruit purity and freshness,finishing with a taut backbone and a long flowing tannin structure.

title: Alexandre Filaine 'DMY' Brut (NV)
bodyHtml:
Alexandre Filaine is the personal label of Fabrice Gass, who until just a few years ago was a longtime winemaker at Bollinger. Fabrice started the Filaine label as a side project while working at Bollinger, only spending his spare time on his own label and quietly growing a niche following for his meticulously crafted wines. He now dedicates his full attention to his Filaine label, doing literally all of the work himself. He produces no more than about 5,000 bottles a year from 10 separate plots that add up to just over a hectare of vines in total.

A well-constructed assemblage, with aromas of honeysuckle and plum while more overtly red fruit appears on the palate; fresh, energetic yet finely-poised to ensure development and harmonious integration.

title: Chateau Haut Bailly 2022
bodyHtml:
Château Haut Bailly is a storied estate located in the heart of Pessac-Léognan, Bordeaux. With origins dating back to the 16th century, the château has been under the ownership of the Wilmers family since 1998. Renowned for its commitment to terroir expression and restrained elegance, the estate practices sustainable viticulture and meticulous winemaking.

Wine Description
The 2022 Haut Bailly is a vibrant, deeply coloured blend showcasing the château's signature finesse and poise. Aromas of blackcurrant, violet, tobacco, and graphite unfurl from the glass, interlaced with hints of cedar and spice. The palate is full-bodied yet remarkably balanced, delivering layers of ripe black fruits, fine-grained tannins, and a vein of mineral freshness. A blend of 57% Cabernet Sauvignon, 34% Merlot, 5% Petit Verdot, and 4% Cabernet Franc, it offers a precise structure and persistent finish.

Accolades

  • Jeb Dunnuck - 98+ Points
  • James Suckling - 97+ Points
  • Vinous - 96+ Points
  • Decanter - 96 Points
  • Wine Advocate - 94+ Points

Food Pairing
This elegant yet structured wine pairs beautifully with herb-crusted lamb, grilled ribeye steak, or duck confit. Mushroom risotto and roasted root vegetables also complement its earthy depth. Together, they create an unforgettable dining experience.

title: Casa Raia Brunello di Montalcino 2006 Library Release
bodyHtml:
• The varietal composition is 100% Sangiovese Grosso. The wine is a strong ruby red, tending towards garnet. 

  • It presents a complex medley of aromas, including herbal, tobacco, and tomato-like notes, with others finding eucalyptus, plum, dried cherry, vanilla, clove, old balsamic, leather, and cigar. The nose is also described as showing underbrush, ripe black-skinned fruit, camphor, toasted nut, and vanilla.

  • On the palate, it is full-bodied, powerful, and structured. It features rich, taut acidity and huge, beautifully ripened tannins. The flavours include cherries and black cherries with some dried fruits, a complex and layered profile with forest floor/tea leaves and spice, and a silky richness of ripe red and black fruits. Stylistically, it is classical and harmonious, boasting great balance and structure. It is a regal and rare wine that is drinking well now but can be laid down for another 10-20 years.

Food Pairing

  • Suggested pairings for this powerful and structured wine include rich dishes such as lasagna or game hen roasted and stuffed with herbed rice and pancetta.

  • A perfect match to enhance the wine's complexity.

Vintage Quality

  • The 2006 vintage for Brunello di Montalcino is considered a new benchmark and one of the greatest modern vintages for Sangiovese. The growing season was consistent, with hot days and cool nights, which is ideal for Sangiovese. The resulting wines are subtle yet rich, structured, and powerful, showing great balance and freshness of acidity, and are built for decades of ageing.

title: Chateau Clerc Milon 2015
bodyHtml:
96 Points - James Suckling

Hot crushed stones and dark berries jump out of the glass. Full body, very dense fruit, and powerful tannins, yet it remains agile and bright with beauty and energy. So muscular and toned. Truly outstanding Clerc for the future. Unwavering nature to this. 

96 Points - Decanter

Always more muscular and powerful than Armailhac, there's no surprise that this has closed down more than its sibling. The complexity of the layers are still on display, showcasing fresh menthol, cranberry, white pepper, black olive, rose, and blackberry, all wrapped up in a tight tannic hold. There are some wonderful toasted caramel notes, subdued but rich and tight, waiting to show their exuberance on the finish. 

95 Points - Wine Enthusiast

Dark and concentrated, this wine offers depth and intensity. It has great ripeness as well as fine tannins that are integrated into the fruit. It is so juicy and exuberant that it's hard to remember the tannins that will allow the wine to age.

title: E. Pira e Figli Chiara Boschis - Barolo 'Mosconi' 2018
bodyHtml: The most recently acquired parcel, the famous Mosconi Cru in Monforte d’Alba was purchased in 2009. The vineyard’s particular heavy clay soil (in some areas calcium carbonate and iron give the soil a reddish-gray color) lends considerable structure to this wine, making it a Barolo ideal for aging. A garnet red color is complimented by open perfumes of flowers and mature fruit with some spicy notes. This is a long-lasting wine of power and concentration with firm, velvety tannins.

title: Chateau Lassegue Vertical Collectors - 3 Bottle Pack (2017/2018/2019)
bodyHtml:
Product Description

This Collectors pack includes 1 bottle of 2017, 1 bottle of 2018 and 1 bottle of 2019.

Ripe plums, black cherry liquor and dried cassis provide sumptuous aromas while hints of orange peel, toasted allspice, fresh cinnamon bark and dried tea leaf beckon. A velvety, Merlot-driven mid-palate slowly opens into a multi-layered bouquet of red fruit, toasted baking spices, truffle and coffee bean. An iron-rich minerality provides a taut, complex structure, while fine-grained tannins and firm acidity grip the palate to sustain a long and elegant finish. This classic expression of Saint-Emilion offers a dual brightness and sophistication that will continue to improve for years to come.

2017

94 Points – Decanter A floral touch from the first nose, smoky but delicate, with a powerful and surprisingly supple touch to the tannins. This must be one of the best 2017s in St-Emilion. So much smoke and grilled chocolate add layers of interest to the berry fruits.

93 Points – Robert Parker's Wine Advocate The 2017 Lassegue displays a deep garnet-purple color and quite a spicy nose giving up black pepper, cinnamon and cloves notes over a core of crème de cassis and preserved plums with a waft of dusty soil. The palate is medium to full-bodied with a firm frame of chewy tannins and tons of black fruit layers, finishing long and spicy.

2018

95 Points – Decanter This is a young wine that is knitted down in flavour but it is not tight or difficult to navigate. You feel the breadth and complexity to the fruit, along with juicy powerful freshness, and the gourmet packing of liquorice and chocolate. These are big wines that are big but expertly balanced by slate and crushed stone minerality, giving balance and succulence.

94 Points – James Suckling Subtle aromas of sweet berries, Spanish cedar and blackberries with some black mushrooms. Medium-to full-bodied with fine yet chewy tannins and a long finish. Solid and racy. Tight now. Drink after 2024.

2019

96 Points – James Suckling This is so fine and refined with currant, crushed stone, lime stone and fresh mushroom. It’s medium-bodied with fine tannins that run the length of the wine. Minerally finish. Tight and racy. Drink after 2025, but already beautiful.

94 Points – Decanter Rich plum in colour, this grips right from the off, and moves slowly and carefully through the palate, revealing brambly blue and red fruits, and a lovely sense of energy and uplift. Extremely good quality, with sage and saffron edges alongside layers of fine tannins that close in towards the finish, slowing things down even more. This will age well, and is an elegant yet concentrated wine.

title: Casanova Di Neri Brunello Di Montalcino 2020 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
Italy’s Tuscany region is celebrated worldwide for its exceptional wines, and the area of Montalcino stands out as one of its crowning jewels. Casanova di Neri, founded in 1971 by Giovanni Neri, remains a family-run estate now led by his son, Giacomo Neri. The winery has earned international acclaim for its relentless pursuit of quality, with vineyards carefully sited across Montalcino’s most prized terroirs. This commitment to excellence has positioned Casanova di Neri among the modern icons of Brunello production.

Wine Description

This Brunello di Montalcino 2020 is crafted exclusively from Sangiovese, known locally as Brunello. It reveals a deep ruby hue with garnet reflections, offering an elegant nose layered with ripe red cherry, wild strawberry, dried rose petals, and subtle notes of spice and tobacco. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied yet remarkably graceful, displaying finely woven tannins and vibrant acidity that sustain flavours of crushed raspberry, black tea, and hints of earthy undergrowth. The finish is long and polished, lingering with notes of minerality and sweet herbs.

Accolades

  • Wine Spectator – 95 points.

  • Vinous – 94 points.

  • James Suckling – 96 points.

Food Pairing

Enjoy this Brunello with dishes that complement its layered complexity and structure. Braised veal shank, roasted game birds, or a rich mushroom risotto will beautifully echo its earthy undertones. Aged Pecorino or Parmigiano also pair exquisitely, highlighting the wine’s depth and finesse. Together, they create an unforgettable dining experience.

title: Chateau Lafite Rothschild 2015
bodyHtml:
Chateau Lafite Rothschild 2015 originates from France, within the Pauillac appellation of the Médoc region in Bordeaux. This legendary estate, a First Growth (Premier Cru Classé) since the 1855 Bordeaux Classification, has been owned by the Rothschild family since 1868. The winery follows a philosophy of excellence and precision, often described as producing 'the wine of kings' due to its long history of serving European royalty and its ability to express the unique gravel and clay terroir of the Plateau des Carruades.

Wine Description

This vintage presents a deep garnet-purple or dark ruby colour with purple reflections. The aromatic profile is complex and multifaceted, offering notes of black raspberries, red currants, and crushed plums, interwoven with scents of cedar, tobacco, lead pencil, and violets. On the palate, it is medium to full bodied and elegantly styled, delivering a vibrant core of fruit balanced by a salty minerality and fresh acidity. The structure is defined by seductively silky yet firm, fine-grained tannins that lead to a very long, racy, and pure finish. The varietal composition for the 2015 vintage is 91% Cabernet Sauvignon and 9% Merlot. It has an ABV typically recorded between 12.5% and 12.8%. While the estate utilizes meticulous viticulture and precise sorting, this wine is not certified organic.

Food Pairing

The aristocratic elegance and firm tannic structure of this Barolo make it a superlative partner for classic, high-quality meat dishes. Suggested pairings include roasted rack of lamb, grilled ribeye steak, veal, and duck breast. It also complements wild game, such as venison or wild boar, and savoury dishes featuring truffles or wild mushrooms. For a cheese course, it pairs best with aged hard cheeses like Comté, Parmesan, or matured Cheddar.

Vintage Quality

The 2015 vintage in Pauillac is considered exceptional, characterized by a temperate growing season with a warm summer balanced by timely August rains that prevented excessive water stress. These ideal conditions allowed the grapes to reach perfect maturity, resulting in a vintage that harmoniously combines power with Lafite's signature finesse. Winemakers utilized their own cooperage, Tonnellerie des Domaines, to age the wine in 100% new oak barrels, ensuring the structure was perfectly integrated with the intense fruit core.

title: Caymus Cabernet Sauvignon 'Special Selection' 2019 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
The Caymus 'Special Selection' Cabernet Sauvignon is an exceptional wine made from this storied Napa Valley estate.

Following some time to open, this incredible Cabernet begins to yield profound aromatics of black cherry compote, blueberry pie and boysenberry along with creosote, black tar, milk chocolate and licorice all soaring from the glass. The mouthfeel is rich, voluptuous and intense, as this wine offers exceedingly dense, concentrated flavors of black cherry reduction, blueberry pie, raspberry liquor and boysenberry, alongside milk chocolate shavings and tar, all cascading on to the long mouth coating finish. 

Each year, Caymus sets aside the best barrels of their Cabernet Sauvignon from Napa Valley to produce Special Selection.

title: Les Forts de Latour 2019
bodyHtml:
Les Forts de Latour 2019 is a red wine from France, specifically from the Bordeaux region and the Pauillac sub-region. This wine is the second label of the esteemed Château Latour. The estate is known for its meticulous viticulture and winemaking, with Les Forts de Latour being produced with the same care as the Grand Vin. The wine's name comes from a historical plot on the estate, and its quality has been developed to the level of a Médoc Grand Cru Classé.

Wine Description

Les Forts de Latour 2019 is composed of a blend of grape varietals, with a higher proportion of Merlot compared to the Grand Vin. The blend for this vintage is 65.8% Cabernet Sauvignon, 31.9% Merlot, and 2.3% Petit Verdot. The wine has a deep garnet-purple or intense violet colour. The nose presents a complex aromatic profile of black fruits like cassis, plum, and black cherry, along with notes of cedar, cigar ash, and lavender. On the palate, it is described as medium to full-bodied, with powerful and ultrafine tannins. The flavour profile includes sweet red fruits, spice, and mineral notes. This wine is noted for its freshness, elegance, and density, and is described as a 'powerhouse'. While it can be approached after decanting, it will benefit from additional aging. It is also important to note that the 2019 vintage of Les Forts de Latour is certified organic.

Accolades

  • James Suckling - 97 points

  • Vinous (Antonio Galloni) - 95 points

  • The Wine Independent (Lisa Perrotti-Brown) - 95 points

  • Decanter (Georgina Hindle) - 94 points

  • The Wine Cellar Insider (Jeff Leve) - 95 points

Food Pairing

A perfect match for roasted duck breast, grilled ribeye, or mushroom risotto. Together, they create an unforgettable dining experience.

Vintage Quality

The 2019 vintage in Bordeaux was a warm, hot, and long growing season, with pockets of refreshing rain. The Pauillac appellation, in particular, had a successful vintage, delivering consistent quality across the board. This vintage of Les Forts de Latour is considered to be particularly serious, with a structure and intensity that nod to its grander sibling.

title: Carruades de Lafite 2000
bodyHtml:
This red wine originates from France, specifically the prestigious Bordeaux region within the Pauillac appellation. Carruades de Lafite is the second wine of the illustrious Château Lafite Rothschild, a First Growth estate owned by the Rothschild family since 1868. The wine is produced from a specific plot of vines known as the Carruades plateau and is crafted with the same meticulous care as the Grand Vin, though it is designed to be more accessible in its youth.

Wine Description

The Carruades de Lafite 2000 displays a deep garnet colour, indicative of its evolution. The nose is complex and classic to the estate, offering aromas of blackcurrant and red berries, layered with distinctive notes of graphite, pencil lead, tobacco, and subtle cedar wood. On the palate, it is medium-bodied and elegant, presenting a softer and more supple texture than the Grand Vin due to a higher proportion of Merlot. The tannins are silky and fully resolved, leading to a refined, lingering finish. The blend consists of 51.5% Cabernet Sauvignon, 42.1% Merlot, 4.8% Cabernet Franc, and 1.6% Petit Verdot. The wine is fully mature and best enjoyed now. The alcohol by volume (ABV) is 12.5%.

Accolades

  • Robert Parker's Wine Advocate - 93 points.

  • Wine Spectator - 93 points.

  • Wine Enthusiast - 93 points.

Food Pairing

This wine's elegant structure and savoury 'cigar box' notes make it a quintessential match for classic Pauillac pairings such as roast lamb with rosemary or a rack of lamb. It also pairs beautifully with roasted game birds, beef wellington, or a selection of mature hard cheeses like Comté or Mimolette.

title: Orin Swift Papillon Bordeaux Red Blend 2021
bodyHtml:
It's rare to find a wine from the Napa Valley composed of all five Bordeaux-style varietals. But, for many years, that has been Papillon's focus. The raw strength and prestige of Cabernet Sauvignon buttressed by the opulence of Merlot, the spiciness of Cabernet Franc, the depth of Malbec and the sheet unctuousness of Petit Verdot come together seamlessly. 

The dark crimson core and brick rim sets the stage, as aromas of currant, blackberry, blue fruits, anise, lavender and brioche float from the glass. Enveloping and coating becomes mixed berry pie, sarsaparilla, cola and blackcurrant with structured heft through the mid-palate. Chalky tannins a la black tea or baking chocolate round out the wine with a pleasing finish of sweet oak.

title: Chateau Branaire Ducru 2023
bodyHtml:
Chateau Branaire-Ducru's 120 acres is located in the St. Julien region of France and has such famous neighbors as Cheateau Gruaud-Larose, Chateau Ducru-Beaucaillou and Chateau Beychevelle.

The name, given by the former owner Monsieur Ducru, means "beautiful pebbles". One of the main features of the vineyard is its richness in pebbles which contribute to the greatness of so many wines of the Medoc.

An attractive bouquet of red and black fruit, lovely and fresh, clear-cut and complex. Dense and round on the palate, it is powerful yet elegant.

title: Chateau Giscours 2014
bodyHtml:
Château Giscours hails from the Margaux appellation in the Médoc region of Bordeaux, France. This historic estate traces its origins back to 1552 when Pierre de Lhomme began planting vines on the wild land of Guyscoutz. Classified as a Troisième Grand Cru Classé in 1855, the winery is celebrated for its winemaking philosophy of reflecting the unique Margaux terroir through powerful yet refined and silken wines.

Wine Description

This deep ruby red wine presents a complex sensory profile with a bouquet of red cherry, blackcurrant, and raspberry intertwined with sophisticated notes of cedar, graphite, and forest floor. On the palate, it is medium-bodied and structured, offering a concentrated core of dark fruits and polished, silky tannins. The blend consists of 70% Cabernet Sauvignon, 20% Merlot, and 10% Petit Verdot, which provides additional substance and density to the mid-palate. It exhibits a beautiful balance and freshness, leading into a precise, long-lingering finish.

Accolades

  • Wine Enthusiast - 96 points

  • Vinous - 93 points

  • Wine Spectator - 91 points

  • Wine Advocate - 92 points

Food Pairing

This elegant Margaux is best served at 15.5°C and pairs exceptionally well with classic meat dishes such as roasted lamb, braised beef, or game birds like duck. It also complements earthy flavours found in mushroom-based dishes and aromatic fresh herbs.

title: Chateau Pichon Longueville Baron 2022 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
This wine hails from France, specifically the prestigious Pauillac appellation in the Bordeaux region. Chateau Pichon Longueville Baron, often simply called Pichon Baron, is a historic estate established in the late 17th century. The estate is celebrated for producing some of the finest wines in Bordeaux, consistently reflecting its deep gravel soils and commitment to meticulous vineyard management.

Wine Description

The 2022 vintage of Chateau Pichon Longueville Baron showcases a deep, opaque ruby colour. Aromatically, it reveals a captivating bouquet of ripe blackberries, cassis, violets, and graphite, interwoven with hints of cedar and subtle tobacco leaf. On the palate, it is full bodied with a layered texture, delivering intense dark fruit flavours complemented by notes of dark chocolate and spice. The wine displays remarkable balance and freshness, with finely polished tannins leading into a long, elegant finish that carries traces of minerality and savoury undertones.

Accolades

  • Vinous - 98 Points

  • Jeb Dunnuck - 96+ Points

  • James Suckling - 96+ Points

  • Decanter - 96 Points

  • Wine Advocate - 95+ Points

Food Pairing

Pair this distinguished Pauillac with herb crusted rack of lamb, grilled ribeye steak, or braised short ribs. Mature hard cheeses like aged Comté or Manchego also make an excellent match. This pairing highlights the wine’s depth and character.

title: Dujac Morey Saint Denis Rouge 2023
bodyHtml:
Louis Seysses, biscuit manufacturer and gastronome, had a taste for good food and fine wines. His son Jacques Seysses quickly came to share his father's passion, and he decided he would not only like to drink the wine but make it as well. With the help of his father, Jacques began his career in wine with an apprenticeship with Gerard Potel at the Domaine de la Pousse d'Or. He spent two harvests there during which time he was lucky enough to talk and listen to the famous Burgundian winemakers of the times whom he greatly admired.

Made from Pinot Noir grapes frown on clay and limestone soils. Fermented in stainless steel tanks, using naturally occurring yeast. The vines have been organically farmed since 2001.

93 Points - Decanter

The village-level Morey from domaine-owned parcels is a stark contrast with the négociant wine, with lovely, ripe mulberry fruit, a bit of smokiness from the cask ageing, and notes of rose petal and mineral. As you might expect, there is a bit more heft than in the Chambolle, more density, and a bit more grip.

90+ Points - Vinous

The 2021 Morey-Saint-Denis Village shows the stem addition slightly more conspicuously than the Chambolle-Village, white pepper and touches of bay leaf. The palate is medium-bodied with fine grain tannins, lightly peppered black fruit with notes of tobacco and dark chocolate towards the finish. This gains complexity in the glass. Promising - quintessential Dujac.

title: Joseph Drouhin Volnay 2024
bodyHtml:
While Gevrey-Chambertin represents the structured, muscular "king" of the Côte de Nuits, Volnay is universally celebrated as the elegant, seductive "queen" of the Côte de Beaune. Located just south of Beaune and adjacent to Pommard, the village of Volnay rests on a steep, privileged east/southeast-facing slope where the soils transition to lighter limestone and colored marls mixed with small pebbles.

Maison Joseph Drouhin utilizes this distinct terroir to craft a Volnay focused on pure, ethereal weightlessness and fragrant charm. Blending select hand-harvested fruit from estate parcels and trusted grower partners, Drouhin manages extraction with absolute precision to favor lace-like finesse over raw power.

Wine Description

The Joseph Drouhin Volnay 2024 pours a bright, vivid ruby color with brilliant luminosity in the glass. The bouquet is extraordinarily pretty, precise, and high-toned, greeting the nose with a classic youthful perfume of fresh violets, redcurrants, and blackcurrants, laced with subtle mineral undertones.

On the palate, the wine delivers a striking sense of roundness and velvety texture without a trace of heavy weight. True to the airy, translucent nature of the 2024 vintage, it is a lighter-bodied, beautifully vibrant expression of 100% Pinot Noir. It dances across the palate with a refreshing, crunchy acidity and powdery, fine-grained tannins.

The fruit underwent total destemming and a gentle 2-to-3-week maceration utilizing indigenous yeasts. It was then aged for 12 to 16 months in fine French oak barrels (20% new) sourced from high forests. The finish is long and persistent, carrying soft hints of candied red fruits and delicate vanilla. This highly graceful vintage can be happily approached after 3 to 5 years of cellaring but will keep nicely for up to a decade.

title: Catena Zapata Chardonnay Adrianna Vineyard 'White Stones' 2023
bodyHtml:
Bodega Catena Zapata, one of Argentina’s most esteemed wineries, was founded in 1902 and remains family-owned, currently led by Dr. Laura Catena. The Adrianna Vineyard, located at nearly 1,500 metres in the Gualtallary subregion, is often referred to as the Grand Cru of South America, thanks to its exceptional terroir and meticulous vineyard mapping. The ‘White Stones’ parcel is named after the white oval stones in the soil, which influence both water drainage and vine stress, resulting in remarkable expression.

This Chardonnay presents a luminous pale gold colour. Aromas are pure and lifted, offering white flowers, green apple, lime zest, and a mineral edge reminiscent of wet stones. On the palate, it is medium-bodied yet intensely focused, displaying layered flavours of citrus, pear, and subtle hazelnut, underpinned by vivid acidity and a saline thread. The texture is chalky and elegant, leading to a long, refined finish.

Accolades

  • Vinous – 97 points

  • Wine Advocate – 97+ points

  • James Suckling – 98 points

Food Pairing
Enjoy with butter-poached lobster, roast chicken with lemon thyme, or creamy mushroom risotto.

title: Domaine Comte Senard Corton Blanc Grand Cru 2022
bodyHtml:
The 2022 Domaine Comte Senard Corton Grand Cru Blanc is a sophisticated white wine from the Côte de Beaune in Burgundy, made from 100% Chardonnay. This Grand Cru showcases the vineyard's hallmark richness and complexity, delivering a nuanced expression of Burgundy’s terroir.

Colour: Bright golden yellow with a luminous hue.
Aroma: Enticing aromas of ripe pear, apricot, and acacia flowers, complemented by notes of hay and a touch of spice.
Palate: The palate is dense and layered, featuring flavors of stone fruits, with a creamy texture and subtle minerality. The wine's complexity is enhanced by hints of nougat and oak.
Body: Full-bodied with a smooth, well-rounded texture.
Finish: Long, with a persistent, elegant finish marked by fresh acidity.

This wine pairs excellently with poultry dishes such as chicken or turkey, and it also complements creamy cheeses and seafood. With an ABV of approximately 13%, the 2022 Corton Blanc promises both immediate enjoyment and the potential for further development with additional aging over the next decade.

This vintage reflects the traditional winemaking approach of Domaine Comte Senard, which emphasizes aging in oak to bring out depth without overpowering the wine’s natural elegance and freshness.

title: Sine Qua Non Syrah 'Distenta IV' 2022
bodyHtml:
Sine Qua Non Syrah 'Distenta IV' 2022 represents an exceptional expression of Rhône varietals crafted with meticulous attention to detail. Known for its depth and complexity, this vintage showcases intense dark fruit aromas layered with spice and nuanced smoky undertones. The palate offers a rich, structured experience balanced by refined tannins and vibrant acidity, reflecting precise vineyard selection and expert winemaking. Ideal for collectors and connoisseurs, it promises both immediate enjoyment and graceful aging potential.

The 2022 Syrah Distenta IV is a blend of 83% Syrah, 6% Grenache, 5% Petite Sirah, and the rest Mourvèdre and white varieties. It sports a dense purple hue and offers stunning aromatics of ripe blue fruits, framboise, liquid violets, white pepper, game, bouquet garni, and spice. These carry to the palate of a full-bodied Syrah that’s concentrated yet balanced, with a broad, layered mouthfeel, velvety tannins, and a great finish. I was able to follow this bottle over multiple days, and it only improved with air, gaining both complexity and texture. While this is clearly a more accessible vintage compared to the 2021s, it still deserves 3-4 years in bottle and should have 15-20 years of prime drinking given its balance, purity, and harmony. Drink 2028-2045. 

99 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

title: Chateau Giscours 2022
bodyHtml:
#1 Wine Spectator Top 100 2025

This red wine comes from France, originating from the Bordeaux region, specifically the Margaux appellation. Château Giscours is a prestigious estate that was designated a Troisième Grand Cru Classé (Third Growth) in the official 1855 Bordeaux Wine Classification. Records of the vineyards date back to 1552, and the estate once charmed the palate of King Louis XIV. The property is currently run by Dutch manager Alexander Van Beek for the Albada Jelgersma family, who continue a tradition of excellence and an unceasing commitment to progress. Their philosophy is holistic, viewing the wines as a reflection of the place, the terroir, and the people who make them.

Wine Description

The colour of the 2022 vintage is deeply coloured, glass-staining, and often described as deep garnet-purple. The aroma is stunning and expressive, packed with cassis, black cherries, violets, and graphite-like aromatics, along with notes of dark mushrooms and forest-floor. Other notes include lilac, peony, mint, rose petals, and pencil shavings.

The varietal composition is 64% Cabernet Sauvignon, 30% Merlot, 3% Petit Verdot, and 3% Cabernet Franc. The palate is medium to full-bodied, concentrated, and intense. It is deep, layered, and textural, showcasing dark, flavourful fruit like succulent black cherry, plum, and blackcurrants. Stylistically, the wine is described as regal, sophisticated, and elegant, possessing a pure, graceful mouthfeel. It is built around lively acids and beautifully ripe tannins that are intense, structural, and finely spreading across the palate in layers. The finish is long, structured, and resonant, concluding with a minty lift and notable vibrancy. The optimal drinking window is noted as starting around 2026 to 2029, with a potential to age for 30–40 years. The alcohol by volume (ABV) is 13.5%. Château Giscours has not used any herbicides, insecticides, or products harmful to health for ten years, and currently, half of the vineyard area is organically cultivated.

title: Francois Mikulski Meursault Pre de Manche 2023
bodyHtml:
Introduction

This white wine originates from France, specifically the Burgundy region, within the Côte de Beaune subregion and the Meursault appellation. The history of Domaine François Mikulski began in 1992 when François Mikulski and his wife Marie-Pierre founded the estate, building on the viticultural knowledge François gained from his uncle. Their winemaking philosophy is rooted in authenticity, elegance, and purity, emphasising the health of the vineyard and the expression of the terroir. The domaine manages its vines, mainly in Meursault, with non-certified organic farming practices, using home-produced composts and ploughing the soil. The vineyard 'Pré de Manchet' (sometimes noted as 'Le Pré de Manche') is located high on the Meursault hillside, known for its shallow, stony, and very mineral soil.

Wine Description

The wine is 100% Chardonnay. It typically presents with a brilliant light gold colour, often with slight green highlights. The aroma is complex and evolving, with notes of white fruits like pear, white peach, and apple, intermingled with vanilla, lactic notes, small white flowers, and citrus. Further exploration may reveal hints of almond, cane sugar, honey, and sophisticated spices. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied, fleshy, and generous, showing layered flavours of ripe fruit, often including pear coulis, apricot, mango, and citrus. It is known for its incredible freshness, minerality, and dynamic zing from the citrus notes. The finish is long and persistent, taut like a bow, supported by a fresh, defined mineral structure. The ABV is approximately 13.5%. Domaine François Mikulski practices organic farming, although the winery may not hold a formal certification. The wine is structured with excellent balance, concentration, and a seductive length. The youthful character is expected to persist for a number of years, suggesting an optimal drinking window after six or seven years of cellaring.

title: Bruno Paillard Dosage Zero (NV)
bodyHtml:
APPEARANCE: Intense, bright, straw gold.  Very fine and persistent effervescence.   

NOSE: Primary notes of white fruits and fresh almonds, generous but not opulent.  This is followed by aromas of chocolate and toast with fresh raspberry, star anise and candied chestnuts.

PALATE: The attack is both lively and rich, blossoming generously on the palate. The same aromatic richness promised on the nose is found on the palate. The texture is both animated and chiselled, with saline notes, and a very long, persistent finish.

92 Points - Vinous

The NV Dosage: Zero is a gorgeous wine from Bruno Paillard. Ample and textured on the palate, with terrific depth, the Dosage: Zero has much to recommend it. This is a distinctly more vinous style than readers are likely to expect from Bruno Paillard. I would prefer to drink the Dosage: Zero at the dinner table, as it is a bit imposing on its own. Apple, pear, slate and white flowers build as this resonant, highly expressive Champagne shows off its personality.

92 Points - Decanter

Nearly 30 different wines compose this bracing Champagne, prepared without any dosage. Only the best quality, first press juice is used for the base wines, to which is added 50% of reserve wine before being aged in small wooden barrels. This is a dynamic, vibrant Champagne redolent of lemon, vanilla and brioche pastry. The palate is taut and finishes with balanced acidity and freshness as well as a discreet salty note.

title: Aalto PS (Pagos Seleccionados) 2021
bodyHtml:
Founded in 1999 by Mariano García, former winemaker of Vega Sicilia, and Javier Zaccagnini, Aalto has swiftly risen to prominence as one of Ribera del Duero’s most esteemed producers. The winery is dedicated to crafting wines of depth and elegance, sourcing fruit from some of the region’s oldest vineyards, many over 60 years of age, and adhering to minimal intervention practices that showcase the unique terroir of each plot. Aalto's philosophy emphasizes precision and patience, with extended ageing and careful vineyard management as cornerstones of their production.

Wine Description

The Aalto PS 2021 is a striking expression of Tempranillo, displaying a deep, opaque purple hue. Aromatically, it unfolds with layers of ripe blackberries, cassis, and plum, interwoven with notes of violets, graphite, and subtle vanilla from its refined oak ageing. On the palate, it is full-bodied and concentrated, offering an opulent core of dark fruit supported by finely grained tannins and vibrant acidity. The texture is plush yet structured, leading to a long, persistent finish laced with hints of dark chocolate and sweet spice. Composed entirely of Tempranillo, this wine balances power with elegance and promises optimal drinking from 2025 through 2040.

Accolades

  • "Wine Advocate - 96 points."
  • "James Suckling - 96 points."
  • "Vinous - 95 points."

Food Pairing

This bold and complex wine pairs beautifully with grilled lamb chops, dry-aged ribeye, or rich mushroom risotto. The depth of flavour and refined structure make it an excellent match for hearty, savoury dishes. Together, they create an unforgettable dining experience.

Vintage Quality

The 2021 vintage in Ribera del Duero was marked by a cooler, wetter growing season, which contributed to wines of remarkable freshness and aromatic intensity. Despite climatic challenges, careful vineyard work and selective harvesting allowed Aalto to craft a vintage of exceptional purity and ageing potential.

title: Colome 'Autentico' Malbec 2016 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
Bodega Colomé 'Auténtico' Malbec 2016 originates from Argentina, specifically from the Molinos area within the Salta province's Calchaquí Valley. Founded in 1831, Bodega Colomé is Argentina's oldest working winery and is currently part of the Hess Family Wine Estates, following a philosophy of high-altitude viticulture and sustainable farming. The 'Auténtico' label is a tribute to the winery’s ancestors and original 19th-century winemaking style, crafted from estate-grown fruit at an extreme altitude of 2,300 metres above sea level.

Wine Description

This full-bodied red wine typically presents an intense, almost black colour with deep violet tones. The sensory profile for the 2016 vintage is concentrated and robust, featuring a fragrant nose of plums, black cherries, and blackberries layered with notes of wild herbs, cloves, and a stony minerality. On the palate, it is described as lush and dark, offering flavours of black raspberries and dark fruit supported by firm, round tannins and a refreshing acidity. The finish is powerful and long, showcasing complexity and depth without the influence of wood.

  • Varietal Composition: 100% Malbec.

  • ABV: Typically 14.5%.

  • Organic Status: The estate utilizes sustainable and low-intervention farming practices, including biodiversity and zero chemical use, though specific organic certification for this vintage is not explicitly stated.

  • Stylistic Notes: 'Auténtico' is an unoaked expression of Malbec produced using ancient techniques such as pigeage (punch-down) and natural fermentations without commercial yeasts. It is matured for 10 months in tanks followed by 10 months in the bottle.

title: Vincent Latour Meursault 'Les Narvaux' 2021
bodyHtml: Brilliant gold in colour, this wine has white flowers and almonds aromas. Powerful on the palate with great minerality. This is the first wine to display any appreciable amount of reduction; in this case, it's enough to mask the underlying fruit. Otherwise, the racy and almost painfully intense middle-weight flavours exude a bracing minerality that adds a sense of lift to the lemony and more complex finale. This is always one of Latour's better wines, simply outstanding.

title: Kosta Browne Pinot Noir 'Santa Rita Hills' 2020
bodyHtml:
Founded in 1997, Kosta Browne is one of North America’s most revered wineries, recognized for making some of the world’s finest Pinot Noirs and Chardonnays. Located in Sebastopol, Sonoma County, and guided by an acclaimed team that includes renowned Winemaker Julien Howsepian, Kosta Browne makes appellation and single-vineyard wines from the most coveted cool-climate vineyards across the Russian River Valley, Sonoma Coast, Anderson Valley, Sta. Rita Hills and Santa Lucia Highlands appellations.

An explosion of red fruit with an understated yet elegant savory quality. Nostalgic notes of cinnamon stick and clove mesmerize. Deeply rich with an earthy core and copious amounts of fruit. Refreshingly light on the palate with well-integrated tannins and unique flair.

95 Points - Wine Enthusiast

Snappy red-cherry aromas meet with tarragon and other fresh garden herbs on the nose of this appellation bottling. The palate is vibrant and fresh with red fruit as well as prominent spices like mace and cinnamon, but that minty tarragon tone is what ups the uniquely delicious quotient.

93 Points - Wine Spectator

Very alluring, with damson plum, griotte and mulberry fruit seamlessly layered with black tea, sous-bois and sandalwood. The long, refined finish lets all the perfume linger prettily.

title: Lewis Cabernet Sauvignon Reserve 2018
vendor: 300575 - Vintage West Wine And Spirits Inc.
bodyHtml:
From an outstanding vintage, this Reserve Cabernet is a full-throttle bottle, packed with fruit yet balanced with a fine-tuned chassis. Showy and complex, the wine is obsidian dark, layered with black currant, berries, coffee and sweet oak spices. Fleshy on entry, the palate soars with brazen youth in a firmly framed structure that tails away with chocolaty fine-grained tannins.

94 Points - Wine Spectator

This is an extrovert, with singed vanilla, mocha and violet notes gilding a ripe, lush core of plum, blackberry and black currant fruit. Ends with a frankly toasty tug on the licorice- and fruit-filled finish.

title: Pio Cesare Barbaresco 2021
bodyHtml:
Introduction

Pio Cesare Barbaresco 2021 is produced in the Piedmont region of Italy, primarily sourcing grapes from the family's own vineyards in Treiso (Cascina Il Bricco and San Stefanetto) and San Rocco Seno d'Elvio (Rocche di Massalupo). Founded in 1881 by Cesare Pio, the winery remains one of the few still operating in the historic centre of Alba, with cellars built upon ancient Roman walls. The family follows a traditional 'formula' by blending Nebbiolo from different estate terroirs to achieve a balanced and classic expression of the appellation.

Wine Description

The wine presents a deep red colour and an exceptionally captivating sensory profile. The aroma is complex and intense, featuring notes of rose petals, black cherries, and dark brambleberries, layered with hints of iodine, graphite, and dried orange peel. On the medium-bodied palate, it offers flavours of fresh cherries and redcurrant accompanied by savory notes of licorice, sweet tobacco, and woodland spices. The structure is defined by firm, linear tannins and a bright acidity that provides remarkable tension and mineral drive, leading to a long and persistent finish. This 100% Nebbiolo varietal has an ABV of 14.5%. While the winery employs sustainable viticulture practices, this wine is not certified organic.

Food Pairing

This Barbaresco is a versatile companion for traditional Piedmontese cuisine, pairing excellently with braised meats such as veal or lamb, and hearty stews. Its acidity and structured tannins also make it an ideal match for duck pasta dishes, mushroom or cheese risotto, and savoury poultry like roast duck. Additionally, it complements aged Alpine cheeses such as Castelmagno or Grana Padano.

Vintage Quality

The 2021 vintage in Barbaresco is considered exceptional and potentially a classic year for the region. A long, cool ripening process with significant diurnal temperature shifts allowed for optimal phenolic maturity and aromatic preservation. The resulting wines are powerful and highly structured with ripe tannins, showing a depth and concentration that suggests significant ageing potential.

title: Mayacamas Cabernet Sauvignon Mount Veeder 2021
bodyHtml:
This legendary and "super-classic" red wine originates from the United States, specifically from the premier Mount Veeder AVA in Napa Valley, California. Established in 1889, Mayacamas Vineyards is one of the most historic estates in the region, perched at elevations up to 2,400 feet on the rugged volcanic slopes of the Mayacamas Mountains. The winery's philosophy has remained steadfast for decades, prioritizing an "old-school" approach that emphasizes freshness, structural longevity, and restraint over the high-alcohol, flamboyant style common in modern Napa.

Wine Description

Mayacamas Cabernet Sauvignon 2021 presents a vivid ruby, mostly opaque hue. The sensory profile is "richly perfumed" and complex, featuring an exotic nose of crème de cassis, ripe cherries, and mulberry, layered with sophisticated mountain notes of graphite, bay laurel, dried herbs, and forest floor. On the palate, the wine is medium to full-bodied and "super-classic," showcasing a piercing intensity of fruit counterbalanced by a savory saline finish. It is characterized by ultra-fine, perfect tannins and a "piercing sanguine hint" that drives a long, acid-driven finish. This 100% Cabernet Sauvignon reached an ABV of 14%. To preserve its mountain identity, the wine was matured for 20 months in neutral large foudres and 500L puncheons, followed by 12 months in 225L neutral French barrels. All estate fruit is certified organic.

Food Pairing

The robust mountain structure and high acidity of this Cabernet make it a remarkable food wine, particularly for hearty and savory dishes. It pairs perfectly with beef tenderloin, roast lamb, or braised short ribs. Its savory and mineral nuances also complement Beef Wellington, aged cheddar, and rich pasta dishes like Roman-style carbonara or wild mushroom pappardelle. For a bold contrast, it is an excellent match for dark chocolate desserts.

Vintage Quality

The 2021 vintage on Mount Veeder is hailed as potentially "legendary" and arguably the finest in the estate's modern history. It was a severe drought year, recording the lowest rainfall in 55 years; which resulted in small, intensely flavored berries with deep concentration and color. Despite the drought, the high-altitude climate remained temperate without extreme heat spikes, allowing for a compact and early harvest between late August and early September. The resulting wines are noted for their "athletic grace," combining immense power with a refined elegance that critics predict will allow the 2021 vintage to age for 50 to 60 years.

title: Domaine Alain Chavy Puligny Montrachet 'Les Charmes' 2022
bodyHtml:
Single vineyard Puligny Montrachet that offers great value. Everything one would expect from a producer of this caliber.

Wines from Puligny-Montrachet are typified by aromas and flavours of green apple and lemon and tend to be tauter and firmer on the palate compared to wines from neighbouring villages. Aging in a small percentage of new French oak barrels lends accents of toast and vanilla. Structured white wines with high acid and grip, Puligny-Montrachet is destined for long aging.

White Burgundy, with its rich texture and toasted flavours, pairs well with white fish and shellfish and its naturally high acidity can counterbalance cream-based sauces. Oak-aged Chardonnay from warmer climates lends itself well to grilled fish, starches, butter, and toasted nuts.

title: Guado Al Tasso 2015
bodyHtml:
• Colour: The wine is described as having an intense and lively colour. Some critics note it is a 'baritone expression' with 'impenetrable black fruit'.

  • Aroma: It offers a rich and complex bouquet with notes of ripe berry fruit, tobacco, toasted coffee, and leather. Other notes include dark fruit, mocha, espresso, spice, and grilled herbs.

  • Palate: The palate is a vibrant one with beautiful intensity and purity, and an overall impression of balanced power. It features a rich concentration of black fruit and a tightly knit, yet supple, texture.

  • Body and Finish: This is a full bodied wine with well present tannins and freshness that contribute to its savour and persistence. The finish and aftertaste are complete, fragrant, spicy, and fruity.

  • Varietal Composition: A Red Bordeaux blend composed of Cabernet Sauvignon (60%), Merlot (20%), Cabernet Franc (18%), and Petit Verdot (2%).

  • Optimal Drinking Window: The wine is ready now, but youthful, with a drinking window suggested from 2022 to 2050 or 2020 to 2045, indicating very important ageing potential.

  • Stylistic Notes: The wine is powerful and explosive, showcasing a sublime balance between power, purity, and lasting persistence.

Accolades

  • Wine Advocate - 97 points

  • James Suckling - 97 points

  • Vinous - 96 points

  • Decanter - 95 points

  • Wine Spectator - 95 points

  • Wine & Spirits - 94 points

  • Wine Enthusiast - 94 points

Food Pairing

Suggested pairings for the structure and flavour profile of this Bolgheri Superiore include rich and structured dishes based on game such as wild boar or duck. Traditional Tuscan dishes like Bistecca alla Fiorentina (Tuscan steak) are an excellent pairing, as the wine's bold structure and tannins complement the richness of the meat. Other ideal combinations include braised lamb with rosemary and garlic, or ossobuco. Together, they create an unforgettable dining experience.

Vintage Quality

The 2015 vintage in Bolgheri was widely considered exceptional and 'magnanimous', meeting all the standards of a 'vintage handbook'. A mild, dry spring led to an early bud break and flowering, and after a hot start to summer, temperatures moderated from late July and throughout August. This, combined with good diurnal (day-to-night) temperature swings, ensured perfect phenolic ripeness, resulting in deep, highly concentrated wines with great character and excellent evolutionary potential.

title: Gerard Raphet Gevrey Chambertin 2020
bodyHtml:
Introduction

This red wine originates from France, specifically from the Gevrey Chambertin appellation within the Côte de Nuits subregion of Burgundy. Established in the 1920s, Domaine Gérard Raphet is a traditional family estate based in Morey Saint Denis, now managed by fourth generation winemaker Gérard Raphet and his daughter, Marion. The winery's philosophy emphasizes a handmade approach 'from field to bottle', utilizing exceptionally old vines—many surpassing 100 years—to create wines that prioritize terroir expression and elegance through minimal intervention.

Wine Description

Gérard Raphet Gevrey Chambertin 2020 displays a delicate ruby colour in the glass. The nose is expressive and surprisingly forceful, offering aromas of red fruit, cherry, and minerals layered with earthy forest floor and delicate spice. On the palate, the wine is medium bodied and firm, featuring a vibrant core of red fruit and cherry balanced by refreshing acidity and a refined tannic structure. It is characterized by its invigorating freshness and a long finish that showcases the classic Gevrey Chambertin minerality. This 100% Pinot Noir has an ABV of 13% and was fermented with indigenous yeasts before ageing for 18 months in older French oak barrels, typically using only 15% new oak to preserve fruit purity. The estate follows sustainable (lutte raisonnée) viticulture practices, managing vineyards predominantly organically without formal certification. The optimal drinking window for this village level wine is generally from release through 10 to 12 years.

Vintage Quality

The 2020 vintage in the Côte de Nuits is regarded as exceptional, characterized by a particularly mild winter and a hot, dry summer that led to the earliest harvest on record for many producers. The grapes reached peak ripeness while preserving remarkable acidity, yielding reds that are notably expressive and energetic with a peppery spiciness and an impressive tannic structure designed for the long term.

title: Chateau Ducru Beaucaillou 2020
bodyHtml:
The style of 2020 is reminiscent of the academic 2010 but with a higher concentration of flavours and greater density of anthocyanins and tannins, underlined with the Ducru’s trademark freshness, giving an exquisite, succulent texture.

Blend: 81% Cabernet Sauvignon, 19% Merlot Noir

100 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

Lastly, the 2020 Chateau Ducru-Beaucaillou is another legendary wine from this château that has been on an incredible run over the past decade. A blend of 81% Cabernet Sauvignon and 19% Merlot that was brought up all in new French oak, it has a saturated purple hue to go with an incredible, mineral-laced bouquet of crème de cassis, liquid violets, graphite, and tobacco leaf. More structured and concentrated than any of the Leovilles, this blockbuster, deep, concentrated, full-bodied Saint-Julien has off-the-charts purity, ultra-fine tannins, and a great, great finish. I wrote in my notes, "Like the 2010, only better." You won't find a more concentrated yet flawlessly balanced and elegant wine out there. It's going to need a decade of cellaring and will have 40, 50, if not 60 years of longevity.

97 Points - James Suckling

Really perfumed and complex with blackberries, blackcurrants and flowers. Gorgeous cabernet sauvignon character. Full-bodied with really fine, polished tannins. Superb length and intensity. Very compact and seamless. Ethereal. Just goes on and on.

98 Points - Decanter

An amazing Ducru, one of the wines of the vintage. Hugely persistent, chiselled and precise, yet succulent in its berry and cassis fruit character. The slate and pencil lead finish slows things down and grabs hold of you, I love the push-and-pull of the tannins. Always a confident and well-finessed wine, really flexing its muscles in 2020. 100% new oak barrels.

95 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2020 Ducru-Beaucaillou unwinds in the glass with aromas of dark berries, pencil shavings, violets and pipe tobacco, all framed by creamy new oak. On the palate, it's medium to full-bodied, fleshy and concentrated, with a deep but tightly wound core that's still quite wrapped up in extract and oak tannin, even if it isn't quite as big-boned as its 2019 counterpart. It will require some patience.

title: Opus One 2019 - 3 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
The essence of time is expressed in Opus One wine by the character of each vintage. Place, often defined as terroir, represents the geography, the climate and the essential human element which is captured in the wine's balance between power and finesse, structure and texture.

Guided by the vision of their founders, winemaker Michael Silacci combines intuition and technical acumen with the dual perspective of viticulturist and winemaker. From tasting berries to careful sorting and extended aging in new French oak barrels, each stage of the winemaking process is afforded the same meticulous consideration and attention.

99 Points - James Suckling

The purity of fruit is really something else here, with currants and fresh flowers, such as violets and roses. Flower stems as well. Fantastic length and structure to the wine, with tightness and focus. Wonderful fruit. Graceful. A blend of 78% cabernet sauvignon, 8% merlot, 7% petit verdot, 6% cabernet franc and 1% malbec. Try after 2028.

97-99 Points (Barrel Sample) - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Winemaker Michael Silacci commented that usually the blends are finished in January or February after the vintage. This year, with the 2019s, he was still tweaking the blend, but he did mention that this is "pretty close to the final blend." Deep garnet-purple in color, the 2019 Opus One leaps from the glass with notes of Black Forest cake, Morello cherries, mulberries and fresh blackcurrants plus hints of licorice, wilted roses, Sichuan pepper and iron ore. Full-bodied, the palate is jam-packed with juicy black, blue and red fruits, framed by velvety tannins and background freshness, finishing on a compelling earthy/mineral note. Tasted as a barrel sample, this is a truly magnificent Opus One in the making!
