97 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

The 2019 Opus One is brilliant and certainly a worthy follow-up to the 2018. Pure cassis fruits, notes of violets, rose petals, and lead pencil, medium to full body, nicely integrated background oak, and terrific tannins all define this beauty, and while it has the vintage's up-front charm, it's going to age beautifully for 20+ years as well.

95 Points - Wine Spectator

This takes the opposite tack from 2018, with more of an opening flourish of enticing fruit in the form of damson pâte de fruit, gently warmed cassis and cherry compote flavors. Very polished, with a subtle alder accent adding some cut through the finish, where hints of red tea, iris and eventually loam peek in. A generous and modern Opus. Cabernet Sauvignon, Petit Verdot, Merlot, Cabernet Franc and Malbec.

title: Shafer Cabernet Sauvignon 'One Point Five' 2023
bodyHtml:
Shafer Vineyards, a family-owned estate in Napa Valley, has been crafting premium wines since the 1970s. The 'One Point Five' Cabernet Sauvignon pays homage to the father-and-son partnership of John and Doug Shafer, symbolizing their close collaboration in winemaking. The winery is renowned for its commitment to sustainable farming and producing wines that reflect the unique terroir of the Stags Leap District.

Wine Description
The 'One Point Five' Cabernet Sauvignon presents a deep garnet hue. On the nose, it offers a bouquet of black cherry, crème de cassis, and ripe black plum, complemented by notes of lavender and savory herbs. The palate is rich and full-bodied, showcasing flavors of dark fruits intertwined with hints of graphite and subtle oak. The wine's structure is supported by seamlessly integrated tannins, leading to a long, elegant finish. Composed predominantly of Cabernet Sauvignon, with small additions of Petit Verdot, Merlot, and Malbec, this wine is approachable in its youth but also promises excellent aging potential over the next two decades.

Food Pairing
This robust Cabernet Sauvignon pairs beautifully with hearty dishes. Consider serving it alongside grilled lamb loin chops seasoned with herbes de Provence and garlic, or a classic filet mignon with a rich balsamic glaze. For a comforting option, short ribs braised with mushrooms and tomatoes will complement the wine's depth and complexity. These pairings highlight the wine's depth and character.

title: Inglenook Blancaneaux 2020
bodyHtml:
In 1879, Finnish explorer and adventurer Gustave Niebaum searched the Napa Valley with the goal of establishing a wine estate to rival the finest chateau of France. For decades his wines won acclaim and remain some of the most admired in American wine history's classic period. By the mid-1960's, his property was divided, and estate-wine production ceased.

A decade later, Francis Ford Coppola purchased 1,500 acres of this historic property and revived Captain Niebaum's fine winemaking tradition. 

Brilliant gold-yellow in color, the wine opens with inviting accents of Meyer lemon curd, honeysuckle, and white peach. Seamless and creamy on the palate, this is a nicely concentrated wine. It closes with lingering notes of chamomile and juicy Anjou pear and retains a vibrant tension throughout.

93 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The latest release of the white wine, the 2020 Blancaneaux boasts greater purity than the 2016, with gentle hints of crushed stone and pencil shavings accenting pear, melon and citrus on the nose. Slightly fuller-bodied as well, it's pleasantly silky in feel, finishing fine and long.

91 Points - James Suckling

Pear and white-peach aromas with some citrus follow through to a full body with layers of fruit and a fresh finish. Mineral undertones. A rather solid and delicious white.

91 Points - Decanter

Caramelised lemons on the nose, aromas of citrus patisserie. This is rich and bold, not in terms of texture - that is smooth and crisp and lifted, but you can feel the alcohol here and the spice from the wood.

title: Chateau Pontet Canet 2019
bodyHtml:
This wine comes from the country of France, specifically the Bordeaux region, and more precisely the subregion of Pauillac. Château Pontet-Canet is a historic estate that was classified as a Fifth Growth in the Bordeaux Wine Official Classification of 1855. Since 1975, it has been owned by the Tesseron family, who were also known for their cognac company. The current philosophy of the estate, led by Alfred Tesseron, is based on a commitment to biodynamic viticulture, which is a major focus of their winemaking. This dedication to working in harmony with nature is believed to contribute to the wine's energy and intensity.

Wine Description

The 2019 Pontet-Canet has a deep, almost black, garnet-purple colour. The aroma is complex and enchanting, featuring notes of prunes, creme de cassis, wilted roses, spice box, iron ore, and underbrush. On the palate, this is a full-bodied, rich, and concentrated wine with layers of black fruit and a touch of mint. It has a framework of fine-grained tannins that are both powerful and velvety, which support the complex, layered flavours and lead to a very long, mineral-laced finish. The wine is a blend of 65% Cabernet Sauvignon, 30% Merlot, 3% Cabernet Franc, and 2% Petit Verdot. It is considered a wine with significant aging potential, with an optimal drinking window after 2028. This wine is certified organic and biodynamic.

Accolades

  • James Suckling - 99 points

  • The Wine Independent - 99 points

  • Robert Parker's Wine Advocate - 99 points

  • Wine Enthusiast - 99 points

  • Decanter - 98 points

Food Pairing

Château Pontet-Canet is a versatile wine that pairs well with classic meat dishes such as veal, pork, beef, lamb, and duck. It can also be a good match for grilled or roasted dishes, rich fish like tuna, and various hard and soft cheeses. The bold tannins and rich fruit flavours complement hearty meals. Together, they create an unforgettable dining experience.

Vintage Quality

The 2019 vintage in Bordeaux followed a mild winter. Despite a cold snap in May, flowering was uniform and quick, and the summer that followed helped the grapes ripen. The vintage is described as having great precision and definition, and it promises to be a great vintage from this biodynamic estate. The winemaker's skill is evident in the excellent balance and integration of this wine.

title: Chateau de Beaucastel Chateauneuf du Pape 'Hommage a Jacques Perrin' 2021
bodyHtml:
Château de Beaucastel, located in the prestigious Châteauneuf-du-Pape appellation of France's Rhône Valley, has a rich history dating back to the 16th century. Since 1909, it has been meticulously managed by the Perrin family, who are renowned for their dedication to traditional winemaking practices and their emphasis on biodynamic agriculture. The 'Hommage à Jacques Perrin' cuvée, first introduced in 1989, is a tribute to the family's patriarch and showcases the estate's commitment to excellence. ​

Wine Description

The 2021 'Hommage à Jacques Perrin' is a masterful blend of approximately 60% Mourvèdre, 20% Grenache, and 20% Syrah. In the glass, it presents a deep, inky hue. The nose is complex, revealing aromas of truffle, tree bark, blackberry, and black cherry, complemented by hints of liquorice and peppery spice. On the palate, it is full-bodied and rich, with multilayered fruit flavors, fine-grained tannins, and a refreshing lift on the long finish. This wine embodies balance, freshness, and remarkable complexity.

Accolades

  • Wine Advocate – 97 points

  • Jancis Robinson MW – 18.5+/20

  • James Suckling – 96 points

  • Decanter – 95 points

  • Jeb Dunnuck – 96 points

  • Vinous – 95 points​

 

Food Pairing

This wine pairs exquisitely with hearty dishes such as roasted lamb, wild game, or aged cheeses. These pairings highlight the wine's depth and character, creating an unforgettable dining experience.

title: Chateau Lafite Rothschild 2022 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
Château Lafite Rothschild, a First Growth estate under the Bordeaux Wine Official Classification of 1855, is one of the world’s most prestigious wineries. Owned by the Rothschild family since 1868, the estate is revered for its tradition of excellence and its influence on the evolution of Bordeaux winemaking. The vineyard’s gravel-rich terroir, coupled with meticulous viticulture, contributes to the refined power and elegance for which Lafite is celebrated.

Wine Description
The 2022 vintage opens with a deep garnet colour and a strikingly expressive bouquet of ripe blackcurrants, graphite, violets, and cedarwood. On the palate, it reveals a full-bodied structure with layers of cassis, black cherries, tobacco, and subtle earthiness, all wrapped in exceptionally fine-grained tannins. The mouthfeel is both rich and lifted, leading to a lingering, harmonious finish that is mineral-driven and precise.

Accolades

  • James Suckling - 100 Points

  • Vinous - 100 Points

  • Decanter - 100 Points

  • Jeb Dunnuck - 100 Points

  • Wine Advocate - 100 Points

Food Pairing
Pair with dry-aged ribeye, rosemary lamb chops, or black truffle risotto. The wine’s complexity and structure make it an ideal partner to dishes that highlight umami and savoury depth. Together, they create an unforgettable dining experience.

title: Chateau Haut Bailly 2022 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
Introduction

Chateau Haut Bailly 2022 originates from the Pessac-Leognan appellation in the Graves region of Bordeaux, France. The estate's history dates back to the 16th century, and it has been under the ownership of the American Wilmers family since 1998, with Véronique Sanders serving as the estate director. Their winemaking philosophy is rooted in the Japanese 'Kaizen' principle of continuous improvement, emphasizing unwavering standards, balance, and a rational, scientific approach to viticulture that avoids excess and opulence.

Wine Description

This vintage displays a deep, bright purple or garnet-purple colour. The sensory profile is highly expressive, featuring a complex bouquet of blackcurrants, black cherries, and raspberries, layered with floral notes of violets, iris, and rose petals, alongside hints of graphite, tobacco, and wood smoke. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied and dense yet remarkably poised, offering an intensity of silky, fine-grained tannins and a deep core of ripe fruit. The structure is defined by seamless freshness and a penetrating, saline finish. The varietal composition for the 2022 Grand Vin is 56% Cabernet Sauvignon, 37% Merlot, 5% Petit Verdot, and 2% Cabernet Franc. It has an ABV of 14.5% and is produced using sustainable viticulture practices, with the estate avoiding herbicides and harvesting entirely by hand.

Food Pairing

The noble structure and power of this wine make it a perfect companion for substantial meat dishes such as herb-crusted lamb, grilled ribeye steak, or roast venison. It also pairs elegantly with duck confit, veal dishes served with delicate sauces, and earthy mushroom risotto. For a cheese course, it is best suited to hard, aged varieties.

Vintage Quality

The 2022 vintage is considered a 'prophetic' and potentially legendary year for Chateau Haut Bailly, characterized by extreme summer heat and drought. Despite these torrid conditions, the vines—many of which are over 50 years old—adapted well, producing small, concentrated berries with exceptional fruit purity. Yields were limited to 30 hectoliters per hectare, but the resulting wines achieved a superb balance of power, dense material, and surprising freshness.

title: Domaine Barons De Rothschild 'Long Dai' 2018
bodyHtml:
From Domaines Barons de Rothschild (DBR) Lafite’s winery in China, Domaine de Long Dai 2018 is the second vintage of the domaine’s main label.

The 2018 vintage of Long Dai is a blend of 75% Cabernet Sauvignon, 17% Marselan and 8% Cabernet Franc. 

The proportion of Cabernet Sauvignon in the 2018 vintage is slightly higher than the inaugural 2017 vintage, giving the wine higher level of tannins and more robust structure.

Domaine de Long Dai’s vineyards are planted on granite soil terraces in the the foothills of the Qiushan Valley in Penglai in China’s northeastern Shandong province.  Harvesting was done by hand in successive pickings. The wine was then aged in French oak barrels from DBR Lafite's own cooperage in the Pauillac region of Bordeaux.

According to Olivier Trégoat, Technical Director of DBR Lafite, the climate condition in 2018 in Qiushan Valley was very beneficial to the Cabernet Sauvignon vines planted on the hillside, leading to very high quality grapes.  "We can say that this vintage is a big wine,” Trégoat said. “With strong yet elegant tannins, Long Dai 2018 shows a personality unique to the granite soils in Qiushan Valley, and that is what me and the team want to achieve,” he added.

Long Dai 2018 is described as having a deep colour, with ripe black fruit aromas and obvious spice signature. The winery said this vintage has a bolder and more aromatic style than the 2017 vintage.

96 Points - James Suckling
93  Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

title: Kongsgaard Napa Valley Chardonnay 2023
bodyHtml:
Kongsgaard Napa Valley Chardonnay 2023 is a highly concentrated white wine produced from family-owned land in the eastern hills of Napa, California.

The Kongsgaard family has owned the parcel of land producing this wine since the 1920s, with John and Maggy Kongsgaard planting the renowned 'The Judge' vineyard in the 1970s. Now a multi-generational endeavor involving their son Alex, the winery is celebrated for its 'archaic,' low-intervention winemaking philosophy. John Kongsgaard, a pioneer of unfiltered commercial white wines in California, crafts these selections with a European-influenced style that prioritizes power, grace, and a vivid expression of the rocky volcanic terrain.

Wine Description

The 2023 Chardonnay is a dense and powerful wine that balances opulent fruit with a signature mineral tension. Its sensory profile features layered aromas of white peach, grilled pineapple, and Meyer lemon cream, transitioning into a core of orange marmalade, marzipan, and toasted hazelnut. On the palate, the wine is rich and beautifully textured, showing ripe pear and baked apple supported by notes of honeysuckle and a distinct flinty minerality. It is characterized by an 'electric' drive and a long, savory finish.

This 100% Chardonnay is sourced from low-yielding vineyards where vines must struggle through rocky hill soils to obtain nutrients. The winemaking process involves indigenous yeast fermentation in old French oak barrels, followed by a long, slow aging period without fining or filtration. This approach maintains the wine's natural energy and textural depth. The estate utilizes organic viticultural practices, and the wine typically reaches a robust ABV level, reflecting the concentrated nature of the fruit.

Food Pairing

The richness and complex structure of this Chardonnay make it a sophisticated partner for decadent seafood dishes, such as lobster thermidor, dungeness crab mac and cheese, or pan-seared scallops in a brown butter sauce. Its toasted nut and mineral notes also pair exceptionally well with truffle risotto, creamy wild mushroom pasta, or roasted poultry served with a herb-infused cream sauce. For a cheese pairing, consider aged hard cheeses like Comté or nutty Gruyère, which mirror the wine’s depth.

Vintage Quality

The 2023 vintage in Napa Valley is noted for its exceptional quality, following a cool growing season that extended the hang time for the grapes. This allowed for gradual sugar accumulation and the preservation of bright, lively acidity, which is evident in the wine's 'mineral tension'. While a late-season heat spike compacted the final harvest, the resulting fruit was highly concentrated and healthy, producing Chardonnays with a rare balance of ripe power and fresh, vibrant energy.

title: Anakota Cabernet Sauvignon 'Helena Dakota Vineyard' 2021
bodyHtml:
This red wine originates from the United States, specifically from the Knights Valley AVA in Sonoma County, California. The Anakota estate was established in the late 1990s by the Jackson family, who sought a site capable of blending the opulence of Napa with the structural precision of Sonoma. Under the direction of vigneron Pierre Seillan, the winery employs a 'micro-cru' philosophy, dividing the vineyard into small blocks to capture the distinct geological nuances of the volcanic, gravelly loam soils.

Wine Description

Anakota Cabernet Sauvignon 'Helena Dakota Vineyard' 2021 displays an opaque ruby or deep garnet-purple colour. The nose is highly aromatic, offering detailed scents of blackcurrant, blueberry, violet, and crème brûlée, accented by deeper notes of pressed sage, pencil lead, and menthol. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied and broad-shouldered, featuring a polished and plush texture that carries concentrated flavours of black fruit, dark chocolate, and graphite. It is characterized by its remarkable power and energy, balanced by a fresh spine of acidity and firm, grainy tannins that lead to a very long, mineral-driven finish. This 100% Cabernet Sauvignon was matured for 15 months in 85% new French oak and has an ABV of 13.8%. While the estate manages its vineyards with meticulous care, this bottling is not certified organic. The optimal drinking window for this vintage is from 2027 through 2050.

Accolades

  • Jeb Dunnuck - 97 points.

  • James Suckling - 97 points.

  • The Wine Independent (Lisa Perrotti-Brown) - 97+ points.

  • Robert Parker's Wine Advocate - 96 points.

title: Torbreck Les Amis 2017
bodyHtml:
Torbreck, founded in 1994 by David Powell, is situated at Marananga on the western ridge of the Barossa. Since that time he has produced some of the world's finest 'Rhone varietal' wines, exclusively from Barossa fruit; this has been acknowledged by the wine press in Europe, America and Australia. 

A wine of immense pleasure on the nose of violets, red currant, wild raspberry, Chinese five spice and pomegranate aromas. Cleansing acidity drives the wine to finish fresh and alive with plenty of mid palate texture and old vine Grenache complexities to give this wine plenty of promised maturity in the cellar.

94 Points - James Suckling

Pomegranate and spiced berry-pastry aromas, together with earthy, leathery and spicy character. The cooler vintage has delivered quite complex style. The palate has a very juicy feel with a bolder oak thread and quite a chiseled palate for grenache. Plenty of structure here.

93 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

No Les Amis was bottled in 2016, so the successor to the 2015 is the 2017 Les Amis Grenache, a wine that spent two years in 50% new barriques. It's smoky (like a barbecue pit), boasting lots of dried spices (akin to a dry rub) and cola. 

90 Points - Wine Enthusiast

Made with French barrique (50% new), there's so much of it that it's currently blanketing the wine, giving it a coat of sweet vanilla cola. Hiding beneath are lovely, ripe black and blue fruit, flowers and spice. The palate shows more fruit purity, a silky texture and a fine tannin structure.

title: Biondi Santi Brunello di Montalcino Riserva 1999 - 2nd Release
bodyHtml:
The 1999 Riserva was produced with their proprietary clone of Sangiovese Grosso called BBS11, which was identified and selected by Biondi-Santi at Tenuta Greppo in the Seventies. For this Riserva they exclusively used grapes from the oldest vines with over 25 years of age.   The 1999 Riserva was aged in Slavonian oak barrels for 3 years. It benefited from a long refinement in the bottle in the quiet and darkness of “La Storica”, the bottle library at Tenuta Greppo where all the historic vintages of Biondi-Santi Riserva are scrupulously kept.

Weather conditions at Greppo: January, February, March, April, May cold and wet; June, July and August dry and hot. September had replenishing rains at the beginning of the month. The harvest started in the second part of the month and was dry and cold.

The 1999 Riserva was a quite cool, balanced vintage.  Garnet in the glass, the bouquet shows cherry notes accompanied by liquorice root and tobacco aromas, undergrowth and a bit of incense in a playful dialogue between freshness and poise. On the palate this quite austere vintage today shows grip and intensity with velvety tannins and firm acidity – the signature of Biondi-Santi. With its vigorous, pure and vertical composition it promises a long life ahead of it still.

title: Catena Zapata Malbec Nicasia 2014
bodyHtml:
The 2014 Catena Zapata Nicasia Vineyard Malbec is a wine from the Altamira region in La Consulta District, Uco Valley, Mendoza, Argentina. Crafted by the renowned Bodega Catena Zapata, this single-vineyard Malbec exemplifies the unique terroir of the Nicasia Vineyard and the winery's commitment to producing premium Argentine wines.

Vineyard and Production

  • Location: Nicasia Vineyard is situated at an elevation of 3,593 feet (1,095 meters) in Altamira, La Consulta District, Uco Valley. The vineyard's soil comprises very shallow loamy topsoil with surface gravel and a gravelly dry riverbed subsoil, ensuring optimal drainage. This terroir contributes to the wine's complexity and depth.

  • Viticulture: The vineyard is exclusively planted with the Catena Cuttings selection of Malbec, a proprietary clone known for its exceptional quality. The 2014 vintage experienced favorable conditions, allowing for balanced ripening and the development of concentrated flavors.

  • Vinification: The winemaking process involves 10% whole cluster and 90% whole berry fermentation, hand-loaded into 225-500 liter new French oak barrels. Fermentation spans 15 days at controlled temperatures to extract intense aromas and flavors, with manual cap management ensuring gentle tannin extraction. Both alcoholic and malolactic fermentations occur in barrel, followed by 18 months of aging in French oak and an additional 24 months in bottle before release.

Tasting Notes

  • Appearance: Deep, inky purple hue.

  • Aroma: Aromas of ripe blackberries, plums, and blackcurrants, intertwined with notes of violet, cocoa, and a hint of minerality.

  • Palate: Full-bodied and well-structured, showcasing flavors of dark fruits, chocolate, and subtle vanilla. The wine exhibits velvety tannins, balanced acidity, and a long, persistent finish with nuances of spice and earthiness.

Serving and Pairing

To fully appreciate its complexity, decant the wine for at least an hour before serving at a temperature of 16-18°C (61-64°F). This Malbec pairs exceptionally well with grilled meats, hearty stews, and aged cheeses. Its robust structure and depth also complement dishes featuring rich sauces and roasted vegetables.

title: Chimney Rock Cabernet Sauvignon Stags Leap 2023
bodyHtml: Situated on the famed Silverado Trail in Napa Valley's renowned Stags Leap District, Chimney Rock is recognized as one of the world's premier fine wine producers. Chimney Rock was established in 1984 with the goal of creating wines that would compete against the best Bordeaux. The estate's location in the Stags Leap District, Napa Valley's smallest and most acclaimed sub-appellation, allows winemaker, Elizabeth Vianna to capture this unique terroir and create wines that rival the most important wines of the world. Chimney Rock is a Terlato Family winery and embodies the family's dedication to producing wines of exceptional quality.

title: Sordo Barolo Riserva Gabutti 2008
bodyHtml:
On the nose it shows itself to be a rich, thoroughbred wine with a long, ample finish. Excellent cleanliness. Noticeable among the robust, but unobtrusive sensations are oak, the aroma of ripe fruit, and the fragrance of dried mountain flowers. A very slight hint of resin brings out overtones of sweet spices and peach leaves.

Sordo Barolo Riserva Gabutti has an intense, warm entry on the mouth is followed by nice, sweetish tannins and a very marked earthy flavor. The aromas and sensations that showed on the nose are confirmed in more depth. Great structure, harmony and balance, combined with a long aromatic finish and complexity, promise a glorious future.

Excellent with all kinds of food, but an ideal match in particular for game, roast and grilled meats. Outstanding with mature hard cheeses. A perfect wine for meditation.

title: Dugat Py Gevrey Chambertin 'Petite Chapelle' Premier Cru 2023
bodyHtml:
This rare and monumental red wine originates from the Gevrey-Chambertin Premier Cru appellation in the Côte de Nuits, Burgundy. Domaine Dugat-Py is widely regarded as a producer of "unobtainium," crafting some of the most concentrated and long-lived Pinot Noirs in the world. The Petite Chapelle vineyard (also known as En la Chapelle) sits immediately adjacent to the eastern boundary of the Chapelle-Chambertin Grand Cru. The winery's philosophy leverages 50+ year-old vines and tiny yields to create a wine that often rivals Grand Crus in intensity and depth.

Wine Description

The Dugat-Py Gevrey-Chambertin Premier Cru Petite Chapelle presents an opaque, saturated dark ruby colour. The sensory profile is exceptionally deep, featuring an aromatic nose of cherry cordial, black plum compote, and wild raspberry, layered with sophisticated notes of iron-like minerality, tea leaves, and exotic spice rack. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied and "bigger boned" than many of its siblings, showcased by a cashmere-like texture and superb structural tension. It is characterized by its remarkable "zen-like" balance, leading to a long finish with hints of violet, dark chocolate, and cedar. This 100% Pinot Noir is crafted from vines planted in 1964, fermented with a high percentage of whole bunches (75–100%), and aged for 16–18 months in 100% new French oak casks.

title: Chateau Mouton Rothschild 2011
bodyHtml:
2011 was one of the hottest, sunniest and driest of the last forty years. Very warm weather in April and May gave the vegetation cycle a head start: flowering was recorded on 15 May, the earliest date in living memory, and veraison started two-and-half weeks earlier than usual. Conditions in July and August were very different, bringing less sunshine and significantly more precipitation. However, by the end of August, only 326 mm of rainfall had been recorded since 1 January, compared with an average of 519 mm. Fine weather returned to the Médoc in early September, and bright sunshine prevailed throughout the two weeks of the harvest, which began on 12 September. These auspicious conditions were highly beneficial, allowing the grapes to ripen fully. Picking ended on 28 September. Low yields, especially at Mouton, have produced structured, deep, and fresh wines. 2011 is thus a classic Bordeaux vintage, to be ranked among the finer, or perhaps even the finest.

96 Points - James Suckling 

This shows lots of opulent aromas of ripe fruit, lightly toasted oak, walnut and dried meat. It's full-bodied, with chewy tannins and plenty of fruit. A muscular, solid wine. Baby 1986. Try in 2020.

95 Points - Wine Spectator

This delivers a gorgeously pure beam of cassis and cherry compote, with singed apple wood, graphite and iron notes hanging in the background for now. Long and polished through the finish, showing profound depth in reserve. Best from 2018 through 2035.

95 Points - Wine Enthusiast

There is a lightness about this vintage of Mouton Rothschild. It doesn't take away from its quality but does give the wine poise and an attractive lift. The wine is based on solid tannins, and the ripe fruit builds layers of fruitiness and freshness. It is not likely to be one of the longest-aging Moutons, but it will be delicious. Drink from 2020.

92 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Tasted at the Mouton-Rothschild vertical in London, the 2011 Mouton-Rothschild is probably the "weakest" of the releases between 2008 and 2012. That would unfairly disparage what is perfectly respectable if rather an unexciting Mouton. Here, it has those graphite and cedar aromas present and correct, the former a little more accentuated and with a light sea-spray note emerging with time. The palate is well balanced with cedar and a slight peat-like note infusing the black fruit, rigid in its youth but nicely delineated. As I discerned out of the barrel, it lacks that peacock's tail on the finish, bolting out of the exit door before you get to know each other.

title: Chateau Beausejour 2021
bodyHtml:
Chateau Beausejour was built in 1851 by the Laporte family. The Laporte family owned several vineyard estates in the Bordeaux region and were prosperous wine merchants. In those days, the large chai was used to store and age the most prestigious wines of the Saint Émilion and Pomerol regions (Cheval Blanc, Petrus, Beau-Sejour, Nénin, La Conseillante and Chateau Beausejour!)

95+ Points - James Suckling

A complete wine for the vintage, with blackberry, stone, black-licorice and light walnut character. Medium-to full-bodied and linear, with very fine tannins running the length of the wine.

95 Points - Decanter

So aromatic and beguiling on the nose - pure, lifted, completely captivating in the intensity of fruit and the liveliness of aroma with tiny touches of milk chocolate and perfumed blackcurrants. Supple, agile and sappy on the palate, but also so delicate and elegant in terms of the overall profile. Tannins are fine and gentle, persistent but with the limestone terroir coming through in the mineral, saline, graphite elements which linger at the end. 

93+ Points - Jeb Dunnuck

93 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

title: Chateau Mouton Rothschild 2020
bodyHtml:
The wine is a deep, dark, garnet-hued cherry red. The refined and complex nose opens on remarkably ripe black fruit aromas, going on with airing to reveal blackcurrant and aniseed notes combined with touches of graphite and a subtle hint of blond tobacco. From a smooth yet full-bodied attack, the palate displays highly precise tannins which sustain an expansion of flavors in harmonious, succulent balance. Nuanced refinements evident in touches of mint and mineral, smoky notes.

Blend: 84% Cabernet Sauvignon, 13% Merlot, 2% Cabernet Franc, 1% Petit Verdot

About the Label: A British painter of Scottish origin who divides his time between London and Trinidad, Peter Doig is the artist chosen by Chateau Mouton Rothschild to create the original artwork to illustrate the label for its 2020 vintage. In his work for the label, the painter combines echoes of Cézanne and van Gogh with a fascinating personal reverie on the nocturnal birth of a great wine, seemingly brought to life by the strange magic of a song played on the guitar.

99+ Points - James Suckling

This is a great and impressive Mouton with plushness and precision. A million layers of tannins. It’s full and very friendly, even seductive, in a rich and opulent way, yet it always remains fresh. Balanced and refined. Nothing sticks out here. Every so fine-grained tannins provide flesh. Looking forward to seeing its evolution. 84% cabernet sauvignon, 13% merlot, 2% cabernet franc and 1% petit verdot. 

100 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2020 Mouton Rothschild is a striking wine and one that I regretted not purchasing en primeur as soon as it landed in my glass. Offering up complex aromas of minty cassis, pencil shavings, loamy soil, cigar wrapper, espresso roast and violets, it's medium to full-bodied, broad and layered, with terrific concentrated, beautifully refined tannins and a long, penetrating finish. Checking in at 12.8% alcohol, its incipient complexity, ineffable sense of completeness and exquisite balance mark it out as the purists' choice among the trio of 2018, 2019 and 2020. In this vintage, the lots that made it into the blend were largely confined to the core gravel terroirs that represent Mouton's heart, meaning that there's a little less to go around. This was the first vintage overseen by Mouton's new technical director, Jean-Emmanuel Danjoy, and he has begun with a flying start. 

98 Points - Decanter

The tannins are carefully wrapped up and finessed, slowly but surely building in power and width, with concentrated blue and black fruits through the palate. Cabernet Sauvignon is dominant on the attack, with a deft, savoury and not overly exuberant delivery of flavour. As the slate and saline side builds up, you also feel a slowing down and a tugging back of the tannins. As the wine relaxes in the glass, it becomes more and more signature Mouton, full of exuberance, finesse and pleasure. There is less sweet black cherry fruit than in a year like 2018 or 2019, more on the cassis and bilberry side, it will behave in a more classical manner in the decades to come. 100% new oak. Harvest September 7 to 24. 2% Cabernet Franc completes the blend. Could go to 100 points after ageing.

97+ Points - Jeb Dunnuck

The 2020 Chateau Mouton Rothschild is in the running for the biggest, baddest, and most concentrated wine in the vintage. Based on 84% Cabernet Sauvignon, 13% Merlot, 2% Cabernet Franc, and 1% Petite Verdot brought up in new barrels, this inky hued beast of wine offers up classic Mouton ripe black fruits, scorched earth, tobacco leaf, and freshly sharpened pencil-like aromatics. These carry to a full-bodied, concentrated, tannic, backward 2020 with terrific purity, building, mouth-coating tannins, terrific balance, and one gorgeous finish. Unfortunately, as with many of the top 2020s, this isn't for those looking for instant gratification, and a decade (or more) of cellaring is advised. This hit 13.1% natural alcohol with a pH of 3.78. It will be a 50-, 60-, 70+-year wine.

title: Domaine Boigey Freres Vosne Romanee 'Aux Jachees' 2021 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
Introduction

This red wine originates from France, specifically from the village of Vosne-Romanée in the Côte de Nuits subregion of Burgundy. Domaine Boigey Frères is a rising star in the region, founded in 2017 by brothers Guillaume and Olivier Boigey, who hail from one of the village's oldest winemaking families. The estate's philosophy is centred on recovering family vineyards that were previously leased to others, employing sustainable viticulture to produce limited-quantity wines that prioritizes terroir quality and fruit purity. The 'Les Jachées' parcel is particularly significant as it is situated just behind the renowned vines of Domaine Bizot.

Wine Description

Domaine Boigey Frères Vosne-Romanée 'Les Jachées' 2021 displays a medium light red colour. The nose is highly perfumed and "transparent," offering a bouquet of lifted crushed strawberries and wilted rose petals layered with floral scents and mild spice. On the palate, the wine is medium-bodied with a poised, elegant structure and filigree tannins. It is characterized by its sapid nature and balanced acidity, finishing with a discrete pinch of cracked black pepper and medium length. This 100% Pinot Noir typically has an ABV of 13% and underwent maceration for 7 to 9 days without stems before being aged for 12 to 16 months in French oak barrels (30% to 50% new). While not certified organic, the estate uses organic treatments in the vineyard and is in the process of obtaining High Environmental Value (HVE) certification. The optimal drinking window is estimated from 2024 through 2036.

title: Sine Qua Non White Wine 'Distenta II' 2020
bodyHtml:
99 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

I know the reds get all of the attention here, but the whites are absolutely at the same level, and I don't know anyone doing white blends like this at the same level. A blend of 32% Roussanne, 26% Viognier, 25% Chardonnay, and the rest Gelber Muskateller and Petit Manseng, from Eleven Confessions, Third Twin, Cumulus, and Bien Nacido, it spent 23 months in 45% new French oak. Incredible aromatics of buttered apricots, acacia flowers, orange blossom, brioche, and caramelized pineapple all define this youthful, primordial white that's full-bodied, has a pure, layered mouthfeel, beautiful freshness, and a great finish. I'd put this up with some of the finest whites yet from this estate.

98 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Drinking the White Distenta II is an omakase-like experience, an unexpected journey that begins with naturally bitter phenolics, blossoms into soaring perfume and finishes with dessert-like honeyed tones. On day one, the wine is overt and bold, while day two reveals a fresher, livelier white with finer detail, as if the wine is coming into focus. In the mouth, it's expansive and luxuriously satiny. Despite its powerful style and unabashed ripeness, it carries its 15.8% alcohol expertly and maintains a focused streak of tangy acidity. The finish is especially unique, offering touches of butterscotch that complement its perfumed fruit—a rare combination of aromatic grape varieties and classy new wood that works surprisingly well!

title: Cathiard Vineyard Founding Brothers 2020
bodyHtml:
The Founding Brothers is produced in homage to James and William Rennie the founders of the original winery on the property and images of both are portrayed on this label. In 1880, the two brothers, said goodbye to their native Scotland and set sail to California with high ambition in Napa Valley. Five years later they had built a stone winery and planted 60 acres of vineyards covering the Rutherford and St. Helena AVAs. The same estate is today owned by the Cathiard family.

Founding Brothers is produced exclusively with estate grapes to capture the energy and singularity of this very special terroir. This bottling offers plenty of fruit but also shows some spice notes on both the bouquet and palate. It lingers with notes of dried cigar on the juicy and mouthwatering finish. The tannins are present but do not dominate.

96 Points - Wine Enthusiast

This massively built wine wraps potent black fruit flavors and sophisticated spices in substantial tannins that will surely guide it to greater complexity and smoothness with time. Minerals, graphite, cloves, cedar and blackberries are layered inside a mouthfilling texture.

94 Points - James Suckling

So pure and beautiful with perfumes and cedar as well as currants. Dark mushrooms and bark. A medium-bodied wine with dark berry, currant, chocolate, hazelnut, and fine tannins. 60% cabernet sauvignon and 40% merlot. Better in two or three years and beyond.

title: Chateau Lafon Rochet 2022
bodyHtml:
France, Bordeaux, Saint-Estèphe. Château Lafon Rochet is a historic Fourth Growth estate in the Médoc, with roots dating back to the 17th century. The Tesseron family owned the property for decades before selling to businessman Jacky Lorenzetti in 2021, who also owns Château Pédesclaux and shares in Château d’Issan. The estate is renowned for combining traditional winemaking with a renewed modern vision under its new leadership.

Wine Description
The 2022 vintage presents a deep, intense ruby colour with purple hues. The nose offers expressive aromas of ripe blackcurrant, plum, damson, and subtle cedar, accented by herbal and smoky nuances. On the palate, it reveals a full-bodied structure with velvety tannins, vibrant freshness, and layers of dark fruit, graphite, cocoa, and spice.

Accolades

  • Vinous – 95+ points.

  • James Suckling – 94+ points.

  • Jeb Dunnuck – 93+ points.

Food Pairing
This structured yet refined Saint-Estèphe pairs beautifully with grilled ribeye, roast lamb with rosemary, or rich mushroom ragout. The wine’s dark fruit intensity and firm tannic backbone also complement aged cheeses like Comté or Pecorino.

title: Gagnon Kennedy Vineyards Cabernet Sauvignon 'Monte Rosso Vineyard' 2020
bodyHtml:
The essence of the historic Monte Rosso Vineyard’s bright red volcanic soils appeared to be magically carried over into the aromatics and color of the wine during fermentation. However, post elevage and assemblage, the wine transmogrified itself into a cabernet of blue/black complexion. The aromatics are effusive of freshly baked mixed berry pie, cinnamon, allspice, bay leaf, and sweet cacaoa nibs from the 60% new French Oak barrels.

On the palate, this wine is possibly the least tannic in their entire portfolio of Cabernets. The pedigree of the Monte Rosso Vineyard is exemplified by the intensity of fruit and electrical minerality. The wine’s extended finish is enveloped with a welcoming intensity of medium-fine tannin.

title: Dal Forno Romano Valpolicella Superiore 2018
bodyHtml:
This structured and 'muscular' red wine originates from Italy, within the Valpolicella D.O.C. appellation of the northern Veneto region. Dal Forno Romano is a legendary, world-renowned estate situated in the Illasi Valley, an area outside the historical classical zone that founder Romano Dal Forno completely elevated to global icon status. Operating under an uncompromising winemaking philosophy of radical low yields and extreme technological precision, the family fundamentally redefines what Valpolicella Superiore can be. While legal standards treat Valpolicella Superiore as a casual, everyday red, Dal Forno treats it with the same majestic reverence as their legendary Amarone. The fruit is sourced from the estate's high-density Monte Lodoletta vineyard, where vines are rooted in deep alluvial soils of clay, silt, and limestone gravel, producing a wine of unmatched concentration, density, and monumental structural longevity.

Wine Description

The 2018 Dal Forno Romano Valpolicella Superiore presents an opaque, ink-like ruby-purple color in the glass, showing virtually no light penetration at its dense core. Its sensory profile is exceptionally deep, complex, and high-toned, offering a monumental explosion of aromas that blur the line between a traditional dry red and an opulent Amarone. The bouquet opens with a captivating, multi-faceted display of macerated black cherries, wild blackberries, and blueberry compote, seamlessly layered with complex undertones of dark chocolate, roasted espresso bean, exotic baking spices, sweet pipe tobacco, and a faint hint of asphalt and resinous smoke. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied, incredibly dense, and beautifully focused, showcasing a powerful, concentrated core of black fruits, licorice, and dark plum reduction. It is characterized by its outstanding inner energy and a surprisingly vibrant, mouthwatering backbone of natural acidity that cuts cleanly through its massive extract. The mouthfeel is broad, viscous, and texturally epic, driven by a firm, muscular framework of fine-grained, grippy tannins that glide into an exceptionally long, savory finish highlighted by lingering notes of bittersweet cocoa, graphite, and toasted cedar wood.

title: Domaine Arnoux Pere & Fils Corton 'Le Rognet' Grand Cru 2020
bodyHtml: Corton Grand Cru from a .5-hectare vineyard located near the village of Ladoix Serrigny. The soils here are primarily comprised of gravel, chalk, and stone. Smoked meat, blackberry, and iron aromas and flavors are the hallmarks of this concentrated red. It's well-structured and lively, the acidity driving its long finish. A terrific combination of fruit, structure, and texture.

title: Vieux Chateau Certan 2019
bodyHtml:
Produced in the heart of the Pomerol appellation on Bordeaux's Right Bank in France, Vieux Chateau Certan is a historic estate renowned for its exceptional terroir and meticulous winemaking. Owned by the Thienpont family since 1924, the property is currently managed by Alexandre Thienpont and his son Guillaume, who have upheld a philosophy focused on purity, elegance, and the pursuit of vinicultural excellence. The vineyard is famous for its diverse soils, including deep clay and gravel, and its signature pink capsule—a legacy of founder Georges Thienpont.

Wine Description

The 2019 Vieux Chateau Certan displays a striking, deep purple-black hue and offers a complex sensory profile. The aromatic bouquet is highly perfumed, unfurling with notes of cassis, black cherries, and raspberries mingled with violets, sweet spices, truffle, and a hint of Seville orange marmalade. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied and multi-dimensional, featuring tightly wound layers of vibrant blue and black fruits supported by silky, powdery tannins and a superb bead of acidity. It is a seamless and harmonious wine that concludes with a long, resonant 'peacock's tail' finish.

Accolades

  • Wine Advocate - 100 points

  • James Suckling - 99 points

  • Vinous - 99 points

  • Decanter - 99 points

  • Jeb Dunnuck - 98+ points

  • Wine Spectator - 97 points

Food Pairing

This rich and elegant Pomerol pairs exceptionally well with feathered game, herb-crusted lamb, or a succulent duck breast served with a cherry glaze. It also complements earthy dishes like mushroom risotto and aged cheeses such as Comté or Gruyère.

title: Solaia 2021 (by Tenuta Tignanello)
bodyHtml:
Hailing from Italy, Solaia 2021 is produced in the renowned Chianti Classico area of Tuscany, specifically within the sun-drenched hills of the Tenuta Tignanello estate in the San Casciano in Val di Pesa commune. This estate is owned by the historic Antinori family, whose winemaking heritage spans over six centuries. Their philosophy seamlessly combines innovation with tradition, crafting iconic wines that reflect the unique terroir of their estates.

Wine Description

Solaia 2021 is a masterful blend of predominantly Cabernet Sauvignon, complemented by Sangiovese and Cabernet Franc. In the glass, it reveals a deep, lustrous ruby hue. Aromas unfold with layers of ripe blackcurrant, dark cherry, violet, and subtle hints of graphite and tobacco. The palate is generous yet refined, showcasing plush dark berry fruit interlaced with notes of chocolate, fresh herbs, and a touch of sweet spice. Its texture is full-bodied and velvety, with beautifully integrated tannins leading to a persistent, elegant finish marked by mineral undertones and remarkable freshness.

Accolades

  • Wine Advocate - 98 points.

  • James Suckling - 97 points.

  • Wine Spectator - 96 points.

Food Pairing

This wine pairs exceptionally well with grilled prime rib, braised lamb shanks, or porcini mushroom risotto. These pairings highlight the wine’s depth and character, allowing its layered fruit and savoury nuances to shine alongside rich, hearty dishes.

title: Grgich Hills Cabernet Sauvignon Yountville Reserve 2017
bodyHtml:
Crafted in the United States, this exceptional wine hails from the Yountville subregion within Napa Valley, California. Grgich Hills Estate, founded by Miljenko “Mike” Grgich—renowned for his role in the 1976 Paris Tasting—has been a pioneer in organic and biodynamic viticulture. The winery's commitment to sustainable farming and minimal intervention winemaking is evident in their estate-grown wines, particularly those from their historic Yountville vineyard.

Wine Description

The 2017 Yountville Old Vine Cabernet Sauvignon presents a deep, inky garnet hue. On the nose, it offers alluring aromas of dark red fruits, including blackberry and plum, complemented by notes of blood orange, rose petals, and hints of cinnamon and gingerbread. The palate is rich and complex, featuring flavours of black olives, blackberries, and subtle undertones of moss and savoury dried herbs. This full-bodied wine boasts a balanced acidity and smooth tannins, leading to a long, harmonious finish.

Food Pairing

This robust Cabernet Sauvignon pairs excellently with grilled ribeye steak, braised lamb shanks, or aged cheddar cheese. The wine's depth and complexity are enhanced when accompanied by hearty, savoury dishes, creating an unforgettable dining experience.

title: Chateau Beau Sejour Becot 2015
bodyHtml:
Chateau Beau-Sejour Becot is located just to the west of the medieval town of Saint-Emilion, in the very heart of this prestigious appellation. 

The estate was named Beau-Sejour in 1787 by General Jacques de Carle, the proprietor at the time. Michel Becot bought the estate from Doctor Jean Fagouet in 1969 and further increased the area under vine from 10.5 hectares to 15 by acquiring 4.5 hectares on the Trois Moulins plateau in 1979. The chateau then took on the name of Beau-Sejour Becot.

96 Points - Wine Enthusiast

This family-owned property at one of the high points in Saint-Émilion has made a rich, opulent wine, full of perfumed Cabernet Franc and generous Merlot. Ripe blackberries and dark plums are permeated with some serious tannins for aging. 

95 Points - Wine Spectator

This brims with ripe, juicy plum, blackberry and açaí berry flavors, studded with licorice and fruitcake notes and backed by a wonderfully integrated apple wood detail through the finish. Pumps a lot of fruit out but does so energetically.

95 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Medium to deep garnet-purple colored, the nose opens with blackberries, black cherries and crushed black plums with touches of spice box, lavender and cedar. Medium to full-bodied, it's rich, velvety and decadent in the mouth with a firm backbone and long, spicy finish. Yum!

95 Points - James Suckling

Very perfumed with crushed berries and blackberries. Wet earth and great intensity. Decadent. Full-bodied, layered and very velvety and intense. Extremely long and intense. A sexy and opulent wine yet poised and tight. One of best ever.

94 Points - Decanter

Deep and reserved on the nose but a fragrant palate. Powerful but refined tannic base. Beautiful smooth texture with the freshness from the limestone terroir. Persistent finish.

title: Produttori del Barbaresco - Barbaresco 'Rabaja' Riserva 2020
bodyHtml:
This red wine originates from the Barbaresco region in Piedmont, Italy, produced within the renowned Rabaja subregion. Founded in 1958, the Produttori del Barbaresco cooperative was established by 19 local growers under the guidance of the village priest to protect the identity and quality of their Nebbiolo grapes. The winery operates on a philosophy of communal excellence, managing 100 hectares of prime vineyards to create wines that serve as a benchmark for the appellation.

Wine Description

The 2020 Barbaresco Rabaja Riserva presents a deep, youthful ruby red colour that often edges toward garnet. The complex nose is dark and explosive, offering intense aromas of forest berry, new leather, dark spice, ripe cherry, and underbrush, balanced by highlights of fresh mint and dusty earth. On the palate, this full-bodied wine is rich and powerful, delivering succulent flavours of black raspberry, plum, licorice, tar, and cloves. It is characterized by its enormous energy, streamlined mouthfeel, and firm, dusty tannins that lead into a long, persistent finish. This 100% Nebbiolo wine has an ABV of 14.5%. While it will require a measure of patience to integrate, the optimal drinking window is estimated from 2026 through 2050.

Accolades

  • Jeb Dunnuck - 98 points

  • Vinous - 97 points

  • Wine Advocate - 95 points

  • Wine Spectator - 95 points

  • Decanter - 93 points

Food Pairing

The wine's robust structure and velvety tannic texture pair excellently with fresh egg pasta dishes such as tajarin with truffles or rich risotto. It is also a suitable match for roasted leg of lamb with rosemary, braised beef cheek, and wild game such as venison. For cheese courses, it complements matured and spicy hard cheeses like Parmigiano-Reggiano.

Vintage Quality

The 2020 vintage in Barbaresco is considered exceptional, featuring a balanced growing season that avoided extreme heat spikes. Consistent warm weather in August combined with cooler temperatures in September allowed for regular, even ripening and the development of deep fruit concentration.

title: Rivetto Barolo Serralunga d'Alba 2010
bodyHtml:
This wine is made from 100% Nebbiolo grapes. The wine presents a colour of garnet red with orange reflections. On the nose, it offers an ethereal, intense, and pleasant aroma, with notes of rose, tar, dried red fruit, violets, rose hips, tobacco, and leather. The palate is austere but velvety, robust, and harmonious, with flavours of cherry, licorice, earth, red fruits, and a hint of smoke. The wine is elegant and well-balanced, displaying sturdy or fine-grained tannins, bright acidity, and a long, elegant finish. It captures the typicality of the Serralunga site with mineral and herb nuances. Rivetto Barolo is made with certified organic and biodynamic grapes, and the optimal drinking window for the 2019 vintage is 2025–2040.

Accolades

  • Wine Enthusiast - 94 points

  • Wine Spectator - 93 points

  • CellarTracker - 91 points 

Food Pairing

Suggested pairings for Barolo from Serralunga include rich, hearty dishes that can stand up to the wine's formidable tannin structure. Classic pairings include beef, pasta, lamb, deer, venison, and traditional Piedmontese dishes like Brasato al Barolo (braised veal). The wine also pairs beautifully with risotto featuring rich ingredients such as truffle, butter, cream, and cheese. Other excellent matches are game, strong cheeses like Castelmagno or Grana Padano, and dishes with truffles. The pairing with truffle highlights the wine's depth and character.

title: Verite 'La Muse' 2015
bodyHtml:
The winter of 2014-2015 was another mild and dry one, which included only two weekend rainstorms. Budbreak came in mid-March and the vines began to bloom early – at the end of April. A cool April and May with some rainy spells meant that bloom did not finish until June. A warm and dry June led to a July veraison kickoff. Vigneron Pierre Seillan recalls that of his 49 vintages, 2015 was the first to begin picking in August – August 31st to be precise. Harvest lasted 12 days and finished on September 12th. Although yields were low, the quality of the grapes in this vintage was outstanding.

The 2015 La Muse opens with a classic ruby-red core and brilliant pink-purple outer rim. A youthful, clean bouquet recalls wildflower bloom in Northern California, aromas of purple flowers rising from the rocks. Crème de Cassis, blueberry pie and black raspberries mingle with red apple in a fresh yet restrained ripeness. Like the rock bed of its loamy Sonoma County vineyard, La Muse bends and turns with seductive aromas of baking spices, juniper berries and dark chocolate. Velvety tannins with a lingering finish complete the wine with signature balance. La Muse’s signature shows hints of clay and alluvial soils, with structure and suppleness that will age beautifully for decades to come. - August 2017.

97 Points - James Suckling     This is dense yet agile young red with aromas and flavors of blackberries, black olives and black truffles. Full-bodied, layered and rich. Pretty ripe and melted tannins. Top merlot. Drink or hold.

97 Points - Robert Parker Wine Advocate      Composed of 90% Merlot, 7% Cabernet Franc and 3% Malbec, the 2015 La Muse sports a very deep garnet-purple color, leaping from the glass with exuberant crème de cassis, blueberry pie and licorice notes plus suggestions of Indian spices, dark chocolate, menthol, sautéed herbs and potpourri. Full-bodied, rich and seductive in the mouth, it delivers tons of black and blue fruit preserves flavors, accented by exotic spices, framed with velvety tannins and finishing on a persistent earthy/mineral note.

95 Points - Vinous      The 2015 La Muse is developing beautifully. Ripe, ample and voluptuous in the glass, the 2015 exudes character. Even with all of its obvious intensity, the 2015 has quite a bit of freshness to balance out the ripe, racy Merlot-based fruit. Super-ripe red cherry, plum, mocha and spice notes build into the racy, inviting finish.

title: Castello dei Rampolla d'Alceo 2014
bodyHtml:
Deep purple in color, this wine offers aromas of espresso, sweet melted licorice, black currant jam, tobacco and toasty oak. It is full-bodied on the palate, with refined tannins.

Perfect with game, chicken, turkey, ham, aged cheese and mushrooms.

95 Points - James Suckling

Wonderful aromas of crushed raspberries, blueberries and violets follow through to a full body, firm and silky tannins and a flavorful finish. Joyful 2014! A blend of cabernet sauvignon and petit verdot. Drink or hold.

95 Points - Wine Enthusiast

Made with 85% Cabernet Sauvignon and 15% Petit Verdot, this focused red offers earthy aromas of moist soil, new leather, cedar and black currant. It’s elegant and racy, delivering cassis, juicy black cherry, licorice, chopped mint and tobacco framed in fine-grained tannins and vibrant acidity. It’s already delicious but hold for even more complexity and to let the tannins unwind.

95 Points - Vinous

The 2014 d'Alceo is more in line with previous years than Sammarco. Deep, unctuous and super-powerful, the 2014 exudes richness and textural intensity from the very first taste. Readers will have to give the 2014 at least a few years in bottle to help some of the baby fat meld away. Inky blue/purplish berry fruit, sage, mint and lavender are some of the many notes that start to emerge as the wine sits in the glass. This is a terrific effort for the vintage.

94 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Fruit for this wine always comes from the same vineyard site, and production was heavily reduced in this difficult vintage. If an average year sees 13,000 bottles made, only 6,200 bottles were made of the 2014 d'Alceo. This wine shows beautiful brightness and linearity with a polished, almost glossy texture that feels like silk on the palate. The wine is mostly Cabernet Sauvignon with a smaller part Petit Verdot. It offers a mid-weight texture with balanced tannins and acidity to seal the deal.

title: Chateau Haut Brion 2022
bodyHtml:
Chateau Haut Brion, located in the heart of Pessac Léognan, is one of the oldest and most prestigious wine estates in Bordeaux. Established in 1533, it holds the distinction of being the only First Growth located outside the Médoc. Owned by Domaine Clarence Dillon since 1935, the estate continues to honour centuries of winemaking tradition, producing wines of extraordinary character and longevity.

Wine Description
The 2022 Chateau Haut Brion displays a deep, garnet-purple hue. On the nose, it exudes intense aromas of ripe blackcurrant, plum preserves, smoked cedar, graphite, and violet. The palate is richly layered with flavours of cassis, tobacco leaf, dark chocolate, and warm earth, underscored by savoury minerality and firm but refined tannins. Full-bodied and powerful, yet remarkably graceful, it shows exceptional balance with a velvety texture and an extraordinarily long, lingering finish.

Accolades

  • Wine Advocate – 96–98 points

  • James Suckling – 97–98 points

  • Vinous – 96–98 points

  • Decanter – 98 points

  • Wine Enthusiast – 98–100 points

Food Pairing
This exceptional Bordeaux pairs beautifully with roast lamb, aged ribeye, or duck breast with blackberry reduction. Earthy mushroom risotto or truffled potatoes also complement the wine’s complexity. Together, they create an unforgettable dining experience.

title: Le Petit Mouton 2021
bodyHtml:
Produced in France, specifically within the prestigious Pauillac appellation of Bordeaux. Château Mouton Rothschild is currently under the stewardship of the descendants of Baron Philippe de Rothschild and Baroness Philippine, including Camille and Philippe Sereys de Rothschild, and Julien de Beaumarchais de Rothschild. The estate is celebrated for its 'Live for the vine' philosophy, which combines traditional winemaking with modern technology to reflect the singular essence of its 82 hectares of terroir.

Wine Description

This wine presents a crimson hued garnet red in the glass. The nose is expressive and complex, revealing aromas of red berry fruits, mint, and blackcurrants alongside delicate floral notes of peony and hints of cigar wrapper and graphite. On the palate, it is medium to full bodied, featuring a dense and muscular attack with juicy, fleshy fruit supported by powdery, silky tannins. The finish is persistent and refined, showing a classic mineral quality and a refreshing, minty edge.

Accolades

  • James Suckling - 95 points

  • Decanter - 94 points

  • Vinous - 92 points

  • Robert Parker Wine Advocate - 91 points

Food Pairing

The structured tannins and vibrant acidity of this wine make it a natural companion for hearty red meat dishes, such as grilled leg of lamb marinated in herbs or a classic beef stew with mushrooms. It also pairs beautifully with earthy flavours like wild boar or blue veined cheeses.

title: Faiveley Meursault 2022
bodyHtml:
A love of wine has been passed on from one Faiveley generation to the next for more than 180 years. The Domaine has always remained in the same family and today Erwan and Eve, the 7th generation of the Faiveley family, are at the helm and are keen to respect the traditions and savoir-faire of the family while looking to the future.

Domaine Faiveley believes that the quality of the wines comes from the fruit. To make sure they are able to get the best fruit and resulting wines, the team has invested in separate winemaking and viticulture teams in the Côte d’Or and Côte Chalonnaise, fine-tuned their barrel selection, and built a state-of-the-art winery in Mercurey. Last year, the family completed the renovation of their cellars in the heart of Nuits-St-Georges.

Touches of honeysuckle, white and yellow fruits with excellent richness, depth and vibrant acidity – finished with toasted bread and vanilla.

title: Kosta Browne Pinot Noir 'Russian River' 2021
bodyHtml:
Representing the 'heartland' of California Pinot Noir, the Kosta Browne Pinot Noir 'Russian River' 2022 is a masterful blend of the region's most esteemed vineyard sites. The winery, founded in 1997 by Dan Kosta and Michael Browne with tip money saved from their restaurant jobs, has evolved into a global icon, cemented by its 2011 'Wine of the Year' title from Wine Spectator. Winemaker Julien Howsepian follows a philosophy of 'purity and finesse,' utilizing minimal intervention and precise timing to capture the soulful expression of the Russian River Valley's fog-drenched terroir.

Wine Description

This Pinot Noir presents a vibrant red colour, leading with captivating aromatics of dark red cherry, raspberry, and blueberry. On the palate, it is medium bodied and poised, balancing robust pomegranate and bramble fruit notes with a refreshing, lifted acidity. Aged for 16 months in a combination of 38% new French oak, neutral oak, and oak foudre, it develops a fine structure with subtle savory nuances of cedar, cassia bark, and dried herbs. The finish is remarkably long, robust, and enduring, showing a captivately elegant texture. Composed of 100% Pinot Noir.

title: Torbreck RunRig 2022
bodyHtml:
Torbreck Vintners, established in 1994, was founded on a vision to honour and rejuvenate the Barossa Valley’s extraordinary old vineyards, home to some of the oldest vines on the planet. The winery takes inspiration from France’s Rhône Valley while championing the Barossa’s rich viticultural heritage.

Wine Description

Complex and lifted aromatics of dense black fruits such as blackberries, satsuma plum and black cherry cassis and mulberry complimented with dark chocolate, cacao bean vanilla pod tar and star anise and Turkish delight. The opulent full-bodied mouthfeel and vibrancy is a real standout on a plush yet mineral strewn, velvety textured palate. The complex layers and fruit characters continue to evolve in the glass with firm but drying tannins seamlessly balanced with long acid and statuesque posture and length.

Accolades

  • Robert Parker's Wine Advocate - 98 points

  • James Suckling - 98 points

  • Vinous - 95 points

  • Wine Spectator - 94 points

Food Pairing

Suggested pairings include beef rib, ossobucco, slow cooked lamb shanks with a rich wine jus, or barbecued and smoked prime-cut red meats, such as A5 Wagyu beef.

title: Carruades De Lafite 2022
bodyHtml:
Carruades De Lafite is the second wine of the legendary Château Lafite Rothschild, located in the Pauillac appellation of Bordeaux’s Left Bank. Under the ownership of Domaines Barons de Rothschild (Lafite), the estate upholds centuries-old traditions and a reputation for precision and elegance in winemaking. The vineyard's gravel-rich terroir contributes to the wine’s refined structure and age-worthiness.

This 2022 vintage displays a deep ruby hue. The nose is expressive, revealing layers of blackcurrant, violet, graphite, and cedar. On the palate, it offers a medium to full body with ripe black fruits, fine-grained tannins, and a silky texture.

Accolades

  • James Suckling - 96 Points

  • Wine Advocate - 92 Points

  • Vinous - 90+ Points

Food Pairing

Ideal with rosemary-lamb chops, mushroom risotto, or grilled duck breast. This pairing highlights the wine’s depth and character.

title: Domaine Alain Chavy Puligny Montrachet 'Les Folatieres' Premier Cru 2023
bodyHtml:
Produced in France within the Puligny Montrachet appellation of the Côte de Beaune, this 100% Chardonnay is sourced from one of the most prestigious Premier Cru vineyards in the region. Alain Chavy established his eponymous domaine in 2003 after a division of his family's long-standing estate, continuing a winemaking heritage that dates back to the 1970s. The winery is celebrated for a philosophy of restraint, utilizing minimal bâtonnage and a careful balance of new and neutral French oak to ensure the authentic minerality of the terroir remains the focal point.

Wine Description

This Premier Cru presents a brilliant yellow hue and a highly expressive nose featuring intense citrus, orchard fruits, and white peach, complemented by delicate acacia flower and a signature smoky reduction. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied and sophisticated, offering a creamy, mealy texture that is balanced by a powerful mineral backbone and vibrant acidity. The finish is exceptionally long and refined, showing nuances of toasted nuts and vanilla from 12 months of aging in French oak.

Food Pairing

The wine’s rich texture and crystalline minerality make it an excellent partner for elegant seafood dishes, such as grilled sea bass, lobster with fennel, or scallops snackées. It also pairs beautifully with poultry in cream-based sauces, such as traditional Poulet de Bresse, or earthy starters like sweetbread terrine.

title: Chateau Mouton Rothschild 2018
bodyHtml:
Chateau Mouton Rothschild 2018 originates from France, within the prestigious Pauillac appellation of the Médoc region in Bordeaux. Acquired by Baron Nathaniel de Rothschild in 1853, the estate's modern era was defined by Baron Philippe de Rothschild, who famously lobbied for its elevation to First Growth (Premier Cru Classé) status in 1973—the only such change ever made to the 1855 classification. The winery follows a philosophy of winemaking as an art form, a tradition highlighted since 1945 by commissioning a different famous artist to design the label for each vintage; for 2018, the label features 'square word calligraphy' by Chinese artist Xu Bing.

Wine Description

This vintage displays an intense, deep black or garnet-purple colour with a violet hue. The aromatic profile is complex and flamboyant, featuring rich notes of blackcurrant, wild strawberry, and cassis layered with secondary scents of nutmeg, mint, liquorice, and cigar box. On the palate, it is full bodied and muscular, described as being 'built like a brick house' with super-firm, grainy tannins and a vibrant freshness that supports dense black fruit and mineral undertones. The finish is exceptionally long and refined, showing great balance between fruit and toasty oak. The varietal composition for 2018 is 86% Cabernet Sauvignon, 12% Merlot, and 2% Cabernet Franc. It has an ABV of 13.8% and is matured for 18 to 22 months in 100% new French oak barrels. While the estate employs meticulous sustainable practices, it is not officially certified as organic.

Food Pairing

The immense tannic power and aromatic wealth of this First Growth make it an ideal match for rich, high-quality meat dishes. Suggested pairings include grilled ribeye steak, roasted rack of lamb with herbs, and prime rib. It also complements wild game such as venison or wild boar, as well as sophisticated dishes featuring truffles. For a cheese course, it pairs best with aged hard varieties like Comté, Parmesan, or mature Cheddar.

Vintage Quality

The 2018 vintage in Pauillac was a year of extremes, starting with heavy winter rains followed by a glorious, hot, and dry summer that allowed the grapes to achieve optimal phenolic maturity. These conditions resulted in small, concentrated berries with high sugar and tannin levels. The winemaking team successfully adapted to these contrasts to produce a wine of 'battleship' proportions that possesses both formidable power and poised elegance.

title: Chateau Leoville Poyferre 2008
bodyHtml:
Due to a division of the large Leoville estate, Chateau Leoville Poyferre was created in 1840 and included as a Second Growth in the famous 1855 Classification. In 1920, the Cuvelier family purchased the estate and Didier Cuvelier has been in charge since 1979.

Major investments were made to bring out the best in the vineyards, and the cellars were also renovated. In 1994, noted consulting oenologist Michel Rolland began to offer his precious winemaking advice. The final blend is made after many careful tastings. 

94 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

One of the finest over-achieving efforts in this vintage as well as a “best buy” for a top-flight St.-Julien, this 2008 is an irresistible success. It reveals an opaque ruby/purple color, lots of unctuosity and a boatload of sweet cassis and black cherry fruit intertwined with notions of licorice, smoke and oak.

94 Points - Wine Enthusiast

Generous and ripe, obviously extracted, this is a wine that is packed with tannins sharpened with black fruits. Spice, wood and acidity add to the depth of flavor.

93 Points - James Suckling

I am impressed with the fruit and velvety tannins. Full and deliciously fruity with soft tannins and rich fruit. Blueberry. Open and gorgeous.

91 Points - Wine Spectator

Very direct, with black currant and fig paste jumping out and driving all the way through the lightly muscular finish, where extra iron, espresso and charcoal notes fill in. An iron edge lingers.

title: Cain Five 2018 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
The Cain Vineyard site is truly spectacular, cradled in a bowl overlooking St. Helena from the top of the Spring Mountain District. In 1980, Joyce and Jerry Cain purchased part of the McCormick Ranch, a homestead dating back to the 1840's. The Cains were in search of a unique mountain property where they could realize their dream of planting the five classical Bordeaux varietals from which to draw one ideally structured wine, which would result as a blend of all five varieties.

Cain Five shows both elegance and grace. The nose gives classic Cain Vineyard aromas of bramble, citrus, and tar. This wine is refreshing on the palate with a nice warmth, soft tannins, and a long finish. It is easy to enjoy now, while also promising a long life ahead.

title: Domaine Dujac Clos Saint Denis Grand Cru 2023
bodyHtml:
Louis Seysses, biscuit manufacturer and gastronome, had a taste for good food and fine wines. His son Jacques Seysses quickly came to share his father's passion, and he decided he would not only like to drink the wine but make it as well.

Possibly Jacques' greatest contribution to the Domaine has been to instill his desire to search for new ways to improve the wine and the way wine is made. Though his vinification style looks relatively simple and non interventionist, it is result of much thought and experimentation. The style of wines must be elegance and finesse, with supple and well integrated tannins. The search is for equilibrium, harmony, length and complexity! 

Made from Pinot Noir grapes frown on clay and limestone soils. Fermented in stainless steel tanks, using naturally occurring yeast. The vines have been organically farmed since 2001.

Upon opening, this wine is characterized by lavish fruit but has the capability of aging quite well.

94+ Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2021 Clos Saint-Denis Grand Cru is brilliant, wafting from the glass with aromas of sweet red berries, summer fruit compote, sweet spices, licorice, peony and coniferous forest floor. Full-bodied, ample and layered, it's fleshy and textural, its satiny attack segueing into a deep, seamless mid-palate and a perfumed, penetrating finish.

title: Domaine Patrick Javillier Meursault Cuvee Tete de Murger 2020
bodyHtml:
Meursault Cuvee "Tete de Murger" comes from the marriage of two Climates: Meursault Les Casse-Tetes, located on the hillside of Meursault, and Meursault Les Murgers de Monthelie, located on the hillside of Volnay.

A fine, fruity palate with notes of honey and sublte hints of flowers and vanilla; the initial vigour and mineral sensations from the Casse-Tete plot combines well with the fullness and length in the mouth from the Les Murgers de Monthelie plot, giving a harmonious wine with a prolonged finish and expressing the nature of the land from which it originates.

title: Solaia 2015 (by Tenuta Tignanello)
bodyHtml:
Solaia is an intense ruby red in color with purple highlights. The nose offers powerful notes of plum jam and berry fruit. Perfectly integrated sensations of chocolate and licorice give way on the finish to hints of fresh mint. Harmonious on the palatewith excellent structure and silky tannins, the wine concludes with an extremely long finish and lingering aftertaste.

100 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

With the 2015 vintage, Solaia is liquid sunshine not just in name but also in fact. The bouquet is immediately soft and sensual with dark fruit, spice and sweet tobacco. The mouthfeel shows intensity and power, but you don't get any heavy residue from the dry extract (measured at 33 grams per liter). Indeed, the wine feels glossy, tonic and fresh. It is composed of mostly Cabernet Sauvignon with Sangiovese and a tiny part Cabernet Franc. There is a bit of crunch or snap that comes thanks to the more acidity-prone Sangiovese grape (the wine measures 3.5 in pH). Finally, the tannins are beautifully sweet and ripe. This wine is meticulously executed, and the 2015 vintage lives up to an ideal of what we imagine Solaia to be.

100 Points - James Suckling

The nose to this Solaia is truly phenomenal with currants, blackberries, roses and violets. So perfumed. Full-bodied and everything is in check and harmony with polished tannins that last for minutes. Purity and focus. Is it the greatest Solaia ever?

98 Points - Wine Spectator 

98 Points - Wine Enthusiast

98 Points - Wine & Spirits

title: Bodegas y Vinedos Pintia 2021 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
This exceptional red wine originates from Spain, crafted in the Castilla y Leon region within the Toro subregion. Bodegas y Vinedos Pintia is a modern, highly expressive project established by the legendary Tempos Vega Sicilia group. The winery operates on a philosophy of capturing the extreme, rugged terroir of Toro while imparting the signature elegance, precision, and balance for which the Vega Sicilia family is globally renowned.

Wine Description

In the glass, this wine showcases an intensely deep purple colour with a brilliant sheen. The nose is precise and complex, unfurling pure aromas of blackberry, raspberry, and dark plum alongside nuanced layers of mint, cedar, cocoa, and roasted spices. On the palate, it delivers a full bodied and opulent structure balanced by a striking, lively freshness and a compact, layered texture.

title: Chateau Beychevelle 2020
bodyHtml:
Chateau Beychevelle is a prestigious Fourth Growth estate located in the Saint Julien appellation of Bordeaux, France. Historically known as the 'Versailles of the Médoc', the estate dates back to the 17th century and is currently co owned by the Castel and Suntory groups. The winemaking philosophy centers on a meticulous balance of tradition and innovation, utilizing a state of the art gravity-fed cellar to express the elegance and unique maritime-influenced terroir of the region.

Wine Description

The 2020 vintage presents a dense, dark purple colour with vibrant black reflections. The nose is seductive and exotic, leaping with aromas of blackcurrant, juicy black plums, and blackberries mingled with darker notes of chocolate, pencil shavings, and violet. On the palate, the wine is muscular and concentrated yet remarkably silky, featuring a core of ripe fruit framed by fine grained, powdery tannins.

Accolades

  • Wine Spectator - 94 points

  • Vinous - 96 points

  • Decanter - 94 points

  • Robert Parker - 93+ points

  • James Suckling - 94 points

Food Pairing

The wine's deep structure and dark fruit profile pair exceptionally well with roasted lamb chops or a classic steak Diane. For a more earthy experience, consider dishes featuring wild mushrooms or savory herbs like rosemary and thyme.

title: Chateau Clos l'Eglise 2021
bodyHtml: It is an incredible charmer, evoking immediate pleasure and certain seduction. When it reveals its elegance, its roundness, its opulence it pays tribute to its origins, rare and inimitable. Clos l’Eglise is a philanthropist who leaves behind, on meeting, the persistent memory of a tender emotion.  This wine is really gorgeous and sexy with super integrated tannins, juicy rich fruit and a bright acidity. It gives an impression of being seamless on the palate.

title: Dugat Py Gevrey Chambertin Vieilles Vignes 2023
bodyHtml:
Produced in France, this exceptional red wine hails from the Gevrey Chambertin appellation within the Côte de Nuits subregion of Burgundy. Domaine Dugat Py is a historic estate dating back to the 17th century, now managed by thirteenth-generation winemaker Loïc Dugat. The winery is renowned for its treasure trove of old vines—averaging 70 years of age—and a winemaking philosophy that has evolved toward greater precision, nuance, and terroir expression.

Wine Description

Gevrey Chambertin Vieilles Vignes is a muscular and concentrated expression of Pinot Noir, displaying a dark fruit profile with light spicy notes and a hint of bay leaf on the nose. On the palate, it is dense and earthy with a burly, 'grunty' grip and a touch of licorice on the finish. This cuvée, sourced from eight parcels with the oldest vines planted in 1915, offers a smooth, richly rippling texture and a savory complexity.

Food Pairing

The wine's savory profile and robust structure make it an ideal companion for rich, gamey dishes such as roast duck, goose, or a classic beef bourguignon. It also pairs beautifully with earthy flavors like wild mushroom risotto or a well-aged Comté cheese.

title: Domaine Harmand Geoffroy Gevrey Chambertin 'Clos Prieur' 2019
bodyHtml:
Domaine Harmand Geoffroy, located in the historic village of Gevrey Chambertin in Burgundy's Côte de Nuits, is a family-run estate that has spent generations refining its craft. With deep respect for tradition and a focus on low-intervention winemaking, the domaine captures the distinct personalities of its terroirs. 'Clos Prieur' is a well-regarded climat situated just below the Premier Cru tier, known for producing wines that combine structure with a refined elegance.

Wine Description
The 2019 'Clos Prieur' displays a bright ruby colour, opening with expressive aromas of red cherries, wild strawberries, and blackcurrants, intertwined with hints of rose petals, damp earth, and subtle spice. The palate is medium-bodied and graceful, offering juicy red fruit flavours, a touch of savoury herbs, and delicate minerality. Polished tannins and fresh acidity provide balance and length, leading to a silky, persistent finish.
