Made entirely from Pinot Noir, this wine is charming in its youth but will evolve beautifully through 2032.

Accolades
Vinous - 90 points.

Food Pairing
This elegant Gevrey Chambertin pairs wonderfully with duck confit, pork tenderloin with sage, or roasted root vegetables. These dishes complement the wine's supple texture and aromatic complexity, creating an unforgettable dining experience.

Vintage Quality
The 2019 vintage in Gevrey Chambertin was marked by warm, dry conditions, resulting in concentrated, ripe fruit and structured wines. Careful vineyard management preserved freshness, allowing wines like 'Clos Prieur' to express both richness and finesse.

title: Chateau Valandraud 2019
bodyHtml:
98+ Points - Wine Enthusiast

This is a dense and luscious wine, the best yet from this estate. Its great structure and tannins show a style that is powerful but all within. This is a magnificent vintage from this Premier Grand Cru Classe estate and fully deserves to be aged for many years.

99 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

The local bad boy of Bordeaux, Jean-Luc Thunevin, continues to fashion truly brilliant wines, and his 2019 is no exception. Based largely on Merlot with a small amount of Cabernet Franc and Cabernet Sauvignon, the 2019 Château Valandraud is a deep purple-hued beauty offering up a kaleidoscope-like bouquet of black and blue fruits, scorched earth, chocolate, gravelly earth, spicy oak, and sappy flowers. Deep, rich, full-bodied, and wonderfully concentrated, it has insane purity of fruit, brilliant tannins, a stacked mid-palate, and just has everything in the right places. It's up with the top wines of the vintage and a tour de force that readers should snatch up. It shows a very different style than the sexier 2018, but it's every bit as good. It needs 4-5 years of bottle age and will evolve for 2-3 decades. 

98 Points - James Suckling

Vivid and focused with brightness and clarity of fruit. Dried flowers, too. Full-bodied with layers of fine, soft tannins that spread across the palate and show class and refinement. It goes on for minutes. A beautiful bottle. Best from 2027, but so attractive already.

96 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Rich and dramatic, the 2019 Valandraud bursts with aromas of berry fruit, plums and licorice, framed by a lavish but far from exaggerated application of creamy new oak. Full-bodied, fleshy and sensual, it's broad and enveloping, its lavish core of fruit framed by ripe, polished tannins and succulent balancing acids. Seamless and integrated despite its ripe, hedonistic style, this has turned out beautifully and has the balance to perform well for at least two decades, even if there's no youthful asperity to preclude near-term enjoyment. 

95 Points - Wine Spectator

Richly textured, featuring cashmere-like waves of dark plum, cassis and blackberry compote flavours that glide through and are laced with light violet, anise and black tea notes. The rumble of tannins can be heard on the finish, but for the vintage, this is extremely suave in the end. Merlot, Cabernet Franc and Cabernet Sauvignon.

title: Le Chiuse Brunello di Montalcino Riserva 'DieciAnni' 2012
bodyHtml:
Very intense, brilliant and deep ruby red with garnet and cherry hues. The bouquet is wide, intense with scents of ripe cherry, tobacco, leather and licorice. Officinal herbs, spicy and mineral notes increase the complexity of this wine. Clean, full, warm, sapid, harmonic and austere made of very good body, aromatic sensation of jam and spices lasts long in the mouth.

Recommended with red meat, roasts, game, stew, mature cheeses and all those dishes which have great sapidity.

98 Points - Wine Enthusiast

Aged for 10 years this compelling red opens with classic Sangiovese aromas of underbrush new leather ripe wild berries and crushed botanical herbs. Showing the depth and complexity of age combined with the freshness of youth the elegantly structured palate features ripe black cherry orange zest licorice and tobacco framed in silky tannins. Fresh acidity keeps it balanced. Drink through 2037.

97 Points - Wine Spectator

This red is beginning to find its sweet spot revealing mushroom leather fading cherry berry earth and mineral aromas and flavors. Still firm with fine equilibrium and an expansive finish that has freshness and grip. Begs for braised beef Bolognese or wild boar ragu. Drink now through 2037.

97 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Sangiovese can age with grace and care and that's what this wine teaches us. Aromas of wild berry dried current red orange earth and rusty nail converge with precision. The wine's color is vibrant and bright despite the nearly 10 years of age and the mouthfeel is light and radiant in intensity. There is a lot of aspiration in this wine and I think you'll be inspired.

96 Points - James Suckling

Here's a late-release Brunello that's showing some wonderful age and beauty. 2012 was a hot year and made rather jammy wines but this has come together beautifully with pure cherry and berry aromas and flavors as well as floral undertones and hints of forest floor. It's long and wonderfully soft and fruity at the end. From organically grown grapes. Drink now or hold.

95 Points - Vinous 

The 2012 Brunello di Montalcino Riserva Dieci Anni is breathtaking pulling you close to the glass with a dark rich display of crushed autumn leaves dried roses and black cherries. This is texturally stunning as well velvety yet somehow lifted offering exotic spices tart berries plums and inner florals that seem to cascade across the senses. The palate aches with youthful tension through the long and almost chewy finale as nuances of licorice and balsam herbs slowly fade. The 2012 leaves a staining of concentration upon the palate. What a gorgeous wine!

title: Caparzo Brunello di Montalcino Riserva 2015
bodyHtml:
The origins of the place named Caparzo are still unknown. According to some people, the name is derived, as shown by ancient maps, from Ca' Pazzo; according to others, the term should derive from the Latin Caput Arsum, indicating "a place touched by the sun.”

In 1998, 30 years after the first rows of vines were planted, the farm estate came to a turning point when Elisabetta Gnudi Angelini purchased Caparzo. With the help of her son, Igino, and daughter, Alessandra, she immediately carried out her objective: combining tradition with innovation to create a high-quality wine that is the expression of an excellent territory.

Ruby and tends towards garnet with age. The nose is penetrating, ample, and very complex, with echoes of wild berry fruit. The palate is dry, warm, solid, harmonious, combining delicacy and austerity, and persistent.

This wine is an excellent pairing with roasts, spit-roasted meats, grilled meats, game, braised meats, and aged cheeses.

96 Points - Wine Enthusiast

Underbrush rose, new leather and camphor aromas mingle with wild berries in this fragrant, classy red. Linear and elegantly structured, the focused palate delivers juicy red cherry, spiced cranberry, star anise and cinnamon set against firm, refined tannins. Fresh acidity keeps it balanced. Drink 2023–2030.

95 Points - James Suckling

A wine with purity and integration, offering black cherry, blueberry and orange-peel aromas and flavours. Hot stone, too. Full-bodied and very tight with integrated tannins that go on. Needs time to show it all.

94 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

First produced in 1980, the Riserva is only produced in great vintages from fruit selected by winemaker Massimo Bracalente. The 2015 Brunello Di Montalcino Riserva offers sweet red cherry, violets, sage, and cedar aromatics. The palate is ripe and inviting, with pure red fruits, clove, and tomato leaf followed by an unfolding but fine tannic grip. The sunniness of the vintage is present, but there is clarity and purity of fruit which will make for a pleasurable wine to drink with some time. Enjoy over the next 20 years.

94 Points - Wine Spectator

This red is opulent and bursting with cherry, and raspberry, rose and earth flavours and an underlying spiciness from the new oak. Harmonious and long, refined tannins detail the finish. Best from 2023 through 2043.

title: Luciano Sandrone Barolo 'Aleste' 2020
bodyHtml: Founded in 1978 by Luciano Sandrone, this family-owned winery is situated in the heart of Italy's Piedmont region. Renowned for producing exceptional Barolo wines, the estate combines traditional winemaking techniques with modern innovations to craft wines that express the unique terroir of their vineyards. The 'Aleste' Barolo is named in honor of Luciano's grandchildren, Alessia and Stefano, reflecting the family's dedication to winemaking across generations.

title: Chateau Lynch Bages 2022
bodyHtml:
Hailing from France, Chateau Lynch Bages is located in the famed Pauillac appellation within the Bordeaux region. This historic estate dates back to the 18th century and is currently owned by the Cazes family, renowned for their dedication to quality and innovation. The vineyard is celebrated for its deep gravel soils and meticulous vineyard management, which together underpin its reputation for producing powerful yet refined wines.

Wine Description

The 2022 Lynch Bages presents a deep garnet-purple hue. On the nose, it opens with expressive aromas of blackcurrants, ripe blackberries, and cassis, interwoven with hints of cedar, pencil shavings, and violets. The palate is full-bodied and concentrated, delivering layers of dark fruits, tobacco, and subtle graphite notes. Firm, polished tannins provide structure, balanced by vibrant acidity that carries through to a long, savoury finish.

Accolades

  • James Suckling - 98 Points : A terrific Lynch from a hot vintage with blackcurrants, mint, dried lavender, graphite and thyme on the nose and palate. Medium- to full-bodied, it shows fantastic tannins with a lovely texture that reminds me of cashmere, becoming slightly chewy in the finish. Give this four to five years of bottle age.

  • Jeb Dunnuck - 99 Points: The 2022 Château Lynch-Bages is based on 66% Cabernet Sauvignon, 28% Merlot, and 3% each of Cabernet Franc and Petit Verdot. Its inky purple hue is followed by a sensational Pauillac that has a blockbuster (and classic Lynch-Bages) style in its darker currants, smoke tobacco, lead pencil, and crushed stone-driven aromatics. These carry to a full-bodied, powerful, massively concentrated 2022 that has a dense, layered mid-palate, velvety tannins, flawless balance, and a rare mix of power and elegance. This is a château that’s clearly firing on all cylinders, and this magical beauty will need a decade (or more) to hit the early stages of its prime drinking window. Don't miss it!

Food Pairing

Pair this Pauillac classic with grilled lamb chops, roast beef, or aged cheddar to accentuate its bold structure and layered complexity. Together, they create an unforgettable dining experience.

title: Ad Vivum Cabernet Sauvignon 2018
bodyHtml:
Introduction

This red wine is from the United States, specifically from the Yountville subregion of Napa Valley, California. Ad Vivum is owned by winemaker Chris Phelps, whose storied career includes crafting 12 vintages at Dominus Estate and eight at Caymus Vineyards. The winery operates with a philosophy of creating 'New World wines with an Old World sensibility', sourcing exclusively from the meticulously farmed Sleeping Lady Vineyard situated on the western flanks of the Mayacamas Mountains.

Wine Description

The 2018 Ad Vivum Cabernet Sauvignon is deep garnet-purple in colour with a violet edge. The exuberant nose offers aromas of blackcurrant jelly, warm plums, and black raspberries, accented by notes of violet, mocha, tobacco, and anise. On the palate, it is full bodied and statuesque, displaying lush layers of blackberry and blueberry fruit supported by firm, ripe, and grainy tannins. The wine exhibits a tight-knit structure with lively acidity and a long finish marked by mineral and chalky undertones. This 100% Cabernet Sauvignon was aged for 20 months in French oak (75% new) and has an ABV of 14.5%. While it is beginning to open, the optimal drinking window extends from 2024 through 2053.

Accolades

  • Decanter - 98 points

  • Wine Advocate - 97+ points

  • Vinous - 97 points

  • Wine Independent - 97 points

  • Wine Enthusiast - 96 points

  • James Suckling - 95 points

  • Jeb Dunnuck - 95+ points

  • Wine Spectator - 92 points

Food Pairing

The robust structure and intense fruit profile of this wine pair exceptionally well with rich red meat dishes such as grilled ribeye steak, braised short ribs, or beef galbi. Its herbal and earthy nuances also complement venison curry or mushroom risotto. For a cheese course, aged varieties like Gouda, Manchego, or Comté are ideal selections.

Vintage Quality

The 2018 vintage in Napa Valley is considered exceptional, characterized by a long and steady growing season without extreme heat spikes. Moderate temperatures through the summer and autumn allowed the grapes to achieve full phenolic ripeness and deep colour while maintaining vibrant acidity.

title: Domaine Michel Gros Chambolle Musigny 2022
bodyHtml:
Chambolle-Musigny, often described as the most feminine and aromatic of Burgundy's communes, is distinguished by its limestone-rich soils and optimal exposure. These natural advantages, combined with Michel Gros' detailed approach to viticulture and winemaking, result in a wine that exemplifies the sophisticated charm of premium Burgundian Pinot Noir.

The wine presents with a brilliant ruby hue in the glass, offering immediate visual evidence of its pedigree. The nose is remarkably expressive, unveiling delicate layers of red berries, violet petals, and subtle Asian spices. With aeration, deeper notes of wild strawberry and forest floor emerge, creating an increasingly complex aromatic profile that is quintessentially Chambolle.

On the palate, this wine demonstrates the hallmark silky texture and refined structure that have made Chambolle-Musigny's reputation. Pure, focused flavors of red cherries and wild raspberries are complemented by subtle hints of rose petal and mineral nuances. The tannins are remarkably fine-grained and elegant, providing just enough structure to frame the wine's generous fruit while maintaining its characteristic ethereal quality. The finish is persistent and harmonious, with waves of subtle spice and mineral notes that continue to evolve.

91+ Points - Vinous

The 2022 Chambolle-Musigny Village offers one of my favorite aromatics amongst the Domaine's wines: black cherries, wild strawberries, sous-bois and light tobacco. The palate is smooth with filigree tannins, well-judged acidity, and a caressing and Vosne-like finish with plenty of allure. Very persistent, this Chambolle punches well above its weight.

title: Vincent Latour Meursault 'Les Grands Charrons' 2022
bodyHtml:
Originating from France in the Burgundy region, specifically within the Meursault appellation in the Cote de Beaune, Domaine Vincent Latour Meursault 'Les Grands Charrons' 2022 represents a rich, precise, and cellaring grade expression of classic Chardonnay. Produced by Domaine Vincent Latour under the direction of Vincent Latour, who took over his family estate in 1998, the domain is celebrated for combining traditional Burgundian technique with modern cellaring precision. Sourced from Les Grands Charrons, one of Meursault's most highly regarded village lieu-dit parcels featuring vines aged between 25 and 60 years planted on deep Jurassic limestone and clay soils, the winemaking philosophy emphasizes gentle pneumatic pressing, native yeast fermentation, aging on fine lees for 12 months in oak casks followed by 4 to 6 months in stainless steel tanks, and no batonnage (lees stirring) to guarantee crisp mineral tension, crystalline purity, and authentic terroir expression.

Wine Description

The wine presents a luminous, clear golden yellow colour with brilliant silver highlights along the rim. An expressive, complex bouquet opens with inviting aromas of ripe yellow apple, white peach, lemon curd, and lime blossom, interwoven with leesy richness, delicate floral notes, toasted hazelnut, vanilla, and a fine stone-dust mineral undertone. On the palate, it is medium-to-full bodied, dense, and creamy yet finely balanced by a vibrant, mouthwatering core of natural acidity. Framed by a satiny texture, subtle baking spice, and a taut, stony structure, it concludes with a long, energetic finish marked by lingering citrus zest, white peach, and persistent limestone minerality. Composed of 100% Chardonnay, this 2022 release offers an optimal drinking window of 2027–2035+. Stylistically, it captures classic Meursault richness and generous texture while maintaining exquisite mineral focus and freshness.

title: Dunn Vineyards Cabernet Sauvignon Howell Mountain 2019 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
#6 Wine Spectator Top 100 of 2023

High atop Howell Mountain, nestled among 150-year-old fir trees, is Dunn Vineyards. Since 1979 the Dunn's have been producing Cabernet Sauvignon. Dunn's signature wine contains only fruit farmed in their vineyards on Howell Mountain.

98 Points - Vinous

The 2019 Cabernet Sauvignon Howell Mountain is outrageously beautiful. A wine of extraordinary purity, the 2019 dazzles right out of the gate. The tannins are nearly silky for a young Howell Mountain Cabernet. Red/purplish fruit, lavender, spice, rose petal and pomegranate all build in this sumptuous, explosive Cabernet Sauvignon.

98 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

Checking in at 13.9% alcohol and revealing a deep purple hue as well as incredible aromatics of pure cr me de cassis, scorched earth, graphite, bouquet garni, and hints of plum, it hits the palate with full-bodied richness carrying ultra-fine tannins, a flawless sense of balance and purity, and incredible length. 

96 Points - Wine Spectator

Lushly fruited, this sends waves of crushed plum, boysenberry compote and blackberry paste out from the core, with a strong undercurrent of cast iron and smoldering tobacco to boot. Grippy and dense, but with a sense of polish and a note of purity in the guise of a pretty violet echo.

title: Arkenstone Estate Red Howell Mountain 2017
bodyHtml: 94 Points Jeb Dunnuck... Deeper coloured, the 2017 Arkenstone Estate Red offers a stunning bouquet of blackcurrants, dark chocolate, graphite and lead pencil shavings. This rich, powerful, concentrated wine has ripe tannins, a stacked mid-palate and a great, great finish. It's going to need 4-5 years of cellaring but will be long lived. The blend is 86% Cabernet Sauvignon, 9% Cabernet Franc, and the balance Malbec and Merlot, all aged 22 months in new barrels.

title: Duckhorn Merlot Three Palms 2018 - 3 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
Introduction

This red wine originates from the United States, specifically from the Calistoga subregion of the Napa Valley in California. Founded in 1976 by Dan and Margaret Duckhorn, Duckhorn Vineyards was a pioneer in North America for treating Merlot as a premium standalone varietal rather than just a blending grape. The Three Palms Vineyard, named for the three iconic palm trees that stand sentinel over its gravelly soils, is widely considered one of the finest sites for Merlot in the New World. The winery's philosophy is rooted in a commitment to quality and consistency, utilizing small lot fermentation and French oak aging to craft wines of remarkable depth and elegance.

Wine Description

Duckhorn Merlot Three Palms displays a beautiful garnet or deep ruby hue. The nose is alluring and complex, offering aromas of huckleberry, fig jam, and cranberry layered with notes of cocoa, rose petals, and spiced plum. On the palate, the wine is elegantly full bodied and velvety, featuring intense flavours of blackberry, cherry, and red licorice accented by molasses and a distinct wet slate minerality. It is characterized by a sumptuous structure, lively acidity, and fine, graceful tannins that lead to a lush and lingering finish. This blend consists of 87% Merlot, 11% Cabernet Sauvignon, 1% Malbec, and 1% Cabernet Franc, with an ABV of 14.5%. While the estate follows meticulous sustainable practices, this bottling is not certified organic. The optimal drinking window is from 2026 through 2036, though its concentration suggests it can be enjoyed through 2045+.

title: Lokoya Cabernet Sauvignon Mount Veeder 2019
bodyHtml:
Established in 1995, Lokoya is a collection of four distinct Cabernet Sauvignons from four of Napa Valley’s most celebrated mountain appellations: Mount Veeder, Howell Mountain, Spring Mountain and Diamond Mountain. These limited-production wines are 100% Cabernet Sauvignon, fermented with native yeast, and bottled unfined and unfiltered, resulting in the purest expression of place.

This wine displays defining characteristics of violets and blue fruit with powerful tannins and exceptional aging potential.

100 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

Cassis, blueberry liqueur, lead pencil shavings, crushed stone, and graphite notes all define the nose, and it hits the palate with incredible power and opulence, yet stays pure, flawlessly balanced, and has a finish that won't quit. This is as brilliant as Cabernet gets, and Carpenter is clearly playing with the best in the business. 

99 Points - James Suckling

Blackcurrant and graphite in a big way in the nose. Some asphalt and sweet tobacco, too. Full-bodied with a dense, velvety texture. Shows suppleness for such a big wine, with luxurious sensibility. Such fabulous length. 

98 Points - Decanter

Powerfully aromatic black fruits, dried herbs, dark-roast coffee beans, toasty oak and dried flowers. Full-throttle, structured and dense, with firm, elongated tannins and compact black-toned fruits, scorched earth, iron shavings and crushed cocoa nibs. A long finish of brandied spiced cherries.

96 Points - Wine Spectator

96 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

title: Chateau Angludet 2003 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
Home to the Sichel family since 1961, Chateau Angludet is one of the oldest properties in the Medoc, with a history which goes back to the twelfth century. It is named after Bertrand d'Angludet, a knight and lord of the noble residence which stood on this site in 1150.

Since 1758, the vineyard of Chateau Angludet has retained a configuration down the centuries which is very close to the original, 93 percent of the current surface area having nurtured vines for more than 250 years – exceptional continuity for a vineyard.

Delicacy and charm often seem to be the hallmarks of Angludet—positive virtues in a world full of alcoholic, powerful wines. This 2003 has perhaps more tannins than usual from small berries, but it retains the property's elegance.

title: Brovia Barolo Villero 2019
bodyHtml:
Originating from Italy, within the renowned Piedmont region and the prestigious Castiglione Falletto subregion, this outstanding expression represents the peak of Nebbiolo. Azienda Agricola Brovia was established in 1863 and has maintained a rich history of organic farming, family craftsmanship, and minimal intervention in winemaking. The estate's philosophy focuses on traditional methods that allow the unique character of single-vineyard terroirs like Villero to express their natural depth and elegance without compromise.

Wine Description

Elegantly structured and delicious, this fragrant red has enticing scents of ripe forest berries, iris, truffle and balsamic whiffs of camphor. Combining body and finesse, the savory, focused palate delivers juicy Marasca cherry, crushed raspberry and baking spice before an almost salty finish. Tightly knit, fine-grained tannins provide support while fresh acidity keeps it well-balanced. 

Accolades

  • Wine Advocate - 96 points.

  • James Suckling - 95 points.

Food Pairing

This wine pairs superbly with classic Piedmontese dishes, such as slow-braised beef, roasted wild boar, truffle-infused tagliolini, and aged hard cheeses like Parmigiano-Reggiano or Castelmagno.

title: Caparzo Brunello di Montalcino Riserva 2016
bodyHtml: Caparzo's Brunello di Montalcino Riserva is only produced in the finest vintages, from grapes selected personally by winemaker Massimo Bracalente. The grapes are in part from from vineyards located in the northern part of the Montalcino Appellation, at an elevation of 220 meters above sea level, and in part from vineyards south of Montalcino, at an elevation of 270 meters. In both cases the vineyards are on sandy-stony south-southeast facing Pliocene terrains. The Riserva begins to show its best several years after bottling. Produced in limited quantities, the Riserva is destined to especially passionate, attentive wine lovers. A classic, complete Riserva able to awaken unique sensations in the most expert palates. The first Caparzo Riserva Brunello di Montalcino DOCG was produced in 1980. The wine has the capacity to age for up to 40 years.

title: Chateau Ausone 2021
bodyHtml:
Chateau Ausone 2021 is a red wine from the Saint Emilion Grand Cru appellation in the Libournais region of Bordeaux, France. Perched on the limestone slopes of the Roc Blancan, the estate has been managed by the Vauthier family since 1690, with Alain and his daughter Pauline currently representing the eleventh generation of winemakers. The winery follows a philosophy of discretion and meticulous manual labour, utilizing organic and biodynamic principles to allow the concentrated minerality of its ancient limestone terroir to express itself genuinely.

Wine Description

This vintage possesses a deep crimson or medium-bodied plum colour with purple tinges. The nose is intensely aromatic and complex, featuring layers of wild blueberries, raspberries, and black cherries mingled with floral touches of violet, rose petals, and peony. On the palate, the wine is medium to full-bodied, described as silky and graceful with a 'shy sense of power' and a concentrated core of juicy fruit. Stylistically, it is lauded for its breathtaking precision, vibrant acidity, and ultra-refined tannins that provide a powdery finish with mineral notes of wet stone, graphite, and white pepper. The varietal composition is a blend of 65% Cabernet Franc and 35% Merlot. The optimal drinking window for this vintage is projected between 2028 and 2059.

Accolades

  • James Suckling – 97 points

  • Decanter – 95 points

  • Robert Parker Wine Advocate – 94–96 points

title: Il Poggione Brunello di Montalcino Riserva Vigna Paganelli 2015
bodyHtml:
One of Tuscany's most highly regarded wineries, Tenuta Il Poggione makes compelling wines for collectors and everyday drinkers alike. Intense ruby red in appearance. Layered aromas of red fruit, savoury spices and leather notes. The tannins are silky, and the fruit comes back in multiple layers. Its long finish confirms that this wine is ready to drink now but can be enjoyed for 20 years or more.

97 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate    

This single-vineyard Riserva delivers a generous, abundant and determined personality. The 2015 Brunello di Montalcino Riserva Vigna Paganelli benefits from a warm, sun-soaked microclimate shielded from cold winter winds. You can taste the grapes' excellent health thanks to the unmistakable aromas of black cherry, plum, tar, campfire ash and chalky mineral. 

95 Points - Jeb Dunnuck    

Vigna Paganelli is the estate's oldest vineyard, planted in 1964, and the wine was aged for over 40 months in large French oak of various sizes. The 2015 Vigna Paganelli Riserva is rich with cola aromatics, liquorice, and black cherry. There is a concentrated core of fruit with vanilla and cedar. The structure is persistent with grippy tannins and acidity that perseveres through the darkness of the fruit. This is an elegant wine that will need time to unravel and soften.

95 Points - Wine Spectator    

This red is subtle and laced with cherry, plum and floral notes, backed by vibrant acidity. Earth and tobacco accents add depth. It took a few moments of aeration to shake off the cobwebs, and this isn't an expressive style, but it has its appeal. It will need time to absorb the substantial tannins.

93 Points - Wine Enthusiast   

Baked plum, new leather, camphor, and scorched earth aromas waft out of the glass on this powerfully built red. Full-bodied and concentrated, the dense palate delivers cherry marinated in spirits, prune, licorice and tobacco framed in tightly knit, close-grained tannins. You'll also notice the heat of evident alcohol on the close, but the ripe fruit supports it.

title: Zenato Amarone Sergio Riserva 2018
bodyHtml:
Ruby red in colour, this Amarone Riserva offers dense and smoky aromas of dark cherries, raisins, chocolate, and anise, framed by fruity tannins and a spicy finish. With the level of complexity and balance that this wine shows, it will evolve beautifully for 10+ years. Pair this wine with Beef Wellington, demi-glaces, fegato alla veneziana, or grilled red meat. 
 
98 Points - James Suckling
 
This is one of those wines where your nose is in the glass for ages, enjoying the complex array of aromas that range from raspberries to dates, perfumed bark to polished wood, pressed flowers to fresh mushrooms. Full-bodied, dense and focused with fine, well-integrated tannins, plenty of fruit flavor and an endless finish.
 
97 Points - Vinous
 
The 2017 Amarone della Valpolicella Classico Riserva Sergio Zenato is totally classic to the Zenato style, with macerated cherries, raisins, sweet herbs, coca, black pepper and shavings of cedar. This deeply textural with a dense wave of mineral-encased dark red fruits and balsamic spice carried across a core of stimulating acidity.
 
95 Points - Decanter
 
Attractive nose displaying notes of prunes, dried flowers, green tea and hints of peppery nuances. Grainy tannins on the palate, textured and complex.

title: Joseph Drouhin Volnay ‘Clos Des Chenes’ Premier Cru 2023
bodyHtml:
This elegant and "charming" red wine originates from France, specifically from the Clos des Chênes vineyard in the Volnay Premier Cru appellation of the Côte de Beaune. Drouhin, a standard-bearer for refined Burgundy since 1880, owns a significant portion of this "Property" vineyard, which sits on a steep, south-facing limestone slope that yields some of Volnay’s most age-worthy wines. The winery's philosophy follows strict organic and biodynamic practices (certified since the 1990s), focusing on indigenous yeast fermentation and minimal intervention to preserve the "signature" violet perfume of the terroir.

Wine Description

Joseph Drouhin Volnay ‘Clos des Chênes’ 2023 presents an intense and luminous ruby color. The sensory profile is highly aromatic and floral, featuring a nose dominated by violets, wild strawberry, and rose jam. On the palate, the wine is medium-bodied and "suave," showcasing a core of ripe red and black berries underpinned by a silky, velvety texture. It is characterized by noble, refined tannins and a "salty minerality" that provides a persistent and focused finish. This 100% Pinot Noir reached an ABV of 14% and was matured for 14 to 18 months in French oak barrels (25% new).

Food Pairing

The refined structure and floral aromatics of this Volnay make it a sophisticated companion for elegant poultry and game dishes. It pairs perfectly with roasted duck with a cherry reduction, herb-crusted rack of lamb, or a classic Coq au Vin. Its earthy and berry-forward notes also complement veal medallions with wild mushrooms, seared quail, and semi-mature cheeses like Brie or mild Comté. For the best expression, serve at 16–17°C to allow the delicate violet and rose notes to fully expand.

Vintage Quality

The 2023 vintage in Burgundy is being celebrated as a "rare bird" a bumper crop that offers both high quantity and exceptional quality. Despite being one of the warmest years on record, the heat was primarily concentrated in the nights and early spring, while a relatively cool, wet summer preserved vibrant acidity and "invigorating freshness". The resulting wines are described as more "Burgundian" and transparent than the blockbuster 2022s, showing a clear sense of place and supple, juicy fruit. Critics have lauded the 2023 Clos des Chênes for its "opulent finish" and accessibility, predicting a drinking window that opens in 2027 and extends comfortably through 2050.

title: Robert Mondavi Cabernet Sauvignon 'The Reserve' To Kalon Vineyard 2018
bodyHtml:
Robert Mondavi Cabernet Sauvignon 'The Reserve' To Kalon Vineyard 2018 is a red wine from Napa Valley's Oakville appellation, crafted by the renowned Robert Mondavi Winery. This wine showcases the exceptional quality of the historic To Kalon Vineyard, reflecting Mondavi's vision of producing world-class Cabernet Sauvignon.

Blend Composition:

  • Cabernet Sauvignon: 94.5%

  • Petit Verdot: 5%

  • Cabernet Franc: 0.5%

Tasting Notes:

  • Color: Deep garnet-purple hue.

  • Aroma: Aromas of blackberry, summer plum, violet, tobacco, licorice, and molasses.

  • Palate: Dark fruits with a cedary undercurrent, firm, grainy tannins, and a finish with great length.

Accolades:

  • James Suckling: 95 Points.

  • Wine Spectator: 94 Points.

  • Wine Advocate: 93 Points.

Serving Suggestions:

  • Temperature: Serve at 16-18°C (60-64°F).

  • Decanting: Decant for about an hour before serving to allow the wine to open up and reveal its full complexity.

  • Food Pairings: Complements ribeye with wild mushrooms and vegetable tarts.

This wine is enjoyable now but has a long future ahead, with the potential to develop further complexity over the next 20-30 years.

title: Jaboulet Hermitage 'La Chapelle' 2021 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
France, Rhône Valley, Hermitage AOC. Domaine de la Chapelle, formerly under the Paul Jaboulet Aîné label, is an iconic estate now managed independently by the Frey family, who have overseen its evolution since acquiring it in 2006. The vineyard’s most famous holding, ‘La Chapelle,’ is named after the small chapel of Saint Christopher that overlooks the steep granite slopes. With vines ranging from 40 to over 100 years old and parcels in the legendary lieux-dits of Le Méal, Les Bessards, Les Greffieux, and Les Rocoules, the domaine combines heritage, precision viticulture, and an unwavering commitment to expressing the distinct character of Hermitage.

Wine Description
This 100% Syrah presents a deep, almost opaque ruby hue. The nose is strikingly complex, opening with wild forest berries, black cherries, and violets, intertwined with aromas of liquorice, cedar, cured meats, and earthy mushroom. On the palate, it is at once powerful and graceful, with layers of ripe blackberry, red plum, raspberry, and subtle peppery spice. Fine-grained tannins support a core of pure fruit, complemented by notes of wild herbs, graphite, and a gentle mineral lift. The body is full yet finely poised, with freshness carrying through to an exceptionally long, savoury finish.

Accolades

  • Jeb Dunnuck – 92 points.
  • Vinous – 92 points.
  • Wine Spectator - 93 points.

Food Pairing
This wine pairs beautifully with roasted venison, braised lamb shanks, or a classic beef Wellington, where the savoury richness and peppery spice of the Syrah complement the depth of the meat. It also finds harmony alongside wild mushroom risotto or aged Comté cheese. Together, they create an unforgettable dining experience.

title: Screaming Eagle 'The Flight' 2020
bodyHtml:
This red wine originates from the United States, specifically from the Oakville appellation within California's Napa Valley. Screaming Eagle, founded in 1986 by Jean Phillips and now owned by Stanley Kroenke, is one of the world's most iconic 'cult' wineries, known for its extreme exclusivity and precision. While the flagship estate wine is Cabernet Sauvignon-dominant, 'The Flight' (formerly 'Second Flight') was introduced in 2012 as a Merlot-focused expression of the estate's younger vines and distinct Oakville terroir. Winemaker Nick Gislason oversees a philosophy rooted in 'energy' and elegance, utilizing meticulous vineyard management and small-lot fermentation to craft wines of remarkable depth.

Wine Description

Screaming Eagle The Flight 2020 presents a deep garnet-purple or dark ruby colour. The nose is extraordinarily perfumed and aromatic, leading with violets, lavender, and crushed flowers layered with wild herbs, graphite, and cedarwood spices. On the palate, the wine is medium to full-bodied and refined, featuring a 'crunchy' energy and purity of red berry fruit—redolent of cranberry, raspberry, and mulberry—alongside dark cherry and blackberry preserves. It is characterized by its silkier texture and tantalizing acidity compared to the flagship, with fine-grained tannins and a mineral core that opens into notes of blood orange, star anise, and spearmint. The finish is long, polished, and sanguine, often revealing hints of black truffle. This blend consists of 64% Merlot and 36% Cabernet Sauvignon, with an ABV of 14.7%. The wine is not certified organic, though the estate is farmed with meticulous care. The optimal drinking window is from 2024 through 2050.

Accolades

  • James Suckling - 98 points.

  • Decanter - 98 points.

  • The Wine Independent - 95 points.

  • Vinous - 94 points.

Food Pairing

The graceful structure and vibrant acidity of this Merlot-dominant blend make it an exceptional partner for high-quality meat and earthy vegetarian dishes. It pairs perfectly with roasted lamb seasoned with rosemary and thyme, or a lean beef tenderloin with a red wine reduction. Its complex aromatic profile and mineral undertones also complement creamy mushroom risotto, braised duck, or eggplant parmesan. For a cheese course, consider serving it with aged Gouda or a mild blue cheese.

Vintage Quality

The 2020 vintage in Napa Valley was defined by extreme heatwaves and devastating wildfires, which led many producers to abandon their crops due to smoke taint. However, the early-ripening nature of the season favoured producers like Screaming Eagle who harvested early, successfully capturing small yields of intensely concentrated fruit before the most severe fire events. The winemaker's skill in this challenging year resulted in a wine that manages to be 'bright and airy' despite the hot growing conditions.

title: Chateau La Mondotte 2018
bodyHtml:
The quality of La Mondotte's clay and the age of the vines (60 years on average) result in a wine that is profoundly marked by its terroir. It is silky, powerful, incomparably elegant, and has great minerality.

98 Points - James Suckling    Blackberry, plum, mushroom and wood undertones. It’s full-bodied with firm, ripe tannins. Savory and fleshy texture on the palate. Well balanced. Flavorful finish with length. Such polish and composure for a young wine. So classy! Try after 2026.

97+ Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate    Deep garnet-purple in color, the 2018 La Mondotte strolls nonchalantly out of the glass with expressive scents of plum preserves, blueberry compote and chocolate-covered cherries, followed by suggestions of candied violets, licorice, hoisin and black truffles with a waft of ground cloves. It's medium to full-bodied with seriously impressive tension and wonderfully ripe, velvety tannin's supporting the generous black fruit preserves layers, finishing with amazing length and loads of panache. It will require a good 4-5 years to unlock some of its finer nuances, then drink this powerhouse over the next 25+ years.

96 Points - Vinous    The 2018 La Mondotte melds together the richness of the vintage with the bright, chalky notes that are such a signature of this tiny estate. Inky dark fruit, graphite, crushed rocks, lavender and spice gradually open in a dense, layered Saint-Émilion loaded with personality. I can't wait to see how it ages.

96 Points - Wine Spectator    This packs in some solid plum sauce, cassis and cherry reduction aromas and flavors, which hold sway throughout while hints of roasted alder, sweet tobacco and ganache fill in. Lovely, buried minerality keeps it all well-supported throughout. Built for the cellar. 

96 Points - Jeb Dunnuck    Coming from a cool terroir situated near Pavie Decesse and based on 75% Merlot and 25% Cabernet Franc, the 2018 La Mondotte reveals a dense purple hue to go with a rich, yet classic, regal, full-bodied style delivering impressive blue fruits, graphite, scorched earth, and liquid violet aromas and flavors. It's concentrated and powerful, yet it's the balance, purity of fruit, and quality of tannins that set it apart. Do your best to hide bottles for 5-7 years, and it's going to evolve for 30+.

93 Points - Decanter    Concentrated, as this wine often is, with a silky texture and rich damson fruits, layered deeply with liquorice and chocolate. The Neipperg polish is on display in abundance. This is serious, poised and impressive. A good decade needed here before opening. Certified organic.

title: Chateau d'Yquem 2021
bodyHtml:
Chateau d’Yquem is an extraordinary place, at the very heart of Sauternes, with a hundred hectares of vineyards are planted on a mosaic of different soils. Through a sublimation process, the grapes reach a level a richness in taste and aromas that is simply unique in the world. Yquem preciously protects its selective harvesting secret, carried out by a team of devoted highly experienced local pickers, who have received their ancestral knowledge from the generations that came before them.

Wine Description

It presents a pale lemon-gold colour. The bouquet offers a complex, perfumed profile with notes of dried quince, clementine, orange peel, juicy peaches, grapefruit, and honeycomb, along with suggestions of jasmine tea, fresh ginger, and lime blossoms. On the palate, the wine is described as medium to full-bodied, fantastically satiny, and layered.

Accolades

  • 'James Suckling - 100 points'

  • 'Vinous - 96 points'

  • 'Robert Parker Wine Advocate - 95 points'

Food Pairing

Suggested pairings should embrace the wine's rich sweetness and vibrant acidity. Blue cheeses, such as Roquefort or a strong Canadian blue, are a classic complement, as are foie gras, or desserts like peach cobbler or vanilla gelato.

title: Beaulieu Vineyard Georges de Latour Cabernet Sauvignon Private Reserve 2020
bodyHtml:
This wine hails from the United States, specifically Napa Valley in California’s Rutherford subregion, one of the most renowned Cabernet Sauvignon growing areas in the world. Beaulieu Vineyard, founded in 1900 by Georges de Latour, is a benchmark estate in Napa Valley. Its Private Reserve Cabernet Sauvignon, first released in 1936, has become a flagship wine of California, reflecting both heritage and modern precision under the stewardship of dedicated winemakers across generations.

Wine Description

Georges de Latour Private Reserve shows a deep ruby hue with purple highlights. Aromatically, it is layered and expressive, offering cassis, black cherry, plum, violet, rose petal, cedar, sandalwood, tobacco, and dark chocolate, accented by graphite, licorice, and hints of wild herbs. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied with concentrated flavours of blackberry, toffee, vanilla bean, and mint, supported by polished, fine-grained tannins often described as ‘Rutherford dust’. Racy acidity gives lift and freshness, while the long finish carries spice, mineral, and floral tones.

Food Pairing

This Cabernet Sauvignon pairs beautifully with herb-crusted rack of lamb, dry-aged ribeye, or braised short ribs. Its structure and richness also complement aged cheeses such as Comté or Parmigiano-Reggiano. These pairings highlight the wine’s depth and character.

Accolades

97 Points - Wine Enthusiast: Cellar Selection! "Fascinating, fresh and ripe fruit flavors fill this full-bodied, velvety-textured wine with blackberries, raspberries and cranberries. Subtle oak spices add interest from the aroma through the finish. Decant this time-tested wine if drinking soon. Best from 2027–2040.”

title: Penfolds Bin 144 Chardonnay Yattarna 2022
bodyHtml:
Introduction

Penfolds Bin 144 Chardonnay Yattarna 2022 is a prestige white wine from Australia, primarily sourced from the cool climate regions of Tumbarumba, Tasmania, and the Adelaide Hills. Launched in 1998 with the 1995 vintage, Yattarna was the result of 144 winemaking trials aimed at creating a 'white Grange' that would set the standard for ultra fine Australian Chardonnay. The name Yattarna is drawn from local indigenous language, meaning 'little by little, gradually', reflecting the winery's patience and commitment to an evolving style that prioritizes fruit quality over a specific single region.

Wine Description

This world class Chardonnay presents a pale lemon colour with green tinges. The nose is highly complex, offering intense aromas of lemon curd, white peach, and grapefruit, underscored by flinty notes, marzipan, and delicate floral scents of jasmine and honeysuckle. On the palate, the wine is powerful and linear, displaying a 'rapier like' precision with flavours of nectarine, watermelon, and sugar figs, balanced by a creamy texture and a fine line of acidity. It features a long, enduring finish characterized by oyster shell minerals, almond meal, and softly spoken oak spice. The 2022 vintage is a 100% Chardonnay composition, matured for eight months in French oak barriques, of which 44% were new. It has an alcohol content of 12.5% ABV and an optimal drinking window from 2025 through 2044.

Accolades

  • Halliday Wine Companion - 97 points

  • Wine Pilot (Jeni Port) - 97 points

  • The Wine Front (Campbell Mattinson) - 96 points

  • Wine Advocate - 90+ points Vinous - 98 points

Food Pairing

The intense power and mineral tension of this Chardonnay make it a superb match for rich seafood and delicate poultry dishes. Suggested pairings include lobster bisque, seared scallops, and whole steamed fish, or more adventurous options like sushi and sashimi. It also complements roast chicken, duck a l'orange, and creamy Cantonese chicken with cashew nuts. For cheese courses, it pairs beautifully with high fat options like triple cream brie, Taleggio, or aged Comté.

Vintage Quality

The 2022 vintage was outstanding for cool climate Chardonnay, particularly in Tumbarumba, which provided the majority of the fruit for this blend. Cooler harvest conditions allowed for excellent acid retention and vibrant fruit development, resulting in wines with significant aromatic intensity and a serious base of natural acidity.

title: Groth Reserve Cabernet Sauvignon 2017
bodyHtml:
This structured and 'aristocratic' red wine originates from the United States, within the prestigious Oakville A.V.A. in the heart of the Napa Valley, California. Produced by Groth Vineyards & Winery—an iconic family-owned estate founded in 1981 by Dennis and Judy Groth, famous for producing California's first 100-point wine (their 1985 Reserve)—this wine showcases the supreme Cabernet terroir of Oakville. Sourced exclusively from Groth’s historic 27.5-acre Reserve Block planted in nutrient-poor, gravelly alluvial soils, the vines benefit from the sweet spot of Napa Valley viticulture. The microclimate features intense daytime solar exposure tempered by morning fog rolling in from San Pablo Bay and cooling evening sea breezes, allowing Cabernet Sauvignon to achieve complete phenolic maturity while retaining a vibrant, age-worthy natural acidity and noble structural frame.

Wine Description

Groth Reserve Cabernet Sauvignon presents a deep, opaque garnet-purple color in the glass with vivid crimson and ruby highlights along the rim. Its sensory profile is exceptionally bold, high-toned, and complex, delivering an expansive, precise, and luxurious portrayal of classic Oakville terroir. The bouquet opens with a soaring, multi-layered display of crème de cassis, wild black cherries, and ripe blackberries, seamlessly integrated with complex underlays of sweet pipe tobacco, dark chocolate, graphite, espresso bean, cedarwood, and a subtle line of crushed stone minerality. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied, muscular, and athletic, showcasing a succulent core of dark stone fruits, blood orange peel, dark cocoa nibs, and savory oak spices. It is characterized by its outstanding inner energy and an incisive, mouthwatering backbone of natural acidity that effortlessly elevates its rich mid-palate fruit density. The mouthfeel is broad, velvety, and linear, framed by firm, fine-grained, and chalky tannins that glide into an extraordinarily long, dry, and savory finish accented by lingering notes of cassis, iron, and polished French oak.

title: Chateau Branaire Ducru 2019
bodyHtml:
Rich, intense colour. An expressive nose, a sophisticated combination of pure black and red fruits. The palate is wonderfully smooth with powerful intensity, maintaining its fineness and elegance—a beautiful acidity, propelling the wine on a long finish.

Blend: 56% Cabernet Sauvignon, 35% Merlot, 5% Petit Verdot, 4% Cabernet Franc

94+ Points - Wine Enthusiast

This richly perfumed wine has bold tannins and dense black fruits. A fine line of juicy acidity cuts through all the richness to lend freshness against all the concentration. This is for long-term aging.

94+ Points - Jeb Dunnuck

Beautiful blue fruits, tobacco, damp earth, and floral notes emerge from the 2019 Château Branaire-Ducru. It's medium to full-bodied, flawlessly balanced, has silky tannins, and perfectly shows the vintage's quality. A blend of 56% Cabernet Sauvignon, 35% Merlot, and the rest Petit Verdot and Cabernet Franc, will benefit from 4-6 years of bottle age and cruise for two decades or more. It reminds me of the 2009.

95 Points - James Suckling

Obvious fruit character of blackcurrants, orange peel and spices. Some walnut, too. It's full-bodied with integrated, polished tannins and shows finesse and focus. I love the focused fruit at the end of this. Strength with finesse. Give it four to five years of bottle age. Try after 2024.

95 points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2019 Branaire-Ducru unwinds in the glass with aromas of raspberries, blackcurrants, sweet soil tones and hints of cigar wrapper, rose petals and cedar. Medium to full-bodied, deep and layered, it's youthfully tightly wound, with terrific concentration, tangy acids, powdery tannins and a long, saline finish. While this is a little reserved out of the gates, its energy and classical proportions will richly reward bottle age. Best after 2029.

title: Chateau Petrus 2021
bodyHtml:
Chateau Petrus 2021 is a red wine from the Pomerol appellation on the Right Bank of Bordeaux, France. Held by the Moueix family since the mid-20th century, the estate is currently managed by Jean-François Moueix, with winemaking led by Technical Director Olivier Berrouet. The winery is world-renowned for its unique 11.4-hectare vineyard situated on a 'buttonhole' of rare blue clay, a terroir that allows the estate to produce one of the most concentrated and iconic expressions of Merlot in existence.

Wine Description

This vintage displays a deep, medium-to-dark purple-black colour. The aromatic profile is distinct from recent warmer years, offering a 'cool and linear' nose of sweet cherries, raspberries, and kirsch, layered with sophisticated notes of rose oil, licorice, and black truffle. On the palate, the wine is medium-bodied and finessed, characterized by a vibrant saline energy and fine-grained, powdery tannins. Stylistically, it focuses on harmony and grace rather than sheer volume, delivering a long, sapid finish with hints of Chinese five-spice and graphite. The varietal composition is 100% Merlot. The projected optimal drinking window for this vintage is between 2028 and 2061.

Accolades

  • James Suckling – 98–99 points

  • Robert Parker Wine Advocate – 94–96 points

  • Vinous (Neal Martin) – 95 points

title: Lignier Michelot Chambolle Musigny Vieilles Vignes 2022
bodyHtml: This wine is ripe and floral in its youth, with plush black fruit and crushed violet on the nose. The palate is dense and ripe with almost liqueur-like ripeness to the cherry tones and a hint of cola. It's austere now, with firm tannins supporting the fruit, but will mellow pleasantly within a couple of years.

title: Torbreck 'The Laird' Shiraz 2019
bodyHtml:
This monumental red wine originates from the Marananga sub-region of the Barossa Valley in South Australia. Established in 1994 by David Powell, Torbreck Vintners is world-renowned for its focus on Rhone-style varieties and its stewardship of some of the oldest vines on the planet. The winery's philosophy is centred on 'The Laird', the estate's pinnacle expression sourced from a single five-acre plot of Shiraz planted in 1958. Known as the Gnadenfrei Vineyard, this site features deep red clay soils over limestone, which produce fruit of extraordinary power and longevity.

Wine Description

The Torbreck The Laird Shiraz 2019 presents an opaque, ink-like purple-black colour. The sensory profile is profoundly concentrated and aromatic, opening with a dense bouquet of blackberry, mulberry, and dark plum, layered with sophisticated notes of anise, roasted coffee, cured meats, and exotic spices. On the palate, the wine is massively full-bodied and textural, showcasing a 'tidal wave' of dark fruit flavours balanced by a vibrant mineral-laced acidity. It is characterized by its seamless integration of fine-grained tannins and a finish that is exceptionally persistent, echoing with notes of dark chocolate and graphite. This 100% Shiraz has an ABV of 15.5% and was matured for 36 months in 100% new French oak barriques from the famous Dominique Laurent cooperage.

Food Pairing

The immense structure and bold profile of this Shiraz make it a natural partner for rich, savoury proteins. It pairs exceptionally well with slow-braised beef cheeks, grilled wagyu ribeye, or roasted venison with a reduction sauce. Its spicy and earthy undertones also complement hearty dishes such as wild mushroom risotto, truffled pasta, and intensely flavoured game meats. For a cheese course, it is best suited to aged hard cheeses like extra-mature cheddar or a vintage Mimolette.

Vintage Quality

The 2019 vintage in the Barossa Valley was defined by an exceptionally dry growing season and a severe frost in late spring, which significantly reduced yields to some of the lowest on record. However, the remaining fruit benefited from a warm summer that produced berries with immense flavour concentration and deep phenolic ripeness. Winemakers consider it a vintage of 'power and poise', noting that despite the heat, the wines retain a remarkable freshness and structural integrity that will allow them to age for decades.

title: Gerard Raphet Clos De Vougeot Grand Cru 2021
bodyHtml:
Introduction

This red wine originates from France, specifically from the prestigious Clos de Vougeot Grand Cru vineyard in the village of Vougeot within the Côte de Nuits subregion of Burgundy. Established in the 1920s, Domaine Gérard Raphet is a traditional family estate based in Morey Saint Denis, now led by fourth generation winemaker Gérard Raphet and his daughter, Marion. The winery's philosophy is rooted in handmade production 'from field to bottle', utilizing exceptionally old vines—many over 100 years old—to create authentic expressions of terroir through minimal intervention and manual techniques passed down through generations.

Wine Description

Domaine Gérard Raphet Clos de Vougeot Grand Cru 2021 displays a delicate ruby colour in the glass. The nose is elegant and powerfully lifted, offering vibrant aromas of red berries, earth, and baking spices. On the palate, the wine is full bodied yet deceptively light, featuring a suave and structured profile with flavours of black cherries and earth balanced by a lovely fruit intensity. It is characterized by its fine grained tannins and a robust, powerful finish that remains balanced and long. This 100% Pinot Noir has an ABV of 12.5% to 14.0% depending on the specific bottling and was fermented on indigenous yeasts before ageing for 18 months in older French oak barrels, typically with only 15% new oak. While the estate follows sustainable viticulture and avoids chemical fertilizers, the wine is not certified organic. The optimal drinking window for this tightly wound vintage is estimated to begin in 2033.

Accolades

  • Burghound - 93 points.

  • Richard Presser (CellarTracker) - 91 points.

Food Pairing

The structured yet suave nature of this Clos de Vougeot Grand Cru makes it a sophisticated partner for rich proteins and classic French cuisine. It pairs perfectly with roast pork or chicken, as well as delicately spiced dishes that do not overwhelm its elegant fruit profile. Its earthy and spicy undertones also complement roast duck, goose, and game birds such as wood pigeon. For a cheese course, it is traditionally enjoyed with Gruyère or other mature, hard cheeses.

Vintage Quality

The 2021 vintage in the Côte de Nuits was a challenging and technical year marked by wild, unpredictable weather including severe frosts and hail that significantly reduced yields. Despite these difficulties, the resulting reds are described as 'pinotte'—classic expressions of Pinot Noir characterized by purity, freshness, and transparency to their terroir, with a more traditional and elegant profile than recent warmer vintages.

title: Stag's Leap Wine Cellars Cabernet Sauvignon 'Cask 23' 2019
bodyHtml:
Considered one of the "first growths" of Napa Valley, Stag's Leap Wine Cellars produces renowned Cabernet Sauvignon from its historic Stags Leap District estate vineyards.

This CASK 23 combines the signature perfume notes of FAY vineyard with the structure and dark fruit of S.L.V. Fragrant and fresh aromas of red and black currant, black tea, anise and nutmeg fill the nose. The wine has a vibrant mouthfeel with savoury and velvety tannins and blackberry and currant flavours. This is an elegant, flavorful vintage of CASK 23 with integrated oak, refined tannins and a lasting aftertaste.

Enjoy this CASK 23 with red wine and porcini braised short ribs with polenta, honey and Calabrian chile pork chops with roasted apples, or truffled goat cheese risotto with prosciutto, arugula, and aged balsamic.

99 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

Sporting a deep purple hue to go with a brilliant bouquet of pure blue fruits as well as violets, lead pencil shavings, and chocolaty nuances. Concentrated, powerful, and full-bodied on the palate, it's a structured, tannic wine delivering ultra-fine tannins, flawless balance, perfectly integrated oak, and one heck of a finish.

96 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Approximately 10% of the wine that went into the 2019 Cask 23 Cabernet Sauvignon was barrel fermented, so expect experimentation in that area to continue. The wine is a terrific example of this cuvée, offering tantalizing floral aromas set against a backdrop of ripe red and black cherries. It's medium to full-bodied, intense, rich and ripe, yet still silky and elegant, with a vibrant, mouthwatering finish.

95 Points - Wine Enthusiast

Dusty and earthy, this is a memorable wine from the great estate. Cedar, compost, tobacco and stemmy fruit embrace a core of sturdy, supple tannin and well-integrated oak. Hints of baking spice, cardamom and clove add complexity, with high-toned acidity always brimming just below the surface.

95 Points - Wine Spectator

Ripe and forward in feel, with lots of seductive plum sauce and blackberry compote flavours leading the way, backed by bittersweet cocoa and alder accents. A nice flash of savoury underneath gives this energy, range and lift through the finish. And despite the flattering showing, this has ample fine-grained structure for cellaring.

95 Points - James Suckling

Blackberry concentrate, tapenade, sandalwood and spices, together with a lift of violets, oyster shell and graphite to the nose. Very concentrated and plush on the palate, with a full body and plenty of fine, resolved tannins clinging to the dark fruit.

title: Armand de Brignac Rose (Ace of Spades)
bodyHtml: Armand de Brignac Rose is among the finest examples of the famous pink Champagne blend ever conceived and is packaged in a brilliant pink-gold bottle with matching adornments. Its beautiful colour is achieved through assemblage, the process by which sparkling white wine is blended with a proportion of still Pinot Noir wine. The Pinot Noir is picked from old-growth vines grown specifically for use in Rose Champagne.

title: Chateau de La Tour Clos Vougeot Grand Cru Cuvee Classique 2019
bodyHtml:
93 Points - Decanter
 
The Cuvée Classique is produced from the younger vines of the Domaine. The result in 2019 was delicious, with a pronounced blackberry and plum fruit that has a distinctly brambly edge, plus a note of menthol, as well as a bit of spice from the Chassin casks. The texture is concentrated and scarcely less powerful than the Vieilles Vignes. Wonderful value in Grand Cru Burgundy.
 
93 Points - Vinous
 
The 2019 Clos de Vougeot Grand Cru "Cuvée Classique" has a fragrant nose with red berry fruit, still that touch of struck flint, fine focus with just a touch of reduction at the moment. The palate is medium-bodied with a fine grip on the entry, quite chalky tannins, and white pepper towards the prolonged finish. This Cuvée Classique is ageing with style.

title: Chateau Angelus 2020
bodyHtml:
Produced in the Saint Emilion appellation of Bordeaux, France, Chateau Angelus is a Premier Grand Cru Classe estate situated in a natural amphitheatre. The Boüard de Laforest family has managed the property for eight generations, with Stéphanie de Boüard-Rivoal currently leading the estate's transition toward 100% organic viticulture. Their winemaking philosophy emphasizes a 'priestlike' devotion to the vines, aiming to exalt the essence of the terroir through a marriage of precision, purity, and balance.

Wine Description

This vintage presents an opaque purple black colour and opens with a captivating perfume of kirsch, Black Forest cake, ripe plums, and violets, underscored by hints of molten licorice, graphite, and black truffles. The medium to full bodied palate is a display of pure energy and tension, featuring a deep core of crunchy red and black fruits supported by exquisitely ripe, fine grained tannins.

Accolades

  • James Suckling - 99 points

  • Wine Enthusiast - 99 points

  • Vinous - 98 points

  • Robert Parker - 97 points

  • Decanter - 97 points

Food Pairing

The wine's structure and depth make it an ideal companion for classic meat dishes such as roast saddle of venison, Chateaubriand, or Filet Wellington. It also pairs beautifully with earthy flavours found in mushroom based pasta or rich Asian inspired beef dishes.

title: Bodega Chacra Chardonnay 2023
bodyHtml:
Bodega Chacra, established in 2004 by Piero Incisa della Rocchetta, is situated in the Río Negro Valley of northern Patagonia, Argentina. The winery is renowned for its commitment to organic and biodynamic practices, aiming to produce wines that authentically express the unique terroir of Mainqué. Collaborating with esteemed Burgundy winemaker Jean-Marc Roulot, Bodega Chacra crafts exceptional Chardonnays that reflect both innovation and tradition.

Wine Description

The 2023 Bodega Chacra Chardonnay showcases a brilliant pale gold hue. Aromas of apple, brioche, flint, pear, and slate, with hints of apple tart, greet the nose. On the palate, it offers a full-bodied experience with gorgeous richness and depth, yet it grows on the palate, displaying a harmonious balance between its vibrant acidity and creamy texture. The wine is intense and energetic, high-pitched and lively, round and austere, refined and mineral.

Accolades

  • James Suckling: 99 points

Food Pairing

This Chardonnay pairs exquisitely with dishes such as roasted chicken, seared scallops, or creamy risotto. These pairings highlight the wine’s depth and character, creating an unforgettable dining experience.

title: Gianni Brunelli Brunello di Montalcino 2019
bodyHtml:
Deep ruby color tending to garnet with floral notes of heather and strawberry tree in the beginning, followed by soft notes of sour cherry and black berries. Concentrated and savory palate, balanced, well structured but fine-grained tannins and good final persistence.

95+ Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2018 Brunello di Montalcino does a great job of capturing the essence and the spirit of Sangiovese, a grape that delivers infinitely nuanced and complex results when in the right hands. This wine reveals wild cherry, blue violet, blood orange, rusty nail and sweet earth. There is a hint of scorched earth or baked clay that underlines the warmest months in this growing cycle. The results are balanced and fresh.

93 Points - Wine Spectator

Laced with cherry and raspberry fruit, this red also offers eucalyptus, mineral, earth and almond flavors. Vibrant and balanced, with an intense, mouthwatering finish.

93 Points - James Suckling

Enticing nose of rosemary, wild cherries, lemon peel, chocolate strawberries and praline. It’s medium-bodied with a bright, fruit-forward palate, framed by fine-grained tannins.

93 Points - Decanter

Mint, lavender and fennel lead on the nose while sweet, succulent persimmon and crunchy pomegranate provide the backdrop on the palate, and the chalky tannins are rather sneaky in their grasp.

title: Chateau Pichon Longueville Baron 2018
bodyHtml:
100 Points - Wine Enthusiast

This great estate in southern Pauillac, facing the Latour vineyard, is at the top of its game. In this release, the tannins are as impressive and dense as the black fruits. Together they form a harmonious ensemble, richly structured, concentrated from the many old vines in the blend, and very age-worthy. Drink from 2027. Cellar Selection

97 Points - Decanter

Grilled cedar and attractive aromatics, with well-handled extraction giving confident but unmistakable oak impact. This is good-quality, showing gentle raspberry leaf aromatics on the opening, savoury cassis and bilberry, with pencil lead and crayon appearing along with the tannins as it stretches out through the palate. There was one week less of maceration than normal, so 21 days instead of 28, which will have helped control extractions. Drinking Window 2028 - 2045

97+ Points - Jeb Dunnuck

A beautiful, majestic Pauillac that reminds me a little of the 2000, the 2018 Château Pichon-Longueville Baron checks in as 78% Cabernet Sauvignon and 22% Merlot that was brought up in 80% new French oak. It shows the estate's more pure Cabernet, focused, elegant style yet offers full-bodied richness and serious depth of fruit as well as awesome notes of crème de cassis, graphite, lead pencil shavings, tobacco, and wet stone-like minerality. With building tannins, a fresh, focused texture, and a great finish, it's not for those looking for instant gratification, and I suspect it will need a solid decade or more of cellaring, but it will evolve for 50 years or more. It's a profound 2018. 

97 Points - Wine Spectator

A very polished and pure expression of Pauillac, but don't go to sleep on it. As charming and vibrant as the cassis, cherry preserve and blackberry paste flavours are, they have a latent saturated feel. And then there's a serious network of iron girders supporting it all, along with sweet tobacco, floral and worn cedar accents. Cabernet Sauvignon and Merlot. Best from 2030 through 2050.

97 Points - James Suckling

Aromas of blackcurrants, blueberries, ash and cedar with hints of conifer. Full-bodied, yet so tight and refined with polished, toned tannins that are creamy and compact with a silky texture. Energetic and driven. Try after 2026.

96+ Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2018 Pichon-Longueville Baron is a blend of 78% Cabernet Sauvignon and 22% Merlot, aged for 18 months in barriques, 80% new and 20% one-year-old. Production of the grand vin represents 50% of the harvest this year. Deep garnet-purple coloured, the nose bursts from the glass with flamboyant scents of stewed black plums, crème de cassis and Black Forest cake, plus suggestions of Indian spices, unsmoked cigars, pencil shavings and espresso. The medium to full-bodied palate delivers impactful black fruit preserves and exotic spice layers, framed by plush tannins and a lively backbone, finishing long and spicy.

title: Fratelli Barolo Gramolere 2020 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml: Picture yourself savoring a glass of this exquisite wine, as a harmonious blend of macerated cherries and savory roasted mushrooms dance on your palate. The umami-rich flavors intertwine with dried flowers and shaved rosewood, creating a sophisticated and alluring bouquet. This wine is a true embodiment of elegance, with a presence that effortlessly captivates your senses. Drink Now - 2040. 95 Points Wine Enthusiast

title: Chateau Malescot St Exupery 2021
bodyHtml:
Chateau Malescot St Exupery is a distinguished Third Growth estate located in the France, specifically within the prestigious Margaux appellation of Bordeaux. The estate can trace its history back to the 18th century, but it was the purchase by the Zuger family in 1955 that sparked a dramatic restoration of its reputation.

Wine Description

The Chateau Malescot St Exupery presents a deep garnet-purple colour and a complex sensory profile. The bouquet is highly aromatic and floral, bursting with scents of black currant, black cherry, and crushed violets, complemented by hints of lavender, mint, and creamy new oak. On the palate, the wine is medium to full-bodied with a fleshy, flamboyant style, showcasing vibrant layers of dark berries, red currants, and plums alongside notes of espresso and spice. Its structure is defined by firm yet silky tannins and a lively core of acidity, leading to a long, polished finish with a touch of savory herbs.

Accolades

  • James Suckling - 94 points

  • Vinous - 94 points

  • Wine Advocate - 93 points

  • Decanter - 90 points

Food Pairing

This wine's robust structure and power make it an ideal companion for grilled or roasted red meats, such as an entrecote, filet mignon, or roast lamb. It also pairs beautifully with mature, soft cheeses with pronounced flavours like Camembert or Brie.

title: Renato Ratti Barolo Rocche dell'Annunziata 2019
bodyHtml:
Garnet red. A delicate and persistent bouquet with traces of licorice, rose and tobacco. Full flavored, warm and moderately tannic.

95+ Points - Jeb Dunnuck

The 2019 Barolo Rocche Dell'Annunziata is spectacular. Aged for two years in 25-hectoliter Slavonian barrels, it is flush with woven aromas of licorice, raspberry liqueur, pressed roses, and crushed stones. Full-bodied, with a weightless feel, fine-grained tannins, and fresh acidity, it offers a seamless arch through the mid-palate, without any harsh edges, and is packed with ripe red cherry, cedar, black tea, and dried flowers. 

93 Points - Wine Spectator

Austere, this red shows cherry, eucalyptus, earth and mineral flavors backed by stiff tannins. Reveals a kernel of fruit at the core and substantial texture and length, so give this time. Features firm grip on the finish.

title: Chateau Palmer 2022
bodyHtml:
Hailing from France, Chateau Palmer is located in the esteemed Margaux appellation within the Bordeaux region. Established in the early 19th century, the estate was named after Major General Charles Palmer. Today, it is owned by the Sichel and Mähler-Besse families, who emphasize biodynamic viticulture, ensuring the vineyard’s long-term health and the production of expressive wines.

Wine Description

The Chateau Palmer 2022 displays a deep, vibrant purple hue. On the nose, it offers an intricate bouquet of ripe blackberries, violets, graphite, and subtle hints of exotic spices. The palate is full-bodied yet finely textured, delivering layers of dark fruits, cassis, and plum, wrapped in polished tannins. It has remarkable balance and freshness, finishing long with mineral undertones and a touch of cocoa.

Accolades

  • James Suckling - 98+ Points

  • Jeb Dunnuck - 97+ Points

  • Decanter - 97 Points

  • Vinous - 96+ Points

Food Pairing

This elegant Margaux pairs wonderfully with dishes such as rack of lamb with rosemary, duck breast with cherry reduction, or aged Comté. Together, they create an unforgettable dining experience, enhancing the wine’s layered complexity.

title: Domaine Michel Gros Vosne Romanee 'Aux Brulees' Premier Cru 2022
bodyHtml:
This parcel is located next to the family parcel of Richebourg to the north. It is believed that the name originates from the natural vegetation catching fire during the summer months because of the highly drained, dry soil. The soil is very stony with a 30 to 35cm thickness, and the subsoil is made of hard limestone. This wine offers a great minerality; similar to Richebourg from which it is separated only by a 3-meter-wide lane. But the soil, which is not as thick as the Richebourg's, which brings more softness to the tannins and makes it more rapidly accessible. The wine is aged in 50% new oak. 

Aromatically the wine is perfumed with a combination of cherries and blueberries, as well as delicately aged purple flowers. On the palate, the wine is medium-bodied with brambly berry fruits, peppercorns, and smooth tannins. 

91+ Points - Vinous

The 2022 Vosne-Romanee Aux Brulees 1er Cru comes from a parcel just next to their new plot in Richebourg. I gave this three or four minutes to open in the glass. Eventually, it offers enticing scents of redcurrant jam, white-tipped strawberries, and dried white flowers. Fine delineation.

title: Chateau Pape Clement 2020
bodyHtml:
Chateau Pape Clement owes its name to its most illustrious owner. A man of the cloth born in 1264, Bertrand de Goth became Bishop of Comminges, in the Pyrenees Mountains, at the age of 31; he later became Archbishop of Bordeaux in 1299.

8 June 1937 was a dark day in the vineyard's history, when a violent hailstorm destroyed virtually the entirety of the estate. Two years later, Paul Montagne bought it and gradually brought it back to life. Thanks to his efforts, the vineyard returned to its former rank and stood up to the surge in urbanization. 

98 Points - James Suckling

Lots of blackberry, iodine and crushed stone here. Some black pepper and graphite, too. Full body and medium, fine tannins that have a powdery texture and open in the mouth. So much going on. Iodine and iron undertones with some raw mushroom bring you back for more. Muscular. 

97+ Points - Jeb Dunnuck

Checking in as equal parts Cabernet Sauvignon and Merlot, aged 18 months in 90% barrels and 10% in foudre, it offers a deep purple hue to go with a powerful, concentrated profile displaying both red and black fruits, lots of spicy, chocolate, flowery incense nuances, full-bodied richness, and an almost salty, bloody character on the finish. This beauty shows the concentrated yet utterly classic, focused, elegant style of the vintage and has so much to love.

95 Points - Wine Spectator

This is snazzed up with flashy toast, but there's ample mulberry, cassis and plum compote fruit to soak it up, while notes of licorice and sweet spice fill in the background. A late tug of warm earth keeps this grounded.

94+ Points - Wine Enthusiast

This ancient estate, an oasis in the suburbs of Bordeaux city, offers a wine that is packed with promising tannins. The important and rich black fruits reveal concentration, density and the potential of the development of a fine balance and structure as it matures.

94 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

94 Points - Decanter

title: Poderi Aldo Conterno Barolo Bussia 2018
bodyHtml:
Aldo Conterno’s Barolo Bussia is produced from five hectares of prime vineyards in Bussia Soprano, the original section of what has become a rather large vineyard in recent years. These five hectares are spread across three separate parcels with vines averaging 35-40 years old, with no vines younger than 20 years old.

93 Points - James Suckling

Pleasant dried red berries, pressed flowers and some brazil nut on the nose. Medium-bodied with spicy fruit flavors. The tannins are more in the back seat this year and this gives the mid-palate quite an open-knit mouth-feel. Finishes a little tighter with good fruit and spice.

93 Points - Wine Spectator

A ripe style, this reveals macerated plum, cherry, spice, hay, tobacco and mineral flavors. This has an elegant feel, despite the dense, refined tannins, with a lasting mouthwatering impression.

title: Domaine Jacques Prieur Beaune Clos de la Feguine Premier Cru Rouge 2022
bodyHtml:
This red wine is a prestigious expression from the Beaune Premier Cru appellation in Burgundy. Clos de la Féguine is a 1.59-hectare monopole (exclusively owned vineyard) of Domaine Jacques Prieur. The vineyard is characterized by its steep, south-facing slopes and thin, fractured limestone soils, the site of a former quarry, which provide perfect drainage and impart a distinct mineral tension to the wine.

Wine Description

The Domaine Jacques Prieur Beaune Clos de la Féguine Premier Cru Rouge is a concentrated and aromatically complex Pinot Noir.

  • Appearance: Intense dark ruby red with deep purple reflections.

  • Nose: Charming and expressive, it reveals a bouquet of ripe black fruits like black cherry, blackberry, and blueberry, accented by floral notes of violet and rose petals. Subtle hints of iron, sweet spices, and vanilla emerge with aeration.

  • Palate: The palate is tasty and juicy, featuring a "cocktail" of fresh black fruit and licorice. It is characterized by a velvety texture and a solid core of ripe, dense tannins that are well-integrated. The wine maintains excellent freshness due to its vibrant acidity, leading to a long, savory finish.

Food Pairing

This fleshy and generous Beaune is a natural partner for musky, firm meats. It pairs exceptionally well with feathered game such as roast duck, pheasant, or goose. It also complements roasted red meats, lamb with herbs, and earthy dishes like mushroom risotto. For cheese, traditional Burgundian options like Epoisses, Soumaintrain, or an aged Comté are ideal matches.

title: Castiglion del Bosco Brunello di Montalcino 2018
bodyHtml:
Situated in the province of Siena where the renown area of "Brunello di Montalcino" is found, Castiglion del Bosco encompasses approximately 4,450 acres of land, 125 of which are vineyards with plans to plant 15 more acres. The farm is located between the historic towns of Buonconvento and Montalcino. Given the truly magnificent geographical position of the estate, perched on a hill looking down onto the surrounding valleys, exposure is optimal resulting in wines of excellent quality. These are very exciting wines, new and classic at the same time.

This Brunello expresses all the peculiarity of the challenging vintage. In the glass, the wine is deep ruby red in color. On the nose, it is very intense and broad, showing off the typical notes of the denomination: small red berries, black cherries, a hint of spices. In the palate, it is complex and deep, with an elegant and refreshing finish, thanks to the excellent acidity. 

93 Points - James Suckling

Ripe berries and hints of red licorice and herbs on the nose, following through to a medium-bodied palate with fine, tightly packed tannins and a taut finish for now.

93 Points - Wine Enthusiast

The nose puts cherries front and center, intertwined with roses with heavier tar and graphite, before umami flavors of mushroom, balsamic vinegar, seaweed and soy slowly emerge. On the chalky palate, dark chocolate pushes up against the showboating cherries before a kick of spice sets up a long, energetic finish.

93 Points - Wine Spectator
