Starts out rich, with a touch of glycerol in the texture, before civilized tannins take over on the finish. Offers plum, cherry, earth, tobacco and iron notes that prevail, with a firm grip of tannins on the finish.

93 Points - Decanter

Rather than exploding with fragrance, the 2018 unveils its evocative floral scents slowly. These reach a crescendo on the palate, melding seamlessly with cheerful pure pomegranate and cherry flavours. Supple tannins are velvety in texture. Unforced and fluid, this is hard to resist now.

92 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Robust and powerful from the start, the Castiglion del Bosco 2018 Brunello di Montalcino shows broad shoulders and ample brawn. But at the end of the day, the wine's concentration remains on the medium to medium-rich side of the spectrum. It stays firmly within the boundaries of Sangiovese. Dark fruit and blackcurrant segue to savory notes of toasted spice, black olive, earth and rusty nail.

title: Joseph Drouhin Clos des Mouches Rouge Premier Cru 2023
bodyHtml:
Introduction

Joseph Drouhin Clos des Mouches Rouge Premier Cru is a red wine from France, produced in the Burgundy region and the Beaune Premier Cru appellation. The Joseph Drouhin house was founded in 1880, and is owned and run by the fourth generation of the Drouhin family. 'Clos des Mouches' is one of Burgundy's most revered vineyards, acquired by Maurice Drouhin in 1921, and is effectively a monopole (meaning the Domaine owns a vast majority of the plot). The winery's philosophy is centred on a dedication to terroir, expressed through organic and biodynamic farming.

Wine Description

The wine is 100% Pinot Noir. It typically has a beautiful, luminous, ruby red colour. The aromatic profile is complex and refined, showing aromas of red berries, particularly cherry and raspberry, that evolve into earthy, forest floor, and spicy notes. Further aromas include rose petal and black fruit.

It is a medium bodied wine. On the palate, it is elegant, silky, and harmonious, offering concentrated fruit flavours balanced by a fine structure and lovely acidity. The tannins are fine and well integrated. Stylistically, it is a magnificent and intense wine that is built for ageing, possessing both richness and finesse. It is aged in French oak barrels (20% new) for 14 to 18 months. The finish is long, complex, and persistent. The ABV is 13.5%. The optimal drinking window is to age for 5 to 10 years, and it can keep for up to 30 years. The vineyards are farmed using organic and biodynamic practices.

title: Gaja Langhe Conteisa Barolo 2018
bodyHtml:
Perched atop a steep hill in the Langhe sits the small village of Barbaresco, home of the GAJA winery. The story of the GAJA Winery can be traced to a singular, founding purpose: to produce original wines with a sense of place which reflect the tradition and culture of those who made it. This philosophy has inspired five generations of impeccable winemaking. 

Intense and enveloping notes, blood orange, plum, and mineral aromas. In the mouth, voluminous with sweet tannins, finishing with an inviting licorice note.

96 Points - James Suckling

The fresh and just ripe strawberry aromas really come through here, together with some licorice and floral highlights. Medium to full body with fine, focused tannins that are vertical and bring your palate down through the wine. A solid and beautiful wine for the vintage. Try after 2025.

95 Points - Decanter

The grapes for Gaja's Conteisa all come from Cerequio. 'Just 5,000 bottles this year, while in the best vintages we could reach 10,000,' said Gaia Gaja. The nose is highlighted by kirsch, dried cherry and earthy tones with subtle mint and peony. Cherry and strawberry dominate the fruit-driven palate, with a touch of coffee. The wine is full, with ripe tannins of great quality and moderate acidity.

95 Points - Vinous

Gaja's 2018 Barolo Conteisa is elegant, gracious and classy to the core. Silky tannins and lifted floral aromatics give this mid-weight Barolo tons of charm. This is classic Cerequio. Sweet red berry, pomegranate, kirsch, blood orange and mint notes, that are such signatures of this La Morra site, are beautifully delineated. All the elements are so nicely balanced. I can't wait to see how the 2018 ages. The Gajas were especially slective in 2018. Bottled production for Conteisa is down 50%.

title: Domaine  Clos Vougeot 'Grand Maupertuis' Grand Cru 2022
bodyHtml:
Domaine Michel Gros, established in 1830 in Vosne-Romanée, France, is a family-run estate now helmed by sixth-generation winemaker Michel Gros. The domaine is celebrated for its meticulous vineyard management and traditional Burgundian winemaking techniques, producing wines that capture the essence of their prestigious terroirs. The Clos de Vougeot 'Grand Maupertuis' comes from a highly regarded 0.20-hectare parcel within the famed Grand Cru vineyard, delivering wines of depth, structure, and longevity.

Wine Description

This Pinot Noir displays a deep ruby hue, indicating its richness and concentration. The aromatic profile is complex, with layers of black cherry, red plum, and delicate floral notes, interwoven with earthy undertones and a hint of menthol. The palate is medium-bodied yet powerful, showcasing dark currant and plum flavours alongside refined tannins and a distinct mineral streak. Aged in 100% new oak, this wine gains additional structure and depth, leading to a robust, compact finish. While it can be enjoyed in its youth, optimal drinking will begin after 5-6 years of cellaring, allowing the wine to reveal its full complexity.

Accolades

  • Neal Martin, Vinous – 91-93 points

Food Pairing

This wine pairs beautifully with rich dishes such as beef tenderloin, duck confit, or venison stew. The depth and structure of the wine complement the savoury intensity of these dishes, enhancing the overall dining experience.

Vintage Quality

The 2022 vintage in Burgundy saw a cool early spring, resulting in a gradual start to the growing season. A rise in temperatures from mid-April encouraged strong vine growth, while timely June rains alleviated early drought concerns and ensured a healthy fruit set. The summer was marked by hot and dry conditions, leading to an early harvest that began on September 3rd. The grapes achieved excellent ripeness and balance, promising wines with remarkable depth, freshness, and aging potential.

title: Bodegas Benjamin Rothschild & Vega Sicilia 'Macan' 2020
bodyHtml:
Macán, crafted by Bodegas Benjamin de Rothschild & Vega Sicilia, is the premier expression of the partnership between these two esteemed wine families. This remarkable wine is a pure representation of Tempranillo from Rioja, embodying the elegance, depth, and refinement synonymous with its producers and the region.

Winemaking and Aging

Macán is made exclusively from Tempranillo grapes, sourced from carefully selected vineyards in Rioja. These parcels, located on high terraces with gravelly, clay-limestone soils, yield fruit of exceptional quality. After fermentation, the wine undergoes malolactic fermentation in a mix of barrels and tanks. It is then aged for 15 months in fine-grain French oak barrels, predominantly new, with a smaller portion in once-used barrels. The wine is further refined in the bottle to achieve its perfect balance before release.

Tasting Notes

  • Appearance: Deep garnet color with a vibrant intensity.

  • Nose: Elegant and layered aromas of ripe blackberries, black cherries, and plums, complemented by notes of cedar, tobacco, and subtle hints of vanilla and spice.

  • Palate: Full-bodied and sophisticated, with flavors of dark fruit, spice, and toasted oak. The wine’s velvety tannins and balanced acidity create a harmonious structure, leading to a long, refined finish with lingering complexity.

Serving and Pairing

Macán is best served at a temperature of 16–18°C (60–64°F). Decanting for at least an hour is recommended to fully reveal its aromatic complexity and depth of flavor. This wine pairs beautifully with roasted lamb, grilled beef, game dishes, and aged cheeses.

title: Domaine Harmand Geoffroy Gevrey Chambertin 'Vieilles Vignes' 2019
bodyHtml:
Domaine Harmand-Geoffroy Gevrey-Chambertin Vieilles Vignes is the product of very old vines; in this instance, the vines were planted 50 to 90 years ago (as of 2019). The result is one of the most powerful wines in the cellar that shows dark, almost somber fruit, a wine that is reticent in its youth and quite profound with seven to ten years of age.

Medium-bodied, big intense bouquet of black cherry, blueberries, wet earth, leather, violets, and a whiff of menthol. Good fruit on the palette. Balance of acidity and tannins.

title: Colome Malbec 'Altura Maxima' 2017
bodyHtml:
94 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The latest vintages of the highest-altitude wine in the world are wilder and riper than the initial 2012 and 2013. The 2017 Altura Maxima Malbec has aromas of malted cereals, peat, black olives and boiled vegetables with a touch of rusticity. With time, it develops notes of soy sauce and dried tomatoes. After all, that's the wild character of the high-altitude Salta vineyards.

title: Catena 'Nicolas Catena Zapata' 2020
bodyHtml:
Nicolas Catena Zapata has an intense, deep purple colour with bluish-black tones. On the nose, aromas of black fruits – blackberries, black cherries, black plums – predominate with subtle notes of vanilla and dark chocolate intermingled with savoury hints of green olive and a stony minerality. On the palate, the wine is tremendously complex, unfolding layer upon layer of red currant, eucalyptus, and black pepper flavours. Black cherries and blackberries give way to cassis, followed by a hint of saline minerality. The wine is remarkably concentrated with a firm tannic structure providing the backbone for the lush fruit. The finish is long, a foretoken of the long aging potential of this Argentine masterpiece.

Let the Nicolas Catena Zapata open in a decanter while you grill a bone-in ribeye steak to perfection. Pour yourself a glass. Bliss.

Blend: 54% Cabernet Sauvignon, 25% Cabernet Franc, 21% Merlot

98 Points - James Suckling

Cassis, tobacco, wet stones, iron and baking spices to the nose, showing class, restraint and complexity. Medium- to full-bodied on the palate with super fine tannins. Dry, super elegant and silky with a lengthy, polished finish. Really Bordeaux-like. Juicy and long. 54% cabernet sauvignon from Gualtallary, 25% cabernet franc from Altamira and 21% malbec from both areas. The highest portion of Cabernet Franc this year helped retain its nervy freshness! This is classy and beautiful. Harvested on March 12th and 13th. Drink or hold.

97 Points - Decanter

Wonderfully aromatic and nuanced on the nose, so alive and open. Energetic and lively on the palate, this has so much spark and brightness to it. Really compelling from the first sip, the tannins ample and cushioning the slick black fruit and accompanying savoury spices. Feels lean and taught, but with so much flair. Really a lovely expression, so generous and well defined. Youthful as you'd expect right now but when this softens it will be a beauty. Just gorgeous, with a minty fresh finish. Wine director Alejandro Vigil, winemaker Fernando Buscema.

95 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

2020 was a very dry and low-yielding year, with 20% to 30% less crop, and the grapes were picked early. The 2020 Nicolas Catena Zapata was produced with a blend of 54% Cabernet Sauvignon, 25% Cabernet Franc and 21% Malbec, higher in Franc than ever, for the first time more than Malbec, to compensate the warm and dry conditions. The wine is ripe and very peppery, with 13.9% alcohol and a pH of 3.64. It matured in new and second-use French oak barrels for 18 months. It was a healthy crop with concentration and ripeness, and the wine comes through as powerful and quite classical, still a little oaky, with power and balance.

title: Bodegas y Vinedos Alion 2022
bodyHtml:
This exceptional red wine originates from Spain, specifically within the prestigious Ribera del Duero region. Established in 1991 by the legendary Alvarez family of Vega Sicilia, Bodegas y Vinedos Alion was created to offer a modern, avant-garde expression of the region's terroir. The winery operates with a philosophy of independence and state-of-the-art precision, focusing on producing a single, highly acclaimed flagship wine that bridges power with contemporary elegance.

Wine Description

In the glass, the wine exhibits a deep, intense ruby red colour with excellent concentration. The nose opens with a serious, elegant, and slightly restrained profile, unfolding aromas of ripe blackberries, dark plums, and prunes intertwined with complex hints of graphite, dark chocolate, tobacco, and subtle floral notes. On the palate, it is remarkably juicy, full bodied, and round, revealing a creamy, velvety texture supported by polished, delicately dusty tannins.

title: Biondi Santi Brunello di Montalcino 2018
bodyHtml:
Biondi-Santi, nestled in the heart of Tuscany's Montalcino region, is renowned for its pivotal role in crafting Brunello di Montalcino wines. Established in 1888 by Ferruccio Biondi Santi, the estate has been instrumental in elevating the Sangiovese grape to new heights. The 2018 vintage marks a significant chapter, being the first entirely overseen by the new team under CEO Giampiero Bertolini and Technical Director Federico Radi, following the 2016 acquisition by the Paris-based EPI holding company.

Wine Description

The 2018 Brunello di Montalcino presents a luminous ruby red hue with subtle garnet reflections. The nose is intricate and aromatic, offering notes of dried herbs, violet, orange zest, forest berries, Morello cherry, and crushed mint. On the palate, it is vibrant and succulent, with a harmonious balance between fresh acidity and polished tannins. The wine concludes with a saline touch, adding complexity to its lingering finish.

Accolades

  • Wine Advocate – 96+ points.
  • Vinous – 95 points. ​
  • James Suckling – 95 points.

title: Chateau Lafite Rothschild 2010
bodyHtml:
Chateau Lafite Rothschild is one of only four classified first growths, thus designation 1st er Cru. The vintage rankings of the Universal Paris Exposition in 1855 officially gave Lafite the rating “Leader among fine wines." 

The name Lafite comes from the Gascon language term "la hite," which means “hillock.” There were probably already vineyards on the property when the Segur family organized the vineyard in the 17th century, and Lafite began to earn its reputation as a great winemaking estate. The estate achieved wide popularity in the 1750s when it became the favourite wine of King Louis XV. Thomas Jefferson was also a steadfast customer and even visited the estate. Today, Saskia de Rothschild represents the 6th generation of the family at the head of the winemaking properties. 

Fine, concentrated colour. Solid and dense on the palate, presenting good structure and well-defined tannins. A long, lingering palate with notes of violets on the finish. 

Blend: 87% Cabernet Sauvignon, 13% Merlot

100 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Deep garnet in colour, the 2010 Lafite Rothschild is a little mute on the nose at this stage, opening to reveal warm blackcurrants, baked plums and boysenberry scents with hints of chocolate mint, violets, cedar chest and pencil lead. Full-bodied, rich and densely packed with perfumed black fruit layers, it has a rock-solid backbone of fantastically ripe, grainy tannins and beautiful freshness, finishing very long and minerally. 

100 Points - Wine Enthusiast

Almost black, this stunning wine is gorgeous, rich and dense. It's grand and powerful, with a strong sense of its importance. The beautiful tannins and the fragrant black currant fruits are palpable. 

99 Points - James Suckling

This is shy and not giving its all at the moment. Yet it is full and intense with a tightly intertwined tannic and fruit structure. Ethereal blackberry, currant, cedar, and nutty flavours. Dried flowers too. Cedar jewel box smell comes out with time. Great finish. So, so long and harmonious.

98 Points - Decanter

The black fruit notes (cassis barely begins to cover it) have deepened and softened just the merest whisper since its first few years, and it's still extremely young and concentrated. The tannins are starting to take on a truly silky, elevated quality, where the bilberry and blueberry fruit starts to melt right into them, finessed with touches of licorice and slate. This is hugely complex, and it's hard to say when it will stop evolving.

97 Points - Wine Spectator

Rather tight, with an alluring whiff of cocoa that lures you in before disappearing into the core of steeped plum, roasted fig and blackberry coulis notes. Sandalwood, black tea and loam elements fill the long and expansive finish. This seems to be lying in wait for what could be a very long time in the cellar before unfurling fully.

title: Tesseron Vineyards 'PYM-RAE' 2018
bodyHtml:
After a slightly late bud break and f lowering due to a rainy winter and moderate sunlight in spring, summer temperatures brought back balance in the vineyard, with sunny days and cool nights. Benefiting from an essential oceanic influence, ripening occurred gently and successfully over time. The organic and biodynamic methods are paying off, bringing exquisite balance to the vineyard and thus the wine. The rewarding result shows intense precise fruit, soft and deep tannins. It is perfectly balanced with great freshness characteristic from our terroir. A mythical vintage!

99 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

The 2018 Pym-Rae can be thought of as a hypothetical mix of the 2016 and 2017, with more sexiness and opulence than the 2017 and a touch more elegance and precision than the 2016. Wonderful cassis, violets, tobacco, lead pencil, and chocolate notes define this beauty, and it's full-bodied, with a gorgeous sense of elegance and purity, perfect tannins, and an incredible finish. This stunningly majestic, flawlessly balanced Mountain Cabernet already offers pleasure yet will benefit from 4-5 years of bottle age, and it should be a 50-year wine. Bravo!

98+ Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2018 Pym-Rae reveals a deep garnet-purple color and a slightly reticent, slowly emerging nose of freshly crushed blackcurrants, ripe blackberries and wild blueberries with suggestions of garrigue, red currant jelly, mossy tree bark and truffles plus wafts of bouquet garni and Sichuan pepper. The palate is full-bodied and fantastically concentrated with tightly wound layers of black and red berry notions, framed by very firm yet beautifully ripe tannins and amazing tension, finishing with epic length and loads of mineral sparks.

97 Points - James Suckling

This is extremely aromatic with blackberries, black pepper and spice. Dried flowers, too. Full-bodied with very tight, fine tannins and a racy, refined finish. Raspberries and currants at the end. Very fine and polished. The center fruit is so pure. Aged in 60% new wood barrels and 40% concrete. Drink in 2023 and onwards.

title: Catena Zapata 'Birth of Cabernet' 2021
bodyHtml:
Founded in 1902, Catena Zapata is one of Argentina’s most iconic and pioneering wine producers. Family-owned for four generations, the winery is known for elevating Malbec and Cabernet Sauvignon to world-class levels, with a deep commitment to terroir expression and high-altitude viticulture. The 'Birth of Cabernet' bottling celebrates the genesis of Cabernet Sauvignon in Mendoza’s Uco Valley, sourced from estate vineyards at elevations up to 1,500 metres.

Wine Description
This 2021 Cabernet Sauvignon displays a deep ruby hue with violet reflections. Aromas of cassis, black cherry, and eucalyptus lead into nuanced notes of graphite and tobacco. On the palate, it is medium to full-bodied with a core of ripe dark fruit, supported by firm yet polished tannins and a vibrant acidity. The wine shows excellent structure, complexity, and balance, with a lingering finish marked by hints of dark chocolate and dried herbs. Composed entirely of Cabernet Sauvignon, it is expected to evolve beautifully over the next 8–12 years. The wine is certified organic, showcasing Catena’s ongoing commitment to sustainable viticulture.

Accolades
Vinous - 93 points
James Suckling - 94 points

Food Pairing
Pair this Cabernet with grilled lamb chops, herb-crusted beef tenderloin, or aged cheddar. A perfect match to enhance the wine's complexity.

title: Andremily EABA 2020
bodyHtml:
At Andremily they are committed to creating truly special handcrafted wines in an artisan manner, their focus will remain on creating wines of distinction, never compromising for the sake of quantity.

99 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

The EABA is more Syrah-dominated and checks in as 65% Syrah, 22% Mourvèdre, 10% Grenache, and the rest Viognier that saw plenty of stems and close to two years in 50% new French oak. Its inky purple hue is followed by a sensational bouquet of bloody blue fruits, black raspberries, iron, ground pepper, baking spices, and who knows what else. Incredibly complex and nuanced (yet intense) aromatically, it hits the palate with full-bodied richness, a deep, layered, concentrated mouthfeel, and a finish that won't quit. It’s certainly one of the biggest, richest wines in the lineup, yet like all of Jim's wines, it remains light on its feet, has brilliant purity of fruit, and is as drinkable as could be.

title: Valdicava Brunello di Montalcino Riserva 'Madonna del Piano' 2016
bodyHtml:
Valdicava, located in the prestigious Montalcino region of Tuscany, is renowned for producing some of the finest Brunello wines. Owned and managed by Vincenzo Abbruzzese, the estate is known for its meticulous vineyard practices and dedication to traditional winemaking. The 'Madonna del Piano' vineyard, the estate's first single-vineyard Brunello, is a benchmark for elegance and power, consistently ranking among the finest wines of the region.

Wine Description

The 2016 Valdicava Brunello di Montalcino Riserva 'Madonna del Piano' is an outstanding expression of Sangiovese, displaying a deep ruby-red color with garnet reflections. The bouquet is layered and complex, offering aromas of ripe black cherries, cassis, dried violets, fresh leather, licorice, and earthy minerality. On the palate, it is full-bodied and structured, with refined yet firm tannins balanced by vibrant acidity. Notes of dark berries, crushed herbs, and tobacco unfold gracefully, leading to a persistent and elegant finish. This wine has remarkable aging potential, promising further depth and complexity with time in the cellar.

Accolades

  • James Suckling: 99 points
  • Wine Spectator: 98 points
  • Robert Parker's Wine Advocate: 96+ points
  • Vinous: 96 points

Food Pairing

This Brunello pairs exceptionally well with rich and flavorful dishes such as wild boar ragù, grilled Florentine steak, or aged Pecorino cheese. These pairings highlight the wine’s depth and character, creating a truly memorable dining experience.

Vintage Quality

The 2016 vintage in Montalcino is widely regarded as one of the best in recent history, offering wines with exceptional balance, structure, and longevity. Favorable weather conditions allowed for optimal ripening, resulting in a Brunello that is both powerful and refined, showcasing the very best of Valdicava's winemaking expertise.

title: Chateau Giscours 2021
bodyHtml:
Château Giscours, a historic Third Growth estate from the 1855 Bordeaux Classification, is nestled in the heart of the Margaux appellation. With roots tracing back to the 14th century, the château is celebrated for its exceptional terroir and winemaking expertise, consistently producing wines of elegance and depth.

Wine Description

The 2021 vintage reveals a deep ruby hue with vibrant reflections. The nose offers an enticing bouquet of blackcurrants, violets, and a hint of cedar, underscored by earthy minerality. On the palate, the wine is medium-bodied, with fine-grained tannins and a silky texture, showcasing flavors of ripe plums, red cherries, and a touch of tobacco. The finish is long and precise, with a subtle spice and refreshing acidity, reflecting the vintage's cool character.

Food Pairing

Pair this wine with roasted lamb, duck breast with cherry glaze, or a selection of hard cheeses like aged Comté. Together, they create an unforgettable dining experience.

Vintage Quality

The 2021 vintage presented challenges with cooler weather, but Château Giscours demonstrated exceptional skill in crafting a balanced and refined wine. This vintage highlights the château’s commitment to quality, even in demanding conditions.

title: Domaine William Fevre Chablis Grand Cru 'Les Preuses' 2022
bodyHtml:
Founded in 1959, Domaine William Fevre is at the very heart of the Chablis vineyards. Since its founding, Domaine William Fevre has been taken up with the desire to produce indisputable genuine and fine wines, bringing along a very personal experience in Chardonnay. All the efforts have but one goal – to finely express the subtle most variations in the greatest Chablis crus. Today, Domaine William Fevre is one of the most established and renowned estates in Chablis.

Chablis Les Preuses Grand Cru has a floral nose, with fruity aromas enhanced by intense mineral notes and developing lightly smoky touches. Very round on the palate, both full-bodied and refined.

Pairs well with fish, shellfish and other seafood, poultry and white meat, all grilled or in a cream sauce.

95 Points - Decanter

One of the domaine's standout wines, this immediately strikes you with its precision and clarity. Fevre's vines are from two different sites, with varying expositions - one lower down and facing south-east, the other high on the plateau. Great elegance with plenty of weight and concentration on the palate, full and fleshy. Grapefruit notes to the fore but plenty of mineral/saline notes on the long, persistent finish. 

94+ Points - Vinous

This has one of my favourite aromatics from Fevre this year with superb delineation and mineralite. The palate is harmonious and poised, very focused and tensile, plenty of energy with a touch of lime and clementine towards the persistent finish. This is an outstanding Chablis that should age supremely well in bottle.

title: Chateau Pichon Longueville Baron 2019
bodyHtml:
Introduction

This red wine originates from France, specifically from the Pauillac subregion of the Médoc in Bordeaux. Established in the late 17th century, the estate became known as Château Pichon Baron following the marriage of Jacques de Pichon Baron de Longueville to the daughter of the estate's creator, Pierre de Rauzan, in 1694. Since 1987, the winery has been owned by AXA Millésimes, and under the leadership of Managing Director Christian Seely, the winemaking philosophy has shifted toward a meticulous 'parcel-by-parcel' approach, ensuring only the highest-quality fruit from the oldest vines is used for the Grand Vin.

Wine Description

Chateau Pichon Longueville Baron 2019 is a dark garnet-purple colour with vibrant violet hues. The bouquet is extraordinarily precise and intense, offering a lavish aromatic mix of blackberries, blueberries, cassis, and licorice, layered with notes of cedar, tobacco leaf, and graphite. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied and powerful yet remarkably elegant, displaying a fleshy, velvety texture and deep vertical resonance. It is characterized by its seamless freshness and firm, finely integrated tannins that lead to a persistent finish with hints of black fruit preserves and sea salt. This blend consists of 87% Cabernet Sauvignon and 13% Merlot—the highest proportion of Cabernet ever used at the estate—and has an ABV of 14.5%. While the winery is an active leader in sustainable viticulture and environmental protection, this bottling is not certified organic. The optimal drinking window is from 2029 through 2065.

Accolades

  • Wine Enthusiast - 100 points.

  • Decanter - 100 points.

  • James Suckling - 99 points.

  • The Wine Independent - 99 points.

  • Wine Spectator - 97 points.

  • Vinous - 96 points.

Food Pairing

The muscular structure and elegant depth of this Pauillac make it an ideal companion for high-quality meat dishes. It pairs perfectly with roast leg of lamb with garlic and rosemary, beef tenderloin with a red wine reduction, or braised short ribs. Its savory and cedar-toned profile also complements roasted game birds, wild mushroom risotto, and mature hard cheeses like Manchego or aged Comté.

Vintage Quality

The 2019 vintage in Pauillac was exceptional, defined by a hot, dry summer that produced grapes with high phenolic potential and concentrated sugars. Despite the heat, timely rains in late September helped stabilize sugar levels and preserve essential acidity. The winemaker's skill in navigating these conditions resulted in a wine that combines the classic power of the region with an open, sunny quality unique to this vintage.

title: San Polino Brunello di Montalcino Riserva 2016
bodyHtml:
Introduction

This prestigious red wine hails from Italy, specifically the Tuscany region within the world-renowned Brunello di Montalcino appellation. San Polino is a historic estate with origins dating back to the 10th century, though its modern era began in 1990 when Luigi Fabbro and Katia Nussbaum restored the property. The winery is a pioneer of sustainability, having been the first in Montalcino to obtain organic certification in 1994, and it now operates under a strict biodynamic philosophy. Their winemaking approach focuses on enhancing the biodiversity of the terroir through obsessive care, utilizing spontaneous fermentation with indigenous yeasts in tronic oak vats to ensure the purity and elegance of the fruit.

Wine Description

The 2016 Riserva presents a lustrous mid-to-deep ruby colour in the glass. The nose is incredibly complex and fragrant, offering a heady mix of brooding cherry, plums, and woodland berries, layered with floral top notes of violets and lavender. As it opens, deeper nuances of cedar, sandalwood, liquorice, and balsamic herbs emerge, alongside hints of exotic spice and white pepper. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied and refined, showcasing a monumental intensity of ripe red and black fruits complemented by savory spices and a tangy, mineral edge.

Crafted from 100% Sangiovese (Sangiovese Grosso), this Riserva is matured for 6 months in French barriques followed by 4 years in large Slavonian oak barrels. Stylistically, it is a beefy and muscular wine that maintains a phenomenal sense of polish and balance. The structure is defined by firm, chewy, and tactile tannins that carry the wine into an eternally long, focused finish. While it shows wonderfully now, this wine possesses massive aging potential, with an optimal drinking window between 2024 and 2045.

Accolades

  • 'James Suckling - 98 points'

  • 'Wine Spectator - 96 points'

title: Borgogno Barolo Riserva 2016
bodyHtml:
Founded in 1761, Giacomo Borgogno & Figli is one of the oldest and most respected Barolo estates. Now led by Andrea Farinetti, the winery combines centuries-old traditions with careful vineyard stewardship, focusing on long fermentations and extended ageing in large Slavonian oak barrels to produce wines of remarkable elegance and longevity.

Wine Description

This Barolo Riserva reveals a deep garnet colour with subtle brick reflections. The nose offers complex aromas of dried cherry, rose, underbrush, and earthy spice, complemented by hints of leather and medicinal herbs. On the palate, it shows vibrant cranberry and red plum layered with savoury spice, truffle, and gamey notes. The wine is full-bodied yet finely balanced, with polished tannins and a long, mineral-inflected finish.

Accolades

  • Wine Enthusiast – 93 points.

Food Pairing

Ideal with braised beef, osso buco, game meats, or mushroom risotto. Aged cheeses such as Parmigiano Reggiano or Castelmagno also pair beautifully.

title: Chateau de Meursault Les Charmes Dessus Premier Cru 2020
bodyHtml:
The 2020 Château de Meursault Meursault Les Charmes-Dessus Premier Cru is a distinguished white wine from the Côte de Beaune region in Burgundy, France. Crafted exclusively from Chardonnay grapes, this wine originates from the esteemed Les Charmes-Dessus vineyard, renowned for producing wines of exceptional elegance and complexity.

Colour: Pale gold with greenish reflections, indicating its youth and vibrancy.

Aroma: An expressive bouquet featuring notes of yellow flowers, nectarine, and light apricot, complemented by hints of walnut and a subtle minerality.

Palate: Medium-bodied with a saline entry, the wine is tensile and focused, offering flavors of citrus and stone fruits, with a lightly spiced, edgy, almost Puligny-like finish.

Body: Medium-bodied with a harmonious balance between acidity and texture, providing a smooth and elegant mouthfeel.

Finish: Long and precise, leaving a lasting impression of its complex flavors and refined structure.

Accolades:

  • 94-95 Points - The World of Fine Wine
  • 92-95 Points - Jasper Morris
  • 94 Points - Bettane + Desseauve
  • 17.5/20 - Bourgogne Aujourd'hui

This wine exemplifies Château de Meursault's dedication to producing wines that are both expressive and true to their terroir, offering a delightful experience for Burgundy enthusiasts.

title: Chateau Ausone 2022
bodyHtml:
Château Ausone is one of Bordeaux’s most legendary estates, located on the limestone-rich slopes of Saint-Émilion. With origins dating back to Roman times, the estate is named after the poet Ausonius and has remained remarkably small in production while globally revered. Owned by the Vauthier family, the winery is known for its uncompromising quality and emphasis on Cabernet Franc’s expression through traditional, biodynamic viticulture and hand-harvesting practices.

Wine Description
Château Ausone 2022 offers a deep garnet-purple colour, signalling its concentration and ageing potential. On the nose, the wine unfurls layers of dark fruit—plum, blackberry, and black cherry—entwined with crushed violets, fresh mint, graphite, and exotic spice. The palate is rich, full-bodied, and structured, presenting a profound core of ripe black fruit accented by licorice, blood orange zest, and floral lift. Fine-grained, powdery tannins give the wine remarkable tension and poise, while its vibrant acidity contributes to a linear, persistent finish.

Accolades

  • Jeb Dunnuck – 96+ points

  • James Suckling – 97+ points

  • Decanter – 96 points

Food Pairing
A natural companion to refined dishes such as roasted duck breast with cherry reduction, filet mignon with truffle jus, or black truffle risotto. Aged cheeses like Comté or Tomme de Savoie also shine beside this wine.

title: Catena 'Nicolas Catena Zapata' 2021
bodyHtml:
Catena Zapata was founded in 1902 by Italian immigrant Nicola Catena. Nicolás Catena Zapata, the third-generation vintner, was the driving force who challenged conventional wisdom in the 1980s and 1990s, pioneering high altitude viticulture in the Andean foothills to elevate the quality of Argentine wine.

Wine Description

On the nose, it is highly perfumed, offering layered notes of black fruits—like blackberries, black cherries, and black plums—alongside savory hints of green olive, tobacco, cigar box, and a stony, saline minerality. There are also subtle touches of vanilla and dark chocolate. This is a full bodied, tremendously complex, and refined wine. The palate unfolds with flavors of black cherry, cassis, red currant, eucalyptus, and black pepper. It is supported by a very fresh, juicy flow and super fine, velvety tannins, giving it a structured, linear, and elegant feel.

Accolades

  • James Suckling - 97 points.

  • Wine Advocate - 96+ points.

  • Decanter - 96 points.

  • Vinous - 96 points.

Food Pairing

Suggested pairings for this richly structured red blend include grilled flat iron steak or a bone in ribeye.

title: Cain Five 2018
bodyHtml:
The Cain Vineyard site is truly spectacular, cradled in a bowl overlooking St. Helena from the top of the Spring Mountain District. In 1980, Joyce and Jerry Cain purchased part of the McCormick Ranch, a homestead dating back to the 1840's. The Cains were in search of a unique mountain property where they could realize their dream of planting the five classical Bordeaux varietals from which to draw one ideally structured wine, which would result as a blend of all five varieties.

Cain Five shows both elegance and grace. The nose gives classic Cain Vineyard aromas of bramble, citrus, and tar. This wine is refreshing on the palate with a nice warmth, soft tannins, and a long finish. It is easy to enjoy now, while also promising a long life ahead.

title: Chateau Troplong Mondot 2015
bodyHtml:
Château Troplong Mondot 2015 is a distinguished red wine from the Saint Emilion Grand Cru appellation in Bordeaux, France. Established in 1745 by the Abbé Raymond de Sèze, the estate occupies the highest point of the Saint Emilion plateau, a significance reflected in its historic name, 'Mondot'. Under the long-term stewardship of the Valette family, the winery has focused on a philosophy of precision and complexity, utilizing its unique clay and limestone soils to produce wines known for their power and racy elegance.

Wine Description

This 2015 vintage displays a deep garnet-purple or inky hue. The bouquet is intense and expressive, featuring aromas of warm plums, blackberry tart, and blueberry pie, layered with scents of mocha, toasted spices, licorice, and a hint of lavender. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied and hedonistic, offering a thick, rich texture often described as 'molten velvet'. It delivers concentrated flavors of dark chocolate, espresso, and black cherry, supported by firm, grainy tannins and a fresh edge that provides balance through an ultra-long, spicy finish.

Accolades

  • Wine Spectator - 95 points

  • Wine Advocate - 96 points

  • James Suckling - 98 points

  • Vinous - 96 points

  • Decanter - 93 points

Food Pairing

This robust Saint Emilion pairs excellently with classic meat dishes such as prime rib, roast lamb, or hearty game like venison. It also complements earthy flavors like truffle-infused pasta, grilled mushrooms, and aged hard cheeses.

title: Chateau Smith Haut Lafitte Rouge 2021
bodyHtml:
Château Smith Haut Lafitte, located in the Pessac-Léognan appellation of Bordeaux, France, is renowned for producing exceptional red wines that exemplify the region's terroir. The 2021 vintage continues this tradition, offering a harmonious blend of grape varieties and showcasing the estate's commitment to quality.

Blend and Production

The 2021 Château Smith Haut Lafitte Rouge is composed of 63% Cabernet Sauvignon, 33% Merlot, 3% Cabernet Franc, and 1% Petit Verdot. This blend reflects the estate's dedication to crafting wines with complexity and balance. The grapes are meticulously harvested and vinified, with the wine aged in French oak barrels to enhance its structure and depth.

Tasting Notes

  • Appearance: Deep, dark ruby-red color.

  • Nose: Aromas of fresh red fruits such as raspberry and strawberry, complemented by black fruits like blackberry and blackcurrant. Hints of sweet spices, licorice, and tobacco leaf add complexity.

  • Palate: Well-balanced with good freshness and vivacity. The wine offers a soft texture and perfect harmony, delivering flavors ranging from fresh fruits to spices, cigar box, and a hint of smoky minerality, faithful to the terroir of Graves. The finish is long and lively, showcasing great energy and complexity.

Critical Acclaim

  • Antonio Galloni, Vinous: 96 points. Described as an engaging, dynamic wine with beautifully delineated notes of gravel, menthol, licorice, mocha, and spice. Praised for its energy, focus, and refinement.

  • William Kelley, The Wine Advocate: 95 points. Noted for its deep, complex bouquet of dark berries, spices, licorice, pencil lead, and flowers intertwined with hints of menthol. Medium to full-bodied with velvety, elegant tannins and a refined, penetrating finish.

Serving and Cellaring

The 2021 Château Smith Haut Lafitte Rouge is best served at a temperature of 60–65°F (16–18°C). Decanting for about an hour before serving is recommended to allow the wine to open up and reveal its full array of aromas and flavors. While approachable in its youth, this vintage has the structure and complexity to age gracefully over the next 15–20 years, reaching its peak between 2026 and 2041.

Conclusion

The 2021 Château Smith Haut Lafitte Rouge exemplifies the estate's dedication to producing wines of exceptional quality and character. Its harmonious blend, vibrant energy, and complex flavor profile make it a standout choice for enthusiasts seeking a refined and expressive Bordeaux wine.

title: Louis Latour Meursault 'Chateau De Blagny' Premier Cru 2023
bodyHtml:
This distinguished and high-altitude white wine originates from the Meursault-Blagny Premier Cru appellation in the Côte de Beaune, Burgundy. Maison Louis Latour, a historic house founded in 1797, is the exclusive producer (monopole) of the vineyards constituting the Château de Blagny estate. The winery's philosophy leverages this unique terroir situated high on the hillside overlooking both Meursault and Puligny-Montrachet where the stony, limestone-rich soils impart a signature mineral tension and "airy" elegance not found in the richer wines from the valley floor.

Wine Description

The Louis Latour Meursault Château de Blagny Premier Cru 2023 presents a bright, pale yellow colour. The sensory profile is remarkably "greedy" and aromatic, featuring an intense nose of acacia flower, white peach, and exotic fruits, layered with sophisticated notes of grilled almonds, brioche, and a hint of smoky oak. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied yet succulent, showcasing a vibrant core of fleshy fruit balanced by a "glassy" acidity and a distinct saline minerality. It is characterized by its tension and "terrific balance," leading to a long, persistent finish with hints of hazelnut, vanilla, and a resin-like edge. This 100% Chardonnay typically has an ABV of 13.5% and was aged in traditional French oak barrels to enhance its structural complexity without overwhelming its aromatic finesse.

title: Roberto Voerzio Barolo 'Rocche dell'Annunziata' 2012
bodyHtml:
Aromas of smoke, black cherries, southern herbs, red roses, licorice. Full-bodied yet suave; impeccable. Pair with grilled steak or roasted fowl; risotto with truffles; well-aged Italian sheep’s cheese.

94 Points - James Suckling

A fresh and clean Barolo with sweet cherry, cedar and light earth aromas and flavors. Full-bodied yet vibrant and clean. Light cedar and citrus undertone. Pretty sweet with ripe fruit.

title: Almaviva 2021
bodyHtml:
Almaviva 2021 originates from Chile, within the Puente Alto subregion of the Maipo Valley. This estate is a prestigious joint venture between Baroness Philippine de Rothschild of Château Mouton Rothschild and Eduardo Guilisasti Tagle of Viña Concha y Toro, established in 1996. The winery's philosophy is rooted in the French 'château' concept, focusing on a single exceptional terroir and a dedicated technical team to produce a wine that blends Hispanic and French traditions.

Wine Description

The 2021 vintage of Almaviva displays a deep, dark ruby colour with a medium to full body. The sensory profile is highly aromatic and complex, featuring an intense nose of ripe blackberries and raspberries, complemented by notes of cedar, tobacco, coffee, and subtle hints of violet. On the palate, the wine is elegant and dense, delivering a concentrated core of fruit supported by fine, polished tannins and a refreshing acidity. The finish is exceptionally long and balanced, highlighting the wine's precision and structural depth.

  • Varietal Composition: 71% Cabernet Sauvignon, 22% Carménère, 5% Cabernet Franc, and 2% Petit Verdot.

  • Stylistic Notes: The wine is celebrated for its purity and tension, having been aged for 20 months in French oak barrels (71% new) to refine its complex layers.

  • ABV: 15%.

  • Organic Status: Not specified as organic; the winery utilizes state of the art technical facilities and gravity fed processes to maintain the integrity of the fruit.

Food Pairing

The robust structure and sophisticated fruit profile of Almaviva 2021 make it a versatile partner for intense savoury dishes.

  • Meats: Pairs excellently with grilled Wagyu beef, herb crusted rack of lamb, or roasted game meats.

  • Savoury and Rich: Suggested pairings include braised short ribs with a red wine reduction or dishes featuring earthier flavours like truffles and wild mushrooms.

  • Cheese: Complements mature and nutty firm cheeses such as aged Comté or extra old cheddar.

  • Dessert: Matches well with dark chocolate desserts, particularly those with a 70% to 85% cocoa content.

Vintage Quality

The 2021 vintage in Puente Alto is regarded as one of the best in the estate's history due to unusually cool and humid conditions. After several years of drought, a massive rainstorm in January refilled water reserves, which, combined with a mild summer, allowed for slow ripening and excellent flavour development. These conditions resulted in a harvest that was three weeks later than the previous year, allowing the fruit to achieve remarkable aromatic intensity and a vibrant, fresh acidity. The winemaker's skill in managing this cooler season produced a wine with superb balance and significant ageing potential.

title: Chateau Pichon Longueville Comtesse de Lalande 2022
bodyHtml:
Chateau Pichon Longueville Comtesse de Lalande is a historic Second Growth estate in Pauillac, with a legacy dating back to the 17th century. Now under the ownership of the Rouzaud family of Louis Roederer, the estate is renowned for its elegance-driven style and biodynamic practices, which reflect a deep respect for terroir and precision winemaking.

Wine Description
This 2022 vintage exhibits a deep, intense ruby hue. Aromas are complex and refined, featuring dark cherries, blackcurrant, violets, and graphite, with subtle undertones of cedar and tobacco. On the palate, it delivers a rich yet graceful expression with velvety tannins, a medium to full body, and remarkable balance. Layers of black fruit, cocoa, and savoury spices unfold toward a long, mineral-driven finish.

Accolades

  • Wine Advocate - 100 Points
  • James Suckling - 99 Points
  • Decanter - 99 Points
  • Vinous - 98 Points
  • Jeb Dunnuck - 98 Points
  • Wine Spectator - 98 Points

Food Pairing
Ideal with herb-crusted rack of lamb, beef Wellington, or aged cheddar. This pairing highlights the wine’s depth and character.

title: Harlan Estate 2021
bodyHtml:
Founded in 1984 by Bill Harlan, Harlan Estate is a prestigious winegrowing estate nestled in the western hills of Oakville in Napa Valley. With a vision to create a Californian 'First Growth', the estate has become a benchmark for luxury and excellence in New World wines. Its vineyard spans approximately 240 acres, of which 40 are under vine, producing wines of remarkable depth and character.

Wine Description
The 2021 Harlan Estate displays a deep garnet-purple colour and opens with captivating aromas of wild blueberries, Morello cherries, violets, and crushed rock. The palate is layered and refined, offering a harmonious expression of black, red, and blue fruits with polished tannins and a medium to full-bodied frame. There is a purity and grace to this vintage, culminating in a long, poised finish. The wine is primarily composed of Cabernet Sauvignon, supported by Cabernet Franc and Merlot. It shows excellent balance and ageing potential, reflective of the estate’s meticulous vineyard and cellar practices.

Accolades

  • The Wine Independent – 100 points
  • James Suckling – 100 points
  • Decanter – 100 points

Food Pairing
Ideal pairings include grilled lamb chops, duck breast with blackberry glaze, or truffle risotto. This pairing highlights the wine’s depth and character.

Vintage Quality
The 2021 vintage in Napa Valley is regarded as outstanding, marked by low yields and exceptional fruit concentration. Cool temperatures during harvest allowed for optimal ripening, contributing to the wine’s precision and complexity. The vintage showcases the winemaker’s skill in navigating a growing season that required careful attention and adaptability.

title: Chateau Quintus 2018
bodyHtml:
Introduction

Château Quintus 2018 is a prestigious red wine from France, produced in the Bordeaux region and the Saint-Émilion Grand Cru Classé appellation. The estate is owned by Domaine Clarence Dillon, the family behind Château Haut-Brion, and benefits from the expertise of their winemaking team. The 2018 vintage is regarded as one of the best produced at the property since the Dillon family took over, offering a blend of power and elegance.

Wine Description

The wine has a deep, almost purple-black colour, or deep garnet-purple. The aromatic profile is flamboyant and complex, bursting with rambunctious scents of stewed black plums, boysenberries, and dried mulberries. Notes of cedar, sandalwood, cinnamon stick, potpourri, dark chocolate, graphite, and camphor add exotic spice and floral lift.

  • Varietal Composition: 72.3% Merlot and 27.7% Cabernet Franc.

  • Body and Palate: Full-bodied, rich, and voluptuously fruited, with a wonderful clarity of fruit. The texture is brilliant, unctuous, and velvety.

  • Structure: The palate is layered with pure, perfumed black fruits and spicy nuances, supported by firm, plush, and polished tannins. The wine balances its richness with just enough freshness.

  • Aging: Aged in French oak barrels (average 35% to 40% new oak).

  • ABV: High for the region, noted at 15.2% to 15.5%.

  • Optimal Drinking Window: Long-term aging potential, typically from 2024 to 2042. It is best with at least 7-9 years of aging.

  • Sustainability: Information on certified organic status is not available, but the wine reflects the excellent vinification practices of the estate.

Accolades

The 2018 is considered a benchmark vintage for the estate.

  • James Suckling - 97 points

  • Jeb Dunnuck - 96 points

  • Robert Parker's Wine Advocate - 94+ points

  • The Wine Independent - 94 points

  • Decanter - 94 points

  • Vinous (Neal Martin) - 92 points

  • Wine Spectator - 92 points

Food Pairing

This wine is best served with all types of classic meat dishes. Suggested pairings include:

  • Veal, pork, beef, lamb, duck, and game.

  • Roasted, braised, and grilled dishes.

  • Hearty fish courses like tuna, mushrooms, and pasta.

title: Signorello Cabernet Sauvignon 'Padrone' 2019
bodyHtml:
Signorello Cabernet Sauvignon 'Padrone' 2019 originates from the United States, specifically from the Napa Valley region in California. The estate was founded by Ray Signorello Sr. in 1977, and his son Ray Signorello Jr. began making wine there in the mid-1980s. The winery's philosophy emphasizes a long term commitment to producing world class wines that express the unique, rocky hillside terroir of their 100-acre Silverado Trail estate. The 'Padrone' bottling is the winery's flagship cuvée, created as a tribute to Ray Signorello Sr. to reflect his character through a wine of deep concentration and complexity.

Wine Description

This red wine is a bold and structured Bordeaux style blend that displays a deep, powerful, and resonant character. The sensory profile features a complex bouquet with aromas of copious dark fruit, crème de cassis, graphite, dark cocoa nibs, and espresso, further nuanced by notes of lavender, violets, and menthol. On the palate, it is opulent and big-bodied, delivering dense flavours of black cherry, plum, and blueberry jam integrated with supple tannins and a savory edge. The finish is long and persistent, showcasing notes of tobacco leaf, herbal tea, and mocha.

  • Varietal Composition: 86% Cabernet Sauvignon, 8% Cabernet Franc, 3% Merlot, and 3% Malbec.

  • Stylistic Notes: The 2019 vintage represents a shift toward a more racy and polished style, aged for 18 months in 55% new French oak and bottled unfined and unfiltered.

  • ABV: 14.9%.

  • Organic Status: The estate utilizes sustainable farming practices, such as water conservation and natural pest control with owl boxes, and has earned the 'Napa Green' award for environmental leadership.

title: Domaine Marc Morey & Fils Chassagne Montrachet Premier Cru 'En Virondot' 2023
bodyHtml:
Fernand Morey founded what would become Domaine Marc Morey after returning home from World War I. His son, Marc, took over the domaine in 1944, expanded their holdings in Chassagne-Montrachet while also introducing domaine bottling. Today, Marc's granddaughter, Sabine Mollard, is in charge of the estate and has been the winemaker since 2003.

Domaine Marc Morey's cellars are located directly under the century-old family home right in the village of Chassagne-Montrachet. Vinification is flexible according to the vintage, with the wines resting on their lees for an average of 10 months for the whites and 15 months for the reds in a maximum of 30% new oak barrels. 

This is one of the most respected estates in Chassagne-Montrachet and Sabine's wines are consistently regarded as among the finest in the village, year after year, regardless of vintage conditions.

title: Romitorio Brunello di Montalcino 'Filo di Seta' 2018
bodyHtml:
Filo di Seta Brunello di Montalcino expresses the bold yet elegant character of the wilder and darker essence of the area’s cooler north-westerly microclimate. The vines of Sangiovese sit at an altitude of approximately 350 meters, and are carefully cared for to ensure that each plant produces harmonious, balanced yields that allow the grapes to reach optimal ripeness.

Dark peony petals mix with violet and scented notes of both fresh and dried cherry. These aromas travel straight to the brain on a lifted note of polished wood. The same aromatic allure becomes immediately apparent on the palate: cherry and fragrant petals enrobe and cushion the fine but utterly taut tannins. A very serious wine that poses a lovely counterpoint of poised structure and flowing, almost billowing elegance; stern and forgiving at once. Every nuance of aroma is illuminated by Sangiovese’s electric acidity. Even in age, when earthier, more savory notes come to the fore the floral, silky allure captures palate, mind and heart in one go.

96 Points - James Suckling

94+ Points - Vinous

title: Elvio Cogno Barolo Riserva 'Vigna Elena' 2018
bodyHtml:
Elvio Cogno Barolo Riserva 'Vigna Elena' 2018 originates from Italy, within the Ravera cru of the Novello commune in the Barolo subregion of Piedmont. The estate was established in 1990 by Elvio Cogno after he left a long partnership at Marcarini to purchase a historic 18th century farmhouse on Bricco Ravera. Now led by his daughter Nadia and son in law Valter Fissore, the winery follows a traditional philosophy of minimal intervention, long fermentations, and extended ageing in large Slavonian oak barrels to emphasize the unique terroir of the Ravera hill. The 'Vigna Elena' plot is a single hectare dedicated specifically to the Nebbiolo Rosé clone, which is prized for its lighter colour and delicate, intense floral aromas.

Wine Description

This Barolo Riserva displays a brilliant garnet red colour. The sensory profile is elegant and complex, featuring an aromatic bouquet of rose petals, tart sour cherries, and raspberries, interwoven with secondary notes of sweet spices like cinnamon, tobacco, and wild thyme. On the palate, it is medium bodied and linear, delivering flavours of strawberry, cranberry, and orange peel with a distinctive saline mineral undertone. The structure is defined by highly refined, polished tannins and a vibrant acidity that ensures a long, expressive finish. Crafted from 100% Nebbiolo (Rosé clone), the wine has an ABV of 14.5%. It is aged for 36 months in large Slavonian oak barrels followed by 24 months of bottle ageing. The estate follows sustainable cultivation practices.

title: Chateau Leoville Las Cases 2015
bodyHtml:
The Grand Vin is the product of exceptional terroirs from the former Leoville estate. These terroirs are located mainly in the Clos Leoville Las Cases, which you pass as you leave Saint-Julien village for Pauillac. They extend over nearly 60ha producing Cabernet Sauvignons and Cabernet Francs with a complex, polished expression and characteristics which are totally unique to the Grand Vin of Leoville du Marquis de Las Cases and have been widely recognized for years.

99 Points - Wine Enthusiast

This wine that comes mainly from a magnificent walled vineyard within sight of the Gironde estuary is structured and dense. Its tannins and firm character show its enormous aging potential. Powerful black fruits come from the 85% Cabernet Sauvignon in this rich, juicy wine.

99 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

A legendary wine in the making from the Delon Family is the 2015 Leoville Las Cases and there are very few wines more impressive in the vintage. A blend of 85% Cabernet Sauvignon, 9% Cabernet Franc, and the balance Merlot, this full-bodied, tight, super-concentrated, focused 2015 boasts an awesome bouquet of creme de cassis, graphite, charcoal, lead pencil, and minerality.

98 Points - James Suckling

Blackcurrant, blueberry and currant aromas with hints of black licorice and hot stones. Full-bodied with dense and integrated tannins and a long, long finish. It is all there and all about proportional harmony.

97 Points - Wine Spectator

Filled with blackberry, black currant, fig and boysenberry preserve flavors, this starts off showy, but a back end of brambly grip, warm tar, and pastis-soaked apple wood emerges slowly before taking an authoritative lead on the finish. All the while, a cool charcoal note weaves in and around everything.

97 Points - Decanter

95 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

title: Chateau Quintus 2020
bodyHtml:
Introduction

Château Quintus 2020 is a prestigious red wine from France, produced in the Bordeaux region and the Saint-Émilion Grand Cru Classé appellation. The estate, located on a high promontory with diverse topography, is owned by Domaine Clarence Dillon, the same family behind the First Growth Château Haut-Brion. Since its acquisition and renaming in 2011, Quintus has been overseen by the winemaking team of Haut-Brion, with a philosophy focused on rigorous vineyard management and precision to showcase the potential of the exceptional Saint-Émilion terroir. The name 'Quintus' is Latin for 'the fifth,' symbolizing the five directions, or the balance between the human horizon and the voice of nature.

Wine Description

The wine has a deep, purple-black color. The aromatic profile is complex and powerful, bursting with concentrated layers of ripe red and black fruit, including crushed blackberries, boysenberries, stewed plums, and black raspberry. Notes of chocolate mint, clove oil, star anise, lilacs, and crushed rocks add sophistication and minerality.

  • Varietal Composition: 62.5% Merlot and 37.5% Cabernet Franc. The high percentage of Cabernet Franc is credited with adding beautiful structure, freshness, and depth.

  • Body and Palate: Full-bodied, seamless, and integrated, with a fleshy, dense, and layered texture. The rich black and blue fruit is supported by an "electric backbone of freshness".

  • Structure: The tannins are impeccable, tightly knit, and finely grained, providing a smooth, juicy texture. Critics note its excellent balance despite the high alcohol.

  • Aging: Aged in French oak barrels (37.2% new for the 2020 vintage).

  • ABV: High for the region, noted at 15.4%.

  • Optimal Drinking Window: Long-term aging potential, from 2025 to 2047.

Accolades

The 2020 vintage is considered the finest, most complex, and complete Quintus yet.

  • James Suckling - 97-98 points

  • The Wine Independent - 96 points

  • Jeb Dunnuck - 94-96 points

  • Robert Parker's Wine Advocate - 94 points

  • Vinous (Neal Martin) - 94 points

Food Pairing

Château Quintus is best served with all types of classic meat dishes. Suggested pairings include:

  • Veal, pork, beef, lamb, duck, and game.

  • Roasted, braised, and grilled dishes.

  • Hearty fish courses like tuna, mushrooms, and pasta.

title: Chateau Pavie 2016
bodyHtml:
Chateau Pavie 2016 originates from France, within the Saint Emilion subregion of Bordeaux. This historic estate traces its roots back to the 4th century, though its modern era began in 1998 when it was purchased by Gerard Perse. Under Perse's leadership, the winery implemented radical improvements, leading to its promotion to the prestigious Premier Grand Cru Classe 'A' status in 2012. The winemaking philosophy emphasizes maximizing the potential of its exceptional limestone and clay terroir through low yields and late harvesting to achieve optimal ripeness.

Wine Description

This vintage presents a very deep purple black or dark crimson colour. The sensory profile is incredibly complex and layered, offering intense aromas of crushed blueberries, raspberries, and black cherries, followed by secondary notes of violets, sandalwood, white truffle, graphite, and exotic spices. On the palate, the wine is full bodied and 'built like a brick house', featuring a rich, unctuous texture with incredible fruit concentration and energy. The structure is defined by firm, velvety, and fine grained tannins, balanced by a seamless freshness and a long, perfumed finish that lingers with notes of coffee bean and minerals.

  • Varietal Composition: A blend typically consisting of 60% Merlot, 22% Cabernet Franc, and 18% Cabernet Sauvignon.

  • ABV: Recorded at 14.5%.

  • Ageing: Matured for 18 to 32 months in French oak barrels, with the use of new oak slightly dialed back in recent years to approximately 70% to 85%.

  • Organic Status: The estate currently practices sustainable viticulture and has expressed intent to convert to organic farming in the future.

Food Pairing

The immense power and concentration of Chateau Pavie 2016 require dishes with significant depth and resonance. Suggested pairings include refined meat dishes such as veal grenadin with morel sauce, beef Wellington with black garlic, and roasted rack of lamb. It also pairs excellently with wild game like roast pigeon or venison and savoury mushroom based recipes like a wild mushroom tarte tatin. For a cheese course, matured, hard varieties such as Old Mimolette, Cantal, or aged Ossau Iraty are recommended.

Vintage Quality

The 2016 vintage in Saint Emilion is considered exceptional, characterized by a rainy spring followed by a hot, parched summer and a golden September that allowed grapes to reach perfect phenolic ripeness. These conditions resulted in wines that are slightly more homogenous in high quality compared to the 2015 vintage, possessing roughly 1% less alcohol and slightly more acidity. Critics have lauded the 2016 Chateau Pavie as a 'head turner' and a classic of the estate, often awarding it perfect or near-perfect scores for its remarkable balance of power and elegance.

title: Vega Sicilia Valbuena No. 5 2020
bodyHtml:
Vega Sicilia Valbuena No 5 2020

Introduction

Produced in Spain, this prestigious red wine hails from the renowned Ribera del Duero region. Bodegas Vega Sicilia, founded in 1864, is widely considered Spain's most iconic winery, a reputation solidified since the Alvarez family took ownership in 1982. The winery's philosophy is rooted in a dedication to excellence and a deep respect for nature, ensuring that each wine, such as the Valbuena No 5, is released only after a rigorous five year maturation process in wood and bottle.

Wine Description

The 2020 Valbuena No 5 displays an intense ruby red colour that is clean and bright in the glass. On the nose, it offers a complex and ethereal bouquet of ripe black fruits, such as blackberries and blueberries, interwoven with balsamic notes, cedar, and a delicate touch of violet. The palate is medium to full bodied and elegantly structured, revealing a silky texture and melted tannins alongside flavours of red cherry, minerals, and a subtle hint of cocoa powder. This vintage is characterized by its refined balance, freshness, and a long, lingering finish that reflects the pure essence of its terroir.

This wine is a blend of 97% Tinto Fino (Tempranillo) and 3% Merlot, sourced from vines with an average age of 33 years situated at high altitudes. The 2020 vintage is approachable from 2025, yet it possesses the structure and concentration to age gracefully for decades, with an optimal drinking window extending toward 2040 and beyond.

Accolades

  • Jeb Dunnuck - 97 points

  • James Suckling - 96 points

  • Decanter - 96 points

  • Vinous - 95 points

  • Wine Advocate - 95 points

  • Wine Spectator - 93 points

title: Lapostolle Clos Apalta 2018
bodyHtml:
Everything started in 1994 when Alexandra Marnier Lapostolle and her husband Cyril de Bournet first arrived in Chile’s Colchagua Valley. They quickly realized its potential for producing world-class wines. This ideal setting, which was revitalized in 1995, was home to vines originating from pre-phylloxera rootstock brought from Bordeaux in the middle of XIX century. 

Deep and inky purple red robe with dark blue edges. The nose is intense, spicy overlapping with layers of red and black fruit, and cedar notes. Elegant tannins open towards a mid-palate that combines finesse and concentration, round and fresh. Exceptionally long finish.

98 Points - James Suckling

So aromatic and fresh with dried flowers, sweet tobacco and hints of straw. Red fruit, cloves and green peppercorns. Medium-to full-bodied with fine tannins that are very fresh and refined. Fine, silky and beautiful. Hints of minerals and granite to the dark fruit. Such gorgeous length and beauty. 

97 Points - Decanter

This is a luxurious red with an aromatic profile of liquorice and black and redcurrant over layers of graphite, clove and cinnamon. In the mouth, the breadth and freshness are brought together by the silky texture which flows into an enjoyable finish with refined tannins.

96 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The wine is not shy at all and hits the scale at 15% alcohol. It's showy, heady, hedonistic, aromatic, full-bodied and lush with abundant velvety tannins and a long and powerful finish where the notes of black peppercorns and tea and tobacco leaves dominate.

96 Points - Vinous

The ripe, complex, clear nose offers prune, blueberries and blackberries along with pepper, tobacco, rosemary, cigar box and a whiff of smoke. Creamy and broad in the mouth with good volume, a firm flow and contained structure. The tannins set the tone while the mellow freshness underlines the sugary profile.

92 Points - Wine Enthusiast

Aromas of chalk and ripe black fruit are subtle and delicate. Well structured and balanced, this red delivers nutmeg, dried herbs and meaty plum over a mineral texture. Firm tannins and good acidity provide support to the savoury mouthfeel. Oak flavours add to the complexity and extend the finish.

title: Le Carillon de l'Angelus 2022
bodyHtml:
France, Bordeaux, Saint-Émilion Grand Cru. Le Carillon de l’Angélus is produced by Château Angélus, one of the most celebrated estates on Bordeaux’s Right Bank. Owned by the de Boüard de Laforest family for eight generations, the estate is renowned for meticulous vineyard management and a philosophy that combines tradition with innovation.

Wine Description
This vintage presents a deep ruby colour with violet reflections. The bouquet is expressive, offering aromas of black cherries, candied violets, coconut, mint, and a subtle cedar note. On the palate, it is full-bodied and vibrant, showing ripe raspberry, plum, and blackberry fruit with floral and mineral undertones. The tannins are velvety and well-integrated, balanced by lively acidity. The finish is long, savoury, and elegant, underpinned by notes of nougat and fine spice.

Accolades

  • James Suckling – 94–95 points.

  • Vinous – 91–93 points.

  • Robert Parker’s Wine Advocate – 91–93 points.

Food Pairing
This wine’s generous fruit and structure make it an ideal partner for roasted duck, beef tenderloin with bordelaise sauce, or game dishes with earthy accompaniments. It also complements rich cheeses and truffle-infused recipes.

title: Patrimony Cabernet Sauvignon 2019 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
This elite red wine originates from the Adelaida District within the Paso Robles AVA of California, United States. Patrimony Estate is a vision of brothers Georges and Daniel Daou, who aimed to produce California 'first-growth' wines that rival the most celebrated estates in Bordeaux and Napa Valley. The winery is situated on Daou Mountain at elevations reaching 2,200 feet, where the unique calcareous clay soils similar to those found in world-class French regions and intense diurnal temperature shifts allow for the cultivation of grapes with extraordinary phenolic concentration. The winemaking philosophy is defined by a relentless pursuit of perfection, utilizing only free-run juice and optical sorting to ensure the highest fruit integrity.

Wine Description

The Patrimony Cabernet Sauvignon 2019 presents an opaque, deep ruby colour in the glass. The sensory profile is immensely powerful yet elegant, exploding with aromas of crème de cassis, boysenberry, and black currant, layered with sophisticated notes of lead pencil, cedar, tobacco, and violets. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied and rich with an astonishingly creamy texture, showcasing flavours of blackberry, dark chocolate, and aniseed balanced by a vibrant, mineral-laced acidity. It is characterized by laser-sharp integration of fine-grained tannins and a finish that is remarkably persistent. This 100% Cabernet Sauvignon has an ABV of 14.9% and was matured for 30 months in 100% new French oak barrels from the world's most coveted cooperages, including custom 'Bois Rosé' pink oak seasoned for five years. The estate employs organic and biodynamic farming practices and relies exclusively on native yeasts cultured from Daou Mountain.

title: Les Perrieres de Chateau Lafleur 2019
bodyHtml:
Les Perrières was born from the idea of creating a new vineyard, planted with Bouchet vines from Lafleur on top of the famous fossil-spotted limestone soils of Fronsac. Nine years of research and life-size experimentation were needed for Baptiste and Julie Guinaudeau to finally realize the vineyard of Les Perrières: terroir selection, soil studies, purchasing parcels, uprooting existing vines and, finally, planting.

Quality and precision of tannins, complexity combined with restrained power, and a very long and mineral finish, all of those make Les Perrières a true grand vin, and undoubtedly a close family member of Château Lafleur.

92+ Points - Vinous
The 2020 Les Perrières from limestone soils is the first vintage with massal-selection Merlot (from Lafleur). It has an exceptionally pure bouquet of intense black berry and blueberry fruit, crushed stone and touches of Japanese nori. The medium-bodied palate is structured, tensile and very saline, with taut tannins and that limestone-driven pixelation clearly apparent on the finish. Vibrant, almost steely, this will require 2–3 years in bottle. 

94 Points - Decanter
This is a wine for those who really love going deep-diving into limestone. It performs the acrobatic, trapeze artist feat of tiptoeing high above the palate with gunsmoke, cool blueberry and redcurrant fruits and flowers curling upwards. Austere and fierce, stretching forward, then softening as it opens, although it takes its time to do so. There is really a feeling that they are doing something different here, thinking deeply about what it means to link wine's sense of a place to its expression in a glass. Brilliant.

title: Les Forts de Latour 2018
bodyHtml:
From the prestigious Pauillac appellation in Bordeaux, France, Les Forts de Latour is the second wine of Château Latour, one of the region’s most revered estates. Owned by François Pinault’s Artemis Group since 1993, Château Latour is renowned for its biodynamic approach and rigorous attention to detail, both in the vineyard and the cellar. Les Forts de Latour, first released in 1966, benefits from the same winemaking expertise as the Grand Vin, offering a glimpse into the château’s legendary style.

Wine Description
Deep garnet in colour, the 2018 Les Forts de Latour opens with an expressive bouquet of blackcurrant, graphite, and cedar, underscored by floral nuances and crushed stones. On the palate, it is full-bodied and structured, showcasing a precise core of dark fruit, fine-grained tannins, and a vibrant acidity that adds lift to its dense texture. Notes of cassis, tobacco leaf, and savoury spice carry through to a long, mineral-driven finish. Composed primarily of Cabernet Sauvignon with Merlot and a small amount of Petit Verdot, this wine is both powerful and poised, with an ageing window extending through 2040 and beyond. A brilliant expression of Pauillac terroir, it combines depth with refined elegance.

Accolades

  • Wine Spectator – 95 points

  • Vinous – 93 points

  • James Suckling – 96 points

  • Decanter – 94 points

Food Pairing
Ideal with grilled lamb chops, roasted duck breast, or a wild mushroom risotto. The wine’s structured tannins and savoury undertones also complement aged cheeses such as Comté or Beaufort. This pairing highlights the wine’s depth and character.

title: Fleur de Miraval Petite Fleur Brut Rose
bodyHtml:
#99 Wine Spectator Top 100 of 2023

Fleur de Miraval's "Petite Fleur" Brut Rosé NV is a distinguished Champagne that exemplifies the artistry of rosé production. Crafted predominantly from Chardonnay (95%) with a touch of Premier Cru Pinot Noir (5%), this cuvée showcases the exceptional terroirs of the Côte des Blancs.

Tasting Notes

  • Appearance: Pale pink hue, reminiscent of delicate flower petals, with fine, persistent bubbles.

  • Aroma: A bouquet of spring flowers, including peony and hawthorn, interwoven with bright red fruits such as raspberry and redcurrant.

  • Palate: Juicy and full-bodied, illuminated with fresh citrus notes of ruby grapefruit and mandarin, leading to a subtly diaphanous finish.

Vinification

The wine is aged on lees in the dark cellars for three years, enhancing its complexity and depth. Disgorged in 2023, it has a dosage of 4.5 g/L, striking a balance between freshness and richness.

Food Pairing

This elegant Champagne pairs beautifully with seafood, light appetizers, and soft cheeses, making it a versatile choice for various occasions.

title: Chateau Clerc Milon 2014 - 1.5 Litre Bottle
bodyHtml:
The wine has a deeper reddish-purple colour. Concentration on the nose is revealed with excellent refinement and complexity. Black cherry and vanilla aromas give way to deeper, smoky, peaty notes, blond tobacco, and dried flowers. Elegance is everywhere on the palate as the lush and creamy attack expands over well-integrated tannins to mingle with generous and varied flavours reminiscent of morello cherry and almonds, with a slightly marine cast. The finish, flavorful and fresh with great tension, displays dark chocolate, saline and mineral notes.

94 Points - James Suckling

Extremely floral and fresh with currants, light chocolate and orange peel. Red clay, too. Full-bodied, firm, silky and long with a flavorful finish and salty undertone. Stones. Serious. Better in 2021.

title: Bussola Amarone Classico 'Vigneto Alto' 2012
bodyHtml:
1. Introduction This wine is from Italy's Veneto region, specifically the Amarone della Valpolicella Classico Denominazione di Origine Controllata e Garantita (DOCG) subregion. Tommaso Bussola began working at his uncle's estate in 1977, before forging his own path in 1983 by personally selecting grapes for the estate's finest wines. The family-run estate, now including his sons Paolo and Giuseppe, practices organic viticulture, striving for precision and elegance while respecting the land.

2. Wine Description The wine presents a deep garnet colour. The complex aroma is inebriating, offering notes of liqueur filled chocolates, vanilla, and balsamic undertones, alongside dark fruit jam, oriental spices, and dried violets. It is velvety textured yet lifted, coating the palate like molten chocolate with a generous body and warmth. Fine tannins are well-meshed with the concentrated profile, leading to a finish of 'dramatic length and potency'. The style is complex and powerful, yet retains a vibrant acidity and freshness.

  • Varietal Composition: 45% Corvina, 30% Corvinone, and 25% Rondinella.

  • Alcohol by Volume: 17%.

  • Optimal Drinking Window: Drinkable now, but anticipated to be best from 2029.

  • Organic Status: This wine is produced using organic viticulture practices ('Biologico, Sì').

3. Accolades

  • Vinous - 96 points

  • James Suckling - 95 points

  • Wine Spectator - 94 points

4. Food Pairing The wine’s profound structure and richness make it an excellent pairing for robust and flavourful dishes. Suggested pairings include game like partridge terrine with truffles or pigeon lacquered with oriental spices. It is also superb with rich braised meats, roasts, or intensely flavoured, aged cheeses, such as a 36-month Parmigiano Reggiano.

5. Vintage Quality The 2012 vintage in Valpolicella was notable for the significant stress placed on the vines, which consequently led to a relatively low yield per hectare. Despite the challenging conditions, the grapes were of excellent health, resulting in a high-quality vintage.

title: Domaine Comte Georges de Vogue Bonnes Mares Grand Cru 2023
bodyHtml:
Domaine Comte Georges de Vogüé Bonnes Mares Grand Cru 2023 originates from France, specifically from the Burgundy region and the Côte de Nuits subregion within the Bonnes Mares appellation. The estate is a cornerstone of Burgundian history, dating back to 1450 and remaining under the same family ownership for 20 generations. Currently co-managed by sisters Claire and Marie de Ladoucette, the domaine recently transitioned its winemaking leadership in 2021 to Jean Lupatelli, who succeeded the long-serving François Millet. The winery's philosophy is rooted in preserving the 'true soul' of Chambolle-Musigny through meticulous vineyard care and a traditional approach that favors longevity.

Wine Description

This Grand Cru presents a clear ruby appearance and a medium to full body with a generous, sappy mouthfeel. The sensory profile is highly complex, featuring an aromatic nose of sweet red cherry, ripe strawberry, and violet, accented by notes of alpine forest, cedar, white pepper, and a touch of cacao. On the palate, the 2023 vintage is described as crunchy and structured yet 'open-knit', delivering layers of fresh dark fruit balanced by ferocious acidity and soil-drenched tannins. The finish is remarkably long and saline, highlighted by a wave of salty minerality.

  • Varietal Composition: 100% Pinot Noir.

  • Stylistic Notes: The 2023 release utilized 50% whole cluster fermentation and was aged in French oak barrels with 30% new wood, resulting in a wine that is currently 'raw and unformed' but possesses immense intensity and tension.

  • ABV: While typical regional levels for this vintage range between 13.3% and 13.8%, specific bottlings for this producer generally maintain balanced alcohol levels consistent with Grand Cru standards.
